title: Artificial-Intelligence-Driven Marine Biosensors: From Smart Materials Design to Intelligent Ocean Monitoring
abstract: Marine environmental monitoring is critical for ecological preservation, climate regulation, and the sustainability of the blue economy. However, traditional marine biosensors face severe bottlenecks when deployed in situ, driven by the overwhelming matrix effects of high salinity, aggressive biofouling, and highly fluctuating physical parameters across variable ocean scales. abstract: Marine organisms represent a rich but underexplored source of bioactive peptides with potential applications in therapeutics, nutraceuticals, and biotechnology. title: Integrated use of remote sensing techniques and machine learning in assessing soil salinity: current approaches, methods, and future perspectives
abstract: Soil salinity, driven by climate change and human activities, threatens global food security across over 412 million hectares, requiring precise monitoring. Traditional methods are accurate but costly and time-consuming. This review synthesizes recent advances integrating remote sensing (RS; UAVs, satellites, hyperspectral) with machine learning (ML; Random Forest, SVM, ANN) for soil salinity assessment. abstract: Coastal regions are increasingly vulnerable to flooding due to extreme events and sea-level rise driven by climate change. Effective Early Warning Systems (EWSs) are essential for enhancing resilience and enabling proactive disaster management. Traditional EWSs often rely on physically-based numerical models to simulate flood scenarios. abstract: Concrete breakwaters, piers, and offshore foundations deteriorate under the combined action of saltwater, temperature cycling, and biological growth. abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has a profound impact on animal and human health and is associated with substantial morbidity, mortality and public health costs. title: Direct prediction of wave transmission by coastal vegetation using artificial neural networks
abstract: Accurate prediction of wave attenuation by coastal vegetation remains a critical challenge in coastal engineering, with no generally accepted empirical formulas currently available. Existing theoretical or numerical models rely on the drag coefficient Cd as an intermediate variable when calculating wave attenuation, but the available empirical formulas for this coefficient lack universality, and have limited prediction accuracy. The present study addresses this problem by applying artificial neural network (ANN) techniques to build models that predict the wave attenuation coefficient directly.

abstract: Protecting and restoring marine coastal ecosystems is essential to achieving Net Zero targets and counteracting biodiversity loss. Seagrass meadows are particularly important marine nature-based solutions due to their ability to store carbon, support biodiversity, and protect coastlines from extreme weather events. abstract: Scientific innovation has become an essential driver of economic growth, technological transformation, environmental protection, and societal development. abstract: Coastal landscapes experience overlapping environmental pressures that require integrated spatial assessment. abstract: Abstract Marine structures such as ships and offshore platforms often suffer structural deformation during service due to factors including collision and corrosion. abstract: Skin cancer is most common diseases find in humans worldwide and early detection can be assist to improve the doctors’ diagnosis. abstract: Abstract As offshore wind develops toward deeper waters and larger turbine capacities, geotechnical challenges are becoming increasingly complex, involving more variable seabed conditions, larger foundation dimensions, and stricter lifecycle reliability and cost-control requirements. abstract: Humans have keen interests with artificial objects. We consume food and drinks containing artificial coloring while FIFA approves the use of artificial turf for football matches. abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) underwater acoustic transmission loss prediction is critical for sonar operational applications and marine environmental monitoring, yet the computational cost of traditional numerical models is prohibitively high. This study addresses this management gap by developing and validating a satellite-based operational monitoring framework for one of the polluted creeks in the Chennai metropolitan city, and adjacent coastal waters of the Bay of Bengal, India. title: Repurposed smart tuna-fishing buoys provide real-time intelligence for marine conservation and ocean observation
abstract: Abstract End-of-use echosounder buoys developed for industrial tuna fishing offer a largely untapped opportunity to expand ocean monitoring using existing fisheries technology. Here we present a technology-transfer and pilot feasibility study testing whether repurposed smart-buoys can operate as short-term autonomous platforms for marine conservation monitoring and ocean observation. title: Web-Based and Mobile AI Tools in Southeast Asian Higher Education: A Systematic Review and Thematic Synthesis
abstract: Web-based and mobile artificial intelligence tools have spread rapidly in Southeast Asian universities, yet evidence on what they achieved in real learning remained fragmented. This systematic review synthesised empirical studies that implemented or evaluated such tools in degree-level higher education in Southeast Asia between 2021 and 2026. Following the PRISMA 2020 guideline, 642 Scopus records were screened, 79 full texts were assessed and 59 studies were included. abstract: Abstract. Low-visibility events (LVEs) threaten transportation safety and human health, yet accurately identifying them at a regional scale remains challenging. title: Detection of trade in products derived from threatened species using machine learning and a smartphone application
abstract: Illegal and unsustainable wildlife trade remains a major conservation challenge and is increasingly shifting to online marketplaces where monitoring is difficult. To address this gap, we used real-world images from online platforms, enforcement seizures, and market inspections to develop a deep-learning object detection framework to identify products derived from three highly traded species: elephant, pangolin, and tiger. title: A framework for genome-wide characterization of DNA methylation and variant effect prediction
abstract: DNA methylation plays a critical role in many essential biological processes, including transcriptional regulation, genomic imprinting, chromosomal maintenance, genomic stability and development, and has phenotypic and disease impacts. However, genome-wide characterization of methylation patterns across cell types and tissues remains a major challenge. title: Evaluating ice shelf basal melt rates in the Southern Ocean high-resolution model against satellite remote sensing
abstract: Ice shelf melt rates by a warm ocean have a critical impact on ice sheet mass balance in Antarctica and in turn on the rates of sea level rise. Validating and tuning modeled ice shelf melt rates is a challenge. Here we discuss the issues by presenting validation of melt rates calculated from the Southern Ocean high-resolution model (SOhi) over the year 2007. abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly become an issue of global governance, raising questions not only about technological development but also about norms, authority, identity, and international order. abstract: Ocean justice seeks to assign responsibility to actors responsible for environmental harm. Yet regulatory efforts to restore ocean health often fail to consider the political and institutional structures that have enabled such injustices. As a result, these governance mechanisms disproportionately shift the burden of remediation to marginalized, underserved, and racialized communities. This article argues that ocean justice needs to reorient its focus to address systemic and structural inequities. abstract: Disaster management in the hospital has become a critical issue especially with the coming of COVID-19 pandemics which caused several losses of lives. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Marine macroalgae rely on interactions with associated bacteria for growth and development. abstract: The deep learning revolution cultivated the emergence of predictive tools, known as oracles, that do not directly improve understanding of predicted phenomena. The rise of oracles conjures an alarming vision of a new physics devoid of understanding. This unsettling prospect raises the question of whether models that offer little understanding can nevertheless be legitimate scientific tools. abstract: Abstract The incorporation of polypropylene fibers (PPF) enhances concrete’s flexural performance but often reduces workability, creating a critical trade-off in mix design. This study employs data-driven modeling using artificial neural networks (ANN) and response surface methodology (RSM) to determine the optimal PPF content by balancing flexural strength enhancement and workability retention. abstract: Abstract Neural networks (NN) are embraced to model complex systems based only on data, but their opacity remains a concern. abstract: Verifying the authenticity of handwritten signatures remains a vital challenge in biometric security systems, especially in financial, legal, and administrative domains. This work presents a deep learning–based framework for automated offline signature authentication using transfer learning with MobileNetV2. abstract: Ocean warming (OW) and ocean acidification (OA) are expected to have wide-ranging consequences for populations in marine systems caused by organism-level responses at a range of life history stages, including early larval stages. The Atlantic sea scallop, Placopecten magellanicus, is an economically important bivalve species that may be vulnerable to ocean change, but larval responses remain unclear. abstract: Assessing maritime risk in seasonally ice-covered seas is challenging, particularly where dense shipping activity, severe ice conditions, and offshore wind infrastructure interact. This study develops a regional-scale framework integrating geographic information systems and multi-criteria decision analysis to assess interaction risks between maritime traffic and offshore wind farms (OWFs) in the Northern Baltic Sea. abstract: This systematic review focuses on the latest developments and challenges in cardiorespiratory monitoring technology, capable of functioning in the unique conditions of space to ensure the health and safety of astronauts during prolonged missions. abstract: Dust deposition is a critical nutrient supply route for ocean ecosystems, yet the ecological implications of vertical transport polarity (updraft vs. downdraft) have not been systematically quantified. abstract: A thorough understanding of the global carbon pools and cycle is essential for understanding and predicting the effects of climate change. Coastal waters play a key role in the global carbon cycle but remain poorly understood due to their optical complexity, high spatial variability, and sensitivity to climate change. Satellite remote sensing data can provide high spatial and temporal resolution for carbon monitoring at local, regional, and global scales. abstract: Coral recruitment depends on the ability of larvae to identify suitable benthic substrates, and non-geniculate coralline algae are among the most important natural facilitators of this process. Within this group, members of the Lithophyllum prototypum complex are repeatedly associated with high coral settlement responses, but the mechanisms underlying this effect remain incompletely understood. title: Inteligencia artificial y autonomía funcional: límites ontológicos a la atribución de subjetividad jurídica
abstract: La rápida expansión de sistemas de inteligencia artificial dotados de capacidades de deliberación instrumental ha intensificado las propuestas orientadas a extender subjetividad jurídica a entidades caracterizadas por formas crecientemente sofisticadas de autonomía operativa, tensionando los fundamentos antropocéntricos de la teoría jurídica contemporánea. El presente artículo analiza si la autonomía funcional constituye fundamento suficiente para la imputación normativa mediante una metodología doctrinal-analítica sustentada en teoría jurídica, filosofía de la mente y filosofía moral. abstract: The People’s Liberation Army (PLA) is turning towards technology-intensive, and increasingly AI-enabled, wargaming. Alessandro Arduino and Rong Yuan contend that the principal divergence with the West lies not in whether AI is used at all, but in the degree to which Chinese writings envision AI as part of a wider human–machine decision architecture. abstract: Spatial art layout in two-dimensional visual design requires coordinated control of information communication, visual balance, element alignment, and geometric feasibility. Existing methods mainly generate compositions or assign global scores, leaving element-level repair underexplored. This study formulates spatial art layout as typed elements on a normalized canvas and proposes a deep-learning-assisted adaptive bounding-box optimization framework. abstract: Machine learning has been widely applied to reservoir fluid prediction; however, its performance strongly depends on the quantity, representativeness, and class distribution of training samples. In practical exploration and development, labeled fluid samples are commonly derived from limited well-log data and are therefore insufficient to capture the range of fluid responses under complex reservoir conditions, restricting model generalization. title: Challenges and Opportunities in Interdisciplinary Training: Analysis of a Virtual Learning Experience in Artificial Intelligence for the Healthcare Sector
abstract: Advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), coupled with processing power and data availability, are rapidly transforming clinical practice, biomedical research, and hospital management. Therefore, it is essential that healthcare professionals acquire new skills to interact with these tools effectively, ethically, and safely. abstract: Introduction Bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ) rely on whistle vocalisations for group cohesion and coordination. Although whistle characteristics are shaped by a wide range of factors, the combined effects of social structure, habitat characteristics and marine traffic remain poorly understood in the eastern Mediterranean. abstract: Lawful cultural extraction may leave chokepoints intact while making them harder to see. This article examines that risk in European Union copyright and AI governance. Combining doctrinal legal analysis with legal political economy, it applies Giblin and Doctorow’s account of chokepoint capitalism to cultural inputs and AI-generated outputs, distinguishing barriers, practical dependency, intermediary control and capture. title: Feeding AI with heritage is not enough: the limits of data must remain interpretable
abstract: Artificial intelligence is used to describe, organise and interpret cultural heritage collections, yet discussion often focuses on what systems can produce rather than on the knowledge embodied in their data. This contribution approaches that problem through underwater archaeology, where the material traces of a shipwreck are encountered through historical documents, nautical charts, acoustic surveys, photographs, oral testimony and family memories. abstract: One of the major challenges in forecasting is the rapid intensification (RI) of tropical cyclones, wherein cyclone intensity can increase rapidly under dynamic and changing atmospheric and oceanic conditions. This paper explores how a hybrid artificial intelligence (AI)-physics model can be used to enhance tropical cyclone RI forecasting. abstract: Delayed detection of anomalies in industrial heat exchangers compromises their efficiency and operational reliability. abstract: In Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), secure and energy-efficient data aggregation has been challenging due to limited energy supply, dynamic nature of the network, and presence of malicious nodes. abstract: Microplastic-associated biofilms can concentrate microorganisms, mobile genetic elements, and co-selective chemicals, but globally comparable measurements of plastisphere antimicrobial resistance (AMR) remain sparse. title: Large-volume sampling enhances eDNA monitoring of endangered marine species
abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has emerged as a powerful tool for detecting marine biodiversity, particularly for monitoring elusive or endangered species. However, traditional eDNA sampling protocols often rely on small water volumes (≤2 L), which can limit detection sensitivity, especially in vast and dynamic marine environments. Here, we evaluated the effectiveness of large-volume eDNA enrichment (5–50 L) for improving the detection probability of endangered marine species, using metabarcoding and quantitative PCR (qPCR) designed for Balaenoptera brydei (Bryde’s Whale). title: Environmental DNA (eDNA) application in bioassessment of complex aquatic environments: Challenges and optimization
abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has emerged as a powerful tool for aquatic biodiversity assessment. However, its application in complex aquatic environments remains constrained by multiple interacting environmental factors. This review systematically synthesizes the major challenges facing eDNA-based monitoring across four representative environmental scenarios: high suspended sediment concentrations, complex water qualities, intensive hydrodynamics, and extreme contrasts in nutrients, all of which can substantially affect eDNA persistence, transport, recovery, and detection. abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of hydrogen sorption in fine-grained geological materials is essential for subsurface energy systems. abstract: The natural degradation of macroplastics (MAPs), particularly polyethylene (PE), takes a long time and can lead to the persistence of microplastics (MPs) in the marine environment. In recent years, research has focused on alternative methods to traditional ones for plastic degradation, particularly biodegradation through microbial activity. abstract: Metal casting by sand molds is one of the most fundamental manufacturing processes. A foundry is where metal castings are produced, and these castings serve as raw material for subsequent processing. Sand molds have conflicting properties, so this research focuses on an optimization problem: balancing these properties to produce high-quality metal castings. title: Seasonal habitat dynamics and anthropogenic exposure of loggerhead turtles at a global scale
abstract: Loggerhead turtles (Caretta caretta) are highly migratory marine reptiles whose seasonal habitat shifts can alter their exposure to fisheries, vessel traffic, and plastic pollution. abstract: Este artículo analiza críticamente la relación entre inteligencia artificial, interoperabilidad de datos y fiscalización tributaria en Colombia. Examina cómo las herramientas analíticas pueden apoyar la gestión del riesgo y qué salvaguardas requieren para respetar el debido proceso y la protección de datos. abstract: La volatilidad del mercado, las nuevas regulaciones y las demandas de sostenibilidad, convierten la salud financiera en un factor clave para la permanencia y la competitividad de las empresas inmobiliarias. Sin embargo, la literatura actual presenta enfoques dispersos y una escasa integración entre los indicadores financieros tradicionales y las variables estratégicas a largo plazo. abstract: Seabirds face myriad threats on land and at sea resulting in widespread population declines. Predictive species distribution models (SDMs) provide a powerful tool to estimate numbers of birds exposed to risks, and to attribute them to source populations. The Atlantic population of Leach’s Storm-petrel ( Hydrobates leucorhous ) has declined rapidly in recent decades; however, information on their exposure to threats at sea is lacking. abstract: This study's central objective is to analyze the environmental impacts of using potable water resources to cool artificial intelligence data centers. abstract: La competencia por el poder global se extiende al control de las infraestructuras digitales, los datos y las capacidades de innovación. abstract: Landslides are a major geological hazard that poses serious risks to infrastructure, transportation networks, and populations. This study develops a framework for evaluating landslide risk in the Uttarkashi District of Uttarakhand, India, using GIS and machine learning. abstract: El presente artículo analiza la relación entre la ciberseguridad y la inteligencia artificial (IA) en México desde una perspectiva comparada con Estados Unidos de América, China e Israel. abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are extensively employed in environmental monitoring, healthcare, industrial automation, military surveillance, and security applications. abstract: This paper analyzes the considerable impact of artificial intelligence (AI) and digitalization on energy markets and trading systems, as well as the expanding electric vehicle (EV) industry and its challenges. abstract: O artigo explora as ideias de Michel Foucault e sua aplicação ao contexto contemporâneo da inteligência artificial (IA). abstract: The success of precision fishing methods using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) heavily relies on the sensor's accuracy in detecting thermal anomalies on the water surface. The survey integrated floating debris tracking, inundation tracing, and local inquiries to determine the seawater inundation edge points, water depths, and overall extent of the flooding. abstract: Abstract Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 has caused extensive damage to forests, particularly in eastern and southern regions with sustained combat, where field shelterbelts have often been used as cover and subsequently heavily destroyed. This study presents a systematic region-scale assessment of pre-war shelterbelt area and war-related loss between 2021 and 2025 using 3 m PlanetScope imagery and deep learning. title: Depreciation
abstract: Depreciation has been and remains a source of confusion and dispute amongst economists. Failure to use clear, valid and self-consistent definitions for output (GDP), depreciation (δ) and income (NDP) is one major cause. Definitions of depreciation are varied and imprecise with obsolescence being the exception. It is usually assumed, without evidence, to be the most important. It is, however, measurable but it has not, as far as I can find, previously been measured. abstract: Brachyura taxa serve as key bioindicators of tidal flat ecosystems, yet traditional monitoring methods are labor-intensive, ecologically invasive, and subject to access constraints. Here, we present a non-invasive monitoring approach combining unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery with a U-Net semantic segmentation model to detect and classify Brachyura species directly on the tidal flat surface. title: An Ensemble of Small Convolutional Neural Networks for Identifying Monogeneans of the Order Dactylogyridea from Digital Photographs
abstract: Fish diseases pose a serious obstacle to the economic stability of aquaculture. Correct and timely identification of the causative agent is a necessary condition for carrying out veterinary and sanitary measures, making it possible to prevent mass fish mortality. However, many fish farms lack the laboratory infrastructure and specialists required for detailed analysis. This paper proposes an ensemble of three compact convolutional neural networks for identifying monogeneans of the order Dactylogyridea in photographs obtained through the eyepiece of a light microscope using a smartphone camera.

title: Alteration in coastal land utilization and prospective modeling for Parepare Bay, Indonesia
abstract: Coastal zones, marked by dynamic natural processes and human activities, require a profound understanding of land use and land cover (LULC) change. abstract: Abstract Seismic noise, particularly the microseism generated by the oceans, is a fundamental limitation on using short period (1–10 s) teleseismic data to study the deep Earth. Here, we provide a demonstration of their potential for improving the quality of deep Earth seismic data, using S diff post‐cursors generated by ultra‐low velocity zones (ULVZs) as a case study. abstract: This text analyzes the differences between a text written by a human and one produced by AI. Based on concrete experiences, the author demonstrates that texts produced by AI supplant what she calls the “voice” of a human author, since they produce impersonal, aseptic, and complacent versions of the content a human wishes to create. abstract: En este ensayo se analiza la relación entre cultura digital, lengua escrita e identidad profesional en la educación universitaria. abstract: Three-dimensional ocean dynamics are expensive to resolve and expensive to learn: fully three-dimensional convolutional networks scale poorly with depth, while two-dimensional networks cannot represent the vertical structure of the flow. We address this trade-off by adapting a super-resolution U-Net -previously validated on two-dimensional shallow-water systems- with explicit vertical-coordinate conditioning, so that a two-dimensional network produces depth-resolved three-dimensional corrections. title: A Graph Neural Network and Keypoint‐Guided Fitting Based Method for 3D Weld Seam Trajectory Extraction
abstract: To address inaccurate keypoint recognition and noise‐sensitive trajectory fitting in automated 3D weld seam extraction, a learning‐to‐fitting framework combining 3DSeamNet and KGC‐LO‐RANSAC is proposed. 3DSeamNet jointly predicts weld regions, centerline offsets, local tangential directions, and keypoint confidence from workpiece point clouds, providing structured geometric priors for subsequent trajectory fitting. KGC‐LO‐RANSAC then reconstructs the weld centerline using offset‐corrected centerline candidates, high‐confidence keypoint guidance, and spatial‐tangential consistency constraints.

abstract: Abstract Hard composite insulators are essential for reliable power transmission, but aging caused by environmental and electrical stresses increases leakage current and failure risks. Existing assessment methods face challenges in prediction accuracy, adaptability, and temporal feature analysis. This research proposes a novel ModABi-LSTMO framework that integrates DWT-based feature extraction, BiLSTM temporal learning, and ModAO optimization for accurate and intelligent aging assessment of power hard composite insulators. title: Transition to a much warmer climate for the global ocean and Antarctic Ice Sheet coupled system, and its reversibility
abstract: Abstract. In Antarctica, two plausible tipping points have been suggested: an ocean tipping point involving a cold-to-warm transition of ice shelf cavities, and an ice sheet tipping point associated with the marine ice sheet instability. This study explores the existence of such tipping points at the scale of Antarctica, using a coupled ocean–ice-sheet model. abstract: Abstract A new version of a neural network model for detecting and recognizing road signs in images and video files using the YOLO convolutional neural network is presented. Based on an analysis of literature sources, the choice was made in favor of using the YOLOv11m convolutional neural network, developed by Ultralytics, in the created system. abstract: ABSTRACT Underwater semantic segmentation is degraded by wavelength‐dependent attenuation, scattering, nonuniform illumination, and low target‐background contrast. abstract: Existing studies on resource and environmental carrying capacity (RECC) have primarily focused on comprehensive evaluation and linear identification. title: A survey of routing protocols for internet of underwater things from a performance evaluation perspective
abstract: Abstract In this paper, we present a review of IoUT routing protocols, categorizing them into four groups: geographic, opportunistic, void-handling, and clustering routing protocols. We compare and evaluate these routing categories using various performance metrics. Furthermore, we analyze the strengths, limitations, applications, and performance trade-offs of existing IoUT routing protocols across the evaluation scenarios considered. Finally, we discuss key challenges and future research directions for the development of IoUT routing protocols.

abstract: To achieve Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) Target 3, the selection of protected areas must consider the condition of ecosystems at sites in addition to the GBF 30% area target. abstract: Sugarcane is one of the major commercial crops cultivated in Andhra Pradesh, India, and accurate yield estimation is essential for agricultural planning, crop management, and food security. Conventional yield estimation methods are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and often limited in spatial coverage. Recent advancements in remote sensing, cloud computing, and machine learning have provided efficient alternatives for large-scale agricultural monitoring and crop yield prediction. title: Enhancing weather radar data by removing non-meteorological echoes, using neural networks trained on synthetic weather data
abstract: Abstract. Meteorological weather radars are essential for atmospheric research, weather forecasting and aviation safety, but they often detect non-meteorological echoes from scatterers such as insects, birds, and ground clutter. These non-meteorological echoes can then lead to misinterpretations in quantitative precipitation estimation and hydrometeor classification, which cause difficulties for atmospheric research and weather forecasting. This paper introduces a novel AI-based approach to identify such non-meteorological echoes in polarimetric radar data using a convolutional neural network.

Restinga is distributed along the entire Brazilian coast, classified as part of the Atlantic Forest, and is a highly heterogeneous environment, with herbaceous, shrubby, and forest vegetation. This study proposes a DEM-centric RF framework for predicting spatially continuous urban flood water depth across various precipitation return periods, emphasizing its robustness to terrain resolution degradation and spatial transferability. abstract: Lake Tana, the source of the Blue Nile in the northwestern Ethiopian highlands, is a climatically sensitive archive at the northern margin of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ). This study presents a machine learning (ML) framework for multi-class classification of wind turbine blade faults using vibration signals. abstract: The growing demand for efficient data management has increased the importance of intelligent data access and query optimization across heterogeneous database systems. This study analyzes dataset-based performance results for PostgreSQL and MongoDB to identify workload-dependent performance patterns and examine their implications for intelligent data access and adaptive query routing. abstract: Urban waterlogging is a growing challenge in rapidly urbanizing cities, yet existing assessments in Bangladesh often rely on expert-based, hydrological, or conventional geospatial approaches that may inadequately capture complex nonlinear interactions among environmental and urban factors. This study develops an integrated hydro-environmental and urban-morphological framework for assessing waterlogging susceptibility in Dhaka City. abstract: ABSTRACT Boiler water quality directly influences the efficiency, reliability and service life of industrial steam generation systems, and inadequate monitoring can cause scaling, corrosion, reduced heat transfer efficiency and unplanned shutdowns. This study presents an intelligent Internet of Things (IoT)-based framework for continuous boiler water quality monitoring and early warning that integrates real-time sensing, statistical process control (SPC), rule-based decision support and machine learning. abstract: Tropical coastal seascapes are valuable ecological systems providing essential services such as shoreline protection, carbon sequestration, and fisheries support. Understanding seascape change requires attention to both spatial scale and habitat composition, yet these aspects are often overlooked in coastal management. abstract: Abstract Satellite-derived soil moisture products provide valuable large-scale information but often exhibit reduced accuracy in heterogeneous watersheds with limited monitoring data. This study evaluated whether a strategically designed monitoring network combined with machine learning could refine Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) soil moisture estimates in the Vacacaí River basin (11,177 km²), southern Brazil. abstract: Soil salinity and seasonal water scarcity constrain barley production in coastal agroecosystems, yet their interactive effects on soil conditions, plant physiological responses, and yield remain insufficiently resolved. This study evaluated four irrigation regimes (0, 50, 75, and 100% field capacity) and four nutrient-management strategies (FRG-2018, IPNS + biochar, IPNS + vermicompost, and IPNS + biochar + vermicompost) for their effects on soil properties, physiological responses, and grain yield of barley ( Hordeum vulgare L.) across two consecutive growing seasons in coastal Bangladesh. abstract: Self-healing materials feature a self-directed process to heal micro-damage, ensuring the recovery of mechanical strength and dielectric properties in the absence of external intervention. Self-healing insulation materials are an exciting development for enhancing the longevity of high-voltage (HV) electrical devices in stringent operating environments. abstract: This study evaluates the hydrochemical characteristics and extent of saltwater intrusion in selected coastal communities of Rivers State, Niger Delta, Nigeria, with particular emphasis on groundwater vulnerability, salinity distribution and suitability for domestic and agricultural applications. Groundwater samples were collected from six (6) boreholes and six(6) hand-dug wells across Sama, Tema, Abalama, Buguma, Ido and Obuama communities and analysed for physicochemical parameters, major ions and selected heavy metals using standard laboratory procedures. abstract: Urban flooding poses a persistent and escalating threat to coastal megacities, particularly in rapidly urbanizing regions where climate variability and unregulated land use intensify vulnerability. This study develops a hybrid GeoAI–Remote Sensing framework for urban flood susceptibility prediction in Lagos, Nigeria. The research integrates nine multi-source geospatial datasets, which include Aspect, Curvature, Slope Length, Slope, Geology, Land Use/Land Cover, TWI, Altitude, and Proximity to River, within a machine learning-driven analytical environment. abstract: Abstract. The knowledge of land-surface variables (LSVs) is essential for an accurate description of the carbon cycle and, hence, for deriving the fraction of anthropogenic CO2 emissions contributing to global warming. abstract: Geogenic arsenic (As) contamination poses a major environmental concern, yet mapping its Natural Background Levels (NBLs) remains challenging in data-scarce, human-impacted regions within heterogeneous sedimentary aquifers. NBLs are essential for distinguishing natural from anthropogenic contributions and for establishing threshold values in environmental policy and groundwater management. abstract: Abstract The contamination of aquatic environments by antibiotics has become a major environmental concern due to their persistence and contribution to antimicrobial resistance. In this study, activated carbon derived from babassu endocarp (BAC) was evaluated for the removal of amoxicillin (AMX) from aqueous solutions under ultrasonic irradiation. abstract: ABSTRACT Tomatoes are very perishable climacteric fruits that require a considerable amount of moisture, soften, and get spoiled by microbes after harvest, causing loss of quality and food. Thus, a sustainable approach is needed to preserve the nutritional quality and microbial safety of the products over a longer period. abstract: The marine power system is the core for propulsion, generating electricity and supporting operation of main equipment. Its operation and maintenance is therefore particularly important. abstract: Rip currents cause most surf-beach lifeguard rescues and most beach drowning incidents, yet automated detection relies on costly instrumentation that scales poorly across the many beaches that lack lifeguards. abstract: Oceanic fracture zones, the inactive traces of former transform faults, are often considered tectonically inactive once relative plate motion across them ceases. title: From pixel-level retrievals to bay-scale nutrient dynamics in Pärnu Bay using Sentinel-3 OLCI
abstract: Monitoring nutrient dynamics is essential for assessing eutrophication in coastal waters, yet conventional in situ observations provide limited spatial coverage. This study evaluated the capability of Sentinel-3 Ocean and Land Colour Instrument (OLCI)-derived nutrient products to represent seasonal and interannual dynamics of total nitrogen (TN) and total phosphorus (TP) in Pärnu Bay, Gulf of Riga, during 2016–2024. Nutrient concentrations were estimated using regionally adapted OLCI retrieval algorithms and compared with in situ observations at pixel, seasonal, and annual scales. An additiona
journal: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Empirical Evaluation of Normalized Temperature-Scaled Cross-Entropy Pre-training in a Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise–Convolutional Neural Network–Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory–Cross-Attention Framework for Unmanned Surface Vehicle Diesel Engine Fault Diagnosis
abstract: Reliable diagnosis of unmanned surface vehicle (USV) diesel-engine faults requires representations that preserve multiscale vibration content and crank-angle-dependent context. Therefore, a CEEMDAN-CNN-BiLSTM-Cross-Attention framework is constructed, and NT-Xent pre-training is evaluated without presuming that it provides a performance benefit. CEEMDAN generates eight multiscale input channels, a CNN encodes local vibration transients, and the BiLSTM represents within-cycle context. title: Projected changes in precipitation and temperature over the KKSD river basin using a machine-learning-based selective CMIP6 multimodel ensemble
abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable climate projections are essential for climate-risk assessment and planning. Yet, uncertainty in Global Climate Models (GCMs) and ensemble construction remains a major challenge. This study developed a machine learning-based selective multimodel ensemble framework to project precipitation, maximum temperature (Tmax), and minimum temperature (Tmin) over the Kangsabati, Keliaghai, Silabati, and Dwarkeswar (KKSD) river basin in eastern India. title: Influence of matrix cementation and soft rock blocks on the mechanical behavior of soil-rock mixture: insights from triaxial experiments and interpretable machine learning
abstract: Soil-rock mixture (SRM) is a complex geological material widely distributed in nature, and its mechanical properties are typically controlled by the block skeleton. However, matrix cementation and soft rock blocks can significantly alter the properties of this skeleton, and the controlling factors of SRM mechanical behavior under such conditions remain unclear. title: Early warning system for non-seismic gravity driven tsunamis
abstract: Gravity-driven mass flows represent a significant near-field hazard in volcanic environments and, increasingly, in coastal regions affected by climate-driven slope instability. Despite their destructive potential, quantitative assessments of real-time detection systems operating under natural conditions remain scarce. Here we present the performance and sensitivity of the tsunami early-warning system currently operating at Stromboli Volcano (Italy), based on offshore pressure gauges and a real-time detection algorithm. title: Energetic potential of a diel vertical migration-mediated marine-to-terrestrial pathway: insights from myctophid fishes and the fishing bat Myotis vivesi
abstract: Diel vertical migration (DVM) structures pelagic food webs by bringing mesopelagic organisms into surface waters at night. Whether this recurrent prey pulse can also support transfers across the marine-terrestrial boundary has received less attention. Here, we combine empirical measurements of the energetic characteristics of two abundant Gulf of California myctophids, Benthosema panamense and Triphoturus mexicanus , with station-level biomass-density data from a published regional survey to characterize the potential energy represented by the vertically migrating prey field. title: Coastal evolution modeling through the coupling of longshore and cross-shore sediment transport processes: The IODA framework
abstract: This study combines two numerical models (LTC and CS-Model) into an integrated numerical framework, IODA (Integrated cOastal Dynamics Assessment). IODA is design for medium- to long-term (years) coastal modelling at regional scales, by coupling longshore and cross-shore sediment transport processes (sandbar-berm-dune dynamics), while balancing physical processes representation, computational efficiency and input data requirements. title: Reducing false alarms in crackmeter-based early warning of small-scale slope deformation via deep learning-driven asynchronous displacement–rainfall data fusion
abstract: Abstract. Real-time crackmeter-based warning systems for rainfall-induced small-scale slope failures suffer from prohibitively high false alarm rates. Across diverse geological settings, existing approaches relying on fixed thresholds or isolated rainfall–displacement relationships are highly sensitive to noise, lacking the robustness to reliably distinguish genuine deformation signals from spurious measurements. title: Comprehensive Review of Leak Detection and Localization in Subsea Oil and Gas Pipelines
abstract: Detection of underwater pipeline leakage is essential in the oil and gas sectors because of its potential to cause environmental harm, financial loss, and safety hazards. This article compares several leak detection systems, including classical and emerging technologies, and addresses localization strategies for pipeline breaches. Significant problems, including sensor malfunctions, data integrity, signal disruption, and scalability, are also discussed. title: AI-Powered Smart Glasses Using the ESP32 Processor
abstract: Vision impairment affects over 2.2 billion people worldwide and continues to impose severe barriers to independent daily life, from safe outdoor navigation to reading signage and recognising familiar faces. Conventional aids such as the white cane provide limited scene awareness and cannot describe objects, read text, or interpret traffic signals. The convergence of affordable edge-computing hardware, mature deep learning frameworks, and free-tier cloud AI services has spawned a new generation of AI-powered smart glasses that begin to close this gap. title: ‘Find-a-HALO’ – An AI-assisted detection and segmentation framework for ecological monitoring of Halophila ovalis using YOLOv8 and the Segment Anything Model (SAM)
abstract: Fragmentation of seagrass habitats impact the ecosystem services of sensitive coastal lagoons, necessitating periodic, high-resolution, non-intrusive monitoring of the spatio-temporal dynamics to adequately support conservation efforts. The present investigation details the development of a “coupled” deep learning framework by combining You-Only-Look-Once (YOLO) v8 model with the Segment Anything model (SAM) to detect the spatial extent of seagrass patches from underwater images. title: CO2 sequestration hybrid solver using isogeometric alternating-directions and collocation-based robust variational physics informed neural networks (IGA-ADS-CRVPINN)
abstract: In this paper we present how Physics Informed Neural Networks augmented with robust loss function computed at collocation points can speed up the explicit dynamics simulations of time-dependent problems. We develop and apply our hybrid solver on a practical yet challenging example - the CO 2 sequestration problem. In this example, we compute the scalar saturation field from the non-stationary solver, and the pressure scalar field from the stationary solver executed in every time step. title: Endogenous rhythms in deep-sea mussel cell culture and molecular clock characterization
abstract: While biological rhythms are crucial to life, the deep sea has long been considered an arrhythmic exception. However, at hydrothermal vents - devoid of diel cues yet shaped by tides - the mussel Bathymodiolus azoricus shows both tidal and, unexpectedly, circadian rhythms at -1700 m. Whether endogenous clock(s) drive these cycles remained unanswered. Here, we report endogenous circadian rhythms in B. azoricus cell cultures under constant conditions: isolated cells display a circadian oscillation despite tidal-dominant rhythms in the natural environment. title: Numerical and artificial neural network prediction of double-stratified magnetized nanofluid flow and heat transfer over a stretchable cylinder with Brownian motion and thermal slip
abstract: The current study aims to investigate the effects of double stratification on magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) nanofluid flow over a stretching cylinder in the presence of thermal radiation. The model incorporates Brownian motion, thermophoresis, and velocity, thermal, and concentration slip conditions to provide a realistic description of the transport phenomena. The problem is formulated in the form of PDEs are converted to ODEs by applying suitable similarity variables. The transformed system is solved numerically using bvp4c solver in MATLAB. title: Dynamic Hydrogen‑Bond Network Accelerates Lattice Oxygen Regeneration for High‑Current‑Density Seawater Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Seawater electrolysis for green H 2 production is hindered by the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and chloride corrosion at the anode. Although the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) can effectively reduce the overpotential, the sluggish mass transport of OH − at high current densities disrupts the oxygen release–regeneration balance, ultimately leading to a trade‐off between activity and stability. title: Physiological markers of low-altitude exercise load for predicting acute mountain sickness: development of an interpretable machine learning model and research web calculator
abstract: Acute mountain sickness (AMS) poses a significant threat to individuals ascending to high-altitude regions, yet early identification of susceptible populations remains challenging. This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning model for estimating AMS risk from exercise-induced physiological responses measured at low altitude. A total of 171 healthy participants were included, with 111 participants (51 AMS events) comprising the development cohort and 60 participants (27 AMS events) forming an external validation cohort. title: A Plume Resolution Enhancement Network-based method for enhancing the resolution of cold seep plume seismic data
abstract: Cold seep bubble plumes serve as critical indicators of submarine gas hydrate deposits, yet their seismic imaging resolution is often limited by the dominant frequency of marine seismic sources and signal attenuation, making clear identification challenging. This paper proposes a high-resolution processing method based on a lightweight deep learning model, Plume Resolution Enhancement Network (PRENet), to achieve end-to-end intelligent enhancement of cold seep plume seismic data from low to high resolution. title: Review of Numerical Simulation for Chloride Transport in Cement-Based Materials: Progress, Bottlenecks and Future Directions
abstract: Abstract Chloride-induced corrosion is the dominant cause of durability degradation in concrete structures, and numerical modeling is an effective approach to reveal chloride transport mechanisms and predict structural long-term service performance. Based on standardized literature retrieval from Web of Science, Scopus and CNKI (2000 to early 2026), this review systematically summarizes the numerical modeling progress of chloride transport in cement-based materials from five key aspects: macroscopic theoretical models, meso- and micro-scale simulation techniques, multi-scale and multi-physics

abstract: Columbite-group minerals are important Nb-bearing minerals that preserve geochemical information related to magmatic evolution, fluid activity, and Nb enrichment processes. However, conventional discrimination approaches based mainly on Nb–Ta and Fe–Mn variations often simplify complex multi-element compositional characteristics into low-dimensional spaces, limiting their applicability to mineral systems affected by multistage magmatic and hydrothermal modification. abstract: Coastal-enclosure assessments commonly emphasize external organic loading, sediment processes, and hydrological exchange but rarely account for living benthic biomass that may become a transient internal organic load after habitat conversion. Omitting this pool may leave early post-closure oxygen budgets incomplete, particularly where water exchange and oxygen renewal are restricted. title: A ResNet50–Vision Transformer–XGBoost Hybrid Framework for Image-Based Ovarian Cancer Classification and Risk Prediction
abstract: Ovarian cancer classification based on histopathological images is complicated by the wide range of morphological patterns and the similarity of cancer types. The article describes a hybrid ResNet50–Vision Transformer–XGBoost ovarian cancer classification model that improves classification accuracy using multiple deep learning approaches. The proposed solution uses the Kaggle UBC-OCEAN database and two classification stages. In the first stage, morphological characteristics are extracted using ResNet50 and Vision Transformer models. title: Hydrodynamic characteristics and an improved model of an underwater dam defect detection ROV under near-wall effects
abstract: Accurate hydrodynamic prediction is essential for evaluating the environmental adaptability and establishing the dynamic model of the ROV used for dam underwater defect detection. This study compares the hydrodynamic characteristics of ROVs with bionic and open-frame configurations under multiple motion modes. The physical mechanism of the wall hydrodynamic forces on the ROV is explained by boundary-layer interaction and vortex structures. title: Development of machine learning models for estimating ambient air pollutants (PM2.5, and O3) concentrations and health risk assessment across cold and warm seasons in 22 districts of Tehran megacity
abstract: Air pollution, especially in Asia, poses a serious threat to public health and the environment, highlighting the need for accurate urban air pollution prediction models for better management and health protection. However, previous studies have often paid limited attention to fine-scale urban variations and the integrated assessment of air pollution and associated health risks. This study develops machine learning models to estimate PM 2.5 and O 3 concentrations in Tehran during warm and cold seasons by integrating meteorological parameters with satellite-derived indices. abstract: Abstract Understanding the implicit regularization imposed by neural network architectures and gradient based optimization methods is a key challenge in deep learning and AI. In this work we provide sharp results for the implicit regularization imposed by the gradient flow of Diagonal Linear Networks (DLNs) in the over-parameterized regression setting and link this to the phenomenon of phase transitions in generalized hardness of approximation (GHA). title: Sustainable Production of Marine Fish Mucus‐Derived Supramolecular Hydrogels for Multifunctional Protective Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Marine fish offer sustainable defense strategies to address the global challenge posed by rising temperatures, which threaten public health, accelerate material degradation, and intensify environmental stress. Through constant interaction with their aquatic environment, fish secrete a natural supramolecular protective mucus hydrogel, rich in gel‐forming glycoproteins (mucins), multiple antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), and ultraviolet‐protective mycosporine‐like amino acids (MAAs). title: Multi-data source based quantifying urban flood severity in major Chinese cities (2000–2024) using a hybrid machine-learning weighting framework
abstract: Abstract. Urban flooding poses a major challenge to sustainable urban development, yet most existing assessments focus on single cities or river basins and rely on limited historical records. This study integrates multi-source data from 20 Chinese cities over 2000–2024 to develop a comparable long-term assessment of urban flood severity. title: Rethinking English Language Learning: A Needs Analysis in Fisheries and Marine Science Education
abstract: This study seeks to analyze the needs of Fisheries and Marine Science students in learning English to be a basis in developing a contextually relevant English for Specific Purposes (ESP) curriculum. The study used a descriptive qualitative design and included 23 participants: 20 undergraduate students in the third to fifth semesters, two English lecturers, and one Marine Science lecturer. title: PhaseNeXt: neural phase picker trained on 20-year records to process the JMA-unified data set
abstract: Abstract To develop a higher-quality seismic event catalog from Japan’s routine seismic observations, which have been continuously recorded at approximately 2000 stations, we trained deep-learning-based phase pickers using 20 years of arrival-time data read by the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA). To enhance performance, we developed a new model, PhaseNeXt, by incorporating techniques proven effective in the field of computer vision—particularly in semantic segmentation—into PhaseNet, one of the most widely used neural phase pickers. title: Hydrogeological controls on seasonal groundwater level dynamics across Greece: A national-scale assessment integrating monitoring data, earth observation, and interpretable machine learning (2013–2022)
abstract: Groundwater monitoring networks typically provide broad spatial coverage but sparse and irregular temporal observations, which limit their direct use for operational groundwater status assessment. Mediterranean groundwater systems are subject to strong seasonal contrasts between winter recharge and summer abstraction, yet national-scale assessments resolving how aquifer type modulates this signal remain scarce. abstract: Questions The Circum-Bohai-Sea saline region possesses abundant halophytic plant resources; however, the specific composition and distribution patterns of these communities, as well as their complex associations with soil factors, remain insufficiently understood. This study aims to elucidate how plant community distribution and species diversity are associated with soil chemical properties in this region. Location The Circum-Bohai-Sea saline region, China. title: A shared vision: regional data harmonization for resilient small-scale fisheries in the Western Indian Ocean
abstract: Effective fisheries management in the Western Indian Ocean (WIO) is currently hindered by a lack of timely, harmonized data, which undermines the formulation of evidence-based policies. To address this gap, this study utilizes the Integrated Data Harmonization Framework (IDHF) to: (1) examine gaps and limitations in existing digital data collection systems in the region; (2) identify challenges and solutions for harmonizing small-scale fisheries (SSF) data; and (3) develop a strategic roadmap for national and regional data integration. title: Trustworthy Transfer Learning in GeoAI: Assessing Pretrained Models for Rooftop Solar PV Mapping Under Geographic Domain Shift
abstract: Abstract The increasing availability of pretrained Geospatial Artificial Intelligence (GeoAI) models has accelerated the operational adoption of deep learning within geographic information systems. However, models developed in one geographic region frequently experience performance degradation when deployed elsewhere because of geographic domain shift. Although transfer learning is widely used to improve cross-regional model performance, it remains unclear whether improved predictive accuracy alone provides sufficient evidence for trustworthy deployment. title: Persistent bistability of Nordic Seas overflow waters over 800,000 years
abstract: The stability of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a major uncertainty in projections of future climate. However, direct evidence for AMOC tipping behavior on orbital timescales remains scarce. Here, we reconstruct the strength of Iceland-Scotland Overflow Water, a key lower branch of the deep Atlantic circulation, over the past 800,000 years by combining 12 current-speed records from North Atlantic sediment cores with a data-driven hybrid model. abstract: This study presents the viral communities in Bay of Bengal abyssal deep-sea sediment (3,747 m depth) characterized by employing metagenome based characterization. Illumina sequencing of virus-enriched sediment generated 39.4 million reads. A large proportion of these reads of ∼70% remained unclassified. The virome was dominated by dsDNA viruses, particularly Caudoviricetes , with Kyanoviridae as the most abundant family. title: A closed-to-open cell mixed-phase cloud transition observed over the Nordic Seas under high aerosol loading and strong surface fluxes
abstract: Abstract. Closed-to-open cell mixed-phase cloud transitions within marine cold air outbreaks subjected to strong turbulent surface fluxes remain poorly understood despite their importance to high-latitude climate. The Cold-Air outbreak Experiment in the Sub-Arctic Region (CAESAR) research aircraft sampled closed-cells with cloud condensation nuclei concentrations surpassing 680 cm-3, decreasing to 90 cm-3 across a transition to open-cells. title: Análisis experimental y drenaje horizontal en mezclas bituminosas porosas para SUDS con apoyo de modelación mediante Machine Learning
abstract: Este trabajo analiza el drenaje horizontal en mezclas bituminosas porosas (PA) diseñadas para Sistemas de Drenaje Sostenible (SUDS). El objetivo es evaluar su comportamiento hidráulico longitudinal mediante ensayos experimentales y modelación con Machine Learning. La metodología consistió en el ensayo de tres mezclas PA11 con distinta porosidad, utilizando placas de pista de diversas dimensiones y cargas hidráulicas en condiciones de flujo horizontal. abstract: ABSTRACT Rational material designs for lithium extraction from unconventional dilute resources have attracted attention to meet the rising demand. Here, a new multifunctional composite is developed that not only extracts lithium but also enables its concurrent optical detection. The material design integrates silica xerogel confined within hollow carbon spheres as a high‐surface‐area matrix, heteroatom‐doped CDs as a fluorescence tag, and a covalently attached benzophenone‐derived ligand as the lithium‐binding site. title: MPD-Net: a maritime port dehazing network for structure-preserving and hue-consistent visibility restoration
abstract: Coastal fog and haze reduce the structural clarity, color fidelity, and visibility of images taken at coastal ports. This study proposes MPD-Net, a dual-candidate restoration network tailored for port scenes. It sequentially applies a color and luminance hint module (CLH) and a frequency-aware refinement layer (FARL) to the base output; the detail branch embeds a detail-guided feature modulation module (DGF) into the backbone network and applies CLH at the output. abstract: Maritime image dehazing is a critical prerequisite for ocean engineering and uncrewed surface vessels (USVs). However, it faces unique and complex challenges compared to terrestrial dehazing, primarily due to spatially inhomogeneous haze distribution, severe blue-green color casts caused by water spectral absorption, and significant cross-domain diversity across varying marine environments. abstract: Background: Marine environments expose metals to chloride and sulfate deposition, moisture, and changing atmospheric conditions that may accelerate corrosion. Understanding these relationships is essential for developing effective corrosion monitoring and maintenance strategies for marine infrastructure. abstract: This study examines projected hydroclimatic changes and streamflow responses in four Central High Atlas headwater basins of Morocco — Ademmaghene (Lakhdar), Aït Sigmine (Ghazzaf), Sgatt (Bernat) and Aït Tamlilt (Tassaout) — using statistically downscaled CNRM-CM5 precipitation scenarios under RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5, combined with a multi-algorithm machine-learning (ML) framework. abstract: Abstract Coastal marshes are critical blue‐carbon ecosystems, yet regional quantification of vegetation‐derived carbon burial and living biomass carbon stocks within marshes remains limited. abstract: Abstract Metakaolin (MK) contains highly reactive alumina, which could be a proper supplementary cementitious material to design low-carbon and durable concrete in marine structures. This review critically examines the characteristics of MK and its effects on cement hydration, mechanical properties, durability, and the chloride-binding capacity. title: Species sorting in coastal wetlands: cross-taxon patterns in bird communities and habitat structure within Grenada’s mangroves
abstract: Abstract Mangroves are inherently biodiverse ecosystems that support a range of avian species, both resident and migratory. This study investigates bird community composition in Grenada’s mangrove ecosystems, examining potential species sorting processes and relationships with plant communities. abstract: This article compares the legislative reforms enacted in the states of Quintana Roo, Aguascalientes, and Colima concerning the use of artificial intelligence in the criminal law context. title: Spatial and Seasonal Patterns of Waterbird Assemblages in Two Coastal Protected Areas of Northern Argentine Patagonia
abstract: ABSTRACT Wetlands are facing numerous threats globally, with a profound impact on Latin America and the Caribbean. Continuous monitoring is essential to maintain up‐to‐date information about their status and to inform adaptive conservation planning. This study provides new baseline information on waterbird assemblages in two poorly studied natural protected areas (PAs) of the San Matías Gulf, in northern Argentine Patagonia. abstract: This study investigates the perceptions of meat quality among urban consumers in three West African capital cities: Dakar, Abidjan, and Abuja, with the goal of assessing the market potential for meat from extensive Sahelian livestock systems. abstract: Abstract Land subsidence is a growing hazard with far-reaching socioeconomic, environmental, and safety implications, especially in densely populated and water-stressed regions. In areas where groundwater is the primary water source, prolonged overextraction causes declines in water tables and destabilizes the ground, leading to widespread land deformation. abstract: Deformation control during deep excavation in coastal soft-soil areas is an important geotechnical engineering issue. Pre-vious studies have focused mainly on regular and symmetric excavations, while the spatial distribution of deformation around asymmetric excavations with irregular plan geometries remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates the asymmetric deep excavations for the Hexi working shaft and the Line A sea-entry section of the Sanya River Estuary Passage Project. title: From human hearing to machine diagnostics: Incipient fault diagnosis of rotating machines using multi-bioscale attention entropy and acoustic signals
abstract: Fault diagnosis in rotating machinery is traditionally performed using vibration signals; however, acoustic signals captured by non-contact sensors provide a promising alternative for early fault detection. Although entropy-based methods have been widely applied for signal complexity analysis, existing multi-scale entropy approaches are not specifically designed for acoustic signals and may not fully exploit their perceptual frequency characteristics. To address this limitation, this study proposes a novel bio-inspired feature extraction method called multi-bioscale attention entropy (MBSAE).

abstract: Lithology identification is a fundamental task in geological surveying and mapping, yet the traditional visual interpretation of remote sensing imagery is labor-intensive and strongly dependent on expert experience. This study proposes a machine-learning-based approach for intelligent lithology interpretation that integrates multispectral remote sensing imagery with terrain features, and evaluates its applicability to supporting geological mapping in karst terrains. abstract: Abstract Coastal cities are highly urbanized regions where ecological sensitivity and the continuous expansion of urban space pose significant challenges to the sustainable development of ecosystems. This study assessed ecosystem services (ESs) from an integrated past–future perspective and elucidated spatiotemporal evolution patterns, as well as trade-offs and synergies among multiple ESs in Tianjin over the past two decades and under three future scenarios. abstract: The incorporation of AI is causing a sea change in the health insurance industry. From boosting client interactions to reducing fraud and expediting underwriting, AI is revolutionising the health insurance market. Today, the healthcare insurance sector is in a transformation process, where Artificial Intelligence (AI) is playing a role from optimising underwriting processes to processing claims, preventing fraud, and tailoring insurance offerings to customers. abstract: Atmospheric temperature prediction is fundamentally a physical problem governed by deterministic equations. This paper introduces a hybrid architecture, Pi-ConvLSTM, to investigate how physical principles can guide neural network design and refinement for forecasting regional temperature variations by embedding existing physical knowledge into optimization. abstract: The acceleration of tourism in the Karimunjawa Islands poses a challenge of cultural disorientation for youth, while vocational education often remains trapped in a technical educational paradigm that sidelines humanist character building. This community service aims to restore and integrate the values of local wisdom and history into the character curriculum learning ecosystem at SMKN 1 Karimunjawa. abstract: ABSTRACT With the radio-frequency (RF) spectrum increasingly congested, Visible Light Communication (VLC) has emerged as a realistic complement to RF in 6G systems. This survey examines VLC along three axes: channel modeling, advanced physical-layer technologies, and standardization, with deployment constraints and techno-economics as their practical dimension. abstract: This study develops an artificial intelligence–driven credibility analytics artifact for English–Chinese information systems. It evaluates whether subsequent observable actions support narrative commitments and transforms bilingual disclosures into transparent, comparable, and traceable credibility signals. abstract: Abstract Carbon partitioning between organic and carbonate‐associated forms remains poorly constrained in arid to semiarid coastal soils, where geomorphic position, salinity, and carbonate accumulation jointly structure surface‐soil carbon patterns. We evaluated landform controls on surface (0–20 cm) soil organic carbon (SOC), calcite‐equivalent soil inorganic carbon (SIC_eq), soil total carbon (STC), and SIC_eq:SOC across six landforms of the southeastern Caspian coastal plain. abstract: Abstract Coastal floodplains are highly dynamic environments that remain perpetually vulnerable, with multiple confluences of flood drivers, including interactions among extreme rainfall, river discharge, and storm tides, which are capable of triggering catastrophic flooding. abstract: Purpose— This study examines Islamic banking innovations to address fintech challenges through a blue ocean strategy. Therefore, the main focus of the discussion is on: External business environment factors of Islamic banking; Internal business environment factors; SWOT analysis; and Blue Ocean Strategy. abstract: ABSTRACT Mangrove tree populations of Rhizophora mucronata and Avicennia marina in the Western Indian Ocean (WIO) comprise distinct evolutionary significant units (ESUs) with contrasting dispersal histories between remote islands and the eastern African coastline. This issue is particularly critical for ship hulls, offshore structures, and welded components exposed to long-term seawater attack, mechanical loading, and localized corrosion damage. abstract: ABSTRACT Waste-derived biochar supports circular wastewater treatment by removing contaminants, recovering resources, and integrating life cycle and techno-economic assessments for sustainable scale-up. Biochar, produced from industrial and agricultural waste, has evolved from an agricultural soil amendment to an effective and sustainable material for wastewater treatment. abstract: Effective water resource management and disaster mitigation require accurate rainfall prediction for planning purposes. Forecasting of rainfall is a difficult time series problem as it is highly non-linear and non-stationary, and dependent on season. This study suggests a hybrid deep learning framework that integrates Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory (BiLSTM) with Transformer Architecture and Attention, as well as the ensemble based on meta-learning. abstract: Abstract Fast‑evolving weather events typically develop on 5–15 min scales and can significantly influence human activities and planning. However, most global atmospheric reanalyses provide data only every 1–3 hours, making it difficult to capture rapid changes such as short-duration heavy rainfall. abstract: This study assesses the level of digitalization of tax administrations in the 27 Member States of the European Union, applying the PROMETHEE II outranking method to 16 evaluation criteria. abstract: Accurate phase prediction is critical for customized high-entropy alloys (HEAs) design. abstract: The expansion of the Blue Economy in Muslim-majority countries has intensified debates over marine economic development, environmental sustainability, and Islamic economic principles, yet whether sustainable marine practices satisfy Sharia requirements remains insufficiently examined. abstract: Nitrogen is one of the most commonly limiting nutrients throughout the world’s oceans and it has long been acknowledged that pelagic Sargassum reliably hosts nitrogen fixing epiphytes, yet very little is known about what controls nitrogen fixation rates within this community. abstract: This study aimed to develop a k-nearest neighbors (KNN)-based algorithm for the automated recognition of planktonic organisms from digital images. Image datasets were used to train and evaluate the classifier, and its performance was assessed based on classification accuracy. The KNN approach achieved accuracy rates comparable to those obtained through conventional image identification by non-specialist observers, suggesting its potential as an alternative computational tool for plankton ecological analyses.

abstract: The Aral Sea crisis raises a question beyond environmental-governance failure: how can governance institutions persist alongside serious ecological degradation? abstract: Saudi Arabia's oil and gas pipeline systems operate across environments where saline soils, coastal exposure, variable water handling, and long asset lives can complicate corrosion control. title: A Critical Review of Heavy Metal Toxicity and Biochar-Based Sustainable Remediation Strategies
abstract: Heavy metals (HMs) and metalloids such as cadmium (Cd), lead (Pb), mercury (Hg), arsenic (As), and chromium (Cr) are persistent, highly toxic pollutants that contaminate soil and water, posing serious threats to ecosystems, microbial communities, plants, and human health. This review critically examines recent research on HMs toxicity and biochar-based sustainable remediation through a systematic review, highlighting key advances, knowledge gaps, and future directions. abstract: Accurate prediction of significant wave height (SWH) is essential for ocean engineering safety, maritime transportation, and wave energy utilization. To address the nonlinear and non-stationary characteristics of SWH time series, this paper proposes a hybrid forecasting model that integrates signal decomposition, mode grouping and reconstruction, and deep learning. abstract: Objectives: To explore the lived experiences of bereaved informal caregivers who provided end-of-life care to patients with cancer in marginalised coastal hamlets of Pondicherry and Chennai during the COVID-19 pandemic. Materials and Methods: This qualitative study used a hermeneutic phenomenological approach guided by van Manen’s interpretive framework. title: Assessing tidal sensitivity to bottom friction: analytical insights for model optimization
abstract: Bottom friction coefficients (BFCs) are critical parameters in tidal modeling, with significant effects on hydrodynamic conditions and sediment transport. A comprehensive understanding of BFC variability and its influence on tidal models is essential for model optimization. In this study, we incorporate BFC perturbations through a Dirac delta function into a modified, depth-uniform idealized shallow-water model. title: Shimia rhodophyticola sp. nov., Neomarinovum algicola gen. nov., sp. nov., and Phycorhabdus gracilariae gen. nov., sp. nov., isolated from marine algae, and the taxonomic revision of nineteen taxa within the family Roseobacteraceae
abstract: Three bacterial strains, W99T, S113T, and S268T, were isolated from marine algae and subjected to polyphasic taxonomic characterization. Phylogenetic and phylogenomic analyses placed W99T within the genus Shimia, whereas S113T and S268T formed two distinct genus-level lineages within the family Roseobacteraceae. The three isolates were Gram-stain-negative, non-motile, and obligately aerobic, with optimum growth at 25, 25, and 30°C, respectively, and at 2.0% (w/v) NaCl. abstract: Abstract Turbidite systems are key marine sedimentary formations found in passive continental margins, serving as major hydrocarbon reservoirs in deepwater fields worldwide. Since the 1970s, prolific hydrocarbon accumulations associated with turbidite deposits have been discovered in post-salt sequences along the Brazilian eastern margin. Recently, the margins of the Equatorial Atlantic, both in South America and Africa, have become major exploration frontiers, whose giant oil fields are found in Late Cretaceous turbidite systems. title: Microplastic leachates: an invisible flux and latent source of environmental toxicity
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) have emerged as ubiquitous pollutants in marine, freshwater, and terrestrial environments. Their amorphous structure, high surface area, and hydrophobicity enable the strong adsorption of environmental contaminants. At the same time, embedded additives such as phthalates, bisphenols, ultraviolet (UV) stabilizers, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) leach into ecosystems during degradation. title: Unbox responsible GeoAI: navigating climate extreme and disaster mapping
abstract: As climate extreme and disaster events become more frequent and intense, Geospatial Artificial Intelligence (GeoAI) has emerged as a transformative approach for large-scale disaster mapping and risk reduction. However, the purely mechanical, performance-driven deployment of GeoAI models can result in amplifying inherent spatial inequalities, preventing effective emergency decision-making, and producing severe environmental carbon footprint. abstract: This article includes the analysis of the effect of technology integration in teacher training, based on the current context of education and highlighting the importance of strengthening pedagogical skills, digital competencies, and innovative methodological practices. The purpose is to identify the challenges and opportunities that teachers face in adopting digital and technological-pedagogical resources, such as artificial intelligence (AI) and open educational resources (OER), to improve teaching-learning processes. abstract: Fine-scale delineation of visible red-tide patches from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) RGB imagery is prone to challenges such as fragmented morphology, weak target–background contrast, and optically complex coastal environments. abstract: Porinaceae is one of the most common families of foliicolous lichens in tropical regions. Despite its abundance, major gaps remain in our understanding of its diversity and phylogeny. This study addresses these knowledge gaps and examines photobiont selectivity in Madagascar and the Indian Ocean Islands. In total, 114 lichen specimens from Madagascar and the neighbouring islands of Mauritius and Mayotte were sequenced. abstract: This reflective article critically examines the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents configured as educational tutors in secondary education. Based on a rigorous review of meta-analyses, international case studies, and specialized academic literature, it explores the conceptual foundations of intelligent tutoring and contemporary models of digital pedagogy. abstract: Background: Haliaeetus leucogaster, or the white-bellied sea eagle, is one of the largest raptors in Indonesia and plays a crucial role in maintaining ecological balance. abstract: Naturally occurring fungal metabolites are ideal candidates for combating multidrug-resistant pathogens in clinical settings. abstract: Increasing coastal-water temperatures, hydrological disturbance and expanding opportunities for human exposure have renewed concern about Vibrio vulnificus . abstract: Abstract With the rapidly evolving digital technology landscape, characterized by cutting-edge technologies such as artificial intelligence, big data, and machine learning, data privacy is increasingly becoming a topic of global urgency in both policy and technical domains. abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) tracking is an important enabling technique for the Internet of Underwater Things (IoUT). However, depth-dependent acoustic propagation and inaccurate filter initialization can significantly degrade the transient performance of nonlinear AUV tracking. abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in daily life, ascertaining whether an agent is human is critical. Here we present TianXing-S2S, a multi-sphere coupled probabilistic deep learning model for global S2S ensemble forecasting.
