abstract: The Kapchagay Hydropower Plant (HPP), one of the largest hydraulic structures in Kazakhstan, is located in a seismically active region. This study was conducted in 2000 after an abnormal drop in the water level in the Kapchagay Reservoir was discovered during its operation. A comprehensive investigation was conducted to identify the causes of water losses and assess the operational and seismic safety of the facility. abstract: Introduction Coastal soil salinization impairs soil structure and microbial functionality, thereby hindering soil organic carbon (SOC) accumulation and constraining rice productivity. abstract: As generative artificial intelligence continues to iterate, mainstream models such as ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Copilot are entering the teaching spaces of universities, and teaching processes, teacher–student relations and assessment practices are changing with them. abstract: Education in conditions of volatility, uncertainty, complexity, ambiguity and hyperconnectivity requires learners to evaluate changing information, connect knowledge across disciplines and justify action. These demands invite a transformation in teaching from the transmission of answers toward the leadership of inquiry. abstract: The absence of an effective waste management system in small island areas significantly contributes to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, particularly from uncontrolled open burning. This study analyzes the potential of an integrated waste management system to reduce GHG emissions in Kodingareng Lompo Island by comparing existing practices with an alternative scenario aligned with Presidential Regulation of the Republic of Indonesia No. 97 of 2017, which targets 30% waste reduction and 70% waste handling. title: Mitigating systematic underestimation in short-term wind speed forecasting via time-dependent weighted quantile loss (TDWQLoss)
abstract: Abstract Accurate short-term wind speed forecasting is pivotal for wind power integration. Deep learning models have shown promise but often suffer from distributional bias. Since wind speed follows a right-skewed Weibull distribution, the scarcity of high-wind-speed samples creates a data imbalance that predisposes deep learning models to systematic underestimation. abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence technology makes machine translation show its great advantages in translating multilingual information; yet there are no systematic explanations about the essential difference between them with regard to their cognitive levels. abstract: Fisheries and aquaculture influence marine carbon cycling, but biological carbon-retention does not necessarily constitute atmospheric carbon dioxide removal. This critical narrative review reassesses carbon sink fisheries, a concept developed in Chinese fisheries research, through an ecological-economic-social framework. abstract: A basic premise of standard machine learning is that the training set and the test set come from the same distribution, but this premise is often broken in practice. Text classification is one of the most fundamental tasks in natural language processing (NLP). The poor robustness of its models to out-of-distribution (OOD) samples has become an important research topic. This study reviews the latest research on OOD generalization in text classification. abstract: Probabilistic machine learning models estimate total dissolved solids (TDS) levels and exceedance probabilities, enabling risk-based regulation and safeguarding public health. This study develops a probabilistic machine learning framework to forecast monthly TDS in the Lam Tsuen River in Hong Kong using long‑term monitoring data from 2000 to 2023, split into 80% for training and 20% for testing. abstract: ABSTRACT Biodegradable polyesters such as polylactide (PLA) and polybutylene succinate (PBS) are increasingly used in packaging, yet the effect of photochemical pre‐aging on their subsequent fragmentation into microplastics remains insufficiently understood. abstract: In this interview, Dmitry Nikolaenko discusses the main ideas of his monograph Learning to Understand the Object: Scientific Recognition Architecture, devoted to the investigation of complex dynamic natural processes. abstract: Purpose The incremental adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) has been emphasized in much academic research and still remains incomplete with regards to the context-based acceptance and utilization. abstract: Abstract Trait evolution and lineage diversification are thought to be driven by selection on the phenotypes of individuals. abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools offer accessible support for English writing, but favourable perceptions do not necessarily translate into sustained use. This study investigated Teaching English as a Second Language (TESL) pre-university students’ perceptions of AI tools in an English writing skills course at a Malaysian public university. title: Building materials and emissions from rebuilding under increasing climate-driven flood hazards
abstract: Abstract Floods threaten lives and infrastructure, while recovery and reconstruction require materials whose production generates greenhouse gas emissions. These material needs and emissions remain insufficiently quantified. Here we assess the impacts of riverine and coastal flooding on building materials across Europe under climate change and land subsidence. abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly featured in education policy across Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), yet evidence on teacher preparation, particularly for primary education, remains limited. This scoping review mapped interventions preparing teachers to use AI and synthesised evidence on teacher readiness in SSA, drawing implications for Tanzanian primary education. abstract: This study applies recently published life cycle assessment (LCA) guidelines for higher education institutions (HEIs) to the Icelandic context and presents the first LCA of the University of Iceland (UI), based on data from the 2024 reference year. The assessment used the Environmental Footprint 3.1 method in Sphera LCA for Experts software to calculate environmental impacts across 16 categories. abstract: Climate Change Impact on Landslides Rising global temperatures contribute to more extreme weather patterns, including intense rainfall events that increase soil saturation and slope instability. Additionally, the melting of permafrost in colder regions due to warming temperatures weakens mountain slopes, heightening the risk of landslides. abstract: The biosynthetic machineries of ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs) are often substrate tolerant. A remarkable example is the class II lanthipeptide synthetase ProcM, which naturally functions as a generalist enzyme that has not evolved to use a specific substrate during its evolutionary history. abstract: This essay analyzes the main cognitive learning theories and their bearing on teaching practice, based on a central thesis: learning does not consist of receiving or reproducing content, but of actively reconstructing, through mediation, the conceptual schemes with which individuals interpret and act upon reality. abstract: Soil creep, as a form of long-term deformation, significantly influences the performance of foundations and earth structures. abstract: Systematic studies on long-term cumulative steel replacement in ships are virtually absent, despite their importance for ship design, maintenance of ageing vessels, and sustainable shipping. Extensive ultrasonic thickness measurement reports and steel renewal records collected throughout the operational lives of 12 bulk carriers were presented and analysed to quantify cumulative steel replacement at both the ship and their lightweight groups. abstract: The aim of this study was to analyze the level of teachers' digital competencies and their perceptions of the opportunities and challenges posed by generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) for pedagogical innovation in Ecuadorian higher education. A quantitative approach was used, with a descriptive and correlational scope and a non-experimental, cross-sectional design. abstract: The Gobi Desert of northwestern China represents a highly prospective yet critically under-explored metallogenic province, where thick, transported overburden and extreme aridity have rendered conventional geochemical surveys largely ineffective. Deep-penetrating geochemistry (DPG) has emerged as a suite of specialized surface methods designed to detect concealed mineralization beneath such exotic cover by targeting mobile forms of ore-forming elements that migrate from depth to the surface. abstract: The current peptide renaissance-driven by metagenomic and proteomic mining, molecular de-extinction, protein language models, and generative or evolutionary design-is producing millions of candidates, but useful machine learning depends on experimentally anchored, context-rich labels. The Database of Antimicrobial Activity and Structure of Peptides (DBAASP) is a manually curated resource linking peptides and peptidomimetics to quantitative antimicrobial, antibiofilm, anticancer, hemolytic, and mammalian-cell cytotoxicity measurements and their experimental conditions. abstract: Abstract Rotary machinery is an indispensable part of modern industry; it greatly reduces labor and improves production efficiency. Therefore, accurate diagnosis and early warning of faults help minimize repair costs, increase efficiency, and prevent problems. Deep learning-based fault diagnostic methods often assume training and testing data are in the same domain and require large amounts of labeled data without taking advantage of the amount of unlabeled data. abstract: Rural higher education institutions (HEIs) in India are expected to meet the same standards of research integrity and intellectual property (IP) governance as metropolitan universities, yet they often have fewer specialist services, less training and thinner support systems. This paper develops an evidence-informed framework for strengthening IP awareness and research ethics in such institutions. abstract: Accurate wave spectra forecasting is essential for marine operations along the diverse Brazilian coast, yet numerical wave models frequently exhibit systematic biases. This study evaluates the Wave Spectra Correction (WASCO) methodology, a data-driven technique combining Principal Component Analysis and Multiple Linear Regression to refine 2D wave spectra forecasts at Recife, Santos, and Rio Grande. abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems increasingly support decision-making across critical domains, yet explainable AI (XAI) approaches prioritise algorithmic transparency over human comprehension. While XAI reveals computational processes for model validation, end users require explanations integrating domain knowledge, contextual reasoning, and professional frameworks. abstract: Abstract Urban trees moderate city climates, yet how their leaf-area density relates to projected future climates is poorly constrained globally. abstract: The emergence of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) in higher education has led to a refounding of the contract between subjects and machines. This article explores how this technology becomes a mediator in reading and writing practices, transforming students' relationship with knowledge within a new learning ecosystem. abstract: This study presents an experimental assessment of a compression-ignition internal combustion engine (CI-ICE) operating in dual-fuel mode with diesel and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), without fuel preheating or combustion enhancers. abstract: Climate change is threatening rice yields more and more, which undermines global food security. abstract: Accurate vehicle speed estimation is essential for Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) and autonomous driving applications. abstract: The rise of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) is transforming reading, writing, and learning practices in higher education, which presents ethical challenges related to authorship, transparency, and critical digital literacy. abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclone (TC) trajectory shifts remain a critical uncertainty in climate risk assessment. abstract: Maritime traffic risk shows significant spatial and temporal differences among vessel activities, navigation conditions, and environments. abstract: Abstract Saline-alkaline soils severely constrain wheat production and have become a major threat to food security, especially in regions experiencing secondary salinization and climate change. title: Perceived and demonstrated generative AI literacy in engineering problem solving: the role of verification behavior
abstract: Introduction Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly used in engineering education, but self-reported literacy may not establish whether students can evaluate its outputs. The distinction between perceived competence and performance on engineering-specific AI scenarios remains insufficiently examined. abstract: The incorporation of generative artificial intelligence (AI) into educational feedback offers opportunities to expand personalisation and accessibility, but it also raises risks of bias, opacity and the erosion of teacher mediation. The objective of this theoretical-conceptual article was to propose a framework to guide the use of generative AI in feedback from the standpoint of inclusive assessment and Universal Design for Learning (UDL). abstract: Reference evapotranspiration (ET₀) is an important variable for irrigation scheduling, agricultural water management, and hydrological applications. This study examines a Physics–Regularized Autoencoder (PRAE): a neural network that compresses daily weather variables into a small set of learned features while being encouraged to keep air temperature, relative humidity, and dew point temperature consistent with one another. abstract: Abstract Accurate characterization of land–atmosphere interactions over the Tibetan Plateau (TP) is hindered by fragmented measurements, inconsistent data-processing standards, and a scarcity of integrated, multi-component observations. While conventional cellular cores offer favorable stiffness-to-weight ratios, their flexural load-bearing capacity and structural integrity are often constrained by geometric limitations and complex, costly manufacturing processes. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper proposes a multimodal fusion‐based cooperative adaptive de‐icing control method. title: An improved CNN-Transformer network for seismic denoising with local–global feature modeling
abstract: In seismic exploration, field data are always affected by noise, reducing the quality of subsequent analysis. Striking a balance between signal preservation and noise attenuation effectively is a major challenge. This study adopts a dual-branch framework with convolutional neural networks (CNN) and Transformer architecture that integrates blind-spot convolution (BS-Conv) for local detail capture, rank-augmented linear attention (RALA) for global feature extraction, and the gated CNN block (GCB) for adaptive feature selection to achieve high-fidelity signal reconstruction and noise suppression.

title: An Introduction to Methods to Quantify Carbon Dynamics in Rangeland Ecosystems
abstract: ABSTRACT Rangeland ecosystems store substantial terrestrial carbon and contribute to climate mitigation, yet their spatial heterogeneity, dynamic disturbance regimes, and multiple carbon pools make accurate quantification challenging. This introduction outlines and compares methodological approaches for measuring aboveground biomass, soil organic carbon, and fire-derived pyrogenic carbon across rangelands, with emphasis on how sampling design, sensor platforms, modeling frameworks, and accounting tools scale across ecological gradients. abstract: Abstract Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is a crucial task in modern communication systems, enabling the identification of modulation schemes in received signals. This paper presents a proposed model to achieve AMC more accurately by using hybrid techniques, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) with spectrograms as input features. title: West Nile virus in Greece: One Health surveillance for early warning
abstract: West Nile virus (WNV) has emerged as a significant public health threat in Greece since 2010. Central Macedonia was the epicentre of the 2010 and 2022 outbreaks, whereas Attica, Eastern Macedonia and Thrace, and Thessaly predominated in other seasons. Climate change and environmental factors are amplifying transmission dynamics, necessitating integrated surveillance approaches. abstract: Abstract Snow water equivalent (SWE), which quantifies the amount of water in a snowpack, is critical for water supply forecasting. This study explores machine learning (ML) models' capability of representing the spatial distribution of SWE across the western United States. abstract: Introduction Studies exploring the molecules and potential mechanisms linking air pollution exposure to depression remain scarce. This study aimed to elucidate the potential regulatory molecules and possible mechanisms associated with air pollutants and depression, thereby providing scientific clues for disease prevention and treatment. title: Domain-Gap Auditing for Electromagnetic Survey Data
abstract: Machine-learning models for electromagnetic and magnetotelluric (EM/MT) interpretation are commonly trained on synthetic or historical data and then applied to new surveys. Standard validation, however, does not establish whether a deployment survey is represented by the development domain. We propose a pre-deployment domain-gap audit that tests whether a stated comparison domain, after field-calibrated corruption, reproduces selected characteristics of a deployment survey. abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid industrialization produces massive oily wastewater and frequent marine oil spills, severely damaging ecosystems and human health. Conventional oil–water separation membranes are restricted by single functions, low efficiency, and severe fouling, failing to cope with complex working environments. abstract: Coastal erosion is a critical global environmental challenge with adverse socio-economic impacts. To better understand this phenomenon, this study utilizes 33 years of topographical observations from the foreshore of the Hasaki coast in Japan to investigate the correlation between extreme erosion events and short-term and medium-term morphological changes ( ΔV S ). abstract: The global decline in biodiversity calls for scalable and efficient species monitoring. Birds, as sensitive ecological indicators with rich vocal activity, are particularly well suited for passive acoustic monitoring (PAM), which enables extensive, non-invasive data collection. abstract: Automatic Short Answer Grading (ASAG) is an important task in educational technology and natural language processing (NLP), enabling efficient and consistent evaluation of open-ended student responses. Although recent neural architectures have achieved strong performance, further improvements are possible in model focus, semantic understanding, and score consistency. abstract: Small-for-gestational-age (SGA) neonates face health risks when undetected, yet machine learning (ML) models are difficult to apply across sites with heterogeneous feature availability. We developed a cross-site pooling framework, incorporating feature-specific imputation and leakage-safe five-fold partitioning, for SGA prediction using Malaysian ( n = 18,582) and Indian ( n = 1,760) antenatal data. abstract: Reliable rainfall forecasting requires not only accurate point predictions but also well-calibrated estimates of predictive uncertainty, particularly during heavy and extreme events where forecast errors carry the greatest operational consequence. abstract: Vessel-source oil pollution remains a central concern in marine environmental governance because oil spills may spread rapidly, persist in the marine environment, and cause serious ecological and socio-economic harm. China has traditionally regulated vessel-source oil pollution through rules dispersed across civil, environmental, maritime, insurance, and administrative law. abstract: Wireless network security is a growing concern in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) as jamming attacks disrupt communication of IIoT entities in Private 5G networks. While machine learning (ML) algorithms detect jamming attacks effectively, centralized data collection from entities compromises sensitive information and privacy in distributed IIoT environment. abstract: Abstract Plague remains a persistent zoonotic threat in Mongolia, where Yersinia pestis (Y. pestis) bacteria responsible for plague circulate in natural foci linked to marmot-flea ecosystems. abstract: Phosphorus (P) and nitrogen (N) concentrations in surface waters are substantially affected by droughts and warm months. However, previous studies of phosphorus and nitrogen concentrations under these hydro-climatic extremes are limited to a small number of regions, mainly in parts of North America, Europe and Australia. abstract: Continuous touch positioning and trajectory tracking are essential for immersive human-machine interaction, yet conventional interfaces are fundamentally limited by rigid power supplies and tethered data transmission. abstract: This paper presents a centralised rolling-horizon framework for dynamic freight matching in port-centric supply chains. abstract: Lignin- based ionogels are promising sustainable materials for flexible electronics, yet their development is limited by a persistent tradeoff between mechanical robustness and dynamic multifunctionality. abstract: In the present work, the machine learning methods were used to develop the predictive models for the Compressive Strength (CS) of the graphene oxide-enhanced self-compacting concrete. abstract: Delta-T Compressional (DTC) well logs provide important sonic information for formation evaluation and subsurface characterization, but incomplete or unavailable sonic-log measurements can limit subsequent interpretation. abstract: Abstract Reliable short-term forecasting of vector abundance is critical for guiding localized mosquito control, yet week-ahead prediction at the Public Health Unit (PHU) scale remains challenging. abstract: The growing requirement for sustainable energy, coupled with greenhouse gas emissions reduction, have resulted in increased research efforts towards the production of hydrogen via biohydrogen as an alternative to fossil fuels. Biohydrogen production methods, though environmentally friendly, have limitations in terms of hydrogen yield and other operational issues. abstract: The expansion of data generated by next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies has increased the importance of bioinformatics in genomic analysis. abstract: Natural products (NPs) have long provided a foundation for drug discovery, offering structurally diverse and biologically active molecules not readily accessible through purely synthetic approaches. abstract: This paper addresses the inherent trade off between rapid convergence and high‑precision disturbance rejection in intelligent vehicle motion control under severe nonlinearities, parametric uncertainties, and time varying external perturbations. abstract: This study analyzes the role of archery in Ottoman military and society between 1567 and 1574 through archival documents from the Mühimme Registers. abstract: Non-compressible hemorrhage (NCH) remains a leading cause of preventable trauma mortality because conventional gauze and oxidized cellulose act as passive barriers, whereas fibrin sealants depend on patient-derived fibrinogen; neither is reliable in coagulopathic patients. abstract: Amid the fragmentation of multilateralism and the securitisation of science, Europe must decide whether international research cooperation can still be organised rather than left to drift. abstract: Data-driven rainfall models normally need long local records, which many stations lack. This study asks whether a transformer pre-trained on data-rich coastal Mumbai can cut both the local data and the computation needed to forecast daily rainfall at Pune, a rain-shadow city 120 km inland. abstract: The Rhino Optimiser is a novel bio-inspired optimisation algorithm inspired by the adaptive movement behaviour of solitary rhinoceroses. abstract: Sentiment analysis has become increasingly important for interpreting customer-generated content across social media and digital technologies. abstract: Ecological degradation and environmental pollution have posed persistent obstacles to sustainable development. abstract: Biodiversity conservation is shifting from the paradigm of species protection to the maintenance of ecological, genetic, and functional integrity. abstract: We argue in this paper that we cannot understand or change seafood systems if we do not look specifically at the history of industrial seafood processing in the U.S. Seafood is a vital part of human food systems that are imbricated with economic, social, and ecological processes, all of which have consequences for individual and collective culture, nutrition and health. Fisheries render seafood into food by capturing/harvesting, processing, and transporting it for human consumption, all within the context of policy and regulatory regimes and market imperatives. abstract: Net primary productivity (NPP) plays a central role in biological carbon pump (BCP) and global carbon cycling, but NPP estimates in high-latitude regions remain highly uncertain despite their disproportional contribution to the global carbon sink. Previous studies identified discrepancies among satellite- and in situ-derived NPP estimates, but the drivers of disagreement remain poorly resolved due to limited high-frequency observations. abstract: ABSTRACT Background Thalassemia trait (TT) and iron deficiency anemia (IDA) represent the most common causes of microcytic hypochromic anemia (MHA) and are challenging to differentiate in clinical settings. Data regarding the genetic and clinical characteristics of TT in Northern China remain insufficient, highlighting an urgent need for rapid and efficient diagnostic strategies for the regional population. title: The Broad Ecological Range of Salmonella enterica Serotype Typhimurium Is Associated With Genomic Diversification
abstract: Salmonella Typhimurium is a versatile foodborne pathogen with a broad ecological range, making it an ideal model to better understand pathogen adaptations that allow them to infect multiple hosts and persist across environments. title: Host-country media discourse and China’s economic presence in Africa
abstract: China’s economic engagement in Africa takes place in changing host-country discourse environments, yet the consequences of adverse media reporting for China’s overseas presence remain unclear. We argue that worsening media tone can signal rising operating risk and may therefore trigger adjustment across different margins of presence. abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) deployments authenticate an increasing volume of heterogeneous device traffic under adversarial conditions, and single-stage classifiers—whether shallow or deep—tend to commit to a label at every operating point, including the ambiguous region where the decision boundary is least reliable. This behaviour inflates both the False Acceptance Rate (FAR) and the False Rejection Rate (FRR) precisely where an authentication system can least afford it. abstract: In this study, the detection of WS events (microburst (MB), wake vortex (WV), sea breeze (SB), and gust front (GF)) was achieved by analysing measurement values based on a newly developed point measurement method (anemometer, temperature/humidity, wind vane, and pressure sensors). The same meteorological data were analysed alongside the generator and rotor RPM values of the nearest wind turbine. title: Socio-economics of elasmobranch fisheries in India: ecological, livelihood and governance dimensions
abstract: Sharks and rays are an important yet heterogeneous component of India’s marine fisheries, contributing to food supply, household income, processing, trade and associated services, while many species have life-history characteristics that make them sensitive to sustained fishing mortality. This review synthesizes ecological, fisheries, livelihood, market and governance evidence on Indian shark and ray fisheries using a structured narrative evidence-synthesis approach with documented information sources, search strings, eligibility criteria, a source hierarchy and fixed extraction fields. abstract: Abstract We show how CO 2 ‐storage sites could be monitored using fibre‐optic cables as sensors and local earthquakes as natural sources. The method uses shear‐wave resonances, which are observable in sedimentary layers with strong shear‐wave velocity contrasts often occurring for shallow sand layers embedded in shale. title: Molecular surveillance of drug resistance markers in Plasmodium falciparum isolates from Ghana
abstract: The emergence and spread of Plasmodium falciparum drug-resistant parasites remain a significant hurdle to malaria control and elimination. However, how changes in transmission affect the evolution of drug resistance remains incompletely understood. We investigated the spatiotemporal prevalence of drug resistance across three distinct eco-epidemiological zones of Ghana (Guinea Savannah, Forest and Coastal) by characterizing genetic polymorphisms in five drug resistance genes ( pfdhfr, pfdhps, pfmdr1, pfk13 and pfmdr2 ). title: Integrating Information From Hydrologic Models and SWOT Remote Sensing Measurements to Estimate Discharge Across River Networks
abstract: Abstract The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite has the potential to improve knowledge of river discharge globally. However, SWOT discharge algorithms are informed by global hydrological model data, and a portion of the model's systematic bias is passed along to the SWOT discharge time series. To address this issue, we present a new algorithm designed to reduce systematic bias in SWOT discharge. abstract: Brackish groundwater is a strategic supply buffer for arid states reliant on energy-intensive seawater desalination, yet the operational condition of legacy well fields and the distribution-side limits on dispatchable volume remain understudied. Both are addressed here for Kuwait, where desalination supplies ∼ 92% of municipal water. title: Characterizing growth patterns of bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops truncatus) in Sarasota Bay
abstract: Growth patterns of specific body structures provide insight into the physiological and developmental processes underlying their function; however, collecting morphological data on these body structures is challenging for large animals in the marine environment due to the logistics of collecting hands-on measurements and the limitations of data provided by other methods (e.g., photogrammetry). abstract: Immersive virtual reality has entered universities with promises of deeper learning, yet the available evidence shows heterogeneous results that depend heavily on the conditions under which it is used. This reflection article critically analyzes the integration of this technology into teaching and learning processes in higher education and asks under which pedagogical, cognitive, technological and ethical conditions it can help improve them. title: MUSEUMS, EDUCATION AND TECHNOLOGY AS DRIVERS OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN ALONISSOS, LESVOS AND KOS
abstract: This study examines the pirate and maritime cultural heritage of Alonnisos, Lesvos, and Kos, three islands that, despite their geographical distance, share a long-standing historical relationship with the sea and the risks associated with maritime activity. It explores how pirate raids, privateering, and maritime rivalries influenced the organization of settlements, the construction of fortifications, economic activity, and the collective memory of local communities. abstract: Understanding how biofilms came to be recognized as spatially organized, three-dimensional (3D) communities (rather than isolated planktonic cells) requires tracing the conceptual shift that redefined bacterial life as architecturally structured. title: Mapping soil salinity and prediction uncertainty across different depths using quantile regression forests
abstract: Accurate assessment of soil salinity across the soil profile is necessary for sustainable agricultural management, yet conventional surface-based observations often provide limited information about subsurface salinity conditions. This study developed a depth-resolved digital soil mapping framework to predict soil electrical conductivity (EC) across five standard depth intervals (0–25, 25–50, 50–75, 75–100, and 100–125 cm) in Shandong Province, eastern China. title: High resolution spatiotemporal modelling of outdoor temperature for assessment of heat-related health inequalities in Accra, Ghana
abstract: Abstract Urban heat exposure is unevenly distributed within cities, often disproportionately affecting socially and environmentally vulnerable populations. In Sub-Saharan Africa(SSA), where warming is occurring faster than the global average, the lack of high-resolution temperature data constrain efforts to characterize exposure patterns and inform epidemiological research and urban heat adaptation. We developed the first ground-based spatiotemporal outdoor temperature surfaces for a major SSA city using an 18-month measurement campaign across the Greater Accra Metropolitan Area (GAMA), Ghana.

title: The agricultural synergistic dividend of environmental regulation and the identification of the net total effect: Evidence from China’s Air Pollution Prevention and Control Action Plan
abstract: This study evaluates the agricultural co-benefits of large-scale environmental regulation. Existing studies often focus on crop yields and condition on production inputs that may themselves respond to policy interventions, potentially understating the overall production effect. abstract: Early successional species like piping plovers ( Charadrius melodus ) rely on storms and other natural disturbances to create and maintain habitat on coastal landscapes, but anticipating year-to-year habitat availability for management purposes is difficult where dynamic conditions persist. Our objective was to understand how piping plover nesting habitat changed over an eight-year period (imagery years 2014–2022) at Cape Lookout National Seashore, North Carolina, United States of America. title: The Promise and Limitations of Metabolic Trait Prediction Across Diverse Bacteria
abstract: Metabolic traits mediate microbial interactions and underpin mechanistic models of community assembly. With the rapid expansion of genomic data and bioinformatic tools, it is widely assumed that metabolic traits such as substrate utilization can be reliably inferred from genomes alone. abstract: Rapid land subsidence is commonly experienced along the northern coast of Java, Indonesia, and this geological natural hazard tends to severely threaten infrastructure, including environmental degradation. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Climate change poses a major global challenge, and forests are increasingly recognized for their role in carbon sequestration. This review employs a dual analytical framework, integrating a systematic bibliometric analysis with a structured thematic synthesis, to assess the carbon storage potential of Morocco’s forest ecosystems across both biomass and soil organic carbon pools. abstract: Structure from Motion photogrammetry has become an increasingly relevant method for digital data acquisition in construction and civil engineering. By using overlapping images, three - dimensional point clouds, digital terrain models, meshes and visual documentation can be generated without the need for expensive scanning equipment. abstract: Abstract. This study evaluates a range of classification strategies for generating snow-covered area (SCA) maps from UAS imagery with 3 cm pixels collected over open areas in southern New Hampshire, USA and offers practical recommendations for producing UAS-derived SCA maps. abstract: In fragile economies, inflation is a critical macroeconomic issue for household well-being in vulnerable nations. As prices increase, at-risk families are forced to diminish essential consumption, remove children from formal education, and forsake long-term developmental goals to satisfy immediate survival requirements. In this regard, this study examines the impact of climate change, food commodity prices, and political stability on inflation in Somalia. abstract: Abstract Meeting the Paris Agreement’s climate targets demands an unprecedented expansion of renewable energy. Despite global commitments, significant implementation gaps persist due to economic, policy, and technical uncertainties. Here, we develop a Global Power Capacity Dynamics Framework, integrating facility-level data, machine learning and transition modeling to assess the feasibility of global power expansion. abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) have emerged as a highly promising technology for sustainable green hydrogen production because of their high energy efficiency, rapid dynamic response, and compatibility with intermittent renewable-energy systems. abstract: Frequent shallow loess slope failures in loess regions pose significant threats to both linear infrastructure and local communities. Millimeter-scale initial cracks induced by water, temperature, and weathering are key factors controlling such loess failures. Early diagnosis and prevention remain challenging, largely because the disaster chain triggered by millimeter-scale initial cracks is not fully understood, and the early failure behavior of these cracks is poorly characterized. abstract: Background Drawing on conservation of resources (COR) theory, this study examines the associations of job continuance insecurity (JCI) and job conditions insecurity (JCO) with proactive work behavior (PWB) and employee innovative behavior (EIB), including age and education profiles. abstract: Abstract Predictive conservation for tropical built heritage is hindered by the persistent separation of continuous environmental sensing from computational deterioration diagnostics. title: An extreme precipitation structural dominance index for summer precipitation patterns over eastern China
abstract: Climate change is altering precipitation across the full spectrum of intensity categories, with potentially profound consequences for the spatial distribution of seasonal rainfall and for regional drought–flood patterns. However, conventional metrics of extreme precipitation focus on its frequency, intensity, or total amount, leaving a critical question unanswered: how does the changing contribution of high-intensity events shape the spatial structure of seasonal precipitation? abstract: Azospirillum baldaniorum Sp245 is a plant growth-promoting rhizobacterium (PGPR) whose ability to benefit host crops depends on robust root colonization, a process driven by the transition from a planktonic state to a sessile, biofilm-associated lifestyle. This study investigated the capacity of A. baldaniorum Sp245 to form Red, Dry, and Rough (RDAR) morphotype biofilms. abstract: Abstract Wildfires are a major source of black carbon (BC) and their increasing frequency and intensity have enhanced BC deposition onto snowpack across western North America, which accelerates snowmelt and triggers multiple feedbacks that can substantially alter atmospheric composition and regional hydrology. title: A UAV-LiDAR based paradigm for rapid forest-vegetation health screening using canopy structural indicators
abstract: Forest health assessment is essential for ecosystem conservation and climate-change adaptation, yet existing approaches often rely on labor-intensive field surveys or complex multi-source remote-sensing workflows. This study developed a rapid structural screening framework for forest health based on unmanned aerial vehicle light detection and ranging (UAV-LiDAR). abstract: Bacterial biofilms are highly structured microbial communities that contain bacterial cells that bind to biotic or abiotic surfaces and are enclosed in a matrix of extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) secreted by the bacteria themselves. abstract: Nowadays, Mediterranean islands are home to several, often endemic, amphibians. Knowledge is limited, however, about amphibian palaeocommunities in the islands and palaeoislands of the Mediterranean Sea, despite the certain presence of fossils in such areas. One case with known but understudied insular amphibian fossils are the Gargano Terre Rosse, a complex of fissures in Southern Italy representing the remaining evidence of a Late Miocene (palaeo)insular fauna. title: The Aftermath of Almost: Communicating Risk Amid Community Narratives of Near Misses
abstract: Unpredictable weather means that serious threats do not always unfold as forecast. Hurricane near misses create an especially challenging communication context: The absence of harm may invite community explanations that make the event feel less threatening, even as future risk persists. This study examines how community narratives and post-event risk messages shape risk perception, collective efficacy, preparedness intentions, message sharing, and credibility after hurricane near misses. This study examines sustainability‐linked evaluation in island and coastal tourism by distinguishing eco‐delight from eco‐friction, defined as environmentally anchored inconvenience rather than generic dissatisfaction. abstract: The long-term success of hip and dental implants is often compromised by stress shielding and poor energy dissipation, leading to aseptic loosening. title: The Mediating Effects of Trust in an Institution on the Relationship between Perceived Transparency and Student Satisfaction in Higher Learning Institutions: Evidence from Tanzania
abstract: Higher learning institutions (HLIs) are essential bases for a knowledge economy by developing human capital and technology. The HLIs fuel developing countries such as Tanzania to remain competitive in the current global economy. This paper explores the relationship between perceived transparency, trust in an HLI and student satisfaction. title: A decade after the implementation of primary healthcare under one roof: policy evaluation and recommendations for integrated quality healthcare delivery in Nigeria
abstract: Abstract This study sought to evaluate the progress made over a decade of implementing the Primary Healthcare Under One Roof (PHCUOR) policy in Nigeria. abstract: Many New England salt marshes are rapidly degrading due to the combined effects of accelerating sea-level rise (SLR) and other anthropogenic stressors, resulting in loss of high-marsh vegetation and threatening marsh-dependent wildlife such as the Saltmarsh Sparrow ( Ammospiza caudacuta ). abstract: Background: PANoptosis contributes to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) pathogenesis. abstract: Large sectors of the Antarctic Peninsula remain incompletely surveyed for breeding seabirds, while historical records often lack the spatial and methodological detail required to assess change. abstract: Abstract Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease, characterised by motor neuron degeneration and intrinsic neuronal hyperexcitability, with a lack of disease modifying treatments. One of the major challenges in therapeutic development for ALS is the genetic heterogeneity. Thus, there is a pressing need for human models of sporadic and familial ALS that enable identification of convergent, genotype-independent neuroprotective mechanisms that correct multiple ALS-associated phenotypes. abstract: Increasing quinoa yields through improved nutrient and water management is critical for smallholder farmers in Morocco. abstract: China faces regional disparities in agricultural development. Understanding the spatiotemporal evolution of agricultural production efficiency and its driving factors is essential for advancing sustainable agricultural development. Using panel data from China’s 31 provinces from 2013 to 2023, we constructed an input–output indicator system and applied the super-efficiency slacks-based measure (SBM) model to evaluate agricultural production efficiency. abstract: Abstract Probabilistic tsunami hazard assessment (PTHA) at the inundation level over large spatial scales remains computationally challenging, requiring many scenarios, fine-resolution modelling, and high-quality digital elevation models (DEMs). Previous studies have addressed either regional offshore hazards or local-scale inundation, leaving comprehensive regional inundation assessments largely unexplored. abstract: Introduction The intestinal microbiota is increasingly recognized as an important contributor to host digestive physiology; however, its potential contribution to digestive capacity during fish larval development remains largely unknown. Here, we investigated the coordinated development of host digestive physiology and gut microbial function throughout larval ontogeny in greater amberjack ( Seriola dumerili ) larvae sampled at 10, 19, 32, 40 and 60 days post-hatching (dph), covering the main dietary transitions from live prey feeding through co-feeding with formulated diets to post-weaning. abstract: Abstract Sudden tropical cyclone (TC) track turns remain a major source of short range forecast error over the western North Pacific because small environmental differences can shift both the turning time and the turning location, rapidly amplifying cross track displacement. abstract: Dolphin skin microbiome is constantly exposed to a microorganism-rich medium and represents the first line of defense from environmental stressors and potential pathogens. While some bacteria cause skin diseases and ulcerating wounds, high water temperature, salinity, and pH seem to lower dolphin wound rates and promote accelerated scar healing. title: Culturable bacterial diversity in a recirculating aquaculture system for sole fish farming: analysis of potential pathogens and putative bioremediation, probiotic and antimicrobial significance
abstract: This study is the first to characterize the culturable bacterial diversity within a Recirculating Aquaculture System (RAS) for sole farming (Solea senegalensis) in Portugal, providing a comprehensive insight into its complex bacterial dynamics. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that Pseudomonadota (76.4%) was the most abundant phylum, followed by Actinomycetota (10.7%) and Bacteroidota (9.8%). abstract: Abstract The increasing strategic importance of rare earth elements is shaped by geopolitical factors, supply risks, and rising demand from high-technology, energy transition, and defense sectors, rather than geological scarcity. For the European Union, rare earth elements represent both a critical vulnerability and an essential resource for achieving policy objectives. title: Climate change adaptation in Mexico: A literature review of progress, evidence gaps, and research priorities
abstract: Adaptation to climate change is key to reducing the vulnerability of human and natural systems. Over the past decades, research on climate change adaptation in Mexico has increased considerably. Previous reviews have focused on specific aspects of climate adaptation in Mexico; however, no study has systematically synthesized adaptation research across sectors, climate risks, responses, adaptation stages, and geographic regions within a common analytical framework. abstract: Abstract The benefits of a rapid communication rate, ultrawide bandwidth, and reduced delay have made Submerged Optical Wireless Sensor Networks (SOWSNs) a popular topic of study. In very and extremely shallow conditions, infragravity wave energy significantly affects spectral wave period and wave steepness. abstract: Las actitudes hacia las matemáticas constituyen un elemento relevante en la formación inicial docente, ya que influyen en la manera en que el futuro profesorado valora y utiliza esa disciplina en contextos educativos. abstract: Landslides are a major rainfall-triggered hazard affecting road infrastructure across the mountainous terrain of western Panama. abstract: Abstract Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar is highly valuable for all-weather autonomous driving perception due to its excellent environmental robustness and range-velocity measuring capability. title: From detections to demography: methodological challenges and opportunities in survival estimation from automated telemetry networks
abstract: Survival is a fundamental demographic process influencing individual fitness and population dynamics. Automated telemetry systems offer unprecedented opportunities to estimate survival of highly mobile organisms across broad spatial and temporal scales. abstract: BACKGROUND: Skin problems are frequently reported among international travelers. However, most existing evidence is from post-travel data, which overrepresent severe or healthcare-seeking disease. The broader daily spectrum of skin events that travelers experience remains poorly characterized. We aimed to quantify the frequency, clinical course, and determinants of self-reported skin-health events during travel using prospective data. abstract: The commercialization of Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) poses a fundamental challenge to the traditional maritime tort liability system, which centers on human fault. To address this challenge, a three-pronged institutional framework centered on the shipowner, comprising strict liability, liability limitations, and compulsory insurance, should be established. abstract: ABSTRACT Environmental impact assessment (EIA) is the core link in environmental decision‐making. Risk assessment (RA) addresses this gap by enhancing the scientific basis of evaluation, supporting more defensible permitting and policy decisions, and improving transparency and public trust. abstract: Abstract: Climate and Earth-system prediction requires simultaneous representation of nonlinear multiscale dynamics, uncertain initial and boundary conditions, incomplete observations, and physical conservation laws. abstract: Abstract Long‐term beach monitoring and satellite‐derived shoreline products are typically validated, and shoreline models calibrated, along cross‐shore transects. abstract: Global change poses significant challenges to water resource management. Water Table Depth (WTD) is a critical variable linking subsurface dynamics to land-surface processes; however, real-world observations remain sparse. As mission complexity increases, the deployment of multiple USVs becomes necessary to achieve scalability, robustness, and operational efficiency. title: Utilizing calcite‐bound phosphate to reconstruct historical phosphorus loading to marl lake ecosystems
abstract: Abstract Reconstructing historical phosphorus (P) concentrations in lakes has been a long‐standing problem for paleolimnology. The most commonly applied method is the use of diatom‐inferred total P models, but there are well‐documented limitations to these approaches. Authigenic calcite co‐precipitated with P is a promising geochemical indicator of ambient P conditions in the water column through time. title: Science Needs for a Terrestrial Biosphere Tipping Point Early Warning System
abstract: Abstract Tipping points in the Earth system have the potential to cause major detrimental impacts to the biosphere and societies. Their inherent nonlinearity implies that even relatively small additional increases in external forcing might result in disproportionately large adjustments to components of the Earth system. In some cases, tipping points may lead to alternative states that would be difficult to return from. title: Enhanced Aquaculture by Water Quality Assessment Using Discriminant Analysis Algorithm
abstract: Water quality is essential for sustainable aquaculture, but its variability makes assessment difficult. This study compares linear and quadratic discriminant analysis for classifying aquaculture water conditions using a public dataset of 4,300 observations with 14 physicochemical and biological parameters. Data preprocessing included outlier removal and feature standardization, followed by a stratified train-test split without hyperparameter tuning. abstract: The fall-cone test is widely used for estimating the undrained shear strength of soft clays, yet its conventional interpretation is largely based on an empirical proportional relationship between soil strength and cone penetration. The applicability of this relationship to clays formed under one-dimensional stress histories remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates the fall-cone response of normally consolidated Malaysian kaolin prepared under K 0 conditions. abstract: Background Malawi’s water security depends on the Lake Malawi-Shire River system, which receives approximately 60% of its inflows from transboundary catchments in Tanzania and Mozambique. This dependence creates cascading cross-border climate risks that threaten downstream water infrastructure. The system exhibits threshold behavior at 474.1 m above sea level (asl), below which hydrological drought conditions emerge and outflows to the Shire River cease. abstract: ABSTRACT Gamma‐ray log motifs provide useful descriptors of vertical grain‐size trends and stacking architecture, but their ability to discriminate reservoir quality is nonunique and requires quantitative testing. abstract: Against the background of big data, clustering algorithms, as a core task of unsupervised learning, have been widely applied, and the related theories and technologies have continued to iterate and develop. abstract: The present study evaluated solid-state Volvariella volvacea- fermented rice bran (VFRB) as a potentially sustainable alternative protein source to soybean meal (SBM) in diets for juvenile milkfish ( Chanos chanos ). abstract: Ultra-shallow gas and hydrate-bearing systems in deep-water Quaternary strata are important exploration targets, but their geological controls and seismic responses remain difficult to quantify because the reservoirs are weakly consolidated, laterally heterogeneous, and commonly occur near the base of the gas-hydrate stability zone. abstract: The increasing digitalisation of maritime systems has raised concerns about cyber threats to shipping operations, port infrastructure and maritime safety. However, existing approaches often examine cyber-risk scenarios, geographical patterns and dependencies among risk factors separately. Therefore, ensuring operational safety is of paramount importance. abstract: “Non-sulfide” Zn-Pb deposits are comprised of a series of non-sulfide minerals and are of crucial economic importance. abstract: Somalia’s fisheries are characterized by substantial but largely unrealized development potential, yet domestic benefits remain limited. The widespread discharge of plastic waste into aquatic systems has led to increasing accumulation of microplastics (MPs) in freshwater environments, posing significant risks to aquatic organisms due to their high persistence. abstract: Introduction Connected healthcare networks link medical sensors, gateways, electronic health record systems and cloud services, which enlarges their exposure to cyberattacks. abstract: Fine-scale wetland mapping is challenged by fragmented patch shapes, spectral confusion between wet and dry surfaces, and the scarcity of annotated high-resolution training samples. This study proposes Wetl-SAM2YNet, a framework based on Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2, a vision foundation model), designed for community level wetland classification in arid regions. title: Distinct intraseasonal pathways driving rapidly escalating heat extremes in North China and their subseasonal predictability
abstract: Rapidly escalating heat extremes, characterized by abrupt onset and limited preparation time, pose disproportionate risks to public health, agriculture, and regional economies, yet their governing mechanisms and subseasonal predictability remain poorly understood. Here we identify 107 such events over North China during the summers of 1940–2024 and classify them into four spatial types. abstract: Abstract The Turkey Lake Watershed (TLW), located in Northern Ontario, forms a cascading lake system that ultimately drains into Lake Superior. Historically, the TLW has served as a key research site for studies on acid rain and climate change. This paper presents LDCNet, a lightweight compression framework for DenseNet-CenterNet. abstract: Microalgal cultivation generates continuous and diverse data streams, including physicochemical sensor measurements, optical and spectroscopic signals, and episodic molecular tests. abstract: Abstract Road infrastructure is central to economic development of the United States. However, particularly in cold climates, the soil temperature and annual freeze-thaw cycles significantly impact road conditions, therefore it is important to accurately predict the number of freeze-thaw cycles and their duration. abstract: High-quality development is the primary task of building a modern socialist country in all respects, which imposes all-round demands on the aerospace information infrastructure for unified benchmarks, ubiquitous precision, multi-dimensional perception, and real-time intelligence. abstract: Introduction The Bashijiqike Formation in the northern Kuqa Depression of the Tarim Basin is critical for Cretaceous petroleum exploration, yet its high-resolution stratigraphic framework remains poorly constrained. This study aims to construct a precise stratigraphic framework of the Bashijiqike Formation and reveal the coupling relationship between astronomical orbital cycles and hierarchical sequence boundaries. abstract: Surface ozone (O3) forms via nonlinear chemistry and is highly non-stationary, complicating 168-h forecasts. abstract: Although 3D shape completion facilitates robotic grasping from partial observations, deterministic completion models overlook regional uncertainty, which can result in suboptimal grasp poses. abstract: Fire, water, and ice pose persistent challenges to personal protective materials used in harsh environments. abstract: As escalating microplastic pollution reshapes aquatic ecosystems globally, the multipurpose freshwater reservoirs of Nigeria remain a critical blindspot in environmental monitoring. abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate long-horizon streamflow forecasting is crucial for water resource management, but existing models often face efficiency and interpretability challenges. abstract: Climate change has led to more frequent occurrences of extreme weather conditions and irregular rainfall patterns, making accurate prediction of rainfall amounts essential. title: On the Design of Reward Function for Reinforcement Learning–Based Trajectory Tracking Control Using the TD3 Algorithm
abstract: Abstract Reward design is one of the most influential factors in determining the performance of reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms in continuous-control tasks. This paper presents a comparative study of three reward formulations for training a TD3 agent to perform three-dimensional path following using a particle kinematic system modeled as double-integrator dynamics. The first reward is a linear formulation that assigns proportional penalties based on normalized position and velocity tracking errors. title: Spectral–temporal autofluorescence analysis for rapid and label-free microplastic differentiation in aquatic environments
abstract: Although plastic products facilitate our life essentially, the resulting pollution increasingly harms the terrestrial and aquatic environment and our health. To mitigate this pollution and to establish effective recycling strategies, analytical methods to specifically detect different plastics are required. However, common analytical methods such as Raman, near-infrared (NIR), and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy are constrained by their complex instrumentation, their signal absorption in water and/or their low signal intensities, resulting in long measurement times. title: A TCN-KANformer-MDN model for engine remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of the remaining useful life of aircraft engines is critical to the safety of aircraft operations. Targeting the two problems of modeling complex nonlinear degradation relationships and quantifying prediction uncertainty, this paper proposes a novel RUL prediction model that integrates a temporal convolutional network (TCN), KANformer, and a mixture density network (MDN). title: Passive Detection and Localization of Low Flying Aircraft in Maritime Environment and Hilly Terrain
abstract: The acoustic signature of an aircraft in flight offers ample tactical information for applications in surveillance, battlefield situational awareness, and unattended ground-sensor technology. Using the acoustic modality and its passive approach, comprehensive flight trials were conducted with low-speed propeller-driven aircraft over maritime environments and hilly terrains. abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible multimodal sensors capable of simultaneously monitoring pressure and temperature are highly desirable for wearable healthcare, physiological monitoring, and human–machine interaction. title: Elucidating the relationships between host-associated (intestinal and gill) and environmental (water and sand) microbial communities across water exchange rates in Babylonia areolata aquaculture
abstract: Water exchange is linked to survival in aquaculture, but its relationship with host–environment microbial interactions remains unclear. We aimed to characterize host-associated and environmental microbiota in Babylonia areolata (ivory shell) aquaculture, focusing on community relationships, environmental source contributions, associations with water quality, and host survival across water exchange rates. abstract: Building a maritime power is a talent problem before it is a technology problem, and application-oriented maritime undergraduate colleges sit where the two meet. Their inherited teaching models, though, were designed for a shipping industry that no longer exists, and the distance between what they produce and what the blue economy needs has widened under digital transformation. This paper asks what collaborative innovation actually looks like inside such institutions, and whether the multi-stakeholder arrangements now promoted in Chinese policy close that distance. abstract: Reliable length–age relationships are essential for the effective management of elasmobranchs. For white sharks ( Carcharodon carcharias ), traditional growth studies, have produced inconsistent results, aggravating the already complex management of this species. Recently, efforts have been made to find non-lethal alternatives that use the length increments from capture–mark–recapture (CMR) data to estimate growth in elasmobranchs. title: Reconstructing Glacier Dynamics in Complex Terrain with ICESat-2 and Gaussian Process Interpolation
abstract: Abstract. We apply Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) to ICESat-2 along-track height change data to generate spatially continuous glacier height change fields across two glaciated regions with complex topography and dynamic behaviour: Larsen-B (Antarctic Peninsula) and central Southern Svalbard. For Larsen-B, GPR-derived height change rates from 2021–2024 average −0.61 ± 0.02 m a–1, corresponding to a volume loss of 4.55 ± 0.17 km³ a–1, similar to independent estimates from TanDEM-X. title: Urban sentinels: quantifying marginal effects of impervious cover on Brachionus–Keratella dominance
abstract: Abstract Urbanization, often quantified as impervious cover, alters catchment hydrology and limnological conditions, yet sensitive bioindicators and quantitative metrics for small urban freshwater ecosystems remain limited. We evaluated whether rotifers with widespread distribution ( Brachionus and Keratella ) can serve as indicators of urbanization across 18 ponds in Berlin along an impervious-cover gradient. This study aimed to characterize the distribution patterns of age- and sex-related differences in CBC and biochemical indicators, identify the age-related inflection points of these indicators, and analyze their correlation patterns across different sexes and age groups. title: Environment-adaptive Acoustic–Optical sensing for fish abundance estimation in complex aquaculture waters
abstract: Abstract Reliable fish abundance estimation is essential for the operation and management of aquaculture systems, but remains challenging under turbidity, bubble interference, target occlusion, and acoustic reverberation. This study develops an Acoustic–Optical fusion sensing framework for robust fish monitoring in complex aquaculture waters. An environment-aware geometric fusion network, termed EAGF-Net, is proposed to integrate optical appearance information with sonar-derived geometric features. title: Securing next-generation edge intelligence: A survey from federated learning to autonomous agents in cyber–physical systems
abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Small Language Models (SLMs) as autonomous agents at the network edge marks a shift in cyber–physical systems and the Internet of Things (IoT). Deploying these non-deterministic reasoning engines in resource-constrained environments, however, disrupts traditional security paradigms. This survey reviews the threats to autonomous edge agents and their defenses. title: Shared-first risk-aware open-set domain adaptation for catalogue-absent structural state identification
abstract: Abstract Bridge structural health monitoring (SHM) models are normally trained with a fixed catalogue of structural states, yet the bridge continues to change after the model is deployed. Traffic, support restraint, ageing, and local cracking can produce target responses for which no source label exists. In that situation, closed-set domain adaptation is risky because alignment may pull an unfamiliar response into a known class. abstract: Overexploitation of wildlife is one of the greatest global drivers of biodiversity loss. Yet, despite this well-established risk, data on extraction and trade are both incomplete and highly fragmented. The IPBES Global analysis estimated 50,000 species to be in trade, yet our review of wildlife trade monitoring programs found at least double that, at 107,356 species in use and trade globally. Standard procedures for counting and characterizing MFs typically involve particle extraction from the sampling matrix, filtration, and detailed inspection of the membranes to identify, classify, and characterize all detected items. Physical characterization often includes morphometric measurements such as surface area, length, and width, which significantly increases processing time. abstract: The adaptability of cyber-physical systems (CPS) can be enhanced through learning-based control, while prediction errors, distribution shifts, and faults make safety assurance challenging. This study evaluated a fault-tolerant verification architecture that separates learned-model trust, fault-relevant evidence, and physical-safety outcomes. abstract: Maritime decarbonisation requires a shift towards low- and zero-emission energy systems, while the viability of electrified vessels depends on how voyage energy is provided onboard and replenished externally. Existing reviews mainly organise the field around technologies, vessel configurations and replenishment solutions, with less attention to how energy provision and system constraints shift across the ship-shore system. title: Environment-Specific Guidance Improves Forecast Skill for Isolated Convection Initiation over South China
abstract: Abstract Is convection initiation (CI) harder to forecast in some large-scale environments? Using 8,607 radar-detected isolated CI events over South China during 2018–2023 and ERA5 fields, we identify two recurrent pre-CI environments: a thermal environment with broad warm-moist support and a dynamic environment with more organized flow. Across 200 forecast models, dynamic cases generally have lower skill than thermal cases. title: Ada-TransGBC: A shadow-aware deformable attention network for multi-class gallbladder ultrasound image classification
abstract: Background Gallbladder ultrasound classification is challenging because of irregular lesion morphology, acoustic shadowing, and overlapping imaging characteristics. This study proposes Ada-TransGBC, a lightweight framework integrating complementary attention and boundary-guided learning mechanisms for five-class gallbladder ultrasound classification. title: Comparative Modeling and Prediction of Sulfur Dioxide (SO₂) Concentrations Across Air Quality Monitoring Stations in Bangladesh
abstract: Air pollution remains a critical environmental and public health concern in Bangladesh, contributing to an estimated 236,000 deaths in 2021 alone and ranking as the country's leading mortality risk factor. Rapid industrialization and urbanization frequently push pollutant levels beyond national air quality standards. Sulfur dioxide ( S O 2 ), a key pollutant of industrial emissions and combustion, has received comparatively less research attention than particulate matter, despite its contribution to acid deposition and secondary pollutant formation. title: A cross-domain fault diagnosis method for high-speed train axlebox bearings based on time-frequency mapping and adversarial networks
abstract: Abstract The health condition of axlebox bearings in high-speed trains is directly associated with operational safety. However, variations in rotational speed, load, and operating environment induce pronounced domain shift in vibration signals, which undermines the generalization capability of intelligent diagnosis models trained under a single operating condition.To address this issue, this paper proposes a cross condition bearing diagnosis method integrating a CNN BiLSTM hybrid network and multi constraint domain adaptation for cross condition diagnosis of high speed train axle box bearings.

abstract: Sustainable local economic development at the village level requires a balance between community welfare, environmental protection, and effective local governance. In Madura, the use of natural resources remains insufficiently aligned with environmental carrying capacity, creating challenges for achieving sustainable village development and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). title: Phase‐Shift‐Assisted Wind‐Driven Triboelectric Nanogenerator With a Ternary Contact Structure for Low‐Ripple Output and Corrosion‐Related Applications
abstract: The wind energy frictional nano‐generator (W‐TENG) can efficiently collect low‐frequency, random mechanical energy from the wind for self‐powered systems, such as smart farms; however, the practical output signal has severe pulse and fluctuation issues. This article introduces a phase‐shift‐assisted wind‐driven W‐TENG with a ternary contact structure. abstract: Super-wavelength uniform linear arrays (SW-ULAs) reduce receive channels, but broad transmit illumination produces grating replicas. title: Unsupervised Wavelet Scattering Autoencoders for Efficient Malicious Client Detection in Federated Coffee Leaf Disease Classification: A Kenyan Arabica Case Study
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables geographically dispersed edge devices to jointly train a shared model without transmitting raw data, which is essential in precision agriculture, where bandwidth constraints, sensor heterogeneity, and data sovereignty preclude centralized processing. Yet FL remains vulnerable to malicious or faulty clients injecting corrupted data, a threat amplified in open-field deployments where nodes can be physically compromised or adversarially controlled. title: Dams not to blame for all reservoir carbon emissions from retained organic carbon
abstract: Dams trap organic carbon (OC) and create carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) emission hotspots within reservoirs, underlying the ongoing debate over their role in carbon emissions. However, even without dams, this labile OC would still decompose and emit CO 2 or CH 4 during downstream transport and after deposition in estuaries. Thus, relying solely on dammed reservoir observations to assess these emissions may introduce considerable bias. Implementing environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices offers a strategic pathway to enhance sustainability performance in this sector; however, it remains difficult to determine which managerial and operational actions can most effectively drive improvements in ESG performance. abstract: Abstract In order to study the source of nitrate pollution in shallow groundwater in the agricultural area, surface water, groundwater and soil samples were collected, and the conventional chemical indicators and nitrogen and oxygen isotopes were analyzed. title: Stochastic Operator Residual Learning with Conformal Calibration for Risk-Aware Wind Turbine Maintenance
abstract: Wind turbine maintenance decisions are frequently made under uncertainty, yet conventional degradation models often provide deterministic predictions that ignore the tail risks associated with unexpected component failure. We propose a stochastic operator residual learning framework with conformal calibration for risk-aware wind turbine maintenance. abstract: Abstract Rolling bearing fault diagnosis is critical for the reliable operation of rotating machinery. However, vibration signals collected under varying sampling rates, devices, and operating conditions often exhibit domain shifts, and only limited labeled samples are available in the target domain. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a multi-scale physics-frequency bidirectional Mamba network (MS-PFMamba) for cross-sampling-rate, cross-device, and few-shot bearing fault diagnosis. title: CLAIRE: A dual encoder network with RIFT loss and Phi-3 small language model based interpretability for cross-modality synthetic aperture radar and optical land cover segmentation
abstract: Accurate land cover classification from satellite imagery is crucial in environmental monitoring and sustainable resource management. However, it remains challenging due to the complexity of natural landscapes, the visual similarity between classes, and the significant class imbalance in the available datasets. abstract: Ports already share data, and system-to-system port-clearance APIs and practical port-to-port trials show that digital exchange is feasible. The unresolved issue addressed here is how sharing should be governed when the next destination is uncertain, especially in tanker, bulk and tramp trades. This exploratory secondary-data case study uses official Indian port statistics, Chennai Port documents, public Maritime Single Window material, IMO and industry standards, and published research. title: Cold stress in fish: global mechanisms, adaptive strategies, and translational solutions for climate-resilient aquaculture
abstract: Water temperature is a fundamental abiotic factor that governs fish physiology, behavior, and survival. Although anthropogenic climate change is characterized by long-term warming and an overall decline in the frequency and intensity of cold extremes, regional climate variability and episodic cold events can still expose wild and farmed fishes to abrupt or physiologically stressful low-temperature conditions. abstract: Accurate load demand forecasting serves as the fundamental prerequisite for data reliability analysis in multi-user heterogeneous load access scenarios. In such environments, the volume of data flows generated by industrial, residential, and commercial loads exhibits complex temporal variation patterns characterized by distinct periodicity and volatility. abstract: This study investigated the anti-inflammatory effects of Spartina anglica extract (SAE) in a human keratinocyte model of inflammation. HaCaT cells were stimulated with tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and interferon-γ (IFN-γ) to induce inflammatory responses. Cell viability was assessed using the MTT assay to determine non-cytotoxic concentrations. title: Does AI predict personality traits? A meta-analytic review of machine-predicted Big Five scores: Convergence and caveats
abstract: The validity of AI prediction on personality remains underexplored. In this study, we examine the convergence between machine-predicted and self-reported Big Five scores through two integrated multilevel meta-analyses(K=121) addressing both regression and classification tasks. Our results reveal convergent validity, with pooled mean correlations ranging from .38 to .44 (95% CI: .16–.58) and mean accuracy scores between 65% and 70% (95% CI: 60%–74%). This study evaluated whether short‐term dietary exposure to fluorescently labeled polyethylene microplastics (PE‐MPs) produced concentration‐dependent changes in growth, survival, intestinal morphology, and skeletal‐muscle integrity in Asian seabass fingerlings. abstract: Welding enables cost-effective fabrication of large structures in shipbuilding, aerospace and automotive industries, but repeated thermal cycles during multi-stage assembly inevitably cause distortions that often exceed design tolerances, degrading structural performance and requiring costly corrections. title: Cross-modal topology decodes battery faults from sparse voltage snapshots
abstract: Battery safety remains the primary bottleneck for mass electric vehicle (EV) adoption, yet field monitoring is hamstrung by a fundamental asymmetry: complex electrochemical faults must be diagnosed via sparse, low-frequency voltage measurements. Existing methods struggle to resolve the signal ambiguity between overlapping fault modes without hardware upgrades. title: Computational Performance of ONNX Runtime and NCNN Frameworks for Real-Time Motorcycle Detection on Raspberry Pi 5: A Yogyakarta CCTV Case Study
abstract: The acceleration of Smart City initiatives across Indonesia has intensified the demand for localized Intelligent Transportation Systems. Although micro-architectures like YOLOv26n offer optimized layer configurations, executing these models for real-time motorcycle detection on standalone edge computers often presents hardware bottlenecks due to software runtime inefficiencies and core thermal stress. This study presents a comparative computational performance benchmarking of the out-of-the-box YOLOv26n architecture across two prominent runtime frameworks: ONNX Runtime and the NCNN framework.

abstract: How to efficiently and reasonably carry out path planning has always been a hot spot of research in the field of warehouse logistics robots. abstract: Airfoil design remains a challenging multi-objective optimization problem requiring precise geometric control for optimal aerodynamic performance. abstract: We review 224 studies of financial data analytics published between 2020 and 2026 and document a mismatch between the questions the field asks and the designs it uses to answer them.
