Although population assignment is a powerful tool, accuracy can be low when populations have unequal odds of being sampled, which may arise from factors such as differences in population sizes, migration patterns, or behavior. title: An operational Sentinel-2 methodology for burned-area mapping in heterogeneous landscapes
abstract: Reliable detection and mapping of burned areas are critical for managing the growing impact of fires on agricultural land and natural ecosystems. In southern and eastern Europe, fires cause economic losses and environmental damage through deforestation, habitat loss and carbon emissions, while disrupting ecosystem services, accelerating soil erosion and altering soil moisture and microclimate in ways that hinder recovery. abstract: Background In cross-subject electroencephalography (EEG)-based driving-fatigue detection, most existing decoders are designed around second-scale short windows, whereas fatigue is a slow drift; short-window spectral features provide little direct evidence of that slow drift, limiting fatigue decisions. abstract: The object of this study is the concept of a “route”, which requires reconsideration. A conventional route is represented by a polyline consisting of waypoints and verified in ECDIS; this is sufficient for a navigator but not for an automatic control system that must execute the route. The article proposes a formalization of the digital route of a Maritime Autonomous Surface Ship (MASS) as an extension of the standard IEC 61174 route format (RTZ) by adding turn arcs with wheel-over points, corridors and safety zones, a speed profile, and time stamps. abstract: Abstract Intense solar eruptions can be followed by solar proton events (SPEs) and geomagnetic storms (GMSs), posing potential risks to spacecraft operations, communication and navigation systems, and power grids. Existing studies mainly forecast a single disturbance type, with limited attention to subsequent disturbances associated with an individual solar eruption. title: Transport and retention of microplastics during riverbank filtration
abstract: Introduction Riverbank filtration (RBF) is a widely used natural water treatment process; however, the fate and attenuation of microplastics (MPs), within river–aquifer systems is not well understood. This study investigated the occurrence and characteristics of MPs within an RBF system to comprehend the MPs transport behaviour. abstract: Microbial symbionts may enhance adaptation to environmental stress, yet their role in nutrient-enriched freshwater habitats remains unclear. We conducted a full-factorial laboratory experiment with least killifish, Heterandria formosa, manipulating water chemistry from four Florida springs and gut microbiota inoculations from conspecifics at those sites. title: Preliminary LEAP-Based Scenario Analysis of Electricity Demand and Renewable Energy Development in South Sulawesi
abstract: South Sulawesi possesses abundant renewable energy potential, particularly from hydro, wind, solar, and biomass resources. However, rapid population growth and increasing energy consumption across sectors create challenges in ensuring sustainable energy supply and planning. This study aims to project the mid-term renewable energy supply and demand in South Sulawesi using the Long-range Energy Alternatives Planning (LEAP) model. abstract: Hydraulic infrastructure inspection is laborious due to the massive scale of structures and the need for precise crack measurement. This study presents a pioneering framework integrating unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based photogrammetry, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), and semantic scene understanding to revolutionize hydraulic structural health monitoring. title: Natural compounds targeting cancer-associated genes: Multi-omics mechanisms and therapeutic potential
abstract: Cancer is caused by excessive expression of oncogenic proteins as well as inactivity of tumor suppressor proteins. In this way, complex gene regulatory processes are altered, leading to uncontrolled proliferation, chromosomal instability, and metastasis. Furthermore, conventional cancer therapy encounters severe challenges associated with drug cytotoxicity and multidrug resistance, as it focuses on a single drug target mechanism. abstract: In cellular networks, wireless traffic forecasting is essential for proactive communication system adaptation. Wireless traffic prediction at the edge using Federated Learning (FL) has garnered a lot of attention due to its improved privacy protection and exemption from raw data transmission. However, existing FL-based traffic prediction methods still require substantial gradient exchange between local customers and a central server, and it remains unclear how to model the spatial dependencies among local customers within the FL architecture. abstract: China’s consolidated maritime enforcement system connects dispersed domestic powers with new obligations under the Ecological and Environmental Code (EEC) and the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement. This study examines the relationship between China’s implementation responsibility and the legality of a specified China Coast Guard (CCG) measure. abstract: The Triassic Yanchang Formation in the QingChengBei (QCB) area of the Ordos Basin, China, hosts an “upper-generation and lower-reservoir” type of tight oil reservoir, indicating that the source rocks must have experienced abnormally high paleo-pressure during the reservoir-forming period, resulting in a strong source-reservoir pressure difference. title: Effect of pH and exposure duration on the deterioration of vegetation-growing concrete attacked by oxalic and acetic acid
abstract: Vegetation-growing concrete supports plant growth through interconnected pores, but root-secreted organic acids progressively degrade its cementitious matrix, threatening long-term durability. However, the coupled effects of acid type, pH, and exposure duration remain insufficiently quantified, and the distinct degradation mechanisms of oxalic and acetic acids are not well understood. title: Red List Index of Western Palearctic freshwater fishes
abstract: The Red List Index (RLI) is a key indicator for global biodiversity targets, but its application to freshwater fishes has been limited by infrequent reassessment and sparse monitoring data. To address this gap, we developed the first comprehensive RLI for freshwater fishes of the Western Palearctic (Europe, West Asia, and North Africa), based on two comparable global assessment rounds. abstract: O avanço dos processos de degradação na zona costeira de Maceió (Alagoas, Brasil) reforça a necessidade de adoção de ferramentas participativas para o monitoramento dos impactos associados às mudanças climáticas. abstract: Accurate prediction of gas turbine maximum power output is critical for electricity market bidding and grid stability in renewable-integrated power systems. Physics-based models cannot adequately capture performance degradation caused by equipment aging, while data-driven models, particularly tree-based ensembles, exhibit poor extrapolation beyond training ranges, posing a critical limitation under increasingly extreme weather conditions. abstract: Abstract Extending previous work focused on tropical cyclone (TC) rainband distinctions, this study employs polarimetric radar observations to examine the multiscale microphysical characteristics of Typhoon Doksuri (2023). abstract: Abstract. Cloud-layer identification is a key prerequisite for automated ground-based lidar processing, but remains challenging in Raman lidar networks because of incomplete near-range overlap, weak high-level cloud echoes, day–night signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) contrasts, energy fluctuations, and aerosol–cloud ambiguity. abstract: Abstract Absolute angular position measurement is critical for automated systems, yet conventional optical and magnetic encoders often suffer from complex alignment, vulnerability to dirty environments, or high cost. This paper proposes a proof-of-concept angular measurement scheme that converts rotational displacement into monotonic distance variations via a helical reference surface, measured by a single-point Time-of-Flight (ToF) distance sensor. abstract: Determination of heavy metals, trace elements and rare earth elements (REEs) in sediments, soils, plants, molluscs, fish, water, aerosols and related environmental matrices is a foundation for pollution assessment, food safety, biomonitoring, geochemical tracing and human-health risk evaluation. abstract: Abstract Context recognition and rare event classification in unlabeled audio represent critical challenges in both academic and industrial domains. These technologies hold significant potential for applications such as IoT-based predictive maintenance, surveillance systems (e.g., crime scene analysis or aviation incident investigations), and urban management (e.g., traffic monitoring). abstract: Robust genotype-to-phenotype (G2P) prediction is essential for accelerating grapevine (Vitis spp.) breeding decisions and genetic gain. However, it remains challenging to measure complex traits under variable field conditions and across years. In this study, we propose a linear-Transformer (LiT)-G2P, an automated predictive framework that integrates additive genetic variance effects with Transformer-based nonlinear interactions using genome-wide single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) data. abstract: L'incorporation de la technologie IoT dans les réseaux d'approvisionnement en eau offre la possibilité d'améliorer la surveillance, le contrôle et l'efficacité opérationnelle, représentant ainsi une révolution dans la gestion des infrastructures urbaines. abstract: Saudi chemical manufacturing depends on reliable water supplies for reaction media, steam generation, cooling, cleaning and utility services, yet conventional wastewater management often treats these interconnected demands as separate engineering problems. abstract: Accurate grid-to-site height correction of tropospheric mapping functions is essential for space geodesy. abstract: Abstract Detecting tiny objects in aerial imagery remains challenging due to their minimal scale, diverse orientations, and complex background interference, limiting the ability of existing methods to capture discriminative features. abstract: Plastic pollution in landfills presents a significant environmental challenge, as macroplastics fragment into persistent and harmful micro- and nanoplastics. abstract: Turkish cuisine, renowned for its rich culinary traditions, is influenced by various cultures and geographical regions of Turkiye. abstract: Introduction Six-wheel rocker–bogie rovers encounter nonlinear dynamics, variable traction, and wheel slip that can degrade the performance of fixed-gain proportional–integral–derivative (PID) controllers. abstract: Lightning-induced canopy gaps are an important form of fine-scale disturbance in mangrove forests, with implications for regeneration, canopy structure, and forest heterogeneity. Reconstructing their long-term dynamics remains challenging because recovery is prolonged and historical high-spatial-resolution imagery is temporally sparse and heterogeneous among sensors. abstract: Abstract The growing variety of flight data, the expanding scope of its applications, and the continuous improvement in data quality have collectively accelerated the digital transformation of the aviation industry. abstract: This study examines the real-world operational applications of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) technologies in smart ports and their implications for port management and digital transformation strategies. abstract: As applications of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) continue to expand across sectors such as logistics, surveillance, and environmental monitoring, the development of safe and robust autonomous navigation capabilities has become increasingly important. abstract: Abstract Public art increasingly contributes to the identity, cultural expression, and experiential quality of contemporary public spaces, particularly along waterfront promenades that function as major urban gathering areas. This study examines the role and spatial integration of public art along the Limassol Promenade in Cyprus and evaluates its contribution to place identity and user experience. abstract: La adopción masiva de herramientas de inteligencia artificial generativa (IAGen) por parte del estudiantado universitario ha superado la capacidad de respuesta de las instituciones educativas, especialmente en disciplinas como la ingeniería del agua donde la fiabilidad numérica de los cálculos es crítica para la seguridad de las infraestructuras y la adecuada gestión del recurso. abstract: Fish-vaccine efficacy in teleosts is still established primarily through pathogen-challenge experiments, which determine whether a formulation protects but provide limited insight into the antigens and immune mechanisms responsible. Proteomics addresses part of this limitation by measuring pathogen proteins and host responses induced by vaccination. abstract: This paper presents the design and experimental realization of a 5th-order Chebyshev microstrip low-pass filter (LPF) based on a Stepped Impedance Resonator (SIR) integrating T-shaped stub topology at center frequency (fc) 5.575 GHz for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system applications. abstract: Accurate prediction of existing tunnel deformation induced by shield undercrossing is critical for construction safety control. abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the transformative potential of AI-based real-time crowding information in shaping travel behaviour, passenger well-being, and environmentally sustainable choices in rail transport—addressing both technological innovation and its socio-economic impacts. abstract: ABSTRACT Floating solar photovoltaics (FSPV) have emerged as a promising alternative to traditional ground‐mounted photovoltaic (GPV) systems. abstract: Monthly rainfall in tropical regions exhibits complex spatiotemporal variability, requiring models to simultaneously capture spatial heterogeneity and temporal patterns. abstract: The local rice varieties have a significant role in maintaining food security, agricultural biodiversity, and livelihoods in rural Indonesia. Nevertheless, local rice farming systems are under pressure in terms of environmental management, technology adoption, and institutional support. abstract: Vibration signal analysis is widely used for bearing fault diagnosis in rotating machinery, but the presence of strong background noise often masks fault-related features, reducing diagnostic accuracy. abstract: Landslides are a prevalent environmental risk in Malaysia, occurring mainly in hilly and tropical locations, often during the optimum time for heavy downpours. This study aims to assess the landslide susceptibility in Batang Kali, Selangor, Malaysia, utilizing the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) based on Geographic Information Systems (GIS). title: Local institutional quality, firm size, and innovation: evidence from Italy
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates whether local institutional quality is associated with firm-level innovation from an economic geography perspective. Focusing on Italian manufacturing firms, we examine whether cross-province differences in institutional quality are related to firms’ patenting activity and whether this relationship varies by firm size. Drawing on a longitudinal dataset of more than 125,000 manufacturing firms observed from 2011 to 2019, we combine firm-level patent data with a province-level measure of institutional quality. title: Exploring flexible sensing strategies toward embodied intelligence
abstract: The field of embodied intelligence emphasizes the adaptive development of systems through interactions with their environments, with perceptual capabilities acting as a core enabler. Accordingly, flexible sensors are increasingly integrated into embodied intelligence systems, owing to their conformability to complex morphologies and adaptability to dynamic movements. abstract: Selecting a colour palette that suits its design context (application domain, audience, and accessibility profile) affects usability, engagement, and accessibility, yet remains a difficult computational problem. Vision–language models (VLMs) have improved performance on this task but share three limitations: deterministic outputs cannot represent the variance inherent in a design brief, single-scalar training fixes the harmony–accessibility trade-off at training time, and post-hoc context filtering leaves the generator itself context-blind. title: Addressing the challenge of missing remote sensing data in cold and high-altitude regions: A Dual-branch Spatiotemporal Fusion GAN based on incomplete images
abstract: Continuous monitoring of surface dynamics in cold and high-altitude regions is of vital strategic importance. However, sensor limitations hinder the acquisition of complete high-spatiotemporal resolution images. Traditional spatiotemporal fusion models rely on cloud-free reference pairs, struggling with incomplete observations. To address this limitation, this study proposes a Dual-branch Spatiotemporal Fusion Generative Adversarial Network (DSTF-GAN) for incomplete images. title: Integrated Drought Vulnerability Assessment and Mapping of Bangalore City, India
abstract: Drought vulnerability mapping is essential for understanding the spatial distribution of water scarcity and its associated socio-environmental impacts. The present study assesses the overall drought vulnerability of Bangalore urban district, Karnataka, India, through an integrated approach combining the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) and Geographic Information System. abstract: Introduction To solve the problems of inadequate scalability, sluggish synchronization of authentication information, and high authentication overhead, an efficient authentication strategy based on a double-layer shard blockchain was presented for the cross-trust domain of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). abstract: Introduction Ecological restoration of submerged macrophytes in highly turbid waters is severely hampered by light attenuation, which imposes significant oxidative stress on plants and disrupts their physiological homeostasis. While suspended planting technology offers a solution by optimizing light exposure, the critical role of planting substrates in modulating plant stress tolerance and rhizosphere resilience remains largely unexplored—a knowledge gap that this study addresses for the first time. abstract: Fine-grained plant species classification is difficult because closely related species can exhibit highly similar morphological characteristics, limiting the effectiveness of image-only recognition. This study developed an Enhanced Multimodal Swin Transformer that combines visual features from PlantCLEF images with contextual metadata describing taxonomic hierarchy, geographical distribution, seasonal occurrence, and ecological characteristics. abstract: Recurrent ruptures of persistent asperities on the fault could explain the pattern of consecutive large earthquakes. title: Read-reference voltage adaptation for 3D NAND flash memory via RBER-aware few-shot transfer learning
abstract: Program/erase (P/E) cycling and retention drift alter the threshold-voltage distributions of 3D NAND flash, causing previously calibrated read-reference voltages to become mismatched to new operating conditions. To update read references when target measurements are limited, we propose a raw bit error rate (RBER)-aware few-shot transfer framework that adapts a Gaussian-parameter predictor from a single characterized source condition without requiring a pre-calibrated multi-condition voltage grid. title: From digital to green: the effect of corporate digital transformation on pollution emission intensity
abstract: Digital transformation is a key driver of the optimization and upgrading of China’s economic structure and a core element in the transition of China’s economic and social development towards green growth. This paper empirically analyzes the impact of corporate digital transformation on pollution emission intensity and its mechanisms. The results indicate that digital transformation significantly enhances corporate pollution emission intensity. title: Moisture content modulates DOM thermodynamic regulation of oxygen consumption in drying streambed sediments
abstract: Abstract Dissolved organic matter (DOM) thermodynamic properties regulate biogeochemical processes (e.g., O 2 consumption rates) in riverbed sediments. This connection has been established under saturated conditions, yet most streams and rivers experience variable inundation in parafluvial zones and go dry at least one day per year. abstract: Abstract Stable isotope analysis (SIA) of eye lenses can provide a retrospective view of resource use over a fish's life. This tool can be valuable for studying long‐term isotopic changes in non‐game species that typically receive limited research emphasis. abstract: Abstract Marimo, a natural microalgal-bacterial consortium, represents a low-carbon solution for nitrate pollution control in low-nutrient waters. However, the adaptation of its nitrogen-cycling network to fluctuating nitrate levels remains poorly understood. abstract: Accurate estimation of vegetation biophysical variables, including the fraction of absorbed photosynthetically active radiation (fAPAR), fraction of vegetation cover (FVC), and leaf area index (LAI), is essential for crop monitoring and management. Although Sentinel-2 provides operational biophysical variable products at 20 m resolution, uncertainties remain across crop types, particularly in woody systems such as vineyards, and this resolution is often insufficient to capture within-field variability. abstract: High-dimensional shapes need reduced representations that are compact, reconstructable, mesh-aware, and predictive of physical performance. title: Mini review of multimodal intelligence for air quality modeling
abstract: Single data sources can miss important information needed for air quality modeling. Ground stations provide accurate local measurements. Satellites, IoT sensors, traffic records, meteorology, and land-use data describe different parts of the same environmental process. These sources improve coverage and representation if they are combined. However, this combination does not guarantee better forecasting performance. title: Long-term asset planning for port facilities: utilising asset service life variation to facilitate smooth replacement efforts and reduce costs
abstract: Many assets deteriorate gradually over time. Their condition is monitored throughout this period. An asset is replaced when it reaches the end of its useful life. This study looks at assets that form part of a larger population and can share functions. These assets are for example found in ports and are used for quay wall facilities. Their service life is shorter than that of the quay wall itself. As assets do not all age at the same rate, this study investigated how these differences in service life could inform better replacement planning. title: Recent extreme heatwaves are no match for future events
abstract: Abstract In recent years, record-breaking heatwaves have occurred over many regions of the Earth causing serious impacts to human and natural systems. Here we show that recently observed exceptional heatwaves are no match to potential future 21 st century events based on multiple metrics. For several observed heatwaves, this holds even under low- and medium-emissions scenarios. In a high- to very high-emissions future, many regions are projected to experience heatwaves that generate several times more cumulative heat and are many times longer (up to several months) than the observed heatwaves.

abstract: Despite numerous meetings and impressive initiatives, floods in Jakarta remain an unresolved challenge. The March 2025 Jakarta flood, particularly in the Ciliwung Watershed, caused by heavy rainfall and worsened by rapid suburban development, became one of the city's worst in recent years, killing nine people, displacing over 90,000 residents, and causing major damage. An evaluation system for municipal new-quality productive forces is constructed covering scientific-technological, green and digital dimensions. abstract: ABSTRACT Indonesia’s relocation of its political and administrative capital from Jakarta to Ibu Kota Nusantara (IKN) has been framed around a ”Forest City” vision, yet rapid development within the Core Government Area (Kawasan Inti Pusat Pemerintahan, KIPP) raises concerns over land conversion, vegetation loss, and carbon stock decline. This study applies remote sensing techniques to systematically assess land conversion and vegetation loss in KIPP from 2021 to 2026 using PlanetScope SuperDove satellite imagery. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper investigates an adaptive fuzzy hybrid optimal event‐triggered output‐feedback control strategy for an unmanned surface vehicle (USV) subject to external disturbances. To estimate the unmeasurable velocities of the USV system and reduce the number of actuator updates, a fuzzy state estimator is designed and two event‐triggered mechanisms are established. title: Toward a Methodology for Geopolitical Analysis
abstract: A geopolítica, historicamente disputada entre o determinismo clássico e a teoria crítica, exige uma abordagem analítica rigorosa e sistemática para que possa produzir resultados relevantes para a formulação de políticas públicas. title: Fine-tuning ASR for corpus linguistics: Singapore English
abstract: Abstract Automatic speech recognition (ASR) is increasingly used to build large spoken-language corpora, yet its role is often treated as a purely technical preprocessing step. This paper argues that ASR configuration, especially model fine-tuning, constitutes a form of corpus design that directly shapes what linguistic analyses such resources can support. abstract: Central Asia (CA) faces rising temperatures and shifting atmospheric conditions, increasing the urgency to address extreme events like heatwaves and dust storms. This study examines the co-evolution and regional co-variability of heatwaves and atmospheric dust loading, represented by dust extinction aerosol optical thickness (AOT). abstract: The article addresses the problem of determining pairwise-adaptive minimum allowable values of CPA and TCPA based on fuzzy logic. title: Assessing the robustness of amortized simulation-based inference to transient noise in gravitational-wave ringdowns
abstract: Gravitational waves (GW) emitted by binary systems allow us to perform precision tests of general relativity in the strong field regime. Ringdown signals allow for probing black hole mass and spin with high precision in GW astronomy. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Tree height-diameter (H-D) models were originally developed to address the difficulty associated with measuring tree height in the field. abstract: ABSTRACT Large language model (LLM)‐based agents combine reasoning, external knowledge access, tool use and multiagent coordination in emerging clinical decision support systems. abstract: De-scattering imaging seeks to recover target information from the scattered images, which has increasingly garnered attention due to its wide-ranging applications across various fields. abstract: Carbon Dots have proven to be a highly important class of material thanks to their minute sizes, which fall in the range of 1-10 nm. abstract: This study aimed to determine the diversity of fish species found in Bagu Village, Pringgarata District, Central Lombok Regency, West Nusa Tenggara Province. Bagu Village has various aquatic ecosystems, including rivers, ponds, reservoirs, swamps, and rice fields that potentially provide habitats for various fish species. abstract: Reliably capturing transient animal behavior in the field and laboratory remains a logistical and financial challenge, especially for small ectotherms. Here, we present a camera system that is affordable, accessible, and suitable to monitor small, cold-blooded animals historically overlooked by commercial camera traps, such as small amphibians. title: Recent Slowing Arctic‐Amplified Warming Drives an Unprecedented Water Recovery in the World's Most Voluminous Freshwater Lake
abstract: Abstract The Lake Baikal, containing one‐fifth of Earth's unfrozen surface freshwater, faces increasing hydrological uncertainty under climate change. Its water balance depends on Selenga River inflow and Angara River outflow. We present a 343‐year combined Selenga and Angara streamflow reconstruction using a tree‐ring network to provide a multi‐century hydroclimatic baseline. title: Many-objective reservoir operation optimization using NSGA-III and decision-support analysis: a sustainable management framework for the Indira Sagar Reservoir, India
abstract: Abstract Efficient reservoir operation requires simultaneous consideration of competing goals related to hydropower generation, water-supply reliability, flood management, and storage regulation. However, deriving balanced operating policies becomes increasingly complex when several conflicting objectives are considered concurrently. This study develops a many-objective optimization framework for the Indira Sagar Reservoir, India, considering four objectives: maximization of hydropower generation and minimization of water deficit, spill losses, and storage deviation. abstract: History matching channelized reservoirs is severely ill-posed: a single best-fitting model is of limited value without an estimate of its uncertainty. title: Value-based principles in sustainability reporting
abstract: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles have become a dominant framework for evaluating corporate sustainability. However, despite the widespread adoption of ESG, issues such as greenwashing, inconsistent accountability, persistent social and environmental injustices, and low trust remain unresolved. To address these gaps, this conceptual paper introduces a value-based ESG framework (V-ESG), which integrates 10 values—stewardship, accountability, leadership, transformation, compassion, justice, community wellbeing, integrity, trust and interconnectedness into ESG reporting. title: An integrated spectral library and analysis workflow for laboratory identification of microplastic polymers
abstract: Abstract Microplastics are an increasing environmental concern, and their reliable identification requires fast, reproducible, and non-destructive analytical approaches. This study presents a reflectance spectral library and a dedicated software tool, the Microplastic Spectral Analysis App version 3.1, for organizing, visualizing, comparing, and classifying microplastic spectra. A three‐dimensional elastoplastic constitutive model incorporating a novel nonorthogonal flow rule is developed to describe this behavior. abstract: Automatic identification of administrative tags is vital for automating administrative form processing. title: Soil erosion response to future climate variability and best management practices in the Kesinga catchment, India
abstract: Abstract Soil erosion poses a growing threat to watershed sustainability under changing climatic conditions, particularly in monsoon-dominated regions. This study integrates the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) with bias-corrected CORDEX–South Asia climate projections to quantify present and future sediment yield and to evaluate the effectiveness of structural best management practices (BMPs) in the Kesinga catchment, eastern India. abstract: Scheduling heterogeneous resources for post-disaster recovery remains a critical challenge, as existing approaches predominantly rely on deterministic models or static heuristics that fail to capture the dynamic, uncertain, and spatially heterogeneous nature of real disaster environments. This study introduces STGR-DRS, a Spatiotemporal Graph-based Robust Disaster Recovery Scheduling framework that utilizes large-scale, multi-source open data to coordinate heterogeneous resources, including repair crews, medical teams, transportation units, and shelter provisions. title: Multi-trophic risk from human superpredators may alter predator–prey coexistence and population dynamics
abstract: Abstract Humans are efficient and deadly predators, yet they may also interact with wildlife in non-lethal ways. This study explores how interactions with lethal and non-lethal human “superpredators” alter predator-prey dynamics using an agent-based modelling approach. Our model incorporates both the consumptive (lethal) and non-consumptive (behavioural) effects of humans, as well as of predators on prey. abstract: Long-distance crude oil and gas pipelines depend on a chain of assurance extending from material acceptance and girth-weld qualification to corrosion surveillance, defect assessment and intervention. These activities are frequently managed as separate programmes, although an undetected construction deviation can later appear as an integrity threat, while uncertain inspection data can distort repair priorities. abstract: ABSTRACT Flood susceptibility maps identify potentially affected land but provide limited guidance on the form of adaptation. abstract: Introduction Phragmites australis (common reed) is a globally distributed and highly productive emergent macrophyte with important ecological functions in wetland ecosystems. However, the genetic diversity and population differentiation of P. australis in eastern China remain insufficiently characterized. Methods In this study, we performed RAD-seq-based reduced-representation genome sequencing of 98 P. australis individuals collected from populations distributed across eastern China to characterize genetic variation, population structure, and geographic differentiation among populations. abstract: Despite substantial advances in aerosol remote sensing, objective characterization of mixed aerosol regimes and their seasonal evolution over West Africa remains poorly constrained, limiting accurate assessments of aerosol–climate interactions and regional air quality. abstract: Abstract Spaceborne Global Navigation Satellite System Reflectometry (GNSS-R) has been increasingly used for inland water detection, but most reflection point based methods mainly exploit single polarization observables. Dual polarization observations may provide additional information on surface scattering conditions, especially over mixed water and land backgrounds. abstract: Abstract Land Use & Land Cover (LULC) optimisation is critical for mitigation of Urban Heat Island (UHI) effects. abstract: Subgrade compaction is a critical procedure in highway construction. To elucidate the dynamic characteristics and energy transfer mechanisms throughout the entire compaction process, this study utilized four test lanes to conduct field experiments on highway subgrade under varying numbers of rolling passes. abstract: Black carbon is a short-lived climate pollutant formed during the incomplete burning of fossil fuels. It has turned out to be a significant cause of global warming, climate change and air pollution. This paper examines the impact of urbanization and fossil fuel energy consumption on black carbon emissions across 125 countries from 2005 to 2022 with the help of both panel regression and multiple linear regression model estimated using OLS. abstract: Abstract Spirochetes are a distinctive phylum of spiral-shaped bacteria, defined by their curved periplasmic flagella, which drive motility by deforming the cell body and enabling efficient corkscrew-like propulsion through viscous environments. Despite their clinical importance, the molecular mechanisms underlying flagellar assembly, curvature and thus motility, remain poorly understood. abstract: Discrete data are prevalent across biology, from nucleotide base pairs to mating systems or petal count on a flower. How much accuracy and confidence they deliver together, and how this varies across scenarios and taxa, has not been quantified systematically. title: The limits of green incentives: a stochastic profitability analysis of sugar kelp farming in Europe
abstract: Seaweed cultivation can deliver carbon sequestration and nutrient removal, which have value beyond the market price of the biomass. If these ecosystem services were quantified, certified and compensated, they could provide additional income for farmers. This study evaluates whether such payments, together with other green incentives, can make sugar kelp ( Saccharina latissima ) farming in Europe profitable, and how much each incentive contributes. abstract: The electrochemical chlorine evolution reaction (CER) is the cornerstone of the energy-intensive chlor‑alkali industry and is also emerging as a versatile platform for on‑demand chemical synthesis and environmental remediation. abstract: Abstract Metagenomic sequencing has transformed our view of the global viral diversity, yet a fundamental bias limits our understanding of the diversity of complete viral genomes. This study developed and evaluated a low-cost hydroinformatics framework that integrates bathymetric surveying, empirical modelling, and an Android-based mobile application to monitor inter-seasonal water availability in small earth dams. title: Damage quantification for beam bridges based on definitive frequency-band transmissibility matrix
abstract: Quantifying damage severity is important for bridge operation and maintenance. Traditional vibration-based damage identification methods often rely on measurements of input excitation, abundant prior damage information, precise initial finite element models, and model updating, making it difficult to accurately and rapidly invert the local damage degree of bridges using only dynamic responses from a limited number of measurement points. title: Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data
abstract: The explosion of microbial omics data has outpaced the ability of many researchers to analyze it, with complex tools and limited computational resources creating barriers to discovery. To address this gap, we present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a free, globally accessible, community-supported platform that combines state-of-the-art analytical power with user-friendly accessibility. abstract: Homotopy is a central concept of algebraic topology with broad theoretical and applied ramifications, whose educational dimension in higher education remains scarcely documented. This systematic bibliometric review, complemented by a thematic classification of content, examined the evolution, productivity, and thematic structure of research on homotopy and determined the place that its educational dimension occupies within this literature. abstract: The restructuring of industrial cities follows various paths depending on local conditions and choices. A novel idea of a local industrial restructuring is to link the industrial park development with the circular economy. The park formations that are based on local government initiatives combine public and private interests, which poses a governance challenge, as they must generate both public value and profits for businesses. abstract: Bioeconomy can make a decisive contribution to the sustainability of agriculture, fisheries, and forestry, if it is guided by clear principles: prioritizing food and feed security, safeguarding ecosystem integrity, promoting the cascading use of biomass, and ensuring the equitable distribution of value. Nevertheless, the transition towards a circular bioeconomy requires the large-scale industrial deployment of transformative, resource-efficient technologies for biomass conversion, separation, and process integration. abstract: Reliable power supply is essential for downhole measurement and intelligent drilling systems operating in deep and ultra-deep wells. This study develops an efficient hydraulic-airfoil optimization framework for a downhole turbine generator using the NACA66 profile. abstract: Optimization algorithms have become vital to the solution of complex optimization problems that are difficult to solve using conventional methods. In this paper, we introduce a novel nature-inspired metaheuristic algorithm called the Night Jasmine Blooming Optimization (NJBO) algorithm, which is inspired by the blooming of the night jasmine plant (Cestrum nocturnum). title: Digital Transformation and Carbon Dioxide Emissions in Arab Countries: The Role of Energy Structure within an Extended STIRPAT Framework
abstract: Digital transformation has become a fundamental element of sustainability strategies across the globe; However, its environmental implications remain inconclusive, particularly in economies that depend heavily on fossil fuels. Although digital technologies can improve energy efficiency, optimize resource allocation, and support low-carbon development, their expansion may also increase electricity demand and energy consumption. title: Unreported mass movement cascades and future Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) hazard in Jammu and Kashmir, Western Himalaya
abstract: Abstract. The Warwan sub-basin in Jammu and Kashmir is a remote glaciated region containing several glacial lakes and has recently experienced population growth and infrastructure development. Due to inaccessibility and geomorphic masking, multiple mass movement events including avalanches and Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) have remained largely unreported. This study analyzes three major avalanche events from the past two decades. title: Soil health and One Health implications in the anthropocene: a perspective on microbiome engineering
abstract: Abstract Background Climate change and Anthropocene pressures accelerate soil degradation, threatening agricultural productivity, ecosystems, and human health. Within the One Health framework, soils are critical living systems. However, while physical and chemical dimensions of soil health are well studied, the biological dimension—particularly microbiome functional diversity—remains heavily underutilized in climate-resilient agriculture. abstract: The scientific characterization and information fusion of complex electromagnetic spectral spaces remain fundamental challenges because existing models often rely on inconsistent electromagnetic representations and loosely organized data structures across dimensions. To address these two problems, in this paper, a subdivision-based electromagnetic map (SEM) model for the unified encoding and fusion of electromagnetic information across six essential dimensions: space, time, frequency, power, polarization angle, and propagation angle, with GeoSOT providing the hierarchical space–time address. title: FineKarstAGB: a 30 m resolution aboveground biomass dataset for Southwest China derived by upscaling plot-level inventory using sub-meter GaoFen satellite data
abstract: Abstract. Southwest China has emerged as a key global carbon stock due to widespread forest expansion and aboveground biomass (AGB) increases driven by major ecological restoration since 2000, making accurate AGB estimations vital for assessing restoration efficacy. abstract: Abstract Natural ecosystems harbor an immense diversity of microorganisms whose metabolic capabilities remain unexplored. Therefore, the investigation of microbial life in diverse environments can reveal bacteria with unique physiological and biochemical traits, which may be useful for biotechnological applications. In this study, we report the complete genome sequencing and functional characterization of isolate BS253, isolated in a hypersaline alkaline lake from Brazil’s Pantanal region. abstract: Groundwater contamination is influenced by the natural processes which involve dispersion, adsorption and advection. These processes determine the movement of solute either in liquid or solid phase. The governing equation was formulated with time dependent dispersion coefficient in an exponential form to reflect hydrological conditions. title: Harnessing speed breeding for next-generation crop improvement through biotechnological platforms
abstract: The current challenge facing global agricultural systems is the increase in food demand against the background of climate change, reduction of arable land and emerging pests and diseases. In such circumstances, speed breeding has been a promising approach to achieve a faster rate of crop improvement by significantly reducing the generation time and enabling the development of better cultivars within a short period of time. abstract: ABSTRACT The selective capture of uranium from alkaline radioactive wastewater remains highly challenging because uranyl carbonate complexes, particularly [UO 2 (CO 3 ) 3 ] 4− , possess remarkable thermodynamic stability and electrostatic repulsion from negatively charged adsorbent surfaces. Herein, we report a secondary‐sphere activation strategy by constructing secondary amine‐phosphonate tandem sites within mesoporous nano‐silica channels (GP@SiO 2 ‐APTES) for efficient uranyl carbonate capture. title: Genomic characterization of plant height and lodging in spring oat ( Avena sativa L.) using time‐series aerial sensor data
abstract: Abstract Plant height is one of the key economic traits in spring oat ( Avena sativa L.) and a major determinant of lodging, and consequently, yield potential. Understanding the genetic basis of the variation in plant height can significantly benefit plant improvement efforts. Although plant height is straightforward to measure, it can be intense when conducted across numerous plots and environments. title: Mapping global organic soil disturbance and associated greenhouse gas emissions, 2001–2024
abstract: Peatlands and other organic soils occupy a small fraction of the land surface but store a large share of global soil carbon, and drainage and fire in these systems are major, poorly mapped sources of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. title: Validation of a lateral flow assay for the qualitative detection of okadaic acid-group toxins in shellfish
abstract: BACKGROUND: Okadaic acid (OA)-group toxins, including OA, dinophysistoxin-1 (DTX1), DTX2, and their acyl esters, cause diarrhetic shellfish poisoning. abstract: Land use and land cover change (LULCC) in semi-arid regions provides important insights into environmental dynamics under climate variability and socio-political disturbance. abstract: The scientific quantification of regional net carbon emissions (NCE) and the elucidation of their underlying mechanisms are of great significance for advancing sustainable development. However, carbon-related research has long suffered from a separation between sources and sinks, and there remains a lack of systematic understanding of the driving mechanisms behind NCE. abstract: Multimodal medical image fusion combines complementary anatomical and functional information from different imaging modalities into a single image to support clearer visualization and more informed clinical interpretation. Conventional fusion methods may introduce blurring, reduce contrast, or lose important edge and texture information, particularly when curved anatomical boundaries are not represented effectively. abstract: Large-scale ecosystem restoration requires spatial planning tools that identify where limited resources are most likely to deliver durable ecological benefits. Yet ecological feasibility is often treated as an exclusion filter or screening criterion; here, we optimize it alongside biodiversity and other ecological criteria. abstract: A hot June followed by exceptionally wet July-August conditions in 2020 caused widespread disruption across East Asia; however, the anthropogenic contributions to such hot–wet compound extremes (HWCEs) and their future risk remain insufficiently understood. This dataset provides subsurface geological information from two underground tunnel sections at European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN): the Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) and the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). abstract: Air pollution is an acute environmental challenge to the sustainability and even human health, but traditional methods of visualization do not always succeed in clearly displaying the multidimensional relationship between the measured multidimensional pollutant and the resulting effects thereof. This paper proposes a Double-Arc Visualization (DAV) framework helping to combine the pollutant concentration variables and the environmental or health impact indicators into a dual-arc framework. abstract: Camellia oleifera orchard navigation presents considerable challenges, including the limited field of view of ground robots, discontinuous crop rows, and complex shadow interference. abstract: This study investigates the machinability of Monel 400 under four machining environments: dry cutting, Minimum Quantity Lubrication (MQL), cryogenic liquid nitrogen (LN₂) cooling, and hybrid cryogenic–minimum quantity lubrication (Cryo-MQL). abstract: The wetlands of the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River provide important habitats for migratory waterbirds, but repeated image-based monitoring in small satellite wetlands is difficult because birds are often distant, partly hidden by vegetation, and photographed against complex backgrounds. abstract: Satellite-derived observations of inland waters are widely used in environmental monitoring and climate research, often forming the basis of long-term analyses in the absence of continuous in situ measurements. abstract: Landslide is a common geohazard that often occurs in mountainous areas. abstract: La incorporación de la inteligencia artificial en las universidades plantea desafíos que van más allá de la adopción de nuevas herramientas y que involucran las capacidades de dirección, control y aprendizaje institucional. In Ibadan, Nigeria, major disposal facilities such as La Awotan dumpsite rely heavily on open dumping and unmitigated burning. abstract: This systematic survey and position paper examines cross-modal retrieval as a pivotal paradigm in multilingual information access, particularly in the context of Indian regional languages characterized by rich linguistic diversity, complex orthographies, and extensive code-mixing. abstract: Tropical peatland drainage accelerates soil subsidence and carbon loss, yet short-term responses to rewetting in agricultural peatlands remain insufficiently evaluated. This study assessed peat subsidence, groundwater-table dynamics, soil properties, and potential carbon loss in three land conditions in Punggur Kecil, Kubu Raya, West Kalimantan, Indonesia, i.e., canal-blocked agricultural peatland (CB), non-canal-blocked agricultural peatland (NCB), and shrub peatland (SB). abstract: This article presents a statistical forecasting framework for wind speed using two well-known classical forecasting models, the autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) and the exponential smoothing state space (ETS) models with the naïve model as a benchmark for comparison. abstract: Abstract Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are widely used for automated urban inspection, and the spatial layout of UAV nests directly affects inspection costs. To achieve efficient and stable city-scale UAV nest network construction, this study takes Guang'an City as an example. abstract: Afforestation is a crucial strategy for conserving biodiversity, mitigating climate change, and preventing land degradation to accomplish Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 15.2. It is the process of establishing forests in previously unforested areas. Accordingly, the study integrates remote sensing and the analytical hierarchy process (AHP) to identify optimal sites for afforestation suitability that support SDGs within the Cross Niger transition forest. abstract: The study examined the dual role of digital technology adoption in tourism growth and the threat of overtourism, highlighting the need to balance digital innovation with sustainable destination management. The findings show that capacity score (-0.70) and visitor volume (+0.69) are the strongest predictors of overtourism risk, while deficient accommodation infrastructure increases risk. abstract: Despite the rapid advances in anomaly detection, many existing methods assume that normal data are homogeneous and can be modeled by a single one‐class boundary. abstract: In 2022, the Copernicus Program launched the European Ground Motion Service (EGMS), providing open-access ground displacement products across Europe. This development created the need for methodologies to evaluate these datasets and integrate them into risk assessment frameworks. This study proposes an operational screening workflow for differential land subsidence risk based on EGMS Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) displacement measurements. abstract: Abstract Wire-Laser Metal Deposition (W-LMD) is a transformative additive manufacturing technology that utilizes a laser heat source to melt metallic wire feedstock for the high-efficiency fabrication of large-scale, near-net-shape components. abstract: The Neotropics are Earth’s most species-rich region, so understanding how this diversity has emerged is of great interest. abstract: Documents related to reservoir flood control scheduling are typically unstructured, posing significant challenges to effective management. Moreover, differences in understanding among practitioners hinder the accurate extraction of complex semantic relationships, thereby reducing scheduling efficiency. abstract: Abstract Ports are increasingly central to decarbonization strategies, but port electrification is defined inconsistently across academic and policy literature. This ambiguity matters because different definitions imply different electricity-demand profiles, peak loads, connection requirements, and grid-upgrade needs. abstract: Chongqing's environmental heterogeneity complicates flash-flood susceptibility assessment. abstract: Aging offshore installations increasingly operate beyond their original design life, yet conventional periodic risk assessments capture barrier degradation only intermittently. This study presents a barrier-conditioned semi-quantitative risk-assessment workflow that integrates Hazard and Operability Study (HAZOP), Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), and bow-tie barrier analysis. abstract: Bovine milk is both a nutrient-rich food matrix and a microbial ecosystem in which composition, food safety and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) intersect. abstract: Heavy metals (HMs) pollution is a global environmental and public health concern due to its persistence, bioaccumulation, and toxicity. Reliable atmospheric HM emission inventories (AHMEI) are essential for identifying source characteristics and supporting air pollution mitigation policies. abstract: Understanding sports actions from visual data has become increasingly important for intelligent coaching systems, athlete performance analysis, and automated video analytics. Tennis presents a particularly challenging problem because many stroke categories differ only in subtle body poses, racket positions, and spatial interactions. abstract: Large dams can produce significant environmental, geological, and geopolitical impacts, particularly in transboundary river basins. abstract: Background Warship crews live and work for extended periods in confined spaces, separated from their families and exposed to high operational demands. While psychosocial risks in naval and maritime work are increasingly documented, little is known about how sailors collectively organize, regulate, and adapt their daily activity aboard combat vessels. title: Politicized science communication and motivated reasoning: social media responses to the Fukushima radioactive water discharge in Japan, South Korea, and China

abstract: In nature, all microbial populations form biofilms. Aggregated microbial communities attached to surfaces form a biofilm, surrounded by biosynthesised polymeric substances. abstract: Malaria is an infectious disease that continues to be a significant worldwide health issue, with Indonesia positioned second in Southeast Asia for the highest incidence rate in 2023. abstract: This study develops an approach to predict personality traits based on the Big Five model through essay text by combining global and contextual information using a Vocabulary Graph Convolutional Network (VGCN) and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT). abstract: As AI systems and their underlying technologies continue to advance at extraordinary speed, eminent scientists are warning of risks, including extreme risks. abstract: Ground penetrating radar (GPR) and electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) are increasingly combined for the condition assessment of reinforced concrete, yet published integration schemes generally rely on empirical curve-fitting or qualitative visual overlay rather than on an explicit physical model for the anomaly thresholds applied. abstract: Panzhou City of Guizhou Province is a core coal-mining base in Southwest China. abstract: The date palm (Phoenix dactylifera L.) plays a vital role in food security, rural livelihoods, and cultural heritage in the hyper-arid United Arab Emirates (UAE). However, increasing climate stress, water scarcity, and persistent production constraints threaten the sector’s long-term resilience. abstract: This work examines hydrophobic polymer coatings based on unsaturated polyester resin modified with additives of various nature to protect machinery and equipment from icing. abstract: Anthropogenic climate change intensifies extreme precipitation, but how it affects flood hazards remains uncertain. In September 2024, Storm Boris triggered catastrophic flooding across central Europe, underscoring the need to quantify the contribution of human-caused climate change to flood intensity for effective risk management. abstract: The development of children’s educational media is typically evaluated through analyses of final products, with limited attention to the processes through which educational value is constructed. This exploratory study examines how educational, narrative, and disciplinary priorities are negotiated during production. abstract: Abstract Infrared (IR) spectroscopy has lost relevance in modern natural product structural elucidation workflows but holds many advantages that can be leveraged with contemporary tools and technologies. abstract: Urban green spaces (UGS) play a central role in mitigating urban heat stress. While urban parks have been extensively studied in this context, other widespread UGS types, such as cemeteries and allotment gardens, have received comparatively less attention. abstract: Abstract A wide body of work has applied the concept of critical slowing down to estimate the stability of different Earth system components. Most of them – such as global vegetation – are inherently non-stationary, for example due to strong seasonal forcing that complicates the estimation of their resilience to external perturbations. abstract: Patient safety remains a defining dimension of health care quality, yet systems rely on retrospective assessment after harm has occurred, limiting visibility into upstream risks, including process failures and near misses. During thunderstorms, there are abrupt changes in temperature, wind speed, atmospheric pressure, rain, and hail. abstract: Climate change has emerged as a major global environmental challenge affecting freshwater ecosystems and aquatic biodiversity through rising temperatures, altered hydrological cycles, acidification, salinity intrusion, eutrophication, and hypoxia. title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of land surface temperature and vegetation cover in Thanjavur district Tamil Nadu India using remote sensing and GIS
abstract: Land Surface Temperature (LST) and vegetation dynamics are widely recognized as reliable indicators of environmental change, urbanization, and climate variability. Understanding their spatial and temporal interactions is essential for sustainable environmental planning, particularly in agriculturally intensive regions experiencing rapid land-use transformation. This study investigates the spatio-temporal variations of LST and the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) in Thanjavur District, Tamil Nadu, India, using multi-temporal Landsat imagery acquired during 2011 and 2021. title: ZOO: A Training-Free Framework for Open-Vocabulary Animal Detection, Segmentation, and Tracking
abstract: Abstract Quantitative extraction of animal visual information often relies on annotated data collected for specific species and recording environments, limiting rapid transfer across biological systems. We present ZOO (Zero-shot Organism Observation), a zero-shot animal visual analysis workflow that requires no additional training or fine-tuning on target species or recording environments. title: Pengembangan WebGIS untuk Pendataan dan Pemantauan Lahan Sawah di Kecamatan Poleang Timur Kabupaten Bombana
abstract: Pendataan dan pemantauan lahan sawah memerlukan integrasi informasi administratif, lokasi, dan riwayat kondisi untuk mendukung pengelolaan pertanian yang sistematis. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan WebGIS untuk pendataan dan pemantauan lahan sawah di Kecamatan Poleang Timur, Kabupaten Bombana, serta mengevaluasi kesesuaian fungsi dan penerimaan awal pengguna. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan pengembangan sistem melalui tahapan analisis kebutuhan, perancangan, implementasi, pengujian fungsional, dan evaluasi pengguna. title: Prioritizing Indigenous-led fishery governance: case studies from the Kuskokwim, Yukon, and Klamath Rivers
abstract: Pacific salmon are more than just food or a commodity: they are vital to the health and well-being of human and more-than-human kin and ecologies. Indigenous Nations have long maintained relationships among salmon, people, and their environments through Indigenous knowledge systems, governance, stewardship, and reciprocal responsibility. The imposition of colonial fisheries governance and the privileging of Western scientific approaches within management and decision-making have disrupted these relationships causing immeasurable damage to Tribes along the Pacific West Coast. title: Microbial conversion of agro-industrial residues to surfactin: a review of fermentation performance, process optimization, product recovery and agricultural applications
abstract: Surfactin, a lipopeptide biosurfactant, has drawn growing attention for agricultural use, but its large-scale production remains limited by substrate cost, low titers, and downstream recovery. This review compiles quantitative data on agro-industrial residues as feedstocks, comparing substrate classes, fermentation performance, optimization routes, recovery methods, and field-level applications reported to date, drawing mainly on Scopus-indexed literature published in 2016–2026 together with earlier key studies. title: Plant invasions in Natura 2000 habitats in Poland are driven primarily by macroclimatic factors
abstract: Invasive plants pose an ecological threat around the world. Their influence can also be observed in protected areas such as the European Ecological Network Natura 2000. Although invasions can endanger protected habitats, the specific impact of invasive species in such areas and the factors that determine their spread remain understudied. This study aimed to analyse the factors influencing the probability of plant invasion in five groups of habitat types protected under the EU Habitats Directive, based on Polish State Monitoring of Natura 2000 data. title: Radioactive fallout legacy of nuclear tests in soils of the Southern Hemisphere
abstract: Abstract Fallout radionuclide (FRN) archived in soils are key tracers of soil redistribution, sediment dynamics, and associated carbon fluxes, yet their global application is limited by poorly constrained baselines in the Southern Hemisphere. Here, we present the first hemisphere-scale baseline and uncertainty maps of 137 Cs and 239+240 Pu soil inventories. abstract: ABSTRACT The escalating threat of antibiotic resistance has emerged as a formidable challenge to global public health, creating an urgent imperative for the development of novel antimicrobial strategies. As crucial elements of the host's innate immune system, Antimicrobial Peptides (AMPs) are viewed as a compelling alternative or synergistic adjunct to conventional antibiotics, owing to their broad‐spectrum antimicrobial activity, unique bactericidal mechanisms, and low propensity for inducing resistance. title: Measuring and Mapping Urban NO 2 Pollution Heterogeneity Using a Custom Pandora Spectrometer Experiment and Observations From TEMPO
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) is a primary pollutant present at high concentrations in urban areas. Ground based measurements remain sparse and satellite observations rely on retrievals, so understanding intraurban, diurnal‐scale changes in NO 2 is challenging. We present a novel methodology leveraging the sky scan capabilities of four Pandora spectrometers deployed around the Boston area to improve our understanding of intra‐urban NO 2 variability. title: Engineered Geopolymer Composites (EGC) with hybrid PVA and bamboo fibers: Strength–ductility–sustainability trade-offs
abstract: Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) fiber is widely used to develop Engineered Geopolymer Composites (EGC), but its relatively high environmental and economic burdens motivate the exploration of renewable alternatives. This study systematically investigated the effects of PVA fiber content and progressive substitution of PVA fiber by bamboo fiber on the mechanical performance, environmental impact, and material cost of EGC. title: Meteorological effects on the vertical variability of aerosol chemical composition at a rural background site
abstract: Vertically resolved aerosol observations are crucial for understanding boundary-layer pollution processes and improving air-quality assessments. This study presents concurrent dual-height measurements of submicron aerosol chemical composition at a rural background site using a compact Time-of-Flight Aerosol Mass Spectrometer at 230 m and a ToF-Aerosol Chemical Speciation Monitor at 4 m, complemented by Sunset OCEC analyzers. title: Marketing Mix Strategy to Increase Wedding Package Sales at Six Senses Uluwatu, Bali
abstract: The wedding industry in Bali is developing as a strategic opportunity for hotels to increase wedding package sales, but Six Senses Uluwatu, Bali experienced a decline in sales from 100 events in 2024 to 87 events in 2025. This study aims to analyze the 7P marketing mix strategy to increase wedding package sales. The study used a descriptive qualitative method. title: Differential colorimetric pH measuring microfluidic manifold with embedded sensors and actuators for textile dyeing industry
abstract: Abstract This work presents a fully integrated microfluidic opto-electro-mechanical platform demonstrating a proof-of-concept for real-time colorimetric pH sensing in intensely colored textile solutions. The system features acrylic manifold with dual spectral sensors, an embedded magnetic mini-stirrer for rapid mixing, custom bidirectional syringe pumps, and automated fluid routing. An automated manifold-based implementation of differential colorimetry is presented, combining upstream and downstream absorbance measurements to mathematically compensate for background dye spectra. title: Spatio‐Temporal Assessment of the Complementarity Between Hydroelectric, Wind and Solar Energy Sources for Northeastern Brazil
abstract: ABSTRACT The growing participation of variable renewable sources in the Brazilian electricity system makes it necessary to understand how their different spatial and seasonal patterns can contribute to the stability of energy supply. In this context, the study evaluated the seasonal dynamics and spatiotemporal complementarity among hydropower, wind and solar resources in Northeast Brazil (NEB), between 1999 and 2022, with a focus on long‐term strategic planning. title: Parameter estimation and identifiability analysis of stability and tipping points in potentially bistable ecosystems
abstract: Abstract Ecological regime shifts are potentially a common property of ecosystems, describing transitions between alternative stable states that can represent healthy or unhealthy conditions under the same environmental drivers. Once a tipping point, defined as a critical threshold separating alternative stable states, is crossed, the system may degrade and recovery can be difficult, making early detection essential for effective ecosystem management. title: Big data-enabled sustainable smart hydrogen energy networks assessment: A fuzzy comparative decision-support framework
abstract: Integrating big data into hydrogen systems is essential for enhancing performance and sustainability by improving efficiency, reducing costs and boosting energy security. The primary objective of this research is to provide a comparative decision framework for evaluating and ranking the big data challenges in hydrogen systems. In the presented approach, the Fuzzy Stepwise Weight Assessment Ratio Analysis (F-SWARA) and Fuzzy Evaluation Based on Distance from Average Solution (F-EDAS) methods are applied to the priority of challenges using the views of specialists in the decision team. title: Fault‐Tolerant Consensus of Semi‐Markov Multi‐Agent Systems: A Quantity‐Limited Controller
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper proposes a solution to the fault‐tolerant consensus problem in linear semi‐Markov jump multi‐agent systems (MASs) by designing a quantity‐limited controller (QLC). Initially, the article establishes the mapping relationship between the system modes and controllers using a stationary probability distribution. Therefore, controllers are constructed in a limited quantity to address the practical issue of mismatch between the number of controllers and the number of system modes. title: Medicinal plants of the Ukraine: from Prince Volodymyr (10th century) to medicinal Cannabis (2026)
abstract: Ukraine has a unique ethnopharmacological heritage shaped by its exceptional floristic diversity, complex political history, and long-standing cross-cultural interactions with neighbouring regions. This narrative review provides a comprehensive and critical synthesis of the historical development of herbal medicine in the territory of modern Ukraine from the prehistoric and medieval periods to the early 21st century. title: A lightweight dual-domain attention YOLO for small object detection in remote sensing images
abstract: Small object detection (SOD) in remote sensing images (RSIs) remains challenging due to limited pixel representation, complex background interference, and the requirement for computationally efficient lightweight models. To address these issues, this paper proposes LDA-YOLO, a lightweight detection framework built upon YOLOv8 that integrates adaptive refinement of multi-level features and dual-domain attention to enhance fine-grained perception while maintaining low computational cost. title: Physics‐Constrained Decomposition of Accumulated Fatigue‐Life Deviations After Static Residual‐Stress Correction in Welded Compact‐Tension Specimens
abstract: ABSTRACT Welding residual stress alters crack‐tip driving forces, complicating fatigue crack‐growth life assessment. Static corrections may leave systematic life deviations that are difficult to interpret. This study develops a physics‐constrained framework for diagnosing and decomposing these deviations in welded compact‐tension specimens. Two as‐welded specimens are assessed against a low‐residual‐stress reference from two post‐weld heat‐treated specimens. title: Time-Resolved Compositional and Redox Evolution of Dissolved Organic Matter During Biochar-Amended Aerobic Composting
abstract: Abstract Aerobic composting is a widely applied strategy for organic waste valorization; however, the mechanistic linkage between the structural transformation and macroscopic redox functionality of dissolved organic matter (DOM) under biochar (BC) regulation remains poorly understood. This study investigated the evolution of DOM composition, molecular weight distribution, and electron transfer capacity (ETC) during cow manure composting with graded BC additions (0%, 5%, and 10%). title: RSDMF-DETR: A Remote Sensing Direction-aware Multi-scale Fusion Detection Transformer
abstract: Abstract With the expansion of wind power scale, UAV-based remote sensing technology has become an important approach for wind turbine object detection in intelligent inspection, operation and maintenance, and wind energy resource assessment. Compared with traditional manual inspections, UAV remote sensing provides advantages of non-contact operation, wide coverage, rapid acquisition, and high spatial resolution. title: A dual-index assessment of warm-season heat stress for a small-island province in Atlantic Canada
abstract: Abstract Heat-stress exposure in maritime regions reflects the combined influence of temperature and humidity, yet these relationships remain poorly characterized in small, cool-temperate regions such as Prince Edward Island (PEI), Canada. Here, we characterize warm-season thermal exposure across PEI during a 2020–2025 observational baseline using Humidex, representing human thermal discomfort, and the Temperature–Humidity Index (THI), representing cattle heat-stress risk. title: Moisture Aggregation and the Cloud Transition Zone Shape Mesoscale Aerosol Properties
abstract: Abstract Mesoscale moisture aggregation and cloud organization in shallow convection have gained much attention regarding their role in Earth's energy budget and cloud feedbacks on climate. Because aerosol particles swell in humid air, mesoscale moisture patterns are expected to be accompanied by corresponding variations in aerosol optical depth (AOD). title: Precipitation trend uncertainty from product choice rivals or exceeds the magnitude of actual trends
abstract: Abstract Gridded precipitation products are widely used to assess long-term rainfall and snowfall change, yet their trend reliability remains uncertain. We evaluate 19 (quasi-)global products for three annual statistics: mean precipitation, daily maximum, and wet-day frequency, screening for temporal homogeneity and benchmarking trends against daily and monthly rain-gauge observations. abstract: Abstract Reliable real-time monitoring of weld quality is essential for the industrial adoption of wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM), because unstable arc and melt-pool behaviour produces defects that are costly to find after deposition. This work proposes the Causal Fusion Transformer with a vision–language module (CFT+VLM) to address this problem. title: How Can Large Language Models Support Learning?
abstract: We discuss a novel approach to Premodern Japanese Language Pedagogy (PJLP) with potential applications in other languages and fields. Drawing inspiration from grassroots initiatives such as the DIY and Maker movements, this paper advocates for an approach to AI in Education that fosters instructional and student agency over the pedagogical process. abstract: The maximum classifier discrepancy domain adaptation (DA) method based on a dual-classifier structure has achieved some success in fault diagnosis of cross-working condition, yet its reliance on the dual-classifier structure may fail to effectively represent the data characteristics of the target domain and may suffers from insufficient classification boundary discrimination. title: Enzyme-Immobilized Nanomaterials for Endocrine Disorders: Therapeutic Innovation and Translational Challenges
abstract: Abstract: Endocrine disorders result from chronic disturbances in the hormonal regulation and feedback control, which cause metabolic, reproductive, and systemic complications. Despite the advances in disease management with current therapies such as hormone replacement or multi-pathway pharmacological therapies, problems with variable patient response, side effects and the need for continuous monitoring and dose adjustment remain. title: Parents’ perceptions of child labor in an indigenous community in Tawi-Tawi, Philippines: an interpretative phenomenological analysis
abstract: Introduction Child labor remains a complex, multidimensional challenge in Indigenous and geographically isolated island communities in the Philippines. While much of the existing literature focuses on quantitative economic metrics or direct child self-reports, this study explores how parents and community leaders in Tawi-Tawi navigate, perceive, and make sense of the contextual barriers surrounding child labor and its multifaceted developmental impacts. title: First report of Daptrius chimachima (Yellow-headed Caracara) for the Greater Antilles
abstract: Abstract We report the first Greater Antillean record of Daptrius chimachima (Yellow-headed Caracara), a bird observed between 24 and 31 March 2023 at the Grand Hotel Excelsior Port Royal in Port Royal, Jamaica. Given that this observation was made nearly 800 km from the species’ core range, the observed bird may have arrived via ship assistance, or it may have island-hopped northward through the Lesser Antilles. title: A multidimensional review of tourism crowding: integrating the dimensions of perception, experience, destination, management, and responses
abstract: This review synthesizes emerging literature on tourism crowding by organizing findings into five dimensions: perception, experience, destination, management, and response. Crowding perception highlights the subjective nature of tourists’ discomfort, shaped by cognitive and emotional evaluations. Crowding experience examines real-time emotional and behavioral engagement, emphasizing adaptive behaviors and changing preferences. title: Modeling and Simulation of Reactive Power Compensation Using a Synchronous Motor with Excitation Control in MATLAB/Simulink
abstract: This study investigates reactive power compensation using a synchronous motor in a three-phase electrical power system without conventional capacitor banks through MATLAB/Simulink-based modeling and simulation. The proposed system consists of inductive loads and a 15 kVA synchronous motor operating as a dynamic reactive power compensator via excitation current control. title: Integrated framework for evaluating iron ore tailings as construction materials: an Australian case study
abstract: Abstract Increasing demand for construction-grade sand and continued generation of iron ore tailings (IOT) from mining create significant challenges for aggregate resource management. Utilisation of IOT in construction remains limited due to variability in mineralogy and particle characteristics, creating uncertainty in performance and restricting industry adoption. An early-stage assessment framework was developed to evaluate site-specific IOT by integrating mine-site characterisation, concrete performance, safety and regulatory compliance, and market feasibility.
