title: Weld Defect Detection in TOFD Images Based on Improved YOLOv8
abstract: Small defect indications, low contrast, and background noise make weld defect detection in time-of-flight diffraction (TOFD) images challenging. This study proposes SCW-YOLO, a TOFD weld defect detector based on YOLOv8n. The model adds a high-resolution P2 detection branch, uses space-to-depth convolution (SPDConv) in the backbone and neck downsampling paths, embeds coordinate attention (CoordAtt) in the neck, and uses Wise-IoU for bounding-box regression. journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Information Technology

title: Reference Electrode‐Free Nitrate Sensing via Differential Temperature‐Modulated Potentiometry in Printed Symmetric SC‐ISEs
abstract: ABSTRACT Nitrate sensors based on solid‐contact ion‐selective electrodes (SC‐ISEs) are a promising technology for low‐cost, continuous ion sensing. However, implementing stable, printable solid‐state reference electrodes that match the scalability of SC‐ISE remains a key challenge. In this work, we exploit the intrinsic thermo‐electrochemical response of SC‐ISEs to extract concentration from temperature‐induced potential modulations without a defined reference potential. title: Genotypic variation and root traits associated with hypoxia tolerance in quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.)
abstract: Waterlogging-induced hypoxia is becoming an increasingly important constraint to crop production under climate change. Although quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) is recognized for its tolerance to drought and salinity, its response to hypoxia remains poorly understood. This study evaluated the effects of hypoxia on growth, root development, biomass accumulation, and individual seed yield in 28 quinoa genotypes. title: Technical note: Evaluation of snow water equivalent from large-scale land-surface products over Italy
abstract: Abstract. Snow water equivalent (SWE) is a critical hydrological variable for water resource management in mountainous regions, where seasonal snowpacks function as natural reservoirs regulating streamflow and water supply. While high-resolution, observation-constrained regional or national snow products provide reliable daily SWE estimates at fine spatial resolution (less than 1 km), their limited temporal coverage often restricts their use for long-term hydro-climatological studies. title: Experimental investigation of magnetic ring fins with variable spacing in a hemispherical solar still: A 4E assessment
abstract: The shortage of freshwater and the high energy consumption of traditional desalination methods require the development of renewable energy-based desalination methods such as solar stills. Although solar stills are simple and low cost, their limited productivity remains a barrier to their widespread use. Therefore, the present study aims to enhance the performance of a hemispherical solar still using magnetic rings within the distillation basin. title: Hybrid ARIMA–TCN–Self‐Attention Control With Superb Fairy‐Wren Optimization for Adaptive BLDC Motor Speed Regulation in Electric Vehicles
abstract: ABSTRACT Electric vehicles (EVs) have gained significant attention in recent years and are rapidly emerging as a sustainable alternative to fossil fuel‐based transportation due to their efficiency and environmental benefits. The primary objectives in EV development are to maximize energy utilization and extend driving range both of which depend heavily on enhancing motor performance. title: Overweight, obesity, and sex differences in the acquisition of aquatic motor competence among 4–5-year-old preschool children: a quasi-experimental study
abstract: Background Childhood overweight and obesity are associated with impaired motor competence, yet evidence on how weight status relates to structured aquatic motor skill learning in preschoolers—and whether sex moderates this relationship—remains scarce. This study compared changes in aquatic motor competence between overweight/obese and healthy-weight 4–5-year-old preschoolers following a common 8-week structured aquatic programme, and examined sex differences. title: Heavy Metals in Freshwater Ecosystems: Occurrence, Risk, and Analytical Advances
abstract: Introduction: Freshwater systems accumulate arsenic, cadmium, chromium, copper, lead, mercury, nickel and zinc from four broad routes: rock weathering, industrial effluent, agricultural runoff and atmospheric fallout. Because these elements persist and move up through food webs, they continue to pose a food-safety hazard. title: Fabrication of Biomass Derived Carbon Supported ZnCo Oxide Composite for Enhanced Oxygen Evolution Reaction
abstract: Metal‐Organic Frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as versatile precursors for the synthesis of metal oxides owing to their high surface area and tunable composition. However, their practical application is often limited by poor electrical conductivity, nanoparticle aggregation, and insufficient structural durability. To address these challenges, a biomass‐derived carbon‐supported Zn–Co oxide composite (ZnCo oxide@C) was developed using jute as a sustainable carbon source, providing a conductive and robust framework. title: EVOLUTION OF INDUSTRIAL SYSTEMS: FROM THE HUMANIZATION OF INDUSTRY 5.0 TO THE BIO-DIGITAL SYMBIOTIC INDUSTRY 6.0
abstract: At the beginning of the 21st century, the world witnessed the Fourth Industrial Revolution (Industry 4.0), which laid the foundations for digitalization, cloud computing, and the Internet of Things (IoT). Despite undeniable technological successes, Industry 4.0 faced criticism for its "technocentricity" a model in which machine efficiency often took precedence over human well-being and ecological balance.

title: Comprensibilidad algorítmica y decisiones públicas en el MERCOSUR: hacia un principio regional de garantía
abstract: La inteligencia artificial puede mejorar la gestión pública, pero también dificultar la comprensión y revisión de decisiones que afectan derechos. abstract: ABSTRACT Hybrid non‐thermal technologies are one of the emerging hurdle technologies capable of providing high quality nutritious food with microbial safety and minimum processing. These technologies are the promising alternative to traditional thermal processing for food preservation. The most effective non‐thermal technologies studied extensively include high‐pressure processing (HPP), pulsed electric fields (PEF), ultrasonication (US), and cold plasma (CP). title: An emergency decision support framework for flight-deck accidents: integrating dynamic adjudication, multi-agent cooperation, and hierarchical path planning
abstract: Abstract The flight deck of a naval vessel is a high-risk operational environment in which a single initiating event can precipitate coupled hazard cascades encompassing concurrent fire propagation, progressive casualty deterioration, and damage-induced stability degradation. Conventional pre-plan-driven response approaches are architecturally ill-suited to such multi-hazard, temporally evolving scenarios, as they cannot adapt to stochastic hazard interactions in real time. title: Smoothed Adaptive Weighting Average (SAWA) interpolation for geotechnical site characterisation using limited data
abstract: Accurate site characterisation is essential in geotechnical engineering, but in practice, it is often constrained by the limited availability of field data such as cone penetration tests (CPTs). When combined with the complex three-dimensional variability of geological materials, this limitation makes the reconstruction of reliable ground models a persistent challenge. title: Development of a computational method for analyzing the remaining service life of corrosion-damaged pipeline elbows with composite bandage
abstract: The object of research is a curved branch of a main pipeline with a local corrosion defect, restored with a composite bandage. The most problematic section in it is a curved section, the development of corrosion on which causes stress concentration, accumulation of fatigue damage, and, ultimately, leads to a decrease in the residual resource. title: Assessing the feasibility of a video-based conversational chatbot survey for measuring perceived cycling safety: A pilot study in New York City
abstract: Bicycle safety is essential for bikeability and transport efficiency, yet conventional surveys often fail to capture how people perceive cycling environments in real time because they depend on retrospective recall. This study proposes a video-based conversational AI chatbot survey, powered by large language models (LLMs), to collect perceptions of cycling safety and the reasons behind them. abstract: OBJECTIVES: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (flexible). abstract: Abstract Community-based conservation initiatives are essential for mitigating climate change and biodiversity loss. Yet, the communities leading these efforts are themselves disproportionately impacted by climate change. Despite this, there is little insight about how resilient community-based conservation institutions are to extreme weather and how contextual factors, such as material wellbeing, further affect their durability. title: Quantitative mobile gamma-ray spectrometry through Bayesian inference
abstract: Accurate quantitative mapping of gamma-ray emitters is critical for applications ranging from radiological emergency response and environmental monitoring to nuclear security and deep space exploration. Here, we show that such mapping can be achieved by combining mobile gamma-ray spectrometry with high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations and full-spectrum Bayesian inference. title: Long-term land use and land cover change impacts on ecosystem carbon storage. Landsat and InVEST analysis in the Ahafo Ano Southeast district, Ghana
abstract: Land use and land cover (LULC) change is a major driver of ecosystem carbon dynamics in tropical regions. This study evaluates the impacts of LULC change on ecosystem carbon storage in the Ahafo Ano Southeast District of Ghana over a 30-year period (1994-2024) using multi-temporal Landsat imagery and a spatially explicit carbon modelling approach. Supervised classification based on Landsat data was applied to derive LULC maps for the reference years 1994, 2010, and 2024. abstract: S in lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries is limited by the bidirectional redox kinetics. title: Tracing Zoonotic Emergence through Evolution and Biodiversity of Reptiles: An Appraisal on One Health Concept from the Indian -Subcontinent
abstract: The Indian subcontinent provides a unique natural laboratory to study the relationships between geological history, biodiversity, evolutionary diversification and zoonotic disease emergence. Subsequent to its splitting from Gondwana, the Indian Plate drifted northward and collided with Eurasia, drastically altering the landscape, temperature and biogeography of the region. abstract: Plastics are synthetic materials based on organic polymers, widely used in all sectors of the global economy. World production reached 431 million metric tons in 2024, having grown at a compound annual rate of 4.8% since the beginning of the 21st century. However, only 9% of the total plastic produced up to 2015 had been recycled, while 79% was discarded in landfills or in the natural environment. title: Land use and vegetation conditions shape the dynamics of ecosystem resilience in an arid and semi-arid region: evidence from the Fenhe River Basin, China
abstract: Quantifying the spatiotemporal dynamics of watershed ecosystem resilience (ER) is crucial for ecological regulation and sustainable watershed management. In this study, long-term time-series remote sensing datasets were utilized to comprehensively characterize the spatiotemporal variations of ER in the Fenhe River Basin (FRB), China and particular emphasized on the role of vegetation cover in slowing the decline of ER. abstract: Lakes and other water bodies change over time and are influenced by natural and anthropogenic processes during the hydrological cycle. abstract: Las turbinas hidrocinéticas, han surgido como una opción atractiva, para aprovechar la energía cinética presente en ríos, estuarios, y corrientes mareomotrices, sin requerir grandes infraestructuras hidráulicas, sin embargo, el rendimiento de estos sistemas, depende de una interacción compleja, entre variables hidráulicas y mecánicas. A pesar del aumento de investigaciones en el área, el conocimiento disponible, permanece disperso entre disciplinas, lo que dificulta una comprensión integrada del estado actual de la tecnología, y de las estrategias más efectivas, para incrementar su eficiencia.

abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have become indispensable tools in programming education and professional software development. However, their output quality remains poorly characterized, particularly in terms of the semantic and linguistic quality of the explanatory text. Traditional evaluation metrics such as ROUGE primarily rely on lexical overlap and therefore only partially reflect the semantic adequacy of code explanations. abstract: This study presents an analysis of the Famennian (Upper Devonian) Fueyo Formation of the southern Cantabrian Mountains. abstract: Stingless bee honey (SBH) is recognised for its unique nutritional and bioactive profile, which varies with its botanical origin.This study evaluated the enzyme inhibitory activities targeted on cardioprotective potential of SBH from eight distinct floral sources in Sabah (Malaysia), using in vitro assays.The phenolic profile of the honey samples was also determined.Inhibition assays were conducted for angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), α-amylase, and pancreatic lipase to evaluate antihypertensive, antihyperglycaemic, and antihyperlipidemic effects, respectively.Anti-hypercholesterolemic pot

abstract: ABSTRACT NiFe (hydr)oxides are among the most active oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts, yet their local structures, active sites, and synergistic effects remain under debate. title: A semantic framework for resilience analytics and AI-assisted decision support in growing and changing socio-technical systems
abstract: Abstract Socio-technical systems are becoming increasingly interconnected, heterogeneous, and dynamic while continuously evolving through new technologies, infrastructures, policies, resources, and operational practices. At the same time, critical infrastructure operators, businesses, and public authorities face growing challenges arising from climate change, cyber threats, geopolitical instability, supply-chain disruptions, and evolving regulatory frameworks. abstract: This paper aims to develop a model for assessing the reliability of thermal spray machine operators using the Technica Empirica Stima Errori Operatori (TESEO) and Human Error Assessment and Reduction Technique (HEART), which have been expanded to include four additional factors. The results of this model support human resources management processes, particularly in competence development, training planning, and risk reduction. abstract: Abstract Farmers rely on weather information to guide crop management; however, outcomes often remain uncertain until harvest. This pilot study evaluated downscaled medium- to seasonal-range forecasts for Austria (2018–2022), focusing on air temperature, precipitation, and six crop-independent agrometeorological indicators (stress and suitability metrics). abstract: The current study, which is entitled Evaluating the Assessing the Acceptance of ChatGPT Among Higher Education Students: A Case Study in Pahang, aimed to assess the behavioural intention of university students with regard to using ChatGPT in various academic levels. The Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) was selected as a cross-sectional survey approach, data were collected from 184 respondents between March and May 2025 through both online and printed questionnaires. title: Lead Contamination in Moroccan Spices Determined by Graphite Furnace Atomic Absorption Spectrometry (GFAAS): Exposure and Environmental Health Risk Assessment
abstract: ABSTRACT Spices are widely consumed in Morocco and may constitute a significant dietary source of toxic metals such as lead (Pb). This study assessed Pb contamination and associated health risks in six commonly consumed spices (turmeric, black pepper, paprika, cumin, ginger, and cinnamon) collected from Moroccan markets ( n = 200). abstract: Drought is a complex and multidimensional phenomenon influenced by both precipitation variability and temperature-driven processes, particularly under evolving hydro-climatic conditions. A comprehensive assessment of long-term drought dynamics across Türkiye is presented using multi-timescale Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) and Standardized Precipitation–Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) based on data from 21 representative cities across seven geographical regions. title: Engineering rice for enhanced abiotic stress tolerance using genome editing
abstract: Rice productivity is increasingly constrained by drought, salinity, heat, cold, submergence, heavy metal toxicity, and herbicide-related stresses. Although conventional breeding has improved stress tolerance, progress remains limited by the complex, polygenic, and environment-dependent nature of abiotic stress responses. Genome-editing technologies, including CRISPR/Cas systems, TALENs, ZFNs, base editors, prime editors, and CRISPR-Combo, provide precise approaches for modifying stress-responsive genes and regulatory pathways. abstract: Irradiance on the PV modules is not distributed uniformly during partially shaded conditions (PSC). Bypass diodes employed to avoid the hot-spot phenomenon modify the power-voltage (P-V) curves such that several points corresponding to maximum power are generated. abstract: Improper solid waste management (SWM) remains a critical environmental and public health challenge in peri-urban regions of developing countries, driven by weak infrastructure, socio-economic disparities and inadequate monitoring. This study investigates the spatial–temporal dynamics and typology of roadside waste dumping in the peri-urban zones of Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, using geo-tagged field surveys integrated with GIS-based hotspot analysis. Algae are a sustainable and versatile source rich in alginate, carrageenan, agar, and ulvan, which exhibit unique structural and functional properties suitable for packaging applications. abstract: Introduction Cyber hygiene is often assumed to enhance individuals' ability to evaluate the veracity of online information, with potential implications for decision-making, social trust, and resilience to misinformation. However, empirical evidence regarding the relationship between cyber hygiene and news-veracity judgment remains limited. abstract: This study examines how supply chain innovation relates to the business success of frozen seafood firms in Bangkok and whether this relationship operates through operational capabilities. Grounded in the Resource-Based View and the Dynamic Capabilities View, integrated into a Resource–Capability–Performance framework, the study positions logistics performance and service quality as parallel mediators. abstract: Antarctic cryptogams and soils harbour diverse microbial communities that are fundamental to nutrient cycling and ecosystem resilience. However, the functional roles of these communities are not yet fully understood. This study investigated the bacterial communities associated with the moss Andreaea regularis, the lichen Usnea aurantiacoatra and adjacent soils in Antarctica. abstract: Introduction: Wound healing is a highly ordered and regulated physiological process for restoring the integrity of the skin after injury. Chronic wounds, such as diabetic ulcers and burns, still represent a significant clinical problem because of compromised cell reactions and disordered molecular signalling. abstract: Global biodiversity loss is accelerating, with approximately one million species facing extinction and ecosystem degradation that compromises the welfare of over three billion people. While there is growing awareness and global consensus on biodiversity protection, nation-state governance alone cannot be counted on to address transborder species protection. abstract: Informal waste collectors recover a considerable share of the plastic produced by Indonesian households. Interviews in Airmadidi District, North Sulawesi, however, revealed that collectors spend much of their working day searching for households with plastic to sell, while residents have no way to tell collectors that their sorted plastic is ready. abstract: Brown carbon (BrC) is a light-absorbing component of organic aerosol that contributes to atmospheric radiative forcing by absorbing ultraviolet and visible light. abstract: Background: Campus Wi-Fi networks are vulnerable to sniffing attacks because of their open-access patterns, diverse user devices, and limited security monitoring. abstract: The psychological fallout of natural disasters is rarely a direct function of the event's physical severity. Instead, it emerges from a complex interplay between hazard characteristics, localized spatial conditions, institutional efficacy, and the psychosocial resources accessible to affected populations. abstract: Heavy-duty commercial vehicles, despite accounting for less than 10% of the total vehicle parc, contribute nearly one-third of the total carbon emissions in the automotive industry. abstract: Sediment transport caused by large earthquakes produces distinctive deposits that help extend our records of these events. abstract: The potential of green banana biomass (GBB) to simultaneously modulate oxidative deterioration and technological quality in fish emulsions during refrigerated storage remains poorly understood. abstract: The Jeju Genome Project (JGP) is a genomic and phenotypic cohort established to provide a comprehensive resource for precision medicine on Jeju Island, South Korea. This study explores the structural characteristics and multifunctional applications of DE, particularly in environmental protection and sustainable agriculture. abstract: Plant virus diagnostics has progressed from symptom-based observation and targeted serological or molecular assays toward untargeted high-throughput sequencing (HTS) approaches capable of detecting multiple known and previously uncharacterized viruses in a single sample. abstract: ABSTRACT Water scarcity has become a multidimensional sustainability challenge driven by climate change, demographic growth, governance quality and technological adaptation. Although desalination is increasingly recognised as a strategic response to water stress, existing assessment approaches remain fragmented and fail to evaluate its adaptive resilience comprehensively. abstract: Facility layout plays a critical role in determining production efficiency, productivity, and the smoothness of material flow in manufacturing systems. This study aims to evaluate and improve the facility layout of a green tea factory at PT X to minimize backtracking and enhance production flow efficiency through the integration of Activity Relationship Chart (ARC), Total Closeness Rating (TCR), and line balancing methods. title: Physics-guided graph Transformer for composite pipeline damage detection
abstract: Composite pipelines are widely used in oil and gas transportation owing to their high specific strength and corrosion resistance. However, guided-wave-based damage localization remains challenging due to multimodal wave propagation, noise interference, complex propagation-path relationships, and limited labeled damage locations. title: Physical Isolation as a Low-Cost Strategy to Mitigate Electrochemical Interference in pH–DO (Dissolved Oxygen) Multisensor Systems
abstract: The integration of pH and dissolved oxygen (DO) sensors in multisensor systems can introduce electrochemical interference, reducing measurement stability and accuracy. This study investigated the interference mechanism and evaluated the effectiveness of a simple physical isolation strategy using non-conductive plastic shielding. abstract: This study systematically investigated the pull-out behavior of irregular recycled steel fibers (RSF) embedded in rubberized high-strength concrete (R-HSC), considering the effects of crumb rubber (CR) content, fiber embedment length, and fiber geometry. title: A replicable tri-scale method for urban flood vulnerability assessment in Chennai, India
abstract: The vulnerability of rapidly growing cities to urban flooding reflects physical exposure, built form, and lived experience, but studies of these dimensions are typically conducted separately. This article presents the Data Integrated Tri-scale Workflow for Assessing Hazard Vulnerability (DITWAH), a rule-based method that links community-reported flood depth, zone-level statistical testing, and site-level urban morphology. title: ChiSao: A fully GPU-resident optimizer for cataloguing the modes of multimodal black-box functions
abstract: Bayesian inference and scientific computing often call for cataloguing all modes of a multimodal black-box objective, not just its global optimum. abstract: Understanding how smallholder farmers want public resources allocated is essential for designing effective agricultural policies, especially in the maize sub-sector, where public interventions often compete for limited fiscal resources. This paper determined smallholder farmers’ preferences for enhancing maize productivity in western Kenya. abstract: Gaussian Dynamic Bayesian Networks (GDBNs) are widely used for learning network structures from continuous time-series data. To capture both time-lagged and contemporaneous dependencies, GDBNs allow for dynamic inter-slice edges and static intra-slice edges. Two Bayesian approaches have been developed for such models, both extending the well-known Gaussian BGe score. We refer to them as the mean-adjusted BGe (mBGe) and the extended BGe (eBGe) models. abstract: The rapid proliferation of renewable energy resources, battery energy storage systems (BESSs), and flexible loads has increased the operational complexity of interconnected multi-microgrid systems, creating the urgent need for effective and decentralized energy management strategies. In this context, this paper proposes a framework for Distributed Transactive Energy Management (DTEM), leveraging the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM), aimed at transactive energy transfer to achieve coordinated operation of interconnected microgrids. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Indoor person-following robots routinely lose sight of their target at corners, doorways, and in crowds, and most local planners then stall at the last seen position. We present IO-TEB (Intermittent-Observation Timed Elastic Band), a local planner that maintains a probabilistic estimate of the hidden person’s position and its growing uncertainty, feeds this estimate directly into trajectory optimization, and actively searches likely paths when the person stays hidden. title: Review of the Current Research Status of Thermal Management Systems for Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells
abstract: Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFCs) is a key technology for the efficient conversion of clean energy, and the thermal management system is a critical auxiliary system for PEMFCs. This paper reviews the multi-field applications of PEMFCs thermal management in areas such as combined heat and power (CHP) and waste heat power generation. abstract: Abstract. The 17th century represented one of the most difficult climatic and social periods in the recent history of Europe, being marked by the transition to the Maunder Minimum, the peak of the Little Ice Age; marked by low thermal values, long and severe winters, rainy and cool summers, numerous dangerous climatic phenomena, a reduced number of normal years and seasons, famines, epidemics, etc. Taking these aspects into account, the present study aims to reconstruct, based on written historical sources, the climatic variability in the Principality of Transylvania during the 17th century. abstract: Abstract We present a survey of approaches to Bayesian inference with simulator forward models, focusing on settings with prohibitively expensive simulators. In this domain, Bayesian optimization-based methods have emerged as the most promising approach. We unify existing methods into a general framework, enabling consistent reasoning about shared algorithmic structure across the fragmented literature. title: Advances on triply periodic hyperbolic surface structures: from biological inspiration to artificial self-assembly
abstract: Triply periodic hyperbolic surfaces (TPHSs) are a class of complex structures that extend periodically throughout three-dimensional space and possess smooth surfaces with non-positive Gaussian curvature. They appear in a wide range of natural systems, from cellular membranes to butterfly wing scales and beetle exoskeletons. abstract: This study is a quantitative, cross-sectional, descriptive-correlational research design that determined the level of visitor awareness and self-reported ecotourism practices at Bauang Bakawan Eco-Tourism Park, La Union. Specifically, it described the demographic profile of the visitors, assessed their level of visitor awareness, determined the extent of their self-reported ecotourism practices, examined the relationship between the two variables, and developed a proposed action plan to strengthen responsible ecotourism practices at the park. abstract: With increasing renewable-energy demand, efficient maximum power point tracking (MPPT) remains essential for photovoltaic (PV) systems operating under nonlinear and varying conditions. This paper proposes a hybrid Q-learning-based fuzzy sliding mode controller (QGFSMC), integrating Q-learning adaptation, fuzzy decision-making, and gain-scheduled sliding mode control to improve dynamic tracking and disturbance rejection. abstract: Entrepreneurship is an important driver of regional economic development. Universities contribute to this goal by conducting state-of-the-art research and educating talent. The academic and policy debate regarding innovative start-up firms has primarily focused on how the outputs of research can be translated into entrepreneurial activities. abstract: Abstract High‐precision trajectory tracking for underground articulated load‐haul‐dump (LHD) vehicles is significantly challenged by strong kinematic coupling and drastic payload variations. abstract: As peer-to-peer prediction markets increasingly allow real-money wagering on environmental events, public scientific agencies are being drawn into the role of financial “settlement oracles,” the designated sources of truth against which contracts resolve. abstract: The global food system simultaneously drives and is threatened by intersecting planetary crises of climate change, biodiversity loss, land degradation and desertification, and pollution and waste. Over 10 days, from day 1 (initial shelf life) to day 10, forty uniformly unripe bananas (Musa Acuminata cv.) were monitored using both non-destructive and destructive methods to assess changes in their properties during ripening. title: TriFusion-Karst: A spatially robust and hydrogeologically validated stacked-ensemble model for groundwater potential assessment
abstract: Abstract Groundwater potential mapping in semi-arid karst regions is often compromised by spatially optimistic validation, limited assessment of predictive variability, and insufficient independent hydrogeological verification. This study introduces TriFusion-Karst, a stacked-ensemble model using RF and LightGBM as base learners and XGBoost as the meta-learner, embedded within a spatially robust and hydrogeologically validated workflow. Thirteen geo-environmental predictors were extracted at 7,313 groundwater monitoring wells, and GTD observations collected during 2018–2024 were pooled and use

title: Assessing rural household food security in flood-prone areas: An integrated FAO–IPCC framework-based analysis in Iran
abstract: Floods are one of the most destructive natural phenomena affecting food security by reducing agricultural production, disrupting food access, and diminishing household income. Given the increasing severity of climate-associated hazards and the vulnerability of communities to their effects, understanding the impacts of floods on food security and identifying the factors associated with it are essential. abstract: ABSTRACT Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) pose an increasing threat to high mountain environments across the world, especially in the Himalayas where climate change is accelerating glacier retreat and permafrost degradation. This study presents a detailed GLOF susceptibility analysis of the western Himalayas covering five major river basins, ie Satluj, Chenab, Jhelum, Beas, and Ravi by integrating high‐resolution remote sensing data with a multi‐criteria decision‐making approach. abstract: Introduction European regions are under increasing pressure to align climate adaptation with innovation-led development. title: Advances and Challenges in Methane Emission Measurement in the Oil and Gas Sector: A Review
abstract: Methane emissions from the oil and gas sector are a major contributor to climate change. It is essential to monitor and mitigate these emissions. In this review, sources of methane emissions, available monitoring techniques, emission estimation models, associated uncertainty, and newly emerging technologies, including AI-based monitoring techniques, are critically evaluated. A review was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A total of 480 records were retrieved from four databases: Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar. abstract: To survive in freezing environments, different organisms have evolved a remarkable class of proteins, known as antifreeze proteins (AFPs), which inhibit the growth of internal ice crystals. abstract: Managed aquifer recharge using floodwater (Flood-MAR) has emerged as a promising multi-benefit strategy to mitigate drought, groundwater depletion, and flood risk by capturing high-magnitude flows for aquifer recharge. abstract: Abstract Hainan Island is China’s largest tropical crop-production base, making its agricultural soil quality important for national food security. We determined total concentrations of eight heavy metals (Hg, As, Cd, Pb, Cr, Cu, Zn, Ni) in 300 surface soils collected across the island in late 2025. abstract: Abstract Energy-dispersive X-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectrometry is commonly used by archaeologists and museum staff to nondestructively characterize the elemental composition of artifacts or other materials of cultural relevance, ranging from obsidian and other lithics, to soils, pigments, metals, ceramics, and brick. abstract: Automated hazard detection in high-resolution satellite imagery of electrical substations presents significant challenges, including complex background clutter, high intra-class defect variability, and the prohibitive cost of pixel-level annotation. abstract: Sulfites are widely used in shrimp processing to prevent melanosis, yet the effect of freezing on sulfite stability during sample preservation for regulatory monitoring remains unexplored. This study assessed whether frozen storage at −18 °C significantly affects sulfite quantification in cooked shrimp, aiming to validate frozen samples as a reliable alternative to refrigerated samples in official control workflows. abstract: Job seekers face two linked problems: finding postings that are genuinely open and suitable, and presenting their experience to automated screening without exaggeration. This paper presents RoleRadar, a full-stack career platform built on one rule: deterministic code decides what is true, and the language model only rephrases it. abstract: Agricultural film mulching is a key agronomic practice for improving water and thermal resource use and ensuring food security, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions. abstract: Marginalization and informal urbanization pose significant challenges in global south countries. This study aims to show the crucial role of social capital in enhancing social resilience in informal urban areas. The research utilizes an applied-developmental approach with a descriptive-correlation methodology. Data collection involves library research and fieldwork in five districts of Urmia, with a sample size of 384 determined using Cochran's formula and distributed randomly. The questionnaire's validity was confirmed by experts, and reliability was assessed using the Cronbach's alpha test.

abstract: Abstract Fatigue damage is a predominant failure mechanism in historical riveted railway bridges, which is intensified by corrosion over time. This paper presents a fatigue-based reliability analysis of a century-old riveted steel railway bridge, decommissioned in 2010 due to significant corrosion-induced fatigue damage. title: ECONOMIC INVERSION IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY: IMPLICIT INTANGIBLE ASSETS AND THE TRANSFORMATION OF CORPORATE VALUE
abstract: The economic nature of implicit intangible assets is examined, and the concept of economic inversion of value is substantiated as a manifestation of the transformation of the sources of corporate value creation in the digital economy. Current trends in changes in the structure of companies’ market value and the sectoral distribution of intangible assets are analysed. abstract: Objective To develop and evaluate a discharge preparation service (DPS) for patients after heart valve replacement surgery. title: Development of Wildlife Identification System Based on Local Alignment Algorithm
abstract: Wildlife crimes seriously threaten biodiversity and public health security. Identifying the species of wild animals and their products involved in such cases is the key to handling them. This study aimed to establish a wildlife DNA identification system based on a local alignment algorithm, thereby providing reliable technical support for public security organizations with high-precision and high-efficiency species identification techniques. title: Prevalence of Self-reported Lifetime Physician-diagnosed Depression in Tunisia: Results of a National Study
abstract: Introduction/Objective Depression is a disabling mental health disorder affecting over 300 million people worldwide. In Tunisia, population-level data on its prevalence and determinants remain limited. Our study aimed to estimate the prevalence of depression in the Tunisian population and identify associated socio-demographic and clinical factors. abstract: The application of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in the Complete Systematic Land Registration (CSLR) and Participatory Systematic Land Registration (PTSL) programs significantly accelerates land mapping through aerial photogrammetry. This method substantially enhances accuracy in land certification processes, boundary identification, disaster mitigation efforts, and spatial planning efficiency. abstract: To address the challenges of small object detection in remote sensing images, such as susceptibility to background noise and difficulties in feature extraction, this paper proposes a method for detecting small objects in remote sensing images based on feature enhancement and scale-adaptive optimization under complex scenarios. title: Ultra-fine Micronized Human Acellular Dermal Matrix Promotes Diabetic Wound Healing in a Mouse Model
abstract: BACKGROUND/AIM: Diabetic wounds are characterized by chronic inflammation, impaired angiogenesis, and abnormal extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, which contribute to delayed wound healing and non-healing ulcers. Because ECM degradation and impaired matrix repair are central features of diabetic wound pathology, we evaluated an ultra-fine micronized human acellular dermal matrix (UFM-hADM; mean particle size approximately 70 μm) as an injectable ECM scaffold for diabetic wound repair. title: Combinatorial Tuning of Multigene Biosynthetic Pathways based on RNA Interference
abstract: Fine-tuning the expression level of multigene pathways remains a major challenge in engineering eukaryotic microbial cell factories. Modifications to individual pathway genes and CRISPR-based approaches often require repeated genome reconstruction, large regulatory components, or complex guide-array assembly. title: Assessing Dothistroma needle blight severity in Pinus radiata using UAV multispectral imagery
abstract: Dothistroma needle blight (DNB) is a major foliar disease of Pinus radiata , an important plantation species in several Southern Hemisphere countries. DNB management and resistance breeding depend on subjective, labour-intensive visual severity scoring that is difficult to scale. Prior UAV studies have used broad severity categories and crown-mean reflectance, discarding both the ordinal structure of the field grade and the within-crown spatial pattern of infection. abstract: The coupling of dynamical systems within living organisms frequently gives rise to emergent synergies, as seen in animal movement and homeostatic control. These natural mechanisms have inspired robotic control strategies, but existing approaches require precise models and significant manual or computational effort to engineer coupling. As the primary audience for Chinese-style content and trendy cultural-and-creative products, Generation Z has formed a unique aesthetic system characterized by a preference for lightweight visuals, complete character narratives and participatory co-creation. abstract: Climate change is increasingly challenging the sustainability, productivity, and welfare of livestock systems worldwide. Rising temperatures, prolonged droughts, water scarcity, changing precipitation patterns, and emerging disease risks directly affect animal health, welfare, feed availability, reproductive performance, and farm profitability. These pressures are particularly pronounced in climate-sensitive regions such as the Mediterranean, where livestock production is closely linked to limited natural resources and highly variable environmental conditions. abstract: Introduction The conditions of climatic elements such as temperature, precipitation, humidity, pressure, and wind in a given area directly affect bioclimatic comfort conditions. Climate parameters and weather variability affect the quality of urban life and influence the harmony of urban living areas with nature and energy consumption patterns. title: Comparison of Hydrochemical Characteristics of Groundwater in the Qihe River Alluvial Fan of North China over the Past 35 Years
abstract: Groundwater resources play a crucial role in socioeconomic development and domestic water use in piedmont alluvial plain areas. In this study, the Qihe River alluvial fan (QRAF) was selected as a representative area to investigate the evolutionary patterns of shallow groundwater chemistry in the North China Plain (NCP). Based on shallow groundwater monitoring data collected during the wet seasons of 1983 and 2017, the spatiotemporal trends in chemical characteristics and their influencing factors in shallow groundwater in the QRAF were studied using multi-hydrochemical and statistical methods.

abstract: BACKGROUND/AIM: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) play a pivotal role in regulating RNA-binding proteins (RBPs), which are crucial in the progression of colorectal cancer (CRC). title: Online education and digital learning paradigms in India: An exhaustive review of the literature
abstract: The purpose of this study is to give an overview of the evolution of digital learning paradigms, its implementation in Indian institutions and the challenges and opportunities which it provides. The review also seeks to identify gaps in the current research that can be used to direct future empirical and theoretical research. abstract: Abstract During the advancement of the nuclear industry, substantial uranium-bearing wastewater is inevitably generated. Given the current scarcity of uranium resources, the separation and recovery of uranium hold great importance.At present, facing a shortage of uranium resources, it is of great significance for separating and recovering uranium. A novel hybrid adsorbent of hafnium phosphate (HfP) decorated with phosphomuscle alcohol (PA) (HfP-PA-x, where x represents the amount of PA) was prepared. abstract: Water scarcity is increasingly coupled with energy insecurity, particularly in remote and arid regions where conventional desalination is constrained by electricity demand, brine management, and infrastructure cost. Solar powered membrane distillation (SPMD) is attractive because MD can operate with low- to moderate-temperature heat supplied by solar thermal collectors, photovoltaic-assisted subsystems, waste heat, or hybrid energy inputs. abstract: Este estudio investiga la influencia de la longitud focal en el rendimiento de un concentrador solar de disco parabólico (CDP) mediante el método de trazado de rayos. abstract: The rapid growth of aquaculture has led to the release of effluents rich in nutrients and heavy metals, posing significant ecological risks. This study evaluated the physiological responses and nutrient removal capacity of Spirodela polyrrhiza and Lemna minor exposed to a Cu(II) gradient (0–5 mg/L) in aquaculture wastewater. abstract: Background Small island cities grow on scarce, steep, and hazard-prone land. Negeri Batu Merah, a customary village in Ambon City, is classified as a heavy slum area with 66,424 people on 911 ha. Its dense settlement relies on septic tanks and shallow wells, linking land limits to water safety, and maternal and child health. abstract: This study quantifies costs underlying dynamic pricing strategies in the tourism industry in the current context. abstract: The object of this research is the process of planning and adjusting ship routes during amphibious operations under conditions of dynamic stochastic threats. The problem lies in the need to promptly adjust pre-planned ship routes in the event of changes in stochastic threats while simultaneously ensuring the necessary level of force survivability. abstract: Thermoelectric generators (TEGs) present a promising technology for recovering thermal energy from waste heat in water streams; however, their performance under low-grade heat and continuous-flow conditions has not yet been fully characterized. abstract: The red swamp crayfish ( Procambarus clarkii ) is a globally significant aquaculture species, yet the biological trade-offs between intensive pond monoculture and integrated rice-crayfish co-culture systems remain poorly understood at the intestinal level. abstract: Abstract Raman spectroscopy is a powerful technique for molecular identification and quantitative analysis, but inherently weak scattering limits its use at low analyte concentrations. Here, we developed a lithography-free route to fabricate three-dimensional metal-decorated silicon nanopores for Raman enhancement. title: Divergent mercury accumulation dynamics in tropical dry and moist broadleaf forests
abstract: Abstract. Forests are major sinks for atmospheric mercury (Hg) due to the efficiency of stomatal uptake and litter deposition. Tropical forests, highly productive ecosystems, remain understudied despite their pronounced climatic and phenological variability. We investigated whether seasonal rainfall regimes and associated tree adaptations regulate the Hg dynamics – its uptake by leaves, deposition through litter, and storage in soils– in secondary tropical moist broadleaf (TMBF) and tropical dry broadleaf (TDBF) forests from Costa Rica. abstract: Abstract India’s Nationally Determined Contribution commits to creating an additional 2.5–3 billion tonnes of carbon sinks by 2030. abstract: International courts and tribunals have converged, across 2024 and 2025, on a standard of due diligence that is ‘informed by the best available science’. abstract: The transition to high-penetration wind power introduces critical frequency stability and low-inertia challenges to modern power grids. Flywheel Energy Storage Systems (FESS), characterized by millisecond-level dynamic response and inherent electromechanical isomorphism, offer a physically backed approach to mitigating these vulnerabilities. abstract: This paper departs from the standard question of whether low out-of-pocket (OOP) spending in Odisha reflects financial protection or forgone care. It asks instead whether the architecture of inequity has been rebuilt as insurance expanded, whether tribal exclusion is produced by supply-side or demand-side failures, and whether the standard equity indicators used to monitor universal health coverage (UHC) are internally consistent. title: Thresholds and spatial effects of urbanization on ecosystem service supply-demand relationships: a multiscale study of the Wuhan Metropolitan Area
abstract: Rapid urbanization continues to reshape the supply–demand relationships of ecosystem services (ESs), posing increasing risks to regional sustainable development. Previous work has looked at the scale dependence and spatial heterogeneity of urbanization and how they independently impact supply–demand relationships of ESs but they have not been considered jointly. title: The potential for large-scale genome editing in finfish aquaculture via germline stem cell culture and transplantation
abstract: Genome editing has emerged as a promising tool to complement selective breeding programmes and accelerate genetic gain in aquaculture. Although CRISPR-based genome editing has been successfully applied in several economically important fish species, its application at an industry-relevant scale remains challenging due to limitations of current delivery methods, which primarily rely on manual embryo microinjection. abstract: Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans ( A. ferrooxidans ) exhibits strong arsenic resistance and plays a pivotal role in biometallurgy and sulfur cycling in ecosystems. abstract: This study evaluated the effects of dietary black cumin (Nigella sativa) powder supplementation on the hematological condition, growth performance, and survival rate of Asian redtail catfish (Hemibagrus nemurus) fingerlings. abstract: Previous terrein reviews have emphasized its isolation, synthesis, production, and broad biological activities. abstract: This study examines the historical foundations and gradual evolution of Pakistan-China relations, highlighting the enduring friendship between the two countries over seven and a half decades. abstract: Aging of poly(vinyl) chloride (PVC) tap water pipes may release microplastics (MPs) into water. Optical fiber sensors that detect MPs by utilizing refractive index (RI) changes in the evanescent field offers potential for in situ detection. This study evaluates the effects of water matrix, MP sizes, and hydrodynamics on the response and sensitivity of optical fiber sensors for PVC-MP detection in water supply pipes. abstract: Financial settlement breaks remain a persistent operational risk. This paper presents a multi-horizon reconciliation architecture coordinating three tiers over one transaction stream: daily batch, hourly incremental partitioning, and real-time listener-based interception. abstract: Animal venoms constitute a rich source of bioactive peptides targeting membrane receptors, including G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) and ligand-gated ion channels. However, identifying receptor-binding ligands directly from complex venom mixtures remains analytically challenging because venoms are highly diverse and conventional screening approaches have limited throughput. abstract: Drought is a main climatic hazard affecting water resources and agricultural activities in semi-arid areas. This study evaluated the spatiotemporal variability of drought in the hot semi-arid areas of Karnataka, India, using the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI), and Rainfall Anomaly Index (RAI). abstract: Rising demand for sustainable energy, together with growing concern over the environmental impact of fossil fuels, has focused attention on alternative biofuels. Waste cooking oil (WCO) is an attractive, low-cost feedstock for biodiesel that simultaneously addresses a waste-disposal problem and reduces reliance on virgin vegetable oils. abstract: Abstract Conventional electromagnetic field (EMF) assessment around Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) antennas is typically performed from accessible ground-level or rooftop locations, which may not adequately capture the spatial variability around elevated directional antennas. abstract: Biofilm formation plays a major role in bacterial persistence across clinical and environmental settings, with particular significance in chronic infections. Achromobacter spp. are environment-borne emerging opportunistic pathogens increasingly recognized in biofilm-associated diseases. abstract: Trend-driven environments change rapidly, and consumers' decision responses may fluctuate. abstract: Abstract The Congolese Copperbelt is a major source of copper and cobalt for the global energy transition, but mineral processing creates substantial and poorly documented local air-pollution risks. title: Equity dimensions of future vulnerabilities to climate hazards: Long-term spatial population projections for New York City consistent with Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
abstract: Projections of future population are important for a myriad of reasons. Large cities, states, and countries routinely produce near- and mid-range population projections. In the context of climate change, the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP) framework is used at global and national scales to project long-term population to inform future emissions scenarios and understand future climate-related exposures and impacts. abstract: Alcoholic liver disease is defined as damage of liver structure and function caused by prolonged heavy alcohol consumption, and novel preventive and treatment options are needed. abstract: Environmental stresses pose a serious threat to global rice production. title: Lithium in North American Produced Waters: Geological Controls, Direct Extraction Mechanisms, and the Gap Between Synthetic and Real-Brine Evidence
abstract: Global lithium demand has increased rapidly, driven largely by expanding battery production, with consumption estimated at 263, 263,000 t in 2025. abstract: Prior work has recommended the use of Wet-Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) to inform operational management of marathons. title: Large-extent Classification of Wetland and Management Types Using Satellite Remote Sensing and Auxiliary Data
abstract: There have been few studies examining how effectively land use / land cover (LULC) classes of wetland types and their management can be detected with remote sensing and auxiliary data. title: Movement characteristics of persistent extreme precipitation events over China during the warm season using high spatiotemporal resolution data
abstract: Abstract Moving persistent extreme precipitation events (PEPEs) can cause severe disasters along their tracks. However, a PEPE typically consists of multiple rain cells that evolve and move differently from one another, rendering the conventional single-center tracking method incapable of capturing their respective characteristics. Here we use a multi-rain cell tracking method to characterize the movement of PEPEs during the warm season (May to September) over China, utilizing high-resolution precipitation data at half‑hourly temporal and 0.1° spatial resolutions for the period 1998–2024. abstract: The extensive use of galvalume roofing in Darul Muttaqin Batu Islamic Boarding School offers practical advantages, including light weight, durability, and ease of installation. abstract: Introduction Bone morphogenetic protein 15 (BMP15), a transforming growth factor β (TGF-β) superfamily member, is well known for its crucial involvement in regulating female reproduction in mammals, and recently also in fishes. abstract: This study proposes a model predictive path integral (MPPI) control method that combines adaptive covariance adjustment with low-pass perturbation filtering for the pose control of a robotic manipulator. abstract: Airborne nanoparticles constitute a significant global health threat. To reduce animal testing and better replicate the exposure of humans to airborne pollutants, environmental toxicology relies on in vitro cell culture and advanced cell-supporting models and platforms. Traditional submerged cell cultures, using either primary cells or continuously-growing cell lines, have provided valuable insights into the toxicity of nanoparticles. abstract: Introduction Groundwater recharge is traditionally understood to be primarily controlled by precipitation and other climatic processes. However, intensive anthropogenic water management and urbanization may weaken this relationship in megacities. This study investigates hydrological decoupling at the municipal scale in Beijing, China, and quantifies the relative contributions of anthropogenic and climatic drivers to groundwater dynamics. abstract: This introduction explores the challenges of integrated sustainable waste management (ISWM) when managing ever-increasing volumes of garbage in fast growing cities. This study presents a 6‐year (2020–2025) regional assessment of major rivers in Telangana using monitoring data from the Telangana State Pollution Control Board. abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the efficiency and air logistics‐based trade competitiveness of five major Asian hub airports: Incheon International Airport, Hong Kong International Airport, Narita International Airport, Singapore Changi Airport, and Beijing Capital International Airport. abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an emerging mosquito-borne alphavirus that causes millions of infections and severe arthralgia annually. title: Modeling branch diameter in Larix olgensis using living branches, knot profiles and stem scars: climate–soil associations
abstract: Branch diameter (BD) strongly influences crown architecture, knot formation and wood quality, yet BD development is commonly modeled using living branches alone, leaving the diameter attained by dead branches at growth cessation insufficiently represented. abstract: Abstract This study presents an empirical investigation of the Tapeworm Foraging Optimization (TFO) algorithm, a nature-inspired metaheuristic search framework motivated by parasitic tapeworm attachment and reproductive segmentation. TFO combines a decaying Gaussian perturbation for exploratory diffusion with an inverted difference-vector displacement toward the current global best for local exploitation, governed by a probabilistic switching parameter. abstract: Infectious disease models are used to predict the spread and impact of outbreaks of a disease. Like other complex models, they have parameters that need to be calibrated, and structural discrepancies from the reality that they simulate that should be accounted for in calibration and prediction. Whilst Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) techniques have been applied to infectious disease models before, they were not routinely used to inform policymakers in the UK during the COVID-19 pandemic. abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) face persistent challenges in maintaining energy efficiency, balanced resource utilization, and reliable data transmission as network density increases. Existing clustering and routing approaches generally address these requirements independently, resulting in inadequate coordination among cluster-head selection, node grouping, routing, and cooperative resource allocation. abstract: Urban areas face the dual challenge of mitigating carbon emissions while halting biodiversity loss, yet longitudinal evidence from Asian megacities on whether biodiversity independently enhances carbon sequestration remains limited. This study examines the biodiversity–carbon relationship using a twelve-year panel dataset from Haidian District, Beijing—a highly urbanized region where green space expansion has largely reached its spatial limits. title: Rotatiridoid, a rare iridoid from Phlomoides rotata (Benth. ex Hook.f.) Mathiesen and its anti-inflammatory activity
abstract: A rare iridoid featuring an unusual 3-O-8 bridged ether bond, named rotatiridoid (1), was obtained from Phlomoides rotata (Benth. ex Hook.f.) Mathiesen, along with five known analogues. Its structure was established by means of HRESIMS, 1D and 2D NMR experiments, and ECD calculations. abstract: Paraphrasing is an essential but demanding skill in EFL academic writing, and AI-based tools such as QuillBot are increasingly used to support it. This qualitative study explored how EFL students perceive QuillBot as a paraphrasing tool. abstract: In this literature synthesis we investigated parent perspectives on how instructional modality affects the type and amount of support parents need to provide their primary/secondary online learners. abstract: The unique microenvironment created by photovoltaic (PV) power stations may progressively reshape ecosystem species composition through sustained effects on aboveground vegetation and soil seed banks. However, the long-term ecological impacts, particularly those on soil seed banks, remain poorly understood. abstract: This study investigates how aortic valve leaflet stiffness affects hemodynamics and structural performance using high-fidelity fluid–structure interaction simulations of a patient-specific aortic arch. We screened 25 clinical isolates from patients with suspected vulvovaginal candidiasis using crystal violet staining. abstract: This article shows how the environmental crisis is understood and conceptualized within the Czech conspiritual milieu. abstract: ABSTRACT Groundwater discharge to headwater streams plays a critical role in maintaining flow during dry periods and buffering stream temperatures, yet groundwater‐stream interactions remain poorly understood in low‐ to moderate‐relief headwater catchments. In this study, we used paired analysis of air, stream and groundwater temperature across 53 site‐years collected over 2 years to assess the relative importance and depth of groundwater contributions in four moderate‐relief headwater catchments in a cold, humid region (eastern Canada). abstract: Introduction This study aimed to develop and characterize a compound seasoning paste containing a Maillard-derived flavor base prepared from quinoa hydrolysate and bovine bone collagen peptides. Methods The flavor base was prepared through the Maillard reaction and subsequently incorporated with beef tallow and other auxiliary ingredients. abstract: This study examines how teaching teams can develop the complementary capabilities in technology application, industry understanding, and translation of expertise into teaching required for AI general education in higher vocational colleges. Taking Jiangsu Maritime Institute as a case, it explores pathways for team development and mechanisms for teaching delivery. title: Isolation and characterization of novel Klebsiella phages from Benin and their antibiofilm activities on multidrug resistant and hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae strains
abstract: Abstract Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae represents a growing clinical threat, particularly where multidrug resistance limits treatment options. Here, we report the isolation and characterization of three novel lytic phages from Benin (Kp1Bj_HH11_M23, Kp2Bj_LN294_M23, and Kp10Bj_LN54_14). These Myoviruses, belonging to the genera Marfavirus and Jiaodavirus , display broad host range activity against multidrug-resistant and hypervirulent K. pneumoniae strains. title: Vegetation cover dynamics in the Modder River Basin, South Africa: evidence from climate drivers and land cover during the 2015–2024
abstract: Dynamic changes in vegetation cover within semi-arid inland river basins are crucial for understanding global climate change and regional ecological security. This study investigated spatiotemporal vegetation dynamics and climatic drivers in South Africa's Modder River Basin (2015–2024) using GEE, Landsat 8, MODIS, and pixel binning. abstract: ABSTRACT Gas‐produced water (GPW) is increasingly recognized as an important low‐quality aqueous lithium resource. abstract: Abstract. The climate effect of aviation is significant and expected to increase. abstract: This study investigates the enhancement of the aerodynamic performance and efficiency of horizontal-axis wind turbine (HAWT) blades through passive trailing-edge morphing. abstract: This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the pharmacological and computational potential of the methanolic extract of Combretum indicum. Mineral profiling by ICP-AES confirmed the presence of essential elements, including K (5.92 ppm), Mg (4.94 ppm), Fe (1.92 ppm), and Zn (1.13 ppm), with no detectable toxic heavy metals. abstract: Abstract As a traditional Chinese double-reed woodwind instrument, the Suona has evolved through representative forms such as the Tang Bili and Qing Sunaiyi. However, systematic studies on its acoustic characteristics across historical evolution remain scarce. This work takes the Qing Sunaiyi and the modern standard Suona as samples, and adopts an integrated approach combining three-dimensional scanning, finite element simulation, and intelligent optimization. abstract: Purpose: This study examines traditional plant knowledge in rural and peri-urban Istanbul, where environmental access, household production and metropolitan connections coexist.Method: Fieldwork within Türkiye’s national programme for documenting traditional knowledge associated with bio-logical diversity covered 30 neighbourhoods in ten districts in 2021–2022. abstract: Background: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by the degeneration and progressive loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra of the midbrain, leading to motor symptoms that affect the functional gait of individuals with this diagnosis. Among non-pharmacological treatment strategies, Aquatic Physical Therapy demonstrates several benefits for gait rehabilitation. abstract: Digital transformation has become central to defense modernization, yet evidence remains limited on how digital capabilities and management capacity interact with national defense-industry self-reliance to shape national defense posture. This study examines the direct effects of digital transformation, management capability, and defense-industry self-reliance, and tests whether self-reliance changes the effects of digital transformation and management capability on defense posture. abstract: This study investigates medium to high rank coal-rock from the Shanxi Fm. and Benxi Fm. in Well S5-3, Ordos Basin. title: Assessment of hydrological response and water balance components using the Variable Infiltration Capacity model in the Cauvery River Basin, India
abstract: Accurate estimation of water balance components at the river basin scale is essential for sustainable water resources management, particularly in regions experiencing increasing climatic variability and growing anthropogenic pressures. The Cauvery River Basin, one among the major river basins of peninsular India is taken up in this study. This study presents a comprehensive water balance analysis of the Cauvery River Basin using the Variable Infiltration Capacity (VIC) model integrated with satellite based remote sensing datasets. abstract: ABSTRACT Ganga River basin supports high biodiversity and provides important ecosystem services, but it is rapidly deteriorating due to anthropogenic activities. In this study, we evaluated freshwater biodiversity restoration interventions in the Ganga River basin under the ‘Biodiversity Conservation and Ganga Rejuvenation’ initiative implemented by the National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG) in collaboration with the Wildlife Institute of India (WII). title: Deciphering molecular mechanisms of synergistic growth reduction in kinase inhibitor combinations
abstract: Targeted kinase inhibitors often yield transient or incomplete responses because tumour cells buffer pathway blockade through signalling cross-talk, motivating synergistic drug combinations. However, it remains unclear whether synergy typically arises from engaging new signalling programs or from reinforcing the dominant effects of each monotherapy at shared downstream control points. Here we analyse two synergistic inhibitor pairs in AGS gastric adenocarcinoma cells: PI3K inhibition combined with inhibition of either MEK (MAP2K1, MAP2K2) or TAK1 (MAP3K7). title: Candidate Dry-season Refugia and Recent Winter Open-water Decline in Hakaluki Haor, Bangladesh (1995–2026)
abstract: Hakaluki Haor is a major freshwater wetland in north-eastern Bangladesh, but the spatial concentration of persistent water and the consistency of recent winter open-water change remain poorly resolved. We combined JRC Global Surface Water v1.4 with Landsat Collection 2 surface reflectance in Google Earth Engine. abstract: ABSTRACT Heterointerface engineering with a built‐in electric field enables tailoring of surface electronic structures, bridging electronic modulation with reaction kinetics for efficient energy conversion. Herein, we construct a Co‐doped V 2 O 3 /VN heterointerface (Co‐VN@V 2 O 3 ), wherein the synergistic interfacial effect optimizes water adsorption, dissociation, and hydrogen desorption, thereby conferring high activity for the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). title: The 2009–2010 Ouazzane seismic sequence: evidence for a possible active horsetail-like termination of the Jebha Fault, Rif belt, Northern Morocco
abstract: The western-central Rif is characterized by diffuse seismicity, including a pronounced earthquake sequence occurring in 2009–2010 near Ouazzane, southwest of the Jebha Fault. The structural significance of this sequence and its relationship to the regional fault system remain poorly constrained. We analyzed the regional earthquake catalogue, performed double-difference hypocentral relocation and GardnerKnopoff declustering, and integrated regional focal mechanisms with mapped geological structures to investigate the spatial organization and seismotectonic significance of the Ouazzane sequence.

title: Lightweight SAR building segmentation via enhanced multi-scale context modeling and bidirectional guided feature fusion
abstract: Accurate building extraction from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery is important for urban mapping, disaster assessment, and remote-sensing interpretation, but remains difficult because speckle noise, heterogeneous scattering, radar shadow, weak texture, and ambiguous building boundaries can degrade pixel-level predictions. At the same time, heavy segmentation networks are difficult to deploy in computation-constrained settings. title: Translational plausibility of honey-derived antimicrobial biomaterials against biofilm-associated infections
abstract: Chronic biofilm-associated infections drive antimicrobial resistance (AMR) via prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy that is often ineffective. Honeys from Apis mellifera and stingless bees (Meliponini) exhibit antimicrobial and anti-biofilm activity via complementary mechanisms: osmotic stress, low pH, hydrogen peroxide, methylglyoxal, bee defensin-1, and phenolic and organic compounds. abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction to hydrocarbon fuels represents a sustainable route toward carbon neutrality, yet selective and efficient C 2 production remains a formidable challenging due to the high thermodynamic barrier and sluggish C–C coupling kinetics. We analysed 4,126 village units in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) at five benchmark years from 2003 to 2023, using an ecological resilience index (ERI) integrating resistance, adaptability and recovery. Five overlapping functional types were examined through city-adjusted comparisons, spatially validated extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) models and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). Creep behavior and particle breakage of carbonaceous mudstone coarse-grained soil: experimental study and discrete element modeling
abstract: Carbonaceous mudstone coarse-grained soil is commonly used as embankment fill in southwestern China. It exhibits significant creep characteristics, and its long-term deformation is closely related to particle breakage. In this paper, large-scale confined creep tests, sieving tests, and single-particle compression tests were carried out, combined with a discrete element model considering stress corrosion effects, to investigate the creep characteristics, particle strength evolution, and mesoscopic breakage mechanisms of carbonaceous mudstone subgrade fill under different gradations. title: Climate-Resilient Spatial Zoning for Temporary Cultural Infrastructures: A framework for Flood-Prone Contexts
abstract: Event spaces and cultural areas are often built temporarily. These temporary structures are built without considering the possibility of defending against extreme weather events like floods. Under unforeseen situations like extreme weather, the accessibility and services will collapse. The impact on this will be particularly significant on the vulnerable population, mainly older adults and children. title: Investigating Lightning Stroke Variability and Ground Stroke Density in Peninsular Malaysia: A Statewise Comparative Study of Fatality Trends
abstract: This study investigates the spatial variability of lightning stroke occurrences and their associated fatality rates across the 12 states of Peninsular Malaysia from 2019 to 2023. A total of 8,427,391 cloud -to-ground strokes were analyzed using data obtained from the Vaisala GLD360 network and processed by ArcGIS Pro with total of 130 fatalities. title: Individual and Interactive Effects of Floods and Tropical Cyclones on Mortality: A Multicountry Time-Series Analysis
abstract: Abstract Floods and tropical cyclones (TCs) are two of the most common and costliest climate disasters worldwide, yet a consistent evaluation of their individual and interactive health effects across events and countries remains lacking. We aimed to quantify the individual and joint all-cause and cardiopulmonary mortality risks associated with flood and TC exposure across countries and regions. title: Race disparities in total PM2.5 and wildfire-specific PM2.5 exposure among disaggregated Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander groups in California
abstract: Introduction Environmental health disparities in the United States (US) are evident in PM 2.5 exposure, but few studies have documented wildfire-specific PM 2.5 disparities. Furthermore, aggregating broad racial groups may hide disparities for Asian American (AA) and Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander (NHPI) groups. title: Effect of Dimple Topology and Ball Mass on the Aerodynamic and Flight Performance of Golf Balls
abstract: The flight performance of a golf ball is governed by its surface geometry, which controls boundary-layer transition, separation and wake formation, yet the effects of convex surface topology and of ball mass remain underexplored. This study experimentally compares three surface patterns of identical diameter and feature count: conventional circular dimples (baseline), hexagonal dimples and circular convex protrusions. title: Climate-based suitability scenario models for high-protein crop cultivation in Europe
abstract: Despite several concurrent environmental and nutritional benefits, protein crop production in the EU remains low, and imports remain high. Therefore, a knowledge gap exists in relation to the suitability of different protein crops in Europe and how this may change under future climates. In this research, we aimed to identify areas conducive to cultivating human-grade, high-protein crops. abstract: La irrupción de la inteligencia artificial generativa (IAg) ha inaugurado una nueva era en la tecnología educativa, replanteando los paradigmas tradicionales de la evaluación formativa y la retroalimentación pedagógica en los diferentes niveles del sistema educativo. title: Hydrogel-Enabled Decontamination and Sensing of Chemical Toxicants: A Review
abstract: Chemical toxicants, including organophosphorus pesticides, heavy metal ions, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, antibiotics, synthetic dyes, phenolic compounds, and PFAS, pose severe threats to ecosystems and human health because of their high toxicity, environmental persistence, and bioaccumulation. Hydrogels are functional polymeric materials with three-dimensional network structures. title: From histopathology to molecular taxonomy: predicting pituitary neuroendocrine tumors invasiveness
abstract: Pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) are among the most prevalent intracranial tumors in adults. Although most follow an indolent clinical course, a substantial subset exhibits local invasion, which can limit gross total resection and increase the risk of residual disease and recurrence. Importantly, anatomical invasiveness should not be equated with clinical aggressiveness. title: From footsteps to wireless events: infrastructure-native battery-free interfaces for human–environment interactions
abstract: Future intelligent environments require infrastructure-native interfaces that can sense human activities and directly generate wireless communication events using standard protocols. Achieving this remains challenging because human footsteps are transient, irregular, and often low-force, whereas standard wireless protocols such as Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) require substantial energy consumption. title: Geo‐Setting Risk Assessment in Eurasia: A Multidimensional Framework and Strategies
abstract: Amid intensifying geopolitical tensions and climate-related pressures, geo-setting risk has become increasingly multidimensional. This analysis of geo-setting risk in 16 Eurasian countries from 2010 to 2023, using a composite framework integrating regional geopolitical, political, economic, social, and ecological indicators, revealed marked spatial and temporal heterogeneity. abstract: The study presents the moment–rotation (M–φ) characteristics of semi-rigid I-profile joints made using header plates and flush end-plates. title: Beyond Survival: A Qualitative Study of Recovery Barriers and Facilitators Following Emergency Laparotomy
abstract: This mixed-methods study aimed to identify multi-level barriers, facilitators, and actionable interventions for recovery following emergency laparotomy, a high-acuity event where traditional clinical metrics often fail to capture the nuances of patients' lived experience during convalescence. We conducted semi-structured interviews and surveys with 15 adults recovering from emergency laparotomy and subsequently completed human-in-the-loop AI-assisted thematic analysis. title: Decoloniality, Posthumanism and the Language Assemblage
abstract: ABSTRACT This review article analyses decolonial and posthumanist thought within critical language studies, highlighting the convergences, divergences and implications of these critical paradigms. Both decolonial and posthumanist frameworks offer critiques of the universalisation of the human, which has implications for how language is understood and mobilised.
