abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is one of the main etiological agents of acute mastitis during lactation, and its ability to persist in biofilms can compromise conventional antimicrobial treatments. Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) have emerged as promising probiotic candidates for mastitis management, but the molecular mechanisms underlying their interaction with S. aureus remain poorly understood. title: Multiplicity Quantifies Intra‐Cluster Diversity in Metagenomic Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Clustering data into operational units is essential in biodiversity studies, allowing researchers to organize observations into biologically meaningful entities such as species, proteins, or genes. However, this step inevitably leads to information loss by concealing intra‐cluster variability—an important component of functional biodiversity—and the extent of this loss depends on the clustering scheme. abstract: Kidney renal clear carcinoma (KIRC) is a common genitourinary malignancy with high morbidity and mortality rates despite multimodal therapies. Programmed cell death (PCD) is an active death process that occurs not only in the normal development of individuals but also in abnormal physiological states or diseases. title: Desafíos de la fe pública notarial en la era digital en Ecuador
abstract: Este artículo analiza, desde una perspectiva sociojurídica, la fe pública notarial en su tránsito hacia la digitalización en Ecuador, en un contexto de tensiones culturales, institucionales y tecnológicas que condicionan la implementación de los actos notariales digitales. abstract: Introduction Methotrexate (MTX) is a potent antineoplastic agent; however, its clinical application is frequently limited by nephrotoxicity, which may result in treatment interruption. abstract: Abstract Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are environmentally ubiquitous and known to have pervasive impacts on cellular homeostasis. abstract: ABSTRACT The 1,4‐butanediol oxidation reaction (BDOR) provides a sustainable platform for producing valuable chemicals, yet its reaction kinetics remain constrained by inefficient proton transfer. abstract: Graphene-reinforced Aluminum Matrix Composites (GRAMC) are promising candidates for hypervelocity shielding. title: Hydrothermal alteration and shortwave infrared (SWIR) spectroscopy exploration of the Hatu gold deposit in West Junggar, NW China
abstract: The Hatu gold deposit in West Junggar, Xinjiang, is hosted by the Lower Carboniferous volcano-sedimentary rocks and records multistage hydrothermal alteration, yet its alteration zonation and associated shortwave infrared (SWIR) responses remain poorly constrained. abstract: Abstract Ultraviolet (UV) radiation in sunlight is well known to harm components of solar modules, especially those of emerging photovoltaic technologies. abstract: Abstract Commercial video games reach billions of people worldwide and may offer a scalable opportunity to engage players in climate and environmental action. abstract: Abstract As landscapes cycle through wetting and drying, stream networks expand and contract, driving material export and biogeochemical transformations with important implications for water quality and ecosystem function. abstract: Microbial manufacturing is emerging as a complementary method to traditional metal processing using microorganisms and their metabolites as functional agents for selective dissolution, recovery, surface modification, and protective mineral formation. abstract: Mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) genes may influence treatment outcomes in affected patients. abstract: Abstract High-pressure flanges are essential components for joining pipes, ensuring sealing, and preventing liquid and gas leakage. abstract: ABSTRACT Limited water availability coupled with increasing soil salinity poses a major challenge to sustainable turfgrass growth and performance. Dactylis glomerata L. (orchardgrass) is a widely distributed cool‐season perennial grass traditionally valued for forage production, with increasing interest in its potential as an alternative low‐input turf‐type species for water‐ and salt‐limited environments. abstract: Abstract Catfishes (order Siluriformes) inhabit diverse aquatic environments worldwide, ranging from tropical lowlands to fast‐flowing mountain rivers. Here, we investigated genome evolution in an extreme environment by focusing on Glyptosternum maculatum , the highest‐altitude‐dwelling catfish known and a basal lineage of Glyptosternoid fishes. abstract: Schatten- p norm optimization has emerged as an effective non-convex relaxation for low-rank matrix completion. In this work, we propose a novel factorized reformulation of the Schatten- p norm by decomposing it into combinations of nuclear and Frobenius norms. title: The Machine’s Voice and Gaze: Discipline, Inscription, and Heterotopia in “Afrika Dansı”
abstract: This article examines resistance in Sevim Burak’s short story “Afrika Dansı” (1982) through close reading of its typographic and acoustic organization. It draws on Michel Foucault’s accounts of disciplinary power and the production of the case, Connell and Messerschmidt’s concept of hegemonic masculinity, and Robert J. Topinka’s reframing of Foucauldian heterotopia into textual heterotopia. The article argues that the narrator’s resistance to medical authority does not constitute escape or emancipation. title: Türkiye in Africa: strategic realignment through soft power, security, and south–south partnerships
abstract: Objectives This study aims to analyze Türkiye’s strategic engagement in Africa, focusing on its evolving foreign policy approach through soft power, security cooperation, and South–South partnerships. It seeks to understand how Türkiye positions itself as an influential actor in Africa and the implications of this engagement for regional and global geopolitics. abstract: ABSTRACT Platinum‐based alloys remain the most promising electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet suffer from activity‐stability trade‐offs, particularly in alkaline media where Pt‐Ni alloys undergo continuous dissolution. Herein, we report the rational design of intermetallic Pt 2 W alloy nanoparticles uniformly anchored on N‐doped carbon nanomeshes (N‐CM), leveraging tungsten's exceptional thermodynamic stability and corrosion resistance to address this dilemma. title: Implementación de prácticas DevSecOps con inteligencia artificial para fortalecer la seguridad y eficiencia en el desarrollo de software en una empresa de fábrica de software
abstract: La creciente necesidad de incorporar la seguridad desde las primeras etapas del desarrollo de software ha impulsado la adopción de prácticas DevSecOps reforzadas con inteligencia artificial (IA). title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and environmental associations of Dynamic Habitat Index components in southwestern China: Nonlinear responses and spatial nonlinear associations revealed by XGBoost–SHAP and MGWR
abstract: The Dynamic Habitat Index (DHI) captures cumulative vegetation activity, minimum activity and intra-annual variability. We derived annual DHI components from MODIS EVI for 2001–2024 and quantified long-term trends using Theil–Sen slopes and Mann–Kendall tests. Environmental associations were examined using spatially validated XGBoost–SHAP, spatial block bootstrap and multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR), with sensitivity analyses across alternative spatial configurations. title: Middle East war-driven energy supply disruptions could influence air pollution in India and China
abstract: Abstract Rapid economic growth has increased energy demand to ~ 11,000 TWh in India and ~ 50,000 TWh in China, where coal accounts for 57.5% and 54.79% of total energy consumption, respectively. Both countries also depend strongly on imported oil, with ~ 45% of India’s and ~ 54% of China’s crude-oil imports originating from the Middle East, creating vulnerability to geopolitical energy-supply disruptions. Here, we investigate whether such disruptions could influence regional air pollution by integrating energy data, sector-resolved emissions, GEOS-Chem simulations, and satellite observations.

title: MORPH – Lessons learnt from the development and application of an individual-based model
abstract: This paper summarises some of the lessons learnt over approximately 25 years from the development and application of the individual-based model, MORPH. The overall purpose of the model is to predict how the survival, condition, and behaviour of populations of animals are influenced by the food resources available and other environmental factors. The model was originally developed for a single bird species at a single site but was designed to be very flexible, hence its name. abstract: ABSTRACT The sharp decline in light yield ( LY ) of X‐ray scintillators under extreme high temperatures remains a key bottleneck for their application in high‐temperature radiation imaging. Herein, 1,2,4,5‐tetra(4‐carboxyphenyl)benzene (H 4 TCPB) are employed as linkers to assemble lanthanide cluster {Eu 4 O 30 } secondary building units, affording ultrabright thermally enhanced Eu‐TCPB‐MOF based X‐ray scintillators. abstract: An experimental program was conducted to evaluate the effect of initial curing temperature on cement grout under sulfate attack by wet-dry cycling. Cement grout with a water-to-cement ratio of 1.0 were initially cured at 20°C, 40°C, 60°C, and 80°C and then subjected to 30 wet–dry cycles in 5% Na 2 SO 4 solution. title: Responsible Green Datafication in Household Low‐Carbon Technologies: Trust, Legitimacy, and Consumer Adoption
abstract: ABSTRACT Household digital low‐carbon technologies can support sustainable consumption while expanding the collection and algorithmic use of domestic data, creating a tension between environmental benefits and the legitimacy of data‐intensive consumer systems. Drawing on privacy‐calculus, digital‐trust, institutional‐legitimacy, responsible‐innovation, and sustainable‐consumption perspectives, this study examines how governance cues and datafication risks relate to consumer adoption through responsible data trust and perceived green‐data legitimacy. title: Agro-Ecofeminist Communicative Language Teaching: Reimagining ELT through Indigenous Women’s Knowledge Systems
abstract: To rethink ELT by focusing on environmental problems and creating new values around women's knowledge systems and AI-assisted learning, we offer the Agro-Ecofeminist Communicative Language Teaching (AEF-CLT) paradigm.We take a qualitative, theorybased methodological approach to developing a context-based model of language learning that foregrounds the role of women farmers as knowledge producers and uses their life stories as authentic resources for teaching critical and sensitive communication.The architecture includes several digital tools: corpus-driven vocabulary and discourse learning sys

title: DESAFÍOS PEDAGÓGICOS DE LA INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL GENERATIVA EN LA EDUCACIÓN SUPERIOR
abstract: La inteligencia artificial está transformando la educación superior. Su integración trasciende la adopción tecnológica y afecta las prácticas pedagógicas, los procesos de evaluación y la relación de los estudiantes con el conocimiento. Este ensayo analiza críticamente la incorporación de la inteligencia artificial en contextos universitarios. Identifica sus aportes pedagógicos y las tensiones derivadas de su uso, especialmente en relación con la autonomía cognitiva, el pensamiento crítico y los desafíos éticos e institucionales. title: Unyielding Resilience of the Schengen Area: Adapting to Crises in a Transforming World
abstract: Abstract The Schengen area has recently experienced many crises. Despite occasional references to its potential end, it has proven its resilience. Whilst researchers explore Schengen's borders and databases, few studies have focused on the discourse on Schengen per se. This article fills this gap by examining discursive shifts in the perception of Schengen's resilience during recent crises, especially since 2015 (refugee crisis, COVID‐19, Russian invasion of Ukraine). title: Technostress and telemedicine in rural communities: insights from healthcare professionals in the Italian Dolomites
abstract: INTRODUCTION: In Italy, many facilities have started adopting telemedicine services since their regulation in 2020. Rural areas mainly benefit from telemedicine implementation due to their geographic features. We investigated the interests, attitudes, and perceptions of healthcare providers operating in the Italian Dolomites regarding the adoption of telemedicine. Furthermore, we explored the relationship between technostress and the intention to integrate telemedicine services during daily practices. title: An Empirical Investigation of Human Resource Management Practices and Service Excellence in Luxury Hotels
abstract: The luxury hotel sector operates in a fluid and highly competitive environment where providing outstanding guest experiences is crucial for long-term success. In this context, employees are the key drivers of service quality, making effective Human Resource Management (HRM) practices essential for organizational performance. This study investigates the effect of HRM practices on service excellence in luxury hotels by examining critical areas such as talent acquisition, employee training, performance evaluation, compensation, employee engagement, and career development. abstract: Counter-poaching patrols are a primary tool for protecting wildlife in threatened landscapes, yet detection rates of active poaching incursions are typically low and patrol planning frameworks that have been operationalised and performance-assessed remain rare. We describe a structured search framework applied over a decade of counter-poaching operations in the Kenyir Core Area, Malaysia, 1,200 km² of mountainous tropical forest critical to Malayan tiger recovery. title: Grundlagen der zuverlässigkeitsbasierten Bemessung | Teil 1 – Methodik
abstract: Abstrakt Die erste Empfehlung des Arbeitskreises 2.15 der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Geotechnik führt in die Grundprinzipien einer zuverlässigkeitsbasierten Bemessung ein. Der hier vorliegende Teil 1 stellt das bekannte Teilsicherheitskonzept als semi‐probabilistischer Ansatz dem zuverlässigkeitsbasierten und dem risikoinformierten Ansatz vergleichend gegenüber. abstract: This study investigates the influence of cryogenic soaking duration on the crystallographic characteristics and corrosion resistance of ASTM A36 structural steel. Specimens were immersed in liquid nitrogen at −196°C for 0, 12, 36, and 60 hours. To this end, we extend the Ordinary Kriging Active Subspace (OK-AS) method into a sequential version. title: Structural and Electrochemical Characterization of Na2CO3/ γ- Al2O3 Electrodes for Supercapacitor
abstract: The development of electrode materials with suitable structural and surface properties is crucial for improving electrochemical energy storage systems. Gamma alumina (𝛾-Al2O3) has attracted considerable interest in electrochemical research due to its unique structural and surface properties. title: Room‐Temperature CO 2 Sorption of NH 2 ‐Appended UiO‐67(Zr) Metal‐Organic Framework
abstract: Fossil fuel combustion elevates atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) to critical levels, driving climate change and intensifying natural disasters. This reality underscores the urgent need for efficient CO 2 capture technologies. In this regard, UiO‐67(Zr) being a highly porous and thermally stable metal‐organic framework (MOF) could be used as a promising candidate for CO 2 sorption. title: Impact of residential urban view features on preference: The mediating role of emotional well-being
abstract: The impact of views on health is well established, yet the mechanisms linking residential urban view features, well-being, and preference remain underexplored. This systematic, large-scale empirical study investigates (1) how the quantity and composition of a broad set of view features influence preference and emotional well-being, and (2) whether well-being mediates view preference. abstract: Abstract Micro- and nanoplastics are pervasive environmental pollutants known to accumulate in human organs. While the hazards of larger plastic particles are under intense investigation, the toxicological impact of molecular-level plastic oligomers with dimensions around 1 nm is a critical and underexplored area. abstract: The object of the study is the heat exchange processes in isotropic 3D media with foreign thermally active thin inclusions. These media reflect individual structural units of control devices of ground robotic complexes. The study is related to the need for more accurate prediction of the thermal state of digital control devices under significant temperature loads. abstract: Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) is highly vulnerable to climate change despite contributing minimally to global greenhouse gas emissions. Climate-related hazards — including extreme heat, floods, droughts, and hurricanes — exacerbate health risks and disproportionately affect Indigenous peoples, Afro-descendant populations, rural communities, women, older adults, and individuals with chronic conditions. abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigated elementary preservice teachers' (PTs) experiences in planning to elicit students' ideas within ambitious science teaching (AST). The study involved 53 elementary PTs in the context of a science teaching methods course at the elementary education program at a public university in Türkiye. abstract: This paper discusses the challenge of reliable maximum power point tracking (MPPT) in solar photovoltaic (PV) battery electric vehicle (EV) charging systems, which face rapidly changing irradiance and temperature. Unlike standard MPPT studies that focus only on standalone PV systems, this work examines MPPT performance within an integrated PV battery grid EV charging framework. abstract: Abstract Precipitation plays a crucial role in Ethiopia’s rain-fed agriculture, ecosystems, and water resources; yet it exhibits, high spatial and temporal variability. abstract: Abstract Combined cycle power plants are among the most efficient technologies for large scale electricity generation. This study presents a comprehensive energy and exergy analysis of an F-class combined cycle power plant equipped with dual three-pressure heat recovery steam generators, supplementary firing, and an air-cooled condenser. abstract: Alcohol-involved sexual assault remains a persistent issue within the U.S. military despite significant institutional reform. To understand how alcohol-involved sexual assault cases are interpreted within the military justice system, this article draws on 23 qualitative interviews with 11 members of the Judge Advocate General’s Corps. abstract: Industrial transformation and regional economic integration have reshaped the spatial distribution and cross-regional spillover patterns of industrial air pollution. Using a spatial panel model and data from 118 prefecture-level units in the Yangtze River Economic Belt (YEB) during 2011–2020, this study examines the direct and spatial spillover effects of industrial structure adjustment and industrial scale expansion on industrial SO2 emission intensity. title: Forest Composition Controls on Water Security in Nepal's Middle Hills
abstract: ABSTRACT Montane watersheds in the Himalayan region are becoming increasingly vulnerable to hydroclimatic extremes that cause floods, landslides, droughts and seasonal water scarcity. These risks are compounded by ecohydrological transformation resulting from shifts in forest composition, notably the widespread establishment of pine plantations, as well as climate variability and intensified land‐use activities. abstract: This study focuses on the design and simulation of a microcontroller-based control and monitoring system for a shipboard sewage treatment plant aimed at improving operational reliability and automation. The system employs a dual microcontroller configuration using PIC16F84A devices to manage the operation of essential components, including the inlet pump, aerator, discharge pump, and dosing pump under both automatic and manual modes. abstract: Water scarcity and environmental degradation are pressing contemporary issues, and the Himalayan regions are especially at risk. The Trans-Himalayas in particular face severe resource scarcity as water availability is totally dependent on the now dwindling supply of glacial meltwater. Women in the Spiti Valley in the Trans-Himalayan region are particularly exposed to these issues because they spend significant time collecting water and fodder for domestic animals and managing agricultural irrigation. abstract: Wound and device-associated infections remain difficult to eradicate because biofilms limit host immunity and antibiotic efficacy, promoting chronicity and resistance. Here, we present a portable, low-cost dual-syringe spray that deposits a thin, self-assembling antimicrobial film directly on wounds and implant surfaces. title: Rethinking climate resilience: How digital transformation reconfigures tourism governance in Vietnam
abstract: Digital transformation is increasingly promoted as a pathway for strengthening climate resilience in tourism, yet little is known about how it reshapes governance and differentiated adaptive capacity within local communities. Drawing on a longitudinal qualitative case study conducted between 2018 and 2026 in a community-based tourism village in Vietnam, this study examines how digital transformation has reshaped information flows, visitor acquisition, and informal coordination among local tourism actors. title: Towards a green China: energy policy, technological innovation, and green investment as drivers of environmental sustainability
abstract: China’s pursuit of environmental sustainability has become one of the defining policy experiments of the twenty-first century, combining an ambitious dual-carbon pledge with the world’s largest deployment of clean-energy technology and green capital. This review synthesizes recent scholarship to examine how three interlocking levers, energy and climate policy, technological innovation, and green investment, jointly shape China’s transition toward a lower-carbon and more resilient development path. abstract: This study aimed to investigate climate-sensitive temporal patterns associated with premature mortality due to cardiovascular diseases (CVD), ischemic heart disease (IHD), and acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in a large subtropical city in southern Brazil. Daily premature mortality records (ages 30-69) from 2010 to 2019 were analyzed together with meteorological data, including temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure, precipitation, wind, and solar radiation, as well as temporally aggregated climatic indicators. abstract: Accelerating ecological overshoot increases the need for spatially explicit ecological accounting, particularly in urban landscapes. Conventional biocapacity assessments often rely on generalized land-cover data that may overlook fine-scale vegetation structures. abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTC) and platelet-derived RNA are emerging liquid biopsy biomarkers in prostate cancer. While AR-V7 expression in CTC has been associated with resistance to androgen receptor-targeted therapies, their low abundance limits molecular characterization. title: Beyond Star Trek: Latin American science fiction and the ELSI of emerging technologies
abstract: Science fiction has been recognized as a place of anticipatory governance, with audiovisual productions such as Star Trek serving as prominent references in ELSI’s research on genetics, biotechnology, and human enhancement. Latin American science fiction has developed parallel and largely unrecognized imaginaries involving genetics, computing, and biotechnology from structurally distinct social positions rooted in inequality, colonial erasure, and the historically expendable body. title: Quorum sensing research in bioluminescent bacteria: a global scientometric mapping of research trends, knowledge structure and emerging research frontiers
abstract: Abstract Background Quorum sensing (QS) in bioluminescent bacteria underpins bacterial cell-to-cell communication, but the global evolution of this field has not been comprehensively evaluated scientometrically. This study maps QS research in bioluminescent bacteria to assess its developmental trajectory, intellectual structure, collaboration networks, and emerging frontiers. abstract: As built environments confront intensifying climate threats, the human capacity to adapt emerges as a critical determinant of resilience increase and vulnerability reduction. However, these human dimensions remain fragmented across disciplines such as psychology, disaster management, engineering, and socio-ecology, often overshadowed by infrastructural or environmental metrics due to conceptual overlaps and inconsistencies. This approach must consider the interplay of individual attributes (e.g., skills and status), structural factors (e.g., informal networks), and organizational contexts (e.g., knowledge-sharing infrastructure and internal competitiveness) from a dynamic perspective. abstract: Purpose This study reviews green high-speed railway (HSR) development in China from a full-life-cycle perspective, focusing on key environmental practices, challenges and future priorities. abstract: Aquaculture frequently employs hormonal induction to trigger spawning, with gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) analogues recognized as among the most effective agents. title: Changing waters: from waterscape to landscape and back again
abstract: Across Sweden, around 2,400 lake-lowering and drainage projects since the early nineteenth century converted wetlands and lakes into fields, fixing a particular vision of progress into ditches, land deeds, and sediment. This article reviews 82 archival, scientific, and policy sources to ask what was done, why, and when, and to trace how these interventions continue to shape contemporary restoration politics. title: Wet-year precipitation anomalies and geohazard economic losses in China: A province-year sensitivity and climate-exposure assessment
abstract: : Wet years can become economically costly when hydroclimatic anomalies coincide with geohazard-prone terrain and exposed socioeconomic systems. However, national-scale evidence on how interannual precipitation variability is associated with geohazard-related economic damage remains limited. Using a province-year panel for mainland China from 2003 to 2022, this study estimates precipitation-damage sensitivity within an administrative annual framework that links province-level wet-year anomalies to reported economic losses. title: From Photon Capture to Barrier Crossing: The Landscape of Full‐Spectrum Photothermal Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional photocatalysis is constrained by narrow ultraviolet response, weak carrier driving force, and slow kinetics for high‐barrier reactions hindering efficient full‐spectrum solar utilization. Photothermal catalysis integrates photochemical effects from photogenerated carriers with photothermal conversion heat, yielding a ‘1+1>2’ synergy that offers a new route to overcome the energy bottleneck. title: Natural hydrogen in the Middle East and North Africa: Geological prospectivity, global analogues, and a play-based exploration roadmap
abstract: Natural hydrogen, free molecular H 2 generated by water-rock reaction and radioactive decay, has moved from curiosity to exploration target since production began at Bourakébougou, Mali. The Middle East and North Africa (MENA) hosts several settings that generate H 2 elsewhere, yet has attracted little dedicated study. This review assesses the region as eleven plays from a documented literature search, each with a chance of detectable surface expression and of a preserved accumulation, given as screening estimates. title: Optimizing open space capacity under heritage constraints in the ancient city of Suzhou: a multi-scale recursive approach
abstract: Abstract Optimizing open spaces in historic urban areas presents a unique challenge: balancing macro-level planning objectives with the preservation of irreplaceable heritage. This study introduces a multi-scale recursive optimization framework that integrates assessment, prediction, and configuration to address these conflicts. Using the ancient city of Suzhou, China (a UNESCO World Heritage site), as a case study, we applied the framework at city, community, and plot scales. title: El Futuro de la Arquitectura Actual, en la Era de la Inteligencia Artificial (IA)
abstract: La Inteligencia Artificial (IA) generativa se ha convertido en una herramienta que ha revolucionado la industria creativa, incluida la arquitectura, al ofrecer nuevas posibilidades para la generación de arte, diseño y contenido con la menor intervención humana. En este contexto, el presente artículo analiza la integración de la IA generativa en la arquitectura actual con los retos que plantea en torno a la autoría, originalidad, valor artístico, propiedad intelectual y autenticidad. title: Pre‐Calcination‐Governed Spatial Architecture Engineering of MOF‐Derived Magnetic Carbon Nanohybrids for Effective Microwave Absorption
abstract: ABSTRACT Precisely steering the spatial distribution of functional units in MOF‐derived carbon‐based hybrids remains a formidable challenge for microwave absorption. Here we reveal that pre‐calcination can govern the intermediate chemistry and final spatial architectures of an identical ZIF‐8@PBA precursor, yielding two structurally distinct nanohybrids (Fe 3 C−N−C and Fe 3 C−N−CNTs). title: Vegetation greening and soil drying in Central Asia: Evidence for bidirectional vegetation-soil moisture feedback
abstract: In arid Central Asia (CA), variations in soil moisture (SM) strongly influence vegetation dynamics, while vegetation can affect SM through evapotranspiration. Although SM variation and its influence on vegetation dynamics have been widely documented, the bidirectional feedback between vegetation and SM remains inadequately explored. title: Protección de datos personales y garantía del derecho a la privacidad en Ecuador
abstract: La circulación masiva de información personal en entornos digitales desplazó la privacidad desde la protección del espacio íntimo hacia el control de cada persona sobre sus datos, de allí que el estudio se planteó como objetivo central analizar el régimen ecuatoriano de protección de datos personales y su capacidad para garantizar el derecho a la privacidad. abstract: Abstract Purpose: This study examines how the openly shared tabular portion of a publicly archived corpus of bibliotherapy-informed recommendations can be independently re-annotated and reorganized into a provenance-aware and media-sensitive framework for smart library wellbeing services. Methods: The analytical corpus comprises 391 unique resources and 447 source-occurrence records, all traceable to the publicly archived data package of X. Wang et al. (2026b). title: The effects of national security assessments in public procurement on competition, sustainability, innovation, and critical technology procurement
abstract: By strategically leveraging public procurement, governments can harness market competition to drive business innovation and sustainable development. It remains unclear, however, how this premise is affected by heightened security awareness due to increasing geopolitical tensions. Focusing on European Union (EU) member states, we examine how security-oriented practices in public procurement affect tender outcomes. title: Recent Advances in Adsorptive Removal of Dyes from Wastewater: Mechanisms and Performance of Advanced Adsorbents
abstract: The increasing discharge of dye-containing wastewater from textile and related industries has become a major environmental concern because of the toxicity, persistence, and poor biodegradability of many synthetic dyes. This review presents an overview of dye classification, chemistry, environmental impacts, and wastewater treatment technologies, with particular emphasis on adsorption as an effective dye removal method. abstract: This study evaluated the performance of six widely used satellite precipitation products, including GPM-IMERG V06 ER, IMERG V07 FR, CMORPH, PERSIANN-CCS, GSMaP-MVK, and MSWEP against observed sub-daily, and daily timescale rainfall. abstract: The five-fold classification of landscapes in Sangam literature is not merely a poetic tradition; it is an ancient Tamil ecological classification that views land, season, living organisms, occupations, food and water as an interconnected whole. This paper proposes a research framework for identifying and assessing the traditional ecological knowledge embedded in this classification by comparing it with the local knowledge systems of farmers, pastoralists, hill communities and water-dependent livelihood groups in present-day Erode District. title: Effects of continuous cropping on yield, medicinal quality, and rhizosphere soil microecological environment of Atractylodes chinensis in the Horqin Sandy land
abstract: Background Continuous cropping is a major constraint that limits the sustainable cultivation of medicinal plants. However, the effects of continuous cropping on yield, medicinal quality, and the rhizosphere soil microecological environment of Atractylodes chinensis , particularly in the Horqin Sandy Land, remain unclear. abstract: Abstract This paper presents a novel optimization methodology to determine optimal graphene platelet (GPL) distribution patterns and GPL volume fraction (GVF) in axially functionally graded GPL-reinforced (AFG-GPLs) composite curved beams. Existing studies are limited to predefined distribution patterns, restricting GPL-efficient structural design. title: The Role of Digitalization Through Internet Access in Strenghening the Economy in Sumtera Utara
abstract: This study aims to analyze the role of digitalization through internet access in strengthening the economy in North Sumatra Province using panel data for the period 2010–2024 with the Vector Autoregression (VAR) method. The variables used include the Human Development Index (HDI), Investment (INV), Internet Access Users (IAU), Labor Force Participation Rate (LFPR), and Gross Regional Domestic Product (GRDP). abstract: ABSTRACT Metatranscriptome mining has dramatically expanded the known diversity of ribovirians at all taxonomic levels. We explored the class Stelpaviricetes in the phylum Pisuviricota that currently includes three orders and six recognized virus families: order Stellavirales with family Astroviridae infecting vertebrates; Patatavirales with families Potyviridae, the largest known family of plant ribovirians, and Potyliviridae; and Hypofuvirales consisting of three families of viruses associated largely with phytopathogenic fungi. title: Evidence for Hunga-Tonga eruption influence on the anomalously strong Northern-Hemisphere stratospheric polar vortex in 2024/2025
abstract: Abstract. The 2022 Hunga Tonga (HT) eruption injected an unprecedented amount of water vapour (WV) into the stratosphere and mesosphere, emerging as a potential multi-year driver of variability in those layers and associated climate feedbacks. Using satellite and reanalysis datasets, and ensemble simulations with the SOCOLv4 model, with and without the HT forcing, we diagnose the chain of processes linking the eruption to the exceptionally strong Northern Hemisphere stratospheric polar vortex (SPV) observed in winter 2024/2025. title: Mathematical Modeling on the Effect of Flood on Farmland: A Nonlinear Dynamical Systems Approach
abstract: Objectives This paper provides a three-dimensional nonlinear ordinary differential equation (ODE) model to clearly understand the effects of flooding on agricultural farmlands. The model uses three interacting state variables: farmland productivity F(t), soil quality index S(t), and floodwater level W(t). title: Fibrocalcific phenotypes in calcific aortic valve disease: imaging characterization, treatment timing, and efficacy assessment
abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease involves two structural processes, fibrous matrix remodeling and mineral deposition, that contribute unequally between patients, so leaflets of similar hemodynamic severity need not share the same tissue composition. Histologic and multi-omics studies have mapped this heterogeneity across sex, age, and valve morphology, and contrast-enhanced computed tomography angiography (CTA) has brought compositional assessment into living patients and into longitudinal follow-up. title: Virtual Flood Experience Enhances Preparedness Through Emotional and Neural Engagement
abstract: As climate change intensifies flood risks, strengthening individual preparedness is essential for sustainable societies. This study tested whether first-person three-dimensional computer graphics (3DCG) flood videos can complement official flood maps in motivating preparedness. We used these materials as operationalizations of experiential and descriptive information, respectively. In a preregistered web experiment with 1000 participants, those who viewed flood videos showed a small but statistically significant increase in preparedness intentions compared with those who viewed flood maps. title: Cryptic diversity highlights the challenge of Linnean and Wallacean shortfalls and the integral role of taxonomy in biodiversity conservation
abstract: Abstract Reliable and current taxonomic data are essential to conservation planning and prioritization. The use of genetic and genomic tools has revealed significant cryptic diversity across taxa and ecosystems, suggesting we are underestimating threatened biodiversity and using outdated species distributions. Taxonomic expertise is the source of much of the data currently used in the IUCN Red List process, and it is in the best interest of the conservation community to support and grow the science of taxonomy. abstract: This study addresses countering unintentional IT insider activity, understood as actions by operators of automated systems that violate official job regulations as a result of behavioural deviation. This problem is reduced to an optimization problem, for which the authors have previously proposed an analytical model and a hybrid method for solving it. title: Exotic catenulid flatworms (Platyhelminthes, Catenulida) and where to find them in a temperate climate – a field study in a botanic garden
abstract: Abstract Catenulids are free-living flatworms, common in eutrophic freshwaters such as ponds, ditches, or peatbogs, with most of the diversity described from tropical regions to date. Although the majority of the species have been described from warmer climates, most molecular studies have been done on specimens from temperate zones in Europe. We addressed this gap by sampling for exotic species in localities available in a temperate climate. title: Regulating Platinum Utilization and Intrinsic Hydrogen Evolution Activity via Carbon Pore Architecture
abstract: Hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is a key process for sustainable hydrogen production. However, its practical implementation remains limited by the high cost and inefficient utilization of platinum (Pt). title: Gender assignment of human nounsin Bantu languages
abstract: Abstract This paper examines how human nouns are distributed across gender values in Bantu languages. In Bantu studies, one gender value is widely described as the “human” gender, and it is generally expected that human nouns are predominantly assigned to it with some notable exceptions. Drawing on lexical data from 45 Bantu varieties in the RefLex database ( Segerer & Flavier 2025 ), the study assesses how consistently this expectation is met across the family. abstract: El presente estudio tuvo como objetivo describir las percepciones asociadas al uso de inteligencia artificial (IA) generativa en el aprendizaje financiero y analizar los patrones de coincidencia y divergencia reportados al contrastar una resolución propia con otra apoyada en IA. abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible tactile sensors are essential components of intelligent robotics, wearable healthcare systems, and human‐machine interfaces. However, most existing tactile sensors have limited capability to discriminate the direction of tangential forces, restricting multidimensional tactile perception under complex loading conditions. title: Comprehensive use of the geological resources of the Cañadón Asfalto Basin by ancient hunter-gatherers of the middle Chubut River valley (Argentine Patagonia).
abstract: This paper presents the results of an integrated study encompassing archaeological and geological fieldwork, laboratory analysis of materials, and surveys of museums and private collections. These findings demonstrate the widespread use of various geological resources from the Cañadón Asfalto Basin by the indigenous populations that inhabited the current Chubut province in the past. title: Multiscale modeling and industrial validation of the water-gas shift reactor in an ammonia unit using COMSOL multiphysics
abstract: The high temperature water-gas shift (HT-WGS) reaction is a central conversion step in ammonia production since it boosts the hydrogen yield and reduces the carbon monoxide content in the synthesis gas mixture before subsequent purification and ammonia synthesis. The industrial reactor was analyzed numerically with COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2. title: The bias of the biomass - different methods to determine spider biomass in ecological samples
abstract: Biomass is an important functional trait in ecology, because body size and the related mass influence biological parameters such as activity, energy demand, metabolic rates, and consequently population and food-web dynamics. In recent arthropod monitoring projects, however, biomass of samples is often used as a surrogate for abundance to detect population trends across larger spatial and temporal scales. In such monitoring programs, arthropods are typically trapped in a preservative, preventing direct measurement of fresh mass. As a result, biomass is commonly estimated using “drained weight”.

title: Recognition-to-signal mechanisms in MXene quantum dots for metal-ion sensing
abstract: MXene quantum dots (MQDs) provide a chemically versatile platform for metal-ion sensing because their surface coordination environments, defect-associated states, and size-dependent electronic structure can couple molecular recognition to measurable optical responses. This review develops a mechanism-centered framework for understanding that coupling rather than treating sensing performance as a collection of isolated analytical metrics. title: Sustainable laser-assisted processes for semiconductor manufacturing: a comprehensive review
abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing is essential for modern electronics, yet conventional fabrication relies heavily on high energy consumption and chemically intensive processes. As sustainability becomes imperative, alternative technologies that lower energy use and carbon footprints are urgently needed. This paper reviews the role of sustainable laser-based processes as potential green solutions for semiconductor manufacturing. abstract: The early period of life is crucial for the development of species-specific traits and, as such, for a correct understanding of the evolutionary constraints and adults’ adaptations. However, this critical aspect of life history is usually inaccessible for extinct mammals. One of the exceptions is the cave bear ( Ursus spelaeus ), whose hibernacula have yielded a sufficient number of cub remains at various ontogenetic stages. abstract: Crystalline covalent organic framework (COF) materials have demonstrated remarkable potentials in the field of adsorption, in particular adsorption of radioactive substances with extremely environmental hazards, owing to their high specific surface area, few structural defects, and excellent stability. abstract: Cooperative localization in dynamic irregular networks estimates node positions from incomplete, noisy, and time-varying short-range measurements. This paper presents a distributed clustering and alignment method that decomposes global stress minimization into cluster formation, relative localization within clusters, and coordinate registration between clusters. title: Deep reinforcement learning control scheme for frequency control of microgrids
abstract: The growing integration of renewable energy sources into microgrids poses substantial challenges to traditional load-frequency control, primarily due to the intermittent nature of generation and continuously changing operating conditions. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an adaptive control strategy based on reinforcement learning, in which a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) agent is used to automatically tune a cascaded PIDF controller for frequency regulation. abstract: Cu/Ti composites combine the complementary mechanical and electrical characteristics of Ti and Cu, but interfacial reactions during thermomechanical processing complicate control of their overall response. abstract: ABSTRACT The sluggish kinetics of oxygen electro‐catalysis, encompassing both oxygen evolution (OER) and reduction (ORR) reactions constitute a major bottleneck for energy conversion and storage devices like water electrolyzers and rechargeable metal‐air batteries. The spin state transitions from singlet ground‐state OH − /H 2 O reactants to triplet ground‐state O 2 products in OER (and vice versa in ORR) play a critical role in catalytic performance. title: Riparian Land-Use Change and Selected Water Quality Parameters in the Upper Brantas River: A 10-Year Buffer Zone Analysis
abstract: Land-use changes and human activities continue to pressure the upper Brantas River. This study investigated land-use change within a 200 m river buffer from 2014 to 2024 and checked its patterns to water quality along the Upper Brantas River. Selected indicators for domestic wastewater, organic pollution, and nutrient input were chosen. title: A multi-scale terrain mapping method using hillshade abstraction
abstract: Terrain generalization aims to selectively simplify terrain details across scales while preserving the overall terrain form and key geomorphic features. An effective representation of terrain structure provides an important basis for preserving terrain structure during generalization. abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved impressive performance in natural language generation but remain vulnerable to hallucinations, particularly in Chinese short-text tasks where evidence grounding is essential. abstract: Tamarix hispida Willd. (Tamarisk; locally known as “zhyngyl” in Kazakh) is a halophyte traditionally used for dysentery, rheumatism, and ulcers, with reported antioxidant and prolyl endopeptidase-inhibitory activities. abstract: Abstract This study presents an integrated approach, coupling rockfall risk assessment with a vehicle-based surveying for the large-scale management of slope assets along transportation corridors. Rockfall risk was assessed qualitatively using relative rating scales. title: Quantifying the contribution of climate change and human activities to NPP in a typical karst area
abstract: Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is an important indicator of ecological sustainability. The karst ecosystem is extremely delicate, featuring limited environmental capacity, severe erosion, and poor self-recovery capabilities. Quantifying the relative contributions of climate change and human activities to NPP in karst areas remains challenging. This study chose a typical karst area, Wiling Mountain in Guizhou Province, China, as the study area. title: Climate-sensitive, spatially explicit multi-objective thinning for stand-structure and living-biomass-carbon trade-offs
abstract: Thinning can improve stand spatial structure but removes living biomass carbon, creating a trade-off that may vary among stand types and future climate pathways. We developed a spatially explicit, climate-sensitive multi-objective computational framework that integrates an individual-tree growth model, five neighborhood-based spatial metrics, species-specific biomass equations, and Monte Carlo optimization. abstract: Eco-anxiety has increasingly drawn public health attention. Although often conceptualized as an individual psychological burden, eco-anxiety may also serve as a catalyst for collective action. However, prevailing coping strategies largely center on individual resilience, with insufficient focus on social connectedness and the human-nature bond. abstract: Structural columns often require strengthening due to deterioration, increased load requirements, or structural modifications, and their complete replacement prior to the end of their design life is economically impractical. Rehabilitation of Reinforced Concrete (RC) columns using modern materials, such as Externally Bonded (EB) Fiber-Reinforced Polymer (FRP) composites, is widely used. abstract: El receptor de andrógenos (RA) es un factor de transcripción nuclear perteneciente a la familia de receptores nucleares esteroideos y constituye una de las principales dianas terapéuticas en el cáncer de próstata resistente a la castración (CPRC). abstract: La preparación para las pruebas estandarizadas muestra que existen desigualdades entre los estudiantes rurales y urbanos en Colombia. Objetivo: analizar la evidencia de acceso abierto sobre el impacto de la inteligencia artificial generativa en la preparación para las pruebas estandarizadas en la educación secundaria, con el fin de sentar las bases para una propuesta conceptual aplicable a contextos rurales. title: Optimal Placement of PV-Based Distributed Generation and EV Charging Infrastructure in IEEE 33-Bus Distribution Networks Using Superb Fairy-Wren Optimization
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) and Renewable Energy Systems (RESs) are increasingly growing in popularity, and this requires the application of advanced planning methods for ensuring their optimal integration into modern power distribution networks. This paper outlines a high-level optimization technique for optimal EV charging infrastructure placement and PV-based Distributed Generation (DG) in IEEE 33-bus Radial Distribution Systems (RDS). abstract: Calcium phosphate biomineralization plays a crucial role in the formation of geological deposits, biological materials, and environmental remediation. While microorganisms are known to influence calcium phosphate precipitation, the relative contributions of bacterial cell surfaces and extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) remain poorly defined. title: Digital Transformation of Work-Integrated Learning in Vocational Education: Microcredential Technology, Collaboration, and Industry Engagement
abstract: Work-Integrated Learning (WIL) is a strategic approach bridging vocational education and industry requirements. This study investigates digitalized WIL implementation in Indonesian vocational schools, focusing on microcredential technology utilization, interdisciplinary collaboration, and industry engagement. A descriptive survey was conducted with 146 respondents from West Java vocational schools, predominantly mechanical engineering programs. title: Estatuto ontológico de los grandes modelos de lenguaje (LLM) desde el realismo moderado de Aristóteles y santo Tomás de Aquino
abstract: La expansión de los grandes modelos de lenguaje (LLM) favorece atribuciones cognitivas que requieren una clarificación ontológica. Esta investigación aborda dicha cuestión desde el paradigma del realismo moderado de Aristóteles y santo Tomás de Aquino. title: Aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial para el aprendizaje personalizado del cálculo: una revisión bibliográfica
abstract: La enseñanza del cálculo diferencial e integral presenta desafíos asociados con la abstracción, la diversidad de conocimientos previos y la dificultad de proporcionar retroalimentación individual en grupos numerosos. abstract: Adverse conditions and work at height affect the safety and efficiency of radio frequency (RF) scanning at telecommunication towers. This study compared the Human-Based (BM) and Drone-Based (BD) methods based on operation time, number of RF readings, and Received Signal Level (RSL). Comparisons were conducted at 10 telecommunication tower sites across the 13 GHz and 18 GHz bands using standardised instruments and parameters. abstract: Abstract This paper explores how pre‐service teachers (PSTs) conceptualise adaptive teaching in relation to differentiation within the contemporary policy landscape in England. Drawing on qualitative focus group data and informed by Bourdieu's theory of practice, the study examines how pedagogical understandings are shaped by social justice concerns, institutional constraints and emerging professional identities. title: Pre‐ and Post‐Conflict Land Use Detection Matrix and Ecosystem Service Value Analysis in Hirmi State Forest, Northwestern Ethiopia
abstract: ABSTRACT Land use and land cover changes (LULC) are driven by anthropogenic activities and, in turn, affect the availability of products and ecosystem services for people and other living organisms. Hence, the aim of this study was to determine the Pre‐ and Post‐Conflict Land Use Detection Matrix and Ecosystem Service Value (ESV) analysis in Hirmi State Forest, Northwestern Ethiopia. abstract: This paper proposes an advanced control strategy for a grid-connected Brushless Doubly-Fed Induction Generator (BDFIG) wind energy system operating under variable wind and grid conditions. The method employs a Fractional-Order Proportional–Integral (FOPI) controller optimally tuned via a novel Cloud Drift Optimization (CDO) algorithm and applied across key control loops, including active/reactive power, DC-link voltage, and grid-side inverter control. title: Microwave-Assisted Extraction of Bioactive Microbial Compounds: Principles and Applications
abstract: Microorganisms are rich sources of high-value bioactive compounds, including lipids, pigments, carbohydrates, and enzymes, with applications across the food, pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and bioenergy industries. The growing interest in sustainable and efficient bioproduct recovery has driven the development of innovative extraction technologies. In this sense, Microwave-Assisted Extraction (MAE) has emerged due to its energy efficiency, rapidity, and reduced environmental footprint. title: Adaptive Energy‐Aware Routing for Wireless Sensor Networks Using Fuzzy Logic‐Driven Greylag Goose Optimization
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) commonly form part of smart monitoring and data collection systems, in which energy‐efficient communication is still a challenging issue caused by the insufficient battery capacity of sensor nodes. A hybrid fuzzy logic‐based clustering and Gray Wolf Optimization (GWO) based routing, ECFGWO, called ECFGGO, is proposed in this paper for sustainable and adaptive data transmission in WSNs. abstract: ABSTRACT Earth‐rock mixed accumulation bodies formed during land development and construction projects are highly susceptible to water erosion and may trigger secondary hazards. abstract: El creciente papel de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en actividades públicas, administrativas y judiciales representa un desafío constitucional que solo puede abordarse a nivel técnico y ético. abstract: La inteligencia artificial generativa permite resolver muchas tareas escolares sin que el estudiante posea la habilidad evaluada, lo que compromete la validez de la evaluación. abstract: Although millions of plant growth–promoting bacteria (PGPBs) are currently used in agriculture and soil health restoration, their potential environmental threats have largely been ignored. Here, rhizosphere soils from Chilean temperate rainforests (CTR) were collected and studied as an attractive, novel source of potentially safer PGPBs. abstract: Nature-based Solutions (NBS) have the potential to provide solutions to a range of societal challenges, such as climate adaptation, and simultaneously contribute toward biodiversity goals. NBS are increasingly implemented in urban sustainability practice, especially in residential districts and business sites. abstract: Introduction Slum and informal-settlement prevalence varies widely across Africa, yet less is known about how countries have followed different paths over time. This study examines long-term patterns across African countries from 2000 to 2022. abstract: Rapid urbanization in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) has expanded informal settlements where residents face extreme heat, yet informal settlement thermal dynamics remain understudied. Nowhere is this more evident than in Nairobi, one of SSA’s most rapidly growing metropolises, which faces critical challenges from unregulated informal settlement expansion, characterized by high population density and threats to urban sustainability and resident well-being. abstract: Abstract STEM-focused and social science skill sets will be required to successfully address many current global problems. Although providing active learning, communication, and technological skills—often lacking in current curricular approaches—is essential for STEM student success, they alone are insufficient to recruit, prepare, and retain students for rapidly evolving STEM careers. abstract: ABSTRACT High‐performance single‐photon light detection and ranging (LiDAR) technology with robust noise resistance provides a powerful means for environmental perception in extreme scenarios. abstract: La enseñanza del algoritmo de la división escrita constituye uno de los núcleos más complejos en la aritmética escolar de la educación básica. abstract: Abstract Digital twins (DT) have been applied across different product life cycle stages, such as design and operation, and have been crucial in advancing various application domains, including Industry 4.0. abstract: Growing concern over the environmental toxicity and biomedical risks of conventional physical and chemical nanoparticle synthesis has intensified interest in sustainable routes to metal nanoparticle production. abstract: The two-spotted spider mite, Tetranychus urticae , is a major constraint in strawberry production, and its management still relies heavily on acaricides. abstract: ABSTRACT Adhesively bonded aluminium joints are widely used in lightweight structures, but their durability is often limited by interfacial crack growth, fatigue damage, moisture ingress, and limited recovery of fracture resistance after damage. abstract: Addressing urban air pollution requires identifying, quantifying, and mitigating emission sources, yet bottom-up inventories often lack fine spatiotemporal precision and rarely capture unpermitted or informally operated sources. abstract: With the boom of e-commerce and increasing policy support, regional logistics serving medium- and short-distance transportation have grown rapidly. Large fuel-powered drones are increasingly adopted in this field due to their flexibility and efficiency, yet their deployment has raised concerns regarding pollutant emissions and environmental sustainability. abstract: Abstract Record-breaking heat extremes are becoming more likely due to anthropogenic climate change, with their probability depending on the regional warming rate. abstract: Climate risk assessments used by the financial sector are often based on empirical data from recent decades that do not span the full range of possible futures. We argue that the financial sector needs to embrace risk analysis for all plausible scenarios, not just for median outcomes.

The results from numerical simulation of heat and mass transfer processes are reported, aimed at solving the task of determining the melting regimes of ingot slabs in a continuous crystallizer. title: Control on paleokarst reservoir heterogeneity: integrating surface-subsurface water systems and paleogeomorphology in the Lungu area, Tarim Basin

abstract: ABSTRACT This study aims to explore how hybrid work models can be integrated into production management processes and how such integration can enhance organisational resilience in the context of emergency management. abstract: The term “Anthropocene” captures humanity’s profound impact on Earth’s geology and ecosystems, and it has become central to understanding the relationship between human societies and the Earth system. title: Analysis of Yield Constraints and Challenges for Sustainable Production of Dry Direct-seeded Rice in Cool Climates
abstract: Dry direct-seeded rice (DDSR) cultivation can eliminate the cost of rice seedling management and transplanting. Its popularity is increasing in Japan; in particular, its area in northeastern Japan increased 4.8× from 2001 to 2021, versus 3.4× nationwide. On the other hand, the yield of DDSR in northeastern Japan tends to be about 10% lower than that of transplanted rice. abstract: Abstract The durability and performance of bituminous pavements in Bangladesh are increasingly challenged by heavy traffic loading and climate-induced distresses. abstract: Qingyuan City, Guangdong, possesses abundant geothermal resources; however, systematic investigations into the hydrogeochemical characteristics and genesis of these thermal fluids remain scarce, hindering their scientific development and efficient utilization. abstract: Many positive impacts of green roofs, such as water retention and thermal insulation of buildings, are well documented. However, systematic assessments of their potential to support insect biodiversity in comparison to other habitat types remain scarce. To investigate the value of green roofs as habitats for insects, we sampled insects with Malaise traps on five green roofs in Austria from May to September in 2023 and 2024. title: THE PARADIGMATICS OF TOPONYMS IN FAIRY-TALE TEXTS
abstract: This article examines the paradigmatic features of toponyms used in fairy-tale texts and explores their role in the semantic and structural organization of fictional narratives. Toponyms in fairy tales are not merely geographical markers; they can also convey cultural, historical, symbolic, and emotional meanings. abstract: La inteligencia artificial generativa (IAg) plantea desafíos para la evaluación de ensayos asíncronos, especialmente cuando su uso no puede verificarse a partir del producto final. abstract: BACKGROUND: Range expansion is often accompanied by reduced genetic diversity and increased environmental stress in populations at range edges, potentially constraining adaptive evolution despite strong selection. title: When a feature becomes a bug: evolutionary mismatch in human–robot interaction
abstract: As robots become increasingly integrated into everyday life, evolved psychological mechanisms originally adapted for human social interaction may shape responses to artificial agents in ways that are no longer functionally appropriate. Drawing on an evolutionary psychology framework, the present study examined how anthropomorphism, empathy, and systemizing influence decisions involving a humanoid home robot. Participants ( N = 519) completed an online experiment in which they viewed one of six robot stimuli varying in appearance (human-like, ambiguous, or robotic) and gender (female or male).

abstract: Disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBI) are common worldwide, and their frequency has risen alongside the dietary shift that has stripped fermentable fibre out of everyday diets. Carob ( Ceratonia siliqua L. ) is a Mediterranean agro-industrial by-product that has mostly been put to low-value uses, although its composition is unusually varied for a fibre source. abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly recognized as emerging environmental pollutants that can disrupt soil biogeochemical cycles and threaten agricultural sustainability. abstract: Objectives Wastewater-based bio-surveillance is essential for monitoring pathogens in communities. abstract: Due to the lack of accurate theoretical deformation models, real-time shape perception and closed-loop shape control of soft snake-like robots severely restrict their deployment in unstructured scenarios including narrow-space inspection, minimally invasive medical operation and post-disaster debris reconnaissance. title: An overview of plant conservation from the perspective of the social sciences and humanities
abstract: Plant populations are embedded in complex social, cultural, and political contexts, yet plant conservation has traditionally been framed as a predominantly ecological and technical challenge. This study examines how plant conservation has been addressed within the social sciences and humanities over the past three decades, analyzing 119 Scopus-indexed publications through a bibliometric co-occurrence analysis of authors’ keywords using VOSviewer. abstract: Plan evaluation supports the development of higher quality plans. We examined whether language models could assist evaluation of wetland conservation in local comprehensive plans through prompt optimization. abstract: Introduction Pumpkin (Cucurbita maxima) pulp is a promising source of natural pigments with potential applications as food colorants. abstract: This study examines the opportunities and challenges facing Turkish hotel equipment exporters in the Saudi Arabian market through the lens of the cultural economy and Institutional Theory. abstract: Mitragyna speciosa, a medicinal plant native to Southeast Asia, has long been used in traditional medicine and is ethnopharmacologically associated with maintaining physical stamina. title: Bridging the Attitude-Behaviour Gap in Biobased Product Consumption: A Comprehensive Behavioural Decision Model
abstract: Market acceptance of biobased products is essential for advancing a sustainable bioeconomy, yet consumer decision-making remains complex and insufficiently understood. This study introduces and validates the Comprehensive Behavioural Decision Model for Biobased Products (CBDM-BBP), designed to bridge the gap between consumer attitudes and actual use behaviour. abstract: As science communication increasingly occurs across borders, students should learn to engage experts and audiences through dialogue rather than dissemination alone. This study examined the design, implementation, and outcomes of an international agricultural and natural resources (ANR) communication course in which United States (U.S.)-based undergraduate and graduate students produced a podcast series featuring Canadian ANR experts. abstract: Strategic decision-making and innovation are critical to the competitiveness of emerging organisations operating in volatile, uncertain, complex and ambiguous (VUCA) environments. This paper examines how emerging organisations can make adaptive strategic decisions while pursuing innovation under conditions of environmental uncertainty. abstract: Rainfall is central to slope-hazard assessment and early warning, yet the meteorological state at release may not represent the pre-failure history of a rock slope. abstract: Rapid urbanization and land use/land cover (LULC) changes have significantly altered land surface temperature (LST) patterns and intensified urban heat island (UHI) effects, particularly in rapidly developing regions of sub-Saharan Africa. abstract: Las lesiones óseas de muñeca, en particular las fracturas de radio distal y las artralgias asociadas a trauma, generan alta demanda asistencial y requieren decisiones terapéuticas oportunas. abstract: This article investigates the brain’s resilience to trauma and adverse experiences, exploring how literature acts as a vital ally in fostering recovery and renewal. Trauma hyperactivates the amygdala, impairs hippocampal function, and fragments memory, hyper activating fear responses and fragmenting memory, yet the brain’s plasticity offers a path to adaptation. title: Optimization of Boiler Feed Pump Maintenance Planning using Reliability-Centered Maintenance: A Case Study at a Thermal Power Plant in Banten
abstract: The Boiler Feed Pump (BFP) is essential to power generation systems because it supplies high-pressure water to the boiler. BFP failures can cause operational disruptions, efficiency losses, unplanned downtime and substantial financial impacts. This study aims to optimize the maintenance plan for BFP Unit 4B using Reliability-Centered Maintenance (RCM). abstract: Abstract In magnetically confined nuclear fusion, the achievement of ignition necessitates the tokamak plasma in a high confinement state known as H-mode. abstract: Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of mortality among women worldwide, highlighting the urgent need for the development of more effective therapeutic agents with fewer adverse effects. This study aimed to analyze the potential of indole–tetrazole hybrid derivatives as anti-breast cancer agents by comparing their performance with the reference compound Bazedoxifen. abstract: The functional genes gcd , phoD , and phoR , which mediate inorganic phosphorus (P) solubilization, organic P mineralization, and P—starvation gene expression, respectively, serve as key proxies for microbial involvement in soil P cycling. abstract: The Mekong River Basin (MRB) supports the world's most productive inland fishery, but is becoming increasingly fragmented by river infrastructure, with more than 13,000 barriers already present and further expansion expected. abstract: Carbonate rock weathering and soil formation form a key link in the global carbon cycle; however, the response mechanism to climate and human activities remains unclear. The problem that was solved in the study is the gaps in static approaches to determining hidden shifts in financial states. title: Designing cognition-driven Human-AI teaming: A Three-Layer Cognitive Framework (TriC)
abstract: As AI shifts from a tool to a teammate, achieving effective human–AI collaboration becomes a central challenge. Human-AI teaming (HAT) promises to combine the strengths of humans and AI through close cooperation. However, recent studies reveal that mixed human–AI teams do not consistently outperform all-human or all-AI teams. The performance gap arises when AI does not align well with human cognitive processes. abstract: Background: Household food-security programs may address information deficits, ecological practices, and small-enterprise development separately, obscuring the connections between community needs and available assets. Objective: This article examines the implementation logic and documented outputs of SMART FAMILY in Dunggala Village, Indonesia, and identifies the evidence required to test its anticipated benefits. abstract: This study presents the first detailed description of bioerosion traces produced by insects in bones from the Santa Cruz Sequence (early Carnian, Santa Maria Supersequence, Brazil). abstract: Abstract This article presents a state-of-the-art review of Brazilian and international studies addressing educational strategies and practices related to karst. The study adopts a qualitative, descriptive, and exploratory approach, examining book chapters, journal articles, theses, dissertations, conference proceedings, and documents retrieved from Google Scholar, Scopus, and ERIC databases. title: Temperature-driven dormancy loss shapes subsequent germination thermal requirements in Centaurium somedanum
abstract: Abstract Seed dormancy is a key mechanism regulating germination timing by determining how seeds respond to environmental cues. However, the extent to which temperatures experienced during dormancy loss alter subsequent germination thermal requirements remains poorly understood. We investigated this process in Centaurium somedanum , a narrow endemic of calcareous mountain springs in northern Spain, with non-deep simple morphophysiological dormancy. abstract: Nasal colonization by Staphylococcus aureus among healthcare professionals represents a potential risk for the spread of resistant strains in hospital settings. Thus, this cross-sectional study aimed to determine the prevalence of nasal colonization by S. aureus and to characterize the antimicrobial resistance profile of the isolated strains from professionals working in a public hospital in Caxias, Maranhão, Brazil. abstract: Introduction Whole-region comprehensive land consolidation (WRCLC), as a spatial governance approach integrating “all elements, all regions, the whole process, and the entire chain,” is of great significance for optimizing regional production–living–ecological space (PLES) functions. title: Language Transformation and Subjectivity: A Lacanian Psychological Literary Criticism of Daniel Keyes’ Flowers for Algernon
abstract: This study examines subjectivity construction, stabilization, and disintegration in Daniel Keyes’ Flowers for Algernon, highlighting language as the main narrative mechanism for producing subjectivity. Using narratological, stylistic, and Lacanian psychoanalytic frameworks, the analysis views subjectivity not as a stable psychological essence but as a fragile, language-dependent formation via narrative discourse. abstract: BACKGROUND: Cervical dystonia (CD) is considered a basal ganglia-thalamo-cortical and brainstem network disorder rather than an isolated focal motor disease. OBJECTIVES: Our aim was to analyze sleep architecture, REM physiology, respiratory patterns, and sensorimotor activity in CD using full-night PSG. title: EMPOWERING VILLAGE-OWNED ENTERPRISES FOR SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN INDONESIA: A MODEL OF ACCOUNTABILITY
abstract: Village-owned enterprises play a critical role in sustainable village development, but often face challenges in financial, social, and environmental accountability, leading to operational inefficiencies and closure. This research aims to develop a holistic accountability model that integrates these aspects to improve governance and performance. The study uses a thematic qualitative approach and examines factors such as management capacity, community participation, and political support. title: Reconfiguring Islamic Legal Authority in Yala, Southern Thailand: Institutional Resilience and the Governance of Muslim Family Law
abstract: This article examines how Islamic legal authority persists and adapts within a state-centred legal order in Yala, Southern Thailand. Questioning the assumption that incorporating religious law into state institutions necessarily displaces non-state legal authority, it explores how Islamic family law is sustained through interactions between state courts, Islamic Councils, religious authorities, and Muslim communities. title: Spatial spillovers and causal configurations of the digital economy driving green manufacturing transformation in China
abstract: The digital economy has emerged as a critical engine for high-quality economic development, yet its specific mechanisms and configurational pathways in empowering green manufacturing transformation remain under-explored. Based on panel data from 31 provinces in China (2012–2023), this study constructs a dual-methodological framework integrating the Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) and fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) to investigate the spatiotemporal evolution, transmission mechanisms, and causal recipes of this relationship. abstract: Amphistomatous plants distribute stomata between the adaxial and abaxial leaf surfaces, but whether this dual-surface allocation follows a predictable scaling relationship, and why species deviate from it, remains poorly understood. Here, we compiled a global dataset of adaxial and abaxial stomatal densities for 559 species across 380 sites and 63 families. abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction (NO 3 RR) to ammonia (NH 3 ) offers a sustainable route for coupling nitrate (NO 3 − ) remediation with NH 3 synthesis. title: Phage N4 uses a SAR endolysin-holin system for host cell lysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Bacteriophages (phages) cause active host cell lysis to terminate their infection and release progeny into the environment. However, some phages have systems to delay their lysis, and thereby increase progeny yield, in specific conditions: a phenomenon called lysis inhibition (LIN). Two dissimilar phages of Escherichia coli are known to exhibit LIN: T4 and N4. abstract: ABSTRACT Foodborne disease remains a major global health and economic burden, with recent World Health Organization estimates attributing roughly 866 million illnesses and 1.52 million deaths annually to 42 major foodborne hazards. title: Spatial assessment of soil fertility in high-Andean potato systems using a multivariate index in the Pasco region, Peru
abstract: Potato cultivation in the central Andes of Peru occurs under highly heterogeneous environmental conditions, where soil fertility is influenced by interactions among lithology, geomorphology, climate, and vegetation. This study evaluated the spatial variability of soil fertility in high-Andean potato systems across three river basins of the Pasco region, Peru, through the development of a multivariate Soil Fertility Index (SFI). abstract: Introduction Water scarcity is increasingly constraining global sustainable development, making it a critical policy challenge to improve economic performance while strengthening resource conservation. Methods Using the 2018 expansion of China’s Water Resource Tax Pilot Policy (WRTP) as a quasi-natural experiment, this study applies a difference-in-differences approach to firm-level and county-level data from 2012 to 2022. abstract: Introduction Understanding the psychological determinants of pro-environmental behavior is critical in addressing the escalating climate crisis. This gap is particularly evident in non-Western contexts such as India. abstract: Lead (Pb (II)) is a persistent contaminant in industrial wastewater. This study evaluated pine bark (PB)-derived biochars produced at different pyrolysis temperatures for Pb (II) removal. Biochar produced at 500°C (PB5) achieved the highest removal efficiency and was selected for subsequent experiments. abstract: Understanding the sequence determinants of antibody affinity within a clonal family is a central challenge in therapeutic antibody discovery. Here, we applied amino acid frequency analysis to a large phylogenetic clonal tree of anti-ST2 monoclonal antibodies, where V(D)J recombination is constant and only somatic hypermutations vary. abstract: A new species of the agamid genus Diploderma Hallowell, 1861 is described from Gula Township, Zayü County, Xizang Autonomous Region (Tibet), China, based on integrated morphological and molecular evidence. abstract: In shipping agency and general supplier services, customers evaluate providers through operational dependability, pricing practices, and confidence in business commitments. This study examined the associations of service quality and price with customer-perceived firm performance and considered customer trust as a potential intermediary at PT Anugrah Karunia Mahakam.
