abstract: Abstract Decarbonization policies aim to electrify the transportation sector by increasing the use of Electric Vehicles (EVs); consequently, Electric Vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) are widely integrated into distribution systems (DSs). EVCSs can be considered a significant additional electrical load on DSs, leading to negative effects such as increased system power losses and reduced voltage profile and voltage stability. title: Spatializing the Circular Economy: Firm-Level Evidence and Socio-Demographic Factors within a National Post-Consumer Sneaker Network
abstract: Post-consumer footwear constitutes a highly heterogeneous and minimally circular segment of the consumer goods economy. Although the sector has a substantial environmental footprint, empirical research on post-consumer footwear collection and reverse logistics remains limited. This study contributes to circular economy scholarship by showing that post-consumer sneaker collection depends largely on intermediary capacity, territorial coordination, and robust reverse-logistics infrastructure. abstract: El artículo aborda los itinerarios didácticos inteligentes como una estrategia para la formación de profesores, específicamente de biología, bajo el enfoque de Educación para el Cambio Climático (ECC). abstract: Heritage buildings adapted for contemporary library use often face difficulties in providing adequate and uniform lighting while preserving their architectural character. This study evaluates the lighting quality of Montgomery Hall, a historic Neo-Classical reading space within the Quaid-e-Azam Library, Lahore, with particular emphasis on illuminance, visual comfort, and compliance with recommended lighting requirements. abstract: Dyadic neurofeedback offers a socially grounded approach for modulating neural processes that unfold between interacting individuals. While recent work demonstrates that dyadic neurofeedback can enhance inter-brain synchrony during interaction, whether its effects extend beyond the trained dyad remains unclear. Here, we examined whether dyadic neurofeedback targeting inter-brain synchrony in the inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) is associated with changes in empathy-for-pain toward unfamiliar social targets. title: High-Temperature Corrosion in Biomass-Fired Systems: Mechanisms, Mitigation, Strategies, and Challenges for the Brazilian Bioenergy Sector
abstract: Abstract Biomass combustion is critical to Brazil’s energy transition, but high-temperature corrosion remains a major operational barrier in industrial boilers. Following a systematic search of Scopus (2000–2026; 977 records screened, 159 included), this review synthesizes the physicochemical mechanisms driving ash deposition and high-temperature corrosion in biomass-fired systems, identifying chlorine-induced active oxidation and alkali-driven hot corrosion as the dominant degradation pathways, and detailing the synergistic, self-reinforcing interaction between the two. title: Promoting International Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) Education by Creativity
abstract: The rising intricacy of international challenges has amplified the necessity for STEM education which goes yonder rote-leaning science and technology procedures. Creativity offers a vital pathway for aiding learners apply knowledge, reconnoitre possibilities, and advance innovative solutions to real-world issues. In this paper, the role of creativity in strengthening Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) education globally was examined with focus on developing contexts like Nigeria. title: Fault Interaction Analysis in Manufacturing Process With Extended FMEA Model by Using Cloud Model Theory and DEMATEL: A Novel Approach for Risk Assessment
abstract: ABSTRACT Failure mode and effect analysis (FMEA) is widely used in numerous manufacturing processes to identify and minimize various problems; nevertheless, its usefulness is dubious until it is more directly associated with the resolution of complex issues. In addition, the disruptions experienced in the production process are interrelated and cannot be considered independent of each other. title: Tropospheric Ozone Assessment Report II: South America regional analysis
abstract: This study presents the first regional assessment of tropospheric ozone over South America for the early twenty-first century. We use observations from 14 combined satellite records, two atmospheric reanalyses, and model simulations to examine the spatial distribution, source contributions and trends in ozone and its precursors. Satellites and reanalysis data reveal enhanced tropospheric column ozone over the mid-latitudes of the west coast and the subtropical east coast, with 2005-2021 median values (±2σ) ranging from 46 [±11] to 49 [±9] nmol mol-1. title: Capital epistémico y visibilidad de los investigadores de educación superior: una revisión sistemática 2022 – 2026
abstract: El capital epistémico se ha convertido en una categoría relevante para comprender cómo los investigadores de educación superior adquieren legitimidad, autoridad y visibilidad dentro de ecosistemas académicos cada vez más mediados por métricas, plataformas digitales, redes de colaboración e infraestructuras institucionales. El objetivo general fue sintetizar las principales categorías del capital epistémico asociadas con la visibilidad de los investigadores de educación superior, y el objetivo específico fue sintetizar sus principales definiciones en la literatura científica. title: Invariant image reparameterisation: Bridging symbolic and numerical methods for identifiability analysis, model reduction, and prediction
abstract: Structural and practical parameter non-identifiability issues are common when mathematical models are used to interpret data. Such issues motivate model reparameterisation and reduction methods. Here, we consider Invariant Image Reparameterisation (IIR), which asks when symbolic reparameterisation conditions can be replaced by numerical derivative calculations at a single reference point. title: FROM COLONIAL POLITICAL ECONOMY TO MALAYSIA MADANI: TRACING THE EVOLUTION OF HUMAN-CENTERED DEVELOPMENT THROUGH THE THOUGHT OF UNGKU AZIZ
abstract: The article examines the intellectual framework of Ungku Aziz in the development of Malaysia's story from colonial times to the present day under the leadership of the MADANI administration under Anwar Ibrahim. It claims that Malaysia's economic development is a gradual shift from a growth-oriented political economy to a more human-oriented developmental approach. In the colonial era, economic systems were mainly geared towards external capitalist interests, leading to socio-economic disparities and rural poverty. title: Rapeseed accessions as a climate smart agriculture strategy and food security in arid regions: yield, oil quality, and soil remediation under saline and wastewater irrigation
abstract: Climate change, water scarcity, and soil salinization are major constraints to crop production in the Eastern Mediterranean impacting food security, particularly in marginal lands where conventional irrigation is limited. Climate-smart agriculture approaches that combine stress-tolerant crops with non-conventional water sources may help sustain production while improving soil conditions. title: Host species identity outweighs life form in shaping the root endophytic bacterial communities of 10 Cymbidium species grown under uniform conditions
abstract: Research on orchid microbiomes has long been dominated by mycorrhizal fungi, whereas the community structure of orchid-associated bacteria remains poorly understood, particularly across host life forms. We compared the root endophytic bacterial communities of 10 Cymbidium species (six epiphytic and four terrestrial), all cultivated in the same greenhouse. title: Farm practice typologies as a strategy for management-relevant land use and land cover mapping in the Great Lakes Region
abstract: Abstract The Great Lakes region (GLR) is dominated by agricultural land use, characterized by diverse land use and land cover (LULC), land management practices (LMPs), and, in turn, diverse land processes. Conventional LULC classification systems often rely on coarse categorizations, summarized into spatial units that are either unmeaningful to management or lack the fidelity to capture human-driven heterogeneity relevant to environmental outcomes. title: A PCA-based composite drought index integrating meteorological and vegetation indicators in the North-Eastern Dry Zone of Karnataka, India
abstract: Abstract Drought is a recurring climatic hazard in the North-Eastern Dry Zone (NEDZ) of Karnataka, affecting agriculture and water-resource availability. This study analysed the spatio-temporal variability of drought and wet conditions during 2000–2024 using daily meteorological observations from KSNDMC and IMD and MODIS MOD13Q1 vegetation data. title: MÉTODO MARTZ 5.0: arquitectura multiescalar de inteligencia territorial, aprendizaje y regeneración
abstract: La fragmentación entre diseño arquitectónico, urbanismo, planeación territorial, analítica digital y gobernanza reduce la capacidad de intervenir sistemas urbanos sometidos simultáneamente a cambio climático, desigualdad socioespacial y transformación tecnológica. Este artículo examina el Método MARTZ 5.0 como arquitectura metodológica orientada a convertir información territorial en ciclos de decisión, aprendizaje y regeneración. title: Postponed Nitrogen Enhanced Waterlogged Summer Maize Soil Nutrients by Regulating Microbial Diversity and Network Complexity
abstract: Waterlogging stress and low nitrogen use efficiency are important factors constraining summer maize production in the Huang-Huai-Hai region. However, how postponed nitrogen application modulates soil micro-ecological properties and mitigates yield loss in waterlogged summer maize fields by regulating soil microbial community diversity, co-occurrence networks, and community assembly processes remained rarely explored. title: SPIRITUAL TRANSFORMATION OF THE JAMA'AH TABLIGH IN WEST JAVA THROUGH RITUAL-BASED RELIGIOUS COUNSELING PRACTICES
abstract: Purpose – This study analyzes how ritual-based religious counseling operates within the Jama'ah Tabligh as a da'wah (Islamic propagation) management strategy, read through the Islamic Guidance and Counseling (IGC) approach, and identifies the forms of spiritual transformation that its members experience. Design/methodology/approach – A qualitative phenomenological design was applied. title: Beyond hot and cold: experiential amplification and the “thermal kick” in contemporary bathing
abstract: Introduction Thermal bathing places the body within intense but highly variable human-centric indoor environments. Similar exposures to heat, cold, and contrast may be experienced as restorative, threatening, socially connective, culturally familiar, or simply unpleasant, suggesting that thermal dose alone does not explain lived outcome. This study examined how thermal settings organize embodied experience and developed the concept of the composed thermal episode. abstract: Selecting a study program at a State University (Perguruan Tinggi Negeri/PTN) is a decision that many senior high school students approach without a systematic review of their interest, aptitude, achievement, and career goals, a gap made more pressing by the limited counseling capacity available at most schools. title: Evaluating Sustainable Development Goal 6 Performance in the European Union: A Multi‐Criteria Assessment of Water Use Efficiency and Water Stress
abstract: ABSTRACT This study assesses SDG 6.4 performance across 27 EU member states using six sector‐specific FAOSTAT indicators for 2021–2023. Three‐year means were equally weighted and ranked using VIKOR ( v = 0.75). Missing agricultural water‐use efficiency values for Ireland and Luxembourg were replaced with country‐specific historical means. Luxembourg ranked first ( Q i = 0.147), followed by Sweden (0.405), Slovakia (0.414), the Netherlands (0.458), and Denmark (0.502); Spain ranked last (1.000). title: Trial architecture in contemporary cardio-oncology: Why parallel-group randomized controlled trials may not fit every cardiotoxicity phenotype
abstract: Cardio-oncology has evolved rapidly with immune checkpoint inhibitors, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies, antibody-drug conjugates, bispecific antibodies, and targeted kinase inhibitors, yet cardiovascular prevention strategies remain largely informed by evidence generated during the anthracycline era.This critical narrative review examines why cardioprotection trials have failed to keep pace with these evolving toxicity mechanisms, analyzing trial populations, endpoint selection, biomarker strategies, imaging approaches, and overall trial design across traditional and newer cancer th

title: Addressing conventional and emerging contamination in resource-limited rural water supplies: a full-scale before-after evaluation of a process upgrade and exploratory surrogate analysis of PFAS and antibiotic removal
abstract: Existing research on emerging-contaminant removal has focused on urban water treatment plants or single contaminant classes under laboratory conditions. However, resource-limited mountainous rural water supplies, where conventional pollutants and trace emerging contaminants—per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and antibiotics—co-occur as a composite pollution burden, cannot be adequately managed by the existing infrastructure. title: Clinical outcomes and safety of finerenone in patients with heart failure: a real-world observational study in China
abstract: Abstract Objective Finerenone is a highly selective nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, but data on its benefits in the treatment of heart failure (HF) in real-world clinical practice remain insufficient. This study investigated the benefits and outcomes of finerenone in patients with HF using a single-center, real-world study design. Methods This single-center, retrospective observational study included consecutive patients diagnosed with HF and treated with add-on finerenone between August 2023 and May 2024 at Tongji Hospital, Shanghai, China. title: The Social Dimensions of a Potential GoTo-Grab Merger: A Review of Employment, Driver Welfare, and Regulatory Implications
abstract: The proposed merger between GoTo and Grab represents a major potential consolidation in Southeast Asia’s digital economy, raising concerns about market competition, employment dynamics, and driver welfare. If completed, the merger could give the combined entity more than 90% of Indonesia’s ride-hailing market, highlighting the need to examine the adequacy of existing regulatory safeguards. This study examines the potential implications of the merger for employment, driver welfare, and regulatory effectiveness. title: Hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning for operations and maintenance disruption recovery in high-end equipment manufacturing under compound risks
abstract: Compound disruptions in high-end equipment manufacturing can simultaneously fragment operations and maintenance (O&M) resource networks and constrain critical resource flows. Using natural disasters and trade sanctions as representative compound risks of topology-based network fragmentation and capacity-constrained flow bottlenecks, this study addresses a recovery problem in which network reconfiguration changes the feasible space of downstream resource scheduling, while scheduling outcomes feed back through system-level evaluation to influence upstream reconfiguration. title: Optimizing acid pretreatment and enzymatic hydrolysis for enhanced valorization of Theobroma cacao pod husk: A study on cameroonian lignocellulosic biomass
abstract: In this study, the valorization of cocoa pod husks was investigated through dilute acid pretreatment followed by enzymatic hydrolysis. The pretreatment process was optimized using a Central Composite Design considering acid concentration, temperature and reaction time as independent variables. The optimum pretreatment conditions were obtained at 1.5% HCl, 150 °C and 29.6 min, leading to a maximum reducing-sugar concentration of 39.15 g/L. title: FISC: a Fluid-Inspired framework for decentralised and scalable Swarm Control
abstract: Achieving scalable coordination in large robotic swarms is often constrained by reliance on inter-agent communication, which introduces latency, bandwidth limitations, and vulnerability to failure. To address this gap, a decentralised approach for outer-loop control of large multi-agent systems based on the paradigm of how a fluid moves through a volume is proposed and evaluated. title: To Understand the Political Climate in Germany, Turn to Art: Review of “Made in Germany? Art and Identity in a Global Nation”
abstract: ABSTRACT The exhibition “Made in Germany? Art and Identity in a Global Nation” ran at the Harvard Art Museums between September 13, 2024 and January 5, 2025. Focusing on labor migration and German re‐unification as its two pillars, the exhibition presented German art since the 1980s and brought new names, many of whom have migration backgrounds, to awareness for the North American audience. title: Efficient Hydrogen Peroxide Generation Modulated by Crystal‐Plane Engineering in Ti 2 O 3
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of stable and selective electrocatalysts for hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) synthesis via the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) is critical for sustainable green chemistry. However, the performance of transition metal oxides (TMOs) is often severely limited by the thermodynamic tendency to expose crystal planes with sluggish kinetics. abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines steady three‐dimensional rotational stagnation‐point flow of an incompressible micropolar fluid over a biaxially stretching or shrinking surface. abstract: Purpose. To determine the effective location of a collective concentrate enrichment plant (CCEP) when develo­ping titanium-zirconium deposits using the principle of circular technology. Methodology. title: A new species of Rana (Amphibia, Anura, Ranidae) from Hainan, Southern China
abstract: A new species of the genus Rana is described from Hainan Island, southern China, based on morphological and molecular evidence. During herpetological surveys conducted in Wanning City and Mt. Diaoluo, Hainan Province, a series of Rana specimens assignable to the R. johnsi group were collected from montane tropical rainforest habitats. Phylogenetic analyses based on mitochondrial 16S, COI, and cyt b sequences recovered the Hainan population as a distinct and well-supported lineage within the R. johnsi group. title: The Relationship between Local and Scientific Knowledge in the Management of Semurup Hot Spring Tourism: An Epistemological and Environmental Ethics Study
abstract: Although local and scientific knowledge have received considerable attention in environmental studies, their epistemological relationship and ethical implications for managing Semurup Hot Springs Tourism in Kerinci Regency, Jambi, remain insufficiently examined. This study analyzed the relationship between these forms of knowledge and its implications for environmental ethics and sustainable tourism management. title: How do relapses among recovering people affect the spread of drugs in the presence of media coverage
abstract: The spread of drugs continues to pose a significant threat to societies. Given the widespread reach of various media outlets and technological advancements, media-based awareness campaigns can contribute to curbing drug abuse and preventing relapse following recovery. This paper suggests and analyzes a mathematical model of drug addiction that incorporates the positive role of media in raising public awareness and addresses the issue of relapse after recovery. title: Case Report: Probable hepatosplenic tuberculosis mimicking undifferentiated connective tissue disease and malignancy
abstract: Background Hepatosplenic tuberculosis is a rare form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis with nonspecific manifestations, often leading to misdiagnosis. Tuberculosis can mimic connective tissue disease by presenting with systemic symptoms and positive autoantibodies, posing a diagnostic challenge. Case presentation We report a 69-year-old woman with polyarthralgia, oral ulcers, and positive autoantibodies including antinuclear antibody (ANA), anti-keratin antibody (AKA), and antiphospholipid antibodies, who was initially diagnosed with undifferentiated connective tissue disease (UCTD). title: The hand of evolution: conservation and divergence of hand paralogs in cyclostomes and gnathostomes
abstract: The Hand family comprises basic helix-loop-helix transcription factors with key roles in the development of the lateral mesoderm, heart, branchial arches and paired appendages in vertebrates. Although Hand1 and Hand2 have been extensively studied in model vertebrates, the evolutionary history and diversification of Hand paralogs in early-diverging vertebrate lineages remain poorly understood. journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology

title: Distribution and Interactions of Soil Nutrients and Organic Carbon at University of Calabar Campus, Nigeria
abstract: Plant biodiversity depends fundamentally on soil nutrient availability. However, nutrient dynamics within university campuses remain poorly studied, and less attention has been given to soil health, plant biodiversity, and the ecosystem services supported by campus soils. This study evaluated the influence of soil depth on the distribution, relationships, and multivariate interactions of soil nutrients and organic carbon across the University of Calabar campus, Nigeria. title: Spin‐State Modulation of Octahedral Co Sites for Enhancing Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Ammonia is vital for agriculture and a promising carbon‐free energy carrier, but its industrial production via the Haber–Bosch process is energy‐intensive and emits substantial CO 2 . Electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction to ammonia offers a green alternative, by using renewable electricity under ambient conditions while enabling nitrogen resource utilization. abstract: El ciberespacio ha evolucionado hacia un entorno de competencia geopolítica permanente, lo que exige transitar de una defensa estática hacia la Defensa Persistente Avanzada (DPA). abstract: We integrated butyrate-associated genes with the GSE32924 atopic dermatitis (AD) transcriptome and identified an exploratory four-gene transcriptomic signature (TP53, JAK2, H2AX, ALDH1A1), with sample-level AUCs of 0.951 in GSE16161, 0.888 in GSE120721 and 0.900 in GSE121212. title: Enhancing tribological performance in laser powder bed fusion produced Ti6Al4V alloys via Cu-induced lamellar spheroidization
abstract: The tribological performance of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF)-processed Ti6Al4V alloys is inherently constrained by their lamellar α microstructure, which promotes strain localization, interfacial cracking, and delamination during sliding. Cu-induced lamellar spheroidization provides an effective microstructural strategy to overcome this limitation in this study. title: Influence of urban spatial structure and land-use distribution on residential and transport emissions in European urban settlements
abstract: Abstract While urban spatial structure and land-use distribution play an important role in shaping greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, their sector-specific effects remain insufficiently understood in comparative urban studies. This study develops a scale-independent comparative framework to examine how functional land-use distribution, spatial configuration, alternative density representations, and broader economic and climatic context jointly shape per capita residential and transport emissions across 104 European cities. title: Solid Waste Disposal and Urban Flooding in Swali, Yenagoa Local Government Area, Bayelsa State, Nigeria
abstract: Solid waste disposal and urban flooding are increasingly occurring simultaneously in many Nigerian cities. This study examined the relationship between solid waste disposal practices and urban flooding in Swali, Yenagoa Local Government Area, Bayelsa State. A descriptive survey design was used. A structured four-point Likert questionnaire was administered to 320 household heads, and 300 copies were correctly filled and returned. Data were analysed with frequency, percentage, mean, median and mode, while Pearson correlation and simple linear regression tested three hypotheses at the 0.05 level.

title: Former field relics across Europe: a review
abstract: Former field relics (FFR) are microtopographic features: ridge and furrow, lynchets, terraces, headland ridges, stone walls, and stone heaps, inherited from past farming practices. In Europe, they are often described as being “everywhere”, particularly in landscapes that have escaped modern agricultural intensification. In this review, we provide quantitative support for this assumption by synthesizing over 150 studies on FFR across Europe. title: Econstellar: An open-source AI-augmented research engine for computational financial econometrics
abstract: Turning a promising economic idea into a credible empirical finding demands much specialised computation, and the results are seldom released in a form that others can check. This is a systems and reproducibility paper. It documents Econstellar, an open, publicly served research engine that runs financial econometrics from a web browser, so that a reader can re-run a finding, vary its inputs, and trace how it was produced. title: Notes on the nesting behavior of the Collared Forest Falcon (Micrastur semitorquatus) in Ceiba trichistandra within a dry deciduous forest of Guayaquil, Ecuador
abstract: The Collared Forest Falcon ( Micrastur semitorquatus ) is a falconid species distributed across the Americas, including Ecuador. Despite its broad geographic range, information regarding its breeding ecology remains limited in many regions. Nesting of this species has been previously reported in caves, human settlements and various tree species. Our observations reveal new data related to the ecology of this raptor in a highly threatened ecosystem, the dry deciduous forest. abstract: El artículo revisita el concepto de subordinación como categoría de poder para distinguir, en él, dos especies jurídico-funcionales visibles en el mundo del trabajo contemporáneo: la jurídica laboral y la algorítmica. title: Water integrity, ecological profiling, and health risk quantification of hand-dug wells in the Oghara-sub-Saharan Ecozone
abstract: Water is essential for human physiological and socio-economic activities; however, increasing dependence on hand-dug wells (HDWs) for domestic water supply in the Oghara-Sub-Saharan Ecozone raises concerns regarding water integrity, ecological quality, and potential human health risks. This study assessed the physicochemical characteristics, heavy metal contamination, pollution status, and associated health risks of groundwater from HDWs in Oghara, Ethiope West Local Government Area, Delta State, Nigeria. title: Spatial Footprint Distribution of Some Heavy Metals in Major Transport Routes in Ramadi City, Iraq
abstract: Rapid urbanization and industrial activity in arid regions can increase the accumulation of heavy metals (HMs) in road dust. This issue is particularly relevant in arid urban environments, where limited rainfall and frequent dust resuspension may enhance the persistence and redistribution of metal-contaminated particles. This study aimed to assess the accumulation of HMs (Zn, Cu, Cr, Pb, and Cd) in road dust and roadside vegetation of Ramadi City, Iraq. title: Reactive oxygen species mediation of pH-dependent biochar effects on soil N2O emissions
abstract: Biochar is widely recognized for mitigating soil N 2 O emissions, yet its efficacy varies markedly with soil pH, showing effective mitigation in alkaline soils but weakened or even reversed effects in acidic soils. The mechanisms underlying this pH-dependent behavior remain unresolved. abstract: Solar energy, a vital renewable resource, is harnessed using photovoltaic (PV) systems; however, challenges such as overcharging, component stress and energy losses due to environmental variations compromise reliability and efficiency. abstract: Helen, Draupadi, and Sita each become the object of a transaction they did not authorize: a divine promise, a wager at dice, a forcible abduction. title: Innovation Environment Matters More Than Policy? Evidence on Technology Adoption From Chinese Manufacturers
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how policy regulation and external innovation environment jointly influence manufacturing firms' adoption of emerging technologies and subsequent operational performance. Drawing on institutional theory and the resource‐based view, we analyse survey data from 451 Chinese manufacturing firms using structural equation modelling. abstract: ABSTRACT Existing studies on asymmetric economic competition and coercion have largely portrayed small and middle powers as passive actors that either accommodate or adapt to pressure imposed by major powers. abstract: Large religious and public gatherings, such as the Kumbh Mela, bring together millions of people in a small area for a short period. This paper presents the design of an IoT Based Smart Safety Wristband that combines two complementary low-power radio technologies. abstract: Diplomacy now moves through websites, cloud servers, and online consular portals. These tools reach citizens abroad quickly, yet the governing treaties were written for physical missions. This study aims to examine whether the Vienna Conventions protect virtual embassies and digital consular services. It also identifies legal changes needed to secure their status. title: A chromosome-level reference genome of the largest cervid species - the European moose ( Alces alces ; Linnaeus, 1758)
abstract: We describe a chromosome-level, haplotype-resolved genome assembly from a male European moose (Alces alces alces). The assembly comprises two pseudo-haplotypes of 3,148 Mb and 3,112 Mb, with sex chromosomes in haplotype one, and 33 autosomes in each haplotype (68 in total). Assembly completeness is high (BUSCO 98.3% and 95.7%), with 21,496 and 20,498 annotated protein-coding genes for haplotypes one and two, respectively. This genome assembly is the most complete so far generated for European moose.

abstract: Abstract Direct air capture of carbon dioxide (CO2) is one of the most promising strategies to mitigate rising atmospheric CO2 levels. Among various techniques, adsorption using porous materials is a viable method for extracting CO2 from air, even under humid conditions. However, identifying optimal adsorbent materials remains a significant challenge. Moreover, the performance of existing materials can be improved by doping with active species that boost gas capture, a relatively unexplored field. title: Optimizing Dormancy-Breaking Methods for Propagation of Four Ecologically and Economically Important Fabaceae Species
abstract: Seed dormancy is a critical issue affecting growth and germination among various species of Fabaceae that hold ecological and socioeconomic significance. The objective of this study is to investigate the effectiveness of four dormancy-breaking chemicals, hot water, hydrochloric acid, sulfuric acid, and coconut water, at four concentration rates (25%, 50%, 75%, and 100%) on Tamarindus indica, Vachellia nilotica, Parkia biglobosa, and Bauhinia reticulatum. title: Ultrasound‐guided pericardiocentesis and histopathological findings of hepatic mycobacteriosis caused by Mycobacterium intracellulare in a river cooter ( Pseudemys concinna )
abstract: Abstract A 15‐year‐old, 1.11‐kg, entire, male river cooter ( Pseudemys concinna ) presented with impaired buoyancy and generalised oedema. Haematological and biochemical analyses revealed nonspecific abnormalities, including hypoalbuminaemia and toxic changes in heterophils. Echocardiography revealed pericardial effusion, and ultrasound‐guided pericardiocentesis was subsequently performed. Treatment was initiated with pimobendan, furosemide, vitamin E and ceftazidime. title: EXPERIMENTAL TEST BENCH FOR INVESTIGATING THE CHARACTERISTICS OF A HYDRAULIC DRIVE WITH AN ANTI-SLIP DEVICE
abstract: The article presents the development and methodological substantiation of a specialized experimental test bench for investigating the characteristics of a hydrostatic drive with an anti-slip control system. The study used hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) modeling methods, stall test (maximum-load test) and transient response test protocols. The scientific novelty lies in the comprehensive assessment of the transition from passive flow dividers to systems of individual electronic control of hydraulic motor displacement. title: Alfabetización digital en comunidades rurales del cantón Esmeraldas: diagnóstico territorial para el fortalecimiento de competencias y acceso a las TIC
abstract: La alfabetización digital es un elemento fundamental de la inclusión educativa, social y productiva en entornos rurales donde las malas condiciones de conectividad, la falta de dispositivos y la falta de capacitación pueden afectar el uso efectivo de las tecnologías de la información y la comunicación (TIC). El objetivo de este estudio es comprender la situación de la alfabetización digital, el acceso, el uso y la apropiación de las TIC en comunidades rurales del cantón Esmeraldas, Ecuador, con el fin de identificar los datos relevantes para el programa de capacitación tecnológica específico d

title: Phylogenomics, spatiotemporal transcriptional dynamics and Cis-regulatory architecture underlying the Portulaca oleracea antioxidant network under extreme salinity
abstract: Global soil salinization severely threatens agricultural productivity. Portulaca oleracea L., an extreme xerohalophyte, displays exceptional salinity tolerance, yet the transcriptional architecture coordinating its antioxidant defenses across organs and developmental stages remains unresolved. In this study, multi-tissue high-throughput RNA-Seq, quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) validation, comparative phylogenomics across 154 plant genomes, and condition-specific gene regulatory network (GRN) modeling were integrated to characterize 436 antioxidant loci in P. oleracea. title: Combustion and Emissions Characteristics of a Dual-Fuel CI Engine under Varying Hydrogen Energy and Equivalence Ratios: A Computational Study
abstract: Hydrogen is widely recognized as a promising zero-carbon fuel for internal combustion engines due to its zero carbon emissions, high laminar flame speed, and wide flammability limits. In dual-fuel compression ignition engines, substituting part of the diesel fuel with hydrogen can significantly reduce carbon-based emissions while maintaining or improving ther-mal efficiency. This study investigates the combined effects of hydrogen substitution ratio (HSR) and equivalence ratio (Φ) on combustion characteristics, engine performance, and emissions in a diesel-hydrogen dual-fuel engine. title: Beyond the Fingerprints: Lived Experiences of Island and Mountain School Teachers on the Centralized Biometrics System
abstract: This study explored the lived experiences of island and mountain school teachers in Talibon I and II Districts, Division of Bohol, regarding the implementation of the Centralized Biometrics System launched in February 2026. It examined teachers’ initial reactions and lived experiences, the effects of the system on their teaching conditions and effectiveness, the challenges they encountered, their coping mechanisms, and the school support systems they received, as bases for a proposed action plan. title: The Synergistic Antibacterial Activity of Curcumin and Quercetin Against Nocardia seriolae and Evaluate Their Therapeutic Effects in the Infected Largemouth Bass
abstract: ABSTRACT Nocardia seriolae is an important bacterial pathogen causing chronic granulomatous disease in cultured fish, and effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. This study aimed to identify natural compounds with synergistic antibacterial activity against N. seriolae and evaluate their protective effects in largemouth bass ( Micropterus salmoides ). A structure‐guided screening strategy targeting N. seriolae isocitrate lyase (ICL) was performed using molecular docking, ADMET prediction, and in vitro antibacterial assays. title: CARBON DIOXIDE: PROPERTIES, SOURCES AND UTILIZATION METHODS
abstract: Environmental problems, such as climate change and global warming (the "greenhouse effect"), are associated with an increase in the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere. Reducing CO2 emissions is of great economic and environmental importance to humanity. At the same time, carbon dioxide is considered an ideal C1 building block in organic synthesis for ease of availability, low cost, non-toxicity and inflammability. Cost-effective and environmentally friendly chemical processes using CO2 in the synthesis of valuable chemicals are one of the technological advances aimed reducing CO

title: Dual-Role Catalyst: Influence of Multi-Nonmetal Incorporation in Bi2WO6 for Comparative Photocatalytic Water Purification and Electrocatalytic Oxygen Evolution
abstract: Sustainable energy generation and environmental remediation heavily depend on the development of highly efficient noble metal-free catalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and advanced photocatalysts for the degradation of contaminants. In this study, we synthesized sulfur-doped, boron-doped, and sulfur–boron co-doped Bi 2 WO 6 via a hydrothermal process to compare dual functional performance. title: Relationship between phytolith morphology and physical and mechanical properties in bamboo Ferrocalamus strictus
abstract: Ferrocalamus strictus is a rare bamboo species native to Yunnan, China, and is notable for its favorable mechanical properties. However, the relationship between phytolith morphology and these properties remains unclear. This study measured nine physical and mechanical traits and 26 phytolith parameters in culms from five provenances aged 1–3 years. title: Leaf spectroscopy detects site-associated functional differentiation in a dominant mangrove species near its northern range margin
abstract: Functional variation within species may be especially important at range margins, yet conventional trait measurements constrain population-level assessments. Leaf reflectance spectroscopy integrates signals associated with pigments, water, chemistry, and structure, potentially revealing functional differentiation. We analyzed leaf spectra from 48 Kandelia obovata trees across a southern reference population (SRP), a natural range-margin population (NRM), and a long-established planted population north of the historical range margin (PNR). title: Building Consensus on Satellite Imagery in Human Rights Investigations across Epistemic Communities: Insights from Journalism and Law
abstract: Abstract Satellite imagery has gained a paramount role in human rights investigations. Once the preserve of state intelligence agencies, the increase of commercially-available satellite imagery in recent years has enabled a broader range of actors to analyze earth observation data as part of their investigations. Investigative journalists were at the forefront of incorporating these techniques, with human rights organizations and international tribunals now utilizing satellite imagery as evidence of atrocity crimes. This article explores the alignment of practices from media and NGOs to courts

title: Engineered d-p orbital hybridization unlocks dilute CO2 electrolysis to byproduct-free CH4-rich syngas
abstract: Electrochemical CO2 methanation from flue gas offers a promising approach for upgrading point-source emissions and synthesizing energy-dense CH4. However, it remains challenging for both the direct utilization of dilute upstream and the extra downstream separation of complex byproducts. Here, we develop a gaseous byproduct-free system with an inlet of flue gas and an outlet of CH4-rich syngas for metallurgy and energy fields, wherein rationally designed Sn-based electrocatalysts are integrated with the direct electrolysis of bicarbonate-rich capture media, facilitated by engineered electrolyte

title: Geochemical characteristics of granitoids suggest a subduction origin for the Singhbhum Craton
abstract: New geochemical results are integrated with existing Paleo- to Mesoarchean igneous and detrital datasets to develop a crust-mantle evolution model for the Singhbhum Craton, India. Granitoid and detrital zircon U-Pb spectra exhibit strong overlap (overlap coefficient = 0.76; Wasserstein distance = 36 Myr) and persistent source-to-sink coupling across three magmatic pulses from ∼3.5–3.0 Ga, constraining magmatic pacing and indicating sustained exposure, erosion, and recycling of evolving granitoid crust. title: Metatranscriptomics Reveals Potential Hybrid Electron Routing in Comammox Nitrospira and NO-Supplemented Cooperation in a Partial Nitritation-Anammox Bioreactor under Dynamic Aeration
abstract: Abstract Intermittent aeration drives partial nitritation-anammox (PN-A) systems, yet how microbiomes regulate aerobic and anaerobic respiration during rapid, oxygen-limited redox shifts remains poorly understood. Here, we applied genome-resolved metatranscriptomics to evaluate transcriptional dynamics in a long-term PN-A bioreactor treating low concentrations of ammonium. Under intermittent aeration, active populations did not follow strict metabolic switching, but instead exhibited complementary regulation by coordinately transcribing aerobic and anaerobic respiratory pathways. title: Engineering probiotics for mucosal vaccination: from the Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 paradigm to a translational vaccine platform
abstract: Mucosal vaccination is attracting renewed interest because many clinically relevant pathogens first encounter the host at gastrointestinal or respiratory surfaces, whereas most established vaccines are administered parenterally and are optimized primarily to induce systemic immunity. Engineered probiotics are emerging as living antigen-delivery vectors that may combine mucosal delivery, transient biological persistence, microbial immune signals, and programmable antigen presentation within a single platform. title: Polypropylene microplastics modify copper associated leaf injury and photosynthetic responses in Nymphaea ‘Black Beauty’
abstract: Introduction Microplastics and heavy metals cooccur in freshwater habitats, yet it remains unclear whether microplastics intensify metal toxicity or redirect the dominant mode of plant injury. Methods We exposed the floatingleaved aquatic plant Nymphaea `Black Beauty' for 28 d to control conditions, copper (Cu) alone, polypropylene microplastics (PPMPs) alone, or combined Cu and PPMP stress. title: Coalition differentiation at scale: measuring intra-coalition rhetorical distinctiveness with supervised classification
abstract: Abstract Coalition parties face a unity-differentiation dilemma: they must uphold compromise to govern effectively, while maintaining distinct identities to maximize electoral success. Existing measures of coalition differentiation almost exclusively rely on static proxies to infer behavior, and the few dynamic measures often only cover a limited sample of governments, limiting comparative analysis. title: Land use dynamics and hydro-climatic variability to hydrological responses in Tawa River Basin, central India
abstract: Quantifying hydrological responses of river basins to combined hydro-climatic variability and land use/land cover (LULC) change (1999–2019) is fundamental to sustainable water resource management in regions experiencing intensifying anthropogenic pressures. This study investigates how climatic variability and land-use dynamics drive hydrological change in the Tawa River Basin, a strategically important tributary of the Narmada River in central India, whose hydrological behaviour underpins regional agricultural productivity, ecosystem functioning, and water supply security. title: Exclusive quark and gluon dijet production as probes of GPDs at collider energies
abstract: We study exclusive electroproduction of dijets in the collinear factorization framework as a probe of generalized parton distributions (GPDs). For quark dijet production, we extend previous analyses by including contributions from helicity GPDs and by assessing an additional leading-order electromagnetic channel governed by elastic nucleon form factors. Furthermore, we investigate exclusive gluon dijet production. We compare our prediction to HERA data and provide projections for measurements at the future Electron-Ion Collider.

title: Beneficial microbes in plant salt stress tolerance: mechanisms, antioxidant defense, and multi-omics insights
abstract: Salinity stress represents a significant environmental challenge that affects plant growth, resulting in adverse impacts on crop productivity and overall yield. Salt accumulation in plants affects cellular homeostasis and provokes osmotic and ionic imbalance. It stimulates higher reactive oxygen species (ROS) production leading to oxidative stress damage and eventual cellular dysfunction. title: Payment bases and performance logic in China’s subnational compensation for cultivated land protection in the context of ecological and environmental law codification: a two-tier content analysis of 155 legal and policy documents
abstract: Introduction China’s policy framework calls for integrated protection of cultivated land quantity, quality, and ecological functions, but how this objective is reflected in subnational compensation rules remains unclear. Methods From 650 initial records, this study constructed a two-tier corpus of 155 legal and policy documents: 108 dedicated compensation documents and 47 containing embedded provisions. title: Infestation Dynamics and Quantitative Impact of the Seed Borer, Trachylepidia fructicassiella (Lepidoptera: Pyralidae), on Cassia fistula Pods
abstract: The lepidopteron seed borer, Trachylepidia fructicassiella, is a pest that causes severe damage to the pods of the golden shower (Cassia fistula L.) and several other forest trees. The caterpillars burrow into the pods, devouring the seeds and pulp, which later impairs seed viability. Molecular characterization and phylogenetic studies of the caterpillars have confirmed that the specimens collected from infested C. fistula pods in this study were T. fructicassiella. title: Quantitative Analysis and Predictive Modelling of 10th–13th-Century CE Hillforts in Eastern Latvia
abstract: Hillforts are important cultural landscape elements in the history of Latvian Bronze and Iron Age research. Hillfort research has expanded significantly since the proliferation of LiDAR-derived digital elevation models (DEM). This paper analyses factors influencing hillfort placement using free software and accessible datasets, focussing on 10th to 13th-century CE hillforts in eastern Latvia. Furthermore, study establishes a statistical basis for identifying the main determinants of hillfort location, which were then applied to create several logistic regression models. title: Mayh dja kunwarddewardde: establishment of long-term biodiversity monitoring and status of small mammals in the Warddeken Indigenous Protected Area, northern Australia
abstract: Landscape-scale biodiversity monitoring embedded within Indigenous governance and management remain relatively uncommon, despite the importance of Indigenous managed lands to biodiversity conservation. In response to Traditional Custodian concerns about declines in biocultural diversity, Bininj Nawarddeken established an Indigenous-governed monitoring program across the Warddeken Indigenous Protected Area (IPA) in northern Australia. title: Concurrent Strong Winds and Heavy Precipitation Contributed to the Early 2010s Mortality Pulse of Korean Fir (Abies koreana)
abstract: Abstract Although climate-induced physiological stress is often considered the primary driver of high-elevation conifer forest decline, mortality pulses implicate episodic physical disturbances. We investigated the early 2010s mortality pulse of Korean fir ( Abies koreana ) using 16 years of tagged-stem monitoring data (2005–2021) on Jirisan Mountain, alongside meteorological records. Typhoons in 2011–2012 produced winds exceeding 30 ms −1 with rainfall above 200 mm day −1 , the most extreme compound wind-rain events in the twenty-year record. title: Micro- and nanoplastics and fecal microbiota transplantation: a conceptual framework linking gut dysbiosis and intestinal barrier dysfunction
abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) is increasingly recognized as a promising therapeutic option for microbiota-related disorders. Its efficacy may be affected by factors related to both donor microbiota and the recipient’s intestinal barrier. Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs), emerging environmental contaminants, have been recognized for their detrimental impacts on intestinal health. Existing studies have shown that MNPs can induce gut dysbiosis, impair intestinal barrier, and alter mucosal immune responses. title: Divine and Human Matters of Ireland: Messianic Allegory in James Joyce's Ulysses
abstract: The present article examines James Joyce’s Ulysses through the entwined lenses of messianic allegory, Benjaminian historical theory, and postcolonial critique. Departing from the conventional understanding of allegory as a system of stable symbolic correspondences, the article proposes a model of ‘messianic allegorical disruption’: a mode of figuration in which the ruins of history accumulate without resolution, salvation is perpetually deferred and meaning is produced not through closure but through interruption. title: Live imaging of largemouth bass virus dissemination in zebrafish
abstract: Introduction Understanding how viruses infect and spread within a living host is an attractive yet formidable goal. However, our understanding of these processes relies primarily on in vitro imaging studies conducted in cell culture models. Methods Here, we developed a zebrafish model of Largemouth bass virus (LMBV) infection, enabling for the first time real-time tracing of iridovirus spread in vivo . title: Nonlinear backstepping control with GWO-based global MPPT for grid-connected photovoltaic systems under partial shading conditions
abstract: Under partial shading conditions (PSCs), grid-connected PV systems exhibit multiple LMPPs, which can cause conventional MPPT methods such as P&O to converge to a local optimum instead of the GMPP, resulting in power losses. To overcome this limitation, this work proposes a hybrid Grey Wolf Optimization–Backstepping Control (GWO-BSC) strategy for reliable and accurate GMPP tracking in a two-stage three-phase grid-connected PV system. title: The hidden cost of forest loss: soil mercury stocks across contrasting land uses in the Amazon, Cerrado, and their transition zone
abstract: The effects of land-use change on soil organic matter (SOM) and mercury (Hg) dynamics across tropical biomes and ecotonal transitions remain poorly understood. We evaluated how the conversion of native vegetation to cropland and pasture influences SOM quality, soil fertility, and Hg dynamics in the Amazon, Cerrado, and Cerrado-Amazon Ecotone. Soil samples were collected to a depth of 1 m under forest, cropland, and pasture systems. title: Simulation of the impacts of a sensor’s PSF on mixed-pixel unmixing: adjacency and overall effect
abstract: The point spread function (PSF) of optical sensors is a critical source of error in mixed-pixel unmixing, and the statistical characteristics of PSF-induced unmixing errors remain poorly understood. Characterizing these statistical behaviours can clarify the underlying mechanisms through which the PSF affects unmixing procedures and provide a theoretical foundation for developing high-precision models for correcting PSF-induced errors. title: Numerical Analysis of the Cofferdam Partial Collapse that Occurred during its Construction
abstract: Building the bridge pier foundation for the Bratislava motorway bypass in Slovakia required the construction of a cofferdam in the Danube River. During construction, a local failure occurred, and its cause had to be investigated. In addition to significant cracks on the inner surface of the cofferdam, one of the struts tore away from the sheet pile wall. title: High-pyrolysis-temperature acidified straw biochar improves soil hydrological functioning and increases maize yield in saline soils
abstract: Biochar contributes to the restoration of soil fertility and crop productivity in saline-affected farmlands. Soil hydrological functioning is a key indicator for assessing the degradation and rehabilitation of saline soils. However, the mechanisms by which acid-modified maize straw biochar produced at different pyrolysis temperatures regulates the hydrological properties of saline soils remain unclear. title: Integrated effects of climate change and land‐use/land‐cover dynamics on streamflow and sediment yield in the Teji Catchment, Ethiopia
abstract: This study evaluates the combined effects of projected climate and land-use/land-cover (LULC) change on streamflow and sediment yield in the Teji Catchment, Ethiopia. The analysis covered historical and future periods from the 1980s to the 2060s, with the 1980s, 2000s, and 2020s representing the historical period. The 2040s and 2060s represent projected scenarios. Observed meteorological data from the Teji, Ginchi, and Kimoye stations characterize historical climate conditions. title: From Accession Conditionality to Strategic Ambiguity: Evaluating the EU’s Influence on Democracy and Human Rights in Turkey (1999–2025)
abstract: This article examines the transformation of the European Union’s efforts to promote democracy and human rights in Turkey from the 1999 Helsinki Summit to mid-2025. The study analyzes the instruments implemented by the EU, reform periods, and democratic setbacks, and examines the internal and external factors that shape these processes. A qualitative and historical-institutionalist method is adopted; EU Progress Reports, Turkey’s legal reform documents, and important political developments are evaluated using discourse analysis and process monitoring techniques. title: How Fire Moves Carbon in North American Ecosystems Shaped by Fire and Grazing
abstract: ABSTRACT Fire interacts with ecosystem carbon in North American fire-grazing rangelands through processes that span chemical forms, soil depths, and temporal horizons. We synthesize empirical evidence on fire-driven carbon redistribution across the continental region where frequent fire and bison grazing historically co-occurred. Across these rangelands, temperate grasses allocate roughly 75–80% of biomass belowground, outside the combustion zone. title: Historical trade-route connectivity predicts the flavour map of world cuisines
abstract: Did two thousand years of Silk Road exchange make the world’s cuisines more or less alike? We construct a cross-cultural flavour network with 104,770 recipes and 1507 ingredients, in which cuisine is treated as measurable intangible cultural heritage (ICH). Connectivity along 18 historical trade routes predicts flavour similarity among 20 modern, English-language national-cuisine corpora (partial Mantel r = 0.479 controlling for geography, p = 2.0 × 10⁻⁴), and the geographic gradient is better explained by historical connectivity than by distance. title: An Evaluation of Gaziantep Nature Park Based on a Content Analysis of TripAdvisor Visitor Reviews
abstract: This study aims to evaluate the visitor reviews of Gaziantep Wildlife Park, Turkey’s largest and the world’s fourth-largest wildlife park, posted on TripAdvisor, through content analysis. To this end, reviews regarding the wildlife park on TripAdvisor were examined and evaluated using the MAXQDA 2018 qualitative data analysis software. The study population consists of 164 visitors who visited Gaziantep Wildlife Park and posted reviews on TripAdvisor. The study examined Turkish online reviews. title: Changes in family knowledge, practices, and perceived competencies after a family-centered home-visiting program for chronic child malnutrition prevention in rural Ecuador: an uncontrolled pre-post study
abstract: Introduction Chronic child malnutrition (CCM) remains a major public health challenge, particularly in socially vulnerable settings, given its association with adverse developmental outcomes. Preventing CCM requires integrated approaches that combine nutritional support, healthcare, and the strengthening of family caregiving capacities. title: An integral soil quality index based on nematodes for mining-impacted Andean soils
abstract: Mining activities, while economically important, have caused significant soil degradation, affecting soil quality, ecosystem functioning, and sustainability in Andean ecosystems. This study developed an integral soil quality index based on physicochemical, microbiological, and nematode indicators to assess soil degradation in the Ollachea mining area, Peru. We collected soil samples from four land-use systems (natural pasture, Zea mays cultivation, Ficus sp. cultivation, and Eucalyptus sp. forest) during two dry and two rainy seasons. title: A review and evaluation of territory mapping methods in bird censuses
abstract: Mapping methods have played a crucial role in bird monitoring and for testing ecological hypotheses, theories and accuracy of other count techniques. The purpose of this review is to describe bird territory mapping methods, their development, principles, types and accuracy, and to compare their estimates with those of other quantitative methods. The mapping method was developed by a US ornithologist, A.B. Williams, in 1936. title: Evapotranspiration From a Mountain Peatland: Potential Impact of Diminishing Snow Cover on Water Yield
abstract: ABSTRACT Peatlands store large volumes of water, playing an important role in catchment hydrology, and thus regional water cycles. Water from peatlands is released both as streamflow and via evapotranspiration (ET) to the atmosphere. ET is linked to snow cover through recharge and water availability; however, the direct impact of snow cover on ET has received little research attention. We hypothesised that snow cover has the potential to influence rates of ET from a mountain peatland. title: Epoxy Resin Recycling: Challenges, Technologies, and the Path to Sustainable Circularity
abstract: Epoxy resins are critical in engineering due to their superior mechanical, thermal, and chemical properties, yet their crosslinked structure poses major recycling challenges.This review presents a comprehensive synthesis of emerging strategies for epoxy resin sustainability, uniting advanced recycling methods, bio-based material innovations, and life cycle assessments (LCA) with patent and policy analyses.It critically evaluates chemical, thermal, mechanical, and hybrid recycling techniques, emphasising scalability, costeffectiveness, and environmental performance.Key developments include solv

title: The bone-biofilm interface: decoding the bidirectional crosstalk in orthopedic implant infections
abstract: Implant-associated orthopedic infections remain difficult to eradicate because biofilm persistence is coupled to progressive changes in bone and local immunity. This narrative review presents the Bone-biofilm Interface (BBI) as an integrative framework linking microbial biofilms, implant properties, bone cells, immune cells, and the mineralized matrix. title: The importance of the regional context for the development of local smart tourism destinations
abstract: This study examines how regional characteristics inﬂuence the development of local Smart Tourism Destinations (STDs) in its territory, highlighting that, beyond city level initiatives, regional contexts play a key role by shaping the enabling conditions for smart transformation. Despite this relevance, the extent to which regional strategies aﬀect the development of local STDs remains largely unexplored in the existing literature, resulting in a gap that this research aims to address. title: Negosiasi Kosmologis: Telaah Semiotik Transformasi Sinkretisme Teologis Tanam Kepala Kerbau dalam Dekonstruksi Teologis Al-Ma’idah Ayat 3
abstract: Tradisi penanaman kepala kerbau dalam berbagai ritus adat di Indonesia—seperti syukuran laut, pembangunan infrastruktur, dan bersih desa—sering menimbulkan ketegangan teologis ketika berhadapan dengan nilai-nilai monoteisme Islam. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengkaji persistensi jejak animisme melalui ritual tersebut dengan menempatkannya dalam kerangka dekonstruksi teologis QS. Al-Ma’idah Ayat 3. Menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif melalui studi kepustakaan dan observasi budaya, penelitian ini menganalisis bagaimana simbolisme animistik bertahan, dinegosiasikan, dan mengalami transformasi semantik
journal: Al-Shamela Journal of Quranic and Hadith Studies

title: Development of a conceptual model for accounting, analytical and audit support for ESG reporting compliance
abstract: The object of the study is the conceptual foundations of accounting, analytical and audit support for ESG reporting compliance. Accounting for ESG indicators is becoming an integrated dimension of management information, encompassing both quantitative measurements and qualitative assessments. The study addresses the problem of the methodological, organizational and technological gap between traditional financial accounting systems, international ESG reporting requirements and long-term sustainable development prospects. Taking the Napahai alpine-cold wetland in north-western Yunnan as the study area, this research assessed the responses of soil and plant systems to different disturbance types and explored the potential relationships among soil properties, microbial indicators, and vegetation characteristics. abstract: Abstract With the rapid urbanization in China, millions of people have moved from rural regions to cities as migrant workers, where many of them face various discrimination and ill treatment. abstract: Piled raft foundation systems (PRFS) have been increasingly adopted as an alternative foundation system in developed urban areas underlain by soft soils. abstract: Water ice clouds are an important component of the Martian atmospheric water cycle. abstract: Abstract This paper examines the thermomechanical behavior of composite materials under axial compression across a wide temperature range, focusing on buckling mode transitions. abstract: OBJECTIVE: Develop prediction models to support care for older adults with fall-related traumatic brain injury (TBI). SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND: Fall-related TBI is a leading cause of hospitalization and death among older adults. Prognostication remains challenging in this population because frailty and comorbidity burden greatly influence recovery trajectories. abstract: The article examines the role of public administration as a key determinant of national resilience in the context of a rapidly changing geopolitical environment. The analysis focuses on contemporary security challenges such as armed conflicts, hybrid threats, cyber risks, energy insecurity, and disinformation campaigns. abstract: Scientific computing applications heavily rely on multi-level loop nests operating on multidimensional arrays. abstract: Youth unemployment remains a persistent challenge in South Africa, prompting interventions such as the Presidential Employment Stimulus (PES), which places unemployed graduates in internships designed to build employability. There is little evidence on whether such benefits are sustained after program completion. title: On the Maturation of Chinese Characters and the Mechanism behind the Contention of Hundred Schools of Thought
abstract: Academic circles hold diverse views on the causes of the “Contention of a Hundred Schools of Thought.” This paper proposes that the maturity, practical application and diffusion of Chinese characters during the Spring and Autumn Period substantially enhanced administrative governance and economic development, bringing the prefecture-county system to dominance. abstract: Canopy light interception is an important physiological trait that is traditionally measured using a light bar. abstract: Abstract Climate change is increasingly reshaping land-use/land-cover dynamics worldwide, yet the magnitude and spatial distribution of these changes remain insufficiently understood at the regional scale. title: Rapid disease progression during adjuvant chemotherapy following concurrent chemoradiotherapy and radical resection for rectal sarcomatoid carcinoma: a case report and literature review
abstract: Background Rectal sarcomatoid carcinoma (RSC) is an exceedingly rare, aggressive malignancy characterized by a dismal prognosis, high recurrence rates, and truncated overall survival. Only 16 cases have been reported. Due to its rarity, optimal therapeutic strategies remain poorly understood. While current management typically mirrors rectal adenocarcinoma paradigms due to a lack of dedicated guidelines, clinical outcomes are frequently unsatisfactory, highlighting the challenges in managing this rare entity. abstract: Forest-residue-derived constituents are increasingly being considered for low-carbon cementitious materials, but their functions differ substantially and should not be treated as a single waste-substitution category. abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) encapsulate a variety of biologically active molecules, such as proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids, and have been recognized as crucial mediators of intercellular communication. The production of EVs has been observed across numerous fungal species. abstract: ABSTRACT Coupling phase‐change buffering with passive radiative cooling offers complementary continuous and transient regulation for personal thermal management (PTM). abstract: The Xuhuai Arc Tectonic Belt (XHTB), located along the southeastern margin of the North China Craton (NCC) west of the Tan-Lu Fault Zone (TLFZ), remains poorly understood in terms of its formation mechanisms due to limited constraints on deep crustal architecture. abstract: State–religion relations in contemporary democracies are increasingly shaped by religious diversity, institutional pluralism, and the growing involvement of public authorities in regulating recognition, accommodation, participation, and access to public resources. abstract: Most anthropology majors do not pursue academic careers or work in traditional anthropological fields. abstract: Ammunition depots are facilities of high strategic, security, and logistical importance, and the selection of an appropriate location directly affects both operational effectiveness and safety. title: Improving nitrogen and phosphorus use efficiency in agriculture: a critical review of management practices
abstract: Introduction Nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) are major nutrients in agricultural production worldwide, but only about half of applied nutrients are recovered, contributing to financial losses, soil degradation, and nutrient pollution. This systematic review and meta-analysis quantified the effects of management practices on nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) and phosphorus use efficiency (PUE), with particular attention to smallholder farming systems in Zimbabwe, especially granitic sandveld soils and fertility gradients between homefields and outfields. title: Ultra‐Broad‐Temperature Mechanoluminescence Enabled by Intrinsic Lattice Disorder
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanoluminescent (ML) materials convert mechanical stimuli into light through carrier excitation and radiative recombination, enabling external‐power‐free stress sensing and visualization. The strict energy matching required for carrier release, transport, and recombination restricts ML to narrow thermal windows. Their application at extreme temperatures, however, is constrained by discrete defect levels arising from relatively uniform local atomic environments. abstract: ABSTRACT The transition to a circular economy (CE) necessitates redesigning products and processes to minimise environmental impacts throughout their entire lifecycle. This study investigates the solar radiation performance of varying courtyard proportions in Ameri's House, Kashan, Iran, through a simulation-based approach validated against site-specific measurements. abstract: Cybercrime as a Service (CaaS) represents a significant and evolving threat, mirroring the legitimate 'Everything as a Service’ model by providing sophisticated, user-friendly toolkits that lower the barrier to entry for malicious actors. abstract: Accurate electricity demand forecasting supports operational planning and energy-efficiency decisions in distribution systems. abstract: ABSTRACT Genetically engineered microorganisms (GEMs) are increasingly being explored as effective tools for removing a wide range of environmental pollutants, including persistent organic compounds, heavy metals, and industrial wastes. abstract: Using the KORTARA Korpus Nusantara application, this study employed a quantitative corpus linguistics approach to examine the lexical density and average sentence length in nine novels by Indonesian women authors. abstract: Abstract Hypertension and glycemia disorders are severe issues in public health, highlighting the urgent need for the discovery of natural bioactive agents with health benefits. title: Total Protein Quantification in Human Milk: Evaluation of Analytical Methods and Associations with Maternal Factors and Infant Outcomes
abstract: Human milk (HM) protein plays a critical role in supporting infant growth and development. Accurate quantification of HM total protein is therefore important for assessing infant nutrient intake and informing nutritional recommendations, particularly for preterm infants, who have high protein requirements but limited milk intake capacity. abstract: Abstract Although cartilage in tetrapod skeletons is typically said to lack blood vessels, this is only true for adult cartilage. In young bird and mammal cartilage, a dense network of vasculature-containing tunnels —cartilage canals— perforate the growing skeleton, helping nourish the cartilage and develop the ossification centers that will later form the skeleton’s epiphyseal bone. abstract: ABSTRACT Preoperative anxiety affects 50-75% of pediatric surgical patients and can lead to adverse perioperative outcomes including difficult anesthesia induction, emergence delirium, and prolonged recovery. Virtual reality has emerged as a promising non-pharmacological intervention, yet evidence from real-world clinical implementation remains limited. abstract: Against the backdrop of global climate change and intensified human activities, grassland soil wind erosion has emerged as a prominent issue threatening ecological security, yet the synergistic driving mechanisms involving multiple factors remain unclear. abstract: Extensively fractionated granitoids are exhibit an intrinsic genetic association with rare-metal mineralization events, but the mechanisms for their unusual geochemical features (e.g., low Nb/Ta ratios) and pronounced enrichment of rare metals remain contentious. abstract: ABSTRACT Quantum dots (QDs) stand out as promising luminescent materials for next‐generation white light‐emitting diodes (WLEDs) owing to their outstanding optical properties and facile solution processability. Unfortunately, current QD‐based WLEDs are still plagued by low color rendering index (CRI) and external quantum efficiency (EQE). title: The Transformation of the Legitimacy of Power in Islamic Politics: From Classical Bayʿat to the Modern Political Mandate
abstract: The transformation of power legitimacy in Islamic politics cannot be understood as a linear shift from bayʿat (oath of allegiance) to general elections, because changes in political institutions also reconfigure the sources of authorization, the subjects granting the mandate, and the mechanisms of control over power. abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive experimental characterization of a rubber composite made from styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR) and polyamide reinforcement cords. The study focuses on determining the mechanical properties of the constituent components of the composite and their interactions under tensile loading. abstract: Abstract Amphibian poisons are one of the most complex chemical defense systems among vertebrates, yet their diversity remains largely unresolved. Here, we present a comparative peptidomic analysis of six Amazonian species of Monkey Tree Frogs (Phyllomedusidae) sampled across three geographic regions. title: Design of the Pesut Mahakam Mascot as a Conservation Education Media in the Central Mahakam Area
abstract: The Mahakam Irrawaddy dolphin (Orcaella brevirostris), locally known as the pesut Mahakam, is a threatened aquatic mammal inhabiting the Mahakam River ecosystem in East Kalimantan, Indonesia. Its survival is increasingly threatened by habitat degradation and various human activities, while public awareness of its conservation needs remains limited despite ongoing protection efforts. This study aimed to design a pesut Mahakam mascot as a visual communication medium to support conservation education and public engagement in the Central Mahakam region. While continuous monoculture typically causes yield decline in cultivated soybean, its wild relative persists in the same soils for decades without apparent decline, suggesting the presence of a protective native rhizosphere. abstract: Introduction Plant-associated microbiomes can shape host phenotypes, yet plant breeding programs rarely incorporate microbiome data into their selection criteria. For example, multi-location trials are central for studying genotype-by-environment interactions, yet the microbiome is a poorly characterized component of environmental variation. abstract: This article introduces exstruction as a new conceptual lens for understanding experiential learning processes in contexts characterized by uncertainty, risk, and direct engagement with the natural environment. In this article exstruction is defined as the intentional withholding of instructions or learning content in order to foster learner driven and inductive learning processes. abstract: Background Atriplex taltalensis is an endangered halophytic species endemic to the Chilean Atacama Desert, for which genomic resources are currently lacking. Complete chloroplast genomes provide valuable resources for comparative genomics, phylogenetics, and conservation genetics because of their conserved structure and informative evolutionary patterns. abstract: Conservation biology has traditionally sought to justify public investment made specifically for biodiversity. I explore an alternative proposition: whether biodiversity can be co-produced through investments that society already undertakes for other public purposes. abstract: Algorithmic management has renewed debate on work rationalization and workers’ experiences. This integrative review examines continuities and transformations between Taylorism and algorithmic management and their possible implications for workforce integration. abstract: La adaptación social de los estudiantes de nuevo ingreso a un nivel universitario es un momento crucial en el avance académico y personal. abstract: La transformación digital es constituida como una capacidad estratégica para fortalecer la competitividad empresarial en los mercados internacionales. abstract: Medicinal plants face growing threats from climate change, habitat fragmentation, selective harvesting, and other human-induced pressures that may diminish genetic diversity and weaken evolutionary resilience. abstract: As technological advances have occurred in medicine, including improvements in rates of resuscitation, descriptions of near-death experiences (NDEs) have increased significantly. abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory disorder driven by profound innate immune dysregulation, wherein intestinal macrophages exhibit robust functional plasticity shaped by local microenvironmental cues. abstract: The use of digital technologies as a teaching and learning tool currently represents an enormous challenge in art education, as well as in the formative field in general, framed in new processes of knowledge and socialization that involve multidimensional learning. abstract: Indonesian universities face a coupled implementation problem: climate policies and sustainability education are expanding, yet campus infrastructure is rarely monitored to verify environmental performance. abstract: The evolving demands of physical education in contemporary school contexts require future teachers to be equipped with pedagogical approaches that are responsive, adaptable, and grounded in the realities of dynamic learning environments. abstract: Background Vaccine supply planning in hazard-prone terrains faces compounding geographic, socioeconomic, and operational barriers. abstract: Introduction: Night vision goggles (NVGs) extend the capability of helicopter crews to conduct night operations, but they do not reproduce daytime vision and may alter the visual conditions in which spatial disorientation (SD) develops. A historical helicopter study reported an approximately five-fold higher SD-related accident rate during night-vision device (NVD) operations than during daytime flight. abstract: Background Contaminated duck litter is a leading cause of flock disease and a bottleneck for the sustainable development of large-scale dry-rearing systems. Methods We applied shotgun metagenomics to litter from four positions within each of three independent compound microbial intelligent membrane fermentation beds, with unfermented litter from the same three batches as the control. title: Epithelial inflammatory memory in ulcerative colitis: molecular mechanisms and translational implications
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) can relapse after clinical and endoscopic remission, raising the question of whether previously inflamed epithelium retains altered responsiveness. Patient-derived colonic organoids and lineage-resolved colitis models show that inflammation-associated chromatin accessibility can persist after removal of the original environment and influence subsequent epithelial behavior. Basal inflammatory transcription, however, can return toward normal during organoid expansion. title: Beyond Connectivity: School-Based Teacher Support and Internet Integration in Teaching Comprehensive Sexuality Education in Rwandan Secondary Schools
abstract: The integration of internet-based technologies in education has transformed instructional practices globally. However, their adoption in developing countries such as Rwanda has been limited because of factors such as a lack of teacher support. This question is especially consequential for Comprehensive Sexuality Education (CSE), a sensitive, cross-cutting subject in Rwanda’s Competence-Based Curriculum (CBC) for which teachers often lack specialised preparation. This study examined the association between school-based teacher support and internet integration in teaching CSE among 207 teachers
