title: An ethnobotanical investigation of consumer profiles and the use of aromatic and medicinal plants in herbal markets in Ankara
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the ethnobotanical uses of medicinal and aromatic plants sold in herbal shops in Ankara and to characterize the consumer profile associated with these products. Data were collected through surveys conducted with 10 herbalists and 130 consumers in the central districts of Yenimahalle, Çankaya, and Etimesgut in Ankara. abstract: La integración de herramientas digitales emergentes en contextos educativos rurales sigue siendo un desafío pendiente en Ecuador. title: Extraction of rotor unbalance characteristics from non-stationary vibration signals during speed fluctuations
abstract: Abstract Speed fluctuations introduce pronounced non-stationarity into rotor vibration signals, which makes the accurate extraction of rotational-frequency, amplitude, and phase characteristics considerably more difficult than under steady-speed conditions. To address this problem, a rotor-unbalance characteristic-extraction method is developed for speed-fluctuation conditions. abstract: The quality of power in medium-voltage distribution grids has become increasingly challenging due to the growing penetration of variable renewable energy sources and the increasing presence of unbalanced loads. Variable distributed generation introduces generation ramps at the Point of Common Coupling (PCC), causing rapid voltage fluctuations and three-phase unbalances that can challenge conventional voltage regulation equipment. title: Media and information literacy teaching in the Global South: Educational contexts and teacher preparedness
abstract: This thematic literature review examines how educational contexts and teacher preparedness shape Media and Information Literacy (MIL) teaching, with particular attention to the Global South and the Philippines. Literature gathered iteratively through Google Scholar, university library resources, and journal websites was organized into three themes: Global South contexts, educational implementation, and Philippine teaching realities. title: Integrating ground observations to improve satellite-based gross primary productivity estimates across Indian flux tower sites
abstract: The Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) provides long-term, continuous global estimates of vegetation productivity and is widely used to assess vegetation responses to climate change. Recent studies using MODIS datasets over India suggest that increases in vegetation greenness have not resulted in higher carbon uptake; however, limited ground validation of these estimates introduces uncertainty. abstract: ABSTRACT Fiber‐shaped zinc‐ion batteries are highly deformable and can store energy in irregular spaces. abstract: Agritourism has increasingly emerged as an important form of sustainable tourism due to its economic, social, cultural, and environmental contributions to rural communities. abstract: Since the rise of social media, discourse analysis has turned to these platforms for the development of corpora of various types. In the analysis of political discourse, the tradition of studies on Twitter (now X) has continued to grow, despite the technological (and functional) changes adopted by the platform. In this article, we examine the average lifespan of these posts and the relevance of temporal normalization in the creation of data corpora. abstract: Background Climate change is intensifying droughts and floods in Sub-Saharan Africa, threatening livelihoods, food security, and habitability in vulnerable landscapes. This scoping review synthesizes evidence on Indigenous knowledge for drought and flood forecasting in Malawi, focusing on forecasting indicators, relationships with scientific forecasting, and implications for climate adaptation and habitability. abstract: Abstract The Mexican highlands, a biodiversity hotspot characterized by complex topography and dynamic paleoenvironments, function as "Sky Islands," isolating temperate-adapted species and promoting in situ diversification. This pattern is exemplified by the Mexican Highland Clade (MHLC) of Thamnophis, a genus exhibiting high ecological and phylogenetic diversity in North America. abstract: Context: The use of multimedia resources has become central to teaching English as a foreign language; however, their effective integration in school contexts with technological limitations remains poorly understood from the teachers' perspective. Objetive: This research aimed to analyze the use of multimedia resources in secondary schools based on the perceptions of English teachers in Lima, Peru. abstract: Abstract Groundwater recharge estimation is fundamental for the sustainable management of water resources, especially in complex hydrogeological systems comprising granular and fractured aquifers. This study investigates recharge dynamics in two sub-basins through the monitoring of Water Table Fluctuation (WTF) in seven wells: five dug wells (DW) located in the granular aquifer (soil) and two tube wells (TW) in the fractured aquifer. title: Towards Comprehensive Deterrence—Rethinking European Deterrence in the 21st Century
abstract: ABSTRACT Deterrence has re‐emerged as a central concept in international politics, but the dominant conception of it remains rooted in Cold War nuclear thinking. The paper argues that the concept of deterrence must be redefined to reflect the complexity of the current threat environment, in which hybrid, non‐military and societal threats increasingly blur the line between war and peace. abstract: This study aims to examine how user-generated content (UGC) influences medical travel decision intention and to explore the mediating role of destination trust in this relationship. The research seeks to clarify the psychological mechanisms through which digital social influence shapes potential travelers' choices in a high-risk medical tourism context. A quantitative research design was adopted using a structured questionnaire administered to potential international travelers. title: Gestión pública de la asistencia técnica y desarrollo sostenible: análisis bibliométrico
abstract: La asistencia técnica agrícola es un instrumento de política pública. Este estudio analizó, desde las ciencias sociales, la producción científica internacional sobre asistencia técnica agrícola, prácticas agrícolas sostenibles y diversificación productiva. Se aplicó un diseño cuantitativo, descriptivo y longitudinal retrospectivo. La búsqueda en Scopus recuperó 3619 registros; tras excluir otros tipos de documento, los años incompletos, las áreas temáticas ajenas a las ciencias sociales y los duplicados, según el protocolo PRISMA 2020, el corpus quedó en 1101 artículos y revisiones publicados

abstract: Introduction Antibiotic resistance is spreading throughout aquatic ecosystems, especially wetlands that receive urban and industrial effluents. These environments are large reservoirs under anthropogenic selection pressure, favouring the persistence and transmission of multidrug-resistant (MDR) diseases. abstract: The CRISPR-Cas systems have been traditionally viewed as adaptive immune mechanisms; however, increasing evidence indicates that they also perform broader regulatory functions. abstract: Background and aims Alpine shrubs coordinate leaf display, stem support, and reproduction within short growing seasons, but the role of developmental stage in trait variation among sites and plant–soil associations remains poorly resolved. abstract: This study examined the relationship between metacognitive reading strategy awareness and critical reading self-efficacy among gifted middle school students and investigated the unique contributions of different dimensions of metacognitive reading strategies to critical reading self-efficacy. abstract: The integration of digital financial solutions has become essential for enhancing the sustainability and competitiveness of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), especially in developing economies. This study examined MSME readiness in terms of digital capability, financial literacy, infrastructure readiness, and strategic orientation in relation to the integration of digital financial systems. title: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Public Health Science Priorities for the 2026 Ebola Outbreak Caused by Bundibugyo Virus
abstract: The ongoing 2026 Ebola outbreak is growing faster than any previous outbreak of Ebola disease. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) initiated an emergency response on May 17, 2026, to help respond to this outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Incorporating CDC’s principles for public health emergency response, a science agenda was developed during May through July to detail scientific priorities and key questions guiding agency response activities. title: Identification of highly specific bacterial L-asparaginase through genome-wide computational screening and experimental validation
abstract: Abstract Background Bacterial L-asparaginases are key therapeutics for acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), but their clinical efficacy is limited by off-target L-glutaminase co-activity, which contributes to severe side effects. This study aimed to identify highly specific bacterial L-asparaginases with minimal L-glutaminase co-activity. abstract: Epoxy composites are vital for high-performance applications, but their high cost and environmental footprint drive the need for sustainable alternatives. This study investigates the mechanical behavior and sustainability of epoxy composites incorporating two specific industrial waste streams, Fir wood dust (5–20 wt%, in two particle sizes) and E-glass chopping waste (0–8 wt%). Works produced by veteran authors that draw attention to the psychological state of the soldiers are often sidelined. title: Knowledge, attitudes, practices and demand for processed fruits and vegetables among low-income consumers and retailers in Kenya
abstract: Postharvest loss of perishable fruits and vegetables is a significant challenge which can be mitigated by processing them into shelf stable products. This study investigated the knowledge, attitude and practices (KAP) on consumption as well as drivers for consumer demand of raw and processed fruits and vegetables among low-income consumers and retailers in Kenya. abstract: Oxidative stress is an early biological response to contaminant exposure and may precede irreversible impairment at the organism and ecosystem levels. However, its evaluation commonly relies on destructive biochemical assays that are poorly suited to rapid or on-site environmental assessment. Here, we report tungsten oxide-embedded nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes (CNTN-W) as an electrochemical interface for detecting extracellular hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) released by living organisms under contaminant-induced stress. title: A new species of extinct trionychid from the Early Oligocene (Orellan–Whitneyan NALMA) Brule Formation of North Dakota, USA
abstract: Softshell turtles ( Pan-Trionychidae ) have a particularly rich fossil record in North America, but only a few fragmentary remains have previously been reported from the Oligocene. abstract: Wireless implantable neurologgers are emerging as miniature autonomous systems for long-term, untethered neural recording in animal studies. However, the development of wireless systems remains constrained by critical engineering bottlenecks, including neural recording, power supply, and data transmission. abstract: Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) experiences are difficult to share with the public because they are essentially processes that rely on physical interactions with embodied, tacit, and situated phenomena in specific cultural contexts. We consume non-interactive media such as videos and books to learn about culinary ICH experiences, but they do not allow us to grasp actual interactive procedures that embody the cultural knowledge. abstract: ABSTRACT Cork oak forests are of significant environmental and socioeconomic importance in the Mediterranean basin. However, these biocenoses are facing a progressive decline due to multiple biotic and abiotic factors. Among these, Phytophthora species, particularly P. cinnamomi , remain among the primary drivers of decline. abstract: Introduction Seasonal variation in plant activity and soil processes can influence soil silicon (Si) cycling, but the season-dependent warming responses of operationally defined reactive soil silicon fractions remain poorly understood. We therefore tested whether warming effects on each of five reactive soil Si fractions depended on sampling season in a northern subtropical secondary Quercus acutissima forest. abstract: Abstract We study how the urban density of the areas where firms are located impacts their stock returns. Using high-resolution satellite images and image segmentation algorithms, we develop measures of building density for the most populated metropolitan statistical areas (MSAs) in the US. We find that firms in urban areas with a higher potential for density increase are perceived as less risky in the stock market because they can feasibly sustain their growth, leading to lower stock returns. abstract: La satisfacción académica se usa con frecuencia como indicador de calidad en la educación superior, pero en México su estudio generalmente se limita al uso de la estadística descriptiva. abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has increased the demand for secure and resource-efficient confidentiality mechanisms in constrained environments. abstract: Osteoporosis is a systemic skeletal disorder characterized by reduced bone mass, microarchitectural deterioration, and increased fracture risk. However, long-term use of current pharmacological therapies is often associated with adverse effects, underscoring the urgent need for safer and more sustainable intervention strategies. abstract: This study examines the relationships among Dark Triad personality traits, work engagement, and organizational citizenship behavior in higher education institutions. abstract: Text-to-image generative models have achieved remarkable capabilities in producing photorealistic images, but raise concerns about misuse for generating harmful content. While safety mechanisms exist, systematic evaluations of their effectiveness against realistic attacks remain limited. This paper presents a comprehensive assessment of harmful content generation across modern text-to-image models using an automated pipeline that transforms legitimate news captions into unsafe prompts targeting sexually explicit content, violent imagery, harmful stereotypes, self-harm, and hate speech. abstract: Abstract Europe finds itself adrift in a world of rising geopolitical uncertainty. Russia has brought interstate war back to Europe. abstract: Abstract: Non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM), a diverse collection of environmentally ubiquitous pathogens, are emerging as a significant global public health concern with rising incidence and prevalence. NTM infections occur predominantly in immunocompromised populations and present as pulmonary, disseminated, and skin/soft tissue infections. abstract: Clarity of knowledge and reasoning is necessary in many cases. Yet vagueness in scientific thinking related to surprise, curiosity, and "ability to engage with not-knowing" (de Freitas) is also a crucially important source of scientific creativity. abstract: La energía solar es una fuente energética renovable con un gran potencial en el importante desafío tecnológico de la transición energética. abstract: ABSTRACT The rare event of an extremely bright explosion of a classical nova in 1901 gave birth to GK Per (Nova 1901). GK Per is one of the closest cataclysmic variables whose central binary consists of a magnetic white dwarf and a K2‐type subgiant. abstract: Biological nitrogen removal in wastewater treatment has long been described as a two-step process, in which ammonia is oxidized aerobically to nitrate and nitrate is reduced anoxically to dinitrogen gas. title: The seeds of tomorrow: SEAD reference panel promotes genomics in Asian human populations
abstract: Success of a genome-wide association study (GWAS) depends on the density of variants available for analysis; these variants are sometimes rare and ancestry-specific. Imputation of un-genotyped variants is used to boost the resolution and power of GWAS; however, majority of large imputation reference panels do not adequately reflect the populations of Asia, which comprise approximately 60% of the world’s population. title: Spatial variation and seasonal dynamics of Earias vittella (Fabricius) and its association with weather conditions in Himalayan okra-growing environments
abstract: The shoot and fruit borer, Earias vittella (Fabricius), is an important pest of okra, and its occurrence may vary considerably across contrasting agro-climatic environments. The present study assessed the spatial variation and seasonal population dynamics of E. vittella at selected low- and mid-hill locations of Himachal Pradesh, India, and examined associations between pest activity and prevailing weather conditions. abstract: This study examined visitor satisfaction and revisit intention at Lakay Ago Nature’s Park in Agoo, La Union. abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) comprises four antigenically distinct serotypes, complicating the development of broadly active antiviral agents. abstract: Agriculture is the cornerstone of Ethiopia’s economy, yet its productivity is constrained by soil degradation, inefficient land management, and uniform application of inputs. abstract: Introduction Digital rural intellectual property (IP) has become a practical means by which villages turn local distinctiveness into transmissible cultural assets, yet little is known about how its visual symbols relate to the emotional bond audiences form with a place, particularly in the ethnic autonomous regions of western China. abstract: As global plastic pollution continues to intensify, microplastics and nanoplastics (MPs/NPs) have become widely distributed in air, water, the food chain, and even the human body, constituting a novel environmental exposure that is difficult to avoid. abstract: Cave-dwelling bats face escalating anthropogenic pressures globally, yet their conservation is frequently compromised by limited community ecological literacy, persistent cultural myths, and inadequate integration of community and institutional perspectives into management. abstract: El objetivo del artículo fue analizar los fundamentos y las condiciones de pertinencia para crear un centro universitario tecnológico en Asunción, orientado al desarrollo económico y social regional, con referencia temporal en octubre de 2026. Se elaboró una síntesis documental de alcance descriptivo, analítico y propositivo a partir de una revisión sistemática de literatura especializada y reportes de organismos internacionales. La organización del material siguió cuatro ejes: problemática formativa y productiva, competencias tecnológicas, vinculación institucional y condiciones de inclusión

title: Fundamental evaluation of distributed optical fiber sensing method for excavation damaged zone during underground cavern excavation
abstract: Rock masses inherently contain numerous fractures ranging from micro- to macro-scale. When excavating caverns within rock masses, these fractures become active. Consequently, the stress field around the cavern is disturbed, leading to stress redistribution. Furthermore, the groundwater environment may also change. Accurately understanding these phenomena enables evaluation of cavern stability and the optimal scale of support structures. title: Assessment of trace metals in irrigation water, soil, and vegetables along the US-Mexico border and their health risks
abstract: The Rio Grande, an important river that borders the USA and Mexico is recharged with untreated and treated wastewaters from binational sources and therefore is known to contain potentially toxic elements (PTEs) like As, Cd, Co, Cr, Pb, and Sb. These elements are nonbiodegradable and can accumulate in soil and crops when contaminated surface water is used for irrigation. title: Dampak Kesulitan Keuangan terhadap Indikasi Praktik Greenwashing: Analisis Peran Mediasi Inovasi Hijau
abstract: Greenwashing has become a critical issue in corporate sustainability implementation; however, research on the impact of financial distress on greenwashing remains limited and yields inconsistent results. This study addresses this gap by examining the role of green innovation as a mediating variable in the relationship between financial distress and greenwashing, drawing upon legitimacy theory and stakeholder theory. The study focuses on energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange from 2020 to 2024, utilizing a sample of 87 companies (comprising 267 observations after outlier

title: Controversy: Anticoagulants need to be maintained after catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation in patients at risk of stroke—Pro and Contra
abstract: The pillars of atrial fibrillation (AF) management include stroke prevention, patient-centred symptom directed decisions on rhythm or rate control, and the proactive management of comorbidities and lifestyle changes. These pillars are not in isolation; they are complementary to each other. While oral anticoagulants (OACs) are highly effective for reducing stroke and all-cause mortality in patients with AF, these drugs confer a risk of major bleeding, including intracranial bleeding. title: A review of cylindrical interfacial instability in viscous and Rivlin–Ericksen viscoelastic fluids under multiphysics effects
abstract: Interfacial instability is important in many engineering and industrial applications involving viscous and viscoelastic fluid systems. This review systematically examines Kelvin–Helmholtz, Rayleigh–Taylor, capillary, and cylindrical instabilities, with particular emphasis on Rivlin–Ericksen viscoelastic fluids, based on a systematic search of seven databases covering publications from 1992 to 2026, from which 285 of 1,256 identified studies met the inclusion criteria. title: A GIS ‐Based Method to Prioritize Railway Links for Climate Resilience Planning Based on Operational Exposure
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional climate risk assessments typically consider hazard, exposure, and vulnerability dimensions, but often restrict exposure to spatial hazard intersections, neglecting the operational intensity of infrastructure. This study proposes a geographic information systems (GIS)‐based framework that uses operational exposure derived from freight and passenger flows as the primary metric for network prioritization. title: Saindhava Lavana in Visha Chikitsa: An Integrative Review of Ayurveda Concepts and Contemporary Scientific Evidence
abstract: Introduction: Saindhava Lavana (rock salt) is unique in Ayurveda, serving as a daily wholesome substance and a therapeutic agent in classical toxicology (Visha Chikitsa).This review explores its dual therapeutic and toxicological profile, formulation roles, and dosage paradoxes.Materials and methods: Classical Ayurvedic treatises (Charaka Samhita, Sushuruta Samhita, Ashtanga Hridaya) and modern scientific literature were reviewed to analyze the mineral composition, bio-enhancement mechanisms, and toxicological impacts of Saindhava Lavana.Results: Textual analysis shows its Deepana (appetizing)
journal: Journal of Indian System of Medicine

title: Phenological characterization and thermal requirements of prominent cultivars of litchi in the Indo-Gangetic Plain
abstract: Aim: Litchi (Litchi chinensis Sonn.) exhibits marked phenological variability among cultivars, which influences productivity and climate adaptability. This study aimed to characterize and compare the phenological behavior of ‘Shahi’ and ‘China’ using the extended BBCH (Biologische Bundesanstalt, Bundessortenamt and Chemische Industrie) scale and to examine the influence of thermal indices on phenophase progression. title: From intestinal barrier sensing to glial immune programming: a barrier–immune–glia relay in microbiota-associated neurodegeneration
abstract: The gut microbiota contributes to host homeostasis through metabolic, immunological, neural, and barrier-related pathways, and its role in the onset and progression of neurodegenerative diseases has received increasing attention. Patients with Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis often exhibit alterations in gut microbial composition, microbial metabolic function, and peripheral inflammatory phenotypes. title: Sustainable biosorptive recovery of Mn2+ from low grade manganese ore leachate using NaOH activated Artocarpus heterophyllus seed derived biosorbent
abstract: Sustainable recovery of manganese from low-grade ores requires efficient and environmentally compatible approaches for treating ore-derived leachates. This study investigates Mn 2+ recovery from an actual manganese-rich pregnant leach solution (PLS) using NaOH-activated Artocarpus heterophyllus Lam. seed biomass (NaOH – Ah SB), an agro-waste-derived biosorbent. title: Beyond antimicrobials: multifunctional biomaterials for tissue regeneration
abstract: Biomaterial-associated infections remain a major obstacle in regenerative medicine, wound healing, and implantology. While conventional anti-infective materials have mainly focused on preventing bacterial adhesion or delivering antimicrobial agents, infection control alone is often not enough to restore tissue function. title: Boosting Visible‐Light Photocatalytic Degradation Performance of Au Nanocatalysts Through O 2 Plasma Activation
abstract: ABSTRACT Gold (Au) nanocatalysts are promising for visible‐light‐driven environmental remediation, yet constructing highly active, stable Au catalysts for liquid‐phase pollutant degradation remains challenging. Herein, plasma activation was employed as an alternative to conventional calcination for TiO 2 ‐supported Au nanocatalysts. title: Educación de jóvenes y adultos en Ecuador: Equidad educativa, inclusión y desarrollo humano
abstract: La educación de personas jóvenes y adultas con escolaridad inconclusa constituye una dimensión del derecho al aprendizaje a lo largo de la vida y un componente potencial de las políticas de equidad en Ecuador; este artículo examina críticamente su relevancia para la inclusión social y el desarrollo humano, con especial atención a las modalidades de alfabetización, educación general básica y bachillerato; se desarrolló una revisión documental crítica de fuentes normativas, publicaciones institucionales y literatura científica, seleccionadas por su pertinencia temática, trazabilidad y capacidad

title: Comparative Case Study of Production Efficiency, Financial Performance, and Business Risk in Laying Hen Farms with Different Housing Systems and Management Conditions
abstract: The laying hen sector continues to expand in response to increasing demand for animal protein; however, productivity remains sensitive to environmental conditions, particularly temperature fluctuations that affect production stability. The housing system represents a key management factor influencing farm performance. This study aims to compare production efficiency, financial performance, and business risk between closed-house and open-house laying hen systems. title: Network toxicology, molecular docking and in vitro validation reveal the molecular mechanisms of bisphenol A-induced MASLD
abstract: Background Bisphenol A (BPA), a ubiquitous endocrine-disrupting chemical, is associated with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Methods This study combined network toxicology and molecular docking to explore BPA-induced hepatotoxicity targets and pathways in MASLD. title: Time-dependent pharmacokinetic changes and renal SGLT2 expression alterations of dapagliflozin under high-altitude hypoxia in diabetic rats
abstract: Objective This study investigated the time-dependent effects of high-altitude hypoxia on the pharmacokinetics (PK), renal sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) expression, and glycemic response to dapagliflozin in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) rats. Methods T2DM was induced in male Wistar rats via high-fat diet and low-dose streptozotocin. title: Continuing Professional Development in Medical Laboratory Sciences, Dental Assisting, Nursing, And Health Administration
abstract: Background: Continuing professional development (CPD) is expected to maintain competence as technology, regulation, service models and patient expectations change. Evidence and regulatory systems are uneven across medical laboratory sciences, dental assisting, nursing and health administration. CPD also informs clinical competence and organizational decisions about training priorities and workforce resources.Objective: To map current CPD practices, requirements, delivery methods, participation patterns, barriers, facilitators, outcomes and future competency needs across the four professions. title: Natural products and extracellular vesicle-associated miRNA networks in perianal infectious wound healing: a critical ethnopharmacological appraisal
abstract: Perianal infectious wounds form a contaminated, moist, mechanically disturbed repair niche that differs from standard cutaneous wounds. This critical narrative review evaluates whether natural-product pharmacology and extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated miRNA biology can be linked credibly in this setting. A structured PubMed search updated through 29 September 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar citation tracking, identified direct human perianal studies, anatomically relevant and infection-relevant animal studies, and mechanistically relevant in vitro and in silico evidence. title: Copper single-atom catalysts and cooperative Cu motifs for CO2 electroreduction: working-state evidence for C1 and C2+ formation
abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction (eCO2RR) can convert captured CO2 and renewable electricity into fuels and chemical feedstocks, but selective C-C coupling to C 2+ products remains a central challenge. Copper single-atom catalysts (Cu-SACs) provide atomic-level control of coordination, electronic structure, and metal-support interactions; however, their isolation can limit adjacent adsorption sites and the local *CO coverage needed for multicarbon formation. title: ECONOMIC VIABILITY ASSESSMENT OF ON-GRID PHOTOVOLTAIC SOLAR POWER PLANTS IN THE NORTH DISTRICT OF THE ANDAMAN AND NICOBAR ISLANDS
abstract: This study investigates the economic viability of on-grid solar photovoltaic (PV) systems in the North District of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands through an integrated techno-economic and econometric framework. The analysis examines 15 grid-connected PV projects, ranging from 50 kW to 2 MW, incorporating project-level observations and technical and financial parameters covering 2015–2025. title: Comparative phytolith profiles of the weed grasses Echinochloa colona and Echinochloa crus-galli (Poaceae): implications for species taxonomy
abstract: Introduction Taxonomic delimitation of closely related Echinochloa species is frequently complicated by morphological plasticity and overlapping vegetative characters, necessitating complementary diagnostic approaches. This study aimed to evaluate whether integrated phytolith characteristics can provide reliable discriminatory features for distinguishing Echinochloa colona and E. crus-galli . title: Effects of structure and conduct on the performance of small-scale dairy farmer groups in Kericho and Nakuru counties, Kenya: a panel data study
abstract: Milk productivity among small-scale dairy farmers in Kenya remains below potential despite widespread participation in farmer groups designed to enhance agricultural practices and managerial skills. Persistent output disparities across similarly trained groups suggest that internal organizational dynamics may be influencing performance. This study used a group-level panel dataset covering 2018–2021 to examine how group structure and leadership conduct affect the performance of small-scale dairy farmer groups in Kericho and Nakuru counties. title: Land use transitions drive ecosystem service supply–demand balance: spatiotemporal assessment and risk zoning in the Three Gorges Reservoir Area (Hubei section)
abstract: Growing human interference with natural ecosystems has positioned land use transition as a dominant force shaping the supply–demand equilibrium of ecosystem services (ESs). Focusing on the ecologically vulnerable Three Gorges Reservoir Area (Hubei section), this study examined how land use changes from 2000 to 2020 influenced water yield (WY), carbon storage (CS), food production (FP), and soil retention (SR). title: Sustained Higher Education Expansion and Firms' Productivity: Evidence From China
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the relationship between China's sustained higher education expansion and the productivity of A‐share listed firms from 2004 to 2020. We find that a larger supply of university graduates is associated with significantly higher firm total factor productivity (TFP) on average, a result robust to extensive testing. Mechanism analysis points to three plausible channels: an increased share of skilled labor, strengthened innovation, and accelerated digital transformation. However, the relationship is asymmetric. abstract: Computing excitonic spectra in quasicrystal and super-moiré systems constitutes a formidable challenge due to the exceptional size of the excitonic Hilbert space. title: Global-scale meteorological-to-groundwater drought propagation and the drivers and patterns of multi-year groundwater drought
abstract: Abstract. Groundwater stores a third of all global freshwater and supports water supply, irrigation and ecosystems across the world. As such, groundwater drought can have wide-reaching financial, social and environmental impacts, particularly when drought events are prolonged or multi-year. title: “We are just blind there”: institutional invisibility of female genital schistosomiasis in South Africa
abstract: Introduction Female Genital Schistosomiasis (FGS) remains severely overlooked within neglected tropical diseases (NTDs), disproportionately affecting women in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Despite its high prevalence and association with adverse reproductive health outcomes and increased HIV susceptibility, FGS receives minimal attention in research, policy, and clinical practice. abstract: Introduction The recovery of multi-trophic soil communities is pivotal to ecological restoration of reclaimed coal mining areas, yet their succession and the driving mechanisms of soil multifunctionality (SMF) across regional gradients remain poorly understood. Methods We investigated three reclaimed coal mining areas in Shanxi Province, China-Pingshuo (north), Gujiao (central), and Qinshui (south)-using a 25-year chronosequence of Pinus tabuliformis plantations ( n = 75). title: The ESPA model as a strategic framework for sustainable human resource management in seasonal hospitality
abstract: This study aims to conceptualize and empirically examine the ESPA Model (Environment–Support–Performance–Appreciation) as a strategic framework for sustainable human resource management (SHRM) in seasonal luxury hospitality. Employing a positivist epistemological stance and a quantitative, cross-sectional explanatory design, data were collected via structured surveys from 312 employees across five-star seasonal hotels in Crete, Greece. title: Experimental investigation of microstructural and performance evolution in ultrasonic-assisted stir-cast AA8011–5 wt.% TiB2 composites during multi-pass equal-channel angular pressing
abstract: The development of aluminium matrix composites with improved structural and tribological performance has attracted considerable interest for lightweight engineering applications. This work investigates the microstructural, mechanical, tribological, and hot-deformation response of an AA8011 aluminium composite containing 5 wt.% TiB2, fabricated by ultrasonic-assisted stir casting and subsequently processed by equal-channel angular pressing (ECAP). title: Exploring the relationship between cultural landscapes and psychological well-being through indigenous environmental design in rural China
abstract: Introduction Indigenous environmental design in rural China is increasingly affected by modernization, tourism development, and ecological change. However, empirical evidence concerning the relationship between cultural landscape fidelity and residents’ psychological well-being remains limited. title: Tumor location in the pancreatic body/tail as an independent risk factor for early recurrence after curative resection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: a single-center retrospective study
abstract: Background Early recurrence after radical resection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a primary cause of poor prognosis. Published definitions of early recurrence use postoperative cutoff points ranging from 6 to 12 months. This study aimed to analyze perioperative clinicopathological features associated with early recurrence after PDAC surgery, with particular focus on the impact of tumor location, to facilitate individualized treatment decisions. title: Chatbots municipales y vacío normativo en la Administración Pública argentina
abstract: En los últimos años, distintos municipios argentinos han incorporado chatbots y asistentes virtuales como canal de atención ciudadana y de acceso a trámites de asistencia social, siguiendo el modelo pionero de Boti, del Gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires. Este artículo analiza dicho fenómeno desde la perspectiva del derecho administrativo y de los estándares internacionales de derechos económicos, sociales, culturales y ambientales (DESCA), a partir de un relevamiento de seis casos municipales (Tigre, San Isidro, Vicente López, Quilmes, Lanús y Zárate) y del caso testigo de Boti (CABA). title: Traditional Medicine Use and Pharmacist Involvement Among Patients with Diabetes and Hypertension in Semarang, Indonesia: A Cross-sectional Study
abstract: Patients with diabetes or hypertension often take traditional medicine alongside prescribed drugs, yet little is known about how they involve pharmacists in that use. This descriptive cross-sectional study enrolled 110 adult users of traditional medicine, recruited by purposive sampling at a community health centre and a private clinic in Semarang, Indonesia, and surveyed them with a structured questionnaire. title: Differential DNA methylation profiling of spermatogenesis-associated genes in patients with idiopathic hypospermatogenesis: a hospital-based case-control study
abstract: Hypospermatogenesis is a histopathological subtype of non-obstructive azoospermia and is characterized by a decrease in the total number of germ cells within the seminiferous tubule as a result of spermatogenic failure. Germ cell epigenetic reprograming during development shows that the methylation status of testicular DNA is highly distinct in which hypomethylated foci predominates. title: Morphological, Palynological and Micromorphological Investigations on Unusual Tanacetum nivale Sch.Bip. (Asteraceae)
abstract: The genus Tanacetum L., is one of the cosmopolitan members of the tribe Anthemideae (Asteraceae), encompassing approximately 160 species. Within Türkiye, 61 taxa are recorded, 27 of which are endemic. This research investigates Tanacetum nivale Sch.Bip. using LM and SEM to assess its morphological, pollen, and achene traits, providing additional characters that may assist in resolving systematic issues within the genus. title: Treeline ecotones as habitat archipelagos for spiders: A case study from the Alps
abstract: Trees surrounded by low–stature alpine vegetation may function as habitat islands for canopy fauna. We examined whether diversity patterns of canopy–dwelling specialist spiders in an alpine treeline ecotone in the French Alps aligned with predictions of island biogeography. We focused on the lower canopy of pine (evergreen) and larch (deciduous) trees, collecting data in Spring, Summer and Autumn. title: “La intuición acompaña el/al experimento” El MDO con predicados reversibles – un ejemplo de métodos mixtos con datos experimentales e intuiciones metalingüísticas expresadas
abstract: Esta contribución enfoca el uso de una metodología mixta, en concreto la combinación de experimentos lingüísticos y entrevistas metalingüísticas. title: A comparative legal analysis of migratory bird conservation along the African–Eurasian flyway
abstract: Despite decades of international agreements aimed at biodiversity conservation, millions of migratory birds continue to be illegally killed each year along the African-Eurasian flyway, particularly in the Mediterranean, posing a persistent challenge to global conservation efforts. We compared legal frameworks in 10 countries to determine how implementation gaps have emerged between conservation legislation and enforcement. abstract: Polysaccharides derived from Ophiocordyceps (Chinese Cordyceps) exhibit notable bioactivities, yet their high molecular weight may limit their fermentability by the gut microbiota, thereby modulating the production of bioactive metabolites. This study aimed to prepare low-molecular-weight Ophiocordyceps polysaccharides (OPs) through enzymatic modification and to elucidate the associated structural alterations and mechanisms underlying intestinal barrier regulation. title: El papel de las inversiones europeas: aprendizajes nacionales
abstract: Las inversiones de la Unión Europea han desempeñado un papel decisivo en la modernización económica de España desde su adhesión, pero su contribución efectiva a la convergencia territorial, la transformación productiva y el crecimiento potencial sigue siendo objeto de debate. abstract: The human extracellular matrix (ECM) is a key regulator of tumor progression, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance, making its accurate reproduction essential for the development of physiologically relevant in vitro cancer models. Among advanced biofabrication technologies, extrusion-based bioprinting enables the fabrication of reproducible three-dimensional (3D) tumor models with controlled structural and mechanical properties. abstract: Introduction Exopolysaccharides (EPSs) are complex carbohydrate structures that play an incredible role in immunomodulation and mitigating inflammatory factors. This study examines the anticancer and anti-inflammatory activities of EPS produced by Pediococcus pentosaceus 4412. Methods We performed probiotic assays on isolated P. pentosaceus 4412 and assessed the in vitro antioxidant potential of the extracted EPS-4412. abstract: Podismopsis kristini sp. nov . (Orthoptera, Acrididae, Gomphocerinae) is described from the Tatras in Slovakia, representing the seventh European species of the genus Podismopsis Zubovski, 1900, and the first record of the genus from the Western Carpathians. title: Development and validation of an optimized spiking strategy for cross‐layer transfer of near‐infrared soil organic matter models
abstract: Abstract Soil organic matter (SOM) is crucial for soil fertility and is strongly linked to soil productivity. The heterogeneity of soil at different depths leads to variations in spectral characteristics. abstract: Objetivo: Se analizó el diseño de un sistema de control industrial basado en un controlador lógico programable (PLC) para automatizar el arranque y fortalecer la protección de motores eléctricos trifásicos, considerando su importancia para mejorar la seguridad y la continuidad operativa en entornos industriales. title: Dual Hydrogen Donor‐Mediated Reduction of Nitroarenes Over a Magnetically Recoverable CoFe 2 O 4 @GO Nanocomposite: Mechanistic and Kinetic Insights
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing high‐performance and sustainable catalytic systems for reduction of nitroaromatics remains an important objective in both environmental remediation and synthetic chemistry. We report herein a CoFe 2 O 4 @GO catalytic system synthesized using co‐precipitation method as a magnetically recoverable heterogeneous catalytic system for the selective reduction of nitroarenes into corresponding amines using sodium borohydride and hydrazine hydrate as reducing agents. title: Beyond electricity generation: Nuclear power plants as circular chemical manufacturing hubs for plastic waste valorization
abstract: Abstract Large nuclear power plants have traditionally been regarded as facilities dedicated to electricity generation. This study proposes a systems‐level concept in which they function as circular chemical manufacturing hubs integrating plastic waste valorization, hydrogen production, carbon utilization, and downstream polymer synthesis within a unified industrial complex. institutions: University of West Bohemia in Pilsen

title: Evaluation of health and economic impacts of atmospheric PM₂.₅ in Tabriz, Iran, using BenMAP-CE and AirQ+
abstract: Air pollution poses a major threat to public health and carries the highest burden of environmentally related diseases. This study evaluated mortality associated with long-term exposure to PM₂.₅ and the corresponding economic burden in Tabriz city. The analysis was conducted using the BenMAP-CE and AirQ⁺ software. We evaluated five scenarios concerning the annual average PM₂.₅ concentration: increases to 35 and 25 µg/m³, decreases to 15 and 10 µg/m³, and a reduction to the theoretical minimum risk level of 2.4 µg/m³. title: Identification of patterns of intra-varietal variation and selection of promising clonal forms of local and introduced grape varieties
abstract: The object of research is the variability and clonal forms within populations of local and introduced grape varieties, analyzing their morphometric and biometric traits. The research material consisted of local and introduced grape varieties cultivated in the Absheron collection vineyard of the Research Institute of Viticulture and Winemaking (Baku, Azerbaijan). A significant challenge lies in the insufficient understanding of the intra-varietal genetic and phenotypic diversity of local and introduced grape varieties, as well as the clonal variations that have emerged within their populations.

title: Drivers of basal respiration rate in intact samples from carbon-rich lowland soils across Denmark
abstract: Soil basal respiration rate (BRR) measured under controlled laboratory conditions is an important indicator of a soil's microbial CO 2 production potential. Although temperature and drainage status are known to control BRR, the relative importance of physical, chemical, and microbial controls remains poorly understood, particularly in organic soils. BRR was measured on intact topsoil samples from 112 carbon-rich lowland soils in Denmark at 15°C at a soil-water matric potential corresponding to field capacity (pF = 2), alongside a range of soil physical, chemical and biological properties. title: If you think twice, you might not forget: inhibition and memory-maintenance trade-offs in Russian single vs. Hausa bipartite negation
abstract: Several approaches have attempted to explain the skewed distribution across languages and regions of bipartite compared to single negation, the latter unequivocally the most common, but still often subject to diachronic change. It is a paradox that double negation arises, among other things, to strengthen negation semantically or define its scope, while at the same time, this fortification may lead to its demise. Several grammaticalization pathways result in double, discontinuous negation typologies negating single events or constituents, but such constructions seem to be inherently unstable.
journal: Slovo Journal of Slavic Languages Literatures and Cultures

title: Thermal radiation and activation energy effects on triple-stratified Darcy–Forchheimer flow of micropolar nanofluid with gyrotactic microorganisms over a porous vertical stretching sheet
abstract: This study presents a unified mathematical model for the triple-stratified Darcy-Forchheimer flow of a micropolar nanofluid containing gyrotactic microorganisms over a porous vertical stretching sheet by simultaneously incorporating thermal radiation, viscous dissipation, activation energy, Brownian motion, thermophoresis, mixed convection, and porous medium effects. The mathematical formulation accounts for momentum, thermal, solutal, nanoparticle, and microorganism stratifications together with bioconvection induced by gyrotactic microorganisms. title: Unexpected fault reactivation during underground gas storage in depleted reservoirs: defining operational pressure bandwidths
abstract: Introduction Underground gas storage and emerging subsurface storage applications for CO 2 , H 2 , and N 2 increasingly rely on depleted, faulted reservoirs. In such settings, pressure recovery and cyclic operations may bring faults close to reactivation even when reservoir pressure remains below the initial value and within the range previously experienced during primary production. We investigate how stress redistribution caused by previous fault slip influences fault criticality during subsequent pressure recovery and storage operations. title: Simultaneous Bayesian quantification and decomposition of structural, parameter, and forcing uncertainty in hydrologic models: A blended model approach
abstract: Disentangling the contributions of structural, parametric, and forcing uncertainty to hydrological model predictions remains a long-standing challenge. This study proposes a unified Bayesian framework that jointly quantifies and temporally decomposes these three uncertainty sources in streamflow prediction. The blended model structure of Mai et al. title: Windthrow of Forest Trees and Its Effect on Tree Regeneration and Diversity of Understory in the Hyrcanian Temperate Upland Forests of Iran
abstract: Windthrow is a major natural disturbance shaping canopy dynamics in temperate forests, yet high-elevation (upland) Hyrcanian forests remain poorly studied, particularly with respect to regeneration responses and topographic controls. This study examined windfall effects in Dashte Daman forests, northern Iran (1027–1629 m elevation). First, 90 systematically distributed 50 × 50 m sample plots were established across a 300 × 300 m grid on a stratified map including affected and unaffected areas. title: Digitally Printed Eco‐Friendly Electronic Devices
abstract: ABSTRACT The sustainable life cycle of electronics is one of the major challenges of modern society. Moreover, the manufacturing of conventional electronics significantly impacts the environment due to the extensive consumption of raw materials, energy, and the release of harmful byproducts. In this regard, manufacturing of electronics using eco‐friendly materials through digital printing routes represents a promising and sustainable solution. title: Algorithmic Recommendation-Driven Value Cognition in the Practical Teaching of Ideological and Political Theory Courses: Double-Edged Effects and Intervention Paths
abstract: The algorithmic recommendation technology has been deeply involved into the information receiving environment of educational subjects that not only change the way of presenting value issues, but also profoundly influence the construction of value cognition. title: Mutual scaffolding: The convergence of smart city and blue-green-grey infrastructure discourses
abstract: Smart-city and blue-green-grey infrastructure (BGGI) scholarship emerged from distinct intellectual traditions—one centered on digital technologies and urban management, the other on ecological planning and nature-based infrastructure—yet a growing body of work now operates at their intersection. This paper presents a qualitative content analysis of the literature operating within the smart-city–BGGI overlap, using a systematic mapping approach, with documented searches of Web of Science, Scopus, EBSCOhost and Google Scholar, reported according to PRISMA 2020. title: Understanding social-ecological vulnerability in goat pastoral systems through a participatory multi-stakeholder spatial assessment
abstract: Dryland pastoral systems are increasingly affected by the interrelation between socioenvironmental variability and change with land degradation. In Mexico, goat pastoralism (CaprinoCultura) represents a key social-ecological system (SES) that sustains rural livelihoods under highly constrained conditions. This study examined how social-ecological drivers operating across household, ejido and regional scales shape the vulnerability of CaprinoCultura in the Altiplano Potosino. title: Morocco’s Energy Mix in the Context of Global Climate Change: A Socioeconomic Perspective
abstract: As global climate challenges intensify, the transition toward low-carbon energy systems has become a central pillar of national sustainability strategies. Morocco, with limited fossil fuel resources and growing energy demand, has embarked on an ambitious energy transition aimed at enhancing energy security, promoting renewable energy, and contributing to global climate mitigation efforts. title: Phylogenetic correlation between the Type IV Secretion System and HIP1 suggest an adaptation for horizontal gene transfer conserved at the phylum level
abstract: ABSTRACT Most cyanobacterial genomes are rich in the GCGATCGC octamer, also known as Highly Iterated Palindrome 1 (HIP1). Despite its description over three decades ago, the biological function of this highly abundant sequence is only beginning to be elucidated. HIP1 is recognized by two DNA methylases, DmtA and DmtC, and is characterized by its evolutionary conservation and a quasi-periodic distribution within genomes. title: The impact of population growth on land-use: a system dynamics model for sustainable land-use planning in the Elgon Region of Uganda
abstract: Land-use and land-cover change poses major environmental challenge in regions where population growth increasingly drives encroachment into ecologically sensitive landscapes. This challenge arises from the dynamics of interacting feedbacks among; demographic change, declining household land size, ecosystem degradation, and delayed institutional responses. Previous studies in the context of Uganda, have investigated these factors, either independently or in pairs, but not holistically. title: Rethinking intraspecific diagnostics in Lymantria dispar: from traditional taxonomy to population genomics
abstract: The spongy moth, Lymantria dispar , provides a compelling example of how advances in genomic methods can reshape the practical interpretation of intraspecific taxonomy. Historically, geographic forms of this species were differentiated on the basis of morphology, geographic range, and female flight capability; subsequently, a three-subspecies framework comprising L. d. dispar, L. d. asiatica , and L. d. japonica became widely adopted. title: High-Order Simulation of Particle-Laden Flows in Moving Domains Using Coupled ALE and Sliding Mesh Approaches
abstract: In practical applications, compressible particle-laden flows in moving geometries involve complex, non-linear, and multi-scale interactions with turbulent structures. Resolving these dynamics numerically requires careful algorithmic treatment to accurately predict particle trajectories. This work presents a high-fidelity Euler–Lagrange framework that couples a high-order discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method for the continuous phase with a Lagrangian point-particle tracking scheme. title: Modelo de Gobernanza para el Uso Responsable de la Inteligencia Artificial en la Gestión del Riesgo Tributario: Una Propuesta Aplicable a Ecuador y América Latina
abstract: La incorporación de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en la administración tributaria ha trastocado la gestión del riesgo tributario y ha brindado a los órganos de control del gasto público herramientas de predicción masiva y de análisis de datos. journal: LATAM Revista Latinoamericana de Ciencias Sociales y Humanidades

title: How Do Soil Properties and Canopy Status Influence Potato Traits while Continuously Monitoring Soil Moisture with Iot-Based Sensors?
abstract: Abstract Many soil-related factors associated with potato yield and quality are implicitly linked to soil water availability (SWA). This soil property also affects potato canopy, which could be indirectly evaluated using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). The objective of this study was to quantify the optimal explanatory soil- and canopy state-related properties that determine potato ( Solanum tuberosum L.) traits: total yield (TY), dry matter (DM) content, and average tuber weight (ATW) over a rainfed production field. title: Mindfulness‐Based Intervention Improves Cognitive Function in Patients With Schizophrenia in Remitted: A Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with schizophrenia exhibit deficits in facial emotion recognition (FER), attention, P300, and quality of life (QoL), which severely hinder functional recovery. This study aims to explore the effects of mindfulness-based intervention (MBI) on these outcomes and the potential mediating mechanisms. METHODS: In this 8-week randomized, single-blind, controlled study, a total of 70 remitted patients with schizophrenia were randomly assigned to the MBI group or the control group. title: How immersive experiences carry over across the customer journey: A two-stage study of virtual reality in heritage tourism
abstract: Despite growing interest in virtual reality (VR) in heritage tourism contexts, empirical evidence on its value beyond single-use applications across the customer journey remains limited. This research examines the effectiveness of VR across the visit and post-visit stages of the tourism customer journey and their interrelated effects across successive stages. Grounded in the integrative stimulus–organism–response framework, the study adopts a two-stage design. title: Antidiabetic potential of cocoa bean shell extract (Theobroma Cacao L.): phytochemical profile, Α-glucosidase inhibition and ex vivo GLP-1 secretion
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) affects approximately 537 million adults worldwide, demanding therapeutic strategies that mitigate postprandial hyperglycemia. This study investigated the antidiabetic potential of the aqueous extract of cocoa bean shell (AECB), an agro-industrial by-product, through phytochemical characterization and biological assays of enzymatic and incretin modulation. title: Investigating the Asymmetric Effect and Moon Cycle of Vietnam Stock Index Returns: An Approach Based on Extended GARCH Models
abstract: The study focuses on investigating the asymmetry and moon cycle effects of the Vietnam stock index (VN-Index) return series by estimating extended GARCH models. The data used are the daily closing prices of the VN-Index traded on the Vietnam stock market on the HoSE from 2000 to 2024, with a total of 1129 trading days. The results show that the VN-Index possesses significant characteristics of time variation and clustering, which are characteristic of the ARCH and GARCH effects of financial time series. title: Study design and rationale for the Dog Aging Project Pack: a prospective, long-term, longitudinal, observational study of biological and environmental determinants of healthy aging in US companion dogs
abstract: Companion dogs are a valuable source of translational discovery about the basic biology of aging because of their well-characterized genome, phenotypic variation in lifespan, aging, and disease profiles, and diverse environmental exposures shared with their human owners. The Dog Aging Project (DAP)'s prospective, longitudinal open cohort study was begun in 2019 to investigate the biological and environmental determinants of healthy aging in companion dogs. title: Integración de tecnologías digitales y calidad educativa escolar: revisión crítica de la evidencia
abstract: El objetivo fue analizar críticamente la contribución de las tecnologías digitales a la calidad educativa escolar. Se realizó una revisión narrativa estructurada en Scopus, delimitada a artículos en español del área de Ciencias Sociales publicados entre 2022 y 2026. Se recuperaron 31 registros; tras eliminar un duplicado y excluir seis por falta de pertinencia, se seleccionaron 24 publicaciones. La síntesis se organizó en cuatro ejes: aprendizaje y desempeño; experiencia educativa y bienestar; equidad e inclusión; y competencias digitales y condiciones institucionales. title: Precision Fermentation for Next Generation Food Ingredients: Technological Foundations, Food Applications, Sustainability, and Regulatory Challenges
abstract: ABSTRACT Precision fermentation has emerged as one of the most transformative approaches in contemporary food biotechnology, enabling the targeted production of high‐value food ingredients through engineered microorganisms. title: An energy-efficient approach to sludge drying: Simulation and optimization of a heat pump assisted low-temperature belt dryer
abstract: Sludge drying is the most energy-intensive and carbon-emitting stage in the sludge treatment and disposal process. The thermal drying technologies currently employed generally exhibit high energy consumption, which increases the overall cost and energy demand of sludge management. To solve this problem, this study designed a novel heat pump-assisted low-temperature belt dryer with a center-return air configuration to enhance drying uniformity and efficiency. title: Integrating heat stress tolerance indices based on grain yield for the selection of resilient wheat genotypes
abstract: Wheat productivity is threatened by terminal heat stress, which hampers yields 6-10% per 1 °C above optimal temperatures during grain filling. Although heat stress tolerance indices offer objective selection criteria, their individual effectiveness varies with genetic background and environment. This study evaluated 230 diverse bread wheat genotypes across six environments (three locations × two seasons, 2021-23) under timely- and late-sown conditions to identify heat-tolerant germplasm using an integrated multivariate framework. title: Ginsenoside Rg1 as an adjuvant enhances immunity in chickens immunized with the H9N2 avian influenza inactivated vaccine
abstract: To investigate the potential use of Ginsenoside Rg1 as an adjuvant for the H9N2 avian influenza vaccine, the study examined Rg1’s immunomodulatory effects on an inactivated H9N2 vaccine. A total of 150 one-day-old non-immunized Arbor Acres (AA) chickens were randomly assigned to three groups ( n = 50 each): one receiving the H9N2 inactivated vaccine, another receiving Rg1 alongside the vaccine, and a control group treated with PBS. title: Comparing Indonesian Patent Law Enforcement with Malaysia, Singapore, and Germany System
abstract: Patent enforcement is a critical element in ensuring legal certainty, enhancing innovation, and strengthening a technology-based investment climate. However, patent enforcement practices in Indonesia continue to face significant structural and institutional challenges. This article identifies three principal issues: the limited institutional capacity of the Directorate General of Intellectual Property (DGIP), prolonged patent dispute resolution processes, and the lack of adequate technical expertise within judicial proceedings. title: The northernmost blind beauty rediscovered: The identity and cryptic diversity of the troglobiotic millipede Typhloiulus polypodus (Loksa, 1960) (Diplopoda, Julidae) from caves of the Western Carpathians
abstract: European blind forms of millipedes in the family Julidae constitute a taxonomically diverse ecological group of mostly cavernicolous species inhabiting primarily the Balkan Peninsula. Their northernmost endemic populations are confined to a few caves in two neighbouring karst areas in the Western Carpathians of Central Europe. The first study of these Carpathian millipedes focused on the description of Allotyphloiulus polypodus Loksa, 1960 from the Bükk Mountains, which was later transferred to the genus Typhloiulus Latzel, 1884. title: Can integrated legal and administrative governance reduce corporate carbon emissions?
abstract: Traditional environmental governance often relies on a single regulatory form, necessitating the exploration of more comprehensive integrated governance models. Utilizing the pilot program of procuratorial public interest litigation in China as a quasi-natural experiment, this study investigates the impact of integrated legal and administrative governance on corporate carbon emissions and the underlying mechanisms. title: A Novel Method for Manufacturing of Poly(butylene adipate‐co‐terephthalate)/Thermoplastic Starch Blends With High Performance Based on Chaotic Field
abstract: ABSTRACT Low cost, bio‐based, and biodegradable macromolecular thermoplastic starch (TPS) is widely blended with poly(butylene adipate co‐terephthalate) (PBAT) to reduce material cost in agricultural films and food packaging. However, this approach often leads to a significant deterioration in overall performance, especially at higher TPS loading. In this work, PBAT/TPS blends were fabricated using a novel dual‐speed non‐twin screw extruder modified with perturbation ring elements (NTSE‐PRE). title: Selection for Targeted Therapy Resistance Indirectly Selects for Cancer Cells with Enhanced Phenotypic Plasticity and Evolvability to Orthogonal Stressors
abstract: Resistance to targeted therapies is frequently associated with stem-like features and partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Understanding whether these programs directly drive resistance or instead reflect increased phenotypic plasticity is needed to guide strategies for overcoming resistance. Here, we found that resistance to ALK inhibitors (ALKi) in non-small cell lung cancer was associated with increased phenotypic plasticity, reflected in enhanced adaptability to orthogonal stressors and increased metastatic potential, without intrinsic cross-resistance in short-term assays.

title: Do crises integrate or fragment energy transition metals markets? Evidence from a connectedness-based crisis typology
abstract: This paper develops a two-dimensional crisis typology that classifies the impact of major crisis episodes on return spillover connectedness across energy transition metals (ETM) markets. abstract: Animal cytokinesis is often described as constriction of a RhoA-dependent actomyosin contractile ring. Yet, this ring operates within a shrinking membrane-cortex interface into which cortical flow continually delivers mechanically engaged material, creating a mass-balance problem: how can the interface close without becoming congested? title: Infant presence and mother-infant conflict predict fetal loss in wild mandrills
abstract: Female fitness depends on reproductive pace and offspring survival, both of which are determined by the ability to balance resource allocation between current and future reproduction. Using 11 years of data on 356 pregnancies (52 of which resulted in fetal loss) from 117 wild female mandrills, we show that females who conceive while still caring for a young infant experience a greater probability of fetal loss as well as increased mother-infant behavioral conflict in the form of maternal rejection. title: Loneliness in women’s experiences in a wartime context
abstract: In the context of a full-scale war, the relevance of research into women’s loneliness takes on a new significance, shaped by profound personal and psychological changes within society, the consequences of which have implications for both the resilience of the social environment and Ukraine’s overall safety. The aim of the study was to identify the levels, forms, types and nature of women’s experiences of loneliness across different age groups during wartime, and to establish whether this state represents a need, an involuntary consequence or an adaptive necessity. title: Color‐Tunable Thermoluminescence From Multi‐Shell Nanocrystals via Ultrasound‐Induced Heating
abstract: ABSTRACT Ultrasound‐induced luminescence (UL) converts mechanical energy into optical signals and has significant potential applications in multi‐parameter sensing, bioimaging, and nondestructive evaluation. However, the mechanisms underlying ultrasound‐triggered luminescence vary substantially among different material systems, complicating the rational design of luminescent materials. Herein, we demonstrate color‐tunable thermoluminescence from multilayer core–shell fluoride nanocrystals via ultrasound‐induced heating. institutions: Kunming University of Science and Technology

title: Beyond vulnerability: a review of gendered resilience, Paris agreement and rural farmers’ adaptation
abstract: Introduction Climate change impacts are not gender-neutral, yet standard reporting relies on aggregate household indicators that obscure intra-household power dynamics and diverse individual vulnerabilities. This review assesses gender-differentiated climate resilience in rural farming households and evaluates the extent to which empirical evidence aligns with the gender-responsive, participatory and transparent mandates of the Paris Agreement. title: Integrated genomic and transcriptomic analysis reveals the biocontrol and plant growth-promoting mechanisms of Burkholderia gladioli PNB20-1 against peanut southern blight
abstract: Introduction Peanut southern blight, caused by Sclerotium rolfsii , is a devastating soilborne disease that threatens peanut production worldwide. Members of Burkholderia have attracted attention as biocontrol agents owing to their diverse secondary metabolites and plant growth-promoting (PGP) capacity. Methods We isolated B. gladioli PNB20-1 from the disease-healthy junction of peanut plants. title: Proximity-based accessibility and socio-economic inequality: rethinking redistributive urbanism
abstract: Proximity-based urban planning is often presented as a means of promoting urban equity, yet concerns persist that accessibility improvements may reinforce socio-spatial inequalities and gentrification. Empirical findings on the socio-economic distribution of accessibility are mixed: while some studies associate higher accessibility with socio-economic advantage, others find that disadvantaged populations also reside in highly accessible areas. title: Mitigating Photoinduced Reactive Oxygen Species From TiO 2 and ZnO UV Filters: Materials Design and Evaluation
abstract: ABSTRACT Titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ) and zinc oxide (ZnO) are widely used ultraviolet (UV) attenuating materials, but photoexcitation of these semiconductors can generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) through interfacial redox reactions. Their oxidative activity is not an intrinsic constant, but depends on crystal structure, particle size and morphology, surface defects, coatings, aggregation, surrounding matrix, and irradiation conditions. title: Integrating a soil temperature module into AquaCrop improves simulation of crop growth and yield under straw mulching
abstract: Introduction Straw mulching is a core practice in conservation agriculture, improving the soil hydrothermal environment, enhancing water-use efficiency, and increasing crop yield, and is widely regarded as an environmentally friendly and sustainable mulching technique. However, most existing crop models simplify or neglect mulch-induced regulation of soil temperature and water processes, thereby limiting their capacity for system-level assessment of crop growth and water dynamics under mulched conditions. title: Establishing Amorphous Organoeuropium Complex Films Through Solvent‐Triggered Self‐Stacking
abstract: ABSTRACT Europium‐based scintillators are attractive for X‐ray imaging because of their high color purity, large Stokes shift, and tunable coordination chemistry. However, the fabrication of large‐area, mechanically compliant scintillation films typically relies on polymer matrices or high‐temperature processing, which inherently dilute the scintillator phase, increase optical scattering, and complicate direct integration with detector backplanes. title: Public traceability of university co-creation and collaborative governance for sustainability. A documentary audit of Ecuadorian higher education
abstract: Introduction This study examines the public visibility and documentary traceability of university co-creation and collaborative governance for sustainability, based on documentary evidence available on the institutional portals of a set of universities in Ecuador. It explores how publicly available records represent forms of territorial articulation that extend beyond traditional university extension models. title: Morphological variation in five edible Capsicum species from Ecuador
abstract: Morphological characterization provides a fundamental phenotypic basis for documenting, managing, and prioritizing plant genetic resources for subsequent breeding-oriented evaluation. abstract: Introduction Gardeniae Fructus oil is a natural and healthy oil widely used in various fields, including food, daily chemicals, and medicine. abstract: Cotton ( Gossypium spp.), a globally important economic crop, is severely threatened by Verticillium wilt caused by Verticillium dahliae ( V. dahliae ). This disease affects more than 40% of cotton fields in China and causes annual economic losses of 2.5-3.1 billion US dollars. Therefore, disease resistance breeding must take into account the inherent fitness trade-offs between disease resistance and fibre yield-quality performance. title: Dopamine release in the medullary reticular formation is related to locomotor velocity
abstract: Dopamine is classically recognized for modulating locomotion through basal ganglia circuits. However, it also modulates motor circuits in the brainstem and spinal cord. The medullary reticular formation (MRF) integrates supraspinal motor commands and relays them to the spinal cord, yet the role of dopamine in this region is poorly understood. title: Surface modification of soft materials (polymers and hydrogels) using plasma: Mechanisms, strategies, and emerging applications
abstract: Soft materials such as hydrogels (natural and synthetic), elastomers, and silicone-based polymers commonly suffer from low surface energy, weak interfacial adhesion, and hydrophobic recovery due to surface aging, which restricts their performance in biomedical and functional applications. Plasma-assisted surface modification has emerged as a controllable and solvent-free technique for modifying surface chemistry and topography without changing the bulk properties. title: Microfluidic fabrication of lipid-coated PLGA nanoparticles co-delivering CuS and curcumin for combined chemo-photothermal therapy
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major global health challenge, with chemotherapy serving as a primary treatment modality. However, its clinical efficacy is often compromised by systemic toxicity, poor drug solubility, and non-specific targeting. To address these limitations, we report the fabrication of lipid-coated poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles (NPs) co-delivering curcumin (Cur) and copper sulfide (CuS) for combined chemo-photothermal therapy using a microfluidic swirl mixer. title: Mcf-7 Cell Line: A Comprehensive Review on Breast Cancer Research, Mechanisms and Therapeutic Screening
abstract: The MCF-7 cell line is one of the most widely used in vitro models for investigating estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer. Since its establishment, MCF-7 cells have contributed substantially to understanding breast cancer biology, endocrine responsiveness, molecular signaling, cell-cycle regulation, apoptosis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, metabolic adaptation, and therapeutic resistance. title: Assessing fire intensity and burned area in Portugal: the influence of meteorological variables using copula functions
abstract: Fire activity is intrinsically linked to severe meteorological conditions, which explain most of the interannual variability of burned area (BA). Nonetheless, the effect of weather conditions on fire intensity is less understood. Using copula functions, the relationship between fire intensity and burned area with meteorological conditions in northern and central Portugal was studied. title: Spatiotemporal warming patterns and future temperature transitions under varied agroclimatic zones of Indian Punjab
abstract: Understanding regional warming dynamics is critical for assessing climate-related risks in agriculturally intensive regions. This study evaluated historical and future temperature variability, temperature transitions and warming trajectories across five agroclimatic zones of Punjab, India, using India Meteorological Department (IMD) temperature data (1951–2024) and bias-corrected CMIP6 EC-Earth3 projections (2025–2100) under SSP1: 2.6, SSP2: 4.5, SSP3: 7.0, and SSP5: 8.5 scenarios. title: Lights Out in the Canopy: Arboreal Camera Traps Offer New Insights Into Sleeping‐Site Partitioning and Sleep Ecology in Primate Communities
abstract: ABSTRACT Sleep is an essential yet costly biological process, leaving animals vulnerable to predation and constraining their use of space and time. Optimal sleeping sites therefore represent valuable, potentially contested resources, yet they remain largely overlooked in primate community ecology. Understanding how syntopic species compete for and partition sleeping sites can reveal mechanisms of coexistence, but community‐level studies remain limited because multiple arboreal species are difficult to monitor simultaneously. abstract: Abstract Background Climate change has become a global concern, influencing water resources, food security, public health, and societal progress worldwide. Floods, droughts, and irregular monsoons, as manifestations of climate change, adversely affect crops, farmers' livelihoods, and food security. A bibliometric analysis of climate change and food security (CCFS) research can indicate progress and emerging research directions on adaptation and risk-management practices, supporting farmers, policymakers, and investors in decision-making. abstract: ABSTRACT The sustainable production of chemicals is critical to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and environmental pollution. Gaseous feedstocks from industrial waste streams and waste gasification, including CO, CO 2 and H 2 , represent abundant and underutilized resources for biotechnology. Syngas fermentation has been predominantly studied under anaerobic conditions, whereas aerobic processes may offer advantages for the biosynthesis of energy‐intensive products. title: Life Cycle Assessment of Solid Oxide Fuel Cell System for Sustainable Power Generation: A Review
abstract: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) are promising technologies for sustainable power generation, offering high electrical efficiency, fuel flexibility and minimal pollutant emissions. Environmental performance of SOFC systems is influenced by operational efficiency, upstream fuel generation, manufacturing, system integration, and end‐of‐life management. This review critically synthesizes the latest life cycle assessment studies of the stand‐alone and hybrid SOFC systems based on the ISO 14040 and ISO 14044 standards.
