abstract: Abstract Mitochondrial targeting sequences are short N-terminal peptides that direct proteins to mitochondria. Notably, their amphipathic α-helical architecture closely resembles that of many potent antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). This structural convergence reflects the endosymbiotic origin of mitochondria and suggests that contemporary mitochondrial targeting sequences may retain latent antimicrobial properties. title: The quest for selfhood and the challenges of the contemporary world in modern narrative: An ecocritical reading of Zahran Al-Qasmi’s the Exile of the Water Diviner
abstract: Ecocriticism is a field of knowledge that bridges literature and the environment. The novel “The Exile of the Water Diviner” by Zahran Al-Qasmi falls within the environmental narrative that engages with the distinctiveness of the Omani environment in its most subtle details, portraying it within a bygone era- before the era of oil - in which water alone is the origin of life, and preserving it is a preservation of life. title: Influence of Gliricidia sepium living support on rhizosphere bacterial recruitment and fruit metabolomics in black pepper (Piper nigrum)
abstract: The ability of the rhizosphere to recruit beneficial microorganisms is central to the sustainable management of crops. Here, we investigated, through shotgun metagenomic sequencing and mass spectrometry techniques, the microbial composition, antimicrobial resistance (AMRs), and metabolomic profiles of Piper nigrum cultivated under two support systems: living Gliricidia sepium support (SL/RL) and dead wooden support (SD/RD). title: Perceptions of police legitimacy and its influencing factors: evidence from Guangzhou, China
abstract: Introduction Understanding the foundations of public trust in law enforcement is critical for effective governance, particularly in non-Western contexts. While procedural justice theory has received growing empirical attention in China, existing studies have produced mixed findings and largely neglected the combined influence of interactional experiences, neighborhood environmental conditions, and institutionally embedded factors on police legitimacy perceptions. title: Temperature as a Key Factor in Cone Initiation of Pinus sibirica: Evidence from a 28-Year Study in Western Siberia
abstract: Siberian stone pine (Pinus sibirica Du Tour) is a long-lived gymnosperm species that dominates the taiga forests, where its successful seeding ensures a balance between forest ecosystems and the sustenance in them of diverse wildlife. Seed cone production is erratic, with exceptionally large cone crops (or mast seeding) occurring once every 3–4 years. title: Diet pattern and human grey wolf conflict in Orakzai District, Pakistan
abstract: Introduction The grey wolf ( Canis lupus ) is an important apex predator whose persistence in human-dominated landscapes is increasingly influenced by livestock depredation and negative human perceptions. This study investigated grey wolf diet composition, reported livestock depredation patterns, and community perceptions in Orakzai District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. abstract: Phaeocollybia is a globally distributed agaricoid genus and remains poorly studied in China. In this study, field surveys were conducted, and specimens of Phaeocollybia were collected in Yunnan Province and the Xizang Autonomous Region of southwestern China from 2024 to 2025. abstract: The object of research is the process of developing investment support for railway transport modernization as a component of the development of Ukraine’s transport system under the conditions of a mobilization economy. The main problem addressed in this research is the identification of the theoretical and methodological foundations for investment formation aimed at the modernization and development of railway transport in a mobilization economy. abstract: There is increasing global interest in developing gluten-free functional foods using composite flours from locally available crops to enhance the agro-economic value of underutilized botanicals in non-wheat-producing countries and to provide gluten-free alternatives for individuals who require or choose gluten-free diets. This study evaluated and genotypically profiled the microbial community associated with three ready-to-eat baked products (bread, biscuits, and cake) prepared from pre-fermented and post-fermented gluten-free composite flours of sweet potato, maize, and pigeon pea. title: Demographic Rates of Tree Species in Subtropical Forests Vary Across Ontogenetic Stages Regardless of Their Biogeographical Origin and Leaf Habit
abstract: ABSTRACT Subtropical forests, particularly the Araucaria Forest, host tree species of both temperate and tropical origins that exhibit contrasting ecological strategies, which may shift across ontogenetic stages. However, whether and how biogeographic origin, leaf habit, and ontogenetic stage influence population growth and demographic rates of tree species remains an open question. abstract: Most weed research has focused on single species, whereas managers of conservation habitats often deal with multiple co-occurring species. Effective multi-weed management in revegetation plantings is crucial to prevent unintended responses to the removal of single species, which can change the successional trajectory of the planting project. title: The Relationship of Maqasid Al-Syari’ah in Building Sakinah Families in Generation Z
abstract: Social changes driven by digital technology, globalization, and shifting life values have shaped Generation Z into a more open, adaptive, and dynamic group. However, these conditions also challenge the formation of a harmonious family, including low readiness for marriage, rising household conflicts, and weaker commitment to Islamic values. This article analyzes the relevance of maqāṣid al-syarī’ah as a conceptual basis for realizing a sakinah family in Generation Z. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper proposes a free‐final‐time sensitivity‐based pseudospectral constrained guidance algorithm for terminal‐speed maximization under control input constraints. Within a free‐final‐time formulation, the sensitivity relationships of terminal outputs with respect to both control updates and final‐time variations are explicitly established, allowing the final time and control history to be optimized in a coupled manner. title: Construction of adaptive model for the recovery of the aviation industry from the crisis conditions based on the assessment of financial stability and the choice of development strategy for airlines
abstract: This work analyzes the process that determines the impact of crisis phenomena and factors on the functioning of airlines and assesses their financial stability, thus substantiating the choice of appropriate development strategies. The task addressed relates to the need for aviation industry to overcome the crisis by improving the financial stability of airlines as market participants. abstract: Abstract Ramadi District, the capital of Al-Anbar Governorate in western Iraq, faces a severe shortage and unbalanced distribution of sports facilities—a challenge common to many post-conflict and rapidly urbanizing cities in developing countries. This study aimed to analyze the spatial distribution of existing sports facilities and identify optimal locations for new ones using an integrated GIS-based multi-criteria decision-making approach. abstract: Selection is a core driving force of evolution. Although genome-wide scanning can identify numerous genomic regions affected by selection, it remains challenging to further reveal the specific cellular contexts in which these selection signals act. To address this issue, we developed scEvoSel, an analytical framework that integrates population-level selection signals with single-cell RNA sequencing data to identify selection-relevant cell types. abstract: Although climate change has been a major factor in the declining health of European beech (Fagus sylvatica L.) stands since the end of the 20th century, it seems that local site and stand conditions may play a key role within the beech’s climax region by exacerbating or mitigating this phenomenon. abstract: Rapid industrialization and urbanization have increased the discharge of complex pollutants into aquatic systems, posing significant environmental and public health challenges. Conventional wastewater treatment technologies often fail to remove trace contaminants such as pharmaceuticals, heavy metals, and emerging organic compounds. title: Tracing millennial climate imprints and emergent adaptation in ancient Chinese roof morphology through jiehua paintings
abstract: Abstract Understanding how human construction practices have responded to climate fluctuations over millennia is a significant challenge in global change research. A key difficulty lies in the scarcity of high-resolution and reliable proxy indicators. This study takes a novel approach by decoding ancient Chinese architectural paintings, specifically Jiehua , as cultural proxies for climate adaptation. abstract: Abstract Circularly polarized room‐temperature phosphorescence (CPRTP) materials combine the dual advantages of long‐lived triplet emission and chiral optical response, demonstrating broad application prospects in information security, bioimaging, and flexible optoelectronics. abstract: Crops aimed at nourishing an exponentially increasing population are frequently vulnerable to a diversity of adverse ecological conditions. abstract: Urban green spaces provide multiple benefits to human beings; however, green space distribution is rarely equal in most cities. Although green space equity has been assessed in cities worldwide, spatio-temporal analyses and cross-age comparisons on this topic are scarce. title: Sensing Bone-Conducted Speech With Earbuds
abstract: Clear capture of the wearer’s own voice (OV) is essential when using earbuds for mobile communication. However, OV capture remains challenging in noisy environments. Bone-conducted speech, which can be sensed as vibrations of the earbud housing, can be used to improve OV capture. title: A predictive multi-agent learning framework for energy-constrained ultra-reliable edge systems under stochastic environments
abstract: Ultra-reliable low-latency systems operating at the network edge are increasingly constrained by stochastic environmental factors, including energy variability, dynamic workloads, and time-varying communication conditions. Existing learning-based resource management approaches predominantly rely on reactive decision-making and assume stable energy availability, limiting their applicability in energy-harvesting edge systems where uncertainty is intrinsic and future conditions critically influence system reliability. abstract: Indonesia faces a severe air pollution crisis, with average PM2.5 concentrations exceeding WHO guidelines by more than sevenfold and contributing to an estimated 13% of annual deaths nationwide. abstract: Thermal insulation and anticorrosion coatings play a critical role in safeguarding industrial equipment and infrastructure. Consequently, the development of high performance, environmentally benign hydrophobic coatings has emerged as a key research priority. abstract: Freight transport is central to economic vitality, yet a major source of congestion, emissions, and social externalities. abstract: Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) have gained recognition as promising nanomaterials for energy storage applications, owing to their distinctive attributes including high surface area, tunable surface chemistry, superior electrical conductivity, and cost-effective production from renewable sources. abstract: Beneficial ownership transparency shapes the quality of the financial intelligence on which anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing (AML/CFT) measures rely. abstract: This article interrogates the Chinese state’s pursuit of ontological security (OS) through the Sinicisation of history, conceptualised as narrative self-grasping. abstract: Background The homeodomain transcription factor Engrailed-1 (EN1) is best known for its roles in developmental patterning and the maintenance of neuronal integrity. abstract: Wildlife damage is often expected to push national park residents toward new sources of income, but the appraisals that turn damage into a willingness to move into tourism remain unclear. Drawing on protection motivation theory and questionnaire data from 513 residents in and around the Wuyishan City section of Wuyishan National Park, China, this study distinguishes perceived tourism adaptive efficacy from tourism self-efficacy and examines how these two beliefs relate to intentions to shift household livelihoods toward tourism. abstract: Introduction The presence of lead ions in water bodies represents a persistent environmental problem due to their toxicity, mobility, and bioaccumulation capacity, which demands the development of efficient and sustainable treatment alternatives. title: The Limits of Europeanization in Turkish Foreign Policy: The EU-Türkiye Statement on 18 March 2016 and the Win-Set Mismatch

title: Healthcare Professionals’ Experiences of Delivering Fertility Care to Pacific Peoples in Aotearoa New Zealand: A Qualitative Study
abstract: Pacific peoples in Aotearoa New Zealand experience high infertility rates yet low use of assisted reproductive technology services. This qualitative study explored healthcare professionals’ experiences of delivering fertility care to Pacific patients. Using talanoa interviews and interpretative phenomenological analysis informed by Pacific holistic health perspectives, 11 healthcare professionals participated. Three themes were identified: delayed presentation to care, systemic barriers to fertility services, and social, cultural, and relational influences on care experiences. Participants hig

title: Audiovisual patterns of emotional advertising and physiological engagement: a marketing science perspective on sport storytelling
abstract: Introduction Sport advertising increasingly relies on emotional storytelling, yet the Marketing Science literature lacks systematic, second-by-second evidence on which audiovisual patterns modulate viewers' physiological arousal in real commercials. Methodology This study maps the audiovisual grammar of sport advertising through a secondary analysis of 750 seconds of group-level electrodermal activity (EDA) synchronized with content coding of 22 nationally aired Spanish sport advertisements (2023-2025), viewed by 30 participants. EDA was decomposed into tonic (EDL) and phasic (EDR) components

title: One-dimensional proton conductor catalyst layers for high-performance proton exchange membrane fuel cells
abstract: Abstract The practical performance of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) is critically hampered by the disordered distribution of ionomers within the catalyst layer, which causes severe sulfonate‑induced poisoning of Pt active sites, discontinuous proton conduction, and restricted oxygen transport to catalytic centers. However, addressing these interrelated limitations simultaneously remains a formidable challenge, as most existing strategies tackle only one aspect at the expense of others. title: Living under a “seismic time bomb”: hyperarousal and insomnia severity in the context of anticipated earthquake threat
abstract: Background Sleep disturbances are well documented following large-scale disasters; however, less is known about insomnia severity among individuals living with anticipated seismic threat before a major earthquake occurs. Aim This study examined the associations among trauma-related symptom dimensions, emotional distress, and insomnia severity in a non-clinical sample of adults residing in Istanbul who had not experienced severe personal loss or major housing destruction due to a major earthquake. title: Out-of-pocket expenditure for neurosurgical care in Uganda: quantifying financial catastrophe and identifying policy pathways to universal health coverage
abstract: Background Out-of-pocket payments remain the primary source of healthcare financing in many low- and middle-income countries, frequently resulting in catastrophic and impoverishing expenditures. Neurosurgical care is particularly costly due to substantial direct and indirect expenses borne by patients and caregivers, typically with little or no financial protection. This study quantifies these OOP costs, estimates the prevalence of catastrophic and impoverishing health expenditures, and examines their socioeconomic impact to inform equitable surgical financing policies. title: ARTP Mutagenesis and Omics‐Guided Target Validation for Improved Human Serum Albumin Fusion Protein Production in Yeast
abstract: Efficient production of human serum albumin (HSA) fusion proteins in yeast remains constrained by the combined demands of folding, secretion, and cellular resource allocation. Rational optimization of endoplasmic reticulum folding and unfolded protein response pathways can improve production, but additional cellular constraints may persist in engineered strains. Here, we combined iterative atmospheric and room-temperature plasma (ARTP) mutagenesis, activity-coupled screening, and genome- and transcriptome-guided validation to improve production of an amylase-HSA fusion protein (AGSH) in Saccha

title: Innate immunity and antibiotic activity in resistant bacterial infections in immunocompromised hosts
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is particularly difficult to manage in immunocompromised hosts, in whom impaired bacterial containment and clearance can coexist with restricted treatment options, altered drug exposure, and anatomically complex infection sites. Susceptibility testing and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) assessment guide antibiotic treatment, while host defenses help determine whether injured bacteria are cleared. This Review examines the host–antibiotic interface in resistant bacterial infection, with emphasis on how innate immunity contributes to antibacterial activity i
journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

title: Wild Edible Plants as Underutilized Agro-Biodiversity in Albania: Traditional Knowledge, Use, Among the Adolescents
abstract: Wild edible plants (WEPs) are an important but underutilized component of agro-biodiversity, providing nutrient-dense food, raw materials, and cultural value, yet across the Mediterranean and the Balkans the traditional knowledge that underpins their use is eroding as rural lifeways change. This study documented WEP knowledge, use practices, and the channels through which such knowledge is transmitted among adolescents in Albania, and assessed the relative nutritional value of the most commonly used species. title: Assessment of burn severity and vegetation recovery following the 2025 Palisades fire using Landsat-based spectral indices
abstract: Background and Aims Wildfires can cause substantial changes in vegetation condition and ecosystem structure, making rapid and reliable post-fire assessment essential for environmental management. This study evaluated vegetation change, burn severity, and short-term post-fire response following the 2025 Palisades Fire in California, USA. Methods Multi-temporal Landsat 8 and Landsat 9 Collection 2 Level-2 Surface Reflectance imagery acquired on 21 December 2024 (pre-fire), 14 January 2025 (active-fire) and 15 February 2025 (early post-fire) was analyzed. title: EU Regional Funds and the Convergence of European Regions
abstract: We analyze whether the European Union’s Cohesion Policy and its broader regional funds have accelerated the economic convergence of EU regions, using eight funding instruments across 239 NUTS-2 regions of the EU27 over 2014–2024. Four findings emerge. First, convergence is real but uneven. Dispersion in GDP per capita fell by about 14%, almost entirely between countries and driven by Central and Eastern European regions; the Mediterranean South shows no internal convergence, a pattern Greece drives, and within-country dispersion is essentially unchanged and now exceeds half of the total. journal: Papers of the Regional Science Association

title: Physiological and biochemical responses of facultative halophytes to differential hydroponic solution salinities
abstract: Abstract Salinity is a major abiotic stressor limiting crop production globally. Unlike obligate halophytes, facultative halophytes adapt to saline environments by enhancing their secondary metabolism, particularly under moderate salinity, offering great potential for Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA). However, the metabolic thresholds of specific edible halophytes under hydroponic salinity management remain unclear. institutions: Lithuanian Research Centre for Agriculture and Forestry

title: Ilmenite Ore-derived Lepidocrocite-type of High Purity Titanate Nanotubes for Methylene Blue Photodegradation
abstract: The synthesis of high-purity lepidocrocite-type titanate nanotubes from natural ilmenite minerals remains challenging due to the presence of iron impurities and the limited understanding of their structural stability during thermal treatment. This study presents a controlled purification and hydrothermal synthesis route for producing high-purity lepidocrocite-type titanate nanotubes from ilmenite-derived titanium dioxide (TiO₂) nanoparticles. title: A Reversed Latitudinal Polyploidy Gradient in the Fern Genus Asplenium
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Polyploids are widely expected to be more frequent at high latitudes, where polyploid vigour may confer advantages under stressful or highly seasonal climates. This expectation, however, rests largely on evidence from seed plants. We tested this prediction in Asplenium , a species‐rich, nearly cosmopolitan fern genus, using global cytogeographic data. Location Global. Taxon Asplenium (Aspleniaceae). title: Sulfuric acid activated water hyacinth root biosorbent for hexavalent chromium removal from synthetic aqueous solutions
abstract: Hexavalent chromium [Cr(VI)] discharged from tannery effluents poses severe environmental and human health risks. This study evaluates sulfuric-acid-treated water hyacinth root powder (TWHRP) as a low-cost biosorbent for Cr(VI) removal and recovery, using synthetic Cr(VI) solutions representative of the polishing/tertiary-treatment stage of tannery effluent. The biosorbent was characterised by proximate analysis, BET, point of zero charge, FTIR, and SEM before and after modification and adsorption. title: Conceptualizing carbon accounting disclosure and firm performance under sustainability committee oversight in Malaysian oil and gas industry
abstract: Abstract In the growing global warming crisis, firms operating in high carbon-intensive industries like the Oil and Gas (O&G) sector are focusing on carbon reduction and transparency. However, Carbon Accounting Disclosure (CAD) in emerging economies, such as Malaysia, remains voluntary and non-standardized, which reduces its effectiveness for firm sustainable performance. title: Hybrid aerogel-loaded ticagrelor cationic hyalurosomes as a platform for wound healing management; in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo studies
abstract: Background This study aims to evaluate the restorative effects of ticagrelor (TIC), a well-known antiplatelet drug, on wound-healing capacity using cationic hyalurosomes loaded into an aerogel. Methods The ethanol injection method was used to produce cationic hyalurosomes, which were then optimized using a D-optimal design with the type of surfactant (X1), hyaluronic acid (HA) amount (mg) (X2), and phospholipid (PC) amount (mg) (X3) as independent variables. The impact of these variables on the entrapment efficiency (EE%, Y1), particle size (PS, Y2), and zeta potential (ZP, Y3) was evaluated.

title: One Europe, Multiple Sovereignisms: Navigating the Transformation of Authority in an Era of Deglobalization
abstract: This study examines the transformation of sovereignty within historical and systemic contexts, with particular attention to the rise of sovereignty claims in Europe during the transitional phase from globalization to deglobalization under the influence of multiple crises. It has been observed that sovereignism, which developed as a reaction to the transfer of competences beyond the nation-state, has crystallized politically, economically, and culturally across Europe. title: Pesticides in agricultural ecosystems: reconciling economic sustainability with environmental toxicity and agricultural chain resilience
abstract: Synthetic pesticides remain the dominant curative technology of global crop protection, yet the terms on which they are justified, chiefly private profitability at the farm gate, increasingly diverge from the terms on which society evaluates them: ecosystem integrity, water quality, pollinator persistence, soil function and rural health. This structured narrative review synthesises evidence published predominantly between 2020 and 2026 to examine how pesticide toxicity propagates through agroecosystems and how those ecotoxicological burdens feed back into the economic sustainability of farming

abstract: هدفت هذه الدراسة إلى الكشف عن مستويات مجالات الكفاية الرقمية لدى معلمي المدارس الابتدائية في الوسط البدوي في منطقة شمال فلسطين، والتي تمثلت في أربعة مجالات، الأول مجال تصميم وإنشاء موارد تعليمية رقمية، والثاني إدارة وتنظيم المعلومات الرقمية، والثالث إعداد وتنفيذ الأنشطة التعليمية، والرابع تكييف وتعديل المحتوى الرقمي الموجود، ولتحقيق هذا الهدف اتبعت الدراسة المنهج الوصفي التحليلي وأداة الاستبانة، حيث تم تطبيقها على عينة عشوائية بسيطة مكونة من (104) معلمين ومعلمات، وبعد تحليل آراء أفراد العينة اتضح من النتائج أن المتوسط الحسابي الكلي لمستوى الكفاية الرقمية لدى معلمي المرحلة الابتدائية كان متوسطا

title: Climate-driven spatial variability of height growth revealed by bitemporal airborne laser scanning data in dry conifer forests
abstract: Airborne laser scanning (ALS) provides spatially explicit measurements of forest height change that can support the development of climate-sensitive growth and yield models. We integrated bitemporal ALS acquisitions (2011 and 2022) with climate and topographic variables to develop age-independent height growth models in interior dry conifer forests of British Columbia, Canada. Height and height increment were derived at a 20 m resolution, models were fit for five species groups using nonlinear mixed-effects modelling with stand-level random effects and residual spatial correlation. title: Bridging Micro and Macro Sustainability: How Sustainable Finance Connects Corporate esg to Sustainable Development Goals
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable finance (SF) has increasingly been conceptualized in the literature as a mechanism linking firm‐level ESG practices to broader sustainable development outcomes. However, the field remains theoretically fragmented, with limited integrated mapping of micro–SF–macro linkages. Using scientometric and bibliometric techniques, this study analyzes 1,024 Scopus‐indexed publications (2004–2025) through performance analysis, keyword co‐occurrence, text mining, and bibliographic coupling. title: PTMsToPathways: An R Package to Turn Post-Translational Modification Data into Networks to Outline Cell Signaling Pathways
abstract: Abstract Protein post-translational modifications (PTMs) in the cytoplasm and nucleus serve as direct molecular readouts of cell signaling pathways that govern cell differentiation, cancer, and other diseases. However, interpreting raw PTM data into pathways requires complex computational steps that may not be accessible to all researchers. We present the R package PTMsToPathways (P2P), which implements previously validated methods to integrate PTM proteomic data with protein−protein interactions (PPIs) and cell signaling pathways to increase access to this analysis pipeline. title: Multilayer structures for daytime radiative cooling and electromagnetic interference shielding
abstract: Abstract We present multilayer thin films that simultaneously provide strong electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding and passive daytime radiative cooling. Using a multi-objective optimization framework, we explored multilayer stacks composed of common dielectric and metallic materials. The optimization shows that shielding effectiveness (SE) exceeding 70 dB across the 1 to 40 GHz frequency range and cooling performance above 70 W/m2 can be achieved simultaneously under 1-sun illumination and the U.S. Standard Atmosphere in the ideal dry limit (precipitable water = 0 mm). title: Sarcopenia oculta en adultos con diabetes tipo 2 y obesidad: limitaciones del índice de masa corporal en la evaluación clínica
abstract: Objetivo: Determinar la prevalencia de sarcopenia oculta en pacientes con diabetes mellitus tipo 2 (DM2) y obesidad, y evaluar el rendimiento diagnóstico del índice de masa corporal (IMC) para su detección. Diseño: Estudio observacional, transversal y analítico. Métodos: Se incluyeron 120 pacientes con DM2 y obesidad (IMC ≥30 kg/m²). title: Optimal control of financial inclusion for women entrepreneurs with bifurcation, statistical and stochastic analysis
abstract: In this paper, we develop a comprehensive mathematical model incorporating market linkages, sociocultural interventions, social capital, and access to finance to examine the dynamics of women entrepreneurs. We extend the deterministic model by incorporating the random variations present in socioeconomic systems, in addition to constructiing and analyzing a stochastic nonstandard finite difference (NSFD) scheme. title: Population trends and habitat preferences of ground‐nesting bees in arable landscapes from public‐based records
abstract: Abstract Bees play a crucial role in maintaining ecosystem services that support a healthy environment and agricultural productivity. Understanding of bee distribution and population changes, particularly in arable landscapes, remains limited, let alone how this varies among different bee groups, including solitary bees and social bees such as bumblebees. This study investigated the distribution and change of ground‐nesting bees in eastern Scotland, an agriculturally extensive region of the UK. title: Climate conditions and international migration: Evidence from Türkiye
abstract: This study examines the effects of climate variability on international net migration to Türkiye over the period 1970–2024, incorporating temperature anomalies (1991–2020 baseline) and drought–wetness conditions derived from the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI). Using annual data, we employ an autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) framework alongside kernel-based regularized least squares (KRLS) to capture both the dynamic and nonlinear relationships. The results indicate a statistically significant negative association between temperature anomalies and net migration

title: Co-application of biochar and poultry manure improves plant water availability and drought tolerance of Ananas comosus in a clayey Ferralsol
abstract: Abstract Enhancing soil water availability is critical for improving the drought resilience of crops in coarse-textured tropical soils. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of charcoal fines and poultry litter on pineapple ( Ananas comosus ) water status, comparing a process-based, flux-based model (FBM) with the traditional FAO-56 method for a mechanistic assessment. The experiment was conducted in a greenhouse using a completely randomized factorial design with nine treatments and four replications. title: Methodological framework for modeling the Triple Bottom Line: analytical integration between financial statements and sustainability reporting
abstract: Este artículo propone un marco metodológico para el modelado del triple impacto mediante la convergencia analítica de estados financieros tradicionales y reportes de sustentabilidad. Para organizaciones que operen en sectores con alta exposición a riesgos regulatorios ambientales o con acceso a mercados de capitales sensibles a criterios Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG), el modelo ofrece una arquitectura que permite estructurar indicadores cualitativos en métricas gestionables, siempre que cuenten con sistemas de captura de datos primarios de granularidad operativa. title: Evaluation of Marketing Performance Levels of Customs Brokerage Firms with Interval-Valued Pythagorean Fuzzy AHP-WASPAS Hybrid Model
abstract: This study aims to systematically evaluate the marketing performance of customs brokerage companies serving international trade enterprises. The objective is to identify and prioritize the key criteria influencing marketing performance in this highly competitive and regulated sector. The research adopts a hybrid fuzzy multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methodology. The main criteria and sub-criteria were identified through semi-structured expert interviews. title: Unlocking the Collective Paradoxical Frame in Creativity: The Role of Inter‐Group Competition
abstract: ABSTRACT The present study examined how collective paradoxical frame training and intergroup competition influence virtual team creativity. A sample of 159 students collaborated in small groups of 3–4 to complete a creative task. Groups were trained on developing a collective paradoxical frame using images and examples from multicultural (highly conflicting ideas) or single–culture (moderately conflicting ideas) contexts. title: A language model-informed minimalistic design of functional coacervate vesicles
abstract: Hierarchical biopolymer interactions in nature yield intricate architectures, while synthetic biomimetics adopt a reductionist approach to create scalable and tunable systems. Inspired by intracellular liquid-liquid phase separation into membraneless, vesicle-like condensates, synthetic coacervate vesicles (CVs) have emerged for drug delivery, protocell design, and catalysis. title: El B-learning como estrategia para fortalecer asignaturas teóricas en la formación gastronómica: una revisión integrativa con énfasis en la Enología
abstract: Las asignaturas teóricas de los programas de gastronomía suelen percibirse como menos atractivas que las prácticas de cocina, aun cuando sostienen buena parte del perfil profesional. Enología es un caso representativo: exige dominar contenidos históricos, científicos y normativos y al mismo tiempo depende de la experiencia sensorial. title: Eficacia y Obstáculos en la Persecución del Delito de Trata de Personas en Chile
abstract: This article examines the criminal prosecution of human trafficking in Chile (Article 411 quáter of the Penal Code) from a practical perspective. title: Denunciar un delito en la cárcel: entre el deber y la arbitrariedad: un estudio desde la perspectiva funcionaria en Chile
abstract: Research on the dark figure of crime has focused primarily on victims’ reasons for not reporting, paying less attention to institutional actors who become aware of potentially criminal acts and are legally required to report them. This study examines how prison staff perceive the factors that may influence the reporting of crimes within prisons, both regarding their own conduct and incarcerated people’s willingness to report. title: Ancient Material Innovations to Modern Nanoscience: Nanoscale Insights, Green Nanotechnology and Nanomedicine
abstract: ABSTRACT Nanotechnology has evolved from empirical traditional material practices to a highly advanced field based on the controlled design and manipulation of matter at the nanoscale. This article aims to provide a critical narrative overview of the evolution of the field of nanotechnology from traditional empirical approaches to modern scientific approaches. title: “There was no one who looked like me”: experiences of historically excluded university students in a summer research program
abstract: Introduction To improve health for all demographics in our society, we need a diverse biomedical research workforce in which those affected by health disparities are in positions of power to prioritize and solve preventable differences in health outcomes across various populations. A strategy for diversifying the biomedical research workforce is to engage students who are from historically excluded, and therefore underrepresented, groups early in research experiences, including through summer research programs. title: High-resolution agricultural landscape models for selected agricultural regions across six European countries for use in the ALMaSS simulation framework
abstract: This data paper presents a harmonized set of spatial datasets describing 60 agricultural landscapes (10 × 10 km each) generated for selected agricultural regions across six European countries—Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, the Netherlands, and Poland—within the Horizon 2020 EcoStack project. title: When circular economy barriers stir emotions: how SME leaders respond
abstract: Emotions shape how small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) leaders respond to barriers in the transition to a circular economy (CE); however, the emotional dimension of CE leadership remains under-explored. To understand how SME leaders engaged in CE appraise and cope with barriers that hinder the adoption of circular business models, this study explores emotions in organisational behaviour. A qualitative hermeneutic phenomenological approach is adopted, drawing on 17 in-depth semi-structured interviews with Spanish SME leaders. abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐blind ultraviolet photodetection is important for low‐background ultraviolet communication, flame and corona warning, environmental monitoring, and space optoelectronics. title: Transición hacia el diseño instruccional mediado por inteligencia artificial: esquema teórico-práctico para educación superior
abstract: El presente trabajo aborda los cambios que se han presentado en el ámbito académico, específicamente, la transición del diseño instruccional tradicional hacia un modelo mediado por inteligencia artificial generativa. El objetivo principal fue desarrollar un esquema teórico-práctico que sirva como guía para el diseño de actividades educativas innovadoras apoyadas en herramientas de inteligencia artificial generativa (IAG). title: Non-volant small mammals recorded from Tyto furcata pellets in a human-modified landscape of Zona da Mata, Minas Gerais, Brazil, with an updated regional checklist
abstract: Owl pellets provide a valuable, non-invasive tool for documenting small mammal assemblages, particularly in areas lacking systematic faunal surveys. We used pellets of the American Barn Owl (Tyto furcata), collected during three sampling events (2022–2024), to document the non-volant small mammal fauna of a human-modified rural landscape in São Pedro dos Ferros, Zona da Mata, Minas Gerais, Brazil, the first faunal record for this municipality. title: Insights into the genetic diversity and population structure of domestic geese in Russia: an exploratory study of native breeds using microsatellite markers
abstract: Introduction Presently, domestic geese remain genetically less studied farm animals. Goose breeding is a traditional branch of animal husbandry in Russia. Currently, the Russian goose gene pool includes 21 breeds of domestic and foreign origin; however, many populations have experienced a substantial decline and some are approaching extinction. Therefore, studies of genetic diversity and population structure are essential for developing effective conservation and breeding strategies aimed at preserving biodiversity. title: High‐Efficiency Laser‐Assisted Manufacturing of Silicon Carbide Wafers and Components: A Critical Review
abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon carbide (SiC) and its composite variants are gaining significant traction in the semiconductor and aerospace sectors, owing to their outstanding mechanical strength, large bandgap, excellent thermal resilience, and strong resistance to radiation. However, these same properties make SiC extremely difficult to process using conventional machining techniques, which often result in low material removal efficiency, severe subsurface damage, and excessive tool wear. abstract: The development of a universal H9N2 avian influenza vaccine is essential to reduce the occurrence of disease and economic losses in the poultry industry. In this study, we developed a recombinant vaccine rTS-mH9-3M2e based on Newcastle disease virus (NDV) avirulent strain TS09-C, containing a chimeric mosaic H9 HA and three copies of H9N2 avian influenza virus (AIV) M2e. abstract: Antimicrobial resistance among phytopathogens poses a growing threat to sustainable crop production, highlighting the need for environmentally compatible antibacterial strategies. This study integrated in vitro antibacterial screening and structure-based computational analyses to investigate plant-derived candidates against Pantoea sp. title: The Motivation for Cognitive Activities Questionnaire: scale development and validation in French and English
abstract: The current research aimed to develop and validate a novel measurement scale, the Motivation for Cognitive Activities Questionnaire (MCAQ), specifically designed to assess individuals’ motivation to engage in everyday cognitive activities. The MCAQ’s development was informed by expectancy-value theory and self-determination theory. Four studies were conducted to validate the MCAQ in both English and French languages. title: Beyond colonial paradigms: academic staff perceptions on transforming agricultural education curriculum to secure food systems and mitigate criminality in Nigeria
abstract: Introduction The education curriculum in any milieu is dynamic and a continuous, evolving process. However, the influence of Western philosophy on educational curricula raises concerns about the harmful impact of crime and food insecurity on Nigeria's food sustainability. Methods A cross-sectional research method was adopted to investigate participants’ perceptions of the potential of a decolonised curriculum to contribute to food security and crime reduction. A survey was administered to 105 Nigerian university agricultural academic staff via Google Forms to conveniently maximise participant
institutions: Lagos State University of Science and Technology

title: A Review of Barriers to Flood-Resilient Retrofitting in Residential Properties
abstract: Riverine flooding poses a significant risk to residential properties worldwide, with climate change exacerbating its frequency and intensity. Although flood-resilient retrofitting (FRR) is increasingly recognized as a mitigation measure for reducing flood damage, its implementation remains low. While existing research has identified numerous FRR implementation barriers, these are often fragmented and lack theoretical integration. This study fills this gap through a theory-driven systematic review of 58 studies, selected from 2,762 articles. A total of 22 barriers were identified and grouped in

title: Type III secretion effectors of Xanthomonas oryzae: molecular functions, evolutionary dynamics and implications for rice resistance breeding
abstract: Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae ( Xoo ) and X. oryzae pv. oryzicola ( Xoc ) are major bacterial pathogens of rice that cause bacterial blight and bacterial leaf streak, respectively. Successful infection by these pathogens depends largely on a functional type III secretion system (T3SS), which delivers diverse type III secretion effectors (T3SEs) into rice cells to manipulate host transcription, immunity, metabolism, and cellular processes. title: Assessment of Physical, Chemical, and Bioactive Properties of Some Neglected Varieties of Yemeni Coffea arabica L. Green Beans
abstract: Coffea arabica L. is an economically important crop grown in diverse geographical regions of Yemen. This study aimed to characterize the physical, chemical, and biological properties of Yemeni green coffee bean varieties collected from eight major coffee-producing areas in Hajjah Governorate. Bean physical traits, including length, diameter, bulk density, and weight, were recorded, and methanolic (MeOH) extracts were prepared to determine total phenolic (TPC) and flavonoid (TFC) contents, caffeine level, mineral composition, antiradical capacity (using DPPH and ABTS tests), and enzyme inhibito

title: Beyond Protein Synthesis: The Multifunctional Role of Functional Amino Acids in Modulating Meat Quality in Ruminants
abstract: ABSTRACT Meat quality is a critical economic trait in ruminant production because it directly influences consumer acceptability, market value, and the long‐term sustainability of the livestock industry. Amino acids (AAs) have traditionally been regarded primarily as substrates for protein synthesis. However, growing evidence indicates that they also regulate multiple aspects of meat quality. Given the increasing demand for high‐quality ruminant meat and the growing interest in nutritional regulation of carcass traits, this review synthesizes current evidence on how functional amino acids (FAAs
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Impacts of shrub coverage for arctic ecosystem carbon uptake and storage
abstract: Abstract. Although shrubs employ distinct water- and carbon-use strategies compared to trees and are increasingly expanding across warming tundra and grassland, they remain insufficiently represented in global land surface models. Here, we incorporated two shrub types, deciduous and evergreen, into the nutrient-enabled terrestrial biosphere model QUINCY, which features a state-of-the-art treatment of soil nutrient dynamics and carbon exchange. We investigate the change in carbon fluxes and storage due to shrub cover, it's response to climate and CO2 fertilization effect and the role of nitroge

title: Exploring Developmental Interactions Between Speech and Orofacial Functions in Preschoolers: A Cross‐Sectional Study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Speech and orofacial functions (breathing, swallowing, and chewing) both develop within the stomatognathic system and share common anatomical structures and motor control mechanisms. Theoretical models suggest that early orofacial motor experiences may shape speech development. However, empirical evidence examining these relationships during the preschool years remains scarce. AIMS: This study explored the relationship between speech and orofacial functions in preschool children. We hypothesised that this relationship is not direct but indirect, with oral motor competence, operatio
journal: International Journal of Language & Communication Disorders

title: Fire and Carbon Dynamics: A Global Review of Knowledge and Gaps Across Biomes
abstract: Abstract Purpose of review Fire is a major driver of terrestrial carbon (C) cycling, rapidly releasing carbon accumulated over decades to millennia and reshaping ecosystem structure and function across biomes. As climate change intensifies fire regimes, understanding fire-induced changes in C stocks and fluxes is increasingly urgent. To address this need, we reviewed fire–C studies published over the past fifteen years, focusing on the geographic and biome distribution of existing research, the effects of prescribed burns and wildfires on C pools and fluxes, and methods used to quantify post-f
institutions: Forest Science and Technology Centre of Catalonia

title: A Comprehensive Review of Various Models of Direct Current Motors: Structures, Operating Principles, Classification, and Industrial Applications
abstract: Direct current (DC) motors have been studied for decades, yet they remain relevant to a wide range of motion-control, precision-drive, educational, and specialized industrial applications. The large variety of DC motor configurations, however, has also led to some inconsistency in the way these machines are classified and compared. Terms related to excitation, commutation, construction, and control are often used at the same classification level, even though they describe different aspects of a motor or drive system. This review brings these aspects together and examines DC motors from both ph

title: Enhancing children’s motor creativity: A methodological pilot study
abstract: Motor creativity is widely recognized as a component of physical literacy, encompassing the ability to adapt movement by generating original and functional solutions to motor challenges in dynamic environments. Positive challenges that encourage exploration and the discovery of action possibilities can promote enjoyment while providing physical and sport-related benefits. Accordingly, the primary aim was to examine the effectiveness of a motor creativity program in enhancing cognitive and motor creativity among young gymnasts as well as their self-efficacy and enjoyment. Thirty-four beginner g
journal: Journal of Physical Education and Sport

title: Polymeric nanocomposites for eco-friendly and industrial applications: a comprehensive review
abstract: Abstract Polymeric nanocomposites (PNCs) are formed by dispersing fillers with at least one dimension in the 1–100 nm range in a polymer matrix, and the resulting materials often outperform either constituent alone. Because the interfacial area per unit volume scales inversely with the smallest filler dimension, a few volumes per cent of well-dispersed nanofiller can alter the mechanical, electrical, optical, magnetic and gas-barrier properties of the host polymer, at loadings substantially lower than those required with conventional micro-scale fillers. title: Identification and Characterization of a Cytosolic Malate Dehydrogenase as a Potential Drug Target in Echinococcus multilocularis
abstract: Abstract Alveolar echinococcosis, caused by the larval stage (metacestode) of Echinococcus multilocularis, is an emerging zoonotic disease with limited treatment options, highlighting the need for new therapeutic targets. Like other helminths, E. multilocularis relies on anaerobic metabolism via malate dismutation, a poorly characterized pathway. In this study, cytosolic malate dehydrogenase (cMDH), a key enzyme in this pathway, was investigated as a potential drug target. Bioinformatic analyses identified three cMDH homologues in E. multilocularis, all exhibiting canonical domain architecture

title: Organic Iron Sulfur Framework With Electron Transfer Capacity Promotes Photosynthetic Carbon Fixation
abstract: Iron-sulfur clusters (ISCs) are crucial prosthetic groups in natural proteins that participate in vital electron transfer processes. Although various artificial ISCs with catalytic activity have been constructed, synthesizing stable ISCs under aerobic conditions remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a hydrothermal synthesis strategy to produce metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) containing discrete ISCs, bridging the gap between biological ISCs and conventional iron sulfide minerals. Using terephthalic acid (TPA) as the organic linker to encapsulate ISCs, we constructed MOF-like nanoshe
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Drought modulates soil hydraulic, biological, and physicochemical responses to one-off tillage in a long-term cover-cropped Mediterranean vineyard
abstract: Sustainable soil management is a crucial factor to maintain soil health and long-term functionality in vineyards. In Mediterranean climates, cover crops have become a sustainable alternative to conventional tillage due to their positive effects on soil structure, water retention, and biological activity. Severe drought episodes are increasingly prompting growers to incorporate tillage to reduce water and nutrient competition between cover crops and grapevines. However, the immediate consequences of this practice on soil attributes remain poorly understood. To evaluate whether reintroducing til
institutions: Institute of Agrifood Research and Technology

title: Gut bacterial extracellular vesicles in glucocorticoid-associated skeletal complications: evidence boundaries and translational challenges
abstract: Long-term or high-dose glucocorticoid (GC) therapy causes major skeletal complications, particularly glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) and glucocorticoid-associated osteonecrosis of the femoral head (GIONFH). Bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs) produced by gut-resident bacteria are candidate inter-organ messengers, but the GC-specific evidence base is extremely limited. institutions: Luoyang Orthopedic-Traumatological Hospital of Henan Province

title: Transformación Digital desde la Mirada del Talento Humano en IPS: Un Estudio Multicéntrico
abstract: Objetivo: Explorar la transformación digital en las Instituciones Prestadoras de Servicios de Salud (IPS) desde la mirada del talento humano en un entorno digital. Metodología: Se empleó una metodología de revisión sistemática; la búsqueda de literatura científica se llevó a cabo entre enero y mayo de 2026, centrada en estudios publicados entre 2015 y 2025. Para ello, se realizaron exploraciones manuales y electrónicas en cinco bases de datos reconocidas por su relevancia académica en el ámbito de la salud: PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, SciELO y Google Scholar. Resultados esperados: Los resul
publisher: Latin American Association for the Advancement of Sciences

title: Environmental correlates of main and secondary sett locations in the Eurasian badger ( Meles meles ) in a lowland landscape
abstract: The main aim of this research was to investigate site selection for two types of Eurasian badger (Meles meles) setts (main and secondary) in relation to environmental factors (soil type and vegetation structure) and distances to meadows, rivers, human settlements, and public roads in the Stobrawa Landscape Park (SLP, southwestern Poland). A total of 53 badger setts were identified, comprising 31 main setts (58,5%) and 22 secondary setts (41,5%). The environmental variables that most clearly differentiated main and secondary setts were distance to water sources and soil type. Our results indica
institutions: Wrocław University of Environmental and Life Sciences

title: Impact Assessment of Geotechnical Hazards in the Floodplain Regions of North Bihar: A Risk-Based Analysis
abstract: North Bihar, situated in the eastern Indo-Gangetic floodplain, is characterized by fertile alluvial soils deposited by major Himalayan rivers such as the Kosi, Gandak, Bagmati and Mahananda. While these river systems support agriculture and regional livelihoods, they also expose the region to numerous geotechnical hazards due to weak alluvial deposits, shallow groundwater conditions, dynamic river morphology and recurrent hydrometeorological events. This study presents a quantitative risk assessment of major geotechnical hazards in North Bihar including soil liquefaction, high groundwater tabl

title: Monitorización anestésica en medicina veterinaria importancia de los parámetros hemodinámicos y respiratorios para prevenir complicaciones durante procedimientos quirúrgicos
abstract: La anestesia general en medicina veterinaria de pequeños animales deprime de forma predecible los sistemas cardiovascular y respiratorio, y las complicaciones intraoperatorias derivadas de esta depresión constituyen un riesgo real de morbimortalidad. El objetivo de este artículo es analizar la importancia de los parámetros hemodinámicos y respiratorios en la monitorización anestésica y su relación con la prevención de complicaciones durante procedimientos quirúrgicos. Se realizó una revisión documental de literatura científica y guías de práctica clínica publicadas entre 2002 y 2025, consultan

title: Intergenerational cohesion, cultural continuity, and ageing in the United Arab Emirates: a qualitative study of older adults’ perspectives
abstract: Intergenerational relationships are central to later-life wellbeing and the transmission of cultural identity, yet older adults’ own accounts of these processes remain underrepresented in Gulf societies. This qualitative interview study explored how older Emirati adults understand intergenerational cohesion, cultural continuity, and the role of family and community institutions in sustaining these ties. Ten Emirati adults aged 60 years and older were recruited through community-based access points and interviewed in Arabic using a semi-structured guide. Interviews were audio-recorded and trans

title: Consecutive adsorption and ozonation treatment of real coffee processing wastewater with coffee husk adsorbent—a circular approach
abstract: Coffee processing waste is a significant source of environmental pollution, as coffee is one of the most merchandised commodities worldwide. Coffee processing generates substantial volumes of solid and liquid waste, and its management is complex. Various physical, chemical, and biological methods were explored for treating coffee processing wastewater (CPWW), but most have failed to achieve optimal performance. This study provides new insights into an integrated approach for treating real CPWW by combining batch adsorption with ozonation. This study utilises a circular approach, in which CPWW

title: Biochar engineered cementitious composites: property-based selection, functionalization economics and deployment readiness
abstract: Biochar is a promising low-carbon cement additive that combines carbon sequestration with biomass-waste utilization. However, its properties vary widely with feedstock and pyrolysis process parameters, and reported effects on cementitious composites are inconsistent. Earlier reviews were largely narrative or limited to compressive strength and offered no measured basis for biochar selection. This review builds that basis from 1165 biochar records, linking production to properties and properties to four cementitious roles. title: Abundance Redistribution Increases Predator‐Prey Interaction Potentials Among North American Birds
abstract: Species are shifting their geographical ranges, yet the consequences of these spatial redistributions for species interactions have not been examined at broad spatial and temporal scales. Here, we characterize shifts in the potential for predator-prey interactions among North American birds over the past 50 years. We first predict potential predator-prey interactions based on existing data, then construct a novel, abundance-weighted metric of interaction potential for each pair of predator and prey species in local communities. We found nearly universal increases in predator-prey interaction p

title: Seeing the Experience or Scanning the Specifications? Media‐Framing Congruence Effect in Phygital Tourism Booking Decisions
abstract: ABSTRACT As tourism enters the phygital era, digital preview media have become key pre‐purchase touchpoints. Drawing on cognitive fit theory, this study challenges the assumption that immersive virtual reality (VR) always outperforms static images by examining how media form (VR panoramic video vs. static images) and information framing (hedonic vs. utilitarian) jointly shape tourism booking intentions. Four between‐subjects scenario‐based experiments in tourism booking contexts test the interaction effect, examine perceived information diagnosticity as a mediator, and validate the mechanism.

title: Nationwide Tracking of A‐Lineage Spread in Western Honey Bees Using Haplotype Sharing, Local Ancestry Mapping, and Migration Inference
abstract: Understanding the spatial dynamics of genetic ancestry is essential for elucidating historical and contemporary patterns of gene flow among populations. Honey bees in the United States have a 400-year history of importation, management, and adaptation to diverse environments. Genetic diversity is a key factor for colony health and resilience. Notably, the most genetically diverse populations in the country originate from the invasive A-lineage (Africanized or 'Killer' honey bees). title: Contrasting climatic niche structure and projected suitability for Canada lynx and bobcat
abstract: Abstract The Canada lynx ( Lynx canadensis ) and the bobcat ( Lynx rufus ) are congeneric felids whose climatic niches and distributional overlap are being reshaped by climate change. We integrated ensemble distribution models, Humboldt niche overlap analysis, and a novel centroid-distance diagnostic—Variable Ecological Restriction Analysis (VERA)—using 6,723 and 9,030 independent occurrence records and 36 climatic predictors to characterize their climatic relationship. title: Projected range contractions threaten mammal-driven ecosystem functions in a conservation mosaic of southeastern Amazonia
abstract: Climate change is predicted to severely impact mammal diversity in southeastern Amazonia. We modeled the distribution of 44 mammal species under optimistic (RCP 4.5) and pessimistic (RCP 8.5) climate change scenarios for 2050 and 2070. Results indicate that nearly half of the species may lose over 90% of their suitable habitat. Functionally important groups such as frugivores and large carnivores are particularly vulnerable. institutions: Universidade Federal do Sul e Sudeste do Pará

title: Association Between Amino Acid Levels and Thyroid Function Among Iranian Adults: A Cross‐Sectional Analysis of Bushehr Elderly Health ( BEH ) Program
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Thyroid hormones regulate key metabolic processes; however, the association between thyroid function and amino acid metabolism varies across studies. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between thyroid biomarkers and circulating amino acid concentrations in adults aged 50 years and older. METHODS: We initially enrolled a random subsample of 824 adults aged 50 years and older from the second recruitment of the Bushehr Elderly Health (BEH) Program. title: Teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (S.M.) in Building an Ideal Marital Life: A Review in the Bangladesh Context
abstract: Objective: This study aims to examine the Qur’anic conception of marital relationships, emphasizing mutual protection, tranquillity, love, security, and companionship between husbands and wives within Islamic family life. Theoretical framework: The study employs the Qur’anic metaphor of spouses as garments for one another, particularly in relation to intimacy, mutual protection, dignity, and shared responsibility. This framework challenges patriarchal interpretations that position marriage as a mechanism for domination by either spouse. Literature review: Existing discussions of Islamic marria
journal: Solo Universal Journal of Islamic Education and Multiculturalism

title: Multi‐year and multi‐trait evaluation of hemp ( Cannabis sativa L.) genotypes using AMMI, GGE, WAASB, and MGIDI
abstract: Abstract In hemp ( Cannabis sativa L.), yield and agronomic performance are influenced by genotype and year‐to‐year environmental variation. This study evaluated the performance, stability, and multi‐trait superiority of 16 hemp genotypes over four consecutive growing seasons (2022–2025) using additive main effects and multiplicative interaction (AMMI), genotype plus genotype × year interaction (GGE) biplot, WAASB, and multi‐trait genotype–ideotype distance index (MGIDI) analyses. AMMI analysis of variance revealed that genotype and genotype × year effects were statistically significant for al

title: Reconfiguring aesthetic values: a power-sensitive framework for AI-mediated visual communication
abstract: This conceptual analysis argues that aesthetic values in AI-mediated visual culture are socially constructed and shaped by power relations rather than being universally shared or psychologically neutral. Visual content is now produced, circulated, and evaluated within socio-technical systems governed by platform infrastructures, algorithmic recommendation mechanisms, and data-driven optimization logic. By asking how aesthetic value systems can be reconceptualized through a power-sensitive framework in order to understand AI-mediated visual communication, the conceptual analysis critically reco

title: Assessing changes in electrical resistivity signals in simulated mass and single graves over 18 months after burial
abstract: Abstract Electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) has been increasingly explored as a non‐destructive technique for searching for unmarked graves. However, its effectiveness remains uncertain as measured resistivity responses are influenced by burial type, time after burial, soil properties and environmental conditions. Previous studies have reported both positive and negative resistivity anomalies associated with graves, highlighting the need for further controlled investigations. title: Green public facilities and residents’ health from a socio-spatial perspective
abstract: Background This study conceptualizes green public facilities as green-space resources embedded in urban public-resource allocation and examines the relationship between their spatial distribution and residents’ health from a socio-spatial perspective. Methods Data on 6,871 respondents from the 2021 Chinese General Social Survey were linked to green public facility and public transport point-of-interest data and statistical indicators for 82 districts/counties. title: Genome-wide association study and candidate gene prioritization for stem architectural traits in Tartary buckwheat
abstract: Stem architecture is a key determinant of lodging resistance, yield potential, and mechanical harvestability in Tartary buckwheat ( Fagopyrum tataricum ), yet the genetic basis of stem-related traits remains poorly understood. In this study, a diverse panel of 244 Tartary buckwheat accessions was evaluated for five stem architectural traits, including plant height (PH), stem diameter (SD), branch number on the main stem (BNMS), node number on the main stem (NNMS), and stem wall thickness (TST), across three field environments (Huize 2025, Songming 2024, and Songming 2025). institutions: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

title: From empowerment to advocacy: A serial mediation model of women’s support for rural tourism development in Saty village, Kazakhstan
abstract: Rural tourism is often promoted as a means of advancing gender equality, yet little is known about how women’s empowerment translates into lasting behavioral support for tourism, particularly outside a few well-studied regions. Drawing on Empowerment Theory, Social Exchange Theory and the Capability Approach, this study tests a model in which women’s economic, social and political empowerment shape their satisfaction with tourism, which influences participation and long-term support for tourism development, both directly and through participation. journal: Journal of the Bulgarian Geographical Society
institutions: Aktobe Regional State University named after K.Zhubanov

title: Brain-wide activity imaging with electron microscopy reveals a distributed brain network for processing threatening somatosensory stimuli
abstract: To understand how brains work, neural activity must be overlayed onto synaptic-resolution circuit architecture. Recent advances in light-sheet microscopy (LSM) enable whole-brain, cellular-resolution imaging of activity of all cell bodies; however, most neurons from such datasets cannot be identified. In most organisms, neurons are identifiable based on their projections (and not based on cell body position), which, when densely labeled, cannot be resolved using LSM. title: Evolutionary and dynamic constraints converge on a conserved coupling sector in thermally adapted GH1 β-glucosidases
abstract: How protein sequences evolve to maintain functional conformational dynamics under thermal stress remains an important question in molecular evolution. Thermophilic enzymes are often considered to achieve stability primarily through enhanced structural rigidity, yet thermal adaptation may also involve the preservation or reorganization of correlated motions across the protein scaffold. title: From Awareness to Agency: Theorising Youth-Led Climate Action Through Design Thinking in Ghanaian Schools – A Conceptual and Framework Contribution
abstract: Abstract This conceptual and framework paper theorises the structural barriers limiting youth climate agency in Ghanaian secondary and tertiary schools and advances the Youth-Led Climate Action Lab (YCAL) as a five-phase, design-thinking-grounded intervention model, drawing on Ghanaian educational research, West African climate policy literature and four bodies of theory: social cognitive theory, transformative learning, postcolonial environmental education and Critical Emotional Awareness pedagogy. title: Liver immune tolerance and regulated cell death in transplantation and hepatocellular carcinoma: shared mechanisms, divergent outcomes
abstract: The liver constantly encounters gut-derived antigens, microbial molecules, and food antigens. This environment has shaped a tissue-specific tolerance network centered on tolerogenic antigen presentation, immune-checkpoint activation, regulatory cell expansion, and metabolic suppression. This feature protects the liver during prolonged inflammation and gives it an immunological identity that most solid organs lack. institutions: Affiliated Hospital of Shandong University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

title: Early career challenges of physical education teachers
abstract: Introduction Early career physical education teachers face challenges similar to those of other novice teachers, in addition to field-specific difficulties. Their professional adjustment depends on the interaction between personal psychological and pedagogical resources and the workplace demands. Successfully navigating this process and ensuring adequate socio-institutional support are essential for career development and sustained professional practice. title: Safe hands or system shapers? Local authority chief executives and the future of place leadership in England
abstract: This paper furthers understanding of the capabilities and skills required to manage complex organisations and processes in a place leadership setting by examining the experiences of local authority chief executives during local government reorganisation in England. It provides new perspectives on place-leadership illuminating challenges and opportunities for senior leaders to lead effectively in a shifting governance landscape and identifying capabilities and skills local authority chief executives have drawn on in response. title: Biostimulant potential of Limnospira platensis biomass fermented with lactic acid bacteria in common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris): strain characterization, biochemical shifts, and growth promotion
abstract: The excessive use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides in conventional agriculture poses significant risks to soil health, environmental quality, and food security. Plant biostimulants derived from microorganisms, microalgae and cyanobacteria offer a sustainable alternative. Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) and cyanobacteria such as Limnospira platensis are recognized for their plant growth-promoting characteristics. title: From welfare to the environment: social policy, natural resources, and ecological sustainability in G20 economies
abstract: Ecological degradation has emerged as a critical challenge to achieving sustainable development, particularly in G20 economies where economic growth, social welfare objectives, and environmental constraints frequently interact. Using annual data for 17 G20 countries over 2000–2021, this study examines the effects of social welfare (SCWF), economic policy uncertainty (ECPX), trade openness (TROP), life expectancy (LIEX), natural resource rents (NARN), and tourism (TRSM) on ecological footprints (ECFP). title: From Trunk Diameter to Crown: Point Cloud-Based Allometric Equations for Urban Trees and a Scalable Approach for City-Wide Biomass Estimation
abstract: Abstract Background Urban trees provide essential ecosystem services, including carbon storage. However, quantifying the wood volume and biomass of urban trees remains challenging, primarily due to a lack of species-specific allometric equations tailored to urban growth conditions. In addition, most existing equations rely solely on diameter at breast height (DBH), which is hard to obtain from remote-sensing data, thus limiting scaling to city level. title: Beyond self, time, and space: exceptional experiences and altered states of consciousness
abstract: Exceptional experiences commonly described as parapsychological or as extra-sensory—including precognition, telepathic impressions, meaningful coincidences, and other forms of anomalous cognition—remain among the most controversial topics in consciousness research. Population studies consistently demonstrate that such experiences are widespread across cultures and appear to transcend ordinary spatial and temporal constraints. institutions: Institute for Frontier Areas of Psychology and Mental Health

title: An Examination of the "Addiction and Addiction Prevention" Course Using Activity-Based Teaching Methods: A Qualitative Study
abstract: This study aimed to examine prospective educators’ experiences, perspectives, and perceived competencies regarding activity-based instructional practices implemented throughout an undergraduate "Addiction and Addiction Prevention” course. The study employed a qualitative descriptive design utilizing inductive thematic analysis. The study group comprised a complete cohort of 55 undergraduate students (100% participation rate) enrolled in the course and meeting predefined inclusion criteria at a public university in Turkey during the 2025–2026 academic year. title: Indonesia’s Palm Oil Trilemma: Reconciling Biodiesel Expansion, Export Competitiveness, and Supply Resilience under Climate and Governance Constraints
abstract: Indonesia’s palm oil sector is being asked to serve an expanding domestic energy market while sustaining food and oleochemical supply, export competitiveness, rural livelihoods, and ecological integrity. This interpretive qualitative literature review examines the resulting policy trilemma using peer-reviewed research published during 2020-2026 and the IPOSS fourth-quarter 2026 industry outlook as a contextual, explicitly prospective source. journal: Journal of Business Research and Reports

title: Recent Advances in LDH‐Based Sorbents for Wastewater Treatment
abstract: ABSTRACT Adsorption is an efficient and environmentally benign technique for wastewater treatment. Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) are low‐cost materials with high adsorption capacities for a wide array of pollutants. This review comprehensively summarizes recent studies on the adsorption of dyes, metal ions, inorganic anions, and organic contaminants using LDH‐based materials. The effects of preparation methods, cation molar ratios, and calcination temperatures on LDH performance are thoroughly examined. institutions: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research

title: Solenostemma argel Dead Leaves as an Eco‐Friendly and Low‐Cost Adsorbent for Effective Removal of Methylene Blue From Aqueous Media: Adsorption Performance and Mechanism
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable, low‐cost adsorbents derived from agricultural waste are needed for the removal of toxic dyes from contaminated water. Solenostemma argel dead leaves (SAL) were evaluated as a biosorbent for methylene blue (MB) removal from contaminated water. SAL was characterized by x‐ray diffraction (XRD), N 2 adsorption–desorption (BET), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). title: Pharmacological and non-pharmacological strategies targeting HIF signaling and hypoxia tolerance: opportunities and limitations for personalized interventions
abstract: For acute mountain sickness prevention and the treatment of respiratory, cardiovascular, and nervous system diseases, pharmacological (prolyl hydroxylase domain inhibitors, plant extracts, erythrocyte pyruvate kinase activators, and hemoglobin oxygen affinity allosteric activators) and non-pharmacological approaches (hypoxic training and hypoxic therapy) are used. title: Sustainable and Multifunctional Biocomposite Materials for Energy Storage Applications: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: The growing demand for sustainable, high-performance energy storage technologies has driven interest in biocomposite materials derived from renewable resources. Combining bio-based polymers with bio-fillers and functional bionanomaterials, these materials offer environmentally friendly alternatives for applications in supercapacitors and lithium-ion batteries, as well as energy-conversion technologies such as fuel cells and solar cells. title: Acoustical Materials from Conventional to Cutting-Edge Innovations─An Overview
abstract: Abstract With rapid urbanization and industrial expansion, noise pollution has escalated into a pervasive environmental and public health crisis. Thus, an imperative need arises for both advanced sound mitigation strategies and, especially, a fundamental shift toward sustainability to meet pressing worldwide environmental policies. title: The materialities of pigments, paints and personhood in San rock paintings: celebrating the inspiration from David Lewis-Williams
abstract: Most rock art research has been influenced by David Lewis-Williams. He has shown the material primacy of rock paintings, the cautious use of ethnography for emic understandings, and the importance of theory. In addition, his recognition of the impact of ‘critical, radical thought’ on our practice. This radical thought is encapsulated by posthuman ontologies which study the entanglements of humans and more-than-humans. Rock paintings are material and have material effects. title: Stochastic assembly outweighs deterministic filtering: crop phenological stages drive bacterial-fungal divergence between bulk and rhizosphere soils in saline-alkali fields
abstract: Soil salinization threatens crop productivity partly by disrupting rhizosphere microbiomes that support plant stress tolerance. However, most studies have focused on single growth stages or bulk soil, limiting a deeper insight into the temporal dynamics and assembly mechanisms of rhizosphere communities across the crop life cycle. We investigated bacterial and fungal communities in a long-term maize field with saline-alkali soil. Bulk and rhizosphere soils were sampled at seedling, heading, and maturity. title: Wildfire severity reshapes soil organic carbon fractions and stabilization pathways in a subalpine forest
abstract: Introduction Wildfire disturbance is a major driver of soil carbon cycling in subalpine forests, yet differential responses of soil organic carbon fractions to fire severity remain poorly understood. Methods We investigated a subalpine forest in northwestern Sichuan, China, 6 years after wildfire. Four fire-severity classes were established: unburned control (UB), low-severity fire (LSF), moderate-severity fire (MSF), and high-severity fire (HSF). title: Microclimatic regulation effects of landscape elements on university campus in a temperate monsoon climate zone: A case study during extreme summer heat
abstract: Although temperate monsoon climate regions are traditionally known for their harsh winter climates, the combined effects of rapid urbanization and global climate change have significantly intensified summer urban heat island effects in these areas, making them a neglected yet increasingly severe challenge in high-latitude urban climate adaptation planning. This study takes a typical campus in Shenyang, a temperate monsoon climate region in Northeast China, as the experimental subject.
