title: Mycobiota associated with diseased Schrenk’s spruce in mountain forest ecosystems of Kyrgyzstan
abstract: Schrenk’s spruce ( Picea schrenkiana ) is a dominant coniferous tree species in the Western Tian Shan forests and plays an important ecological role in maintaining mountain forest ecosystems in Kyrgyzstan. In recent years, the Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve has seen a significant increase in diseased and declining spruce trees, raising concerns about forest health and ecosystem stability. The present study aimed to investigate the fungal communities associated with diseased roots, stems, and needles of Schrenk’s spruce in the Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve, Kyrgyzstan. title: Study on Gas Drainage Mechanisms and Techniques in Low-Permeability Coal Seam
abstract: This study investigates gas drainage mechanisms and techniques for low-permeability coal seams. It examines coal structure, gas-flow behaviour, permeability controls, and internationally applied drainage methods. Permeabilityenhancement approaches, including hydraulic fracturing, hydraulic slotting, and controlled blasting, are evaluated alongside borehole design and operating factors. Sensitivity analysis assesses the effects of coal-seam permeability, gas pressure, and drainage configuration on performance. title: Navigating the BERMUDA triangle of scientific software: A modular approach to data, hardware, and algorithm design in quantum chemistry and its realization in Python
abstract: Modern quantum-chemistry software must support increasingly complex methods, heterogeneous hardware, reusable data structures, and user-facing workflows without losing maintainability. Using PyBEST as a case study, this work discusses how such complexity can be organized within the Python programming language through modular interfaces rather than scattered across method-specific implementations. title: When Politics Enters the Waiting Room: Far-Right Electoral Victories Exacerbate Discrimination in Access to Healthcare
abstract: Abstract Far-right political shifts have been linked to increased racism, raising concerns about their impact on minority access to public services. This study investigates whether far-right electoral victories encourage discrimination by street-level bureaucrats, who are expected to act impartially. We conducted a nested research design in Italy, combining a field-experimental audit with a regression discontinuity design focused on municipalities near the electoral threshold for far-right mayors. title: Extracellular vesicle surface proteins in tissue recognition, organotropism, biomarkers, and therapeutic engineering
abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs), including exosomes, carry donor-cell-derived molecular features that influence their interactions with recipient cells. This review links EV biogenesis and the assembly of surface recognition cues to cellular interactions, tissue distribution, and translational applications, with an emphasis on the evidence required to interpret surface localization, biomarker value, and therapeutic outcomes. title: Perspectives of Biomaterial‐Based Sustainable Integrated Micro‐ and Nanophotonics
abstract: ABSTRACT Biomolecular photonics is emerging as a pathway toward sustainable alternatives to fully semiconductor‐based devices, leveraging the unique optical properties and solution processability of proteins, nucleic acids, and other biogenic molecules. This review covers recent advances in nano‐ and microscale biophotonic devices, spanning biopolymer waveguides (with optical losses down to 0.24 dB cm −1 ), bio‐organic LEDs and lasers (luminous efficiencies up to 130 lm W −1 ; lifetimes >3600 h), biohybrid photovoltaics (PCE up to ∼20%), photodetectors, and optoelectronic memristors. title: A Comprehensive Review on Advancements in Photocatalytic Applications of Nanostructured Metal Oxides Toward Environmental Remediation
abstract: ABSTRACT The increasing energy crisis and environmental contamination have become one of the most pressing global challenges, prompting the advancement of eco‐friendly and effective advanced treatment technologies. Although photocatalysis enabled by semiconducting materials has garnered intense research interest for pollution remediation, large‐scale application of widely studied semiconductor photocatalysts remains constrained by inefficient utilization of the visible‐light, fast recombination of charge carriers, and limited operational stability. title: Chikungunya virus: from global emergence to immunopathology and therapeutic frontiers
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), a re-emerging mosquito-borne alphavirus, has transitioned from an endemic pathogen to a global public health threat. In May 2026, the World Health Organization’s second rapid risk assessment classified the global public health risk of CHIKV transmission as moderate. Although two vaccines (IXCHIQ ® and VIMKUNYA ® ) have been authorized in selected countries, no antiviral therapy has been approved, and supportive care remains the mainstay of clinical management. We synthesize current knowledge of CHIKV epidemiology, replication, host immune signaling, and immune evasio

title: From ‘yuck’ to ‘ahhh’: a focused review on the bacteriophage-based strategy for malodour mitigation to improve the aspirational quotient of toilets
abstract: Most of the user-interface of toilets is associated with in-situ , decentralised wastewater treatment systems. Specifically, on-site sanitation systems (OSS) and decentralised wastewater treatment systems (DEWATS) are mainly used to treat toilet blackwater (faeces, urine, and flush water). Though ideal, malodour generated within these systems can hinder their adoption, especially where sanitation infrastructure is limited. title: Entomophagy at India’s nutrition-sustainability nexus: biodiversity, nutritional evidence, food safety, regulatory gaps and a conceptual commercialization roadmap
abstract: India is among the most entomophagically diverse countries in the world. Peer-reviewed inventories document more than 300 edible insect species across at least 14 states, together with a documented but taxonomically separate tradition of arachnophagy in Nagaland and Manipur. Despite this biological resource, India has not converted its edible arthropod tradition into a regulated protein sector. title: From wind-solar accommodation to potential coal-generation displacement: spatial coordination and operational CO2 mitigation in China’s power system
abstract: Wind-solar accommodation does not necessarily yield equivalent reductions in coal generation or emissions. Using 2022 hourly output for 2880 county-level units, 8760-h loads for 31 provinces and data for 2985 coal units or project phases, we compare provincial self-accommodation, neighboring-province pairing, nationwide pairing and national aggregation. abstract: Introduction Nitrogen (N), an essential plant nutrient characterized by the lowest use efficiency and multiple loss pathways, challenges its management in rainfed castor. Therefore, a field experiment was conducted over three consecutive Kharif seasons (2022-2024) to develop an adoptable N management strategy for rainfed castor cultivation. title: Long-term sex-specific consequences of prenatal hypoxia on systemic hemodynamics and baroreflex sensitivity in rats
abstract: Background Intrauterine hypoxia is a common pregnancy complication that programs long-term cardiovascular dysfunction. However, stage-specific effects on cardiac vs. vascular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Aim We investigated baroreflex coefficient (BRC) and cardiac reactivity in peripubertal and adult rats exposed to acute hypobaric hypoxia at different gestational stages, examined autonomic mechanisms, and differentiated between cardiac and vascular components of the programed phenotype. title: From chronic airway injury to lung cancer: epithelial memory, field cancerization, and premalignant evolution
abstract: Chronic airway injury induced by tobacco smoke, environmental pollutants, and persistent inflammatory lung diseases provides a biological foundation for lung carcinogenesis, yet the cellular and molecular trajectory from repeated epithelial damage to invasive malignancy has only recently come into focus. title: Revisiting a 50-year-old ecological study of Ephemeroptera, Plecoptera, and Trichoptera species in Estaragne River (French Pyrenees): why taxonomy matters?
abstract: Long-term ecological surveys (LTES) and historical species inventories are essential for assessing changes in biodiversity. However, comparisons over time may be heavily biased if they disregard the evolution of taxonomic knowledge. To investigate, at a later date, changes in the distribution of aquatic species over the last 50 years, we revisited the Ephemeroptera, Plecoptera, and Trichoptera (EPT) species inventory conducted by Pierre Lavandier in the 70’s in the Estaragne, a subalpine and alpine catchment area in the French Central Pyrenees. title: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi enhance growth, mineral nutrition, metabolic traits and essential oil bioactivity in Thymus satureioides Coss.
abstract: Thymus satureioides is a native plant of the Moroccan Atlas Mountains and is valued for its culinary, medicinal, and cosmetic uses. The increasing pressure on its populations and its vegetation calls for sustainable farming. Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) are among the beneficial microbes that promote growth, phytochemicals, and bioactive properties. title: Power system expansion in Ecuador: A stakeholder driven sustainability assessment of generation technologies
abstract: Ecuador experienced severe power shortages in 2024, with blackouts lasting up to 14 h a day, exposing the vulnerability of an electricity system that relies heavily on hydroelectric plants, is affected by drought, and has seen limited investment in new capacity since 2018. In this context, the central government has begun promoting nuclear energy as a medium- and long-term option, despite the country’s lack of experience with this technology and the Electricity Master Plan’s identification of substantial renewable potential. title: Acid-sensing ion channels in pain and psychiatric disorders: from basic properties to comorbidity mechanisms
abstract: Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are proton-gated cation channels that mediate Na + and Ca 2+ influx upon activation by extracellular acidification. Beyond protons, endogenous ligands, toxins, and small molecules modulate ASIC gating through direct or synergistic mechanisms. ASICs have emerged as key players in pain and psychiatric disorders. Tissue acidosis drives hyperalgesia via sustained ASIC activation, synaptic plasticity disruption, and central sensitization, thereby promoting chronic pain. title: Between #Mädelbund and #Ostmullen – Making sense of everyday territorializations of far-right women on German TikTok
abstract: This study represents the first systematic survey of far-right female influencers in the German-speaking TikTok community since the rise of a new neo-Nazi youth cultural movement in 2024, thereby filling a key research gap in the fields of digital far-right studies and political geography. The methodological focus is on multimodal discourse analysis, which examines TikTok videos as complex compositions of text, image, and sound. title: Discriminatory spaces and psychological distress: the role of responses among unaccompanied minor migrants. A mixed-methods study
abstract: Introduction Unaccompanied minor migrants in Europe face heightened vulnerability, yet little is known about how discrimination unfolds in their daily lives, how they respond to these experiences, and the impact on psychological distress. The aims of this study are (1) to examine the everyday experiences of perceived discrimination among unaccompanied minor migrants and (2) to test whether responses to discrimination mediate the association between perceived discrimination and psychological distress in this population. title: A novel biodegradable gelatin capsule platform for input-efficient herbicide delivery in transplanted rice
abstract: Background Weed management in transplanted rice requires effective herbicide delivery while improving input-use efficiency and reducing reliance on conventional application practices. This study developed and evaluated a biodegradable gelatin capsule-based herbicide delivery system, subsequently protected through a design patent, as an alternative approach for herbicide application. title: Why is the right side of the brain responsible for the left side of the body? The evolutionary history of a puzzling trait
abstract: In humans, the right motor cortex controls the spinal motoneurons that cause the limbs on the left sides of our bodies to move. Similarly, the right side of the cerebral cortex predominantly receives sensory information about the left side of our bodies and the left side of the outside world. Although there have been numerous papers (dating back at least to Cajal) speculating on the adaptive value of this contralateral organization, to date none appears to have examined its evolutionary history. title: La exclusión escogida. quienes deben quedar fuera del mundo
abstract: Este artigo discute a noção de exclusão escolhida como uma categoria analítica para compreender as persistentes desigualdades digitais na contemporaneidade. Parte-se da hipótese de que a exclusão digital não decorre apenas de limitações tecnológicas ou infraestruturais, mas também de decisões políticas, econômicas e institucionais que definem quais territórios, grupos sociais e populações serão incorporados aos ecossistemas digitais e quais permanecerão à margem. title: Engineering functional perfusion in vascularized cardiac grafts through bioactive biomaterials and biofabrication
abstract: Vascularized cardiac grafts are being developed to overcome the limited survival and incomplete integration of engineered myocardial tissues after implantation. Although many platforms can now generate endothelial networks, the central challenge is no longer the presence of vascular-like structures alone, but the establishment of networks that remain perfusable, mechanically stable, and functionally coupled to the host circulation. This review discusses cellular design, bioactive biomaterial selection, biofabrication strategies, flow-mediated endothelial maturation, and preclinical evaluation

title: Developing an outcomes framework for greenspace programmes supporting individuals experiencing problem substance use: a scoping review and analytical synthesis
abstract: Background Greenspace programmes are known to support health and wellbeing, yet limited research exists on their impact for individuals experiencing problem substance use. Early findings are promising, but systematic exploration of appropriate outcome measures and evaluation methods remains sparse. This paper addresses that gap by developing an outcomes framework tailored to this population. Methods A mixed methods approach was used. title: Recurrent pulmonary infection, a vicious cycle of multifactorial interactions, and prevention/treatment strategies
abstract: Recurrent pulmonary infection (RPI) refers to the frequent and repeated episodes of lower respiratory tract infections. At its core, it represents a vicious cycle arising from the disruption of the homeostatic balance among pathogens, host immunity, and pulmonary architecture. RPI accounts for a considerable proportion of pediatric pneumonia cases, and the cumulative incidence among elderly patients hospitalized for pneumonia is also markedly elevated, imposing a substantial disease burden. title: Triterpenoids – future multi-target compounds against obesity and towards restoration of metabolic health
abstract: Obesity and its associated diseases represent one of the most urgent public health crises of our time, affecting billions worldwide. Current pharmacological agents, such as GLP-1 and GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists, have demonstrated high clinical efficacy in diabetes and weight management. However, the required lifelong medication is often limited by high economic costs and severe side effects, including gastrointestinal complications. title: Influence of LED spectral quality and natural growing conditions on flowering, yield, and fruit biochemical quality of okra (Abelmoschus esculentus (L.) Moench)
abstract: Introduction Climate change poses significant challenges to open-field production of okra ( Abelmoschus esculentus (L.) Moench), a tropical vegetable crop of high nutritional and economic value. This study evaluated the effects of light-emitting diode (LED) spectral quality on reproductive development, fruit characteristics, yield, mineral composition, antioxidant activity, and total phenolic content of okra. title: The Cross-Border Care Model, a middle-range nursing theory for mobile populations in Latin America and beyond: Discussion paper
abstract: Background Research on migrant and refugee health in Latin America and the Caribbean points to a finding with direct clinical consequences. The conditions that borders create appear to shape the health of people on the move more consistently than cultural difference does. Administrative status, racialised exclusion and the physical conditions of crossing affect presentation, access and outcomes, often long after the crossing. title: Explosive price dynamics consistent with bubble-like behavior in clean and traditional energy investments: A GSADF approach amidst global events
abstract: This study examines explosive price dynamics consistent with bubble-like behavior in clean and renewable energy ETFs, index, and equities compared to traditional energy counterparts, using the Generalized Supremum Augmented Dickey-Fuller (GSADF) test across four subperiods: Pre-Paris Agreement, Paris Agreement, COVID-19, and Russia-Ukraine War. title: Contextualizing a process information approach in material passports: a case on modelling circular façade product requirements
abstract: Information gaps are a key challenge in transitioning to a circular economy, particularly beyond the first use of building products. Material passports could bridge these information gaps by acting as shared information repositories across actors and product stages. However, current material passport research primarily defines product-centric information requirements addressing the here and now, while process-related information to enable future reuse remains less examined. title: cGAS–STING signalling in triple-negative breast cancer: a functional-state framework for biomarker-guided intervention
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) combines genomic instability with heterogeneous immune responses. Cyclic GMP–AMP synthase (cGAS) detects mislocalised DNA and produces cyclic guanosine monophosphate–adenosine monophosphate (cGAMP), which activates stimulator of interferon genes (STING). The resulting response can support antigen presentation or sustain inflammatory adaptation. title: The cultural origins of the demographic transition in France
abstract: Abstract This research shows that secularization accounts for the early fertility decline in France. Why the demographic transition began in France a century before any other country is one of the big questions of history because it challenges traditional explanations and because of data limitations. Using a novel dataset crowdsourced from online genealogies, I comprehensively document the decline and its timing. title: Epidemiological patterns of black pod (Phytophthora spp.) and frosty pod rot (Moniliophthora roreri) in cocoa plantations of Tequendama, Colombia
abstract: Cocoa is an important crop in Colombia and a key productive alternative in post-conflict rural areas. Similar to other tropical production systems, yields are constrained by diseases such as black pod disease and frosty pod rot. This study evaluated the temporal and spatial epidemiological patterns of both diseases on three cocoa farms located in the Tequendama region of Colombia through analyses of disease incidence, severity, disease progress, and spatial distribution. title: The aging secretome as a candidate driver of bone remodeling imbalance: myokines, adipokines, and senescence-associated secretory factors
abstract: Bone homeostasis depends on the spatial and temporal coupling of osteoclastic resorption to osteoblastic formation. With aging, this balance shifts toward net bone loss alongside sarcopenia, marrow adipose expansion, and chronic low-grade inflammation. These parallel changes may be linked by a shared set of secreted signals, termed here the aging secretome. title: Sustainable desulfurization through coupled extraction-catalytic oxidation strategy: Mechanisms, materials, and process intensification
abstract: In response to the imperative for sustainable energy and environmental protection, ultra-deep desulfurization of fuels poses a critical challenge. Conventional hydrodesulfurization and emerging non-hydrogenation techniques face limitations in efficiency, economic viability, and ecological sustainability, particularly for refractory sulfur species. Among alternatives, extractive catalytic oxidative desulfurization (ECODS) has emerged as a prominent approach by integrating catalytic oxidation and liquid-phase extraction under mild conditions. title: Solid CO2 sorbents for medium- and high-temperature carbon capture: material design, shaping, and deployment for hydrogen-related processes
abstract: Abstract Due to their high-temperature resistance and potential for process intensification, medium- and high-temperature solid CO 2 adsorbents offer significant advantages in combining carbon capture with thermochemical fuel conversion and hydrogen production. title: Neuroimmune communication: from CNS-resident cell networks to the glioblastoma microenvironment
abstract: Neurons, glial cells, and immune cells engage in extensive bidirectional communication within the central nervous system (CNS) through shared receptors, ligands, and secreted mediators. Glial cells — particularly astrocytes and microglia — serve not merely as structural support but as central immunomodulatory hubs that relay neural signals to immune effectors. title: Reflexões sobre o conceito de preservação na Arquivologia Brasileira: uma análise a partir da legislação federal e da produção científica
abstract: This study addresses the concept of preservation in the field of Archival Science, starting from federal legislation and academic production on the subject. It comparatively analyzes the presence and uses of the term "preservation" in Brazilian archival legislation and academic production, seeking to identify continuities, shifts, and changes in how the topic is formulated over time. The research adopts a qualitative approach, of a basic nature, with a deductive method, articulating documentary and bibliographic research. title: Current advances on the phytochemical composition, pharmacological applications, and toxicology of Micromeria graeca
abstract: Background Micromeria graeca ( M. graeca ) is a species belonging to the Lamiaceae family, regarded as a shrub that is widespread throughout the world and widely cultivated in many countries. It is used traditionally in food, cosmetics, and medicines. Objective The objective of this review is to examine the pharmacological, phytochemical, and toxicological activities of M. graeca . Moreover, the research aimed to gather and record all the currently available evidence and information on the medicinal applications of this plant. title: The Institutionalization of REIT Sustainability Reporting: Cross‐Country Evidence From ESG Disclosure Regimes and Building Sustainability Policies
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the institutionalization and textual evolution of sustainability reporting among listed real estate investment trusts (REITs) in the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, Singapore, and Japan between 2020 and 2025. Reporting is framed as the joint product of two institutional layers: capital‐market environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure regimes and building‐level sustainability policies. title: Morphological and phylogenetic analyses reveal taxonomic insights in Marasmiaceae, including ten new species from Northeast China Ecological Region
abstract: Based on morphological characteristics and phylogenetic analyses using ITS, nrLSU, rpb 2, and tef 1-α sequence data, six new species belonging to subg. Globulares were identified and described. In addition, this study addressed the taxonomic confusion surrounding ser. Haematocephali through detailed discussions. title: Climate change risk and corporate pension funding
abstract: This paper investigates how climate change risk influences corporate pension funding decisions. Based on the precautionary motive, we hypothesize that firms facing greater climate-related uncertainty will increase pension funding to protect against potential financial disruptions. Using 13,871 firm-year observations of U.S. publicly traded firms from 2001 to 2023, we find a positive correlation between climate risk exposure and pension funding. title: From Sea Surface Height to Velocity - A Machine Learning Approach
abstract: Inferring upper-ocean velocity from altimetric sea surface height (SSH) remains challenging below 50~km, scales now resolved by the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission. Conventional methods rely on geostrophic or cyclogeostrophic balance. Here, we demonstrate that deep learning can predict the full velocity vector from SSH and environmental data and recover derivative-based diagnostics, including spectral energy flux. abstract: Sea-ice stage of development (SoD) describes the age and associated thickness of sea ice and provides important information for navigation, operational ice monitoring, and assessment of ice conditions. SoD labels are obtained from operational ice charts, where trained analysts interpret satellite observations and assign standardized stage codes to regions with similar ice conditions. title: Machine learning applications in the heliosphere
abstract: Space weather is the study of the near-Earth impact of the processes on the Sun. In a this era of technology, space weather emerges as a crucial area of study wherein the state of the near-Earth conditions need to be modeled and forecasted. Crucially, the advent of machine learning provides us with opportunities to study this subject in a rather comprehensive manner. In this chapter, we treat the the processes arising from Sun to the impact on the ground as a set of coupled systems, which can be studied in isolation or in a coupled manner. title: A Deep-Learning Framework for the Generalized Emulation of Atmospheric Radiative Transfer at Microwave Frequencies
abstract: This paper presents an application of machine learning to the problem of the computational expense of atmospheric radiative transfer calculations from physics-based models. While in recent studies individual emulators have been created that emulate certain radiative transfer schemes for different sensors, we show that a general framework can be applied to emulate the radiative transfer method itself. title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in the Management of Climate Change-Related Health Issues in Africa
abstract: While climate change disproportionately impacts African public health, AI predictive modeling remains heavily constrained. Using a Synthetic Knowledge Synthesis approach and VOSviewer, we conducted a bibliometric analysis of Scopus-indexed literature, comparing Global and African corpora. Network analysis reveals stark divergences: global research emphasizes complex, predictive models for planetary health, whereas African research focuses on localized, reactive solutions for immediate infectious disease triage. title: SHAPE: Solar Heliospherical Analysis and Prediction of Eruptions A machine learning approach to solar flare forecasting
abstract: Solar flares are the most energetic impulsive events in the solar system, and reliable operational forecasting of the rarest and most destructive M- and X-class events remains an open problem. We present Solar Heliospherical Analysis and Prediction of Eruptions (SHAPE), a two-phase deep-learning pipeline that bypasses sunspot proxies in favour of direct soft X-ray observations from the GOES X-ray Sensor (XRS). title: Deep Learning for Cervical Cytology Screening: Methods, Algorithms, Challenges and Prospects
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer death among women, with more than 90\% of deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries, where cytology screening is constrained by a shortage of trained cytopathologists. Deep learning has made automated cytology screening increasingly feasible, but the literature is fragmented across cell, patch and whole-slide-image scales, task formulations and supervision regimes, hindering comparison and clinical translation. This Review synthesizes the deep learning literature for cervical cytology screening, organizing the field along three axes-

title: Estimating Vertical Ocean Velocity from Horizontal Currents: Linear and Depth-Conditional Neural-Network Approaches on a High-Resolution Regional Ocean Model
abstract: The vertical component of the ocean velocity, w, is several orders of magnitude smaller than the horizontal components u and v, yet it controls vertical tracer transport, upwelling, and mixed-layer ventilation. Because w is extremely difficult to measure directly and is normally obtained only diagnostically from the continuity equation, predicting it from the horizontal velocity field is a problem of both practical and physical interest. We address this problem with two data-driven methods, a physically-motivated linear baseline and a convolutional neural network conditioned on depth through F

title: CoraLive: Ultra-Low-Power Underwater Vision for Long-term Coral Reef Monitoring
abstract: Effective coral reef protection and restoration demands continuous, long-term underwater monitoring. However, current solutions largely rely on fragmented, manual labor and costly infrastructure, or are severely limited by constrained battery lifespans. In this paper, we present CoraLive, an ultra-low-power underwater camera system for long-term, continuous coral reef monitoring. CoraLive presents a decoupled underwater-shore co-design that minimizes on-board computation and storage, offloading heavy reconstruction and segmentation tasks to offline shore-side processing. title: A Multidimensional Evaluation Framework for Artificial Intelligence-Based Ocean State Forecasts
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) based ocean state forecasts now approach or surpass those produced by operational ocean forecasting systems as measured by conventional pointwise metrics. However, these metrics may favor spatially smoothed forecasts and cannot determine whether forecast variables remain physically coherent. Forecast evaluation should therefore move beyond overall pointwise accuracy toward assessing forecast trustworthiness. We propose a multidimensional framework comprising overall pointwise accuracy, physical consistency, and distributional consistency. Overall pointwise accuracy

title: FASST: A Compact Stateless Atmosphere Model for Long-Term Ocean Coupling
abstract: Coupled climate simulations are computationally expensive, largely because of the atmosphere. We introduce FASST, a coupled climate model that retains the prognostic POP2 ocean while replacing the atmosphere and sea ice with lightweight U-Net emulators. The atmospheric emulator is diagnostic, predicting surface fluxes from the evolving ocean-ice state every $6$ simulated hours, while the sea-ice emulator advances the ice state monthly. title: Learning to Adjudicate: Verifier-Guided Multi-Agent Reasoning for E-Commerce Relevance
abstract: Relevance modeling is fundamental to e-commerce search, determining how well retrieved products satisfy the needs expressed in a user's query. Accurate judgments require interpreting user intent, comparing product attributes, and applying business-specific matching criteria. Current methods based on large language models (LLMs) leverage contextual understanding and reasoning, focusing on incorporating domain-specific context and enhancing reasoning performance. Despite these advances, difficult query-product pairs remain challenging when evidence from different perspectives supports conflictin

title: Edge intelligence for distributed acoustic sensing with ultracompact neural networks
abstract: Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) transforms optical fibres into dense arrays of vibration sensors for continuous, long-range monitoring with high spatial resolution. Yet converting these large-scale measurements into actionable information with compact models that retain task performance remains challenging. Existing artificial-intelligence approaches are typically optimized for specific sensing environments and tasks, but their computational requirements can hinder deployment in compact, power-constrained field systems. Here, we introduce DAS-NanoNet, a framework that automatically construc

title: CodeJeNN: A simple C++ neural network generator for physics applications
abstract: Machine learning has shown promise in physics applications, but integrating Python-based libraries into high-performance C ++ solvers can create performance bottlenecks. We present CodeJeNN , which addresses this gap by auto-generating self-contained C ++ code from trained Keras models for inference. This eliminates external dependencies through inlined functions, allowing seamless integration into existing frameworks. title: An all-weather microwave-based AI retrieval of pan-Arctic melt pond fraction
abstract: Melt pond fraction (MPF) is a key variable governing Arctic sea ice albedo and seasonal sea ice predictability, yet existing pan-Arctic MPF products rely almost exclusively on optical sensors, limiting availability under cloud cover and seasonal darkness. This study presents PRISM-MPF, the first pan-Arctic, multi-year, all-weather MPF dataset, derived from PRISM (Polar Retrievals through Intelligent Sensor Merging), a machine learning framework fusing multi-source microwave observations with auxiliary thermal and spatiotemporal information to complement optical products. An XGBoost model was t

title: Generative Refinement Learning for Temporal Interpolation in Scientific Machine Learning
abstract: Computationally expensive simulations and real-world observations often provide data at a lower temporal resolution than downstream tasks require. Averaging observations at fixed grid points can introduce errors, and motion estimates alone do not determine how the physical field values change. In this work, we study whether learning to correct a simple numerical interpolation improves the reconstruction of intermediate scientific fields. title: SATFRONT: Detecting Atmospheric Fronts with Satellite Data using Machine Learning
abstract: Atmospheric fronts are associated with much of the high-impact weather in the mid-latitudes, yet their identification and classification remain largely manual and subjective. Existing deep learning approaches rely primarily on gridded reanalysis or forecast data, limiting their applicability to satellite observations available for time-critical applications. We introduce SATFRONT, a machine learning framework for detecting cold, warm, and occluded fronts over Europe from geostationary satellite observations, with reanalysis data as an optional additional input. title: A fully convolutional neural network to classify UXOs using multicomponent electromagnetic induction data
abstract: Unexploded ordnance (UXO) clearance relies on electromagnetic induction (EMI) methods to detect and classify buried and submerged metallic objects, but the standard classification workflow requires physics-based inversion and manual expert review. We present a fully convolutional neural network (CNN) that classifies UXO directly from multicomponent time-domain EMI data, bypassing the inversion step entirely. The CNN uses a segmentation-like architecture that preserves the spatial dimensions of the input and outputs a high-resolution classification map suitable for generating a diglist. Two CNN

title: The MASSIMAL Dataset: UAV Hyperspectral Images and Ground Truth Observations for Coastal Habitat Mapping in Norway
abstract: The MASSIMAL dataset was collected in an effort to develop new remote sensing methods for mapping shallow water coastal habitats, such as kelp forests, seagrass meadows and maerl beds. The main component of the dataset is a set of hyperspectral images collected using a unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). Images were collected during 45 UAV flights performed at 4 main areas along the Norwegian coast, spanning across a wide latitude range, from 59 to 67 degrees north. The ground sampling distance of the hyperspectral images is 3.5 cm, and the spectral range is 400-1000 nm, sampled across 300 spectral

title: Lightweight Underwater Acoustic Vessel Classification for Embedded Deployment
abstract: We propose a Raspberry Pi-based underwater vessel classification system for edge deployment under limited connectivity, bandwidth and power in offshore acoustic surveillance. Using ShipsEar, we compare six classifiers on a Raspberry Pi 5 through a complete audio-to-prediction pipeline. We assess classification performance, processing latency, CPU utilisation, memory consumption and monitored power. title: Assisted Turbulence Modeling via Data Assimilation and Machine Learning for Turbomachinery Flows
abstract: Abstract This work presents the development and assessment of a hybrid framework coupling numerical simulation, experimental samples, data assimilation (DA) and machine learning (ML) to investigate the flow within an axial compressor stage. The methodology first implements a Multi-Fidelity Ensemble Kalman Filter (MFEnKF) which integrates experimental PIV data with a two-fidelity numerical simulation setup, combining steady-state RANS on a fixed grid with unsteady hybrid RANS/LES simulations on a moving grid. title: Causal-prior-constrained deep learning for rapid-intensification warning of western North Pacific tropical cyclones
abstract: Rapid intensification (RI) is one of the most dangerous and unpredictable phases of tropical cyclones, and its environmental and structural drivers are difficult to identify and separate in observations. Here we introduce CausalVisionRI, a causal-prior-constrained deep-learning system for 24-h RI warning in the western North Pacific. It integrates infrared remote sensing imagery, atmospheric and oceanic fields, and an observationally discovered causal graph into a unified model. title: Nereus: A Large-Scale Underwater Dataset for Fine-Grained Attribute Understanding and Grounded Counting Perception
abstract: Underwater imagery records rich ecological information and supports applications such as science communication, fishery monitoring, ecological conservation, and oceanographic research. Beyond general scene understanding, these applications require models to recognize fine-grained biological traits and reason over spatially grounded evidence. However, existing underwater datasets often provide coarse category labels, generic captions, or total-count supervision, which limits their use for organism-level analysis and ecological reasoning. title: From Frege to ChatGPT: Compositionality in Language, Cognition, and Deep Neural Networks

title: Adaptive Uncertainty Quantification on Simplicial Complexes with Conformalized Simplicial Neural Networks
abstract: Simplicial neural networks (SNNs) are powerful tools for prediction tasks on higher-order relational datasets stored on simplicial complexes (SCs), a higher-order generalization of graphs. However, SNNs usually lack rigorous uncertainty quantification (UQ), limiting their usefulness in high-stakes scenarios. We propose conformalized SNN (CF-SNN), a framework that, given a simplicial-complex entity with m prediction targets, generates prediction sets for all m targets simultaneously. title: Sonny-ENS: demystifying machine-learning ensemble weather forecasting
abstract: Every weather forecast is uncertain, and decisions from flood warnings to energy trading depend on how well that uncertainty is quantified. Machine-learning (ML) ensembles now quantify it better than the best physics-based ensemble, yet two things about them remain opaque: whether their skill requires hundreds to thousands of accelerator-days of training, and how a network with a simple source of randomness produces a spread that follows the flow. title: New Wine in an Old Bottle -- NeuralPOM: A Hybrid Ocean Forecast Model with Differentiable Dynamics and Staged Learning
abstract: Coarse-grid ocean circulation models rely on empirical subgrid parameterizations that struggle to capture mesoscale eddies, whereas purely data-driven neural forecasters accumulate trajectory drift, violate tracer conservation, and damp small-scale variability over extended integrations. Here we present NeuralPOM, a hybrid ocean forecast model that couples differentiable explicit mode-split and semi-implicit free-surface implementations of the Princeton Ocean Model (POM) to a conservation-constrained neural corrector. title: Revealing Imaging Characteristics of Thermal Wakes from Underwater Vehicles Without Cooling-Water Discharge
abstract: Small uncrewed underwater vehicles are proliferating and threaten maritime security, yet evade sonar and magnetic sensors built for larger submarines. Infrared thermal wakes, generated by hydrodynamic displacement that modulates the cold-skin layer, offer a non-acoustic, non-magnetic alternative even without cooling-water discharge. Existing studies, however, rely on idealized simulations that fail to capture real-world backgrounds, offering limited guidance for target-background discrimination. title: Label-Free Performance Estimation of Deep Learning Based Radar Detectors in Time-Varying Environments
abstract: Deep-learning-based radar target detectors can achieve strong performance in complex sensing environments. However, in time-varying environments, changes in clutter characteristics may cause the distribution of echoes to deviate from that of the training data, thereby degrading detector reliability. Timely identification of such degradation requires an accurate assessment of the deployed detector's performance; however, ground-truth labels for radar echoes are typically unavailable during deployment. title: AquaProbe: Efficient Adaptation of Frozen Vision Models for Underwater Images
abstract: Reliable visual perception is essential for safe autonomous underwater exploration. Yet vision models pretrained on terrestrial images become less reliable underwater, where turbidity, backscatter, and wavelength-dependent attenuation alter scene appearance. Existing adaptation methods either spread adapters equally across the encoder depth or select layers using the divergence between two fixed domains. title: Spatially-Adaptive Neural-Network Based Extraction of Significant Wave Heights from HF Radar Data
abstract: Significant wave height (SWH) retrieval from high-frequency (HF) radar data conventionally relies on Doppler-spectrum processing and interpretation of the weak second-order scattering continuum. This article investigates adaptive spatial processing for time-domain SWH estimation using ordered envelope statistics. title: Expert lithological labels do not improve learning when used to predict marine sediment properties
abstract: Scientific drilling has produced large archives of physical, chemical and magnetic measurements linked to descriptions of the rock recovered. These archives are mostly incomplete: instruments sample at different intervals, recovery is partial, and destructive analyses preclude later measurement of the same material. title: Multi-level Constrained Learning for Underwater Image Enhancement
abstract: Underwater image enhancement aims to correct color and recover detail degraded by wavelength-dependent attenuation, scattering, and noise. Paired-reference supervision constrains output similarity, but does not by itself specify the color mapping, the strength of local detail corrections, or consistency with the degraded observation. We propose MCL-UIE, a paired-supervised framework that addresses these requirements by constraining restoration operations and the training objective. title: Mathematical Formulation and Comparative Performance Evaluation of Machine Learning Algorithms for Maize Land Suitability Prediction
abstract: Addressing the food needs of a growing population is one of the major challenges of developing countries like Ethiopia. Various policies aimed at increasing food production have been enacted by governments and development partners. Although efforts in this regard have been made, there is still inadequate emphasis on increasing food production through the use of high technology practices. Precision agriculture using technology has been utilized to increase crop yield. Precision agriculture also relies on identifying land for a crop, which is a key factor that affects crop yield. title: Open-set multi-view seahorse re-identification from underwater photograph sequences
abstract: Automated animal re-identification from photograph sequences can facilitate minimally invasive Capture-Mark-Recapture studies at scale. Yet, photographs taken during an observation session can vary greatly in quality, not always providing the necessary information for accurate re-identification. In this paper, we present new methods for taxonomic classification, sex determination, and open-set re-identification from image sequences. title: TERA: Task-Evidence Restoration for Underwater Object Detection under Bandwidth-Constrained Transmission
abstract: Underwater object detectors are typically evaluated on pre-transmission images, overlooking additional degradation from bandwidth-constrained downscaling and compression. We introduce AquaTX, a controlled benchmark built from real underwater detection datasets with seen and held-out codecs. We also propose TERA, a metadata-blind receiver-side framework combining task-guided pixel restoration and dual-state feature correction while keeping the detector frozen. title: Surface Conditioning for Zero-Shot Multivariate Correction in a Marine Biogeochemistry Emulator
abstract: Bias correction in process-based models usually means iterative data assimilation with explicit covariance modelling. We propose a lightweight alternative based on a neural emulator of marine biogeochemistry (BGC), showing that the conditioning pathway of its autoencoder can serve as an observation injection point. The decoder is conditioned on surface variables via Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM), originally designed to incorporate physical boundary forcings. title: Wave Physics as Representation: Tensor-Structured Neural Reconstruction for Ocean Acoustic Fields
abstract: Reconstructing three-dimensional (3D) complex ocean acoustic fields from sparse measurements is challenging due to highly oscillatory wave structures and restricted sensing patterns/routes. Learning-based approaches fall into two categories. First, purely data-driven models can learn complex field patterns, but do not explicitly exploit wave physics that may enhance interpretability and reduce training costs. title: Patch-Based Deep Kernel Learning for Data Assimilation and Bias Correction with Extremely Sparse Observations
abstract: Data Assimilation (DA) reconstructs the state of a spatio-temporal system by combining sensor observations with the output of a numerical model. Since model states are high-dimensional while observations cover only a small fraction of the domain, DA is a challenging large-scale estimation problem, central to weather forecasting and oceanography. Classical variational methods such as 3D-Var rely on a hand-crafted background error covariance that assumes unbiased errors, and therefore cannot capture state-dependent correlations or systematic model biases. title: Networked AI: Architecture, Theory, and Applications
abstract: Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly large-scale deep learning, have been driven by monolithic or offline training on massive curated datasets. While successful, these approaches face structural limitations: escalating data and computational demands, limited online adaptability, and a lack of system-level intelligence in open, non-stationary environments. This paper presents Networked AI - a networked intelligent system composed of interacting, heterogeneous, and continuously evolving AI agents. title: GNN-VIEW: Visual Inspection and Explanation of Graph-based Earth-System Models
abstract: Machine learning Earth-system models are becoming increasingly important, and so is their development. Graph-based models, one of the most prominent approaches, allow developers to constrain the learning process before training via graph connectivity. Yet, developing these models remains challenging: the graph is built algorithmically with little intuition about the final result beyond static plotting, which requires extra work and is often not detailed enough. title: Autonomous fixed-wing interception using reinforcement learning
abstract: Medium altitude, long endurance unmanned aerial systems such as Shahed-type strike drones are an unanswered threat in modern conflicts. Conventional air defense systems are too expensive to provide a feasible large-scale solution. Quadcopter interceptors are a cheap, battle-proven alternative, but their extremely limited flight time restricts them to low altitude targets at short range, whereas fixed-wing platforms have the endurance to reach higher altitude targets from longer distances. However, such interceptors are still operated manually. Recent developments in learning-based controllers

title: Physics-Guided Flow Matching: A Generative AI Framework for Global Total Electron Content Forecasting
abstract: Accurate forecasting of global total electron content (TEC) is important for space weather monitoring and the reliable operation of satellite communication and navigation systems. We propose a physics-guided generative artificial intelligence (AI) framework for day-ahead global TEC forecasting. The framework builds on flow matching, which learns to gradually transform samples from an initial distribution into new samples that share the statistical characteristics of the target data. abstract: Model discrepancy may prevent a single calibration parameter from reproducing a physical response across the context domain. In addition, uncertainties in observations and contexts affect calibration and must be accounted for and quantified. We construct a family of localized posteriors by weighting observation likelihoods according to their proximity to a target context. title: Zonal-Aware Prostate Cancer Detection and Classification via Hadamard-Fused Mamba-UNet
abstract: Accurate clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) detection from prostate MRI requires a detailed understanding of the prostate anatomical context. Deep learning approaches have achieved promising results in zonal and lesion segmentation; however, the joint analysis of prostate zonal anatomy and lesion morphology in a unified framework remains relatively underexplored. abstract: Small heritage and nature sites need a few days' notice of busy days to plan staff, overflow parking and shuttles, but most have neither sensors nor forecasting expertise. We test what one artificial intelligence (AI) camera counter per site, a public holiday calendar and a free weather forecast can predict. title: From Stochastic Transport Models to High-Dimensional Bayesian Inference
abstract: The Stochastic Transport in Upper Ocean Dynamics project introduced a new paradigm for representing uncertainty in geophysical fluid dynamics through stochastic transport models calibrated from data. This paper provides a synthesis of the principal theoretical and data assimilation developments achieved as part of the project. title: Stability-Performance Trade-off in Maritime Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Computation: A Lyapunov-Guided Dual-Timescale Hierarchical RL Approach
abstract: Driven by the ever-growing demand for intelligent maritime services, cooperative unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and unmanned surface vehicle (USV) operations, together with wireless integrated sensing, communication, and computation (ISCC), have become pivotal in maritime environments. title: CARM: Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking for Reliable Scientific Super-Resolution
abstract: Deep learning-based super-resolution (SR) can reconstruct fine-scale Earth-observation fields from coarse observations, but reconstruction accuracy alone does not provide a calibrated rule for identifying reliable spatial regions. Conformal Mask Calibration (CMC), built on conformal risk control, converts a spatial uncertainty score into a trust mask and controls the expected worst-case local distortion under exchangeability. title: KAUSTics-Net: Diffusion-Based Through-Water UAV Restoration with a Semi-Synthetic Dataset
abstract: Accurate mapping of shallow-water environments using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery is challenged by water-induced distortions, including refraction, caustics, and wavelength-dependent attenuation. The scarcity of paired distorted and reference imagery further limits the development of supervised restoration methods. title: Dynamic conditional density network of wind vectors
abstract: We propose the dynamic conditional density network (DCDN) to correct the bivariate normal predictive distribution commonly used to postprocess ensemble forecasts of wind vectors. The conditional distribution of the observed wind vector given the ensemble forecast may depart from the bivariate normal distribution. DCDN multiplies a bivariate normal reference density by a correction density. title: Moving bits instead of watts: Accelerating global AI data-centre deployment at the energy-digital-water-land nexus
abstract: Artificial intelligence is driving an unprecedented expansion of data centres. However, this growth is increasingly stalled by grid transmission constraints that trap new data centres in years-long connection queues. Unlike electricity, computation can be moved across the globe through fibre-optic networks, but whether this spatial transfer can bypass constrained grids and accelerate global AI data-centre deployment remains unknown. title: Multistep and Multivariate Time Series Explainability with GradientSHAP: A Wind Power Case Study
abstract: As the effects of climate change become increasingly apparent, the demand for renewable energy sources such as wind power continues to grow. However, renewables' variable and intermittent nature presents significant challenges in their integration into energy grids. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful tool to address these issues. Still, its adoption in the energy sector has been hindered by the opacity of many AI models, which often function as black boxes. title: AI for Science in Space: Orbital Laboratories, Planetary Fieldwork, and Embodied Autonomy
abstract: Artificial intelligence for science (AI4S) is extending from interpretation of existing data to the design and execution of experiments. Space offers distinctive scientific opportunities while restricting physical support. Microgravity and extraterrestrial environments expose phenomena that terrestrial experiments cannot fully reproduce; finite samples, constrained resources, and limited opportunities for intervention complicate sustained investigation. This critical review examines orbital laboratories and planetary in situ science across biology, materials, fluid and thermal physics, and ada

title: Local Spatial TreeSHAP: Geographically Explainable AI Revealing Urbanization-Dependent Spatial Heterogeneity in Flood Resilience
abstract: Urban flood resilience emerges from complex interactions among natural, built, and socio-economic systems, yet most recovery policies implicitly assume that resilience mechanisms are spatially uniform. To address this gap, this study develops a spatially explainable machine learning framework that integrates geographically weighted random forests with a novel Local Spatial TreeSHAP algorithm, enabling nonlinear resilience mechanisms to be identified and interpreted at the community scale. title: Directional Statistics on Circles and Spheres: A New Angle on Data
abstract: Two compass bearings near north can have an ordinary arithmetic mean pointing south: the difficulty is that angles live on a circle, not a straight line. Using real wind observations, diffusion-MRI orientations, and geometric examples from machine learning, this article introduces circular and axial averages, directional variability, and probability models on circles and spheres. The guiding principle is to identify the geometry and symmetries of the observations before choosing a statistical method.

title: Scale-aware and spatially-localised optimisation of kilometre-scale MLWP models
abstract: Preserving fine-scale structure without degrading spatial accuracy is a central challenge for kilometre-scale machine-learning weather prediction (MLWP). We introduce a loss based on the dual-tree complex wavelet transform that constrains atmospheric fields jointly by scale, location, and orientation. We evaluate its performance using an experimental joint global--regional FastNet configuration, which produces \SI{1.5}{km} forecasts over the UK alongside $\sim$\SI{31}{km} global forecasts. title: MARINER: A 3E-Driven Benchmark for Fine-Grained Perception and Complex Reasoning in Open-Water Environments
abstract: Fine-grained visual understanding and high-level reasoning in real-world open-water environments remain under-explored due to the lack of dedicated benchmarks. We introduce MARINER, a comprehensive benchmark built under the novel Entity-Environment-Event (3E) paradigm. MARINER contains 16,629 multi-source maritime images with 63 fine-grained vessel categories, diverse adverse environments, and 5 typical dynamic maritime incidents, covering fine-grained classification, object detection, and visual question answering tasks. We conduct extensive evaluations on mainstream Multimodal Large language

title: Robust 3DMA GNSS Positioning in Urban Areas Using Conservative Candidate Set Determination Based on GNSS Shadow and Reflection
abstract: In urban environments, global navigation satellite system (GNSS) positioning is often degraded by signal blockage and reflection caused by surrounding buildings. To address this problem, various three-dimensional mapping-aided (3DMA) GNSS techniques have been proposed. Among them, zonotope shadow and reflection matching (ZSRM) has demonstrated effective positioning performance by determining the candidate receiver position set using predicted GNSS shadow and reflection regions. However, ZSRM remains vulnerable to satellite signal misclassification, which may lead to positioning failure. To add

title: Satellite Intelligence: Distributed Training, Collaborative Inference,and LLM Adaptation in LEO Constellation
abstract: The proliferation of orbital sensing data and the real-time demands of emerging global services are pushing low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks from bent-pipe relays toward intelligent onboard processing. This shift confronts a fundamental tension, where modern artificial intelligence (AI) training paradigms require intensive computation, abundant memory, and stable connectivity, all of which are scarce under the dynamic topologies, intermittent links, and severe size, weight, and power (SWaP) constraints of satellite networks. Addressing this tension demands rethinking AI workflows, from
institutions: Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust

title: Value of Adding AI Weather Model Ensembles to a Multi-model Probabilistic Blend
abstract: Many weather forecasting organizations use a multi-model blend of ensemble members from different prediction systems to obtain a more accurate forecast. Recent studies have shown that blending deterministic AI-based models alongside physics-based models improves the overall forecast skill. However, the incorporation of an ensemble AI-based model into a multi-model blend is yet to be investigated. This study explores the value of blending the ensemble version of the Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System (AIFS-CRPS) with the Met Office's convection permitting physics-based ensemble, MOGREPS

title: Short-Term Forecasting of Heterogeneous Wind Power Fleets: Global Temporal Fusion Transformer Leveraging Static Covariates
abstract: Accurate short-term wind power forecasting is critical for grid stability and electricity trading. While transformer-based deep learning is state of the art, industry practice relies mostly on local models trained for individual assets. This study investigates whether a global temporal fusion transformer (TFT), trained jointly on a heterogeneous portfolio of wind farms across Germany, outperforms site-specific local models in 48-hour-ahead forecasting. Using numerical weather prediction (NWP) data from the regional ICON-D2 and the global ECMWF HRES models, we compare the global TFT against loc

title: Exploring perceptual straightness in learned visual representations
abstract: Humans have been shown to use a "straightened" encoding to represent the natural visual world as it evolves in time (Hénaff et al. 2019). In the context of discrete video sequences, "straightened" means that changes between frames follow a more linear path in representation space at progressively deeper levels of processing. While deep convolutional networks are often proposed as models of human visual processing, many do not straighten natural videos. In this paper, we explore the relationship between network architecture, differing types of robustness, biologically-inspired filtering mechani
institutions: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

title: Tunable Spatial Task Allocation with Application to Maritime Swarms
abstract: In this chapter, we explore how a team of autonomous agents can flexibly reconfigure the distribution of its members across many spatially embedded tasks using a task allocation strategy grounded in a generalization of the recently proposed Nonlinear Opinion Dynamics model. Motivated by an adaptive maritime survey application, we couple opinion dynamics directly to spatial movement and examine how the emergent macroscopic allocation is shaped by the interplay between environmental geometry, nature of social interactions, and task demands. title: Efficient Closure Learning in Dynamical Systems: A Comparison of Data-Assimilated and Embedded Approaches
abstract: Increased computing power has transformed computational science and improved predictive capabilities for complex systems, but many phenomena still exceed current simulation capabilities or require rapid evaluations for fast design iterations. Closure models address this challenge by approximating unresolved effects in reduced or incomplete dynamical systems. Data-driven closures offer a flexible mechanism for improving model accuracy and applicability, but approaches that embed the closure within a computational model for construction and training phases can be computationally expensive and ca

title: TSB-SEG: A Systematic Time-Series Segmentation Benchmark
abstract: Time-series segmentation, studied as either Change Point Detection (CPD) or State Detection (SD), underpins a broad range of monitoring and diagnostic applications. However, the field suffers from a persistent divide between the statistical community (focusing on CPD) and the machine learning and data mining communities (focusing on SD). Consequently, the literature remains fragmented: evaluations typically cover narrow methodological families, datasets are often small or homogeneous, and CPD and SD are rarely evaluated together. We address these gaps with TSB-SEG, a unified benchmark comprisi
institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Water at the molecular frontier
abstract: Much of the water that matters most - flowing through biological cells and membranes, percolating through soils and rocks, or processed by filtration and desalination technologies - is not bulk water. It is water in nano- and molecular-scale confinement or at interfaces. Nanoscale water is therefore central to many challenges of our time, from the global water crisis and the water-energy nexus to catalysis, electrochemistry, and health. Beyond its applications, nanoscale water has emerged as a rich scientific field in its own right: discoveries are accumulating rapidly, revealing that confinem
institutions: Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research
Laboratoire de Physique de l'Ecole Normale Supérieure

title: CONSORT: Uncertainty-Constrained Multi-Robot Planning for Cooperative Localization in GPS-Denied Environments
abstract: Centralized multi-agent path planning with cooperative localization in GPS-denied environments is generally computationally intractable when formulated in full belief space due to tightly coupled uncertainty dynamics. Prior work typically approximates belief dynamics or restricts inter-agent coupling. This work examines a multi-agent planning problem in which a primary agent must reach a goal in minimum time subject to a chance-constrained collision-avoidance requirement and a terminal bound on localization uncertainty. We obtain a tractable surrogate of the underlying belief-space problem by

title: Submerged Immiscible Oil Jet: Breakup Dynamics and Droplet Size Modelling
abstract: Immiscible liquid-liquid jets occur in numerous industrial and environmental settings, including oil spill response and liquid-liquid extraction, yet the coupled evolution of turbulence, interfacial instability, and droplet size distribution across transitional to turbulent regimes remains poorly understood. We present a combined experimental and theoretical investigation of a silicone oil jet injected into refractive-index-matched sugar water, employing simultaneous Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) and Planar Laser-Induced Fluorescence (PLIF). Beyond the breakup region, mean velocity and Reyn

title: Generated storm lifecycles fill the rare-event tail of short rainfall records
abstract: Historically rare ''one-in-a-generation'' storms are occurring with unprecedented frequency, causing catastrophic damage and mounting casualties, and exposing the vulnerability of infrastructure designed around short observational records. To overcome the limitations of sparse data, we present StormGen, a generative machine-learning model that transforms an observed storm's initial hours into complete, physically plausible hourly rainfall lifecycles in minutes. Evaluated on a decade of southeast Texas rainfall, StormGen produced close counterparts for 4\5% of the most severe 2\% of storms--com

title: Meta Models: Models that Model Learning
abstract: Every neural-network training run produces not only a model, but also evidence about how models learn. Can these accumulated experiments enable us to predict and compare new training runs before executing them? We study meta-models: models that predict the learning behavior of other models. From this perspective, final-performance prediction, learning-curve prediction, and hyperparameter selection are different queries to the same training response function. title: Variational wavefunctions for ideal anyon gas: superfluid and skyrmion Hall crystal
abstract: The ground state of an ideal gas of anyons with statistical angle $θ\in(0,π)$ is a long-standing open problem, with renewed interest from the recent observations of fractional Chern insulators. In this work we construct variational wavefunctions that build in the exact anyon statistics and combine theory-guided composite-boson, composite-fermion and parton wavefunctions with neural-network correlations on the sphere. title: An end-to-end CNN search for ultra-short-period planets in TESS: from the blend ceiling to the independent validation of TOI-6662 b
abstract: We trained a convolutional neural network to detect ultra-short-period planets in TESS photometry, following the procedure now standard in the field: synthetic transits as positives, eclipsing binaries as negatives. Measured that way it reaches an area under the ROC curve of 0.97. Keeping the same model and the same planets, but replacing the negatives with false positives that the TESS Follow-up Observing Program has actually rejected, the area falls to 0.50 -- the value of a random classifier. title: EvoBench: An Evolving, Diagnostic Benchmark Framework for Environmental Modeling
abstract: Machine learning models are now widely used to predict environmental variable dynamics in domains like hydrology, climate science, agriculture, and ecology. These models are usually compared on fixed benchmark datasets using a single average accuracy score. As models improve, their scores become very close when averaged over large regions and long time periods, so the benchmark can no longer tell them apart, and a single number hides \emph{where} and \emph{when} a model fails. institutions: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

title: A Common Language for Dynamic Graphs: Interaction Tokenization Enables Foundation Models
abstract: Dynamic graphs capture evolving interactions in Web systems, including online communication, user engagement, and recommendation. Graph foundation models aim to reuse predictive capabilities across networks, but extending this capability to dynamic graphs faces two challenges. First, node identities are graph-specific, and similar interaction patterns can appear at different temporal and activity scales, making histories difficult to represent consistently across networks. Second, the predictive roles of historical patterns vary across interaction dynamics, limiting transfer from a narrow rang

title: PhysicsNeMo-Mesh: GPU-Native Meshes and Simulation Cases for Physics AI
abstract: PhysicsNeMo-Mesh is the mesh module of the open-source PhysicsNeMo library. It provides mesh processing similar to PyVista, but on the GPU, in batches, and inside PyTorch's automatic differentiation. Like xarray for unstructured meshes, it attaches semantics to data: fields on points, cells, and whole meshes have names and shapes, and a simulation case keeps the complete PDE problem specification, including boundary conditions and their prescribed values. title: TOWARDS PRECISION-CONTROLLED PARTONIC STRUCTURES FROM FIRST PRINCIPLES
abstract: The internal structure of hadrons is governed by nonperturbative Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and is being probed with increasing precision by modern high-energy experiments. This dissertation presents first-principles calculations of partonic observables using lattice QCD together with effective field theory methods, with controlled systematic uncertainties, advancing from collinear structure to transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (TMDs) that encode the three-dimensional partonic structure of hadrons. Within the large momentum effective theory (LaMET) framework, this work presents sta

title: Data Center Agglomeration and Power Infrastructure Capacity in the United States
abstract: The continuous expansion of digital infrastructure especially data centers has imposed unprecedented and geographically concentrated stress on existing power grids. However, rigorous causal evidence quantifying how these facilities reshape local power infrastructure supply remains limited. This study constructs a comprehensive county-level panel dataset spanning the United States from 2010 to 2024, uniquely integrating individual data center building area footprints with power plant additions. To overcome endogeneity and high-dimensional confounding, this study employs Double Machine Learning

title: Universal Short-Time Fourier Transform: Data-Adaptive Window-Length Selection for Time-Frequency Analysis
abstract: The short-time Fourier transform (STFT) characterizes the local frequency content of time-varying signals by evaluating the discrete Fourier transform over a sliding analysis window. The STFT is governed by a fundamental resolution trade-off: a short window localizes rapid transients in time at the cost of frequency resolution, whereas a long window resolves closely spaced harmonics at the expense of temporal resolution. title: Trajeform: Embedding Crowd Data
abstract: Crowd simulation aims to generate agent behaviours that are rich, natural, and appropriate to their surrounding environment. Recent advances in Machine Learning have enabled such behavioural patterns to be learned directly from trajectory data, allowing simulation models to capture increasingly complex crowd dynamics. However, the capabilities of these systems remain strongly dependent on the type and diversity of the data used during training. When evaluating how well crowd simulators generalise to real-world datasets, most existing metrics focus primarily on trajectory-level differences rath

title: The Hidden Value of Soft Infrastructure for Urban Flood Adaptation
abstract: As sea level rises and flooding events become more frequent, cities are tapping into a range of engineering and planning solutions to reduce flood losses. Beyond traditional ``hard'' infrastructure (e.g., sewage, seawalls), ``soft'' infrastructure that supports and empowers the role of citizens in preparedness has been hailed as a promising avenue for improving adaptation. Despite its promise, there have been very limited attempts to quantify its effectiveness in reducing losses relative to hard infrastructure, particularly in urban environments. This study fills this knowledge gap using gener

title: Inference for conditional Fréchet means via Riemannian Robust Bias Correction
abstract: We develop an intrinsic framework for inference on conditional Fréchet means with predictors and responses taking values in finite-dimensional Riemannian manifolds. We derive a second-order expansion of the smoothing bias, represented in the tangent space via the logarithm map, and show that this bias can affect first-order inference. We propose Riemannian robust bias correction (RRBC), which estimates the leading smoothing bias using a local quadratic regression in the response tangent space and corrects the estimator through the exponential map. title: The Structure of Disagreement in Emotion Annotation
abstract: Calculating inter-annotator agreement is an established practice in NLP, and disagreement-aware work increasingly retains the distribution of human judgments rather than reducing annotations to a single gold label. Keeping the distribution, however, does not explain why annotators disagree. This paper examines the types of disagreement that occur in emotion annotation, starting from multilabel annotations of 1,677 sentence-level units from Ernest Hemingway's The Old Man and the Sea and testing the patterns they reveal against individual-level annotations from BRIGHTER and GoEmotions. Across th

title: Dolphin broadband transient vocalization detection in impulsive ambient noise
abstract: Passive acoustic monitoring in tropical waters such as those in Southeast Asia is hampered by the persistent, high-level impulsive noise of snapping shrimp. This is a particularly daunting challenge for detecting broadband transient vocalizations of dolphins - clicks, buzzes and burst-pulses. These vocalizations, unlike frequency-modulated whistles, share the broadband, impulsive character of the shrimp snaps and cannot be easily separated from them by frequency-localized or energy-based means. We develop TRIDENT, a lightweight waveform-based detector for these vocalizations, and apply it to 5

title: ODC: Orthogonal Drift Correction for Improved Text-to-Image Semantic Alignment at Inference
abstract: Text-to-image models have achieved remarkable success in generating high-quality images from textual descriptions. However, they often struggle with "semantic drift," where the generated output fails to precisely align with complex or nuanced text prompts. While recent approaches have attempted to address semantic errors regarding attribute binding or object presence, there remains a gap for a more holistic method that addresses these issues by directly refining the text embeddings of the initial user prompt. In this work, we introduce Orthogonal Drift Correction (ODC), an inference-time guida

title: Comparative study of global pooling for pre-departure ship fuel consumption prediction: Advantages over per-ship and adaptation-based approaches
abstract: Most fuel oil consumption (FOC) models for voyage planning are per-ship models and thus generalize poorly beyond each vessel's records. Transfer and federated learning have been reported to perform better, but under different protocols that often use inputs unavailable before departure or random data splits. It therefore remains unclear which approach performs best. In this study, we compare 11 per-ship, adaptation-based, and global methods on 21 vessels. To prevent leakage, all methods receive identical inputs known or forecast before departure, excluding engine RPM and shaft power, and are t

title: Spectral delocalization and central limit theorems for Fourier functionals of stationary Gaussian fields
abstract: We characterize Gaussian fluctuations of Fourier-Hermite functionals of stationary Gaussian fields on locally compact Abelian groups via spectral delocalization: conditional on the total spectral sum being near the probed frequency, no partial sum concentrates. Under suitable assumptions, this reduces Gaussian convergence to small-ball estimates for convolution powers of the spectral measure, without model-specific contraction estimates. title: Spatial-Spectral Interactive POCS Network for Large-Gap Seismic Data Interpolation
abstract: Large gaps in seismic acquisition disrupt reflection events and hinder spectral recovery. Existing seismic interpolation deep unfolding networks primarily rely on localized spatial priors, limiting their ability to aggregate the global context necessary for reconstructing these extensive missing regions. We propose a spatial-spectral interactive projection-onto-convex-sets network (SSI-POCS) to tackle this severely ill-posed problem.
