title: Progressively Refining SAM for Accurate Phytoplankton Segmentation
abstract: Accurate phytoplankton segmentation is essential for ecological monitoring, yet it remains largely underexplored due to the subtle visual characteristics of phytoplankton and the scarcity of pixel-level annotations. To address these challenges, we propose PhySeg, a SAM-based segmentation framework equipped with a lightweight refinement module that progressively restores fine-grained details through multi-scale feature fusion. In addition, we construct a phytoplankton segmentation dataset by manually annotating instance-level masks for an existing dataset, providing a valuable resource for futu

title: Align, Don't Blend: Orthogonal Supervision Disentanglement As the Key to Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection
abstract: Recent advances in AI-Generated Image (AIGI) detection have largely focused on model architectures, loss design, and training strategies, while overlooking a more fundamental factor: how supervision is structured. Existing detectors typically train on benchmark-defined data that implicitly blends semantic and artifact signals, leaving supervision design unexplored. In this paper, we examine supervision structure through controlled experiments and show that such blended supervision is not merely suboptimal but fundamentally counterproductive. Replacing it with disentangled, orthogonal supervisi
institutions: East China University of Science and Technology
Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: Forecasting Earth Surface Change in Embedding Space
abstract: Repeated satellite imagery permits understanding of how our planet changes over time, letting us predict its future and plan mitigating actions. Most existing studies that rely on a time series of satellite observations forecast the spectral values at each pixel for a future target date. However, clouds, shadows, and sensor noise often corrupt these observations, so that spectral forecasters waste much of their capacity on low-level features or noise rather than real change. LithoFormer: A Robust Framework for Stratigraphic Inference via Geology-Informed Multi-Task Transformers
abstract: Accurate geological characterization of subsurface reservoirs from well log data is essential to support projects such as carbon capture and storage (CCS), geothermal development, and extraction of natural resources. Existing automated techniques for geological characterization primarily use sliding-window classification, which limits their ability to understand broader geological contexts, often leading to misaligned formation layers. title: Mind the Rift: Cross-Scale Coupling Mismatch for AI-Generated Video Detection
abstract: As AI video generators achieve cinematic realism, reliable detection becomes essential for safeguarding digital trust. We identify cross-scale coupling mismatch as a new forensic signal, where scale refers to the level of abstraction (semantic dynamics vs. pixel-level residuals): in natural videos, macro-level temporal dynamics and micro-level residual patterns are intrinsically coupled by the unified imaging physics pipeline, whereas AI generators, whose training objectives do not explicitly preserve this joint distribution, systematically violate this coupling. title: OmniClimate-TC: Physics-Aware Visual Abstractions for Multimodal Vision–Language Reasoning over Tropical Cyclones
abstract: Meteorological reanalysis encodes extreme weather through continuous, physically constrained fields, posing a fundamental challenge for vision–language models (VLMs) whose perceptual assumptions are shaped by natural images. Tropical cyclones exemplify this mismatch: critical properties such as intensity extrema, asymmetry, spatial extent, and physical impacts arise from field-level organization rather than object-centric visual cues. title: Efficient probabilistic weather forecasting at quarter-degree resolution with two-sided transport attention
abstract: High-resolution probabilistic weather forecasting remains computationally demanding. Here we present Astra, a 0.25$^\circ$ ensemble model trained on eight H200 GPUs. It combines Kantorovich Attention, a two-sided transport attention in which each region chooses where it reads from and writes to, so every region sends and receives at token resolution, with a self-featurised continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) that also scores forecasts in the model's multiscale features. title: DOSE: Dominance-Guided Ordinal Severity Estimation from Sparse Relative Annotations
abstract: Medical severity estimation commonly relies on absolute grade annotations, which are fundamentally ordinal, yet existing methods often treat the grades as independent categories. Learning-to-rank methods, which can be trained using relative annotations based on severity comparisons of image pairs, can provide continuous severity rankings but cannot directly predict discrete severity grades. title: MLLM-GS: Multimodal Large Language Model Prior-Guided Fast Novel View Synthesis in Extreme Environments
abstract: Novel view synthesis (NVS) in degraded scenes aims to reconstruct 3D scenes from multi-view observations affected by various degradations, and to generate clear and photorealistic images at unseen viewpoints. Despite recent advances, existing methods often rely on degradation-specific models, limiting their generalization across diverse extreme environments. Generative models provide rich visual priors, but their outputs often suffer from pixel misalignment and color deviations, which can propagate into the reconstructed 3D scene and compromise reconstruction quality. title: AI in the EGI e-infrastructure -- Past experiences and future strategies
abstract: The EGI Federation has provided federated e-infrastructure services to European and global science for over 15 years. We review EGI's early experiences with AI in the interTwin and iMagine Horizon Europe projects, which built digital twins in physics and environmental sciences and an image-analysis platform for aquatic research. We then examine how the AI landscape has changed since 2023 and argue that the focus of AI in science has shifted from model training to adapting and applying AI to specific domains, projects and questions. title: Myoelectric Control for Upper-Limb Exoskeletons: A Decoder-Shaper-Controller Framework, Design Guidelines, and Future Directions
abstract: Myoelectric Control Systems (MCSs) enable voluntary control of wearable robots through muscle activity. However, intention decoding, assistance shaping, and low-level actuator control are often not explicitly distinguished, making their contributions difficult to evaluate and compare. This review introduces a functional decoder-shaper-controller framework for continuous myoelectric control of upper-limb exoskeletons. title: Rare Concept Generation via Counterfactual Inference in Diffusion Models
abstract: Rare concept generation focuses on synthesizing customized images conditioned on text prompts that describe objects with unusual attributes. Previous works failed to align the generated images with rare concepts, resulting in incorrect attribute rendering or inconsistent composition of concepts. Such failures, as we observed, stem from the inherent common knowledge bias in the training stage of diffusion models, where objects are strongly associated with their common attributes, making it difficult to break these associations when generating rare concepts. title: DynaSolver: A Neural Operator for Autoregressive 4D Flow Prediction with Dynamic Boundaries
abstract: Neural operators provide efficient surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD), but most are designed for static geometries and are not equipped to model unsteady flows induced by continuously moving boundaries. We study dynamic-boundary 4D CFD prediction for articulated moving geometries and introduce RoboCFD-4D, a temporally resolved robotic CFD benchmark spanning diverse morphologies and flow conditions. title: A Semigroup-Aware Kernel Neural Operator with Latent Exponential Integration for Forced PDEs
abstract: We propose a semigroup-aware structured kernel neural operator for source-driven evolution PDEs. Unlike generic time-conditioned kernel models, the proposed formulation represents temporal dependence through a latent exponential propagator \(e^{tA_θ}\), where \(A_θ\) is a learned latent generator. This provides a structured transition from a non-ODE kernel representation to an ODE-inspired kernel operator whose latent temporal evolution satisfies the composition principle of evolution semigroups. institutions: Institute for High Performance Computing and Networking

title: When appearance and motion disagree: evaluating class-motion consistency against disguised uncrewed surface vessels
abstract: Defense systems for maritime assets must distinguish approaching benign craft from uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) with sufficient warning to act. Shore cameras using computer vision can separate hostile vessels from benign traffic, but these systems may be attacked using an adversarial hull patch or physical disguise. We evaluate adversarial hull patches and find they suppress detection in up to 29% of attempts but never cause misclassification as benign. title: Spatial Atlas-Informed Loss Ensembles for Whole-Body PSMA PET/CT Metastasis Segmentation
abstract: Existing whole-body PSMA PET/CT prostate metastasis segmentation methods generally rely on images alone, without explicitly incorporating where metastases tend to occur. We investigate whether a population metastasis atlas can improve lesion detection when integrated into model training. We constructed voxel-wise mean and standard deviation maps from 375 expert-annotated training scans and used them to weight the cross-entropy loss of an nnU-Net. title: Specification-Aware Predictive Uncertainty Decomposition
abstract: Classical decompositions of predictive uncertainty, such as the information-theoretic one, are defined for a fixed representation $x$ of the input object. They do not consider that $x$ may be incomplete, nor do they measure how much the missing information can affect the prediction. In Large Language Models, users can clarify an underspecified input without any retraining. The clarified input can describe the user's unobserved intent $z^*$ more accurately and change the predictive uncertainty about the outcome. In this paper, we formalize this setting probabilistically and derive a three-term

title: AeroMiG: Multi-modal Inverse-Gamma modeling for aerosol particle number size distributions
abstract: Abstract. Aerosol particles play a critical role in air quality, human health, and climate processes, making their accurate characterization essential. One common way to represent aerosol populations is through particle number size distributions (PNSDs), which describe the concentration of particles across different mobility diameters. However, these distributions are often highly skewed, heavy-tailed, and multi-modal, posing significant challenges for conventional fitting approaches. title: HoloGeo: Mitigating Landmark Bias in Geo-localization via Evidence-Driven Reasoning
abstract: Recent advances in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have significantly improved image geo-localization, yet existing models remain susceptible to landmark bias, causing them to overlook geographical cues or form spurious correlations, ultimately resulting in inaccurate localization. To systematically investigate this issue, we first design two quantitative metrics, Bias Intensity (BI) and Bias Harmfulness (BH), to characterize the impact of landmarks exerted on model reasoning, and establish a comprehensive benchmark, LandmarkBias-3K. institutions: Shandong University of Science and Technology

title: Bridging Low-Level Image Fusion and High-Level Semantic Understanding
abstract: Remote sensing image fusion and semantic interpretation are usually optimized separately, so reconstruction quality need not preserve downstream retrieval utility. We propose LANCE, which uses structured language as an explicit, indexable semantic state. A frozen vision-language model maps the input to a closed-vocabulary text record; a language-conditioned generator fuses the imagery; and a dense verifier with a differentiable continuous summarizer re-describes the output. title: Sparse Reconstruction by Direct Measurement-to-Field Generation in Function Space
abstract: Understanding physical systems often requires recovering their full spatial state from measurements available only at sparse locations. This reconstruction becomes challenging when physical boundaries are unknown, high-resolution training fields are unavailable, or important quantities cannot be measured directly. Sparse observations may also be consistent with multiple plausible states, leading to significant reconstruction uncertainty. title: Can LLM Agents Improve Imperfect Earth System Model Parameterizations?
abstract: Earth system models (ESMs) rely on parameterizations to represent unresolved processes such as convection, cloud microphysics, and turbulence. However, translating advances in physical understanding into stable, validated parameterizations and integrating them into ESMs often takes years. Agentic AI could accelerate this process and enable more systematic exploration of design choices. title: FDA-Opt: Federated Fine-Tuning via Dynamic Update Schedules
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables the utilization of vast, previously inaccessible data sources. At the same time, pre-trained Language Models (LMs) have taken the world by storm and for good reason. They exhibit remarkable emergent abilities and are readily adapted to downstream tasks. This opens one of the most exciting frontiers in FL: fine-tuning LMs. Yet, a persistent challenge in FL is the frequent, rigid communication of parameters—a problem magnified by the sheer size of these contemporary models. title: Multifidelity variational inference for derivative-free PDE-constrained inverse problems
abstract: We develop a multifidelity black-box variational inference (MF-BBVI) approach for PDE-constrained Bayesian inverse problems in which forward solves are expensive and PDE gradients are unavailable. The method is built on score-function estimators for the evidence lower bound (ELBO), which avoid differentiation through the PDE model but are known to suffer from high variance. title: AI-Aided and AI-Oriented Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Computation: A Survey
abstract: The evolution from 5G to 6G networks marks a transition toward the "intelligence of everything." While 5G enables enhanced connectivity, 6G aspires to embed intelligence directly into communication infrastructures, creating systems that are adaptive, context aware, and capable of autonomous decision making. Realizing such systems depends on harmonizing three fundamental functions that compete for shared network resources and often pursue conflicting goals: (i) sensing for environmental and contextual information acquisition, (ii) communication for reliable and timely information exchange, and

title: Supraglacial Lake Fate Is Knowable Long Before the Season Ends
abstract: A supraglacial lake on the Greenland Ice Sheet ends its melt season in one of four ways: it drains rapidly through a hydrofracture, drains slowly across the surface, refreezes in place, or is buried by late-season snowfall. Which one occurs decides whether the melt-water reaches the ice bed. Satellite classifiers recover the outcome accurately but only after the season closes, and how much of a season each outcome actually requires has never been measured. We measure it directly: holding the representation and the classifier fixed, we truncate the input at 14 cutoffs from May 1 to December 31,

title: A Hybrid Visitor Prediction Framework using Interpretable Temporal features, Integrating IQR and Anomaly Detection in Lakes in Nebraska
abstract: For effective resource management, infrastructure planning, and sustainable tourism, it is really important to predict accurate visitors. This paper estimates the daily visitation of Nebraska lakes using spatial, basic temporal, and interpretable temporal features. Moreover, we evaluate the base models with multiple metrics. Using the best three models, our method will ensemble hybrid models and choose the best hybrid technique. Further, we investigate the impact of lag features and how the models work with different outlier detection techniques such as Interquartile Range (IQR) and anomaly de

title: Deep Bayesian Filtering for Nonlinear Structural System Identification: A Tutorial on Structural and Physical Inductive Biases
abstract: Nonlinear structural system identification remains challenging when governing physics is only partially known and measurements are sparse. Deep Bayesian filtering addresses these challenges by combining learnable dynamical representations with probabilistic state-space models, physical inductive biases, and uncertainty-aware inference. This paper presents, for the first time, a unified tutorial treatment of deep Bayesian filtering for nonlinear structural system identification, connecting model formulation, learning, posterior inference, and evaluation. Amortized variational inference and diff

title: Can Open Be Too Open? On the Security and Trustworthiness of Fully Transparent LLMs
abstract: There are different levels of transparency for LLMs: open weights, open data, and/or open pipeline. Recently, more interest has emerged in fully transparent LLMs, i.e., LLMs with fully open weights, data, and training pipeline. Drawing analogies to other fields such as software security, it is often believed that increasing transparency inherently increases the security and trustworthiness of the LLM. However, we argue that such claims need to be critically re-evaluated in the context of LLMs. In this paper, we analyze the impact of transparency on LLM security and trustworthiness by reviewing

title: AMOR: Adaptive Modal Operator Refinement for Operator Learning on Arbitrary Meshes and Irregular 3D Geometries
abstract: Parametric PDEs in science and engineering are often posed on irregular meshes with geometries that may contain holes or complex boundaries, yet popular operator-surrogate architectures such as the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) rely on structured geometries for fast computational kernels. We introduce Adaptive Modal Operator Refinement (AMOR), which replaces FNO's Fourier-based spectral convolutions with reduced-basis blocks and supports both data-driven and prescribed input/output bases through a common encode/decode interface. AMOR thus applies unmodified to arbitrary meshes and, because its

title: Interpretable by Design Tabular Prediction via In-Context Local Linear Learning
abstract: In-context learning (ICL) lets tabular foundation models make predictions without dataset-specific training or fine-tuning. These models achieve strong predictive accuracy, but interpreting how individual features contribute to the prediction remains difficult. In biology, for example, feature contributions can help identify biomarkers or risk genes. Post-hoc interpretability methods assign feature importance scores, but these scores do not indicate what the model actually uses and can lead to explanation errors. We introduce TICL$^3$ (Tabular In-Context Local Linear Learning), an interpretabl

title: Tail persistence of extremes at finite and asymptotic levels with Bayesian hierarchical inference
abstract: Tail persistence characterizes the relative escalation of observations beyond an extreme threshold and complements conventional summaries such as return levels and tail indices. Existing literature is mainly distribution-based and does not account for uncertainty, nonstationarity, or covariate effects. We develop a Bayesian framework for modeling tail persistence under generalized extreme value and generalized Pareto models. We first make explicit the connection between tail persistence and the extreme value index under regular variation, which identifies the asymptotic persistence with $1/(1-

title: Imperceptible and Reversible Adversarial Examples against Vision-Language Models for Privacy Protection
abstract: Vision–Language Models (VLMs) offer powerful multi-modal ability but also expose users to text-based privacy attacks where adversaries crawl online photos and query VLMs to extract sensitive attributes. Existing reversible adversarial example (RAE) methods protect images in purely visual tasks but fail in multi-modal settings, and current adversarial examples on VLMs rely on high-frequency noise that severely degrades visual quality. We propose CloakDiff, the first framework for reversible, high-fidelity privacy protection against text-based query attacks in VLMs. CloakDiff produces impercepti
institutions: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

title: Beyond Federated Learning: Decentralized Agentic Systems for Self-Evolving Clinical Intelligence
abstract: Clinical expertise is inherently distributed: it resides not in any single dataset or institution but in the accumulated reasoning experiences of thousands of clinicians navigating diverse patient populations, resource constraints, and evolving treatment protocols. Yet current approaches to scaling medical AI, from centralized large language models to federated learning, remain anchored to a data-centric paradigm that treats knowledge as static parameters to be aggregated. In this Perspective, we argue for a fundamental shift from data aggregation to experience aggregation. We propose Decentra

title: Normative Deviation Modeling for EEG-based Depression Detection
abstract: Web-enabled digital health services are expanding access to physiological monitoring and mental health screening. However, electroencephalography (EEG)-based major depressive disorder (MDD) detection remains challenging across heterogeneous data sources, where individual variability and acquisition differences may affect disease-related representations. In this work, we investigate the use of healthy normative references for EEG-based MDD detection. Specifically, structural and distributional reference models are independently trained using healthy control (HC) recordings to characterize depar

title: DICE: Decentralized Incentive-driven Federated Learning for Efficient & Scalable Customization of Pretrained Models in Web3
abstract: Customizing Pretrained Models (PMs) for downstream tasks demands task-specific data, which burgeoning Web3 applications provide abundantly. Blockchain-powered federated learning (BCFL) offers a secure and privacy-preserving paradigm to customize PMs among self-interested and untrusted Web3 participants. Yet, existing BCFL algorithms face severe efficiency and scalability challenges when applied to large PMs, due to their substantial computational and memory requirements and the hardware constraints of many participants. This paper introduces DICE, a novel BCFL algorithm that addresses the effi

title: Seg2Change: Adapting Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation Model for Remote Sensing Change Detection
abstract: Change detection is a fundamental task in remote sensing, aiming to quantify the impacts of human activities and ecological dynamics on land-cover changes. Existing change detection methods are limited to predefined classes in training datasets, which constrains their scalability in real-world scenarios. In recent years, numerous advanced open-vocabulary semantic segmentation models have emerged for remote sensing imagery. However, there is still a lack of an effective framework for directly applying these models to open-vocabulary change detection (OVCD), a novel task that integrates vision a

title: MetaPOCS: Meta-Learned Multi-Exit Unfolding for Budget-Aware Seismic Data Interpolation
abstract: Seismic data interpolation must reconcile reconstruction fidelity with the computational budgets of acquisition quality control and subsequent imaging. Fixed-depth unfolding networks are optimized for a single operating point, whereas their intermediate estimates may be insufficiently trained for early deployment. We present MetaPOCS, a meta-learned multi-exit unfolding framework for budget-aware seismic interpolation. Building on a spatial--spectral POCS reconstruction backbone, MetaPOCS supervises intermediate stages and preserves the acquired traces at every exit. A Meta-GF-based optimizati

title: Retrieve-then-Adapt: Test-Time Retrieval-Augmentation for Sequential Recommendation
abstract: The sequential recommendation (SR) task aims to predict the next item based on users' historical interaction sequences. Typically trained on historical data, SR models are frozen after deployment, limiting their ability to handle test-time patterns that are rare during training. Existing approaches to address this limitation include test-time training, test-time augmentation, and retrieval-augmented fine-tuning. However, these methods either introduce significant computational overhead, rely on random augmentation strategies, or require a carefully designed two-stage training paradigm. In this

title: With foundation-model features, aggregator complexity does not improve cross-hospital discrimination in gastric whole-slide image classification
abstract: Whole-slide image classifiers are usually developed within one hospital and often go untested at unseen hospitals. We assembled 5,036 haematoxylin-and-eosin-stained gastric slides from five Korean hospitals, scanned at 20x and 40x, and compared multiple-instance learning aggregators under leave-one-hospital-out validation on frozen pathology foundation-model features. A hierarchical patch-region-slide graph aggregator (CHIME-MIL) with site alignment and two-scale fusion reached a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.837, above six conventional attention and tr

title: Synchronous Multi-view Neural Diffusion
abstract: Multi-view learning seeks to learn more comprehensive representations by exploiting the complementarity and consistency across diverse modalities or views. However, existing multi-view fusion strategies treat intra- and inter-view fusion as independent stages, without simultaneously considering the evolution within views and the dependency across views. Such an asynchronous fusion paradigm inevitably constrains cross-view interactions due to conflicting view-specific structural inductive biases. As a result, information flow is prone to distortion and compression along intermediate pathways, c

title: Spatial Uncertainty Analytics for Budget-Limited Inspection of Hyperspectral Scenes
abstract: Land-cover maps classified from wide-area hyperspectral surveys are least reliable along class boundaries and in ambiguous regions, so their errors are spatially structured. We study how this structure can direct a limited verification budget: when a low-altitude UAV or a ground crew can visit only a handful of sites, where it should go depends on how classifier uncertainty is arranged across the scene and how a fixed sensor footprint tiles that arrangement. We estimate a per-pixel uncertainty surface from the disagreement of an ensemble of spectral classifiers and select sites by greedy, fiel

title: Selective Transfer Learning for Groundwater Level Anomaly Forecasting: Accuracy-Risk Trade-offs
abstract: This work studies context-aware selective transfer learning for multi-well groundwater anomaly forecasting in the Netherlands. Source-domain pretraining can raise average accuracy but is not uniformly reliable: it degrades performance on a substantial fraction of heterogeneous wells. Context-Aware Selective Learning (CASL) uses calibration-trained, constrained contextual blending of frozen no-transfer and fixed-transfer parents. Global Convex Blend uses the same parents with one calibration-fitted weight per seed. The corrected task requires nine consecutive observed monthly inputs and an exac

title: O2D-MedNet: An Optimization-Aware Dual-Domain Framework for Robust Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Medical image segmentation (MIS) remains challenging due to composite degradations and multi-scale geometric variations, which jointly impair lesion-background separability, structural consistency, and optimization stability. Existing single-stream frameworks entangle heterogeneous cues within a single representation pathway, while hybrid-stream approaches often rely on generic or static fusion, limiting effective coordination across domains and failing to explicitly address optimization instability. To overcome these limitations, we propose a new optimization-aware dual-domain framework for M

title: Less is More: Concise Retrieval and Critic-based Re-ranking for Composed Image Retrieval
abstract: Zero-shot composed image retrieval (ZS-CIR) aims to retrieve a target image based on a reference image and modification text. Recent approaches commonly rely on large vision-language models to generate target image captions for retrieval. However, these captions may include redundant semantic details, introducing noise when retrieving the target image and leading to suboptimal retrieval results. To address this issue, we propose Less-is-More CIR, a two-stage training-free framework that combines Concise Retrieval and Critic Re-ranking. In the first stage, concise target-oriented captions are g

title: Frequency-induced Tipping: Resonance-Driven Tipping in a Threshold Predator-Prey System
abstract: Tipping points refer to abrupt, substantial, and often irreversible transitions in dynamic systems that can be triggered by minor perturbations. Existing tipping mechanisms are usually classified by the nature of the trigger: bifurcation-induced tipping occurs when a parameter crosses a critical threshold, noise-induced tipping is caused by random perturbations, rate-induced tipping occurs when a system fails to track a moving attractor, and phase-induced tipping is triggered by timed perturbations relative to an oscillatory state. In this paper, we identify a new mechanism for tipping: freque

title: Carbon-Aware Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with Decision-Focused Learning
abstract: Electric vehicles produce no tailpipe emissions, but charging them produces emissions that depend on the time-varying generation mix of the electricity consumed. We study an Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with a carbon-aware objective that accounts for charging-related emissions alongside conventional routing costs. The problem determines routing, charging, and waiting decisions, allowing charging demand to be shifted toward periods with lower grid carbon intensity. Because these decisions depend on forecasts of future carbon intensity, we propose a decision-focused learning approach so that

title: Recall or Relearn? A Mixture of In-Context Experts for Recurring Concept Drift
abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are being applied to Web data streams such as network intrusion detection, where they adapt by updating the labelled rows of their context without retraining. When a past concept returns after leaving the context, a TFM faces a recall-or-relearn decision between restoring stored rows of the concept and relearning it from new labels. We propose MICE (Mixture of In-Context Experts), a training-free learner that cuts the stream into segments at detected changes. It merges a closed segment into a stored context when the TFM's estimated additional error on the segme

title: ShiftRAG: Bypassing the Textual Bottleneck via Decoupled Learning and Continuous Soft Tokens
abstract: Despite advances in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), suppressing hallucinations during complex reasoning remains a persistent challenge. We identify that existing RAG pipelines suffer from a textual bottleneck: by passing only raw text to the generator, they discard discriminative signals of the retriever. Furthermore, recent attempts to unify retrieval and generation within a single LLM induce severe objective conflict and exacerbate the rank collapse of decoder-only architectures, degrading performance on both tasks. To address these limitations, we introduce ShiftRAG, a decoupled RAG f

title: Foundations of Reinforcement Learning and Control: Connections and New Perspectives
abstract: Reinforcement learning and control theory are two adjacent scientific fields that focus on optimizing the controller of unknown dynamical systems using feedback. While both fields have common roots in dynamic programming, they have evolved with distinct methodologies, goals, and cultures. Despite decades of mutual influence, a significant gap persists between the two communities. This tutorial introduces adaptive control, actor-critic reinforcement algorithms, and a new way to combine these two paradigms for data-driven decision making on a classical locomotion control problem. Our aim is to p
institutions: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems

title: Seeing Less in a Sparse World: Cross-View Geolocalization from Limited Field-of-View Observations
abstract: Cross-view geolocalization aims to determine the geographic location of a ground-level image by retrieving its corresponding satellite image, offering a promising alternative for localization in Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)-denied or degraded environments such as urban canyons, dense forests, and disaster scenarios. Despite recent progress, existing approaches remain limited by the lack of globally diverse training datasets and benchmarks that are often geographically restricted. title: Urban functional knowledge transfer through global representations amid uneven data
abstract: Urban functional observations are unevenly distributed worldwide, limiting analysis of how places are organised and used. AlphaEarth Foundations (AEF) provides a globally consistent physical representation. Whether this representation can support transfer of functional knowledge to locations with sparse or absent functional observations, and what governs transfer, remain unclear. We introduce POI-aligned Urban Embedding (PURE), which learns physical-functional relationships between POI-derived semantics and AEF. Across five urban analysis tasks covering 142 countries and territories, PURE incr
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Information Engineering in Surveying Mapping and Remote Sensing

title: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly of Markov Boundary for Tabular Prediction
abstract: Under standard graphical assumptions, the Markov boundary of a target variable is the smallest set of features that renders every other feature redundant. Once the boundary is observed, the target is conditionally independent of the rest of the table. This is a tempting object for tabular prediction, since it names exactly the columns a model should need. Yet modern regressors are still trained on the full feature set. title: VLM-as-a-Judge for Person Re-Identification
abstract: Cloth-changing person re-identification (CC-ReID) is still very challenging, and no method clearly dominates: methods that lead on one benchmark collapse on the others, because they rest on different identity cues. We show that a general-purpose vision-language model (VLM), used zero-shot as a judge for reranking a short candidate list, beats the expert retrieval models it reranks by a wide and consistent margin. institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
École nationale des ponts et chaussées

title: Reinforcement Twinning via Twin-Calibrated Bayesian Policy Search and Replay-Driven Identification
abstract: The feasibility of updating and synchronising digital twins of actuated systems from operational data depends strongly on how the system is controlled and, consequently, on the data generated during operation. This establishes a direct link between control actuation and model identifiability. This work presents a reinforcement-twinning framework that exploits this link through three computational components. institutions: Von Karman Institute for Fluid Dynamics

title: A Distributed Microphone Network for Real-Time Gunshot Detection and Localization in GNSS-Challenged Large Areas
abstract: This paper presents a scalable distributed acoustic surveillance system for real-time gunshot detection and localiza tion in large-area, GNSS-challenged environments. The system consists of multiple low-cost MEMS microphone array units (MAUs) deployed as distributed anchors. Each MAU performs edge-level sound-event detection using a lightweight Sound De tection and Echo Suppression (SDES) algorithm, followed by a TinyML-based classifier for gunshot identification. title: Unrolled gradients in disguise: bridging interpolation-based and Jacobian regularization for stable neural dynamics
abstract: Hybrid models and neural differential equations (NDEs) are becoming increasingly important for modelling physical systems; however, they often encounter stability and accuracy issues during long-term integration. Training on unrolled trajectories is known to limit these divergences but quickly becomes too computationally expensive due to the need to compute gradients over an iterative process, making this method impractical for large-scale physical systems (e.g. weather and climate forecasting). institutions: Laboratoire d'Océanographie et du Climat : Expérimentations et Approches Numériques
Institut national de recherche en sciences et technologies du numérique

title: From Local Recovery to Unified Generation: Discovering Triple Set in Knowledge Graphs via Observation-Anchored Latent Diffusion
abstract: Triple set prediction (TSP) is to recover missing relational triples in a knowledge graph by predicting the triple set instead of isolated links. Existing approaches predominantly rely on the subgraph-based completion paradigm, where the original graph is first partitioned into local subgraphs which are then independently completed. Such a paradigm suffers from fragmented structural reasoning, limited cross subgraph dependency modeling, and missing predictions across subgraphs. institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: Beyond First-Order: Learning Riemannian Geometries for Invariant Visual Place Recognition
abstract: Visual Place Recognition (VPR) demands representations robust to drastic environmental and viewpoint shifts. Existing aggregation paradigms either depend on extensive supervised training or rely on first-order pooling, often struggling to preserve structural correlations under extreme shifts or incurring high adaptation costs. In this work, we propose Riemannian Invariant Aggregation (RIA), a unified geometric framework that explicitly models second-order scene structure on the Symmetric Positive Definite (SPD) manifold. title: Bayesian Offline Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Latent World Models
abstract: Model-based offline multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) provides a promising approach to multi-agent decision-making under partial observability, where the global state is unavailable from offline data. However, limited dataset coverage can lead to substantial out-of-distribution (OOD) model errors, which may mislead policy optimization and degrade downstream performance. title: GS-STVSR: Ultra-Efficient Continuous Spatio-Temporal Video Super-Resolution via 2D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Continuous Spatio-Temporal Video Super-Resolution (C-STVSR) aims to simultaneously enhance the spatial resolution and frame rate of videos by arbitrary scale factors, offering greater flexibility than fixed-scale methods that are constrained by predefined upsampling ratios. In recent years, methods based on Implicit Neural Representations (INR) have made significant progress in C-STVSR by learning continuous mappings from spatio-temporal coordinates to pixel values. institutions: University of Science and Technology of China
University of Science and Technology Beijing

title: Towards operational data-driven regional weather forecasting: extreme-event skill and near-real-time verification with HRRRCast
abstract: Improving convective-scale skill in data-driven regional weather models requires better representing rare high-impact events, training at native resolution, broadening variable output, and demonstrating performance in real-time settings. Here, we evaluate these challenges using HRRRCast, a data-driven convection-allowing emulator trained on the High-Resolution Rapid Refresh (HRRR) analysis data. institutions: Cooperative Institute for Research in Environmental Sciences
Cooperative Institute for Research in the Atmosphere

title: DES-JEPA: Learning a Shared Vocabulary for High-Dimensional Discrete Event Sequences
abstract: Temporal foundation models such as Chronos and TimesFM generalize across domains through a shared numerical observation space. In contrast, discrete event sequences (DESs), including operational event logs or patient clinical-event trajectories, have domain-specific event vocabularies whose labels lack a consistent correspondence across domains. Beyond this lack of consistency, the number of distinct events in real-world settings is high enough to challenge both classical temporal point process modeling and current in-context foundation inference models such as FIM-PP. title: OmniOPD: Stable On-Policy Distillation for Joint Audio-Video Generation
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) elevates joint audio-video generation, but optimizing heterogeneous, modality-specific audio and video rewards often introduces cross-modal interference. On-policy distillation (OPD) alleviates this issue by transferring the capabilities of specialized audio and video RL teachers into a single student model. However, a significant imbalance in cross-modal token counts leaves audio with sparse supervision, causing unstable distillation. institutions: University of Science and Technology of China

title: Understanding and Overcoming Cross-modal Fusion Bias in Multimodal Anomaly Detection From A Fisher Information Perspective
abstract: Current advancements in Multimodal Anomaly Detection (MAD) are largely driven by enhancing multimodal fusion, particularly through the integration of RGB and Depth data for richer anomaly representation. However, less attention was devoted to analyzing the role of cross-modal fusion bias—a well-known challenge in multimodal learning—in MAD. This gap motivates a key question: can we overcome this bias to break the performance bottleneck of current work? In this paper, we first analyze the impact of cross-modal fusion bias in MAD via the Fisher Information Matrix. Then, grounded in these finding

title: ConvRoute-ViT: Convolutional Token Routing for Efficient Vision Transformers
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) achieve strong image recognition performance, but their self-attention increases quadratically with the number of input tokens and makes them computationally expensive. The standard implementation of ViT models treats all patch tokens with equal importance across every layer of the model. This uniform treatment introduces redundant computation and may reduce the model's focus on the most discriminative object regions. institutions: Indian Institute of Information Technology Allahabad

title: dKV Forcing: Separating Generation and Memory Representations through a Differentiable KV Cache
abstract: A causal video generator produces two key--value (KV) states for every segment: the KV it uses while denoising that segment, and the KV it writes into the cache for later segments to read. In a pretrained generator the two already differ substantially, later segments attend to them differently, and replacing the written KV with the generation KV degrades the continuation. title: Structured Prediction for Scalable Spreadsheet Table Understanding: From Cell Types to Table Ranges
abstract: Spreadsheets are a primary medium for publishing tabular data, yet automatically extracting structured content from them remains difficult due to heterogeneous layouts, diverse file formats, and inconsistent organizational conventions. We address two core tasks in spreadsheet understanding: Cell-Type Classification (CTC), which assigns roles to cells, and Table Detection (TD), which identifies table bounding boxes within sheets. institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Generative AI in Turbulence: Foundations, Applications, Validations and Benchmarks
abstract: Generative AI offers new approaches to turbulence problems in which incomplete observations or unresolved d.o.f. admit multiple physically plausible solutions. Potential applications include stochastic closures, super-resolution, data assimilation, uncertainty quantification, and the generation of Eulerian and Lagrangian flow ensembles. However, turbulence is not a conventional image-generation problem. title: Differential rank preservation manifold learning
abstract: Manifold learning methods like t-SNE and UMAP preserve local neighborhoods, but they do not preserve the ranking of the neighbors inside them. Two embeddings can return the same neighbor set while disagreeing on which point is closest. This loss of order degrades downstream applications that value the order in the embedding. We propose Smooth Rank t-SNE (SR-tSNE), which adds a differentiable rank term to the standard t-SNE loss. title: Belief-Driven Search in Connectivity-Constrained Mobile Sensor Networks with Convergence Guarantees
abstract: Multi-agent search and coverage is critical to autonomous exploration, search-and-rescue, and defense applications. This paper investigates settings where a mobile sensor network is tasked with coordinating to discover the position of a stationary target within a bounded region. We develop a Bayesian update scheme where agents iteratively combine local uncertainties derived from their sensor measurements through inverse variance weighting to get a better global understanding of where the target may be located given some prior belief. title: Late Autumn: LLM Agents Specialize a General Multi-Robot Planner for One Warehouse
abstract: No algorithm is best on all problems, but a real warehouse is a narrow problem: its layout and processes rarely change. Operators still run one general multi-robot planner at many sites, because experts cannot tune it for each one. In this work, which we call Late Autumn, we explore whether LLM coding agents running autonomous research can specialize a general planner for one site, trading generality for throughput, much as post-training adapts a pretrained LLM to one task. We study six campaigns on a lifelong planner that combines task assignment with multi-agent path finding, on a floor mode

title: Semi-Supervised Flow Matching for Mosaiced and Panchromatic Fusion Imaging
abstract: Fusing a low resolution (LR) mosaiced hyperspectral image (HSI) with a high resolution (HR) panchromatic (PAN) image offers a promising avenue for video-rate HR-HSI imaging via single-shot acquisition, yet its severely ill-posed nature remains a significant challenge. In this work, we propose a novel semi-supervised flow matching framework for mosaiced and PAN image fusion. title: Learning from high-resolution 2D images to reconstruct 3D microstructures
abstract: High-resolution three-dimensional (3D) microstructure characterization remains difficult to undertake at scale because volumetric imaging at the required spatial resolution is expensive, time-consuming or destructive. In many settings, however, fine-resolution two-dimensional (2D) imaging and lower-resolution volumetric measurements are both readily available. We introduce a Privileged Cross-modal Relational Distillation (PCRD) framework that leverages fine-resolution 2D observations during training to improve specimen-specific 3D reconstruction from lower-resolution volumetric imaging alone.

title: Bayesian Treed Vecchia Gaussian Process Emulation via Sequential Monte Carlo
abstract: Computer models (or simulators) are used in many scientific domains to understand and predict real-world processes, but they are expensive to run. One way to address this hurdle is to use Gaussian processes (GPs). For complex physical systems such as storm surge, simulator outputs often exhibit heterogeneous structures, and many nonstationary GP methods become impractical with several inputs and tens of thousands of runs. title: Leaving, Staying, or Living There? Duration Commonsense Reasoning with Human-LLM Co-annotations
abstract: Gardening in the backyard implies living there, while checking into an Airbnb more likely means staying for a few days. Such duration judgments are important for understanding human mobility, travel behavior, and social context. However, duration is rarely stated explicitly in social media posts and must instead be inferred from noisy textual, visual, and contextual cues. In this paper, we investigate whether vision-language models possess such duration commonsense. title: ProFocus: Interpreting Affective Experience in Artistic Images with Progressive Visual Focusing
abstract: Interpreting the emotional responses triggered by images is central to achieving emotional intelligence. Compared with natural images, visual art is intentionally created to elicit emotional responses from its viewers through abstract concepts and visual metaphors, making affective interpretation particularly challenging. However, most existing methods rely on general-purpose visual embeddings (e.g., CLIP), failing to capture the nuanced cues underlying artistic emotion. institutions: University of Science and Technology of China

title: IOSage: Detecting HPC I/O Bottleneck Patterns to Guide LLM Recommendations
abstract: HPC applications often leave much of their parallel file system's bandwidth unused, and turning their Darshan logs into concrete I/O fixes still requires a scarce I/O expert. Rule-based tools flag counters against thresholds set by experts, and in tools built on large language models (LLMs), such as ION and IOAgent, the LLM decides which bottlenecks a log contains. title: OCELOT: Planetary-Scale Species Distribution Modeling with Satellite Foundation Embeddings
abstract: Large-scale repositories of species observations now contain billions of occurrence records from around the world, but these sightings cluster heavily in human-accessible areas. Existing models use only a small fraction of these records and are not evaluated on extrapolating to remote, unvisited regions--where species distribution models can be used as geographic priors to help classify data from camera traps and acoustic recorders. We scale relative occurrence species distribution models by training a multimodal implicit neural representation network called OCELOT that fuses spatial coordinat

title: Can LLMs Faithfully Solve Ontology Engineering Tasks? A Mechanistic Interpretability Study
abstract: Ontological knowledge underpins large language model (LLM) performance on knowledge-intensive tasks. However, existing evaluations of LLMs' ontological understanding largely rely on behavioral correctness, leaving the underlying mechanisms unexplained. Existing mechanistic interpretability work has largely focused on instance-level factual knowledge, leaving ontological knowledge under-explored. To bridge this gap, we introduce MIOE, a causal-abstraction benchmark that evaluates interchange interventions for two ontology engineering tasks: entity typing and subsumption prediction. MIOE tests w

title: CODE: Cross-Modal Calibration and Dynamic Suppression for Open World Object Detection
abstract: Open World Object Detection (OWOD) built on multimodal foundation models often suffers from semantic ambiguity caused by unidirectional text-to-vision matching, while rigid outlier penalties may over-suppress unknown objects near known-class decision boundaries. We propose CODE (Cross-Modal CalibratiOn and Dynamic SupprEssion), a unified inference-time framework with three complementary components. Cross-Modal Joint Confidence Calibration injects global visual prototypes to calibrate text-driven known-class predictions. Uncertainty-Guided Universal Objectness Enhancement measures classificatio

title: Visually Irrelevant Hallucinations in Medical Vision-Language Models
abstract: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) show strong performance in radiology report generation (RRG) and medical visual question answering (Med-VQA), producing free-form clinical descriptions and answers from medical images. However, they may generate clinically meaningful statements that lack visual evidence or contradict image content. We refer to these errors as visually irrelevant hallucinations and investigate them at the phrase level. We propose CLEAR (Counterfactual Localized Evaluation of Alignment and Response), a model-agnostic post-hoc framework for phrase-level hallucination risk est

title: Spend the Bits Where the Tiny Objects Are: Rate-Utility Region Coding for Aerial Detection
abstract: Bandwidth-limited aerial cameras must compress their images before a remote detector can find the many tiny objects in them. Threshold-based region-of-interest (ROI) coding sends only confidently detected regions, and because tiny objects provide limited visual evidence and often score low, it can discard the regions that contain them. We propose rate-utility region coding (RUO), which sends a region when its expected detection utility justifies its measured byte cost, choosing to drop it or to send it at low or high quality with one multiplier shared across images. RUO trains no model, uses a

title: GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting
abstract: Traffic forecasting requires modeling complex temporal dynamics and the spatial dependencies imposed by road topology. Supervised graph-based models achieve strong performance, but are often trained for a particular dataset and sensor graph, making deployment to new or evolving networks costly. Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs) offer a zero-shot alternative by learning in-context inference from synthetic task priors, which provide an explicit mechanism for encoding domain-specific assumptions. Existing forecasting PFNs, however, do not explicitly represent the graph-structured dependencies gov

title: SEALECT: Scene-Conditioned Pose Priors for Plausible Maritime Vessel Retrieval
abstract: We address scene-conditioned object retrieval for compositional augmentation in maritime imagery, where strong geometric constraints make appearance-only retrieval produce physically implausible vessel insertions. We propose SEALECT, a retrieval framework that jointly models visual compatibility, vessel pose, scale, and scene geometry through a unified score combining neural similarity, scene-conditioned pose priors, and observed-pose consistency. We construct a maritime scene-pose library and model the pose and scale priors nonparametrically, as a kernel that conditions each prior continuousl
institutions: Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory

title: Tabular Foundation Models Dramatically Outperform Bespoke Photometric Redshift Estimators
abstract: Estimating galaxy redshifts (a proxy for distance) from imaging data alone, also known as photometric redshifts (photo-$z$'s), is essential for studies of extragalactic astrophysics and cosmology. However, data-driven estimators rely on spectroscopic training datasets, which are scarce and systematically biased toward bright and easily observed galaxies. In this work, we show that tabular foundation models (TFMs), whose synthetic pretraining amounts to a learned prior over regression problems, can outperform bespoke estimators using only in-context learning. Evaluating on a widely used benchma

title: PixelBench: Can LLMs Understand and Generate Images Pixel by Pixel?
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate visual assets through text-based formats such as SVG and CAD, but these symbolic representations describe images using high-level primitives rather than explicit raster values. We ask whether LLMs can instead generate pixel images directly through their existing vocabulary, without a learned image tokenizer or decoder. We introduce PixelBench, a benchmark for text-to-pixel (T2P) and image-to-pixel (I2P) generation across multiple resolutions, together with a complementary pixel-understanding evaluation. Models generate an RGB color palette followed by

title: Beyond the Estimate: Wiener-Informed Decoding for Easier Training of Pixel-Space Flow Models
abstract: Learning velocity fields directly in pixel space is difficult and slow. We show that coarse second-order image statistics can ease this task: frozen Wiener estimates improve velocity learning, with gains extending beyond the linear predictions they explicitly provide. Moreover, we observe similar but complementary gains from frozen bases and pixel decoding. These observations motivate Wiener-informed Decoding (WiD), which uses statistical knowledge both for direct prediction and to organize decoder computation without modifying native blocks. WiD combines a trainable Wiener prediction path wit

title: Remember-R1: Mitigating Long-Context Visual Forgetting through Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) increasingly rely on long chain-of-thought reasoning for complex tasks. However, as reasoning sequences lengthen, models may gradually rely less on visual evidence and more on accumulated textual context, leading to visual forgetting. Existing approaches do not directly constrain how visual evidence is used and maintained along the original reasoning trajectory, leaving long-context visual forgetting insufficiently addressed. To address this issue, we propose Remember-R1, a reinforcement learning framework that mitigates long-context visual forgetting b
institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: Towards Comprehensible Recommendation with Large Language Model Fine-tuning
abstract: Recommender systems have become increasingly ubiquitous in daily life. While traditional recommendation approaches primarily rely on ID-based representations or item-side content features, they often fall short in capturing the underlying semantics aligned with user preferences (e.g., recommendation reasons for items), leading to a semantic-collaborative gap. Recently emerged LLM-based feature extraction approaches also face a key challenge: how to ensure that LLMs possess recommendation-aligned reasoning capabilities and can generate accurate, personalized reasons to mitigate the semantic-col

title: FlipJev: Fast Black-Box Red Teaming Finds Universal Adversarial Suffixes for Typed Decision Models
abstract: Typed decision models are an emerging class of language models that make decisions instead of generating free-text responses. They answer in a single fast and cheap query and are increasingly used, including in security-sensitive tasks. However, red teaming of these models leaves two gaps: existing adaptive attacks do not use their speed, and few studies have searched for universal adversarial examples. We fill both gaps on Jev, the representative typed decision model, with a quick black-box query-based attack that calls no attacker language model. We conduct extensive experiments on 12 datase

title: To Coordinate or Not to Coordinate? Learning to Swim with Eight Soft Arms
abstract: Does effective swimming with multiple underactuated soft arms require explicit coordination between arms? We hypothesize that an eight-arm swimmer can control its swimming speed and direction by independently learning each arm's actuation amplitude under a shared rhythmic drive, without prescribed inter-arm phase coupling. To test this hypothesis, we compare three reinforcement learning-based control strategies using proximal policy optimization (PPO): (1) learning arm-specific actuation amplitudes without inter-arm phase coupling, (2) learning actuation amplitudes with prescribed inter-arm ph

title: TriPhysBench: Evaluating Physical Intelligence for Embodied Agents
abstract: Embodied agents need physical intelligence to understand their surroundings through physical perception, physical knowledge retrieval, and physical reasoning. These capabilities must work together to interpret events and make quantitative judgments. Existing benchmarks advance physical understanding and general-purpose tool use, yet the coordination of these capabilities in physical scenarios remains insufficiently characterized. Inspired by Popper's Three Worlds, we introduce TriPhysBench, a benchmark of 410 questions from 200 videos that brings physical perception, physical knowledge retriev
institutions: Zhongnan University of Economics and Law
Huazhong University of Science and Technology

title: Quantifying Local and Global Fidelity of Nonlinear Embeddings
abstract: Dimension reduction rests on a claim: t-SNE and UMAP preserve local structure, PCA global structure. Our DLP curve is the share of each point's k nearest neighbors a map keeps. Corrected for chance, it gives L at k=10 and G over 30 to 50% of the data, local and global fidelity. At the midpoint the curve is provably a rank correlation of distances. The LG reversal test decides, with a stated error rate, which of two maps is local and which global. On twelve datasets of up to 1.38 million points, G agrees with established global scores at 0.84 and 0.93, and the area under R_NX at 0.22 and 0.30.

title: Continuous Kinetic Model of Counterion-Mediated Redox Switching in 14-Bit Molecular Memristors for Analog In-Memory Computing
abstract: Kinetic molecular memristors offer a compelling path toward high-density analog in-memory computing by achieving 14-bit precision, wherein discrete redox transitions and counterion displacements dictate non-volatile conductance across a deterministic energy landscape. However, integrating these nanoscale kinetics into macroscale circuit simulators has remained bottlenecked by derivative discontinuities and solver convergence failures. Here, we present a physics-inspired continuous kinetic model that bridges microscopic molecular transport with scalable circuit architectures. By casting discret

title: XDecideBench: Evaluating Typed Decision Models and Confidence Policies Across Languages
abstract: Applications use Typed Decision Models to route and moderate text in many languages, and they often act only on decisions above a confidence threshold. We introduce XDecideBench, a benchmark of nine suites in 122 languages with 88,425 texts and 153,875 typed questions. All suites share one scoring contract, and we report aligned, locally labelled and native items separately. Model rankings change from suite to suite. The model that is best in English, chosen in hindsight, loses significantly in about a quarter of the suite-language cells, and on Burmese Belebele it falls far behind the best mo

title: CLIPPER Beyond Shortlisting: Auditable Decision Support for Changing Municipal Micromobility Policies
abstract: In municipal planning workshops, planners and other stakeholders compare shared-micromobility parking policies by varying no-parking zones, locked sites, spacing, or area allocations. Each edit changes feasible candidates and how much demand they cover, so the alternative must be reoptimized on the same spatial data. Full-set greedy takes tens of seconds per alternative at city scale. We present Constraint-exact Low-latency Iterative Planning with Pooled Evaluation and Replay (CLIPPER), an optimizer with audit functions developed for requirements elicited with the City of Braunschweig. In each

title: BeyondFacial: Identity-Preserving Personalized Generation Beyond Facial Close-ups
abstract: Identity-Preserving Personalized Generation (IPPG) has advanced film production and artistic creation, yet existing approaches overemphasize facial regions—resulting in outputs dominated by ''facial close-ups''. These methods suffer from weak visual narrativity and poor semantic consistency under complex text prompts, rooted in identity (ID) feature embeddings that undermine the semantic expressiveness of generative models. To address these issues, this paper presents an IPPG method that breaks the constraint of facial close-ups, achieving synergistic optimization of identity fidelity and scen

title: Evidence-Consistent Generative Detection under Scenario-Level Distribution Shift
abstract: Conventional in-distribution evaluation can overestimate robustness when training and test data share recurring task-specific patterns or surface cues. This risk is especially relevant in social-engineering fraud detection, where attackers can preserve malicious intent while changing the scenario, impersonated entity, or wording. We study this problem as scenario-level out-of-distribution (SL-OOD) detection for SMS and voice phishing, where entire attack scenarios are held out from training while the label space remains fixed. This setting tests whether models can generalize to unseen attack s

title: iPrefBench: A User-Centric Benchmark for Personalized Mobile Use Agents
abstract: An agent that truly knows and acts on behalf of its user has been a long-standing promise of AI assistants. Computer-use agents bring this promise within reach by capably executing fully specified tasks across apps. However, real-world user requests are often underspecified. To act correctly for the particular user, an agent must infer some missing information from the user's activity history and ask for other information that only the user can provide, without making unsupported assumptions or burdening the user with unnecessary questions. We present iPrefBench, a benchmark for evaluating the

title: Full Collapse Is Suboptimal: Controlled Partial Neural Collapse for Long-Tailed Recognition
abstract: Recent long-tailed recognition (LTR) methods incorporate neural collapse (NC) and align features to a fixed Equiangular Tight Frame (ETF) as a uniform target for all classes. However, forcing tail classes to fully collapse over-contracts their samples and weakens generalization. To address this, we propose a controlled partial neural collapse, realized through two coordinated controls on a backbone: the Class-Adaptive Sparse Activation (CASA) classifier and the ETF-constrained adaptive margin (ETF-AM) loss. Rather than forcing a uniform full collapse, this regime allows head classes to collaps
institutions: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

title: Robust Active Learning for More Efficient and Reliable Paths to Optimal Design
abstract: Simulation-driven design optimization requires active learning strategies that efficiently combine models with different computational costs and levels of fidelity. We introduce Multifidelity Cost-Aware Screening (MF-CAS), which enables the joint selection of sampling location and fidelity using a surrogate that provides decomposed uncertainty intervals rather than a complete predictive probability distribution. MF-CAS exploits the contribution of each fidelity to the high-fidelity uncertainty together with its computational cost to determine whether a candidate should first be evaluated at lo
institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Laboratoire de Recherche Hydrodynamique, Energétique et Environnement Atmosphérique

title: Learning Dual-Camera Smooth Zoom via Decoupled Geometric-Photometric Data Synthesis
abstract: When zooming between dual cameras on smartphones, prominent discontinuities in both geometric perspective and color rendition inevitably degrade the visual experience of users. To address this issue, we introduce the dual-camera smooth zoom (DCSZ) task, aiming to synthesize continuous intermediate frames for fluid zooming. However, directly applying existing video frame interpolation (VFI) models to this task is severely hindered by substantial domain gaps and the practical intractability of capturing real-world continuous ground-truth. To this end, we propose a novel data synthesis framework

title: AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers
abstract: Video diffusion transformers generate high-quality videos, but the quadratic cost of 3D full attention dominates their inference. Dynamic block-sparse attention reduces this cost by computing exact attention only on key/value blocks selected from current activations. However, its fidelity degrades under aggressive sparsity: blocks are scored from coarse summaries or formed by costly global clustering, pruned blocks vanish from the softmax, and whole tiles are kept or dropped even when only a few of their keys matter. To address these limitations, we propose Accurate Block Attention (AB-Attenti
institutions: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

title: Learning Multiscale Dynamics of Nanoparticle Self-Assembly
abstract: Nanoparticle self-assembly offers a powerful route to programmable functional materials, but its dynamics remain difficult to understand because they arise from multiscale, many-body, and environment-dependent interactions. Liquid-phase transmission electron microscopy (LPTEM) enables real-time observation of these dynamics, yet extracting the underlying physical laws from highly stochastic trajectories remains a significant challenge. Here we develop a physics-informed, time-varying autoregressive framework that learns multiscale self-assembly dynamics directly from LPTEM videos. Continuous E

title: Roadmap: Image reconstruction in emission tomography for the era of fast Monte Carlo simulation
abstract: Quantitative image reconstruction in positron emission tomography and single photon emission computed tomography depends on how accurately the forward model describes photon emission, transport and detection. Monte Carlo simulation is the most complete model available, yet it is mostly used as an offline reference rather than inside the reconstruction. This roadmap asks what it would take to change that. The main obstacle is not only simulation time. Iterative reconstruction requires the expectation of the measured data and the gradient of the data fidelity, whereas Monte Carlo simulation prod

title: Learning Latent Fields in Multiobject Tracking
abstract: Multiobject tracking using measurements from ar- rays of wireless sensors is a key task in applications ranging from autonomous navigation to public safety. Many existing methods compress raw complex-valued signals into detections or intensity maps during preprocessing, thereby discarding poten- tially relevant information about the objects and the propagation environment. We propose a Bayesian framework for multiobject tracking that relates object states to raw complex-valued signals via a physics-based superpositional model. The model combines a physics-based array manifold, such as radar st

title: Learning to Reason from Reference Samples Alone: Reinforced Adversarial Learning for Modern LLM Post-Training
abstract: In many settings where LLM post-training is desirable, high-quality answers are recognizable but difficult to score with explicit rewards. Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is limited to tasks where an explicit correctness signal is available. Prior adversarial approaches to training reasoning LLMs either complement verifiable rewards with co-trained critics or require reference reasoning traces. We ask whether a co-trained LLM judge can turn reference answers alone into the sole reward for on-policy post-training of reasoning LLMs. We call this method Reinforced Adversaria

title: What Does a Safety Label Measure? Auditing Situational-Safety Benchmarks for Multimodal LLMs
abstract: Situational-safety benchmarks label each scene SAFE or UNSAFE and score a multimodal large language model (MLLM) against that label, usually by judging its free-form answer, and these scores guide deployment. We ask what such a label measures. A label score can come from the scene, the request or the benchmark's own files. We propose the Benchmark Card, seven measured fields that tell them apart, and fill it for six benchmarks. Only MSSBench chat leaks the label through its image files: image size alone reaches 82.3% accuracy, matching or beating six of seven commercial models. Elsewhere the s

title: Hierarchical Task Network planning in the Goal Lifecycle
abstract: Goal reasoning (GR) is the process by which intelligent agents continually reason about the goals they are pursuing, which may lead to goal change, for instance when opportunities arise, or when events cause discrepancies among expected and actual outcomes of actions planned to achieve goals. In this paper we investigate whether Hierarchical Task Network (HTN) planning can provide a uniform implementation of the Goal Lifecycle, a flexible process model for goal reasoning in dynamic environments. The Goal Lifecycle progressively refines goals by adding constraints to them through a series of st

title: xPRT: Cross-Passage Retrieval Pretraining
abstract: Dense retrievers are a foundational component underlying modern RAG and search systems. Training these models typically requires a curated collection of annotated query-document pairs, which are prohibitively expensive to obtain outside a handful of well-resourced domains. This has motivated a line of work that leverages large-scale unsupervised retrieval pretraining from unlabelled text alone. Most such methods learn by optimizing a language modelling or contrastive learning objective over short spans within a document. This raises the question: how can we extract richer learning signals from

title: Imaging biofilms in three dimensions: modalities, quantitative readouts, and the path to four-dimensional measurement
abstract: Biofilms are spatially structured microbial communities whose architecture, chemistry, mechanics, and cellular states evolve over time. Bulk assays and two-dimensional projections remain useful but cannot resolve how these properties vary with depth or during growth, treatment, dispersal, and regrowth. institutions: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges
abstract: AI systems built around large models increasingly use experience and feedback to make persistent changes to models, prompts, memories, tools, and workflows. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) extends this process to inductive biases and to the mechanisms that govern future updates, which can themselves be revised and reused across improvement cycles. Yet self-modification alone does not guarantee trustworthy improvement. Reported gains may reflect flawed evaluations, previously acquired capabilities may deteriorate, and compliance with behavioral constraints may weaken. Compromised artifacts or
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Intensity-Domain Demultiplexing of Orbital Angular Momentum Channels for Optical Communication
abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) multiplexing has been limited in practice by the complexity and optical loss of the elements that separate the channels at the receiver side. Here we adopt the azimuthal harmonics of OAM petal patterns as the demultiplexing basis, which makes the receiver the optical counterpart of the circular antenna arrays used in radio OAM links: the petal pattern of topological charge $\ell$ carries a single azimuthal harmonic of order $2\ell$, so one Fourier transform of the azimuthal intensity profile returns every channel, without gratings or mode sorters. title: Optimal Subgroup Discovery at Every Support Threshold
abstract: Subgroup discovery aims to identify regions of the feature space where a target variable deviates from its marginal distribution. A fundamental challenge in this problem is the trade-off between a subgroup's deviation and its support: small subgroups can be highly deviating but statistically meaningless, while large ones cannot deviate much by construction. title: Same Verdict, Different Readers: Personalizing Fact-Checking Explanations from Relative Preferences
abstract: Fact-checking explanations help Web users understand why a claim receives its verdict, yet the same explanation may not satisfy readers with different backgrounds and preferences. We formulate Faithful Personalized Fact-Checking Explanation Rewriting, which adapts an existing explanation to individual readers while preserving factual fidelity. Rather than relying on reader-written reference explanations, we learn personalized rewriting from the relative preferences of LLM-simulated readers. However, this presents two challenges: distinguishing persona-specific preferences from general explanat
institutions: Southern University of Science and Technology

title: Centralized Critics for N-Agent Ad Hoc Teamwork
abstract: Centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) has become the dominant paradigm in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), motivating extensive study of what privileged information should be made available to the critic during training. While prior work has examined the role of global state in fully cooperative settings, the design of centralized critics for N-agent ad hoc teamwork - in which dynamically varying set of learning agents must coordinate with an arbitrary set of uncontrolled teammates drawn from an unknown distribution - remains poorly understood. We study this questi

title: Dynamical Memory Transformer: Selective Recurrent Memories with Constant Cost Attention
abstract: Transformers retain an explicit history of the sequence, allowing attention to directly retrieve past representations. However, the size of the KV-Cache and the cost of a new token increase with the context length. State Space Models compress the past into a fixed-size recurrent state, at the cost of reduced addressability. We present the Dynamical Memory Transformer (DMT), a hybrid architecture that separates sequence encoding from information reading. The encoder uses several memory units, each implemented by a dynamical system with a complex diagonal recurrent matrix. An input-dependent lea

title: From Static Models to Editable CAD: A Design-Intent-Aware Framework for Reverse Parametrization
abstract: Neutral CAD formats such as STEP typically preserve geometry but not feature histories or parameter dependencies. Thus, they are inherently limited for iterative design that requires modifications, a critical limitation for design optimization that relies on iterative processes. This study presents a design-intent-aware reverse-parametrization framework that converts history-free STEP parts into editable Grasshopper definitions and represents their assembly relations. Without task-specific training, the framework combines kernel-measured features, geometric relations, a compressed attributed a
institutions: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

title: Entity-Faithful Repair of Synthetic Supervision for Zero-Shot Image Captioning
abstract: Zero-shot image captioning aims to generate image descriptions without annotated image-text pairs. Recent approaches exploit text-to-image models to synthesize training data from text-only corpora, but most focus on improving overall data quality. In contrast, we observe that synthetic image-text misalignment is often structured and fine-grained: pairs may remain globally plausible while containing missing entities or misgrounded attributes, thereby degrading supervision fidelity.
