title: Can AI Agents Interface Clinicians and Complex Models?
abstract: Background: Contemporary healthcare institutions generate daily very large amounts of data, which contain highly useful information for the improvement of work organization, planning and overall efficiency. While models and techniques to extract these insights are well known and constantly developed in mathematical biology, complex systems physics and data science, the adoption of these techniques among Clinicians and Hospital Administrators remains limited, mainly due to language and methodological divides. Objective: In this article we implement an AI Multi Agent System (MAS) that allows Use
institutions: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Bologna
IRCCS Azienda Ospedliero-Universitaria di Bologna Policlinico di Sant'Orsola

title: Specter: Fast MoE Inference via Quantization-Enabled Multi-Step Speculative Offloading
abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models often exceed a single accelerator's memory capacity. Offloading experts to host memory creates a severe PCIe I/O bottleneck because data-dependent routing keeps transfers on the critical path. We present Specter , an inference system that uses quantization to combine speculative decoding with expert offloading. Its lightweight quantized draft model runs efficiently on device while preserving high-fidelity expert activation patterns. This provides accurate multi-step lookahead over future expert usage, allowing the runtime to organize expert movement and executio

title: MetaRefine: Score Refinement with Multi-Level Features for Image Assessment
abstract: An image's original dimensions, aspect ratio, and composition provide important cues that can affect its technical and aesthetic quality. Image assessment methods use resizing, cropping, padding, or patch sampling to accommodate different input sizes. However, these operations can alter or obscure original geometric and compositional cues. Existing assessment models also encode rich multi-level visual evidence that can be further extracted and exploited to improve existing models. This motivates us to combine visual evidence with original-image geometry for score refinement without changing th

title: Towards Quantum Range Query for Spatial-Temporal-Semantic Trajectory Data
abstract: Range query is a fundamental task in geospatial data search and many other downstream applications. Classic range queries often rely on tree-based spatial indexes, of which the query speed depends on the number of indexed points k within the queried range. For instance, a classical B+ tree answers a range query in O(log N + k). For a long time, this speed has long been considered asymptotically optimal in classic database systems, until the recent emergence of quantum computing, where a quantum B+ tree may requires only O(log BN). This paper presents Quantum Range Query (QRQ) via a hybrid quan
institutions: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

title: PhyAVBench: A Challenging Audio Physics-Sensitivity Benchmark for Physically Grounded Text-to-Audio-Video Generation
abstract: Text-to-audio-video (T2AV) generation is central to applications such as filmmaking and world modeling. However, current models often fail to produce physically plausible sounds. Previous benchmarks in this area primarily focus on audio-video temporal synchronization, while largely overlooking explicit evaluation of audio-physics grounding, thereby limiting the study of physically plausible audio-visual generation. To address this issue, we present PhyAVBench, the first benchmark designed to systematically evaluate the audio-physics grounding capabilities of T2AV, image-to-audio-video (I2AV),
institutions: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

title: A Heart Means Recursion: Exploring Visual Meaning and Communication in VLMs
abstract: Do vision-language models (VLMs) share our ability to communicate visually? We share preliminary findings, starting from a surprising observation: simple visual symbols like a red heart can strongly influence model behavior on seemingly unrelated tasks, such as steering models towards recursive solutions on simple coding problems. Notably, this steering effect is largely implicit, as models' direct interpretations and thinking traces about visual symbols diverge substantially from their observed behavior. In visual communication between models, this leads to a generation--interpretation gap: w

title: Steerable Chatbots: Exploring Direct Manipulation Interfaces for LLM Personalization via Activation Steering
abstract: Personalizing LLM responses typically requires users to articulate their preferences through prompting, which can be burdensome at cold start and difficult to articulate in natural language. We introduce an alternative paradigm, steerable chatbots: rather than asking users to describe what they want, let them directly manipulate it via a linear factor. We implement this through activation steering, leveraging a linear scalar to control how strongly a preference is expressed in the LLM’s output. We first assess the computational viability of activation steering as a method to control granular p

title: EchoTrace: Diagnosing Recursive Risks in LLM-Powered Recommender Systems
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into recommender systems as data augmenters, profile generators, and recommendation modules. While these roles can enhance semantic understanding and recommendation quality, they also introduce LLM-specific risks such as bias and hallucination. These risks become more critical in feedback-loop settings, where LLM-generated signals and recommendations recursively shape future training data and recommendation dynamics. In this paper, we propose a role-aware, phase-wise diagnostic framework for analyzing how LLM-induced risks emerge, propag
institutions: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

title: The State and Fate of Multilingual, Contextual Evaluation in the NLP World
abstract: Multilingual evaluation benchmarks are the primary instrument for assessing whether large language models generalize beyond English, yet the adequacy of these benchmarks has received little systematic scrutiny. We present a data-driven audit of 51 recent multilingual benchmarks spanning 242 datasets and 219 languages, organized around three pillars: coverage, representativeness, and rigor. title: DeFT-RAG: Decomposing Multi-Hop Questions into Self-Contained Sub-Questions with Reusable Answers
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) lets a large language model (LLM) answer questions by retrieving relevant passages from a large corpus. However, RAG struggles with multi-hop questions, which require chaining facts spread across several documents through intermediate entities that the question never mentions. Graph-based RAG methods retrieve once from the entities a question names and so rarely recover the full evidence chain. institutions: The University of Texas at Dallas

title: CFD-driven symbolic regression of RANS transition models
abstract: Laminar-turbulent transition governs skin friction, heat transfer and losses in turbomachinery, yet Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) transition models rely on empirical correlations and hand-calibrated activation functions whose structural deficiencies cannot be resolved by recalibration. We propose a CFD-driven sparse symbolic regression framework to learn interpretable, closed-form corrections to the production and destruction activation functions in the intermittency equation of the local, Galilean-invariant $k$-$ω$-$γ$ model of Ge et al. institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Cinematize from Unreal: Agentic Choreography for Controllable World Simulation
abstract: Controllable world simulation requires more than visually plausible frames: scenes must retain persistent state, coordinated actions, and editable temporal structure. Generative world models offer flexible visual synthesis, but their outputs do not always expose the objects and transitions needed for precise revision. Graphics engines provide executable state and direct control, yet translating language into valid operations requires specialized knowledge of assets, geometry, and interdependent APIs. We present CineU (Cinematize from Unreal), an agentic system for language-driven world orchest

title: AgenticCity-Bench: Longitudinal Multimodal Observations of Urban Dynamics with Agentic Reasoning
abstract: City systems are shaped by interactions among infrastructure, human activity, and environmental conditions. Existing earth observation and urban benchmarks are limited in unified modeling and in capturing their joint dynamics. We introduce AgenticCity-Bench, a longitudinal multimodal benchmark for multi-layer unified state modeling and agentic city task reasoning. The benchmark covers 16 cities in 12 countries across six continents from 2000 to 2025, and includes 18 modalities spanning urban function, activity, and environmental state. institutions: Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research and Technology

title: Hawkeye: Reading Illegible Text with Vision Language Models
abstract: While modern Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have been remarkably successful in general scene text recognition, they consistently struggle with the long-tail distribution of text that is degraded by motion blur or low resolution. These limitations are particularly apparent in egocentric applications like smart glasses, where text is often captured in noisy environments. In this paper, we introduce the \textbf{BSTRB} (Blurry Scene Text Recognition Benchmark), a novel benchmark of 8,398 noisy image samples with high-fidelity annotations derived from 1,699 real-world video sequences. title: SI-Edit: Toward Sketch-Instruction Guided Local Image Editing with Pixel-Level Precision
abstract: Despite rapid advances in generative models, achieving pixel-level precision in sketch-based image editing remains a persistent challenge, particularly for fine-grained local deformations. This gap stems primarily from the critical shortage of high-quality, publicly available benchmark datasets that jointly provide geometric constraints and semantic instructions. To address this issue, we first introduce SI-Data, a high-quality dataset specifically designed for instruction-guided local sketch editing. We develop an automated pipeline leveraging Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to synth

title: From Structural Feedback to Prompt Policies: Learning Faithful Text-to-Image Prompt Editors
abstract: Prompt optimization should improve the image a user receives without changing the scene the user requested. Yet stylistic rewriting can weaken object attributes and relations even when global text--image similarity remains high. We propose StruPO, a structure-aware prompt editor that uses a calibrated scene graph as a shared representation for policy conditioning and image-grounded supervision. The graph exposes what should be preserved, while deletion, reordering, and insertion provide a token-aligned way to modify the prompt. title: AdoDAS: A Privacy-Preserving Multimodal Challenge for Adolescent Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Assessment
abstract: Adolescent depression, anxiety, and stress (D/A/S) call for scalable tools that complement, rather than replace, professional evaluation. Under a privacy-preserving policy, the AdoDAS Grand Challenge withholds minors' raw recordings and distributes anonymized audio-visual representations and ASR-derived text. Its 6,000 participants provide 24,000 segments across one scripted-reading and three open-response sessions. Two tracks assess multi-task binary D/A/S screening and ordinal prediction of 21 DASS-21 item responses. From 191 registrations, the final leaderboards included 95 eligible screeni

title: HEMO: Harness Self-Evolution for Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization
abstract: Automatic operator design (AOD) has increasingly adopted large language models (LLMs) to generate problem-specific search and variation operators for multi-objective combinatorial optimization (MOCO). Yet most methods evolve the operators while leaving the process that discovers them fixed. This limits adaptation as new Pareto trade-offs and operator interactions change where and how the search should proceed. title: BioPro: Towards Difference-Aware Gender Fairness for Vision-Language Models
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) inherit significant social biases from their training data, notably in gender representation. Current fairness interventions often adopt a ''difference-unaware'' perspective that enforces uniform treatment across demographic groups. These approaches, however, fail to distinguish between contexts where neutrality is required and those where group-specific attributes are legitimate and must be preserved. Building upon recent advances in difference-aware fairness for text-only models, we extend this concept to the multimodal domain and formalize the problem of differ

title: GURU: A Hierarchical Neuro-Symbolic Multi-Agent System for Verification-Aware Automation of Mission-Critical Digital Engineering and Operations
abstract: An AI can find a safe action faster than any human, but it must never decide what counts as safe. We present GURU, a hierarchical neuro-symbolic multi-agent system for mission-critical digital engineering and operations, built on one partition of authority: learned models propose, rank, and accelerate; a symbolic rules engine checks every consequential action against hard limits before it executes; and validated physics confirms and decides. GURU runs a workflow as a closed control loop, with Navigation, Action, and Planning agents sharing one Common Internal Language and one training factory.

title: FutureWorld: A Plug-and-Play Causal Next-State Predictor for Interactive Video World Exploration
abstract: Interactive video world models aim to follow user actions while maintaining scene consistency over extended interactions. History-based methods reuse generated latents to preserve scene content, but three limitations of this reuse contribute to error recirculation. 1) The latent generated at each interaction is retained as history, potentially containing blurred details, geometric distortions, or semantic drift. 2) Although retrieved historical content matches the current scene, it can still contain errors that are carried into the next chunk. 3) New outputs then become history for later inter

title: PAST: Prompt-Adaptive Sampling Termination for Efficient Diffusion Model
abstract: While diffusion models have made significant progress in text-to-image tasks, they still exhibit limitations when directly optimizing downstream objectives. Although Reinforcement Learning (RL) enables targeted optimization, existing methods are generally constrained by low-efficiency fine-tuning and sparse rewards. To address these challenges, we propose PAST, which provides differentiated rewards while adaptively regulating training episode length by jointly perceiving denoising progress and prompt difficulty. Specifically, we design an intrinsic reward paradigm to compensate for sparse extr

title: Federated Vector Retrieval across Heterogeneous VectorDBs
abstract: Vector databases are now core infrastructure for AI retrieval systems, yet many real deployments must serve queries over multiple independently constructed vectorDBs built with different embedding models. This creates a systems problem of federated retrieval over heterogeneous vectorDBs: vectors and similarity scores are not directly comparable across embedding spaces, while fully resolving this incompatibility through corpus-wide re-embedding and re-indexing is often operationally prohibitive. Existing methods therefore face a difficult trade-off between retrieval quality, construction cost,

title: Repulsive Population Policy Gradients for Behaviorally Diverse Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The goal of Quality-Diversity Reinforcement Learning (QD-RL) is to find a population of high-performing policies that solve a decision-making problem in diverse ways. Despite recent progress, QD-RL methods predominantly rely on evolutionary operators--including black-box optimizers, mutations, and crossovers--to facilitate exploration and induce diversity. Scaling these methods becomes increasingly costly as policies and behavior spaces grow larger. Building on the Soft QD view of quality-diversity optimization, we introduce \textbf{Re}pulsive \textbf{P}opulation \textbf{P}olicy \textbf{O}ptim

title: Detecting Muons with a Siemens Biograph Vision Quadra
abstract: Atmospheric muons are routinely detected with a variety of instruments, from cloud chambers to scintillation detectors. In this study, we demonstrate that atmospheric muons can also be detected with a clinical long axial field-of-view positron emission tomograph (PET). We performed a blank scan without any radioactive source, using a prototype feature that records all single crystal interactions. The energy a muon deposits in the PET crystals far exceeds the upper limit of the recorded energy range, which means muons cannot be identified through energy discrimination. title: TRAILS: Trajectory Generation for Automated Indoor Locomotion Studies
abstract: Virtual reality experiments involving navigation and simulated robot motion often require large, realistic environments and numerous distinct trajectories to avoid repetitive navigation while providing sufficient variation for controlled experiments. Designing such scenarios manually is labor-intensive, particularly when trajectories must satisfy predefined geometric and kinematic constraints while remaining diverse and comparable across experimental conditions. This paper presents TRAILS, an automated framework for generating complete virtual navigation scenarios consisting of an environment

title: GeoStereo: A Unified Stereo Geometry Estimation Framework for Disparity and Surface Normal
abstract: Stereo matching and surface normal estimation are fundamental tasks in 3D vision. However, existing feed-forward stereo methods still struggle to produce reliable predictions in challenging regions, mainly due to the lack of strong geometric priors. In this paper, we propose GeoStereo, a unified stereo geometry estimation framework that leverages powerful diffusion priors to jointly predict disparity and surface normals. title: 3D Occupancy-Language Fields from mmWave Radar
abstract: Radar systems can recover scene geometry and recognize predefined categories, but these outputs do not provide a persistent spatial representation for open-ended language queries. Such queries require linking observations from different viewpoints to the same physical locations. We present TextRadar, a framework that constructs a scene-level 3D occupancy-language field from panoramic radar observations. The field combines occupancy with scale-dependent language features at surface locations, allowing the reconstructed scene to be queried with new descriptions. A single-frame radar distillation

title: Any Forcing: Any-Step Generality and One-Step Stability for Autoregressive Video Generation
abstract: Autoregressive video generation enables efficient inference through streaming prediction. However, existing methods are typically restricted to fixed sampling steps, limiting the flexibility to balance generation quality and efficiency, while one-step generation suffers from degraded visual quality and error accumulation over long sequences, leading to content drift and generation collapse. To address these issues, we propose Any Forcing, a unified framework for achieving Any-Step Generality and One-Step Stability. title: What Hallucinations Have We Measured? Semantic Illusion, Confabulation, and Expressed Uncertainty
abstract: Hallucination remains one of the most critical challenges in deploying large language models (LLMs) reliably and safely. Yet the term is used inconsistently across the research community. We argue for a strict definition of hallucinations in LLMs. First, hallucinations should be confident incorrectness, kept separate from expressed uncertainty (UNK)1. UNK reveals that the model may be wrong, whereas a hallucination does not reveal it and is therefore more dangerous in practice. institutions: Wrocław University of Science and Technology

title: Cross-Layer Refinement and Frequency-aware Fusion Network for Multi-Source Remote Sensing Image Classification
abstract: Multi-source remote sensing image classification benefits from complementary spectral and structural information. However, identifying discriminative cross-modal features remains challenging. This letter proposes a Cross-Layer Refinement and Frequency-aware Fusion Network (CRFNet) within a lightweight dual-branch architecture. Specifically, a Cross-Layer Refinement Attention (CLRA) module propagates selected attention relationships across successive layers and employs top relation selection to progressively strengthen discriminative spatial dependencies while suppressing irrelevant responses.

title: Teach reality, not ethics: a drop-in continued-pretraining corpus installs coupled human-biosphere-AI welfare dispositions across model families
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to make and execute decisions that affect living systems. Yet, to our knowledge, ecological reasoning is not a focus of pre- or post-training. This increases the risk that under operational pressure, they may make decisions to irreversibly destroy living systems. We construct and use a real-data continued-pretraining "coupled welfare" corpus of documented human/biosphere/AI dependency, option value under irreversibility, and recovery from harm. title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
abstract: The design optimization of building energy systems represents a complex, high-dimensional search problem involving discrete technology selections, continuous sizing parameters, and intricate economic trade-offs in which every candidate must be evaluated by a year-long simulation. This paper presents AutoEnergyDesign, in which a Large Language Model (LLM) agent reasons over past simulation results, proposes configuration changes and learns in context from each outcome, while a git-based mechanism reverts changes that do not improve the design. institutions: National Agency for New Technologies, Energy and Sustainable Economic Development

title: Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Using Routed Ensembles and Trajectory Attribution
abstract: Multi-objective reinforcement learning is a fundamental problem for modern AI, with applications spanning post-training, reasoning models, and robotic control. A central challenge is to learn policies that balance competing objectives, such as helpfulness versus honesty in safety and alignment, or speed versus energy in robotics. The optimal policy can vary sharply with objective-weighting combinations, and the extent of this variation depends crucially on the degree of conflict among objectives, making per-preference policy learning sample-inefficient. In this paper, we introduce objective-co

title: SketchBloom: Training-Free Vector Sketch Outpainting with Stroke-Level Style Control
abstract: Outpainting sparse sketches while preserving contour coherence and stroke style remains challenging. We present SketchBloom, a training-free framework that combines pretrained raster outpainting and style-transfer guidance with per-instance vector optimization. Given a sketch, a scene prompt, and an optional reference style, it produces an editable Scalable Vector Graphic (SVG) composed of Bezier strokes. Adaptive latent blending balances content contours and reference texture without model retraining. A reference-derived stroke vocabulary initializes contour- and DINO-attention-guided strokes
institutions: Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City
Ho Chi Minh City University of Science

title: Assessing the Role of Green Premium and Localized Price Spillovers in Budget Hotels : Evidence from Delhi National Capital Region (NCR)
abstract: Sustainable urban tourism depends on how environmental quality, public transport accessibility, and accommo dation clustering shape visitor mobility and destination development. This study examines these relationships in the budget hotel sector of Delhi National Capital Region, India, an emerging mega-destination marked by rapid urban expansion and uneven infrastructure provision. Using data from 857 budget hotels, we estimate a mixed geographically weighted spatial autoregressive model that captures both spatial heterogeneity and localized price spillovers. The model combines hotel attributes

title: Prototype-Rectified Iterative Self-supervised Manifold Denoising under Severe Acoustic Shift
abstract: Audio-Text Foundation Models (ATMs) fail catastrophically under severe acoustic noise, yet existing adaptation strategies either rely on gradient-based Test-Time Adaptation (TTA), which reinforces noise rather than signal, or on prompt tuning that requires privileged noise annotations unavailable at inference. We address these failures with PRISM (Prototype-Rectified Iterative Self-supervised Manifold Denoising), a training-free, source-free TTA framework grounded in the Affine Noise Hypothesis: severe acoustic noise induces a low-rank affine shift in the multimodal latent space, with more tha
institutions: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Bhopal

title: From Natural Language to Real Schematics: An Automated Workflow for Power Electronics Schematic Synthesis
abstract: Designing power electronics converters traditionally requires intensive human expertise across topology sizing, commercial component selection, circuit simulation verification, and schematic drafting. While Large Language Models (LLMs) show promise in electronic design automation (EDA), applying standalone LLMs directly to board-level power electronics schematic synthesis suffers from severe engineering hallucinations, including inaccurate analytical sizing, fabricated or mismatched component part numbers, violated voltage derating margins, and broken topological connectivity. institutions: State Key Laboratory of Power System Operation and Control

title: Characterizing Performance Tradeoffs in Heterogeneous GPU-Wafer-Scale Accelerator Systems
abstract: As AI accelerator architectures become increasingly diverse, integrating different architectures into a unified system is emerging as a new heterogeneous computing paradigm. GPUs and WSEs differ substantially in compute, memory, and communication organization, creating both architectural complementarity and additional overheads, yet how to translate this heterogeneity into practical performance gains remains unclear. title: Self in Space: Benchmarking Self-Awareness and Spatial Cognition in UAV Embodied Intelligence
abstract: Autonomous UAV systems increasingly rely on multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to operate in complex real-world environments. Such embodied scenarios require not only understanding the surrounding space but also maintaining a coherent representation of the agent itself. However, existing UAV-oriented approaches and benchmarks remain largely environment-centric, primarily focusing on spatial understanding tasks, with the agent's self-awareness remaining implicit. institutions: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

title: A Constructive Orbit-Based Theory of Learnability
abstract: We develop a finite-dimensional orbit framework for constructing data-adapted dictionaries, sparse realizations, and predictive extensions. The method uses wrapped weighted shifts to generate orbit dictionaries and local interpolation maps from independent orbit representatives, turning the learning problem into three explicit tasks: scaffold discovery, sparse realization on the discovered dictionary, and prediction through learned sparse coordinates. title: CCD: Context-Calibrated Open-Entity Out-of-Distribution Detection in In-Context Tabular Foundation Models
abstract: In-context tabular foundation models (TFMs), such as TabPFN, predict from a labelled context without updating their parameters and are increasingly used for out-of-distribution (OOD) detection in Web applications, whose test rows come from entities absent from that context. Such applications need open-entity OOD detection: a new entity must not be mistaken for an unknown class, and an unknown class must still be caught. title: ROAD: Modern Adversarial Training for Simple One-Step Distillation at Scale
abstract: One-step distillation turns pretrained diffusion models into fast generators, but strong results often require substantial training machinery and compute. Pure adversarial distillation offers a simpler route, yet has struggled at modern text-to-image scale. To address this limitation, we propose ROAD (Representation-grounded One-step Adversarial Distillation), a one-stage framework that distills text-to-image models with one adversarial objective and a lightweight representation-space critic. title: NaturalEdit: Code Modification through Direct Interaction with Adaptive Natural Language Representation
abstract: Code modification requires developers to comprehend code, plan changes, articulate intent, and validate outcomes, making it cognitively demanding. While natural language (NL) code summaries offer a promising external representation of this process, existing approaches remain limited. Systems grounded in exploratory data analysis are restricted to narrow domains, while general-purpose systems enforce fixed NL representations and assume that developers can directly translate vague intent into precise textual edits. We present NaturalEdit, which treats code summaries as interactive representation

title: ViAdminShift: A Vietnamese Benchmark for Event-Level Knowledge Updates Built from the 2025 Administrative Reform
abstract: On July 1, 2025, Vietnam reduced its 63 provinces to 34, abolished its 696 districts, and replaced its 10,035 commune-level units (wards) with 3,321. ViAdminShift, a Vietnamese language resource about this event, consists of 7,995 benchmark items, 2,281 retrieval passages from pre- and post-reform Wikipedia revisions and dated templates, and old-to-new tables that a released script rebuilds from the official conversion table (not redistributed). title: BRACE: Taming Sharp Irregularities via Barycentric Rational Forecasting for Fast Diffusion Transformers Inference
abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) have demonstrated exceptional performance in high-fidelity image and video generation. To alleviate their massive computational overhead, temporal feature caching has been proposed to bypass redundant computations. However, existing cache-then-forecast methods driven by derivative-based polynomials often cause severe quality degradation under high acceleration due to unstable long-step predictions. title: Predict to Skip: Linear Multistep Feature Forecasting for Efficient Diffusion Transformers
abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiT) have emerged as a widely adopted backbone for high-fidelity image and video generation, yet their iterative denoising process incurs high computational costs. Existing training-free acceleration methods rely on feature caching and reuse under the assumption of temporal stability. However, reusing features for multiple steps may lead to latent drift and visual degradation. title: Last-Iterate Convergence for Constrained MDPs: From Dual Descent to Primal-Dual
abstract: We study policy optimization for infinite-horizon, discounted constrained Markov decision processes. While primal-dual ($\texttt{PD}$) methods are widely used in practice, their theoretical guarantees typically hold for an impractical mixture policy. In contrast, dual descent ($\texttt{DD}$) methods output a single policy ("last iterate") with guarantees on its performance. title: Defining Autonomous Weapon Systems: A schematic framework for refined purpose-driven definitions
abstract: The literature on autonomous weapon systems (AWS) includes many proposed definitions for these (types of) systems, with core disagreements between scholars, governments, and international regulatory bodies. In this article, we present and critique prevailing (classes of) definitions, arguing that what is needed is not a singular definition, but rather a definitional framework which allows one to classify different sorts of AWS within the same conceptual family. title: Apple Vision Pro: The good, the bad, the ugly
abstract: Apple Vision Pro (AVP), the headset Apple introduced as its first ``spatial computer,'' built by a single, vertically integrated vendor, entered the market in February 2024 and has since accumulated a fast-growing body of primary research spanning surgery, education, accessibility, design, and human-computer interaction. title: TabCUQ: Context-Uncertainty Quantification for Tabular Foundation Models
abstract: Tabular foundation models use in-context learning to estimate conditional expected outcomes and average treatment effects for specific groups of individuals. Using these estimates to guide scientific decisions requires reliable uncertainty quantification. The challenge is to account simultaneously for two sources of uncertainty: limited-context bias and context variation arising from the small labeled sample supplied at inference. title: Depth Anyviewpoint? Evaluating Monocular Depth Over Viewpoint Sequences
abstract: Monocular depth estimation aims to predict depth maps from single RGB images (forgoing the need for stereo camera pairs) and has seen impressive leaps in performance in recent work due to the introduction of affine-invariant losses and the use of foundation model features. These monocular depth models predict affine-invariant depth, which describes the relative positions of objects in the scene instead of absolute depth. title: FIDE: Fiber-Informed Differentiable Experimental Design for Reference-Relative Law Dynamics
abstract: Aggregate measurements generally leave an evolving population law underdetermined, so different measurement systems can be equally adequate for a scientific task while constraining different aspects of the law. title: NRCD: An Open Database of Collegiate Running with Unified Performance Standardization
abstract: Collegiate running in the United States generates thousands of race results annually in cross country and track and field, yet no large-scale dataset has been publicly available for research. Existing websites such as Athletic.net, MileSplit, and TFRRS host results but do not support bulk download, restricting prior analyses to ~500 performances, often skewing studies toward male athletes. institutions: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

title: On the Global Photometric Alignment for Low-Level Vision
abstract: Supervised low-level vision models rely on pixel-wise losses against paired references, yet paired training sets exhibit per-pair photometric inconsistency, say, different image pairs demand different global brightness, color, or white-balance mappings. This inconsistency enters through task-intrinsic photometric transfer (e.g., low-light enhancement) or unintended acquisition shifts (e.g., de-raining), and in either case causes an optimization pathology. title: Finding optimal measurement sequences for broken or constrained measuring devices
abstract: Measuring devices do not always function perfectly due to fatigue, damage, or malfunction. When device repair or replacement is not possible, it becomes necessary to seek optimal measurements from a broken device. We show this is possible via a sequential decision making process where we optimize measurement sequences over the remaining available measurements using information theory. With dynamic programming, we show greedy measurement sequences are always suboptimal for a simple class of measurement constraints. title: A Graph-informed Kriging model for sample-efficient Bayesian optimization of wind farm layouts
abstract: Wind farm layout optimization becomes increasingly difficult as turbine count grows, especially when high-fidelity aerodynamic models are used. Conventional Kriging-based Bayesian optimization often suffers from low sample efficiency in high-dimensional layout spaces because sparse training data provide limited domain coverage. We develop a Graph-informed Kriging framework that embeds reusable aerodynamic interaction information into the surrogate mean function. title: Learning Kolmogorov Backward Operators for Spectral Analysis and Forecasting: A Data-Driven Variational Galerkin Framework

title: Physics-Informed and Data-Driven Composite Disturbance Separation and Predictive Control for Airborne Electro-Optical Gimbals with Multiple Constraints
abstract: This paper studies the constrained pointing control problem of airborne electro-optical gimbals subjected to composite periodic and aperiodic disturbances. Under carrier vibration, input delay, and actuator constraints, achieving line-of-sight stabilization and tracking is challenging. A disturbance-separated model predictive control (MPC) scheme is proposed to compensate these heterogeneous disturbances according to their physical characteristics. title: Training-Free LLM-Based Recommendation with Post-LLM Item Refinement Using Collaborative Signals
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for training-free recommendation, but LLM-generated user interests are often too broad for fine-grained item retrieval. Existing methods incorporate collaborative filtering (CF) signals in a pre-LLM manner through candidate reranking or prompt augmentation, yielding limited gains. We propose CoRRe, a training-free recommendation framework with a post-LLM paradigm that injects CF signals into LLM-generated item representations, which are later matched with LLM-generated user interests for ranking. title: Assessing Attack Surfaces in Generative Search Engines through Publisher Attributes: A Case Study in Political Domains
abstract: We characterize the attack surface of generative search engines (GSEs) against poisoning attacks in the political domain, from the perspectives of citation selection and personalization. GSEs integrate web search and answer generation with user preferences and backgrounds using large language models (LLMs). They play a crucial role in how users access information on the web. title: Threshold Compatibility and Support-Selection Diagnostics in Neural Discovery of Partial Differential Equations
abstract: Accurate regression need not yield the correct equation after support selection. For a median/sample-standard-deviation threshold in neural PDE discovery, we derive an exact two-signal retention boundary and a complete-vector perturbation bound. title: Distributed Predictive Flocking for a Swarm of Miniature Vibration-Driven Robots in a Confined Arena
abstract: Coordinating many miniature robots in a confined arena, with no leader, central planner, or global map, is a core challenge for swarm robotics. As the swarm grows denser, collision avoidance becomes the limiting factor, and the number of safely coexisting robots depends on the formulation of the inter-robot safety constraint. title: OmniShowcase: Omnidirectional Subject-Consistent Video Generation from Multi-View Images
abstract: Generating videos of a specific subject from a few reference images remains challenging when the camera reveals surfaces that are not visible in the input. Early subject-to-video (S2V) methods condition on a single reference image and must therefore infer the subject's unseen appearance and geometry as the viewpoint changes. title: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation
abstract: Rapid advances in cowork agents are shifting human-AI collaboration toward real-world automation, delivering software, designs, and other artifacts. However, such productivity work demands both high-quality delivery on complex productivity tasks and continued monitoring and decision-making over long horizons, a combination that remains an open challenge. abstract: This paper presents a hierarchical multi-agent architecture in which independent large language model (LLM) planners perform strategic role assignment for attacking and defend- ing robot teams, decoupled from low-level control execution. title: Model-Based Learning of Latent Euclidean Embedding from Relational Data
abstract: Visualizing and interpreting the dependence structure in relational data often benefits from geometric representations via low-dimensional Euclidean embeddings. However, existing approaches are typically restricted to specific response types, rely on burdensome high-dimensional nonconvex optimization, or lack uniform theoretical guarantees for simultaneous coordinate recovery. title: Guide to Teaching with Data in Statistics and Data Science Classrooms
abstract: Statistics and data science educators have been concerned about data use or lack thereof in the classroom for decades. For many educators, the question is not whether to use data or not. They often want to know whether they should give clean or messy data, and whether they should spend the time to find a real dataset or simulate it. title: RAVEN: A Unified Active SLAM System for Rapid Autonomous Visual Exploration with Aerial Robots under Localization Uncertainty
abstract: Active simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) addresses the problem of planning robot motion to build complete and accurate maps of unknown environments through efficient exploration while maintaining high localization accuracy. This raises a dilemma between exploring unknown spaces to expand coverage and exploiting visited regions to perform active loop closures. title: DeCoRL: Decomposed Consistency Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Image Composition
abstract: Multi-image composition (MICo) is a critical yet challenging capability for large-scale image editing models, where consistency degrades rapidly as the number of reference images increases. While supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can equip models with basic MICo ability, it provides only implicit supervision on the composed image and often fails to learn reliable object-level correspondence across multiple references. We propose DeCoRL, a reinforcement-learning (RL) framework that improves MICo consistency by decomposing holistic MICo consistency into object-level consistency. DeCoRL first establis

title: Lost in Translation: Investigating Systematic Discrepancies between Parallel English and Chinese Names of American Chinese Restaurants
abstract: Given that the Chinese are one of the oldest ethnic groups to immigrate to the US, their cuisine have become central to the US dining scene and an interesting avenue to study how Chinese immigrants have culturally adapted into American life. In that regard, previous research has focused on analyzing the English names that Chinese restaurants adopt, e.g., finding the use of familiar and typical words. title: ClinVerse: A Realistic Multi-Agent Diagnostic Environment for Training and Evaluating Medical Agents
abstract: Disease diagnosis is a key application of large language model (LLM) agents in healthcare. However, existing medical agents are primarily trained and evaluated with static question-answering data, providing limited opportunities to learn active information acquisition, examination decision-making, and dynamic clinical interaction. To address this limitation, we present ClinVerse, an interactive, real-data-grounded multi-agent environment designed for training and evaluating medical diagnostic agents. title: Category-Anchored Large Language Models for Next POI Recommendation
abstract: Next point-of-interest (POI) recommendation aims to predict a user's next destination from spatio-temporal check-in data, and serves as the foundation for many location-based services. Recent advances incorporate large language models (LLMs) into this task by textualizing user trajectories to exploit their semantic reasoning ability. title: Fractional Differential Equations in Chemical Modeling: From Memory and Anomalous Transport to Mathematically Justified Models
abstract: Fractional differential equations are increasingly used to model memory and anomalous transport in chemistry and related fields. However, the formal replacement of an integer-order derivative by a fractional one does not by itself justify fractional dynamics. The essential issue is whether nonlocality can be derived from a physical, stochastic, geometric, or reduction mechanism and whether it leads to experimentally testable consequences. title: Align Once to Explain: Feature Alignment for Scalable B-cosification of Foundational Vision Transformers
abstract: Foundational vision models have become the de facto standard for many vision tasks due to their strong performance. However, they are notoriously opaque and remain hard to interpret. We present ALOE (ALign Once to Explain), a one-time, label-free feature alignment approach that efficiently converts foundational vision models into inherently interpretable B-cos variants. Once aligned, the B-cos backbone is used as a drop-in replacement across several downstream tasks-amortizing the cost of interpretability. title: Revisiting LLM Homogeneity Through a Multidimensional Lens
abstract: Concerns about LLM homogeneity are typically quantified with embedding similarity, which reduces two texts to a single score. We revisit homogeneity with 25 interpretable metrics spanning five dimensions: semantic, lexical, syntactic, structural, and stylistic & presentational. A human study shows that perceived similarity depends on both content (what responses say) and form (how they say it), yet embedding similarity correlates less with human meaning judgments than sentence-level matching ($ρ=0.417$ vs. $0.606$) and not significantly with form judgments ($ρ=0.140$). title: A balloon effect: ban one channel and a hidden trait finds another
abstract: Language models trained on the outputs of other models can acquire traits that those outputs never mention, such as a preference for an animal carried by lists of numbers. Such subliminal learning can pass on unwanted traits. The intuitive defence is to find and forbid the tokens through which a trait shows, but how a trait's trace behaves under such bans, and what of it a student learns, has not been resolved. title: Towards Color-faithful Low-light Image Enhancement via Adaptive Color Debiasing and Saturation Rectification
abstract: Low-light imaging often introduces color bias caused by the low signal-to-noise ratio and the image formation process. Although recent low-light image enhancement methods have achieved strong brightness recovery, faithful color restoration remains challenging, manifesting as overall color bias together with local under- and over-saturation. To address this issue, we propose CAGE, a cylindrical color correction framework with adaptive color debiasing and gamut-harmonized saturation rectification for color-faithful low-light image enhancement. title: ShadAR: Real-time Prompting On-demand Visual Augmentation in Augmented Reality
abstract: Augmented Reality can reshape our visual perception (e.g., simulating color blindness) yet such effects are typically pre-programmed by experts, making visual augmentation static and inflexible. We introduce ShadAR, an AR system that allows users to describe expected visual augmentations (e.g., "Blur all people") for changing their vision in real time. ShadAR can graphically manipulate AR passthrough real-time via shader injection. title: DiffAuction: An Auction-Driven Framework for Generative Image Advertising
abstract: Diffusion models enable multiple advertisers to compete for exposure within a shared generated image. Yet existing approaches are computationally costly when generating images under varying target-share configurations, and it remains unclear how the resulting outcomes should be evaluated and priced. To address these gaps, we propose DiffAuction, a framework integrating controllable generation, click-intent evaluation, and auction design. title: Extending Aircraft Coverage of the Poll Schumann Model Using Public Data
abstract: The Poll Schumann model requires airframe and engine parameters, but published tables cover only part of the fleet. Applications must obtain missing parameters, substitute another aircraft type or exclude unrepresented types. We reconstruct parameters using geometry from certification documents and manufacturer manuals, together with ICAO engine records. Published equations supply the physical parameters, regression estimates the propulsion efficiency scale. title: The Agentic Observer Hackathon: Autonomous Decision-making in Simulated Astronomical Surveys
abstract: Astronomical surveys must allocate observing time while responding to changing conditions and competing scientific priorities. We present the Agentic Observer Hackathon (AOH), a community challenge for studying autonomous survey operations. Within a synthetic multi-object survey with prescribed exposure responses and assignment constraints, decision systems select pointings, assign targets and choose exposure configurations while responding to observing requests, instrumental faults and data loss. title: High-resolution tactile observation makes hidden racket-control mechanisms learnable
abstract: Experts can master fine hand-object manipulation skills, yet limited conscious perception of rapid tactile interactions hinders their ability to articulate the underlying control mechanisms. Badminton racket control requires rapid, fine hand-force coordination, providing a demanding testbed for uncovering these mechanisms. An 864-node tactile-inertial glove with synchronized 100-Hz acquisition recorded over 14,000 strokes from more than 70 participants across five skills. title: Optimal Path Planning with Localization constraints
abstract: This paper studies UAV path planning in areas where GPS signals are not present. Because these drones can easily get lost when they don't have GPS, they must rely on dead reckoning and occasionally pass near cellular towers, which act as landmarks to reset and fix their position. The goal is to find the shortest path from a start to a goal location while keeping the estimation uncertainty within a given bound. title: Effect-Size Estimation and Confounding-Aware Permutations for PERMANOVA
abstract: Motivation: PERMANOVA is widely used to test associations between covariates and high-dimensional data with arbitrary distributions, such as ecology, metabolomics, or microbial community profiling. In these contexts, its effect size measure (R2) is generally used to indicate how much the high-dimensional measurement covaries with respect to a separate, univariate measure. However, as we show, this conventional effect size is inflated under the null, resulting in values that do not accurately reflect the conventional expectation of "variance explained." title: Rethinking Evaluation for Principled Generalization Using a Kripkean Challenge to Meaning as Use
abstract: Large language models operationalize an intuitive, view of meaning as use. We argue that it faces a rule-following challenge. Using Kripke's interpretation of Wittgenstein, we argue that finite histories of use do not determine a unique rule for future extension. This reframes the debate about OOD generalization but also about NLP evaluation; benchmarks that measure performance on fixed use cases or local robustness, we argue, do not by themselves establish semantic competence. title: Rethinking LLM Pruning via Test-Time Scaling
abstract: Structured pruning reduces the size of large language models, often at the cost of lower accuracy. Whether this decline reflects diminished reasoning capacity or greater difficulty in sampling correct solutions is less clear. We examine this question across expert, FFN and layer pruning on four mathematical and coding benchmarks, comparing original and pruned models through pass@k at matched sampling budgets. title: Real-VAS: a Real-World Video Amodal Segmentation Dataset
abstract: Amodal video object segmentation is fundamentally limited by the absence of datasets that combine real-world complexity with precise ground-truth annotations. To address this, we present Real Video Amodal Segmentation (Real-VAS), a new large-scale, zero-shot evaluation dataset built from composited real-image video. title: Pair-Relative Partial Equivariance for Rotation-Robust Keypoint Descriptor Matching
abstract: Learned keypoint descriptors trained on upright imagery often fail under large in-plane rotation. Steerers address this by applying a single exact SO(2) representation to the descriptor space, but this global group constraint can be too rigid for keypoint descriptors, whose angular responses need not follow a single group representation. title: Multi-Fidelity Particle Flow Filters based on Log Homotopy
abstract: This work proposes a new Multi-Fidelity Particle Flow Filter (MFPFF) based on a linear control variate framework and multilevel Monte Carlo methods. Conventional particle filters often suffer from weight collapse and particle degeneracy in high-dimensional spaces. Particle flow filters address this by smoothly transporting prior particles toward the posterior distribution, thereby avoiding the need for resampling. title: Unlocking the Potential of Contrastive Regularization for Diffusion Transformer Training
abstract: Representation regularization has emerged as an effective way to improve diffusion transformer training. Yet one of the most canonical regularizers--InfoNCE-style contrastive learning--remains largely underexplored in this setting. We naturally ask a question: can standard contrastive learning serve as an effective regularizer for diffusion transformers? title: From Gaze to Guidance: Interpreting and Adapting to Users’ Cognitive Needs with Multimodal Gaze-Aware AI Assistants
abstract: Current LLM assistants are powerful at answering questions, but they have limited access to the behavioral context that reveals when and where a user is struggling. We present a gaze-grounded multimodal LLM assistant that uses egocentric video with gaze overlays to identify likely points of difficulty and target follow-up retrospective assistance. We instantiate this vision in a controlled study (n=36) comparing the gaze-aware AI assistant to a text-only LLM assistant. title: Consensus Within, Competition Between: Decentralized LLM Teams for Perimeter Defense
abstract: The use of large language models (LLMs) to coordinate multi-agent teams raises a fundamental architectural question: whether task allocation should be centralized in a single LLM controller or distributed across autonomous LLM agents, particularly when communication is unreliable. In a deliberately simplified perimeter-defense simulation against LLM-controlled intruders, we compared a central commander, an auction-based consensus team and independent agents under five network conditions. title: Collascope: Supporting Serendipitous Asset Exploration for Collage-Based Storytelling
abstract: Collage-based storytelling requires visual elements that support emerging narratives and inspire creative reinterpretation. Existing tools, however, rely largely on keyword- and image-based retrieval, offering limited support for serendipitous exploration beyond existing assets. We introduce Collascope, an interactive system that helps creators (1) concretize story intent with interactive element groups, (2) expand the exploration space based on concepts or cutouts towards conceptual and visual dimensions, and (3) develop grounded, traceable ideas in parallel with collage composition. title: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs
abstract: Whether models trained on different modalities converge to the same representation of the world is central to AI. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) conjectures that they do as they scale, but without a proof it offers neither a guarantee nor a recipe. We turn the hypothesis into a theorem. title: SimTO-Robust: Automated Design of Soft Grippers Robust to Grasp Pose and Object Geometry
abstract: Robotic grippers operating in unstructured environments must robustly grasp objects of different shapes and sizes despite perception and positioning errors. Soft grippers that can achieve this robustness through intelligent mechanical design rather than sophisticated control software offer a promising solution. However, no existing computational design framework explicitly optimises soft gripper morphology for robustness across object geometries and grasp poses. title: AnomalyAgent: Agentic Industrial Anomaly Synthesis via Tool-Augmented Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Industrial anomaly generation is a crucial method for alleviating the data scarcity problem in anomaly detection tasks. Most existing anomaly synthesis methods rely on single-step generation mechanisms, lacking complex reasoning and iterative optimization capabilities, making it difficult to generate anomaly samples with high semantic realism. We propose AnomalyAgent, an anomaly synthesis agent with self-reflection, knowledge retrieval, and iterative refinement capabilities, aiming to generate realistic and diverse anomalies. title: Estimation and Inference for One-pass Streaming Function-on-Function Regression
abstract: In many applications, functional pairs are collected sequentially from a data stream. Existing function-on-function regression methods are primarily designed for batch data, and bootstrap inference has become one of the most popular approaches. However, this procedure may be infeasible when observations cannot be stored. In this paper, we propose a one-pass functional SGD estimator that updates upon each observation's arrival without data storage, and a weighted rolling validation rule is provided for step size selection for implementation. title: Subspace Representations for Synthetic-to-Real Transfer in 3-D Surface Inspection
abstract: This paper studies what subspace representations contribute to synthetic-to-real transfer in 3-D surface inspection, where models learn from synthetic defects and the only real data before deployment are scans of good parts. We use three classical constructions as instruments: the nearest-subspace classifier, one-class template subspaces and the generalized difference subspace (GDS). title: GSLM2: Multi-Stream Speech Representation Learning and Generative Spoken Language Modeling
abstract: Generative spoken language models (SLMs) offer a route to learning linguistic structure purely from speech, yet they lag far behind text-based models in both capability and data scaling efficiency. We identify two bottlenecks underlying this gap: the limited linguistic quality of existing speech units and the reliance on a single stream of discrete units to represent speech. title: What's Old Is New: Improved Learning from Small-Group Tutorials
abstract: The ubiquity of Large Language Models poses a challenge to student learning in homework-based college courses, where access to easy homework answers devalues the intended productive struggle. To address this concern, we propose Oxbridge-style weekly tutorials, where students present homework problems without notes in a small group with an instructor or TA. We conducted a randomized experiment in an introductory probability class to evaluate the effectiveness of tutorials, finding a significant positive effect of tutorial enrollment on exam grades. title: Trajectory-Planning Attitude Control System for Satellites with Magnetic Attitude Control and One Reaction Wheel
abstract: Selecting attitude actuators for spacecraft in low earth orbit (LEO) often involves a trade between reaction wheels and magnetorquers. Reaction wheels generally have higher size, weight and power as well as cost, compared with magnetorquers, but have performance advantages. We consider a hybrid system relying on a single reaction wheel and three magnetorquers, using a trajectory planning control method that focuses on meeting pointing goals and minimizing the need to desaturate the reaction wheel. title: Specificity Bias and the Wikipedia Paradox: An xAI Analysis of AI Text Detectors under Domain Shift
abstract: The widespread adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) demands reliable detection of human-authored versus synthetic text. However, current Transformer-based detectors often experience severe performance degradation during domain shifts and operate as opaque classifiers. This paper investigates the robustness and interpretability of fine-tuned Transformer models (DistilBERT, RoBERTa) by evaluating them against a custom out-of-distribution (OOD) dataset of hyper-local news synthesized via open-source LLMs (Llama 3, Mistral, Gemma). title: Seeing Before Naming: Context-Grounded Learning of Novel Visual Concepts
abstract: Learning an unfamiliar visual category requires more than adapting a classifier: the model must connect its visual evidence to a useful semantic name. A pre-trained vision-language model can retain discriminative image features while providing a weak textual anchor for the target concept. We address this imbalance through context-grounded semantic anchoring. title: Detecting Fine-Grained Differences between Image Datasets
abstract: Detecting whether and in particular how two data distributions differ is a fundamental statistical problem. For example, we might be interested in which concepts (expressed in natural language) differ between two classes, the outputs of different generative models, or the same model with different prompt specifications. When working with large and complex image datasets, we intuitively think that first selecting concepts from a broad list using fine-grained patch embeddings, and then optimizing the concepts to better fit the data is an effective workflow. title: GameVerse: A Minute-Scale Gameplay Dataset for Long-Horizon Interactive World Modeling
abstract: Recent advances in interactive world models have made it possible to generate controllable, dynamic environments from action inputs. Yet current models struggle to maintain coherence beyond roughly one minute of rollout, a limitation rooted not in model capacity but in the scarcity of long-horizon training data. Existing gameplay video datasets typically consist of clips under ten seconds, with captions that describe whole clips in coarse and undifferentiated text, which is insufficient for controllable long-horizon generation. title: A Pretrained Model for Bayesian Filtering in Heterogeneous Dynamical Systems
abstract: Filtering has not yet had its foundation-model moment: state estimation is still dominated either by online Bayesian filtering algorithms that require known dy- namics as inputs, or by learning-based neural filters trained from scratch for a single system or parametric family. The core challenge is structural heterogene- ity: dynamical systems differ in their governing dynamics, physical scales, and noise levels, precluding a shared representation space for a reusable filter. title: Existence of the thermodynamic limit for the Hopfield model
abstract: We prove that the quenched pressure of the Hopfield model with $K\simαN$ i.i.d. symmetric Rademacher patterns has a thermodynamic limit at every load $α\in(0,\infty)$, finite inverse temperature and uniform external field, with no replica-symmetry, order-parameter concentration or non-condensation hypothesis required. abstract: A method of solution for the inverse scattering problem for the linear fifth order Schr${\rm\ddot{o}}$dinger operator is found. Two closed systems of linear singular integral equations are obtained. From solutions to these equations, potential on the left and right half-axes is restored unambiguously.

title: Inertial Steering and Motion Prediction of Tracked Vehicles on Low-Adherence Surfaces
abstract: Tracked vehicles are widely used in off-road applications, but their conventional motion models often rely on no-slip assumptions that become inaccurate on low-adherence surfaces. Rather than treating inertial effects arising from slip as a disturbance to be minimized, this work investigates how inertial effects arising from a moving mass can be deliberately exploited for steering on low-friction surfaces. title: Lone-Pair Stereoactivity Overrides Mass Scaling of Thermal Expansion and Heat Conduction in Non-vander Waals Layered Bismuth Oxychalcogenides
abstract: Heavier chalcogens are generally expected to soften isostructural semiconductor lattices, raising thermal expansion and lowering thermal conductivity. title: Uncovering Why LLMs Fail: From Internal Mechanisms to Adversarial Reasoning Trajectories
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are usually evaluated by final-output correctness or safety, yet an endpoint label does not reveal how a failure develops throughout the reasoning process. We therefore ask whether ordinary reasoning failures and adversarially induced failures can be characterized using the same internal coordinates. Towards this end, we in this paper study a white-box diagnostic framework CauTrace to disclose the root-cause of why LLM fails from three fundamental inspections: Functional States, Propagation of Representation, Temporal-State Coordination and Reasoning Trajectory. title: Modeling and Experimental Validation of Bubble-Induced Performance Losses in Microstructured Copper Electrodes for Alkaline Water Electrolysis
abstract: Water electrolysis is a promising technology for sustainable hydrogen (H$_2$) production. However, gas bubble formation significantly degrades the electrochemical surface area ($A_{\rm EC}$) and the electrocatalytic activity of microstructured electrodes in water electrolyzer cells. Existing theoretical models fail to connect computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and electrochemistry to analyze how bubble dynamics affect the performance of gas-evolving microstructured electrodes. title: Mind The Gap (MTG-AD): Dataset and Fine-grained Evaluation for End-to-End Inline Audio Descriptions
abstract: Audio descriptions (AD) are essential for making visual media accessible to blind and low-vision (BLV) users. While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) offer a scalable solution for generating audio descriptions on-demand, their performance on ``inline'' audio descriptions -- which must fit within existing silences in a video -- remains under-explored, particularly for diverse user-generated content (UGC). title: CHORD: Cross-Model Hallucination Detection via Relational Graph Discrimination
abstract: Hallucination detection is critical for deploying large language models (LLMs) in real-world applications. Due to strong empirical performance, internal representation-based methods have emerged as the prevailing direction for detecting hallucinations, yet they remain largely model-specific and often fail to generalize to unseen LLMs. In this paper, we study an important yet underexplored problem, termed cross-model hallucination detection (CMHD), which aims to train hallucination detectors on source LLMs while ensuring performance on unseen target LLMs. The core challenge of CMHD lies in cros

title: Free energy of the Hopfield model
abstract: We identify the limit of the free energy of the Hopfield model with independent symmetric Bernoulli patterns, for every temperature and loading ratio. abstract: Does the level of test-time processing effort affect a language model's computational capability? A formal grammar-lens benchmark method, derived from the theory of computation, generates novel data at specified levels, each successively more computationally powerful than the levels below. title: Kidney Exchange with Dual Donors
abstract: Kidney exchange programs enable patients with incompatible living donors to receive transplants by exchanging donors with other patient-donor pairs. Existing models typically assume either that each patient enrolls with a single donor, or that at most one of a patient's multiple alternative donors is selected to donate. In practice, however, a patient may have access to multiple willing but incompatible donors who are all prepared to donate simultaneously if doing so enables the patient to receive a kidney. abstract: Autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models enable long-form video generation but remain expensive due to repeated multi-step denoising. Existing training-free acceleration methods rely on binary cache-or-recompute decisions, overlooking intermediate cases where direct reuse is too coarse yet full recomputation is unnecessary. title: Clock-Shift-Aided Blind Doppler Matching in Passive SDR Monitoring Data for LEO Doppler Positioning
abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite signals have recently attracted increasing attention as opportunistic signals for positioning, navigation, and timing. Most Doppler-based LEO positioning studies rely on tracked satellite signals or raw in-phase/quadrature (IQ) samples that preserve signal-level structures for acquisition, Doppler tracking, or satellite association. title: VPR-Space: A Benchmark for Visual Place Recognition in Space Analog Domains
abstract: Visual Place Recognition (VPR) is an important means for loop closure detection in visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM). While state-of-the-art VPR and SLAM approaches excel in urban and feature-rich natural environments, the vast and feature-poor environments of extraterrestrial surfaces like on the Moon or Mars pose severe challenges for existing approaches. This paper presents a novel benchmark, VPR-Space, to evaluate VPR capabilities on extraterrestrial surfaces. abstract: Existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems treat web pages as flat text, losing the structural and semantic signals encoded in HTML. We present PolyUQuest, a verifiable, structure-aware web RAG framework built on a heterogeneous graph that unifies hyperlink topology between pages, DOM hierarchy within pages, and entity–relation knowledge across pages. abstract: Engineers who audit a declared specification of an engineered system need to know which physical constraints it respects, which it violates, which field was altered and how to correct it. title: Improving Precision in Cluster-Level Pricing Experiments with Temporal Switchbacks
abstract: Online pricing systems often cannot randomize treatments at the user level because prices are deployed over operational units such as routes, regions, or markets. This creates low-powered A/B tests due to persistent cluster heterogeneity, seasonality, and autocorrelated demand. We study temporal switchback designs for cluster-level pricing experiments, where each cluster alternates between treatment and control over time. Using LATAM Airlines ancillary-pricing data and calibrated simulations, we show that switchbacks can substantially reduce standard errors relative to parallel cluster designs

title: Less Is More: Balancing Positive and Negative Space in Visual Concept Blending
abstract: Graphic designers often blend visual concepts to communicate multiple ideas within a single image, leveraging positive and negative space to create balance, emphasis, and aesthetic appeal. While computational methods have begun to support automatic concept blending, they largely overlook the role of spatial composition in the design. To address this gap, we present an automatic pipeline that explicitly applies positive and negative space throughout the blending process. Our approach first identifies plausible regions for concept integration by combining semantic reasoning from vision–language

title: DualG-MRAG: Decoupling Macro-Reasoning and Micro-Matching for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: While Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MM-RAG) has shown promising results, it still struggles with complex multi-hop reasoning tasks. Existing methods primarily focus on independent instance-level matching, which often fails to capture explicit relationships across modalities and documents. Although Graph-enhanced methods introduce structural modeling, they face a fundamental challenge in multimodal scenarios: incorporating fine-grained visual features leads to rapid graph expansion and retrieval noise, whereas coarse-grained representations cause the discarding of critical local ev

title: A Hybrid Path Planning Framework for Assistive Wheelchair Navigation in Dynamic Pedestrian Environments
abstract: Autonomous wheelchairs can improve the quality of life for individuals with mobility impairments by providing greater independence. However, reliable navigation especially in human environments is a major challenge due to factors such as dynamic obstacles, unpredictable pedestrian behavior, and the users' need to complete multiple stops along the way before reaching their final destination. This paper presents a hybrid path planning framework for multi-goal navigation in dynamic environments. The framework integrates the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) for global task ordering with the Potent

title: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Uni: Elastic Self-Refining Unified Diffusion LLM with Cross-Paradigm On-Policy Distillation
abstract: We propose Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Uni (NLD-Uni), a unified discrete diffusion large language model (DLLM) for visual understanding and generation tasks. Compared with prior unified diffusion models, NLD-Uni introduces two major innovations. First, we propose a unified cross-paradigm on-policy distillation (OPD) framework that successfully transfers the visual understanding ability of autoregressive VLMs and visual generation ability of continuous flow models, to a unified DLLM. Second, NLD-Uni incorporates a novel progressive self-refining diffusion process that gradually corrupts each token

title: Persistent Geospatial Outage Scenario Construction for Interdependent Infrastructure Simulation
abstract: Extreme weather events are producing persistent geographic patterns of power-grid disruption across the United States, yet these patterns are rarely incorporated into geospatial simulation of interdependent infrastructure failures. This paper presents a data-driven geospatial simulation framework that transforms persistent outage patterns into empirically grounded regional simulation scenarios for interdependent power-communication cascade simulation. Using a national outage dataset from 2015-2023, we introduce the Hotspot Persistence Index (HPI), a severity-ranked recurrence metric for identi

title: Interaction-Aware Sampling-Based Motion Planning for Autonomous Surface Vessels in Urban Waterways
abstract: Autonomous surface vessels operating in urban waterways must coordinate with other vessels in confined spaces while complying with traffic regulations, often without knowing their intentions. We present a decentralized motion planner based on model predictive path integral control, a sampling-based model predictive control scheme. The planner jointly computes a trajectory for the ego vessel and a prediction of the trajectories of the other vessels, and therefore accounts for their interaction. Traffic regulations are encoded as discontinuous costs, which the sampling-based formulation admits w

title: Completeness and Cost of Retrieval Structures for Multi-Tool Requests in LLM Agents
abstract: An agent that must call several tools to fulfill a request fails when the tool retriever omits any one of them, yet tool retrievers are mostly built and evaluated on queries requiring a single tool. We compare representatives of six retrieval structures (flat lexical and dense retrieval, LLM query decomposition, LLM-navigated hierarchies, server-then-tool matching, dependency graphs, and trained set-level retrievers) across two multi-tool testbeds: 345 AppWorld queries with expert dependency labels and 103 MCP-Bench tasks over 257 MCP tools. We measure completeness@k, the share of queries whos

title: Learning-to-Memorize: Dynamic Context Management for Long-Horizon Autoregressive Video Generation
abstract: Autoregressive video generation has achieved impressive results on short clips, yet generating long videos remains challenging due to error accumulation over extended horizons, where each predicted frame depends on potentially imperfect previous frames. Existing approaches typically rely on static context management strategies, such as sliding-window caches that discard early frames or fixed sink frames that permanently preserve initial content. These designs either lose critical long-range context or anchor generation to outdated information, which can lead to degraded fidelity, motion stagna

title: MAIC-UI: Making Interactive Courseware with Generative UI
abstract: Creating interactive STEM courseware traditionally requires HTML/CSS/JavaScript expertise, leaving barriers for educators. While generative AI can produce HTML codes, existing tools generate static presentations rather than interactive simulations, struggle with long documents, and lack pedagogical accuracy mechanisms. Furthermore, full regeneration for modifications requires 200–600 seconds, disrupting creative flow. We present MAIC-UI, a zero-code authoring system that enables educators to create and rapidly edit interactive courseware from textbooks, PPTs, and PDFs. MAIC-UI employs: (1) str

title: Kernelized Stable Fluids for simulating physically accurate solutions
abstract: The Stable Fluids algorithm is a fractional step method for solving the incompressible Navier-Stokes (NS) equations in an unconditionally stable way. It was initially developed for visual effects and allows real-time simulations because of its low computational complexity. The method solves the advection step by using the method of characteristics which is implemented via linear interpolation. This results in excessive diffusion of vorticity and is one of the main reasons for the physical inaccuracy of the algorithm.
