title: PageLLM: A Multi-Grained Reward Framework for Whole-Page Optimization with Large Language Models
abstract: Whole-page optimization (WPO) decides how search and recommendation results are surfaced to users, and large language models (LLMs) open a new route to it by treating page generation as sequence generation. Adapting LLMs to web-scale WPO, however, remains bottlenecked by the need for costly human annotations and by the mismatched granularity between page-level coherence and item-level placement. In this work we show that these two challenges are coupled: implicit user feedback alone suffices for alignment, provided the reward signal is decoupled into two complementary granularities. We propose

title: Belief-Conditioned Multi-Agent Actor Critic for Decentralized LLM Collaboration
abstract: Recent work has explored optimizing LLM collaboration through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), but many approaches still rely on predefined workflows, limiting efficiency and scalability. Decentralized LLM collaboration is challenging because agents execute independently with limited communication, share a joint objective, and must infer useful information from communication traces. In this paper, we propose BCMAAC, a Belief-Conditioned Multi-Agent Actor-Critic method that maintains beliefs over contextual information and uses them to facilitate training. Experiments on Minecraft gam

title: TestHallVQA: Exploring LVLMs' Document-Level Reasoning under Redundant Contexts from Scientific Exams
abstract: Large Vision–Language Models (LVLMs) are increasingly expected to perform visual question answering (VQA) over planar media. However, existing planar VQA benchmarks typically emphasize isolated challenges: some emphasize long-document understanding with limited reasoning depth, while others require complex visual reasoning but remain restricted to single-page, noise-free settings. Moreover, through theoretical analysis, we identify the impact of irrelevant visual tokens, which leads to measurable performance degradation but has received little attention with respect to systematic quantificatio

title: PhysCount: Do MLLMs Count Visual Appearances or Physical Entities?
abstract: Images reveal appearances, but counting often asks about physical objects. A single entity may be visible directly, in several reflections, or through glass, so detecting every visible occurrence does not determine how many entities are present. Existing visual counting benchmarks rarely separate these two operations. We introduce PhysCount, a benchmark for evaluating whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can distinguish what appears in an image from what physically exists in the scene. title: PosIR: A Multilingual Benchmark for Diagnosing Position Bias in Information Retrieval
abstract: Position bias—the systematic effect of where key information is located on retrieval effectiveness—is a critical concern in information retrieval. Although recent studies have identified such bias in dense retrievers, existing analyses focus predominantly on monolingual English, fail to disentangle document length from information position, and lack a standardized framework for controlled evaluation. institutions: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

title: LiveSearch: Questions as Executable Verifier Code for a Live Benchmark of Professional-Source Financial Search Agents
abstract: In finance, the answer that matters is usually the current one: prices, rates, and disclosures hold only as of a given day, so retrieving up-to-date facts is a core capability of a financial agent. Yet most financial benchmarks overlook timeliness. They fix each answer at annotation time, so the gold goes stale as markets move and, once leaked into training data, rewards recall rather than search and analysis. title: RFW-A: Agentic Procedural Generation of 400K Articulated Assets over 500 Categories
abstract: High-quality articulated assets are essential for embodied perception, simulation, and manipulation, yet constructing them at scale remains difficult. Manual annotation and procedural modeling require substantial human effort. Recent agentic systems automate asset construction through program synthesis, but repeat costly reasoning and refinement for every new asset. Our key observation is that assets within a category can share construction logic despite variations in structure and appearance. Agentic synthesis and procedural generation are therefore complementary: agents can construct reusabl

title: PACEE: Parent-Centered AI Scaffolding for Emotion Education in Early Childhood Conversations
abstract: Emotion education is critical for children aged 3 to 6. However, existing technologies depend substantially on direct child-AI interaction, overlooking the central role of parents in guiding early emotional development at home. To address this gap, we conducted co-design sessions with five kindergarten teachers and five parents to identify key parental challenges and opportunities for AI support in family emotion education. Based on these insights, we developed PACEE, an LLM-based assistant designed around an asymmetric triadic interaction framework: AI primarily supports parents while preserv

title: AutoCSF: A Provably Safe Indexing Framework for Filter-Augmented Compressed Static Functions
abstract: We consider the problem of building space-efficient indexes for static key-value datasets with highly skewed value distributions. A standard technique for this task is to augment a compressed static function (CSF) with an approximate set membership prefilter to handle a dominating value and break the one-bit-per-key barrier. However, we observe that prior approaches decide when to apply such a prefilter using idealized cost models or data-driven heuristics, and, as a result, can recommend using a prefilter in regimes where it actively increases space usage. institutions: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

title: Rydberg atomic field-enhanced feed beyond electrically small antennas
abstract: The reception of electromagnetic signals becomes increasingly challenging at longer wavelengths, as conventional antenna feeds must scale with the operating wavelength, making it difficult to reconcile compactness with high sensitivity. Rydberg atoms enable direct field-to-optical conversion within deeply subwavelength sensing volumes, yet an effective receiving feed that couples incident fields into the atomic interaction volume remains underdeveloped. title: Integrating Domain Adaptation and Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Saline-Alkali Land Reclamation Planning
abstract: Reclamation of saline-alkali land requires management plans that account for soil and water conditions, treatment evidence, and financial constraints. This study develops Wenyao, an agricultural decision-support system integrating domain adaptation with retrieval-augmented generation. A bilingual corpus of 8,664 research papers was processed using a 110-indicator schema to construct SA-Bench, comprising 4,860 paper-level planning instances. A QwQ-32B model was adapted through low-rank supervised fine-tuning and combined with case retrieval for budget-conditioned planning. Evidence extraction a

title: Spherical Brownian Diffusion for Language Modeling
abstract: Continuous diffusion language models involve two coupled design choices: how to corrupt continuous token representations and how to invert that corruption at generation time. Recent work has explored language generation on the unit sphere through geodesic and von Mises--Fisher (vMF) paths, raising the question of which forward process to use on this geometry and how much that choice matters relative to inference. title: Efficient Quantum Optimization via Dissipative False Vacuum Decay
abstract: Efficient quantum solvers for computationally hard problems are highly desirable for near-term quantum platforms. Here, we propose a cavity-based dissipative quantum solver for a class of NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems encoded in atomic-spin Hamiltonians with a few discrete single-spin-flip transition energies. We show that the cavity-based quantum solver exploits dissipative false-vacuum decay in configuration space to facilitate escape from metastable local minima in rugged energy landscapes. title: Aerodynamic Shape Optimization of unsteady flapping wings
abstract: This study introduces a new approach for building surrogate models, in the form of Reduced Order Models (ROMs), for PDE-constrained optimization. A physics-constrained data-driven framework is developed to transform large-scale non-linear optimization problems into ROM-constrained optimization problems. Unlike conventional methods, which suffer from instability of the forward sensitivity function, the proposed approach projects optimization problems to system dynamics optimization problems in Hilbert space to increase stability, diminish memory requirements, and lower computational cost. title: Hyperspectral Unmixing using a Structured Linear Mixing Model with Additive Spectral Variability
abstract: Linear hyperspectral unmixing aims at retrieving pure material spectra present in an observed scene and their associated abundance fractions in each pixel. In most practical situations, hyperspectral images are affected by spectral variability (SV) also known as intra-class variability, which is caused by different physical phenomena including atmospheric effects, intrinsic variability of the pure materials and illumination or topographic changes. Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Institut de Recherche en Astrophysique et Planétologie

title: On-the-fly Estimation of Quantum-Corrected Thermodynamics in LAMMPS
abstract: We present a native implementation of the Two/Three-Phase Thermodynamics (xPT, $x \in \{2,3\}$) method within the LAMMPS molecular dynamics framework, termed FixXPT. xPT is an approach for obtaining absolute, quantum-corrected thermodynamics (entropy, enthalpy, free energy, heat capacity, diffusivity) from the density of states function, obtained from the velocity autocorrelation function of an equilibrium trajectory. title: LucidLyra: Feed-Forward Generative 3D Scene Reconstruction and Joint Understanding via Multi-Task Distillation
abstract: We present LucidLyra, a framework that makes generatively reconstructed 3D scenes directly queryable for semantics and instances in a feed-forward manner from video latents. While generative 3D reconstruction can synthesize virtual environments from a single image, downstream applications in robotics and physical AI require not only visual realism but also access to scene semantics and object identities. institutions: University of Modena and Reggio Emilia

title: Pareto climate economics: optimism, pessimism and the polarization of societies
abstract: We argue that simple conceptual models of the relation between short-term efforts in climate mitigation and adaptation policies (STECM&AP) and possible climate damages can help understanding the difficulties of increasing public support for a transition towards sustainable, decarbonized economies. Specifically, we show that, under fairly general conditions, mistrust and pessimism tend to polarize support for either minimal ``business as usual'' policies or maximal ``all-in climate mitigation efforts'' choices. Under the same conditions, trust and optimism tend to de-polarize societies towards
institutions: Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research

title: Compound Climate Risk-Aware Electricity Dispatch: Trajectory-Based Modeling for Power System Resilience
abstract: In recent decades, emerging compound hazards in a changing climate have increasingly threatened power system resilience and posed new challenges to electricity dispatch. Conventional Value-at-Risk (VaR)-based risk-aware dispatch provides a tractable means of managing stochastic net demand deviations caused by distribution feeder outages. title: When to Intervene? An Empirical Study of Errors and Self-Recovery in LLM Agents
abstract: LLM agents interact with Web services to perform tasks on users' behalf. Errors during these interactions can disrupt execution and prevent task completion, motivating external intervention. However, agents may self-recover through continued execution, raising the question of when to intervene and when to wait for self-recovery. We present an empirical study of errors and self-recovery in LLM agents. We construct ReInBench, a dataset containing 1,259 agent traces and 1,403 error events across computer-use and Web tasks. institutions: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

title: Decision and System One models in rheumatology: accuracy and calibration on specialty-training examination questions and diagnostic case vignettes
abstract: Objective: To evaluate the accuracy and calibration of Decision and System One models on rheumatology examination questions and diagnostic vignettes. Methods: Two benchmarks were analysed: 172 text-based rheumatology questions from Spanish specialty-training examinations (expanded RheumaMIR dataset) in Spanish and English, and 70 English diagnostic vignettes from RheumBench, each with 5-18 candidate diagnoses, 52 of which included the correct reference diagnosis. Four System One models (i.e., Jev 1.13, Clef, Microsoft-Decision-1, Laya) and GPT-6 Luna, evaluated as a decision model through the

title: Definability and Interpolation in Philosophy
abstract: This paper offers a light tour of occurrences of Craig’s interpolation theorem and Beth’s definability theorem in philosophy. There is no coherent research program with a central agenda around this theme in the literature, but extending the discussion in [9], we trace some lines and identify some issues in establishing contacts at this interface between the realms of logic and the philosophy of logic, of science, of language and information, epistemology, and metaphysics. Our presentation can also be viewed as a case study for more general aspects of the logic–philosophy interface.

title: FATE-5: Faithful Alignment of Trait Expression for Continuous Big Five Personality Control
abstract: Controlling personality in large language models is important for building conversational agents that can be customized to different users and interaction settings. However, existing personality control methods often face a tradeoff between strong trait expression and natural dialogue generation. We introduce FATE-5, Faithful Alignment of Trait Expression for the Big Five, a two-stage framework that separates personality encoding from naturalness alignment. FATE-5 first learns continuous soft prompt representations of Big Five profiles using dialogue supervision and an auxiliary survey objecti

title: Sweep Less, Steer More: Using Activation Steering Geometry for Reduced Hyperparameter Search
abstract: Representation steering methods like difference-in-means (DIM) offer a lightweight approach to controlling LLM behavior, but their effectiveness varies widely across concepts, datasets, and layers, making principled deployment costly without exhaustive hyperparameter sweeps. We build on the discriminability index $d'$, a compute-cheap geometric measure of how well contrastive training activations separate along the steering direction. title: sDMD: Sinkhorn Distribution Matching Distillation
abstract: Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) distills multi-step diffusion models into few-step generators by minimizing reverse KL divergence. Despite its strong performance, DMD guides samples by local density alone, which introduces two limitations: teacher scores can be unreliable in regions of low teacher density, and the mode-seeking behavior of reverse KL can collapse the student onto a subset of the teacher modes. title: NumTrace: Auditing the Number Provenance of Financial Analyst Agents
abstract: A numerical claim generated by a financial analyst agent can match a number in a company filing but refer to the wrong entity, concept, period, unit or scope. A check based on reference answers can mark such an answer as wrong but does not explain why it fails. In this paper, we present NumTrace, a new benchmark that audits the provenance of each numerical claim made by financial analyst agents: its source and financial semantics. title: Look Over There! Dynamic Visual Guidance for AI-Narrated Slides
abstract: Slides present information spatially, but narration unfolds linearly, leaving the viewer struggling to locate what the narration refers to. This split attention between audio and visual channels forces viewers to search the slide manually, imposing extraneous cognitive load and disrupting comprehension. The problem is especially acute on mobile devices, where dense layouts compressed onto small screens make visual search particularly effortful. In teacher-led settings, however, instructors naturally direct attention through pointing, pacing, and emphasis. Inspired by this, we present GuideSlid

title: How timing and mode of selection shape ancestral genetic contributions
abstract: We examine a population that evolves according to a biparental Moran model with two distinct types of individuals. Each individual's type is determined by the allele they carry at one biallelic locus, which is transmitted in a Mendelian way. This type influences the individual's mating preferences. We investigate two specific mating patterns: (i) where the type determines the level of attractiveness, and (ii) where the type dictates the level of homogamous choosiness. institutions: SIMBA: Inférence Statistique et Modélisation pour les Applications Biologiques
Laboratoire Traitement et Communication de l’Information

title: PRISM-Bench: An Audio-Centric Diagnostic Benchmark for Text-to-Audio-Video Generation
abstract: Text-to-audio-video (T2AV) generation has advanced rapidly, but its evaluation still underestimates the audio modality. Existing benchmarks either treat audio as an auxiliary component of video quality or assess it in isolation from audiovisual grounding, making it difficult to diagnose where current systems truly succeed or fail in audio generation. We present PRISM-Bench, the first audio-centric diagnostic benchmark for T2AV generation. title: LongVidSearch: An Agentic Benchmark for Multi-hop Evidence Retrieval Planning in Long Videos
abstract: Long video question answering (Long-Video QA) increasingly relies on agentic tool use to retrieve evidence from long videos. In realistic settings, this process often requires multi-hop retrieval, where agents must iteratively gather multiple discontinuous evidence clips. However, existing long-video benchmarks are largely static: they rarely enforce strict multi-hop retrieval and typically lack a standardized evidence-access interface, making it difficult to separate failures in retrieval planning from those in answer generation. title: Time-Aware Urban Flood Routing with Sticky Edge Closure on Forecast Depth: A Hanoi Case Study
abstract: During urban flash floods, commuters and guiding agencies require awareness towards which roads remain passable when a vehicle actually arrives, rather than relying solely on which links appear open at initial departure. Most existing flood-routing tools apply a single static snapshot to each route; meaning that corridors that appear clear initially can become flooded before arrival. This paper presents a routing engine that ingests a two-hour water forecast, renewed every 15 minutes, and plans each journey around roads that the forecast closes for that specific vehicle class. title: The Evolution and 'Chineseness' of Urban Screens in China: From Propaganda Posters to Smart City Interfaces
abstract: Urban screens have become a global feature of the media city, yet their developmental paths are not universal. This paper argues that the evolution of urban screens in China constitutes a distinct paradigm of media urbanism, termed Chineseness, understood here not as cultural essence but as a relational, historically situated configuration of three linked elements: deep-rooted lineages of public communication; state-steered technological leapfrogging driven by industrial policy and mega-events; and a regulatory paradox that enables spectacular scale while tightening operational control. title: Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Evaluation
abstract: Embodied systems can update policies, world models, skills, and executable programs from deployment experience, allowing one interaction to benefit later tasks. When a system also revises and reuses its data-acquisition, feedback, or learning procedures, experience changes the process that produces capability, introducing recursive self-improvement. This paper surveys research in physical AI through the connection between persistent capability and its improvement process. Southern University of Science and Technology

title: IntReal: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Multimodal Interleaved Generation
abstract: Humans routinely consume multimodal content, where textual and visual information is naturally interleaved. Although Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) can jointly generate text and images, multimodal interleaved generation remains largely underexplored. Progress in this area is hindered by two key limitations: (1) the lack of well-defined interleaved generation tasks and corresponding training data, and (2) the absence of fine-grained evaluation protocols that can reliably diagnose model performance across different capability dimensions. title: Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation
abstract: Real-time long-video generation requires continuous output with consistent appearance and natural motion. Existing chunk-wise autoregressive methods face challenges in both generation efficiency and long-video quality: serialized denoising and history-cache refresh require two forward passes even with one-step denoising, and longer rollouts can degrade quality and cause camera drift. We propose Wave Forcing (WF), which co-designs generation, training, and execution for continuous video output with multi-step denoising. title: Nuclear fission: from fundamentals to frontiers
abstract: Nuclear fission, the division of a heavy atomic nucleus into lighter fragments, is a process of fundamental importance to nuclear physics, energy production, and the origin of the elements. This chapter, part of the Encyclopedia of Nuclear Physics, provides a pedagogical introduction to a broad array of topics in fission physics, progressing from the macroscopic liquid-drop model and microscopic shell corrections through fission dynamics, observables, modern theoretical frameworks, and experimental techniques ranging from traditional double-energy methods to inverse kinematics at radioactive-i

title: Rotation-driven suppression and re-emergence of unsteady flow past a circular cylinder
abstract: The flow past a rotating cylinder undergoes substantial changes in its wake dynamics and aerodynamic response with increasing rotation rate. This study investigates these changes in two-dimensional compressible flow at \(Re_\infty=3800\) and \(M_\infty=0.1\), with the rotation rate systematically varied over \(0.1\leqΩ\leq10\) using 130 high-fidelity simulations. title: Steering Readerly Dynamics: Trajectory-Guided Story Generation with Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate stories, but these stories struggle to reproduce engaging readerly dynamics, the evolving reader responses that shape narrative experience. To address this challenge, we propose a framework that learns readerly dynamics from high-quality human-written stories and uses them to guide story generation. Instead of directly modeling high-dimensional story content, we train a small LLM to predict future reader responses as low-dimensional trajectories. institutions: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

title: Impact of Surface Preparation on the Propulsion of Catalytic Janus Colloids and Implications for Reproducibility
abstract: Platinum-coated polystyrene (PS) Janus particles (JPs) propelled by the catalytic decomposition of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) are a widely used model system for active matter, yet reported speeds for similar particles and fuel concentrations differ by more than an order of magnitude. Broad adoption of these materials requires increasing consistency in the preparation and achieving improved repeatability in their behavior. title: MERIDIAN: Memory-Encoded Rituals for Intimacy across Distance in an Interactive, Asynchronous Neighbourhood
abstract: How can shared memories become playable structures for partners who live in different time zones? We present MERIDIAN, a pre-deployment design case of Yi Town, a bilingual browser game developed by one member of a long-distance couple as a gift for the other. Nine levels translate personally meaningful events, places and cultural references into tasks within a navigable pixel town. A birthday prologue and a fictional wedding frame the intended experience. title: MemGUI-Bench: Benchmarking Memory of Mobile GUI Agents in Dynamic Environments
abstract: Current mobile GUI agent benchmarks systematically fail to assess memory capabilities, with only 5.2-11.8% memory-related tasks and no cross-session learning evaluation. We introduce MemGUI-Bench, a comprehensive memory-centric benchmark with pass@k and staged LLM-as-judge evaluation. Our contributions include: (1) a systematic memory taxonomy analyzing 11 agents across 5 architectures; (2) 128 tasks across 26 applications where 89.8% challenge memory through cross-temporal and cross-spatial retention; (3) MemGUI-Eval, an automated pipeline with Progressive Scrutiny and 7 hierarchical metrics;

title: SemanticSlider3D: Training-Free Continuous Semantic Editing for 3D Objects
abstract: Fine-grained control over continuous semantic attributes of 3D objects is essential for 3D content creation, but is not well supported by conventional 3D modeling workflows or prompt-based interaction with existing generative AI tools. While slider-based methods have proven effective for fine-grained semantic control in 2D image generation, no equivalent approach exists for 3D. Extending these 2D methods to 3D is non-trivial due to challenges unique to 3D, including geometric integrity and cross-view coherence. title: Early warning of critical transitions: Distinguishing supercritical and subcritical bifurcations from noisy observations
abstract: Early-warning methods can indicate that a system is approaching a loss of stability, but they do not usually reveal whether the approaching bifurcation is supercritical or subcritical. We investigate whether this distinction can be made from noisy pre-transition observations. For this investigation, we extend a regression-based stability method by including the leading cubic nonlinear term, whose sign is used to predict the bifurcation type. title: How I Aligned Your Model: Scaling Up Multilingual Safety Training with Templates
abstract: Safety alignment for Large Language Models is heavily focused on English with limited multilingual representation, particularly damaging low-resource language performance. Related open training datasets are often limited in size or do not follow region-localized harmful topics to broaden the scope of alignment beyond cultures. title: An Input Skip Can Reparameterize a VAE Without Improving the Generator
abstract: An input skip can reduce reconstruction error while leaving a model's distribution of new samples unchanged. For a Gaussian variational autoencoder (VAE) with constant input skip $0\leqα<1$, a model without a skip can be written in skip form by multiplying its decoder output by $b=1-α$ and its noise variance by $b^2$. title: Optimizing Tugboat Emissions within Port Areas Using Data Fusion
abstract: Abstract Maritime transport is essential for global trade but remains a major source of greenhouse gas and air pollutant emissions, especially near ports and coastal communities. Tugboats, which play a crucial role in vessel manoeuvres, are significant contributors but their emissions are poorly quantified due to the inadequacy of conventional estimation methods. abstract: Powderham Banks, in Devon, UK, is a critical flood defence embankment protecting agricultural land, residential areas and the Great Western Main Line railway. The earthen embankment has a long history of repairs and recurring issues such as seepage and revetment damage. title: AI Use, Environmental Awareness and Moral Disengagement Among Gen Z Business Students
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has become a defining feature of how Generation Z business students learn, work, and produce knowledge. It is also among the most resource-intensive consumer technologies ever deployed, requiring substantial water and electricity for both training and use. abstract: The Himalaya is increasingly affected by high-mountain disasters driven by the interactions among cryospheric change since 1990, slope instability, thawing of glacial deposits and rock-mass permafrost, avalanches, and river systems. title: Environmental and Socioeconomic Impacts of Disrupted Rail Freight from Asia and Europe: A Scenario Analysis
abstract: Abstract With modern, globalized value chains, disruptions to transportation systems may have large, far-reaching economic and environmental effects. In this work, we investigate a hypothetical scenario with a widespread disruption to intercontinental rail freight transport between Asia and Europe. In addition to the disruption, we examine mitigation scenarios where alternative transport routes are adopted. The environmental and socioeconomic effects of the disruption and mitigation scenarios indicate negative effects both in Asia and in Europe, with the greatest impacts occurring in Asia.

Reanalysis datasets based on coupled ocean circulation and ecosystem models are essential tools for understanding coastal environmental variability and supporting water quality management. However, the development of such datasets for highly enclosed coastal systems remains limited, particularly those incorporating subsurface biogeochemical observations, such as dissolved oxygen (DO). This study presents the Ise Bay Reanalysis (IBRA), a 12-year (2011–2022), high-resolution reanalysis dataset of hydrodynamic and biogeochemical variables for Ise Bay, Japan. title: Declining spring production in the Barents Sea ice zone under climate forcing
abstract: Under anthropogenic forcing, Barents Sea greening and increased annual production are well-documented, yet seasonal differences in production trends are less clear. Here, using satellite ocean color data, we report a 45% decline in spring (April-May) primary production in the nitrate-limited Barents Sea ice zone between 1998 and 2023, corresponding to a reduction of 90.43 mg C m−2 day−1 per decade (p < 0.05). abstract: Abstract Thin-walled structures are widely used as lightweight energy absorbers, but conventional corrugated tubes still suffer from limited deformation controllability and high peak crushing force (PCF). Inspired by the periodic joints of natural bamboo, this study proposes a bionic bamboo-joint corrugated tube (BBCT) to improve crashworthiness. abstract: Abstract In the Southern Ocean, upper ocean processes are important for water column stability, affecting air‐sea‐ice fluxes. Eddies can facilitate exchange with deeper layers, affecting heat and salt fluxes, though observations are lacking. New novel observations from an acoustically tracked profiling float, trapped within an eddy for 6 months, present the first direct vertical heat flux estimates due to eddy‐sea ice interactions. abstract: In one-way dynamical nesting, constraining the nested model only at the open boundaries may allow its interior to diverge from the large-scale state of the driving solution. A spectral nudging technique was implemented in the NEMO ocean model to relax large-scale components of temperature and salinity in the inner domain toward ocean reanalysis fields imposed at the lateral boundaries, while allowing smaller-scale dynamics to evolve freely. title: The 2025 Record Low in Arctic Sea Ice Extent: Dual Forcing from La Niña and Southern Indian Ocean Warm Anomaly
abstract: Abstract In February-March 2025, the Arctic experienced record-low sea ice extent, despite a decadal slowdown in ice loss [1,2]. Although a weak La Niña was present, its influence alone is insufficient to explain this extreme event. Here, we demonstrate that this record low on an interannual scale was driven by the synergistic effects of La Niña and concurrent South Indian Ocean warm anomaly (SIOW). abstract: The Weddell Sea influences global ocean circulation and sea level through modulating Antarctic Bottom Water formation and Antarctic Ice Sheet discharges, but the history of ice‐sheet dynamics in this region remains poorly constrained due to limited well‐dated geological records. To provide a new geochemical perspective on ice‐sheet dynamics since the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM), this study presents paired authigenic and detrital Pb isotope records from sediment core PS1599‐3 recovered from the continental slope north of the Filchner Trough. abstract: Abstract Tubular auxetic metamaterials are attractive for lightweight protection and energy absorption because their deformation can be regulated through structural design. abstract: The Great Barrier Reef (GBR) is increasingly threatened by marine heatwaves and mass coral bleaching events, with local atmospheric conditions playing a critical role in modulating sea surface temperatures and heat stress. This study examines how synoptic-to-mesoscale meteorological processes shape cloud formation, precipitation, and the ocean surface heat budget across the central GBR during the 2021/2022 austral summer. title: Marine heat waves in vulnerable coral reef regions are skillfully predictable on multi-year timescales
abstract: Marine heat waves (MHWs) increasingly threaten coral reefs, but their predictability beyond seasonal timescales remains poorly understood. Here we assess the seasonal-to-multi-year predictability of MHW frequency, cumulative intensity, and duration across 12 coral reef regions. title: Evaluation‐Constrained Projections Reveal a Potentially Navigable Arctic by the 2030s
abstract: Abstract The rapid decline in Arctic sea ice thickness (SIT) is reshaping Arctic navigation prospects. However, large uncertainties in climate model skill hinder robust projections of future navigability. Here we evaluate SIT simulated by the CMIP6 using satellite, airborne, reanalysis, and in situ data sets across freezing and melting seasons. abstract: Abstract Marine heatwaves (MHWs) in the Gulf of Mexico (GoM) have become more frequent and intense, yet the mechanisms governing basin‐scale events remain incompletely understood. EOF–k‐means clustering of event‐mean sea surface temperature anomalies (SSTA) during 1982–2024 identifies four recurrent, seasonally dependent spatial regimes: two stronger, longer cold‐season regimes and two weaker, shorter warm‐season regimes. abstract: Abstract Most coupled Earth system models do not include fully interactive ice sheets, introducing uncertainty in future projections of polar climate and global sea level. title: Expansion of the Wave Action Season Across Alaska's Marginal Seas
abstract: Abstract Rapid loss of Arctic sea ice is transforming wave dynamics across Alaska's marginal seas, expanding the period when surface waves actively develop and propagate. This study quantifies how the wave action season (WAS) has evolved in the past 45 years across northern and western Alaska using a multi‐decadal hindcast validated against satellite altimetry from the ESA Climate Change Initiative and ICESat‐2 ATL12 data sets. abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclones (TCs) induce strong oceanic responses that in turn modulate air-sea heat exchange and subsequent TC development, yet the cumulative impacts of multiple sequential TCs are insufficiently explored. This study investigates the ocean response to four sequential TCs in the northern South China Sea (SCS), emphasizing the interaction between TC forcing and pre-existing ocean thermal conditions. abstract: Abstract Future global and regional mean sea level (MSL) changes have been widely quantified, yet projections of extreme sea level (ESL) remain limited, despite their substantial environmental and socioeconomic risks to densely populated coastal regions such as the marginal seas near China. title: Mapping oil spill hazards in the coastal Mediterranean
abstract: This study presents a general framework for quantifying coastal hazard along Mediterranean national coastlines resulting from recurrent and small operational oil spills, which have been shown in recent years to have a greater cumulative impact than large accidental spills in the Mediterranean Sea. abstract: Abstract. This study presents cSINGV v1.0, a high-resolution (1.5 km) regional coupled atmosphere–ocean–wave modelling system developed for the Western Maritime Continent (WMC). abstract: To help investigate ocean acidification states in the western Seto Inland Sea, Japan, we developed and applied a numerical modelling approach to evaluate present conditions and make future projections of ocean acidification. abstract: Tomini Bay, located near the equator within the Indonesian archipelago, represents a unique marine system where mesoscale and regional-scale oceanic processes regulate regional productivity. title: Why the least nocturnal convection initiation yields the most upscale convective growth over South China

abstract: Oceanic vortex streets are a representative wake phenomenon generated by the interaction between oceanic currents and bluff bodies such as islands, reefs, and offshore wind-energy infrastructures. abstract: Species distribution modelling is a widely used approach for studying species’ environmental niches and identifying the main drivers of species distribution. These modelling frameworks have been gaining popularity owing to the growing need among conservation ecologists and nature managers to understand and anticipate the distribution shifts accompanying ongoing environmental changes. To investigate the drivers of marine groundfish community composition in the subarctic, a joint species distribution model (JSDM) was applied to fish community data from the continental shelf and slope of Iceland.

abstract: Abstract The South China Sea (SCS) is one of the most active marginal seas for tropical cyclones (TCs) worldwide and a key region for TC hazards along the coasts of southern China, Philippines and Vietnam. title: Iceberg‐Generated Waves From SWOT: Disintegration of Iceberg A‐76A in the Southern Ocean
abstract: Abstract Amid rising global temperatures, icebergs are calving more often and drifting into open waters. Their disintegration processes can trigger energetic surface gravity waves that propagate away from the iceberg remain poorly documented. This study presents an analysis of 12 iceberg‐generated wave fields associated with the disintegration of iceberg A‐76A, utilizing sea surface height anomaly data from the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission. abstract: Abstract In boreal winter, orographic blocking by the Iranian Plateau and Tibetan Plateau splits the upper-tropospheric westerly jet and gives rise to the South Asian subtropical westerly jet (SAJ) along the southern flank of the two plateaus. title: SwimmingIndividuals: A high-performance agent-based model for marine ecosystems
abstract: Abstract Mechanistic models are essential for projecting ecosystem responses to novel conditions, yet the application and biological realism of agent-based models (ABMs) has often been limited by computational constraints. This paper introduces SwimmingIndividuals , an open-source agent-based model (ABM) framework that advances our ability to simulate complex biological processes at large ecological scales. title: Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Hydrological Extremes, Waves and Storm Surges During the 2013–14 Winter Storms, UK
abstract: Abstract The 2013–14 UK winter storm series was characterised by an exceptional frequency and persistence of storm events, with impacts arising from cumulative hydro-meteorological forcing rather than the intensity of individual storms. Sustained atmospheric forcing resulted in ten fatalities, extensive flooding, coastal erosion, and damage to critical infrastructure. abstract: Abstract The Kerguelen Plateau in the Southern Indian Ocean sustains intense phytoplankton blooms through local iron enrichment. Changes in mixed‐layer depth (MLD) can therefore affect regional ecosystem functioning and air–sea carbon exchange. Using 17 years (2007–2023) of observations from animal‐borne sensors and Argo floats, we reconstruct monthly MLD from sparse in situ data using principal components analysis through conditional expectation (PACE). abstract: Abstract Climate stabilization pathways limiting global warming to 1.5-2\(\:℃\) targets require emission reductions with additional carbon dioxide removal (CDR) of ~ 2–3 PgC year − 1 . abstract: Coastal lagoons are highly vulnerable to biological invasions due to their environmental heterogeneity, hydrodynamic confinement and increasing anthropogenic disturbance. Despite the rapid expansion of the invasive Atlantic blue crab (Callinectes sapidus) across Mediterranean transitional ecosystems, the processes shaping its establishment remain poorly understood. abstract: Aerosol influences on local thunderstorms are complex and often contradictory. Within aerosol-laden city environments, these interactions are further complicated by additional thermodynamic and kinematic effects related to the urban landscape. abstract: High-altitude wind energy offers a vast and comparatively stable renewable resource, yet its development in China lacks systematic assessment that integrates generation system characteristics. abstract: Abstract The Saharan Air Layer (SAL) is a warm, dry, and stable air mass that carries millions of tons of dust annually, disrupting otherwise intense convection in the tropical North Atlantic Ocean. Because the SAL is a statically stable air mass, convective instability parameters can help identify the presence of a SAL event, though most convective indices are designed for forecasting mid‐latitude convection, and struggle when applied to more barotropic settings. abstract: Abstract Central Pacific (CP) El Niño‐Southern Oscillation (ENSO) variability has intensified since the late 1990s. abstract: Abstract Carbon dioxide removal (CDR) has been identified as a necessary complement to industrial decarbonization for climate change mitigation. abstract: Abstract Purpose Cultural ecosystem services (CES) are absent from current Life Cycle Impact Assessment (LCIA) methods. abstract: Understanding how weather and climate influence fire risk is important for many purposes, including climate adaptation planning and decision-making in sectors such as emergency management, finance, health and infrastructure (e.g. for energy and water availability). In this study, bias-corrected 20CRv2c (Twentieth Century Reanalysis ver. 2c) reanalysis data are used to investigate the climatology and long-term trends of weather conditions associated with landscape fires in Australia. title: The Enhancing Effect of Double Low‐Level Jets on Heavy Rainfall Over the Northern South China Sea in Autumn
abstract: Abstract Low‐level jets (LLJs), including boundary‐layer jets (BLJs) and synoptic‐system‐related low‐level jets (SLLJs), are key factors influencing autumn rainfall over the northern South China Sea (NSCS). title: Mitochondrial Phylogeography of the Proboscis Monkey ( Nasalis larvatus ) Reveals Riverine and Coastal Population Structure Across Eastern Borneo
abstract: ABSTRACT The proboscis monkey ( Nasalis larvatus ) is an endangered colobine endemic to Borneo, largely confined to mangrove, peat‐swamp, and riverine forest and capable of swimming across the rivers and tidal channels that structure its habitat. How this riparian specialization influences the spatial distribution of genetic diversity across the species' range in Indonesia has not been characterized. title: Decomposing Cloud Trends: A Satellite Perspective on Size–Occurrence Compensation and Cloud Overlap Biases in Low-Level Clouds
abstract: Long-term satellite observations of cloud amount provide critical constraints on climate sensitivity and are essential for reducing uncertainties in climate projections. Different cloud types exert distinct radiative effects and exhibit divergent responses to warming. Yet, their relative contributions to trends in total cloud amount remain inadequately quantified. This study analyzes 17 years (2003–2019) of MODIS observations and reveals that, although global and zonal (60°S–60°N) mean trends in total cloud amount are weak, significant local signals persist. title: Redistribution of Light Absorption by Chlorophyll Decline Delays Warming by Up to a Decade
abstract: Abstract Chlorophyll regulates solar radiation absorption in the upper ocean, influencing the ocean's mean state and climate. However, its response to climate change in Earth System Models (ESMs) remains unclear. Here, we show that in addition to well‐known effects on the carbon cycle, projected chlorophyll decline reduces the absorption of solar radiation within the ocean's mixed layer, effectively redistributing 0.1–0.87 W m −2 of globally‐averaged radiative flux to the upper thermocline underneath it. abstract: Abstract The pre-flood season (PFS; April–June) marks the onset of the rainy season over southern China (SC). Using observational and reanalysis datasets, we show that the relationship between El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and subsequent PFS precipitation over SC is nonstationary, exhibiting a pronounced strengthening since the mid-1990s. title: Spatial and temporal reorganization of Polychaeta assemblages and trophic structure across the main habitats of the Mar Menor lagoon, Spain
abstract: Coastal lagoons are heterogeneous and highly dynamic ecosystems that are particularly sensitive to anthropogenic pressures. This study analyses how polychaete assemblages in the Mar Menor lagoon (Spain) reorganized their taxonomic and trophic structure across main habitats between 1980s and 2017-2018 periods. We tested whether species composition, assemblage structure and trophic-group structure differed among habitats, and habitat-specific temporal changes. abstract: Abstract While the decadal weakening in the coupling between the Northern Hemisphere (NH) stratospheric polar vortex (SPV) and the Arctic Oscillation (AO) has been well documented, a critical gap remains in our understanding of the corresponding decadal dynamics involving the Antarctic Oscillation (AAO) in the Southern Hemisphere (SH). abstract: Abstract. This study presents a comprehensive catalog of the extreme seasonal rainfall events of northern Chile between 1979 and 2019. We analyzed its meteorological patterns across three latitudinal bands (17.5° S–23.5° S, 23.5° S–27° S, and 27° S–30° S) using daily precipitation and mean daily temperature from the CR2METv2.5 product, and vertically integrated water vapor transport (IVT) data from ERA5 reanalysis. Basin water renewal in land-locked fjords with shallow threshold sills: impacts from natural and anthropogenic change
abstract: Abstract At higher latitudes there are many land-locked fjords with shallow threshold sills or channels and deep basins inside. The renewal of water within these deep, semi-enclosed, basins is essential to maintaining water quality (e.g. dissolved oxygen levels), particularly at depth. Deep water renewal events are episodic and controlled primarily by the density difference between water masses inside and outside the fjord basin, as well as the balance between external tidal forcing across the threshold sill and freshwater runoff into the fjordic basins. title: Co-occurrence of atmospheric deserts over Europe with strong positive temperature anomalies, thunderstorms, and dust events
abstract: Abstract. Elevated mixed layers are known to influence near-surface temperatures and the formation of thunderstorms. Here we investigate the generalisation of elevated mixed layers, so called “atmospheric deserts”: air masses originating in hot, dry, deep, convective boundary layers over arid and/or elevated regions. Atmospheric deserts are frequently advected over Europe and can modify temperature profiles throughout the free troposphere, with implications for convective potential. We therefore investigate their co‑occurrence with positive temperature anomalies and thunderstorms over Europe.

abstract: Concrete-core stiffened deep cement mixing (SDCM) retaining walls provide effective lateral support, making them particularly suitable for deep excavations in coastal areas with poor geological conditions. These retaining walls can be constructed in various composite configurations; however, the retaining performance of different configurations in soft ground has not yet been systematically investigated. abstract: Abstract The diversity of anthropogenic organic substances in aquatic environments creates a need for analytical workflows that combine chemical coverage with reliable quantification, in order to assess global chemical pollution. Here, we present an integrated workflow that combines non-targeted and targeted liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) for the analysis of xenobiotics in river and coastal environments. abstract: Insulating a heritage masonry wall from the inside is often the only option when the façade must be preserved — and it is also the most likely to fail, because it traps moisture where the insulation meets the wall. Large-scale drivers of compounding hot and dry events in three breadbasket regions
abstract: Abstract. Compound hot and dry events cause damage to ecosystems and society. While these events have been widely studied individually, their co-ocurrence and the associated large-scale atmospheric drivers remain less understood. Here, we use reanalysis products and observational data to identify compound hot and dry events in the historical period from 1960 to 2020. abstract: Obtaining a reliable estimate of in-situ stress is important for planning of underground structures. Overcoring and hydraulic fracturing measurements are widely used methods to determine in-situ rock stress in underground works. These measurements are also used as supplements to develop in-situ rock stress models that are particularly useful for planning and designing unlined pressure tunnels and shafts. abstract: Landslides entering fjords or lakes can generate tsunamis that threaten communities far beyond the source area. abstract: Abstract. The North Pacific storm track shapes precipitation and temperature patterns over the Arctic and western North America, yet how its sensitivity to springtime East Asian dust remains poorly understood. title: OceanTracker 0.5: fast adaptable Lagrangian particle tracking in structured and unstructured grids
abstract: Particle tracking is frequently used to compute particle movements within hydrodynamic ocean models; however, modelling millions of particles is computationally challenging. OceanTracker is designed to minimise the time required to obtain results from particle tracking. Firstly, by being computationally fast, it enables users to scale to large numbers of particles, thus obtaining better statistics or exploring a wider range of cases within acceptable run times. title: Sustainability Pathways and Policy Efficacy in a Rapidly Urbanizing Megacity
abstract: Shanghai's industrial dynamism and rapid urbanisation have put strain on numerous aquatic habitats, extending from the Huangpu and Suzhou Creek networks to the Yangtze River delta. The purpose of this study is to present both primary and secondary research on Shanghai's water-quality issues and assess the sustainability performance of major policies influencing the city's results: the Yangtze River Protection Law (2021–), the Sponge City Program (2014–), China's Water Pollution Prevention and Control Action Plan (the "Water Ten Plan," 2015), and national water reuse/resource recovery programs.

abstract: Springtime strong winds on the east side of the Taebaek Mountains in Korea constitute a critical meteorological hazard that not only causes direct damage but also triggers serious secondary disasters such as rapid spread of wildfires, threats to aviation safety, and dispersion of atmospheric pollutants. abstract: The western North Pacific is one of the most active regions for tropical cyclone activity worldwide, and the reliability of long-term typhoon best-track data is critical for assessing storm surges and marine disasters along the Korean Peninsula. This study quantitatively analyzed the inter-agency consistency of the center position, central pressure, and maximum sustained wind speed among the KMA, JMA, and JTWC best-track datasets for 1977-2024. Victoria mode drives the strengthening of tropical Atlantic SST influence on El Niño-Southern oscillation since the mid-20th century
abstract: Abstract Spring tropical North Atlantic (TNA) sea surface temperature (SST) anomalies serve as an important precursor of El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) development in the following winter. The influence of TNA SST on ENSO has strengthened significantly since the mid-20th century, yet the underlying mechanism remains unclear. abstract: Abstract Data-driven weather prediction (DWP) offers advantages in computational efficiency and demonstrates superior synoptic-scale performance compared with numerical weather prediction. However, global DWP models typically operate at coarser resolutions and remain limited in their ability to accurately predict tropical cyclone (TC) wind structure and rainfall. abstract: Abstract This study investigates the synoptic and mesoscale atmospheric conditions of the precipitation system causing the August 2026 Chiba Heavy Rainfall Event in the Kanto Plain, Japan (13–14 August 2026). Synoptically, peripheral flow from a high-pressure system northeast of Japan advected a deep moist layer, which backward trajectories traced to tropical regions far east. title: Tectonic Forcing of Diachronous Salt Deposition During the Badenian Salinity Crisis Revealed by U–Pb Dating of Tephra Overlying Tuzla Basin Evaporites
abstract: ABSTRACT During the Middle Miocene Badenian Salinity Crisis (BSC), extensive evaporites formed across different tectonic settings in the Central Paratethys. Limited age constraints hamper evaporite correlation and identification of driving mechanisms. Here, we use U–Pb dating of zircon by LA‐ICP‐MS from tephra overlying the Tuzla Basin evaporites. title: Large-scale spatial distribution of the soft flesh-inducing fish parasite Kudoa thyrsites (Cnidaria, Myxozoa) in the NE Atlantic
abstract: The myxosporean Kudoa thyrsites is a parasite of marine fish that may cause post-mortem myoliquefaction (soft flesh) and reduce fillet quality. In the Northeast (NE) Atlantic, its distribution remains poorly known and is largely inferred from scattered records. Southern and western regions are generally regarded as established transmission areas, whereas in northern waters the parasite has mainly been reported in migratory Atlantic mackerel ( Scomber scombrus ). title: 3D Modeling of the 2010 Mentawai Tsunami Using Optimal Time Stepping
abstract: The 2010 Mentawai tsunami was a major disaster in Indonesia, triggered by a 7.7 Mw underwater tectonic earthquake southwest of Pagai Island. To enhance disaster mitigation, efficient and accurate computational analysis is essential. This study develops a three-dimensional (3D) tsunami propagation model implementing the Optimal Time Stepping (OTS) method to address the high computational costs typically associated with conventional 3D simulations. abstract: Biofouling-induced surface roughness is a critical issue affecting the hydrodynamic performance of marine propellers, leading to increased energy consumption and emissions. This study investigates the effects of varying roughness heights on the thrust, torque, and open water efficiency of a B-series B4-70 marine propeller using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). abstract: Abstract Summer 2024 observed a record‐low tropical cyclone (TC) landfall activity over China, with only two landfalls representing a 59.8% reduction from the 1979–2023 climatological mean. This study investigates the characteristics and underlying mechanisms of this extreme suppression, revealing distinct monthly variations driven by divergent genesis‐related factors. abstract: In recent decades, rapid Arctic warming has intensified Arctic amplification (AA), and its potential impacts on mid-latitude extreme weather events have received increasing attention. Using meteorological station observations and reanalysis datasets from 1979 to 2024, this study investigates the variations of regional extreme cold events (RECEs) over Northern China and their associated circulation characteristics under different Arctic amplification periods. abstract: Renewable energy assets are certified against hazard functions that classical reliability theory treats as fixed in time, yet the climate driving heat stress, humidity, wind extremes, and flooding is shifting in ways that make stationarity untenable for long‑lived infrastructure. abstract: Abstract. The convective rainfall event responsible for the flood was favored by the passage of warm, moist air masses that interacted with the Central Apennines. title: How Thunderstorms Are Changing in Mexico: Trends and Characteristics
abstract: ABSTRACT Thunderstorms are among the most hazardous and common meteorological phenomena in Mexico, yet comprehensive assessments of their long‐term trends and associated characteristics remain absent. This study investigates changes in thunderstorm days and their environments in Mexico during 1992–2024 using a multisource approach that integrates surface weather station records, proximity soundings based on reanalysis data, and gridded lightning observations. abstract: The revised IACS North Atlantic wave scatter diagram changes sea-state probabilities and the wave-period definition used in ship fatigue assessment. title: Major volcanic eruptions episodically disrupted the continuity of polar warming through aerosol forcing
abstract: Abstract The polar regions are warming rapidly, exceeding the global average due to greenhouse gas emissions from human activities. Using CMIP6 simulations, HadCRUT5 data, and MERRA-2 aerosol records, this study shows that major 20th-century volcanic eruptions, Agung (1963), El Chichón (1982), and Pinatubo (1991) temporarily offset polar warming through sulfate-induced cooling. title: Subsurface Weakness Amplification and Progressive Capacity Loss in Piled Port Structures under Repeated Operational Loading
abstract: Piled port structures experience repeated operational loading that may degrade soil–pile interaction and reduce foundation capacity over time. This study investigates subsurface weakness amplification and progressive capacity loss using three-dimensional finite element modelling of coastal soil profiles and pile systems under cyclic loading. abstract: The operation of port handling equipment that has been in long-term service under marine conditions is accompanied by intensive cyclic loading, corrosion, fatigue damage, deformation, and mechanical wear. The integration of engineering diagnostics, condition-based maintenance, structural assessment, and residual service-life evaluation provides a reliable basis for decision-making regarding repair, strengthening, modernization, controlled operation, and service-life extension. abstract: Based on the patterns identified in Part II for the variation of steel strength properties across different microstructural states, a phenomenological numerical model was developed to describe the mechanical behavior of pipeline steel after strain aging (SA). For estimating the increase in yield strength due to bake hardening (BH), it is proposed to use an empirical relationship that accounts for the concentration of carbon dissolved in alpha iron, as well as the aging temperature and time. title: Free surfaces in turbulence: A unified framework from water surfaces to elastic solids
abstract: What do the ocean surface and a swaying flag have in common? Both are deformable surfaces exhibiting chaotic motion when exposed to turbulent flows. Whether such motion is primarily driven by flow turbulence or by nonlinear dynamics intrinsic to the surface remains debated. abstract: Characterizing compound drought–heat extremes remains challenging because inferred event characteristics are sensitive to event definition and dataset representation, including climate-variable dependence. Here, we compare monthly compound dry-hot events (CDHEs) and heatwave-based compound drought–heatwave events (CDHWs) using observation-based datasets (CRU, BEST, and GPCC), ERA5 reanalysis, and the ERA5-derived bias-corrected WFDE5 dataset over global land. abstract: Abstract Western North Pacific (WNP) tropical cyclone (TC) activity is strongly modulated by the North Pacific Meridional Mode (NPMM), yet how this influence responds to global warming remains unclear. Using high-resolution atmosphere-only simulations that reproduce the observed NPMM-related environmental and TC responses, we show that global warming strengthens and reshapes the influence of the NPMM on TC genesis and tracks through an amplified tropical Pacific atmospheric response. title: Experimental wind tunnel dataset of wake and turbine measurements for wind farm control
abstract: Abstract. Open-access experimental datasets play a central role in validating and benchmarking numerical models used in wind energy and wind-farm control research. However, publicly available datasets providing time-resolved turbine loads, actuator commands, and inflow characterisation under controlled operation remain scarce. This paper presents a new open-access experimental dataset from wind-tunnel experiments featuring actuated, instrumented, scaled wind turbine models. abstract: As a key component for perception of the environment and structural response, the normal operation of sensors is crucial for the safety assessment of pipe-rack offshore platforms. title: Anthropogenic climate change intensifies rainfall in extreme compound rainfall-wave events in the NW Mediterranean
abstract: Abstract The concurrent occurrence of extreme rainfall and energetic wave conditions can generate compound coastal hazards with impacts exceeding those produced by either driver alone. Although recent studies have identified changes in rainfall-wave extremes along the northwestern Mediterranean coast, whether these changes can be attributed to anthropogenic climate remains unclear. title: Numerical investigation of ship-induced drawdown waves in confined waters
abstract: During navigation, ships generate both long-period primary waves and short-period secondary waves, which can transfer energy to canal boundaries and thereby disturb aquatic ecosystems and alter shoreline morphology. Despite increasing interest in ship hydrodynamics, existing numerical models remain ship-centred and pay limited attention to ship-induced environmental impacts. abstract: Abstract Lakes on the Tibetan Plateau are sensitive indicators of climate change and important regulators of local land–atmosphere exchanges. However, continuous in situ observations remain limited, especially for mesoscale lakes with lake areas of 100–500 km 2 . abstract: The characteristics of Madden–Julian Oscillation (MJO) propagation over multi-decadal periods in the Maritime Continent remain relatively understudied, despite the fact that variations in its duration and propagation success may significantly influence long-term convection patterns. This study analyzes MJO propagation during the period 1996–2025 and its impacts on Outgoing Longwave Radiation (OLR) anomalies, wind divergence, and moisture transport using NCEP–NCAR Reanalysis data and the Real-time Multivariate MJO (RMM) index. title: Vortex dynamics and air entrainment in dam-break wave impacting on vertical walls: A multiphase lattice Boltzmann study
abstract: Air entrainment often plays a crucial role in determining impact loads exerted by free-surface wave flows interacting with structures, yet its modeling is often oversimplified in numerical approaches. In this study, a two-phase numerical model, based on the Lattice Boltzmann Method coupled to a conservative Allen–Cahn interface-capturing equation, is employed to perform three-dimensional simulations of dam-break waves propagating over a dry bed and impacting vertical walls. abstract: ABSTRACT In this paper, open‐hole compression (OHC) tests were conducted on quasi‐isotropic (QI) laminates to compare the performance of drilled and molded holes. Concurrently, finite element analysis (FEA) models were established for both drilled and molded laminates based on the Hashin and Puck failure criteria, respectively, to characterize the stress field around the hole. abstract: The European Commission set a goal of 1GW of ocean (wave and tidal) capacity by 2030 and 40GW by 2050. The wave energy se ctor is currently at a pre-commercial development, with numerous designs that are yet to demonstrate economic viability. The LiftWEC project developed a new type of cyclorotor wave energy converter that simplifies power-take off requirements. abstract: Abstract To better identify emission sources of airborne plastics, we employed nine plastic-associated chemicals (PlsACs) in 240 daily PM2.5 samples collected in Singapore during 2018–2020. abstract: Abstract As a typical cloud type in the Arctic, the microphysical characteristics of Arctic stratiform mixed‐phase clouds (MPCs) are essential for understanding interactions among Arctic clouds, aerosols, and radiation. This study uses 1‐year of shipborne observations from the Multidisciplinary drifting Observatory for the Study of Arctic Climate (MOSAiC) expedition in the Arctic Ocean. abstract: Abstract. This study investigates the impact of Asian sulfate aerosols on regional summer extreme precipitation under both pre-industrial and pre-industrial +1 K climate states, using the reduced-complexity climate model Fast Ocean Rapid Troposphere Experiment version 2 (FORTE2) with Systematic Regional Aerosol Perturbations simulations. abstract: Driven by the strategic development of maritime infrastructure in Morocco and the expansion of port systems in the world, settlement control of quay structures founded on soft soils remains a critical geotechnical challenge affecting serviceability and long-term performance. abstract: The South Asian High (SAH) is an important component of the Asian monsoon system. Studies have indicated that meridional movement of the SAH can exert substantial influences on the weather and climate over surrounding and remote regions. This study shows that the meridional movement of the SAH can be divided into three types. The first type represents the meridional movement of the whole SAH (WBSM). abstract: Scour around pile foundations is a growing concern in marine renewable energy development. While riprap dumping remains the most widely adopted countermeasure, current practice typically applies uniform-sized stones regardless of scour pit depth. title: Calculation of range-height indicator (RHI) scan eddy dissipation rate (EDR) map based on Doppler Light Detection and Ranging (LIDAR) velocity data
abstract: An algorithm based on a structure function approach is developed to calculate the Eddy Dissipation Rate (EDR) map from range-height indicator (RHI) scans of short range Light Detection and Ranging (SRLs) at the Hong Kong International Airport (HKIA). With particular consideration on the temporal and spatial resolution of the Doppler velocity data from SRLs as compared with EDR maps from long-range Light Detection and Ranging (LIDARs) already in use at HKIA. abstract: A growing number of multistatic meteor radar networks are being established worldwide. abstract: Abstract Central Mozambique encompasses coastal, inland, and high-elevation environments, yet long-term climate trend assessments based on meteorological station data remain limited. Spatial and temporal trends in mean air temperature and total precipitation were analyzed across ten locations over the period 1994–2023. abstract: The extent of organic matter (OM) degradation in sunlit surface soils and shallow marine sediments is critical to global carbon and nitrogen cycling. abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigated the combined effects of temperature and media grain size on nitrate and colloid transport in saturated porous media using laboratory column experiments and numerical modelling. abstract: In the highly competitive home appliance market, the dispensing and crushing performance of built-in ice makers has become a critical quality attribute affecting both user satisfaction and product competitiveness. However, conventional product development processes still rely heavily on reactive trial-and-error approaches, which may lead to substantial economic losses during the later stages of mass production. abstract: Abstract Context Jack pine budworm (JPBW), Choristoneura pinus pinus, is a major defoliator in Canada, yet remains absent from theoretical discourse on outbreak synchrony, despite sharing key life history traits with the archetypal “cross-scale” pest, spruce budworm (C. fumiferana). abstract: Abstract In steelmaking, inert gas injection is widely employed during ladle refining to enhance mixing and promote chemical reactions. Argon is injected through the bottom of the ladle, inducing a turbulent recirculating flow that improves heat and mass transfer. This agitation promotes molten metal homogenization, inclusion removal via the slag layer, alloy mixing, and slag-metal reactions. abstract: Airborne plastic additives (PAs) occur as complex mixtures, yet their regional distribution and exposure relevance remain poorly characterized in school-associated outdoor air. abstract: ABSTRACT The high demand for fiber‐reinforced composite materials generates large quantities of uncured prepreg waste, still in pristine condition, usually landfilled or incinerated. abstract: ABSTRACT Lake Woods, Jurrkulu, is northern Australia's largest freshwater lake filled today in strong Indo–Australian summer monsoons (IASM) to maximum depths of ~5 m. abstract: Against the backdrop of rapid population aging and the continuous expansion of the elder care system in China, disaster risks facing elder care institutions under multiple hazards have emerged as a critical challenge for public safety and social governance. title: Temporal and climatic drivers of uncomplicated malaria in Ghana: Regional Generalised Additive and Generalised Additive Mixed Model analysis
abstract: Malaria remains a major public health challenge in Ghana despite recent reductions in cases attributable to various interventions, with disease endemicity varying across regions due to diverse seasonal and temporal factors that support mosquito proliferation. This study used Generalised Additive Models and Generalised Additive Mixed Models to explore the nonlinear effects of climatic conditions on uncomplicated malaria in Ghana. title: Integrated in vivo Anti-Inflammatory, Antioxidant-Related, and Preliminary Acute Oral Toxicity Responses to Gracilaria gracilis Extract
abstract: Inflammation and oxidative stress reinforce one another and are important targets in the development of marine-derived pharmacological candidates. This study evaluated the in vivo anti-inflammatory and antioxidant-related effects of an ethanol extract of BRIN-authenticated Gracilaria gracilis and included a separate preliminary single-dose oral toxicity assessment. Dried seaweed (300 g) was macerated with 96% ethanol in three 24-h cycles at a 1:3 (w/v) ratio, producing 24.5 g extract (8.17%, w/w). title: North American Monsoon Sensitivity to Soil Moisture in a Regional Climate Model
abstract: Abstract Past work suggests a possible connection between spring soil moisture conditions in the southwestern United States and the onset of the North American Monsoon (NAM). We test the NAM's response to both moist and dry spring soil moisture perturbations under different synoptic circulation regimes using high-resolution numerical simulations. Anomalously high soil moisture led to a robust increase in latent heat and a decrease in sensible heat fluxes, whereas anomalously low soil moisture led to a robust decrease in latent heat and an increase in sensible heat fluxes. title: Past and future projected radiative effects from irrigation
abstract: Abstract. Irrigation is the most dominant freshwater-use practice on Earth, yet its effect on the top of atmosphere (TOA) radiative budget remains highly uncertain because past estimates have relied on idealised experiments or single-model frameworks. title: Equivalent linearization modeling and experimental validation of natural frequency and vibration isolation performance in metal braided hoses
abstract: Metal braided hoses are widely used in the petroleum industry, marine engineering, aerospace, and other fields for their excellent displacement compensation and vibration damping. Stiffness properties have attracted most of the research so far, while the dynamic behavior of the hose remains comparatively understudied. This paper therefore establishes single-degree-of-freedom axial and bending dynamic models based on the Bouc-Wen hysteresis model and linearizes the nonlinear equations through energy-equivalent linearization, using the energy dissipated by the hysteresis loop. title: Impact of geomagnetic storm intensity on thermospheric density and orbital decay of LEO satellites: a G1–G5 per-event analysis
abstract: Abstract Geomagnetic storms enhance thermospheric density and increase atmospheric drag on low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites, accelerating their orbital decay, as illustrated by the loss of 38 Starlink satellites following the modest February 2022 storm. Prior multi-event analyses have characterized this response primarily through superposed epoch analyses of Challenge Minisatellite Payload (CHAMP) and Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) observations. title: Production-Stage environmental and Techno-Economic assessment of green hydrogen production in Ghana: Comparing Solar, Wind, and biomass pathways
abstract: Country-specific assessments of suitable green hydrogen pathways remain limited for resource-endowed Sub-Saharan African countries, including Ghana. The study assesses the cradle-to-gate environmental impacts and techno-economic performance of four hydrogen production pathways using solar, wind, and biomass. GIS screened sites for technical potential, while life-cycle impacts per kg H 2 followed ISO 14040/14044. title: Radiation regimes shape microbial light-harvesting strategies and network organization on glacier surfaces
abstract: Glacier cryoconite hosts metabolically active microbial communities despite exposure to solar radiation, which both provides energy and imposes stress. However, how radiation regimes are associated with microbial energy acquisition strategies and ecosystem organization remains unclear. Here, we analyzed 85 cryoconite metagenomes, including 47 from Arctic glaciers and 38 from Tibetan Plateau glaciers, representing contrasting long-term radiation environments. institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: RAFT-ports: an application for risk assessment for tsunamis in ports demonstrated at Tanjung Gerem Port, Indonesia
abstract: Abstract The development of tsunami fragility curves and vulnerability functions has expanded in recent years, including those specifically for port environments. Given the importance of ports in global trade and supply chains, there is a need for operational tools that can support the assessment of potential tsunami impacts on port structures. In this study, we contribute to bridging the gap between published tsunami fragility curves and vulnerability functions and their practical application through the development of RAFT–Ports (Risk Assessment For Tsunamis in Ports). title: Ambitious goals for global mangrove conservation and restoration
abstract: Abstract Generic global conservation targets lack the ambition required for certain habitats of critical value for biodiversity and human well-being. Developing more challenging targets for such habitats may offer a solution. Mangrove forests provide an example: any and all future loss will have negative repercussions, while many impacts could be reversed through extensive restoration. The Global Mangrove Alliance, an international grouping of 100 civil society and academic partners, has set goals to halt anthropogenic losses, accelerate restoration and greatly enhance protection by 2030. title: Seasonal Modulation of ENSO Teleconnections to Horn of Africa Rainfall
abstract: Abstract Rainfall over the Horn of Africa (HoA) exhibits pronounced interannual variability linked to the El Niño‐Southern Oscillation (ENSO). However, the seasonal evolution of ENSO‐driven rainfall anomalies is not adequately explained by the ENSO, particularly the Niño3.4 index. The results here show that nonlinear interactions between ENSO and both semiannual and annual migration of the Intertropical Convergence Zone generate a combination mode (C‐Mode) that modulates the timing and amplitude of the HoA regional rainfall. title: Corrosion Hotspots Strongly Localize Crack Origins But Provide Conditional Timing Information
abstract: ABSTRACT Published specimen‐level data from 36 pre‐corroded structural‐steel fatigue specimens relevant to offshore applications were re‐analyzed to separate crack‐origin localization from crack‐initiation timing. Localization was available for 34 specimens and digital‐image‐correlation‐based timing for 21. Crack origins coincided with the global finite‐element hotspot in 20/34 specimens (58.8%) and with a global or near‐global hotspot in 31/34 (91.2%). journal: Fatigue & Fracture of Engineering Materials & Structures

title: Grid Shells Shaped on the Basis of Natural Forms
abstract: Curvilinear steel bar structures are increasingly applied in the design of various roof coverings. The primary aim of this study was to develop highly efficient steel grid shells inspired by the principles of nature - based solutions and biomimicry. The methodological framework integrated form - finding via 3D scanning, parametric grid generation, and structural optimization. Spatial geometries were created by capturing high - resolution mesh data from natural marine shells using a high - precision optical 3D scanner. title: Enhancement Pathways for Urban Water Ecological Resilience
abstract: Enhancing urban water ecological resilience (UWER) is increasingly essential as climate change, rapid urbanization, and ecological degradation intensify pressures on urban aquatic systems. However, knowledge of the mechanisms required to systematically enhance UWER remains fragmented across the ecological, technological, and governance domains. This narrative review synthesizes the current understanding of UWER by examining its conceptual foundations, key drivers, mechanisms, and enhancement pathways.
