title: Global warming and the Pacific Decadal Oscillation drive seasonally varying increases in extreme fire weather over the southwestern US
abstract: Abstract Wildfire activity has increased across the western United States (US), with evidence linking these trends to anthropogenic climate forcing. Here, we analyze the frequency, intensity, and drivers of fire weather extremes in the southwestern US over the past 83 years. These extremes exhibit strong seasonality: wintertime changes align with long-term warming trends, while summertime variations are dominated by decadal fluctuations modulated by the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO). title: 40 °C heat extremes are no longer implausible in the Nordic countries
abstract: Abstract The Nordic countries of Norway, Sweden, and Finland have traditionally been characterised by less intense heatwaves than continental Europe. However, during recent events, such as the 2026 heatwave, exceptionally high temperatures have been observed across large parts of Europe, with temperatures of 40 °C reaching further north than previously observed. Such temperatures would pose substantial risks in the Nordics, as people and infrastructure are generally less adapted to extreme heat than in warmer climates. title: Greenhouse gas forcing dominates the recent strengthening of North Pacific Meridional mode influence on ENSO
abstract: Abstract The North Pacific Meridional Mode (NPMM) is a key extratropical trigger of El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) events, and its influence on ENSO has increased markedly in recent decades, offering a pathway to improve ENSO predictability. Yet, the relative contributions of external forcings versus internal variability to this intensified influence remain uncertain. title: Persistent influx of atmospheric microplastics and nanoplastics to Mount Everest driven by large scale circulation
abstract: The Third Pole receives long-range transported pollutants, yet atmospheric micro- and nanoplastics inputs remain poorly constrained. Here we report year-long monitoring on the northern slope of Mount Everest using dry, wet, and total deposition sampling. Microplastic deposition fluxes at Qomolangma Station (64.0 n m−2 d−1) significantly exceed those at Everest Base Camp (23.0 n m−2 d−1), reflecting topographic and anthropogenic differences. title: Development and application of dynamically similar model materials for blasting in reef limestone
abstract: To address the difficulty of sampling reef limestone and poor dynamic replication by conventional similar materials, this study introduces wave impedance as a key dynamic index for designing similar materials for reef limestone blasting. An orthogonal experiment examined five parameters: barite powder content, aggregate-to-binder ratio, cement-to-gypsum ratio, foaming agent dosage, and fiber content, using range and linear regression analyses. journal: Journal of Ocean Engineering and Science

title: Fabrication, Transportation, and Installation of Fixed and Floating Offshore Wind Turbines: A State of the Art Review
abstract: The rapid growth of offshore wind energy has increased the size and complexity of Offshore Wind Turbines (OWTs), making fabrication, transportation, and installation critical to project cost and schedule. However, previous studies have mostly examined these phases separately. This study presents a PRISMA-based Systematic Literature Review (SLR) of 49 peer-reviewed studies to identify key trends, challenges, and optimization opportunities in OWT construction. abstract: Abstract The Historical Experiment (HE) assesses CMIP6 climate models against the known climate (1850–2014) where carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), the global temperature and aerosols have followed similar, low frequency, rising trajectories and models are required to use “forcings based as far as possible on observations.” To assess the effect of three equatorial, continental scale aerosol plumes over South East Asia (SEAP), Amazonia and West Africa on global and Nino 3.4 temperatures I filtered 23 CMIP6 data sets with a High‐Pass Filter (HPF) and find that the SEAP causes: reduced surface radiation (4

title: Biases and predictability limits of Northern Hemisphere extratropical cyclones in subseasonal prediction systems
abstract: Abstract Subseasonal prediction of Northern Hemisphere extratropical cyclones (ETCs) is critical for anticipating associated weather extremes, yet biases and predictability limits of ETC activity in current forecast systems remain insufficiently quantified. Here, using hindcasts from ten state-of-the-art subseasonal-to-seasonal (S2S) prediction systems within a Lagrangian tracking framework, we uncover a common and pervasive bias: the multi-model ensemble consistently predicts fewer and weaker cyclones at a one-month lead, underestimating frequency by 10-18% and intensity by approximately 13%,

title: Participación, comunicación y gobernanza del litoral valenciano: lecciones de dos procesos deliberativos
abstract: Esta investigación tiene como objetivo analizar las barreras, oportunidades y prioridades para avanzar hacia una gobernanza costera integrada y adaptativa en la Comunidad Valenciana, un territorio con elevada fragmentación institucional, presiones urbanísticas y vulnerabilidad climática. Se emplea un enfoque cualitativo, exploratorio y preliminar, basado en el análisis de las dinámicas deliberativas de dos procesos participativos celebrados en 2024 y 2025: la creación de una red de gobernanza litoral y el primer taller del proyecto europeo Horizon-BlueGreen Governance. title: Climate change effects on analogues of contrasting extratropical cyclones over the UK, Ireland and France
abstract: Abstract. Extreme extratropical cyclones present major socio-economic risks in the United Kingdom and are sensitive to anthropogenic climate change. Robust projections of the aggregate properties of extreme cyclones based on climate-model output have emerged in recent years. However, such projections average together cyclones with a range of contrasting dynamical characteristics potentially obscuring climate change effects on particular types of cyclones and the airstream structures within them. title: The impact of atmospheric rivers on the water level and hydrology in a lake in south-Central Chile
abstract: Atmospheric rivers (ARs) are major drivers of hydroclimatic extremes in mid-latitude regions, with important implications for water resource management and climate services. This study evaluates the hydroclimatic and hydrological response of Lake Villarrica in south-central Chile to AR landfalls during 2000–2024. ARs were identified using an ERA5-based catalog and classified as Zonal (ZARs) or Tilted Atmospheric Rivers (TARs) according to integrated vapor transport direction. title: Science and policy to manage nitrogen with cover crops—The Maryland experience
abstract: During the 1980s, research showed nitrogen-stimulated eutrophication was contributing to the Chesapeake Bay's deterioration, and cover crop research shifted from legumes to replace fertilizer, to winter cereals to reduce nitrogen (N) leaching. The Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) adopted nutrient regulations and added technical and financial resources promoting N-capturing cover crops and N-use efficiency. title: Attributing compound flood impact from tropical cyclone Idai in Mozambique to climate and population change
abstract: Abstract Impacts of extreme weather events are a complex interplay of compounding climatic and socio-economic drivers. In this paper, we attribute the effect of climate and population change on the number of people exposed to flooding from tropical cyclone (TC) Idai, making landfall in Mozambique in 2019. We apply an extended storyline attribution framework based on a globally-applicable model chain to simulate compound flooding and exposed population as a proxy for impact under factual and counterfactual climate and population conditions. title: Forcing dataset updates impact regional but not global Earth radiation budget trends in the GFDL AM4 climate model
abstract: The availability of up-to-date forcing datasets is critical for reconciling Earth system model simulations with contemporary observations. With the newly released CMIP7 forcing dataset, which extends the historical record through 2021, this study provides a systematic evaluation of how using updated forcings over the "middle-of-the-road" SSP2-4.5 scenario forcings influences the simulated radiation budget in the GFDL AM4 climate model. title: Melanosome evolution shaped sensory biology and terrestrial adaptations in early aquatic vertebrates
abstract: The photic environment is a key driver of fish ecology that shapes adaptations to aquatic habitats. The evolutionary history of these adaptations, however, is difficult to trace. Melanosomes, melanin-rich organelles, offer unique insights into physiology and ecology and often fossilise. Here, we present a comparative analysis of melanosomes from extant and fossil fishes to trace the evolution of ecological and physiological adaptations through deep time. title: A coupled Terzaghi – Biot model for blast-induced liquefaction
abstract: We investigate the impact of short-wave impulses on soil liquefaction and fluid pressure dynamics. Using a Biot poroelastic model with an elasto - plastic representation of the sand matrix, numerical simulations are conducted to evaluate soil displacement, pore pressure, and wave velocities. Comparisons between coupled (Biot) and decoupled (Terzaghi) models reveal critical differences in displacement and pore pressure predictions. title: Hydrokinetic energy recovery using a controllable-pitch propeller on a kite-assisted ship: Propeller performance mapping and a notional route case study
abstract: To enhance the efficiency of wind-assisted ships, the propeller may operate as a turbine. Because harvesting efficiency is strongly dependent on blade pitch, this study maps the propulsive and generative performance of a controllable pitch propeller (CPP) by simulating the Potsdam Propeller Test Case (PPTC) across a wide range of blade and advance angles. The power coefficient ( C P ) reaches 0.22 at design pitch, but achieves a global maximum of 0.44 at a 215° reversed pitch. title: Long-term climate variability and implications for groundwater recharge potential and saltwater intrusion vulnerability in the Cape Flats Aquifer, South Africa
abstract: The Cape Flats Aquifer (CFA) is a critical groundwater resource supporting urban, agricultural, and ecological needs in the Western Cape, South Africa. However, its sustainability is increasingly threatened by seasonal climate variability, which strongly influences groundwater recharge. This study examined seasonal rainfall and temperature variability and their potential implications for groundwater recharge and susceptibility to saltwater intrusion in the CFA. title: Nonlinear oscillatory flow regimes with mixing in a two-layer fluid under a rigid lid
abstract: Abstract We propose a nonlinear long-wave model describing the propagation of internal waves and turbulent mixing in a two-layer fluid under a rigid lid in the Boussinesq approximation. This model allows for the inclusion of non-hydrostatic effects in the lower layer, density non-uniformity and flow vorticity in the upper layer, as well as mixing at the interface. title: Convection‐Permitting Simulations of Extreme Hourly Rainfall and Land‐Surface Impacts in the Middle‐Lower Yangtze River Basin
abstract: Abstract Extreme precipitation events frequently cause severe socioeconomic losses, making accurate forecasting critical. However, prediction of extreme precipitation remains challenging due to multi‐scale nonlinear interactions. Previous studies have largely attributed extreme rainfall to large‐scale circulation or mesoscale convective systems, the role of complex underlying surfaces remains insufficiently understood. title: Selective Waiting-Time Reduction in Indonesian Fiberglass Shipbuilding: A Digital Lean Simulation Framework
abstract: Background: Uniform waiting-time reduction in fiberglass shipbuilding may compromise essential technical processes, including curing, inspection, and safety checks. Therefore, waiting time must be classified according to its technical function and potential for reduction. Objective: This study develops a simulation-based Digital Lean Manufacturing framework for selectively reducing waiting time in Indonesian engineer-to-order fiberglass shipbuilding. title: An Investigation of the Characteristics of Indian Summer Monsoon Low‐Pressure Systems Under Stratospheric Aerosol Geoengineering
abstract: Abstract Monsoon Low‐Pressure Systems (LPSs) that govern the rainfall of the Indian Summer Monsoon (ISM) contribute more than half of its rainfall and extreme rainfall events. In this study, we explore how LPS activity changes under greenhouse warming and Stratospheric Aerosol Intervention (SAI) using simulations from the fully coupled CESM2.1.3 climate model. title: Novel Filament‐Wound FRP Composite Tubes Integrated Grid Ribs and Multi‐Angle Winding Layer: Manufacturing, Interfacial Behavior and Proof‐of‐Concept Validation
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial slip between concrete and fiber‐reinforced polymer (FRP) tubes remains a key concern in concrete‐filled FRP tube members. This study proposes a novel concrete‐filled FRP tube integrated with designable grid ribs and multi‐angle winding layers (GR‐CFFT). The internal grid ribs are intended to enhance rib–concrete mechanical interlocking, reduce interfacial slip, and improve the contribution of longitudinal reinforcement layers to flexural resistance. title: Can advanced sand-based models predict the behaviour of silty sands? A comprehensive experimental and numerical assessment
abstract: This article presents a comprehensive experimental and numerical investigation into the monotonic and cyclic behaviour of five natural silty sands. Based on an extensive laboratory programme comprising drained and undrained monotonic triaxial tests, as well as undrained cyclic triaxial tests, four advanced constitutive models originally developed for clean sands, Hypoplasticity with Intergranular Strain (Hypo+IGS), Sanisand, Hypoplasticity with Intergranular Strain and semifluidized state and fabric change effects (Hypo+ISA-SF), and Sanisand with memory surface and semifluidized state (Sanisan

title: Quiet Time Ionosphere‐Thermosphere Predictability During Sudden Stratospheric Warmings in TIE‐GCM
abstract: Abstract We investigate the predictability of the ionosphere‐thermosphere (IT) region during sudden stratospheric warmings (SSWs) by using subseasonal hindcasts in the Community Earth System Model, version 2 with the Whole Atmosphere Community Climate Model (CESM2 [WACCM6]) to force the lower boundary of the TIE‐GCM. The extension of subseasonal hindcasts into the IT region enables the first comprehensive investigation of IT predictability during SSWs. title: A hybrid statistical–dynamical approach for seasonal prediction of the boreal winter stratosphere
abstract: Abstract The winter variability of the Northern Hemisphere Stratospheric Polar Vortex (SPV) is characterized by extreme events known as Sudden Stratospheric Warmings (SSWs). SSWs feature a rapid temperature increase and a reversal of the zonal winds in the SPV, exerting a downward impact on the troposphere. Yet, despite their importance, current seasonal prediction systems (SPSs) show limited skill in forecasting SPV variability and SSW occurrence. title: Numerical investigation of partially submerged H-type porous barrier in front of a seawall
abstract: This study examines the hydrodynamic response of an H-type porous breakwater positioned at a specified distance from a partially reflecting seawall using linear wave theory. The boundary value problem is solved using the dual boundary element method (DBEM) to acquire numerical results for various values of barrier porosity, relative submergence depth, wave steepness, and seawall porosity. title: Global Rossby wave rivers connecting remote wave activity to the East Asian summer monsoon
abstract: We introduce a sink-oriented Rossby wave river (WR) framework that traces remote wave activity along continuous propagation pathways converging toward specific sinks, and use the Li-Yang wave ray flux to diagnose the global WRs converging into the East Asian summer monsoon (EASM) region. At 850 hPa, Southern Hemisphere and pan-tropical pathways dominate and converge near the Philippines; at 500 hPa, low-latitude easterly and midlatitude westerly WRs become comparable in strength; at 200 hPa, WR propagation becomes concentrated along the jet waveguide. title: Impacts of Convective Microphysics Parameterization on MJO Simulation in E3SM
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the impact of convective microphysics parameterization on the simulation of the Madden–Julian Oscillation (MJO) in the Energy Exascale Earth System Model (E3SM). Specifically, the two‐moment, five‐class convective microphysics parameterization (CMP) scheme from Song et al. title: Evolution of the Fiastrone Gorge from Jurassic Rifting to Apennine Orogeny. Insights from new detailed geological mapping
abstract: A new 1:10,000-scale geological mapping of the Fiastrone Gorge (Northern Apennines), provides a revised interpretation of its Jurassic palaeogeographic and tectonic evolution. The Meso-Cenozoic evolution of the Umbria–Marche succession, exposed in the area, was controlled by the complex palaeogeography inherited from Early Jurassic rifting of the Western Tethys. title: Climate change induced hydrological regime shifts in the transboundary Zarafshon River Basin in Central Asia
abstract: Mountain river basins in Central Asia are highly sensitive to climate-driven changes in snow and glacier melt, yet the magnitude and timing of the resulting hydrological regime shifts remain poorly quantified. To address this gap, we assess present and future hydrological shifts in the transboundary Zarafshon River Basin with the SPHY glacio-hydrological model. We improved the representation of snowmelt and snow infiltration, which redistributes water to delayed baseflow and improves winter and spring discharge. title: From Fish-Landing Inventories to Microplastic Monitoring: Development of a Proposed Surveillance Protocol for Pasacao, Philippines
abstract: Background: Fish-landing inventories may provide an entry point for local microplastic monitoring, but their suitability depends on traceable sampling and analytical quality assurance. Objective: To assess the documentation readiness of a Pasacao, Camarines Sur fish-landing study and specify a prospective microplastic surveillance protocol. title: Relative dispersion and eddy diffusivity in laboratory experiments of β-plane turbulence
abstract: We present the first experimental measures of relative dispersion and turbulent diffusion in rapidly rotating turbulence in the zonostrophic regime, i.e. in the presence of instantaneous and dominant zonal jets. Synthetic Lagrangian trajectories are computed from time-resolved experimental velocity fields, from which we measure relative (two-particle) dispersion. title: How Does Terrain Relief of the Tibetan Plateau and the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau Individually Modulate Summer Regional Hourly Extreme Precipitation in the Sichuan Basin, China?
abstract: Abstract The influence of terrain relief over the Tibetan Plateau (TP) and the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau on summer regional hourly extreme precipitation (RHEP) in the Sichuan Basin (SCB) under two dominant synoptic patterns remains poorly understood. Here, this study uses multi‐case Weather Research and Forecasting sensitivity experiments, in which the terrain relief of two plateaus is individually smoothed, to systematically investigate these modulation mechanisms. title: A synoptic overview of the EUREC 4 A field campaign
abstract: Abstract We present an overview of the important synoptic features that occurred during the EUREC 4 A field campaign. These results are based on workshops bringing together forecasters and researchers to look in detail at cloud patterns in the region of interest (Barbados and the upstream trade winds) and how they were influenced by synoptic features. Consistent with previous studies, we found that the influence of, or lack of, midlatitude and subtropical features was important for cloud patterns. title: Hydrogel‐Based Method for High‐Resolution Measurements of Contact Mechanics in Rapid Biological Adhesives: A Case Study in Cuttlefish Tentacle Strikes
abstract: ABSTRACT Cuttlefish and squid attach to various substrates in their environment remarkably well using arms and extensible tentacles lined with arrays of suckers. Each sucker has a stiff internal ring with terminal teeth and microstructured rim. Previous studies have measured attachment forces of amputated suckers; however, in vivo investigations are lacking given the short time scales of attachment (milliseconds) and complex array geometries. title: Tropospheric Ozone Assessment Report II: Stratosphere–troposphere exchange of ozone
abstract: Stratosphere-troposphere exchange (STE) of ozone is a significant source of tropospheric ozone, influencing air quality, atmospheric chemistry and climate forcing. This assessment synthesizes recent advances in understanding the magnitude, mechanisms, variability and future evolution of ozone transport across the tropopause, updating earlier reviews using observations, reanalyses and global chemistry-climate models. title: Secondary ice production affects tropical convective clouds under different aerosol conditions
abstract: Abstract. Secondary ice production (SIP) modulates tropical convection, but its interactions with aerosol loading remain uncertain. Using the UK Met Office Unified Model with detailed SIP parameterizations, this study investigates how multiple SIP mechanisms affect a Hector storm under weak instability and varying cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) concentrations. At moderate aerosol loading (Nd = 400 cm–3), SIP substantially enhances the ice phase. title: A physics-based two-dimensional reduced order model for hydro-elastoplastic response of panel under bow flare slamming impact: Validation and application
abstract: While high-fidelity methods, such as Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD)- Finite Element Analysis (FEA) coupling, can accurately capture structural collapse under severe slamming when the modeling and analysis conditions are appropriately specified, their high computational cost makes them impractical for repeated use in early-stage design or risk screening. In this paper, a physics-based two-dimensional reduced-order model (ROM) is proposed and developed to efficiently estimate the dynamic elastic-plastic response of plate panels between stiffeners subjected to slamming loads. title: A new method for detecting aerosols: combining atmospheric detection LiDAR technology with intelligent driving technology
abstract: Abstract. The existing aerosol mobile detection system has problems such as over-reliance on labor power and difficulty in conducting continuous operations in toxic and polluted environments. This paper presents a new method for detecting aerosols. The method combines atmospheric detection LiDAR technology and intelligent driving technology. Through modular design (including control module, aerosol detection module, environment sensing and positioning module, and wire control chassis module), an intelligent cruise detection system for aerosols was built. For path planning, Gaussian pseudo-spec

title: Climate risk assessment in tropical wetlands through integrated hydroclimatic, land cover, and community knowledge
abstract: Abstract Climate-risk assessments in tropical wetlands increasingly combine hydroclimatic and land-cover data, but rarely integrate them with structured community evidence on experienced impacts and adaptation priorities. We address this gap in six communities around the Complejo Cenagoso de Zapatosa, a Ramsar site, and the Morales wetland in the Colombian Caribbean. We integrated hydroclimatic records and climate-extreme indices (1991-2020), land-cover change and runoff-potential analysis (1991-2020), flood-susceptibility modelling, and structured participatory evidence from 106 participants.

title: Black carbon aerosols intensified India’s 2015 mega heatwave and expanded heat stress exposure
abstract: Abstract Large-scale climatic drivers are known to amplify heatwave temperatures, whereas aerosols have complex regional temperature responses depending upon aerosol composition. With the help of recent observations and chemistry-coupled regional climate model simulations, we show that coincident aerosols—black carbon in particular—elevated the heatwave intensity of India’s deadly 2015 heatwave event. title: How Can Local Knowledge and Infrastructure Engineering be Bridged for Tsunami Resilience? A Systematic Scoping Review of Socio-Technical Mitigation Framework
abstract: Tsunami resilience research has advanced significantly in both indigenous knowledge and engineering-based mitigation. However, these domains are often treated in isolation, which limits the development of integrated socio-technical catastrophe risk reduction solutions. This review examines how recent literature conceptualizes the relationship between local knowledge and tsunami mitigation engineering and operational planning, identifies mitigation functions that bridge these domains, and highlights existing knowledge gaps in socio-technical tsunami resilience. journal: Bulletin of Social Studies and Community Development

title: The Standardized Soil Moisture-Temperature Compound Index (SSTCI): daily scale global data set and event catalogue for compound dry-hot extremes (1961–2023)
abstract: Abstract. Compound dry–hot extremes (CDHEs) are among the most damaging climate hazards. Most metrics used to diagnose them are estimated at monthly or seasonal resolution or rely on precipitation-based drought proxies that can miss fast soil moisture-driven land–atmosphere feedbacks. This paper delivers two tightly linked products for global CDHE monitoring over land (excluding Antarctica) at 0.1° resolution for 1961–2023: (i) a continuous, daily severity index, i.e. the Standardized Soil Moisture–Temperature Compound Index (SSTCI), and (ii) a companion, event-based CDHE catalogue derived fro
institutions: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology

title: The Eco‐Digital Dimension in Children's and Young Adult Literature for Early Childhood and Primary Teacher Education: An Exploratory Inquiry
abstract: ABSTRACT Although ecological topics are gaining increasing relevance in children's and young adult literature, the intersection between environmental sustainability and digital media remains under‐researched. The two main research questions of this qualitative exploratory study are: how the eco‐digital dimension manifests within contemporary children's and young adult literature formats (RQ1), and how an eco‐digital webbook format can be integrated into initial teacher education for kindergarten and primary school (RQ2). The theoretical framework combines eco‐digital pedagogy and utopia as a m

title: Wave Energy Conversion Systems Dynamic Performance Enhancement Using Pied Kingfisher Optimization–Based Control Approach
abstract: This paper presents a model of a wave energy conversion system (WECS) consisting of an oscillating water column (OWC) and a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) connected to a grid. It introduces a control strategy for a generator-side converter (GSC), the purpose of which is to optimize the PMSG’s active power generation and reduce PMSG losses. This is achieved by adjusting the stator direct and quadrature (dq) axis current components. title: Effects of microphysics and gray-zone convection on MCS organization: A case study of unprecedented extreme rainfall in South Korea
abstract: Mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) embedded in quasi-stationary fronts are major drivers of extreme precipitation over South Korea, yet simulating their organization and rainfall structure remains challenging. This study investigates how cloud microphysics and gray-zone convective parameterization modulate MCS and non-MCS precipitation and the phase and amplitude of precipitation in extreme event that recently occurred in South Korea. title: Urbanization Enhances Inner‐Core Rainfall During Tropical Cyclone Landfall
abstract: Abstract How urbanization modulates precipitation in landfalling tropical cyclones (LTCs) remains poorly understood. Previous studies disagree on whether the mechanism is primarily dynamical or thermodynamic, particularly within the inner core under intense wind–rain conditions. Using high‐resolution simulations and storm‐relative framework, we quantified the effects of urban land‐cover change (ULCC) and anthropogenic heat (AH) on peak inner‐core precipitation during Typhoon Bebinca's 2024 landfall in Shanghai. title: Experimental and numerical study of a scaled Airfish 8 wing-in-ground vehicle
abstract: This paper investigates the influence of a stationary ground plane on the performance of a scaled-down Airfish 8 wing-in-ground vehicle at Reynolds numbers Re of 200 000, 250 000, and 300 000 in cruise. Experimental results show that reducing the spacing between the vehicle and the stationary ground plane leads to a substantial lift augmentation of up to ∼50% at the smallest spacing h investigated: h/c̄=0.25, where c̄ is the mean aerodynamic chord. title: Conservation of migratory species at risk: environmental conditions experienced from pre‐gestation to parturition affect fall recruitment in migratory caribou
abstract: Annual variations in environmental conditions can strongly affect vital rates such as survival and recruitment. These effects are likely to be exacerbated in highly seasonal environments and in species facing substantial energetic needs during specific seasons. For instance, pregnant migratory females must balance energy expenditure between long-distance travel and gestation. Little is known, however, on the environmental factors influencing recruitment in species exhibiting long-distance migrations. title: More than meets the eye: artificial eyelashes as an unrecognized source of microplastics and heavy metals
abstract: Despite growing concern over microplastic pollution, leave-on cosmetic products such as artificial eyelashes remain largely unexplored as sources of microplastics and associated contaminants. Here, nine artificial eyelash products were characterized for polymer composition, heavy metal content, and fiber release under simulated environmental conditions. Three polymers were identified: PBT (55.56%), PET (33.33%), and PVC (11.11%). Metal profiles varied widely across samples, with several metals of toxicological concern (Al, Ba, Co, Cr, Cu, Pb, Sb, Zn) detected but not declared on product labels

title: Methodological Approaches to Analyzing the Economic Impacts of Geoclimatic Risks in Russia
abstract: Global geoclimatic shifts pose substantial risks to the Russian economy, including infrastructure degradation, declining agricultural productivity, and structural challenges associated with the energy transition. The study is motivated by the need to critically evaluate existing climate-economic modeling approaches and assess their applicability to Russian conditions. The objective is to propose an ensemble framework capable of addressing structural uncertainty in climate-economic projections. Method . title: Influence of groundwater seasonality on suspended sediment dynamics, in a 20 km 2 Mediterranean mountainous catchment
abstract: Abstract. This study investigates the interplay between groundwater and surface runoff in controlling suspended sediment dynamics within the Galabre catchment, a 20 km² Mediterranean mountainous catchment characterized by extensive badland areas. Using an End-Member Mixing Analyzing framework that accounts for event-specific variability in end-member chemistry, the study quantifies surface runoff and groundwater contributions during 86 flood events spanning three hydrological years. title: Creating forecasts of cattle heat stress for Australia: challenges and prototypes
abstract: In Australia, a heatwave is defined as a run of unusually high daytime and night-time temperatures persisting for three or more days and is routinely forecast by the Bureau of Meteorology through its heatwave service, primarily to support human health and community safety. No equivalent spatial heat stress forecasts currently exist for Australian cattle or other grazing livestock, creating an important information gap. title: Heat extremes threaten cattle and outdoor workers across northern Australia’s extensive grazing systems
abstract: Australia is projected to warm throughout the 21st century, raising the risk of dangerous heat for livestock and the people who work with them, yet these changes have not been quantified for the extensive grazing systems of northern Australia. Here we employ a seven-model ensemble of regionally downscaled climate projections to quantify future changes in cattle heat load and the maximum safe metabolic rate for outdoor work under lower- and higher-emission pathways (Shared Socioeconomic Pathway (SSP) 1-2.6 and SSP3-7.0) at mid- and late-century. title: Project Management Maturity Profiles in Turkish Shipyards: A P3M3® Assessment
abstract: Shipbuilding is a complex project-based production environment in which maturity scores averaged across shipyards can obscure important organizational differences.This study assesses project management maturity in 32 Turkish shipyards using the Portfolio, Programme and Project Management Maturity Model (P3M3 ® ) version 2.1 Self-Assessment Tool and examines whether an aggregate result conceals distinct maturity configurations.One manager from each participating shipyard completed a Turkish questionnaire distributed through the Turkish Shipbuilders' Association (GİSBİR).The analysis covered 24

title: PROTEÇÃO HIDROLÓGICA EM UNIDADES DE CONSERVAÇÃO E TERRAS INDÍGENAS NO PARÁ: UMA REVISÃO SISTEMÁTICA
abstract: Os sistemas de água doce na Amazônia brasileira oriental estão cada vez mais vulneráveis à expansão do uso da terra, à mineração, à intensificação agrícola e ao enfraquecimento da governança ambiental. Este estudo sintetiza evidências revisadas por pares publicadas entre 2020 e 2025 para avaliar a eficácia hidrológica das Unidades de Conservação e Terras Indígenas na proteção dos recursos hídricos no estado do Pará. title: A Lower Bound on the Altitude of the Hiroshima Firestorm Plume From Ray Optics
abstract: Abstract Projections of nuclear winter are critically sensitive to the height of soot lofted by firestorms, yet direct observations of firestorm plumes are scarce. Here, a lower bound is established for the height of the Hiroshima firestorm plume 97 min after detonation. This bound is obtained via a ray‐optics calculation using the Enola Gay 's flight log, which gives the location and time when the plume was last visible. title: Uncertainty-aware overturning stability and operating boundaries of a compact transport vehicle-mounted crane boom
abstract: A compact transport vehicle with a crane boom is assessed using signed moments about support edges. The framework links seven specified configurations to operating boundaries and conditional uncertainty propagation; it introduces no new overturning criterion. A parameter audit separates mechanism-design coefficients from whole-machine screening assumptions, uses a common gravity and inertia centre for each travel state, and corrects the loaded-turn moment. title: Effect of sub-critical fluid shear flow on granular bed strength
abstract: Interactions between fluids and granular materials are prevalent on the Earth's surface. In the case of fluid flow over a sediment bed, the fluid imparts a shear stress to the granular materials. When the applied shear stress is above a critical value, the grains become entrained in the fluid flow. Prior experimental studies have shown that granular beds subjected to a sub-critical fluid flow can strengthen in the same direction as the sub-critical flow. title: Corrosion lifetime prediction of electro-galvanized iron using potentiodynamic polarization and multiphysics simulation under different process and environmental conditions
abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, a process- and environment-dependent corrosion lifetime prediction model was developed for electro-galvanized iron (EGI). EGI specimens with different crystallite sizes were fabricated by controlling the plating current density. The differences in crystallite size were evaluated using X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis. title: Carbonation of silicate minerals contributes to atmospheric CO2 drawdown in glacier-fed streams
abstract: Abstract Glacierized landscapes produce abundant fine-grained reactive minerals that play a pivotal role in high-altitude inorganic carbon cycling, mainly through geochemical weathering. However, our understanding of the relationship between glacially comminuted mineral dissolution, precipitation of secondary phases and inorganic carbon cycling in the world’s glacier-fed streams (GFSs) remains elusive. title: Experimental investigation of a multi-buoy cooperative point-absorber wave energy
abstract: We present a proof-of-concept experimental investigation of a multi-buoy cooperative point-absorber wave energy converter array with a shared closed-loop hydraulic power take-off system, where energy is extracted through the collective motion of the buoy array. Pressurised flow generated by individual buoys drives a turbine within the hydraulic circuit. A downscaled model was tested in the wave tank at the University of Oslo. title: Magma fragmentation processes during a large-scale explosive phreatomagmatic eruption constrained from volatile contents of volcanic glass
abstract: Phreatomagmatic eruptions are one of the most common and hazardous eruption styles on Earth. To understand the explosive phreatomagmatic eruptions, it is essential to constrain the mechanisms of magma–water interaction and the environments in which they occur. title: A representative subarray method for radiation hydrodynamic modelling of large floating arrays with modularized configuration
abstract: Radiation hydrodynamic modelling of large floating arrays requires constructing immense influence coefficient matrices, with computational costs increasing rapidly with array size. Because these arrays typically feature modularized configurations, the surrounding-module arrangements of different modules exhibit repeated spatial patterns. title: Microclimate persistence in island montane cloud forests
abstract: Abstract Montane cloud forests (MCFs), ecosystems critically dependent on persistent cloud immersion and high moisture availability, have been presumed vulnerable to regional warming and atmospheric drying. Yet their microclimatic resilience under regional climate variability remains poorly understood. Here we show that MCFs maintain remarkably stable near-surface relative humidity (RH), despite sustained regional warming, using a 42-year (1980–2021) high-resolution (2-km, hourly) climate dataset from Taiwan. title: Global sampling characteristics and coverage complementarity of 12 GNSS radio occultation constellations

This study uses observations from COSMIC-2, FY-3, GRACE-C/D, KOMPSAT-5, MetOp-A/C, PAZ, PlanetiQ, Sentinel-6A, Spire, TerraSAR-X/TanDEM-X, TM-1, and YY-1 during 1–7 January 2026 to compare their spatial distributions, grid coverage, local-time sampling, and retrieval accuracy; it also assesses the benefits of multi-mission integration and the potential effects of COSMIC-2 retirement on the integrated observing capability. title: Breaking the Ice: Contributions and Challenges for Andean Glaciological Research Led by Women
abstract: Abstract This study examines the participation of women in Andean glaciology over the past four decades, combining a bibliometric analysis of 204 peer-reviewed articles (1983–2022) and a survey of female first authors (2018–2022). Results show a steady increase in women-led publications, rising from 8 percent in the 1980s–1990s to 30 percent in the past decade. title: A multi-indicator framework for assessing the likelihood of ENSO impacts across southern Africa
abstract: The El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is the dominant source of seasonal predictability for southern Africa, yet operational guidance rarely conveys which agriculturally relevant variables it can skillfully predict, or where ENSO impacts are most likely. We present an operational analysis framework that converts an ENSO state, classified by phase and strength, into gridded, analogue-composite outlooks for 15 indicators spanning rainfall, evaporative demand, related standardized indices (SPI, SPEI), crop water balance, dry-spells, rainfall-season timing, and heat extremes. title: Active wave absorption method for force-controlled wavemakers based on amplitude–phase fitting
abstract: Reflected waves at flume boundaries adversely affect the accuracy of wave simulation experiments, motivating the development of active absorption techniques. The absorption methods of force-controlled wavemakers, however, remain limited due to the complexity of their transfer functions. This study first derives the absorption transfer functions of piston-type and flap-type wavemakers in the frequency domain based on force control, and then uses them to design an active absorption system based on infinite impulse response (IIR) filters. title: Quantifying and attributing CO emissions over Central Asia using TROPOMI and explicit observational uncertainty
abstract: Abstract. Carbon monoxide (CO) is a crucial atmospheric constituent influencing both air quality and climate. Using TROPOMI CO and HCHO column retrievals within the Model-Free Inversion Estimation Framework (MFIEF), this study quantified daily, gridded CO emissions in Central Asia (Xinjiang-China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan) for 2019–2024. title: Otters appear to have declined throughout Ireland amid increased pressures on water quality, but remain ubiquitous
abstract: Abstract Governments must report on the conservation status of species designated as protected. We assessed changes in the Near Threatened Eurasian otter Lutra lutra population throughout Ireland (the whole island) from the 1980s to the 2020s using four National Otter Surveys (6,060 sites surveyed) and citizen science data (10,980 records). In 2023–2024, otters were recorded at 65% (95% CI 62–68%) of sites in the Republic of Ireland and 66% (95% CI 58–74%) of sites in Northern Ireland. It examines five broad domains: (1) health hazards, exposures and impacts; (2) adaptation, planning and resilience for health; (3) mitigation actions and health co-benefits; (4) economics and finance; and (5) public and political engagement. abstract: Abstract Particulate matter (PM) pollution is a critical aspect of urban air quality degradation, and vegetation mitigates atmospheric PM concentrations via dry deposition, offering a natural, sustainable, and cost-effective strategy for pollution mitigation. abstract: ABSTRACT Groundwater overexploitation can lead to land subsidence, posing risks for infrastructure, ecosystems, and long-term aquifer sustainability. However, detecting and prioritizing groundwater-related subsidence at the national scale remains challenging due to limited pumping data and heterogeneous monitoring networks. This study presents the first nationwide assessment of potential groundwater-related subsidence across Spain by integrating satellite observations and hydrogeological information at the groundwater body (GWB) scale. abstract: Abstract Understanding the influence of regional and long-range atmospheric transport on greenhouse gas (GHG) variability is essential for interpreting ground-based observations in urban environments. abstract: Study region Southwest China (SWC). Study focus This study identifies the decadal drought background of frequent droughts in SWC since the early 21st century, quantifies the roles of precipitation and potential evapotranspiration (PET), and evaluates vegetation impacts. title: Climate change impacts on the predicted performance of optimized building-integrated photovoltaics
abstract: Building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV) are a promising strategy for enhancing building energy performance and reducing carbon emissions. However, most design optimization studies rely on historical climate datasets that may fail to capture the operating conditions buildings will experience under climate change. This study develops a computational framework for the multi-objective optimization of BIPV envelope systems using future climate projections from the CanESM5 model under the SSP3-7.0 scenario. abstract: Abstract Although temperature variability (TV) has been linked to an increased mortality risk, the independent effect of intra‐day TV remains insufficiently understood. This study aimed to examine the association between intra‐day TV exposure and cause‐specific mortality in a Chinese population. We collected daily mortality data and meteorological variables from 2016 to 2022 in Jiulongpo District, Chongqing, China. abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the effects of carbonization temperature and fiber dosage on the mechanical properties, thermal conductivity, and rapid chloride penetration test (RCPT) response of bamboo fiber-reinforced C40 concrete. Bamboo fibers were incorporated at dosages of 1.5%–4.5% and used in three states: uncarbonized, carbonized at 300 °C, and carbonized at 800 °C. abstract: Abstract An early period of cometary bombardment has long been speculated to provide an important source of prebiotic feedstock molecules, required for the origins of life on Earth. In support of this interpretation, comets boast a rich diversity of volatile organic molecules, with many thought to be limiting for prebiotic chemistry. abstract: Rock-art replicas generally are judged as more or less faithful substitutes for inaccessible originals. While previous studies have demonstrated the value of replicas for individual archaeological experiments, we reconceive them as persistent interdisciplinary research infrastructure. abstract: Abstract To assess the climate impact of black carbon (BC), accurate emission inventories are crucial for climate model simulations. However, bottom‐up emissions inventories have substantial uncertainties regarding anthropogenic BC emissions from China and struggle to capture rapid changes in emissions. Top‐down analysis using atmospheric observations is an useful method to evaluate inventories and to immediately estimate BC emissions. title: Impacts of Cover Crops and Compacted Soils on Water Table Response Dynamics in an Agricultural Setting
abstract: ABSTRACT Water table dynamics play a crucial role in the hydrologic cycle, impacting dominant runoff generation mechanisms, root zone soil moisture conditions, surface water‐groundwater connectivity and more. In agricultural settings, they impact crop production but may vary significantly in space. The duration and frequency with which water tables occupy certain soil depths may provide key information to define ‘optimality’ in water table depth (WTD) for soil hydrology and agricultural productivity. title: Regional covariation between climate-normalized storm rarity and landslide magnitude in Taiwan is sensitive to rainfall timing
abstract: Abstract Climate-normalized rainfall rarity may facilitate comparisons across climates, but pooled rainfall–landslide associations can obscure regional structure and rainfall timing. abstract: Friction stir welding (FSW) of dissimilar aluminium alloys is accompanied by non-uniform thermal expansion and contraction that can generate significant residual stresses and influence joint response. abstract: Abstract In view of the problem of strong water sensitivity and susceptibility to dry and wet alternating damage of red clay, this study proposes to use plant-source Enzyme-Induced Carbonate Precipitation (EICP) technology for eco-friendly stabilization. title: An assessment of overbank flow-statistics within the context of environmental flow rules
abstract: Characterizing diversity in river flow regimes is crucial in informing river flow management guidelines for protecting freshwater ecosystems. In partly-confined reaches, river exhibit substantial lateral and vertical interaction when flow inundates its floodplain patches. A knowledge gap exists at the intersection of environmental flow assessment, overbank exceedance flow dynamics, and real-world policy application. title: Hydrodynamic Flood Modelling and GIS-Based Risk Mapping for Identifying Urbanization-Safe Zones in Hanwella, Sri Lanka
abstract: Urban expansion in flood-prone regions increases exposure to hydrological hazards and makes flood-informed land-use planning increasingly important. Hanwella, located in the Kelani River basin of Sri Lanka, is particularly vulnerable to flooding due to intense rainfall, river overflow, and growing urban pressure. This study develops a two-dimensional hydrodynamic flood modelling framework based on the shallow water equations and applies a Godunov-type finite volume method with the Harten–Lax–van Leer (HLL) Riemann solver to simulate water-level dynamics in the Hanwella region. title: Increasing the critical shear stress in sandy beds to control bed scour using alkali-activated cement
abstract: Scouring during flood events is a critical problem in hydraulic and geotechnical engineering, threatening the stability and service life of bridge piers and abutments, foundations, and embankments. This study evaluates the use of alkali-activated cement (AAC) derived from ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) for the prevention of streambed scour and to enhance the erosion resistance of sandy soils. title: Extreme event assessment and model diagnostic for attribution of the record-breaking July 2025 heat in Shandong, China
abstract: Abstract In July 2025, Shandong Province, China, experienced a record-breaking regional extreme heat event. Based on observational data from 77 meteorological stations (1961–2025), this study assessed the event’s extremity and systematically examines the feasibility of its attribution using Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) models. The event reached a magnitude close to that of a 1-in-50-year event in the current climate, with 84.4% of stations recording high-temperature days (HTD, Tmax ≥ 35 °C) ranking among their top three historical values and 50.6% setting new records.

title: Fluid mixing at the origin of a Ba-Pb mineralization in Triassic sandstones of the Geneva Basin (France–Switzerland)
abstract: Unconformity-related fluorite-barite-Pb-Zn mineralization is a key indicator of paleo-fluid circulation and tectonic evolution in sedimentary basins. This study investigates fracture-controlled barite-Pb veins in Triassic sandstones of the Geneva Basin (France–Switzerland) using petrography, stable (S, O) and radiogenic (Pb, Sr) isotopes, fluid inclusion microthermometry and elemental analysis, and basin thermal modeling. title: Sustained crustal helium enrichment associated with postseismic viscoelastic relaxation following the 2025 Myanmar earthquake
abstract: Earthquakes can alter fluid flow far from a rupture, but the processes that sustain such changes for months remain uncertain. Here we report a sustained increase in gas-phase helium concentration at a thermal spring on the Red River Fault, about 600 kilometres from the 2025 magnitude 7.7 Myanmar earthquake. title: Accelerating anthropogenic influence on annual peak wood density and associated carbon accumulation across northern conifers
abstract: Northern coniferous forests hold significant climatic and ecological importance, yet the optimal air temperature (OAT) governing their annual peak wood density remains unknown. Here, using tree-ring maximum latewood density (MXD) from 14,000 samples at 551 sites, we reveal an OAT range of 15–21 °C governing annual MXD variability, a more sensitive thermal metric than seasonal temperature. title: Coseismic Surface Deformation and Fault Slip Distribution of the 2026 Mw 6.8 Kumamoto Earthquake from Multi-Sensor InSAR and GNSS Observations

title: Global health impacts of the 2018–2019 heatwaves and air pollution events under warmer climates
abstract: Extreme temperatures and ambient air pollution are closely linked and impose substantial global health burdens, yet their regional responses to additional warming remain poorly understood across the world. Using a storyline approach based on the exceptionally warm years 2018 and 2019, we examine how heatwaves (HWs), fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ), ozone (O 3 ), and their separately estimated mortality burdens respond to two counterfactual climates at +2 K and +2.75 K warming levels. title: Modelling-Based Assessment of Managed Aquifer Recharge: Impacts on Groundwater Quantity and Quality in the Upper Friuli Plain (Italy)
abstract: In the Friuli Venezia Giulia (FVG) region of northeastern Italy, declining groundwater levels and changing precipitation patterns have raised concerns about the long-term sustainability of groundwater resources. This study evaluates the potential of Managed Aquifer Recharge (MAR) in the upper Friuli Plain, with a focus on the Sammardenchia site. title: Comparing surface albedo and land surface temperature of reflective roofs across five United States Cities
abstract: Abstract Rapid urban expansion and increasingly intense summer heat have heightened interest in reflective roofing as an urban heat-mitigation strategy. This study evaluates associations among roof type, surface albedo, and land surface temperature (LST) across five climatically distinct U.S. urban regions: Chicago, New York City (NYC), Las Vegas Valley (LVV), Los Angeles (LA), and Houston. title: An explicit large-displacements method for multi-point lifting analysis and optimization of pipelines and cables
abstract: Pipeline lifting operations involve large displacements and rotations, evolving suspended lengths and pronounced curvature variations, while the equilibrium configuration is generally unknown a priori. Classical catenary models provide highly efficient descriptions of perfectly flexible suspended lines but neglect bending stiffness, whereas geometrically nonlinear finite-element models can reproduce the complete structural response by solving computational heavy nonlinear systems and, when required, unilateral contact problems. title: Dynamic and thermodynamic drivers of regional drought changes in Africa under different global warming levels
abstract: Abstract Drought events pose severe threats to socio-economic stability, with impacts particularly pronounced across Africa due to limited adaptive capacity. This study provides a comprehensive assessment of projected changes in drought characteristics, their physical drivers, and socioeconomic implications under different global warming levels (GWLs) and emission scenarios. In this study, we use 31 Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) models and identify drought events using the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI). title: Solar-driven cogeneration of electricity and water vapor via photovoltaic-enabled contactless evaporation
abstract: Solar-driven cogeneration systems integrating photovoltaic (PV) technology with waste-heat-driven interfacial evaporation offer a sustainable route to the simultaneous production of electricity and water vapor. However, salt accumulation in conventional contact-based interfacial evaporators remains a major obstacle to long-term operation. title: Cuencas piggy-back de Limón Sur, Costa Rica
abstract: A morphotectonic analysis of the piggy-back basins of southern Limón, Costa Rica, is presented to evaluate their geomorphic evolution and relationship with active tectonic deformation. Seven basins were analyzed using geomorphic metrics derived from digital elevation models, including basin area, elevation, mean slope, local relief, and the normalized channel steepness index (ksn), complemented by drainage network analysis. abstract: ABSTRACT In the manufacturing of fiber‐reinforced composites, different stacking configurations are commonly adopted in dry fabric preforming, while the resulting inter‐ply angle difference ratio can affect the through‐thickness deformation of the preform. Dry fabrics also exhibit time‐dependent and irreversible deformation during compaction, which should be considered for accurate prediction of preform thickness evolution. abstract: Subsea pipelines are vulnerable to anchor-induced structural damage during ship mooring operations, particularly from raising and dragging interactions. abstract: Simulators are pivotal in advancing mobility technology, yet human adaptation in the context of these technologies remains underexplored. This study investigates the role of core executive functions (working memory, inhibitory control, and cognitive flexibility) in adaptive performance within driving simulators based on a scoping review identifying a research gap and conducting a driving simulator study addressing it. title: Decadal variability reveals contrasts in solar-resource stability across China
abstract: Abstract Solar resource assessments traditionally focus on how much solar radiation is available and how it changes over time, while overlooking how stable that resource remains throughout the decades. Here, we quantify the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of decadal variability in downward surface solar radiation (DSSR), commonly known as global horizontal irradiance (GHI) in the solar energy sector, across China’s seven major power grids during 1960–2024. abstract: ABSTRACT Calcium leaching degrades concrete durability through progressive dissolution and decalcification of cement hydrate phases, yet it is commonly modelled by assuming local equilibrium between the pore solution and solid hydrates. abstract: Continental pumped-storage hydropower (PSH) atlases omit schemes built from small reservoirs, although such sites could provide distributed flexibility. abstract: Assessing regional economic recovery after major earthquakes is critical for disaster risk reduction. This study aims to evaluate the disaster resilience of the Wenchuan earthquake-stricken area and explore its spatially varying influencing factors. Based on night-time light data, we constructed a counterfactual development baseline to quantify four resilience indices: Instantaneous Disturbance (D), Recovery Rate (R), Recovery Time (T), and Cumulative Economic Loss (L). abstract: Industrial infrastructure in Saudi Arabia is undergoing expansion and renewal with the environment being as much a factor as the infrastructure itself with exposure to extreme heat, flash flooding, complex supply chains and highly interdependent utility services. abstract: ABSTRACT Meteorological dry–wet abrupt alternation (M‐DWAA) is an important compound climate extreme that can impose complex stresses on agricultural and ecological systems through rapid shifts between water deficit and excess moisture. Its impacts on land‐surface and ecosystem processes depend partly on whether and how meteorological signals are transmitted into soil moisture. abstract: Individuals selected for the Inca capacocha ritual, sacrificed at high-altitude sites to act as messengers to the mountain deities, are occasionally found preserved as frozen mummies, providing key insights into Inca life and religious practices. Here, the authors present results of toxicological analyses of hair and nail samples from eight human sacrifices interred near volcanic peaks in Peru and Argentina. abstract: Abstract Understanding how climate change alters hydrological connectivity and associated nitrate dynamics remains a key challenge in lowland, mixed land‐use catchments. abstract: Abstract. Deep geological repositories for high-level radioactive waste (HLW) rely to a large extend on the long-term hydraulic integrity of host rocks to limit fluid flow and radionuclide migration. title: A climatic-regional classification framework for exotic species plantation forestry in Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Plantation forestry underpins rural livelihoods, wood and energy security and landscape restoration in Ethiopia, yet the country lacks a forestry-specific climatic classification to support species deployment and plantation planning. This study developed the first national climatic classification framework for exotic plantation forestry in Ethiopia by integrating temperature and a temperature-adjusted moisture index and quantifying regional temperature–elevation relationships. abstract: Abstract On 29 March 2026, a localised swathe of damaging winds affected parts of northern and eastern England, producing notable damage from southeastern Yorkshire to north Lincolnshire. Analysis of damage reports indicates that ‘straight‐line’ winds were the dominant cause, occurring near shallow convection no more than 3–4km deep. abstract: Abstract Rising thermal stress has emerged as a critical challenge for socio-economic systems and public health in the ongoing climate change scenario. In Northern India states like Uttar Pradesh, where a large population share is engaged in climate-sensitive livelihoods, increasing heat-related thermal stress poses substantial risk of income and productivity loss, alongside an escalating burden of heat-related health outcomes and healthcare expenditure. abstract: Abstract. title: Linking climate projections with farmer perspectives to inform agricultural adaptation in northern Tanzania
abstract: While there is growing evidence about how African farmers are adapting to climate change, there remains a lack of research highlighting direct linkages between future climate scenarios, impacts on agriculture, and viable adaptation strategies. abstract: Summary Leaf‐level photosynthesis acclimates to growth conditions over days to weeks, with the instantaneous optimal temperature for photosynthesis ( T opt ) increasing with growth temperature ( T growth ). We investigated how this behaviour emerges in the P model, a primary production model based on eco‐evolutionary optimality hypotheses. title: Limited anti-biofouling effect of surface-patterned membranes in spacer-filled feed channels over longer time periods
abstract: Topographical membrane surface patterns are a promising approach for increasing transmembrane flux and reducing foulant deposition. In this study, we investigated the anti-biofouling propensity of TFC membranes with micrometer-scale patterns. Unlike most studies in literature, where biofouling of patterned membranes was investigated without feed spacers and in short-term tests, we considered a) spacer-filled channels and b) advanced biofouling stages. abstract: The article substantiates the theoretical and methodological provisions for developing a mechanism aimed at enhancing the transfer potential of agricultural holdings’ logistics centers. abstract: Construction risk in shield tunnelling is closely related to the tunnel face stability. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Due to attractive inter-particle forces, cohesive particles suspended in turbulence undergo a complex process of aggregation, breakup and restructuring. abstract: A three-dimensional conjugate heat transfer model of a 400 W high-power LED fishing lamp (Scheme A) was established in COMSOL Multiphysics by coupling Heat Transfer in Solids, Heat Transfer in Fluids, laminar flow, and non-isothermal flow. abstract: Carbon emissions from the electrical energy and transportation sectors are two of the largest contributors to global greenhouse gas emissions. Reducing these emissions will be key to mitigating the worst impacts of global climate change. This study models the economic and lifecycle carbon impacts of transitioning California toward a deeply decarbonized electric power grid and light-duty electric vehicle fleet. abstract: Abstract Reliable initialization of in situ $${K}_{0}$$ K 0 stresses and efficient stability analysis are fundamental to robust finite-element modeling of infinite slopes. title: Role of hydrometeorological variables and catchment area to flood generation over the monsoonal climate region of India
abstract: Abstract. Indian River basins experience frequent flooding during the Indian summer monsoon rainfall and pose several challenges to the large population of the region. To effectively manage flood risk in the region, a better understanding of flood-generating mechanisms is essential, yet hydrometeorological and catchment drivers controlling flood processes are poorly explored across India. abstract: Cereal production in South Asia faces rising temperatures, erratic monsoon rainfall, and diminishing returns to input intensification. This study examines how weather and farm inputs shape cereal yields across the conditional yield distribution in Bangladesh, India, Nepal, and Pakistan, which account for about 99% of the cereal area of South Asia outside Afghanistan, over 2000–2023. abstract: Honeycombs have garnered significant research interest owing to their multifunctional attributes and exceptional mechanical performance. This study develops an improved variant of the multi‐arc enhanced reentrant honeycomb (MAERH) inspired by the multi‐arc reentrant auxetic honeycomb (MARAH). title: Continuous measurement of oxygen consumption rate in hypoxic conditions with adherent cells using an oxygen-sensitive optode
abstract: Cellular oxygen consumption rate (OCR) is a widely used readout of mitochondrial respiration and oxidative metabolism. However, many OCR assay workflows are limited by short assay durations, expensive specialized instrumentation, and reduced flexibility under controlled low-oxygen conditions. Here, we describe an in-incubator method for continuous, non-disruptive OCR measurement in adherent cell cultures using the PreSens OxoDish optical oxygen-sensing system. title: Investigating the thermal properties of hollow blocks building envelope composite sections used across Egypt
abstract: Studying the thermal properties of building materials used in building envelope cross-sections is crucial for enhancing indoor thermal comfort and improving energy efficiency. This study aims to experimentally determine the thermal properties of building envelope wall sections using the heat flow meter (HFM) technique. The thermal properties, including thermal conductivity, thermal resistance, U-value, and specific heat, were investigated for the most common building materials and composite wall sections used in the Egyptian context. abstract: Abstract Dust events motivate separate monitoring of atmospheric dimming and potential photovoltaic (PV) surface soiling. We developed Dust-to-Power as an event-specific monitoring framework across eight northern Chinese provinces. The CERES analysis covers 20–24 March 2023, a 5-day subset of the documented 19–24 March event. abstract: Flooding remains one of the most frequent and destructive hydro-meteorological hazards in South Africa, causing substantial socio-economic losses, infrastructure damage, and threats to human life. In response to increasing flood risks associated with climate variability and extreme weather events, the South African Weather Service has increasingly adopted impact-based severe weather early warning systems designed to communicate not only meteorological hazards but also their likely consequences for communities, infrastructure, and livelihoods. abstract: This numerical study investigates flow characteristics around a uniformly porous-coated, infinitely square cylinder in subcritical flow regimes, analyzing the effects of porous media parameters on surface pressure distribution, aerodynamic loads (lift fluctuations and drag), and vortex shedding patterns. abstract: Energy consumption of the word increasing year by year, however, the world cannot afford the generation of energy through conventional means of fossil fuel. To meet the growing demand of energy, various sources of renewable energy is utilized across the globe. abstract: The ‘democratic wave’ in relation to citizen involvement in climate change policy challenges is illustrated here in the Irish context through the Citizens’ Assembly on Climate Change. The National Dialogue on Climate Action (NDCA) has sought to broaden the time and space for citizen input into climate change policy formation. abstract: Elucidating the origin of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays remains a central challenge in modern astrophysics. The Southern Wide-field Gamma-ray Observatory (SWGO) will deploy a kilometer-scale detector array on natural water surfaces, where detector position deviations must be constrained within 2 m to enable high-fidelity observations. title: Wave breaking in Newtonian and viscoplastic vertical falling liquid films
abstract: We examine the onset of wave breaking in highly viscous gravity-driven vertical falling liquid films in a quiescent atmosphere via multiphase direct numerical simulations. Both Newtonian and Herschel–Bulkley liquids are considered. Analysis of the force balance acting on wave humps shows that the transition from travelling waves to breaking states is governed primarily by the competition between gravitational and capillary forces. abstract: Abstract. This study introduces a new hybrid implicit–explicit (IMEX) time-integration method for simulating injection-induced fault reactivation within a fully coupled hydromechanical extended finite element (XFEM) framework. Modeling these systems is inherently difficult because of the extreme difference in temporal scales – ranging from days for fluid diffusion to less than milliseconds for dynamic rupture. abstract: ABSTRACT The liquefaction susceptibility of saturated sands is commonly evaluated using macroscopic indices such as relative density and confining pressure, whereas the role of particle morphology remains less well understood. In this study, a coupled computational fluid dynamics‐discrete element method (CFD‐DEM) framework is used to investigate particle‐shape effects on liquefaction under a unified deposition and cyclic loading protocol. title: Characterizing variability and vertical structure of water vapor in the extratropical lower stratosphere
abstract: Abstract. Stratospheric water vapor strongly affects Earth’s radiative balance, especially in the extratropical lower stratosphere, yet large uncertainties remain regarding its variability, long-term trends and relationships to tropopause behavior. Here we characterize the seasonality, vertical structure, and variability of water vapor near the extratropical tropopause and the extratropical transition layer (ExTL). abstract: Abstract The Camelopardalids meteor shower (#451, CAM), produced by comet 209P/LINEAR’s historic dust trails, has exhibited a strong outburst only once, on 2014 May 24, since the discovery of the parent body in 2004, and although this event was well predicted, its activity was substantially lower than forecast. title: Post‐Fire Surface Energy Partitioning and Thermal Responses in Arctic Boreal Forests and Tundra
abstract: Abstract Rapid Arctic warming intensifies wildfire activity across high‐latitude ecosystems, yet post‐fire surface responses of boreal forests and tundra remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate land surface temperature (LST) and energy partitioning responses during the first post‐fire summer across the pan‐Arctic using satellite observations and surface energy‐balance diagnostics. abstract: Abstract The Representative Concentration Pathways (RCPs) are a set of four harmonized greenhouse gas emission and concentration trajectories, representative of scenarios from the literature, that would result in radiative forcings of 2.6, 4.5, 6.0, and 8.5 Wm − 2 by the year 2100. title: Legionella Risk Management in Building Water Systems: Current Perspectives from Industry Practitioners
abstract: Building water systems are internationally recognised reservoirs for opportunistic premise plumbing pathogens, including Legionella, the causative agent of Legionnaires’ disease. Inadequate design, operation and maintenance can promote Legionella proliferation and expose building occupants to potentially fatal infection. Effective management is therefore critical; however, there is limited international evidence regarding how guidelines for controlling Legionella risk are implemented in practice. abstract: The non-stationary interaction between elastic structures and compressible fluids is investigated using a displacement-based Lagrangian formulation. Motivated by recent studies indicating transient viscoelastic effects in oscillating liquids, the fluid is described by a viscoelastic constitutive model expressed in terms of displacement. title: The fetal phenotype is a trajectory, not a snapshot
abstract: The fetal phenotype is a trajectory rather than a fixed observation: features emerge, progress, or resolve across gestation, and the anomaly present at 20 weeks is often not the anomaly present at 32. Sequence variants, however, are interpreted against the phenotype supplied when the test is requested, and phenotypic specificity carries evidence weight in variant classification. title: Dynamic modeling, efficiency analysis, and hierarchical control of industrial airborne pulp dryers
abstract: Industrial airborne pulp drying is governed by strongly coupled moisture transport, heat transfer, psychrometric behavior, airflow distribution, pressure dynamics, and fan operation. A nonlinear multi-zone dynamic model was formulated to represent these interactions through coupled mass and energy balances, pressure-driven deck-to-deck airflow, centrifugal-fan dynamics, and through-thickness moisture and temperature transport. title: Tailings flocculation and settling in a lab‐scale thickener by multiscale CFD modeling approach
abstract: Abstract Flocculation‐thickening is an important solid–liquid separation operation in chemical engineering. The flocculation in the thickener feedwell plays a key role in the tailings slurry thickening process. This study develops a sequential multiscale model for a lab‐scale deep cone thickener to examine the effects of feed solids concentration on flocculation and settling. abstract: Temperature strongly influences plant carbon balance by modifying the coordination between photosynthesis, respiration, and carbon allocation. However, the integration between these processes during thermal acclimation remains poorly understood in quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.). Here, we investigated the physiological and metabolic responses of two contrasting quinoa ecotypes, UdeC9 and Lisio Putre, grown under low (15°C), optimal (25°C), and high (35°C) temperatures. abstract: ABSTRACT Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has demonstrated its usefulness for population-level monitoring of many biomarkers in near-real time. As a source of data, it has continued potential across many applications, but with resources finite and uncertainties potentially large, methodological advancements are required for this potential to be achieved. abstract: ABSTRACT Aiming at the coordinated speed regulation in multiple permanent magnet synchronous motors (multi‐PMSMs) under signed directed communication relationships, this paper presents a speed coordination strategy using a distributed nonsmooth bipartite consensus protocol (DNBCP). abstract: This study compares droplet size, velocity, and sampled computational-parcel distributions in upward and downward full-cone water sprays under atmospheric and sub-atmospheric pressures. title: Finite Element Analysis and Structural Performance of Composite Vehicle Bumpers
abstract: Background: The increasing demand for lightweight, durable, and impact-resistant automotive components has accelerated the adoption of composite materials in vehicle structural applications. Conventional metallic bumpers provide adequate strength but contribute significantly to vehicle weight, which adversely affects fuel efficiency and environmental sustainability. Fibre-reinforced polymer composites, particularly carbon fibre composites, offer a promising alternative because of their high strength-to-weight ratio, corrosion resistance and superior energy absorption characteristics. title: The Grammaticalization of ‘One’ in Slavic at the Syntax-Semantics Interface
abstract: This paper investigates the grammaticalization of the numeral ‘one’ in Slavic languages at the syntax-semantics interface. abstract: This study develops an interactive economic management framework for electricity–carbon trading in renewable-rich communities by coordinating photovoltaic (PV) prosumers through an Aggregator of Prosumers (AOP), Storage e-Transportable (SET) units, and coupled market signals. abstract: Abstract Wetland water quality plays a vital role in controlling emissions of methane, a strong greenhouse gas, and it is regulated by the sequestration of nutrients and toxic metals on iron‐rich soils. abstract: This article examines the results of a comprehensive study of the simulation modeling of hydraulic head in complex engineering mesh structures, such as trawl bags. The relevance of the study is stipulated by the need to optimize the hydrodynamic characteristics of fishing gear to minimize the energy consumption of a fishing vessel. abstract: ABSTRACT There is a growing interest in the use of nature-based solutions (NbS) to mitigate natural hazards. However, limited parameterization exists for runoff, erosion, and mudflow models, preventing upscaling of NbS effects to the catchment scale for management purposes. In this study, a parameterization of NbS such as fascines, hedgerows, grass strips, and ponds is proposed and implemented in a catchment-scale runoff and erosion model applicable by non-experts (WaterSed). title: Early childhood education as a seedbed for civic and planetary justice
abstract: Early childhood education is often treated as preparation for civic life. abstract: Climate-driven socio-economic change during Late Antiquity remains a topic of debate, especially over the extent to which climatic instability shaped economic structures and subsistence strategies within the Roman Empire. While the effects of political fragmentation have been extensively documented for urban contexts, responses of rural households remain less understood. abstract: Restricted access to architectural heritage limits expert observation, documentation, and preservation planning. This study examines how mobile augmented reality (AR) can support stable, structured observation when the deployment space differs from the heritage site. Because one-to-one physical–virtual correspondence and global registration rarely hold, we prioritized cognitive coherence over geometric accuracy.
