title: Cropland and population exposure to extreme precipitation events in Central Asia under future climate change
abstract: Central Asia (CA) is experiencing rapid warming and an intensifying hydrological cycle, with important implications for extreme precipitation events (EPEs). However, future changes in cropland and population exposure to EPEs remain insufficiently quantified in this climate-sensitive dryland region. Here, we projected changes in EPE characteristics and associated cropland and population exposure across CA using daily precipitation simulations from five bias-adjusted ISIMIP3b global climate models under SSP1-2.6, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5. abstract: Abstract. Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellites have emerged as a crucial technology for real-time flood monitoring in the face of escalating flood disaster hazards. However, current flood extraction techniques still have a lot of drawbacks when it comes to solving the twin problems of accurate urban flood detection and extensive monitoring. abstract: Abstract The increasing demand for resilient and sustainable infrastructure has encouraged the development of advanced cementitious composites with enhanced impact resistance. This study investigates the impact performance of reinforced concrete columns incorporating rubberized engineered cementitious composites (RECCs) through finite element modeling. The primary objective is to evaluate the influence of material composition and reinforcing steel detailing on the dynamic response of bridge columns subjected to low-velocity lateral impacts. abstract: The frequency and intensity of heat waves are increasing, but how these trends translate to changes in the ambient heat to which children are potentially exposed (hereafter, exposures) is not well established. One complicating factor is that it is not only extreme temperatures that change over time, but also the geospatial distribution of children. abstract: Absorption muography infers path-averaged density from the attenuation of atmospheric muons. Transient flux variations driven by weather, solar activity, and geomagnetism bias sequential measurements that rely on a non-simultaneous background. Here we show a real-time dual-telescope normalization in which two identical plastic-scintillator telescopes operate in parallel, one viewing open sky as a reference and one viewing the target. abstract: Converter-interfaced wind turbines inherently lack the inertial response of synchronous generators, reducing frequency stability in low-inertia power systems. While virtual synchronous machine control enables wind turbines to emulate inertial behaviour, the practical limits of inertia provision and the dominant mechanisms constraining performance remain poorly understood. abstract: The study investigates the principles of public-private partnership (PPP) development as a key instrument for the post-war reconstruction of Ukraine. It is substantiated that traditional approaches ignore systemic interconnections and disrupt the integrity of the economic environment. abstract: Abstract Few fragments of Earth's earliest crust have survived, and so this formative period of our planet's history is shrouded in mystery. To leverage the limited data available, it is important to understand all the processes that could have shaped our young planet. Here, I explore a previously neglected aspect of early‐Earth dynamics: rotation. abstract: Abstract Urban heat stress poses an increasingly critical challenge in the context of climate change and rapid urbanization, prompting the adoption of Green-Blue Infrastructure (GBI) as a key mitigation strategy. abstract: Abstract Global climate models (GCMs) robustly predict that precipitation will become flashier (i.e., more concentrated in time) as the climate warms, with extremely wet events accounting for a larger share of total precipitation at a given location. Here we test this prediction across the western United States, where precipitation is modulated by orographic mechanisms that GCMs do not resolve. title: Correlation of conventional histopathology and GeneXpert MTB/RIF in the diagnosis of spinal tuberculosis.
abstract: Introduction: Spinal tuberculosis (STB) remains a significant health burden in tuberculosis-endemic regions, including India. Diagnosis is challenging because conventional microbiological methods, including acid-fast staining and mycobacterial culture, have limited sensitivity in paucibacillary disease. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of GeneXpert MTB/RIF in comparison with conventional histopathological examination (HPE) for the diagnosis of STB. abstract: ABSTRACT Frugal and social innovations are considered more likely to support sustainability than conventional innovations. However, indicators for assessing their sustainability impacts remain scarce. Although the need for such indicators, especially for frugal innovation, has been emphasized repeatedly, only a few studies address this issue, and even fewer propose quantitative measures. abstract: Some invertebrate lineages are known to have lost their ability to methylate DNA cytosines. These lineages have often lost the enzymes responsible for cytosine methylation (DNMT1 and 3), as well as other enzymes that interact with methylated cytosines. Previous studies showed that myxosporeans, a group of parasitic cnidarians, lack recognisable DNMTs and other canonical methylation enzymes, and observed a lack of cytosine methylation in two myxosporeans using whole genome bisulfite sequencing. abstract: Steel–concrete debonding in concrete-filled steel tube (CFST) members reduces composite action by delaying or suppressing the mobilization of confinement. Debonding is commonly described through scalar geometric parameters, such as debonded area ratio or arc-length ratio, although different gap morphologies may induce different confinement mechanisms. abstract: Fossil microbialites resulting from the interplay of sedimentation and precipitation are among the oldest evidence of life on Earth and help geobiologists to interpret many sedimentary environments. However, the factors governing their internal structure and external morphology are still poorly understood. abstract: Agricultural workers are routinely exposed to extreme heat, posing serious health risks. Effective communication of information about heat risk requires fast, easy-to-use, real-time tools for the relevant stakeholders. For this purpose, we have developed the iHeatApp web-based application, accessible via smartphones, tablets, or computers, to visualize forecasted Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) and to quantify the risks at given WBGT levels. abstract: Slope failure is a geotechnical problem that can threaten the safety and functionality of road infrastructure, particularly in areas with steep terrain and high rainfall intensity. abstract: Litter layer removal by commercial pine straw raking has the potential to increase forest floor evaporation (Es) by strengthening soil surface-atmosphere coupling; however, its effects on Es and soil water availability remain poorly quantified. We investigated the influence of pine straw raking on Es within a closed-canopy loblolly pine (Pinus taeda L.) plantation using non-weighing box lysimeters with both intact and removed litter layers (litter and rake treatments, respectively) over a one-year period, hypothesizing that raking would increase annual Es. abstract: Xolography enables contactless volumetric additive manufacturing by suspending objects in a viscous resin. This avoids the build platforms and shear forces that distort soft materials in layer-by-layer printing. However, low-viscosity resins such as hydrogels allow printed parts to sediment, and conventional thickeners can compromise the final material. abstract: Abstract Transformational faulting in olivine has been widely invoked as a possible triggering mechanism for deep‐focus earthquakes, yet its dynamics remain debated. It is unclear whether it requires the combined effects of heat release, volume change and mechanical strength contrast, or whether it can be triggered by any one of these alone. abstract: The Engineer-Procure-Construct (EPC) model has become a dominant project delivery method for large-scale infrastructure projects globally. While existing research has extensively documented cost and schedule overruns in EPC projects, limited attention has been paid to how engineering uncertainties systematically undermine projects' commercial viability assessments. abstract: Abstract Surface texturing serves as an effective method for enhancing lubrication performance in high-speed sliding contacts operating in the fluid-film lubrication regime. abstract: Abstract The accurate prediction of magnetic fields generated by ferromagnetic housings in large-scale engineered systems is essential for magnetic signature control and magnetic field management. This work aims to provide a general analytical framework for evaluating the static magnetic signature of complex ferromagnetic components by employing a formulation based on the magnetic scalar potential together with volume-averaged magnetization and effective relative magnetic permeability. title: Assessment of whether tree-ring hydroclimate reconstructions are useful for characterising extreme drought in East Anglia (England)
abstract: Region East of England Focus Paleoclimate proxies are used here to characterise extreme droughts including those corresponding to a 1:500-year return period. We evaluate four tree-ring hydroclimate (precipitation or drought index) reconstructions representing similar geographical regions across East Anglia and Southern England. abstract: Abstract Colloids strongly adsorb pollutants and promote their co‐transport in aquatic environments, posing substantial ecological contamination risks. However, quantifying the size exclusion effect (SEE), a critical mechanism that enhances colloid transport, remains challenging in multi‐sized colloid systems, owing to limited high‐resolution labeling methods and ion‐induced dynamic aggregation. abstract: Citizen Science Hubs (CSHs) are increasingly proposed as institutional infrastructures that anchor citizen science within universities and connect academic, public, business, civil-society and environmental actors. Yet empirical evidence on the early-stage performance of CSHs, particularly in emerging citizen-science ecosystems with low public awareness and limited institutional support, remains scarce. abstract: The study investigates the potential effect of changing the release regime from the Karachunivske Reservoir when applying the impulse flushing method to the Inhulets River on the transport, settling, and export of suspended material. The relevance of the study is determined by the fact that previously proposed impulse flushing regimes were assessed mainly in terms of water quality and water-use efficiency, whereas the possible sedimentation consequences of changing the temporal structure of releases were not considered separately. abstract: Abstract Human occupation of Central Europe during the Late Pleistocene was strongly influenced by climatic fluctuations, resulting in discontinuous settlement patterns and repeated phases of regional abandonment and recolonization. Southern Poland represents a key frontier zone within these dynamics, yet the chronological resolution of many sites remains limited, particularly for assemblages excavated during the early twentieth century. title: Heterogeneous impacts of temperature extremes on climate attitudes and Green voting
abstract: In the past decade, the public in Europe has become more concerned about climate change and expresses stronger proenvironmental policy preferences. Based on data from the European Social Survey (2012-2022, 25 countries), we show that the increased exposure to temperature extremes has contributed to the observed changes in climate change attitudes and electoral support for environmentalist policy platforms. abstract: Wysoki status leków przeciwdepresyjnych wynika z faktu, że depresja jest jednym z najczęstszych stanów patologicznych w medycynie. 70 lat temu, w związku z rewolucją farmakologiczną w psychiatrii, pojawiły się środki działające terapeutycznie na depresję, czyli leki przeciwdepresyjne. abstract: Vinyl ester composites reinforced with treated coconut (shells and fibers) and glass (powder and fibers) have been investigated using numerical, experimental, and statistical methods. Tensile and bending tests were applied. Numerical simulation was conducted using the Finite Element Method (FEM) with the ABAQUS CAE 2019 program for tensile and flexural samples. title: Short fire-return intervals modify fuel structure, changing flammability and fire behavior in dry forests of southeastern Australia
abstract: Abstract Shortening fire-return intervals are pushing fire-tolerant ecosystems in temperate Australia beyond their ecological limits, producing alternative vegetation states with markedly different composition and structure. While the structural effects of these regime shifts on fire-tolerant eucalypt forests are increasingly documented, their consequences for flammability remain largely untested. title: Lead-free soft hybrid materials for piezoelectric sensors: A paradigm shift from toxic lead-based ceramics to sustainable electronics
abstract: The development of piezoelectric materials has significantly transformed modern electronic and sensing technologies, and their use has extended from extremely precise actuators to wearable self-powering devices. But the problem is that these materials are commonly made out of lead-based ceramics, and for example, lead zirconate titanate (PZT) contains 60% of lead. title: Do protected-area enclaves constrain NPP gains in forest landscapes? Counterfactual evidence from Hainan tropical rainforest national park, China
abstract: Protected-area enclaves are areas geographically surrounded by protected areas (PAs) but outside the jurisdiction of their management authorities, yet their implications for conservation effectiveness remain understudied from a counterfactual perspective. Using estimated net primary productivity (NPP) data from 2014 to 2024, we examined five large enclaves in Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park within a propensity score matching–difference-in-differences (PSM-DID) framework. abstract: Abstract This paper presents a pattern of complementizer displacement in the Ethio-Semitic language Tigrinya (Ethiopia, Eritrea) that argues for the existence of a morphosyntactic operation of lowering that may involve successive steps (Embick and Noyer 2001; Arregi and Pietraszko 2021). abstract: Abstract This study proposes a novel continuous arched composite cross‐section caisson‐type underground garage structure to meet urban underground space development demands. Through scaled model tests, the mechanical performance and failure mechanisms under different rise‐span ratios (0, 0.1434, and 0.3) were systematically investigated. abstract: Open pit coal plans rely on geological models built from widely spaced drill holes, so errors in seam continuity pass directly into tonnage and stripping ratio forecasts. This study quantifies how integrating infill drilling and electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) with existing drill hole data changes the seam model, and the coal tonnage, overburden volume and stripping ratio derived from it, within an unchanged pit boundary. abstract: To reduce the NO emissions of hydrogen-enriched industrial gas boilers caused by temperature enhancement, the flue gas recirculation technology was implemented in hydrogen-enriched industrial gas boilers to achieve low-nitrogen combustion. A Diffusion Flamelet model with the reaction mechanism of GRI-Mech 3.0 and an iterative method for calculating boundary conditions was built to numerically investigate the effects of hydrogen blending ratio and flue gas recirculation ratio on the combustion performance and NO emissions. abstract: Rapid urbanization and population growth have substantially increased municipal water demand in Kigali, Rwanda, creating an urgent need for sustainable and economically efficient groundwater development strategies. This study presents an integrated hydro-economic framework for optimizing groundwater wellfield development in the shallow alluvial and weathered rock aquifers of the Nyabarongo River basin. abstract: The China Jinping Underground Laboratory (CJPL), located $\sim 2,400$~m beneath Jinping Mountain, is one of the world's deepest and largest ($\sim 300{,}000~\mathrm{m}^3$) underground facilities, hosting dark matter, nuclear astrophysics, and neutrino experiments. abstract: Application-oriented simulations, such as automotive crash simulations, often utilize large shell elements to optimize computational efficiency. This study applies the crack band approach typically used for concrete materials to steel sheets. The aim was to examine this regularization method for different stress states with plane stress shell elements to reduce mesh sensitivity, in respect to element size as well as to element shape. abstract: Pelvic spine loss has evolved repeatedly in stickleback species and represents an intri-guing opportunity to study genetically parallel adaptation. While previous work has identified key loci associated with this trait, the extent to which different populations rely on the same genetic mechanisms remains unclear. The genetic basis of pelvic spine loss in Culaea incon-stans (Kirtland 1840) has only been investigated in three populations. abstract: Urban overheating, intensified by climate change and rapid urbanization, poses a major challenge to livability in arid environments. Green infrastructure (GI) and cool materials are increasingly being implemented to reduce urban heat. Numerous constitutive models are available in the literature and can be calibrated to capture select features of the soil response, typically the numbers of cycles to liquefaction. abstract: Abstract Geological carbon dioxide storage is central to meeting many national climate change commitments, but large-scale deployment may be limited by both techno-economic rates of growth and physics-based processes imposed by subsurface geology. abstract: Abstract Deep Cement Mixing (DCM) columns are widely used for improving soft-soil bridge foundations, but the influence of cross-sectional configuration is commonly assessed at a single design load. abstract: This study evaluates biophysical agricultural land suitability across the twenty districts of Erzurum, the fourth-largest province of Türkiye by surface area, by integrating Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). abstract: Understanding past hydroclimatic variability is important for sustainable water resource management in semi-arid mountainous regions. abstract: Abstract A FeCoCrNiAl high-entropy alloy (HEA) coating was deposited on a Ti-6Al-4V (TC4) alloy substrate by high-velocity oxygen fuel (HVOF) thermal spraying to enhance its sliding wear performance. abstract: Wind-driven rain (WDR) can cause water ingress through residential window-frame assemblies during tropical-cyclone events, even when structural failure does not occur. abstract: Flood-control structures are evaluated for reducing inundation, yet their effects across flood magnitudes and land-use exposure remain insufficiently understood in ungauged tropical basins. abstract: Abstract A key component of the widely used Wang‐Sheeley‐Arge model is the tracing of magnetic field lines in the solar corona, as that largely determines the modeled open/closed field regions and in turn the predicted large‐scale solar wind structure. However, small closed field regions interspersed among the open field lines inside coronal holes (CHs) often hinder determination of the large‐scale open–closed boundary. title: Pesky Metals: Historical Perspective, Advances, and Challenges for Remediation of Problematic Metal Contaminants
abstract: Abstract Persistent and problematic toxic metal and metalloid pollutants (in particular, As, Hg, Pb, Cd, and Cr) have long been challenging and expensive remediation targets in contaminated surface and subsurface environments. Since the advent of environmental regulations and cleanup in the late 20th century, much progress has been made to address sites of legacy metal pollution and limit new contamination. title: How Coffee Farmers Respond to Climate Stress in East Java’s Mountain Regions: A Social-Ecological Resilience Perspective
abstract: Tropical mountain coffee farms integrate crop production with tree cover, soil functions, water use, and rural livelihoods. In East Java, farmers reported irregular rainfall and interacting pressures affecting coffee production and household decisions. This study examines farmers’ response breadth and interprets these patterns through a social-ecological resilience perspective without treating response counts as direct measures of resilience. We used a comparative case design based on 33 transcript-verified coffee-farmer interviews from Semeru (n=23) and Arjuno (n=10), conducted from 17 April
institutions: National Pingtung University of Science and Technology

title: Potential Operational, Economic and Carbon Consequences of Geopolitical Airspace Restrictions for Philippine Long-Haul Aviation: A Scenario Analysis
abstract: Geopolitical airspace restrictions can alter long-haul routing, fuel use, costs and emissions. This study evaluates the conditional consequences of assumed path extensions for eight Manila airport pairs. Published Fuel Estimation in Air Transportation coefficients for the Airbus A350-900, Boeing 787-9 and Boeing 777-300ER were combined with five assumed path increments, yielding 120 deterministic cases. abstract: Abstract Dynamic rupture models have been widely used to enhance our understanding of earthquake processes and associated hazards. A commonly held insight among modelers is that if the initial stress, rheological parameters, and space and time coordinates are scaled by certain factors in a specific manner, the solution will scale accordingly and remain similar. title: Eccentric compression behavior and design of aluminum alloy tube-confined geopolymer concrete columns
abstract: Concrete-filled aluminum alloy tubular columns have been studied mainly with ordinary Portland cement concrete (PCC), whereas the eccentric-compression response and design of geopolymer concrete (GPC)-filled aluminum alloy tubes remain insufficiently quantified. This study combines tests on 11 hollow 6063-T5 square aluminum alloy columns, six existing eccentric-compression tests on PCC-filled aluminum alloy tubular columns, and validated finite element analysis to examine the behavior of GPC-filled members. title: Reconstruction of the 1989 Laguna del Cerro Largo GLOF: an interdisciplinary understanding of GLOF Impacts
abstract: Abstract. The March 16, 1989, glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) from Laguna del Cerro Largo in Valle Soler, Aysén, Chile, is one of the largest recent moraine-dammed GLOFs in the region. This interdisciplinary approach reconstructs the GLOF downstream impacts using HEC-RAS 2D and GeoClaw from witness accounts. Model results are then validated through field analysis of sediment deposition, dendrogeomorphic surveys, radiocarbon dating. abstract: The detection of extended very-high-energy (VHE, E > 0.1 TeV) gamma-ray emission surrounding the middle-aged pulsars Geminga and PSR B0656+14 by the HAWC Observatory in 2017 provided the first clear observational evidence for an extended inverse Compton component produced by electron-positron pairs diffusing away from pulsars, a component whose existence under conditions of suppressed diffusion had been anticipated theoretically. abstract: The potential of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) was investigated as reinforcements to enhance the deformation behavior and energy absorption of composite foams (CFs) under high strain‐rate impact (over 100 s −1 ). Split Hopkinson pressure bar (SHPB) tests were performed at 650 and 1300 s −1 to characterize the dynamic compressive properties of closed‐cell CNTs/Al–Cu–Mg foams with 0, 0.25, and 0.5 wt.% CNTs. title: Vine Copula-Based Multivariate Value-at-Risk for Extreme Rainfall Risk Assessment
abstract: Extreme rainfall occurring simultaneously across multiple locations can generate spatially dependent risks that are not adequately captured by independent univariate models. This study develops an R-vine copula-based framework to model spatial dependence and quantify joint extreme rainfall risk across seven rainfall stations in DKI Jakarta and West Java, Indonesia. Station-specific marginal distributions were fitted using a mixed discrete-continuous framework to account for zero and positive rainfall observations. title: A Physically Based Storage‐Runoff Relationship for Steep Hillslopes and Its Application to Distributed Flood Modeling
abstract: Abstract Kinematic wave models are widely used to represent hillslope runoff in distributed hydrological models. However, their simplified descriptions often prevent the effective use of observed soil hydraulic parameters during calibration. To address this limitation, we derived a new analytical storage–runoff relationship that explicitly incorporates percolation under wet‐soil conditions and rapid drainage through subsurface pipes. title: Blast protection for headforms: a review of experimental studies
abstract: This review discusses the limitations of experimental protocols using headforms and military helmets employed for protection against blast-related traumatic brain injuries (bTBIs), which have become more prevalent with the increased use of improvised explosive devices (IEDs). To assess and improve helmet effectiveness against blast waves, researchers have conducted experiments using post-mortem human subjects (PMHS), existing headforms such as the Hybrid III or Facial and Ocular Countermeasure Safety (FOCUS) model, and custom-designed headforms. title: Resolution effects on digital rock characterization of tight diatomite reservoir rocks using μCT
abstract: Diatomites combine high porosity with fine, hierarchical pore systems that challenge pore-scale characterization by micro-computed tomography (μCT). This study evaluates how μCT resolution affects pore-space representation, connectivity, and simulated permeability in reservoir diatomite from the Lark Formation, with Fur and Lompoc outcrop diatomites used for comparison. Laboratory petrophysical measurements provide independent reference properties. title: Stationary Resistive MHD Solutions near an Isolated Three-dimensional Magnetic Null
abstract: Abstract Magnetic null points define the topology of magnetic fields in stellar coronae, planetary magnetospheres, and astrospheres and are commonly associated with magnetic reconnection. We investigate the local structure of stationary 3D resistive, incompressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) flows in the vicinity of an isolated magnetic null and an isolated velocity stagnation point, assuming that the two nulls are colocated. title: Performance Assessment of Solar Thermal Systems with Heat Storage in Multifamily Buildings Under Real Climatic Conditions
abstract: This study evaluates the long - term performance of a solar thermal system coupled with thermal energy storage (TES) for a reference multifamily building in northeastern Poland using 14 consecutive years (2010 – 2023) of hourly PVGIS - SARAH3 meteorological data . The reference building comprises 16 dwellings and 48 occupants. Domestic hot - water (DHW) consumption was assumed at 50 L per person per day, with cold - and hot - water temperatures of 10 and 55 °C, respectively, and a lumped DHW distribution and storage ef ficiency of 70%. title: Unsteady early-stage behaviour of horizontal cryogenic hydrogen releases in crosswind
abstract: The impact of crosswind on horizontal hydrogen releases under low pressure-ratio (PR) conditions is investigated using Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) simulations. The simulation results are validated against the existing data in the literature. Our results highlight the transient nature of hydrogen plume development as well as the impact of initial momentum, crosswind, and buoyancy. title: Impacts of the heterogeneous ammonia uptake on air quality in the North China Plain
abstract: Abstract. Previous studies have revealed that the heterogeneous uptake of ammonia (NH3) on secondary organic aerosols (SOA) profoundly influences the NH3 budget, nitrate aerosol chemistry, and the regional PM2.5 burden, also constituting an important source of nitrogen-containing organic compounds (NOCs). However, current regional modeling efforts are hindered by large uncertainties in uptake coefficients (γ) and a persistent lack of field-based observational constraints. title: Is public participation addressing just transition outcomes? Lithium extraction in the Chilean Maricunga salt flat
abstract: With the introduction of environmental impact assessment (EIA) regimes across Latin America, public participation has become a central procedural requirement for projects with significant environmental impacts. Drawing on the Salar Blanco lithium extraction project in Chile as a case study, we examine whether the institutionalisation of procedural environmental rights is sufficient to secure substantively just outcomes in the context of critical minerals extraction for the global energy transition. abstract: Abstract This study presents a wall-modeled large-eddy simulation (WMLES) framework to simulate high-Reynolds-number daytime unstable sheared convective boundary layers (CBL). The framework is implemented using the open-source computational fluid dynamics code OpenFOAM, which employs finite-volume discretization on both uniform and non-uniform grids, and incorporates Hargreaves–Wright-based wall functions to model surface momentum and heat transfer. title: Superconducting hydrogen-powered propulsion: Enabling technologies, coupling mechanisms, and system optimization
abstract: Superconducting hydrogen-powered propulsion, synergizing the high specific energy of Liquid Hydrogen (LH 2 ) with the superior power density and efficiency of superconducting technologies, represents a transformative pathway toward zero-carbon aviation. This paper provides a critical review and a dedicated optimization framework for this emerging domain. Fundamental principles of hydrogen and superconductivity are elucidated, with the Hydrogen-Electric-Thermal (HET) coupling mechanism highlighted as the governing nexus of thermodynamic and electromagnetic synergy. abstract: Omnidirectional photonic flatbands combine enhanced density of states with angular robustness, yet integrating these properties with optical chirality remains challenging. Here, we experimentally realize an omnidirectional chiral flat-band resonance in a nonlocal silicon membrane metasurface patterned with periodic square-lattice air holes. title: Slip effects in gravity currents of power-law fluids
abstract: We investigate the propagation of gravity currents of power-law fluids spreading over a slippery substrate. We develop a one-dimensional lubrication model that incorporates a Navier slip condition at the substrate and accounts for shear-dependent viscosity. The resulting formulation shows that the current dynamics is governed by three independent parameters: the injection exponent, the rheological index, and a slip number quantifying the relative importance of substrate slip with respect to bulk viscous transport. title: Exploring wake interactions in a counter-rotating dual-rotor system for different yaw configurations: an experimental study
abstract: Abstract. As an opportunity to increase turbine and wind park efficiencies, multi and dual rotor turbines have received great attention among research and industry. Goal of this experimental study is to validate and add findings to numerical simulations on dual rotors. It will be shown that the rotational sense greatly influences the lateral interaction and hence the downstream evolution of a dual wake. abstract: Lightweight materials and structures have shown potential in addressing global-warming challenges, and one approach to developing such structures without compromising their properties is to design functionally graded materials (FGMs). Existing FGM fabrication methods via friction stir processing (FSP) require complex procedures (machining grooves to host reinforcement particles), entail extensive particle loss during fabrication, and are limited to the near-surface region. abstract: The problem of poor energy management and rapid degradation of components in single-source electric vehicles is addressed in this article. To solve this problem, a hybrid energy system combining a lithium-ion battery, supercapacitors, and hydrogen fuel cells is proposed. The vehicle's performance during acceleration and regenerative braking is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink. abstract: Embryonic development is shaped by maternal and zygotic factors but how the interplay between these factors contributes to phenotypic variability and impacts specific populations of brain cells, and subsequently neurodevelopment, remains largely unknown. Here, we reveal a double hit phenomenon that impacts microglia and microglia precursors during development. abstract: Coseismic rupture length is a key parameter for predicting earthquake magnitude and strong ground motion. In contrast to the conventional assumption of fault segmentation, multi-segment earthquakes and partially ruptured earthquakes occur. Therefore, a probabilistic approach to evaluating rupture propagation plays a crucial role in hazard assessment. abstract: The long range propagation of acoustic waves in Earth's atmosphere is sensitive to winds and temperature variations in the upper atmosphere. Thus, infrasound observations have a strong potential to improve numerical weather models by data assimilation methods. However, because acoustic waves propagate slowly, the atmospheric parameters can change during the propagation of the acoustic waves. title: Recent advances in numerical modeling of solar inertial modes
abstract: Inertial modes are low-frequency global oscillations in rotating fluids, restored by the Coriolis force. Long-term observations of horizontal flows on the solar surface have led to the detection of various inertial modes on the Sun, opening a new window into the structure and dynamics of the solar interior. title: Closed-Loop Adaptive Sampling on a Generative Ocean Model
abstract: Adaptive sampling can substantially improve the value of sparse ocean observations by directing mobile robots toward measurements that are most informative for an evolving environment. Recent learned generative ocean models can produce high-resolution forecasts and ensembles at substantially lower computational cost than traditional numerical models, creating an opportunity to use rich predictive forecasts directly in closed-loop robotic sampling. title: Climate change, sea level rise, and the agricultural revolution
abstract: We test various hypotheses for the invention and spread of agriculture: higher temperatures, increased seasonality, carbon dioxide fertilization, sea level rise, and technological progress on the extensive margin. We successfully replicate Matranga (QJE 2024). His seasonality hypothesis survives alternative data, estimators, and competing hypotheses. Population density played a role in the invention of agriculture, while spatial diffusion was important for its spread. title: Modeling Broad-Frequency-Band Water-Wave Experiments with Generalizations of the Nonlinear Schrodinger Equation
abstract: Waves generated by storms gradually disperse, forming swells that can travel thousands of kilometers across the ocean's surface. The evolution of deep-water swells, which are unaffected by the seafloor, can be modeled by the nonlinear Schrodinger (NLS) equation and its generalizations. These models typically assume that the wave trains are comprised of a narrow band of frequencies. We present measurements from a new series of laboratory experiments in which the broadbandedness is increased and show that generalizations of the NLS equation can accurately model these measurements.

abstract: The presence of extreme ocean waves poses substantial threats to the safety of marine engineering applications and navigational activities. Accurate prediction of the nonlinear wave loads on offshore structures in large-diameter cylindrical configuration, such as monopile wind turbines and platform columns, requires a robust solution to the high-order wave diffraction problem. abstract: Reconstructing physical dynamics from fixed sparse sensors and missing frames is a fundamental challenge in scientific research. Sparsity leaves large regions of the field unconstrained, making the inverse problem ill-posed: a model may fit the observed sensors while producing inaccurate off-sensor structures or unreliable predictions between support frames. abstract: We present Super Dynamics on the Cube (SD3), the first operationally-proven, fully heterogeneous-accelerated global kilometer-scale model. Through a full-stack reconstruction in native CUDA C, SD3 introduces an "Inline Physics" architecture that deeply couples its non-hydrostatic cubed-sphere dynamical core with fast physical processes. title: Fast nonparametric estimation of sparse precision matrices with a priori sparsity structure
abstract: This work describes a computational approach for rapidly estimating and characterizing the covariance structure of a Gaussian random field from a modest number of i.i.d. replicates by formulating the problem in terms of a sparse inverse Cholesky factor of the data's covariance matrix. title: Sensitivity of the IceCube atmospheric muon rate to decadal trends in the effective atmospheric temperature
abstract: Decadal changes in the Antarctic stratosphere, generally associated with ozone recovery and shifts in polar circulation, are of broad geophysical interest. However, independent long-term measurements of the atmosphere above the Antarctic interior are scarce. We assess whether the atmospheric muon rate recorded by IceCube could constrain decadal changes in the effective atmospheric temperature, $T_\mathrm{eff}$, a weighted average of temperature through the atmosphere that is most sensitive to the stratosphere. title: Which wind and solar modelling choices matter? Effects on capacity factors, energy droughts and European power system configuration
abstract: Europe's future power system will rely heavily on wind and solar power and must remain resilient during prolonged periods of low wind and solar generation, known as variable renewable energy (VRE) droughts. To capture such rare events, adequacy assessments increasingly draw on decades of weather data, but the conversion of weather into power is largely treated as fixed. It remains unclear which modelling choices in this conversion matter for representing these droughts, and whether they matter as much as the weather itself. title: Fractional quantum Hall effect at ν=1/2 in wide GaAs quantum wells: Subband structure, exact diagonalization, and the magnitude of the gap
abstract: Recent experiments on a wide GaAs quantum well report a fractional quantum Hall state at filling factor ν=1/2 with an unusually large activation gap, a sharp maximum of the gap as a function of density, and a possible transition from the non-Abelian Moore-Read Pfaffian to the Abelian Halperin 331 state. We analyze this system theoretically, with self-consistent subband calculations, exact diagonalization, and a reanalysis of the published transport data. abstract: This work investigates the appropriate initial condition for tsunami propagation that allows replacing a kinematic system with its corresponding static formulation, where the bottom is fixed at its final earthquake-induced deformation. Using the two-dimensional (2D) nonlinear shallow-water equations (NSW) and a 2D dispersive $abcd$-Boussinesq system, we prove that for the NSW system, the appropriate initial free-surface condition is exactly the final bottom deformation. title: Impact of Cumulus Parameterization and Cloud Microphysics on WRF Simulation of an Extreme Rainfall Event over Maharashtra, India: A 3 by 3 Factorial Assessment
abstract: Simulating extreme monsoon rainfall over the Konkan coast and Western Ghats remains challenging at 9 km resolution, where convection is partly resolved and partly parameterised. This study evaluates the sensitivity of Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) simulations of the 5-7 July 2026 Maharashtra rainfall event to cumulus and cloud microphysics schemes. Nine simulations employed a 3 x 3 factorial design combining WSM6, WDM6 and Thompson microphysics with Kain-Fritsch, Tiedtke and Grell-Freitas cumulus schemes. title: WRF-JAX v1.1.28: a differentiable regional weather model with fully coupled physics, numerically consistent with WRF and matching 128-process CPU performance on a single GPU
abstract: Porting a regional weather model in its entirety to a graphics processing unit (GPU) requires complete implementation of the dynamical core and all physical processes, and improved computational efficiency. This paper introduces WRF-JAX v1.1.28, a JAX reimplementation of the WRF 4.5 dynamical core and the complete CONUS physics suite. title: PyPSA-Libya: An Open-Source Energy System Model for National Decarbonization and Hydrogen Export Pathways
abstract: Libya possesses significant renewable energy potential that remains largely untapped. This paper presents PyPSA-Libya, a national-scale model built on the PyPSA-Earth framework, designed to explore optimal transition pathways for the Libyan power sector. We present two primary studies: (1) an electricity-only capacity expansion analysis comparing a zero-emission constraint against an unconstrained baseline at 36-cluster resolution, and (2) a sector-coupled hydrogen export study evaluating the levelized cost of exporting 70 TWh/year of hydrogen to Europe under three technological scenarios and

title: A unifying view of averaging for wave-mean flow decomposition
abstract: Geophysical flows are routinely decomposed into mean flow and waves, and the procedure used determines how the motion is divided between the two. Ideally, the wave and mean motions of interest evolve on distinct timescales, in which case they can be separated by taking an infinite-time average over all wave periods. title: Analysis of CONUS+ run 2: Detector performance, background model and CE$ν$NS measurement
abstract: Coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$ν$NS) provides a uniquely sensitive probe of neutrino properties, but its detection requires pushing energy thresholds to the sub-keV scale while controlling backgrounds. The CONUS+ experiment, located at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant, reported the first observation of CE$ν$NS using reactor antineutrinos in 2025. title: GOWC: an open tool for observing-conditions prediction and observation planning, tested against site monitors and an exposure-time calculator
abstract: GOWC (Global Observing-conditions Weather Catalogue) is an open web application that takes the user from a target to an exposure plan across 2,642 catalogued observatory sites. It computes seeing, airmass, extinction, precipitable water vapour, sky brightness and signal-to-noise from live Open-Meteo meteorology, including pressure-level profiles, and tests most of these outputs against an independent reference. title: Migrating a Legacy Scientific Application with an AI Coding Agent: NICAM from Fortran to Kokkos
abstract: Migrating from Fortran to C++/Kokkos broadens access to hardware accelerators through backends such as CUDA and HIP while offering greater flexibility in software design. However, legacy Fortran applications often have large codebases, making manual porting time-consuming and costly. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and AI coding agents have made large-scale code migration increasingly feasible. In this study, we ported NICAM (Nonhydrostatic ICosahedral Atmospheric Model), a legacy Fortran climate model accelerated with OpenACC, to C++/Kokkos with the assistance of Claude Code.

abstract: To understand the mantle evolution that has caused the observed histories of mare volcanism and radius change of the Moon, we developed a 3-D regional spherical shell mantle convection model with magmatism. title: WorkIng: A Real-World and Synthetic Highway Work-Zone Benchmark Dataset for Autonomous Navigation
abstract: Highway work zones are critical edge cases for autonomous vehicles (AVs), combining atypical geometries and jurisdiction-specific regulations that existing benchmarks fail to capture: real-world datasets lack 360° multi-modal, full-scene 3D work zone annotation, and no single recorded site can span the layouts and regulatory variants needed for generalizable models. We present WorkIng, a dual-domain benchmark and training resource. title: A model-based adaptive sampling framework for infectious disease surveillance
abstract: Longitudinal surveillance must choose each round's sampling design before the next observations arrive. Fixed sample-size rules treat each round as an isolated cross-sectional survey and ignore the evolving uncertainty in the epidemic process, which changes as transmission, vaccination, interventions, variants, and behavior change. We present a model-based adaptive sampling framework for choosing the next-round design. A state-space model represents the epidemic process and maps latent states to surveillance estimands. title: Two teams that cancel: a didactic analysis of a teaching progression for signed numbers from Grade 5 to Grade 7
abstract: Signed numbers make learners revise what addition, subtraction and the minus sign meant for whole numbers. This paper presents the design rationale and a critical analysis of a three-level source progression for signed numbers (Grades 5-7, nominal ages 10-13), from which French-curriculum and International Baccalaureate chapters published at https://commeunjeu.org are assembled. title: Pollutant Concentration Reconstruction in Porous Media from Localized Measurements
abstract: Reliable environmental monitoring and groundwater protection heavily rely on the ability to reconstruct full pollutant concentration fields from sparse, partial field measurements. In porous media, dissolved contaminants are transported by groundwater flow while undergoing hydrodynamic dispersion and complex chemical or biological reactions. To address practical contamination challenges, this work investigates the reconstruction of pollutant distributions using water samples collected at discrete locations in unsaturated or saturated soils via sampling tubes equipped with ceramic tips. title: An Analysis of High-Dimensional Land-Water Transitions in the Great Lakes via a Bayesian Discrepancy Model for Multinomial Data
abstract: Global water-level systems have undergone large changes in recent years. Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) land cover data can be used to monitor and understand these changes. However, such data are extremely high-dimensional making them difficult to process while accounting for all sources of uncertainty. Bayesian hierarchical models are commonly implemented using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods which can be computationally expensive for large datasets. title: A two-stage diffusion-driven morphogenesis model with evolving connectivity
abstract: Morphogenesis of diatom silica shells involves a sequence of topological transitions: initially separate ribs grow and branch, then merge through bridges, leaving a regular network of pores. Existing models based on diffusion-limited aggregation or reaction-diffusion reproduce either branching or pore formation, but not both within a single framework. Here we propose a two-stage model of diffusion-driven morphogenesis with evolving connectivity. The model is formulated on a fixed finite element mesh with a density field on an active layer. title: Chirality inversion and odd transport in a suspension of living rotors
abstract: Chiral symmetry breaking is a defining feature of life, visible at all scales from molecules to organisms. Yet how microscopic chirality propagates to shape the macroscopic properties of living matter remains poorly understood. Here, using a new experimental system of spinning microalgae, we show that a living chiral fluid behaves fundamentally differently from an externally driven one. As their density increases, cells self-assemble hydrodynamically into small rotating clusters which merge into a percolating chiral fluid. abstract: The complete Wess-Zumino (WZ) action and stress-energy tensor (SET) of the conformal anomaly in both two and four dimensions is given. title: QNETSIM for memory assisted design of satellite and hybrid quantum networks
abstract: Space-based quantum information networks require simulation tools that capture orbital dynamics, probabilistic quantum operations, and classical coordination. We introduce QNETSIM, a modular discrete-event simulator for the design and performance evaluation of satellite and hybrid space-ground quantum networks. The framework integrates orbital geometry, free-space optical and fiber channels, quantum memories, entanglement generation, and Bell-state measurements within a common event-driven architecture. title: Optimal climate policy in incomplete electricity markets
abstract: Incomplete long-term contracting in electricity markets can expose investors and consumers to inefficient levels of risk. This paper investigates how incompleteness impacts the optimal choice of climate policy. We develop a game-theoretic model of optimal policy-making in anticipation of how electricity market agents react to a given policy when gas prices and demand are uncertain and contracting is incomplete. title: Towards an Astronomical Use of New-Generation Geodetic Observations
abstract: This thesis explores the astronomical use of observations from the VLBI Global Observing System (VGOS), a next-generation geodetic network designed to improve the precision of terrestrial and celestial reference frames and Earth orientation parameters. Although primarily conceived for geodesy, its wide frequency coverage and regular monitoring of compact active galactic nuclei (AGN) provide valuable opportunities for astrophysics. title: Local Climate Change Reporting: Do Locality Framing and Interactive Maps Impact Risk Perception and Memory?
abstract: Considering the impact of local journalism in the context of climate change, this research investigates how locality framing and interactive features as important elements of digital local journalism affect news audiences. We used an article on heavy rainfall with a map visualizing data to test how local versus national framing and interactive versus static maps influence risk perception, responsibility attribution, article memory, and enjoyment in a 2 × 2 between-subjects online experiment with 632 German participants. title: Google Earth y mapas interactivos para el desarrollo de la orientación espacial y la cartografía básica: una revisión bibliográfica
abstract: La orientación espacial y la cartografía básica son aprendizajes esenciales para comprender la ubicación de personas, objetos y fenómenos en el territorio. En la educación, estas competencias permiten interpretar planos y mapas, utilizar referencias cardinales, reconocer escalas, identificar símbolos y describir relaciones entre lugares. Google Earth y los mapas interactivos ofrecen entornos digitales en los que el alumnado puede explorar el espacio desde diferentes escalas, observar imágenes satelitales, recorrer rutas, medir distancias y relacionar representaciones cartográficas con paisajes

title: Isotopic Insight Into Nitrate Sources and Cycling in Polar Sea Ice
abstract: Abstract Sea ice alters nitrate (NO 3 − ) availability in polar oceans, yet the influence of sea‐ice type on NO 3 − sources and cycling remains poorly constrained. We analyzed NO 3 − concentrations and isotopic compositions ( δ 15 N, δ 18 O, Δ 17 O) in Antarctic one‐year and Arctic multi‐year sea ice to investigate NO 3 − sources and transformation processes. title: Association patterns of ferromanganese nodule abundance with seafloor topography based on shipborne multibeam bathymetric data in the Pacific Clarion–Clipperton fracture zone and its application
abstract: Deep-sea ferromanganese nodules (FNs) are important mineral resources, and their abundance is a key parameter for resource assessment. In this study, the association between FN abundance and seafloor topography near 113 geological sampling stations in the Pacific Clarion–Clipperton Fracture Zone is investigated. Results reveal that FNs are widely distributed on gentle slope terrain with gradients of ∼0.7°–4.6°, where FN abundance is 5–20 kg/m2. title: High spatial resolution Greenland Ice Sheet mass change linked to Greenland Blocking and North Atlantic Oscillation
abstract: The low spatial resolution (300–400 km) of Gravity Recovery and Climate Experience (GRACE) and the 11-month data gap between GRACE and GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO) complicate the evaluation of long-term ice mass loss at sub-region scale. Although several studies have downscaled GRACE data for water storage evaluation, efforts to downscale ice mass change are limited. Here, we utilized multiscale geographically-weighted regression (MGWR) to improve the spatial resolution of GRACE-derived ice mass change from 0.25° to 5 km in Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS). title: Evidence of a reduced Greenland Ice Sheet during Marine Isotope Stage 3 based on modelling of in situ 14C and 10Be nuclides
abstract: The extent of the Northern Hemisphere ice sheets during Marine Isotope Stage 3 (MIS 3, 57-29 ka) is generally poorly constrained due to limited stratigraphic control, a lack of geological deposits, and inconclusive dates. For the Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS), it is typically assumed that the ice extended beyond the present-day coast during MIS 3, although some data suggest a more limited ice extent. title: Agricultural Waste-derived bio-sorbents used for the analysis of UV filters in sea water samples: An in-depth comparison with commercial sorbents
abstract: The development of sustainable sample preparation strategies is increasingly important for reducing the environmental footprint of analytical methods. In this study, waste-derived biosorbents were investigated as low-cost and green alternatives to commercial materials for the extraction of organic UV filters from sea water samples. Banana (BAN), lime, orange, and pomegranate peels, alongside with activated carbon derived from waste chestnut shells (ACCHE), were evaluated for the extraction efficiency of oxybenzone, enzacamene, avobenzone, octocrylene, and ethylhexyl salicylate. title: Seasonality and the effect of a marine heatwave on the metabolism of Red Sea coral reefs
abstract: Coral reefs are in global decline due to climate change, shifting reef ecosystems from 24-hour net heterotrophy to autotrophy, altering carbon cycles and reducing resilience to stressors. Red Sea coral reefs experience some of the warmest waters globally, exceeding 30 °C and reaching up to 38 °C on reef flats during summer. Despite these extreme environmental conditions, the metabolism of Red Sea coral reefs remains understudied. title: Marine Heatwave and Extreme Hypoxia Coincide With Rapid Coral Bleaching and Mortality on a Central Red Sea Coral Reef
abstract: ABSTRACT Coral bleaching and mortality are commonly associated with heat stress during marine heatwaves (MHWs), yet attributing these responses solely to heat stress may overlook the complexity of contemporary MHWs. Here, we document a severe MHW affecting a central Red Sea reef in mid‐2024 that coincided with repeated nighttime low‐oxygen events. abstract: This study focuses on optimizing the energy-absorbing characteristics of bio-inspired thin-walled structures (BTS) based on naturally inspired structural features. Three design parameters are investigated: wall thickness t, inner diameter d, and number of diaphragms n. title: Holocene and last interglacial relative sea level changes in Sri Lanka based on geological indicators
abstract: Earth’s climate oscillations between interglacial and glacial periods have driven significant sea level changes. Sri Lanka, located in the Indian Ocean, provides an ideal natural setting for studying paleo sea level changes. This study compiles 92 Holocene sea level records and identifies last interglacial stratigraphic evidence from Point Kudrimalai to reconstruct paleo sea level fluctuations in Sri Lanka. abstract: Abstract Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) forms the largest reservoir of reduced carbon in the ocean, yet its bioavailability and the microbial processes governing its transformation remain poorly constrained. Traditional seawater batch cultures have been indispensable for measuring bioavailable DOC (BDOC), but their long incubation times and limited throughput constrain comparisons across environmental gradients and treatments. title: Stony coral symbioses show variable responses to future ocean conditions
abstract: Coral reefs support over a quarter of marine species and nearly a billion people worldwide but are also among the ecosystems most threatened by anthropogenic impacts. There is long-standing debate about whether coral symbioses will be disrupted or respond adaptively under future ocean conditions. Using a factorial 2.5-year future-ocean mesocosm experiment across eight coral species representing the major coral lineages, we tracked symbiont community shifts within replicate fragments from the same individual coral. title: A Topo - Bathymetric Data Integration Approach to Study the Dynamics in the Danube Delta
abstract: Accurate acquisition of topographic data at the land - water interface is a fundamental step in bridging the gap between terrestrial and hydrographic datasets. In the complex fluvial environment of the Danube Delta, achieving a unitary representation of the riverine relief is hindered by dynamic morphological features and significant water - level fluctuations. title: Tissue-specific occurrence and characteristics of microplastics in marine fish from coastal China
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) in marine fish has raised concerns regarding potential human dietary exposure. This study investigated the occurrence of MPs in the muscle, gastrointestinal tract, and gill tissues of 131 marine fish (19 species) collected from the Bohai Sea in 2022 and from the East China Sea and South China Sea in 2023, with water, sediment, and feed samples. abstract: The United Nations World Ocean Assessment II (WOA II) synthesizes oceanographic research through 49 chapters citing over 3500 scientific articles. Exploring a corpus of this scale requires users to connect its document structure with topical, temporal, citation, and geographic information. title: Status of Common Salt in Seawater: Students’ Misconceptions Unlocked
abstract: This study investigated chemistry students’ misconceptions about common salt in seawater and their implications for the chemistry education curriculum. Using a phenomenological design within the Model of Educational Reconstruction framework, the research engaged forty-five (45) first-year chemistry students at the University of Education, Winneba (UEW), Ghana. abstract: Abstract. abstract: ABSTRACT Estuarine–coastal systems exhibit strong hydrographic gradients and vertical heterogeneity, yet the spatial distribution and vertical characteristics of depth-resolved primary productivity (DRPP) remain insufficiently understood. Here, seasonal field observations were combined with a DRPP model to assess temporal, water-mass, and vertical variability in phytoplankton productivity across the Yangtze River Estuary-Coastal Continuum. abstract: Abstract Most studies rely on course-resolution satellite-derived sea surface temperature (SST) data to analyze Marine Heatwaves (MHW) in coral reef regions, limiting their ability to capture fine-scale thermal variability. Our study integrated satellite SST with high-resolution in situ temperature and coral cover data from six sites across three geomorphic reef types (fringing reef, backreef, forereef) in Moorea reef. abstract: Abstract. In many glacial settings, winter outflows of proglacial water create stratified domed ice structures on glacial forefields. These structures, called naledi, provide an opportunity to characterise the solute fluxes of hydrological systems in winter which are poorly constrained compared to summer outflows which are dominated by supraglacial meltwater input. abstract: INTRODUCTION: Neurosurgical advancements in Parkinson's disease (PD) treatment can significantly improve symptoms. However, the use of these modalities in Southeast Asia (SEA) faces barriers. METHODS: We conducted an online cross-sectional survey among movement disorder specialists in SEA. Respondents provided country-level estimates of utilization, targets, financial coverage, and limitations in the utilization of four neurosurgical modalities. abstract: Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) is an increasingly popular tool for marine mammal monitoring. abstract: This paper articulates the conceptual and formal architecture of Oceanic Narratology within contemporary Indian English fiction, challenging the entrenched land-centric paradigms of postcolonial literary criticism. abstract: ABSTRACT Large‐scale biodiversity patterns are increasingly reshaped by climate change, yet long‐term empirical comparisons across aquatic systems remain scarce. Using 3–4 decades of incidence data from fish monitoring in Sweden we analyzed long‐term trends in species richness (SR), turnover, beta diversity, functional characteristics and individual species trajectories, for lakes of different sizes and coastal areas representing different salinity conditions. title: Movements and habitat use of the invasive blue crab Callinectes sapidus in Mediterranean coastal lagoon
abstract: Abstract The Atlantic blue crab ( Callinectes sapidus ), an invasive and ecologically impactful decapod species, has rapidly proliferated across the Mediterranean Sea, prompting concerns over its effects on native ecosystems and local economies. Despite its growing presence, knowledge of its behavioural ecology in Mediterranean coastal systems remains limited. This study presents the first acoustic telemetry-based assessment of C. sapidus within its invasive range, focusing on movement patterns, activity levels, and habitat preferences in Biguglia Lagoon, Corsica (Northwestern Mediterranean).

title: A physical coastal vulnerability index for site-specific assessment
abstract: Assessment of coastal vulnerability is essential for protecting coastal areas from natural hazards and extreme weather events. In the United Kingdom (UK), low-lying coastal zones frequently experience inundation, flooding, landslides, coastal erosion, and cliff failures, all of which are intensified by climate change. Although the UK possesses one of Europe's longest and most geomorphologically diverse coastlines, this diversity limits the effectiveness of standard assessment tools such as the Coastal Vulnerability Index (CVI), which often fail to capture site-specific characteristics. abstract: Understanding coral community composition is essential for reef conservation, particularly in data-limited tropical regions such as Indonesia. This study compares genus-level coral detections from Underwater Photo Transect surveys and environmental DNA metabarcoding on nearshore reefs of Gili Genting and Gili Labak, Madura, Indonesia. abstract: Abstract Ocean acidification threatens marine calcifiers, but the independent effects of seawater pH and total alkalinity on shell formation remain poorly understood. Here, we experimentally decoupled pH and alkalinity to examine their effects on shell growth and density in the large benthic foraminifer Amphisorus kudakajimensis . abstract: Abstract The Yangtze River Estuary (YRE) serves as a critical land‐ocean interface where hydrodynamic mixing and biogeochemical processes jointly regulate dissolved organic matter (DOM) cycling. Here, untargeted metabolomics was applied to investigate the structural diversity and spatial variation of DOM in surface waters across the freshwater, transition and adjacent marine zones of the YRE. abstract: Abstract The Deep Scattering Layer (DSL), formed as an antipredator refuge, shapes the ecology of the mesopelagic system. abstract: Ocean acidification and warming (OAW) are expected to alter physiology, growth and reproduction of marine ectotherms, yet their combined effects on life-history traits remain unresolved, particularly under poorly defined future food conditions. title: Global Patterns in the Nutrient Composition Delivered by Seabirds to Coastal and Island Ecosystems
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Consumer‐mediated nutrient dynamics are crucial for sustaining ecosystems. While most research has focused on the magnitude of seabird‐derived nutrient fluxes, the role of species and diet composition in shaping nutrient quality remains largely unexplored. title: The Influence of the Antarctic Circumpolar Deep Water on Deep‐Sea Eukaryotic Biodiversity and Distribution in the Western Pacific Ocean
abstract: The Antarctic region, a centre of biodiversity origin, influences deep-sea ecosystems by supplying species to distant regions. Understanding the influence of Antarctic Upper Circumpolar Deep Water (UCDW) on deep-sea eukaryotic diversity is therefore essential for outlining global biodiversity patterns. Our results showed the UCDW community exhibited ~1.5-fold higher taxonomic and phylogenetic diversity than the Caroline Basin control community and contained a substantial proportion of unique taxa across multiple eukaryotic lineages. title: Paleosalinity of Ediacaran fossils in South Australia
abstract: Ediacaran fossils of South Australia have been interpreted in two contrasting ways: marine invertebrates vs soil lichens. Paleosols with desert roses and eolian interbeds with adhesion warts are two lines of evidence, among many, for non-marine deposition. Geochemical paleosalinity indices provide new tests of these divergent interpretations. Boron content is low in freshwater, but high in marine rocks, and as a paleosalinity proxy can be compared with gallium (freshwater has B/Ga <3). Boron can also be compared with potassium, after correcting for burial alteration using Weaver crystallinity

title: From Water Scarcity to Resilience: A Policy-Oriented Framework for Community-Based Drought Management in Southeast Asia
abstract: Drought has evolved into a persistent governance challenge across Southeast Asia. Its impacts cannot be attributed to climatic variability alone. Rather, they emerge from the interaction between climate change, fragmented institutional arrangements, and intensifying competition over water resources. Together, these dynamics undermine long-term water security and disproportionately affect rural livelihoods. title: Local hydrology and seasonality outweigh the influence of Phragmites australis on coastal bacterial communities across two Baltic Sea bays
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aquatic macrophytes shape microbial habitats in shallow coastal systems, yet the relative influence of plant-driven effects versus local hydrology and seasonal environmental variation remains poorly resolved. We investigated how Phragmites australis influences sediment, water, and phyllosphere bacterial communities in two shallow Baltic Sea bays, Haapsalu and Pärnu, that are approximately 83 km from each other. title: Circular Economy Practices and Firm Financial Performance: Empirical Evidence from FMCG Companies in Southeast Asia
abstract: This article examines how circular economy practices influence financial performance and market valuation among fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies in Southeast Asia. It focuses on two operationally consequential dimensions: waste-management practices and compliance with green regulation. These dimensions are considered alongside resource efficiency, circular product and packaging design, reverse logistics, and the quality of environmental disclosure. title: A compact set of sea star footprint proteins mediates the adhesion of Asterina gibbosa
abstract: Abstract Sea stars achieve strong yet reversible underwater adhesion using a duo-gland system in their tube feet. While adhesive footprint proteins (Sfps) are well characterized in Asterias rubens, comparable molecular data for other asteroids are limited. Here, we generated a high-quality de novo genome assembly of the starlet cushion star, Asterina gibbosa, enabling full-length gene identification of Sfps. title: Stable Isotope Research for Human Bioarchaeology in Southeast Asia: A Review of Research Trends, Gaps, and Opportunities
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite the increasing number of studies undertaking isotopic analyses on archaeological material, some regions of the world and certain research foci remain underresearched and underrepresented. One of these regions is Southeast Asia, where bioarchaeological research was only comparatively recently established compared with other regions of the world. title: A biofilm-derived peptide as an underwater adhesive
abstract: Abstract Wet adhesives that perform under water have broad applications in industrial and biomedical settings. To date, molecular designs for underwater adhesives have largely been inspired by marine animals including mussels and barnacles. Here, we propose bacterial biofilms as an alternative source of inspiration for underwater adhesives. Specifically, we demonstrate the application potential of a peptide derived from biofilms formed by the notorious pathogen Vibrio cholerae . title: Charting the Voyages of Acinetobacter baumannii in Southeast Asia: Mapping the Regional Genomic Landscape
abstract: ABSTRACT Acinetobacter baumannii is a critical‐priority nosocomial pathogen, yet its genomic epidemiology in Southeast Asia remains fragmented. We analysed publicly available genomes to define the regional A. baumannii population structure, resistome, mobile genetic elements, and phage defence repertoire. title: Seasonal timing separates algal bloom records from marine heatwave exposure
abstract: Abstract Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are increasingly invoked in explanations of coastal algal blooms, yet shared seasonality can confound apparent MHW–bloom coincidence. We assembled a source‐resolved catalogue of 48 algal bloom records and a satellite‐derived regional daily sea surface temperature series for Sansha Bay, China, to evaluate bloom‐record timing against MHW exposure during 2005–2020. title: Shell hash promotes growth in Pacific littleneck clams ( Leukoma staminea ) by altering pore water chemistry
abstract: Abstract. Bivalves that build calcium carbonate skeletons are at particular risk from ocean acidification, and mitigation strategies will be needed to keep coastal populations healthy. It can be energetically costly for organisms like clams and mussels to build their shells under low pH conditions, and acidification can lead to shell dissolution. Adding crushed shells (shell hash) to beach sediments, a practice used by some Indigenous communities and aquaculturists, may mitigate the negative effects of ocean acidification by altering the chemistry of the pore fluids they live in. title: DELINEATING THE INTELLECTUAL STRUCTURE OF SOCIO ECONOMIC RUBBER FARMING RESEARCH: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS
abstract: Over the past twenty years, increasing worries about rural livelihoods, market instability, and changes in land use have triggered a rise in socio-economic studies on natural rubber farming. Understanding the findings of this growing body of research is crucial. This bibliometric analysis examines 226 publications indexed in Scopus from 2006 to 2025, aiming to chart the productivity trends, thematic structure, and collaborative dynamics within this research area. title: Pathways of positive youth development, hope, and life satisfaction: A multi‐country study among Southeast Asian youth
abstract: Positive Youth Development (PYD) has gained prominence through models such as the 7Cs-competence, confidence, connection, character, caring, contribution, and creativity-yet relatively little is known about how these dimensions function in Southeast Asian contexts, where young people navigate diverse cultural values, socio-economic structures, and access to resources. Further, although PYD attributes are linked to life satisfaction, limited work has explored mechanisms that may explain these associations. title: Anthropocene mineralogy and geochemistry of nearshore surface sediments from urban-influenced coastal zones of Athens (Greece) and Fujairah (UAE)
abstract: Abstract Coastal zones adjacent to urban areas and harbors are often impacted by marine traffic, shipyard activities, sewage discharge, and waste accumulation. These pressures interact with seafloor sediments composed mainly of inorganic particles, mixed with organic matter and marine biota. While most sediments contain common minerals such as quartz, clays, and Fe oxides/oxyhydroxides, increasing attention has focused on "Anthropocene minerals" introduced since the Industrial Revolution and the Atomic Age. title: PREFERENCES OF HIPPOCAMPUS GUTTULATUS INDIVIDUALS FROM THE BLACK SEA FOR IRON AND STAINLESS STEEL ARTIFICIAL REEFS
abstract: The implementation of artificial habitats made from recycled materials can significantly enhance marine habitats for seahorses and other species, especially in areas where the natural habitat has been altered by anthropogenic factors such as pollution, trawling, beach enlargement, eutrophication, invasive species, and climate change. title: Fine‐Scale Variability of Cold‐Water Coral and Sponge Communities on Protected Northeast Pacific Seamounts
abstract: ABSTRACT Cold‐water corals and sponges (CWCS) on Northeast Pacific seamounts form important biogenic habitat that is intersected by a broad oxygen minimum zone (OMZ) and exposed to ongoing deoxygenation. Many seamounts in this region lie within marine protected areas (MPAs), making an understanding of fine‐scale community structure particularly relevant for conservation and management. title: Spatial and Seasonal Structuring of Bacterial Communities and Putative Pathogen‐Associated Bacterial Taxa at Four Korean Coastal Locations
abstract: Coastal marine environments are dynamic transition zones where offshore water masses and terrestrial inputs shape microbial community structure. However, standardized comparisons of bacterial communities across geographically distinct Korean coastal waters remain limited, constraining the development of microbial baselines for long-term monitoring. Surface seawater bacterial communities from four Korean coastal locations were analysed using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. title: AIS-based noise models underestimate vessel noise exposure risk to marine mammals
abstract: Vessels are the dominant source of anthropogenic underwater noise, with well-documented effects on marine mammal behaviour and physiology that may ultimately compromise individual fitness. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) provides standardized, global, high-resolution positional information for most commercial and passenger vessels, making AIS-based noise models widely used to assess exposure risk. abstract: Chemical defenses shape ecological interactions across marine food webs, yet their reproductive and evolutionary consequences in macroalgae-grazer systems remain largely unexplored. Here, we integrate physiological, developmental and molecular assays to investigate how secondary metabolites from two brown algae, Ericaria brachycarpa and E. crinita, modulate reproduction and early development of their natural grazer sea urchin Arbacia lixula. title: Distribution of Seahorses ( Hippocampus spp.) Along the Brazilian Coast Highlights Habitat Associations and Regions of Conservation Interest
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the geographic distribution and habitat associations of seahorses is fundamental for developing effective conservation strategies, yet comprehensive syntheses at national scales remain scarce. Brazil encompasses a wide diversity of coastal and marine ecosystems inhabited by three seahorse species ( Hippocampus reidi , H. erectus and Hippocampus patagonicus ), but available information has remained fragmented across scientific publications, museum collections, technical reports and monitoring programmes. title: From co‐occurrence to temporal coupling in a coral defender guild
abstract: Coral‐dwelling decapods can improve host fitness by defending corals against corallivores and sediment accumulation, yet the temporal dynamics linking co‐resident defenders remain poorly understood. Guard crabs Trapezia and snapping shrimp Alpheus provide complementary benefits to pocilloporid corals, and previous, largely cross‐sectional work has reported behavioral accommodation, non‐random co‐occurrence, and effects on host‐associated community assembly, patterns that suggest their association reflects facilitation instead of independent use of shared habitat. title: C:H:N:O:P stoichiometry and oxygen demand of marine organic matter are driven by phytoplankton ecophysiology
abstract: Although the hydrogen and oxygen content of marine phytoplankton plays a critical role in determining oceanic O 2 consumption rates, shaping habitat for anaerobic metabolism, they are often assumed to be constant in biogeochemical studies, resulting in biased estimates of respiration rates. Here, by simulating phytoplankton allocation in a general circulation model, we predict latitudinal variations in phytoplankton C:H:N:O:P composition and corresponding O 2 demand. title: Assessing the spatio-temporal variability and environmental drivers of European anchovy Engraulis encrasicolus eggs distribution in the gulf of Cadiz (SW Spain)
abstract: Quantifying the spawning area of marine species is essential for developing management strategies that ensure the sustainability of natural populations. The European anchovy ( Engraulis encrasicolus ), one of the most abundant pelagic fish species in the Gulf of Cadiz (GoC), spawns in this region due to favorable environmental conditions. However, understanding the spatiotemporal variability of its spawning area remains a key gap in improving management strategies. title: Eddy‐Induced Forcing Reshapes Taxon‐Specific Copepod Gut Contents and Feeding Preference in the South China Sea
abstract: Abstract Mesoscale eddies reshape pelagic habitats by modifying water‐column structure, primary production, and plankton distributions, yet how these changes affect zooplankton feeding across taxa and depths remains poorly understood. To address this gap, we tracked a cyclonic‐anticyclonic eddy pair and sampled zooplankton across cyclonic, frontal, anticyclonic, and outside‐eddy regions in the northwestern South China Sea.
