title: Critical Thermal Tolerance and Physiological Stress in the Estuarine Catfish, Mystus gulio
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding critical thermal tolerance and physiological stress responses is crucial to evaluating fish resilience to environmental changes. This study evaluated the critical thermal maximum (CTmax) and minimum (CTmin) under normoxic (sufficient oxygen supply; dissolved oxygen (DO) > 6.0 mg/L) and hypoxic (deficient oxygen supply; DO < 2.0 mg/L) conditions in long‐whiskered catfish ( Mystus gulio ), a commercially important, climate‐sensitive estuarine species from the Bay of Bengal. title: A 4000-year record of parallel collapse in the ecological niche of Black Sea top predators
abstract: Marine ecosystems face multifaceted threats stemming from historical overexploitation and environmental degradation. Despite existing research, there are notable gaps in understanding the long-term dietary dynamics of marine organisms in the context of anthropogenic impacts. title: A coastal beach seed bank shows high diversity, but low similarity to the adjacent forest vegetation in an Amazonia Marine Extractive Reserve
abstract: Abstract Marine Extractive Reserves (RESEX-Mar) play a fundamental role in conserving Amazoniana coastal biodiversity, maintaining ecosystem services, and supporting the livelihoods of traditional communities. However, the relationship between seed taxonomy and adjacent vegetation remains poorly understood. This study evaluated whether the taxonomic composition of seeds deposited on the beaches of the RESEX-Mar in the municipality of Soure, Brazilian Amazon, reflects the composition and diversity of the adjacent vegetation. title: Culture and Isolation of Bacteria Associated with Mediterranean Corals
abstract: ABSTRACT Corals harbor a diverse bacterial community that facilitates adaptation and sustains their health. In coral holobiont research, culture-independent approaches have transformed the existing paradigm. Molecular techniques, such as metabarcoding, revealed a high diversity of previously unrecognized bacterial symbionts. Coral microbiota characterization has relied on these techniques over the last decade, but relying solely on them does not provide a detailed understanding of the dynamics of the coral holobiont complex. title: Tubastraea coccinea (Cnidaria: Anthozoa) is the globally dispersed species of Sun Coral
abstract: Species of the genus Tubastraea (sun corals) have dispersed globally over recent decades, but morphological trait identification has led to taxonomic confusion, with multiple authors proposing conflicting species identifications due to high morphological plasticity and overlapping diagnostic traits. We combined global-scale molecular phylogenetics with chromosome-level genome assemblies to resolve this taxonomic issue. title: Effects of Sustained Tensile Stress on Localized Corrosion Evolution of 5A06 Aluminum Alloy in Natural Seawater
abstract: ABSTRACT In marine engineering structures, components made of 5A06 aluminum alloy are often subjected simultaneously to sustained tensile stress and corrosion in natural seawater; their initial surface condition may further influence the initiation and propagation of localized corrosion. abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the environmental niche and potential distribution of the Pacific sierra ( Scomberomorus sierra ) is critical for fisheries management across the eastern Pacific Ocean (EPO). title: Morphological characterization of the Hypanus guttatus (Bloch and Schneider 1801) female reproductive tract in the Amazonian estuarine gradient during the non-gestational stage
abstract: Abstract Stingrays exhibit a wide diversity of reproductive strategies and modes of embryonic nutrition, yet comprehensive morphological descriptions of the female reproductive system remain scarce for many marine species. The present study characterizes in detail the macroscopic and microscopic morphology of the female reproductive tract of the marine stingray Hypanus guttatus , collected from an Amazonian estuary in northern Brazil. title: Documenting the Undocumented: The Case for Integrating Local Water Ownership Into Marine Governance in Åland
abstract: Efforts to protect marine and coastal environments in Åland, Finland, increasingly emphasise integrating local water ownership into formal governance. This study examines how such integration can be strengthened, particularly in contexts where privately owned coastal waters and established management traditions are highly significant. By using Avelino’s empowerment framework, with a mixed-methods approach, the study addresses two questions: What approaches can be employed to identify biologically valuable marine areas in Åland that are not currently recognised or justified by the government? title: Coupled carbonate-shale thallium isotopes reveal the evolution of deep-marine anoxia during the end-Permian mass extinction
abstract: Ocean anoxia played a key role in the end-Permian mass extinction, the most severe biotic crisis in Earth's history, yet reconstructions of oxygenation through this event have lacked a focus on deep-water oxygen loss. Thallium isotopes, which track deep-ocean oxygenation via manganese oxide burial, offer a potential solution but have only been applied to siliciclastic sections, limiting spatial and temporal coverage. abstract: Abstract The most widespread animal life cycle includes a planktonic larval stage that is environmentally induced to settle and rapidly metamorphose into a benthic juvenile. Although this transition is critical for survival, how planetary cues such as light interact with local ecological signals to prepare the genome for such rapid reprogramming remains poorly understood. abstract: Marine sediments remain among the least characterised components of the Antarctic microbial landscape. Here, bacterial communities were investigated in sediments from three sites within the Antarctic Specially Protected Area No. 161, in Terra Nova Bay (Ross Sea, Antarctica). Samples were collected during the XXXIII Italian Antarctic Expedition. title: Assessing Diversity, Carbon Stock Quantification and Economic Valuation of Mangrove Forest along the Coastal Areas of Davao Oriental, Philippines
abstract: This study assessed the diversity, aboveground carbon stock, and economic value of mangrove forests along the coastal areas of Davao Oriental, Philippines. Field-based mangrove inventories were conducted using three 100-m transects comprising 20 plots and a total sampled area of 2000 m². The sampling was intended to characterize the mangrove community at the assessed field sites and is not treated as statistically representative of all mangrove forests in the province. title: Cascading impacts of Atlantic meridional overturning circulation weakening and collapse on marine biogeochemistry
abstract: Abstract As anthropogenic emissions continue to increase Earth’s surface temperature, the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is at risk of weakening substantially and crossing a tipping point. Then, multiple Earth system components may be significantly and irreversibly altered. abstract: Introduction: Coral reefs are essential ecosystems for the functioning of the planet and human well-being, providing three-dimensional habitats for a great diversity of marine life and multiple ecological, economic, and cultural services. Coral reefs are constructed by hermatypic corals, which maintain a symbiotic relationship with dinoflagellates of the Symbiodiniaceae family, which provide them with up to 90-95% of their energy in exchange for shelter and nutrients. title: Analysis of Coastal Abrasion Vulnerability at Pasar Bawah Beach, South Bengkulu, Using Landsat Imagery
abstract: Recently, Pasar Bawah Beach has been facing the risk of rapid abrasion, threatening damage to the infrastructure around the beach. This study aims to identify the rate of abrasion and map changes in the coastline and the characteristics of parameters that influence abrasion at Pasar Bawah Beach in Manna, South Bengkulu. title: Riverine biogeochemistry from the Andes to the ocean: longitudinal patterns along a Mediterranean Andean catchment in central Chile
abstract: Abstract. Rivers act as dynamic connectors between terrestrial and marine ecosystems, transporting and transforming materials along the aquatic continuum. We investigated longitudinal biogeochemical patterns across the Rapel catchment (central Chile) by integrating dissolved organic matter (DOM) characterization, dissolved metals and nutrients, and microbial community profiling from the Andean headwaters to the Pacific Ocean. title: Hydrogeochemistry and suitability assessment of surface and groundwater for drinking, irrigation, and corrosive potential in the Coastal District Porbandar of Gujarat, India
abstract: Abstract Surface and groundwater resources in semi-arid coastal regions are highly susceptible to salinity buildup, hydrochemical changes, and human activities, which compromise their usability for drinking, irrigation, and industry. This study assesses the hydrogeochemistry, spatial variation, and suitability of surface and groundwater in Gujarat's Coastal District Porbandar (CDP). title: Temperature-induced shift in the rare microbiota of the sponge Haliclona
abstract: ABSTRACT Ocean warming is currently leading to distributional shifts of species and an alternation of coastal communities. Vulnerable species that are most sensitive to ocean warming are able to use several acclimation mechanisms, with one of the fastest being a shift in and shuffling of their partnerships with symbiotic microorganisms. title: International legal challenges and State practice relevant to marine environmental protection obligation in the context of climate change
abstract: Abstract Given the unprecedented climate-induced impacts on the marine environment, the conduct-oriented marine environmental protection obligation (MEPO) has become highly inadequate. This article argues for a normative evolution of the obligation in response to the global climate crisis. By examining key advisory opinions of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea and the International Court of Justice, this study analyzes the interpretation of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea as a dynamic instrument. title: Preferences of Australian and Chinese tourists for behavioural restrictions during snorkelling in Fiji: implications for marine environmental conservation
abstract: This study explores the preferences of Australian and Chinese tourists for restrictions on marine-based tourism activities in Fiji. Given the importance of marine ecosystems in the Pacific, for both ecological and economic outcomes, and potential consequences of tourists on these systems, restrictions on tourist behaviour during recreational activities could be important policy mechanisms. title: Phenol degradation and synthetic dye decolorization by marine plastisphere-associated bacteria: Implications for mitigating environmental pollutants
abstract: The plastisphere is a unique microhabitat that supports diverse microbial communities, including bacteria with potential bioremediation capabilities. This study aims to isolate and characterize phenol- and synthetic dye-degrading bacteria inhabiting the marine plastisphere along the Cochin coast, Kerala, India. title: Observations of Mammalian Predation on Pacific Sleeper Sharks in Southeast Alaska
abstract: The predator-prey relationship between marine mammals and sharks may not be as well defined as originally believed. Both groups can be either predator or prey. In the case of the Pacific sleeper shark, previous studies have documented the sharks predating upon juvenile Steller sea lions and scavenging whale falls, while other studies have reported offshore killer whales predating upon Pacific sleeper shark. title: Feeding, growth, and hatch timing of juvenile chub and blue mackerels in a coastal nursery of western Japan
abstract: Early life history traits strongly influence survival and recruitment in small pelagic fishes, yet regional variation in these traits remains poorly understood for young-of-the-year (age-0) mackerels in Kuroshio-influenced coastal systems. We examined diet composition, onset of piscivory, otolith-based growth, and hatch-date composition of juvenile chub mackerel Scomber japonicus and blue mackerel Scomber australasicus collected from the Uwa Sea, western Japan, in 2021, 2022, and 2025. title: Governing seawater desalination: Connecting technical fixes and socio-political realities
abstract: As the global water stress intensifies, seawater desalination (SWD) is increasingly deployed as a supply-side strategy for enhancing freshwater availability. Critical scholarship has questioned whether technically oriented approaches to desalination adequately address the socio-political drivers of water scarcity and the governance conditions shaping desalination policy. Metabarcoding as a Tool in Characterizing Nordic Deep‐Sea and Arctic Benthic Ecosystems
abstract: ABSTRACT Deep‐sea and Arctic soft‐bottom organism communities remain severely underexplored. Sediment environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding can complement existing survey methods, but its ability to discriminate among habitats and to reliably assign taxa must be critically evaluated. Here, we analyzed sediment samples from 10 areas in the Nordic Seas and adjacent Arctic, including the Arctic Mid‐Ocean Ridge (AMOR), continental slope habitats, and abyssal environments. title: Development and application of cryomilled heterogeneous micro- and nanoplastics labeled with upconverting nanoparticles for tracking interactions with freshwater plankton
abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics ( MNPs ) pose environmental and health risks, yet their detection and tracking in biological matrices remain challenging. To facilitate the study of their fate, model luminescent MNPs are frequently used; however, they often lack environmental relevance and are limited by the drawbacks of conventional fluorescence labeling. Here, we developed more realistic, non-uniform, and luminescent MNP models – top-down-prepared polystyrene MNPs labeled with upconverting nanoparticles ( UCNPs ) – to track their distribution, uptake, and effects in freshwater microalgae and rotifers
institutions: Centro de Estudos do Ambiente e do Mar

title: Cutaway Single-Cylinder Marine Diesel Engine
abstract: This study aimed to design, fabricate, and utilize a cut-away single-cylinder marine diesel engine as an instructional device to enhance the theoretical and laboratory learning experiences of Bachelor of Industrial Technology Management (BITM) students. Specifically, it sought to improve the instructional materials of the Engineering and Technology Department and supplement the existing equipment in the BITM laboratory. title: The evolution of Upper Circumpolar Deep Water in the Southwest Pacific Ocean since 30 ka: evidence from Neodymium isotopes
abstract: The geometry and ventilation of upper deep-water masses in the Pacific sector of the Southern Ocean are critical to glacial carbon storage, yet their evolution since the Last Glacial Maximum remains poorly constrained. Here, we present the foraminiferal neodymium isotope composition (ε Nd ) from core MD97-2115 (eastern Chatham Rise, 2160 m water depth), which is located at the present-day boundary between Upper Circumpolar Deep Water (UCDW) and modified North Pacific Deep Water (mNPDW) in the Southwest Pacific, to reconstruct the upper deep-water mass changes since 30 ka. title: Public perceptions and knowledge of nationwide shellfish reef restoration
abstract: Large-scale restoration of coastal and marine ecosystems is increasingly used to address biodiversity loss, yet its long-term success depends on public awareness, understanding, and support. Despite rapid expansion in shellfish reef restoration worldwide, little is known about how the public perceive these ecosystems or the value of restoring them. We surveyed 867 coastal and metropolitan residents living within ~50 km of shellfish reef restorations across Australia to assess public knowledge, perceptions, and perceived benefits of shellfish restoration. title: Geochemical and granulometric fingerprints of 8200 years of westerly wind variability in inner‐fjord lake sediments from Svalbard
abstract: The Arctic is warming faster than any other region on Earth. As sea-ice diminishes, surface boundary conditions (roughness and air-sea coupling) change and open-water fetch increases, potentially strengthening the effective wind forcing on Arctic coasts. These changes can be recorded in lake sediments through the deposition of wind-blown grains and elements, offering insights into past wind and climate dynamics. We reconstruct ca. 8,200 yrs of wind-climate variability using laminated sediments from a closed-basin lake in the Central part of the High Arctic Svalbard archipelago. By integrating

title: The Noisy Work of Uncertainty Visualization
abstract: Better representation of the uncertainty in a data visualization is a focus of recent research activity. A problem with the current literature is that there is a lack of clarity about the definition of uncertainty and what it means to represent it in a plot. This confusion has led to conflicting results in the literature, especially in experiments that assess the effectiveness of different uncertainty representations. In this review, we summarize the current literature, provide workable definitions, and illustrate these definitions with examples. In doing so, we ask what it really takes to ach
journal: Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application

title: Topographical Determinism and Cultural Landscapes: a GIS-based Spatial Analysis of the Religious Triad in Nha Trang City, Vietnam
abstract: This study examines the spatial relationships among three religious landmarks in Nha Trang, Vietnam: the Ponagar Cham temple complex, Long Son Pagoda and its hilltop Buddha statue, and the Catholic Stone Church. It combines interpretation of historical cartography, reported Google Earth Pro measurements, and a cultural reading of mountain–water landscapes. The supplied architectural azimuths are 81.64∘ for Ponagar, 123.92∘ for the Buddha statue, and 348.04∘ for the church. title: When marine turtles and vessels overlap: Mapping encounter risk along Florida's Atlantic coast
abstract: Abstract Marine turtle encounters with vessels can alter their behavior and habitat use and may lead to collisions causing injury and/or mortality. Despite existing protective measures, recreational vessel activity in coastal areas remains a significant threat due to limited understanding of the spatiotemporal dynamics of turtle–vessel interactions at regional scales. To address this, we assessed the spatiotemporal overlap between turtles and vessels along a section of Florida's Atlantic coast, an area with high incidence of stranded turtles with vessel strike injury (VSI) and investigated whi

title: Dynamics of diffusive-convective staircases in the ocean
abstract: Diffusive-convective (DC) staircases in the ocean are observed across a wide range of settings, but their formation, structure and persistence are not fully understood. Theories for DC staircases are reviewed to identify mechanisms governing their development and evolution. Staircase evolution through layer merging and possibly interface splitting, including the relationship to background turbulence, is assessed. Oceanographic examples illustrate the variety of settings in which DC staircases are found, and how they can persist under weak turbulence but are disrupted when turbulence becomes su
journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A Mathematical Physical and Engineering Sciences

title: Negative Residual Topography in Global Back‐Arc Basins Scales With Slab Dip
abstract: Abstract Dynamic topography above subduction zones is widely inferred, but its magnitude and controls remain poorly constrained at the global scale. Here, we estimate residual topography across a range of back‐arc basins by correcting bathymetry for sediment loading, crustal structure, and lithospheric age, and compare the anomalies with slab geometry and subduction parameters. Most basins show negative residual topography, and the anomalies become more negative with increasing slab dip. title: Cryptic Carriers of Resistance: A Metagenomic Sentinel Case of Vibrio and CARB-7 β-Lactamase in a Lagos Marine Crab
abstract: Metagenomic characterization of foodborne pathogens in Nigerian seafood remains critically limited. This sentinel case investigated Vibrio species in a single crab (Callinectes spp.) from Eleko Beach, Lagos, Nigeria, using shotgun metagenomic sequencing on the PacBio Onso platform. Taxonomy was assigned via Kraken2/Bracken with Krona visualization. Diversity analyses used the vegan package in R. Phylogenetic analysis employed MAFFT, RAxML, and ape. title: Climate-driven spatial distribution and ecogeographical analysis of Cyperaceae using GIS and remote sensing
abstract: The research is dedicated to the study of the ecogeographic distribution of the Cyperaceae Juss. family in Azerbaijan, related to the dynamic changes occurring in plant communities formed under the influence of landscape diversity and climatic factors through RS (Remote Sensing) and GIS. Based on the results of the study, 115 taxa consisting of 14 genera belonging to the Cyperaceae family were identified. title: Sensitivities of a simulated Arctic stratocumulus to aerosol and microphysical parameters
abstract: Abstract. Low-level, mixed-phase clouds are a key component of the Arctic energy budget and can impact the extent and thickness of sea ice. These clouds are influenced by aerosols and microphysical processes that can determine the phase partitioning and thereby cloud lifetime and radiative impacts. Atmospheric models often struggle to represent phase partitioning in Arctic mixed-phase clouds correctly. Temperature Carryover Effect Revealed for Marine Fishes Using Spatio‐Temporal Distributed Lag Models
abstract: Understanding the impact of changing temperature on population densities is necessary to predict the likely impact of climate anomalies (e.g., marine heatwaves) or forecast distribution shifts under future climate scenarios. Population densities are often analyzed using spatio-temporal models (STMs), which typically predict densities based on local habitat conditions while also estimating latent spatial and spatio-temporal variation. title: Phylogenetic, Ecological, and Physiological Factors as Modulators of the Intestinal Microbiota in Stranded Marine Mammals in Uruguay
abstract: ABSTRACT Gut microbiota plays a key role in host physiology and may reflect ecological and health‐related processes, yet it remains poorly studied in marine mammals. We characterized and compared the gut bacterial communities of seven marine mammal species stranded along the Uruguayan coast between 2022 and 2024, including pinnipeds and cetaceans with different trophic habits. Tissue samples from 21 individuals were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding targeting the V3–V4 regions, with amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) inferred using DADA2 and taxonomic assignment based on SILVA 138.1. title: Yaylatepe Höyük: Ceramic Evidence and Intervisibility of a Newly Identified Bronze Age Coastal Settlement in the Troad
abstract: Known as the Troad in ancient sources, the Biga Peninsula has been one of the principal settlement regions of northwestern Anatolia since prehistoric times. The coastal settlements lining the Çanakkale Strait provided an important geographical setting for interregional interaction throughout prehistory. During the 2024 field season of the Çanakkale Strait Bronze Age Harbours Research Project, a previously unknown coastal settlement was identified on the Anatolian shore in the central part of the Strait and named Yaylatepe. title: Lightweight Instance Segmentation for Underwater Grout Overflow Monitoring in Offshore Wind Turbine Jacket Installation
abstract: The installation of grouted connections in deep-water offshore wind turbine jackets faces severe visibility constraints and limited diver operation time, necessitating an unmanned, real-time monitoring solution using remotely operated vehicles (ROVs). However, the lack of dedicated datasets and the challenge of balancing segmentation accuracy with edge-deployment efficiency remain major obstacles. This paper addresses these gaps by constructing, to the best of our knowledge, the first underwater grout overflow instance segmentation dataset reported in the published literature, comprising 2088
institutions: Suzhou University of Science and Technology

title: Sea-level rise drives unequal erosion of global ecosystem service value
abstract: Abstract Sea-level rise (SLR) is rapidly reshaping coastal ecosystems, yet its global implications for ecosystem-service value (ESV) remain poorly quantified. Here, we assess global ESV exposure to SLR under five shared socioeconomic pathways (SSPs), integrating IPCC AR6 projections with detailed valuation modeling over 2030–2100. Across the five SSP-aligned SLR pathways, annual income-adjusted ESV losses attributable to SLR in 2100 range from 130.06 billion Int$2020yr−1 under SSP3-7.0 to 339.41 billion Int$2020yr−1 under SSP5-8.5. title: Technological Transitions and Material Culture in the Ancla Macuca Shipwreck (Late 18th to Early Nineteenth Century): An Archaeometric Study from Alacranes Reef, Gulf of Mexico
abstract: The Ancla Macuca shipwreck, located within the Alacranes Reef National Park in the Gulf of Mexico, represents a palimpsest context resulting from the superposition of material remains from at least two distinct wrecks, the late eighteenth to early nineteenth-century Ancla Macuca site and the R.M.S. Forth (1849). This study presents the results of an interdisciplinary project integrating underwater archaeological survey, documentary research, archeometallurgical characterization, and conservation science. title: Hollow Glass Microsphere/Polymer Composites for Thermal Insulation: Mechanisms, Fabrication, and Performance‐Driven Multifunctional Expansion
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermal insulation materials play an important role in industrial thermal insulation and high‐end equipment. Traditional polymers often suffer from relatively high thermal conductivity, while highly porous polymers demonstrate insufficient mechanical properties. Hollow glass microspheres (HGMs) offer a solution with low thermal conductivity, high strength, low density, and robustness. This paper thoroughly reviews the factors and mechanisms influencing the intrinsic thermal conductivity of polymers, and details the fabrication methods of HGM/polymer composites. title: Theoretical Investigations to Aid in the Prediction of Combined Sewer Overflows in Coastal Urban Watersheds: Case Study of San Francisco
abstract: Abstract Combined sewer systems (CSS) function in about 700 U.S. municipalities, with over 100 near vulnerable coastal waters. Predicting changes due to rainfall, sea level rise (SLR), and groundwater rise is vital for adaptation. This study compares a hydrologic‐hydraulic model (PCSWMM) and a hybrid mass balance method for estimating combined sewer overflow (CSO) volumes. The mass‐balance approach is used as a screening tool, not a replacement for the calibrated hydraulic model. Both are applied to San Francisco's Eastside CSS, the only coastal system in California, in a replicable way. Manag

title: A feasibility demonstration of integrated deionization and electrolysis for portable hydrogen production from seawater
abstract: Reducing the water purification footprint for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) can enable portable hydrogen production from impure water sources. Here, we report a critical first step in the design of a thermally integrated deionization and electrolysis (TIDE) device for portable hydrogen production from seawater. The TIDE concept intends to leverage vapor-fed PEMWE operation, utilizing the waste heat from electrolysis to vaporize water through pervaporation to supply reactant water for electrolysis. title: Resilience Communication Model for Coastal Communities Facing Slow-Onset Disasters: A Netnographic Study of Jakarta
abstract: Climate change has shifted the global disaster paradigm from the dominance of rapid-onset disasters toward slow-onset disasters that develop gradually, such as sea-level rise, coastal abrasion, saltwater intrusion, and land subsidence. Coastal communities in Muara Angke and Marunda, North Jakarta, represent urban coastal areas that face the simultaneous accumulation of these ecological pressures. This study aims to develop a Coastal Community Resilience Communication Model (CCRCM) that is participatory, adaptive, and sustainable in facing slow-onset disasters. journal: Journal of Asian Multicultural Research for Social Sciences Study

title: Development of an interdisciplinary coastal erosion vulnerability index for urban communities in the eastern sector of the Togolese coast
abstract: Abstract The coasts of West Africa are particularly vulnerable to coastal erosion due to the interaction of physical, climatic, and anthropogenic factors. This study assesses the composite vulnerability of urban communities to coastal erosion along the eastern sector of the Togolese coastline, which spans 39 km and is subdivided into three coastal sections. The methodology combines remote sensing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), vulnerability scoring, and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). A coastal erosion vulnerability index (CVI) was calculated based on two complementary sub-indice
institutions: Institut de Recherche pour le Développement

title: Culinary Heritage Mapping for Sustainable Gastronomic Tourism: A Spatial Planning Framework for Thanh Hoa Province, Vietnam
abstract: Gastronomy has been recognized as a source of place-based advantage for destination differentiation and territorial development. Culinary inventories are commonly used tools for documentation and planning purposes but often remain descriptive in nature and do not readily support spatial tourism analysis. This research created a Food Heritage Spatial Framework for Thanh Hoa Province, Vietnam, by converting a previously compiled inventory of 122 recorded culinary specialties into an analytically usable spatial database. Culinary specialties were coded based on seven traits, including ingredient

title: Applying CITES for sea cucumber conservation: A structured review across the Indo-Pacific
abstract: International trade regulation under CITES is increasingly used as a market-based mechanism to conserve marine invertebrates, yet implementation of trade provisions remains heterogeneous across regions and taxa. This review evaluates the implementation of CITES Appendix II listings for sea cucumbers with a focus on the Indo-Pacific region. Using a structured review of published and grey literature, contextualised with export data, we examined the preparation of Non‑Detriment Findings (NDFs) and reported trade of sea cucumbers. institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Influence of Sea Surface Temperature and Chlorophyll-a on Biomass Availability and Body Size of the Black Skipjack (Euthynnus lineatus) in the Mexican South Pacific
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the relationship between oceanographic variability, specifically sea surface temperature ( SST ) and chlorophyll- a (Chl- a ) concentration, and the abundance and size structure of Euthynnus lineatus (black skipjack) along the southern Pacific coast of Mexico from October 2022 to October 2024. The region experiences two distinct seasons: a dry season with strong “Tehuano” winds causing upwelling, and a rainy season influenced by the Costa Rica Coastal Current. High-resolution satellite data were integrated with biometric and catch data from local artisanal fish
journal: Thalassas An International Journal of Marine Sciences

title: Global review of bull shark Carcharhinus leucas (Valenciennes, 1839) museum specimens: summary of records, geographic analysis, and assessment of their scientific value
abstract: Background Museum specimens provide critical data for taxonomy, systematics, biogeography, and conservation. Well-preserved vouchers are essential for documenting both historical and contemporary distributional records, supporting a better understanding on species distribution in a world undergoing constant environmental changes. Regarding the euryhaline bull shark, Carcharhinus leucas , voucher specimens reliably confirm occurrences in areas where the species' status was previously unclear and clarify the identity of morphologically similar shark species found in freshwater environments. title: Diversity, stability and ecosystem functioning relationships across marine fish communities facing contrasting environmental and anthropogenic pressures
abstract: Abstract Understanding the mechanisms that underpin ecological stability has traditionally focused on the role of diversity, and particularly through biodiversity and ecosystem functioning (BEF) relationships. Yet, BEF relationships and the drivers of stability remain poorly explored across contrasting systems exposed to multiple pressures, such as exploited marine fish communities. title: Initial Fisheries Bycatch Estimates for Threatened Marine Mammals in Cambodia
abstract: ABSTRACT Bycatch is the biggest threat to marine mammals globally. To estimate bycatch and investigate bycatch drivers for Irrawaddy dolphin ( Orcaella brevirostris ), Indo‐Pacific humpback dolphin ( Sousa chinensis ), Indo‐Pacific finless porpoise ( Neophocaena phocaenoides ) and dugong ( Dugong dugon ) in Cambodia, questionnaires were conducted with 449 vessels (gillnet, trap, longline, trawl and surrounding net) across Cambodia's coastline between September and October 2023. journal: Aquatic Conservation Marine and Freshwater Ecosystems

title: Harnessing GIS to map trawl fishing grounds and reduce carbon footprint along India’s west coast
abstract: Aim: This study examines the spatial and temporal dynamics of key commercial fish species along the west coast of India through GIS-based mapping, aiming to reduce the environmental footprint of trawl fisheries by optimizing fishing effort, minimizing scouting time, and lowering carbon emissions. Methodology: Data from customised logbooks for each fishing operation were geo-referenced using recorded latitude–longitude coordinates to delineate the spatial extent of fishing grounds. title: Spatiotemporal Differentiation and Driving Factors in the Distribution of Cultural Heritage Sites: A Multi-Period GIS–Geodetector Analysis of Zhejiang Province, China
abstract: The spatiotemporal distribution of cultural heritage sites reflects long-term human–environment interactions. Using Zhejiang Province as a case study, this study integrates GIS-based spatial analysis with the Geodetector model to investigate the spatiotemporal differentiation of heritage distribution and the changing influence and interaction of natural and social environmental factors across historical periods. title: Optimal wind energy site selection in Egypt using a GIS–AHP and remote sensing-based approach
abstract: Abstract Delivering affordable, reliable, and sustainable electricity in lower-middle-income countries requires spatially explicit tools that translate remote-sensing and infrastructure data into decision support for sustainable development planning. Focusing on Egypt, we update the national wind-energy suitability map using a Geographic Information System (GIS) and a multi-criteria decision analysis framework. journal: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science

title: What drives the winter behaviour and ecology of the temperate coral Astrangia poculata? An examination of thermal and nutritional cues
abstract: Abstract In temperate ecosystems, accessing subtidal environments in the winter is challenging, and therefore, winter ecology and seasonal variation are understudied. For the temperate coral Astrangia poculata, winter is thought to be a period of biological ‘reset’, in which many cellular processes slow or stop, and the microbiome and symbiont community shift dramatically. The period of quiescence, when corals enter a dormant state with limited feeding or metabolic activity, is primarily driven by cold temperatures. title: Spatio-temporal variation of the pocilloporid coral-associated symbiotic crustaceans (Decapoda) of the central Mexican Pacific
abstract: Introduction: Coral symbiotic crustaceans maintain close associations with their hosts, which may be obligate or facultative. In addition to their dependence on corals for survival, these organisms play an important role in the health and persistence of their hosts. However, there is still limited information regarding the spatio-temporal variation in their biomass and the factors regulating it. title: Paleogene Basin Evolution in Southern Patagonia as a Result of Plate Dynamics and Global Sea Level Changes
abstract: Abstract The Paleogene stratigraphic record of the Austral‐Magallanes foreland basin (southern Patagonia) reflects a complex interplay between Andean orogenesis, plate kinematics, and global climate shifts. We present 17 new detrital zircon U‐Pb geochronology data and one tuff U‐Pb age from Cenozoic strata exposed in the Río Turbio region (∼51.5°S). Our data constrain three depositional stages—the Cerro Dorotea (∼65–59 Ma), Río Turbio (∼47–35 Ma), and Río Guillermo (∼26–21 Ma) formations—bounded by two protracted hiatuses. title: Acrylic binders with covalently bound quorum sensing inhibitor units for copper-free marine antifouling coatings
abstract: The control of marine biofouling remains a major environmental challenge, as current commercial coatings still rely largely on copper oxides and organic booster biocides. Although efficient, these formulations raise serious concerns due to ecotoxicity, bioaccumulation, and increasingly restrictive regulations, especially in confined environments such as harbors, lakes, and freshwater reservoirs. title: Revealing the Widespread Bias of Extinction Risk in the Antarctic and the Southern Ocean
abstract: Accelerating environmental change in the Antarctic and Southern Ocean (ASO) necessitates robust extinction risk assessments to inform conservation priorities. Nevertheless, no systematic, region-wide baseline of extinction risk currently exists for tracking ASO biodiversity responses to ongoing change, a significant barrier to global biodiversity monitoring. Here, we conducted the first ASO-wide synthesis of current extinction risk knowledge for plants, animals and Fungi. This included examining biases in current assessments, the distribution of Threatened species and their associated threats.

title: Sediment dispersal of PE and PVC primary microplastics in a coastal archipelago surrounding a plastic production industrial complex
abstract: Abstract Microplastic pollution is a global environmental concern, yet the distribution and fate of primary microplastics, particularly small pre-production particles, remain poorly understood. This study investigates the occurrence, distribution, and sources of microplastics in surface sediments of a fjord system on the Swedish west coast, adjacent to a major petrochemical industrial complex. Microplastics were detected in all 9 samples, with concentrations ranging from 6.7 to 48 particles g⁻¹ dry weight. title: Physiological and multi-omics analyses reveal osmotic effect, ionic function, and expression network underlying sperm activation and movement in giant grouper (Epinephelus lanceolatus)
abstract: Sperm activation and movement underpin reproductive success in marine teleosts, yet their mechanistic basis remains largely unresolved in coral reef fishes. Giant grouper ( Epinephelus lanceolatus ), the largest coral reef fish and a species of major aquaculture value, faces reproductive limitations due to the scarcity of mature functional males and suboptimal fertilization efficiency. title: Ict-enabled Environmental Sustainability in Coastal Communities: Assessing Digital Governance and Blue Economy Development in Mombasa County, Kenya
abstract: Coastal communities face increasing environmental challenges; including habitat degradation, pollution, and climate-related shocks that threaten livelihoods built around the ocean economy. Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs) are increasingly promoted as instruments of environmental governance, yet the extent to which digital governance capacity translates into sustainable blue economy outcomes in African coastal counties remains under-researched. This paper investigates the relationship between ICT-enabled digital governance and environmental sustainability in the context of blue

title: Formal Description of Cladocopium proximale sp. nov., a Coral Photosymbiont From the C1 Radiation
abstract: ABSTRACT Coral reefs are among the most biodiverse ecosystems on Earth and rely on endosymbiosis with Symbiodiniaceae, a diverse family of dinoflagellates essential for coral nutrition and which also play an important role in thermal tolerance. Despite their ecological importance, resolving species boundaries within Symbiodiniaceae remains challenging, partly due to limited phylogenetic signal in commonly used genetic markers and the absence of broadly accepted criteria for species delimitation. title: UCD-LFE: An Underwater Crack Detection Model for Hydraulic Structures in Complex Environments via Lightweight Design and Feature Enhancement
abstract: Underwater crack detection in hydraulic structures is difficult in complex underwater environments, where blur, uneven illumination, low contrast, and rough surface textures can weaken crack cues and introduce background interference, while multiple cracks further increase detection complexity. Practical inspection also requires compact models with low computational demand. To address these coupled challenges, this study develops UCD-LFE, an underwater crack detection model combining lightweight design with feature enhancement. title: Pole-to-pole LOV-domain receptor diversity points to an early stramenopile origin and global dominance of aureochromes
abstract: Light regimes are a fundamental environmental cue for marine organisms. Yet molecular adaptations of photoreceptors to the extreme seasonality of polar regions remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that the diversity of candidate blue-light-sensing LOV-domain proteins increases at higher latitudes. We identify aureochromes, blue-light-sensitive transcription factors unique to stramenopiles, as the most frequent LOV-domain receptors across ocean latitudes. title: A quantitative framework for identifying umbrella taxa in the supralittoral zone of wave-exposed sandy beaches
abstract: Sandy beach biodiversity is under increasing pressure from anthropogenic stressors across the ocean-land interface, creating an urgent need for cost-effective conservation tools. Umbrella taxa can serve as proxies for co-occurring biodiversity in spatial conservation planning and guide habitat-based conservation actions that benefit broader communities. title: Biological status and coastal resource management of Anadara tuberculosa in the Eastern Tropical Pacific
abstract: Anadara tuberculosa is a mangrove-associated bivalve of high ecological, economic, and sociocultural importance in the Eastern Tropical Pacific, where it supports coastal livelihoods and contributes to ecosystem functioning. abstract: Vernacular dwellings and dialects are material and linguistic carriers of regional culture. abstract: Synthetic samples and analogs of marine endoperoxides derived from mycaperoxides and plakortides were screened for their antileishmanial and antimalarial activities. abstract: ABSTRACT Ocean acidification and sulfide intrusion are key environmental stressors affecting seagrass bed ecosystems. abstract: The blue economy is commonly framed as a pathway to sustainability, promising the reconciliation of economic growth with environmental protection and social equity. abstract: Offshore wind farms (OWF) play a major role in addressing the climate change crisis. abstract: Marine-ranching carbon sink (MRCS) is defined as an additional, verifiable net climate benefit attributable to a bounded ranching intervention after considering baseline conditions, carbon fate, life-cycle emissions, and uncertainty. Marine ranching is increasingly discussed in China as a means to align fisheries with the national carbon-neutrality agenda. However, terms such as additional biomass, harvested carbon, long-lived storage, avoided emissions, and offset credits refer to different outcomes. title: Microbiological quality of inland and coastal springs: Escherichia coli, other coliforms, and implications for public health
abstract: Untreated springs remain important domestic water sources in rural communities, yet their microbial safety and spatial and seasonal variability are insufficiently characterised. This study evaluated concentrations of Escherichia coli and other coliforms in inland and coastal springs within the King Sabata Dalindyebo Local Municipality, South Africa. Ten springs, five inland and five coastal, were sampled on five occasions during both wet and dry seasons, producing 100 water samples. abstract: The occurrence of a Carcharopsis sp. tooth in the Cantabrian Mountains (Spain) extends the palaeogeographical distribution of this chondrichthyan genus beyond Laurussia to the northern margin of Gondwana. Recovered from late Viséan pelagic carbonates ( Lochriea ziegleri conodont Zone), the specimen was analysed using micro-computed tomography (micro-CT). title: Marine Algae‐Derived Starch and Polysaccharides for Sustainable Bioplastics: Processing, Properties, Environmental Performance, and Future Prospects
abstract: ABSTRACT Marine algae present a promising foundation for developing sustainable bioplastics, distinguished by rapid growth, abundant carbohydrates, and minimal land and freshwater demands. This paper examines the utilization of marine algae‐derived starch and other polysaccharides in bioplastic manufacturing, encompassing algal characteristics, carbohydrate and polysaccharide recovery, bioplastic formulation and properties, and environmental implications. abstract: Malnutrition continues to be a persistent global challenge, frequently affecting small-scale producers. Nutrition-focused social marketing has been shown to increase nutrition awareness and improve diets and nutrition outcomes, but less is known about the pathways to these positive outcomes as well as impacts on other nutrition-related behaviors like household food expenditure. abstract: Abstract To quantify aquatic carbon budgets, it is important to accurately measure dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC). The standard approach requires the use of mercury chloride (HgCl 2 ) poison to preserve samples, but the real need and overall constraints of using such a toxic compound remain elusive. Here, we evaluate the need for filtration and mercury poisoning to maintain DIC stability in six contrasting water types across the freshwater–seawater continuum. title: Epidemiological surveillance of bacterial pathogens in cultured European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax) along the Aegean coast of Türkiye
abstract: Intensive aquaculture of European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax) along the Aegean coast of Türkiye faces continuous production challenges from infectious diseases, yet comprehensive multi-year baseline data remain limited. This study presents a multi-year retrospective surveillance program (2020-2025) monitoring bacterial pathogens associated with 748 distinct cage-level disease outbreaks in fish across 19 discrete offshore commercial sea farms. abstract: A study on assessment of diversity in banana and plantain cultivars available in coastal salt ecosystem of Bangladesh and performance of selected plantain genotypes was accomplished during July 2022 to May 2023 in in situ and ex situ conservation sites. A survey was done according to a questionnaire to assess the plant diversity and crop husbandry of banana and plantain. title: Integrated Framework for Valuing Urban Wetlands as Flood-Mitigation Infrastructure in Rivers State, Nigeria
abstract: Urban wetlands provide key services and support natural hydrological regulation; yet the values and flood-mitigation services they provide could be under-quantified in rapidly urbanizing coastal areas of Africa. title: Microplastic ingestion is ubiquitous in threatened stingrays from the Amazon estuary
abstract: Microplastic pollution has become pervasive across freshwater ecosystems worldwide, including the Amazon Basin, where increasing levels of plastic contamination have been reported. Despite growing evidence of microplastic (MP) ingestion in aquatic organisms, studies focusing on threatened species remain extremely scarce, particularly for estuarine elasmobranchs. title: Integrated proteomics and transcriptomics provide insights into molecular basis of ascidian metamorphosis
abstract: Shallow-water ascidians are invasive, fouling marine organisms that rapidly metamorphose from planktonic larvae to sessile forms. To gain insights into their environmental adaptability and develop methods for biofouling control, it is crucial to explore the molecular and cellular orchestration of metamorphosis. title: Impact of climate change on long-term corrosion of offshore wind turbine monopiles
abstract: Offshore steel structures are subjected to deteriorating environmental actions affecting their performance and structural reliability. Marine corrosion is recognized as a leading factor reducing service life and reliability of offshore wind turbine (OWT) monopiles. This paper evaluates the influence of corrosion on the structural performance and reliability of OWTs’ monopile using a bi-modal corrosion model. title: The power of blue entrepreneurial pedagogy: A heutagogical and resource orchestration perspective on learning-to-venture readiness
abstract: The global transition toward a sustainable blue economy requires education systems to prepare young people who can transform coastal and marine resources into responsible entrepreneurial opportunities. However, entrepreneurship education remains focused on intention, business-plan production, or generic competence, with limited attention to blue entrepreneurial readiness in vocational settings. This study draws on heutagogy and resource orchestration within a Learning-to-Venture Orchestration Framework to examine blue entrepreneurial readiness for initial venture-oriented action. abstract: Aim . abstract: Abstract Non‐native ant establishment is one of the greatest threats to native biodiversity on oceanic islands. Interactions with native ant species may provide beneficial ecological resistance that prevents non‐native ants from spreading across island landscapes. We linked the fine‐scale co‐occurrence of non‐native and native ants with the island‐scale establishment of non‐native ant species across the Caribbean island of Montserrat. title: Analysis of Land Use Suitability in Relation to Flood Risk in Belitung Regency
abstract: Flooding poses a threat to spatial utilization and community activities in coastal areas, including Belitung Regency. This study analyzes land-use suitability in relation to flood risk to support disaster risk-based spatial utilization control. A descriptive quantitative approach was employed using Geographic Information Systems (GIS). abstract: Abstract Plastic waste in the environment has a significant adverse effect on ecosystems and human health. Plastic biodegradation has been observed in certain environments as a potential strategy for end-of-life plastics management. Recent research has focused on plastispheres, a microbial biofilm that forms on plastic surfaces. abstract: Abstract Deep intraseasonal variability (ISV) in weakly stratified marginal basins remains poorly understood, especially where complex bathymetry may modulate abyssal motions. Here we examine its structure and driving mechanisms in the northern Philippine Basin (NPB) using multi‐year, nearly full‐depth mooring observations at 128°E, 20.45°N. title: Shared transport system, different liveability realities: residents’ and tourists’ perspectives from seasonal coastal destinations
abstract: Transport systems in seasonal tourism destinations are shared by residents and tourists, yet little is known about how these groups experience transport-related liveability while using the same infrastructure. This study examines how transport conditions shape transport-related liveability from the perspectives of residents and tourists in two seasonal coastal destinations on the southern Baltic coast of Poland: the Hel Peninsula and the Vistula Spit. title: Integrated GIS–AHP and 2-D Electrical Resistivity Tomography for Environmental Assessment of Solid-Waste Dumpsites in Gombe Metropolis, Nigeria
abstract: Open dumping of municipal solid waste can expose surface water and groundwater to leachate, yet surface environmental constraints and subsurface conditions are often assessed separately. This study aimed to integrate the GIS-based Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) with two-dimensional electrical resistivity tomography (2-D ERT) to assess the environmental setting and potential subsurface contamination pathways of existing solid-waste dumpsites in Gombe Metropolis, northeastern Nigeria. abstract: Maritime universities today proudly showcase a growing number of female students training to become officers. However, the real test does not happen in the simulator room. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper reports archaeological investigations at the Howard Creek site, a Late Holocene open‐air site in the sub‐coastal Moreton region of southeast Queensland. The site adds to a regional record based largely on rockshelter excavations. Development‐led salvage investigations included excavation, radiocarbon dating, lithic analysis, and use‐wear and residue studies. abstract: The desiccation of the Aral Sea has resulted in the formation of the Aralkum, one of the largest anthropogenic deserts in the world. Despite profound environmental transformation, spatially comprehensive assessments of vascular plant diversity across the Uzbek sector of the dried seabed remain limited. This study presents a grid-based floristic analysis of vascular plants on the dried bed of the Aral Sea (DBAS) based on field surveys conducted between 2020 and 2023. In the Northeast Cape Fear River (CFR) watershed of North Carolina, RSLR from both anthropogenic global warming and dredging of the CFR contribute to saltwater intrusion. title: Reflection Seismic Insights Into the Pleistocene An-Nafud Sand Sea and the Underlying Paleozoic to Ediacaran Geology North of the Arabian Shield
abstract: The An-Nafud sand sea formed during the Pleistocene and occupies approximately 60,200 km 2 of northern Saudi Arabia. The erg has regional significance within the North African – Arabian Pleistocene desert trend, recording aeolian system development and early hominin migrations, while the underlying geology represents the poorly-documented Ediacaran and Paleozoic history of the northern sector of the Arabian plate. Reflection seismic data and deep wells have been used to establish the first description of the 3D geometry of this erg and the tectonostratigraphy of the underlying bedrock geology.

abstract: ABSTRACT Long‐distance dispersal sustains genetic diversity across populations and facilitates recovery from disturbance, and dispersal also may shape how ecologically important morphological traits shift in response to environmental change. abstract: Cultural heritage in tropical coastal settlements faces recurrent climatic pressures, yet its resilience depends on more than the survival of built fabric. This article examines how vernacular practices, adaptation strategies, and institutional action shape heritage conservation and resilience in Navala (Fiji), Sandwip (Bangladesh), Stone Town (Zanzibar, Tanzania), and the Island of Mozambique (Mozambique). abstract: Chronic wound infections caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa are difficult to manage because biofilm formation can support bacterial persistence and reduce antimicrobial effectiveness. This study framework examined relationships between biofilm-associated virulence genes, biofilm formation, antimicrobial resistance, and clinical characteristics using a dataset of 120 patient–isolate records. abstract: Carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) structures in marine environments are continuously exposed to coupled humidity, salinity, and temperature, which progressively deteriorate carbon fiber-epoxy interfacial integrity. abstract: Urban flooding is an increasing challenge in coastal cities, particularly in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, where rapid urbanization and limited adaptive infrastructure exacerbate vulnerability. This study develops an integrated Geographic Information System (GIS-based) framework to assess the effectiveness of nature-based solutions (NBS), specifically sponge city systems, in enhancing the resilience of urban open spaces against flood risks in Alexandria, Egypt. abstract: Geographical inequalities and limited access to educational resources remain major challenges to equitable numeracy learning, particularly in remote areas of Papua, Indonesia. abstract: This study explores aquaculture-based tourism as a tool to improve public perceptions of aquaculture, promote sustainable development of marine industries, and advance Blue Growth. abstract: Tropical cyclones continue to cause extensive economic and non-economic losses across coastal Bangladesh. Empirical assessments often focus narrowly on monetary damage while ignoring spatial disparities and non-economic impacts. abstract: Egypt’s policy toward Gaza has been characterized by a persistent tension between its asserted role as a regional mediator and the imperatives of national security and regime stability. abstract: Interspecific competition is a key process shaping species distributions and biodiversity. In the western bioregion of the Galapagos archipelago, two endemic and endangered pinniped species coexist: the Galapagos sea lion (GSL) and the Galapagos fur seal (GFS). abstract: How do commodity price benchmarks adapt when their material foundations erode? We answer through the 2023 reconstitution of Brent, the world's most widely used oil price benchmark. abstract: Monitoring veterinary drug residues in aquaculture is essential for food safety, regulatory compliance, and the determination of reliable withdrawal periods. title: Soil organic carbon and nitrogen responses to cover crops in Norfolk soil under long‐term contrasting tillage systems
abstract: Abstract Cover crops have garnered increased attention as a conservation strategy to increase soil organic carbon (SOC) and nitrogen (N) while improving overall soil health in agricultural systems. However, their effect on SOC and N dynamics in sandy soils of the US southeastern (SE) Coastal Plain is poorly understood. This study evaluated the response of SOC and N pools to cover crops in a Norfolk loamy sand under long‐term (>40 years) conventional (CvT) and conservation (CnT) tillage systems and short‐term (5 years) winter cover cropping. abstract: Specialized maps and registers are an important source of spatial and thematic information in spatial planning and investment project design. The aim of this study is to systematize the main types of specialized maps and registers used in the surveying, design, construction, and operation of investment projects. abstract: Abstract Microorganisms dominate aquatic ecosystems, yet the evolutionary forces shaping their biogeography remain poorly understood. Freshwater habitats, acting as “isolated islands", may generate distinct evolutionary patterns in contrast to globally connected marine systems. Here, we investigated the globally abundant freshwater SAR11 genus Fontibacterium using a comparative population genomics framework. abstract: Abstract Aquaculture in the Tena River Basin (Ecuador) is a key contributor to the local economy and food security; however, it also poses environmental risks, including water pollution and the decline of native species. This highlights the need for land‐use planning to identify suitable areas for its development, considering environmental, socioeconomic, and legal criteria. abstract: ABSTRACT Control over liquid wettability and droplet mobility is essential for several emerging applications including open microfluidics, anti‐icing, self‐cleaning, and heat transfer. Existing strategies generally rely on permanent chemical modification or continuous external stimuli to regulate droplet spreading, pinning, and sliding. abstract: In this study, we utilize a controlled cellulose nanofiber (CNF) platform to investigate how synthesis parameters of delaminated 2D MXene components influence cellular response, photothermal behavior, and antimicrobial activity of the resulting composite materials. abstract: Abstract Photothermal evaporation offers a sustainable solution for brine and seawater desalination, yet its long-term operation is fundamentally limited by salt accumulation arising from diffusion-limited ion transport, especially under high evaporative flux. abstract: This article proposes a framework for assessing the environmental sustainability of food products, with potential applications in product assessment and decision support. The framework applies to both domestically produced and imported food products and aggregates multiple environmental indicators into a weighted score on a defined scale. abstract: Baselines matter in our perception of which is the climate ‘normal’ and what benchmark we use to track climate changes. abstract: One of the most effective non - invasive geophysical techniques for detecting and characterizing buried or submerged ferromagnetic objects is the magnetometric method, widely used in marine, environmental, and archaeological applications. Identifying sources of metallic pollution in sensitive ecosystems such as the Danube Delta is essential for assessing ecological risks and implementing remediation measures. title: Mapping Urban Land Transformation in Dehradun City, Uttarakhand, India (2001-2025): A Remote Sensing and Land Transformation Analysis
abstract: The modern world is the absolute example of an urbanized world. The pace of urbanization keeps on constantly varying the physical dimension of an urban area, changing the spatial distribution of its built-up area, green cover and various other land use classes. The present research examines the transformation in the urban land use pattern in Dehradun city, Uttarakhand, from 2001 to 2025, using multi-temporal satellite data and remote sensing as well as GIS technology. title: A pH-responsive cascade oxygen-generating sodium alginate hydrogel with self-moisturizing and adhesive properties for infected diabetic wound healing
abstract: Hypoxia impairs infected diabetic wound healing by suppressing angiogenesis, sustaining inflammation, and delaying tissue repair. We developed CSZM, a self-moisturizing, adhesive, and injectable calcium-crosslinked sodium alginate hydrogel containing ZnO 2 and MnO 2 nanoparticles. In acidic wound microenvironments, ZnO 2 releases antibacterial Zn 2+ and H 2 O 2 , whereas MnO 2 converts H 2 O 2 into O 2 and limits peroxide accumulation. abstract: This community service activity aimed to identify fish farming activities and analyze and map the water quality of the Payaman River as supporting information for introducing fisheries-based ecotourism potential. The activity was conducted from July to August 2026 through field observation, identification of aquaculture potential, water sampling, water quality analysis, and GIS-based mapping. Water samples were collected at 20 observation points and analyzed for temperature, pH, TDS, and DHL. title: Transcriptomic analysis implicates microtubule-dependent motor proteins and mitochondria in spermatid development and seasonal reproduction of Phascolosoma esculenta
abstract: This study investigated the molecular mechanisms governing seasonal reproduction in the commercially important marine invertebrate, Phascolosoma esculenta, via transcriptomic analysis of male coelomic fluid, complemented by immunofluorescence and transmission electron microscopy validation. Sequencing identified 30,897 differentially expressed genes. title: Integrative taxonomy and biogeography of unusual deep-water fishes from the western North Atlantic
abstract: ABSTRACT A combination of morphological and molecular approaches was used for the species identification of uncommon deep-water fishes caught at depths between 620 and 1,372 m. Sampling was conducted during the annual bottom trawl cruises in the Flemish Cap and Grand Banks of Newfoundland, located in the western North Atlantic, between 2013 and 2025. A total of 23 specimens belonging to 12 families were identified, comprising 20 species. title: Targeting P23 by PM534 suppresses glioblastoma via disruption of SFPQ-mediated phase separation
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is one of the most lethal human malignancies, with a five-year survival rate of approximately 5% and limited effective therapeutic options beyond standard-of-care regimens, underscoring an urgent need for novel therapeutic agents and druggable targets. Here, we report that PM534, a marine sponge-derived synthetic compound, potently suppresses GBM malignancy in orthotopic patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models and in vitro , with IC 50 value of 1.86 nM in patient-derived GBM#P3 cells. title: A multi-criteria decision framework for the holistic design of remotely operated vehicles using the analytic network process
abstract: The design of a Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) for underwater exploration requires careful consideration of multiple interrelated factors, including structural integrity, hydrodynamic performance, energy efficiency, and cost-effectiveness, among others. However, traditional ROV design methods often fail to adequately account for the complex relationships between these various factors, resulting in designs that lack optimal efficiency. title: Using Photography as a Tool for Critical Urban Diagnosis: An Undomestication Strategy
abstract: This research describes a teaching experience of urbanism using photography as a critical pedagogical strategy of educating the look to raise awareness among undergraduate students about the problems of their context, employing the objective worldview of each participant regarding their perception of the city and understanding their role as knowledge builders.This was a descriptive field research, based on participant observation methodology, structured in four stages, through a process of categorizing photographs taken by the attendees, shaping positive and negative aspects of the experience.

title: Consumer preference and willingness to pay for low-commercial-value small pelagic fish in Sri Lanka: Evidence from a choice experiment
abstract: Small pelagic fish play a key role in the livelihoods of coastal fishers; however, most species face persistent marketing challenges that affect fishers’ incomes. This study examined consumer preferences and willingness to pay (WTP) for products derived from low-commercial-value species, with Sardinella gibbosa as the focal species, using a discrete choice experiment (DCE) with urban supermarket buyers (n = 199) in the Gampaha District of Sri Lanka. abstract: Kelurahan Kawal, Kecamatan Gunung Kijang, Kabupaten Bintan memiliki beragam potensi ekonomi pesisir, seperti usaha pengolahan hasil laut, kuliner, perdagangan, pariwisata, serta fasilitas pendukung aktivitas pesisir. Namun, informasi mengenai persebaran potensi tersebut belum tersedia dalam bentuk peta khusus yang terintegrasi dan mudah diakses oleh masyarakat. Kegiatan ini bertujuan untuk mengidentifikasi dan memetakan persebaran potensi ekonomi pesisir di Kelurahan Kawal sebagai media informasi mengenai potensi lokal. title: When dates disagree: radiocarbon and sighting-based models reveal range-wide variability in great auk ( Pinguinus impennis ) extinction estimates
abstract: Methods for inferring extinction are well established for events that either occurred on millennial time scales (e.g. the late Quaternary) or are unfolding in the present. However, these methods employ distinct data types inherent to palaeontological or neontological settings, yielding a potentially disjointed view of the extinction process. title: Stone and water governed early human settlement of the desert
abstract: Abstract Models of early human dispersal rely on climate to predict where populations could settle, with freshwater assumed to govern the timing and geography 1,2 , particularly across the Saharo-Arabian arid belt, where humid windows episodically opened corridors into the desert interior 3 . Yet Pleistocene dispersals into ‘Green Arabia’ were brief and geographically constrained 4,5 , a pattern not explained by water availability alone. title: An isolated population of relict Pterocarya fraxinifolia at the NW limit of its distribution range
abstract: Since the mid-Miocene, climatic cooling and Quaternary climatic oscillations have significantly reduced plant diversity. Consequently, Cenozoic plant communities across the Northern Hemisphere experienced range contractions, surviving as relict floras in southern refugia. Anatolia has served as a critical refugium during Pleistocene glaciations due to its geographic and paleoclimatic features, thus maintaining a rich relict flora. title: Cooper’s Ferry/Nipéhe, stratigraphic integrity, and confirming early inland dispersal: Evaluating peopling of the Americas modeling
abstract: Statistical models shape debates over the timing and geography of the initial peopling of the Americas, but their value depends on testing their assumptions against archaeological evidence. We examine the Apparent Stratigraphic Integrity Index (ASI), used to infer postdepositional mixing at Late Pleistocene sites and support a relatively late occupation of temperate North America. ASI describes vertical discontinuity in binned artifact-frequency profiles; it does not directly measure artifact movement or stratigraphic integrity. title: Beyond the slash-and-burn narrative: evidence on forest and land fire drivers from oil palm enclaves in West Kalimantan, Indonesia
abstract: Abstract Forest and land fires in Indonesia are frequently attributed to oil palm expansion and slash-and-burn land clearing, yet the social and institutional dynamics underlying fire occurrence remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates the drivers of forest and land fires through case studies of two oil palm concessions in West Kalimantan, Indonesia, with particular attention to enclave areas within concession boundaries. title: Spatial Analysis of Flood Risk Zones in The Usuma Watershed Federal Capital Territory, Nigeria
abstract: This study examined flood risk zones within the Usuma Watershed in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nigeria, with the aim of identifying spatial patterns of flood vulnerability and informing sustainable flood risk management. The objectives were to map flood-prone areas, analyze flood frequency, and evaluate the biophysical and anthropogenic factors contributing to flood risks. Data were collected through satellite imagery, Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) digital elevation data, hydrological datasets, and field observations. title: First juvenile production of Florida Pompano (Trachinotus carolinus) through captive reproduction and larval rearing in southeastern Mexico
abstract: The Florida Pompano (Trachinotus carolinus) is an emerging species for marine aquaculture due to its rapid growth, high market value, and adaptability to captive conditions. However, the reliable production of hatchery juveniles remains a major bottleneck limiting commercial expansion. The present study evaluated the technical feasibility of captive reproduction, larval rearing, nursery rearing, and juvenile production of T. carolinus under tropical hatchery conditions. title: Relationships between birds, macro-litter, and vegetation in artificial urban wetlands in Greater Melbourne, Australia
abstract: Artificial urban wetlands provide valuable habitat to birds in extensive urban areas. However, these wetlands are often designed primarily for ecosystem services such as stormwater and wastewater remediation and tend to accumulate pollution. The potential impact of macro-litter pollution on birds in these ecosystems is poorly understood. We explored this relationship by surveying birds, macro-litter, and vegetation at 27 artificial urban wetlands across Greater Melbourne, Australia, during the austral summer of 2024/2025. title: Construction of 0D/2D M/rGO@EuMOF multiscale heterostructures for integrated high-efficiency microwave absorption and corrosion protection
abstract: Abstract Developing multifunctional materials with integrated microwave absorption and corrosion resistance is crucial for expanding the practical application scope of functional materials in complex marine environments. In this work, a series of multiscale zero-dimensional/two-dimensional (0D/2D) heterostructure composites (denoted as MG@E) were successfully fabricated via a facile in-situ hydrothermal method. title: IRIS-VCE: A UNIFIED CFD-BAYESIAN FRAMEWORK FOR REFINERY VAPOUR CLOUD EXPLOSION RISK FROM ACCIDENT EVIDENCE TO CORRIDOR AND CLIMATE IMPACT
abstract: Vapour cloud explosions (VCEs) at Jaipur, Amuay and Buncefield produced loads far beyond screening estimates, yet accident frequency, barrier health, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) severity, off-site exposure and climate stress are still assessed separately. title: The Impact of Land Use and Land Cover Changes on Runoff Volume for Hydropower
abstract: ABSTRACT This research investigates the complex relationship between land use and land cover (LULC) changes and runoff for hydropower. Remote sensing and Geographic Information System (GIS) approach were employed to conduct the analysis on LULC changes over the period of 21 years. In conjunction, the Soil Conservation Service Curve Number (SCS‐CN) method was employed to estimate runoff volumes based on the LULC changes. title: Synergistic Effects of UV Radiation and Water Immersion on the Photo-Oxidative Degradation and Thermal Stability of CFRP Composites
abstract: Abstract The photo-oxidative degradation of the epoxy matrix is a factor limiting the long-term environmental stability of carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites. This study investigates the physicochemical and thermal degradation mechanisms of DGEBA-based CFRP laminates exposed to prolonged (1000 h) ultraviolet radiation. To evaluate the synergistic effects of environmental factors, standard photoaging (PN-EN ISO 4892-2) was compared with a novel in-house method utilizing narrow-band UV radiation (UVA, UVB, UVC) in both dry and continuous underwater immersion conditions. title: Capturing the midnight sun: Ernst Herrmann’s film and photography of Svalbard in the 1930s
abstract: The German geographer Ernst Herrmann was the first explorer to make a colour film of the Arctic while on an expedition to Svalbard in the summer of 1937. The following year, he returned to conduct a series of flights above the archipelago and to further explore the Arctic Ocean. Returning home to Germany, Herrmann brought his film and thousands of photographic images back to present to audiences. This paper explores the impact of Herrmann’s visual work on the development of polar imaginaries. title: Analyzing the effectiveness of urban water bodies in mitigating Urban Heat Island using geo-statistical methods
abstract: Urban water bodies significantly contribute to mitigating the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect, particularly during hot summer months. However, most studies have primarily focused on large water bodies, often overlooking the role and efficiency of smaller or medium-sized artificial ones. This study addresses this gap by examining the cooling performance of water bodies across different spatial contexts. title: Functional consequences of acanthocephalan infection in Homarus americanus and advances in understanding of parasite-associated changes in lobster immunity
abstract: Profilicollis botulus is an acanthocephalan parasite with larval stages developing in arthropod intermediate hosts and adult stages maturing in vertebrate definitive hosts, typically seabirds. Despite its widespread occurrence in coastal ecosystems, the physiological and molecular consequences of P. botulus infection in the American lobster ( Homarus americanus ) remain unclear . title: Northward shifts and range contractions: future distribution of Plicosepalus acaciae in Vachellia woodlands of AlUla, Saudi Arabia
abstract: Parasitic plants such as Plicosepalus acaciae act as keystone species but can exacerbate host stress under warming and drying conditions. To inform adaptive woodland management, this study models the current and future potential distribution of P. acaciae under climate change scenarios in AlUla, Saudi Arabia. The maximum entropy model was used to analyze a dataset of 124 georeferenced occurrences collected between March 2023 and April 2024. title: The Role of Territorial Planning Policies in Groundwater Recharge
abstract: Identifying and preserving groundwater recharge potential zones (GWRPZs) is essential for integrating water security into territorial planning. While maintaining high recharge potential theoretically supports subsurface water storage and landscape resilience against extreme weather events, long-term spatial evaluations of how land-use policies preserve these functions remain limited. Despite the abundance of water resources in Brazil, insufficient coordination between land-use planning and groundwater management compromises water security. title: Enhanced weathering of glacial rock flour drives coupled inorganic and organic carbon sequestration in a five-year field experiment
abstract: Abstract. Enhanced rock weathering (ERW) has been proposed as a scalable carbon dioxide removal strategy, yet long-term field-based constraints on weathering rates and associated carbon sequestration remain limited. Here, we present a five-year field assessment of Greenlandic glacial rock flour (GRF) applied at 50 t ha-1 to a sandy agricultural soil in Denmark. Using a soil mass balance approach, we estimate that approximately 56% of the applied GRF dissolved over five years. title: Novel halotolerant microbial system enhanced by gamma irradiation for advanced multimetal bioremediation
abstract: BACKGROUND: Saline industrial effluents are difficult to treat because elevated ionic strength can inhibit biological treatment and alter metal speciation. This study evaluated two moderately halotolerant microorganisms recovered from seawater and shark-associated samples and examined whether gamma selection altered the performance of the more radioresistant isolate. RESULTS: The isolates were identified as Serratia proteamaculans PX875896 and Rhodotorula mucilaginosa PX876763 by 16 S and 18 S rRNA gene sequencing, respectively.
