title: Geophysical investigation at Sainte‐Marguerite‐sur‐Mer (Normandy, France): From a supposed landfill to a forgotten military network?
abstract: Abstract This study focuses on characterising a strong and unexpected anomaly observed during an electromagnetic induction (EMI) survey conducted on the chalk cliff plateau at Sainte‐Marguerite‐sur‐Mer, in the Normandy region, France. The site was selected for a long‐term study of chalk cliff coastal erosion that began in 2017 and has been studied for stability risk assessment through hydrogeophysical and thermal approaches since 2022. title: Magnetite Oxidation and Matrix Lithology Affect Sedimentary Recording of Geomagnetic Field Intensity: Evidence From Synthetic Sediment Deposition Experiments
abstract: Abstract Magnetite and maghemite are the most common carrier minerals of paleomagnetic information in marine and terrestrial sediments. Previous research has shown that environmental factors such as salinity, flocculation, bioturbation, and sediment lithology affect depositional remanent magnetization (DRM) intensity. title: Spatial assessment of wildfire risk using remote sensing and environmental variables in Thung Salaeng Luang national park, Thailand
abstract: This study aims to analyze factors influencing wildfire occurrence and generate a wildfire risk map for Thung Salaeng Luang National Park. Hotspot data were acquired using the satellite sensor of Suomi NPP and the VIIRS system over the study period ranging from 2021 to 2025, having a total of 420 hotspot records. Maximum Entropy Modeling was conducted on the relationship between the presence of wildfire hotspot occurrences and five environmental geographic variables extracted from the remote sensing data such as Elevation Above Sea Level, Slope, Aspect, NDVI, and LST. title: Evolución de las condiciones habitacionales y el acceso a servicios básicos en los distritos de Panamá : análisis comparativo de los censos de 2000 y 2023
abstract: This study compares the socioeconomic conditions of households across the districts of the Republic of Panama based on the 2000 and 2023 censuses. Variables related to basic services and the conditions of occupied private dwellings were analyzed at the district level, primarily applying Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to identify factors of housing deprivation and construct the Housing Quality Index (HQI). title: Fluid–structure interaction in a square array of submerged flexible stems
abstract: The evolution of flow structure is fundamental to establishing an accurate framework for predicting turbulent energy dissipation, momentum transfer, and sediment and nutrient transport within and above flexible stem arrays. The dynamics of flexible stems plays a crucial role in shaping these physical features. title: Bioactivity-based molecular networking reveals betaine lipids as potential antimicrobials in macroalgae
abstract: The global presence of multidrug-resistant bacteria underscores the need for novel antimicrobial agents. Marine organisms, especially macroalgae (seaweeds), are a promising source of new antimicrobials due to their unique metabolome, proliferative biomass, and widespread distribution. In this study, we investigated fourteen macroalgae species from ten genera for their antimicrobial activity against the pathogenic bacterium Bacillus cereus (ATCC 10987 & 11778). title: First Report of Vibrio harveyi From Starry Flounder ( Platichthys stellatus ) With Phenotypic, Pathogenicity and Whole‐Genome Characterization
abstract: ABSTRACT Vibrio harveyi is a prominent bacterial pathogen of marine aquaculture. Vibrio harveyi has not previously been reported in starry flounder. In this study, phenotypic and genotypic characterizations and pathogenicity assessments of V. harveyi isolated from starry flounder in South Korea were conducted. Phylogenetic analysis identified strains VH‐SF‐1, VH‐SF‐2, VH‐SF‐4 and VH‐SF‐5 as V. harveyi . Motility assays showed that VH‐SF‐2 displayed the highest activity at 27°C. title: Alcohol use and its associations with mental health across the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: BACKGROUND: While the COVID-19 pandemic caused major disruptions to social connections and lifestyles, many countries continued the sale of alcohol as an essential commodity. Evidence on change in alcohol use, and its association with mental health and wellbeing during the pandemic is, however, mixed and limited to initial periods of the pandemic. This study aimed to address these research gaps. title: River Health Assessment of the Ganga River via Geomorphic Metrics: The Anthropocene Context
abstract: ABSTRACT Rivers, particularly large river systems, constitute one of the most fundamental life‐support systems that have sustained civilisations and are projected to be a critical determinant for the future sustenance of human civilisations. A river can be termed a healthy ecosystem only when all the flora and fauna are in and along the river, the cultivation in floodplains is healthy, and the river's form is in equilibrium. title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Urban Expansion and Vegetation Cover Using Remote Sensing and NDVI in Mwanza City, Tanzania (2015–2025)
abstract: Rapid urban expansion can alter vegetation cover and the spatial distribution of urban green spaces. This study examined the spatiotemporal dynamics of urban expansion and vegetation cover in Mwanza City, Tanzania, between 2015 and 2025 using Landsat 8 imagery and a geographic information system (GIS)-based Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) analysis. Images acquired in August 2015 and August 2025 were assessed using consistent NDVI intervals to distinguish three categories: built-up areas/bare land, moderate vegetation and dense vegetation. title: Analysis of Spatial-Temporal Changes in Rainfall and Temperature of Baringo County from 1994-2024
abstract: Climate change is reshaping the ecological foundations of pastoralism in the drylands of Africa, where livelihoods depend heavily on seasonal rainfall. In Baringo County in Kenya, changing climatic conditions are increasingly altering rangeland systems that sustain pastoral livelihoods. However, despite growing evidence of climate variability and change in Kenya, there is limited spatially and temporally disaggregated evidence of how rainfall and temperature patterns are changing across Baringo County. title: COMPARATIVE EFFECT OF PRACTICAL DIETS FORMULATED WITH Chlorella, Spirulina, OR SOYBEAN MEAL MATRICES ON THE GROWTH AND DIGESTIVE ENZYMATIC ACTIVITY OF Macrobrachium tenellum PRAWNS
abstract: Developing nutritionally effective plant-based feeds is important for reducing dependence on animal-derived ingredients in freshwater prawn aquaculture. Wild juvenile Macrobrachium tenellum prawns were collected from a coastal river in Oaxaca, Mexico, and transported to the laboratory. Prawns were reared using a completely randomized experimental design with three dietary treatments featuring different plant protein matrices (Diet 1: Chlorella, Diet 2: Spirulina, and Diet 3: soybean meal), with four replicate tanks per treatment (15 prawns per tank). title: EDUCATIONAL STAND FOR PROGRAMMING AND CONTROL OF AN INDUSTRIAL PROCESS USING PLC AND HMI
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of an educational stand intended for programming and control of an industrial process using a Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) and a Human-Machine Interface (HMI). The proposed system aims to provide a practical learning platform for students in the field of industrial automation, enabling the development of essential skills in programming, configuration, and operation of modern control systems. title: Advancing multi‐objective optimization in spatial planning
abstract: Abstract Growing demands for food, energy, minerals and other natural resources are intensifying pressure on ecosystems. Meeting these demands while reducing biodiversity loss requires making decisions about which areas can simultaneously support sustainable development, conserve biodiversity and maintain or restore ecosystem services. title: Impact of the designation of Ciletuh-Palabuhanratu UNESCO Global Geopark (CPUGGp) on space utilisation in Ciemas District, Sukabumi Regency, Indonesia
abstract: The designation of Ciemas District as part of the Ciletuh-Palabuhanratu UNESCO Global Geopark (CPUGGp) has had an impact on land-use changes. Ciemas District has become a new growth center that attracts and increases the number of visitors. Therefore, land-use must be in harmony with spatial patterns and provide protection for its primary function as a conservation area. title: DEVELOPMENT OF A PROBABILISTIC METHODOLOGY FOR ASSESSING THE ENVIRONMENTAL SAFETY OF A NATURAL-TECHNICAL SYSTEM BASED ON THE RELIABILITY INDEX β (CASE STUDY: THE VOLGOGRAD BRIDGE)
abstract: The study aims to justify the transition from deterministic methods of assessing the aeroelastic stability of long-span girder bridge structures to a probabilistic paradigm based on the reliability index β (ISO 2394) and stochastic simulation. title: An integrated assessment framework for comparing and enhancing flood resilience in heterogeneous floodplains
abstract: Climate change is intensifying flood hazards in deltas, challenging agricultural communities dependent on hydrological conditions. Flood resilience has therefore emerged as an alternative to traditional risk management. Yet, comparative resilience studies often overlook how resilience measures vary across floodplain hydrological regimes (FHRs) within a delta. title: Linking soil erosion to phytoplankton communities: roles of suspended sediment and water quality in a sediment-laden river on the Loess Plateau
abstract: Soil erosion has a substantial impact on riverine ecosystems in the Loess Plateau. However, how these effects propagate through suspended sediment (SS) and water quality to influence phytoplankton communities and how these pathways vary across terrains remain inadequately quantified. In this study, we used models and in situ monitoring to analyze the cascading effects of the soil erosion modulus, SS concentrations, water quality parameters, and phytoplankton community structure in the Beiluo River Basin on the Loess Plateau. title: Cedar Tree in Assyrian Reliefs
abstract: This study examines the representation of cedar and timber acquisition in Assyrian royal discourse and visual culture, with particular attention to the Neo-Assyrian period. It considers how a valuable building material could become a sign of royal provision, access to distant landscapes, and participation in imperial networks. The method is an interpretive comparison of published royal inscriptions, museum catalogue records, and scholarship on Assyrian narrative art. title: VIR-GO: Indigenous Knowledge-Based Virtual Reality Media for Enhancing Students’ Disaster Literacy in Science Learning
abstract: Indonesia is located within the Ring of Fire, making it highly vulnerable to various natural disasters, such as earthquakes, tsunamis, and volcanic eruptions. However, this high disaster potential is not yet fully accompanied by adequate student knowledge and understanding of disaster phenomena and appropriate mitigation actions. This study aims to develop Virtual Reality Based on Indigenous Knowledge (VIR-GO) as an educational medium for natural disaster mitigation in science learning for junior high school students. title: Tourism, gentrification and loss of habitability in Teacapán and Chametla
abstract: Tourism and real estate development are advancing on the coastal localities of southern Sinaloa, Mexico, yet the perceptions of their residents are rarely measured. Using the preliminary data cut from the pilot survey of project FZ-HAB-0021 on the Factoriza UAS platform, this study described the initial behaviour of a fifteen-item scale with three dimensions, Presence of tourism, Living conditions and Rootedness, in Teacapán (Escuinapa) and Chametla (El Rosario). title: Digital Transformation of Cross-Border Logistics in Landlocked Countries: Drivers, Barriers, and Pathways
abstract: Landlocked developing countries (LLDCs) face structural disadvantages in cross-border logistics, with trade costs up to 74% higher than the global average and border crossing times twice as long as those of coastal countries. Digital transformation offers a pathway to overcome these geographic constraints, yet the drivers, barriers, and implementation pathways specific to LLDC contexts remain poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Motivated by the potential safety hazards posed by cracks in flow around bluff bodies in ocean engineering applications, this study investigates incompressible viscous flow around a sphere containing a central cylindrical bore at Re = 300. title: Structural characterization of laminarin and its preventive effects on the gut microbiota–butyrate–pancreas axis in severe acute pancreatitis
abstract: Dietary β-glucans are structurally diverse polysaccharides whose prebiotic functions are strongly dependent on their molecular architecture. Laminarin, a water-soluble β-(1→3)/(1→6)-glucan from the edible brown alga Laminaria digitata, has attracted interest as a functional food ingredient, yet its structure-dependent biological effects remain insufficiently defined. title: Place attachment and perceived insecurity on the Mazatlán malecón
abstract: The Mazatlán malecón is a coastal public space valued by local residents and, at the same time, a setting for experiences of insecurity. This study examined, using a preliminary data cut from the pilot survey of project FZ-HAB-0003 on the Factoriza UAS platform, the initial psychometric properties of a ten-item scale with two dimensions, Bond with the malecón and Fear on the malecón, and the association between them. title: Delineation of hazardous regions in the unit hypercube: A copula-based approximation for the identification of low-frequency compound occurrences
abstract: Abstract The probabilistic characterization of compound extreme events, defined as those arising from the joint action of several (generally dependent) drivers, is a central problem in engineering hydrology and water resources. The copula-based scenarios customarily used in the literature (i.e., OR, AND, Kendall, and survival Kendall) summarize multivariate risk by tracing a single boundary in the unit hypercube and assigning to it a target probability, or equivalently a return period. title: Clinically derived micro- and nanoplastic uptake drives spatiotemporally confined metabolic stress revealed by bond-selective imaging
abstract: Although microplastics and nanoplastics (MPs/NPs) are pervasive environmental contaminants, our understanding of cellular toxicity remains incomplete, as adverse effects are often attributed to long-term intracellular accumulation, while the spatiotemporal onset of cellular damage remains poorly defined. title: Forest fragmentation susceptibility assessment using the weight of evidence model in Mizoram, India
abstract: Forest fragmentation represents one of the major threats to biodiversity and ecosystem sustainability. Despite having the highest proportion of forest cover percentage to total geographical area among Indian states, forest fragmentation susceptibility in Mizoram remains a serious concern. The present study assesses forest fragmentation susceptibility in the state of Mizoram using RS-GIS based Weight of Evidence model (WOE). abstract: Assessing seismic site conditions through the time-averaged shear-wave velocity of the upper 30 meters (Vs₃₀) is fundamental for understanding local geological response and supporting seismic microzonation. This study investigates the subsurface characteristics of the Ketahun region, North Bengkulu, by integrating the Horizontal-to-Vertical Spectral Ratio (HVSR) method with Monte Carlo inversion to obtain a robust estimation of Vs₃₀. title: Storage, Connectivity, and Stream Drying in Headwater Systems: Modeling Across Hydrogeomorphic Features
abstract: Abstract Headwater streams play a critical role in the physical, chemical, and biological functions of downstream waters. However, predicting their specific impact on a landscape scale remains a grand challenge, prompting the development of the river corridor framework to integrate the study of stream channels and hyporheic zones with that of adjacent hillslopes and riparian zones. title: From plant blindness to plant awareness: a narrative and visual framework for botanical literacy
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Plants underpin terrestrial, freshwater and marine ecosystems, yet they often remain unnoticed in public consciousness, reflecting what is increasingly described as plant awareness disparity. This perceptual and emotional bias limits botanical understanding, weakens conservation engagement, and contributes to broader ecological disconnection. In this Perspective, I argue that narrative and visual storytelling can help shift attention from plant invisibility to plant awareness. abstract: Transformasi digital pada operasional lepas pantai mendorong perubahan mekanisme pelaporan kapal dari proses manual berbasis berkas dan surat elektronik menuju sistem terintegrasi. title: Journeys Toward Impact: A Critical Reflection on Participatory Evaluation in Five European Citizen Science Initiatives
abstract: Evaluating the impacts of citizen science is challenging, and existing approaches often fail to capture the complexity of outcomes across domains. The MICS project (European Union Horizon 2020 Measuring the Impact of Citizen Science, 2019–2022) addressed this by developing a framework to measure the impacts of citizen science across five domains: society, science and technology, environment, economy, and governance. abstract: Abstract This study investigates the main environmental factors causing deterioration in Al-Fustat archaeological area in Historic Cairo. A multidisciplinary approach was applied, combining field observations, hydrochemical analysis, remote sensing, and GIS techniques. Water samples were collected and analyzed to evaluate groundwater quality, while land use/land cover (LULC) and land surface temperature (LST) changes between 1996 and 2022 were assessed using Landsat data. abstract: The Union Territory of Ladakh, located in the Western Himalayan agro-climatic zone, represents an ecologically sensitive cold desert environment characterised by low precipitation, limited arable land, and a short growing season. Agricultural production in this region is highly dependent on efficient land and water resource management, primarily supported by glacial meltwater irrigation. abstract: Ekosistem mangrove, padang lamun, dan terumbu karang membentuk mosaik habitat pesisir yang dapat menopang tahapan hidup, sumber pakan, dan pergerakan ikan. abstract: Solidification Cracking Susceptibility of Commercial Copper-Based FeedstocksCopper alloys offer an excellent balance of corrosion resistance and strength and are of interest for marine and other applications. abstract: Electrolyte feeding strategy critically influences hydrogen production performance of anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMWEs), yet the mechanistic influence of electrolyte feeding strategy on bubble transport inside the electrolyzer remains unclear. title: Bridging the gap: Turkish English teachers’ experiences with technology-enhanced vocabulary teaching in rural areas
abstract: This study investigates technology use in teaching English vocabulary in rural primary and secondary schools in a city within Türkiye’s Black Sea region. Addressing the educational quality and resource gap between rural and urban areas, it focuses on how teachers utilize technology into young learners’ vocabulary teaching. abstract: Abstract Hydrokinetic turbines (HKTs) are promising devices for extracting energy from marine and riverine currents and open channels. title: Bioactive Compound from Nypa fruticans Endophytic Fungi: Isolation, Identification, Biological Screening, and In Silico Studies
abstract: Nypa fruticans is one of the unique and dominant mangrove species of tropical coastal areas that is traditionally used for the treatment of many different illnesses. The objective of this study was to isolate and identify bioactive secondary metabolite from endophytic fungi from trunk of Nypa fruticans. abstract: Urban pluvial flooding poses critical challenges to the operational continuity of transport infrastructure, yet city - scale assessments of flood - induced road disruption remain limited. abstract: Flood susceptibility mapping based on Multi-Criteria Evaluation (MCE) and the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) typically produces a single final map without examining whether the expert-derived weights would yield the same spatial classification if the weights were slightly altered. The invasive pasture pest weevil, Listronotus bonariensis (Kuschel), has established in both New Zealand and some of its offshore islands, causing significant economic damage. title: Examining microbial assemblage differences on plants preferred and avoided by threatened Hawaiian land snails to identify important food resources
abstract: The Hawaiian Islands, an isolated oceanic archipelago in the Pacific, had one of the world's most spectacular land snail radiations. abstract: BACKGROUND: Timely access to emergency medical services (EMS) is essential for improving survival outcomes and public health. In rapidly urbanizing Chinese cities, disparities in EMS accessibility are increasingly shaped by the spatial distribution of hospitals, population concentration, transport infrastructure, and built environment conditions. abstract: Green waqf has increasingly moved from a static charitable asset toward a productive instrument that can connect Islamic social finance, agroecological management, and rural economic empowerment. This study analyzes the contribution of Green Waqf to green job creation in integrated agriculture in East Java, focusing on the Sustainable Green Waqf ecosystem developed around Pisang Mas Kirana in Klungkung Village, Sukorambi, Jember. title: Taxonomic Revision of the Globally Widespread Cryptic Rhynchomonas Morphospecies Complex
abstract: Rhynchomonads are ubiquitously distributed, small, colorless, heterotrophic flagellates with confirmed occurrences in diverse aquatic and soil habitats. To date, Rhynchomonas nasuta (Stokes 1888) Klebs 1892 is the commonly accepted species. However, phylogenetic studies revealed considerable genetic divergence, suggesting that isolates of this highly successful morphotype do not all belong to the same species. title: Gastroprotective effects of Sapodilla fruit powder against ethanol‐induced gastric injury in Sprague–Dawley rats: In silico prediction and in vivo validation
abstract: Abstract Background Gastrointestinal disorders are rapidly increasing worldwide due to the disturbance of mucosal defenses. Manilkara zapota possesses significant therapeutic attributes to improve individual well‐being. Objectives The current study was conducted to evaluate the antioxidant activity, phytochemical characterization, and in silico and in vivo gastroprotective potential of Manilkara zapota fruit powder (MZFP) in ethanol‐induced gastric injury in Sprague–Dawley rats. title: Apatite fission track reveals uplift-denudation processes of granitoid mountains in East China: a case study of Mount Tianzhushan
abstract: Mesozoic granitoid mountains are widely exposed across East China, and their uplift and denudation evolution remain a key challenging scientific issue in the tectonic geomorphology of orogenic belts. Low-temperature thermochronology serves as a powerful tool to quantitatively constrain such geological processes. This approach is adopted in this study to investigate the uplift-denudation history of Mount Tianzhushan. title: Micritization and development of microporosity in miocene platform carbonates from NE Iberia: diagenetic processes and controls
abstract: Abstract Microporous limestones formed by micritization are widespread in Mesozoic and Cenozoic carbonate successions and constitute major hydrocarbon reservoirs worldwide. Despite the strong control of microporosity on petrophysical behavior, uncertainties surrounding its origin and evolution hinder accurate diagenetic modeling and subsurface heterogeneity interpretations. This study characterizes micritized carbonates from the Neogene Penedès Basin (NE Spain), which represents the onshore analogue of the offshore hydrocarbon-bearing Amposta Limestone. title: Integrated environmental assessment of plastic pollution in the São Francisco River estuary, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Plastic pollution has emerged as a major environmental concern due to its persistence, fragmentation, and capacity to release chemical additives into aquatic systems. Estuaries are particularly vulnerable, functioning simultaneously as accumulation zones and transfer pathways for plastic debris and associated contaminants. This study provides a combined assessment of macroplastics, microplastics, and plasticizers (bisphenol A – BPA and dibutyl phthalate – DBP) in the São Francisco River estuary, northeastern Brazil. title: Evaluating the evaluators: what are the trends and patterns in studies on mangrove conservation policy effectiveness?
abstract: Abstract INTRODUCTION: Mangrove forests provide critical ecosystem services but have been extensively converted or modified. With more than half of global systems at risk of collapse, global efforts are being undertaken to reforest, protect, and restore mangrove forests, but a comparison of the diverse interventions to conserve mangrove systems and their documented effectiveness remains lacking. abstract: This study presents a spatially explicit, high-resolution life cycle assessment (LCA) of short-rotation coppice (SRC) willow on land previously identified as suitable for willow production across 21 biorefinery facility supply zones in New York State (NYS). Using a fully linear weighted least squares (FL-WLS) regression model, we estimated annual soil organic carbon (SOC) change rates from direct land-use change (dLUC), ranging from 0.09 to 0.42 Mg C ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ (median: 0.24). title: PM2.5 and PM10 in industrial-suburban Chonburi, Thailand: Seasonal patterns and modeled mortality indicators
abstract: Ambient particulate matter remains an important environmental health concern, with concentrations influenced by interactions among diverse emission sources and seasonal meteorological conditions. Mixed land-use industrial-suburban areas within Thailand's Eastern Economic Corridor, where industrial activities, transportation, residential expansion, agriculture, coastal influences, and tourism coexist, remain relatively underrepresented in long-term air pollution studies. abstract: Abstract Soil salinization and alkalization often suppress microbial functional activity, triggering negative feedback loops in microbial metabolism, degrading nutrients and agricultural productivity. title: Effect of Paleosalinity and Paleoclimate on Organic Matter Accumulation in Lagoonal Environments: Insights From the Biluo Co Jurassic Black Shales in the Qiangtang Basin
abstract: ABSTRACT The lagoonal environment is a favourable facies for organic matter (OM) enrichment. However, the controls on OM accumulation in such a setting remain unclear. Based on high‐resolution organic and inorganic geochemical data of the Jurassic lagoonal OM‐rich black shales from the Biluo Co section in the Qiangtang Basin, the paleosalinity, paleoclimate, redox and biotic productivity were investigated to reveal the OM accumulation mechanism in a lagoonal environment. title: Functional Morphology of the Inner Ear of Southern Bluefin Tuna, Thunnus maccoyii (Scombridae, Teleostei): Adaptations for Hearing Within a Pelagic Environment
abstract: ABSTRACT The inner ears of teleosts are structurally diverse, reflecting the crucial role of audition in sound detection, balance, and social communication within each species’ ecological niche. However, very little is known about the inner ear morphology of large pelagic teleosts. This study investigates the functional morphology of the inner ears of southern bluefin tuna Thunnus maccoyii , using scanning electron microscopy and magnetic resonance imaging, and examines the auditory sensory epithelia (maculae) of the three otolithic end organs (saccule, lagena, and utricle). title: Geocentric spatial concepts in Mandarin: comparing empirical evidence with theoretical models
abstract: The goal of this paper is to analyse geocentric spatial concepts in Mandarin, i.e. spatial relations defined via reference to salient locations (“anchors”) in the geographic environment. We connect this analysis to the SocioTopographic Model, which introduces a complex taxonomy of spatial relation types. We show that Mandarin expresses cross-linguistically well-documented geocentric relations (e.g. Béi ‘North’, Dōng ‘East’), but also language-specific concepts (e.g. yán-hǎi lit. ‘around-sea’ for ‘seaside’). title: Beyond richness: seasonal and spatial responses of fish functional and phylogenetic structure to edge-interior gradients in Cymodocea nodosa seagrass meadows
abstract: ABSTRACT Seagrass meadows provide key ecosystem services, including shelter, nursery grounds and food resources for numerous fishes. Meadow boundaries create edge-interior gradients that can reorganize community structure, yet most assessments emphasize species richness or density rather than complementary biodiversity dimensions. Here, we quantified functional diversity and taxonomic-distance proxies of phylogenetic structure across edge and interior positions in three Cymodocea nodosa meadows in Gran Canaria Island (NE Atlantic), while also testing for seasonal variation. title: Screening legacy long-closure static-chamber records for greenhouse-gas interpretation in wastewater stabilization ponds: a reproducible case study from the arid Peruvian Andes
abstract: Legacy static-chamber records from wastewater stabilization ponds may retain information on gas buildup but can be unsuitable for flux estimation when closures exceed conventional protocols. We applied a reproducible screening workflow to chamber-headspace records of CH₄, N₂O and CO₂ from the Omo wastewater treatment plant, southern Peru (1,410 m). title: Microplastic distribution and potential ecological risk in the Amazon River estuary: No detectable differences in composition among environmental compartments in a mesotidal, high-discharge system
abstract: The Amazon River estuary is a highly dynamic system characterized by the world’s largest freshwater discharge (~200,000 m³ s⁻¹) and a strong mesotidal regime, with a tidal range of 2–4 m. Together, these hydrodynamic conditions strongly influence microplastic transport, redistribution, and fate. This study characterized microplastics in surface water, mid-depth water, and bottom sediments collected from five sampling stations in the northern sector of the Amazon River mouth, totaling 15 independent field samples. title: Magmatic sulfide segregation generates heavy sulfur isotope signatures in global arc systems
abstract: How sulfur is transferred from subducting slabs to the mantle and returned to the surface is central to understanding sulfur cycling in subduction zones. Arc magmas and volcanic gasses are commonly enriched in 34 S relative to the mantle, a signature widely attributed to slab-derived sulfur inputs. Sulfide saturation and segregation are widespread during magma generation and differentiation, yet their effects on sulfur isotope fractionation remain poorly constrained. title: Comparative post-hatching histogenesis of gallbladder and extrahepatic bile ducts in chickens, ducks, and pigeons
abstract: Introduction The post-hatching development of the gallbladder and extrahepatic bile ducts play an important role in the functional maturation of the avian digestive system. However, post-hatching histogenesis is poorly characterized among species. This comparative study investigated the histogenesis of these biliary structures in chickens ( Gallus gallus domesticus), ducks ( Anas platyrhynchos ) and pigeons ( Columba livia ) from one day after hatching to eight months of age. title: Species-specific bioaccessibility of microplastics by benthic macroinvertebrates
abstract: Effect and bioaccumulation tests have mainly used monodisperse microplastics, whereas natural microplastics are diverse. Consequently, understanding of their actual biological accessibility remains limited, which constrains risk assessment. The goal of this study was to investigate species-specific uptake of an environmentally representative microplastic mixture (ERMP; 9-5386 μm; PE, PP, PET and PS) in 11 freshwater and marine benthic macroinvertebrate species. Reconstructing the glacial–interglacial biogeographic history of closely related North American Andrena Fabricius, 1775 bees
abstract: Over the past 2.6 million years there have been ~52 glacial-interglacial cycles, which have had profound implications for species’ distributional changes through time. Despite the ecological importance of bees, the long-term historical distributional shifts of most species have not been studied using ecological niche models (ENM) or analyzed in depth biogeographically. title: Mosquito community structure, host-feeding patterns, and molecular xenomonitoring of zoonotic Brugia in Klang Valley, Malaysia
abstract: Lymphatic filariasis remains a public health concern in Malaysia, with zoonotic Brugia species occurring at the animal-human interface and presenting a potential risk of spillover to humans. This study investigated mosquito community structure, host-feeding patterns, and the presence of zoonotic Brugia in a non-endemic area of Malaysia. Entomological surveys were conducted in two locations; Bukit Gasing (forested area) and Pulau Carey (coastal area), between April–July 2024 and November 2024–February 2025 using Human Landing Catch and Mosquito Magnet traps. title: Algal symbiosis adaptively restructures the cnidarian microbiome to enhance holobiont metabolism
abstract: Abstract Microbiomes are integral to the function and resilience of cnidarian holobionts, yet the spatial and functional integration of microbial communities within host tissues remains poorly understood. Here, we show that symbiosis with photosynthetic dinoflagellates induces adaptive, tissue-specific restructuring of the microbiome in the cnidarian model Aiptasia, fundamentally enhancing holobiont nitrogen assimilation and metabolic flexibility. title: Influence of eco-friendly diesel fuel additives on fuel properties, engine performance and exhaust emissions
abstract: Diesel fuel used in transport, marine applications, and stationary power systems is vulnerable to storage-related degradation, especially in the presence of bio-components, which creates a need for environmentally benign additives that preserve fuel quality without compromising engine operation. This study investigates the effect of four eco-friendly diesel additives—liquid Effective Microorganisms EM(F), ceramic EM carriers EM(C), silver solution (SS), and colloidal nanosilver (CNS)—on fuel properties, engine performance, and exhaust emissions. title: The Freshwater Fish Cultivation Development Strategy in Ponjong District Lake, Gunungkidul Regency
abstract: Freshwater fish cultivation in lakes is an important form of aquatic resource utilization that contributes to food security and improves the economic well-being of rural communities, particularly in areas with limited water resources, such as Ponjong District, Gunungkidul Regency. One of the main challenges in managing lake-based fish cultivation is water availability, which is highly dependent on rainfall and consequently affects the sustainability of fish production. title: Asynchronous timing of hypoxia and thermal stress induces diel vertical movement
abstract: Abstract In heterogeneous landscapes, mobile organisms can track habitat conditions across multiple spatial and temporal scales, but selecting one condition often comes at the expense of another. In aquatic ecosystems, trade‐offs between temperature and dissolved oxygen (DO) are ubiquitous, and diel cycles of solar heating and photosynthesis can make them dynamic. title: Macro constraints and local eutrophication shape sediment nitrogen removal in the Eastern China Plain lakes
abstract: Abstract. Eutrophication poses a profound threat to the provisioning of ecosystem services in lakes worldwide. Understanding how eutrophication, alongside other biotic and abiotic factors, drives sediment nitrogen removal is essential for maintaining the intrinsic purification capacity of ecosystems and safeguarding water security. title: Drivers of Spatial Change in Seagrass Carbon Stock Amid Shifting Species Dominance
abstract: Abstract Seagrass meadows are recognized for their significant role in blue carbon sequestration and storage. However, these ecosystems are being altered by climate change, and consequently so too are the ecosystem services they provide. Here, we evaluate drivers of spatial variation in carbon storage among seagrass meadows in the Lower Chesapeake Bay, which underwent a temperature-driven shift in species dominance from Zostera marina to Ruppia maritima in the last decade. title: Seasonal hypoxia and nitrate depletion in water chestnut ( Trapa natans ) beds: Implications for nitrogen cycling
abstract: Abstract Dense beds of floating macrophytes can alter water quality by modifying dissolved oxygen (DO) and nitrogen (N) dynamics. Water chestnut ( Trapa natans L.), a non‐native annual macrophyte, forms extensive seasonal beds in freshwater systems in North America. The species is intensively managed to reduce negative impacts on native species, yet its effects on DO and nitrate (NO 3 − ) remain poorly studied. abstract: ABSTRACT Local adaptation in species with high gene flow can be facilitated through different genomic mechanisms. For example, multiple studies have demonstrated that chromosomal inversions (CIs) are important for adaptive divergence in systems with high gene flow because they help protect locally adaptive alleles from recombination. Although much focus has been given to the importance of CIs in harboring adaptive alleles, there are other mechanisms that can facilitate genetic divergence. title: What shapes public support for mangrove restoration? The role of perceptions of ecosystem services and disservices
abstract: Mangroves offer a wide range of ecosystem services, yet have historically attracted negative perceptions, often tied to real or perceived disservices. While global interest in mangrove restoration is increasing, success remains uneven, partially due to persistent social barriers, including limited stakeholder engagement. Understanding how public perceptions of mangroves influence restoration support could inform more effective strategies. title: Evaluation of Sargassum spp. Meal Inclusion in Diets for Prejuvenile Nile Tilapia
abstract: This preliminary study evaluated dietary inclusion of Sargassum spp. meal in feeds for prejuvenile Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) through method-specific feed characterization and a 67-day feeding trial. Two experimental diets containing 10% and 15% Sargassum spp. meal were compared with a commercial reference feed using 54 fish distributed among nine aquaria, with three independent aquaria per treatment and six fish per aquarium. title: Assessing greenhouse gas measurement consistency and traceability in the UK and Ireland atmospheric monitoring network using whole and synthetic air reference materials
abstract: Abstract. Atmospheric greenhouse gas (GHG) measurements are essential for assessing climate change and verifying national emission inventories. As global networks rely on high-precision observations of potent GHGs such as carbon dioxide (CO₂), methane (CH₄) and nitrous oxide (N₂O), ensuring accuracy between observation stations is essential. title: Adaptation of EU policy during geopolitical change: the impact on forest use, bioenergy, and climate security in the Baltic region
abstract: Abstract Background Forests in the Baltic Sea region store carbon, harbour biodiversity, sustain rural livelihoods and supply wood for materials and heating. Since Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, sanctions on Russian and Belarusian wood and energy have disrupted these supply chains. This raises concern that the pursuit of energy security may increase pressure on forests, weaken carbon sinks and shift environmental impacts abroad. abstract: Cadmium (Cd) accumulation in Portunus trituberculatus raises food safety concerns, yet its tissue-specific distribution during gonadal maturation remains poorly understood. Previous studies commonly combined hepatopancreas and gonads as “brown meat”, making it difficult to determine the relative contribution of individual tissues to Cd accumulation. title: Assessment of microplastics in the Mahananda, Barnoi, and Baral rivers of Bangladesh and their ecological risks
abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution has become an emerging threat to freshwater ecosystems, yet limited information is available for river systems in Bangladesh. This study assessed the occurrence, characteristics, and ecological risks of microplastics in the Mahananda, Barnoi, and Baral rivers. The analysis results revealed widespread contamination in both water and sediment, with clear spatial and compositional differences among the rivers. abstract: The Sassandra-Dagbégo Ramsar Site, along the coast in southwestern Côte d’Ivoire, is a wetland of major ecological importance because of its forest ecosystems, associated wetlands, and hydrological regulation functions. This area is subject to increasingly intense anthropogenic pressures in connection with the exploitation of forest resources and local populations’ needs for food and well-being, resulting in numerous spatial dynamics. title: Passenger Terminal Performance as Maritime Transportation Infrastructure in Supporting Port Area Development
abstract: Passenger terminals are not only service facilities for maritime travelers but also transport nodes that shape accessibility, mobility, and the functional relationship between ports and their surrounding areas. This study evaluates passenger-terminal facility performance and translates service-improvement priorities into implications for port-area development. A mixed survey and field-evaluation design was applied at Tanjung Perak Surabaya, Tanjung Emas Semarang, Benoa Bali, and Lembar Lombok. abstract: Abstract We investigate experimental observations of megaripple formation and migration near a shore‐parallel nearshore breaker bar. Experiments were conducted in the 2D Large Wave Flume at the O.H. Hinsdale Wave Research Laboratory at Oregon State University, USA. abstract: Introduction Micro- and Nanoplastics (MNPs) are pervasive environmental contaminants with increasing concern for human health and ecosystems. Their small size, persistence, and physicochemical diversity permit bioaccumulation, long-range transport, and trophic transfer covering aquatic, terrestrial, and atmospheric systems. abstract: SUMMARY Hypnea species are distributed across tropical, subtropical, and temperate regions. They exhibit high intraspecific morphological variation, which complicates species delimitation based solely on morphological characteristics. Recently, molecular analyses have enabled the validation of numerous species, the identification of cryptic species, and the description of new taxa. title: BRIDGING AMATEUR METEOROLOGY AND HURRICANE MONITORING: A PORTABLE WEATHER MONITORING SYSTEM FOR ISLAND COMMUNITIES
abstract: Hurricanes are extreme meteorological events with significant consequences for island communities, where geographical isolation, exposure to strong winds, and infrastructure vulnerability can intensify their social and operational impacts. In this context, real-time local weather monitoring can support preparedness, situational awareness, and emergency response. abstract: The tope, also known as soupfin or school shark ( Galeorhinus galeus , Linnaeus, 1758), is a medium-sized elasmobranch with a broad distribution, high mobility and globally classified as critically endangered. Like many elasmobranchs, G. galeus is undergoing significant population decline, with a 76% reduction reported in the Northeast Atlantic stocks. abstract: Abstract This study describes, for the first time, the morphophysiological development, allometric growth patterns, and the main initial ontogenetic events of Moenkhausia oligolepis , a species of ecological and ornamental importance in the Amazon region. Hatching occurred 16 hours after fertilization, under an average temperature of 25.36 ± 0.64°C with a pH of 7.28 ± 1.11. abstract: Hydrocarbon contamination from anthropogenic activities remains a major environmental challenge in the Niger Delta. Accurate geospatial mapping of contaminant plumes is required for targeted remediation. To assess the geospatial distribution and lateral extent of hydrocarbon-impacted soils in two selected communities. Auger hole sampling was conducted at seven locations (AH1-AH7) plus a control (C) in Ajeokpori (Study Area 1) and Aabue-Korokoro Well 003 (Study Area 2). title: Climate and market shocks drive productive diversification and income resilience in Chilean small-scale fisheries
abstract: Abstract This study analyses how climate and market shocks drive diversification strategies in Chilean small-scale fisheries (SSF) and their effects on household income. Using panel data (1998–2022) from CASEN surveys, fisheries landings, and environmental indices, we estimate instrumental variable models within a sustainable livelihoods and site assessment framework. title: Environmental triggers of resting spore germination in the chytrid parasite Staurastromyces oculus
abstract: Abstract Many parasites rely on a resting stage to endure across adverse environmental conditions or over periods of host scarcity. However, maturation conditions of the resting stage during dormancy and the proximate cues that trigger germination remain unknown for most parasite species, limiting our ability to predict when parasites reinitiate infection. title: Quantifying physical and market losses of hilsa fish (Tenualosa ilisha) value chain: a nationwide assessment of fishers and traders
abstract: Post-harvest loss of fish remains a critical challenge affecting food security and economic sustainability in Bangladesh. This study assessed the magnitude and causes of post-harvest loss of hilsa fish across Bangladesh at both the fishers and traders’ levels to estimate physical and market losses and identify the key factors contributing to these losses. A total of 4025 respondents, including 1312 fishers and 2713 traders, were surveyed using structured questionnaires. title: Trophic relationships at a restoration reference site identify key plant resources for a declining songbird
abstract: Abstract Introduction Habitat loss and degradation threaten many taxa, and restoring habitats requires understanding how management influences resource availability for imperiled species. Restoration often focuses on plant composition, yet identifying plants that support essential trophic interactions remains a critical need. Maritime grasslands are an imperiled, understudied ecosystem where this knowledge is limited. title: Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances as Emerging Pollutants in the Global South: Occurrence, Distribution, and Challenges in Latin America
abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are globally recognized as persistent environmental contaminants with significant implications for ecosystem and human health. However, knowledge of PFAS occurrence and management in Latin America remains fragmented. Thus, the present review systematically compiles and critically evaluates the peer-reviewed studies reporting PFAS occurrence and distribution in abiotic environmental matrices across Latin America and assesses international and regional regulatory frameworks. title: Metal enrichment and downstream concentration gradients in an agricultural ditch draining a long-term fertilisation experiment
abstract: Agricultural sediment surveys seldom quantify the downstream extent of metal enrichment. We measured Cd, Co, Cr, Cu, Ni, Pb and Zn in 24 surface sediment samples below the Palace Leas long-term fertilisation experiment at Cockle Park, UK. Eighteen samples formed a 452.5 m ditch transect, with three samples each from the receiving stream and an adjacent diffuse runoff line. title: Assessing ecological monitoring design using a hybrid approach to guide changes to long term monitoring: A zooplankton case study
abstract: Ecosystem monitoring frequently focuses on populations, but a community perspective better reflects food web ecology. We asked a common question among natural resource managers – how much sampling is needed to understand the community in my system? We identified two objectives: (1) provide a community perspective and (2) ensure computational effort does not become unwieldy. title: Spatial distribution, clustering and locational correlates of aquaculture enterprises in Nyeri County, Kenya
abstract: Abstract Spatially explicit information is necessary for aquaculture support, management and environmental planning. This study described the distribution of aquaculture farmers and production units, assessed spatial patterns, and examined locational correlates of aquaculture enterprises across the eight sub-counties of Nyeri County, Kenya. We analysed 1,203 registered farmer records, including 1,176 valid georeferenced locations for nearest-neighbour analysis and 1,191 farms for water-proximity analysis. title: Associations of redox conditions and organic matter with nickel and chromium partitioning in the Bahodopi River, a tropical lateritic mining river in Central Sulawesi

title: Strong Spatial Gradients in Habitat Suitability for Salmonids in a Proglacial River
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate change is causing the rapid retreat of glaciers, leading to the formation of new lakes and rivers as well as the evolution of downstream floodplains that could provide new habitat for species such as Pacific salmon ( Oncorhynchus spp.). However, these habitats downstream of glaciers may initially have hyper‐cold temperatures, elevated turbidity and high rates of sediment movement that could preclude successful spawning and rearing by salmonids. title: Soil nitrogen dynamics in riparian zones of two pristine Arctic rivers
abstract: Abstract Riparian zones act as protective buffers, filtering land-to-river nutrient inputs through retention and nitrogen (N) gas losses. While rapid Arctic warming and permafrost thaw may enhance terrestrial nutrient inputs to aquatic systems, comprehensive assessments of N cycling in Arctic riparian soils are lacking. Conventionally, these zones are considered inactive due to N limitation of Arctic soils and low temperatures, leaving their N cycling unexplored. title: Hydrogeochemical Indicators of Water Quality Degradation and Inferred Biological Stress in Razzaza Lake, Central Iraq
abstract: Razzaza Lake is considered one of the largest lakes in central Iraq. It extends across the governorates of Karbala and Anbar. The lake's surface area has markedly decreased, and its water level has dropped due to severe climatic changes in recent years, which have caused a significant decrease in freshwater recharge coupled with high evaporation rates. This study aims to evaluate the evaluation of the lake's hydrochemical and environmental characteristics, as well as its pollution levels, in order to determine water quality and its suitability for aquatic life and human investment. title: Deciphering morphometric and terrain-driven controls on groundwater recharge and agricultural suitability using geospatial and multivariate modeling
abstract: This study presents an integrated assessment of basin morphometry, groundwater recharge potential, and agricultural suitability in the Lower Thamirabarani River Basin, Tamil Nadu, using geospatial datasets and statistical analyses. The morphometric results indicate an elongated basin (Rf = 0.268; Re = 0.584) with a moderate drainage density (1.4 km/km 2 ), reflecting a balanced runoff response and a reduced tendency toward flash flooding. title: Seasonal and Spatial Variation in Acoustic Activity of Two Insectivorous Bats in the Galápagos Islands
abstract: Los murciélagos insectívoros se encuentran entre los mamíferos nativos menos estudiados en Galápagos, los cuales pueden ser vulnerables a presiones antropogénicas emergentes. Este estudio evaluó los patrones espaciales y estacionales de la actividad acústica de Lasiurus borealis brachyotis y L. villosissimus en tres sitios contrastantes de las Islas Galápagos: dos áreas húmedas de tierras altas en la isla Santa Cruz (Santa Rosa y El Camote) y un sitio árido de tierras bajas en la isla Baltra. title: Affinity, morphology, and diagenesis of Mesozoic conical nannofossils from the family Eoconusphaeraceae
abstract: Abstract Mesozoic calcareous nannofossils of the family Eoconusphaeraceae have traditionally been interpreted as nannoliths of uncertain biological affinity. However, their morphology, crystallographic organization, and occurrence in articulated coccospheres strongly suggest that they represent coccoliths produced by haptophyte algae. This study re-examines the genera Eoconusphaera Jafar, 1983 and Conusphaera Trejo, 1969 using light and scanning electron microscopy from an Upper Triassic section of the Northern Calcareous Alps and published Jurassic material. title: NUTRITIONAL COMPOSITION AND COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF LATES NILOTICUS (NILE PERCH) AND BARBODES BINOTATUS (SPOTTED BARB) FROM TUNGAN KAWO RESERVOIR, KONTAGORA, NIGER STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: Fish is a critical component of global food security and human nutrition, providing high-quality protein, essential fatty acids, vitamins, and minerals. Despite its importance, comprehensive nutritional data for locally consumed fish species in many Nigerian freshwater reservoirs remain limited. This study assessed and compared the proximate and mineral composition of two commonly consumed fish species, Lates niloticus (Nile Perch, family Latidae) and Barbodes binotatus (Spotted Barb, family Cyprinidae), from Tungan Kawo Reservoir, Kontagora, Niger State, Nigeria. title: Microplastics Are Prevalent in Striped Bass and Shiner Surfperch Tissues across San Francisco Bay, California
abstract: The ingestion of microplastics by fish is widely documented, but the drivers of contamination and the movement of particles within organisms are still not well understood. We investigated microplastic contamination in sport fish caught from San Francisco Bay in California, USA. We compared microplastic contamination in striped bass (Morone saxatilis) and shiner surfperch (Cymatogaster aggregata). title: Assessment of Heavy Metal Contamination and Associated Health Risks in Gomati River water in Lucknow
abstract: Heavy metal contamination in urban rivers poses significant ecological and public health challenges, particularly in rapidly urbanizing regions. This study evaluated the spatial distribution of heavy metal contamination along a 61 km stretch of the River Gomti in Lucknow, India, using the Heavy Metal Pollution Index (HPI), human health risk assessment, and multivariate statistical analyses. The HPI results revealed severe water quality deterioration, with 30% of the sampling sites categorized as highly polluted (HPI > 30) and 60% as critically polluted (HPI > 100). title: Sustainable replacement of fishmeal with Artemia biomass in diets for Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus )
abstract: ABSTRACT This study evaluated the effects of substituting fishmeal with Artemia biomass in aquaculture diets on growth performance and whole‐body composition of Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ). Four dietary treatments were administered in triplicate to juvenile Nile tilapia (44 g) stocked in 1m 3 cages in a pond at 30 fish per cage for 84 days. The diets were AT 0 (0% Artemia biomass), AT 50 (50% replacement), AT 100 (100% replacement), and COMM (Commercial pellets). title: Nanoplastic Exposure Impairs Host Fitness and Parasite Transmission With Transgenerational Maternal Reproductive Costs in the Daphnia ‐Fungal Parasite System
abstract: ABSTRACT Nanoplastics are emerging contaminants in aquatic ecosystems, but their direct and maternally transmitted effects on host–parasite interactions remain poorly understood. We investigated the effects of polystyrene nanoplastic exposure (50 nm, 5 mg L −1 ) on Daphnia magna infected with the fungal parasite Australozyma monospora across two host generations. title: Flooding‐Driven Greenhouse Gas Emissions From Global Upland Croplands
abstract: ABSTRACT Greenhouse gas emissions from temporarily flooded upland croplands remain poorly characterized in the global greenhouse gas budget. We combined field measurements from 11 maize‐field sites temporarily flooded across the North China Plain with a global synthesis of 23 flooded upland cropland sites to quantify diffusive emissions. title: Physiological biomarkers and hemoparasites in two gull species from human-altered landscapes
abstract: Abstract Human-altered landscapes expose wildlife to interacting stressors, including contamination, habitat modification, and altered food resources, potentially causing sublethal and often overlooked effects on health, immune function, and parasite dynamics. We assessed these effects by evaluating the physiological condition and hemoparasite prevalence and intensity of two gull species breeding in contrasting anthropogenic contexts in eastern Spain: yellow-legged gull ( Larus michahellis , YLG) and Audouin’s gull ( Ichthyaetus audouinii , AG). title: Analysis of Fishing Household Income in Leato Selatan Urban Village, Dumbo Raya Subdistrict, Gorontalo City
abstract: Fishers' income from fishing is seasonal and uncertain, so fishing households often seek other sources of income. This study aims to analyze fishing household income from the fisheries sector and to determine its contribution to total household income in Leato Selatan Urban Village, Dumbo Raya Subdistrict, Gorontalo City. The study employed a survey method with descriptive statistical analysis of 35 fishing households selected from a population of 70 households. title: Trophic Cascade of Shrimps, Ephemeropterans and Periphyton in a Neotropical Stream
abstract: ABSTRACT Food web theory predicts that a top omnivore would not induce a trophic cascade through intermediate consumers and basal resources. We test this prediction by performing a perturbation experiment in a three trophic level stream assemblage with a top omnivorous shrimp, two primary consumers (ephemeropterans and chironomids) and periphyton as the basal resource. title: Process-dependent recovery, characterisation and biological activities of crude carbohydrate-rich hot-water extracts from Halymenia durvillei
abstract: Hot-water extraction offers a practical and food-compatible method for recovering soluble constituents from Halymenia durvillei , but extraction conditions may affect extract concentration and biomass-based recovery differently. This study evaluated the effects of biomass-to-water ratios (1:25 and 1:50, w/v), temperature (70 and 90°C), extraction times (1 and 2 h) and sequential extraction cycles on crude carbohydrate-rich extracts from sun-dried H. durvillei . title: A High‐Resolution Stable Isotope Database Revealing Within‐City Tap Water Variability and Source‐Water Connectivity in Trinidad
abstract: ABSTRACT This Data Note presents a georeferenced stable isotope dataset from the island of Trinidad, comprising 309 water samples collected between 2018 and 2026. The dataset includes measurements of δ 18 O, δ 2 H and d ‐excess. title: Predator loss amplifies the disruptive impacts of heatwaves
abstract: Heatwaves are intensifying under climate change, often triggering the catastrophic loss of predators. Still, it remains unclear whether their ecological impacts on ecosystems arise from direct thermal stress or from altered food web dynamics following predator loss. Using experimental tri-trophic fresh water food webs, we independently manipulated heatwave intensity (none, moderate or severe) and predator persistence (fish removed during the onset of heatwaves versus fish persisted during heatwaves) to disentangle these pathways. title: Interfacial processes govern the differential release of dibutyl phthalate (DBP) and bisphenol A (BPA) from microplastics under dam-induced water-sediment changes: A combined kinetic and ecological perspective
abstract: Dam construction significantly alters hydrological and sediment regimes, creating novel environmental contexts for the fate of emerging contaminants. However, the release mechanisms of plastic-associated compounds from microplastics under these engineered water-sediment conditions remain poorly quantified. This study systematically investigated the release of DBP, a typical phthalate plasticizer, and BPA, a bisphenol-type plastic-associated compound, from polyvinyl chloride (PVC) microplastics in response to key water-sediment parameters. title: Ecological variability of Hippopotamus antiquus from the late Early–Middle Pleistocene of Megalopolis Basin (Greece): Evidence for dynamic habitats in a glacial microrefugium
abstract: This study investigates the ecology of the extinct European Hippopotamus from the late Early–Middle Pleistocene ( c . 900–400 ka) sequence of the Megalopolis Basin, a glacial microrefugium for temperate taxa in southern Greece. Using stable carbon (δ 13 C) and oxygen (δ 18 O) isotope analyses and microwear analyses of Hippopotamus dental elements, we reconstruct dietary variability, past habitat conditions and hydrological or climatic changes at intra‐annual, multi‐annual and millennial scales. title: Spatiotemporal Analysis of Temperature Extremes Under Future Climate Scenarios in the Borana Zone, Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Climate change has intensified temperature extremes worldwide, with particularly severe implications for semi-arid regions such as southern Ethiopia. This study assessed historical and future temperature extremes across the Borana Zone using ENACTS observational datasets (1985–2014) and bias-corrected outputs from nine CMIP6 global climate models under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios. Extreme temperature indices recommended by the Expert Team on Climate Change Detection and Indices (ETCCDI) were computed using the Climate Data Tool. title: Modelling the Source of 2017 Casamicciola Earthquake (Ischia Island, Italy): A Critical Review and New Insights into the Interaction Between Volcanic and Tectonic Processes
abstract: Abstract We investigate the source of the 21st August 2017, Md 4.0 Casamicciola volcano-tectonic earthquake (Ischia Island, Italy), which caused heavy damage on the northern flank of the Mt. Epomeo resurgent block of the Ischia caldera. We adopt a multidisciplinary approach that combines geophysical, geological and coseismic ground deformation data mapped since after the earthquake occurred. title: Experimental diagenetic transformation of biogenic aragonite to calcite in sulfate and/or phosphate-bearing fluids
abstract: The transformation of biogenic aragonite to calcite in phosphate or phosphate-sulfate bearing fluids was investigated through hydrothermal experiments at 60–80 °C up to 90 days. A phosphate-only system (BF) and a phosphate-sulfate system (BFS) were characterized by XRD, FTIR, and aqueous geochemical analyses supported by PHREEQC modelling. title: Attribution science and climate change litigation in India
abstract: Abstract In climate change litigation, attribution science is increasingly being used as an evidentiary tool to ascertain responsibility, accountability, liability, and provide redress the impact on human life and the environment. The Indian judiciary implicitly uses scientific evidence in an unstructured or fragmented manner without it being clearly labelled as attribution science. title: Drought characteristics of European river basins derived from GRACE and GRACE Follow-On total water storage (2002–2026)
abstract: Hydrological drought, i.e. a persistent deficit of water stored on and below the land surface, is poorly represented by traditional climate indices based on individual meteorological data. Now, well-established geodetic techniques provide a reliable insight into total water storage (TWS) anomalies. title: Spatiotemporal modulation of microalgae to boost biofuel generation from CO2 by the stick-to-culture strategy
abstract: The accelerating global energy demand, coupled with diminishing fossil fuel reserves and growing carbon emissions, underscores the urgent need for sustainable energy solutions. Autotrophic microalgae are promising cell factories for converting CO2 into renewable biofuels. However, conventional microalgal biofuels typically depend on energy-intensive or nutrient-deficient regimes that suppress microalgal proliferation, resulting in a critical trade-off between biomass growth and lipid biosynthesis. title: Interspecific Interactions Constrain Individual Niche Divergence and Reveal Energetic Cost of Niche Expansion
abstract: ABSTRACT Individuals vary in resource use, generating trophic niche variation that shapes a population's niche width (PNW). Interspecific interactions are predicted to constrain PNW, though individual responses are often heterogeneous. The keystone niche individual (KNI) framework identifies individuals that disproportionately expand PNW by exploiting resources beyond the population's realized niche, but whether interspecific interactions limit their emergence is unknown. abstract: Abstract Predicting the geoneutrino signal at underground detectors requires a local crustal reference whose precision matches the experimental uncertainty. title: Depositional bias governs fossil assemblages' structure in one of the world's most extinction-impacted megafaunal systems
abstract: The Quaternary collapse of megafauna ranks among the most profound ecological disruptions of the Cenozoic, yet its fossil signature remains deeply entangled with preservational bias. Nowhere is this challenge more acute than in the Brazilian Intertropical Region (BIR), one of the world's most extinction-impacted and taxonomically distinctive megafaunal systems. title: DIA-based proteomic insights into quality deterioration and spoilage biomarkers of chilled anchovies (Stolephorus commersonii)
abstract: Anchovy ( Stolephorus commersonii ) rapidly undergoes postmortem autolysis. This study investigated chilled anchovy degradation over 7 days at 4 °C using physicochemical, histological, and enzymatic analyses, coupled with DIA-based comparative proteomics between day 1 and day 7 samples. title: Comparative analysis of claw morphology, handedness, and brachychely in Austruca annulipes and Austruca perplexa (Decapoda: Ocypodidae) in Ca Mau, Vietnam
abstract: This study compares external morphology, claw handedness, and relative claw exaggeration in two sympatric fiddler crab species, Austruca annulipes and Austruca perplexa , collected from Ca Mau Province, Vietnam. A total of 206 adult males were measured across 19 morphometric traits, including carapace size, claw elements, and walking leg proportions. title: Turnover and ecological release drove biogeographic shifts during the Ordovician/Silurian transition
abstract: Abstract Whether mass extinctions consistently drive global homogenization or instead produce phase-dependent restructuring remains debated. Here, we evaluate the impact of the Late Ordovician mass extinction on global biogeographic structure and its relationship to biodiversity dynamics across the Ordovician/Silurian transition. title: Quantifying shark depredation and post-release survival in the Queensland East Coast Spanish mackerel Scomberomorus commerson fishery
abstract: Context Fishers report high levels of shark depredation and post-release mortality in the Queensland East Coast Spanish mackerel fishery, yet little empirical data exist for these sources of cryptic mortality, limiting the precision of stock assessments. title: Potential ecological and human health risks associated with heavy metals in agricultural soils and edible crops of Nagarkanda Bangladesh
abstract: Heavy metal contamination in agricultural soils and edible crops raises concerns about environmental quality and food safety in Bangladesh. This study investigated arsenic (As), lead (Pb), chromium (Cr), and cadmium (Cd) in 15 paired soil and edible crop samples from Nagarkanda Upazila, Faridpur. title: Individual and joint effects of heatwaves and resuspension on the aquatic food web depend on nutrient loadings: Implications for shallow lake restoration
abstract: ABSTRACT Shallow lakes provide many vital ecosystem services, particularly when dominated by submerged macrophytes. However, they face increasing ecological degradation due to multiple stressors, such as eutrophication and climate change, which lead to enhanced frequency of short-term heatwaves and storms. title: Russia and Norway on Svalbard in Russian Media: Morphosyntax and the Construction of Arctic Actors
abstract: This study examines how the Russian mainstream newspaper Rossijskaja Gazeta represented Russia and Norway in the context of Svalbard during 2022–2025. Svalbard is a Norwegian Arctic Archipelago with a unique legal status that allows other countries, including Russia, to conduct economic activity there. Using Keymorph Analysis, grounded in Corpus-Assisted Discourse Studies and Cognitive Linguistics, the study investigates how grammatical case patterns shape portrayals of the two states. title: Evolutionary oxidation of proteins in Earth’s history
abstract: Abstract Evidence for Earth’s oxygenation during the Great Oxidation Event (GOE) and Neoproterozoic Oxidation Event (NOE) comes primarily from the geological record. We report rising oxidation state of carbon (Zc) in proteins over billion-year timescales, a consistent trend recovered from diverse genomic datasets. abstract: Intensive Litopenaeus vannamei culture generates organic loading that degrades pond water quality, yet nutrient status, phytoplankton composition, and Vibrio abundance are rarely examined together within a single production system. This study characterized these parameters in four production ponds of one intensive farm in Probolinggo, East Java, sampled at three weekly intervals during November and December 2025. abstract: Denizyolu liner taşımacılığı, ülkelerin küresel ticaret ağlarına erişiminde ve düzenli mal akışlarının sürdürülmesinde önemli bir rol üstlenmektedir. title: Assessment of the accumulation of selected trace elements in agricultural and non-agricultural soils using contamination indices: a case study from Kahramanmaraş (Türkiye)
abstract: Soil serves as the foundation of our food system. Therefore, consistent and reliable information about soil is essential for understanding, managing, and protecting it. This study examines the concentrations of trace elements of environmental importance, including vanadium (V), antimony (Sb), tungsten (W), thallium (Tl), and bismuth (Bi), in agricultural and non-agricultural areas in Kahramanmaraş (Türkiye) and evaluates their accumulation levels using contamination indices (i.e., enrichment factor (EF) and contamination factor (CF)). title: From green-tide biomass to biochar: An integrated framework linking pyrolysis, properties, and carbon stability in Ulva prolifera
abstract: Recurrent Ulva prolifera green-tide threatens ecosystems, and greenhouse-gas release during the decomposition of accumulated biomass can diminish the climate benefits of algal carbon fixation. Pyrolysis offers a route to convert labile algal carbon into biochar with enhanced resistance to degradation. However, the relationships between macroalgal pyrolysis behavior, biochar properties, and carbon stability remain poorly understood. title: Leachate-Induced Groundwater Contamination Near the Pugu Kinyamwezi Dumpsite, Dar es Salaam, Tanzania: Hadrochemical Facies and Pollution Risks
abstract: This study assessed the impact of leachate induced groundwater contamination near the Pugu Kinyamwezi dumpsite and associated pollution risks - the region's largest dumpsite by landmass and waste volume. Groundwater samples were collected from ten stations around the dumpsite, including one control station, with physicochemical parameters analyzed at Ardhi University’s Environmental Engineering Laboratory. Key parameters analyzed included pH, electrical conductivity (EC), total dissolved solids (TDS), major cations (Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, Na⁺, K⁺), anions (NO₃⁻, Cl⁻, SO₄²⁻, HCO₃⁻), and selected heavy met

title: Evaluating the Suitability of Health Tourism Development from the Perspective of “Therapeutic Landscapes”: A Case Study of Hainan Island
abstract: This study explores a methodology for evaluating the component elements of health tourism destinations from the perspective of “therapeutic landscapes”. An index system for evaluating suitable areas of health tourism was established, and an empirical analysis was conducted using Hainan Island as a case study. The findings revealed that the primary constituent elements of health tourism area are natural and cultural environments, health tourism resources, and health facilities. The evaluation indicators for developmental suitability include a healthy environment, health tourism resources, healt
institutions: Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research

title: Incipient motion of microplastic particles: conformity with the Shields diagram under its original experimental premises
abstract: Abstract Predicting the transport and fate of microplastics (MPs) in aquatic environments requires a reliable understanding of the incipient motion of deposited particles. While several previous studies have attempted to apply the Shields diagram to MPs, they have commonly reported that low-density MPs deviate from the threshold curve and have proposed various correction frameworks. However, it remains unclear whether these deviations stem from the intrinsic material properties of plastics or from experimental conditions that depart from the fundamental premises underlying the Shields diagram.

title: Evaluating the Environmental and Biological Safety of Phosphonium-Based Porous Liquid Systems
abstract: Abstract Porous liquids have emerged as a promising class of advanced materials that combine permanent porosity with fluidity. They are often proposed as “green” alternatives in separations and catalysis, although their biological safety remains underexplored. Here, we present a comprehensive evaluation of the toxicity of two representative porous liquid systems based on methyltriphenylphosphonium bromide ([P1Ph3][Br]) and trihexyltetradecylphosphonium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)amide ([P66614][NTf2]), combined with glycerol and ZIF-8, across a spectrum of biological models. title: Effect of Foetal Bovine Serum in Oil‐Adjuvanted Vaccines on Spinal Deformities and Growth in Atlantic Salmon ( Salmo salar )
abstract: Numerous studies have shown that oil-adjuvanted vaccines (OAV) can induce a variety of different side effects in Atlantic salmon including spinal deformities (SD). Of these, a pathology first described in 2020 and named cross-stitch vertebrae has been associated with the use of inactivated salmonid alphavirus (SAV) vaccines. Historically, most viral vaccines for fish contain inactivated whole virus propagated in cell cultures. The inactivated viral component of the vaccine will, in addition to viral particles, also contain cell culture remnants such as cell debris, foetal bovine serum (FBS) an

title: ADMINISTRATIVE CAPACITY AND DISASTER RISK GOVERNANCE IN SMALL ISLAND PROVINCES: LESSONS FROM NORTH MALUKU, INDONESIA
abstract: Small island provinces face acute disaster risks due to their geographic isolation, ecological vulnerability, and exposure to natural hazards. Effective disaster risk governance in these regions fundamentally hinges on public administrative capacity. This study examines how administrative capacity shapes disaster risk governance in North Maluku, an archipelago province in eastern Indonesia. Employing a qualitative case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews with local government officials, emergency management agency (BPBD) practitioners, and community leaders, alongside
journal: UNIBRAH Journal of Education Social and Humanities Studies

title: Horizontal gene transfer and reciprocal chimerism in Compactonostoc (Nostocales, Cyanobacteriophyta) with evidence for two new species in the genus
abstract: The genus Nostoc has long been known to be polyphyletic, and recent taxonomic work has segregated several Nostoc-like lineages into new genera, including Compactonostoc. Until now, C. shennongjiaensis was the only described species in the genus. In a survey of biological soil crusts from Santa Catalina Island (California, United States), we isolated two Nostoc-like strains that phylogenetically affiliate with Compactonostoc. institutions: University of South Bohemia in České Budějovice

title: Manganese-dependent ammonium oxidation associated with sulfur redox cycling in lake sediments
abstract: Abstract The release of fixed nitrogen as dinitrogen gas (N2) back to the atmosphere plays a major role in global nitrogen cycling. One major pathway of N2 production is anaerobic ammonium oxidation (anammox). Anammox is often considered a nitrite-dependent process, despite the fact that other electron (e) acceptors such as metal oxides are more abundant in various natural settings. Here we present experimental evidence for a two-step relay process of manganese [Mn(IV)]-dependent ammonium oxidation associated with a functionally novel bacterial lineage in a lake system. title: Development of an Engineering Geological Zoning Map of Iraq Based on the Reclassification of an Existing Geological Map
abstract: This study presents the development of a nationwide engineering geological zoning map of Iraq through the reclassification of an existing geological map. The aim is to extend the available engineering geological information for Iraq and provide a regional - scale framework applicable to land - use planning, foundation engineering, infrastructure development, and other engineering activities. The geological formations exposed at the surface were analysed according to their lithological characteristics and subsequently classified into engineering geological zones using ArcGIS Pro. The engineerin

title: Too threatened to try: how extinction risk drives research neglect in rays and skates
abstract: Global biodiversity loss demands that research effort be directed towards species most at risk. Yet conservation science is biased by species' accessibility and perceived charisma, raising concerns that threatened species may be overlooked. We apply a structured causal modelling framework to 651 species of rays (superorder Batoidea), a highly threatened yet understudied lineage of cartilaginous fishes, to disentangle the drivers of research effort. We quantify the causal effects of taxonomy, extinction risk, accessibility (range size, depth, economic context, year of description) and charisma
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
