title: A Museum‐Curated, Voucher‐Backed 12S Barcode Reference Library for Fishes of the Ecuadorian Amazon
abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding is an emerging method that promises to expedite and improve biodiversity surveys by identifying species from the genetic material they shed into the environment. eDNA methods offer many advantages over conventional specimen-based surveys, but their effectiveness hinges on reference libraries, which for highly biodiverse regions such as the Ecuadorian Amazon are too often incomplete, inconsistently curated and disconnected from morphological voucher specimens needed to reliably identify and revise taxa. To address this gap, we collected approximately 5000

title: Web-based Direct-to-Consumer Marketplace for Small-Scale Fisheries Products: Rapid Application Development and Functional Evaluation in Jaring Halus Village, Langkat, Indonesia
abstract: Fishery and micro-enterprise products in Jaring Halus Village, Langkat Regency, Indonesia, are sold primarily within the village through face-to-face transactions and manual record keeping. This condition limits producers’ market reach to physically present consumers and provides no persistent transaction data for monitoring or business development. journal: International Journal of Engineering Science and Information Technology

title: Quantitative assessment of Raney nickel desulfurization for sulfur-bound hydrocarbon biomarkers in geological samples
Whale swimming evolution recorded in vertebral microanatomy from the Eocene to present
abstract: Among modern aquatic amniote clades that evolved pelagic locomotion, whales are a prime example, but timing and mode of evolutionary changes in their swimming are poorly understood. Here, we use 3D vertebral microanatomy derived from CT scanning to investigate swimming patterns in extinct whales. All vertebral centra from a single specimen of the extant common dolphin Delphinus delphis were used to provide a baseline for the correlation of microanatomical parameters and spinal movements in our dataset of fossil whales. title: Differential effects of moisture on surface versus mineral soil microbial communities in the High-Arctic
abstract: Microorganisms play key roles in nutrient/carbon cycling and greenhouse gas fluxes in High-Arctic soils. However, the influence of soil conditions on tundra microbiomes remains poorly understood. Using high-throughput sequencing, we studied bacterial, fungal and micro-eukaryotic communities in surface soil-biocrust matrices and the underlying mineral soil along two environmental gradients in Svalbard. title: Earth as a wasted planet: An ecocritical study of anthropogenic waste in Kim Stanley Robinson’s 2312
abstract: The Earth has long served as a nurturing habitat for both living and non-living entities. However, humanity’s anthropocentric invasion has culminated in profound ecological degradation. It reflects a fundamental rupture in the ethical relationship between Anthropos and the Anthropocene. The novelist, Kim Stanley Robinson, invites the attention upon the scattered geo-engineering and planetary manipulations in his novel 2312. journal: International Journal of English Language and Literature Studies

title: Ecology and morphology as drivers of passerine song differentiation across an island archipelago
abstract: We conducted an integrative analysis to explore possible explanations for the song differentiation in bird populations from the mainland and the Tres Marías Archipelago (TMA) on the central‐western Pacific coast of Mexico. We first analysed the effect of isolation on cultural transmission by comparing repertoire size and genetic fixation in four phylogenetically distantly related passerines for which previous studies have documented significant genetic divergence between island and mainland populations. title: Sediment-driven bioaccumulation of phthalates and bisphenol A in tropical freshwater fish: Species-specific exposure pathways and human health implications
abstract: Chemicals such as phthalates and bisphenol A (BPA), pose significant threats to aquatic biodiversity and freshwater ecosystem health, yet their partition dynamics and bioaccumulative pathways in understudied tropical river systems remain poorly understood. Herein, six (6) priority endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs) in surface water, sediments, and edible muscle of two commercially important fish species: black-chinned tilapia ( sarotherodon melanotheron ) and bagrid catfish ( chrysichthys nigrodigitatus ) from Ghana’s Densu River were analyzed. title: Sustainable Technologies for the Sequestration of Aqueous and Gaseous Pollutants: Role of Chitosan Based Biomaterials
abstract: The increasing pollution in aquatic systems with harmful substances and the persistent build up of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere have emerged as major environmental concerns, necessitating sustainable and efficient remediation strategies. The aquatic pollutants in question are highly toxic, persistent, and not easily removed by conventional treatment methods and are therefore a serious threat to aquatic ecosystems and human health. title: How concentration, temperature, and pH affect soapberry’s cleaning power compared to commercially available detergents
abstract: The widespread use of synthetic cleaning products significantly contributes to environmental pollution, creating the need for natural alternatives. In this study, the capillary tube method was used to investigate the effect of concentration, temperature and pH on the effectiveness of soapberry as a plant-based detergent and compare its effectiveness to commercially available detergent and bio-detergent. title: Gas permeation in flexible multilayer pipes: Multiphysics modelling and experimental validation
abstract: Flexible pipes used in oil and gas and emerging energy applications are subject to gas permeation through polymeric layers, leading to the accumulation of species such as CO 2 , CH 4 , H 2 O, and H 2 S in the annulus and potentially driving corrosion-related failures. Accurate prediction of annulus conditions is therefore critical for design and life assessment. title: Runtime Bias Correction of Parameterized Lakes in Climate Models
abstract: A novel approach is presented for improving atmosphere-lake heat and evaporative fluxes in global and regional climate models. The method involves deriving and applying runtime corrections to lake surface water temperature and lake ice, to reduce biases in the climatological annual cycle of these quantities. The bias correction procedure is developed for a particular single-column thermodynamic lake model but could, in principle, be applied to other lake schemes, including fully prognostic models with hydrodynamics. journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems

title: Effect of predation on the performance and microbial ecology of a membrane-based biofilm photobioreactor
abstract: Eukaryotic predation can have a significant effect on the performance of bacterial biofilm processes, yet little is known about the effect of predation on photosynthetic biofilms. This study evaluated the effects of predation on a membrane-based biofilm photobioreactor (MB-PBR) by introducing enriched mixed protozoa in the system. The effects of predation on performance were compared to a control in which predation was inhibited by the addition of cycloheximide, a eukaryotic growth inhibitor. title: Biodiversity footprint of public procurement in Finland
abstract: Abstract Halting biodiversity loss requires systematic action from all sectors of society. The public sector is a significant actor globally in creating markets for goods and services, public procurement representing on average 13–20% of national gross domestic product. In this study, we assessed the biodiversity footprint of public procurement in Finland in 2022. title: Environmental Trade-Offs in port energy Systems: Global evidence and transition challenges for West African ports
abstract: The global push for sustainability has increased pressure on ports to decarbonize. This review critically examines the environmental trade-offs of port energy systems and assesses how global experience can inform the energy transition of West African ports. It considers biofuels, hydrogen, onshore power supply, renewable energy and hybrid systems alongside the infrastructure, economic and institutional conditions affecting implementation. title: Can omnivores be considered keystone species? Bears as a study case
abstract: Abstract The functional roles of herbivores and carnivores in ecosystems have been relatively well studied: both can shape ecosystems through strong direct and indirect top‐down controls on other guilds. By contrast, the role omnivores play has been rarely explored, even though their diet spans several trophic levels and potentially has numerous effects on ecosystems through trophic and non‐trophic interactions. title: What shapes indicator politics? Analyzing the representation of gender equality in governance for the Sustainable Development Goals in subnational India
abstract: Indicator development for earth system governance involves choices that influence which issues are considered legitimate. This makes indicators inherently political, rather than merely technical tools that objectively inform policy decisions. This article proposes a framework of indicator politics and applies this to the development of inequality indicators under the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) in the Indian states of Tamil Nadu and Haryana. title: Assessment of Arsenic and Mercury Contamination in Water and Sediments Around the Jaboi Sabang Geothermal Area Using ICP-OES
abstract: The Jaboi Sabang Geothermal Area in Aceh, Indonesia, comprises four active craters that release geothermal fluids and gases into surrounding water sources used by local communities for daily activities. Despite the known toxicity of arsenic (As) and mercury (Hg) in geothermal environments, baseline data on their occurrence and distribution in local water and sediment remain limited. This study assessed As and Hg contamination in water and sediment samples using Inductively Coupled Plasma–Optical Emission Spectrometry (ICP-OES). title: Horizontal Gene Transfer from Fungi to Myxozoa: Genomic Evidence and Evolutionary Implications
abstract: Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) is increasingly recognized as an important mechanism driving evolutionary innovation in eukaryotes, yet its functional significance in parasitic lineages remains poorly understood. Myxozoans are obligate cnidarian parasites characterized by extreme genome reduction and complex two-host life cycles, making them an intriguing system for investigating the evolutionary role of HGT. institutions: Instituto de Ciências Ambientais, Químicas e Farmacêuticas

title: Dietary Interventions May Mitigate Health Risks of Per‐ and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Exposure Through Modulation of the Gut Microbiota: A Review
abstract: ABSTRACT Per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have emerged as a global public health concern owing to their extreme environmental persistence and multisystem toxicity. In recent years, accumulating evidence has highlighted a pivotal role of the gut microbiota in regulating the intestinal accumulation and elimination of PFAS. Distinct Cyanobacterial Taxa are Associated with Microcystin and 2-Methylisoborneol Production (MIB) in a Mixed Bloom
abstract: Cyanobacterial harmful algal blooms (cHABs) threaten drinking water supplies through the production of cyanotoxins and taste-and-odor (T&O) compounds, yet identifying the organisms responsible remains challenging in mixed cyanobacterial communities. We characterized a July 2025 bloom in Lake Kickapoo (Texas, USA), a primary drinking water source for the City of Wichita Falls, using microscopy, quantitative PCR, and Nanopore sequencing for targeted amplicon and 16S rRNA community analyses. title: Occurrence and characteristics of microplastics in dug-eell groundwater of the Kandy District, Sri Lanka
abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution is an emerging environmental concern, yet groundwater systems remain inadequately studied, particularly in Sri Lanka. Groundwater, which remains under-researched, is the primary drinking water source for some rural and semi-urban areas in the country. This study aimed to evaluate the occurrence, abundance, and characteristics of MPs in groundwater across Kandy District. Thirty wells representing urban, semi-urban, and agricultural settings were sampled. title: How lake sediment records inform archaeology: examples from the Americas and potential future applications in Colombia
abstract: Paleolimnology, the study of lake and wetland sediments, provides a powerful means of reconstructing long-term interactions among climate, environment, and human societies. Drawing on examples from across the Americas, where sediment records have clarified the environmental contexts and ecological consequences of agriculture, deforestation, hydraulic engineering, and demographic change, this paper examines how such archives can strengthen archaeological interpretation. title: What do fluid lithium isotopes record: Insights from long-term water-rock interaction experiments
abstract: Lithium isotopes are widely used to trace silicate weathering and its role in the long-term carbon cycle, yet whether fluid δ 7 Li values track weathering congruency, fluid residence time, or the reaction rate of solids remains debated. Here, we investigate this question using year-long water-rock interaction experiments with a range of lithologies (including gneiss and granite), and two starting-fluid compositions, combined with quantitative Li mass-balance modelling. title: Systematic Evaluation of Cyanidioschyzon merolae Across Photobioreactor Systems: Linking Reactor Design to Biomass Production and Biochemical Composition
abstract: ABSTRACT Extremophilic red microalgae are promising platforms for sustainable biotechnology, combining robust growth under selective thermoacidophilic conditions with production of thermostable phycobiliproteins and carbon‐rich biomass. However, reactor‐dependent effects on growth, product formation, and biomass composition remain insufficiently resolved. Here, we systematically evaluated the extremophilic red microalga Cyanidioschyzon merolae across cultivation scales and reactor formats and benchmarked its performance against the well‐established Galdieria javensis and Limnospira platensis .

title: Hovering in turbulent rock‐array microhabitats: Multidimensional kinematic responses of S chizothorax grahami
abstract: Abstract The interaction between flow and riverbed structures creates spatially heterogeneous turbulent microhabitats that influence fish station‐holding strategies and energy allocation. This study investigated the hovering behaviour of Schizothorax grahami in complex turbulent microhabitats formed by rock arrays of different scales using flume experiments. title: Complex evolutionary history and possible unrecognized diversity in Philippine waterside skinks (Squamata: Scincidae: Tropidophorus) inferred from molecular and morphological evidence
abstract: We present the first robust geographical characterization of variation and phylogeographic population structure in Philippine Tropidophorus (spiny waterside skinks), based on extensive sampling from throughout the archipelago and a combined focus on genetic and morphometric variation. Last revised more than 40 years ago, the Philippine Tropidophorus have never been the subject of an integrative study to evaluate their evolutionary relationships, genetic diversity, population structure, and species boundaries. title: A case study on attempts to remove invasive Largemouth Bass from two small lakes in Québec
abstract: Abstract Objective The intentional and accidental introduction of nonnative fishes has damaged freshwater ecosystems around the world. The Largemouth Bass Micropterus nigricans (LMB) is regarded as one of the most commonly introduced nonnative species globally. In 2021, LMB were detected for the first time (as an introduced species) in Lac Kingsmere (13 ha) and Lac Mulvihill (1 ha) within Gatineau Park, Québec, Canada. title: Generative inference model reveals political and economic motivations for road construction in past societies
abstract: Abstract The construction of roads in past societies reflects a trade-off between a preference for straightness and the influence of slope gradient. This trade-off is, however, also conditioned by other factors, principally the political and economic motivations of a past society. Our understanding of this trade-off and its relationship to these motivations is poor, hindered by qualitative studies that fail to explain variability in road construction, and non-comparative quantitative approaches. title: Weathered microplastics reshape gastrointestinal responses to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances during co-exposure
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are ubiquitous environmental contaminants, yet the biological consequences of their co-exposure remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the individual and combined effects of weathered polyethylene MPs and three representative PFAS (PFOA, PFOS, and PFBA) using Caco-2 cells and a mouse oral-exposure model, complemented by tissue distribution analysis and multi-omics profiling. title: How an endemic became widespread: the peculiar situation of the groundwater amphipod Niphargus boulangei Wichers, 1964 (Amphipoda, Niphargidae)
abstract: Abstract Niphargus boulangei (Amphipoda, Niphargidae), a rare groundwater amphipod from the northern continental range of the genus, was long known only from Pas-de-Calais (French Channel coast). Recent phylogenetic studies added records from Moselle (France) and Wallonia (Belgium). title: Vehicle interiors as mobile reservoirs of urban microplastics: seasonal accumulation, polymer composition and occupant exposure inferred from car wash vacuum debris
abstract: Vehicle cabins are enclosed, plastic rich spaces that people occupy daily, yet the microplastics that accumulate inside them are rarely measured. Debris removed by car wash vacuum cleaners offers a direct and largely unexploited window on that accumulation and is itself an unmanaged urban waste stream. Long-term effects of stocking density on biofloc quality, growth performance, and physiological responses of red tilapia in a hypersaline groundwater biofloc system

title: Early Climate Impact Assessments Targeted 2025—How Did They Perform for Global Water Resources?
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate impact studies from the 1990s produced projections for global water resources extending to 2025. We evaluate the first two global water resource assessments and the IPCC's 2001 statements on future water resources against subsequent observations. Temperature projections were broadly consistent with what has since been observed. title: DEVELOPING AN INTEGRATIVE STRATEGY AND STRUCTURE FOR SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION AND PRACTICE IN OKE- OSUN FARM SETTLEMENT IN OSOGBO
abstract: This study presents a conceptual and three-dimensional (Autodesk 3Ds Max) model of an integrated mixed farming system designed for the wetland ecosystem at Agric Farm Settlement, Oke - Osun, Osogbo, Osun State, Nigeria. abstract: Background: Engineers often apply published, generic SPT–CPT correlation ratios to estimate one test from the other when only one is available. abstract: Peatlands store large carbon reservoirs, but the landscape controls on their lateral carbon losses remain insufficiently resolved. We investigated dissolved organic carbon (DOC) concentrations and export along a bog–swamp forest–Klyuch River continuum within the Great Vasyugan Mire, Western Siberia. Peat-profile characterization, pore-water chemistry and hydrometeorological monitoring were combined to assess spatial and seasonal DOC patterns. title: Extracellular polymeric substances drive Curvibacter host adaptation and cospeciation with Hydra
abstract: Abstract The interactions between hosts and their microbial symbionts play a crucial role in shaping biological diversity and ecosystem function. Bacteria can adapt to specific host environments over evolutionary timescales, leading to co-speciation and the formation of specialized host-microbe relationships. Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying these adaptations provides key insights into the evolution of symbiosis and the stability of microbial communities. abstract: Mars is reputed to lack ongoing volcanic activity. However, marsquakes were revealed recently, and clues to volcanism younger than tens of million years have accumulated. abstract: ABSTRACT Regional variability and long‐term changes of past ecosystems likely had a strong impact on hunter–gatherer population dynamics, including the expansion of anatomically modern humans and the disappearance of Neanderthals. However, our understanding of these ecosystems remains limited, even when looking at large‐scale patterns, such as the extent and distribution of forested areas. abstract: Cellularization is the coordinated division of a multinucleate cell into many cells, a common life cycle transition across eukaryotes. In the best-studied model of this process, Drosophila melanogaster , cellularization requires actin and microtubule networks, as well as membrane vesicle delivery to drive the synchronous invagination of plasma membrane furrows. abstract: By snapping their claws, snapping shrimp create cavitation bubbles that release supersonic pressure waves when they collapse. Previously, we discovered that helmet-like orbital hoods protect snapping shrimp from blast-induced neurotrauma by damping the shock waves they generate and use as weapons. title: Trends in climate variables and their associations with crop yields in Fogera and Pawe districts, northwestern Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Understanding climate variability and its relationship with crop productivity is important for developing appropriate adaptation strategies in rainfed agricultural systems. This study assessed temporal trends and variability in rainfall and temperature and examined their associations with crop yields in Fogera and Pawe districts of northwestern Ethiopia. abstract: Abstract The tight sandstone reservoir in a certain block of the Dagang Oilfield exhibits a dual-porosity structure, comprising nanoscale matrix pores (average diameter: 11.99 nm) and natural fractures (50–100 μm). abstract: Natural predation where rarity meets rarity raises an important conservation paradox: when one threatened species feeds on another and conservation decisions can be challenging. abstract: The present research study focuses on how food can be interpreted as a sort of indentured resistance in Khal Torabully's selected poems. abstract: Microplastics (MPs) provide surfaces for microbial colonization, yet field-based comparisons between plastisphere and surrounding sediment communities in urban rivers remain limited. abstract: Mineral dust is one of the major light-absorbing impurities in snow and ice, and affects snowpack and glacier melting. However, the origin and composition of mineral dust deposited on snow surfaces, and how these vary over time and space, remain poorly understood. This study examined the temporal and spatial variability in the composition of mineral dust in an alpine snowpack in the Tateyama Mountains, Japan and evaluated the relative contributions of long-range-transported and locally derived dust to dust deposition on the snow surface. abstract: The match/mismatch hypothesis (MMH) predicts that consumers that are asynchronous with a key ephemeral resource will have reduced fitness. abstract: Tire-wear particles release diverse additive mixtures into aquatic environments, but the formulation-level drivers of species-specific molecular toxicity remain poorly resolved. abstract: INTRODUCTION: Rapid industrialization in Bangladesh, especially in Gazipur District, has raised concern over heavy metal contamination of soil and water and the associated health risks to nearby residents. This study compared the concentration, spatial distribution, probable sources, and non-carcinogenic health risk of five heavy metals (Hg, Ni, Mn, Zn, and Co) in soil and water in the Turag River areas in Gazipur District. abstract: The kernel oil of Balanites aegyptiaca Delile represents a significant yet underutilized natural resource in Senegal, possessing high nutritional and therapeutic potential that rivals common commercial edible oils. abstract: Abstract: The accelerating processes of global population growth and urbanization have led to increased use of transportation systems. This intensifies urban mobility and poses various environmental sustainability challenges. In this context, sustainable urban mobility has become increasingly significant. abstract: Ogoniland, in Nigeria's Niger Delta, has experienced more than six decades of oil exploration, environmental pollution, and population pressure, yet its landscape change remains poorly quantified at the local scale. abstract: H14 avian influenza viruses (AIVs) are rare, with limited data on their circulation in mainland China. abstract: Abstract This paper proposes Nobel Prize-winning economist Elinor Ostrom’s social-ecological systems framework as a basis for systematically identifying the actors, governance systems and resources that shape live music scenes. abstract: Environmental impacts endured by the Lowland Maya during the Classic Period (250 to 920 CE) included droughts, deforestation, and soil erosion. abstract: ABSTRACT Glass fiber fabrics used in exterior wall insulation systems are susceptible to alkaline corrosion and mechanical degradation in the highly alkaline environment of cement mortar. abstract: Decades of biomedical research have developed robust tools in molecular and cell biology, including cell culture systems, for model vertebrate species. Logistical constraints associated with remote fieldwork limit the application of these techniques to non-model species. abstract: Abstract Clouds strongly impact net surface radiation, creating differential heating patterns, and trigger land breezes that in turn organize cloud development. abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic seems to be something of the past, but the virus is still here and causing disease. We are not genuinely back to "normal." abstract: The eco-friendly and scalable metal displacement technique was used to synthesize silver and copper nanoparticles (CuNPs and AgNPs). abstract: Floating offshore wind (FOW) is moving from demonstration projects towards commercial-scale deployment, but the lifecycle greenhouse-gas implications of its anchoring systems remain poorly resolved. This paper presents a state-of-the-art review of how FOW anchors are represented in life cycle assessment (LCA) studies, focusing on system boundaries, functional units, lifecycle-stage coverage, anchor disaggregation, and the links between environmental impacts and engineering function. abstract: Placing cratons, orogens, terranes, and igneous whole-rock U-Pb zircon samples in their past positions within paleogeographic reconstructions provides insight into global geodynamics, enables testing of reconstruction models, and stimulates new hypotheses. We integrated these data with recent full-plate paleogeographic reconstructions spanning 1800–0 Ma. abstract: ABSTRACT For species with limited mobility, leveraging highly mobile species through animal transport can provide a mechanism for dispersal and range expansion. As such, migratory birds may serve as vectors to disperse mobility‐limited species long distances to potentially novel geographies. abstract: Abstract Aging drives tissue-specific lipidome remodeling, but comprehensive multi-tissue lipidomic profiles in rodents remain scarce. abstract: Abstract The modular architecture of multi-domain enzymes is a key source of functional diversity. GH18 chitinases exemplify this, possessing a variety of auxiliary domains that have been postulated to underpin their role as essential global nutrient cyclers. abstract: Mantle redox conditions and halogen budgets influence crustal ore formation, yet mantle domains beneath intraplate magmatic provinces remain poorly understood. abstract: Groundwater is vital for drinking and irrigation needs worldwide, emphasizing its major role in sustainable development. Monitoring groundwater quality is critical, particularly in rural areas, where it serves as a key resource, to avoid the potential health and economic repercussions of water contamination. The wells of the Mamozin watershed, located southeast of Duhok City, are an essential groundwater resource for the local population, providing both drinking and irrigation fulfillment. abstract: The expansion of shrub communities in the High Arctic significantly alters carbon (C) and nutrient cycling, yet distinct species are often treated as functionally equivalent in ecosystem models. abstract: Indonesia aspires to achieve high-income status and become the world’s fifth-largest economy by 2045, leveraging its natural resources, demographic advantages, and large domestic market. abstract: Fishing vessel safety remains a persistent gap in global maritime governance, particularly for distant-water fleets operating across multiple jurisdictions. title: Microplastics as vectors and reservoirs of pharmaceuticals and drugs of abuse: experimental evidence, mechanistic predictions and analytical challenges
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly investigated as particulate phases capable of interacting with emerging organic contaminants in aquatic environments. This review critically evaluates experimental evidence for pharmaceutical-MP interactions and distinguishes it from mechanistic extrapolation for drugs of abuse, for which direct sorption data remain largely unavailable. title: The ‘Great Frost’ of 1708–9 in Britain and the Condescensions of Posterity
abstract: Abstract This article explores the ‘great frost’ of 1709 and its impact on economic life in Britain, challenging a popular view that, based on gross domestic product (GDP) estimates, it was catastrophic. It shows that the annual GDP figures for the period have such wide error margins that they cannot establish the scale of the disruption; that the severe winter was felt in southern but not northern Britain; that there were, in any case, means of partially mitigating such disruptions; and that the economic difficulties that were experienced had various causes, not just those of a bad winter. abstract: This study aims to evaluate the effects of nuclear electromagnetic pulses, with a particular focus on source region electromagnetic pulses (SREMP), on essential urban infrastructure, notably telecommunications systems. Through systematic analysis, the investigation seeks to clarify the extent of disruption and the vulnerabilities SREMPs pose to urban communication networks, contributing to a deeper understanding of critical infrastructure resilience in the face of such electromagnetic threats. abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are tiny pieces of plastics, less than 5 mm in size. They cause a type of pollution that has become a public health concern worldwide.. abstract: Chilled mutton is highly nutritious; however, oxidation and microbial contamination during refrigerated storage can lead to quality deterioration, safety risks, and economic losses. abstract: Abstract This study explores how social network mapping and analysis can be applied to support community‐based conservation practice, and what benefits and challenges emerge in doing so, enlisting the Northern Rivers, New South Wales, Australia as a case study. abstract: Abstract Livestock systems in high-Andean environments can modify vegetation structure and soil conditions through changes associated with grazing management and land use. abstract: How was burial wealth distributed within a Neolithic fisher-forager society? This paper explores this question by analyzing the distribution of burial goods at three different Middle Neolithic Pitted Ware Culture (PWC) cemeteries located on Gotland, Sweden, dating to c. 3000–2300 BCE. abstract: Abstract Poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) is a widely used biodegradable polyester. Hence, the current study aimed at unravelling the chronic toxicity of an organophosphate insecticide, chlorpyrifos (CPF), on a battery of blood biomarkers, somatic indices and histopathological aberrations of liver and kidney in banded gourami ( Trichogaster fasciata ). abstract: ABSTRACT While solar‐driven photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting offers a promising route for sustainable hydrogen production, sluggish interfacial charge transfer and long‐term instability remain critical bottlenecks. title: Longitudinal Surface Water Viral Surveillance Following the 2024 Extreme Flood: One-Year Monitoring in Porto Alegre, Brazil
abstract: Extreme flood events can overwhelm sanitation infrastructure and drive the widespread dispersal of viral pathogens into aquatic environments. In May 2024, Porto Alegre (southern Brazil) experienced an unprecedented flood that caused record-breaking overflow of the Guaíba hydrological system and prolonged urban inundation. Here we report a one-year longitudinal environmental viral surveillance study, comprising seven campaigns between May 2024 and April 2025. title: Co-benefits of managing saline cropland for the Sustainable Development Goals
abstract: Soil salinization can constrain food production and alter nitrogen (N) losses to air and water, with implications for agricultural and environmental sustainability. These processes are linked to multiple Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), yet their implications for SDG-related outcomes remain poorly quantified. abstract: Gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) were successfully synthesized through a simple and green route using dried Citrus aurantiifolia extract as a bioreductant. abstract: This study evaluates the performance of Precise Point Positioning with Ambiguity Resolution (PPP-AR) using Wuhan University (WUM) final precise products for coordinate consistency and deformation velocity estimation at five InaCORS stations in northern Central Java. abstract: Sound is present in many ways in and around hydropower infrastructure, from environmental impacts and equipment monitoring to structural safety and the management of aquatic species. Yet these uses of sound are often separated by disciplinary and institutional boundaries, limiting what we can learn about the relationships between energy infrastructures, markets, and environments. abstract: Volcanism was once the primary source of sulfur transport on Mars, and its present-day surface preserves a geological record of these mineralogical processes. Sulfur plays a key part in the eruption process, forming sulfides, and less commonly sulfates in the magma chamber, and being expelled as sulfur dioxide-rich gas. abstract: Large dams have resurged in recent decades both to meet growing energy demand and to mitigate climate change effects. Historically, they have been associated with the exercise of State power, nation-building, and territorial control. In Chile, where water access and control are shaped by market mechanisms, the study of large dams requires an approach that accounts for their inherently political nature. abstract: Abstract Resistance to fluoroquinolone antibiotics is rising across bacterial pathogens, including the important pathogen Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( Mtb ), posing a major threat to global health. abstract: This study investigates how the same experiential attributes play different roles in shaping visitor experience evaluations and emotional responses across six theme park types. Based on 1660 questionnaires, a theme park experience scale was developed for cross-type comparison. abstract: Adult salmon enteritis (ASE) is a severe intestinal disease affecting spring Chinook Salmon (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha) in the Pacific Northwest. title: Compensatory abundance dynamics between an omnivore and a herbivore in agricultural landscapes
abstract: Population ecology grew from a question about how competition governs animal abundance, and its classic models center on intraspecific competition, by which a population is regulated toward its own carrying capacity. But abundance also responds to competition between species. Where two species draw on a shared carrying capacity, density compensation can occur, a decline in one offset by an increase in another. abstract: Acute heart allograft rejection remains a major barrier to long-term transplant survival, yet the mechanisms by which environmental factors influence recipient alloimmunity remain poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Nutrient cycling in freshwater ecosystems is an essential ecosystem service, partly facilitated by animals through transport and release of bioavailable nutrients needed for sustaining primary production. We hypothesized that societal extinction leads to reduced conservation efforts for the affected species, which may, in turn, be associated with their biological extinction. title: Cortical lacunae, not xylem embolism, drive interspecific differences in freeze–thaw hydraulic dysfunction of conifer fine roots
abstract: Winter snowpack loss exposes fine roots to freeze-thaw cycles at high latitudes and elevations, but the mechanisms of injury and reasons for species differences in vulnerability are not well understood. Motivated by yellow-cedar decline, we evaluated competing mechanisms of freeze-thaw hydraulic dysfunction (xylem embolism and cortical lacunae) and whether root economics strategy predicts susceptibility. title: An Anion‐Exchange Sorbent as a Support for Voltammetric Determination of the Ionic Form of Ti(IV) in Soil Extracts
abstract: Agricultural and industrial applications of fertilizers containing titanium components lead to the release of ionic Ti(IV) and TiO 2 into the soil environment, making them mobile and potentially bioavailable. title: Para-excavation: Geophysics as Partner, Not Prelude, in the Archaeology of Large Buried Sites
abstract: Abstract Archaeologists investigating large, stratified sites face a persistent problem of scale: research questions that demand diachronic, site-wide understanding are constrained by the cost, logistics, and ethics of extensive excavation. Near-surface geophysical techniques offer a powerful alternative for subsurface mapping, and a growing body of work has demonstrated the value of integrating these methods with targeted subsurface interventions in iterative, collaborative workflows. title: High-resolution mapping of pluvial flooding in ungauged agricultural catchments
abstract: Abstract. Accurate pluvial flood mapping in ungauged agricultural catchments is often constrained by a lack of calibration data. This study evaluates a parsimonious, high-resolution (1 m) distributed framework assessing peak discharge along concentrated flow paths, validated against 39 events in two nested experimental catchments (84 and 111 ha). abstract: Microbially induced calcium carbonate precipitation (MICP) is governed by the coupling between bacterial physiological activity and mineral nucleation; however, regulating such bio-mineral coupling remains challenging. Nanomaterials (NMs) offer reactive nano–bio interfaces that can link bacterial immobilization with heterogeneous CaCO₃ nucleation, yet their contribution to biomineralization efficiency remains mechanistically unclear. abstract: We investigate some statistical and transport properties of the relativistic standard map. title: Discrepancia entre superficie planimétrica y topográfica en San Andrés Tuxtla: implicaciones para la gestión municipal
abstract: El estudio aborda la discrepancia entre superficies planimétricas y topográficas en San Andrés Tuxtla, Veracruz, subrayando sus implicaciones fiscales, jurídicas y ambientales. La cartografía oficial reporta una extensión planimétrica de 955,3 km², pero el análisis con datos LiDAR de alta resolución (5 m) revela que la superficie real topográfica es mayor, de un incremento superior al 1,3%, lo que implica una diferencia efectiva de más de 12,3 km² adicionales respecto a la cifra oficial. title: A Waterfowl Reproduction Model to Predict Carryover Effects of Oil Spills
abstract: ABSTRACT For wintering and migrating birds, contamination from oil and other substances may delay arrival on the breeding grounds and lead to lower body mass upon arrival. These delays and losses of body mass could lead to smaller clutch sizes and lower propensity to renest. To determine potential effects of these consequences on breeding, we used an augmented version of an existing mallard ( Anas platyrhynchos ) reproduction model. title: Compositional Analysis of Transatlantic‐Era Glass Beads From Peki, Ghana: Provenance, Chronology, and Local Transformation of European Imports in the Gold Coast
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper reports elemental analysis results of 51 glass beads from Peki, an inland transatlantic trade node in southeastern Ghana. Using laser ablation–inductively coupled plasma–mass spectrometry (LA‐ICP‐MS), 91 compositional measurements were obtained, identifying three principal glass types: high‐soda, high‐lead, and potash‐lime glasses. Most beads likely originated in European centers such as Venice and Bohemia and were imported to the Gold Coast between the 17th and 19th centuries. title: Green synthesis of silver nanoparticles facilitated by cyanobacterium Lyngbya confervoides with their metabolite profiling, characterisations and antibacterial evaluations
abstract: This study aimed to culture the cyanobacterium Lyngbya confervoides (Lc) biomass for the preparation of crude aqueous and methanol extracts, and for a preliminary phycochemical investigation and molecular docking study. Biosynthesis of Lc-silver nanoparticles (Lc-AgNPs) was carried out, and nanoparticles were characterised using spectroscopic and microscopic techniques, followed by assessment of in vitro antibacterial efficacy against four multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens. title: Revisiting fertiliser strategies: Customised fertilisers for enhanced nutrient uptake, yield and profitability
abstract: Fertilisers are essential for increasing agricultural output and ensuring food security. In India, fertiliser consumption has increased substantially to 32.93 million tonnes by 2025 and the imbalanced and excessive use of fertilisers has led to declining soil fertility and reduced fertiliser use efficiency (FUE). In this context, customised fertilisers (CFs) have emerged as an effective strategy to address these challenges by providing balanced nutrition tailored to specific soil and crop requirements. abstract: Abstract Moringa oleifera (MO) leaf powder, a low-cost natural resource, has been extensively used for the removal of heavy metals from water. To overcome challenges associated with powdered adsorbents, including difficult separation and low recovery, this study details the synthesis and evaluation of MO-alginate (MO-Alg) bead adsorbents for the adsorption of arsenic, cadmium, iron, chromium, zinc, and lead from oil-polluted aqueous samples. title: Dating the Colonisation and Source of Adaptive Genetic Variation in the Iago Sparrow ( Passer iagoensis )
abstract: Ancestral adaptive variation is thought to play an important role in facilitating adaptation to insular environments. However, to properly evaluate its role, we need to determine the age of genetic variation. In this study, we investigate the Iago sparrow (Passer iagoensis), a generalist endemic to the Cabo Verde archipelago, to understand how genetic diversity is maintained in an island lineage where populations are likely ephemeral and adaptation to environmental extremes is ongoing. title: Implementación y Validación Funcional de un Sistema de Riego en dos Zonas para Invernadero Mediante Sensores De Humedad y Control por Histéresis
abstract: La automatización del riego en invernaderos requiere integrar medición de humedad del suelo, procesamiento local, actuación hidráulica y supervisión remota. title: Seroepidemiology of human leptospirosis in subtropical Bhutan, 2024
abstract: BACKGROUND: Leptospirosis causes approximately 1.03 million cases and 58,900 deaths annually worldwide yet remains underrecognized because infections are often mild or self-limiting and require serological confirmation. In Bhutan, limited diagnostic capacity constrains surveillance, and data on human exposure in high-risk subtropical areas are limited. This study aimed to estimate seroprevalence, identify circulating serovars, map geographic distribution of seropositive cases, and assess potential risk factors for Leptospira exposure among adults in subtropical Bhutan. title: Habitat selection models help inform critical habitat identification for a wide-ranging migratory ungulate
abstract: Assessing seasonal habitat preferences is crucial to understand patterns of habitat use in highly mobile species. Such knowledge can also help identify habitat essential to the recovery of endangered populations. Migratory caribou ( Rangifer tarandus caribou ) in Eastern Canada have experienced sharp declines during the last decades, and their habitat is under increasing pressure from climate change and human development. title: Optical Trace Ammonia Sensors with Ultra-Fast Response Time and Stability
abstract: Free ammonia poses a threat to aquatic systems already in very low concentrations (<25 µg·L-1) but is currently challenging to continuously monitor at these levels using effortless and compact analytical tools. Herein, we present an optical chemical sensor which overcomes the stability limitations of ammonia sensors based on pH-sensitive dyes. title: Investigating the impact of slash and burn (jhum) cultivation on sediment-discharge-nutrient dynamics in high-rainfall tropical hilly catchments
abstract: Slash and burn, also known as jhum cultivation, is the oldest agricultural practice in South and Southeast Asia. This study investigated the impact of jhum cultivation on catchment-scale processes, such as streamflow, sediment, and nutrient dynamics. Three experimental catchments, out of which two are under jhum cultivation (JH01 and JH02) and one forested (KF) catchment, in the Mizoram district, India, were identified. title: Substantial Neotropical bat diversity likely remains undescribed and vulnerable to extinction
abstract: Numerous undescribed species face extinction before formal scientific recognition. Despite research advances, the exceptional bat diversity of the Neotropics remains overlooked, with accelerating habitat loss threatening unrecognized lineages with silent extinction, requiring urgent conservation prioritization. title: Expression of a Nitric Oxide Synthase Modifies Arginine Metabolism and Accelerates the Response to Nitrogen Deficiency in Cyanobacteria
abstract: Nitric oxide (NO) is a signal molecule in organisms of all kingdoms of life, acting as a second messenger during stress responses, growth and developmental processes. Nitric oxide synthases (NOS) are enzymes that produce NO by catalyzing the oxidation of L-arginine to citrulline and NO. title: Modelación hidrológica e hidráulica del riesgo de inundación en la quebrada San Francisco, Piura, Perú
abstract: En cuencas con escasa información hidrometeorológica, delimitar zonas inundables exige combinar datos alternativos, evidencia de campo y modelación. Se modeló el comportamiento hidrológico, hidráulico y geoespacial de la quebrada del caserío San Francisco (Tambogrande, Piura, Perú) para identificar zonas inundables y estimar el riesgo. abstract: Pelabuhan merupakan tempat kerja berisiko tinggi yang memerlukan pengawasan K3 berkelanjutan. title: Geomorphic and topographic controls on metal and metalloid distributions in tropical rice-growing soils
abstract: Potentially toxic elements in agricultural soils can pose environmental concerns, particularly in tropical floodplains where rice cultivation interacts with geomorphic, hydrological, and edaphic processes. We evaluated total concentrations and environmental associations of Fe, Mn, Cr, Cu, Ni, Zn, Pb, and As in surface soils from three rice-growing areas of the Yuna River basin, Dominican Republic, with primary emphasis on Arenoso. title: SEASONAL AND LAND USE INTERACTION ON WATER QUALITY IN THE CAMPO ALEGRE STREAM, GOIANO CERRADO: EVIDENCE OF URBAN IMPACT
abstract: Freshwater ecosystems in the Brazilian Cerrado face escalating degradation from agricultural expansion and urban growth. Understanding the synergistic interaction between land use and seasonal hydrological pulses is critical for water resource management. This study evaluated the spatial-temporal dynamics of water quality and potential ecotoxicological risks in the Campo Alegre Stream basin (Santa Helena de Goiás, Brazil). abstract: Polynomial transformation is a classic mathematical tool in geodesy, used to convert coordinates between different reference systems. It is mainly used in cases where the exact geometric or physical model of the relationship between the systems is unknown, as well as in the presence of significant local deformations in the source data. title: Assessment of Pump- Based Drinking Water Quality Compliance with World Health Organization Standards in Central Gondar, Ethiopia.
abstract: Access to quality water is critical for public health; however, Ethiopia is grappling with challenges stemming from inadequate infrastructure and limited resources. This study evaluated the quality of drinking water sourced from large and medium-sized pump-based systems in Central Gondar, comparing the findings against WHO water quality standards. Employing an explanatory mixed methods research design, 415 respondents were selected through systematic sampling. abstract: The distinction between cultural and creative intellectual property (IP) in cities is becoming increasingly difficult to make, and the culture of landmarks tends to be treated only superficially. This study takes the landmarks of Xiamen as an example and develops an AIGC method that turns their visual identity into a design language. abstract: Aim of study: To assess the financial and economic feasibility of adopting agricultural Best Management Practices (BMPs) in lemon farming, accounting for environmental externalities and comparing them with conventional and organic production systems. Area of study: Region of Murcia (SE Spain). Material and methods: The study applies a financial and economic investment evaluation framework to lemon farming systems. title: Pangolin scales as a potential retrospective biomonitoring matrix for environmental and rescue-associated chemical exposures in endangered wildlife
abstract: ABSTRACT Pangolins are among the world's most trafficked and endangered mammals, yet their exposure to emerging organic contaminants (EOCs) remains largely uncharacterized. Their keratinous scales represent an untapped matrix for potentially non-invasive biomonitoring. This study developed and validated a modified QuEChERS-based extraction coupled with liquid chromatography–quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (LC-QTOF/MS) for suspect screening and targeted quantification of EOCs in pangolin scales. title: Hagen-Poiseuille distributed-pressure model of osmotically-driven cytoplasmic flow in severed axons
abstract: Repair (sealing) of traumatic plasmalemmal lesions involves the formation, movement, and accumulation of vesicles at the injury site by active transport and by passive bulk flow of cytoplasm. title: Biases and gaps in freshwater mollusks research in Latin America and the Caribbean: a multi-decadal bibliometric analysis (1976–2024)
abstract: Abstract Freshwater molluscs play key ecological roles in aquatic ecosystems, yet they are among the most threatened and least studied invertebrate groups worldwide. This study evaluates how scientific knowledge on freshwater molluscs is structured across Latin America and the Caribbean, testing the hypothesis that research effort is uneven and shaped by multiple knowledge shortfalls that constrain ecological understanding and conservation planning. title: DNA barcoding of freshwater fish species from Upper Lake: A Ramsar site, Bhopal, India: Implications for species authentication and reference barcode database development
abstract: Upper Lake, Bhopal, a Ramsar designated wetland and one of the largest natural freshwater lakes in central India, supports rich fish diversity and provides important ecological, economic, and fisheries resources. Accurate identification is expected to make proper conservation of any animal species, yet traditional morphometric methods are challenging and time consuming. abstract: Phase-transitional robots have long intrigued the scientists from multidisciplinary fields, yet their realization remains a formidable task due to the lack of soft materials that seamlessly integrate phase transition with actuation functionality. Here, we report phase-transitional hydrogel robots enabled by chemical reaction-powered supramolecular gelation of a peptide solution followed by a dehydration process. title: Age of weaning impacts the growth performance, intestinal morphology and gene expression of the tambaqui Colossoma macropomum larvae
abstract: Abstract Fish larvae feeding management represents one of the critical points for survival and aquaculture success. The larvae of many fish species require live feeds during early development, typically before being transitioned to formulated feeds through a process known as weaning. Despite the importance of tambaqui ( Colossoma macropomum ) , to Brazil’s aquaculture industry, the optimal timing for weaning and its effects on larval development remain unclear. title: More stopovers facilitate migratory waterfowl tracking shifting vegetation green‐up
abstract: Climate change is altering the phenology of food resources, and migratory birds may respond by adjusting migration timing to track shifting food availability (i.e. their phenological sensitivity). The ability to adjust migration timing can vary among species according to traits such as ecological guild, body size and migration distance. Stopover sites are critical components of migration, allowing birds to refuel and acquire updated environmental information. title: Emissions Poised to Rocket: Modeling the Environmental Impacts of Low Earth Orbit Satellite Constellations
abstract: Abstract The proliferation of satellite megaconstellations in low Earth orbit represents a significant advancement in global broadband connectivity. However, we urgently need to understand the potential environmental impacts, particularly greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions associated with these constellations. This study addresses a critical gap in modeling current and future GHG emissions by developing an open‐source life cycle assessment methodology, applied to 12 launch vehicles and 24 megaconstellations. abstract: The pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P. aeruginosa) is recognized as an international pathogen of significance due to its multidrug resistance and strong ability to create biofilm as the basis of chronic and device-associated infections. The two-component regulatory system PprAB is important in the biofilm network, where the response regulator PprB regulates binding, aggregation, and biofilm production in the extracellular environment. abstract: ABSTRACT Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly recognized as soil contaminants, yet their time‐dependent associations with dissolved organic matter characteristics, redox behavior, biochemical constituents, and biofilm‐associated responses are often investigated separately. abstract: Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) are bio-based plastics produced by bacterial fermentation from renewable resources. PHAs with unsaturated bonds can undergo post-biosynthetic chemical modification or crosslinking to improve material properties. Previous studies have demonstrated that sulfur-vulcanized PHAs exhibited rubber-like properties and increased toughness. title: Differential Patterns in β‐Diversity Among Plants, Soil Fungi and Insects Across Two Subarctic Landscapes
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Whether different organism groups show similar β‐diversity across space has major implications for biotic interactions. abstract: Specialised professional skills are required for sustainable facilities management to achieve operational effectiveness in commercial green buildings. The interest in the development of green buildings in Nigeria is on the increase, but empirical evidence on the competencies required to manage these facilities after occupation is still limited. abstract: ABSTRACT The present study evaluated the consequences of dietary β‐glucan on growth, haematobiochemical parameters, and stress‐related gene expression in stinging catfish, Heteropneustes fossilis . A basal diet was supplemented with 0%, 0.05%, 0.1%, and 0.5% yeast β‐glucan and administered to fish at 7%–4% of body weight per day for 100 days. title: Process-dependent shifts in conspecific negative density dependence during boreal forest succession
abstract: Abstract Conspecific negative density dependence (CNDD)—the stronger negative effects of conspecific than heterospecific neighbours on plant demographic performance—is a key process proposed to stabilize forest diversity, yet how it changes during succession remains poorly understood. Using a 25-year spatially explicit dataset from 148 post-fire plots in boreal forests, we show that species richness increases with stand age and that CNDD varies in process- and abundance-dependent ways across recruitment, survival, and growth. abstract: H9N2 avian influenza viruses are characterized by significant genetic diversity. Deletions within the hemagglutinin (HA) receptor-binding domain represent a notable, albeit rare, evolutionary trajectory. Here, we systematically characterized the multifaceted impact of a single-amino-acid deletion at residue 227 of HA (designated HAΔ227), a naturally occurring deletion within the 220-loop that overlaps a key antigenic epitope, using isogenic reverse genetics H9N2 viruses. title: Experimental study on performance and durability of Guangzhou soft soil solidified by a new slag-fly ash based cementitious material
abstract: The development of sustainable alternatives to Portland cement for soft soil stabilization is of great significance for reducing carbon emissions and enhancing infrastructure longevity. This study investigates a one-part slag-fly ash geopolymer binder containing solid sodium silicate for stabilizing Guangzhou soft clay. title: Perceived green-shipping knowledge and competency demands among Chinese enterprise respondents: an exploratory network analysis
abstract: Workforce-needs surveys can conflate broad endorsement, uniform answering and specific relations among knowledge domains. We applied a measurement-aware diagnostic analysis to perceived green-shipping knowledge and competency demands. abstract: Unambiguous evidence of sophisticated woodland and land-use management in Bronze Age southern Europe is presented from the Terramare culture in northern Italy. abstract: Abstract We present comprehensive data of daily subsurface temperature profiles for ten Egyptian cities, derived from Typical Meteorological Year (TMY) data. While ground temperature is a critical parameter for geothermal energy applications and building thermal performance, long-term measured subsurface temperature data across Egypt remains scarce. title: Isolation of High‐Purity Rutin and Quercetin From Tartary Buckwheat By‐Products Using HPLC Separation and MS Quality Control
abstract: Tartary buckwheat (Fagopyrum tataricum) is a nutrient-rich cereal abundant in flavonoids, including rutin, with excellent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and other health-promoting properties. Cultivated for its grain-like seed, the vegetative tissues of buckwheat are considered feedstock or agricultural waste. In this study, we found that the rutin content in vegetative tissues such as leaves and stems is significantly higher than that in grains and seed hulls. A simple and efficient extraction approach was developed to extract rutin from Tartary buckwheat leaves via a mass spectrometry-direc

title: The Teachers 'Perceptions of Elementary School Students' Critical Thinking Skills in Social Studies Learning
abstract: Critical thinking is a fundamental competency that requires systematic cultivation from the elementary school level, including through social studies instruction, which is closely related to students' social lives. This study aims to describe teachers' perceptions of elementary school students' critical thinking skills in social studies instruction. Employing a descriptive qualitative approach, this study involved seven fifth-grade teachers across five elementary schools in School Cluster X, Purwakarta District. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews based on four critical thin

title: A double diamond model-based design and evaluation method for medical transfer beds
abstract: This study aims to improve patient experience and healthcare professionals' operational efficiency during patient transfer by proposing an integrated design and evaluation method for medical transfer beds within the Double Diamond framework.First, initial user requirements were identified through User Journey Map (UJM) analysis and multi-stakeholder interviews to explore key challenges and potential design needs during the medical transfer process. title: SIKENDALI AMBON: Data Integration, Early Warning, and Supply Chain Control for Transforming Inflation Control in an Archipelagic Region
abstract: Inflation control in archipelagic regions faces distinct challenges: dependence on inter-island supply, weather and shipping risks, and data fragmented across agencies. This article describes the design of SIKENDALI AMBON, a governance change project that integrates price, production, stock, demand, distribution, and logistics data into a logistics balance, an Early Warning System (EWS), and a Decision Support System (DSS) for Ambon City's Regional Inflation Control Team (TPID). A qualitative descriptive case-study approach was applied using secondary data from Statistics Indonesia (BPS), Bank

title: Effect of dietary supplementation with Clostridium butyricum on growth, intestinal microbiota, metabolome and transcriptome in a hybrid fish ( Megalobrama amblycephala ♀ × Culter alburnus ♂)
abstract: Abstract This study investigated the effects of dietary supplementation with Clostridium butyricum on the growth performance, intestinal microbiota, metabolome and transcriptome of a hybrid fish ( Megalobrama amblycephala ♀ × Culter alburnus♂ ). Experimental fish were diet supplemented with C . butyricum at 0 (control group [CG]), 4.02 × 10 8 (L), 1.66 × 10 9 CFU/kg (T), respectively, for 8 weeks feeding. The results showed that the growth performance of fish followed the trend of T > L > CG. Compared to group CG, the microbial community structure in group T shifted significantly. The relative

title: Beyond Fragmentation: A Conceptual Taxonomy of Existing Methodologies for a Layered Analysis of Historic Urban Landscape
abstract: Urban analysis of historic cities faces a persistent methodological fragmentation. Existing approaches tend to operate within disciplinary fields, addressing either historical evolution, present spatial configuration, or cultural meaning, but rarely in an integrated manner. This paper proposes a taxonomy for the layered analysis of historic urban landscapes, and at the same time , it tests the validity of a conceptual framework developed around the proposed taxonomy. Conducting a systematic literature review , the taxonomy is structured around the 30 papers selected out of 169 retrieved. Scale

title: Enhancing urban water resilience through green infrastructure in Kathmandu, Nepal
abstract: Rapidly growing cities in developing countries, including Kathmandu, Nepal, are struggling to handle water issues driven by both urban growth and climate change. Conventional grey infrastructure is unable to address the rising problems of flooding, polluted water, and declining groundwater recharge. This work evaluates how Green Infrastructure (GI) might help make Kathmandu Valley more sustainable and enhance ecosystem resilience through better water management. This study develops an integrated urban water resilience framework for Kathmandu Valley by combining geospatial analysis, hydrologica

title: Broadscale Distribution and Pronounced Mitochondrial Phylogeographic Structure in the Freshwater Minnow Opsariichthys bidens Across China's Major River Basins
abstract: ABSTRACT China's complex river basins constitute a critical biogeographic setting for investigating genetic differentiation and lineage divergence in freshwater fishes. Opsariichthys bidens is broadly distributed among multiple, hydrologically isolated river basins, rendering it a well‐suited system for assessing mitochondrial phylogeographic structure across major river basins. Here, we used newly generated mitochondrial data to characterize broad‐scale genetic variation in O. bidens across China's major river basins. We analyzed 379 cytochrome b ( cyt b ) sequences sampled from 13 geographic
institutions: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

title: Governance-mediated value in sustainable trail tourism: shared responsibility, legitimacy, and stewardship in a nonprofit network
abstract: Long-distance walking trails support sustainable rural tourism, generating economic, environmental, and social value for host communities. Their viability often depends on governance arrangements involving public agencies, nonprofit organizations, and local tourism businesses that collectively manage environmental resources and visitor infrastructure. Although value co-creation is widely studied in tourism, less attention is given to how value is negotiated within stewardship networks supporting public tourism assets. This study examines how tourism businesses along Scotland’s West Highland Wa

title: Climate change impacts on hydrology and electricity production – a case study from Drammen river basin in Norway
abstract: In this paper, we have assessed how climate change might impact hydrology and electricity production in the Drammen River basin. To assess climate change impacts, downscaled scenarios from several combinations of GCMs, RCMs and bias correction algorithms from both CMIP5 and CMIP6 were used by a gridded hydrologic model (HBV) to simulate runoff for a reference period and a future period. Thereafter the energy market model EOPS has been used to simulate electricity production, reservoir water levels, bypass and flood flows. journal: International Journal of River Basin Management
institutions: Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate

title: Selective feeding and niche differentiation in adult boreal Odonata revealed by DNA metabarcoding
abstract: Abstract Diet choice plays a key role in shaping species interactions, trophic dynamics and ecosystem function, yet the extent to which insect meso‐predators exhibit dietary specialisation and prey selection remains poorly understood. Understanding how meso‐predators partition resources and respond to prey availability is therefore important for interpreting food web structure and ecosystem dynamics. title: Deciphering the construction of the ancient city of Palenque and its effects on the landscape
abstract: The ancient city of Palenque, in the Mayan territory, was established in a strategic position between the piedmont of the Sierra de Chiapas and the alluvial plain of the Michol River. The city became prominent during the Classic period (250–900 AD), when landscape modifications were carried out at different scales and with varying degrees of intensity during its construction. In this work, we present a combined study of natural and urban soils together with technogenic materials and geomorphological analysis based on LiDAR survey. The natural soils and Technosols (backfills) properties were de
journal: Boletín de la Sociedad Geológica Mexicana

title: Rancang Bangun Aplikasi Bank Sampah Digital Berbasis Web Dan Mobile Untuk Pengelolaan Bank Sampah Unit Di Desa Rawa Panjang
abstract: Bank sampah di Desa Rawa Panjang, Kecamatan Bojonggede, Kabupaten Bogor telah beroperasi sejak 2021 melalui 32 unit yang tersebar di 24 RW, tetapi pencatatan transaksi, tabungan, dan pelaporan masih dilakukan secara manual sehingga rawan kesalahan, lambat, dan tidak sinkron antarunit. Kegiatan pengabdian ini bertujuan merancang dan membangun aplikasi bank sampah digital yang mendukung pengelolaan lintas unit di tingkat desa serta menyosialisasikannya kepada calon pengguna. Kegiatan menggunakan pendekatan partisipatif melalui enam tahap, yaitu identifikasi kebutuhan, analisis kebutuhan dan sosi
journal: Jurnal Pengabdian Masyarakat Sapangambei Manoktok Hitei

title: Algae as Bio-Cell with Zero Emission Next Generation Energy Source
abstract: Traditional batteries demand a lot of energy to maintain and constantly need recharging. Once discarded, the heavy metals and chemical solutions inside them can leach out and poison the environment. With roughly 745 million batteries thrown away every year, they add a massive amount of unnecessary waste to our landfills. publisher: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology (IJRASET)

title: Challenges of soil arthropod community assessments: Large site-related variation and hidden species-level diversity
abstract: Arthropods are essential for maintaining soil ecosystem functioning. However, their full diversity remains insufficiently explored due to their taxonomic complexity, the limitations of traditional methods such as morphotaxonomy, and constraints associated with DNA barcoding approaches. In this study, we applied COI-based DNA metabarcoding to survey soil arthropod richness and community composition at a single timepoint across 28 long-term monitoring sites in Switzerland representing three land-use types, i.e., arable land, permanent grassland, and forest. A total of 6464 arthropod amplicon seq

title: Dynamic Supercooled Crystal–Gels for Ultrafast, Reversible Mechanical Adaptative Materials
abstract: Endowing synthetic materials with adaptability and responsiveness to dynamically optimize their states represents a premier frontier in biomimetic science. However, achieving life-like, rapid yet reversible adaptation under benign triggers remains hindered by high reconfiguration energy or delayed structural recovery. In this work, we present dynamic supercooled crystal-gels that achieve ultrafast, reversible stiffening without requiring continuous energy input. institutions: State Key Laboratory of Oral Diseases

title: Overtourism, Consumer Protection, and Destination Authenticity: A Comparative Legal Analysis of Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand
abstract: Despite its role in local economic empowerment and broader economic growth in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand, tourism activities can also present negative impacts for a tourism destination and tourists as consumers, particularly when the activities threaten the authenticity of the said destination. This phenomenon, often referred to as overtourism, raises legal issues regarding whether existing consumer-protection duties and remedies address losses from changed destination conditions. Employing doctrinal legal research with statutory and comparative approaches, this study compares business-

title: Therapeutic potential of sewage-derived lytic bacteriophages against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa: An in vitro study
abstract: Objectives Multidrug-resistant ( MDR ) Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a significant global health concern due to its high prevalence in nosocomial infections and limited treatment options. Lytic bacteriophages offer a targeted, antibiotic-free strategy to combat these resistant pathogens. This study aimed to isolate and characterize lytic bacteriophages from municipal sewage and evaluate their antibacterial efficacy against MDR P. aeruginosa strains collected from clinical samples. title: On- and Off-Design Endwall Aerodynamics of a High-Speed Low-Pressure Turbine Linear Cascade: Sensitivity to the Inlet Turbulence Profile
abstract: In current low-pressure turbine cascades, around a third of the losses are determined by the complex interaction between endwall boundary layers and blade profiles. Research has focused on the origin of secondary flow structures through numerical and experimental approaches, which shed light on vorticity transport throughout the cascades. This paper details the study of the endwall flow characteristics in the newly published open-access high-speed low-pressure turbine cascade SPLEEN. journal: International Journal of Turbomachinery Propulsion and Power
institutions: Von Karman Institute for Fluid Dynamics

title: Environmental DNA-derived indicators reveal species turnover and connectivity-related ecological patterns across patch-corridor-matrix framework
abstract: Habitat fragmentation alters biodiversity patterns and ecological connectivity across agricultural landscapes. Here, we investigated how Patch-Corridor-Matrix (PCM) landscape components influence animal community structure within a vineyard-dominated landscape in Southern Italy. Biodiversity was assessed using leaf-surface environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding, integrating arthropod and vertebrate detections with multivariate analyses, beta-diversity partitioning, indicator species analysis, and co-occurrence networks. title: Geomorphological mapping of the municipality of Chía, Colombia: methodological contributions and proposed classification
abstract: This article presents the application of a geomorphological mapping methodology developed in Brazil to the municipality of Chía, located in the Colombian Andes. The research relies on the interpretation of geological maps, topographic charts, satellite images, geotechnologies, and fieldwork, enabling geomorphological characterization across various scales of analysis. The methodology employed originated in Brazil driven by the RADAMBRASIL project (1970–1985) and is currently used with modifications and adaptations specific to the regions being mapped. title: AKUNTABILITAS KEUANGAN BUMDesa DALAM HILIRISASI PARIWISATA KREATIF DAN PENYERAPAN TENAGA KERJA
abstract: Penelitian ini menganalisis bagaimana akuntabilitas keuangan BUMDesa berfungsi dalam proses hilirisasi pariwisata berbasis ekonomi kreatif serta implikasinya terhadap penyerapan tenaga kerja di Kabupaten Lamongan. title: A novel nudivirus from the Jonah crab (Cancer borealis: Brachyura)
abstract: Nudiviruses are double stranded DNA viruses known to infect arthropod hosts. Around 20 different nudiviruses have been identified from crustacean hosts alone. In crustaceans, the hepatopancreas is the primary target of infection, where nuclei appear hypertrophic under histological preparation due to a growing intranuclear viroplasm. The Jonah crab, Cancer borealis, is the target species of an emerging fishery located in the New England (USA) region. title: Preferential Orientations of Subjovian Patera and Northern Hemisphere Mountain Populations on Io
abstract: Abstract Io's surface hosts numerous mountains and volcanic paterae generated by processes that occur at depth, including tidal heating and the resultant crustal recycling and subsidence stresses. Global trends in the shape and orientation of surface features could provide insight into these subsurface processes. Here, we present a global analysis of the shapes and orientations of Io's mountains and paterae. title: Perceptions of Opisthorchis viverrini infection and raw fish consumption among villagers in Champasak Province, Lao PDR: a qualitative study
abstract: Opisthorchis viverrini ( O. viverrini ) infection is a major public health concern in the Greater Mekong Subregion. Lao People’s Democratic Republic (Lao PDR) has been reported to have a remarkably higher prevalence. This study aimed to explore local perceptions and practices related to O. viverrini infection and raw fish consumption. We conducted a qualitative study on O. viverrini infection in villages in Champasak Province, Lao PDR. We investigated villagers’ perceptions and practices, focusing on the consumption of raw fish dishes. Focus group discussions (FGDs) were carried out in Septemb

title: Cell size asymmetry regulates neural stem cell proliferation and lineage expansion in the Drosophila brain
abstract: Asymmetrically dividing invertebrate and vertebrate stem cells can produce unequal sibling cell sizes but the function of cell size asymmetry (CSA) remains underexplored. Here, we use Drosophila neural stem cells (NSCs) to investigate how changes in CSA affect cell fate decisions and neurogenesis. Using live-cell imaging, NSC lineage analysis, and gene expression profiling, we find that altering CSA expands the NSC pool but restricts lineage expansion. title: Robust multi-criteria decision-making of additive manufacturing processes under preference variability: a Monte-Carlo and graph-based framework
abstract: Abstract Metal Additive Manufacturing (AM) process selection is affected by uncertainty in techno-economic data and decision makers’ preferences. When competing technologies achieve similar overall performances, deterministic Multi-Criteria Decision-Making methods may produce strict rankings that do not adequately reflect the robustness of the underlying evidence. This work proposes a methodological framework for interpreting probabilistic Analytic Hierarchy Process results obtained through Monte Carlo simulation. title: Carbon Sequestration Capacity of Sudlon Watershed in Barangay Central, Mati City, Davao Oriental
abstract: The study was conducted to quantify the biomass and carbon storage of the vegetative cover of Sudlon Watershed in Barangay Central, Mati, Davao Oriental. The specific objectives of this study were to determine the total area of the vegetative cover, to determine the vegetative structures, to identify the status of the vegetation, and to provide recommendations in relation to the management of the watershed. Actual surveying of the area as to the hectarage of various vegetative covers of the area was done with the aid of a Global Positioning System (GPS). The determined hectarage was then used

title: Recent Advances in Polymeric Hydrogel Materials for Fat, Oil, and Grease Mitigation in Sewer Systems
abstract: Abstract Fat, oil, and grease (FOG) accumulation in sewer systems is a major environmental and operational challenge, leading to sewer blockages, reduced hydraulic capacity, increased maintenance costs, and the formation of persistent deposits known as fatbergs. These deposits arise from complex physicochemical processes involving the hydrolysis of triglycerides into free fatty acids, followed by their reaction with divalent metal ions, particularly calcium (Ca2+) and magnesium (Mg2+), resulting in insoluble metallic soaps.
