title: Co-culture of Acetobacter pasteurianus and Lactobacillus plantarum enhances biofilm formation and improves vinegar characteristics
abstract: Abstract Acetic acid bacteria and lactic acid bacteria are core microbial components in traditional Chinese vinegar brewing, where biofilm-associated microflora form unique and stress-resilient consortia. This study explored bacterial adaptive responses and biofilm development in bicultures of Acetobacter pasteurianus with individual Lactobacillus strains. Across all bi-cultures, A. pasteurianus exhibited a competitive dominance over Lactobacillus strains. title: Cross-linked chitosan-nicotinic acid beads (CLC-NAB)—a novel adsorbent for the removal of Hg(II) ions from aqueous medium
abstract: Abstract An adsorbent, cross-linked chitosan-nicotinic acid beads (CLC-NAB) were fabricated in a sustainable green method and used effectively for the selective adsorption of mercury(II) from aqueous solutions. The CLC-NAB were characterized by swelling study, FTIR spectroscopy, SEM and elemental analysis. Optimum conditions for the adsorption process were determined by varying various operational parameters including initial pH, adsorbent dosage, initial mercury(II) concentrations, contact time, temperature. title: DNA Metabarcoding Reveals Flying Arthropod Diversity and Community Turnover Across Ancient Tea Agroforestry Landscapes in Southwest China
abstract: Ancient tea agroforestry landscapes in Southwest China are structurally complex systems that may support high arthropod diversity, yet their biodiversity value remains poorly documented. We used COI metabarcoding of Malaise-trap bulk samples to assess flying arthropod assemblages at four tea-associated sites in the Mengku Ancient Tea and Cultural System, Yunnan, China: a wild ancient tea tree community, a village-adjacent cultivated ancient tea garden, a forest-adjacent cultivated ancient tea garden, and a young-shrub tea plantation. Samples were collected from May to October 2024 and analyzed

title: Study on the biological characteristics of a new germplasm of grass carp (gynogenetic grass carp ♀ × gold grass carp ♂)
abstract: This study developed a novel grass carp variety, designated improved grass carp (IGC), by crossing gynogenetic grass carp (GGC, 2n = 48) females with gold grass carp ( Ctenopharyngodon idella red var., RGC, 2n = 48) males, aiming to integrate desirable parental traits and generate new hybrid germplasm. Using common grass carp ( Ctenopharyngodon idella , GC, 2n = 48) as a control, we systematically compared the muscle nutritional composition and genomic structural characteristics among RGC, IGC, and GC. title: Indirect costs of floods: a case study of highways road users
abstract: Abstract. Hydrometeorological events have a significant impact on road infrastructure and traffic flow. Floods can lead to the collapse or weakening of bridges, compromise river protection, and inundate riverine roads, thereby restricting or halting the traffic. These events incur additional user costs owing to the increased travel times resulting from the rerouting and reduced speeds on the affected roads. title: Chitosan oligosaccharide: prebiotic mechanisms and protective effects against obesity-induced metabolic syndrome
abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) encompasses a range of metabolic abnormalities, such as overweight, abdominal obesity, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and immune-inflammatory responses. The aggregation of these risk factors elevates the likelihood of diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Chitosan oligosaccharide (COS) is a low-molecular-weight polymer consisting mainly of D-glucosamine units. It is produced from chitin, the second most abundant natural polymer, through deacetylation and subsequent hydrolysis. title: Breastfeeding duration and residential setting in relation to childhood exposure to organochlorine pesticides and PCBs: a longitudinal study of the Rhea cohort in Crete
abstract: Despite decades-old bans, persistent organic pollutants (POPs), including organochlorine pesticides (OCPs) and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), remain a public health concern owing to persistence and bioaccumulation. Previous Rhea mother-child cohort analyses (Crete, Greece) reported notably high DDE (DDT's main metabolite) in children, raising questions about postnatal pathways sustaining this post-ban burden. title: Biocatalysts for Peptide Geranylation With Linear and Cyclic Prenyl Groups
abstract: Prenylation improves the bioactivity and therapeutic properties of peptides from natural product and synthetic origin. Prenyltransferases (PTs) catalyze peptide prenylation under mild conditions with often remarkable chemo- and regioselectivity. Representatives from structurally distinct prenyltransferase families involved in ribosomal peptide biosynthesis revealed a large potential for chemoenzymatic peptide functionalization with linear prenyl donors. title: Interfacial Electronic Coupling and Surface Reconstruction in Co(OH) 2 @NiFe‐btz for Durable Alkaline Oxygen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Coupling metal hydroxides with coordination frameworks offers a route to active and durable oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrodes. A binder‐free Co(OH) 2 @NiFe‐btz heterostructure, where btz is 1,4‐bis(4H‐1,2,4‐triazol‐4‐yl)benzene, is constructed on nickel foam through solvothermal growth followed by electrodeposition. Microscopy reveals close contact between Co(OH) 2 nanosheets and the framework. title: Some like it hot, but others might not: the implications of climate change for the conservation of South African freshwater crab species
abstract: Abstract Primary freshwater crabs are keystone aquatic species, yet the potential impact of climate change on their distribution and conservation status remains unknown, particularly in biodiversity-rich areas such as South Africa. We employed maximum entropy and climatic niche modelling to evaluate the effects of climate change on the distribution of 17 Potamonautes species in South Africa and estimate protected area coverage for suitable habitats under both current and future climate projections of increased temperature, and the impact on the conservation of these species. title: Density optimization of pearlspot, Etroplus suratensis (Bloch, 1790), fry and fingerlings for live transportation
abstract: Aim: The study aimed to identifying optimal stocking densities and transport durations of Pearlspot (Etroplus suratensis) of varying sizes (1–3 inches) in closed, oxygenated systems. Methodology: Pearlspot fry and fingerlings were transported for 6, 12, 18, and 24 hr in 30 l polythene bags containing 5 l of oxygenated 15 ppt brackishwater. In Trial one, 1-inch fry (2.5-2.7 cm) were packed at stocking densities of 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100 fish l-1. title: Overall material sustainability assessment of earthquake debris rca in pavement base layers using an entropy-weighted adaptive SAFE–fuzzy model
abstract: Abstract The massive accumulation of debris following the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes necessitates sustainable resource recovery strategies for resilient infrastructure reconstruction. This study establishes a multi-criteria decision-making framework to evaluate the Overall Material Sustainability (OMS) of pavement base layers incorporating earthquake-induced Recycled Concrete Aggregates (RCA) at varying replacement ratios (0% to 100%). title: Predator Becomes Prey: Records of Intraguild Predation Between Velvet Worms (Onychophora) and Arthropods (Arthropoda) With an Expanded Review of Predation on Velvet Worms
abstract: From 3954 citizen-science observations screened, we report novel cases of predation by omnivorous arthropods on velvet worms, including the first confirmed records for harvestmen and a cave wētā. Using photographic evidence derived from citizen-science observations, we document multiple predation events involving harvestmen (Opiliones: Cranaidae and Triaenonychidae) and a cave wētā (Orthoptera: Rhaphidophoridae), encompassing both intraguild predation and higher-order opportunistic predation within cryptic terrestrial habitats. institutions: Museo del Instituto de Zoología Agrícola

title: Characterization of clinical isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii and comparative proteomic profiling among strong and weak biofilm formers
abstract: ABSTRACT Acinetobacter baumannii , a critical priority pathogen, is also notable for its biofilm-forming abilities on medical devices like ventilators, catheters, and surgical drain tubes. The biofilm formation causes increased tolerance against antibiotics, making treatment difficult. The clinical isolates of A. baumannii present varied biofilm-forming capacity; hence, understanding the molecular determinants responsible for strong biofilm is crucial. institutions: National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research

title: The Application of Total Quality Management (TQM) Approaches to Disaster Risk Reduction and Recovery in Nigeria
abstract: Nigeria has lived with floods, erosion, drought, pollution and conflict-driven displacement for decades, yet the performance of its disaster programmes is still judged more by activity than by the reliability of results. This article asks whether the principles and tools of Total Quality Management (TQM) can make disaster risk reduction (DRR) and recovery more dependable. Using a structured narrative review of the quality-management and disaster-management literatures, together with a descriptive analysis of figures published by the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) for the 2022, 202
journal: International Journal of Advanced Multidisciplinary Research and Studies

title: Crystallized labor, commodity fetishism, and the logic of food waste in hospitality and tourism
abstract: This conceptual paper approaches the phenomenon of food waste in hospitality and tourism through the Marxist theory of labor. It re-interprets labor as a physical process shifting from gaseous intentions and skills to liquid monetary exchange and solid crystallization. In the hospitality and tourism food supply chain, the paper identifies three major strata of actors: farmers, chefs, and customers. title: Rigid-in-flexible caragana cellulose-integrated chitosan/poly(AMPS) hydrogels with reinforced network architecture for ultrahigh diclofenac capture
abstract: Natural Caragana cellulose fiber (CKC) extracted from the stems of Caragana korshinskii (CK) were incorporated into a chitosan/poly(2-acrylamido-2-methylpropanesulfonic acid) (CS/PAMPS) hydrogel matrix to evaluate its effect on network structure and diclofenac sodium (DCF) adsorption performance. SEM and compression testing revealed that the composite hydrogel containing 2.5 wt.% CKC (CAC0.2) exhibited a more open and interconnected macroporous morphology and enhanced compressive strength compared to the CKC-free hydrogel. title: Optimizing roadside green infrastructure: a hybrid MCDM–i-Tree Eco decision framework for high-traffic corridors
abstract: Introduction Road-transport corridors in dense metropolitan areas concentrate air pollution while providing little space for mitigation. Methods This study develops an integrated decision-support framework for roadside vegetation selection and ecosystem-service screening at Istanbul’s D-100 Göztepe Junction. Twelve criteria were examined with DEMATEL, SWARA, entropy weighting, and TOPSIS. title: Moisture-related opposing N2O and CH4 gas exchange in mineral upland tundra soils of West Greenland: Linking gas fluxes to soil horizons
abstract: Arctic tundra soils are sources or sinks of the greenhouse gases (GHGs) nitrous oxide (N 2 O), methane (CH 4 ) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), but the simultaneous regulation of these GHGs by soil types remains unclear. We measured GHG fluxes across mineral soil types differing in organic-layer thickness (OLT) and moisture in a West Greenlandic upland tundra. Drier soils functioned primarily as N 2 O sources and CH 4 sinks, with both functions weakening as moisture increased; consequently, wet soils emitted CH 4 and took up N 2 O. title: Physiological, behavioral, and genetic factors that shape interactions in the plant growth-promoting maize rhizosphere synthetic community
abstract: ABSTRACT Profiling microbiomes is an important way to understand the function and composition of communities in the wild, but natural microbiomes are often highly complex and often unamenable to experimentation to reveal cause-and-effect relationships. By using a small group of cultivable strains to represent those found in the wild, synthetic communities are one solution to this problem. Here we describe the ma ize r hizosphere s ynthetic c ommunity (MARSc), a genome-enabled 31-member bacterial community representative of the diversity found on the roots of maize grown in Iowa soils. title: Logistics and product quality in perishable food trade
abstract: Growth in trade of perishable foods has significantly increased global access to fresh foods, but important trade-offs arising from perishability are not captured in standard trade models. In this paper, we develop a model of age-related product freshness that places importer logistics choices at the center of the analysis. The model highlights order size and order frequency as key trade margins, alongside the nonlinear pricing that arises from scale economies in trade. title: Driver-specific temporal shifts in post-fire vegetation recovery: a multi-year Landsat-based analysis of the 2022 Uljin forest fire, South Korea
abstract: How the relative importance of environmental factors shifts during post-fire vegetation recovery remains underexplored in temperate forests with complex terrain and mixed-species canopies. title: Hydraulic behavior and solute redistribution of saline-alkali black soil: Implications for stormwater source control
abstract: Study Region Daqing, northeastern China, has saline-alkali soils, strong evaporation, and shallow groundwater that constrain infiltration-based stormwater source control. Study Focus We examined hydraulic behavior and water and solute redistribution in black soil amended with 0, 0.5, and 2.0% Na 2 CO 3 . Saturated hydraulic conductivity ( K s ) was measured after 0~4 wetting-drying cycles. Soil water retention was determined by the filter paper method, and unsaturated hydraulic conductivity ( K u ) was estimated with the van Genuchten-Mualem model. title: Digital Reforms in The Public Distribution System and Policy Outcomes: An Assessment of Cooperative-Run Fair Price Shops in Tamil Nadu
abstract: The Public Distribution System (PDS) has progressively moved from a predominantly manual welfare-distribution arrangement towards a digitally enabled governance system. In Tamil Nadu, this transformation has been supported by electronic Point of Sale (e-POS) devices, Smart Family Cards, Aadhaar-linked authentication, online transaction recording, digital stock monitoring and other technology-enabled administrative mechanisms. title: Determination of characteristic length scale in insect flight
abstract: Diffusion models are widely used to describe insect dispersal, but their validity depends on the time and length scales over which movement is observed. Motion can only be approximated as random at long length scales, in which the combined effects of many non-random processes become indistinguishable. In this study, simple random walk (SRW) and correlated random walk (CRW) simulations examine how directional persistence affects effective diffusion in five insect test-cases derived from literature. title: Urban-to-downwind variations in aerosol composition and optical properties in the Paris urban plume from coordinated airborne and ground-based observations
abstract: Abstract. Aerosols play a critical role in Earth’s climate, but substantial evolution in their physicochemical properties after emission introduces uncertainties in predicting their climate impacts. Observational constraints on how aging modifies aerosol properties remain limited. Here, we investigate the effects of ~2–6 h of aging on aerosol physicochemical properties using coordinated airborne and ground-based measurements in Paris and its downwind regions. title: PERANCANGAN APLIKASI PENGADAAN BARANG DI FOTOCOPY AMBASSADOR DENGAN MENGGUNAKAN FRAMEWORK LARAVEL
abstract: Pengelolaan pengadaan dan persediaan barang yang efektif menjadi faktor penting dalam menunjang kelancaran operasional usaha. Fotocopy Ambassador masih menggunakan pencatatan stok secara manual sehingga sering mengalami kesulitan dalam memantau ketersediaan barang, keterlambatan pengadaan, serta risiko kehilangan data. title: Intensification of intraguild interactions between top predators in a climate change impacted environment: a new potential evolutionary pathway
abstract: Adaptations of coexisting species to climate-driven environmental changes might not necessarily lead to extinctions, but rather to trait variations that generate new competitive hierarchies in ecosystems. Top predators have a pivotal role as indicators or even generators of high biodiversity in ecosystems, but effects of climate change on top predators have not been sufficiently explored. title: Operational Viability on NISQ Hardware: Pre-execution Analytical Modeling
abstract: Este trabajo describe un modelo analítico pensado para analizar el éxito operativo de algoritmos en procesadores de escala intermedia ruidosa (NISQ) mediante un enfoque probabilístico. A partir de métricas estáticas de calibración, se propone un marco de diagnóstico para lograr una estimación de la viabilidad operativa —entendida como la probabilidad de obtener resultados confiables y útiles— antes de la ejecución física del circuito. title: Spatio-temporal coupling relationship and interactive response of land space utilization efficiency and high-quality development in Fujian Province
abstract: Studying the spatio-temporal changes and interactions between land space utilization efficiency and high-quality development can assist in making decisions that optimize regional high-quality development. This paper used the Super-SBM model, ESDA, Coupling coordination degree model and the panel VAR model to analyze the spatio-temporal evolution and interactive response of land space utilization efficiency and high-quality development level in Fujian province from 2005 to 2023. title: Molecular Variation of Local Pineapple (Ananas comosus L.) from Central Kalimantan Based on rbcL Gene Sequences
abstract: Central Kalimantan is a significant pineapple-growing area in Indonesia, where cultivated pineapples exhibit morphological differences across production sites. This research analyzed sequence variation in local pineapple (Ananas comosus) utilizing the chloroplast rbcL marker. Six samples were gathered from Central Kalimantan and East Java, and two A. comosus sequences from Johor, Malaysia, were retrieved from GenBank for comparison. title: Leveraging Multi‐Isotope Systems to Investigate Conflict, Food Insecurity, and Elevated Nitrogen Isotope Values in the Nazca Highlands of Peru During the Late Intermediate Period (1000–1450 CE)
abstract: ABSTRACT Objectives The physical effects of interpersonal violence are well documented in archaeology, but its broader impacts on population health, mobility, and resource access remain less understood. This article assesses how chronic warfare restricted movement and access to critical resources, altering dietary practices and contributing to persistent food insecurity. title: Emulate the Leader? Explaining Crisis Policy Change in the Canadian Federal System
abstract: ABSTRACT In times of crises, do governments coordinate or do they make their own choices independent of what others do? Convergence of COVID‐19 policy at the beginning of the pandemic has been widely studied in federal countries. Yet, there is limited literature looking at the mechanisms that made policy between jurisdictions so similar. Utilizing Canada's decentralized federal system, this paper posits that convergence can be explained by a process of policy diffusion through emulation and a series of leader‐follower relationships. title: Electrochemical Capture and Accumulation of Uranium Using a Layered Uvanite Electrode
abstract: Abstract Extracting uranyl ions (UO22+) from uranium mining leachates can enhance national uranium security and mitigate the environmental impact of nuclear energy. Conventional techniques such as ion exchange and iron-based reductive precipitation have notable limitations. This study reports that the uvanite (U2V6O21) electrode, a layered uranium-vanadium oxide, enables potentiodynamic decoupling of UO22+ and proton intercalation/deintercalation, as well as proton-induced UO22+/UO3 precipitation and dissolution reactions. title: A split nozzle and two-protein chain-like fibers define the tail architecture of Pseudomonas aeruginosa podophage A1002
abstract: Phage therapy offers unique advantages against antibiotic-resistant bacteria. However, high-resolution structural studies of phages targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa-a top-seven global pathogen-particularly podophages, remain severely limited, directly impeding structure-based development of novel antimicrobials. In this study, we utilize cryo-EM to resolve the high-resolution intact structure of mature phage A1002, a podophage infecting carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa. title: Amorphous‐Crystalline CoNiS Heterojunctions with Optimized Interfacial Charge Transfer for Highly Efficient Oxygen Evolution and Urea Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling catalyst crystallinity is crucial yet challenging in electrocatalysis. Herein, ZIF‐67‐derived cobalt–nickel sulfide (CoNiS) with continuously tunable crystallinity from amorphous to semi‐crystalline and fully crystalline was synthesized by controlling sulfurization time. The semi‐crystalline CoNiS (a/c‐CoNiS, ∼35% crystallinity) delivered optimal oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and urea oxidation reaction (UOR) activity, requiring only 292 mV and 1.379 V to reach 100 mA cm −2 , respectively, outperforming both amorphous and crystalline counterparts. title: Design of the “SI AKA” Domestic Wastewater Treatment System Based on Wastewater Characteristics and Flow Rate
abstract: This research sets out to profile the domestic wastewater produced at the study site, quantify the discharge generated by the surrounding community, and develop an appropriate Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP), named Si Aka, that fits actual field conditions while meeting the applicable regulatory standards. The assessment covers physical, chemical, and biological parameters that together define the pollution level and the resulting treatment burden. journal: Journal of Emerging Supply Chain Clean Energy and Process Engineering

title: Optimizing chlorine management in garlic to improve nitrogen use efficiency and agronomic performance
abstract: Chloride (Cl − ) depletion has emerged as a potential constraint in intensive garlic production, where chlorine (Cl)-containing fertilizers are rarely applied. We evaluated the agronomic, nutritional, economic, and environmental effects of Cl fertilization using a two-year field experiment with six Cl application rates (0–300 kg ha −1 ) in a major garlic-producing region of China. Chloride accumulated predominantly in stems and leaves and promoted nutrient accumulation, photosynthetic performance, bulb development, and nutritional quality. title: Spatial metabolic insights of Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm treatments using stable isotope labeling with DESI mass spectrometry imaging
abstract: Bacteria form biofilms on diverse substrates, and these communities can cause persistent infections owing to their elevated antibiotic resistance. Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a major cause of chronic infections because of its ability to form biofilms, which makes it difficult to eradicate with conventional antibiotics. The metabolic response of P. aeruginosa biofilms to antibiotic treatment, however, remains only partially understood. title: Pre-bilaterian roots of the chordate body plan
abstract: Abstract Similarity of body-plan features across distant phyla provides striking testimony to the Darwinian concept of common descent throughout Metazoa. In both the cnidarian Nematostella and chordates, gastrula organizers direct the initial establishment of embryonic axes. Whether these domains share a common evolutionary origin is a fundamental question for understanding the origin of the chordate body plan. title: Identifikasi Bencana Ekologi Di Lubuk Minturun Kota Padang
abstract: Daerah Aliran Sungai (DAS) Air Dingin, khususnya di Kelurahan Lubuk Minturun, Kota Padang, mengalami tekanan lingkungan akibat perubahan tutupan lahan, pertumbuhan permukiman, dan aktivitas masyarakat yang tidak sepenuhnya memperhatikan daya dukung lingkungan. Kondisi ini meningkatkan kerentanan wilayah terhadap bencana ekologi, khususnya banjir bandang (galodo), yang berdampak luas terhadap lingkungan serta kehidupan sosial-ekonomi masyarakat. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui bentuk-bentuk aktivitas masyarakat di wilayah DAS Air Dingin yang berkaitan dengan terjadinya bencana ekologi

title: Gadolinium as an Emerging Contaminant: Environmental Cycling, Human and Plant Interactions, and Mitigation Strategies
abstract: ABSTRACT Gadolinium (Gd) is a rare earth element whose anthropogenic cycle has expanded rapidly, driven primarily by the widespread medical use of gadolinium‐based contrast agents (GBCAs) in magnetic resonance imaging, alongside its use in selected electronic and energy‐related technologies. Because conventional wastewater treatment plants are largely inefficient at removing kinetically stable Gd chelates, GBCA‐derived Gd persists in effluents and propagates through coupled aquatic and terrestrial pathways. title: Does the Conversion of Biogenic Organic Nitrates to Nitric Acid Control the Lifetime of Atmospheric Nitrogen Oxides Over the Eastern U.S.?
abstract: Abstract Airborne measurements over the Southeast US during the summer of 2013 revealed the evolution of nitrogen oxides and nitric acid that was markedly different from that over the Northeast US during the winter of 2015. We can reconcile the observed trends by invoking nitrogen oxide reservoir species formed under elevated NO x environments that then convert to HNO 3 . This process may represent a daytime loss pathway of NO x that is faster by many factors than the oxidation of nitrogen dioxide by hydroxyl radicals. title: Alternative pathways for recognizing effective governance of Indigenous territories are critical to achieve global biodiversity targets: Lessons from Asian spiritual landscapes
abstract: Global conservation policy and state governance remain grounded in resource-oriented, secular frameworks. These can conflict with Indigenous peoples' and local communities' (IPLCs) relational ontologies, in which landscape elements are sentient beings, ancestral territories, and abodes of 'more-than-human' entities. title: Occupational Risk and Students’ Perceptions of Solid Waste Handling at the South Campus of the University of Education, Winneba
abstract: Solid-waste handling in university settings may expose sanitation workers to occupational hazards while leaving the nature of their work largely outside students’ awareness. This study explored sanitation workers’ accounts of occupational hazards and students’ perceptions of waste handling at the South Campus of the University of Education, Winneba, Ghana. title: Pressure-driven regime shifts in graphitization rewrite carbon fate during metamorphism
abstract: The fate of organic carbon at convergent margins depends in part on its transformation into relatively inert graphite, yet the influence of precursor composition remains poorly constrained. Here we show that two organic precursors, vitrinite and liptinite, follow distinct graphitization pathways under high-pressure and high-temperature conditions. Vitrinite undergoes progressive structural ordering, whereas liptinite transforms more slowly at intermediate pressures owing to inherited defects and inhibited structural coalescence. title: Risk Analysis of CD-BIM Integration in Structural Jetty Schematic Design: Time Performance
abstract: The early design stage of jetty infrastructure is crucial for setting the project's budget and time. However, current digital processes often do not fully integrate these tasks. Computational design and Building Information Modeling (BIM) have sped up design cycles through faster iterations and improved coordination. Still, they have also increased the likelihood of mistakes, extra work, and project delays. title: What shapes urban planning trade-offs of NBS in compact city agendas: a case study of the Catharijnesingel restoration in Utrecht, the Netherlands
abstract: The current research examines the intersection of urban nature-based solutions (NBS) and the compact city model, interrogating how processes of the compact city influence the manifestation of NBS-related trade-offs across the urban planning cycle. We conceptualise and operationalise a synthesis between the types of urban NBS trade-offs, processes of compact urbanism and environmental justice dimensions. title: Bridging Faiths Through Tradition: The Role of Jojao Leadership in Fostering Religious Harmony in Misool, Raja Ampat
abstract: Gamta village is predominately populated by Muslims, while Magei village is predominately populated by Protestant Christians. The strong sense of brotherhood that existed between the two villages, however, led to a number of joint activities. The fact that the crops grown by the Magei villagers must first be tasted by their relatives in Gamta village is one of the brotherhood’s peculiar customs. title: Effect of water management on nitrous oxide emission and heterotrophic soil respiration from drained grassland on peat soil
abstract: Abstract Raising groundwater levels in drained peatlands used for dairy farming aims to reduce peat decomposition, land subsidence and associated carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions. However, higher groundwater levels also affect soil biological nitrogen (N) transformations by decreasing N mineralization and influencing microbial processes such as nitrification and denitrification, which may affect nitrous oxide (N₂O) emissions. title: Tracing the spread of Germanic languages using ancient genomics
abstract: Abstract Germanic languages, including German, English, Frisian, Dutch and the Nordic languages, are widely spoken across northwest Europe. However, the timing and location of the prehistoric arrival of this Indo-European linguistic phylum, as well as its Iron Age diversification, remain contentious 1–3 . Here, by sequencing 712 ancient human genomes and analysing them alongside 4,009 previously published genomes, we identify an archaeologically elusive population that entered Sweden, likely from the Baltic region, by around 4000 bp . title: Nano-Boron Enhances Boron Accumulation and Alters the Tomato Leaf Metabolome: Molecular Modeling of Leaf-Surface and Boron Transporter–Metabolite Interactions
abstract: Abstract Boron (B) deficiency severely limits tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) productivity and fruit quality, particularly in alkaline or low-organic-matter soils, while conventional foliar boron fertilizers suffer from low uptake efficiency and environmental losses. In this study, we developed and characterized a novel nanoboron (NB) formulation and evaluated its efficacy compared with boric acid using physicochemical characterization, molecular simulations, greenhouse studies, metabolomics, and field validation. title: A distinct class of conjugative megaplasmids is associated with prophages in distantly related bacterial lineages
abstract: Closely related prophages have been found in phylogenetically distant bacteria in the human gut, despite limited evidence of productive phage infections across broad host ranges. It remains enigmatic how the wide distribution of prophages could emerge. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized association between a distinct group of conjugative megaplasmids and prophage genomes. title: Spatial and Seasonal Assessment of Physicochemical Water Quality in the Lower Tapi River
abstract: Deteriorating of river water quality has become an important environmental challenge in India, particularly where river system is relied upon for drinking water supply. The Tapi river serves as major water resources for Surat. The study evaluates the seasonal variation and quality of water status of Tapi river in Gujarat, India, using the Weighted Arithmetic Water Quality Index (WAWQI) method. This study presents a yearlong assessment (Dec. 2024 to Nov. 2025) of seasonal and spatial variations in water quality at five selected sites: Galteshwar, Kamrej, Utran, Causeway and ONGC Bridge. journal: Research Journal of Chemistry and Environment

title: Limited effect of basalt amendment and mycorrhizal inoculation on soil chemical properties and maize growth on a nutrient-rich soil
abstract: Abstract Enhanced weathering (EW) of silicate minerals has emerged as a promising carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategy, with potential benefits for soil fertility and crop performance. However, the soil processes that determine these co-benefits remain poorly constrained. In particular, interactions between basalt amendments and soil biota such as arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) may influence nutrient mobilization and plant uptake, but these effects have rarely been quantified. title: A ≈3.0 Ga zircon core in an Early Cambrian (meta)granitoid from the basement of Mt. Papuk (Croatia): a trifle or treasure for palaeogeographic reconstructions?
abstract: The U-Pb age spectrum of zircon grains including rim and xenocrystic core domains from an Early Cambrian peraluminous (meta)granitoid in the eastern part of Mt. Papuk (Croatia) was determined using laser ablation inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry. Zircon cathodoluminescence images reveal an unusually high proportion of xenocrystic cores surrounded by oscillatory-zoned magmatic rims. title: Simulating an imaging atmospheric radio telescope to observe cosmic gamma rays and cosmic neutrinos
abstract: Observations of cosmic gamma rays with energies above the 10 12 electronvolts (TeV) regime are often a direct probe of events where our theoretical predictions are challenged by extreme conditions. Because high energetic cosmic gamma rays are rare, one needs collection areas with the size of roughly a dozen football fields (10 5 m 2 ) or more to gather significant counting statistics in a short time. title: The densified city and the powerline right-of-way encroachment in Nigeria: Greening as an important intervention.
abstract: Urban densification is generally promoted as a strategy for sustainable development. However, it may also produce unintended consequences, such as exposure to environmental hazards. This study examines potential electrical hazard exposure in relation to the powerline right-of-way (ROW) encroachment in Port Harcourt Metropolis, a rapidly densifying oil and gas industry hub in southern Nigeria, using a mixed-method approach that combines geospatial datasets and social survey data. title: A Basic Matrix Protein Songin Selectively Promotes Aragonite Aggregation and Modulates Calcium Carbonate Crystallization in Hyriopsis cumingii
abstract: Abstract In China, the pearl industry of Hyriopsis cumingii contributes approximately 80% of pearl production. Matrix proteins play crucial roles in shell and pearl biomineralization. However, the functions of basic matrix proteins in H. cumingii remain poorly understood. In this study, we identified a novel predicted secreted basic matrix protein, designated Songin, from the freshwater pearl mussel H. cumingii. title: Redirecting gypsum scaling in pervaporation desalination via activated alumina granules
abstract: Membrane scaling, particularly CaSO4 (gypsum) crystallisation, severely limits the practical application of pervaporation (PV) desalination for high-salinity wastewater treatment. Herein, an online interception strategy using nitric acid-activated alumina granules (AAG) is proposed to redirect gypsum scaling from the membrane surface to a sacrificial medium. title: Hematological profile, morphology, and morphometry of blood cells from healthy free-ranging neotropical Paraguayan hairy dwarf porcupines (Coendou spinosus) from the State of São Paulo, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Hematologic analysis is a fundamental tool for screening, diagnosing, treating, and monitoring animal diseases, and it requires constant multidisciplinary collaboration to expand knowledge for exotic and free-ranging animals worldwide. The study aimed to determine the hematological parameters, morphology, and morphometry of blood cells from the wild Paraguayan hairy dwarf porcupine ( Coendou spinosus ), a medium-sized rodent relatively common in Southeastern Brazil, extending to Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay. title: Incidence of and household responses to paediatric diarrhoeal disease and acute respiratory infection in Chitwan, Nepal: protocol for a prospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Introduction Diarrheal diseases and acute respiratory infections (ARI) disproportionately affect young children and families facing disadvantages at the individual, household, and neighborhood level. This unequal burden especially impacts children in low-and middle-income countries, such as Nepal. Data limitations impede the ability to understand children’s illness episodes and treatment trajectories across the course of early childhood and their relationship to household- and neighborhood-level social determinants of health. title: HOMO‐Level Alignment as a Design Descriptor for Donor–Acceptor Covalent Organic Frameworks in Aqueous Zinc‐Iodine Batteries
abstract: Aqueous zinc-iodine batteries (ZIBs) offer high voltage and inherent safety, but face a persistent trade-off among fast kinetics, long cycling stability, and high iodine loading. Donor-acceptor (D-A) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as promising iodine hosts, yet the rational design is hindered by an unclear understanding of what truly governs charge-transfer efficiency-with most studies empirically pursuing higher energy density without clear design rules. title: Reindeer habitat selection and movement change with cumulative impacts from mining and wind power development
abstract: Industrial expansion often occurs in landscapes already affected by multiple disturbances, resulting in cumulative impacts on biodiversity and local communities. Although societal pressure for a rapid ‘green transition’ accelerates land-use change, most impact assessments remain local and project-based and are therefore unable to adequately address cumulative impacts. abstract: Efficient regulation of the hydrogen and hydroxyl binding energies (HBE/OHBE) lies at the core of developing high-performance alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts, yet it remains challenging due to the inherent correlation between the two binding energies. title: A dual-strategy approach for heavy metal mitigation in date fruit and syrup using physicochemical treatment and inactivated lactobacillus biomass
abstract: This study established a dual-strategy framework for heavy metal mitigation in date palm products by integrating physicochemical washing of whole Zahidi fruit with biosorption by inactivated Lactobacillus biomass in date syrup. title: Aging‐ and Moisture‐Resistant Pectin‐Based Aerogels: A Breakthrough in Bio‐Based Thermal Superinsulation
abstract: ABSTRACT Bio‐based aerogels are a compelling class of sustainable materials, with some of them distinguished by their exceptional thermal superinsulating performance, i.e. conductivity lower than that of air. However, their practical use is limited by poor stability in humid environment. Pectin/polyurea aerogels were developed to address this issue. title: PCOMMUNITY EDUCATION ON GREEN BELT STRUCTURING AND PARTICIPATORY ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY MONITORING AROUND COAL-FIRED POWER PLANT X
abstract: Coal-fired power plants secure baseload electricity but expose neighbouring settlements to fly ash, stockpile dust, flue gases (SO2, NOx) and noise, while residents are usually treated as passive recipients of these impacts and have no means of checking air quality themselves. This participatory action research designed, implemented and evaluated an education programme on multi-strata green belt structuring and citizen-science environmental monitoring for communities around Coal-Fired Power Plant X. title: “And why here?” Reading Hong Kong in Nick Joaquin’s The Woman Who Had Two Navels
abstract: Nick Joaquin (1917–2004) is a Filipino literary master and national artist whose numerous works include the prize-winning novel The Woman Who Had Two Navels (1961). Its plot revolves around the Manilan protagonist Connie Escobar’s flight into Hong Kong and her insistence that “she [has] two navels” (1). Her assertion is complicated by her request for Hong Kong-born-and-based Pepe Monson to perform “an operation” on them (1). title: Optimizing seismographic network strategies for earthquake surveillance under linguistic pythagorean fuzzy dynamic knowledge
abstract: Global seismographic networks (GSNs) capture fine details of ground motion signals, assisting scientists and governments in detecting and characterizing earthquakes and other seismic events worldwide. Continued improvements in these networks enhance knowledge about Earth structure, atmospheric interaction, and geological hazards. Because seismic stations operate under changing environmental and operational conditions, decision-making for network optimization requires tools that can handle uncertainty, linguistic assessments, and time-varying information. title: Tailored Graphene Oxide Incorporated PES/CA Mixed‐Matrix Loose Nanofiltration Membranes for Water Softening and Divalent Salt Removal
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving a simultaneous enhancement of permeability and selectivity remains a central challenge in nanofiltration membrane design. Here, we report the fabrication of high‐performance polyether sulfone–cellulose acetate (PES/CA) mixed‐matrix membranes via phase inversion, employing polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) as a pore‐forming agent and graphene oxide (GO) as a hydrophilic nanofiller to precisely tailor membrane structure and transport behavior. title: Hormonal and metabolic adaptations in Omega-3-supplemented rabbit does during their first reproductive cycle
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of dietary n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFA) supplementation on endocrine and metabolic profiles of forty-five nulliparous rabbit does during their first reproductive cycle. Animals were randomly assigned to one of three diets: control (CNT), 5% extruded linseed (L), and 5% extruded linseed plus 0.2% Padina pavonica extract (LPP). title: Cosmogenic Selection: How Retained Organization Shapes Future Possibilities
abstract: Cosmogenic Selection (CGS) is proposed as a conceptual framework for examining how organized reality develops across physical, biological and cognitive domains. Its central proposition is that what persists changes what can happen next: differences enter relationships, some consequences are retained, and retained organization reshapes or expands subsequent possibilities. The framework does not assume that one selection mechanism operates at every scale. title: QUALITY OF LIFE OF RESIDENTS IN GAS FLARING COMMUNITY IN AKWA IBOM STATE, NIGER DELTA REGION, NIGERIA
abstract: Gas flaring remains a persistent environmental and public health issue in Nigeria’s Niger Delta, particularly in Akwa Ibom State, where crude oil extraction is widespread. This research compares the quality of life (QoL) of residents of a gas flaring community (Mkpanak) and a non-gas flaring community (Okposo) in the Niger Delta region of Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. A cross-sectional, comparative survey was conducted. Multistage sampling was used to sample 389 respondents. The analysis was conducted using the four components of QoL: subjective wellbeing, objective wellbeing, psychological wellbe
journal: International Journal of Renewable Energy and Environment

title: Isoprenoid quinone profiling using a novel semi-quantitative HPLC-MS/MS method: application to wastewater sludges
abstract: Isoprenoid quinones are ubiquitous redox lipids that mediate electron transfer in various cellular processes across all domains of life. These molecules also serve as taxonomic and metabolic markers, facilitating the characterisation of microbial communities. However, their structural diversity and extreme hydrophobicity are challenging for comprehensive detection and quantification in complex biological matrices. title: Statistical and Perceived Ethnic Diversity in Urban Activity Spaces: Evidence from Auckland, New Zealand
abstract: The study of segregation in activity spaces has received renewed attention, fueled by the increasing availability of mobility data from mobile phones and social media. These new data sources enable high-resolution analysis of how people move through cities and interact across diverse neighborhoods. A key goal of this work is to inform the design of inclusive spaces that foster intergroup contact, which is presumed to enhance social cohesion. title: Metabolomic and Transcriptomic Characterization of Actinokineospora bangkokensis 44EHWT: Enhancing Anti-anthracnose Production Through N-Acetylglucosamine Supplementation
abstract: N -acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) serves as a key carbon source and regulatory signal for secondary metabolism in actinomycetes, yet its role in Actinokineospora remains poorly understood. Here, genome mining, transcriptomics, and untargeted metabolomics were integrated to investigate GlcNAc-supplemented Actinokineospora bangkokensis 44EHWT. title: Multi-hazard assessment of the eastern slope of the Sistema de Famatina, La Rioja province (Argentina)
abstract: Abstract In the eastern sector of the Sistema de Famatina, both natural processes and anthropogenic activities pose considerable risks to the landscape and its inhabitants. This study investigates the geohazards and environmental agents that have historically affected the region, with a focus on their implications for local communities and territories. The analysis integrates case studies of documented natural events, identification of mitigation strategies, satellite imagery interpretation, landform recognition, and direct field observations. title: Experimental investigation of suction flow enhancement in submerged jet pumps via perforated mixing chamber
abstract: Liquid–liquid jet pumps are essential in dredging, slurry transport, and submerged mixing applications, yet their suction performance remains constrained by the limited entrainment area in conventional solid-walled mixing chambers. This study experimentally investigates the geometric modification of using perforated mixing chambers that enable distributed radial suction driven by the hydrostatic pressure differential between the surrounding fluid and the low-pressure core induced by the motive jet. abstract: The study synthesized a list of Sudanese ant diversity by integrating historical records, and recent surveys.Historical records from Magretti, Weber, Karavaiev, Werner and Ebner, Sweeney, Trägårdh, and others establish a baseline for assessing temporal and spatial changes in ant distributions.These data correspond with existing Sudanese faunal compilations, including the Ants of Africa database.Recent datasets provide an integrated framework for evaluating Sudanese ant diversity, distribution, community structure, and ecological change.The list documented 19 Myrmicinae genera, 116 species and

title: Fibrinolytic and coagulation activities of crude extracellular preparation from Bacillus cereus group strain SF-4
abstract: Fibrinolytic enzymes have attracted considerable attention as potential alternatives to conventional thrombolytic agents because they degrade fibrin, a major structural component of blood clots. Fermented seafood products are promising sources of protease-producing microorganisms; however, fermented bamboo clam (Solen sp.) rusip remains underexplored as a source of bacteria with fibrinolytic potential. title: Development of CeO2 coated functional CNT-reinforced thin film for enhanced bonding and electrochemical nitrite sensing
abstract: Nitrite (NO₂⁻) contamination in water poses serious environmental and health risks, necessitating sensitive and reliable detection platforms. However, achieving strong film adhesion alongside high electrocatalytic performance remains a key challenge in electrochemical sensor design. This study aims to develop a mechanically robust and electrochemically active coating for nitrite sensing by reinforcing cerium oxide (CeO₂) nanoparticles with functionalized multi-walled carbon nanotubes (f-MWCNTs), forming a CeO₂@f-MWCNT nanocomposite (NCs) that combines enhanced substrate bonding with efficient

title: Lipoprotein(a): Bridging the gap between risk prediction, measurement, and emerging therapeutics
abstract: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined lipoprotein and a well-established causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Despite increasing recognition in clinical guidelines, Lp(a) testing remains underused, and targeted therapies are only now emerging. This narrative review summarizes the biology, cardiovascular risk, measurement challenges, emerging therapies, and translational barriers of Lp(a), highlighting its role in contemporary cardiovascular prevention. journal: International Journal of Cardiology Cardiovascular Risk and Prevention

title: Molecular Phylogeny and Color Variation of Two Large-size Octannulate Species of Orobdella, O. octonaria and O. nakahamai (Hirudinea: Orobdellidae), with Insights into Their Distribution
abstract: Understanding species distributions is essential for biogeographical and ecological studies. This study reports the geographical ranges of two large-size octannulate species of the leech genus Orobdella Oka, 1895, O. octonaria Oka, 1895, and O. nakahamai Nakano, 2016, based on newly collected specimens. In addition, intraspecific genetic variation was investigated via phylogeographic analyses using mitochondrial markers, i.e., cytochrome c oxidase subunit I, tRNALeu, NADH dehydrogenase subunit 1, tRNACys, tRNAMet, 12S rRNA, tRNAVal and 16S rRNA. title: ENVIRONMENTAL SATISFACTION AS A MODERATOR IN THE HARNESSING OF COMMUNITY-BASED TOURISM FOR SUSTAINABLE GROWTH
abstract: Community-based tourism (CBT) has come up as a viable solution towards development of sustainable tourism. Against the conventional tourism models, CBT focuses on the active participation and empowerment of the local communities in the planning, management, and decision-making processes in tourism. Through prioritization of local ownership, cultural preservation and environmental conservation, the CBT seeks to achieve more equitable distribution of tourism benefits and minimizing negative impacts. title: Assessing Urban Growth Patterns of Agroha Town of Hisar, Haryana Using Directional and Geostatistical Approaches
abstract: This study investigates the spatiotemporal dynamics, direction and intensity of urban expansion in Agroha Town, a historically significant and rapidly urbanizing peri-urban center in the Hisar district of Western Haryana, India. Employing multi-temporal high-resolution satellite imagery from Google Earth (2015 and 2024), administrative boundary data from the Bhuvan platform and spatial benchmarks from the Town and Country Planning (TCP) Haryana Agroha Draft Development Plan 2031, land use and land cover (LULC) transformations across a 15.10 sq. km municipal boundary were systematically quantif

title: Aflatoxins contamination of aquafeed: Toxicological impacts and mitigation strategies in finfish and crustacean aquaculture
abstract: Mycotoxins are toxic secondary metabolites produced by fungi that pose a significant challenge to the safety, productivity, and sustainability of global aquaculture. Aquafeed ingredients, particularly cereals, oilseed meals, and other plant-derived protein sources, are frequently contaminated with mycotoxins, including aflatoxins (AFB1, AFB2, AFG1, and AFG2), ochratoxin A (OTA), fumonisins (FB1), trichothecenes (T-2 toxin), and zearalenone (ZEA). title: Performance of AC systems under future climates and heatwaves: From degradation to temperature regime optimization and dehumidification control
abstract: Rising outdoor temperatures and the increasing frequency of heatwaves raise pressing challenges to the resilience of building cooling systems, particularly in tropical regions where cooling demand is continuous, and dehumidification is essential. This study investigates the impact of future climate scenarios, including typical meteorological years and heatwave years provided by the International Energy Agency’s Annex 80, on the seasonal performance of conventional vapor-compression cooling systems: unitary systems, represented by split units. title: Phytochemical Profiling and Anticancer Potential of Ipomoea hederifolia L. Root Extract: LC–MS Characterization and Molecular Docking Insights
abstract: ABSTRACT Cancer remains a major global health burden, with millions of new cases reported annually. Plant‐based products are gaining popularity due to their remarkable biological activity and fewer side effects. The Convolvulaceae family exhibits promising anticancer effects; Ipomoea hederifolia is one of the species rich in bioactive secondary metabolites. This is the first study that aims to investigate the anticancer potential of the plant against HepG2 cells. title: Status and ontogenetic structure of rare wild populations of Vitis vinifera (Vitaceae) in Uzbekistan
abstract: Vitis vinifera is an ancient fruit crop whose wild populations constitute a valuable genetic resource for grape breeding. In Uzbekistan, these populations are rare and fragmented, and the species is listed under Category 3 in the national Red Data Book (2019). This study assessed the ontogenetic structure, demographic characteristics, and conservation status of six wild cenopopulations of V. vinifera in Uzbekistan. title: Metrological framework for Ground-Based measurement of gaseous emissions from turbine aircraft engines
abstract: This article focuses on discussing and comparing the most critical aspects of metrology in testing gaseous emissions from aircraft engines during ground tests, such as choice of measuring equipment, its layout on site and its technical parameters. By referencing actual measurement campaigns and research projects, the study characterizes the objects of investigation – turbojet (specifically turbofan) engines used in commercial aviation – as well as global policies regarding emission analysis, the objectives and scope of engine trials, and the environmental conditions accompanying these tests. abstract: This study presents a preliminary assessment of organic matter source and thermal maturity of coal samples from the Muara Teweh Mine, Barunang Area, Warukin Formation, Barito Basin, Central Kalimantan, using GC–MS based on Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAHs) biomarker proxies. Due to the absence of independent maturity indicators such as Rock-Eval pyrolysis and vitrinite reflectance, these results should be interpreted as a molecular-based assessment of the thermal evolution stage. abstract: Abstract Milk thistle ( Silybum marianum (L.) Gaertn.) is an important medicinal plant, yet limited research has addressed its agronomic performance and genetic diversity under water‐limited conditions. This study evaluated the potential of 28 Iranian ecotypes and one foreign accession to assess variation in agronomic traits, oil concentration, and methanol extractable dry matter under normal irrigation and drought stress during two growing seasons. title: Mass spectrometry imaging reveals the metabolic geography underlying spatial programming of necrotrophic infection in postharvest sweet cherry
abstract: Brown rot, caused by Monilinia spp., is a destructive postharvest disease of cherry. title: Evaluation of soil fertility status of Shivpur village in Pathalgaon block of Jashpur district, Chhattisgarh
abstract: The present study entitled “Evaluation of soil fertility status of Shivpur village in Pathalgaon block of Jashpur district, Chhattisgarh” was conducted during 2025–26 at the Department of Soil Science, College of Agriculture, Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, Raipur. The study aimed to assess soil fertility status, nutrient variability, nutrient index values and soil-test-based fertilizer recommendations. title: People and bats in Fiji: perceptions and interactions
abstract: Abstract The management of wild bat populations often presents challenges in balancing the needs of biodiversity conservation and public health risks from zoonotic diseases. In Fiji, the most important recognized zoonotic infection is Leptospira, which was recently detected in wild bat populations. Five out of six species of Fijian bats are considered threatened to critically endangered on the IUCN Red List. title: A practical guide to using Q‐methodology in conservation science
abstract: Abstract Conservation scientists and practitioners are increasingly incorporating social research methods into their work. Q‐methodology is an established social research tool with multiple potential applications in conservation, but its uptake remains comparatively limited. Q‐methodology integrates qualitative and quantitative approaches, providing an accessible, effective technique for identifying subjective perspectives on conservation topics. title: Spatio-temporal dynamics of reservoir storage in the Algarve region (Southern Portugal): implications for regional water security
abstract: ABSTRACT The Algarve region in southern Portugal relies heavily on reservoirs to support domestic water supply, irrigation, tourism, and other economic activities. This study examined the spatio-temporal dynamics of storage in six major reservoirs: Bravura, Arade, Funcho, Odelouca, Odeleite, and Beliche, using monthly and annual storage data from 2012 to 2025. Time-series analysis, inter-reservoir comparisons, and assessment of combined regional storage were conducted to evaluate temporal variability and drought-related changes in water availability. title: Nested economies of scale in global city mass
abstract: Abstract A long-standing puzzle in urban science is whether there is an intrinsic match between human populations and the mass of their built environments. Existing models assume proportionality: each additional resident demands the same amount of building material. Our analysis of more than 3,000 cities worldwide challenges this linear assumption. title: Recent advancements in photosynthetic microalgae for microbial activity, nutrition, and health benefits
abstract: Abstract Microalgae, with their complex aerobic photosynthetic system, contribute 40%-50% to atmospheric oxygen (O2), and are increasingly recognized as a source of nutrients in many countries (including China, Japan, and India). Although numerous reviews discuss microalgae for biofuel production and wastewater treatment, a few reviews address their applications in health benefits, food ingredients, microbial activity, and regulatory considerations for safe consumption. title: Impact of the 1 April 2026 Artemis II Rocket Launch on the Upper Atmosphere: TIMED/GUVI Observations
abstract: Abstract The NASA Artemis II rocket was successfully launched at 06:35 p.m. ET (22:35 UTC) on 1 April 2026 from the Kennedy Space Center (28°35′28″N 80°39′03″W). The rocket plume caused enhanced Lyman α emission (up to ∼3 kR) observed by TIMED/GUVI on 2–6 April (5 days). Its peak intensity decreased linearly from April 3 at a rate ∼740 R/day. The half‐maximum width of the zonal Lyman α intensities at 20°–30° latitude (at ∼01:30 p.m. local solar time) increased from ∼3,000 km on April 2–∼9,000 km on April 6. title: Conjugation of metal-organic framework (MIL-125) to NiFe2O4@CdS nanoparticles for enhanced photocatalytic hydrogen generation
abstract: Abstract Harnessing solar energy with semiconductors offers a feasible path toward sustainable hydrogen production via photocatalytic water splitting. In this study, a ternary photocatalyst, MIL-125(Ti)/NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS, was fabricated by integrating a Ti-based metal–organic framework with a green-synthesized NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS binary core–shell heterostructure for visible-light-driven hydrogen evolution. title: Diachronous evolution of Himalayan drainage: comparing the western and eastern syntaxes through detrital zircon U-Pb geochronology of Middle Siwalik sandstones
abstract: Abstract Detrital zircon U–Pb ages from a Middle Siwalik Nagri Formation sandstone (~ 11–9 Ma) in the Kohala section, Hazara–Kashmir Syntaxis (western Himalaya, Pakistan), are used to assess sediment provenance and drainage connectivity in the western Himalayan foreland basin. The 98 concordant ages are dominated by Neoproterozoic–early Paleozoic grains (~ 1000–400 Ma; ~59%), with subordinate Mesoproterozoic (~ 20%) and Paleoproterozoic (~ 16%) populations. title: Integrating Spirulina cultivation as a bioregeneration step in a closed loop CO2 absorption process: Experimental validation
abstract: The integration of microalgal cultivation with CO₂ capture via chemical scrubbing can improve carbon utilization efficiency while reducing operational costs. However, the reciprocal effects between absorption and cultivation units need further investigation. This study evaluated the integration of carbonate-based CO₂ capture with cultivation of the alkaliphilic cyanobacterium Spirulina sp. in a Bicarbonate-based Carbon Capture and Algae Production System (BICCAPS). title: Antarctic Krill‐Derived Umami Peptides With Bitter‐Masking Activity: Identification and Molecular Mechanism
abstract: This study systematically investigated the extraction and identification of umami peptides, as well as their mechanism for masking bitterness. The hydrolysate of Antarctic krill was isolated and purified, and umami components were identified through sensory evaluation and instrumental analysis. 12 potential umami peptides were obtained via virtual screening using databases. title: Living on the edge: A qualitative exploration of informal life under flyovers in Dhaka
abstract: Homeless populations face multiple and intersecting vulnerabilities in rapidly urbanizing cities; however, the lived experiences of individuals residing beneath flyovers in Dhaka remain underexplored. This study explores their lived experiences, with particular attention to shelter, food security, safety, and personal identity, and challenges related to food, income, housing, safety risks, extreme weather, and sexual violence. title: The Quaternary paleo-lacustrine deposits of Bamako and their significance for the development of the Niger River course
abstract: Sills play a crucial role in shaping river courses. They are typically natural dams that obstruct water flow and create lakes along the river. This study examines the case of the Sotuba sill in the Niger River's development in West Africa. It discusses four Quaternary outcrops in Bamako, the Niger Valley, composed of lacustrine deposits covered by fluviatile sediments, indicating a change in depositional environment. title: From climate hazards to diet and physical activity pathways: Investigating policy intersections for health in five global South Cities
abstract: Introduction Climate change, rapid urbanization, and non-communicable diseases (NCDs) pose intersecting threats to public health in low- and middle-income countries. While evidence supports integrating health into climate policy, limited attention has been paid to how climate change and urban resilience policies address key NCD-related pathways, particularly diet and physical activity. title: Can the Spatial Planning of Livestock Production Tackle Future Nitrogen Pollution in China?
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen (N) pollution from livestock production significantly threatens China’s air and water quality, necessitating innovative solutions to balance food security and environmental sustainability. Studies have mostly overlooked the spatial heterogeneity of N-related environmental impacts and the trade-offs between reducing ammonia (NH3) emissions and N concentrations in water. abstract: This study investigates the role of ecotourism in strengthening local economies in Bintang District, Central Aceh by identifying key potentials within natural and socio-cultural resources. It explores how assets such as Lake Laut Tawar, agrobased livelihoods, and community enterprises can drive sustainable economic development. The study analyzes stakeholder collaboration, focusing on governance, participation, and community empowerment. abstract: Mapping of soils and depicting spatial variability across agro-ecological regions remains underexplored, especially in Nepal's hilly areas. The current study aimed to assess spatial variability and map key soil properties such as pH, soil organic matter, total nitrogen, available phosphorus, and available potassium across the Kaski district, Nepal. abstract: Background: Stunting remains a major nutritional problem in Indonesia, highlighting the need for locally developed, nutrient-dense supplementary foods. Objective: This study aimed to develop a beverage powder formulated from lemuru fish protein hydrolysate and Moringa leaf powder (HPILK) and evaluate its sensory characteristics, nutritional composition, and potential nutrition claims. title: Enzymatic Transformation of Soluble Nonreactive Phosphorus Compounds to Improve Phosphorus Removal and Recovery Potential from Wastewater
abstract: Abstract A substantial fraction of total phosphorus (TP) in the environment exists as soluble nonreactive phosphorus (sNRP). These compounds can resist treatment processes and therefore persist in wastewater effluent, posing challenges for meeting stringent TP limits and long-term eutrophication risks. We employed an integrated experimental and chemoinformatics approach to evaluate the chemical diversity of sNRP and its impact on the fate of sNRP during enzymatic treatment. abstract: Abstract Vibrio bacteria possess multiple quorum-sensing systems, each of which conveys information into the cell concerning the cell density and species composition of the vicinal community. Germane to the present work is the CqsA-CqsS quorum-sensing pathway that vibrios use for intra-genus communication. title: Analysis of Cost and Returns in Rice Production among Contract and Non-Contract Smallholder Producers in Benue and Niger States, Nigeria
abstract: This study analyzed the costs and returns of rice production among contract and non-contract smallholder producers in Benue and Niger States, Nigeria. A multi-stage sampling design was used to select 400 contract and non-contract rice producers. Primary data were collected using a well- designed questionnaire. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, farm budgetary technique, and ordinary least squares (OLS) regression model. title: The bacterial swarming factor SwrD belongs to a diverse family of proteins that form hexameric rings
abstract: Prokaryotic swarming is a collective surface-associated behavior that supports rapid colonization, biofilm formation, and host interactions. Swarming requires enhanced flagellar motor (FM) torque generation under high-load conditions. In many bacteria, this adaptation is achieved through increased stator unit recruitment and coordinated transcriptional regulation of motility genes. title: Effects of Pre‐Existing Crack Location and Orientation on the Aero‐Structural Response and High‐Stress Influence Zones of a Carbon/Glass Hybrid Composite Wind Turbine Blade
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the effects of crack location and orientation on the structural response and high‐stress influence zone (HSIZ) of a 1.5 MW carbon/glass hybrid composite wind turbine blade using laminate tensile tests, digital image correlation (DIC), computed tomography (CT), and one‐way aerodynamic–structural coupling analysis. Laminate tests revealed orientation‐dependent strain localization and damage paths. title: Hot deformation behavior and phase-dependent deformation mechanisms of 00Cr27Ni7Mo5N hyper duplex stainless steel
abstract: Hyper duplex stainless steels (HDSSs) with high nitrogen and alloying element contents exhibit excellent mechanical properties and corrosion resistance, making them promising for extreme service environments. However, their high nitrogen and alloying element contents can exacerbate deformation incompatibility between ferrite and austenite, resulting in heterogeneous strain partitioning, distinct phase-dependent softening behavior, and deteriorated hot workability. title: Temporal fluctuations in retinal artery occlusions: an 11-year German cohort study
abstract: PURPOSE: Cardiovascular events have been shown to follow seasonal and monthly distributions. It is unclear whether this applies to retinal vascular diseases. This study aims to determine the existence of seasonal variations in the onset of retinal artery occlusions (RAO) in a European population. METHODS: This retrospective, monocentric study included 646 eyes of 646 patients who were treated for RAO at the University Hospital Münster, Germany, between 2014 and 2024. title: Detrital Zircon Double Dating Reconstructs the Missing Grenville Foreland and Great Unconformity Exhumation
abstract: Abstract The c. 1090–980 Ma Grenville Orogeny that resulted in final amalgamation of the supercontinent Rodinia is not associated with extensive preserved foreland basins common in other convergent margins, which has generated controversy about why these basins are absent and the nature of Meso‐Neoproterozoic orogenesis. The c. 993 Ma Jacobsville Sandstone and correlative units preserved in the North America Midcontinent region are the only known syntectonic units associated with the final stage of Grenville orogenesis. title: New insights on Suretta nappe structure and lithostratigraphy revealed by high-resolution geological survey of Val di Lei (Central Alps, Italy)
abstract: This contribution presents a 1:10.000 scale geological map of the Val di Lei basin (Italian Central Alps), produced within the framework of the Italian National Geological Mapping Project (CARG). The area mainly exposes rocks of the Suretta nappe (Middle Penninic) and minor portions of the Avers nappe (Upper Penninic). The Suretta nappe comprises a polymetamorphic basement, Carboniferous–Permian metaplutonites, and a Permian–Mesozoic metasedimentary cover. title: Optimizing Renewable Energy Capacity Development Using Standard-Pseudo Multi-Mode Gradient Descent Algorithm for Australia’s 2050 Net-Zero Transition
abstract: Australia’s transition toward net-zero emissions (NZE) requires the integration of renewable energy (RE) sources with substantially different capacity requirements and operational characteristics. However, existing transition assessments provide limited quantitative evaluation of how “Proposed”, “Anticipated”, and “Committed” renewable capacity additions may influence the required capacity pathway. title: Ammonia and methane mitigation from dairy manure using sulfur‐based manure storage additives
abstract: Abstract Dairy manure storage is a major source of greenhouse gas emissions and other air pollutants, including methane (CH 4 ) and ammonia (NH 3 ). Easily deployable mitigation strategies, such as manure storage additives, can help reduce the environmental impact of dairy production. Sulfur‐based manure storage additives, specifically gypsum (CaSO 4 ), have been proposed as low‐cost manure amendments that may influence CH 4 emissions; however, their potential to mitigate NH 3 emissions and their effectiveness across sulfur dosages remain unclear. This study evaluated two gypsum additives at l

title: From Monomer to Mesh: The Biochemical Maturation of Gel-Forming Mucin Glycoproteins
abstract: Abstract Secreted mucin glycoproteins, which form the scaffolds of the mucus hydrogels coating tissue epithelia, are among the most complex molecules in nature. Mucin protein backbones are typically more than 5000 amino acids in length, become stapled into domain folds by over 100 disulfide bonds, and contain thousands of potential sites for O-glycosylation. The glycans added to these sites vary in chemical composition, length, and degree of branching, producing mucins with diverse biochemical and biophysical properties. title: Food waste to biomass approach: A sustainable strategy for the production of alternative microbial culture media for filamentous fungi growth
abstract: The valorization of organic waste is still one of the challenges in the path towards environmental sustainability and a circular bioeconomy. This research aimed at assessing the ability of three substrates of organic residues (olive pomace, potato peels and the green seaweed Ulva lactuca) to be used as alternative culture media for filamentous fungi. Mycelial growth on these media was compared with the conventional Potato Dextrose Agar (PDA) and Sabouraud media using three fungal species namely Fusarium oxysporum (F1), Fusarium solani (F2) and Alternaria alternata (N2) as biological models. institutions: Université Djilali de Sidi Bel Abbès

title: Vaccinia virus growth factor induces divergent signaling programs and biological outcomes from cellular epidermal growth factor
abstract: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling is a major pathway that controls cellular growth, survival, proliferation, and differentiation. Viruses often hijack this pathway to create a favorable environment to support their replication. Vaccinia virus (the prototype member of poxviridae) encodes its own viral growth factor (VGF). VGF is a secreted viral polypeptide with sequence and structural homology to the cellular EGF, which binds to and activates EGFR signaling. Studies from our lab and others have shown that VGF promotes metabolic reprogramming, cell motility, virulence, and sprea

title: Climate variability and change as an emerging operational challenge to malaria control among district malaria focal persons in Dar es Salaam Tanzania
abstract: Malaria transmission in Tanzania has declined significantly over the past decade, following the scale-up of vector control and case management interventions. However, climate change may threaten these gains through long-term changes in climatic conditions that could influence mosquito breeding patterns and transmission dynamics. Short-term and seasonal fluctuations in rainfall and temperature, may also influence malaria risk and disrupt vector control activities, particularly during heavy rainfall. District malaria focal persons are responsible for implementing and coordinating malaria control
institutions: Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences
Mbeya University of Science and Technology

title: Genome shock in a migratory songbird hybrid zone
abstract: The genome shock hypothesis proposes that hybridization destabilizes genome regulation, leading to increased chromatin accessibility, derepression of transposable elements (TEs), and potential reductions in hybrid fitness, contributing to speciation. While extensively studied in plants, evidence in vertebrates is limited. Here, we tested this hypothesis in a hybrid zone between two subspecies of Swainson's thrushes (Catharus ustulatus). We quantified genome-wide TE proportions, TE expression, and chromatin accessibility during both the migratory and non-migratory state using whole genome reseq

title: Traceable Privacy and Cybersecurity Compliance Control Baseline for Indonesian Academic Information Systems
abstract: Academic information systems process student identities, academic records, library transactions, authentication logs, learning analytics, and third-party service integrations. In Indonesia, privacy and cybersecurity compliance is difficult to operationalize because legal obligations are often separated from system risks, IT governance controls, ownership, and audit evidence. This study develops a traceable privacy and cybersecurity compliance control baseline for Indonesian academic information systems. The method applies structured literature-based conceptual synthesis and design science-insp

title: Quantifying urban heat: A spatiotemporal study of climate change and population growth in Ikorodu, Lagos, Nigeria
abstract: Climate change and rapid urban growth are increasingly altering local climatic conditions in cities across the Global South.One important manifestation is the urban heat island (UHI) effect, whereby built-up urban areas experience higher temperatures than surrounding less-developed areas.This study examines the relationship between climate change, urban growth, and rising temperatures in Ikorodu, a rapidly expanding peri-urban area of Lagos State, Nigeria.Using simulated but realistic datasets derived from Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NIMET) records, Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Chang
journal: African Journal of Environmental Science and Technology
institutions: Lagos State University of Science and Technology

title: Occurrence and distribution of plant-parasitic nematodes in flooded rice-producing regions of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Rice ( Oryza sativa L.) is a crop of great economic and social importance for many countries around the world. Brazil is among the countries with the highest rice production in the world, and the state of Rio Grande do Sul accounts for more than 70% of national production. However, biotic threats, including plant-parasitic nematodes, may limit rice production across the state’s producing regions. This study surveyed the occurrence and genus composition of plant-parasitic nematodes in irrigated rice fields across different regions of Rio Grande do Sul. Fifty-four composite soil and roo

title: Financial and economic performance of coconut plantation rejuvenation assisted by engineered wood products: A Fijian case study
abstract: Coconut plantations support the livelihoods of millions of smallholder families globally, including a high proportion who live in poverty. Many growing regions are caught in a ‘senility trap’, with large areas over the age of 60, with nut yields well-below their potential. Presently, senile palm removal incurs high direct costs and opportunity costs associated with foregone nut production before replanted coconuts become commercially productive. title: Determinants of Enrollment in Storm, Flood, and Earthquake Insurance by Product Type: Focus on Fixed-Effects Models
abstract: This study analyzed the effects of paid claims, government subsidy rates, and disaster relief grants, among other factors, on enrollment in Storm, Flood, and Earthquake Insurance by product type. The study employed a fixed-effects model and proposed policy improvements to analyze panel data constructed from the insurance records of 229 local governments from 2013 to 2025.
