title: Mitigating Weld Defects in AISI 4145 Medium-Carbon Steel During Shielded Metal Arc Welding
abstract: Welding defects pose significant challenges to product quality and productivity in manufacturing industries. Shielded metal arc welding (SMAW) is the most widely used welding method in developing countries such as Ethiopia. This thesis identifies and addresses the root causes of welding defects in SMAW of medium carbon steel (AISI 4145) at Akaki Basic Metal Industry (ABMI), and optimizes welding parameters to enhance weld quality and reduce defect rates. title: Contrasting Spatial Genomic Structure in Two Widespread Grassland Species Across Norway Supports Species‐Specific Seed Sourcing
abstract: ABSTRACT Ecological restoration typically relies on locally sourced seed material, yet seed sourcing in many countries is based on broad administrative regions rather than empirical genetic data. Whether these generalized zones reflect biologically meaningful population genomic structure, particularly among co‐occurring species used together in restoration, remains poorly understood, thus limiting genetically informed restoration practices. title: Revealing the Values of Eco-theological Islamic Education in the Blora Manganan Tradition through the Perspective of Scientia Sacra Nasr
abstract: The global environmental crisis stems from the modern desacralization of nature. This study explores the Manganan tradition in Blora, Indonesia, as a living system of Eco-theological Islamic Education through Seyyed Hossein Nasr’s Scientia Sacra. Using a qualitative phenomenological design, this study collected data through participant observation, semi-structured interviews with six informants, and documentation in Panolan Village, Blora, in July 2025. title: Regulatory aspects of risks posed by veterinary medicinal products to European necrophagous birds: A case study with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)
abstract: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are used in human and veterinary medicine to treat pain and inflammatory diseases. However, the uncontrolled treatment of free-roaming and sheltered livestock with NSAIDs, mainly diclofenac, has caused catastrophic impacts on the biodiversity of necrophagous birds. For instance, a decline of up to 95 % in populations of various species of vultures occurred in South Asia from the late 1990 s to the early 2000 s. title: Ecology and conservation of subterranean biodiversity of Greater Lisbon, Portugal
abstract: Abstract Subterranean ecosystems harbour fauna moulded by extreme and stable conditions such as absence of light, narrow temperature ranges, high humidity and low availability of organic matter. The adaptations of cave fauna, coupled with the isolation of populations, often lead to a higher incidence of endemics and greater vulnerability to environmental changes. These ecosystems face severe threats caused by pollution and overexploitation, habitat loss and climate change, particularly evident in areas of increased human pressure as capitals of countries. institutions: Museu Nacional de História Natural e da Ciência

title: UAV-based method for measuring CO 2 emissions in forest ecosystems
abstract: Abstract. This study addresses the difficulty of accurately quantifying CO2 emissions in forest ecosystems due to spatial heterogeneity, complex terrain, and the combined effects of horizontal and vertical transport. A UAV-based platform, capable of three-dimensional CO2 emission observation, was developed, evaluated and applied to a forest ecosystem. title: One-Step Growth Curve Analysis of a Bacteriophage Infecting Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: Background: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic gram-negative bacterium associated with the contamination of edible bird’s nest (EBN) production systems. Pseudomonas aeruginosa may infect swiftlets and produce pigments that cause greenish staining of EBN, thereby decreasing the product's quality and market value. Bacteriophages are promising biocontrol agents owing to their host specificity and environmental safety. journal: Journal of Applied Veterinary Science And Technology

title: Membrane mechanical resilience across bacteria and eukaryotes: A comparative molecular dynamics study under surface tension
abstract: The mechanical properties of biological membranes are essential for cellular function, yet the molecular determinants of their responses to mechanical stress remain incompletely understood. Here, all-atom molecular dynamics simulations were used to investigate four biologically relevant membrane models: the inner membrane of Pseudomonas aeruginosa containing cyclopropane-modified acyl chains, the Bacillus subtilis plasma membrane enriched in branched-chain lipids, a simplified bacterial membrane, and an asymmetric eukaryotic plasma membrane (EPM). title: Charting the Course: Practical Steps for Philippine HEIs to Embark on Internationalization
abstract: In response to a global imperative and local legislative mandates like the Transnational Higher Education Act (RA 11448), this paper provides a practical seven-step roadmap for Philippine Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) to systematically initiate and strengthen their internationalization efforts. By integrating UNESCO’s regional student mobility data with a case study of Panpacific University and comparative insights from University of Santo Tomas (UST) and Mariano Marcos State University (MMSU), this study proposes a Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) -based framework of seven strategic actions th

title: Trajectory-aware intervention withdrawal in high-risk logistics systems: A reciprocal nonlinear dynamical framework
abstract: High-risk logistics systems face a timing problem: intensive intervention is costly, but withdrawing it before collaboration is durable can leave persistent risk unresolved. We develop a seven-state reciprocal nonlinear dynamical framework in which stakeholder adaptation co-evolves with governance capability, data credibility, collaboration capability, and logistics risk. These persistent states feed back into subsequent payoff differences, allowing earlier behavior to reshape later incentives. title: Systematic Comparisons between Long-Read- and Short-Read-Based Amplicon Sequencing to Characterize Mixed Microalgal Communities
abstract: Abstract The 18S rRNA gene has emerged as the primary molecular marker for amplicon-based characterization of microalgal communities, including in wastewater treatment systems, yet trade-offs between short- and long-read approaches remain poorly defined. We systematically compared V8–V9 short-read sequencing (SR; Illumina MiSeq), near-full-length long-read sequencing with ss5ss3 primers (LR; PacBio Sequel II), and computationally extracted V8–V9 regions from LR data (LS). title: Molecular Recognition of Dental Resin Monomers by Salivary Proteins: Integrated Docking, DFT, Molecular Dynamics, and MM/PBSA Analysis
abstract: An in silico investigation was performed to study the interactions between the commonly encountered resin monomers and the major salivary proteins. Bisphenyl diglycidylmethane (Bis-GMA), hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA), and triethylene glycol dimethacrylate (TEGDMA) were assessed for molecular docking, density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics (MD), MM/PBSA binding free-energy calculations, and per-residue energy decomposition. α-amylase, lysozyme, and albumin emerged as critical predicted targets from the docking process. title: Listado de fauna silvestre en categoría de riesgo de conservación en Isla del Carmen y Laguna de Términos, Campeche, México
abstract: Los listados documentales de fauna en riesgo pueden sobreestimar el número de taxones cuando los registros de ocurrencia a nivel de especie se cruzan directamente con categorías normativas asignadas a subespecies. El objetivo de este estudio fue elaborar un listado actualizado de las especies de fauna silvestre registradas en Isla del Carmen y Laguna de Términos, Campeche, México, incluidas en alguna categoría de riesgo de la NOM-059-SEMARNAT-2010. title: The Use of Space in Neanderthal Campsites: Evidence from Spatial and Taphonomic Analyses of Charcoal Remains from Level Ra of Abric Romaní (Barcelona, Spain)
abstract: Abstract This work aims to investigate the formation processes of the charcoal assemblage from level Ra at Abric Romaní, a well-preserved Middle Palaeolithic rock shelter in north-eastern Spain that was occupied by Neanderthals. To this end, we adopted an anthracological approach that combines both taxonomic and taphonomic observations. Spatial patterns and potential formation processes were explored through spatial analysis using Kernel Density Estimation and the Moran’s index across the excavated layer. title: Sustainable valorisation of aquatic macrophytes in German rivers for biomass utilisation and ecosystem management
abstract: Aquatic macrophytes are fundamental components of river ecosystems, regulating primary production, nutrient cycling and habitat structure. In human-impacted rivers, native and non-native aquatic species, particularly submerged and free-floating taxa, form dense stands that alter hydraulics, deplete oxygen, displace native vegetation and restrict water use, a phenomenon termed aquatic weed proliferation. title: DIGITAL HEALTH ADOPTION IS ASSOCIATED WITH BETTER HEALTHCARE PERFORMANCE BUT PERSISTENT INEQUITY IN BANGLADESH: A NATIONWIDE CONVERGENT MIXED-METHODS STRUCTURAL EQUATION MODELLING STUDY
abstract: Background: Bangladesh is scaling digital health under its Digital Health Strategy 2023–2027, yet empirical evidence on how adoption relates to health-system performance and equity is fragmented. We examined how governance, change management and implementation barriers shape digitalization adoption, and how adoption relates to performance, patient-reported outcomes and perceived health inequality. Methods: A convergent parallel mixed-methods study was conducted in all eight administrative divisions. title: Flood Regime Structures Small Mammal Assemblages in Riparian Forests Along the Upper Paraguay River
abstract: ABSTRACT The diversity of small non‐volant mammals is shaped by multiple environmental factors, with habitat structure as a key driver. Horizontal and vertical heterogeneity influence shelter, food, and movement, guiding how species with different locomotor and dietary traits partition space. Across a~200 km riparian corridor in the Upper Paraguay River, Brazil, we aimed to: (1) examine richness, abundance, and functional group composition, primarily among terrestrial and scansorial small mammals in riparian forests; (2) relate species richness and abundance to local habitat and hydrological c

title: Differentiation in ant-eating spiders based on offensive and defensive exploitation of ants
abstract: Abstract Ecological speciation via host-race has been documented in several herbivores and parasitoids. Analogous prey-race has recently been suggested to explain the diversity of specialised ant-eating spiders. Two sister species from the Iberian Peninsula, Zodarion alacre and Z. andalusiacum (Zodariidae), possess almost identical copulatory organs, but differ in body size and colouration. Zodarion spiders exploit different ant species offensively (as prey) and defensively (as mimetic models). title: Pluvial flood impacts on ambulance travel and spatial disparities in emergency healthcare accessibility in Thessaloniki, Greece
abstract: Urban pluvial flooding can disrupt road networks, delay emergency medical services and produce spatially uneven losses of access to urgent healthcare. This study evaluates how flood-induced road disruption affects ambulance travel performance and identifies buildings, neighbourhoods and populations that experience reduced emergency healthcare accessibility under rainfall events with return periods of 10, 20 and 100 years in Thessaloniki, Greece. title: The Trichoptera of Panama XXX. Trichoptera of the Piedra Jabón Geosite with description of a new species
abstract: Herein we report on preliminary data for the Trichoptera assemblage for the Piedra Jabón Geosite, a proposed UNESCO defined geological site located in Coclé Province, near Penonomé. Seven streams were sampled during 2022–2023. A total of 81 species were identified distributed among 12 caddisfly families. title: Hydrogeochemical controls and human health risk assessment of trace metals in groundwater from volcanic aquifers in Kikatiti Ward, northern Tanzania
abstract: Groundwater hydrochemistry, seasonal variations, and human health risks associated with trace metals ( Pb , Hg , and As ) were evaluated across the volcanic aquifer system of Kikatiti Ward, northern Tanzania. Hydrochemical conditions were strongly influenced by seasonal hydrological shifts, silicate weathering, and volcanic geology. Major ion evolution progressed from Ca HCO 3 to Na HCO 3 water types, with dry-season samples exhibiting enhanced mineralization due to reduced recharge and extended water–rock interaction times. title: foxQ2 marks fast-acting interneurons including dopaminergic neurons of mushroom bodies and central complex in the beetle Tribolium castaneum
abstract: Abstract The brain is one of the most complex animal organs and the development of the many different neuron types remains enigmatic. A set of brain-specific transcription factors is involved in brain patterning but their specific contributions mostly remain to be elucidated, including foxQ2II . This transcription factor is conserved in anterior neuroectodermal patterning of most animals while it has been lost from vertebrates. title: Efficacy of raccoon removal in urban and rural sites in northern Illinois
abstract: Abstract Raccoons ( Procyon lotor ) are opportunistic and highly adaptable mesopredators that may negatively impact avian and reptilian species. Although wildlife professionals often utilize predator control techniques to manage raccoons, information to guide management activities is lacking. We analyzed the efficacy of raccoon removal within urban and rural sites in northern Illinois, USA, during 2022–2024. title: Upcycling waste polyester into cobalt-molybdenum sulfide-decorated carbon foam for photothermal desalination and parametric optimization using Taguchi design of experiments
abstract: Photothermal desalination is an emerging solar-powered technique for water desalination. One of the primary open issues in the field is the development of new materials that guarantee high photothermal efficiency and evaporation rates. In this study, waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles are upcycled into carbon foam, which is then decorated with Co-Mo2S3 via hydrothermal synthesis to prepare a photothermal evaporator. title: Visitors’ perceptions and demand preferences for cultural ecosystem services in urban parks for sustainable tourism management
abstract: Abstract Urban parks serve as vital public spaces for recreational activities. However, key scientific questions remain regarding how, and to what extent, socio-demographic characteristics influence visitors’ perceptions of different types of cultural ecosystem services (CESs). Two further questions concern how park visitor typologies and their characteristics can be systematically identified, and how the demand preferences of different visitor groups for CESs can be understood. title: Thermal stress reduces dung burial, brood production, and the development of dung beetles: a challenge for climate resilience
abstract: Increasing temperatures can impair ecosystem services and the reproduction of dung beetles. We investigated the effects of increased nest temperatures on reproduction, dung burial, and the development of 2 dung beetle species (Onthophagus binodis and Digitonthophagus gazella). Three pairs of sexually mature F1-beetles at 15 days of age were housed in temperature-controlled chambers for 2 weeks. title: Hierarchically Wrinkled Silver Ink as a Platform for Fully Integrated Stretchable Electronic Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of high‐performance stretchable electronics continues to be limited by the fundamental trade‐off between electrical conductivity, mechanical resilience, and cost‐effective manufacturability. This work introduces a Silver Hierarchical Responsive ink (SHRink), a universal approach for the fabrication of highly stretchable interconnects, wirings, and skin‐interfaced electrodes. title: Participatory Mapping of Village Potential to Support Local Development Planning in Puuhialu Village, North Konawe Regency, Indonesia
abstract: This community service program identified, classified, documented, and mapped the development potential of Puuhialu Village, North Konawe Regency, Southeast Sulawesi, between 1 May and 1 June 2026. We combined a participatory approach with descriptive analysis, treating the village government and residents as partners who checked and corrected our findings rather than as mere respondents. title: Farmer and advisor perspectives on soil amendments: motivators, barriers, and insights for scaling
abstract: Soil amendments such as gypsum, structure lime, and pulp and paper mill sludge have multiple localised agronomic and broader environmental benefits, but their uptake by farmers remains limited. This exploratory mixed-methods study examined farmers’ and advisors’ perceptions of factors influencing soil amendment adoption through interviews with 11 farmers and 5 agricultural advisors in Southwest Finland, complemented by a nationwide survey of 20 advisors, which provided supplementary perspectives on advisor perceptions. title: Additive genetic effects of two large effect loci shaping age-at-maturity in Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar )
abstract: Fitness-related traits are shaped by both additive and non-additive genetic effects, resulting in a complex and context-dependent genetic architecture. However, the relative contribution of these components remains poorly understood, particularly for major-effect loci underlying life-history traits. In this study, we investigated the additive genetic contributions and potential epistatic interactions between 2 unlinked major-effect loci, vgll3 and six6, that influence age-at-maturity in Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar). title: Assessment of possible interactions between Citrus aurantifolia leaf alkaloid-rich compounds and relevant protein targets in scopolamine-induced amnesic rats
abstract: Aim: This study assessed the neuroprotective effect of lime (Citrus aurantifolia) leaf via the interaction of its inherent alkaloid compounds with specific neuronal protein targets [acetylcholinesterase (AChE), adenosine deaminase (ADA), and monoamine oxidase (MAO)] in scopolamine-induced amnesic rats. title: Phase engineering of Mo x C regulates electronic structure and interfacial hydrogen-bond networks over Ru sites for pH-universal hydrogen evolution
abstract: Abstract Metallic ruthenium (Ru) represents a promising Pt alternative for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). title: Tracing the spread of Celtic languages using ancient genomics
abstract: Abstract Celtic languages are today restricted to Europe’s Atlantic fringes but were widely spoken across the continent during the Iron Age 1–3 . How Celtic achieved this early distribution remains contested 4 , with alternative archaeological and linguistic models proposing different homelands and dispersal routes. Here we analyse genome-wide data from 4,587 ancient individuals, focusing on Bronze and Iron Age Europe, to test the extent to which these models fit reconstructed demographic histories. title: Comparative Analysis of Aerobic Bacteria, Green Microalgae, and Diatoms in Domestic Wastewater Treatment: Pollutant Removal, Lipid Profile, and Biodiesel Properties
abstract: Microalgal systems are receiving significant attention for wastewater treatment because of their effective treatment performance while simultaneously generating valuable biomass for energy recovery. This study compares the performance of three biological systems - green microalgae, diatoms, and aerobic bacteria for the treatment of real domestic wastewater. Each system was operated in semi-continuous mode at different solid retention times (SRTs) of 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12 days. title: Integration of Landscape Aesthetics and Sustainable Business Models in Kaliaren Village Land Utilization
abstract: This research aims to identify and optimize land use in Kaliaren Village through the integration of landscape aesthetic aspects and the development of sustainable business models. Using a descriptive-exploratory qualitative approach, this study maps the existing conditions of land use, analyzes aesthetic and economic potential, and explores the perception of the community and stakeholders through observation, in-depth interviews, Focus Group Discussions, and spatial analysis. title: Berberine-functionalized biogenic silver nanoparticles inhibit quorum-regulated curli mediated biofilms in emerging MDR uropathogenic Enterobacter hormaechei
abstract: Abstract Multidrug-resistant Enterobacter hormaechei is being increasingly reported in urinary tract infections (UTIs), where its ability to form quorum-regulated, curli-rich biofilms contributes to antibiotic tolerance and persistence. Targeting both quorum sensing (QS) and amyloid-mediated biofilm stability may provide an alternative strategy to conventional antibiotics. title: Computational prioritization of fungal-derived H1 receptor ligand candidates for allergy-related research
abstract: Activation of the G-protein-coupled histamine H1 receptor (H1R) contributes to allergic responses such as bronchoconstriction, vasodilation, and pruritus. This study aimed to computationally prioritize novel fungal-derived compounds for H1R-targeted investigation based on predicted binding characteristics, pharmacokinetic and toxicity profiles, and BBB permeability. abstract: This research presents a robust and effective approach for enhancing the active corrosion protection of UiO-66 through in-situ and physical hybridizations with nanodiamond (ND) in epoxy coatings under neutral, acidic, and alkaline conditions. To maintain UiO-66 as the dominant component in nanocomposite coatings, the composition of the in-situ synthesized (UiO-66@ND) and physical (UiO-66&ND) nanohybrids was set to 80:20 for UiO-66:ND. title: Quantification of influencing parameters on plug-holing and smoke extraction efficiency for multi-point lateral vents in tunnel fires
abstract: In tunnel smoke extraction systems, the multi-point lateral vent configuration is critical for fire emergencies. However, variations in the fire heat release rate and the vent layout often cause non-uniform plug-holing at individual vents, which reduces the smoke extraction efficiency. To address this challenge, a theoretical method was developed to identify and quantify plug-holing. title: Targeted degradation of a constitutively active GPCR oncoprotein
abstract: To assess the feasibility of using proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) to target G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), we constructed a degron-tagged GPCR library in which a HaloTag7 protein fusion tag was engineered into the cytoplasmic carboxyl terminal tail. title: Estimating the causal effect of extreme flooding on urban property markets: A case study of Porto Alegre, Brazil
abstract: The May 2024 floods in Porto Alegre, Brazil, triggered a pronounced spatial repricing of climate risk in the city’s housing market. Using a Bayesian structural time-series framework, we estimate an average causal impact of a 4.7% increase in sale prices and a 9.1% increase in rental price indices, driven primarily by price appreciation in elevated, flood-resilient neighborhoods. Our econometric approach accounts for nonlinear trends and macroeconomic controls, isolating the causal effect of the disaster. title: Strain Rate Triggered Network Locking in Shear‐Stiffening Gel/Wood Fibres Composites for Adaptive Impact Protection
abstract: ABSTRACT Lightweight structural materials capable of simultaneously sustaining mechanical load‐bearing and dissipating extreme impact energy remain a long‐standing challenge, as conventional systems are constrained by the intrinsic trade‐off between stiffness and toughness under dynamic loading. In this work, we address this limitation by introducing a strain rate triggered network locking strategy that enables adaptive mechanical reconfiguration in poplar fibres (PFs) and shear stiffening gel (SSG) composites (PSCs). title: Asymmetric hill equations arising from bilinear oscillators with state-dependent parametric excitation
abstract: Abstract This study presents an analytical and numerical investigation of bilinear oscillators subjected to piecewise parametric excitation, where both the excitation amplitude and damping are state-dependent. The governing equations are formulated as asymmetric Hill’s equations with asymmetric parametric excitation. title: Tunable Porosity and Dye Removal Performance of Kaolin-Based Geopolymer Membranes via H2O2-assisted Foaming
abstract: Indonesia’s abundant Bangka-Belitung kaolin provides a locally available raw material for developing geopolymer membranes for dye-contaminated water treatment. The kaolin was thermally activated at 650 o C to produce reactive metakaolin and subsequently fabricated into porous geopolymer membranes using methylene blue (MB) solution as model dye-contaminated water. Porosity was tailored using 5 and 7% v/v H 2 O 2 solutions as foaming agents at dosages of 1–3 wt.% relative to metakaolin mass. title: Pace-dependent reorganisation of shoulder-hip coordination in front crawl swimming
abstract: Shoulder and hip roll are distinct but coordinated components of body roll during front crawl swimming, yet shoulder-hip coordination has largely been examined using discrete measures. This study applied continuous relative phase (CRP), Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM), and complementary coupling analyses to a previously published kinematic dataset, to examine shoulder-hip coordination during sprint and 400 m pace front crawl. title: Nanoparticle-Based Antibacterials: Microbial Techniques, Bacterial Defence Responses and Antimicrobial Resistance Detection
abstract: Objectives The escalating threat of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has necessitated the development of alternative therapeutic strategies. Among the many approaches, nanoparticle-based antimicrobial agents have shown significant promise. These nanoscale systems offer targeted drug delivery, enhanced penetration and potential to overcome resistance mechanisms. However, there is a need for rigorous and diverse microbial techniques to evaluate their efficacy and the risk of inducing resistance/persister cells. title: Andrographolide Combined With Voriconazole Enhances Antifungal Activity Against Aspergillus Species
abstract: Azole resistance in Aspergillus fumigatus is increasing globally, necessitating novel combination strategies to restore the efficacy of first-line antifungals such as voriconazole (VCZ). Andrographolide (ADR), a natural diterpene lactone, has shown limited direct antifungal activity but exhibits synergistic effects with amphotericin B and immunomodulatory properties. However, its potential as an adjunct to VCZ against Aspergillus species remains unexplored. title: Structural vulnerability regimes of water supply systems under climate change: A robustness-based analysis using multi-dimensional sustainability indicators
abstract: Climate change is expected to intensify hydrological variability and extreme events, increasing the vulnerability of basin-scale multi-sector water supply systems. Conventional assessments commonly summarize vulnerability using failure probability, providing limited insight into how failure-prone conditions are organized across system states. This study develops a multi-dimensional sustainability framework to characterize structural vulnerability regimes in the Seomjin River Basin, Korea. title: Decoupling Sustainability Reporting and Social Media Communication After a Sustainability Scandal: Strategic Silence, Selective Disclosure and Legitimacy Stabilisation
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how corporate sustainability disclosure evolves across a legitimacy‐threatening event by analysing the interaction between formal sustainability reporting and social media communication. Using a qualitative, longitudinal, event‐centred single‐case design, the study investigates a major Italian organic meat producer over the 2021–2024 period through formal sustainability reporting, Facebook content and stakeholder interactions, regulatory and contextual documents and selected economic indicators. title: A century of soybean breeding increased photosynthetic capacity but not NPQ relaxation
abstract: Accelerating photoprotective regulation to improve carbon assimilation is a promising strategy to increase crop productivity. Although rapid non-photochemical quenching (NPQ) relaxation has been validated as a target through metabolic engineering, it remains unclear whether conventional breeding has improved this trait. Here, we investigated whether more than a century of soybean breeding enhanced NPQ relaxation alongside light-saturated carbon assimilation and seed traits. title: Food perceptions and breakfast choices among school-age children and parents in southern Peru: A cross-sectional study using projective techniques
abstract: Peru's school feeding program applies largely uniform menus across regions with very different food cultures, yet little is known about how children and parents in these regions represent food. This cross-sectional study compared food perceptions and breakfast choices among school-age children (10-12 years) and their parents in five cities of southern Peru (Arequipa, Cusco, Moquegua, Puno and Tacna). title: Reconciling resource demand and environmental loss in urban phosphorus metabolism through bidirectional optimization of dietary consumption structure
abstract: Phosphorus (P), a non-renewable mineral resource embedded throughout the food system, links resource security with environmental health. However, urban P metabolism shaped by dietary preferences generates unavoidable quantity-quality tensions between resource demand and environmental loss. title: First-time versus repeat tourists: A multi-destination data mining comparison of actual behavior
abstract: Given that the intention to return is not a valid proxy, understanding tourists’ actual repeat behavior is crucial. This study aims to systematically compare the actual behavior of first-time and repeat tourists across multiple destinations. This research employed a large-scale dataset of user-generated content collected through big-data mining (N = 8,059) and conducted t-tests and chi-square tests across different types of tourist destinations (N = 298). title: Integrating ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 Management Systems with Community-Based Disaster Risk Reduction in Niger Delta Oil Operations
abstract: Oil operations in the Niger Delta sit inside the same floodplains, creeks and villages that host millions of residents. Hazards such as spills, fires, floods and pipeline failures rarely stop at the fence line, yet the management systems that govern them usually do. This paper argues that ISO 45001 (occupational health and safety) and ISO 14001 (environment), both built on the same high-level structure, can be deliberately extended to include community-based disaster risk reduction (CBDRR). title: Identifying Middle Paleolithic Residential Units Through the Spatial Organization of Combustion Structures at Abric Romaní (Barcelona, Spain)
abstract: Abstract The habitual and controlled use of fire among Neanderthal groups, together with the residential use of caves and rock shelters, represents a major turning point in the emergence of Paleolithic camp bases. In Middle Paleolithic sites, the interrelation between shelter geomorphology, fire-use locations and activity areas has been interpreted as evidence of spatial organization. abstract: Organophosphorus flame retardants (OPFRs) are chemical additives used to prevent combustion and slow down the speed of flame propagation. We evaluated levels of urinary OPFRs metabolites, serum sex hormones, and semen quality among men in southern Taiwan. OPFR exposure was assessed by quantifying the concentrations of five OPFR diesters in urine samples. title: Dynamic redox reactivation of platinum sites for long-term glycolate electrosynthesis from polyethylene terephthalate wastes
abstract: Glycolates are indispensable in the health, chemical and pharmaceutical industries, whereas their mainstream production involve toxic chemicals and harsh operating condition. An alternative route for glycolate production is electrifying ethylene glycol (EG) that originates from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) but suffers from poor durability of active platinum site that tend to deactivate. abstract: Bacterial wilt caused by Ralstonia solanacearum species complex is a major constraint in tomato production in Kenya, resulting in yield losses of up to 100% in heavily infested fields. This study used high-throughput shotgun metagenomic sequencing approach to characterize the rhizosphere microbiomes of tomato plants in three of the major production areas in Kenya (Kirinyaga, Kiambu, and Laikipia counties) focusing on detecting Ralstonia phage sequences. Comparative assessment of floristic composition and diversity following anthropogenic disturbance in Nigerian lowland rainforest
abstract: Nigerian lowland rainforest, a biodiverse ecoregion with widespread vegetation, has experienced selective anthropogenic disturbances. Understanding the current species composition and forest recovery following a decrease in disturbances is critical for forest biodiversity and conservation. This study assessed the species composition and diversity of a once disturbed forest site in comparison with two (2) neighboring undisturbed forest sites within Nigerian lowland rainforest along Warri River. title: SPATIAL VARIATION OF TUBERCULOSIS OCCURRENCES IN ILORIN, KWARA STATE NIGERIA
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) is one of the deadliest infectious diseases globally. It was responsible for 1.6 million deaths in 2019 and the leading cause of mortality from a single infectious agent, especially in developing countries. In Africa, the incidence of TB was estimated to be rising, with 1500 deaths daily. Despite current global efforts to reduce TB, Nigeria’s TB prevalence is increasing in many communities. title: Cryptic variation within and among islands in the ultraviolet reflectance of lizard throat coloration
abstract: Cryptic polymorphism can bias tests of intraspecific phenotypic variation across space and time. Because many colours exist outside the range of human perception, colour variation is not always easily detected even when it plays an important role in organismal biology. In colour polymorphic lizards, recent work has demonstrated the presence of cryptic variation in ultraviolet (UV) reflectance, but the factors influencing this variation across space and time are less well known. abstract: Abstract Assessing genetic diversity at loci putatively involved in fitness, such as immune genes, could provide important insights into the survival and vulnerability of endangered species. Research on immune genes in wild species has traditionally focused on the Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) genes, which represent only a small proportion of the immune gene repertoire, thereby limiting our understanding of immunity in non-model species. title: Shifting Dietary Ecologies of Early Ungulates Across the Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum in the Bighorn Basin, Wyoming
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the interplay between climate change and ecology is crucial when attempting to reconstruct the evolutionary history of species, as well as predicting how modern species may fare in light of current anthropogenic climate change and habitat destruction. Here we use dental microwear texture analysis (DMTA) to infer the foraging ecologies of three lineages of early ungulates (the phenacodontids Copecion and Ectocion and the early perissodactyl Sifrhippus ) across the Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum (PETM) in the Bighorn Basin of western North America. title: Regulatory mechanism of LuxS/AI-2 quorum sensing system on biofilm formation of Listeria monocytogenes on the surface of fresh-cut iceberg lettuce
abstract: ABSTRACT Listeria monocytogenes ( L. monocytogenes ) readily forms biofilms on the surfaces of leafy vegetables, but the regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the role and mechanism of the LuxS/AI-2-mediated quorum sensing (QS) system in biofilm formation by L . monocytogenes during its colonization of fresh-cut iceberg lettuce (FCIL). title: From Climate Futures to Future Migration: The Groundswell Reports and Their Reception in German Media Discourse
abstract: Over the past decade, international organizations have sought to raise awareness about climate migration and secure its place on national political agendas. Scholars have critically examined how these organizations frame climate migration and what assumptions inform their efforts to set the agenda. Yet, little attention has been paid to the temporal logic and futurity underpinning this discourse: It treats climate migration as an anticipated threat, rather than an observable phenomenon. title: Pragmatic Approaches to Formal Verification in Safety-Critical Systems: A Comparative Study of Model Checkers for Broader Adoption
abstract: Testing helps detect defects; however, it cannot confirm their absence. This paradox is especially evident in complex applications where testing all possible scenarios is unfeasible. Formal Verification (FV), on the other hand, is a proven method for demonstrating a system’s correctness through mathematical and logical reasoning. Surprisingly, FV is yet to see widespread adoption, even in fields where safety is critical. title: Decoupling environmental suitability from realized recruitment through ontogenetic environmental filtering in a long‐lived Mediterranean palm species
abstract: Abstract Long-lived plants facing anthropogenic disturbance often exhibit recruitment failure despite persistent reproductive adults, generating extinction debt masked by longevity. However, whether adult presence reliably reflects environmental suitability for recruitment remains unclear. Here, we examine ontogenetic niche differentiation and its consequences for recruitment in Jubaea chilensis , an endangered long-lived Mediterranean palm with an aging population. title: Proteasome Inhibitor MG132 Facilitates Antiviral Effects by Inhibiting TFEB Degradation and Activating Autophagy
abstract: Abstract The ubiquitin-proteasome system, which serves as one of the most common cellular degradation pathways, plays a critical role in maintaining proteostasis. Yet, the correlation between the ubiquitin-proteasome system and antiviral defense remains to be defined. In this work, pharmacological inhibition of proteasomes via treatment with MG132, which inhibited proteasome activity during viral infection, facilitated antiviral effects in vitro. abstract: ABSTRACT The hydrogen economy is commonly organized around four separate tasks: production, storage, transport, and release. This Perspective redefines decoupled water electrolysis (DWE) as a framework in which these functions can be integrated within a single electrochemical redox loop. title: Effect of Filler Metals on Microstructure, Mechanical Properties, and Corrosion Resistance of Gas Tungsten Arc Welded 316UG Stainless Steel
abstract: The welding of 316UG stainless steel, widely used in oil and gas industries, plays a critical role in ensuring structural integrity and corrosion resistance under harsh service conditions. This study investigates the effects of different filler metals (ER316L, ER310, and ER347) on the microstructure, mechanical properties, and corrosion behavior of Gas Tungsten Arc Welded (GTAW) joints of 316UG stainless steel. abstract: Freight operators face a persistent decision problem: a route that appears economical at dispatch may become expensive after congestion, a missed connection, additional handling, or cargo damage. The problem is particularly visible when a domestic road movement must be compared with a cross-border movement involving several carriers and transport modes. title: Planetary-scale metagenomic analysis reveals CRISPR targeting dynamics across ecosystems
abstract: Interactions between microorganisms and their mobile genetic elements (MGEs), including viruses and plasmids, impact microbiome dynamics. CRISPR-Cas systems are important regulators of these host-MGE interactions, but a global understanding of the diversity, activity and roles of CRISPR spacers across Earth's biomes is still lacking. abstract: La gestión de la capacitación articulada con las competencias laborales es un requisito normativo en la industria automotriz, establecido por las normas IATF 16949:2016 e ISO 9001:2015; sin embargo, en muchas organizaciones estos procesos todavía se administran con formatos físicos y hojas de cálculo. abstract: ABSTRACT The sluggish kinetics of oxygen reduction and evolution reactions (ORR/OER) at air cathodes restrict the practical performance of rechargeable zinc–air batteries (ZABs), driving the urgent demand for low‐cost, robust non‐noble metal bifunctional electrocatalysts. title: The Short-Term Fertility Impact of Abortion Law Restrictions: A Research Note
abstract: Poland's 2020 abortion ruling led to a sharp 6% drop in births 37 weeks later. The decline exceeded the number of legal abortions previously performed. The decline was strongest among younger and childless women. Abortion bans may reduce fertility when they heighten risks of childbearing.

While Nairobi, Mombasa and Kisumu are extensively studied, towns like Mbale-Vihiga County’s administrative capital absorb over 60% of Kenya’s urban growth with no commensurate infrastructure. title: Dye-ligand functionalized collagen fibers as an affinity chromatography stationary phase for efficient protein separation
abstract: Dye molecules serve as promising affinity ligands with significant potential in bioseparation applications. In this study, a series of dye-affinity collagen fibers (CFs-Dye) stationary phases was fabricated by immobilizing reactive dyes (reactive red 118, reactive blue 171, reactive blue 19, reactive blue 114, reactive blue 21, and reactive blue 116) onto CFs for the selective separation and purification of lysozyme (LyZ). title: Liquid crystalline nanoparticle-mediated co-delivery of gentamicin and rhDNase against mature Escherichia coli biofilms
abstract: Biofilm-associated infections remain a major clinical challenge due to restricted antibiotic penetration, matrix-mediated antimicrobial tolerance, and rapid degradation of biofilm-disruptive therapeutics in protease-rich environments. Here, liquid crystalline nanoparticles (LCNPs) were developed as a nanostructured co-delivery platform for gentamicin (GEN) and recombinant human DNase I (rhDNase), integrating antibiotic delivery with enzymatic disruption of the biofilm extracellular matrix. title: Interfacial Co–Ni Dual‐Site Synergy in Confined Co 9 S 8 –Ni 3 S 2 Heterostructures for Electrocatalytic Water Splitting
abstract: Although heazlewoodite‐type nickel sulfide (Ni 3 S 2 ) exhibits promising hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity, its application in overall water splitting remains limited by sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics associated with insufficient water activation. Herein, Co 9 S 8 –Ni 3 S 2 heterostructures confined in nitrogen‐rich spongy carbons are constructed to regulate interfacial electronic properties and unlock Co–Ni catalytic synergy for efficient water electrolysis. title: Two Ume6 target gene classes in the biofilm regulatory network of Candida albicans
abstract: ABSTRACT Biofilm formation by the fungal pathogen Candida albicans is a major source of infection. The biofilm regulator Ume6 forms complexes with partner transcription factors Efg1, Ndt80, and Upc2 to drive expression of biofilm-related genes. Here we present chromatin immunoprecipitation with sequencing (ChIP-seq) data for Ume6-chromatin association in both wild-type and efg1 Δ/Δ ndt80 Δ/Δ upc2 Δ/Δ backgrounds. title: Interface engineering of crystalline–amorphous hollow c-Co₃S₄/a-CoxP nanocages for all-pH hydrogen evolution
abstract: Exploring highly active and stable non-noble-metal electrocatalysts is critical for the widespread adoption of hydrogen energy technologies. In this work, we report the synthesis of hollow crystalline–amorphous nanocages composed of crystalline cobalt sulfide (c-Co 3 S 4 ) and amorphous cobalt phosphide (a-Co x P), derived from ZIF-67, through precise morphology and structural modulation. title: Nutrition in abrupt sunlight reduction scenarios: a scenario-based modeling study of malnutrition prevention in low-income regions
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Abrupt sunlight reduction scenarios (ASRSs), triggered by nuclear war, volcanic eruption, or asteroid strike, risk global agricultural collapse. Despite resilient food interventions, economic inequality may leave low-income countries (LICs) at severe risk of malnutrition even where global food production is partially maintained. Objectives To assess the nutritional adequacy of low-cost ASRS-resilient food baskets (~$1/person/d) for LIC populations across 2 postdisaster periods, and to identify micronutrient gaps requiring targeted intervention. title: Integrating Sentinel-2 Remotely Sensed Data into Center-Pivot Irrigation Management for Sustainable Water Resource Use: Evidence from the Nasho Irrigation Scheme, Rwanda
abstract: The Nasho Irrigation Scheme, one of Rwanda's largest centre-pivot irrigation schemes, faces challenges in aligning irrigation management with spatial and temporal variations in crop conditions. This study evaluated how Sentinel-2 remotely sensed data can support sustainable water resource management and crop productivity by assessing spatial and temporal variation in crop health using the Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Normalised Difference Moisture Index (NDMI), examining the relationship between NDVI and crop yield, and identifying barriers to the adoption of geospatial to

title: Breaking the Halide Concentration Reliance of Four‐Electron Zinc‐Iodine Batteries via Interfacial Halide Enrichment
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐valence iodine redox chemistry in aqueous batteries is fundamentally constrained by the requirement of highly concentrated halide environments, which stabilize reactive iodine cations but inevitably induce electrolyte corrosion and sluggish interfacial kinetics. In this study, we demonstrate an interfacial halide enrichment strategy that circumvents this long‐standing concentration dependence in four‐electron zinc‐iodine batteries. title: Hollowing Out Nanofibers for Enhanced Visual Brightness and More Effective Solar Heating
abstract: The temperature rise of a solar-heating textile is controlled by both generation and dissipation of heat. However, current designs mainly focus on increasing light absorption to generate more heat, often darkening the material while leaving thermal management largely overlooked. Herein, hollowing the nanofibers in a nonwoven mat produces a counterintuitive "brighter-yet-hotter" advantage over their solid (core-shell) counterparts. The polyacrylonitrile/polypyrrole double-shelled tubular nanofibers are fabricated by selectively removing the poly(ε-caprolactone) core from core-shell nanofibers.

title: Conical Roofs in Vernacular Architecture: Transformation and Integration into the Cultural Landscape
abstract: Vernacular architectures with conical roofs constitute distinctive morphological elements within rural landscapes associated with productive activities such as agriculture, livestock farming, and water management. This study examines how these architectural typologies contribute to the transformation and integration of the cultural landscape across different territorial contexts, through a qualitative comparative approach applied to case studies in Portugal, Spain, and Peru. title: A scoping review of equine musculoskeletal therapy interventions to inform evidence-based decision making
abstract: BACKGROUND: Equine musculoskeletal therapy interventions are increasingly used in management and rehabilitation of musculoskeletal disorders. Consolidation of the evidence base would facilitate collaboration between veterinarians and veterinary physiotherapists. AIMS/OBJECTIVES: This scoping review aimed to identify, categorise, and summarise the current evidence on equine musculoskeletal therapy interventions. title: Shallow Cumulus Cloud Statistics in Real‐Case Large‐Eddy Simulations and Their Dependence on Soil Moisture
abstract: Abstract The ability of weather and climate models to reproduce the statistical properties of shallow cumulus clouds (SCCs) is critical for representing boundary‐layer transport, cloud cover, and cloud‐radiative effects. This study investigates statistical properties of SCC ensembles using the Icosahedral Nonhydrostatic model in large‐eddy simulation mode for three cases during the Field Experiment on Submesoscale Spatio‐Temporal Variability in Lindenberg campaign. title: Integrated geochemical and spatial analysis of trace element redistribution in salinized arid agro-landscapes: Evidence from the Turyanchay River basin (Azerbaijan)
abstract: Arid agro-landscapes are highly vulnerable to the soil degradation caused by long-term irrigation and climatic constraints.This study investigated the spatial patterns and geochemical characteristics associated with trace element redistribution in salinized irrigated soils of the Turyanchay River basin (Azerbaijan).A geochemical dataset comprising 22 depth-specific sampling units from representative sampling sites was analyzed for trace element composition using energy-dispersive X-ray fluorescence spectrometry (EDXRF).A separate physicochemical dataset comprising 22 depth-specific sampling un

title: Retrospective evaluation of repeated dose dermal toxicity studies in North American agrochemical risk assessment
abstract: Current North American pesticide regulations mandate route-specific repeated-dose dermal toxicity (RDDT) studies for dermal exposure risk assessment. To evaluate the scientific necessity of this study requirement, a proof-of-concept retrospective analysis was conducted on conventional active pesticide ingredients with Syngenta end use product registered in North America (NA) from 2001 to 2025, examining publicly available risk assessments for 51 pesticides assessed by the United States Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA) and 43 by the Health Canada Pesticides Regulatory Directorate (PRD).

title: Biodiversity and ecosystem multifunctionality show contrasting recovery patterns across tropical forests with different logging histories
abstract: Globally, a growing proportion of logging‐disturbed tropical forest is recovering, holding great potential for biodiversity conservation and ecosystem functioning. However, how ecosystem multifunctionality (EMF) and its trait‐based predictors in these secondary forests differ from those in old‐growth forests remains unknown. title: Spatiotemporal NDVI Analysis of Kipengere Forest Reserve Dynamics in Tanzania: Evidence from 1995 to 2026
abstract: Forest ecosystems are of great importance for biodiversity conservation and water resource regulation but are increasingly subject to environmental and land-use changes. The study analysed the spatiotemporal dynamics of vegetation condition in the Kipengere Forest Reserve, Southwest Tanzania from 1995 to 2026 using the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) generated from Landsat satellite images. journal: American Journal of Environment and Climate

title: Remote sensing-based analysis of land use in spring protection zones in Southern Brazil
abstract: Springs are important ecosystems that help maintain water quality and quantity and are legally protected in Brazil as Permanent Preservation Areas (PPAs). They play a key role in aquatic ecosystems and help maintain biodiversity. The study aimed to characterize land cover in PPAs surrounding springs in the micro-watersheds of Jacarezinho, Paraná, Brazil. We mapped the springs of four micro-basins in the municipality and assessed vegetation cover in their PPAs using MapBiomas remote sensing data and geoprocessing tools. title: A Telomere-to-Telomere Genome Assembly and Demographic History Inference of Ostrya rehderiana
abstract: Ostrya rehderiana is a critically endangered plant species with an extremely small population size. However, the absence of high-quality genome assembly has impeded the understanding of the causes and genetic consequences of its endangered status, especially how theses genetic consequences result in the failure of its population regeneration. In this study, we integrated PacBio HiFi, Oxford Nanopore (ONT) long-read sequencing, Hi-C, Illumina resequencing, and RNA-seq data to generate a telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome assembly and annotation for this species. title: The resilience contract: Comparing climate resilience planning and community realities in Dominica
abstract: Climate resilience plans are proliferating globally, yet whether the priorities they formalise align with what communities themselves are identifying as essential for resilience remains unclear. Dominica has pledged to become the world's first climate-resilient nation by 2030; its Climate Resilience and Recovery Plan (CRRP) was produced following Category 5 Hurricane Maria in 2017, which resulted in losses of approximately 226% of GDP ( The Government of the Commonwealth of Dominica, 2017 ). abstract: ABSTRACT A chemical investigation of the 95% EtOH extract of Typhonium blumei led to the isolation of a new polyketide‐derived tetrahydropyran‐containing conjugated fatty acid derivative ( 1 ), together with four known compounds ( 2 – 5 ). The structure of compound 1 was elucidated through comprehensive spectroscopic analyses, including 1D and 2D NMR spectra ( 1 H NMR, 13 C NMR, DEPT, HSQC, HMBC, COSY, and NOESY), as well as HR‐ESI‐MS data. title: DESIGN AND REALIZATION OF A PROFILE NOTCHING DEVICE FOR AUTOMOTIVE ELASTOMER COMPONENTS
abstract: This paper presents the engineering design and constructive realization route of a profile notching device intended for automotive elastomer components manufactured in small and medium batches. Secondary profiling operations on rubber-based parts are difficult because elastomers combine low stiffness, large recoverable deformation, and sensitivity to local compression, which can generate dimensional scatter, tearing, or edge defects when conventional manual trimming is used. title: Integrated fertilizer management and agrometeorological conditions associated with yield and nutritional quality of Boro rice
abstract: Increasing rice production while improving grain nutritional quality is essential for global food security. We hypothesized that integrated fertilizer management combined with a suitable rice variety would enhance grain yield, nutrient uptake, and nutritional quality compared to conventional fertilizer management, while agrometeorological conditions would help explain variations in crop performance. title: Isolation, Structural Elucidation, and Anti‐Melanogenic Activity of a Novel Pectic Polysaccharide From Alhagi camelorum Fisch
abstract: Hyperpigmentation disorders motivate the search for structurally defined and effective natural depigmenting agents from plant-derived polysaccharides. The present study characterized the structural features and evaluated the anti-melanogenic activity of ACP-II-1, a novel pectic polysaccharide isolated from Alhagi camelorum Fisch. ACP-II-1 had a molecular weight of 26.145 kDa and contained GalA, Rha, Gal, Ara, GlcA, and Xyl at respective molar proportions of 0.798, 0.072, 0.053, 0.052, 0.016, and 0.009. title: Estimation of Dietary Microplastic Ingestion: Empirical Analysis for Delhi-NCR
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly detected in food products and may contribute to human exposure through daily dietary consumption. However, information on dietary MP exposure in Delhi-NCR, India, remains limited. This study aimed to investigate MP contamination in commonly consumed food items and assess their potential contribution to dietary exposure among residents of Delhi-NCR. An online survey involving 175 participants was conducted to determine the consumption frequency of eight food items: potato, egg, apple, potato chips, whole wheat flour, instant noodles, honey, and chicken. title: Characterization and multi-response optimization of epoxy–castor oil composites reinforced with coconut shell and marsh barbel powders
abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable polymer composites has led to the use of agricultural waste and natural materials as alternative reinforcements. The present work deals with the characterization and multi response optimization of epoxy castor oil composites reinforced with coconut shell powder (CSP) and marsh barbel powder (MBP). Hand lay-up casting technique was used to prepare six formulations with different loadings of natural powder and with 20 wt% castor oil, cured at room temperature. title: When policy uncertainty hits iron ore: dynamic spillovers to steel-related stock markets
abstract: Using data from September 2011 to November 2023, this paper examines how shocks to economic policy uncertainty (EPU) and the China Iron Ore Price Index (CIOPI) propagate along China’s iron ore–steel chain. TVP-VAR estimates show the clearest adverse short-run EPU response in the steel-sector index; the direct CIOPI response is not distinguishable from zero, while downstream responses are heterogeneous. abstract: Abstract Heatwaves are increasing in frequency and severity due to anthropogenic climate change and may play a role in recent insect declines. Heatwaves can occur during any season, and how insects are affected by heatwaves may depend on an insect's phenology and life stage when the heatwave occurs. Most research investigates summer heatwaves; however, winter heatwaves may have greater negative impacts on insects than summer heatwaves, but further investigation is necessary. title: Effects of 4R nitrogen management on corn silage production
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen (N) is one of the critical and costliest inputs for corn silage ( Zea mays ) production. Excessive N applications decrease profits for growers via increased cost of production and raise environmental concerns. The four core principles of the 4R nutrient stewardship framework—right source (S), right rate (R), right time (T), and right place (P)—aim to optimize N management. Most previous studies evaluating N management for corn silage only examined one or a few 4R practices. title: Socio-Ecological Risks Identification and Governance Transition of Natural Forest Protection and Restoration: A Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment from Guizhou, China
abstract: As forest landscape restoration advances, balancing ecological protection and local development has become a key challenge in natural forest governance. This study examines natural forest protection and restoration in Guizhou Province from a socio-ecological system perspective. By combining policy text analysis with stakeholder interviews, we review the evolution of natural forest protection and restoration policies from 1998 to 2024 and apply a strategic environmental and social assessment framework to identify environmental risks, social risks, and policy gaps. title: Surface Subsidence as an Effective Indicator of Methane Emissions From Underground Coal Mines
abstract: Abstract Methane (CH 4 ) emissions from underground coal mining remain a major and uncertain anthropogenic source. This study tests whether surface subsidence, a direct consequence of underground mining, can serve as an indicator of CH 4 emissions. We use the Changzhi coal belt in Shanxi of China, a major emission hotspot, as a case study. title: Influences of sex and time interval on reliability of neuromuscular and motor performance measurements in isometric plantar flexor exercise
abstract: PURPOSE: Reliable assessment of neuromuscular function is fundamental for interpreting physiological adaptations, yet sex-related influences in the reliability of these assessments remain poorly characterized across different temporal designs. We determined the within-session and between-days reliability of neuromuscular measurements in physically active men and women across multiple time intervals. abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the individual and combined effects of dietary L-carnitine (500 mg/kg) and stevioside (450 mg/kg) on growth performance, physiological responses, stress tolerance, immunity, antioxidant status, and molecular regulation in Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ; initial weight 3.84 ± 0.12 g) over 90 days. title: Mixture-dependent mechanical response of asphalt mixtures under saline freeze–thaw conditioning
abstract: Saline freeze–thaw exposure can alter the mechanical response of asphalt mixtures, yet these changes may depend on mixture characteristics and salt concentration. This study investigated two dense-graded asphalt mixtures, Binder and Topeka, under an accelerated saline freeze–thaw conditioning protocol. Specimens underwent eight freeze–thaw cycles in distilled water or NaCl solutions with nominal initial mass concentrations of 5% and 10%, while unconditioned Dry specimens were retained as reference groups. title: Cytoplasmic crowding drives intracellular viscoelastic increase during epithelial maturation
abstract: The cytoplasm is a crowded, active medium whose mechanical properties underpin essential cellular functions, yet how intracellular rheology adapts during tissue maturation remains unclear. Here, we examine the evolution of cytoplasmic viscoelasticity in Madin-Darby canine kidney epithelial monolayers as cell density increases. Using magnetic rotational spectroscopy, an active microrheology technique, we quantify zero-shear viscosity and elastic modulus throughout monolayer maturation. title: Formulation of Lutjanus johnii (Snapper) fishballs with concentrated syrup and Levisticum officinale (lovage) extract: Assessing integrated antioxidants for enhanced fishery products
abstract: Fishballs, ready-to-eat products with high nutritional value, can utilize lower-value fish species more efficiently. However, rapid spoilage from lipid oxidation and microbial growth is a major challenge. In this study, fishballs were prepared with varying lovage extract concentrations (T1: 0%, T2: 0.25%, T3: 0.5%, T4: 0.75%, T5: 1%) and 5% concentrated syrup, frozen at −38°C and stored at −18°C, with evaluations on days 1, 15, 30, and 45. abstract: Trait network analysis have been widely used to unravel the effects of variable environments on submerged macrophytes communities. However, few studies focused on the response of submerged macrophytes to variable water depths in impounded lakes from a whole plant trait network perspective. Here, we carried out a field study aimed to evaluate variation of functional traits, detect hub traits and clarify trait network topologies among different water depths. abstract: A major goal of regeneration biology is to uncover the molecular mechanisms that allow a wide range of animals to replace body parts through regeneration. Glycogen synthase kinase-3 (GSK3) is known to have significant regulatory influence on developmental pathways that are integral to successful regeneration in several animal groups. Annelids include some of the most highly regenerative animals known and, although GSK3 has been studied during regeneration in several species, its major roles remain unclear. title: Transcriptome Profiling Reveals Differential Expression of Virulence Genes in Xylella fastidiosa Cultured Under Different Nutrient Conditions
abstract: ABSTRACT Xylella fastidiosa is a xylem-limited, insect-vectored pathogen. To capture the metabolic changes that underlie its adaptation to both nutrient-rich and xylem-like environments, we performed transcriptome analyses on two reference strains, Temecula1 and 9a5c, sampled at early and late exponential phases in a complex laboratory medium (PWG) and a defined, xylem-mimicking medium (PIM6). title: Bacterial pathogen-dependent responses to high-frequency ultrasound-based hurdle treatments
abstract: High-frequency ultrasound (HFUS) is a promising non-thermal technology for food decontamination, although its antimicrobial mechanisms and interactions with natural antimicrobials remain poorly characterised. This study evaluated HFUS at 760 kHz, alone and in combination with green tea extract (GTE), against a panel of Gram-positive and Gram-negative foodborne bacteria. title: Estimating ecosystem-scale non-structural carbon dynamics in a shortleaf pine forest
abstract: Plants allocate photosynthetically fixed carbon (C) between metabolic needs, biomass production (BP), and non-structural carbon (NSC), a buffer between carbon supply and demand. While conceptual representation of alternative regulatory mechanisms of NSC has advanced significantly in recent decades, quantitative assessments of NSC's contribution to the ecosystem C budget have not been possible. abstract: Although fiscal and monetary instruments are calibrated for economic stabilisation rather than for environmental ends, they act directly upon the volume and composition of the activity that generates environmental pressure, and the literature has largely assessed their consequences on the implicit assumption that expansions and contractions are reflection of one another. abstract: Relcobatinib (ELVN-001) is a next-generation, investigational, BCR::ABL1 active-site tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) with a unique P-loop folded-in binding mode designed to deliver best-in-class efficacy with an improved tolerability profile over that of other TKIs for the treatment of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). abstract: Abstract Background While lactic acid bacteria (LAB) are widely recognized as probiotics, their genomic safety remains understudied. Method This study integrates phenotypic characterization, whole genome sequencing (WGS), and horizontal gene transfer (HGT) analysis to evaluate the safety of two LAB strains isolated from healthy equines. title: Beyond heatwave vulnerability rankings: Sustainability dimensions and urban vulnerability profiles
abstract: Heat vulnerability indices are widely used to rank urban areas, yet they provide limited information about how heat vulnerability is embedded into urban sustainability or why similar aggregate scores may reflect different component configurations. This study examines whether different sustainability dimensions are associated with heatwave vulnerability and identifies associated urban profiles across 72 Hungarian urban units: the 23 districts of Budapest and the 49 largest cities. title: Integrating tectonically guided fractured-rock groundwater exploration and community based governance for water security in Pakistan
abstract: Pakistan faces a growing water crisis driven by climate change, groundwater depletion, declining water quality, and increasing demand. We propose a hybrid framework that integrates regional structural geology with community-based water governance to improve long-term water security and climate resilience in the Indus River Basin. title: Early Maize Growth In Rhizoboxes Under Ageratum Conyzoides Leaf Extract And Chicken Manure
abstract: Maize requires adequate nutrients during vegetative growth, and organic fertilizers can serve as an alternative nutrient source to inorganic fertilizers. Babadotan (Ageratum conyzoides L.) leaves contain nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium and may therefore be used as a aqueous leaf extract. This study evaluated the effect of babadotan leaf extract and chicken manure on the vegetative growth of maize (Zea mays L.) grown in rhizoboxes. title: Biological Activities of the Endemic Plant Colchicum figlalii: Cytotoxic, Antioxidant, and Antimicrobial Properties
abstract: Throughout history, plants have been used in the treatment of various diseases, forming the foundation of traditional medicine and inspiring modern pharmaceutical research. Notably, Colchicum species, recognized for their therapeutic potential, represent an important group of plants evaluated in both traditional use and modern pharmacology. This study investigates the in vitro cytotoxic, antioxidant, and antimicrobial activities of the methanol extract of Colchicum figlalii, an endemic species found in Muğla, Türkiye. title: The Role of Information Technology in Revitalizing Afghanistan’s Position along the Historical and Modern Silk Road
abstract: Afghanistan sits where the northern, southern and western branches of the Silk Road once met, and for most of two thousand years that position paid for itself in trade, taxes and ideas.Today the country is landlocked, thinly connected digitally and exposed to border closures that can idle a corridor within days.This paper asks what information technology (IT) can realistically do to restore Afghanistan's role as a connector between Central, South and West Asia.The study combines a structured review of historical and economic literature, an examination of recent connectivity data, a three-layer

title: Recent Advances in Carbohydrate Polymer-Mediated Cancer Immunotherapy
abstract: Cancer immunotherapy has changed oncology by improving the immune system’s ability to recognize and destroy tumor cells. However, issues like immune suppression, ineffective drug targeting, and harmful side effects still limit its effectiveness. Carbohydrate polymers have emerged as promising materials for cancer immunotherapy due to their compatibility with the body, ability to break down naturally, ability to modify immune responses, and potential for targeted drug delivery. title: Lesion Profiles and Tissue Pathology of Clinostomum Metacercariae in Oreochromis niloticus From Lake Tana and An Adjacent Aquaculture Pond, Bahir Dar, Ethiopia
abstract: BACKGROUND: Oreochromis niloticus is the most commercially important and widely cultivated freshwater fish species in Ethiopia due to its rapid growth rate, adaptability to different environmental conditions, tolerance to handling stress and high nutritional value. However, infection with Clinostomum metacercariae (MC) is a major problem for both aquaculture and wild fish populations and poses a significant zoonotic risk to human health. abstract: ABSTRACT As of this writing, there are 4 years remaining for countries to reach their Sustainable Development Goals deadline of 2030 as agreed to by the member countries of the United Nations. Countries are, therefore, naturally interested in projections of progress toward these goals. A variety of statistical measures have been used to report on country‐level progress toward the goals, but they have not utilized methodologies explicitly designed to obtain optimally predictive measures of rate of change as the foundation for projecting trends. title: Identification of esculin as a direct modulator of IGF1 in cervical cancer with integrated computational and experimental studies
abstract: Aberrant activation of the insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) signaling axis plays a central role in tumor proliferation, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance. Although most therapeutic strategies have focused on inhibition of the IGF1 receptor (IGF1R), direct targeting of the IGF1 ligand remains largely underexplored. title: Effects of land‐use systems on macroaggregate pore structure, hydraulic conductivity, and physical protection capacity
abstract: Abstract Reclamation of saline–alkali land relies on salt leaching and restoring soil fertility. However, the micro‐scale pore‐architectural changes associated with different land‐use systems remain insufficiently characterized, particularly in relation to their potential implications for water transport and fertility retention. This study selected natural land‐use systems (wasteland [WL] and degraded grassland [GL]) and artificial land‐use systems (upland field [UF] and paddy field [PF]) in Jilin, China, and scanned 5–7 mm macroaggregates for computed tomography imaging. title: Skeletal Development During Metamorphosis of the Rice Field Frog Hoplobatrachus rugulosus (Wiegmann, 1834) (Anura: Dicroglossidae)
abstract: The rice field frog (Hoplobatrachus rugulosus) is an important native species in Southeast Asian agricultural wetlands and a major commodity in the aquaculture industry. Despite its ecological and economic importance, and its use as an animal model in various studies, detailed data regarding its skeletal ontogeny remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by presenting a comprehensive chronological atlas of osteogenesis for H. rugulosus from Gosner stages 28 to 46. title: Atomic-scale facet-defect coupling enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn 2 S 4 for reductive photocatalysis
abstract: Atomic-scale regulation of photogenerated electrons remains a central challenge in reductive photocatalysis because highly reductive electrons are intrinsically prone to rapid recombination and spatial delocalization. Although crystal-facet engineering and defect modulation have independently improved photocatalytic performance, their synergistic coupling in governing electron accumulation and carrier kinetics remains poorly understood. title: Evaluation of the DAT angle in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: A cross-sectional study
abstract: Introduction: Palmar dermatoglyphics serve as permanent biological records of genetic and prenatal developmental events. title: Predicting tree growth using light availability as an indicator of competition
abstract: Tree growth modelling and predictions are essential components of forest planning and ecological research. Airborne laser scanning data can provide detailed information about tree crowns, where primary photosynthesis happens. The aim of this study was to investigate, whether intercepted solar radiation received by tree crowns, modelled using drone-based Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) data, can be used as an indicator of competition in individual tree growth models instead of traditional competition variables such as basal area or basal area of larger trees. title: Effect of city site, size, and some meteorological factors on NO2 and O3 concentrations
abstract: This study compares the spatiotemporal behavior of NO2 and O3 in Baghdad and Mosul using 2022 monitoring data to assess the influence of meteorological factors. Baghdad recorded substantially higher annual NO2 concentrations (36.7 µg/m³) than Mosul (21.2 µg/m³), while Mosul exhibited higher annual O3 levels due to weaker NO-titration. Both cities frequently exceeded the WHO 8-hour O3 guideline. title: Financiamiento Popular y Solidario: Percepción y rol en el fortalecimiento emprendedor en Machala, Ecuador
abstract: El fortalecimiento del emprendimiento se ha convertido en un aspecto trascendente para el desarrollo socioeconómico en Ecuador. Este estudio se enfocó en analizar la incidencia del Sistema Financiero Popular y Solidario en la experiencia de crédito de emprendedores del cantón Machala-Ecuador. Se optó por un enfoque cuantitativo de alcance explicativo, recolectando los datos para el modelo logístico ordinal mediante una encuesta aplicada a 300 emprendedores, de este total solo 233 recibieron financiamiento procedente del Sistema. title: Slaves facing the Inquisition in the Crown of Aragón (1570-1660): crimes, repressive dynamics and defence strategies
abstract: This article analyses the encounters between enslaved individuals and the courts of the Inquisition in Barcelona and Valencia between 1570 and 1660. Through a systematic analysis of the case reports and the inquisitorial processes of the aforementioned courts on the aforementioned dates, we have established the ethno-cultural and demographic characteristics of the slaves prosecuted, their criminal patterns and the differences between them and those of the free population, as well as the strategies implemented by the enslaved individuals to defend themselves against the Holy Office. title: Actor-Network Dynamics in Cultural Development: Indigenous and Religious Leaders as Relational Nodes in Penginyongan Cultural Sustainability
abstract: Local cultures in Indonesia face growing pressure from globalization, modernization, and shifting orientations among younger generations, yet little is known about how relations among cultural actors keep these cultures alive. This study analyzes how networks of traditional (adat) and religious leaders develop and sustain Penginyongan culture in the Banyumas Raya region of Central Java, using Actor-Network Theory (ANT). title: DEVELOPMENT OF AN INTERACTIVE ETHNOMATHEMATICS-BASED E-LKPD ON MAGETAN LOCAL ARCHITECTURE TO IMPROVE UNDERSTANDING OF SOLID GEOMETRY CONCEPTS
abstract: Learning flat-sided solid geometry requires students to connect abstract mathematical concepts with visual representations and real-world objects. However, mathematics instruction at the junior high school level may still rely on conventional teaching methods, printed learning materials, and limited integration of local cultural contexts. This study aimed to develop and evaluate the validity, practicality, and effectiveness of an interactive mathematics electronic student worksheet (E-LKPD) based on the ethnomathematics of Magetan’s local architecture. title: Formal Total Synthesis of (±)‐Carexane L Enabled by a PPA‐Mediated Fragmentation–Cyclization Cascade and Heck Coupling
abstract: ABSTRACT We present a succinct formal total synthesis of the rearranged aromatic sesquiterpene (±)‐carexane L, an indanone‐based natural product derived from the roots of Carex distachya Desf., a species indigenous to the Mediterranean maquis, commencing from benzoic acid. The synthesis strategically employs a combination of one‐pot polyphosphoric acid (PPA)‐mediated cyclization and Heck cross‐coupling as pivotal reactions.

title: Event‐Scale Controls on Suspended Sediment–Discharge Hysteresis in an Agricultural Headwater Watershed of the Upper Blue Nile Basin, Ethiopia
abstract: ABSTRACT In rivers, suspended sediment concentration (SSC) may not respond instantly or proportionally to discharge (Q), peaking before or after peak Q during runoff events. In the Upper Blue Nile Basin, sediment load is highly episodic and storm‐driven, yet these dynamics remain poorly understood. This study characterizes SSC–Q hysteresis using 10 min–resolution hydrometric and sediment data from 48 events. title: Exploring the Structural Information Content of Super-Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons via Degree-Based Graph Entropies
abstract: Graph entropy is an information-theoretic measure that offers a compact, inexpensive description of the structural information content of a molecule. This study examines two super-polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons derived from hexa-peri-hexabenzocoronene, superphenalene and supertriphenylene .
