Genome and methylome of the root crop table beet (Beta vulgaris)
abstract: Abstract Table beet ( Beta vulgaris subsp. vulgaris var. vulgaris ), also known as red beet, garden beet, or beetroot, is an important crop with both nutritional and agricultural value, yet high-quality genomic resources for this taxon are limited. We present the chromosome-scale genome assembly RefTab-1 based on PacBio and Hi-C data of the inbred table beet genotype W357B. The assembly has a size of 668.6 Mbp and an N50 of 72 Mbp, with 96% of the assembly anchored to nine pseudo-chromosomes. title: Flood Risk in Critical Points of the City of Juliaca: Geospatial Analysis and Citizen Perception of Sustainable Drainage
abstract: Flood risk management in urban areas is crucial for mitigating the impacts of extreme weather events, yet the integration of geospatial analysis and citizen perception remains underexplored. In the city of Juliaca, Peru, this study aimed to assess flood hazards through spatial analysis and gauge public perception of sustainable drainage systems. Utilizing a combination of geospatial data, including terrain slope, NDWI from Sentinel2 imagery, geological maps, and projected precipitation under the SSP1-2.6 scenario, we delineated flood-prone areas across Juliaca's urban polygon. title: Comparative Analysis of Exonic SSR ‐Containing Genes in Three Diving Duck Species Reveals Shared Functional Themes
abstract: ABSTRACT Simple sequence repeats (SSRs) are ubiquitous components of eukaryotic genomes that contribute to genome evolution, genetic variation, and gene regulation. Although genome‐wide SSR landscapes have been extensively characterized across vertebrates, the cross‐species distribution and functional associations of exonic SSR‐containing genes remain poorly understood, particularly in non‐model birds. title: Developing a PBL-Based E-LKPD Integratung Local Temperature Data to Improve Global Warming Conceptual Understanding
abstract: This study aims to develop and examine the effect of using a Problem-Based Learning (PBL)-based E-LKPD integrated with temperature pattern changes on students conceptual understanding of global warming material. The research uses the Research and Development (R&D) method with the 4D model (define, design, develop, and disseminate), but is limited to the develop stage. abstract: Heat-damaged reinforced concrete members can continue their service after proper retrofit. In this investigation, the performance of heat-damaged RC beams retrofitted by different methods such as the use of FRP and steel plates has been experimentally investigated. Eleven reinforced concrete beams, including beams containing micro-silica (MS) and polypropylene fibers (PPF), have been made. title: Racial disparities in glucose sensor and insulin pump use and formal access through Brazil’s Unified Health System among people with type 1 diabetes: a cross-sectional study
abstract: AIMS: To evaluate racial disparities in glucose sensor and insulin pump use among people with type 1 diabetes in Brazil and associations of race/skin color with formal requests and approvals through the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS). METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 2454 adults with type 1 diabetes or caregivers of children and adolescents. title: Autonomous top-perching with an asymmetric bistable claw
abstract: Long-duration in situ observation in constrained natural environments (e.g., caves and dense arboreal canopies) is crucial for ecological monitoring. While unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) provide cross-terrain access, their operational feasibility is limited by substantial power demands and acoustic disturbance from sustained hovering. Here, we present an autonomous top-perching UAV system that leverages overhead structures for stable suspension and enhanced adaptability in confined spaces. title: Temporal controls on fluid–rock interaction in the evolution of the Abovyan iron oxide–apatite deposit, Armenia
abstract: Iron oxide–apatite (IOA) deposits are globally significant sources of Fe, P, and Rare Earth Elements (REEs). Although input of hydrothermal processes into their origin is acknowledged, direct temporal constraints on the duration and style of their hydrothermal evolution remain scarce. The Abovyan deposit in central Armenia, hosted by late Miocene andesites, is one of the youngest known IOA systems worldwide and the only example in the Lesser Caucasus, providing a rare opportunity to address this problem. title: Disease burden of rotavirus infection and its complications among children under 14 years old with acute gastroenteritis in China: a multicentre and retrospective study
abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the positivity rate, disease burden, and complications of rotavirus gastroenteritis (RVGE) among Chinese children under 14 years of age presenting with acute gastroenteritis (AGE). METHODS: A multicentre, observational, and retrospective study was conducted at 11 centres across China (July 2013 - June 2023). abstract: The research analyses the production and distribution of ceramics from the Kietrz 7 site, a cemetery dating back to phase C of the Roman Period, located in the Kietrz/Nowa Cerekwia micro-region in Upper Silesia, Poland. The Kietrz 7 site is distinguished by the fact that approximately 20% of the vessels are wheel-thrown. title: Hierarchical hollow carbon spheres as advanced flow electrodes for high-efficiency capacitive desalination
abstract: Flow-electrode capacitive deionization (FCDI) has emerged as an intriguing desalination technology. However, the performance of FCDI is fundamentally limited by the transport properties of the flow-electrode materials. In this study, hierarchical hollow carbon nanospheres (HCNSs) were evaluated as advanced flow-electrode materials for FCDI. abstract: Abstract HFO-1336mzz(E) is a novel environmentally friendly insulating gas with a low global warming potential and favorable dielectric properties, and it has been regarded as an important potential substitute for sulfur hexafluoride (SF6). However, its systemic toxicological characteristics and underlying mechanisms under inhalation exposure remain insufficiently investigated. abstract: are mixed feeders that browse and graze, with woody vegetation contributing substantially to free-roaming diets. title: Large-eddy simulation and time-lagged correlation analysis of aerodynamic interference between tandem 4:1 rectangular cylinders at various spacings
abstract: Large-eddy simulation is applied to study the flow around two tandem 4:1 rectangular cylinders at a Reynolds number of 1.1 × 104 and four gap ratios of 0.4, 1.0, 2.0, and 4.0. The inter-cylinder aerodynamic coupling is measured by time-lagged correlation analysis. title: A dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle delivery system for precision phage therapy against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria
abstract: The escalating crisis of antimicrobial resistance, particularly among Gram-negative bacteria, demands innovative therapeutic strategies. Here, we present a dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle-chimeric phage (AbLCP) system engineered to combat multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacteria. title: Efficacy of ozone nanobubble treatment for controlling Listeria monocytogenes biofilms on food-contact surfaces
abstract: Listeria monocytogenes biofilms on food-contact surfaces pose a persistent contamination risk in fresh produce packing and processing environments. This study evaluated the efficacy of ozone nanobubble (ONB) treatment against L. monocytogenes biofilms formed on stainless steel (SS), polyester (PET), and rubber surfaces. abstract: All-solid-waste cementitious materials (ACMs) represent a promising pathway for the sustainable and high-value engineering application of solid waste. title: Gamma irradiation-induced modification of B4C reinforcement for controlling microstructure and mechanical–corrosion behavior of Al/B4C composites
abstract: This study investigates gamma irradiation-induced modification of B 4 C reinforcement and its effect on the microstructure, mechanical properties, and electrochemical corrosion behavior of Al/B 4 C composites. B 4 C micropowders irradiated at 50, 100, and 150 kGy were incorporated into aluminum sheets through accumulative roll bonding. title: Quicklime plus humic acid improves rice yield and starch pasting properties on acidified paddy soil in association with prolonged inferior-grain filling and phytohormone changes
abstract: Soil acidification constrains rice yield and grain quality in southern China, yet how acidity amelioration affects the filling of inferior grains (IG), and the associated hormonal and starch-quality traits, remains unclear. A two-year field experiment on an acidified Red-yellow soil (pH 5.19) compared farmer conventional fertilization (FCF), quicklime (QL), and quicklime plus a humic acid soil conditioner (HA). title: RESILIENT HYBRID RADIO COMMUNICATION NETWORK USING RADIO RELAY LINKS AND TROPOSCATTER LINKS WITH FAILOVER MECHANISMS
abstract: The paper presents the design and simulation of a hybrid microwave radio communication network based on the integration of radio relay and troposcatter links, aimed at ensuring communication continuity under various propagation conditions. Radio relay systems provide high capacity and low latency but require line-of-sight (LoS), while troposcatter links enable long-distance communication without LoS, at the cost of lower capacity. title: Disruption of arn lipid A aminoarabinosylation confers AmpCmediated cephalosporin resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance in chronic cystic fibrosis infections caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa is shaped by pathogen-specific adaptation, yet the mechanisms driving cephalosporin resistance in epidemic clinical lineages remain incompletely defined. abstract: Abstract During high rainfall events, one reason for flooding in urban rivers is hydraulic blockages or obstructions in channels. These may cause damming and an immediate increase in upstream water levels, leading to inundation of surroundings. The accuracy of flood models is strongly dependent on the representation of the topography of floodplain and river geometry, so incorporation of such blockages and obstructions in rivers' model geometry needs to be taken into account. title: Using brewing industry byproducts to create feed additives for aquaculture-raised rainbow trout under thermal stress
abstract: The aquaculture industry helps meet the seafood demands of a rapidly growing human population. The goal of this study was to determine the effects of feed additives, generated from byproducts of the beer brewing industry, on the growth rate, production parameters, and intestinal bacterial composition of aquaculture-raised rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss). abstract: This study investigates the global (GSV) and local (LSV) structural vibration behavior of hollow steel monopiles embedded in soil. abstract: ABSTRACT Contact‐electro‐catalysis (CEC) is an emerging mechanically driven strategy that facilitates chemical reactions through contact electrification and charge transfer at solid–liquid or liquid–liquid interfaces. abstract: Population structure and environmental features often capture major axes of genetic variation in many species. Yet the impacts of human activity often remain unquantified. Maize is a staple crop of enormous cultural importance to indigenous peoples of the Americas, but cannot survive or disperse without farmers. abstract: ABSTRACT Following a tick bite, Borrelia burgdorferi spirochetes replicate in human skin and disseminate through tissues, including subcutaneous adipose tissue. Adipose is a complex organ containing both immune and non-immune cells that play a significant role in the immune response, yet little is known about adipose-specific immune signaling after B. burgdorferi infection. Herbivorous insects are expected to respond both to direct climatic constraints and to bottom‐up regulation mediated through host‐plant diversity, yet the relative importance of these pathways at continental scales remains unresolved. abstract: This article explores how the strategic culture prevalent among member states can enable or hinder regional organisations, extending strategic culture analysis beyond the level of state behaviour to institutionalised multilateral cooperation. title: Fire history and atmospheric drying jointly control forest reburn severity
abstract: Abstract Background Wildfire activity is increasing across western United States forests, leading to more frequent reburns, or areas that burn multiple times within short intervals (approximately two decades). Prior fire can reduce subsequent burn severity through fuel limitation, but this effect is not consistent across landscapes or climate conditions. abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are ideal for precious metal recovery due to their high surface areas and tunable binding sites. abstract: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), inherited maternally and without recombination, is crucial for tracing maternal lineages and studying population history. title: More rainy days at Science Garden station, Metro Manila, Philippines, 1961–2025
abstract: Abstract Daily rainfall at Science Garden, Quezon City, Philippines, was analysed for 1961–2025. abstract: Abstract Sustainable energy trajectories evolve through processes of knowledge accumulation and recombination within the same trajectory and hybridization between several of them. abstract: Fire is a key disturbance in forests around the globe. Fire shapes the structure in forests that provide essential habitat for wildlife. The post fire recovery of forests have often been characterised as a function of time since fire, overlooking the influence of additional fire characteristics, and post-fire environmental conditions. This knowledge is vital to support wildlife conservation under rapidly changing fire regimes arising from climatic extremes. title: Strategic Management of Health Tourism in India: Opportunities and Challenges in Telangana
abstract: Medical tourism is a strategic growth sector in India, with foreign visitors for treatment in 2025 at 507,244, and the market is expected to grow from USD 8.7 billion to USD 16.2 billion by 2030. With Hyderabad's recognized hospitals and exemplary aviation connectivity, Telangana, with its vision of creating a regional hub under the Telangana Tourism Policy 2025-30, has set its sights on becoming a regional hub. abstract: The study of the degradation of archaeological objects is essential for guiding their conservation and restoration, alongside understanding possible formal and aesthetic changes that may have occurred since their burial. Several difficulties hinder these studies as numerous factors, both intrinsic and extrinsic, are involved in the degradation processes. In the present work, we focused on a group of representative green and honeydew transparent glazed fragments from Pamela Castle, dated between the 9th and 11th centuries. title: Decoding cryptic diversity of moss populations in a forest-tundra ecotone
abstract: ABSTRACT Cryptic speciation is widespread among bryophytes, and it appears common in arctic and subarctic mosses where cryptic lineages may occur sympatrically in the environment. However, cryptic lineages are rarely considered in genetic diversity assessments. This situation poses a challenge, as the complex population structure resulting from cryptic speciation, along with factors like the predominance of clonality, can lead to inaccurate estimates of biodiversity. title: A cross-cultural study of harbour scene paintings of the Thirteen Factories in Guangzhou from 1760 to 1860
abstract: During the Canton System, the Thirteen Factories in Guangzhou formed a cross‑cultural visual field in which Harbor Scene Paintings (HSPs) served as both commodities and sites of Sino-Western visual negotiation. Drawing on visual culture studies and the pictorial turn, this study constructs a comparative cross‑cultural visual analysis framework. title: Friction surfacing of Al2O3 reinforced aluminium coatings on low carbon steel with microstructural and tribological characterization
abstract: Friction surfacing (FS) was employed to create Al–7.5 wt% Al 2 O 3 metal matrix composite coatings on low carbon steel (AISI 1018), enhancing surface performance by solid-state processing. Two parameter sets were examined to identify their effects on coating microstructure and tribology. title: Curing-state-dependent rheology governs electrospinning of silicone elastomers for hydrophobic surface coatings
abstract: Fibrosis around cochlear implant electrode arrays increases impedance and disrupts predictable stimulus propagation. Electrospun hydrophobic silicone coatings represent a promising strategy to mitigate fibrosis. However, electrospinning silicone elastomers remains challenging because their low glass transition temperature causes deposited fibers to collapse before curing is complete. Previous approaches have focused on developing in situ curing systems, such as heated collectors. Although fiber-like structures have been generated, nonwovens with interconnected pores have not yet been achieved.

abstract: Background The relationship between polymyxin B (PMB) concentrations in alveolar epithelial lining fluid (ELF) and pathogen clearance in carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacilli (CRGNB) pneumonia remains unclear. abstract: ABSTRACT The development of multifunctional hydrogels combining mechanical robustness, autonomous self‐healing, electrical conductivity, and stimuli responsiveness remains challenging. title: When seeds change hands: gender, intersectionality, and access to seed in rural Senegal
abstract: Abstract Despite advances in understanding seed circulation in rural communities, little is known about the gendered and intersectional power relations that shape farmers’ access to seed. Based on a case study in a Bassari community of southeastern Senegal, we examine the roles of women and men in seed circulation and explore who maintains and who controls access to seed for six staple crops. abstract: The disposal of chrysotile asbestos waste poses significant environmental hazards, while heavy oil residues demand costly pretreatment to remove toxic metals and sulfur. This study presents a circular economy approach to convert acid-leached chrysotile asbestos waste into a functional chemisorbent for the simultaneous demetallization and desulfurization of heavy petroleum residues. abstract: Abstract Voucher specimens are central to studying threatened taxa. However, errors in their locality data can distort understandings of these species’ distributions, and in extreme cases may even misguide assessments of species’ conservation statuses. The Perth slider, Lerista lineata , represents an informative exemplar of this situation. abstract: ABSTRACT Modulating the electronic structure and interfacial wettability of cathode catalysts is crucial for enhancing intrinsic activity and broadening triple‐phase interfaces for oxygen reduction reactions (ORR) in zinc−air batteries (ZABs), yet achieving their synergistic regulation faces a big challenge. abstract: Classical Differential Evolution (DE) solves the Multi-Depot Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (MDVRPTW) efficiently but struggles to maintain time-window feasibility. abstract: Redox conditions strongly influence mantle phase equilibria and arc magmatism, yet the processes driving elevated oxygen fugacity ( f O 2 ) in subarc mantle remain unresolved. title: Caco-2-derived spheroids and organ-on-a-chip for food safety risk assessment: mechanisms of intestinal inflammation induced by 20 nm polystyrene nanoplastics
abstract: Microplastics released from food packaging have become an emerging food safety concern and may contribute to intestinal inflammation. This study employed Caco-2-derived spheroids combined with self-developed microfluidic organ-on-a-chip technology to systematically investigate the effects of 20 nm polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) on oxidative stress and functional homeostasis in the three-dimensional (3D) intestinal epithelial microenvironment. title: Creatio ex nihilo, ordenación del caos y la teoría de la información en Génesis 1
abstract: Partiendo de una visión ontológico-teológica de la creatio ex nihilo, se aborda la creación en Génesis 1 como la ordenación de un caos que también depende ontológicamente de Dios. Se argumenta que la información es crucial en el proceso creador, con la palabra divina como fuente de información constituyente. Para ello se muestra que la estructura del relato sacerdotal de la creación presenta la palabra divina como principio organizador del espacio, el tiempo y la vida. Se hace notar también cómo el ser humano, creado a imagen de Dios, tiene la tarea de mantener el orden.

title: The origin of Group B Streptococcus in Australian dogs, cats and cows
abstract: Streptococcus agalactiae, known in human medicine as Group B Streptococcus (GBS), affects numerous animal species, including dairy cattle and companion animals such as dogs and cats. In cattle, where GBS is a common cause of mastitis, host-specialist and host-generalist clades have been detected, whereas data on the origin of companion animal GBS is limited and somewhat contradictory. abstract: ABSTRACT This study aimed to characterize the chemical constituents of the methanolic extract of Euphorbia anacampseros using high‐performance liquid chromatography (HPLC–DAD) and gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) analyses. The cytotoxic activity of the extract was assessed using the MTT assay, and its light‐enhanced cytotoxic effects were evaluated to investigate its potential for future photodynamic applications. abstract: Despite their distinct geographic origins, specific meat quality variations between Seduogangjian (SD) and Shenzha (SZ) Tibetan sheep remain unclear. We hypothesized that these distinct cohorts exhibit differences in muscle fiber architecture and lipid metabolism, ultimately contributing to variations in their meat quality and flavor profiles. abstract: Unaccompanied refugee adolescents in Europe experience high levels of distress, yet little is known about how adolescent boys navigate this already challenging life stage during migration transit, which involve long periods of uncertainty and family separation. This qualitative study examines how unaccompanied refugee boys (ages 13-17) in Greece cope with stress and prolonged uncertainty. title: Staphylococcus aureus coagulases increase survival of Pseudomonas aeruginosa during coinfection
abstract: Polymicrobial infections involving Staphylococcus aureus are often more severe than single-species infections. S. aureus typically initiates the infection, creating conditions that allow secondary pathogens like Pseudomonas aeruginosa to establish. abstract: Efficient pH-universal hydrogen evolution catalysts with low noble-metal loading are highly desirable for scalable water electrolysis. Nevertheless, most existing crystalline and amorphous materials fail to achieve favorable activity, stability, and pH universality. abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising pressure-responsive luminescent materials, but precise control of their emission under pressure remains a substantial challenge. Here, we engineered the piezofluorochromic response of zirconium-based MOFs by tuning the polarity of the emissive moieties through noncoordinating phenyl substituents. abstract: Salmonella is a pathogen that causes gastrointestinal illness in consumers. Animal protection regulations are frequently disregarded by certain local populations, and the microbial risks associated with their consumption make this practice a serious public health concern. abstract: INTRODUCTION: Invasive aspergillosis (IA) represents one of the most frequent invasive fungal infections in paediatric patients with risk factors. abstract: As data becomes an increasingly important production factor in the digital economy, its role in shaping environmental outcomes has attracted growing attention. This study examines how data factor marketization affects urban ecological resilience. abstract: Cinnamomum spp. has been used as a spice and a flavoring agent for centuries. title: Residual error modelling for process-based flood frequency analysis
abstract: Flood frequency analysis (FFA) is essential for flood risk management and infrastructure design, yet the uncertainty associated with flood quantile estimates is often poorly characterized or disregarded—especially under data-scarce conditions. Existing uncertainty quantification methods are frequently subjective, overly complex, or impractical for routine engineering use. abstract: The study explores the impact of climate change and variability on pesticide usage for rice production in Zanzibar. The study used anecdotal data from interviewer responses, climate datasets from the Tanzania Meteorological Authority (TMA), while rice production records (in tones) and pesticide (in liters) data were acquired from Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Natural Resources. abstract: This work investigated incorporating Cd into sulphurated ZnAl layered double hydroxide (LDH)-derived materials, then using them as photocatalysts for hydrogen production. abstract: Agricultural communities in the Culiacán Valley live next to intensively farmed fields, which raises questions about how residents perceive environmental risk and how they relate to their community. Using the preliminary data cut from the pilot survey of project FZ-HAB-0032 on the Factoriza UAS platform, this study described the initial behaviour of a ten-item scale with two dimensions, Environmental concern in the community and Community attachment, among residents of agricultural communities in the Culiacán Valley. title: Effects of vermicompost and mycorrhiza on summer savory growth and nutrition
abstract: Abstract Vermicompost and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) are sustainable soil amendments that can improve crop productivity and nutrient‐use efficiency under organic farming systems. This study evaluated the independent and combined effects of vermicompost and AMF on growth, yield, and foliar nutrient status of summer savory ( Satureja hortensis L.) under organic field conditions. abstract: Background Non-target screening by LC-HRMS is increasingly used to investigate complex environmental samples, but its reliability strongly depends on data-processing parameters and on the ability to distinguish chemically meaningful signals from noise, blank-related features and poorly resolved chromatographic contributions. title: Spotted Patterns of Glass Frogs Can Disguise Imperfections in Transparency to Improve Camouflage
abstract: Transparency could be considered the idealized version of camouflage, capable of producing effective concealment across heterogeneous habitats. However, although examples of highly transparent species do exist, 'transparent' species are highly variable and are often either only partially transparent or better described as translucent. Exactly how these different forms of 'imperfect' transparency may act as camouflage remains largely unknown. title: The state of leprosy: increasing trends of Hansen’s disease in Florida, USA, 1996–2025
abstract: Leprosy, also known as Hansen´s disease (HD), is a chronic infectious disease which mainly affects the skin, the peripheral nerves, mucosa of the upper respiratory tract, and the eyes. According to the National Hansen's Disease Program (NHDP), there were 225 new cases of leprosy reported in the United States of America (USA) in 2023, with Florida ranking as one of the top reporting states. title: Assessment of genetic variability in indigenous rice germplasm based on morphological traits
abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) is one of the most important staple food crops worldwide and serves as a major source of calories for a large proportion of the global population. Indigenous rice germplasm represents an important reservoir of genetic diversity containing valuable traits associated with grain yield, grain quality, biotic and abiotic stress tolerance, and environmental adaptation. title: Fractionation of Terminalia mantaly stem bark extract enhanced antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and antioxidant activities: In vitro and multi-target in silico evaluation
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance remains a significant global threat, leading to a high mortality rate and the need for alternative treatments. This study aimed to determine the antimicrobial and antioxidant properties of liquid-liquid fractions from Terminalia mantaly stem bark extract and to investigate their potential multi-target interactions using in silico approaches. abstract: Abstract In this study, an original and simple method was employed to modify polyacrylamide (PAm) with sodium phosphate (Na₃PO₄), yielding a sodium phosphate-modified polyacrylamide hydrogel (PAm@P) with promising swelling and adsorption properties compared to pristine, unmodified polyacrylamide. abstract: Abstract Slide-ring gels are innovative materials characterized by their unique mechanical interlocking structures, where sliding rings, acting also as cross-linking points, are threaded onto a backbone chain, forming a dynamic and adaptable network with distinctive mechanical behaviors. abstract: Particulate matter (PM) can interact with environmental factors, contributing to the chemical and physical degradation of cultural heritage materials. Although the influence of PM on polymeric materials has been widely reported-often linked to degradation in both functional and aesthetic properties-its specific impact on chemical stability remains insufficiently explored, necessitating further study to elucidate potential implications. abstract: Background and Aims: Plant–soil feedbacks and their underlying mechanisms have received renewed interest in the light of climate change. Soil microbial communities mediate a variety of important functions for plant health, but whether these interrelationships will persist under sustained warming remains an open question. We investigated whether soil microbial communities influence the health of plants in increasingly warmer temperatures. title: Dung beetle-mediated dung incorporation reveals hidden effects of veterinary drug residues on soil chemical attributes
abstract: Dung beetles are key drivers of nutrient cycling in livestock systems, yet the ecological consequences of veterinary drug residues for their soil-building functions remain poorly understood. Here, we evaluated how dung incorporation by the dung beetle Dichotomius bos affects soil chemical attributes, and whether residues of ivermectin or levamisole in cattle dung modify these responses. title: METTL3-mediated m 6 A modification of DNMT1 enhances ovarian cancer progression
abstract: Abstract High-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC), the most lethal subtype of ovarian cancer, is often diagnosed at advanced stages owing to its asymptomatic progression and lack of early detection markers. In this study, we identified a critical oncogenic role of the RNA methyltransferase METTL3 and the N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) RNA modification pathway in HGSC. title: Characterization of corynacin K411, a leaderless bacteriocin from Corynebacterium jeikeium
abstract: Abstract Bacteriocins are ribosomally synthesized antimicrobial peptides that are emerging as natural preservatives and alternatives to conventional antibiotics in response to the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance. title: Turning Palmaria palmata into a natural food colorant: Integrated downstream processing and spray drying optimization of R-phycoerythrin
abstract: R-phycoerythrin (RPE) from Palmaria palmata is a natural pink-red protein pigment with promising potential as a natural colorant. While being considered a more sustainable ingredient, its industrial implementation remains limited by costly, processing-intensive purification and stability challenges. abstract: Background Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) have been increasingly associated with liver injury in human populations, raising concerns about their potential health effects; however, the relationship between PFAS exposure and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains inconsistent. abstract: Abstract: Ungulates play a vital role in maintaining the integrity of the high mountain ecosystem by sustaining plant community structure and regulating predator populations. title: The Unequal Paths of Progress: Intergenerational Occupational and Wealth Mobility in Rural Spain (1850-1936)
abstract: This article examines intergenerational occupational and wealth mobility in rural Spain between 1850 and 1936, a period of major structural change. Using linked household censuses and wealth tax records from La Mancha, the study uses transition matrices, intergenerational elasticities, and halving-time estimates to trace long-run mobility dynamics. abstract: This article proposes socio-techno-ecological imaginaries (STEI) as a conceptual extension of sociotechnical imaginaries (STI). While STI has been valuable for showing how social order and technological change co-produce “desirable futures,” we argue it tends to leave implicit how visions of ecology – beliefs about what nature is and acts, how it is valued, and how humans ought to relate to it – are entangled in this process. title: From Vulnerability to Resilience: Assessing Africa’s Climate Adaptation Strategies Under the Paris Agreement
abstract: Africa remains one of the regions most vulnerable to climate change despite contributing a relatively small share of global greenhouse gas emissions. abstract: This paper analyzes critically two graphical methods of representing sampled signals, which are exploited in the literature. abstract: Antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in lake ecosystems with salinization remain insufficiently understood, particularly with respect to water-sediment differentiation. abstract: Carbapenems are last-resort antibiotics used to treat severe infections caused by multidrug-resistant bacteria. abstract: This trial explored how dietary pre-feeding SFA/MUFA ratios regulate low-FO finishing efficiency in Yellow River carp ( Cyprinus carpio haematopterus ). Four isonitrogenous and isolipidic diets (soybean oil control SO, mixed-oil BO1.0/1.5/2.0 with SFA/MUFA 1.0/1.5/2.0) were used for an 8-week pre-feeding, followed by a 4-week uniform low-FO finishing for all groups. Pre-feeding showed no intergroup differences in carp growth and morphological indices, but BO1.5 and BO2.0 had lower muscle crude lipid, and BO1.5 had higher ash than SO. title: Fungal Launchers: The Biophysics of Active Fungal Spore Discharge
abstract: Energy-powered spore-launching strategy is an evolved feature of many fungal species, facilitating dispersal into the surrounding environment, thereby contributing to reproductive success and completing their life cycle. With a focus on the underlying biophysical principles and their broader implications for fungal ecology, this review explores current knowledge of spore discharge biomechanics across different fungal groups. abstract: Abstract Environmental pollution poses a growing threat to male reproductive health. Mono-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (MEHP), a pervasive plasticizer metabolite, is known to disrupt male reproductive function through oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have attracted significant interest as therapeutic biomolecules due to their low immunogenicity and ability to cross biological barriers. abstract: Abstract This study presents multi-epoch photometry from the Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer to investigate variability in white dwarf debris disks, utilizing the full 14.5 yr mission datasets pre- and post-cryogen. abstract: BACKGROUND: Measles remains a major public health concern in Nigeria, contributing disproportionately to the global burden. abstract: Abscisic acid (ABA) plays a critical role in plant immune responses. The 9-cis-epoxy-carotenoid dioxygenase ( NCED ) gene family encodes pivotal rate-limiting enzymes in ABA biosynthesis. abstract: This research paper explores the connection between urban form, pedestrians’ movement, diversification of the land use, the public realm and human activity on Church Street and MG Road in Bengaluru’s Central Business District. The study focuses on the impact of street connectivity, commercial use of the area, the quality of public realm, and place identity on urban life. abstract: Clostridium perfringens (CP) can proliferate in the bovine intestine after disruption of intestinal homeostasis and cause toxin-associated disease. This study clarifies acidity accumulation under limited water exchange by integrating field monitoring, hydrodynamic–tracer simulation, and a soil-column experiment reproducing tidal cycling in paddy soils. title: Life cycle assessment of iRE-SOLVE process for the pre-disposal management of spent ion-exchange resins
abstract: The management of radioactive spent ion-exchange resins (SIERs) lacks universally adopted technologies and environmental impact data. This study applies the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methodology to the patented iRE-SOLVE process for SIER treatment and conditioning, restricting the boundaries to the process itself and primary reagent production. Results show that the most significant environmental impacts stem from the large consumption of H 2 O 2 and NaOH, guiding future R&D optimization. title: Estimating soil water retention curves from co‐located in situ water content and matric potential sensors
abstract: Abstract The soil water retention curve (SWRC) governs water storage and redistribution in the vadose zone and is a key input for hydrologic and agroecosystem models. Laboratory evaporation methods provide high‐quality SWRCs but are destructive and represent static conditions that may not reflect in situ soil behavior under natural field conditions. Co‐located field sensors measuring volumetric water content ( θ ) and matric potential ( h ) offer a continuous, nondestructive alternative for estimating field‐based SWRCs. abstract: While previous research has identified accessibility barriers and recommended inclusive communication practices, less attention has been given to explaining the underlying principles that make risk communication accessible. This study sought to develop a conceptual understanding of accessible emergency communication to inform the design of more inclusive communication systems. abstract: Wild edible fruits are not considered popular food despite their high nutraceutical potential. Artocarpus lakoocha Roxb., belonging to the family Moraceae, is commonly used as a fodder plant in Nepal, and its fruit is consumed locally. The present research investigates the nutraceutical potential of A. lakoocha ripe fruit. abstract: Habitat degradation is one of the primary drivers of biodiversity loss and ecosystem alteration. In streams, leaf litter decomposition plays a key role in energy and nutrient cycling, which is influenced by leaf litter quality, microbial and invertebrate consumers, and environmental conditions. Land use changes alter stream habitats and can modify decomposition rates and dynamics, but large-scale assessments of these anthropogenic impacts remain limited. abstract: Dewatered sludge is the residual solid remaining after moisture is removed from wastewater treatment plants. Sludge pH ranged from slightly acidic to alkaline (6.43–8.13). abstract: ABSTRACT Invasive bullheads of the genus Ameiurus are actively expanding across Eastern Europe, yet accurate species identification remains problematic owing to phenotypic plasticity and high intraspecific morphological variability. This study aims to resolve the taxonomic identity, spatial distribution, and invasion dynamics of Ameiurus populations within the Dnipro River catchment, Ukraine, where mapping the current frontiers of these non‐native species is critical for freshwater conservation. abstract: Sparse and spatially biased occurrence records complicate survey planning for freshwater invertebrates. abstract: Antimicrobial-resistant infections are rising globally, with synanthropic pests such as cockroaches facilitating spread through food and environmental contamination in urban low-resource settings. Despite their close association with human habitats, cockroaches remain an underestimated vector in AMR transmission. This study investigated the abundance and antibiotic resistance profiles of Enterobacteriaceae isolated from the gut of the domestic cockroach ( Periplaneta americana ) in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. abstract: Abstract Decarbonising the hard-to-abate maritime and aviation transport sectors will be challenging. While alternative renewable fuels, such as biofuels and E-fuels, show promising potential for substituting traditional fossil fuels, they carry challenges regarding the required expansion of variable renewable energy (VRE) and the availability of sustainable biomass. abstract: Agroforestry is increasingly recognized as a nature-based solution (NbS) to interconnected global and local challenges, including climate change, land degradation, biodiversity loss, and livelihood insecurity. By integrating trees with crops and livestock, agroforestry enhances ecosystem services such as carbon sequestration, biodiversity conservation, and soil fertility, and diversifies farm income. abstract: Brinjal (Solanum melongena L.) requires considerable soil moisture throughout its life cycle, therefore, its cultivation in water constraint area is difficult. abstract: This study aims to analyze the environmental-concern campaign strategy developed by the D’Bone Collector Museum in Davao City, Mindanao, Philippines, through its museum collections, storytelling, and exhibition design. The study employed a qualitative approach with a single-case study design. abstract: Monkeypox virus (MPXV) continues to emerge as a global health threat. While genetically diverse, its genomic structure and evolution remain undercharacterized. abstract: Sustainable and quality papaya production faces challenges, especially under the unstable tropical summer agroecosystems. However, biostimulants offer a promising approach to improve crop performance, even under unfavorable conditions. Therefore, the study explored the effects of chitosan and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia on papaya productivity and fruit quality under tropical conditions. abstract: Migrating cancer cells release diverse extracellular vesicles (EVs) that carry cargo capable of influencing tumour progression and intercellular communication. abstract: Abstract Can Saudi Arabia use its financial system to build durable industries outside of the energy sector? abstract: The rapid expansion of digital infrastructure intensifies the environmental burden of data centers through high energy consumption, freshwater depletion, land-use change, and waste heat emission. Conventional sustainability strategies focusing on efficiency and carbon offsets prove insufficient to address these escalating ecological challenges. abstract: Indramayu Regency in West Java, Indonesia, persistently records the highest poverty rate in the province. abstract: Rechargeable lithium-ion batteries (LiBs) are central to the clean energy transition, but their production, use, and disposal may introduce contaminants into drinking water systems. abstract: ABSTRACT This article critically examines INDIAsize—an Indian government–funded anthropometric initiative to “decolonize” body size standards used in clothing production. abstract: Oral nicotine pouch (ONP) use has increased in recent years due to the perception that these products are a safer alternative to combustible tobacco products. abstract: OBJECTIVE: Deep brain stimulation of the superolateral branch of the medial forebrain bundle (slMFB-DBS) has shown promising therapeutic effects in treatment-resistant depression and obsessive-compulsive disorder. Here, we explore for the first time the electrophysiological connectivity between the stimulation target and cortical sites in humans. METHODS: Electrophysiological responses to single slMFB-DBS pulses were mapped in 7 patients using epidural electrocorticography (ECoG; n = 4) or high-density electroencephalography (EEG; n = 3) over 11 sessions. title: Organomineral fertilization with sewage sludge on the production and nutrient accumulation in Urochloa brizantha cv. Paiaguás
abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the effects of sewage-sludge-based organomineral fertilizers, produced using different technologies, as a sustainable alternative to mineral fertilization for biomass production and nutrient accumulation in Urochloa brizantha cv. BRS Paiaguás. The experiment was conducted for 120 days in a greenhouse under a randomized block design with four replicates. Treatments included mineral fertilizer (NPK), granulated biochar (GB), powdered biochar (PB), granulated composted sludge (GS), powdered composted sludge (PS), and a control (Test) without fertilization. title: Environmental life cycle assessment of forestry biochar for low-carbon concrete: influence of biogenic carbon accounting
abstract: Abstract As global interest grows in innovative and sustainable uses of biomass, understanding the environmental implications of integrating timber-derived biochar into concrete is increasingly important. This study presents a cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA) of biochar production and its application as a 15% sand replacement in 32 MPa concrete, evaluating four portable biochar production systems, the 6050 Carbonator, Air Curtain Burner, Oregon Kiln, and Biochar Systems Incorporated, using feedstocks sourced from forest residues and plantation-derived timber. title: Rebalancing Taxing Powers in Nigeria: The Case of Rivers State
abstract: This article critically investigates the constitutional, statutory, institutional, and fiscal arrangements governing the allocation and exercise of taxing powers in Nigeria, focusing on the position of Rivers State within Nigeria’s federal structure. title: The subcommissural organ secretes SCO-spondin, associated with stress response and mood
abstract: The subcommissural organ (SCO) is an evolutionarily conserved structure in the brains of vertebrates, but its function remains largely unknown. The protein SCO-spondin, exclusively produced by the SCO, may hold the key to understanding its function. Here, by whole exome sequencing of a family with schizoaffective disorder, we identified a protein-truncating variant (PTV) mutation in the SCO-spondin gene ( SSPOP ) segregating with this disease. To explore the potential role of this gene in this mood disorder, we generated a mouse model carrying this mutation in the SCO-spondin gene ( Sspo ). We

title: Impact of Policies on the Development of Geothermal Industry in China: An Empirical Analysis of Panel Data
abstract: ABSTRACT Geothermal energy is a clean, low‐carbon, widely distributed, abundant, safe and high‐quality renewable energy. According to a survey of China's geothermal resources, China's annual recoverable geothermal energy resources are equivalent to 2.6 billion tons of standard coal and thus have great development and utilization potential. Using geothermal energy to realize clean heating is highly important for achieving the goals of peak carbon and carbon neutrality. title: The Impact of Ants and Vertebrate Predators on Arthropods and Plants: A Meta‐Analysis
abstract: The trophic interactions between plants, insect herbivores and their predators are complex and prone to trophic cascades. Theory predicts that predators increase plant biomass by feeding on herbivores. However, it remains unclear whether different types of predators regulate herbivores to the same degree, and how intraguild predation impacts these trophic interactions. Specifically, we lack a more comprehensive view of the effects of various groups of predators on a global scale. Czech Academy of Sciences, Biology Centre

title: Three New Species of Thelymitra (Diurideae, Orchidaceae) Endemic to Aotearoa New Zealand
abstract: Abstract Three new species of sun orchid ( Thelymitra ) endemic to Aotearoa New Zealand are here described: T. palustris , T. scabrifolia and T. semaphora . The morphological distinctiveness of these three species has been acknowledged for decades; however, their taxonomic status has remained unresolved. Evidence from existing karyological data, recently generated DNA sequence data ( LFY and ycf 1) and morphological studies from historical and fresh collections are used here to support their formal description. Both T. palustris and T. semaphora are restricted to wet habitats north of Auckland

title: Interseccións posthumanas entre Mal Mor, de Emilio Araúxo, e Ill Seen Ill Said, de Samuel Beckett

title: Exploring Potential EGFR Inhibitors from Isodon Serra Phytochemicals: Molecular Docking, Dynamics, and ADMET Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT The human epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), a key oncogenic driver in various cancers, particularly non‐small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), was selected as the molecular target for this investigation. A validated molecular docking protocol was employed using AutoDock Vina, with re‐docking of the co‐crystallized ligand (PDB ID: 1M17) yielding an RMSD of 1.4095 Å, confirming reliability. title: Mixing performance analysis of single screw extruders using Computational Fluid Dynamics
abstract: This study uses single-screw extruders (SSEs) as a promising last stage mixing unit for the continuous production of thermoplastic polyurethanes (TPUs). In this process, a pre-mixing static device – opposed jet mixers - is coupled with an SSE, where monomers are fed and homogenized before the injection into the extruder. Mixing studies in opposed jet mixers are widely reported in literature; however, the fundamental and quantitative analysis of mixing performance in the SSE is proposed to optimize the reactive extrusion process. title: Exploratory screening of faba bean germplasm for winter adaptation and seed quality in Northwestern Europe
abstract: Abstract Faba bean ( Vicia faba L.) is a high-protein legume suited to Northwestern Europe, yet adoption is hindered by limited winter survival, acute cold events, and seed anti-nutritional factors notably vicine and convicine (VC) that constrain food use despite high protein content. We conducted a two-year, two-season study in Belgium (2022–2024) directly comparing winter versus spring accessions via field phenotyping, intact-seed NIRS (n=343), and standardized breadmaking (10% wheat-flour substitution). institutions: Institute of Biological, Environmental and Rural Sciences

title: Bioinformatic-Guided Discovery of O -Dealkylation Activity in Cytochrome P450 Monooxygenases
abstract: Abstract The O-dealkylation of alkyl ethers—or the removal of small alkyl protecting groups (PGs)—remains a significant challenge in organic synthesis. While traditional chemical methods require harsh reaction conditions and lack sufficient selectivity, biocatalytic approaches represent valuable alternatives. However, enzymes facilitating the desired O-dealkylation reactions are scarce. title: A lncRNA–miRNA axis regulates the balance between proliferative and invasive states in melanoma
abstract: Abstract Melanoma is a highly aggressive malignancy characterized by significant phenotypic plasticity, allowing tumor cells to transit between different phenotypic states. This process, known as phenotype switching, drives metastasis and therapeutic resistance. While the primary transcriptional markers defining these states are well-established, the non-coding regulatory networks that stabilize these phenotypes remain incompletely understood. title: Trading the Globe’s Flora from the German Provinces: The Unio Itineraria in Esslingen, 1827-1845
abstract: Abstract In the first half of the nineteenth century, a scientific society called the Unio Itineraria was formed in Esslingen, a small town near Stuttgart in what was then the German states. Operating as a joint-stock company for the collection, sale, and distribution of botanical specimens, it became well-known and well-respected as a mechanism to acquire plants from around the world in Europe. title: NARRATIVE TRANSLATION AND CINEMATIC INTERPRETATION: CHARLES MATTHAU'S ADAPTATION OF TRUMAN CAPOTE'S LYRICAL-PHILOSOPHICAL NOVEL THE GRASS HARP
abstract: The article examines the relationship between Truman Capote's novel The Grass Harp and Charles Matthau's 1995 film adaptation through the lens of adaptation studies, narratology, and intermedial analysis. While Capote's novel is distinguished by its lyrical prose, introspective narration, and subtle exploration of memory, individuality, and human relationships, Matthau's film translates these literary qualities into a visual medium by employing cinematic narrative techniques, performance, music, and symbolic imagery. The study investigates how the adaptation negotiates the transition from verb
institutions: Ferenc Rakoczi II Transcarpathian Hungarian University

title: Subsidence inversions – the surface water vapour thief
abstract: Abstract A deep anticyclonic subsidence inversion reached near‐surface levels over southern England on 25 April 2026, resulting in relative humidity levels falling below 15% widely and sub‐10% in the Reading and Wokingham area. Such low levels in lowland England have very few historical precedents within the last century or more. Furthermore, careful analysis of the automatic weather station psychrometer records from the University of Reading Atmospheric Observatory on this occasion suggests that the relative humidity here may have fallen briefly below 6%.

title: Full-scale fatigue and burst testing of girth-welded steel pipe under combined internal pressure and bending has consequences for pressure safety margins
abstract: Abstract The strategic role of hydrocarbon transmission pipelines is unquestionable today. This role can be interpreted within a country, but also between neighbouring countries, or within larger regions, continents and between continents. An incident on such a pipeline can therefore cause disruption both within a country and beyond, in wider regions. The critical elements of high-pressure gas transmission pipelines are often the girth welds. title: “I Have Nothing Left in the Tank”: Parental Burnout‐Relevant Experiences Amid Climate Change
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective To explore how parents describe climate‐related depletion in the parenting role and how a parental‐burnout framework can inform its interpretation. Background Climate conversations can place emotion‐regulation demands on parents, including managing a child's distress while containing their own and reassuring without credible closure. Yet how parents experience these demands remains underexplored. title: ‘Scattered remnants of identity’: translanguaging and multimodality as agentive choices in plurilingual youths’ identity artifacts
abstract: The identity development of children growing up speaking multiple languages has become a recent research concern in an increasingly diverse society. What has received less attention is the intersection of translanguaging, semiotic choices, and identity development as represented in the agentic choices made by plurilingual children when asked to explain their unique identities and contexts to others. title: Preparation of silver nanoparticles using microwave plasma jet and study of their physicochemical properties and applications in photocatalysis
abstract: Microwave plasma is considered a crucial engineering technology and an effective method for preparing silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) with controllable properties, thereby opening up numerous possibilities for their application in environmental remediation and water treatment technologies.The structural and optical characteristics of the prepared AgNPs, as well as their photocatalytic activity toward methylene blue dye degradation, were investigated.AgNPs were prepared using a microwave plasma system at operating voltages of 150, 160, and 170 V. title: Prevalence and Management of Suspected and Confirmed Bloodstream Infections Among Acute Leukaemia Patients Receiving Chemotherapy at Kenyatta National Hospital, Kenya
abstract: Patients with acute leukaemia receiving chemotherapy are highly susceptible to infection because of disease-related immune dysfunction, chemotherapy-induced neutropenia, mucosal injury, and frequent use of invasive vascular devices. However, evidence on bloodstream infection and its management in this population in Kenya remains limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of suspected and confirmed bloodstream infection and to evaluate antibiotic utilisation and adherence to evidence-based treatment guidelines among patients with acute leukaemia receiving chemotherapy in adult wards
journal: African Journal of Pharmacy and Alternative Medicine

title: Development and validation of a low-cost, wearable near-infrared spectroscopy system for quantifying tissue water fraction in the human brain
abstract: Significance: Cerebral water fraction is physiologically relevant to brain fluid dynamics, glymphatic function, cerebral edema, and dehydration, yet it is not routinely measured in wearable neuroimaging. Aim: We aimed to develop and validate a low-cost, wearable, light-emitting diode (LED)-based continuous-wave near-infrared spectroscopy system capable of concurrently monitoring changes in cerebral hemoglobin concentration and water fraction from the forehead. title: Wind energy development alters breeding habitat of the Bicknell's Thrush, a threatened range-restricted boreal songbird: evidence for opportunities in biodiversity-informed spatial planning
abstract: Understanding how wind energy infrastructure affects breeding habitat for species with restricted distributions is essential for reconciling climate mitigation ( e.g. , renewable energy) with biodiversity conservation. We evaluated how the development of four wind farms in a mountainous landscape of eastern Québec (Canada) affects breeding habitat for the globally Vulnerable Bicknell's Thrush ( Catharus bicknelli ). title: From Genomics to Diagnostics: Combating the Spread of Vascular Streak Dieback in North America
abstract: ABSTRACT Vascular streak dieback (VSD) has emerged as a major threat to woody ornamental production in the United States (U.S.), currently affecting at least 50 tree and shrub species across 25 botanical genera in at least twelve U.S. states. The putative causal agent, here termed the VSD‐associated Ceratobasidiaceae lineage ( Csp ), presents diagnostic challenges due to its fastidious growth requirements and vascular colonization pattern. title: Design, Synthesis, in silico Studies, and Biological Evaluation of N4-Acetyl/Benzoyl Piperazinyl Ciprofloxacin–Amino Acid Conjugates as Broad-Spectrum Antimicrobial Agents
abstract: This study reports a second-stage optimization of our previously reported ciprofloxacin derivatives through molecular hybridization, with structural modifications aimed at improving antimicrobial potency and activity against resistant strains. Their structures and identities were confirmed by spectroscopic techniques, elemental analysis, and HPLC. In vitro antimicrobial activity showed enhanced potency across a panel of bacterial strains. title: Nephroprotective and Gastroprotective potential of Aerva javanica (L.) green synthesized nanoparticles, supported by Molecular Networking
abstract: NSAIDs pose a significant risk to the stomach and kidneys, with oxidative stress being a key driver in the development of indomethacin-induced gastric ulcers and acute kidney injury by disrupting the balance between oxidation and antioxidation. Effective management of oxidative stress and bolstering antioxidant defenses are crucial strategies for preventing and treating these conditions. This study explored the potential of Aerva javanica, a plant abundant in Saudi Arabia and used in traditional medicine, to mitigate these adverse effects. title: Phenotypic diversity of a wild Solanum population from the Ecuadorian Andes: morphological characterization and conservation relevance
abstract: Abstract The genetic resources of wild Solanum plants constitute reservoirs of variability of interest for the conservation and improvement of Andean crops. In this study, a wild population of Solanum sp., "tomatillo," located in Cascarillas, Bolívar, Ecuador, was characterized. Twenty independent individuals were evaluated using vegetative, fruit, and seed characteristics, complemented by principal component analysis (PCA) and cluster analysis. title: Enhancement of Recombinant Protein Expression of Human Glucose-6-phosphate Dehydrogenase Using Escherichia coli System
abstract: The structural and functional characterization of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) typically requires large amounts of high-quality protein. In our previous study on the functional and structural analysis in G6PD proteins, we found that the expression yield of some G6PD variants was relatively low compared with the yield of the wild-type G6PD (G6PDWT) protein and that these proteins were mainly expressed in inclusion bodies. title: Synthetic microbial communities enable sustainable restoration of coal gangue-impacted soils by reprogramming nutrient cycling
abstract: Coal gangue disrupts microbial diversity and impairs nutrient cycling, constraining sustainable regional development. Traditional bioremediation relies on functional microbial traits, yet they often fail to colonize and perform in carbon-limited environments despite exogenous carbon inputs. We designed activity-oriented synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) to leverage exogenous carbon amendments and subsequently evaluated carbon use efficiency (CUE) as a community-level functional trait. title: Spectroscopy of low-lying valley states in hot Si/SiGe quantum dots
abstract: The presence of low-lying valley states in Si may hinder the development of large-scale spin-based quantum processors. Rapid prototyping of novel Si/SiGe heterostructures and gate stacks will be central to identifying pathways that increase the valley splitting. We compare the performance of pulsed-gate spectroscopy (PGS) and detuning axis pulsed spectroscopy (DAPS) at temperatures up to 700 mK. We find that DAPS outperforms PGS, with DAPS resolving valley splittings as small as ∼86 μeV, while the energy resolution of PGS is only ∼210 μeV. title: Actors, technology and geography: arenas of political economy for industrial decarbonisation policy in the United Kingdom
abstract: Industrial decarbonization (ID) involves significant uncertainty about technical and economic pathways, and it interacts with industrial and trade policy. The UK has been an early leader in ID efforts, developing a specific strategy and a set of deployment policies in the early 2020 s, with a strong focus on carbon capture and storage (CCS) and hydrogen, and a regional 'cluster' approach. In this article, we assess the policy choices the UK has made, through the application of a novel framework for analyzing their 'arenas of political economy'. title: The genetic landscape of RAG deficiency: Novel and founder variants in a large Algerian cohort
abstract: RAG1/RAG2 deficiency causes diverse SCID phenotypes, but large, systematically characterized cohorts from North Africa remain lacking. We retrospectively characterized 128 confirmed RAG1/RAG2-deficient patients diagnosed over 14 years in Algeria, classified per PIDTC 2022 criteria. Consanguinity was high (70.3%), with RAG2 (57.0%) outnumbering RAG1 (43.0%), a reversal of patterns reported elsewhere. Classical SCID (61.0%) and Omenn syndrome (23.4%) predominated. title: Spatially resolved near-wall velocity fluctuations at the onset of compliance-induced transition in soft microtubes
abstract: Abstract Wall compliance in soft conduits can trigger flow instability at Reynolds numbers far below the classical rigid-pipe threshold, yet the near-wall spatial structure of this transition remains experimentally unresolved. Here, we address this gap using high-speed particle tracking velocimetry in PDMS microtubes with systematically varied wall compliance (G′ = 14–392 kPa). title: Investigating consumer’s preferences for recyclable and bioplastic food packaging
abstract: Aim of study: Understand consumer preferences and willingness to pay (WTP) for grapes packaged in 100% recyclable, biodegradable, compostable, or conventional fossil-based plastic. Area of study: Aragón (Spain). Material and methods: Data were collected via an online survey of 401 consumers. A discrete choice experiment (DCE) was estimated using a latent class (LC) model to capture preference heterogeneity. title: Atomic structure of selenium incorporated into mackinawite unveiled by density functional theory
abstract: Selenium-79 is an important contributor to the long-term radiological hazards in deep geological repositories for high‑level radioactive waste. Investigating the environmental behavior of selenium (Se) is crucial for its safety assessment. In this study, the stable structures of Se incorporated in mackinawite, an iron sulfide mineral, were elucidated using density functional theory (DFT) calculations. journal: Journal of Nuclear Science and Technology

title: Silence to story: Mapping water stewardship and relational literacies of early childhood teachers
abstract: Early childhood education is increasingly recognized as a critical site for climate learning, yet there is a need for further exploration around how educators introduce ecological responsibility in developmentally meaningful and emotionally attuned ways. This qualitative multi-case study examines how three preschool teachers engaged young children in water-centered storytelling and inquiry as an entry point into climate literacy. title: Global arable land redistribution toward the tropics and drylands under human settlement expansion
abstract: Abstract Arable land has been expanding since the advent of agriculture, and now sustains over eight billion people by supplying food, fiber, and fuel. However, the rapid expansion of built-up areas is increasingly displacing arable land across diverse regions, raising concerns about the long-term sustainability of global food systems. Addressing these concerns requires a fundamental understanding of global arable-land dynamics, which remains largely unknown. title: Evaluation of the antifungal activity of Moringa oleifera leaf and stem bark extracts against Fusarium species causing potato wilt
abstract: Abstract Fungal infections cause significant losses in many economic crops. Chemical control may be available to effectively and extensively reduce the effects of the most fungal disease but field application of these chemical fungicides may present a danger to the health of humans, animals, and the environment. This study was aimed to assess the antifungal activities of crude extracts of Moringa oleifera Lam. stems bark and leaves against Fusarium species. Four crude extracts (acetone and ethanol extract of stem bark and leaf) were tested for their effect on 10 Fusarium isolates at three diff

title: Performance evaluation of a biomass-fired parallel-flow tray dryer for orthodox black tea processing
abstract: The uniform and efficient drying process is still a big problem in the decentralized orthodox tea industry, especially in the field of using cost-effective and eco-friendly thermal drying equipment. In this study, an experimental evaluation of a biomass-fired parallel-flow tray dryer with 15° inclined airflow-guiding plates was conducted to explore the drying performance, moisture uniformity, and energy-efficiency for the drying system. title: Circular, Reconfigurable DNA-Surfactant Materials for Coatings with Tunable Oil and Water Barrier Properties
abstract: Abstract Commercial coatings for paper often rely on nonrenewable, nonbiodegradable polymers, thereby restricting the end-of-life options of the composite to noncircular pathways. The application of biopolymer–surfactant complexes composed of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acids) and cationic lipids as barrier coatings resolves these issues. title: Honey as a potential bioindicator of environmental change: chemical and pollen composition reveal spatial trends correlated with weather and landscape parameters
abstract: Understanding how environmental conditions shape floral resources is critical for pollinator health and ecosystem monitoring. Changes in the environment can alter the nutritional landscape for pollinators by altering the quantity and quality of resources available in their environment. In this study, we analyzed honey from different environments across a geographical scale using both melissopalynology and chemical profiling to determine pollen composition and honey physiochemical traits. title: Heat treatment optimization and Chromium Nitride precipitation control in heavy-section Superduplex Stainless Steel forgings
abstract: The optimization of mechanical properties in superduplex stainless steel forgings requires precise control of phase balance and precipitation kinetics. This study investigates the effect of different heat treatment routes, including single- and double-step solution annealing and varying cooling rates, on Cr nitride precipitation and secondary austenite formation in S32760 superduplex stainless steel. title: A novel method for the preparation of haemoglobin-based oxygen carriers via near-complete polymerization under static conditions
abstract: The clinical development of haemoglobin-based oxygen carriers (HBOCs) is hindered by residual haemoglobin (Hb) from incomplete polymerization, which causes vasoconstriction and hypertension, while its removal requires complex and costly purification. To overcome this, we developed a static polymerization strategy for synthesizing near-completely polymerized haemoglobin (PolyHb) using Hb purified from porcine blood. title: Seroprevalence, Risk Factors, and Farmer’s Knowledge and Practices on Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia in Morogoro Rural District, Tanzania
abstract: Background: Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia (CBPP), a highly contagious disease of cattle, is a major constraint to cattle production in Tanzania. Purpose: This study aimed to determine the seroprevalence of CBPP, identify animal and herd level risk factors of the disease, and assess the knowledge and practices (KP) of cattle farmers regarding CBPP. Method: Data were collected from August to November 2025 through a cross sectional study involving three cattle production systems; pastoral, agropastoral, and ranching. journal: Journal of Applied Veterinary Science And Technology

title: Three-dimensional seed morphology and evolutionary diversification in the grape family (Vitaceae)

title: Pollination syndromes poorly predict main flower visitors in a disturbed Atlantic forest fragment
abstract: Abstract Pollination syndromes are often used to guide pollinator conservation and ecosystem restoration, but their effectiveness in predicting main pollinators is contested. This study characterized floral traits and pollination syndromes of 69 plant species in a Mixed Ombrophilous Forest fragment and assessed whether observed floral visitors matched the expected syndromes. Floral attributes (anthesis, color, odor, size, shape, symmetry, orientation, stamen position, nectar guides, resources) and plant characteristic (habit, sexual system, plant status, and occurrence) were recorded. title: Evolutionary dynamics of adaptive introgression and balancing selection in domestic and wild Capra species
abstract: Abstract Introgression is increasingly documented, yet its detection remains challenging because patterns used to infer gene flow may reflect multiple processes, including the persistence of ancestral polymorphism under balancing selection. Domestic species, like goats, and their wild relatives provide informative models for testing the biological feasibility and genomic consequences of interspecific gene flow. We analyze whole-genome sequences from 164 individuals of the genus Capra , including 36 newly generated, to investigate hybridization and signatures of introgression within the genus.

title: Confluence: Linking Citizen Science and Extension Education to Inspire Environmental Stewardship
abstract: Citizen science has rapidly moved beyond simply crowdsourcing data to become a novel platform for environmental and informal science education. However, few studies document the informal learning outcomes of citizen science, particularly in youth or Extension education. This quantitative study evaluated individual learning outcomes of an environmental education and citizen science experience about water quality at 4-H summer camps. institutions: United States Fish and Wildlife Service

title: Sound advice: A calibration framework for defining detection space in passive acoustic monitoring
abstract: Passive Acoustic Monitoring (PAM) has emerged as a transformative tool for biodiversity assessment in recent years. Despite widespread acceptance and application for conservation-related outcomes, the interactive effects of hardware limitations, signal propagation, and environmental conditions on how far a signal can be reliably detected remain critically understudied. abstract: BACKGROUND: Vertebrates rely on phosphorus intake for skeletal mineralization. abstract: Abstract Zika virus (ZIKV) is a mosquito-borne flavivirus that has recently emerged as a global health threat. The majority of ZIKV infections are mild or asymptomatic; however, clinical diagnosis is inaccurate. abstract: Abstract The escalating global challenges of food waste and environmental pollution from conventional plastic packaging necessitate the development of sustainable and intelligent food packaging solutions. This study presents a novel bio-composite material fabricated from Nata de Coco (NDC), reduced Graphene Oxide (rGO), and food-grade gelatin, designed for smart and sustainable packaging applications. abstract: ABSTRACT The selective recovery of aromatic pollutants from saline wastewater remains a central challenge in sustainable chemical engineering. We present a bio‐derived Janus membrane that couples a sorption‐active, mechanically robust wood scaffold with an ultrathin polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) layer for soft‐gated aromatic transport. abstract: ABSTRACT The cosmetics industry faces increasing pressure to integrate upcycled agro‐food by‐products, yet consumer adoption remains constrained by contamination concerns that are strongest for products applied directly to the body. Linear attitudinal models offer limited insight into how meaning is constructed around novel “waste‐derived” claims. title: Untangle air connectivity and tourism development in China’s domestic market
abstract: This paper examines how domestic air connectivity shapes spatial patterns of tourism development in China. abstract: Abstract Diffuse sources and resulting surface water quality impairments are major challenges for achieving advanced environmental goals as formulated in the EU Water Framework Directive or in the Zero Pollution Ambition of the European Green Deal. However, the effectiveness of legal and practical interventions is to date insufficiently understood. abstract: This paper addresses target interception in contested, GPS-denied environments with multiple finite-range, moving defenders. title: Limits to adaptation: Agroforestry buffers but does not offset climate change impacts on maize yields in Dodoma, Tanzania
abstract: Abstract Agricultural productivity in the semi-arid region of central Tanzania is low and projected to further decrease due to climate change, exacerbating the already high levels of food insecurity among the rural population. Agroforestry is actively promoted in the region as an adaptation strategy due to its multiple biophysical and socio-economic benefits, but whether it can buffer future climate change impacts on maize yields has not yet been quantified. abstract: Abstract Background Most emerging infectious diseases originate in wildlife populations. As demonstrated by the 2013–2016 Ebola epidemic in West Africa, pathogen spillover from zoonotic reservoirs can have devastating public health impacts. Contact between humans and wildlife reservoirs determines spillover risk, but these interactions remain poorly understood. title: Improvement of germination properties in barley (Hordeum vulgare) seeds damaged by Sitophilus oryzae infestation via dielectric barrier discharge plasma treatment
abstract: Abstract Insect‑damaged barley seeds typically exhibit poor germination and are often discarded. abstract: Abstract The cellular mechanisms of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid (ω3 PUFA) supplementation were investigated in inflammatory arthritis. Mice fed a prophylactic ω3 PUFA-enriched diet displayed reduced arthritis and paw oedema, with a discrete regulation of innate and stromal cell phenotypes in arthritic joints. abstract: Abstract Given the complex nature of secondary organic aerosols (SOA), knowledge of their interactions with clouds is highly limited. In this study, we developed a molecular‐level cloud parcel model, CSVA‐cloud. A key feature is its unified microphysical framework for gas‐particle partitioning of water and organic molecules. abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Understanding how life history strategies vary among sympatric taxa along environmental gradients is fundamental to predicting biodiversity responses to climate change. abstract: The genus Ferula (Apiaceae) is widely distributed across Central and Southwest Asia and is recognized for its diverse secondary metabolites and traditional medicinal uses. However, the phytochemical composition of Ferula songarica and Ferula foetida from Kazakhstan remains poorly explored. abstract: Melanin synthesis in gametes is exceptionally rare among vertebrates. Among amphibians, egg pigmentation patterns range from unpigmented or subtly melanic eggs, such as in foam-nesting frogs to the heavily pigmented eggs known from some poison frogs and salamanders. Winter barley ( Hordeum vulgare L.) shares similar agronomic requirements and equipment needs with winter wheat, and Nebraska's large cattle industry provides an established market for barley as feed or grazing, supporting its adoption with minimal infrastructure changes. abstract: Low-digestible carbohydrates (LDCs), including dietary fibers and sugars that resist absorption, are generally considered beneficial for the gut microbiota. title: Dynamical plausibility of triple-assisted interaction in Be-star multiple systems
abstract: Classical Be stars are rapidly rotating B-type stars surrounded by gaseous circumstellar disks. The origin of the angular momentum required to sustain their near-critical rotation remains uncertain. Binary interaction is a promising spin-up channel, and in hierarchical multiple systems a tertiary companion may drive the secular evolution of an unresolved inner binary.
