abstract: Abstract Dynamic stall is a highly unsteady aerodynamic problem that restricts the performance of pitching airfoils used in helicopters, wind turbines, and UAVs. Effective suppression of dynamic stall is crucial for improving aerodynamic efficiency, structural stability, and energy output. Several flow techniques have been developed in the past decade to mitigate dynamic stall, but a thorough assessment of their capabilities, limitations and potential remains limited. abstract: Water temperature is a key driver of aquatic ecosystems, yet thermal heterogeneity across river networks at fine spatiotemporal scales remains poorly understood. title: Where There Was Fire… Changes in the Community of Nest Predator in Burned Grasslands of the Southern Pampas, Argentina
abstract: ABSTRACT Fire plays a key role in grassland ecosystems by modifying vegetation structure and, consequently, influencing predator–prey interactions that can affect the reproductive success of grassland birds. The reduction in vegetation density and height resulting from fire affects the reproductive success of birds by increasing the likelihood of nest predation and may modify the relative importance of different predator types to nest fate. Streams grasslands are preferred breeding sites for grassland birds in the Southern Pampas of Argentina, in a context of intensive agriculture and grazing.

abstract: We evaluated Ecuador's trauma care system capacity by analyzing the discrepancy between hospital infrastructure and the individual dimensions of the Knowledge, Attitudes, Practices, and Safety (KAPS) framework among medical specialists. abstract: We introduce an interacting ideal limit of rhombohedral graphene in which interactions spontaneously generate a correlated Chern insulator. Our analysis reveals that this Chern insulator can be understood as a layer-pseudospin skyrmion lattice stabilized by electronic interactions, and that it gives rise to genuine skyrmion lattice physics, complete with dynamics. abstract: Objective: Comparative evidence for fig and kiwifruit extracts standardized to equivalent protease activity and combined with ultrasound treatment remains limited. abstract: Delivery service companies in Indonesia face a decline in the number of shipments due to the large number of competitors and uncompetitive shipping price offers. This study aims to analyze the mechanism of the relationship between tariff setting and the revenue performance of courier service companies and evaluate the behavior of revenue and profits in various tariff scenarios and demand conditions. title: Short‐term surface soil responses to compost rate during peach orchard establishment on sandy Ultisols
abstract: Abstract Compost amendment can improve soil health, but rate‐dependent responses in sandy orchard soils remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated the short‐term effects of compost application on soil physical, chemical, and biological properties during the first 2 years of peach ( Prunus persica (L.) Batsch) orchard establishment on a sandy Ultisol at Clemson University's Musser Fruit Research Center in South Carolina. abstract: Boron (B) is a micronutrient closely linked to tree productivity and stem quality in eucalyptus, with important implications for industrial wood utilization. However, the field response of Corymbia citriodora subsp. variegata (CCV) to B fertilization remains poorly understood. abstract: This paper investigates how local and Indigenous knowledge systems (LIKS) are produced and reproduced through food systems in three Anishinaabe First Nations communities in northern Ontario: Red Rock Indian Band, Biinjitiwaabik Zaaging Anishinaabek, and Netmizaaggamig Nishnaabeg. title: A citizen science approach to model water and food circularity in schools
abstract: Promoting circularity in schools for climate adaptation requires detailed assessments of their resource metabolism, which is typically challenging due to lack of data. This paper proposes a bottom-up methodology for mapping and quantifying water and food flows in schools that combines the principles of Material Flow Analysis (MFA) and citizen science. abstract: Abstract Ion selective electrodes represent a promising approach for ion detection based on potentiometric sensing principle. abstract: Informal settlements are commonly characterized by concentrated populations, inadequate infrastructure and poor living conditions that may constrain household water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. abstract: Poly (lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) is a promising biodegradable material for food packaging, but its behavior under representative food-contact conditions remains insufficiently understood. title: Changes in Long‐Term Care Needs, Healthcare Costs, and Mortality Risk After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Japan: The Longevity Improvement & Fair Evidence Study
abstract: AIM: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is increasingly performed in older adults with severe aortic stenosis, but there is limited evidence on their post-procedure changes in care needs, healthcare costs, and mortality risk. title: Bryophyte functional traits regulate root and soil microbial responses to reduced snow cover in boreal forests
abstract: Boreal forests store substantial soil carbon yet are experiencing climate change characterized by reduced snowpack and increased soil freeze-thaw cycles. Mosses, particularly Sphagnum spp. and Pleurozium schreberi, dominate boreal forest floors, contributing to soil insulation and moisture retention, but their role in buffering belowground carbon processes under reduced snow cover remains poorly understood. title: Biomimetic Nanoparticles With Overexpressed Adhesion Proteins for Targeted Delivery of Gambogic Acid in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
abstract: Cancer cell membrane coating offers a promising strategy for targeted drug delivery, yet its homotypic targeting mechanism and optimization remain insufficiently understood. This study identifies epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM), rather than Galectin-3, as the pivotal mediator of homologous uptake in hepatocellular carcinoma. Through genetic engineering, HepG2 cells overexpressing EpCAM are generated, and their membranes are used to coat gambogic acid-loaded PLGA nanoparticles. title: Estimating the urban heat island effect with lichens and bryophytes: a citizen science protocol
abstract: The urban heat island effect (UHI), whereby urban areas are warmer than the surrounding rural areas, has become an increasing threat to human health and affects biodiversity. Counteracting this public health concern requires large-scale monitoring of urban heat. One cost-effective way to obtain this data is by using bioindicators, such as lichens and bryophytes. They are well-known bioindicators readily available in the urban environment, and have proven to respond to the UHI. abstract: Abstract Citizen science is widely used in biodiversity monitoring, yet its application to bats remains limited, particularly regarding how participation influences public understanding and support for conservation. This study examined short‐term changes in ecological knowledge, attitudes toward bats, and connection to nature following participation in a bat‐focused citizen science program. abstract: In a substantial number of her texts – poetry as well as prose – Marina Ivanovna Cvetaeva (1892–1941) constructs contrasting dimensionalities: one-dimensional lines, two-dimensional planes, and three-dimensional objects are set in contrast to one another. abstract: In ectothermic vertebrates, seasonal dietary shifts and temperature fluctuations are major ecological drivers of gut microbiota remodeling, with important implications for host adaptation. The widely distributed nocturnal reptile Gekko japonicus provides an effective model for exploring seasonal gut microbiota dynamics under natural conditions. abstract: Insects can experience a loss of fertility under acute heat stress, but impacts vary among species and depend on life stage and sex. title: Testing the theory of planned behavior in predicting evacuation intentions during storms
abstract: The Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) has been widely applied to predict human behavior across diverse domains; however, its application in disaster contexts remains limited. This study addresses this gap by examining the utility of TPB in predicting intentions to prepare evacuation plans in hurricane-prone areas. abstract: Sarvar-e A'zam Bakuchi, known by the pen name "Sepideh Kashani," is a prominent figure in Persian poetry. abstract: Kutaja (Holarrhena antidysenterica Wall. ex A.DC.; family Apocynaceae) is an important Ayurvedic drug, particularly indicated in Atisara, Pravahika, Grahani and Arsha. abstract: Abstract Background/objectives Street-involved youth experience overlapping behavioral and structural vulnerabilities that increase the risk of adverse health outcomes. abstract: Abstract Aging-related cognitive decline, including impairments in spatial orientation and memory, has been linked to dysfunction within the hippocampus and medial entorhinal cortex (MEC). abstract: The development and evaluation of Lidar-Inertial Odometry (LIO) and Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) systems require a precise reference trajectory. The Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) is often used as a foundation for this, but its signals can be unreliable in obstructed environments due to multi-path effects or loss-of-signal. title: Expressive Priority and Goal Structure and Complexity During Collegiate, Faculty, and Professional Chamber Music Rehearsals
abstract: The purpose of this study was to discover the artistic conceptualizations and priorities of collegiate, faculty, and professional musicians during the moment-to-moment decision-making of a rehearsal. We utilized musicians’ verbalizations during chamber music rehearsals as a vehicle for exploring their thought processes. Analysis 1 investigated the rehearsal targets ensembles prioritized as a percentage of total rehearsal time allocated to each. title: Development of NiO/borophene hybrid platform for non-enzymatic electrochemical sensing of malathion
abstract: Malathion (MAL), a widely used organophosphate pesticide effecting environment and causes serious health hazards. Herewith, this work introduces a highly sensitive electrochemical sensor for the sensitive detection of MAL in various environmental samples by utilizing NiO/borophene nanomaterial. The sensor was fabricated via solvothermal method and was characterized to confirm its structural and electrochemical properties. title: Multi‐Omics Analyses Identify Candidate Genes Associated With Stage‐Specific Quality Formation in Mulching‐Treated Moso Bamboo Shoots
abstract: Bamboo shoots are nutrient-rich edible resources, and organic mulching promotes earlier shoot emergence and increases yield. However, the molecular mechanisms regulating mulching-treated shoot (MtS) development remain unclear. Field experiments across three Moso bamboo forests, combined with biochemical profiling, metabolomics, and transcriptomics, examine MtS development. title: Valorization of endemic sigupai aceh rice husk as a renewable cellulose source for nanocellulose production via sulfuric acid hydrolysis
abstract: Endemic rice varieties can create locally abundant lignocellulosic residues. This study evaluates Sigupai rice husk, an Aceh endemic biomass, as a feedstock for cellulose nanocrystal production through alkaline delignification, hypochlorite bleaching and controlled sulfuric acid hydrolysis at 1, 2 and 3 mol/L. The work tests how increasing acid concentration affects yield, residual non-cellulosic material, crystallinity, surface chemistry and particle-size distribution. title: Linking geography, isolation source, and genomic diversity in a global Candida albicans phylogeny
abstract: Abstract Candida albicans is a common commensal species in the human microbiome at multiple sites and an opportunistic pathogen. Previous phylogenomic analyses identified major clades but often relied on imprecise genomic methods, limited geographic and ecological sampling, and non-standardized strategies for phylogenetic resolution. abstract: The adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-regulated GroEL/ES chaperonin of Escherichia coli promotes protein folding by transiently encapsulating unfolded substrate protein in a nano-cage formed by the cylindrical GroEL and the lid-shaped GroES. title: Mid-zone hepatocytes trade proliferation for survival via Atf4-Chop axis in early acute liver injury
abstract: Abstract Hepatocytes undergo extensive proliferation to facilitate liver repair after injury, yet early adaptive changes prior to proliferation remain unclear. Here, we report that during early acetaminophen (APAP)-induced liver injury, hepatocytes exhibit transient proliferation suppression that is most pronounced in mid-zone hepatocytes, consistent with zonal APAP metabolism. title: Ultra-lightweight mid-IR methane sensor for in-situ UAV-based measurements: Design and demonstration
abstract: Abstract. We developed an ultra-lightweight mid-infrared laser spectroscopic sensor for precise, rapid mobile measurements of atmospheric methane concentrations aboard small uncrewed aerial vehicles. The design is simple and compact, featuring a Herriott-type multi-pass cell in an open-path configuration. A single board computer with two on-chip microprocessor units allows rapid data acquisition and onboard wavelength modulation spectroscopy, making the sensor a stand-alone turnkey instrument. Including the dedicated battery, the sensor weighs 1.2 kg and consumes up to 11 W of electrical power

title: Bacteriocin-producing lactic acid bacteria as silage inoculants to reduce methane emissions in late lactation dairy cattle
abstract: Abstract Enteric fermentation in ruminants is the largest agricultural source of methane (CH₄) and contributes to global warming. Practical mitigation strategies are therefore needed for sustainable dairy production. This study evaluated a silage inoculant composed of bacteriocin-producing lactic acid bacteria (LAB) strains, Lactococcus lactis subsp. lactis SL242 and Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LP58 in late-lactation, spring-calving Holstein cows. title: Germination Responses of Black Cumin (Nigella sativa L.) Seeds to NaCl Induced Osmotic Stress Expressed
abstract: Salinity is one of the major environmental stress factors limiting agricultural production. The objective of this study was to determine the effects of different NaCl concentrations on seed germination and early seedling development in the Çameli variety of black cumin (Nigella sativa L.). The experiment was conducted using NaCl concentrations of 0, 50, 100, 150, and 200 mM NaCl concentrations, which corresponded to osmotic potentials of 0, -0.244, -0.487, -0.731, and -0.974 MPa, respectively. abstract: Epoxy composites can undergo time-dependent deformation under sustained loading, limiting their dimensional stability, while agricultural residues offer potential as sustainable reinforcements. This study evaluated the effect of hybrid castor nutshell (CNS) and pineapple leaf fiber (PALF) powder loading on the displacement response and fracture-surface morphology of epoxy composites. title: Nutraceutical-rich oil from passion fruit by-products of beverage processing by green extraction
abstract: Processing passion fruit beverages generates substantial agro-industrial by-products that are rich in bioactive compounds. Valorizing these by-products through green extraction offers a sustainable route to transform them into high-value oils while supporting responsible food-waste reduction. title: Structural analysis of ribbon-bounding faults in Tessera terrain, Venus
abstract: Tessera terrain preserves locally the earliest tectonic processes on Venus. Ribbon extensional fabric is one of the most pervasive structural features of Tessera, characterized by alternating radar-bright and dark scarps interpreted as long, narrow graben. Here we have determined the geometry of ribbon-bounding scarps to understand their origin and post-formational evolution. title: ROS‐Responsive Micellar Delivery of Bergapten for Coordinated Attenuation of Oxidative Stress and Neuroinflammation in Neonatal Hypoxic‐Ischemic Brain Damage
abstract: Neonatal hypoxic-ischemic brain damage (HIBD) represents a leading contributor to neonatal death and persistent neurological impairments, yet effective therapeutic options beyond hypothermia remain limited. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and Toll-like receptor (TLR)-mediated neuroinflammation contribute to neuronal loss during hypoxic-ischemic injury. abstract: Abstract Nivicolous myxomycetes fruit at snowmelt in mountains, while their amoeboid trophic stages persist unseen in soil. title: Sexual Dimorphism in the Facial Morphology and Skin Color in Sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Abstract In human faces, sexual dimorphism manifests itself in both morphological traits and skin color differences between males and females. Existing research has focused mainly on facial shape, but less is known about the interplay between dimorphism in facial structure and skin color, particularly in African populations. title: An Introduction to the Typology of Idiomatic Phrases in the Literature of Chinese Chán Buddhism
abstract: This article examines aspects of the typology and historical development of idiomatic phrases (chéngyǔ 成語) in premodern Chinese Chán Buddhist literature, situating them within broader debates on the origins of Chinese idioms. Challenging the prevalent view that idioms primarily derive from classical written sources, the study argues—based on a large-scale database analysis—that many idioms originated in the colloquial language of a respective period and eventually were incorporated into Chán texts, or were “invented” in the context of Chán literary creativity. abstract: The greater wax moth, Galleria mellonella L. (Lepidoptera: Pyralidae), is a major pest causing serious damage to honeycombs and apicultural products. In this study, 9 indigenous Beauveria isolates were screened for their pathogenicity, and HpA-5 was identified as the most virulent isolate based on mortality, LT50, and LC50 values. abstract: Urban plant communities assemble from a regional species pool shaped by both ecological processes and horticultural trade, yet how these two forces jointly structure its functional composition remains poorly understood. title: Gifted Students' Views on Global Warming: An Explanatory Study
abstract: The purpose of this study is to examine 7th-grade gifted students’ awareness of the factors contributing to global warming and their behaviors related to mitigating it. In line with this aim, a sequential explanatory design, one of the mixed-methods research approaches, was employed. The study group consisted of 168 7th-grade students attending three Science and Art Centers (SAC) in Istanbul. abstract: ABSTRACT Background The diagnosis of many male reproductive disorders still relies on invasive surgical procedures, revealing the need for new, non-invasive approaches capable of providing deeper molecular information. Seminal plasma represents a promising diagnostic specimen because it directly reflects the biochemical environment of the male reproductive tract. title: The Residual Effect of Temporal Heat Exposure Increases N 2 O Emissions by Accelerating Organic Matter Decomposition in Black Soil
abstract: ABSTRACT Black soil (Mollisol), characterized by high soil organic matter (SOM), is becoming more vulnerable to extreme heat events, yet the effects of heat on decomposition of SOM, thus N 2 O emission remain unclear. title: Scientific Understanding Across Disciplines: In Varietate Concordia?
abstract: Abstract Understanding is a generally acknowledged aim of science, but the way in which understanding is pursued and criteria for when it is achieved differ widely across scientific disciplines. This paper offers a comparative analysis of this disciplinary variation, aimed at revealing differences as well as commonalities in methods and criteria for achieving understanding. title: A platinized Pt wire as an affordable platform for the voltammetric determination of ammonia
abstract: Abstract Ammonia is a major contributor to eutrophication, making its reliable monitoring essential for protecting aquatic ecosystems and safeguarding water quality. Here, we report a miniaturized electrochemical platform based on a platinized Pt wire for the voltammetric determination of ammonia in natural and drinking water samples. abstract: Kusum (Schleichera oleosa), a member of the Sapindaceae family, is a valuable non-timber forest product commonly found in dense forests across Asia. With a long history in Ayurveda and growing recognition in modern research, every part of the Kusum tree including its leaves, bark, fruit, peel, seeds, oil, and deoiled cake hold unique properties and applications. Although its pathogenic mechanisms have been extensively investigated, its specialized metabolism remains largely unexplored. abstract: Reliable foundation design for power-transmission towers in mountainous terrain requires accurate knowledge of shallow weathering and bedrock geometry, yet steep relief, irregular bedrock, and uneven weathering limit point-based drilling and conventional surveys at the approximately 22 m × 22 m tower footprint. abstract: Abstract The molecular mechanisms that drive (lymph-)angiogenesis are crucial to understand diseases, such as lymphedema, that are caused due to malformations of the lymphatic vasculature. title: Interaction of outer membrane vesicles of the oral pathogen Porphyromonas gingivalis with human red blood cells disclosed by proteome analyses
abstract: Porphyromonas gingivalis is a keystone oral pathogen implicated in periodontitis and several other pro-inflammatory or degenerative diseases. Previous studies showed that outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) produced by this Gram-negative bacterium are loaded with virulence factors, including the P. gingivalis peptidyl-arginine deiminase (PPAD). However, our understanding of strain-specific OMV features and the impact of PPAD on OMV cargo composition was so far limited. title: Physiochemical Characterization of the Asedo Feldspar Deposit, Mozambique Belt, Southern Ethiopia: Implications for Ceramic and Glass Industries
abstract: This study evaluates the industrial viability of the newly identified Asedo feldspar deposit, hosted within Neoproterozoic pegmatites of the Mozambique Belt in southern Ethiopia. Geochemical analysis of ten feldspar samples reveals a major oxide composition averaging 69.02 wt.% SiO 2 , 21.19 wt.% Al 2 O 3 , 4.04 wt.% Na 2 O, 3.10 wt.% K 2 O, 2.96 wt.% CaO, 0.31 wt.% Fe 2 O 3 , and 0.11 wt.% MgO, with a low Loss on Ignition (LOI) of 0.43 wt.%, reflecting high mineralogical purity. title: Interspecific Cohabitation and Associated Zoonotic Risk in the Burrows of Niokolo‐Koba National Park, Senegal
abstract: ABSTRACT In arid and semi‐arid ecosystems, burrows serve as vital sanctuaries providing wildlife shelter, nourishment, and thermal buffering. These benefits attract multiple species into confined spaces, potentially facilitating interspecific pathogen transmission. This study provides a comprehensive assessment of burrow use in Senegal's Niokolo‐Koba National Park, quantifying interspecific cohabitation, identifying influential characteristics, and documenting the potential for zoonotic pathogen transmission. Its fundamental vibrational band locates around 4.6 $\upmu$m and has larger absorption line strength than that of overtone band, which is more suitable for the precise identification and concentration detection of CO. title: How to manage meadows effectively? Flagship, keystone & diagnostic species perspective
abstract: We investigated the long-term effects of meadow management regimes (abandonment vs. mowing, and its frequency), plant invasion, and habitat availability on three different meadow ecosystem components. The system consists of (1) native plant Sanguisorba officinalis, (2) ant assemblages, and (3) butterfly species of the genus Phengaris, known as flagships for biodiversity conservation. title: Functional Genomics of a Zinc‐Solubilising Kosakonia cowanii RL ‐16 and Its Application for Zinc Biofortification in Oryza sativa L.
abstract: Zinc (Zn) is assumed to be the most important micronutrient due to its involvement in different biochemical processes. The daily requirement of Zn for the human body, however, cannot be fulfilled by traditional staple crops such as rice due to its low availability to plants, especially in alkaline soils. The present study was carried out to investigate the potential of indigenous microbial flora, isolated from different agroecological zones, for Zn solubilization and combating Zn deficiency in rice. title: An Early Jurassic soft eggshell provides insights into the evolutionary history of dinosaur eggs
abstract: Early eggshell fossils offer invaluable insights into evolutionary innovations in over 300 million years of amniote egg history. However, the incompleteness of the dinosaur eggshell fossil record hinders ancestral state reconstruction and leads to uncertainty about whether the first dinosaur egg was soft-shelled, semi-rigid-shelled, or rigid-shelled. Herein, we present a fossilized soft eggshell (Mutabilisoolithus dawaensis) from an Early Jurassic basal sauropodomorph. title: Peptide Bioconjugates: an Emerging Strategy in the Pharmacotherapy of Dermatological Diseases (2015-2025). A Review
abstract: Peptide-based bioconjugates are emerging as a highly versatile and powerful class of therapeutics in modern dermatology, offering precise molecular targeting combined with the flexibility of advanced chemical design. These systems demonstrate broad applicability — from antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory interventions to photodynamic and antineoplastic therapies — while addressing key limitations of conventional treatments through controlled delivery, sustained release, and enhanced cellular selectivity. title: Ginkgolide K restrains pulmonary fibrosis by disrupting a STING–FTH1 proteolytic ferroptosis axis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is driven by persistent fibroblast activation and excessive extracellular matrix deposition. Stimulator of interferon genes (STING) has been implicated in tissue fibrosis, but whether it directly regulates ferroptosis and iron homeostasis in fibroblasts through noncanonical mechanisms remains unclear. Ginkgolide K (GinK), a bioactive diterpene trilactone from Ginkgo biloba, has antioxidant and immunomodulatory properties, but its role in PF is poorly understood. abstract: “Chemistry Organic” category stands at the confluence of materials science, life sciences, and green sustainability. Therefore, the rapid diversification of this literature has made the systematic identification of influential research themes increasingly important. This study presents a cross-sectional bibliometric analysis of 568 Highly Cited Papers and Hot Papers published from 2014 to 2025. abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of pediatric hospitalization, yet data on children hospitalized with RSV in their second year of life are limited. OBJECTIVE: To compare clinical characteristics and management practices of children hospitalized with RSV during their second versus first year of life. title: Research on Modular Design Method of Wind Turbine Gearbox
abstract: ABSTRACT The design of wind turbine gearboxes presents increasing challenges in balancing efficiency, reliability, and cost as turbines trend toward larger scales. Despite their critical role in power transmission, current modular design methodologies suffer from a lack of systematic mathematical modeling and inadequate leveraging of existing product data. Consequently, development cycles are protracted—often lasting 1–3 months—due to iterative calculations and cross‐disciplinary coordination, which can lead to project delays and client dissatisfaction. abstract: 1 Abstract Effective population size ( N e ) is a critical parameter for evaluating the evolutionary and persistence potential of endangered populations and for designing sustainable conservation strategies. Captive breeding and release programs are widely used across taxa to reduce risk of extinction when natural reproduction is insufficient or no longer possible, making it essential to assess their consequences. title: Comparative Effects of Sponge Gourd and Kidney Bean on Olfactory Preference and Fitness of the Leafminer Liriomyza trifolii
abstract: ABSTRACT Liriomyza trifolii is an invasive pest causing severe damage to crops worldwide. This study examined its olfactory responses and life history traits on sponge gourd and kidney bean to evaluate their potential for ecological pest management. Y‐tube olfactometer assays showed that L. trifolii adults preferred damaged sponge gourd leaves over damaged kidney bean leaves but showed no preference between intact leaves. title: Biogeographic Barriers and Gut Microbiome Turnover Across the Peromyscus maniculatus Species Complex
abstract: Biogeographic barriers are fundamental in shaping the distribution of animals and plants, yet the role of discrete landscape features in constraining microbial dispersal remains poorly understood. Identifying the barriers that partition gut microbial communities is essential for modelling the distribution of hosts and their symbionts across physical space and evolutionary time. title: Combined toxicity of copper–nickel co-exposure on growth, digestive function, antioxidant status, and transporter- and inflammation-related gene expression responses in Oreochromis niloticus , with potential mitigation by watermelon rind ( Citrullus lanatus )
abstract: Abstract Although copper (Cu) is an essential trace element for fish, excessive concentrations can induce toxic effects. In contrast, nickel (Ni) is generally regarded as a non-essential heavy metal with potential toxicity. Collectively, exposure to concentrations exceeding safe thresholds for either metal poses a significant risk to fish health. Therefore, the combined toxicity of Cu–Ni co-exposure in Oreochromis niloticus was assessed with or without supplementation with watermelon rind (WMR). title: Semantic and stylistic transformations of lexemes in the media discourse of the Russo-Ukrainian war: psychological and sociological dimensions of interpersonal and intergroup relations
abstract: The article examines semantic and stylistic transformation of lexemes in modern Ukrainian media discourse during the Russo-Ukrainian war, with particular attention to their pragmatic, psychological and sociological functions. The study focuses on commonly used lexical units from festive and etiquette communication, precedent names from cinema and fiction, biblical and historical nominations, as well as military slang that acquire new meanings and stylistic characteristics in wartime media contexts. title: Local wisdom to agribusiness viability: market empowerment and institutional support among smallholder Pak Liang farmers in Southern Thailand
abstract: This study explores the relationships among local wisdom, market conditions, institutional support, and agribusiness viability among smallholder Pak Liang farmers in southern Thailand. The constructs include local wisdom (farmers’ knowledge), which encompasses production-oriented knowledge of Pak Liang cultivation; market conditions (economic environment); market participation (selling through traders); market empowerment (control over pricing and branding); and institutional support (political/institutional framework), including public programs and coordination. abstract: ABSTRACT Multibody systems with rotating beams serve as critical simplified models of core components in engineering systems; however, existing analytical and numerical methods have limitations in analyzing their complex dynamic behavior. This paper proposes the Finite‐Difference Reduced Multibody System Transfer Matrix Method (FD‐RMSTMM), which innovatively integrates the Reduced Multibody System Transfer Matrix Method (RMSTMM) with the finite‐difference method. abstract: Herein, we report a mild and effective synthesis of steroid-azobenzene molecular switches from steroid sapogenin precursors. The strategy employs a sequence of stereospecific transformations at the C3 position, starting with an iodine-mediated substitution. title: The Ecology of Beech Bark Beetle Mycobiomes: Similar Fungal Composition Despite Host, Elevation and Site Gradients
abstract: Bark beetles form varying associations with fungi, yet the mycobiomes of many deciduous phloem-feeding species are poorly studied and their ecological significance remains underexplored. Here, we used ITS2 metabarcoding to characterize the fungal communities of the beech bark beetles Ernoporicus fagi and Taphrorychus bicolor collected from 61 forest patches across six regions in Germany. title: Wrinkling Pickering Emulsions via Endospore Germination
abstract: Pickering emulsions are stabilized by coating droplet surfaces with solid particles that provide exceptional stability and suppress coalescence. However, these particles are typically inert and lock emulsions into fixed morphologies, limiting their functionality. Creating smart emulsions, which can change their morphology in response to triggers, remains a major challenge. abstract: Abstract The incredible diversity of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) creates a difficult challenge for predicting the steady-state partition ratios indicative of cellular health and function. Many PFAS are amphiphilic surfactants, often with ionic or polar headgroups driving their aqueous solubility and nonpolar tails driving the molecules to interfacial environments. abstract: Understanding how species interactions relate to biodiversity requires linking complex interaction networks to coexistence mechanisms. In diverse communities, interactions span trophic levels and include pairwise and higher‐order effects, yet their relative importance for explaining population dynamics remains poorly understood. We analyse demographic data from 36 plant species exposed to six grasshopper species in a two‐year grassland experiment. title: A preliminary integrated experimental and in Silico assessment of insulating oil leakage effects on soil microbiota and plant germination
abstract: Abstract Leakage of high-voltage insulating oils into soil represents an underexplored source of environmental contamination with potential biological consequences. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of insulating oil (ISOLEC KL 2-3) on soil microbial communities and plant germination under realistic field conditions. Soil samples were collected from an actual leakage site, including both contaminated and uncontaminated soils. abstract: The erosion of the Western-led international order and the resurgence of great power competition in the last decade have led to a more fragmented international system, rendering regionalcooperation more significant. title: Influence Of Vertical Soil Moisture To Root Growth And Biomass Allocation In Acacia Senegal Linn Seedlings From Two Provenances
abstract: Acacia senegal is an important drought-tolerant species, but limited information exists on how vertical soil moisture affects its early growth from different provenances. Uneven moisture distribution in drylands may influence root development and biomass allocation, affecting seedling establishment. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the influence of vertical soil moisture gradients on root growth and biomass allocation in Acacia senegal seedlings from two provenances, to determine best provenance and moisture condition for survival. abstract: Sauropod dinosaurs achieved unprecedented terrestrial gigantism, raising questions about the biomechanical limits of bone under extreme gravitational loads. We estimated static gravitational pressures (Pg) on appendicular cortical bone in neosauropods, including diplodocoids, brachiosaurids, and titanosaurs. We did this by measuring cortical thickness, estimating body masses, and calculating pressures on limb bones. title: Tracing the origin of non-brittle rachis TtBTR1 alleles in wheat
abstract: Abstract The evolution of non-brittle rachises, controlled by the TtBTR1 genes, was a key step during wheat domestication. Here, using k -mer-based approaches applied to a large diversity panel, we refine previous estimates of the geographical and temporal origins of the three known Ttbtr1 loss-of-function alleles and show that they emerged in distinct wild emmer subpopulations. abstract: This study investigates the relationship between knowledge management processes and sustainable earthquake awareness among enterprises operating in the Aydın Efeler Organized Industrial Zone (OIZ), Türkiye. abstract: The global energy transition is expected to substantially increase the deployment of renewable electricity technologies in the European Union (EU), intensifying both consumption and dependency on critical raw materials. Existing studies do not support robust comparisons between electricity generation technologies for decision-making in energy planning and policy. abstract: Aim of the study: To investigate myrrh production and marketing channels in the El-Weyni district of Ethiopia’s Somali Region, identify the roles and relationships of market participants, analyze market structure and practices, and determine factors influencing household-level myrrh supply. Area of the study: The research was conducted in El-Weyni district, an area with substantial but underutilized potential for non-timber forest products (NTFP), particularly gums and resins. abstract: Sugarcane bagasse is a readily available lignocellulosic waste material with potential for use as a renewable reinforcement in polymer composites. abstract: Malaria control has faced repeated challenges due to the emergence and spread of antimalarial resistance. In the present study, temporal trends in Plasmodium falciparum resistance mutations were analyzed using molecular inversion probe sequencing of 625 samples from 11 Kenyan sites (1998-2021), spanning multiple frontline treatments. title: Increased soil organic carbon in organically managed croplands: Evidence from on-farm monitoring in Bavaria (Germany)
abstract: Organic farming is widely associated with environmental benefits and is commonly assumed to promote soil organic carbon (SOC). However, it remains unclear to what extent organic farming leads to higher SOC contents under practical farming conditions. This study compares SOC contents and their temporal changes in organically and conventionally managed arable soils across Bavaria using data from the Bavarian Soil Organic Matter Monitoring Program. abstract: Gene expression signatures (“molecular phenotypes”) are extensively utilized in cancer research. title: Fire risk to U.S. structures nearly triples by mid-century
abstract: Fire is a nationwide crisis, driven by climate change, land use, and continued development into fire-prone landscapes. As these processes blur the boundary between wildland fuels and the built environment, living with fire is becoming a reality for a growing number of communities. We reconstruct fire risk to structures from 1945-2023 and project its evolution through 2060 across the U.S. using high-resolution historical data on area burned, settlement patterns, and fire impacts. title: Regulated but not chromatically codified: a comparative study of cross-regional color grammar in Ming-Qing Paifang
abstract: Paifang in the Ming-Qing ritual architectural system were closely regulated in form and function, but not governed by a unified chromatic code. This paper examines how local color practices emerged within this regulatory gap. Drawing on representative cases from five sites, it combines field records, standardized image-based color sampling, CIELAB metrics, statistical tests, and comparative case analysis to assess three mechanisms: material properties, functional classification, and period-related material change. title: Healthy diets and heart rate variability in a cross-sectional analysis of over 7000 adults attending the Maastricht study
abstract: A limited and conflicting body of evidence exists on the association between adherence to healthy diets and HRV. The current study aimed to investigate the association between the Mediterranean Diet, Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH), Dutch Healthy Diet (DHD), and the Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay (MIND) diet and HRV in adults. title: Robotic versus laparoscopic right hemicolectomy: a retrospective single-center comparative cohort study
abstract: We compared perioperative outcomes after robotic (rRC) and laparoscopic right hemicolectomy (lapRC) and assessed temporal changes in surgical approach and minimally invasive completion. This retrospective cohort included patients operated between January 2023 and March 2026. Primary outcomes were operative duration, open conversion, and 30-day morbidity. title: Evaluation of Rice (Oryza sativa L.) Genotypes under Controlled Submergence Conditions
abstract: The cultivation of rice (Oryza sativa L.) in flood-affected areas of Bangladesh is severely hampered by submergence stress, particularly during the Aman season. This study aimed to identify suitable rice varieties for flood-prone locations and evaluate the submergence resistance of particular genotypes. Eleven advanced breeding lines along with three tolerant check varieties (Binadhan-11, Binadhan-12, and BRRI dhan52) and one susceptible check variety (BRRI dhan28) were used in the study, which was conducted at the Bangladesh Institute of Nuclear Agriculture (BINA) in Mymensingh. title: Evolution and function of genetic polymorphisms in the Helicobacter pylori type IV secretion pilus protein CagL in gastric carcinogenesis
abstract: BACKGROUND: The cytotoxin-associated genes (cag) type IV secretion system (T4SS) of the gastric pathogen Helicobacter pylori constitutes a key determinant in gastric cancer (GC) development. The CagL protein represents a VirB5 ortholog that acts as a signalling factor at the surface of the T4SS pilus, which facilitates binding to host target cells to inject T4SS substrates such as the CagA oncoprotein and ADP-heptose. title: Integrative multi-omics analysis identifies molecular signatures associated with high-risk of systemic reactions to honeybee venom and olive pollen
abstract: Abstract Background Disease manifestation in IgE-mediated allergies is highly heterogeneous, partly due to the distinct exposure patterns of different allergens. High-risk of systemic reactions to immunotherapy is characterized by molecular patterns that are still not well defined. Methods Two patient cohorts, one of bee venom and one of olive pollen allergic patients, were recruited and stratified into two groups, according to the risk of developing systemic reactions (low-risk or high-risk). title: Inflammatory biomarker profiles and their associations with Nordic dietary habits and metabolic outcomes in adults affected by MAFLD
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is commonly accompanied by chronic low-grade inflammation. The Aggregate Index of Systemic Inflammation (AISI) is an accessible inflammatory marker, while the Healthy Nordic diet may have favorable metabolic effects. This study investigated relationships among AISI, healthy Nordic Food Index (HNDI), and metabolic health in adults with MAFLD. In this cross-sectional study, 253 adults with MAFLD were evaluated. title: Sawdust biochar as a dual cement and sand substitute for strength‐optimized and low‐carbon mortar with life‐cycle benefits
abstract: The building industry is a major contributor to global CO 2 emissions, highlighting the need to develop low-carbon cement-based products. Biochar emerges as a promising additive for cementitious composites, owing primarily to its inherent capacity for long-term carbon sequestration, chemical stability, and sustainability benefits. title: Controlled-temperature microwave drying of whole silver rasbora (Rasbora argyrotaenia): Drying kinetics and apparent moisture diffusivity
abstract: Silver rasbora ( Rasbora argyrotaenia ) is commonly consumed whole and presents a heterogeneous anatomical matrix for drying. This study characterized moisture removal during controlled-setpoint microwave drying at 55, 60, 65, and 70°C using dry-basis moisture histories, five thin-layer models, and a simplified Fickian slab analysis. title: SELLER RELIGIOUS IDENTITY AS A HALAL SIGNAL IN INFORMAL FOOD MARKETS: A SIGNALING-THEORY PERSPECTIVE FROM INDONESIA
abstract: Purpose: This study examines whether sellers' religious identity functions as an observable halal signal in informal food markets when Muslim consumers have limited access to formal, verifiable halal information. Drawing on Signaling Theory, the study conceptually investigates how seller religious identity shapes consumers' perceived halalness and consumer trust in the informal food market of Tembilahan, Indonesia. title: Participatory assessment of potato landrace diversity and conservation vulnerability in northern Peru
abstract: Crop genetic diversity is fundamental to the resilience and adaptive capacity of agricultural systems. However, the conservation of native potato varieties is increasingly under threat. This study assessed the diversity currently maintained, varietal vulnerability, locally lost varieties, and farmer-perceived factors associated with varietal loss in 12 high-Andean communities of Cajamarca, Peru. title: Negative Role of the Receptor‐Like Kinase GbMIK2 in Regulating Cotton Verticillium Wilt Resistance
abstract: The leucine-rich repeat receptor-like kinases (LRR-RLKs) function in multifaceted processes in plant growth, reproduction, cell differentiation and immunity. However, the role of the RLK gene MIK2 (Male discoverer 1-Interacting receptor-like Kinase 2) in regulating cotton resistance to Verticillium dahliae remains unclear. title: Envenomation Leads to Venom Protein Reduction and a Recovery Period in Bumblebee Workers
abstract: ABSTRACT The evolution and deployment of venom systems in animals have been central to their ecological success, though not without costs. For social bees, venom plays a key role in nest defence; yet for species such as honeybees, the act of stinging generally leads to death. However, for other social bee species such as bumblebees, where stinging is not apparently fatal, it raises the question of what, if any, are the consequences associated with venom usage (envenomation). title: Embedding research in Living Labs: insights from a case comparison of knowledge co-production processes
abstract: Abstract Increased focus on collaborative change-making in Living Labs creates a need to better understand how knowledge co-production enables experimental investigation of and engagement with sustainability challenges. Tracing how knowledge co-production in Living Labs supports learning processes beyond local contexts is equally important. This study uses a multiple-step reflection process to compare four workshop series about improving water and landscape governance within Living Labs in Sweden, Germany, Finland, and Latvia. title: Sequencing-based quantification of Erwinia amylovora strains identifies contribution of strain × strain × host interactions underlying apple fire blight severity
abstract: Multiple pathogen strains coexist in the field, and their interactions with host genotypes can strongly affect disease severity and management. Fire blight, caused by the bacterium Erwinia amylovora , is one of the most devastating bacterial diseases of apple and pear worldwide. The interaction between the genetics and phenological stage of the host, the genetics of pathogen strains, and environmental conditions results in outbreaks and changes the severity of the fire blight infection. title: Global assessment of flood-related environmental hazards and dengue risks: the roles of population exposure, duration, and societal resilience
abstract: Population flood exposure and flood duration may have distinct associations with dengue transmission. We analysed a country-month ecological panel using negative binomial models with a log link, population offset and country, year and month fixed effects. The main analysis included 4,840 country-months from 125 countries during April 2010–August 2025. title: THE AXIOLOGICAL PROFILE OF THE AESTHETIC-COSMOLOGICAL DOMAIN OF EVALUATION IN OLD ENGLISH
abstract: The article reconstructs the axiological profile of the aesthetic-cosmological domain of evaluation in Old English texts (7th–11th centuries) and explains its distinctive features. The domain is treated not as a theme or a stylistic genre but as a field of experience, an environment in which a language community regularly assigns a particular value profile to what is evaluated. title: Hsa-miR-141-3p as a modulator of ZBTB16 expression in cervical cancer pathogenesis
abstract: Abstract Objective This research investigated the function of Zinc Finger and BTB Domain Containing 16 (ZBTB16) in cervical cancer (CESC), along with its regulatory mechanisms linked to specific miRNAs. Methods ZBTB16 expression in CESC was explored using the GEPIA2 database. ZBTB16-associated miRNAs were predicted and their expression patterns investigated using the R language, based on the CESC dataset from the TCGA database. title: Seasonal Variation in Milk Quality and Somatic Cell Count of Friesian Crossbred Cows in Southern Highlands, Tanzania
abstract: Seasonal variations in environmental conditions and forage availability can substantially influence milk composition and udder health, yet information from dairy production systems in the Southern Highlands of Tanzania remains limited. This study evaluated the effects of season on physicochemical milk quality parameters and somatic cell count (SCC) in Friesian crossbred cows managed under a semi-intensive production system at the Tanzania Livestock Research Institute (TALIRI) Uyole Dairy Farm. title: Multispectral and Computational Modeling Analysis of the Kinetic Inhibition and Binding Properties of Inonotus obliquus Extract on Xanthine Oxidase
abstract: Xanthine oxidase (XO) is a key enzyme in uric acid (UA) metabolism. The extracts of Inonotus obliquus (I. obliquus) have the potential to inhibit the activity of XO. In this study, the contents of protocatechuic aldehyde (PAH) and protocatechuic acid (PA) from I. obliquus were quantitatively analyzed using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). abstract: Existing microgrid modeling often ignores the electrical mismatch in the modules and obstructions in the vicinity, creating unrealistic estimates of energy production. To fill this gap, this study combines weather data from Meteonorm 8.1 with PVsyst for accurate 3D spatial shading analysis and Hybrid Optimization Model for Electric Renewables Pro for life-cycle cost optimization of an off-grid solar-wind-battery system in Dibo, Ethiopia. title: Screening of nearly equivalent component groups and mechanism investigation of Si Miao San for treating rheumatoid arthritis
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic systemic disease involving synovitis, cartilage damage, and bone erosion. Si Miao San (SMS), a traditional Chinese formula, shows anti‑RA potential, but its complex composition and mechanisms remain unclear. We developed a novel systems pharmacology strategy combining node importance scoring and Component Contribution Weight (CCW) modeling to identify the nearly equivalent component group (NECG) from SMS. title: iota‐Carrageenan/Psyllium Composite Hydrogel for Cationic and Anionic Dye Removal From Wastewater
abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents the in‐air synthesis of a novel hydrogel through chemical crosslinking of iota‐carrageenan (ι‐CG) and psyllium (PSY) using epichlorohydrin (EPH) as the crosslinking agent, aimed at the efficient removal of the dyes Crystal Violet (CV) and Fuchsin Acid (FA). title: Bacterial sialidases subvert the complement system through desialylation
abstract: Bacterial sialidases (neuraminidases) are widely studied virulence factors, yet their impact on the complement system, a central component of innate immunity, remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the effects of six sialidases from five human pathogens, including Bacteroides fragilis, Clostridium perfringens, Tannerella forsythia, Treponema denticola, and Vibrio cholerae on complement immunity using an integrated approach combining genetics, biochemistry, glycobiology, mass spectrometry, and structural biology. abstract: ABSTRACT In today's rapidly changing and highly competitive environment, internationalization has become a strategic necessity. It is no longer merely a source of competitive advantage, but a fundamental requirement for organizational survival. This need is particularly pronounced in the food industry, which faces stringent quality requirements and growing pressure to comply with international regulations. title: Green Synthesis of Multifunctional EA‐CuO Nanoparticles Using Elytraria acaulis (L.f.) Lindau Leaf Extract: Assessment of Antimicrobial, Antioxidant, and Antidiabetic Activities
abstract: ABSTRACT The increasing demand for sustainable nanotechnology has encouraged eco‐friendly approaches for nanoparticle synthesis. In this study, copper oxide nanoparticles (EA‐CuO NPs) were synthesized using Elytraria acaulis (L.f.) Lindau leaf extract as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent. The nanoparticles were characterized using UV–Vis, FTIR, SEM, TEM, EDX, XRD, DLS, and zeta‐potential analyses. title: A Review of Starch‐Based Bioplastics From Plant and Agro‐Based Sources: Extraction, Characterization, and Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT The persistence of nonbiodegradable petrochemical plastics, which can endure for centuries, poses ecological challenges. Their accumulation and toxic emissions during disposal contribute to plastic pollution, an escalating environmental and public health concern. Starch‐based bioplastics are promising because they are low‐cost, recyclable, and available from plant sources and agricultural waste, including potato, corn, rice, wheat, cassava, banana peel, jackfruit seed, mango seed, avocado seed, and lucuma seed. title: Contrasting Roles of Geothermal Energy and Fossil Fuels in Indonesia's Carbon Emissions
abstract: The transition toward renewable energy is essential for improving environmental quality and mitigating climate change, particularly in fossil fuel-dependent emerging economies. Indonesia has substantial geothermal energy potential, yet its energy mix remains heavily reliant on fossil fuels, highlighting the importance of assessing geothermal energy's contribution to carbon emission reduction. This study investigates the dynamic impacts of geothermal energy in comparison with coal, oil, and gas on environmental quality in Indonesia, proxied by CO2 emissions from 1990Q1 to 2024Q4. title: Characterizing gas diffusivity, air permeability, and extracellular enzyme activity in an early‐stage comparison of conventional and regenerative pasture
abstract: Abstract Regenerative pasture is an emerging agricultural framework characterized by high forage diversity, adaptive grazing, and reduced external inputs. However, early‐stage soil structural transitions and associated microbial activities remain unclear, particularly given the higher spatial variability expected in these systems. abstract: The P* index has been commonly referred to as the “isolation” index in segregation studies because it isolates (more generally, separates) the distributional pattern of a particular group from other mutually exclusive groups. Since the P* index has been conceived to possess useful mathematical properties for capturing the exposure dimension of residential segregation, its spatial versions have been developed by different researchers. title: Mechanisms by Which Lipid-Lowering Agents Modulate the Lipid-Inflammation Circuit and Their Stratified Clinical Use in Rheumatic Immune-Mediated Diseases
abstract: Rheumatic immune-mediated diseases, including rheumatoid arthritis (RA), systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and spondyloarthritis, combine persistent inflammation with increased cardiovascular risk. Inflammation alters lipoprotein production, remodeling, function, and clearance, explaining why low or apparently normal cholesterol concentrations may coexist with accelerated atherosclerosis. abstract: ABSTRACT BK polyomavirus (BKPyV) and chronic latent DNA virus infections frequently reactivate after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), where they contribute to major complications in humans with limited options for prevention or treatment. Mauritian cynomolgus macaques (MCMs; Macaca fascicularis ) serve as an important animal model for transplantation research due to their limited major histocompatibility complex diversity. abstract: ABSTRACT Aim The aim of this prospective clinical study was to investigate whether patient history, preoperative clinical findings and intraoperative parameters, including pulpal biomarker profiles, are associated with the outcome of vital pulp therapy (VPT) in mature permanent teeth and to evaluate their potential prognostic value. title: Fish welfare: MS-222 sedation in juvenile Xenocypris davidi transport, dose screening, and exploratory gill transcriptomic profiling
abstract: Transport stress remains a significant challenge in aquaculture. To optimize sedation protocols, we evaluated MS-222 (tricaine methanesulfonate) for juvenile Xenocypris davidi by combining behavioral dose screening (32–50 mg L⁻¹) with gill transcriptomics and histology analysis. title: Polydopamine-modified hyaluronic acid hydrogel incorporating Bi2S3 for photothermal antibacterial therapy and wound healing
abstract: The development of smart wound dressings that combat bacterial infection and promote tissue regeneration remains a clinical challenge. Here, we report a chemically modified hyaluronic acid-based hydrogel (Bi 2 S 3 /PDA-HA) with injectability, self-healing, and tissue adhesion, enabled by dopamine functionalization of the hyaluronic acid backbone. abstract: ABSTRACT Background Goats are vital for livelihoods and food security in tropical regions such as Ethiopia. However, poor‐quality feed, especially during dry seasons, limits their growth, health and overall productivity. Objective To evaluate the effect of supplementing Terminalia brownii tree leaves on growth performance, hematobiochemical profile and methane (CH 4 ) emission of goats. title: Factors influencing the adoption of e-scooters for sustainable tourism in cultural heritage sites
abstract: Cultural heritage sites represent invaluable repositories of human history and collective memory, offering visitors immersive experiences beyond conventional tourism. However, the growing intensity of global tourism necessitates sustainable strategies to minimize environmental impacts while enriching visitor engagement. In this context, e-scooters have emerged as an innovative micro-mobility solution, providing low-carbon, accessible, and flexible transportation aligned with sustainable tourism principles. abstract: ABSTRACT Contemporary governance is increasingly characterized by coordinated engagement among diverse actors in addressing sustainability challenges under the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), where network governance strategies play an important role in developing collaborative capacity. This study investigates the role of network governance strategies in enhancing partnership outcomes for implementing SDGs, with a particular focus on SDG 15.3 combating desertification and restoring degraded land. title: Common transcriptional changes in the brain during hibernation and Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Hibernation demands rapid brain adaptations, involving cycles of reduced metabolic rate during torpor, followed by brief periods of arousal. Previous studies show hibernation induces a drastic increase in Tau hyperphosphorylation, but a mechanistic connection to disease remains unclear. Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing on hippocampi of golden hamsters, we unveil large transcriptional shifts across the hibernation cycle in all cell types, especially glia. title: Hierarchical Porous Silica Nanoparticles for Interfacial Engineering and Thermomechanical Enhancement of Basalt Fiber Composites
abstract: Fiber-reinforced polymer composites (FRPCs) are pivotal in aerospace and automotive sectors; however, their limited thermal stability under extreme conditions remains a challenge. title: A place-based perspective on local wind energy acceptance: the role of place attachment, motivations, and social norms
abstract: Wind energy is widely supported, yet specific projects encounter local contestation. Moving beyond NIMBY-based interpretations, this research examined social acceptance of wind energy as a place-based and socially situated judgment. abstract: This study examines income convergence across Turkish provinces over the period 2004-2023 by combining traditional convergence analysis with spatial econometric methods. Both unconditional and conditional convergence models are estimated using provincial data. abstract: This study investigates the environmental, economic, and technological determinants of sustainability in ASEAN and SAARC using panel data techniques, including FGLS, PCSE, Fixed-Effect OLS, and two-step System-GMM, alongside quantile regression. Sustainability is assessed through two complementary indicators: renewable energy consumption (REC), capturing energy transition, and adjusted net savings excluding emission damage (ANS), reflecting long-run resource-based sustainability. abstract: Abstract Protein bioconjugates possess widespread utility as potential therapeutics necessitating an expansion of the chemical toolbox used for their production. One particularly promising methodology is the application of noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) as a route to produce homogeneous and rationally engineered conjugates. abstract: Global food price volatility threatens food security, yet how international shocks amplify differentially across developing regions, and why food prices structurally diverge from general inflation, remain poorly understood. This study examines global food price dynamics and sub-regional transmission patterns using monthly Consumer Price Index data for 24 world regions across Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Americas (2001–2025), with particular attention to African and Asian sub-regions. abstract: Abstract Control of magnetic order through optical manipulation of orbital states can be realized in a wide range of materials, including insulators. abstract: Abstract Reproduction is a core feature of life, yet it is still unclear why sex determination systems are conserved for hundreds of millions of years in some taxa but repeatedly turn over in others. abstract: Combating the spread of arboviruses in the Amazon relies on understanding the diversity of Culicidae, particularly potential vectors. abstract: Piezoelectric nanogenerators (PENGs) are electromechanical energy-conversion devices constructed from piezoelectric materials. They convert physiological motion, local tissue deformation, or externally applied mechanical stimuli into localized electrical signals and have attracted considerable interest in self-powered neural interventions. title: Effects of dairy manure acidification on soil pH and nitrogen transformation processes in silt loam and loamy sand soils
abstract: Abstract Manure acidification is increasingly recognized as an effective strategy to reduce ammonia (NH 3 ) volatilization and curb methane (CH 4 ) emissions. However, its implications on soil nitrogen (N) dynamics following land application in agricultural soils remain underexplored. abstract: Abstract Universities generate substantial volumes of paper waste, yet much of this valuable resource remains underutilized despite increasing commitments to circular economy and sustainable campus initiatives. Paper recycling within university campuses has the potential to reduce solid waste generation, lowering paper procurement costs, and supporting sustainability-focused education. Here, we identify the tryptophan-derived microbial metabolite indole-3-propionic acid (IPA) as a direct modulator of hepatic glucose production. abstract: ABSTRACT Larvae of Helicoverpa armigera (Hübner) (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae) can cause complete defoliation of Lagenaria siceraria (Molina) Standl., commonly known as bottle gourd, resulting in substantial yield losses in India. abstract: Conventional enhanced oil recovery (EOR) methods often exhibit reduced efficiency under high-temperature and high-salinity (HTHS) reservoir conditions, necessitating sustainable and high-performance alternatives. abstract: Abstract Variability of greenhouse gas (GHG) fluxes and emissions among replicates in a study area can have an impact on results depending on the statistical tools used to assess significant differences among fixed effects. The objective of this study was to assess the effect of site and time (i.e., date) and the variability within and between sites on soil GHG (carbon dioxide [CO 2 ], methane [CH 4 ], and nitrous oxide [N 2 O]) fluxes and emissions from two fields under the same management practices during late‐season corn ( Zea mays ) production in Mississippi. title: When carbon counts differ: the complexities of biogenic carbon accounting in BECCUS and why accounting choices matter
abstract: Bioenergy with Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (BECCUS) is an important pathway towards net-zero and net-negative emissions. Its mitigation potential depends on net atmospheric CO2 removal into durable storage after accounting for system-wide emissions and removals. However, lifecycle assessment, national greenhouse gas inventories and carbon-market frameworks apply differing accounting approaches, producing divergent mitigation estimates. title: CHARACTER ANONYMITY IN THE DIALOGI OF SULPICIUS SEVERUS
abstract: Abstract In approximately 403 c.e. Sulpicius Severus, a Gallo-Roman litterateur, composed his Dialogi , following on from his hagiographic tour de force, the Vita sancti Martini. Anonymous characters feature throughout the three books. This article argues that the dialogue genre is ideally positioned to interrogate the dynamics of character anonymity. title: Investigating the effects of dexmedetomidine in cecal ligation and puncture‑induced septic rats
abstract: Sepsis is a leading cause of mortality, and ferroptosis has been implicated in sepsis-associated organ injury. Dexmedetomidine (DEX), an α2-adrenergic agonist with anti-inflammatory properties, may modulate this process. We examined whether DEX protects against cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)– induced septic lung injury and alters ferroptosis-associated markers in rats. title: Timing matters: Maternal stress and mental health symptoms from pregnancy to postpartum in shaping infant development
abstract: Maternal perceived stress, mental health, and physiological dysregulation during pregnancy can alter the intrauterine environment, shaping infant development through fetal programming processes. Nonetheless, few longitudinal studies in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) have jointly examined psychological and biological factors in relation to infant outcomes. This longitudinal study followed 146 Pakistani mother-infant dyads at early to mid-gestation (T1), mid- to late gestation (T2), and postpartum (T3). title: Microbiome structure, function, and drivers across different soil groups in an agricultural region of Serbia
abstract: Abstract. Soil is the largest reservoir of biodiversity, with distinct physical, chemical, and biological properties. Microorganisms play essential roles in soil formation and fertility. This study aimed to analyze the microbiomes of three selected soil groups in an important agricultural region of Vojvodina (Serbia) by 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding and explore their association with soil properties. title: Migration and the Geography of Life Expectancy: Selective Sorting and Spatial Dependence Across 172 Countries
abstract: ABSTRACT International migration has grown rapidly in recent decades, yet its relationship with population health is difficult to disentangle from the economic, structural and geographic characteristics of the places migrants move to. This study examines whether international migration is associated with population‐level life expectancy after accounting for confounding and the data's spatial structure. title: Saccadic suppression enhances saliency of ecologically relevant stimuli in the zebrafish optic tectum
abstract: Saccadic suppression, a reduction in visual sensitivity around the time of rapid eye movements, is well-documented in primate psychophysics, but its mechanisms and functions remain debated. Here, we use zebrafish to trace the origins of saccadic suppression, and we demonstrate how saccadic suppression selectively enhances the visual salience of ecologically relevant stimuli. abstract: This paper extends the concept of regional resilience to address economic inactivity as a key economic outcome, and to consider health and demography as sources of regional vulnerability and resilience. Economic inactivity in Great Britain rose sharply following Brexit and the COVID-19 pandemic, but in geographically uneven ways. abstract: Hybrid seed production in chili is more efficient when using male-sterile plants. abstract: Hides and skins are important livestock by-products and the principal raw materials for Ethiopia’s leather and leather-products industries. Their value, however, depends not only on the number of animals slaughtered but also on how promptly and correctly the pelts are removed, preserved, stored and transported before tanning. abstract: African horse sickness (AHS) is a severe, vector-borne viral disease of equids associated with high mortality and substantial socioeconomic losses. This study aimed to describe the temporal, seasonal, and spatial distribution of reported AHS outbreaks and assess vaccination coverage in North Shewa Zone, Ethiopia. abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is the most common heart disease of cats and is conventionally characterised by its ventricular phenotype. The clinical events that determine quality and duration of life in affected cats, however, are atrial in their proximate pathophysiology. Existing outage cost estimates are largely derived from mainland U.S. data and short-duration interruptions, limiting their applicability to prolonged outages in islanded systems. title: Spatial pattern of soil properties and earthworm communities in oak- based traditional wood pastures of Romania
abstract: Abstract Solitary trees such as oak ( Quercus spp.) play a central ecological role in wood pastures. They alter the surrounding soil and abiotic conditions, with largely unclear consequences for the soil fauna such as earthworms. We investigated how solitary oak trees alter soil properties and whether those alterations impact earthworm communities. abstract: Serious games teach players skills or knowledge applicable outside the game, but the choice of game mechanics may influence the underlying perceptual, memory, and cognitive processes involved, potentially affecting quality of learning. abstract: Soil fertility depletion caused by declining organic matter and imbalanced nutrient inputs is a major constraint to barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) production in the Ethiopian highlands. A field experiment was conducted during the 2022/2023 main cropping season at Holeta Agricultural Research Center, Ethiopia, to evaluate the effects of integrating nitrogen fertilizer, vermicompost, and farmyard manure on soil properties and barley productivity under a randomized complete block design with three replications. title: UAV-based CWSI estimation for tomato water stress monitoring
abstract: Thermal infrared (TIR) imaging has been widely applied as a prominent remote sensing technique to assess plant water conditions. Recent advances in TIR imaging, primarily the use of high-resolution TIR cameras mounted on unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and their integration with water-sensitive indicators, have further enhanced its applicability for crop water stress monitoring. abstract: This study presents a low-temperature chemical recycling process for glass fibre-reinforced recyclamine epoxy composites, in which the epoxy matrix was solubilised, allowing the reinforcement materials to be retrieved and recovered at full fabric scale. abstract: Strawberries are valued for their sweet-sour taste, color, and aroma. Dynamic changes in aromatic compounds affect aroma characteristics across ripening, storage, and processing, often leading to aroma loss or deterioration. abstract: Abstract Racial residential segregation constitutes a central dimension of urban inequalities, as it shapes how population groups are distributed across the territory and how they access infrastructure, public services, and opportunities. This article analyzes racial segregation in Salvador’s neighborhoods, comparing the 2010 and 2022 Demographic Censuses of the Brazilian Bureau of Statistics. abstract: Liquid crystal monomers (LCMs), released from electronic products and e-waste, can enter agroecosystems and accumulate in edible crops, raising concerns about crop health and food safety. title: Evaluating tree susceptibility to bark stripping by Asiatic black bears through multi-scale analysis and field surveys addressing time-varying environmental factors
abstract: Bear bark-stripping presents a significant global challenge, resulting in considerable timber loss and forest ecosystem degradation. While tree attributes, such as size and nutritional content, have been identified as determinants of damage occurrence, previous research often overlooks the spatial hierarchy in bear behavior and the temporal disparity between damage and field observation, potentially leading to spurious associations and an underestimation of risk factors. abstract: Semi-dry grasslands are among the most species-rich ecosystems in Europe. abstract: Roses hold significant ornamental, economic, and cultural value, particularly for their diverse fragrances. Among the volatiles, 1,3,5-trimethoxybenzene (TMB), unique to ancient Chinese roses, contributes to their tea-like scent. Despite its significance, the molecular mechanisms regulating TMB synthesis remain poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Resident songbirds in seasonal environments are adapted to fluctuating conditions and show marked phenotypic flexibility of metabolic rates. abstract: Bioorthogonal chemistry enables selective reactions within complex biological environments. Visible‐light photocatalysis expands this toolbox by generating carbon‐centered radicals through single‐electron transfer under mild conditions, enabling selective bond‐forming transformations with spatiotemporal control. title: Influence of Sustainable Agricultural Practices on Microbial Aspects of Soil
abstract: Abstract Soil is a non-renewable natural resource essential for supporting plants, animals, and microorganisms. The intensification of conventional agriculture has substantially affected soil health, including its microbial component. This review evaluates how sustainable agricultural practices, including crop rotation, intercropping, cover cropping, organic amendments, and agroforestry, influence microbial aspects of soil health, with particular emphasis on microbial biomass, diversity, community composition, and functions related to nutrient cycling. abstract: Abstract Overshoot scenarios, in which global temperatures peak and then decline through emission reductions and CO 2 removal, are increasingly central to climate policy as we are already approaching 1.5 °C warming. abstract: Iran is expected to experience increasingly severe economic consequences from climate change, given that its annual precipitation is less than one-third of the global average. This study investigates the potential impacts of climate change on economic output across different sectors of the Iranian economy using a dynamic input-output (IO) modeling framework. abstract: In Nigeria, tomato production plays a major role in food security and income generation for farmers and traders Northern Nigeria. abstract: Abstract Winter wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) in Eastern Canada is under increasing pressure from stresses associated with climate change. Breeding programs must increase efficiency to keep pace with these changes, and marker‐assisted selection (MAS) remains an efficient tool to retain or introgress favorable alleles of key traits and improve their genetic gains. abstract: Influenza A/H5Nx viruses continue to diversify and undergo gene reassortment as they infect avian and mammalian hosts worldwide. abstract: Abstract White lupin ( Lupinus albus L.) is a high‐protein and nitrogen‐fixing leguminous plant with potential in rainfed systems, although approaches to maximize its yield, seed quality, and safety of quinolizidine alkaloids (QAs) remain inadequate in subhumid South Asian regions. title: Deciphering salinity tolerance during germination in bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L) through systematic phenotypic screening
abstract: Wheat is the major staple crop contributing about 20% of global calorie intake and ranks second to maize in worldwide production. It is vital to increase the production of wheat by about 70% by 2050 to feed world population. However, soil salinity is a critical constraint that impairs plant growth and development during germination stage. Therefore, identifying salt-tolerant bread wheat genotypes at germination stages is critical for mitigating yield losses. title: Integrating soil carbon and nitrogen dynamics into a tipping point framework: Weak land-use signals, strong climate forcing in southwestern Amazonia
abstract: Deforestation and intensifying extreme climatic events are reshaping ecosystem functioning globally and increasing the risk of crossing tipping points in social-ecological systems. To understand the sensitivity of key soil properties to these stressors, we assessed soil organic carbon (SOC) and total nitrogen (TN) along a west-to-east precipitation gradient in southwestern Amazonia (1800-3980 mm; mean annual precipitation: MAP). title: Southern Solutions to Fill Gaps in Global Development and Climate Finance: How the World’s Most Vulnerable Countries Are Deepening a Fourth Wave of Public Banking
abstract: This article addresses the question of what financial resources are available to the world’s most climate exposed and vulnerable countries, and how this fits within and contributes to the broader South-South financial landscape. It presents original empirical data and institutional analysis to show new trends where emerging Southern-led public banks and financial institutions are deepening and broadening the global financial architecture, and why they feel compelled to do it.
