title: Microbial Siderophores for Sustainable Agriculture: Stress Tolerance, Biocontrol, Mechanism, and Omics Integration
abstract: Microbial siderophores play an important role in improving plant tolerance to abiotic and biotic stresses. Beyond iron acquisition, they support plant health by regulating oxidative stress, chelating toxic metals, and mediating beneficial plant–microbe interactions. This review highlights the role of siderophore-producing microbes in mitigating salinity, drought, alkaline stress, and metal toxicity, as well as in the improvement of nutrient solubilization and uptake. abstract: Abstract Four sets of dual-responsive statistical copolymers are synthesized from N,N-dimethylacrylamide and acrylamide comonomers bearing photoresponsive 4-aminoazobenzene (AzBn) side groups linked by various amino acid spacers. title: Comprehensive analysis of the therapeutic effect of lipid-coated hybrid nanoparticles for breast cancer therapy
abstract: Abstract: Background: Nanoparticles have gained considerable attention as versatile platforms for the diagnosis and treatment of different diseases, particularly cancer. Lipid-coated hybrid nanoparticles (LCHNPs), comprising a polymeric core enveloped by a lipid shell, offer improved targeting and potential solutions for multidrug-resistant cancers. Objective: To develop and preclinically evaluate a dual-drug LCHNP system co-delivering Tamoxifen and Gemifloxacin for enhanced breast cancer therapy. title: Cave‐Dwelling Planariidae in Dinaric Karst Exhibit Differing Levels of Cave Trait Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT The Dinaric karst encompasses a network of over 10,000 caves and represents one of the world's most important subterranean biodiversity hotspots. It is inhabited by remarkably diverse and often endemic species, including planarian flatworms. Although cave planarians have long been known from the region, they have not yet been investigated using an integrative approach, and their evolutionary relationships with surface‐dwelling relatives remain unresolved. title: Topographic gradient as a determinant of phylogenetic diversity patterns in the understory of a neotropical forest
abstract: Abstract Topography is a well-known driver of changes in plant community organization in the tropics. However, we have a limited understanding of how the evolutionary history of component species shapes the organization of these plant communities along topographic gradients. We investigated how the phylogenetic structure of an understory plant community changes along a topographic gradient. We expect closely related species to occupy higher elevations along the gradient, leading to clustering, and to observe overdispersion at lower elevations. title: Constraining binary alpine karst spring recharge using Ensemble Rainfall-Runoff analysis (ERRA) and artificial tracer tests
abstract: Karst systems sustain a substantial share of global freshwater supply, yet their internal discharge dynamics are difficult to characterize because conduit networks are often inaccessible to direct observation. Fluorescent tracer tests can quantify recharge-area-to-spring connections and travel times, but only under the conditions at the time of testing. Rainfall-runoff deconvolution methods such as Ensemble Rainfall-Runoff Analysis (ERRA) offer a complementary, data-driven approach resolving nonlinear, non-stationary discharge responses across catchment wetness and precipitation intensity. title: Using topography to estimate the productivity of Retrophyllum rospigliosii plantations: a case study in the Colombian Andes
abstract: Abstract Despite the great diversity of tree species in the Neotropics, most commercial reforestation efforts in this region continue to rely on exotic species. Over the past few decades, with the aim of promoting the use of native species such as Retrophyllum rospigliosii , experimental plantations have been established in the tropical Andes to assess their viability for commercial reforestation projects. title: Development and Validation of a Measurement-Based Fatigue Load Model for Railway Bridges
abstract: Accurate fatigue assessment of existing railway bridges requires traffic load models that are both conservative and representative of actual operating conditions. This study develops and validates a measurement-based fatigue load model using four years of railway traffic data recorded by a Track Performance Detection System on a major mixed-traffic corridor in Hungary. title: Future of rare and endangered medicinal material substitutions: key strategies, challenges, and prospects
abstract: Owing to the combined impacts of anthropogenic and natural factors, rare and endangered traditional medicinal materials are experiencing progressive depletion, thereby necessitating urgent acceleration of research into viable substitutes. This article comprehensively reviews policies and strategies governing the development of substitutes for rare and endangered traditional medicinal materials, with particular emphasis on critically evaluating the respective advantages and limitations of natural versus artificial replacement strategies. title: Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Brain Network Dynamics Reveal Cognitive Function Variability During Acute High-Altitude Exposure
abstract: Abstract After acute exposure to high altitude (HA), the mechanism underlying hemodynamics-related cerebral function remains unclear and comprehensive and systematic studies are lacking. In this paper, functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) was used to characterize cerebral activation and brain network dynamics during acute exposure to HA. Thirty healthy volunteers were recruited and divided equally into two groups, the HA group and the low-altitude (LA) control group, to perform a resting-state experiment. institutions: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

title: Climate Events and Life Satisfaction: The Role of Migration in Rural Bangladesh
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate change is increasingly displacing rural populations, and migration may reduce economic losses from environmental stress. However, climate events and migration can also entail social and psychological costs overlooked by economic measures. This paper examines the relationship between climate events and life satisfaction in Bangladesh and whether migration mediates this relationship. title: MR imaging and spectroscopy reveals metabolic changes in glioblastoma driven by treatment with temozolomide and lonidamine
abstract: Abstract Resistance to temozolomide (TMZ) limits the efficacy of treatment in glioblastoma (GBM) and it is fuelled by a metabolic reprogramming of the cancer cells. Lonidamine (LND), a glycolytic and mitochondrial inhibitor, was used in combination with TMZ to evaluate metabolic and microstructural changes in a GBM model. title: Multiple mineral chemistry records the melt-fluid evolution history and rare-metal enrichment of the Murong spodumene pegmatite deposit, SW China
abstract: Rare metals are becoming increasingly important in the modern world due to their irreplaceable roles in strategic sectors and are largely extracted from highly evolved granites or pegmatites. Nevertheless, the precise mechanisms governing their enrichment remain poorly constrained. The Murong deposit, located in southwestern China, reserves abundant Li-Ta-Nb-(Be-Sn) resources within LCT (Li-Cs-Ta) pegmatites and adjacent altered wall rocks, making it an ideal natural laboratory for investigating enrichment processes. title: A framework for spatially quantifying household-level water-energy-food security: Application to South Africa
abstract: To be secure of Water-Energy-Food (WEF) resources is crucial for individual and public health and well-being, livelihoods and, ultimately, achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). While national level WEF security can be achieved, spatial inequalities exist due to the variations in local socio-economic and biophysical environments that determine WEF security. title: Effects of emissions labels on consumer choice of lower-emission flights
abstract: Air travel generates disproportionate greenhouse gas emissions, without viable supply-side mitigation options. Demand-side measures, such as emissions information at the point-of-sale, are thus gaining interest. In a pre-registered experiment with a nationally representative sample ( N = 1,000), we tested whether current emissions labelling systems shift consumers towards lower-emission flights. title: Psychiatric Pharmacotherapy and the Problem of Mechanistic Validation: A Critical Review
abstract: Psychiatric pharmacotherapy is among the most widely practiced and epistemically contested domains of contemporary medicine. Antidepressant consumption has risen significantly across OECD countries over the past decade, yet the neurobiological hypotheses used to justify these prescriptions remain unvalidated. This critical review examines the principal psychiatric drug classes, including antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, benzodiazepines and related anxiolytics, and psychostimulants. abstract: Abstract Cryptochromes and photolyases are blue-light-sensitive flavoproteins that generally bind flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) and have distinct functions. title: Biosynthesis of selenium nanoparticles with orange peel waste in microwave: characterization, and spectral properties
abstract: Abstract The objective of this study was to reuse agroindustrial waste from orange peels to obtain an orange peel aqueous extract (OPEa), used in the biosynthesis and characterization of selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs). The OPEa acted as a reducing and stabilizing agent in the synthesis of SeNPs, due to its polyphenolic compounds, such as flavonoids, alkaloids, terpenoids, and coumarins, identified by UHPLC-HRMS/MS. abstract: : Gene therapy holds considerable promise for treating a wide range of intractable diseases through the modification of specific genes. However, gene therapeutics such as plasmid DNA, messenger RNA, and CRISPR-based systems are susceptible to degradation, face challenges in crossing cellular barriers, and may induce immune-related adverse effects, thereby limiting their clinical translation. abstract: Carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), commonly used as the sodium salt (NaCMC) and also known as cellulose gum, carmellose or E466, is an ionic cellulose ether widely used in foods, pharmaceuticals, drilling fluids, detergents, paper products and lithium-ion battery slurries. abstract: This contribution argues that language, as well as individual languages, are not autonomous objects merely described by epistemic practices. Rather, they are social phenomena brought into being – in other words, ontologized – through such practices. abstract: Introduction Since the 1990s, East Asia has prioritized the production of scientific knowledge based on monitoring and modeling data, devoting significant effort to understanding the source-receptor relationships of transboundary air pollution among countries in the region. However, the lack of a common understanding of the causal mechanisms underlying air pollution in the region has persisted for decades. abstract: Beginning with the famous advertising slogan for Cadbury’s Cocoa, “Absolutely Pure, Therefore Best,” this article examines how British cocoa and chocolate manufacturers shaped evolving meanings of food purity to their advantage across legislative and commercial domains, from the 1850s until the eve of the Second World War. title: Critical mineral removal from mining‐impacted waters using microalgal biomass
abstract: Abstract Rising demand for critical minerals has led to increased mining and mineral processing activities, resulting in the release of metal‐contaminated waters requiring treatment. Conventional treatment methods, such as lime neutralization, effectively precipitate metals; however, they are less effective at low metal concentrations and produce large volumes of sludge. abstract: A bstract We compute the gluonic contribution to the gravitational form factors of the proton using the improved holographic QCD model, in which the proton is described in terms of bulk Dirac fermions. title: Pyelonephritis in cats and dogs - a scoping review
abstract: There is a lack of consensus regarding the diagnosis and treatment of bacterial pyelonephritis (PN) in dogs and cats. The aim of this scoping review was to increase knowledge by describing published scientific literature on the subject, specifically to collate definitions and diagnostic criteria, antimicrobial regimens, reported outcomes, and to identify knowledge gaps. abstract: The Globally Important Agricultural Heritage Systems (GIAHS) Programme is a flagship initiative of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), aimed at identifying and preserving Agricultural Heritage Systems for future generations. GIAHS represent a rural development model based on dynamic conservation principles, provisioning of ecosystem services, and sustainability. This perspective paper aims to assess the evolution, impacts, and future development of the GIAHS Programme after more than 20 years since its establishment. title: Redox Orchestration of organ regeneration
abstract: Abstract The evolutionary transition from anaerobic to aerobic life imposed significant oxidative challenges, while also enabling the emergence of reactive oxygen species (ROS) as key regulators of cellular signaling. This review synthesizes current knowledge on how ROS, once considered merely toxic byproducts, have been co-opted as essential signaling molecules that orchestrate organ regeneration across phylogenetically diverse species. title: Beyond experience: Rating quality and rater behaviors in integrated writing
abstract: Assessing source-based writing is challenging for raters due to the complexity of language usage and source integration (Plakans & Ohta, 2021). During the rating process, raters draw upon their prior experience, but despite a substantial body of research (Barkaoui, 2010a; Lim, 2011), no consensus has been reached regarding the impact of experience on assessment quality. title: Immune dysregulation and adaptive resilience in response to air pollution
abstract: Air pollution is increasingly recognized as an important environmental factor associated with immune dysfunction and disease susceptibility. This narrative review critically synthesizes current evidence on the molecular and cellular mechanisms by which airborne pollutants may alter immune homeostasis and influence adaptive resilience. Particular attention is given to particulate, gaseous, semi-volatile, and biologically derived pollutants, including particulate matter, ozone, nitrogen dioxide, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, metals, wildfire smoke, pollen, and microbial aerosols. title: Spatial and seasonal variation in soil organic matter responses to landfill disturbance in the Hyrcanian Forests
abstract: Forest ecosystems are increasingly exposed to anthropogenic pressures that threaten soil functioning and long-term ecosystem stability. Among these pressures, landfill-based waste disposal has emerged as a growing concern in developing regions, particularly where forest soils play a central role in organic matter turnover and nutrient retention. However, the responses of these systems to waste-derived inputs under contrasting climatic settings remain insufficiently constrained. title: The role of salinity in Snowball Earth: A simplified coupled atmosphere--ocean--ice model
abstract: The Neoproterozoic Snowball Earth events represent among the most extreme climate states in Earth's history, with ice covering all or nearly all of the ocean. Despite its control on the seawater freezing point and on the partitioning of water between the ocean and ice, salinity has not been well-represented in Snowball Earth models---typically prescribed, simplified, or ignored. abstract: As expansion and scalability in underwater oper- ations becomes more important and challenging, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) become more relevant and the necessity for reliable autonomy more critical. A fundamental challenge in any autonomous underwater operation, from control to safe navigation and mapping, is state estimation; a notorious hard problem to address, especially in low visibility conditions. abstract: Calls for shifting visualization research to general audiences outside of professional contexts have been put forward since the early 2000s, but expanding outwards means contending with a diversity in visualization's communicative purpose beyond transmitting insights from data. After our own experiences studying public-facing visualizations, we sought a set of considerations to help early-career visualization researchers reason through designing empirical visualization studies for the general public that confronts the various ways visualizations are interpreted. title: Bottom-boundary identification using asymptotic observers in dispersive shallow-water models
abstract: In this paper we consider the problem of identifying the bottom-boundary of an ocean basin, particularly in the coastal region where shallow-water theory applies. In particular we develop an observer-based approach of identifying the bottom-boundary profile from measurements of the free-surface. In particular, we prove that the true profile can be obtained by minimising the long-time observation-error as computed from the observer equations associated with a class of linear dispersive shallow water-wave models. We provide an explicit easy-to-implement observer design guaranteeing convergence.

title: H-SPAR: Hydrodynamic-aware Simulation for Particle Transport and Autonomous Robots
abstract: Abstract Environmental robotic sampling requires considering the dual influence of water currents on robotic motion and particle transport. Existing marine robotics simulators generally model flow, autonomy, and sampling targets separately, limiting joint evaluation of mission cost and sampling performance. H-SPAR integrates spatially and temporally varying velocity fields, Lagrangian particle transport, probabilistic sampling, and ROS 2/Gazebo-based uncrewed surface vehicle (USV) autonomy. title: New Election, Same Old Story: How Tropes Form a Grammar of Election Rumors
abstract: Recent elections in the United States have seen online rumors become a regular feature of election discourse as voters and election officials work to navigate a sea of digitally spread claims and propaganda. For the uninitiated, these rumors can feel overwhelming and random, sowing doubt about the integrity and legitimacy of recent elections. In this paper, we reviewed and qualitatively coded a large dataset of 590 election rumors collected during the the 2020 and 2022 national elections. title: Experimental Realization of Higher-order Topological Water Wave Crystal
abstract: Free-surface water waves provide a macroscopic platform in which topological localization can be measured through surface-elevation fields. Higher-order topological phases offer a route to localizing wave modes at structural corners, yet their experimental realization in water-wave systems remains largely unexplored. title: Neighborhood Deprivation Shapes Post-Flood Population Losses in Pune and Bandung
abstract: Disaster research in high-income settings shows that better-resourced communities see population inflows and faster recovery, while disadvantaged communities suffer prolonged population loss. Whether this pattern holds in rapidly urbanizing cities of the Global South remains unclear. Here we show, using mobile phone data from Pune, India, and Bandung, Indonesia, how neighborhood-level changes in phone presence, a proxy for short-term population movement, relate to flooding and neighborhood deprivation. title: Can You Say This for Me? Speaking Up by Proxy in Co-Located Discussion
abstract: Equal participation in co-located discussion is important for effective collaboration, yet people often hold back when they anticipate negative interpersonal or professional consequences, especially when raising a point requires voicing it themselves. We present SecondVoice, a mixed-reality system that enables people to speak up through an embodied virtual proxy. abstract: Simplifying large or noisy time-series is often a prerequisite for producing interpretable line charts, yet existing methods vary widely in how they alter visual features such as trends, extrema, periodicity, curvature, roughness, and overall complexity. We introduce a feature-based taxonomy of line chart simplification that evaluates 19 commonly used algorithms across three families: Transformers, Reducers, and Aggregators. abstract: The spatial chromatic model (SCM) is a novel entity-oriented spatial data model proposed in recent years. abstract: Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) trains a few-step student using the difference between a teacher's score and an online critic's estimate of the student distribution's score. abstract: Visual commissions require image agents to integrate heterogeneous source materials, preserve requirements across dependent stages, and produce coordinated deliverables. Existing evaluations examine specific capabilities and execution settings, leaving end-to-end commission completion less understood. abstract: We study the propagation of ferrons, the quanta of electric polarization waves, through a ferroelectric texture. title: Measuring Healthcare Accessibility and Resilience for Smart and Connected Rural Communities: A Florida Panhandle Case Study
abstract: Rural communities in the United States face persistent healthcare disparities, with fewer providers and facilities, longer trips to care, lower health literacy, and weaker transportation and broadband infrastructure than their non-rural counterparts. abstract: Handwriting and sketching help people develop ideas around information. As this work unfolds, users may seek assistance with finding, understanding, and organizing materials. We investigate how ink can initiate and steer agent assistance in this process. abstract: The structural accessibility and perimeter shell properties of branched macromolecules are studied using Monte Carlo simulations on a simple cubic lattice. Constituent polymer chains of these macromolecules are constructed in an algorithmic way as: a set of collinear monomers; a self-avoiding walk (SAW); tigthly packed monomers. These mimic the ground states for a rigid rod, flexible chain, and collapsed chain conformational states, respectively. title: The impact of an in-situ stress gradient on the growth of a fluid-driven frictional rupture
abstract: Models of injection-induced aseismic slip commonly assume uniform in-situ stresses along the fault, and thus predict rupture growth symmetric about the injection point. We relax this assumption and account for linear variations with depth of the resolved shear and effective normal tractions. We consider a planar fault with constant friction under plane-strain conditions, subjected to fluid injection at constant overpressure. title: Hyaluronic acid over-expression drives tissue architecture in both healthy and diseased states
abstract: Tissue architecture is shaped by a variety of biomechanical and biochemical mechanisms, including morphogen patterning, differential growth, and spatial variations in cellular contractility. These mechanisms typically emphasize forces generated within cells. Here, we explore a complementary mechanism in which intercellular space itself exerts forces that shape tissue architecture. More specifically, we focus on hyaluronic acid (HA), a glycosaminoglycan of the extracellular matrix, that draws fluid into the spaces between cells through osmotic pressure, allowing these spaces to expand and mecha

title: Toolpath Overhang Optimization for the Large-Format 3D Printing of Bespoke Shapes
abstract: This paper presents a closed curve trimming algorithm for overhang optimization in large-format support-free 3D printing of bespoke manifold shapes. Large-format 3D printing enables efficient fabrication of complex, bespoke shapes. Because of the material properties and surface quality requirements, such shapes are typically printed without support structures and have to be designed as support-free. title: SeCo-SBIR: Semantically Consistent Prompt Learning for Zero-Shot Sketch-Based Image Retrieval
abstract: Adapting CLIP for zero-shot sketch-based image retrieval (ZS-SBIR) via prompt learning faces a fundamental tension: the model must bridge the sketch-photo domain gap through task-specific adaptation, yet the added flexibility risks overfitting to seen training categories and eroding CLIP's zero-shot generalization. We present SeCo-SBIR, a semantically consistent prompt learning framework that resolves this tension from both sides. title: LesionStudio: A Patient-Informed Platform for Task-Specific Optimization of Emission Tomography Reconstruction and Analysis
abstract: Purpose: For task-specific PET and SPECT reconstruction optimization, we developed LesionStudio, an open-source platform incorporating patient background heterogeneity, realistic lesion morphology and texture, and lesion-background interactions beyond conventional phantoms. Methods: LesionStudio, a Python framework built on PyTomography, inserts lesions into PET/SPECT data using modality-specific forward projection and stochastic background ablation. title: Why delivered costs understate prices in an integrated global hydrogen market
abstract: Delivered-cost estimates are often used as proxies for hydrogen import prices. Yet they measure average supply-chain costs, whereas marginal prices measure the system value of an additional unit. Market interactions can make the two diverge, potentially biasing long-term price assumptions. We quantify this gap using an 81-region global hydrogen-market model, comparing each region's costs and prices when only its demand is active and when all regions' demands are active. title: Nucleon Wave Functions from QCD Vacuum Topology
abstract: Instantons, as topologically nontrivial gauge field configurations, provide a microscopic mechanism for chiral symmetry breaking and the $U_A(1)$ anomaly in QCD. Within the instanton liquid model (ILM), instantons generate multi-fermion interactions governed by their density and size. Using this framework, we develop a microscopic description of the nucleon based on instanton-induced quark--quark correlations. title: Light-Cone Friedel Oscillations: a Window into van Hove Superconductivity
abstract: Van Hove (vH) singularities can enhance superconductivity by generating a large pairing susceptibility. Yet, it remains challenging to experimentally establish whether pairing really occurs near these points. We show that the saddle-point dispersion near a vH point gives rise to a `light-cone' vH-selective behavior of Friedel oscillations, which is drastically different from the familiar concentric circles. Each vH point maps onto its own real-space light-cone sector, allowing STM around a single impurity to measure whether---and how strongly---that saddle-point quasiparticle sector is gapped.

title: Restoring Semantic Fidelity for Training-Free High-Resolution Image Generation in Diffusion Transformers
abstract: Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based text-to-image models have recently achieved remarkable success in image synthesis. However, when directly applied beyond their training resolution, these models often suffer from severe semantic degradation, where meaningful semantic content disappears. Although existing training-free high-resolution generation methods can mitigate this issue, the inherent semantic degradation at high resolutions remains largely unresolved, leading to degraded fine-grained details. title: AirForesight: Current-to-Future Spatial Map Imagination with Cross-Space Planning Consistency for UAV-VLN
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Vision-Language Navigation (UAV-VLN) requires agents to follow language instructions, infer spatial structure from sparse multi-view observations, and execute feasible 3D motion in complex outdoor environments. Despite recent progress with large language models, most existing methods still map vision-language inputs directly to actions, providing limited explicit scene grounding and future-aware spatial reasoning. We propose AirForesight, a current-to-future spatial map imagination framework for UAV-VLN. AirForesight first learns a structured current-map representation

title: Language Scent: Exploring Cross-Language Information Navigation
abstract: While multilingual users often switch between languages when seeking information, this process remains undersupported by current systems where information is typically siloed by language. Our formative study reveals that users select their search language based on its perceived value for their current information need, a concept we formalize as language scent. Language scent extends Pirolli and Card’s information foraging theory — which explains how users navigate among already-encountered sources — to the multilingual case, where users’ choice of query language determines which sources they c

title: Catastrophes in Reconnections of Optical Vortex Rings
abstract: A small change in parameters leads to a small change in the outcomes, in most cases. For instance, an optical vortex ring, created in the superposition of two laser beams, can slightly shrink if the phase changes minutely. However, dynamical systems can also experience significant changes due to small perturbations in parameters; the vortex rings can reconnect, nucleate or collapse into a point. Parameters that cause such striking outcomes are at the focal point of catastrophe theory - a branch of bifurcation theory that studies degenerate critical points of a potential function. title: Singular Perturbations for Control Systems Safety
abstract: Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) offer a powerful theory for enforcing safety in dynamical systems. Yet, applying this framework to complex systems is challenging when subsystems are feedback-interconnected and operate at different timescales. Such structures arise naturally in multiphysics systems and in control architectures where physical plants interact with optimization, estimation, and control algorithms. title: Dramarrator: Object-Based Audio Editing for Audio Drama Production from Books
abstract: Audio dramas weave dialogue, sound effects, and music into immersive stories. Creators often adapt books into audio dramas, but this process remains labor-intensive, requiring them to interpret source material, author scripts, generate audio assets, and assemble them on a timeline. Because story elements like characters and scenes manifest across many interdependent assets, a single change can ripple into manual updates across the entire project. We present Dramarrator, an audio drama authoring tool built around object-based audio editing, where these story elements are represented as editable

title: Brillouin comb line amplifiers for optical atomic clocks
abstract: Optical atomic clocks outperform the microwave clocks at the heart of current timing and navigation infrastructure by orders-of-magnitude, and recent progress in on-chip integration provides the opportunity to widely deploy them. Conventionally, a narrow linewidth laser interrogates the atomic transition, and an optical frequency comb divides its stabilised frequency (hundreds of terahertz) down to a microwave that is electronically countable. The laser(s) impose a significant size, weight, power and cost penalty, which is a current barrier to low-cost, scalable, fully on-chip optical clocks.

title: Settlement percolation reveals shrinking critical distances across the urban hierarchy
abstract: Measures of urban expansion quantify land consumption but obscure how separated settlements coalesce. We examine India's 50 largest urban agglomerations (1975-2025) using percolation-like analysis. Critical distances marking the largest settlement-merger events contracted in 47 cities, the median falling 46% from 650 to 350m. This longitudinal shrinking of settlement connectivity length scales reveals a morphological mechanism shaping land-consumptive settlement growth through distinct forms of inter-cluster coalescence (compact, corridor, satellite, regional). title: Empirical rather than simulated spectral band adjustment of MODIS to Sentinel-3 OLCI for European vegetation monitoring
abstract: Spectral band adjustment derived from convolved spectra describes sensor differences under controlled conditions, but its applicability to operational products requires assessment. We compare this approach with adjustment estimated directly from MODIS and Sentinel-3 OLCI observations for European vegetation monitoring. Both streams undergo atmospheric correction and Ross-Thick/Li-Sparse Reciprocal BRDF normalization to nadir viewing and local solar noon. title: Quantum Popcorn: the shape of a phase transition bubble
abstract: A quantum tunneling event in field theory is usually depicted as the materialization of a spherical bubble of true vacuum. The bubble appears at rest, and its profile is the time-symmetric slice of Coleman's bounce, the Euclidean solution that controls the decay rate. However, the bubble is spherical only in the leading semiclassical approximation: at the next order the configuration is a Gaussian ensemble of fluctuations around the bounce. title: Estimating cosmogenic backgrounds in nEXO at SNOLAB using Geant4 and FLUKA
abstract: The nEXO experiment was designed to search for neutrinoless double beta decay in the isotope $^{136}$Xe, using a five-tonne, isotopically-enriched liquid xenon time projection chamber (TPC). To meet nEXO's sensitivity goal, significant effort is placed on background mitigation strategies. Here, we evaluate the expected cosmogenic background rate for nEXO if placed at its preferred underground host site, SNOLAB. title: MEV: A Multi-Event Video Dataset for Long-Take Generation
abstract: Current datasets for text-to-video generation are largely limited to short clips depicting a single event or coarse-grained captions. As a result, they provide limited supervision for modeling long-take temporal dependencies, often leading to temporally inconsistent generations when describing multiple events. In this paper, we introduce MEV, a multi-event video dataset designed for long-take video generation. abstract: Biostimulants are substances, either natural or synthetic, that enhance plant growth without functioning as fertilizers or pesticides. According to the European Biostimulants Industry Council and EU regulations, biostimulants improve the efficiency of nutrient use, help plants withstand challenging conditions, and increase crop yields by activating specific plant functions. Unlike biofertilizers, which supply nutrients through living microbes, biostimulants influence plant development and interactions with beneficial microbes. title: The DARS (Drone‐Based Aerosol Remote Sensing) System: A Solar Spectrometer Platform—Instrumentation, Calibration, and First Experiments
abstract: Abstract Accurate, high‐resolution measurements of Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) are essential for radiative forcing assessment and air quality management. However, a critical observational gap exists between ground in situ monitoring networks (e.g., AErosol RObotic NETwork) and satellite products compromised by low revisit frequency, and sparse resolution. To bridge this gap, we present a novel Drone‐based Aerosol Remote Sensing (DARS) platform equipped with a designed solar Spectrometer, observing direct‐sun, multi‐wavelength radiation measurements. title: From Stream to State: Engaging Communities in Approved Water Monitoring Frameworks
abstract: Abstract More than 50% of Oklahoma's surface water systems are classified as impaired by the US EPA, with limited funds designated toward surface water monitoring. Community science data can contribute to increasing the amount of quality‐controlled government water quality reporting. A framework is presented for implementing a community‐based approach to generating quality‐controlled water field data to support water quality monitoring by local and regional governments. title: Marine Gravity Field Refinement Using Iterative Frequency-Domain Combination
abstract: Summary High-accuracy marine gravity fields are essential for resolving fine-scale seafloor structures and supporting marine geophysical studies. However, the recovery of short-wavelength gravity signals from conventional satellite altimetry is limited by track spacing, measurement noise and filtering. The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission provides dense wide-swath observations and improves the recovery of shorter-wavelength sea-surface slopes. title: Microbial selenoprotein: classification, distribution, and bioactivity
abstract: Abstract Selenium (Se)-enriched microorganisms, particularly probiotics such as Saccharomyces cerevisiae, lactic acid bacteria, bifidobacteria, and Aspergillus oryzae, are distinguished by their capacity to accumulate Se, predominantly in the form of selenoproteins. This review systematically analyzes these microorganisms and their selenoproteins, evaluates their biological activities, and summarizes current progress and challenges regarding the extraction, purification, and identification of microbial selenoproteins. abstract: Nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions from fertilised oil palm (OP) systems remain poorly quantified despite their importance for regional greenhouse gas inventories and life-cycle assessments. This study measured N 2 O emissions following 18 fertiliser application events across 12 smallholder OP farms in Indonesia and Malaysia between 2022 and 2025. Cumulative fertiliser-induced emissions were estimated over a 21-day measurement period and used to derive N 2 O emission factors (EFs) for individual fertilisation events. abstract: Cycas pectinata Buch.-Ham. is a threatened cycad native to Northeast India and Southeast Asia. Folk medicine uses its aerial parts to treat various diseases and disorders, yet its female cones remain chemically uncharacterised. In this study, hydroalcoholic extract of female cone part of Cycas pectinata (CPE) was screened for the physicochemical properties and in vitro antioxidant activity. abstract: Refractory solid tumors are characterized by pronounced antigen heterogeneity, dense tissue barriers, and immunosuppressive microenvironments, which limit the tumor coverage and durable immune clearance achieved with conventional monospecific antibodies. Bispecific and multispecific antibodies (BsAbs and MsAbs) can recognize two or more antigens or epitopes, thereby integrating tumor targeting, immune-cell recruitment, and regulation of multiple signaling pathways within a single therapeutic system. title: Evaluating Elemental and Petrophysical Data From Scientific Ocean Drilling for Sedimentary CaCO 3 Reconstruction and Application to Cenozoic Deep‐Sea Carbonate Burial
abstract: Abstract The variation in calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ) content with water depth in deep‐sea sediments is critical for reconstructing paleo‐oceanic events, global carbon cycling, and climate change. High‐resolution (e.g., centimeter‐scale) CaCO 3 measurements in Cenozoic marine sediments remain limited, and proxy‐based estimates have not been sufficiently validated. This study evaluates CaCO 3 conversion models using proxies in sediments recovered by scientific ocean drilling. abstract: Automated classification of healthy and bleached coral in underwater photographs can scale reef monitoring, but accuracy reported on public image collections is inflated when near-duplicate frames are shared between training and evaluation partitions. This study introduces a reusable leakage-mitigated, scene-aware benchmarking protocol and applies it to the Coral Reefs Images collection of 10,382 photographs. abstract: Abstract The representation of turbulent vertical transport of heat and moisture in the marine atmospheric boundary layer (BL) remains a major source of uncertainty in weather and climate models, especially during extreme marine Cold Air Outbreaks (CAOs). This case study of In situ vertical velocity, water vapor, and temperature observations from the Cold‐Air‐outbreak Experiment in the Sub‐Arctic Region airborne campaign's “golden case” demonstrates the unique capability of wavelet analysis to provide spatially‐ and scale‐resolved flight‐level vertical turbulent transport estimates. title: Seagrass sediment organic carbon burial rates are globally significant
abstract: Abstract Crucial for coastal carbon sequestration, global seagrass organic carbon (OC) burial rates remain uncertain as early estimates were derived from mixed methodologies across geographically and taxonomically biased datasets. Here, we present a data-driven reassessment from a synthesis of 332 sediment cores spanning the last century. Results show that seagrasses bury OC at 25 ± 3 g OC m −2 yr −1 (geometric mean), with an area-weighted global average of 33 ± 9 g OC m −2 yr −1 . abstract: The HY-2B/C/D constellation delivers routine altimeter significant wave height (SWH) and sea-surface wind speed over the Chinese coastal seas through four product streams (GDR, IDR, ODR, and SDR), yet whether the three satellites are mutually consistent, and whether that consistency is the same for both parameters, has not been established. abstract: En la manufactura automotriz, la entrega de vehículos conformes en el primer intento es prioritaria para la eficiencia operativa y la reducción de costos por retrabajos. abstract: Corals face exposure to numerous chemical contaminants, yet toxicity data is limited even for common coastal contaminants. While representative standard toxicity test organisms are typically used to assess environmental risk, these may not be good surrogates for species with unique attributes, including coral symbiotic relationships. Because hard corals are ecologically important yet challenging to obtain and maintain under laboratory conditions, we evaluated the utility of Galaxea fascicularis, a common and globally available aquaculture species. title: ASSESSMENT OF THE SUSTAINABILITY OF THE MARINE INSURANCE MARKET IN THE BLACK SEA UNDER HEIGHTENED OPERATIONAL AND FINANCIAL RISK
abstract: This paper analyzes the sustainability of the marine insurance market in the Black Sea region amid ongoing geopolitical instability and an escalating risk environment. It examines the impacts of operational risks (military actions, sea mine hazards, rerouting) and financial risks (surging war risk premiums, sanctions regimes, elevated freight rates) on vessel insurance coverage. The adaptation mechanisms of insurers and Protection & Indemnity (P&I) Clubs are evaluated alongside the broader implications for maritime supply chain security and transport economics in the Black Sea basin.

title: Multi-omics reveals context-dependent microbial community and transcriptional responses to trace-metal enrichment in the Indian Ocean
abstract: Bioactive trace metals, including iron (Fe), manganese (Mn), copper (Cu), and zinc (Zn), are essential micronutrients that regulate marine microbial metabolism and biogeochemical cycling. Although their role on phytoplankton productivity is established, their effects on mixed oligotrophic microbial assemblages comprising heterotrophic bacteria and picocyanobacteria remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how short-term enrichment with Fe, Mn, Cu, Zn, and a mixed-metal treatment influenced microbial community composition and functional potential across six stations in the Indian Ocean.

This study examines two research questions: whether the use of pair trawl by Vietnamese fishing vessels complies with Law No. 45 of 2009 on Fisheries (Fisheries Law) and the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS 1982); and how the applicable legal framework has been enforced. This study combined surface measurements at the coastal Linyuan site and the inland Wanluan site with 191 unmanned aircraft system (UAS) profiles collected during the Kao–Ping Experiment (KPEx) from February to March 2024. title: BELOW ARTICLE 5: THRESHOLDS OF RESPONSE TO SUSPECTED SABOTAGE, CABLE DAMAGE AND DRONE INCURSIONS

abstract: The Eocene Baoshi Formation (BAF) and Pinghu Formation (PIF) are the main source-rock intervals in the western slope belt of the Xihu Sag, East China Sea Shelf Basin. This study integrates TOC and Rock-Eval pyrolysis, major and trace element geochemistry, and biomarker data from five wells to reconstruct the Eocene paleoenvironmental evolution and evaluate the controls on organic matter (OM) enrichment. title: Maritime Law Enforcement and Delimitation of Indonesian Sea Boundaries: Legal Certainty and Protection of Sovereign Rights
abstract: Introduction: Maritime boundary delimitation and law enforcement in border areas are important issues for Indonesia as an archipelagic state. However, maritime delimitation and the enforcement of maritime law concern distinct legal questions and require separate but coordinated analyses. Purposes of the Research: This study examines the legal framework for maritime boundary delimitation under UNCLOS 1982 and analyzes the urgency and challenges of law enforcement in Indonesia’s maritime border areas. title: High-Resolution Nearshore Wave Direction Retrievals from X-Band Radar Using an Adapted Slope-Array Method
abstract: Abstract Coastal observing platforms typically lack the spatial resolution needed to monitor the transformation of surface gravity waves, which impact nearshore circulation patterns, wave-driven runup, and sediment transport. Previous studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of deriving surface wave information from X-band radar by applying three-dimensional Fast Fourier Transforms (3D FFTs) to backscatter images in the open ocean. Near the coast, however, X-band retrievals are more challenging to interpret since wave fields are spatially inhomogeneous due to bathymetrically driven shoaling
journal: Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology

title: Marine bioindicators of volcanism: Trace metal patterns in Anemonia viridis across two eruptive events
abstract: Volcanic eruptions release trace metals that can accumulate in marine biota, yet few studies have compared bioaccumulation patterns between submarine and subaerial events using the same sentinel species. We measured eight metals (Al, Cd, Cu, Fe, Li, Ni, Pb, and Zn) in the sea anemone Anemonia viridis at one volcanic and one control site on each of two Canary Islands: El Hierro, affected by the submarine Tagoro eruption of 2011 and 2012, and La Palma, affected by the subaerial Tajogaite eruption of 2021. title: A curated global checklist of polychaetes (Annelida) from deep‑sea chemosynthetic and reducing habitats

title: Updated Estimates of Radiocarbon‐Based Deep Ocean Circulation Age
abstract: Abstract The deep ocean circulation age based on radiocarbon was last determined almost 20 years ago, when digital archiving was not standard practice. This work updates the circulation age while making two improvements by using new nutrient data and modifying the calculation. The newly calculated circulation age is spatially more coherent and older in the deep North Pacific than before. The basin‐averaged circulation age for the Atlantic, Pacific, Indian, and Southern Ocean is respectively 256, 930, 689, and 326 years. The study confirms the centennial timescale of the world oceans.

abstract: Coastal and offshore fisheries play a vital role in the Pacific Island economies, food security and cultural heritage. While the past two decades has seen increased recognition of gender dimensions of fisheries, managers, practitioners and industry partners have not yet tackled the problem of gender‐based violence (GBV) in the sector. abstract: International maritime transport plays a central role in the global economy while significantly contributing to greenhouse gas emissions, thus positioning itself within the contemporary debate on climate change. abstract: Rasa Śāstra is an important branch of Ayurveda concerned with the identification, processing, pharmaceutical transformation, and therapeutic use of metals, minerals, and other Rasa Dravyas. Rasa Dravya Vargikarana provides a systematic framework for understanding these substances based on their properties, pharmaceutical applications, therapeutic importance, and role in Parada Karma. abstract: Coccoloba uvifera (L.) L. is widely cultivated in coastal regions of Vietnam, but phytochemical data on Vietnamese-grown material remain limited. This study investigated the flavonoid constituents and antioxidant activity of C. uvifera leaves using a bioactivity-guided approach. title: Transposon mutagenesis identifies lon , csgF , and rfbF as critical genetic determinants of biofilm architecture and adhesion in multidrug‐resistant Salmonella Typhimurium
abstract: Salmonella Typhimurium relies on biofilm formation to withstand environmental stressors, resist antimicrobials, and establish persistent host infections. However, the genetic networks governing biofilm development remain poorly understood. Here, we assessed the biofilm-forming capacity of 708 S. Typhimurium isolates. title: Beyond Aggregate Import Dependency: Commodity-Specific Food Price Transmission in Developing Asia
abstract: Global food-price shocks pose a challenge for developing Asian economies, but aggregate import-dependency measures can obscure differences in exposure across commodities. Whether commodity-specific import dependence predicts differential transmission to national food inflation remains insufficiently understood. This study examines whether predetermined, commodity-specific import dependency conditions the transmission of global food-price shocks to domestic food inflation in 19 developing Asian economies. abstract: Organic orchards and their associated hedgerows can function as important ecological infrastructures in agricultural landscapes by providing shelter, alternative prey, floral resources and overwintering sites for arthropods involved in natural pest regulation. This role is particularly relevant on oceanic islands, where agricultural mosaics include endemic, native non-endemic and introduced taxa, and where biodiversity-friendly production systems may contribute to both ecosystem-service provisioning and early detection of potentially invasive species. abstract: Abstract Accurate source discrimination of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in industrialized coastal sediments remains challenging because multiple pyrogenic sources often exhibit overlapping molecular signatures. Despite frequent elevated PAH contamination in sediments near shipyards, the dominant sources remain poorly constrained. abstract: Urban growth and expansion have aggravated the volume of fine particulate matter pollution, especially in the high-rise cities. abstract: Abstract Monofloral honeys, particularly Iranian Sidr honey, are highly valued for their unique sensory and medicinal properties; however, they are also prone to fraud. To address this issue, it is essential to create reference databases documenting the physicochemical and pollinological profiles of these honeys. abstract: Climate change increasingly threatens tropical crop production through erratic rainfall, rising temperatures, and more frequent extreme weather events that reduce crop productivity and disrupt farm management. abstract: An intense debate broke out between China and France over the sovereignty of the Xisha Islands in the early 1930s, in which meteorology played a key role. Scholars have paid increasing attention to the relationship between science and politics; this article demonstrates the multifaceted role of meteorology in asserting sovereignty in the context of East Asian international politics. abstract: Biodiversity refers to the structural, functional and evolutionary variability among living organisms across genetic, species and ecosystem hierarchical tiers. title: Atmospheric Stilling Reshapes Algal Blooms and Eutrophication Risk in Shallow Lakes
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric stilling, defined as long‐term decline in wind speed, has emerged as a widespread climate signal, yet its role as an independent driver of eutrophication in shallow lakes remains poorly understood. Taking Lake Taihu as a representative case, we applied a coupled hydrodynamic‐ecological model (GOTM‐WET) to quantitatively estimate the impacts of declining wind speed on a large shallow lake, while keeping external nutrient loading constant. abstract: Abstract Objective The Pacific white shrimp Penaeus vannamei is of great relevance in the Americas and forms the prime aquaculture activity in Mexico. Novel feed additives like fish by-products increase production profitability and support shrimp health and performance. We aimed to study the effects of tuna liquid hydrolysate (TLH) on the performance of Pacific white shrimp reared in an intensive commercial system under brackish-water conditions, analyze the associated return on investment, and examine TLH-induced modulation of the gut microbiota. title: AstroComb(v.1.0): non-linear, multi-channel, probabilistic cyclostratigraphic analysis
abstract: Abstract. We present a new algorithm for constructing floating astronomical timescales with explicit uncertainty estimates from sedimentary sequences. The method integrates probabilistic spectral analysis with inverse geochronological modeling, applied to ultra-high-resolution, multiproxy datasets such as core scanning X-Ray Fluorescence (XRF) elemental records. title: Feed conversion ratio of Litopenaeus vannamei farming in China: evidence from multi-province surveys (2016–2023)
abstract: The feed conversion ratio (FCR) is a key indicator of efficiency and sustainability in aquaculture, yet existing evidence on its farm-level determinants remains dominated by nutritional experiments, with little rigorous identification of the causal effects of managerial inputs or their heterogeneity across production regimes. title: Validation of ATLID stratospheric aerosol retrievals using SAGE III/ISS and ground-based lidar observations
abstract: Abstract. We present a systematic validation of EarthCARE ATLID stratospheric aerosol retrievals against SAGE III/ISS and ground-based lidars at the Table Mountain Facility (TMF) and the Observatoire de Haute-Provence (OHP), using 895 SAGE III/ISS, 55 TMF, and 26 OHP collocations over August 2024-April 2026 and spanning background, volcanic, and wildfire smoke conditions. title: Occurrence of PCDD/Fs and PCBs in Parks of the Porto Metropolitan Area
abstract: Persistent organic pollutants accumulate in urban soils, yet information on the occurrence, spatial variability and human health implications of polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins and dibenzofurans (PCDD/Fs) and dioxin-like polychlorinated biphenyls (dl-PCBs) remains limited, particularly in Portugal. Surface soils were collected from six urban and peri-urban green spaces across the Porto Metropolitan Area, encompassing contrasting land-use histories and anthropogenic settings. title: Animal-derived extracellular vesicles and vesicle-like nanoparticles: linking natural bioactivity to precision therapeutics
abstract: Animal-derived extracellular vesicles (AEVs) and animal-derived vesicle-like nanoparticles (AVLNs) are emerging natural nanocarriers with diverse bioactive cargoes, potential biocompatibility, and capacity for cross-species molecular communication. This narrative review distinguishes naturally released AEVs from AVLNs obtained through tissue processing without sufficient evidence of natural extracellular release. title: Long-term spatio-temporal dynamics of sediment-associated heavy metals in a large river system
abstract: Abstract Despite the widespread use of geochemical and ecological indices, our understanding of long-term heavy metal dynamics in large river systems is still limited, particularly when it comes to capturing temporal variability and interactions between multiple elements. In this study, we examine patterns of sediment-associated metal contamination and ecological risk in the Vistula River (Poland), using monitoring data collected between 2015 and 2022 from 23 sites distributed along the entire river course. title: Review of the Radon Tracer Method for GHG emission estimates: development, application guidelines, improvements, and caveats
abstract: Abstract. The Radon Tracer Method (RTM) is an established, independent top-down method that can be used to cross-check bottom-up greenhouse gas (GHG) emission estimates. Furthermore, as uncertainties of Atmospheric Transport Models are reduced, the RTM can provide a convenient means of quantifying continual improvement of inversion-based top-down GHG emission estimates. title: Vertical profiling and aerosol typing using fluorescence Raman and depolarization lidar measurements over Thessaloniki, Greece
abstract: Abstract. In this study, we present the first fluorescence lidar observations over Thessaloniki, Greece, (40.63° N, 22.96° E; 60 m a.s.l.) using a multiwavelength Raman and depolarization lidar with fluorescence capabilities. For the first time in the Eastern Mediterranean fluorescence backscattering coefficient and the spectral fluorescence capacity parameter are retrieved and combined with particle depolarization ratio, lidar ratios, and Ångström exponents to characterize the aerosol load over Thessaloniki, a region influenced by diverse aerosol sources. title: Detecting monotonic and non-monotonic rainfall trends across Pernambuco using innovative trend analysis and Mann-Kendall test
abstract: Abstract Annual precipitation can change differently across low, medium, and high annual totals, yet this non-monotonic behavior has not been mapped across Pernambuco’s three climatic regions. We analyzed annual precipitation from 820 BR-DWGD grid cells for 1961–2022 using Innovative Trend Analysis (ITA), the Mann-Kendall (MK) test, and Sen’s slope. abstract: Polychaetes have been investigated as aquaculture feed ingredients because of their nutritional characteristics, particularly for broodstock diets of commercially important fish and shrimp species. However, the use of polychaetes from Latin America as feed resources for industrial aquaculture remains poorly documented, and microbiological data are an essential requirement for the development of new aquaculture ingredients. title: Contrasting Responses of Carbon Dioxide and Methane Fluxes Following Thermokarst Erosion Across Tundra‐Lake Interfaces in the Western Canadian Arctic
abstract: Abstract Erosion from ice‐rich permafrost thaw (“thermokarst”) alters tundra vegetation cover and soil moisture, and laterally transports organic material into lakes, altering net fluxes of carbon dioxide (F CO2 ), methane (F CH4 ), and nitrous oxide (F N2O ). Tundra and lakes are rarely examined together, although a joint view is necessary to understand their coupled biogeochemical responses to widespread thermokarst erosion. title: El turismo cultural como producto diversificador de la oferta turística de Acapulco
abstract: This research aimed to analyze tourists' knowledge of Acapulco's cultural offer, with the purpose of establishing strategies that enable decision-makers to have the necessary elements to diversify the tourism offer, promote the preservation of cultural heritage, and contribute to the economic and social development of the destination. To achieve this, a methodology based on the identification of cultural resources and the application of a survey to tourists was employed. title: Pollutants in Surface Water: Toxicological Consequences, Challenges, and Measures towards Conserving Water Quality
abstract: Surface water quality degradation from increasing pollution is a major worldwide threat, particularly in Morocco, a country with limited water resources, where preserving available clean water is therefore of the utmost importance. A systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA methodology, using scientific databases and Moroccan official reports. title: Introduction: branding post-war Mediterranean Europe: tourism and national identity
abstract: In the post-war period, Mediterranean Europe became the world’s pre-eminent tourist destination. This introduction to the special issue argues that this transformation was not solely economic but also profoundly representational and political. title: From farm gate to market stall: How supply chain and macroeconomic conditions shape retail price adjustments among agri-food retailers in selected markets in Ghana's Central Region
abstract: Retail food prices in Ghana are usually read as an echo of what happens on farms and in wholesale yards. The stall, however, is where costs, spoilage risk and customer resistance actually collide. Drawing on Price Transmission Theory, Transaction Cost Economics and bounded rationality, this study examined how supply chain and macroeconomic conditions shape retail adjustment in the Kasoa, Kotokuraba and Mankessim markets of Ghana's Central Region. title: Talaud Steam Power Plant Jetty Structure Design Using Soldier Pile Reinforcement to Increase Ship Berthing Capacity from 5,000 Dwt to 10,000 Dwt
abstract: The Talaud PLTU jetty is an important infrastructure that functions as a berthing facility for coal transport ships to ensure the continuity of the power plant's fuel supply. The increase in operational needs requires the ship's berthing capacity to be increased from 5,000 Dead Weight Tonnage (DWT) to 10,000 DWT based on a request from PLN due to the unavailability of 5,000 DWT ships at the local location, which was then assessed with document no. assessment/01/A4. title: Beyond the Gangway: Seafarers' Shore Leave Experiences and Mental Well-Being
abstract: Shore leave has long been regarded as a key recovery mechanism for seafarers, yet access to it has become increasingly rare and brief. Existing studies tend to treat shore leave as a minor component of seafarer welfare or to measure it through access and frequency, so little is known about how seafarers' lived experiences of both access to and restriction from shore leave shape their mental health and emotional well-being. title: Inland fisheries market feasibility of sharptooth catfish (Clarias gariepinus) in the Eastern Cape, South Africa
abstract: Despite increasing interest in inland fisheries as a means of supporting food security, livelihoods, and rural development, inland fisheries in South Africa remain poorly integrated into food systems, with significant uncertainty regarding supply chains, consumer demand, and product quality. We assessed the market feasibility of sharptooth catfish (Clarias gariepinus) harvested through the Darlington Alien Fish Harvest Project in the Eastern Cape, South Africa. Over a 9-month trial, 761 kg of catfish were procured, processed into retail products (fillets, burgers, smoked portions, and offcuts)

title: Do tripwires deter? How small forward deployments contribute to deterrence
abstract: Forward-deployed tripwire forces are one tool used to enhance the credibility of security guarantees. Cold War conventional wisdom holds that these vulnerable deployments improve deterrence by increasing the credibility of the sending state’s commitment to fight to defend the host, but recent scholarship has challenged their effectiveness. These new critiques argue that because tripwire forces lack capability, and publics do not punish leaders who back down, they do not deter. title: Lead Exceedance in Vegetables Grown on Guideline-compliant Soils: Heavy Metal Contamination and Human Health Risk in Cumilla, Bangladesh
abstract: Cumilla district combines intensive year-round vegetable production with an export processing zone, dense brick-kiln clusters and heavily trafficked national highways, yet no systematic soil-vegetable survey of toxic metals has been reported for the district. This study quantified copper (Cu), chromium (Cr) and lead (Pb) in five widely grown vegetables (potato, tomato, chili pepper, cauliflower and cabbage) and their matched surface field soils (0-15 cm) across six upazilas spanning an industrial-to-rural gradient, and tested the hypothesis that crop contamination tracks soil contamination clo

title: Assessing the Enterprise Risk Management and Financial Sustainability of Retail Micro and Small Enterprises in Dagupan City, Philippines
abstract: Retail micro and small enterprises (MSEs) are vital to Dagupan City’s commercial economy, yet many owner-managed firms lack formal systems for managing business risks. Philippine evidence on how such enterprises practice enterprise risk management (ERM), and what constrains systematic risk monitoring and documentation, remains limited. This study examined ERM practices, perceived financial sustainability, and implementation challenges in six retail MSEs. title: Modelling extreme rainfall events using extended generalized extreme value distributions in the megacities of India
abstract: The aim of the current study is to develop a statistical model for extreme rainfalls using Extreme Value Theory (EVT). title: Knowledge gap in vertebrate genetic diversity in a northern remanent of neotropical rainforest
abstract: Los Tuxtlas Biosphere Reserve is one of the last remaining areas of primary tropical rainforest in Mexico. This fragile ecosystem heavily reduced by human perturbations is part of the Mesoamerican hotspot. The reserve harbors many endemic species. Thus, identifying, cataloging, and studying the biodiversity of this ecosystem has been of utmost importance. A promising approach for fast species identification to assess biodiversity is the use of DNA barcoding techniques. However, these techniques are limited by reliable DNA databases. title: The Role of Village Facilitators in Community Empowerment in Kenanti Village, Tambakboyo District, Tuban Regency
abstract: This study aims to analyze the role of village facilitators in community empowerment in Kenanti Village, Tambakboyo District, Tuban Regency, and to identify factors that influence the effectiveness of this role. This study uses a descriptive qualitative approach, located in Kenanti Village, which is known to have an active village facilitation program. title: ‘What We Teach Is True to Us’: Non‐National Students and the Boundaries of Belonging in Dubai's Schools
abstract: ABSTRACT ‘What we teach is true to us’, one social studies teacher reflected when describing the curricular standards guiding his Dubai classroom. But who, in Dubai's multinational classrooms, gets to be part of that ‘us’? Private secondary schools in Dubai have become productive sites for state‐led civic nationalist projects. title: From Cell Block to Cash Book: Entrepreneurial and Digital Accounting Literacy for Incarcerated Adults Preparing for Reintegration in Jakarta
abstract: Prison-based entrepreneurship and financial education is increasingly promoted as a pathway to reintegration, yet evidence from Southeast Asian correctional settings is thin, and short community-engagement programs rarely disclose what their evaluations can and cannot show. This paper reports a lecturer–student program delivered to 31 inmates of the Class II A Salemba Correctional Institution in Jakarta on 15 July 2026. A 45-minute session on digital marketing and opportunity identification was followed by a 45-minute session on simple digital bookkeeping built around a worked cash-book case.

title: Geochemical characterization and hydraulic interpretation of formation waters in the reservoirs of the North African cratonic basin
abstract: This study characterizes formation waters from three fields within a North African hydrocarbon concession to determine their genetic origin, assess hydraulic connectivity, and evaluate implications for hydrocarbon preservation. More than fifty water samples from seven formations, Cambrian to Carboniferous, were analyzed for major ion concentrations and total dissolved solids. title: Ruins in the Field: Materiality, Spectres and Pluritemporal Encounters of the Oxford University Arctic Expedition
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper examines how encounters with ruins and spectres in the field inform (post)colonial trajectories of exploration and research. It does so by illustrating how the material indeterminacy and haunted materialities of ruins play into the relationship between self, landscape and history that explorers (and researchers) construct during fieldwork. Empirically, the paper traces the 1924 Oxford University Arctic Expedition to Svalbard—a significant event in the evolution of elite undergraduate exploration which continues to haunt the present. title: Climate‐Associated Genetic Variation in Native and Introduced Populations of Eustenopus villosus , a Biological Control Agent for Yellow Starthistle
abstract: ABSTRACT Contemporary evolution in biological control systems is rarely studied, though biological agents are repeatedly exposed to novel environmental conditions upon introduction. Their ability to adapt to new conditions could influence management efficacy and reveal important aspects of environmental selection. abstract: ABSTRACT Governments and international agencies routinely justify investments in weather and climate services by citing a single global figure: every dollar spent returns several dollars in economic benefits. This figure is useful for advocacy but says nothing about whether a specific national service in a specific country is actually delivering value to the people and institutions it serves. title: Variations in dv / v Susceptibility to Earthquake Shaking Along the Alaska Subduction Zone
abstract: Abstract Earthquake‐triggered decreases in relative seismic velocity ( dv / v ) of the crust have been reported for many events, but regional variations in dv / v susceptibility to shaking are not well understood. title: Genomic selection to enhance disease resilience in an endangered species
abstract: Abstract Chytridiomycosis caused by the amphibian chytrid fungus ( Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis , Bd) is one of the most devastating wildlife diseases of our time 1,2 . With no effective methods to control its spread, captive breeding programs have become essential to prevent frog extinctions 3 , but serve only as a temporary safeguard until threats can be mitigated 4 . title: Quality characteristics of frozen horse mackerel (Trachurus trachurus) treated with starch–glycerol coatings containing plant extracts
abstract: Starch-based coatings are biodegradable food-contact materials, but their performance depends on plasticizer level, incorporated active compounds, and the food surface to which they are applied. This study developed starch-glycerol polysaccharide coating formulations containing aqueous extracts from persimmon fruit calyces, cherry laurel leaves, and bilberry/likapa leaves and evaluated their application to whole horse mackerel ( Trachurus trachurus ) during frozen storage at -20 ± 2 °C for 6 months. title: Hope, temporality, and wonder at the end of the world
abstract: This article interrogates the conceptual terrains of hope, temporality, and wonder in the context of the Anthropocene, arguing that dominant framings of hope – anchored in ontological loss and critique – risk reproducing modernist binaries they seek to dismantle. While hope has been widely deployed as a tool for imagining alternatives to modernity, its reliance on affirmation or negation often tethers imaginaries to reactive postures vis-à-vis the modernist project. title: Integrated assessment of mercury-tolerant plant-associated bacteria from a chlor-alkali site identifies candidates for bioaugmentation
abstract: Mercury (Hg)-contaminated environments harbour microorganisms with traits that may be useful for plant-assisted remediation, but high Hg tolerance alone may not identify the most suitable strains for inoculation. In this study, plant-associated bacteria isolated from a chlor-alkali site were evaluated through phenotypic screening, whole-genome analysis, genome-scale metabolic modelling, and willow inoculation assays. abstract: This study aimed to develop and provide preliminary psychometric evidence for a School-Based Management (SBM) implementation instrument integrating Maluku’s local potential, Indonesia. The study employed an instrument development and preliminary validation design consisting of construct conceptualization, item development, expert content validation, empirical testing, and psychometric evaluation. Content validity was assessed by four experts using Aiken’s V, followed by empirical testing involving 107 senior high school teachers. abstract: BACKGROUND: Vector-borne diseases remain a major and evolving public health challenge in South America, where arboviruses such as dengue, chikungunya, Zika, and malaria continue to expand in incidence and geographic distribution. Insecticides remain central to vector control programs; however, the rapid emergence and spread of insecticide resistance across multiple vector species increasingly threaten the effectiveness and sustainability of these interventions. abstract: The Lower Miocene Asl Sandstone of the Upper Rudeis Formation is evaluated in four wells (ET-A3, ET-A4, NO159-6ST1, and GS160-5A) in the north-central Gulf of Suez using integrated wireline-log analysis, petrographic observations from ET-A3, and structural and depositional interpretation. title: EXPRESS: Hyperammonemia in cats with acute (on chronic) kidney disease: associations with urea cycle amino acids, azotemia and acid–base status
abstract: Objectives Hyperammonemia occurs in cats with kidney disease although the pathophysiology is poorly understood. The objective of this study was to determine if hyperammonemia in cats with kidney disease is associated with decreased concentrations of plasma amino acids involved in the urea cycle and more severe acid-base derangements. title: Drought resistance is influenced by soil water uptake depth in dryland shrubs
abstract: Abstract Climate change exacerbates aridity in dry shrublands leading to different responses of coexisting shrubs to drought, including different resistance (capacity to sustain growth during droughts). However, it is unknown how resistance depends on shifts in soil water uptake depth and functional traits. To address this issue, we studied seven shrub species in two semi‐arid Mediterranean sites. abstract: the study on " Association analysis among growth parameters and yield attributes of rice genotypes under irrigated condition and was conducted at the Research Cum Instructional Farm of the, Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, Raipur, Chhattisgarh, during the kharif seasons 2021-22 and 2022-23. title: Alexander the Great at the Hyphasis
abstract: Did Alexander actually want to cross the Hyphasis (Beas) River and advance to the Ganges? The historians present an inconsistent picture: most do not say that he did—indeed, no one would have asserted that he did not for fear of tarnishing the man’s reputation—and the evidence overwhelmingly supports the view that he had other plans and that such an undertaking would have been an aberration, a very foolish one at that. title: The Biodiversity biobanks of South Africa
abstract: Biodiversity biobanks can be defined as collections of biological materials, preserved and managed according to rigorous scientific standards to ensure the viability and quality of the materials, and include collections of seeds, microbial and cell cultures, tissues, DNA and environmental samples that are generally stored at ultralow temperatures. The value of biodiversity biobanks as critical research infrastructure has been acknowledged globally, but there is generally a lack of awareness of the role of biobanks more broadly than threatened species, crop and livestock breeding programmes. title: Metal‐containing hydrogen‐bonded organic frameworks with alternating electrostatic environments for trace SO 2 capture
abstract: Abstract Trace SO 2 capture from flue gas remains challenging in deep desulfurization because of its low partial pressure, corrosive conditions, and competition from coexisting gases. Here, we present a family of isostructural metal‐containing hydrogen‐bonded organic frameworks (M‐HOFs) featuring alternating electrostatic pore environments for efficient trace SO 2 capture. abstract: Objectives The aim of this article is to demonstrate the European Union’s hard power in its response to international migration. To illustrate the importance of hard power in EU migration policy, an analysis of the set of tools and mechanisms through which the European Union and its member states project their power and exert pressure on other actors in international relations is conducted. abstract: The Early Devonian Rhynie chert Konservat Lagerstätte in Aberdeenshire, Scotland, contains an abundance of structurally preserved fossils of organisms that lived together in an early terrestrial geothermal-wetland ecosystem, including cyanobacteria, fungi and fungus-like organisms, algae, land plants, and animals ranging from testate amoebae to nematodes and aquatic crustaceans to the earliest harvestmen, which were fully adapted to life on land. abstract: The global impact of the COVID-19 pandemic underscores the critical need for a comprehensive understanding of SARS-CoV-2 replication mechanisms. While the central roles of the RNA dependent RNA polymerase (NSP12), primase protein (NSP8), and nucleocapsid protein (N) in the virus life cycle are extensively studied, the precise nature of their interactions with the full-length viral RNA genome remain incompletely characterized. abstract: Abstract Polylactic acid microplastics (PLA-MPs) are ubiquitous environmental contaminants that can act as carriers for antibiotics such as azithromycin (AZI). However, the manner in which PLA-MPs shape modulates antibiotic-induced disruption of the gut microbiota remains poorly understood. title: Early Metabolic Reprogramming in the Placenta Shapes Resilience to Gestational Hypoxia in High‐Elevation Deer Mice
abstract: Environmental hypoxia at high elevations is linked to increased rates of gestational complications. Evolutionary adaptation to high elevation environments mitigates these complications across mammals, in part through changes in placental function that shape foetal growth potential in late pregnancy. To investigate the developmental origins of placental adaptation to hypoxia, we acclimated pregnant deer mice (Peromyscus maniculatus) derived from low- and high-elevation populations to normoxia or hypoxia (equivalent to 4300 m) and characterized the structure and transcriptome of foetal placentas

title: Multi-omics insights into rare earth element recovery by microalgae under salinity gradients
abstract: Conventional rare earth element (REE) extraction methods are resource-intensive and generate secondary pollutants, whereas biomining using microorganisms such as microalgae offers a more sustainable alternative. Microalgal growth and metal recovery are strongly influenced by environmental factors, especially salinity; however, the molecular mechanisms driving REE recovery in microalgae exposed to saline conditions remain largely unexplored.
