title: Heavy metal contamination assessment of the Taloka and Wurno aquifers, Sokoto Basin, northwestern Nigeria
abstract: A comprehensive heavy metal pollution assessment of the Taloka and Wurno aquifers within the Sokoto Basin, northwestern Nigeria, was carried out. Field mapping, borehole logging and water quality analysis were integrated to describe the distribution of heavy metals in groundwater. Heavy metal evaluation points to variations between the Taloka and Wurno aquifers. A plausible hypothesis is that the dissolution of iron-rich lithologies in the Taloka aquifer contributes to the elevated iron (Fe) concentrations observed in the Taloka Formation. title: The Construction of Religious Education Ideology and the Representation of Power in Wisran Hadi’s Play Perguruan: A Deconstructive Study
abstract: Background. Narratives of the Padri War in Minangkabau have generally framed the conflict as a binary struggle between religious reformists and adherents of customary law (adat). Wisran Hadi’s play Perguruan places a religious school at the heart of this conflict, yet it has not been examined in terms of ideological construction and power. Purpose. This study aims (1) to explain how the ideology of religious education is constructed in Perguruan, (2) to identify the forms of power it represents, and (3) to show how the text destabilizes the binary oppositions between adat, religion, and power.

abstract: Abstract The economic and social development of piassava extraction can contribute to forest conservation in the Atlantic Forest, but a clear understanding of the activities that make up its value chain is essential. In view of this, we sought to analyze the activities that make up the value chain of broom from Attalea funifera , from extraction to marketing. abstract: Nano-SiO₂ (NS) is widely used to enhance cement-based materials; however, its role in governing the coupled evolution of pore structure, damage behavior, and mechanical response remains insufficiently understood. In this study, ordinary and white Portland cement mortars incorporating NS (0-0.8%) were investigated using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), uniaxial compression, and acoustic emission (AE) monitoring. abstract: Abstract Island ecosystems often host endemics that are highly vulnerable to invasive species. In the Mediterranean biodiversity hotspot, the Endangered Aeolian wall lizard Podarcis raffonei is undergoing severe population decline. Its largest remaining population, on Vulcano Island, dropped by c. 60% from 2017 to 2022. title: Writing After Srebrenica: The Grammar of Grief and the Ethics of Testimonial Representation
abstract: This paper examines testimonial literature emerging from the Srebrenica genocide as a crucial site of ethical witnessing, moral resistance and memory-making. Drawing on survivor-authored memoirs and essays, it explores how trauma is transformed into language through a grammar of grief: a fragmented, hesitant mode of expression that articulates loss and survival without resolving suffering into narrative closure. abstract: Hydrogen production via water electrolysis represents a scalable and zero-emission pathway for sustainable energy applications. This study evaluates the effects of water source and electrolyte pH on hydrogen generation efficiency using a membrane-based electrolysis system integrating Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) and Membrane-Based Reactor (MBR) technologies. title: MaREA: diseño de una herramienta multidimensional para la autoevaluación de recursos educativos abiertos
abstract: Open educational resources (OER) are defined not only by their availability free of charge or by the presence of an open licence, but also by the legal, technical, documentary and accessibility-related conditions that enable them to be effectively located, adapted, reused and preserved. abstract: Asian populations are the fastest-growing racial ethnic group in the United States (US) and have the highest biomarker concentrations of several heavy metal(loid)s compared to other groups. abstract: The selection of wall material for affordable housing is a multi-attribute decision problem that has to reconcile structural safety, economic circumstances, local implementation conditions, and environmental performance under various regional contexts. This study develops an integrated Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP) and Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) framework for the most appropriate wall material for affordable housing in Banjarnegara, Cilacap, and Tasikmalaya regencies, Indonesia. abstract: Este estudio analiza el proceso de acreditación de programas de licenciatura desde la perspectiva de quienes los coordinan, actores clave en la gestión de la acreditación. El objetivo principal fue explorar sus experiencias, identificar buenas prácticas, desafíos, y lecciones aprendidas. abstract: Objetivo: Compreender como os sentimentos e os padrões discursivos expressos no conteúdo gerado por usuários (CGU) configuram a imagem digital do litoral do Piauí como destino turístico emergente. This study develops a household-level livelihood sustainability indicator framework that combines aggregate and household-level measures of occupational diversity with indicators of perceived change in five livelihood capitals, and applies it to 238 households in the Trang An World Heritage Site, Vietnam. title: Phytochemical composition, antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and quorum-sensing inhibitory activities of Citrus medica L. cv. ‘Liscia’ essential oil supported by molecular docking, molecular dynamics, DFT, and ADMET evaluation
abstract: The global rise of antimicrobial resistance underscores the urgent need for novel therapeutic agents, with medicinal aromatic plants representing a promising source of bioactive compounds. Citrus medica L. cv. ‘Liscia’ has traditionally been used for its pharmacological properties; however, its essential oil remains insufficiently characterized. This study provides the first integrated evaluation of C. medica cv. ‘Liscia’ essential oil (CMLEO) for its antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and anti-quorum-sensing activities using complementary in vitro and in silico approaches. title: Morphophysiological diversity in rice: A trait-based framework for carbon capture, allocation, and genotype selection
abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) provides a primary source of caloric intake for over half of the global population. Aligning grain production with climate mitigation requires understanding how plant traits influence carbon balance under contrasting water regimes, which affect both trait expression and the fate of plant-derived carbon in soil and greenhouse-gas emissions. Here, the morphological and physiological attributes that govern carbon acquisition, allocation, and retention in rice were reviewed. title: Interaction between the East Asian summer monsoon and Westerlies as shown by desert shrub-ring records from the Alxa Plateau, Northwest China
abstract: Abstract. The variations, driving mechanisms, and interactions between the mid-latitude westerlies and the Asian summer monsoon represent a critical focus in global change research. Extensive research has investigated climate change and its drivers across multiple timescales in the core regions of both westerlies Asia and monsoonal Asia. However, studies are far fewer in the arid inland deserts at the interactive margin of these two circulation systems, where precipitation restrict the distribution of trees. title: Responsible Management Education and Its Potential as an Epistemic Object of Change
abstract: Abstract This study examines whether and how RME can be performed as an epistemic object to broaden business schools’ education on climate change. The research builds on a qualitative case study involving 10 Finnish business schools. The analysis reveals that RME is performed as both an epistemic object and a boundary object, with different implications for its embeddedness within institutions. Our findings show how accreditations have introduced RME as a boundary object enforcing performativity around sustainability themes yet enabling disciplines to maintain their distinct or limited roles.

title: A COI barcode reference dataset for Polish land gastropods supports biodiversity monitoring in Central Europe
abstract: Terrestrial molluscs are important components of terrestrial ecosystems, yet they remain poorly represented in molecular biodiversity assessments. Although they occur in a wide range of habitats, their inclusion in such studies is constrained by the lack of reliable genetic reference data, particularly in Central Europe. In Poland, despite a well-documented malacofauna comprising approximately 179 species, genetic data remain scarce. abstract: Sustainable destination development calls for a view of sustainability that extends beyond its economic, sociocultural and environmental pillars to political and technological considerations. Drawing on the stimulus– organism–response (S-O-R) framework, this study examines how Generation Z tourists' perceptions of destination sustainability relate to perceived value, tourist satisfaction and electronic word-of-mouth (e-WOM) intention. title: Water–energy–food nexus perspectives on small-scale cassava processing: A case study of a processors’ association in Egbeda LGA, Oyo State, Nigeria
abstract: Nigeria produces over 63 million tons of cassava annually, making it the world’s largest producer. However, in smallholder communities in Nigeria, there is a disparity in production quantity and processing efficiency compared to economies like Thailand, which produces less. This study examines the operational practices, constraints, and opportunities within a cassava processing association in Egbeda Local Government Area of Oyo State, Nigeria, through lens of Water-Energy-Food (WEF) nexus. The Bayesian simulation technique originally proposed by Wolfinger was utilized to develop the two-sided Bayesian guaranteed coverage tolerance interval. abstract: This paper conceptually examines the National Assessment of Educational Progress (NAEP) in the United States and draws strategic lessons for Nigeria's basic education assessment system. Despite substantial investments in the Universal Basic Education (UBE) programme since 1999, Nigeria faces a persistent learning crisis exacerbated by weak assessment structures that prioritize certification over systemic improvement. title: Spatial Distribution and Hydrogeological Controls On Hydrocarbon Contamination in Groundwater in Ogale, Niger Delta, Nigeria
abstract: Groundwater contamination by petroleum hydrocarbons is an environmental concern in the Niger Delta, where oil-related activities threaten groundwater resources used by surrounding communities. This study investigated the spatial distribution of total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), and benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene and xylenes (BTEX) in groundwater in Ogale, Rivers State, Nigeria, and examined their relationships with selected hydrogeological parameters. title: Urbanisation drives parallel genomic divergence across cities and bumble bee species
abstract: BACKGROUND: Urbanisation imposes pervasive environmental change, yet it remains unclear whether evolutionary responses to cities are largely idiosyncratic or whether similar selective pressures across cities repeatedly generate predictable genomic outcomes. RESULTS: Here, we analyse whole-genome data from 524 individuals of three widespread bumble bee species sampled across nine independent urban-rural pairs in Central Europe to test whether urban environments drive parallel evolutionary responses across cities and species. title: Hedonic Analysis of Cassava Product Attributes' Influence on Observed Market Prices. A Case Study of Smallholder Farmers in Kilifi County, Kenya
abstract: Cassava commercialisation is increasing in Kenya, mainly due to recent emphasis on its role in enhancing food security and income generation. However, smallholder cassava farmers still receive low prices for their products, constraining their ability to maximise returns. There is limited empirical evidence on how cassava product attributes influence market prices. Understanding the product attribute-price relationship will enable farmers to orient their production, marketing and value addition to attract better prices. title: Social Work Licensure with a Criminal Record: A Legal Mapping Project of 56 U.S. States and Territories
abstract: This legal mapping paper aims to aggregate state-specific policies on the impact of criminal legal system contact—more specifically, the impact of criminal convictions—on social work licensure. Situating these policies within an abolitionist analysis and the larger history of social work in the United States, the paper attempts to expose the contradictions alive within the profession’s discourse. title: Public attitudes toward speed safety camera enforcement and critical elements of support in British Columbia, Canada
abstract: Background This study aimed to determine the views of British Columbia (B.C.) residents on acceptance and wider adoption of automated speed enforcement (ASE) in their province and local communities. The specific objectives of this study were to determine 1) the proportion of B.C. residents who approve/disapprove of ASE; 2) the characteristics of people who approve/disapprove of ASE; and 3) the critical elements that would engender support for ASE. abstract: Kulit jeruk yang sering dianggap sebagai limbah agroindustri mengandung berbagai senyawa bioaktif yang berpotensi memiliki aktivitas farmakologis, termasuk antibakteri. title: Moments of pleasure in the lives of older adults: why do they matter?
abstract: While research has recently focused on pleasure associated with deeply engaging pursuits such as hockey or dance, limited attention has been given to pleasurable momentary experiences in the lives of older adults. Examined through the lens of pleasure, the purpose of this secondary analysis was to explore the role of everyday moments of leisure in the lives of older adults. title: Functional Food Innovation of Mekai Leaf (Albertisia Papuana Becc.) Catfish Sticks Based on Community Empowerment in Tuwung Village
abstract: The community service program in Tuwung Village, Central Kalimantan, aims to address overproduction and fluctuations in catfish prices through downstreaming and food diversification. The solution offered is the transfer of technology for producing catfish sticks seasoned with natural Mekai leaf (Albertisia papuana Becc.) as an organic, non MSG flavor enhancer. abstract: The rapid global expansion of photovoltaic (PV) systems, driven by rising energy demand, is expected to generate substantial module waste at end-of-life, with global PV waste projected to exceed 4 million tonnes by 2030, 50 million by 2040, and 200 million tonnes by 2050. Based on 102 publications identified through Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and IEEE Xplore databases, this review provides a comparative, literature-based assessment of recycling, second-life applications, and disposal as end-of-life (EoL) management strategies for PV modules, examining the relationship between modu

title: Lower post-irrigation nitrous oxide pulses on diversified organic strawberry farms
abstract: Abstract Diversified organic farming systems are promoted for the ecosystem services they provide, but their potential to mitigate nitrous oxide (N₂O) emissions has not been evaluated in strawberry production, where emissions are delivered largely in short pulses following irrigation. We measured N₂O fluxes from automated soil chambers before, during, and after a single irrigation event on 48 focal plots across 34 certified organic strawberry farms on California’s Central Coast, over two growing seasons. title: Screen kiss in China: kissing performance and its social acceptability in Chinese feature films during the “Seventeen Years” period (1949–1966)
abstract: The claim that the “first kiss” on the screen in the People’s Republic of China (P.R.C.) appeared in Romance on Lushan Mountain (1980) needs to be corrected. This study argues that the first kiss on screen in the P.R.C. should be in the film Caravans with Ring, produced by Shanghai Film Studio in 1954. Besides, under the dual influence of traditional Chinese culture and mainstream ideology at that time, the depiction of kissing on screen, while broadening the scope of film expression, exceeded the cultural limits that the era could bear and construct. title: Investigating emerging contaminants in dams from the Vhembe District in Limpopo and, for the first time, in the Orlando Dam, Gauteng Province, South Africa
abstract: Endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs), including certain organophosphate pesticides, herbicides, fungicides, and metals, as well as pharmaceuticals such as antiretroviral drugs (ARVs), are contaminants of increasing concern in freshwater sources in South Africa (SA). One surface water sample from each site was collected from dams in an urban area, Gauteng Province, and from a rural area, the Vhembe District in the Limpopo Province in SA. title: Phenolic Diglycoside Biomarkers: Assessing 2020 Wildfire Smoke Impacts on Oregon Pinot noir Wines Alongside Sensory and Marketplace Data
abstract: This study presents the first AVA-resolved retrospective assessment of wildfire smoke impacts on 2020 Oregon Willamette Valley Pinot noir by merging phenolic diglycoside (PDG) biomarker concentrations with sensory appraisals and marketplace performance. Analysis of 90 commercial wines representing all 12 Willamette Valley AVAs revealed that most lots lacked molecular evidence of substantial wildfire smoke exposure. title: (De)Sacralization of the Totalitarian System in Anthony Doerr’s Novel “All the Light We Cannot See”
abstract: This study investigates the artistic representation of the processes of (de)sacralization and the totalitarian system in Anthony Doerr’s novel “All the Light We Cannot See”. Combining historical-political, cultural, and literary approaches makes it possible to trace the narrative mechanisms behind the formation of a quasi-religious model of Nazi ideology and the specifics of its subsequent demythologization in the novel. title: Im/mobilities and the Occupying Gaze
abstract: This article considers how the occupying gaze transforms bodies and objects into suspended sites of gendered and political violence. While in peacetime waiting suggests ennui and stasis, the im/mobility that occurs at Israeli checkpoints is entangled with power, including who decides how time is valued, and how and whose bodies move (and where to). Against this backdrop, the gaze transforms bodies and objects into political and gendered sites of violence. title: Secure Authentication Model for Enhancing Single Sign-On Security against Credential Compromise
abstract: Biometric data, such as fingerprints has the potential to mitigate risks, enhance user experience, and inform cybersecurity practices. Finding SSO vulnerabilities is the first step in the research objectives' well-defined process that also includes designing and implementing an authentication model and finally evaluating how well it prevents unauthorized access. title: Plant diversity–mediated variation in root exudates regulates anaerobic nitrogen transformations in soil
abstract: Abstract Plants can regulate soil biogeochemical processes via root exudates, yet how exudate quantity and composition influence soil nitrogen (N) transformations remains unclear. We conducted complementary pot and microcosm experiments across gradients of plant species, phylogenetic and functional group diversity to examine effects of root exudates on anaerobic N transformation processes in soils, including dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA), denitrification and anaerobic ammonium oxidation (anammox). institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Haematology and biochemistry parameters for koalas ( Phascolarctos cinereus ) on Raymond Island, Victoria : use of point‐of‐care analysers
abstract: Biochemistry and haematology analytes can provide information on the health status of individual animals or populations in direct comparison to expected values or reference intervals developed using the same analysis methodology from a healthy reference population of the target species. Point-of-care analysers are increasingly used in the assessment of wildlife health; however, their effective use in wildlife species requires establishment of appropriate expected values from clinically healthy animals. title: Genomics Reveals Anthropogenic Fragmentation and Introgression in a Highly Endangered New Zealand Freshwater Fish
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim The endemic freshwater fish fauna of New Zealand has been severely impacted by drainage modifications and the introduction of salmonid predators. We aim to test for the impacts of anthropogenic population fragmentation on genetic diversity in a critically endangered endemic fish, to inform future conservation management of this species. Location Teviot River and surrounding drainages, South Island, New Zealand. title: From Global Emergence to Local Anchorage: Evolution of the CSR Concept, Morocco's Commitment and Integration into the Educational System
abstract: Since the 20th century, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) has been widely explored by researchers and practitioners across different contexts. Over time, the concept has evolved into a complex and multidimensional framework, characterized by diverse interpretations and the absence of a unified theoretical consensus. While industrialized countries began to engage with CSR as early as the 1950s, Morocco’s commitment to sustainability emerged later. title: Awareness and factors associated with improved cookstove choice among end users in Kericho County, Rift Valley, Kenya
abstract: Abstract The understanding of the user engagement, selection and adoption of Improved Cooking Stoves (ICS) in developing countries is important to deploy measures to sustain their use. As part of a project developing, deploying, and empowering communities in developing countries with ICS, this study screened the awareness and choice selection factors for end users selected for ICS adoption. This was achieved through a survey of 1200 households in Kericho County in the Rift Valley, Kenya. title: Environmental enrichment is associated with changes in the gut microbiome and resistome of captive pythons
abstract: Environmental enrichment is widely used to improve the welfare of captive animals, yet its effects on reptilian gut microbiota remain poorly understood. Here, we used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to investigate the gut microbiome and resistome of two captive python species: Burmese python (Python bivittatus) and reticulated python (Malayopython reticulatus), before and after environmental enrichment. title: A Comparative Study of VR Therapy and Traditional Methods for Stress Management
abstract: Stress arising from academic, professional and financial demands is common among students and young professionals, and the coping methods within easiest reach, such as listening to music, do not always suffice. This paper presents a survey-driven design for a virtual reality (VR) gadget that combines selectable immersive natural environments, environment-matched sound therapy and heart-rate biofeedback for short relaxation sessions. title: Multilayer pH ‐Responsive Hydrogels Upcycled From Carrageenan‐Based Capsule Residues for Colon‐Targeted Delivery of 5‐Aminosalicylic Acid
abstract: ABSTRACT Softgel capsule manufacturing generates substantial carrageenan‐containing byproducts that are typically discarded, despite their intrinsic gel‐forming and polyelectrolyte‐complexing capability. This study reports a sustainable strategy for upcycling carrageenan‐based capsule residues (CCR) into multilayer pH‐responsive hydrogel beads for colon‐targeted delivery of 5‐aminosalicylic acid (5‐ASA). title: Evaluation of Wheat Genotypes for Combined Heat and Drought Stress Tolerance
abstract: A field experiment was carried out from November 2021 to April 2022 to assess the tolerance of five wheat genotypes to combined heat and drought stress. The study followed a split plot design with three replications. The main plot treatment consisted of two growing conditions (normal condition and combined heat and drought condition) and the sub-plot treatments consisted of five wheat genotypes (BARI Gom 29, BARI Gom 30, BARI Gom 31, BWMRI Gom 3 and BAW 1290). title: Sustaining Life under Extraction: Environmental Justice and Community Capabilities in Anindita S. Thayf’s Tanah Tabu and Korrie Layun Rampan’s Api Awan Asap
abstract: Extractive pressures threaten collective life despite economic gains. This study examines how environmental injustice reshapes substantive opportunities to sustain livelihoods and pursue valued collective futures. Environmental justice and community capabilities frame readings of Anindita S. Thayf’s Tanah Tabu [Taboo Land] and Korrie Layun Rampan’s Api Awan Asap [Fire, Clouds, and Smoke]. title: Human in vitro airway models to assess point-of-contact respiratory toxicity of surfactants: development and evaluation of a repeated-exposure study design
abstract: Repeated-dose exposure studies can provide insights into the toxicity of test substances, including dose-response relationships, cumulative effects, delayed responses, and reversibility of effects. A limited number of in vitro studies have assessed the effects of repeated exposure of respiratory cells to chemicals applied as liquids (via direct pipetting). The work presented in this paper builds upon these published in vitro repeated-dose studies to develop and evaluate a repeat-exposure study design for use with reconstructed human respiratory epithelium (RHRE). title: An Integrated Navigation and Obstacle Avoidance Scheme for Indoor Mobile Robots
abstract: Indoor mobile robots are expected to reach a goal, build a usable representation of the surrounding space, and avoid obstacles that were never present on any prior map — all simultaneously, and on hardware compact enough to be carried on board the robot. Most published navigation stacks rely on a desktop computer or an embedded Linux board running ROS, which is convenient for research but heavy, power-hungry, and difficult to certify for real-time behavior. title: Heat exposure and perceived academic functioning among nursing students in a tropical higher education setting: a qualitative study
abstract: Background: Extreme heat presents a growing challenge for nursing education in tropical regions. However, there is limited qualitative evidence regarding students' experiences across commuting, campus, and learning environments. Aim: This study explores nursing students' experiences of heat, its perceived impact on academic functioning, and both personal and institutional responses. Methods: A qualitative descriptive design was employed. title: Law Audit on Violation of Fundamental Right in Context of Water Shortage in Bengaluru
abstract: This research paper presents a comprehensive legal audit investigating the systemic water shortage in Bengaluru and its direct implications on fundamental rights, particularly the right to life, dignity, and livelihood under the Constitution of India. With a population exceeding 13 million heavily reliant on distant river supplies and rapidly depleting groundwater, Bengaluru faces a recurring structural deficit, marked by a documented official shortfall of over 500 million liters per day and widespread drying of borewells. title: Unveiling digital vulnerabilities: Integrating online risks into community-based contextual child protection
abstract: : Background Adoption of digital technologies is impacting child protection outcomes. There is a significant convergence of offline vulnerabilities into the online environment, necessitating the inclusion of online safety within established offline safeguarding approaches to address both online and offline threats. Objective Grounded in a contextual prevention framework, this study assesses online and offline risks experienced by young people in Indonesian rural communities. title: Ancestry-specific and multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies of restless legs syndrome
abstract: Abstract Restless legs syndrome is a neurological disorder that disrupts sleep and quality of life, but its genetics have mostly been studied in individuals of European ancestry. Here, we perform GWAS of restless legs syndrome using data from individuals of African, Latin American, and European ancestry, followed by a multi-ancestry meta-analysis. We leverage biobank-based cohorts that established RLS diagnosis using validated clinical criteria, allowing for precise phenotypic characterization. title: SOIL STABILIZATION USING INDUSTRIAL BYPRODUCTS
abstract: —Soil stabilization is used when natural ground cannot provide the strength, volume stability or bearing capacity required for construction. Conventional lime and cement treatments are effective but involve energy use and environmental burdens. This review synthesizes six principal review/technical papers supplied for this work, together with two quantitative experimental studies, on fly ash, cement kiln dust (CKD), ground-granulated blastfurnace slag (GGBS), silica fume, calcium carbide residue (CCR), rice husk ash (RHA), quarry dust, red mud, copper slag and waste-plastic reinforcement. title: Plant Germplasm Registration Notice*
abstract: A total of 121 proposals were received online for consideration of registration of germplasm for unique/superior traits. The member-secretary, Plant Germplasm Registration Committee (PGRC), thoroughly screened the applications, and experts reviewed 65 proposals complete in all respects, which were presented at the 51st PGRC meeting held virtually on November 22, 2023. abstract: OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to conduct an exploratory assessment of the incidence and factors associated with severe postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) in women with posterior low-lying placenta and prior cesarean without prenatal suspicion of placenta accreta spectrum (PAS). METHODS: The study population was derived from the PACCRETA population-based study conducted in the 176 maternity units of 12 French regions from November 2013 through October 2015. title: Molecular Characterisation of Bacteria Associated with Dental Infections in Jos, Nigeria
abstract: Purpose: This study aims to molecularly characterise the bacteria responsible for dental infections by identifying key bacterial taxa, clarifying their genetic pathogenicity determinants, and assessing the prevalence of antibiotic resistance genes. Design/Methodology/Approach: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 120 patients presenting with clinically diagnosed dental infections. title: A mixed expansion model of East Asian agriculture into northern Pakistan: demic via southern route but cultural from the northern
abstract: While East Asian agriculture notably impacted northern Pakistan's prehistory, its diffusion model into this region remains unclear. Here we generated 115 high-coverage whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data from three northern Pakistani populations (Burusho (Hunza), Shina, and Hazarewal), and integrated 2,029 modern and 4,358 ancient genomes from Eurasia. title: How did borders get so bad?
abstract: Recent anthropology theorizes borders primarily as technologies of exclusion that perpetuate structural inequality and racialized violence. This perspective downplays the varied cultural meanings of boundaries that shape identities within and amongst countries of the global south, ultimately resting on a neo-functionalist model of borders and boundary-making. title: Quality and shelf life of filled pasta with meat analogs made from durum wheat meal and pea proteins
abstract: This study investigates the use of meat analogs in fresh filled pasta, a relatively underexplored application with significant potential for innovation. Beef meat (M) was replaced with plant-based meat analog (MA), and the effects on technological properties, quality attributes, consumer acceptance were evaluated. Shelf-life was also assessed under two different packaging systems, namely modified atmosphere (MAP) and vacuum-skin packaging (VSP). title: UnChartered territory: The unprecedented recognition of two previously dead languages under the European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages
abstract: The European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages recently broke new ground by supporting two languages that had previously died; and not just under its fairly tokenistic, unburdensome Part II, but the much more extensive (and expensive) Part III. Manx Gaelic, having been recognised by the United Kingdom under Part II in 2003, went on to Part III status in 2020, followed by Cornish in 2025 (CoE, 2021; 2025a, 2026). title: Literature Review of the Potential of Miana Leaf Extract as an Antibacterial Agent Against Escherichia coli in Urinary Tract Infections
abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are among the most common infectious diseases, with Escherichia coli recognized as the predominant causative pathogen. The ability of E. coli to form biofilms and increasing antibiotic resistance have encouraged the exploration of natural antibacterial agents. Miana leaves (Coleus scutellarioides (L.) Benth.) contain bioactive compounds, including flavonoids, tannins, saponins, alkaloids, and essential oils, which may exhibit antibacterial properties. title: Evaluation Of Consumer Preference Level For Lempuk Durian Products As A Traditional Food From Bengkalis Island: Hedonic Testing With Organoleptic Quality Attribute
abstract: Lempuk durian is a traditional durian confection and culinary emblem of Bengkalis Island, yet producers have long judged its quality through inherited intuition rather than systematic sensory evidence. This study examined how four organoleptic attributes, namely color, aroma, taste, and texture, influence consumer preference for the product, and used interviews with a producer and community informants to interpret the numerical results. title: A Practical Formulation for Seismic Damage Accumulation on Multiple Mainshock‐Aftershock Sequences Based on Disaggregation of the Mainshock Hazard
abstract: ABSTRACT Earthquakes often occur in clusters (foreshocks, mainshocks, and aftershocks) and can lead to cumulative structural damage. Many studies have extended traditional performance‐based earthquake engineering (PBEE) to account for damage accumulation in multiple mainshock‐aftershock (MS‐AS) sequences using Markov chain processes and state‐dependent fragilities. title: From Palm Refinery Residues to Vaccine Adjuvants: Qualifying PFAD Derived Squalene Through Quality-by-Design and Immunological Comparability
abstract: Squalene-based oil-in-water emulsions underpin established vaccine-adjuvant platforms, while palm fatty acid distillate (PFAD) provides a potentially recoverable non-animal source of squalene. This qualitative literature review critically integrates research on PFAD separation, pharmaceutical impurities, squalene-emulsion mechanisms, formulation stability, clinical vaccine evidence, and sustainable manufacturing. title: The desired and the desiring: Helen as ālambana and the courses of kāma in Homeric epic
abstract: Helen of Troy is usually read through her beauty, her abduction, and her responsibility for the war. This article asks a different question: why does the presence of one desired woman occasion such different courses of response in those who meet her, and how does each of those courses change over time? title: Combination of dispersive solid phase extraction using Fe₂O3@ZIF-8@CeO₂ nanocomposite and dispersive liquid–liquid microextraction as an efficient sample preparation method for the extraction of heavy metal ions from honey
abstract: A Fe₂O 3 @ZIF-8@CeO₂ core–shell nanocomposite was reported as a highly effective sorbent for the dispersive solid phase extraction of Pb(II), Cd(II), and Cu(II) ions from honey. The combination of porous ZIF-8 network with Fe and CeO₂ resulted in a high density of accessible sites, providing strong affinity toward heavy metal ions. title: Ultrasonication-assisted magnesiothermic synthesis of cast in-situ graphene-MgO reinforced AZ91 magnesium hybrid nanocomposites
abstract: A sustainable liquid metallurgy route was developed for the in-situ synthesis of graphene (Gr)@MgO hybrid reinforcements in AZ91 magnesium alloy via simultaneous CO 2 bubbling and ultrasonication. The magnesiothermic reduction of CO 2 enables the formation of multilayer Gr decorated with nanoscale (< 5 nm) MgO particles, as confirmed by Raman spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). title: Multi-omics reveals metabolic shifts by Candida-enhanced fermentation in improving cigar tobacco quality
abstract: Traditional natural fermentation of cigar tobacco leaves is stochastic and often yields inconsistent quality. To elucidate how Candida inoculation improves cigar tobacco quality, we performed integrated metagenomic and metabolomic analyses on leaves fermented with or without Candida metapsilosis . title: Early-life forage modulation is associated with ruminal microbiota and metabolic profiles in yak calves
abstract: Abstract Early-life dietary intervention plays a critical role in shaping ruminal microbial colonization, fermentation capacity, and functional maturation in young ruminants. However, how forage composition regulates rumen microbiome establishment and microbiota-associated metabolism during early yak development remains poorly understood. abstract: The genus Ipomoea (Convolvulaceae) consists of medicinal herbs that have been traditionally used for the treatment of diabetes, inflammation, anti-microbial, as laxative and against kidney stones. abstract: Abstract Invasions are narrated. They are narrated afterwards, when it comes to the construction of their meaning and legacy, and they are narrated in advance, when their logic and supposed necessity are first established. In fact, invasions—notwithstanding their very real and horrific physical and social consequences—cannot be fully understood without studying the stories that are told about them. abstract: This structured narrative review examines the opportunities, barriers, and policy implications of digital transformation in Vietnam during 2020–2026. abstract: Abstract An authorized medical device may still need outside capital before its sponsor, the firm responsible for it, can manufacture and launch it. The paper asks what public U.S. records can show about whether authorization timing relates to access to that capital, and what a credible test needs. It does not estimate a financing or commercialization effect. abstract: Abstract Climate change is expected to intensify drought frequency and variability, threatening agricultural productivity and food security, particularly in vulnerable regions such as the Andean highlands. abstract: This paper presents a methodology that integrates Quality Function Deployment (QFD), Value Engineering (VE), and Lean principles to prioritize control tests in product design. abstract: Abstract Typically high levels of ammonium in landfill leachate necessitate biological nitrogen removal at wastewater treatment facilities. Furthermore, landfill leachate often contains elevated concentrations of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), which calls for new removal methods. abstract: Growing environmental concerns regarding petroleum-based plastics have accelerated the search for sustainable food-packaging alternatives. abstract: Optimizing the business environment is a pivotal aspect of China’s governance modernization. abstract: The understanding of changes of rainfall patterns and climate extremes are crucial factors for addressing agricultural risks and sustaining water resources in Ethiopia. This study aims to investigate baseline rainfall climatology (1991-2020) and long-term spatiotemporal changes (1981-2022) of Kiremt seasonal rainfall totals (PRCPTOT) and selected ETCCDI-based rainfall indices across Ethiopia. abstract: The strength of the Australian studies community in China has long been cited as a standout achievement of the field. abstract: Malaysia hosts millions of migrants: willing and coerced, with legal status and without. Despite relying on migrant workers, Malaysian policies do little to alleviate exploitation. abstract: As climate change intensifies, sugar beet ( Beta vulgaris L.) crops face unprecedented threats from severe drought, soil salinity, and extreme temperatures. Safeguarding this vital source of global sugar production and bioethanol feedstocks requires an urgent shift toward climate-smart agriculture. abstract: Understanding the role of social relationships in shaping livelihood outcomes is critical to addressing persistent food insecurity among smallholder farmers in Nigeria. title: Conservation status of New York's pollinators
abstract: Abstract The global decline of insect pollinators is now well documented and recognized publicly from all over the Earth in a wide variety of ecosystems. Because a great deal of pollinator‐relevant environmental regulation (e.g., pesticide limitation, invasive species control) happens at the subnational level, an understanding of the subnational conservation status of these organisms is needed for targeting actions and monitoring their efficacy. abstract: Smallholder farmers in southwestern Ethiopia face overlapping challenges that trap them in cycles of poverty and land degradation, yet the feedback mechanisms sustaining these traps remain poorly understood. abstract: There remains considerable debate about the exact relationships between climate, conflict, and migration. This article draws on appeal applications to the Administrative Review Tribunal in Australia from asylum seekers from Sudan and South Sudan to trace links between climate-related conflict and asylum migration to Australia. abstract: Abstract Town criers were ubiquitous civic officials in early modern Europe. Their voices contributed to a continuous cycle of noise that informed, regulated and shaped urban life. title: Precision determination of $B_c$ and $B_c^*$ meson decay constants from lattice QCD
abstract: We present a lattice QCD study of heavy-heavy meson decay constants using the HISQ gauge ensemble generated by the MILC Collaboration. Employing the HISQ action for both charm and bottom valence quarks tuned to their physical masses, we determine pseudoscalar, vector, and tensor decay constants for heavy quarkonium and $B_c$ systems. abstract: Robotic missions involving spatially distributed tasks often require jointly selecting rewarding locations and planning feasible motions under limited travel budgets. This paper proposes Reward-Guided RRT*, a new sampling-based framework that constructs a budget-feasible mission through a sequence of locally joint task-selection-and-motion-planning stages, evaluated directly in the continuous state space, without requiring a precomputed task-transition graph. abstract: Abstract JWST has uncovered a population of compact high-redshift galaxies, `little red dots' (LRDs), exhibiting broad Balmer emission lines that often show narrow absorption features and strong Balmer breaks --- spectral signatures attributed to dense gas surrounding rapidly growing black holes, but whose small-scale structure remains unknown. title: Base Models Can Detect Hidden Intentions that Prompted Classifiers Miss
abstract: The Persona Selection Model (PSM) posits that post-training selects a persona the model learned during pre-training. Work on subliminal learning has shown that models can impart covert signals (like "love of owls") into semantically unrelated outputs like strings of numbers, and that students trained on these outputs inherit those traits. In this work I show that by evaluating the likelihood of such outputs under the base pre-trained model with an appropriate header, a method I call persona-header likelihood evaluation (PHLE), one can decode these subliminal signals and classify between them.

title: Recursive Self-Improvement of Exoskeleton Assistance Policies through Human-in-the-Loop Feedback
abstract: To reduce reliance on manual design and extensive parameter tuning, a framework for the autonomous evolution of exoskeleton assistance policies through human feedback is proposed. Assistance policies are autonomously generated as executable control code by an intelligent agent and evaluated in experiments with human participants. Subjective user feedback, movement performance, and muscle activation measurements are incorporated into policy assessment. Based on these assessments, policy deficiencies are autonomously identified and the control code is revised by the agent for subsequent trials.

abstract: Control surface aerodynamics plays a crucial role in aircraft performance, both in cruise and low speed conditions, where fuel consumption and stability are most critical. abstract: Fire regulates terrestrial carbon storage and land–atmosphere carbon exchange, yet its response to past warm climates is strongly region dependent. abstract: Abstract Emergent constraints are increasingly used to reduce uncertainty in regional climate projections by exploiting relationships across models between observable historical predictors and projected changes. abstract: Globally, cities account for 78% of energy consumption and 70~75% of greenhouse gas emissions. abstract: This paper presents a finite element strength assessment of a ship double bottom structure. abstract: Wildfires alter land surface albedo and temperature, modulating the radiative budget and climate. Previous studies have predominantly reported enhanced shortwave absorption induced by post-fire surface darkening over forests. title: Military experience and ethical restraint: Evidence from CEO insider trading
abstract: Abstract We examine the relation between CEO military experience and insider trading in U.S. public firms. Military CEOs earn significantly lower insider trading profits than non‐military CEOs, particularly those who attained commissioned ranks or served in the Air Force, Army, or Marine Corps. The negative relation holds for both purchase and sale transactions. Military CEOs also exhibit longer investment horizons and are less likely to trade in the month preceding earnings announcements. abstract: The presence of linguistic expressions of gender-fair language has experienced a steady increase in recent decades. abstract: ABSTRACT Caravan and mobile‐home parks combine tourism, housing and communal infrastructure but remain weakly represented in flood‐risk assessment and disaster appraisal. abstract: Entrepreneurship education is often presented as a route to employability and innovation, yet its transformative capacity depends on the regional and institutional conditions through which it is enacted. This comparative case study examines Hangzhou Normal University (HZNU) and Chongqing Normal University (CQNU), two teacher-education institutions located in contrasting innovation ecosystems. abstract: This study investigates the structural paradox of waste compensation policies in the Bantargebang Integrated Waste Treatment Plant (TPST), Bekasi, which has emerged as a consequence of megapolitan Jakarta's massive waste accumulation. abstract: The Merchant Shipping Act, 2025 marks a significant transition in India’s maritime legal framework by consolidating and restructuring the law governing maritime casualties in closer alignment with international conventions. This paper examines the liability, response obligations and limitation rights arising from a maritime casualty involving a collision between an oil tanker and a container vessel in Indian territorial waters. abstract: Single-use plastics (SUPs) remain a major obstacle to a circular plastics economy. abstract: This article examines how populist actors articulate democratic principles in their political communication. Rather than focusing on whether populism is compatible with liberal democracy, the study analyses how populist leaders themselves interpret and mobilise democratic language. Drawing on a comparative analysis of Twitter communication by Nigel Farage, Matteo Salvini, Giorgia Meloni, and Marine Le Pen between 2013 and 2022, the article investigates how democratic discourse is structured along three institutional dimensions: pluralism, parliamentarism, and constitutionalism. abstract: This study aimed to examine and analyze the role of corporate governance in moderating the influence of green intellectual capital and blue accounting disclosure on corporate sustainability performance. title: Women at the Core of Climate-Smart Agriculture: Advancing Equity and Food Security through Empowerment
abstract: Climate volatility threatens global food security, particularly in developing nations where female farmers face severe resource barriers. This narrative review synthesizes empirical research published between 2010 and 2026 to evaluate women’s empowerment, climate-smart agricultural adoption, and household food security. Applying structured narrative frameworks, 44 academic studies and policy reports were synthesized across four major academic databases. The selected literature was analyzed using Feminist Political Ecology and the Women’s Empowerment in Agriculture Index conceptual frameworks.

abstract: This paper explores responses of host communities to offshore wind energy infrastructure through a case study of the Aberdeen Offshore Wind Farm (OWF), situated 2.4 km off the coast of northeast Scotland. Adopting a longitudinal mixed-methods research approach, the nearby communities’ evolving responses are explored across four phases of OWF development: pre-consent, consent, construction, and early operation. abstract: Abstract. Headwater streams in agricultural landscapes can contribute substantially to nitrous oxide (N₂O) emissions, yet the environmental controls on stream N₂O dynamics remain poorly resolved, particularly in systems with low pH. abstract: The Russian and Norwegian presence on Svalbard, a Norwegian Arctic Archipelago with a unique legal status, is characterized by constrained functional cooperation and diplomatic tension. This study aims to clarify how Svalbard is perceived in Russian public discourse by analyzing a selection of articles from mainstream Russian federal media published between 2010 and 2025. title: Indigenous Peoples and the Rights of Nature: A comparative analysis of environmental justice from the Philippines to the global stage
abstract: Abstract The Rights of Nature (RoN) framework provides that nature has inherent rights independent from economic and environmental rights of humans. To realise this, nature's own legal standing in court needs to be recognised. This article discusses the interconnection of the RoN framework and the rights of Indigenous Peoples, emphasising the need to fully integrate the RoN framework into State‐based legal systems to protect the rights of Indigenous Peoples and the environment. abstract: Biodiversity refers to the structural, functional and evolutionary variability among living organisms across genetic, species and ecosystem hierarchical tiers. Accelerating industrialization, habitat fragmentation, deforestation, agrochemical saturation and anthropogenic climate change have initiated a modern mass extinction event that compromises ecological stability and human survival. abstract: The 2011 9.1 Tohoku earthquake generated strong seismic waves that were recorded globally. This study examines the relative influence of finite-fault slip model representation and 3D crustal velocity structure on reproducing teleseismic ground motions recorded at 20 seismic stations across India. title: The Alternative to “Harm” in the ESA “Take” Claims
abstract: Wildlife agencies recently finalized major changes to regulations interpreting the Endangered Species Act (ESA). These regulations remove longstanding habitat protections for endangered and threatened species. To better protect wildlife and to solidify habitat protection’s role in Section 9 ESA litigation, conservation groups should bring more claims arguing that proposed projects “harass” wildlife by changing or destroying their habitat. This Note explores the potential effectiveness of “take” claims that allege “harass,” rather than “harm,” in the habitat modification context.

abstract: The accelerating challenges of climate change, resource depletion, urbanization, and social inequality have placed humanity and the planet at a critical juncture, where sustainability is no longer a choice but a necessity. abstract: Abstract Physical climate risks are a source of vulnerability in financial systems, yet existing risk measurement approaches struggle to translate them into decision-relevant metrics, reflecting a mismatch between how climate risk evolves and how financial risk is assessed. Drawing on workshops and interviews with 35 finance and risk professionals (33 from a large financial institution, two from a global insurance broker), we identify six interacting risk domains through which physical climate risk cascades to credit loss, creating decision bottlenecks where routine practice breaks down. abstract: Offshore wind power (OWP) and offshore energy hubs (OEHs) have recently become stable components of decarbonisation efforts across the EU. title: From real-world governance to playable action: translating three environmental cases into game mechanics in Eco Stewards
abstract: Environmental problems often take a long time to deal with, but a turn in a board game is short. When real problems are put into a game, some details have to be left out. Can players still understand why the actions are needed? This paper discusses this question through three cases in Eco Stewards: the Great Pacific Garbage Patch, methylmercury pollution in Minamata Bay, and soil erosion on China's Loess Plateau. title: Rules for the Calculation of Common Pecuniary Losses
abstract: The common allowance calculation rules are an important guarantee for the common allowance system to achieve risk sharing and interest balance. With the development of shipping practices, existing calculation rules face new issues concerning expense recognition, procedural connection, and special risk handling. This paper takes the 2022 "Common Maritime Loss Calculation Rules of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade" as the main research object and compares them with the 2016 "York-Antwerp Rules" and the current "Maritime Law of the People's Republic of China". Based on ex
journal: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media

title: Estuary and Ecofantasy: The Everyday Lives of Nipa Palm between Builder and Botanist
abstract: Abstract This text follows a well-known botanist along the shoreline of a Philippine island as he takes photographs of nipa palm ( nypa fruticans ), in its passage from plant to building part. It is January 1940 and David Fairchild is interested in plants for the collection of his new botanical garden in Miami, nicknamed ‘the kampong’. He takes a photograph of nipa being woven into roof shingles by women sitting cross-legged, watched by children. At the lens of Fairchild’s camera, the material forms of two world orders converge. One is the process of building construction in archipelagic South
journal: Transactions of the Royal Historical Society

title: ADMINISTRATIVE LAW AS A RESPONSE TO CLIMATE CHANGE: REFLECTIONS ON LOCAL EXPERIENCES IN BENIN AND SENEGAL
abstract: The fight against the effects of climate change at the central level does not exclude the need for local authorities to also adapt. The role of municipalities is often overlooked, but remains essential due to their proximity to social realities. While the state is committed to combating climate change at the international level, the effective transfer of some of its powers to sub-state entities would require them to resort to national law. Administrative law, because it aims to serve the public interest, must logically include the fight against climate change through its tools and enforcement
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: Enhancing Misalignment Tolerance and CC/CV Output in Hybrid Power Transfer Systems via Generalized Parity‐Time Symmetry
abstract: ABSTRACT Enhancing the power density of coupling mechanisms has been the dominant research focus in hybrid power transfer (HPT) systems in recent years. However, investigations into improving system‐level robustness and misalignment tolerance remain relatively limited. Moreover, conventional parity‐time (PT) symmetric systems impose an inherent requirement of strict topological symmetry, which further restricts their practical application. journal: International Journal of Circuit Theory and Applications

title: Development of a climate change jurisdictional vulnerability index in South Africa
abstract: Climate change threatens ecosystems and human well-being, making the identification of regional vulnerabilities essential for targeted adaptation. This study developed a Climate Change Jurisdictional Vulnerability Index (CC-JVI) for South Africa through the integration of socio-economic indicators (Statistics South Africa) and environmental variables (NASA online database). Indicators were normalised and aggregated across exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity to compute provincial CC-JVI scores for two periods: 2001–2011 and 2012–2022. title: The Exercise of Local Government Authority in the Governance of Sustainable Tourism in Central Halmahera Regency
abstract: Pemerintah daerah memiliki kewenagan melalui otonomi daerah untuk melaksanakan pembangunan di daerahnya, salah satunya yaitu pembangunan dan pengelolaan dalam sektor kepariwisataan yang bertujuan untuk mensejahterahkan masyarakatnya. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menjawab implementasi kewenagan pemerintah daerah sekaligus mengungkap tata kelola pengembangan pariwisata yang baik dan berkelanjutan di Kabupaten Halmahera Tengah. Penelitian ini menggunakan tipe penelitian hukum empiris, dengan menggunakan data yang bersumber dari fakta-fakta pengelolaan pariwisata di lapangan yang selanjutnya dia

title: Andean Glaciers in Times of Planetary Crisis
abstract: Abstract This special dossier examines how understandings of Andean glaciers transform under the planetary crisis, defined by humanity’s impact on geophysical processes at a planetary scale. Once regarded as remnants of deep geological time, glaciers have become emblematic casualties of anthropogenic global warming, their accelerated melting compressing geological history into human timescales and raising urgent ethical and political questions about protection, mitigation, and loss. This interdisciplinary collection, including contributions focused on Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and the wider r

title: Dis-spiriting and emplacing Moodjar trees: Nuytsia floribunda in gin production in southwestern Western Australia
abstract: Moodjar (Nuytsia floribunda), a sacred Noongar tree from southWestern Australia, is known colloquially as the Christmas tree because it flowers at the end of the year. Moodjar is a place where our spirits go when we die, a food source in hard times and a women’s tree. Early 2022 media reported two distillery businesses in Western Australia utilizing Moodjar’s flowering for flavouring the spirit gin. This use angered Noongar peoples who sought to stop Moodjar’s use for this purpose. This paper explores the temporal and spatial significances of Moodjar for Noongar peoples; and the new emplacemen

title: El himno de carácter ritual: el caso de los Himnos órficos
abstract: This article proposes an approach to the hymn genre in the Greco-Roman world to analyze its forms, functions, and how, through its composition and performance, it became a type of poetic offering to the gods. As an example, we examine the Orphic hymns, an imperial-era hymnal used by a Dionysian cult association. This collection invokes the favorable presence of numerous gods through the accumulation of epithets that highlight their genealogy, exploits, and power, not only to obtain divine favor but also to honor them through the power of the word and the burning of aromatic offerings.

title: Climate justice: Is there an individual right of citizen to climate neutrality?
abstract: This paper analyzes citizens' access to climate justice under European and Spanish law. Despite ambitious legislation rendering climate neutrality targets binding and imposing corporate sustainability due diligence (CSDDD), procedural standing (legitimación activa) remains strictly constrained. Both CJEU and Spanish jurisprudence require proof of direct, individualized harm, preventing citizens from challenging public or corporate inaction on an individual basis. Currently, regulatory mechanisms reduce citizens to submitting administrative complaints or claiming post-damage civil compensation.
publisher: Alcide De Gasperi University of Euroregional Economy in Józefów

title: "Neither Dead nor Lost – Uncovering Critical Law Stories at a Critical Time"
abstract: Law reform, in part at least, is about trying to see a way forward when there just does not seem to be one, or when the way forward is just too hard to bring into being. By many people putting their feet in front of each other, change can happen. Lecretia is testament to that. It is my honour to share with you tonight just some of the work and thinking of several people working on the Borrin-funded research project Te Rauhī i te Tikanga – a Tikanga Companion. Through that work we seek to help law students to understand tikanga Māori as a system of law; to take account of, respect, and protect
journal: Victoria University of Wellington Law Review

title: Understanding Trends in Inclusive Travel for People with Disabilities in Laiya, Batangas: Basis for a Tourism Accessibility Development Plan
abstract: This study assessed the status of inclusive travel for persons with disabilities (PWDs) in Laiya, Batangas, Philippines, as a basis for proposing a Tourism Accessibility Development Plan. Anchored on the Social Model of Disability and Inclusive Tourism Theory, it examined the destination in terms of the 5 A’s of tourism (attractions, accessibility, accommodation, activities, and amenities), the barriers perceived by PWDs, and their travel inclusivity trends. title: Tourism Facilities, Price, Cultural Performances, and Service Quality as Determinants of Visitor Satisfaction: Evidence from Balekambang Heritage Park Indonesia
abstract: The increasing number of visits to tourist destinations does not necessarily translate into higher visitor satisfaction. Previous studies have primarily examined the effects of tourist facilities, prices, and service quality, while the role of cultural performances in shaping visitor satisfaction remains relatively underexplored, particularly in public-space and cultural heritage destinations. This study examines the effects of tourist facilities, prices, cultural performances, and service quality on visitor satisfaction at Balekambang Park, Surakarta. title: Safeguarding and Promoting the Cultural Values of the Khmu People in Nghe an Province: A Stakeholder-Based Approach
abstract: Safeguarding the cultural heritage of the Khmu (Khơ Mú) people in Nghe An requires attention to living practices and to the relationships among communities, authorities, cultural professionals, educational institutions, and market actors. This study analyses stakeholder roles, potential tensions, and governance conditions in safeguarding and promoting Khmu cultural values. Qualitative document analysis integrates heritage-management scholarship, Vietnamese legislation, UNESCO instruments, and publicly documented initiatives in Nghe An. journal: Social science and human research bulletin.

title: Saudi Arabian and Emirati Climate Diplomacy toward Pacific Island Countries: Motivations, Practices, and Limits
abstract: Why do hydrocarbon-exporting states pursue climate diplomacy toward Pacific Island countries that call for an accelerated fossil-fuel transition? This article compares Saudi Arabian and Emirati engagement from 2010 to September 2026 through a qualitative analysis of official documents, regional communiques, climate-policy texts, project records, and scholarly literature. It combines status seeking, niche diplomacy, institutional assets, and recipient agency in a framework linking motivations, practices, and outcomes. title: Changes in Migratory and Breeding Status of One Great Egret Over Eight Years
abstract: GPS and accelerometer data from a Great Egret (Ardea alba) tagged in September 2018 on Tomales Bay, Marin County, California, U.S.A. were recorded for eight breeding seasons. Following the first two breeding seasons after being outfitted with a GPS tag this individual migrated south (1535 km and 472 km, respectively) but remained resident in subsequent years, consistent with an age-related shift in migratory behavior. title: SIRKEL-JKT: A Producer-Responsibility Model for Flexible Plastic Waste Recovery in Jakarta
abstract: Background: Jakarta’s plastic waste reduction policy has focused on restricting single-use shopping bags, while low-economic-value multilayer plastic packaging, particularly sachets, remains inadequately managed. Objective: This article examines this policy imbalance and formulates a Jakarta-wide model for implementing producer responsibility. journal: Journal of Law and Social Politics

title: Beyond Nusantara: Assessing the cross-border economic spillover effects of Indonesia's new capital on Sarawak, Malaysia
abstract: Indonesia’s decision to relocate its national capital from Jakarta to Ibu Kota Nusantara (IKN) in East Kalimantan is reshaping the development landscape of Borneo. While much of the discussion has focused on the implications for Indonesia, the project also raises an important question for neighbouring Sarawak: under what conditions can a major investment and administrative centre in Kalimantan generate meaningful economic benefits across the border? This article examines the potential economic spillovers from IKN to Sarawak, drawing on an interpretivist qualitative case study involving semi-st
journal: International Journal of Accounting, Finance and Business

title: Djing.gii Gudjaagalali (children stars) school clinic; evaluation of a novel primary care led rural school based integrated model of care
abstract: Abstract Background There are more than 1.36 million children living in remote, rural and regional Australia. These children and young people have significantly worse health outcomes than their urban peers and experience inequities in healthcare access. This study explored key components of the integrated care model, including access, coverage, availability, affordability, improved health and equity. Methods General Practitioner (GP) clinical records for 105 students aged 4–18 years were analysed to demonstrate their care journey through the clinic between May 10th, 2022, and June 30th, 2024.

title: WEATHER-TALK AS A PHATIC REGULATOR AND AN INSTRUMENT FOR RELIEVING COMMUNICATIVE TENSION
abstract: The article is devoted to a comprehensive pragmalinguistic characteristic of the phenomenon of weather-talk as an important phatic regulator and an effective tool for relieving communicative tension in interpersonal and professional interaction. The paper notes that human communicative behavior is subordinated to global interaction goals, which requires a thorough analysis of speech strategies and tactics. title: The Empow(her)ment of the Mic a Qualitative Study of Female Podcasters Redefining News Narratives in Egypt

title: ECOTOURISM AS A PATHWAY TO SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN SULTANATE OF OMAN: IMPACTS, OPPORTUNITIES, AND FUTURE POTENTIAL
abstract: Ecotourism is to provide conservation and responsible behavior among its stakeholders. Oman seeks to diversify its economy and reduce its dependence on oil; ecotourism has emerged as a promising approach to promote economic growth while safeguarding the environment and engaging local communities. This research focuses on the perspectives of key stakeholders understanding of how ecotourism is being perceived, the benefits it generates, and the challenges it encounters. title: Deployment Optimisation of Land-Based Close-in Weapon System for Counter-Drone Port Protection
abstract: The increasing use of swarm drones in recent conflicts has highlighted the vulnerability of critical infrastructures, particularly ports, to low-altitude saturation attacks. This study examines how distance-based defence priorities affect land-based close-in weapon system (CIWS) deployment and simulated penetration outcomes under spatial constraints, permitted coverage conditions, and a limited number of available units. title: Global Value Chain Participation and Inequality in Agro‐food Industries in the Global South
abstract: ABSTRACT Since the 1990s, global value chains have been a central vehicle for development strategies in Global South countries, driving their integration into the global economy. Much critical scholarship has highlighted the adverse social and environmental costs, the asymmetries of power in inter‐firm relations, and the unfair distribution of benefits that often arise from value chain participation. title: Tracing the Evolution of Air Ionisation Research in Romania. Nearly a Century of Scientific Progress and Interdisciplinary Perspectives
abstract: Air ionisation is an important component of atmospheric electricity, with implications for environmental quality, bioclimatology, and human health. Although research on this phenomenon has a long tradition in Romania, its historical development and diversification across scientific disciplines require systematic synthesis. This study employs a historical-descriptive review of scientific publications, research reports, conference proceedings, and studies conducted in Romania from 1938 to 2026. The literature was examined chronologically and thematically, focusing on major scientific contributio

title: Influence of Particle Morphology on Hydraulic Conductivity of Granular Materials: Quantification of Kozeny–Carman Shape Factor
abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate estimation of hydraulic conductivity ( K ) is essential for the design and stability of geotechnical structures. Although the Kozeny–Carman equation is widely recognized for its theoretical robustness, its application is often hindered by the subjective selection of the particle shape factor ( SF ). This study transforms SF from a qualitative estimate into a quantifiable parameter derived from objective morphological data. title: Stuck in place? Intergenerational occupational mobility in Türkiye
abstract: Abstract This study analyzes intergenerational occupational mobility in Türkiye using 2021 Family Structure Survey data (N = 13,076). Applying mobility matrices, Altham's statistics, and rank-rank correlations across four birth cohorts (1951 1994), we separate structural economic change from genuine social fluidity. Results reveal a stark divergence. While absolute mobility rose significantly due to de-agrarianization and service-sector expansion, relative mobility stagnated or declined after controlling for these shifts. title: Place-based decarbonisation in the United Kingdom: Spatial dynamics, community engagement, and co-benefits
abstract: Based on a socio-technical literature review and comparative case studies, this paper analyses the place-based processes of industrial decarbonisation in the United Kingdom (UK). It addresses three questions: how industrial clusters with concentrated versus dispersed spatial configurations contribute differently to the UK’s industrial decarbonisation; what the spatial determinants are that influence the success and challenges for place-based decarbonisation; and how spatial analysis and geographical considerations can enhance targeted strategies for industrial decarbonisation across diverse UK

title: The diversity of resilience patterns of natural populations decreases closer to human activities
abstract: Abstract Quantifying the resilience of wild populations is essential to predict their viability in the Anthropocene. Many species have become threatened and even gone extinct because they have failed to cope with human disturbances. We use demographic data for 956 plant and animal populations to assess their responses to increasing levels of human activities. We show that in areas characterized by high human activities, there is a smaller diversity of resilience patterns compared to areas with lower human activities. title: Reimagining Sustainable Natural Resource Governance through the Paradigm of Maqāṣid Al-Sharī‘ah and Ecological Justice
abstract: The exploitation of natural resources and environmental degradation call for sustainable governance grounded in ethical and normative values. This study aims to identify Islamic principles in responding to contemporary environmental governance challenges and their relevance to sustainable natural resource management. This study employs a qualitative-descriptive approach through an integrative literature review of 25 scientific publications, primarily from 2021–2026, using content analysis and thematic synthesis. title: Erozja odporności państwa jako wyzwanie dla bezpieczeństwa wewnętrznego – propozycja ramy analitycznej umożliwiającej wczesne rozpoznawanie zagrożeń społecznych i instytucjonalnych
abstract: Celem artykułu jest przedstawienie erozji odporności państwa jako użytecznej kategorii analitycznej w badaniu bezpieczeństwa wewnętrznego oraz zaproponowanie trójpoziomowej ramy analitycznej umożliwiającej obserwację symptomów osłabienia odporności państwa przed wystąpieniem jawnego kryzysu. title: WHAT DOES A CHOKEPOINT COST, AND WHO PAYS? OIL EXPOSURE, FISCAL RESILIENCE AND THE DISTRIBUTION OF DISRUPTION IN CHINA, INDIA, PAKISTAN AND THE UNITED STATES
abstract: A blocked shipping lane is a security problem and a budget problem at the same time. It is also a distribution problem: a price rise is a loss for those who buy oil and a gain for those who sell, ship, insure or store it. This paper asks whether the amount of oil a country imports, or the buffers behind those imports, better explains how badly a chokepoint disruption hurts it, and who inside each country ends up paying. title: Erosion of state resilience as a challenge to internal security – proposal for analytical framework enabling the early identification of social and institutional threats
abstract: The aim of the article is to present the erosion of state resilience as a useful analytical category in the study of internal security and a proposal for a three-level analytical framework for monitoring signs of a weakening of the state’s resilience before an overt crisis arises. The article is based on the analysis of the relevant literature, comparative analysis and model synthesis. title: TOURISM AND HOSPITALITY AS DRIVERS OF ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT IN BANGLADESH: A REVIEW OF ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES
abstract: Bangladesh, a nation rich in cultural heritage and natural beauty, possesses significant untapped potential in its tourism and hospitality sectors. Despite this, the contribution of these industries to the national Gross Domestic Product (GDP) has historically been modest compared to global averages. Recognizing tourism as a catalyst for economic growth, there is a growing imperative to understand and enhance its role in the country's development trajectory. title: Complex Ecological Relationships and Scientific Non Recognition
abstract: This overview examines three contributions on Hector’s and Māui dolphins through an expert–AI inquiry into complex ecological relationships and scientific non-recognition. It asks how research programmes can produce accurate observations while leaving consequential causal connections untested. The contributions address the exclusion of records, the limited causal reach of demographic models, and allegations of institutional obstruction. title: Regulatory Trends in Ukraine’s Port Sector: Rules, Policies, and Risks
abstract: The article examines Ukraine’s port-sector regulatory framework for establishing public-private partnerships (PPPs), the risks to private investment in strategic maritime infrastructure, and how pre-war contracts cannot address military threats, destruction, operational disruption, and prolonged force majeure. title: Mesolithic discoveries at Dagsmosse
abstract: The Mesolithic of eastern Central Sweden is strongly associated with knapped quartz, pecked axes and a lack of preserved organic materials like bone, antler and wood. This picture stands in sharp contrast to the Mesolithic assemblages of Southern Scandinavia, rich in preserved organic remains. Many of the latter finds come from wetland sites. In this paper it it is argued that wetlands are often overlooked within contract archaeology and research in Central Sweden, exacerbating the problem. title: Decomposing drivers of global temperature change after net zero
abstract: Abstract Net-zero CO2 (NZCO2) and greenhouse gas emission (GHG) targets are central to the development of mitigation scenarios. Projected global surface air temperature (GSAT) change after NZCO2 depends on several factors that broadly fall into two categories: scenario-specific factors that account for the diversity of possible mitigation pathways to net zero and beyond, and model-specific factors that describe the climate system response, captured in the zero emissions commitment (ZEC). title: Artificial protein in the Capitalocene: Blade Runner 2049
abstract: This article approaches the alternative protein transition by noting with the EAT-Lancet Commission that the existing world-food-system is a main driver of global warming. Building on eco-feminist and eco-Marxist critiques of the world-food-system, the article notes how this system organizes not only agriculture, animal husbandry, logistics, diets, and markets across the planet, but also profoundly unjust social relationships. abstract: This paper examines whether the Cholas, Pandyas, Keralaputras and Satiyaputras stood under Mauryan authority during the reign of Aśoka (r. 268/272–232/235 BCE), and if so, in what sense. It assembles five bodies of evidence — Aśokan epigraphy, the Pali chronicle tradition, Tamil-Brāhmī inscriptions, Sangam poetry, and the later tradition of Aśokan presence in the Tamil country — and tests eleven propositions advanced in support of the hypothesis of Mauryan overlordship.
