title: Analysis of job performance in the administrative area of a high specialty hospital in the city of Villahermosa, Tabasco.
abstract: The objective of this project is to analyze the job performance of administrative staff at a high-specialty hospital in Villahermosa, Tabasco. The methodology will utilize the Likert scale technique, considering a population of 751 administrative staff members. A sample of 260 individuals will be surveyed, with a 95% confidence level. The research is of a mixed-methods, cross-sectional type, employing both qualitative and quantitative methodologies, and is situated within the current timeframe.

title: Exploring the impact of corporate governance and external audit quality on creative accounting practices
abstract: The current study adopts a multivariate model to investigate the impact of board size, board independence, managerial ownership, audit committee independence, and external audit quality (proxied by audit fees) on creative accounting practices. Data for the study were obtained from commercial banks’ annual reports published on the Amman Stock Exchange (ASE) during the period from 2017 to 2021. title: FROM SUBJECT MATTER TO EMBODIED EMOTION: EVALUATING AMY LOWELL'S IMAGIST FRAMEWORK IN EZRA POUND'S RIPOSTES AND LUSTRA
abstract: Imagism – introduced by Ezra Pound – informs a theoretical paradigm for modern poetry writing. Imagists liberated poetry writing from observing the strict standards of meter or rhythm and introduced the use of free verse, where natural rhythm is carried through each cadence in the embodied new emotion. This study will explore the experimentation with formal features of the imagistic strains, extended by Amy Lowell, in the poetics of Ezra Pound found in his two poetry collections: Ripostes (1912) and Lustra (1916), that include poems “In a Station of the Metro”, “Portrait D’Une Femme”, “The Gar

title: Pintar para salvar la vida. Sally Gabori, memoria y reparación
abstract: La obra de Sally Gabori, singular artista de la comunidad Kaiardilt, en Australia, es un acto de cuidado y reparación frente al borrado colonial. Empieza a pintar con 81 años, y sus lienzos dan cuenta de su lengua, su cultura, su pueblo y el territorio en que vivió su infancia hasta que un desastre natural, en forma de ciclón y maremoto, obliga a su comunidad a trasladarse a otra isla en la que se impone una política de segregación por la que niños y niñas son separados de sus progenitores, de su lengua materna y sus referentes culturales. title: Conservation governance challenges in the Karakoram: Analyzing the institutional transitions of Central Karakoram National Park, Pakistan
abstract: Global commitments to conserve 30% of land by 2030 place renewed emphasis on protected areas (PAs), yet governance shortcomings and distributional conflicts often undermine both conservation and socio-economic development outcomes. This paper examines PA governance in Central Karakoram National Park (CKNP), Pakistan’s largest national park in Gilgit-Baltistan (GB), a region marked by constitutional ambiguity, contested land tenure, and infrastructure-driven market integration. title: Implementation of Local Finance Laws in the Management of the Regional Budget for Poverty Alleviation in Tidore Kepulauan City
abstract: This study aims to analyze the implementation of local finance laws in the management of the Tidore Kepulauan City Regional Budget in efforts to alleviate poverty, as well as to identify the normative and empirical barriers that affect its effectiveness. This study employs a socio-legal approach, using data collection techniques such as literature review, interviews, observation, and documentation. title: SOMER: an assessment tool for social acceptance in wetland conservation contexts
abstract: Abstract Social acceptance plays an important role in wetland conservation, yet existing studies often rely on context-specific approaches that limit systematic assessment across wetland contexts. To fill this gap, this paper introduces the Social Monitor for Ecosystem Relations (SOMER), an assessment tool designed to examine social acceptance in wetland conservation contexts. In this study, social acceptance is operationalized through individuals’ perceptions of the costs and benefits of wetlands. To demonstrate the empirical applicability of SOMER, the assessment tool was applied in a survey

title: Enhancing Risk Knowledge in Civil Society Organization Leadership: Case‐Based Evidence From China
abstract: ABSTRACT The escalating complexity of China's disaster risk landscape demands a new strategic leadership from civil society organizations (CSOs) to navigate systemic and cascading risks. While the national policies increasingly formalize the role of CSOs in disaster risk reduction (DRR), existing training provisions do not adequately develop the risk‐informed competencies required in practice. abstract: This article examines the structural inadequacies of international climate law in addressing loss and damage experienced by small, climate-vulnerable states, with particular reference to Timor-Leste. Grounding its analysis in Article 2 of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and Article 3 of the Paris Agreement, the article interrogates the tension between the aspirational language of climate justice and the operational constraints embedded within existing legal frameworks. abstract: This study examines Joe Ushie's deployment of the locust motif as political commentary in A Reign of Locusts, analyzing how the poet transforms this biblical symbol into contemporary criticism of Nigeria's governance failures. abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has been linked to increased net migration gains in suburban, peri-urban, and rural areas, at the expense of larger cities, contributing to suburbanization in many Western countries. Post-pandemic trends are less understood, but recent evidence indicates a return to pre-pandemic levels of internal migration intensity. abstract: The treatment of agricultural wastewater is a challenging process as pollution is comprised of a mixture of excess nutrients, pesticides, heavy metals, organic material, pathogens, pharmaceutical substances and salts. Treatment of such an extensive form of pollution necessitates techniques which can deal with various types of pollutants, chemically and physically, without causing pollution in any other compartment of the environment. abstract: Abstract Across sub‐Saharan Africa, tree‐based restoration efforts are dominated by exotic tree species due to their rapid biomass accumulation and short‐term economic returns. However, their limited contribution to biodiversity and ecosystem functioning has renewed interest in native‐tree restoration as a more sustainable strategy. abstract: Infectious disease modelling plays a critical role in understanding and addressing global health challenges. abstract: This study evaluated the effectiveness of an extension field day in increasing participants’ knowledge, perception of sustainability, and willingness to adopt climate-resilient alley cropping (CRAC) in Glen Arm, Maryland. abstract: This study examines the determinants of student dropout in Tanzanian government secondary schools over the period 2020–2024. abstract: In the Lubuk Larangan tradition, communities temporarily close sections of a river to fishing before reopening them for communal harvesting. title: A review of the governance challenges in the regional integration of the ASEAN Single Aviation Market
abstract: Purpose This article aims to critically examine the governance challenges in the ASEAN Single Aviation Market (ASAM) at policy and operational levels. Design/methodology/approach An integrative review framework was adopted to synthesise diverse sources, including academic literature and policy documents. The data were examined through qualitative document analysis with content analysis and thematic coding to identify obstacles in implementing ASAM. title: The impact of Trumpism upon the European Green Deal
abstract: Abstract The article, based on theoretical and empirical analysis, provides a deeper understanding of the content, scale, and potential of Trumpism as a strategic challenge to the European Green Deal (EGD). Through interdisciplinary and comparative approaches, methods of political ecology, neo-cleavage theory and case study, the impact of Trumpism on the implementation prospects for the EGD is investigated. title: The effects of early years services (Sure Start) in Northern Ireland on social services interventions
abstract: Abstract Sure Start is an area-based intervention which offers support for families with children under four living in some of the most deprived areas in Northern Ireland. This study uses administrative data on almost every child born in Northern Ireland between 2006 and 2013 (n = 108,000). We use a quasi-experiment (Regression Discontinuity design) to measure the impact of Sure Start on interactions with social services in the first five years of life. Our results suggest that Sure Start substantially reduces rates of children who are referred to social services and become a ‘child in need’.

title: A qualitative exploration of variations in social prescribing in primary care for people living with dementia in England: Barriers and enablers to positive service experiences
abstract: The number of people living with dementia and related costs continue to grow worldwide. Although generally associated with memory difficulties, non-cognitive symptoms of dementia are common and usually stem from unmet needs. Evidence emerging suggests that social prescribing improves the wellbeing of people living with dementia. This study explored adaptations to key elements of social prescribing for people living with dementia, as well as barriers to and enablers of positive experiences among people living with dementia and service providers. title: Using Public Relations to Modify Ethics and It`S Legal Framework in an Organization
abstract: This study investigated many organisations that have ethics problems even though they have many laws. For example, some managers harass staff because of colour, like threatening a brown employee with a cane or whip and telling a white colleague not to sit with him. Oil companies also have problems like oil spills, corruption and pollution. Public Relations (PR) is supposed to help organisations behave ethically and be the conscience of the organisation, but many companies do not allow PR to do this job. title: Single-Candidate Local Elections in Indonesia: Electoral Cartelization, the Empty Box, and Siyasah Dusturiyyah
abstract: This study examines the legal problems and democratic implications of single-candidate regional elections in Indonesia’s 2024 Simultaneous Regional Elections, in which 37 regions had only one candidate pair. Although Constitutional Court Decision Number 100/PUU-XIII/2015 and Articles 54C–54D of Law Number 10 of 2016 provide a legal basis for conducting elections through an empty-box mechanism, the existing framework leaves unresolved questions concerning the legal consequences of an empty-box victory and the possible re-nomination of a candidate defeated by the empty box. abstract: Trifluoroacetate (TFA) is the most abundant PFAS in environmental media, with evolving regulatory frameworks and risk data. Commercially available technologies to separate TFA from drinking water are primarily limited to membrane separation using reverse osmosis (RO) or nanofiltration (NF) membranes, with relatively low concentration factors around 5-10. These and other technologies have inherent tradeoffs, where targeting effective removal of small compounds like TFA produce larger residuals volumes. title: Pagpangalimug and Narrative Experience: Hearing Metaphysical (Hi)Stories in Panay Bukidnon Vocal Music Genres
abstract: Abstract Grounded in the idea that vocality is linked to narrativity, this article argues that pagpangalimug (intoning) functions as a proto-narrative that sonically structures and mediates narrative experience among the Panay Bukidnon community in Panay Island, Western Visayas, Philippines. Beyond preparing the voice and body for singing, pagpangalimug is central to how narratives are evoked. I frame this process in two ways: a “tuning in” that prepares the vocal-narrative frame, and a “tuning out” that recalls other narratives from personal and collective memory. title: ANALYSIS OF LOCAL OWN-SOURCE REVENUE IN STRENGTHENING FISCAL INDEPENDENCE IN TIDORE ISLANDS CITY, 2021–2025
abstract: This study analyzes the fiscal independence of Tidore Islands City during 2021–2025, identifies factors associated with low Local Own-Source Revenue (PAD), and formulates measures to strengthen local fiscal capacity. A descriptive approach was employed by combining financial-data review with qualitative information obtained through interviews, observation, and documentation. The analysis used PAD and intergovernmental transfer data, while fiscal independence was measured by the ratio of PAD to intergovernmental transfers. title: Concerns about air quality and associated health effects in a Nigerian steel producing community
abstract: Air pollution remains a major environmental and global health concern, particularly in industrial areas where emissions from factories impact air quality and human well-being. This study examines the perception of air pollution and its associated health risks among residents living near a steel factory in Ifelodun Local Government, Kwara State, Nigeria. A structured questionnaire was administered to 120 residents, of which 105 valid responses were analyzed. The survey evaluated awareness of air pollution, perceived air quality, and self-reported health concerns. Descriptive statistics and chi-

title: Loopholes in Australian wildlife, cultural heritage, human tissue and biosecurity laws: four case studies
abstract: Abstract We provide a novel investigation into where Australian legislation, meant to mitigate commerce in material cultural heritage, wildlife products and human tissue, clash in both their scope and practical application. Through an exploratory analysis of the legal context surrounding three recent Australian auction house sales and a social media post (demonstrating an example of successful import into Australia of human remains posing clear biosecurity risk), we identify legal loopholes through which these categories of trafficking can converge. title: Framework for Change: Progressing Planning for Disability Equity and Inclusion in Australia
abstract: Inclusive cities discourse is gaining prominence through global urban agendas, including the UN’s Sustainable Development Goal 11 and the New Urban Agenda, which link ideas of equity, inclusion and sustainability. Despite this global policy context, there remains little tangible progress towards equity and inclusion for diverse people with disabilities, including in Australia, where this research is grounded. This article addresses this gap by presenting a framework of change to progress planning for disability equity and inclusion. The framework was generated from participatory community-base

title: Economic Patronage in Tin Mining Governance and Regulatory Implementation in the Province of the Bangka Belitung Islands
abstract: Tin mining in the Bangka Belitung Islands Province has long contributed to local economic activity, but its governance remains affected by economic dependence, informal practices, unequal power relations, and gaps between formal regulations and their implementation. This article examines how economic patronage influences tin mining governance and the implementation of mining regulations in the region. title: WHOSE CARBON, WHOSE BENEFIT? PANCASILA SOCIAL JUSTICE AND COMMUNITY BENEFIT-SHARING IN INDONESIA'S FOREST CARBON GOVERNANCE
abstract: Indonesia is rebuilding its forest carbon market at the same time as it accelerates the recognition of customary forests, yet the rules that decide who receives carbon revenue have received little legal scrutiny. This article asks whether Indonesia's emerging benefit-sharing arrangements meet the standard of social justice that the state's foundational philosophy, Pancasila, and the 1945 Constitution impose on the use of natural resources. title: Unrequited: Zero‐sum asymmetry in the political domain fuels affective polarization
abstract: Abstract Zero‐sum beliefs about political relationships—the conviction that one party's gains are inevitably offset by another party's losses—have often been cited as drivers of partisan conflicts. However, across five studies with diverse samples of U.S. residents ( n = 1383), four of which were preregistered, we find that overall zero‐sum endorsement shows weak and inconsistent associations with affective polarization. title: La preuve par la Chine ? Jesuit networks, academic politics, and the shape of the Earth in 1730s Paris
abstract: This article argues that the Maupertuis-Cassini controversy over the shape of the Earth in the 1730s was intricately connected to Eurasian intellectual networks and academic politics. It focuses on the alliance of two Parisian pro-Cassini savants, Dortous de Mairan and Nicolas Fréret, and on their private correspondence with French Jesuits Antoine Gaubil and Dominique Parrenin in Beijing. title: A phenomenological study of mutual respect in aquaculture governance: the case of an intensive shrimp farm in Indonesia
abstract: Despite many technical factors such as water quality, biosecurity, and infrastructure impacting the success of intensive shrimp farming, the successful implementation of these requirements also depends on the workers' engagement. Engaged workers may be more willing to report problems to their superior so immediate actions can be taken. This study examines how workers in an owner-managed shrimp farm interpret the involvement of farm leaders and how these experiences shape their engagement through mutual respect mechanism with the leaders. title: La identidad traducida: multilingüismo e imaginarios culturales en la ficción audiovisual ambientada en Catalunya
abstract: This article analyzes the role of multilingualism in recent audiovisual works set in Catalonia —the two‑part BBC special The Split: Barcelona (2024/2025) and the German series Der Barcelona‑Krimi (ARD, 2017–2025)— and how translation strategies mediate the construction of identities and the circulation of cultural imaginaries. title: Appraisal Practices and Cultural Intelligence Impact Young Talent Performance
abstract: This study examined the influence of Performance Appraisal Practice and Cultural Intelligence on Employee Performance mediated by Employee Engagement among Generation Z and millennial employees in Jakarta's creative industry. With these generations dominating the workforce and projected to drive Indonesia's economic growth, understanding factors affecting their performance became critical, particularly as traditional HRM practices might not align with younger generations' expectations regarding performance evaluation, cultural dynamics, and engagement mechanisms. title: Stoichiometric Optimisation of Vat Dyeing for Sustainable Colour Fastness in Cotton Fabrics
abstract: Purpose: Vat dyes are widely recognised for their superior colour fastness on cotton substrates; however, the efficiency of their reduction–oxidation cycle is highly dependent on the stoichiometric balance among the dye, sodium hydroxide (NaOH), and sodium hydrosulphite (Na₂S₂O₄). This study investigates how controlled variations in reagent ratios influence colour fastness, to develop a stoichiometrically grounded optimisation framework applicable to artisanal and semi-industrial dyeing systems in Ghana. institutions: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology

title: Directed evolution and characterisation of light harvesting complexes with altered spectral properties in purple non-sulfur bacteria
abstract: Abstract Purple non-sulfur bacteria (PNSB) are metabolically versatile microorganisms that inhabit diverse environments by taking advantage of a remarkably efficient photosynthetic machinery. In this work, we describe the creation of a workflow for experimental studies that aim to compare the energy transfer mechanisms occurring within structural variants of the light-harvesting complex 2 (LH2) of PNSB. title: Carbon capture potential of recycled concrete aggregates from a full-scale recycling plant in the Brazilian federal district: A laboratory carbonation study
abstract: Accelerated carbonation of recycled concrete aggregates (RCA) can fix CO₂ while modifying aggregate properties, but most reported uptake values come from laboratory-produced aggregates that do not reproduce the heterogeneity of material leaving a real recycling line. This study assesses the carbon uptake of recycled sand and two coarse RCA fractions from a single industrial recycling plant in the Federal District, Brazil, sampled in two production campaigns. title: Food security and wealth vs. environmental impact of agriculture as seen from a perspective of poor countries
abstract: Aim: The purpose of this article was to identify the determinants of low GDP per capita levels accompanied, and driven by, extreme food insecurity in the 25 countries with the lowest GFSI (Global Food Security Index). Methodology: The countries were divided into five groups for descriptive purposes, while the determinants of GDP per capita were examined using a fixed effects panel regression model. title: Segregated Power: Women’s Underrepresentation and Committee Assignments in the Canadian Parliament
abstract: Abstract Parliamentary committees are critical venues of legislative work. Yet women, already underrepresented in most legislatures, are often further marginalized within these powerful substructures. This note examines women’s representation in the Canadian House of Commons’ 24 standing committees, 2006–2025, using an original dataset capturing committee membership and leadership across six Parliaments and four major parties. title: Voices at Risk: Exploring Language Shift and Dialect Drift in the Survival of the Eastern Subanen
abstract: The decline of indigenous languages threatens linguistic diversity, cultural identity, and the intergenerational transmission of heritage. This study examined the factors influencing language shift and dialect drift in the survival of the Eastern Subanen dialect in Purok 4, Lampasan, Don Victoriano, Misamis Occidental, Philippines. Employing a qualitative case study design, the research purposively selected 15 participants aged 20–30 years who were of Subanen ancestry, resided in the community, and were no longer fluent in the dialect. title: Mapping Scientific Agreement and Disagreement: The Case for a Dedicated Center
abstract: Abstract From 2022 to 2025, initial steps were taken toward establishing a dedicated center for systematically mapping scientific agreement and disagreement. This paper examines whether creating such a body is both desirable and feasible. We summarize lessons from three pilot studies (COVID-19; the existence of extraterrestrial life; claims of extraterrestrial life discovery), outlining key design choices. title: Khalifah Fil Ardh sebagai Landasan Pengelolaan Pariwisata Berkelanjutan di Indonesia
abstract: The growing environmental crisis threatening the sustainability of tourist destinations in Indonesia calls for a management framework that is not only ecological and economic, but also ethical-theological. This study examines the concept of Khalifah Fil Ardh (vicegerency on earth) in Islam as a philosophical and operational foundation for sustainable tourism management in Indonesia. title: The critical role of political trust in the energy transition
abstract: Abstract Achieving net‐zero CO 2 emissions requires sustained collaboration between civil society and the private and public sectors across time and geographies, but low trust in and among these actors impedes coordinated action. This multidisciplinary review examines how different forms of trust, in particular political trust (i.e., trust between actors with differential power), shape the energy transition, addressing four core questions: How does trust impact energy project development and outcomes? title: A Semantic Service-oriented Advertisement Management System for Embedded Public Transport System
abstract: Contemporary public transportation systems ubiquitously employ audio-visual advertising platforms. However, traditional methodologies typically broadcast content in a fixed, sequential order, irrespective of environmental or contextual variables, thereby failing to ensure effective reach within the intended demographics. This study proposes a semantic web service-oriented framework designed to optimize target audience engagement. title: Good Manners and Right Conduct: Teaching Practices, Learners' Moral Development and Classroom Behavior
abstract: This study examined the influence of Good Manners and Right Conduct (GMRC) teaching practices aligned with the Philippine Professional Standards for Teachers (PPST) on learners’ moral development and classroom behavior in public elementary schools in Loay District, Bohol, during School Year 2025–2026. title: Spatial and environmental influences on the assembly of silk microbiomes in a social spider
abstract: Abstract In nesting animals, the nest structure can play an important role in host‐associated microbiome assembly; however, the processes structuring the resulting microbiome remain underexplored. In the social spider Stegodyphus dumicola , philopatric sisters collectively build and maintain a silken nest, capture prey, and exhibit alloparental care. title: Life cycle assessment of an electrochemical hydrogen compressor for green hydrogen production
abstract: While green hydrogen is essential for decarbonizing the energy matrix, its storage remains challenging due to hydrogen's physical properties. Electrochemical Hydrogen Compression (EHC) offers a promising, noiseless alternative to mechanical systems by enabling isothermal compression and simultaneous purification. This study presents a cradle-to-gate Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of a lab-scale EHC, evaluating the environmental impacts of manufacturing materials and operational energy. title: Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Judgments in Nigeria in The AfCFTA Era: Challenges and Reform Imperatives
abstract: The recognition and enforcement of foreign judgments is a cornerstone of private international law and a critical index for cross-border trade and investment. In Nigeria, this regime is governed by a tripartite system: the common law action on a judgment debt, the Reciprocal Enforcement of Judgments Ordinance of 1922, and the Foreign Judgments (Reciprocal Enforcement) Act of 1960. This article critically appraises the challenges undermining the effectiveness of this framework. title: Beyond exposure: Pathways between urban greening, nature connection and wellbeing in Australian policy frameworks
abstract: Urban greening initiatives are increasingly positioned as strategies to improve health and wellbeing in cities. While academic research has long acknowledged the role of psychological connections to nature in shaping wellbeing, it is unclear whether and how this relationship is recognised in urban greening policy. This study examines how Australian urban greening and biodiversity strategies conceptualise and evaluate wellbeing and nature connection. title: Valoração de serviços ecossistêmicos e o modelo de Pollination as a Service: as contradições da captura de valor pelas AgTechs no Brasil
abstract: Esta pesquisa analisa a valoração econômica da polinização e as barreiras enfrentadas por empresas de tecnologia agrícola (AgTechs) para converter esse serviço ecossistêmico em preço de mercado no Brasil. Inserido na Economia Ecológica e na Administração, o estudo investiga o contraste entre o elevado valor estimado pela literatura e sua limitada captura comercial. Adotou-se abordagem qualitativa e exploratória, combinando revisão sistemática da literatura e entrevistas em profundidade com dez stakeholders da cadeia de bioeconomia e polinização. title: Turkish Mediation Diplomacy: Institutional Mechanisms, Track Records and the Ankara Process
abstract: Türkiye has become a prominent player in mediation diplomacy since 2003, as the Justice and Development Party (AKP) have prioritized mediation engagements across the world, leveraging it as a strategic instrument of Turkish foreign policy. In this regard, the present paper examines the implications of Turkish mediation diplomacy, with a particular focus on the Ankara process that deescalated tension between Ethiopia and Somaliland over the Ethiopia-Somaliland 2024 Memorandum of Understanding. title: AGROFORESTRY MANAGEMENT INSTITUTIONS IN ENGKANGIN VILLAGE, AIR BESAR DISTRICT, LANDAK REGENCY
abstract: Agroforestry is an effective system for sustainable land use and provides significant benefits to community life. The success of agroforestry is highly dependent on strong institutional support. This study aims to explain the institutional management of agroforestry in Engkangin Village, focusing on organizational aspects and applicable rules. The approach used is descriptive qualitative, with data collected through observation, interviews, and documentation of agroforestry managers in Engkangin Village. title: Life cycle assessment of cement-bonded composite boards with municipal waste wood
abstract: Abstract The utilisation of waste wood in cement-bonded composites addresses pressing ecological challenges by diverting municipal waste wood from incineration. In this study, a life cycle assessment (LCA) was conducted on a pilot-sized wood-cement composite board (1 × 1 m²; 18 mm thick) incorporating 25 wt% waste wood converted into wood chips. Environmental impacts were quantified for standard categories, including global warming, acidification, eutrophication, etc., in accordance with ISO 14044 guidelines. title: Food affordability and moral impartiality in Ghana, A Singerian analysis of households in the Central Region
abstract: Ghana's national Cost of a Healthy Diet bulletins exclude the Central Region for want of price data. Three things are therefore unknown: what an adequate diet costs there, how that cost falls across households, and whether the resulting distribution can be defended. Anchored in Singer's principle of equal consideration of interests and his preventable harm argument, and tested against the partiality and institutional critiques, this study addressed all three. title: The Impact of Cross-Border Data Regulation on the Resilience of China’s Industrial and Supply Chains
abstract: Digital transformation has created huge economic benefits for cross-border data flow around the world, but it has also caused real problems such as violating privacy and leaking business secrets. For China, how to manage data well and maintain the stability of the industrial supply chain is a difficult policy problem in the negotiation of international rules. title: Reactualizing Fiqh al-Bi’ah as an Evaluative Framework for Strict Liability and Ecological Restoration in Indonesia
abstract: Indonesia’s environmental liability rules changed when Article 88 of Law Number 32 of 2009 was amended through the Job Creation Law, and Supreme Court Regulation Number 1 of 2023 later set new procedures for environmental cases. These changes raise doubts about whether the law adequately protects against ecological damage and ensures that damaged environments are actually restored. abstract: Este capítulo examina cómo las mujeres lesbianas perciben y negocian la representación de sus identidades en las redes sociales a partir de los contenidos que seleccionan para ellas los sistemas de recomendación algorítmica. abstract: Badem (Prunus amygdalus Batsch), Türkiye’de özellikle Elazığ ve Malatya gibi uygun ekolojik koşullara sahip bölgelerde yaygın olarak yetiştirilen ve ekonomik değeri yüksek bir meyve türüdür. title: Governing trade, governing carbon: How environmental provisions in RTAs affect carbon inequality within global value chains?
abstract: Environmental provisions in regional trade agreements (RTAs) play an important role in aligning trade with environmental objectives and mitigating carbon inequality. Using data covering 80 economies and 50 industries, we apply a multi-regional input–output model to construct a bilateral measure of carbon inequality from a value-capture perspective and examine whether deeper environmental provisions mitigate it. title: Transformative, Iterative or Performative? Conceptualising Patterns of Fossil Fuel Phaseout Leadership
abstract: ABSTRACT Global leadership in phasing out fossil fuels is an important new frontier in climate governance, yet remains undertheorised within existing scholarly accounts of climate leadership. In this paper, we argue that ‘phaseout leadership’—climate leadership centred on curtailing fossil fuel supply—is a distinct kind of leadership that dominant typologies fail to capture. We develop a novel conceptualisation of phaseout leadership around three characteristics: material, institutional, and symbolic. title: Examination of Media Diversity in the Era of Potential Diversity Loss
abstract: This study examines equal employment opportunity (EEO) statements in media companies’ job posts to assess the current state of diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) hiring practices in the broadcast news industry and how the shifting political climate impacts these practices. As DEI has increasingly become a contested terrain in the current political landscape, understanding how media organizations communicate their equal opportunity commitments in their hiring practices has become more critical than ever. title: Extreme Climate Events, Governance Deficits, and Adaptation Failure in Africa: A Policy and Framework Review
abstract: Africa accounts for less than four per cent of cumulative global greenhouse gas emissions, yet it absorbs some of the most severe consequences of anthropogenic climate change. The literature documenting this disparity has grown substantially over the past decade, but most reviews stop at cataloguing impacts and listing recommendations. This paper goes further. title: The Khoisan people on the precipice of extermination in the 18th Century: The impact of the 1713, 1755 and 1767 Smallpox Epidemics on the Khoisan Communities at the Cape
abstract: Literature abounds on the smallpox epidemics of 1713, 1755 and 1767 at the Cape, and how the epidemics destroyed the Khoisan way of life. Historians agree that these epidemics decimated most of the Khoisan clans and further eroded their social, economic and political strength, and in the process, exposed them to the naked sky of the ruthless marauding forces of colonialism whose sole intent was to feed their insatiable appetite for arable land and mineralogical riches. title: The Preparedness-Performance Puzzle: Adaptive Governance and the Limits of Global Health Security
abstract: Abstract Why did Ghana, classified as weakly prepared under dominant global health security frameworks, perform more effectively than expected during the COVID-19 pandemic? Existing preparedness models often equate crisis capacity with biomedical infrastructure, surveillance systems, stockpiles, and formal emergency planning. abstract: The article focuses on the issue of Pakistan being able to turn these short term tactical victories into long term strategic advantages without losing its old time allies in China and Saudi Arabia. Based on recent trends in Pakistani foreign policy and precedents in the strategic behavior of middle power nations, this discussion maintains that the best way ahead of Pakistan is to practice calibrated opportunism, that is, maximizing the quality of the relations at the moment with the U.S. whilst gradually developing alternative relationships. title: Bridging Outlooks: A Scoping Review on Commonly shared Indigenous, African, Asian and Non-Western Worldviews of Wellbeing
abstract: ABSTRACT Although wellbeing has been widely examined across disciplines and cultural contexts, its broader conceptualizations remain fragmented and largely rooted in Western paradigms. In contrast, non-Western frameworks (Indigenous, African, Asian, and among other collectivist traditions) offer alternatively rich and critical understandings of wellbeing that remain insufficiently integrated into mainstream interventions, research and policy frameworks. title: Foundational economy, geography and ‘left behind places’
abstract: Foundational economy (FE) is part of the proliferation of alternative approaches following the Global Financial Crisis in 2008. FE is an influential agenda in urban and regional studies, but its geographical dimensions are under-developed. This paper explains and demonstrates the value and challenges of a more geographically grounded and sensitive approach to FE. It uses spatial ontology, scale and place to make FE more geographical by mapping, understanding, and explaining the differentiated and uneven geographies and interrelations of the FE zones and their governance and institutions. abstract: Esta investigación ex post facto, transversal, descriptiva y relacional analiza cómo se configuran los estereotipos de género en la percepción ciudadana española en relación con los atributos asignados a mujeres y hombres dedicados a la política. Para ello, considera la figura ideal de liderazgo, los niveles de confianza diferencial y las preferencias de liderazgo por género, aplicando como técnica cuantitativa una encuesta panel online profesional a 403 personas residentes en España. title: Mainstreaming Disaster Risk Reduction into Sector-Level Policy and Corporate HSE Systems: An Alignment with NEMA’s National Push
abstract: Nigeria has spent most of its disaster history reacting. The 2022 floods, which NEMA’s Director-General later put at 662 deaths and more than 2.4 million displaced people, showed how costly that habit has become, and the launch of the National Disaster Risk Reduction Strategy (2025–2030) and the NEMA Strategic Plan (2025–2029) signals a deliberate move toward prevention. Yet a national strategy only changes risk on the ground when ministries, regulators and companies rewrite what they do every day. title: Active Filtration of Airborne eDNA for Vertebrate Surveys in Tropical Caves
abstract: Hidden from sunlight, caves are remarkable subterraneous ecosystems that host a wide range of animals, including unique species. Conventional cave biodiversity surveys can be physically challenging, disturb sensitive vertebrate communities, or require animal collection. Here we evaluate the use of metabarcoding of airborne environmental DNA (eDNA) as a non-invasive method for surveying cave vertebrates. title: From Cherry to Cup: The Transformative Role of Women in Specialty Coffee in Latin America
abstract: This essay analyzes the transformative role of women in traditional coffee farming and their strategic transition into the dynamic specialty coffee market in Latin America. Although women make up as much as 70% of the workforce during key stages such as harvesting and manual sorting, their role has historically been rendered invisible under the classification of unpaid family labor. This exclusion is perpetuated by structural gaps, notably unequal access to land titles, critical barriers to obtaining agricultural credit, and a rigid gender-based division of labor. title: Woody Species Diversity, Structures and Regeneration Status of Riparian Vegetation in Case of Duko River, in Shabe Sombo District, Southwest Ethiopia
abstract: Riparian habitats are significant ecosystems that perform a range of ecosystem services and act as ecological causes for better river health. In the Shabe Sombo District's Duko River, this study was conducted. This study's objective was to assess the Duko River's woody species, structures, and regeneration state. Methods. title: Enhancing Aquatic Persistence Assessments: Effects of Photosensitizers and Surfactants on Photochemical Degradation in the Environment
abstract: Photochemical processes substantially influence the environmental fate of chemicals, yet current persistence assessments rarely account for indirect photochemistry or interfacial effects. Here, we systematically investigated the photodegradation of the fungicide carbendazim, which is classified as persistent in aquatic environments according to current regulations. title: Can we justify the environmental and human health costs of reducing PFAS-4 in drinking water? A life cycle assessment in Sweden
abstract: PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) contamination of drinking water is a critical environmental and public health concern. As regulations become more stringent, water utilities are increasingly evaluating treatment technologies to ensure safe drinking water supplies. This study applies life cycle assessment to compare five treatment trains for PFAS-contaminated groundwater, each including pre-treatment, PFAS removal, post-treatment and PFAS destruction steps. title: Empowering Women Farmers in Nueva Ecija through Entrepreneurship: The Role of Corporate Social Responsibility in Sustainable Economic Development
abstract: This study examined the role of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) in empowering women farmers in Llanera, Nueva Ecija, through entrepreneurship and sustainable economic development. Specifically, it assessed the level of awareness of women farmers regarding CSR, the types and scope of CSR programs implemented by local businesses, their participation and engagement in entrepreneurship initiatives, the socio-economic impacts of CSR-driven activities, and the challenges that hinder program effectiveness. title: First direct measurement of food transit time through the gastrointestinal tracts of plant-eating primates using isotopic tagging
abstract: Abstract The time it takes for food to transit animal gastrointestinal tracts is essential information to fields from organismal evolution to ecosystem ecology. Nevertheless, current estimation methods do not measure food directly, are impractical for many species and often require unnatural conditions to administer. We overcome these limitations by adopting techniques from organic geochemistry. We trace isotopically tagged greens in lemurs, from ingestion to excretion, through isotopic analysis of higher plant biomarkers recovered in faeces. title: Linguocultural Construction of Archetypal Characters in English Fairy Tale Discourse: A Discourse-Analytic and Cognitive-Linguistic Perspective
abstract: While character archetypes in fairy-tale discourse have been extensively studied from folkloristic and psychological perspectives, limited attention has been paid to their linguocultural realization, the specific linguistic means through which these archetypal images are linguistically constructed in English fairy-tale discourse. This article addresses this gap by examining the linguocultural representation of recurrent character archetypes, namely the Mother/Stepmother, the Sage/Wise Old Man, and the Trickster, in English fairy-tale discourse through the analysis of folk tales. title: Meditation Breathing Training and Short-Term Recovery in Patients Undergoing Thoracoscopic Lung Cancer Resection: A Non-Randomized Historical-Control Study
abstract: Objective: To investigate the association of meditation breathing training with short-term physical and mental recovery in lung cancer patients after thoracoscopic lobectomy. Materials and Methods: A non-randomized historical control study design was adopted. A total of 62 patients (31 per group) diagnosed with lung cancer and receiving thoracoscopic surgery at our hospital between January 2023 and June 2024 were enrolled. title: The Cimolai case: A comparative analysis on cross‐border restructuring in Italy and the United Kingdom
abstract: Abstract This article provides a comparative analysis of the restructuring framework in the United Kingdom and Italy, focusing on two devices: the restructuring plan, introduced by the Corporate Insolvency and Governance Act 2020, and the Italian concordato preventivo . In the wake of Brexit and the EU Preventive Restructuring Directive 2019, the study demonstrates that, although European legislation is no longer binding on the United Kingdom, the new approach to business rescue has spread beyond its borders and realised a sort of ‘cross‐fertilisation’ between legal systems. abstract: Based on panel data from 2003 to 2018, this study analyzes the spatiotemporal characteristics of haze pollution, resource dependence, and industrial structure transformation in 284 Chinese cities, and explores the relationship between resource dependence, industrial transformation, and their interaction on haze pollution using the GS2SLS model. title: Drilling in ‘paradise’: environmental governance, local communities and oil exploration in the Okavango Delta, Botswana
abstract: Abstract Oil exploration in ecologically sensitive landscapes presents significant environmental governance challenges, particularly where extractive development intersects with wetland conservation and community livelihoods. This study examines how international, regional, and national policy and legislative frameworks regulate oil exploration in the Okavango Delta, Botswana, using a qualitative desk-based review of legal, policy, and documentary sources. title: Can China Solve the Global Climate Catastrophe?
abstract: At a time of unprecedented environmental crisis, when the second Trump administration has abandoned even the pretence of combating climate change, ideas addressing this existential threat should be welcomed. The People’s Republic of China (PRC) may be the largest emitter of carbon pollution in the world, but it is also the world’s biggest investor in renewable energy. title: The Effects of Brand Equity and Sales Promotion on Customer Loyalty with Purchase Decisions as a Mediating Variable
abstract: This study examines brand equity, sales promotion, purchase decisions, and customer loyalty among Purbasari body scrub consumers on TikTok Shop in Yogyakarta City. Questionnaire data from 100 purposively selected respondents were analyzed using multiple regression and Sobel tests in SPSS 26. The reported regressions indicate positive associations of brand equity and sales promotion with loyalty and purchase decisions. A separate test reports a purchase decision–loyalty association. title: Floodplain ecosystems' resilience to extreme seasonal floods: Predisposition of Upper Guinea floodplains, republic of Guinea
abstract: Floodplains are of great ecological and agricultural importance worldwide. However, the increase in extreme weather events, including severe floods and prolonged droughts, raises concerns about the sustainability of their ecosystems and farming practices as primary sources of income for developing countries. The Upper Guinea Savanna (UGS) features extensive floodplains that are vital to local food security but are increasingly subject to extreme seasonal flooding and human disturbances. abstract: An introduction to Hans Peter Duerr’s severely neglected classic , Dreamtime (1978) 1985b . German anthropology is finally receiving much-needed attention; hence, the present work is partly intended as a contribution to these ongoing efforts to explicate it for an Anglophone audience. title: Delegating Digital Policing: The Evolution of China’s Security-Industrial Complex
abstract: Abstract How did China build its formidable digital policing apparatus so rapidly? While prevailing narratives emphasize top-down state direction, this statist perspective obscures critical local dynamics. This article argues that China’s security-industrial complex actually emerged from decentralized administrative pressures. Burdened by unfunded, time-sensitive central security mandates, resource-strapped local security agencies abandoned state-led technological development and outsourced to the private sector. abstract: This article evaluates how a key missionary society negotiated the evangelistic impulse to introduce the Bible through the vernacular with huge societal pressures, across the British Empire, to promote English literacy among indigenous peoples. It assesses attitudes and pragmatic adjustments to the relationship between language, education and missionary work from the Society’s founding in 1811 to the Education (Scotland) Act of 1872 which institutionalised English medium education. title: Secondary school student and teacher perspectives about citizen science-based environmental education and youth agency
abstract: Education is thought to play a key role in driving positive environmental action. This study explores Hong Kong student (ages 11–19 years) and teacher perceptions about experiential environmental education and citizenship action, after engaging in environmental citizen science. We conducted semi-structured interviews with 46 students and 18 teachers across eight local and international schools, informed by behavioural psychology constructs such as motivation, self-efficacy and agency. title: Structured coupling beam control of six-wave mixing: from Helical Ince-Gaussian to Laguerre-Gaussian modes
abstract: Abstract We theoretically investigate six-wave mixing (SWM) in a coherently driven six-level atomic system using a structured coupling field. The probe and generated-field responses are obtained using the density-matrix formalism combined with the Maxwell Bloch equations. A Helical Ince–Gaussian (HIG) beam is introduced as the coupling field, and its ellipticity is varied to study the influence of its transverse structure on the nonlinear mixing process. title: Plant Life and Plant-Worship in Tripuri Folktales: A Reading of Ethnobotany in Select Tripuri Folktales

abstract: This study subjects Palestinian filmmaker Kamal Aljafari's personal film Recollection (2015) and American contemporary artist Shimon Attie's installation project The Writing On The Wall (1991-1992) to a comparative narratological analysis along the axes of nostalgia, memory and form. title: Traducción e interpretación en entornos paratextuales del ámbito de los videojuegos
abstract: The video game industry has been growing in an exponential and constant way for decades, and it became in one of the most economic-relevant industries in the whole world. The importance this industry has nowadays has lead to an expansion to other fields thanks to paratextual productions that are directly linked to the original games. title: Putin’s Bestowals and ‘Care for the People’
abstract: This article examines a little-studied technique of governance in contemporary Russia: the public bestowal of grants, prizes, payments and honours associated with Vladimir Putin and other powerful figures. Drawing on online research and accounts from Russian interlocutors, particularly cases from Siberia, it explores how competitions and exceptional rewards are framed as personal acts of care while addressing needs inadequately met through regular state provision. abstract: Abstract Traditional drinking water disinfectants such as chlorine not only deactivate pathogenic microorganisms in source water but also react with dissolved organic matter (DOM) from natural and anthropogenic sources, leading to the formation of numerous toxic halogenated disinfection byproducts (DBPs). The strong oxidants generated through catalytic decomposition of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) by iron oxide (Fe3O4) are proposed to reduce dissolved organic carbon (DOC), a DBP precursor, as well as to disinfect pathogens in drinking water treatment. title: A revision of the Australian leafcutter bees, previously placed in Megachile (Eutricharaea) (Hymenoptera: Megachilidae), with descriptions of seven new species
abstract: The species in the subgenus Eutricharaea Thompson, 1872 (genus Megachile) construct brood cells from pieces of leaves or petals cut from a diverse array of plants. abstract: The innovative Novel Drug Delivery System (NDDS) known as nanoemulsions provide the ability of controlled or regulated drug release, biologically active ingredients, and genetical material. A nanoemulsion is an oily, a surfactant, and a hydrophilic phase, which is a thermodynamically or kinetically stable liquid solution that is optically clear and typically has droplet diameters between 10 and 500 nm. abstract: One of the ubiquitous problems of the African economic integration process is multiple and overlapping memberships in different regional economic communities (RECs). One solution for this is the merger of these RECs into a single, larger entity. This study examined the rationale for the merger of IGAD and EAC as one larger new regional economic community in the greater Horn of Africa and assessed its potential benefits and challenges for the region. title: Imaging shallow magma storage and fluid pathways beneath Aso volcano using ambient-noise tomography
abstract: Abstract To investigate the high-resolution three-dimensional internal structure of the large caldera-type volcano Mt. Aso, we deployed a temporary seismometer network and applied ambient-noise surface-wave tomography. We resolve the shallow crustal structure with high spatial resolution and identify an ellipsoidal low S-wave velocity ( Vs ) anomaly at depths of 2.5–4.5 km beneath the Nakadake crater. abstract: INTRODUCTION: Agriculture is a major economic activity in Guatemala. Workers in sugarcane, banana, and African palm plantations face high risk of chronic kidney disease of non-traditional causes (CKDnT). During 2021- 2023, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) implemented a project in Guatemala to provide comprehensive care for CKDnT. abstract: Sudden changes in environmental conditions can lead to evolutionary shifts not only in the optimal trait value (θ), but also in the diffusion variance (σ2) under the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) model. While several methods have been developed to detect shifts in optimal values, few explicitly account for concurrent shifts in both evolutionary variance and diffusion variance. abstract: Today, businesses and consumers face a significant challenge in protecting and conserving the earth’s natural resources and environment. Both organizations and consumers have become increasingly conscious of environmental issues and recognize that their production and consumption decisions have a direct impact on the natural environment. Green marketing has the potential not only to transform the existing competitive practices of businesses but also to create a distinctive competitive advantage by addressing the environmental needs and expectations of customers. title: Determinants of Purchase Intent in The Freight Forwarding Sector in Jakarta
abstract: The increasing competition in the freight forwarding industry requires companies to improve Logistics Service Quality to build Customer Trust and encourage customers to use freight forwarding services. This study aims to analyze the effect of the dimensions of Logistics Service Quality on Purchase Intention through Customer Trust in the freight forwarding sector in Jakarta. A quantitative approach was employed by distributing questionnaires to 240 respondents selected through purposive sampling. title: Reconceptualizing Teacher Professional Competence through Medical Biochemistry: A Biopsychological Framework Linking Biochemical Health, Cognitive Function, and Educational Effectiveness
abstract: Teacher professional competence has traditionally been theorized through pedagogical, cognitive, and motivational lenses, treating biological health as a peripheral concern rather than a core determinant of instructional capacity. This paper proposes a biopsychological reconceptualization of teacher competence that positions medical biochemistry-specifically micronutrient status, hormonal regulation, gut-brain signaling, sleep architecture, and stress-biomarker profiles-as a foundational layer underlying cognitive function and, by extension, classroom effectiveness. title: Cost Accounting and Product Costing for Farm Biogas: Evidence from a Dairy Farm in Uzbekistan
abstract: Biogas plants on livestock farms turn manure into electricity, heat and digestate, yet farm cost accounting in Uzbekistan has no rules for recording such plants or costing their outputs. This study develops a costing methodology for farm biogas production and tests it on a project model built on the manure of a dairy farm in Samarkand region (18,307 t/yr). Following ISO 14051, physical flows are measured first and costs are then assigned to products. title: Microstoria : Reducing the pro‐elite bias in management research
abstract: Abstract Much management research, more than perhaps any other neighbouring social science, and especially in recent times, has been organised around elites—founders, CEOs, top management teams and board members—as the privileged locus and production site of meaningful knowledge. abstract: The role of courts in clarifying and interpreting existing climate law and, in doing so, contributing to its progressive development is crucial to addressing the climate emergency at all scales.The three books together provide domestic, regional, comparative and international legal perspectives on climate litigation.Each book has the potential to inform the other by identifying applicable climate law, framing litigation strategies and contributing to climate change governance through climate litigation.Since each book discusses climate cases in different legal and policy contexts, the extent t

title: Keeping an eye on the moose population: evaluating monitoring via hunter observations
abstract: Hunter‐based monitoring programs offer a cost‐effective approach to large‐scale wildlife monitoring, but their performance depends on sufficient observation effort and robust assessment of estimate precision. We evaluated the performance of ÄlgObs, Sweden's nationwide hunter‐based moose observation program, using data from six hunting seasons (2019/2020–2024/2025) across Moose management areas (MMA). title: La teoría ante la violencia: una cartografía de sus operaciones
abstract: Este artículo propone una cartografía conceptual de los modos de posicionamiento teórico ante la violencia. Su punto de partida es que las teorías sociales y políticas no solo definen, describen o explican la violencia; al hacerlo, realizan operaciones diferenciables: la vuelven inteligible, la juzgan, la condenan, la autorizan, la justifican, la excusan, la afirman o desplazan el marco en que algo aparece como violencia. title: Escaping the Broken Social Elevator: Youth Migration, Privilege, and Global Inequality
abstract: In recent decades, growing numbers of educated youths across the Global South have embraced geographical relocation to escape blocked social mobility at home. Using literature review, comparative case analysis, and critical examination of secondary datasets, this paper examines youth migration as a response to the collapse of the traditional "social elevator" linking educational credentials to stable employment and middle-class status. abstract: Paired speaking tests, in which learners interact with one another, have been regarded as an effective format for assessing interactional competence (IC). title: Policy adaptation frequency: central interventions and local policy outcomes in China’s governance system
abstract: Policy adaptations by central governments are often viewed as essential for institutional agility. However, little is known about how often such adaptations should be implemented to improve policy outcomes at the local level, particularly in hierarchical governance settings. To address this gap, we considered policy adaptation frequency as a structural driver of local outcomes, using China’s Business Environment Optimization reform as a case study. abstract: This paper presents twelve AMS radiocarbon analyses for Ongamira and Characato (Southern Pampean Hills, Argentina) using a problem-oriented strategy. title: Moral Injury and Resilience in Military Personnel: An Integrative Review
abstract: Military service exposes personnel not only to life threat but also to events that violate deeply held moral beliefs, such as killing, failing to prevent harm, or being betrayed by trusted leaders. The psychological aftermath of such events has been termed moral injury, a construct that overlaps with, but is distinct from, posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). title: Reclaiming the commons of the sky: drones and the limits of property law
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the concept of the commons in the context of the emergence of convenience-based delivery drone networks around the world. It contends that the drone-facilitated commodification of our skies constitutes a modern form of enclosure, facilitated by a legal architecture that centres around questions of ownership. title: Ethiopia and the United Arab Emirates Economic Diplomacy: Trajectory and Trends
abstract: This article examines the trajectory and trends of economic diplomacy between Ethiopia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) from 2014 to 2023. abstract: The discovered textile fragment at Mohenjo-daro provides age-old evidence of textile production in India. Since ancient times, various regions of India had developed distinct techniques for producing different types of textiles. The quality and diversity of Indian textiles earned widespread recognition and acceptance among foreign traders and consumers. abstract: El principio de publicidad de los juicios es un principio constitucional dinámico, adapta su modo de realización cuando cambian los medios de acceso, las tecnologías de difusión y la forma en que se construye la opinión pública. abstract: This article examines the handling of the Hopen crisis of 1978 in light of the overall effort by the Norwegian authorities to curtail the self-rule, or autonomy, of the Soviet mining towns on Svalbard. abstract: La participación de las mujeres en la caficultura familiar comprende actividades productivas que, particularmente en el beneficio poscosecha, pueden articularse con las tareas domésticas y ser interpretadas como una forma de “ayuda” familiar. abstract: Greta Thunberg’s environmental crisis speech at the UN Climate Action Summit 2019 was publicly and widely recognized. abstract: This article explores the ways in which the use of regulation, through the use of law, ethics, policies and standards, raises complex and deeply important questions about the ways in which our systems enable health (in)justice. title: Racialised dimensions of the 2026 schools white paper and SEND reform consultation: An intersectional analysis of special educational needs and race
abstract: Abstract This article uses Critical Discourse Analysis to examine the racialised implications of the 2026 Schools White Paper: Every child achieving and thriving and the associated open consultation, SEND reform: putting children and young people first. Drawing on scholarship in critical race theory, disability studies, and intersectionality, the paper argues that policy frameworks often obscure the structural inequalities experienced by pupils who occupy multiple marginalised identities, particularly those at the intersection of special educational needs and different racial backgrounds. abstract: Este artículo analiza de forma cualitativa la información y los mensajes disponibles en los debates presidenciales de Argentina en 2023 por medio de técnicas de la sociosemiótica, del marketing político y de la teoría funcional. title: The effective use of delivery partners to enhance client capability in megaprojects
abstract: A capable client is crucial in managing the complexities of megaprojects, requiring a wide range of organizational capabilities. However, client organizations are often temporary and rely on delivery partners to build capability. This research explores how delivery partners can enhance client capability, using the case of High Speed Two (HS2), the UK’s largest infrastructure megaproject. abstract: Abstract: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of programmed cell death characterized by the accumulation of intracellular iron and lipid hydroperoxides, accompanied by an imbalance in the antioxidant system. Iron metabolism, lipid metabolism, and dysregulation of antioxidant systems play critical roles in the regulation of ferroptosis. abstract: Abstract Recent national allometric equations developed by Nepal’s Forest Research and Training Centre (FRTC) were calibrated using aboveground biomass (AGB) measured above a 30-cm stump, thereby excluding stump biomass from the modelled boundary. title: CHALLENGES OF RENEWABLE ENERGY INDUSTRY IN MALAYSIA
abstract: The purpose of this study is to highlight the challenges faced by the Renewable Energy (RE) industry in Malaysia. This conceptual review examines previous research and articles on renewable energy in Malaysia and internationally, including current statistics, developments, and the status of renewable energy worldwide. The review covers key areas related to renewable energy, including its definitions, purposes, barriers, problems, challenges, principles, policies, strategies, and recommendations. title: Managerial Perception of the Application of the Circular Economy in the Hotel Sector
abstract: Despite growing interest in the circular economy (CE) in the hotel sector and extensive research identifying the conditions associated with its implementation, evidence remains insufficient on the organisational processes through which CE implementation takes shape. This research gap is the focus of the present study, which, recognising managers as agents of organisational change, addresses the following research question: How do managerial interpretations shape CE implementation? abstract: This study is motivated by the rapid growth of the online motorcycle taxi (ojek online) industry in South Jakarta, which has triggered intense competition and affected drivers' welfare. Drivers face challenges such as fluctuating income, job insecurity, and policy changes by the application platforms. An important yet often overlooked aspect of circular economy concerns the presence of hazardous chemicals in recycled materials. abstract: This study examines the impact of institutional quality and income inequality on environmental degradation for the selected South Asian and ASEAN countries for the time span 1985-2022. abstract: This study focuses on the methodological gap in the integration of nature-based concepts in basic design education and examines the phenomenon of crown shyness within the context of the conceptual–formal transformation process, addressing it as a structured teaching model supported by criteria-based evaluation parameters. abstract: This study investigates the trade intensity relationships between Azerbaijan and the Caspian littoral countries—Iran, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Russia—during the period 2006–2024. abstract: Abstract Behavior analysis has a long history of using nonhuman animals in basic research, classroom teaching, and applied practice, yet discipline-specific guidance for competent and ethical animal work remains limited. This paper reviews historical and contemporary trends in animal use within behavior analysis, including the decline of traditional animal laboratories, growing interest in invertebrate models, and expansion of behavior-analytic work into homes, shelters, zoos, and other applied settings. abstract: Abstract More than thirty years after the adoption of the UN Convention on Climate Change, fossil fuel still provides 80% of the world’s total energy consumption. The escalation in renewables makes a dent in fossil fuel use, but cannot, in itself, address the climate problem. abstract: Abstract Action on climate policy in the UK has been at a crossroads since 2021. The UK's previously world‐leading performance in emissions reduction was derived largely from eliminating coal from electricity supply and relied on a broad political consensus regarding the issue's importance. abstract: This article develops the concept of platformed atmospheres to address how digital platforms reshape domestic life. Platformed atmospheres are defined as the multisensory and affective environments that emerge when platforms become infrastructural to family life, shaping not only what families communicate but the felt, sensory, and temporal conditions through which homes are inhabited. abstract: Social media has emerged as one of the most powerful tools of the modern age, capable of serving both constructive and destructive purposes. In today’s interconnected world, it shapes public opinion, influences perceptions, and drives social trends. However, its misuse has become widespread, with talented individuals spending excessive time on unproductive online activities and entire societies increasingly influenced by its addictive nature. abstract: Este artículo propone una lectura textual del star system en el Hollywood clásico (1930-1945), centrándose en la representación de la vulnerabilidad emocional masculina en la pantalla. title: Odesa-teksten
abstract: This article examines the transformation of the Odesa Text in independent Ukraine. It traces three coexisting modalities: a post-Soviet nostalgic vision rooted in Odesa’s Russophone and Soviet past; a reinterpretation that challenges the old Odesa myth and foregrounds Ukrainian history and new urban spaces; and a wartime Odesa Text shaped by Russia’s invasion and the importance of testimony. title: Agroforestry ambitions fifty years after launch of a governance-people-science boundary concept
abstract: A novel word connecting agriculture and forestry, agroforestry, originated in 1976 with ambitions for radically better land use. abstract: As the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) reshapes trade conditions for carbon-intensive industries, the relationship between environmental regulations and logistics capabilities remains underexplored. abstract: The folk population of India has a mycophilic inclination, and wild mushrooms may help sustain their livelihood. abstract: Carnivores can have different habitat requirements and vary in their sensitivity to disturbance across stages of their life cycle, particularly during reproduction. abstract: Creating puffed snacks from protein-rich byproducts like salmon skin poses challenges in balancing drying efficiency, energy consumption, and product quality. This research focused on developing a ready-to-eat puffed snack using salmon skin through a multi-stage drying technique. The process involved initially drying the skins with hot air at 90 °C, followed by microwave puffing, and then returning them to hot-air drying until the moisture content fell below 4% (d.b.). title: Reinterpreting Restrictive Phrases in the ITE Law on Freedom of Expression: A Study of Constitutional Court Decision No. 105/PUU-XXII/2024
abstract: This study analyzes Constitutional Court Decision No. 105/PUU-XXII/2024 concerning the judicial review of the ITE Law sought by environmental activist Daniel Frits Maurits Tangkilisan, who faced criminalization after expressing his views on social media as part of the #SaveKarimunjawa campaign against the expansion of illegal shrimp farms that caused environmental damage. Using a normative juridical approach, the study examines Law No. 1 of 2024, the second amendment to the ITE Law, and the Constitutional Court's decision. title: ESCHATOKRATIA AS THE IDEAL REGIME IN HOMER
abstract: This paper explores the ideal regime in Homeric epics from the perspective of political philosophy, challenging both the "pre-political" taxonomies of political anthropology and the exclusionary Platonic-Aristotelian legacy. By adopting Luc Ferry’s distinction between moral and existential values, the study argues that Homeric sovereignty is rooted in the human encounter with mortality and finitude. title: Understanding the Basic Concepts of International Law
abstract: International law is often described as a system lacking a legislature, a compulsory judiciary and a central enforcement authority. These institutional limitations have long prompted questions about its status as law. This article reviews the fundamental concepts that give the discipline its structure and coherence. Adopting a doctrinal and conceptual approach, it draws on principal treaties, the jurisprudence of the International Court of Justice and leading scholarship, while setting aside historical narrative and detailed institutional analysis. It examines the nature of international law,
journal: International Scholar Journal of Arts and Social Science Research

title: The Closure Problem in Discourse Ethics: Ecological Truth and the Limits of the Tripartite Model
abstract: ABSTRACT Discourse ethics rests on the assumption that validity claims fall into a closed triad: facts about the objective world, norms about the intersubjective world, and self‐expressions disclosing the subjective world. This paper challenges that assumption. I argue that the tripartite framework is not exhaustive, and that treating it as such generates a previously unrecognized form of exclusion: not at the level of access, power, or expression, but at the level of intelligibility itself. To make this case, I introduce “ecological truth” as a candidate for a distinct kind of validity claim.

title: La criminalización de la pobreza: un enfoque desde la Criminología y el Derecho Penal
abstract: The criminalization of poverty raises questions about how socioeconomic conditions shape exposure to institutional control and the consequences of criminal justice involvement. This study aimed to analyze the normative, procedural, and sanctioning mechanisms associated with this relationship and their criminological and legal implications. A critical synthesis of recent empirical research was organized around three dimensions: coercive regulation of subsistence activities, inequalities during criminal proceedings, and the economic effects of sanctions. Findings identified interventions targeti
journal: Journal of Economic and Social Science Research

title: Medicine and Mass Incarceration
abstract: American jails and prisons are ripe for analysis by medical humanities scholars. Carceral institutions have been an especially salient feature of American history since the late-twentieth century, when U.S. incarceration rates began surging and culminated in what has come to be known as "mass incarceration." This article suggests a handful of topics medical humanities scholars might consider in relation to mass incarceration, including correctional medical care privatization, the drug war, and HIV/AIDS, chronic diseases, women's health, aging, and death in prisons. title: Effect of a solar-powered spatial emanator on malaria prevalence in Uganda (Mossie-GO trial): A double-blinded, cluster-randomised, and placebo-controlled trial
abstract: The continued threat of malaria has driven investigations into the efficacy of a range of new tools, including spatial emanators which release active ingredients that can affect mosquito host-seeking vector behaviour and reduce human contact. This study aimed to estimate the effect of a novel solar-powered spatial emanator in reducing the prevalence of malaria in rural and peri-urban settings. The Mossie-GO trial was a prospective, cluster-randomised, controlled trial conducted in Jinja and Buikwe in Eastern Uganda. Fifty-six clusters were randomised at a 1:1 ratio to receive either the spatia
institutions: London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine

title: Divergent approaches to the accommodation of substate demoi in Canada and the United States
abstract: Abstract Canada and the United States both have populations in which racial and ethnic minorities, substate national societies, native peoples and majority groups coexist. In this article, I contrast the United States and Canada, focusing on their contrasting political cultures, models of federation, legal nation-building mechanisms and so forth, in order to evaluate these states’ potential for accommodating minority nations. First, I analyze how Canada’s multicultural and multinational political culture has encouraged the recognition of substate national societies through a decentralized mode

title: The Influence of Human Resource Competencies, Internal Control Systems, and Service Innovation on Financial Performance
abstract: This study aims to analyse the influence of human resource (HR) competence, internal control systems, and service innovation on the financial performance of PT Pelindo Jasa Maritim Region 4. The research employed a quantitative approach by distributing questionnaires to 53 respondents consisting of management, finance, and operational staff across five operational areas of PT Pelindo Region 4. The data were analysed using multiple linear regression. The findings indicate that HR competence has a positive effect on financial performance, particularly in the understanding of accounting standards

title: Floristic Composition, Structure, and Regeneration Status of Wakani Forest in Guagusa Shikudad District, Awi Zone, Northwestern Ethiopia
abstract: Understanding the floristic status of remnant forests is essential for future forest management interventions. This study aimed to investigate the floristic composition, vegetation structure, and regeneration status of Wakani Forest in the Guagusa Shikudad District of Ethiopia. A systematic sampling method was employed to collect vegetation data along three transect lines across altitudinal gradients. In total, 63 main sample plots (20 x 20 m) were established. title: Sustainable Green Marketing as a Business Model
abstract: This paper seeks to investigate sustainable green marketing as a business model in the African context. Promoting products or services that are eco-friendly is called green marketing. It involves incorporating sustainable principles into various aspects of marketing. Broadly, the sustainable business principles include investing profits in renewable energy, responsible waste disposal practices and avoiding printed materials. journal: International Journal of Business Ecosystem and Strategy (2687-2293)

title: LANGUAGE IN THE POETRY COLLECTION MUSĀFIR WA-NĀSIK BY MUḤAMMAD IBN ʿABD AL-RAḤMĀN ĀL ʿABD AL-QĀDIR
abstract: This study examines the linguistic levels in the poetry collection Musāfir wa-Nāsik by Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Āl ʿAbd al-Qādir, at four levels: the syntactic, the morphological, the phonological, and the lexical. It follows a reciprocal approach that joins grounding in theory with the application of rules to texts, combining the descriptive and the inductive methods by tracing selected examples in the collection and then recording the phenomenon each illustrates. title: Improved European native seed supply chains are essential for the implementation of the Nature Restoration Regulation
abstract: Abstract To support the implementation of the EU Nature Restoration Regulation (NRR), there is an unprecedented need to scale up ecosystem restoration, which requires radical improvements to the European seed supply chain, especially for herbaceous species. The fundamental tradeoff between the need for local provenance and climate resilience, as well as practical constraints on seed availability, generates a bottleneck for restoration practice and may jeopardize the implementation of the NRR.
