title: Una Reflexión Autoetnográfica desde el Análisis Político del Discurso
abstract: Este artículo presenta una reflexión docente autoetnográfica sobre la experiencia de enseñar español como lengua extranjera (ELE) en una Universidad Históricamente Afroamericana (HBCU) en los Estados Unidos, desde el Análisis Político del Discurso (APD). Se examinan cuatro incidentes críticos (clases cortas, ausencia de libro de texto, barreras lingüísticas e irrupción de la IA) que generaron una dislocación en las prácticas pedagógicas sedimentadas del facilitador. title: Intelligent Democracy and Intelligent Epistocracy
abstract: In Intelligent Democracy, Jonathan Benson defends democracy’s epistemic merits. However, rather than focusing on the abilities of individual democratic institutions, Benson advocates a systemic perspective according to which we must understand how different institutions, each with their own strengths and weaknesses, interact to achieve more in aggregate than any could alone. title: Supporting health system resilience capacities in fragile and shock-prone settings: A qualitative synthesis of six years of learning from the ReBUILD consortium
abstract: Conflicts, crises and chronic stressors such as climate change are growing threats to health systems, which has led to increased focus on the concept of resilience. However, while there is an expanding literature on resilience, it has largely focused on conceptualization and measurement, rather than on understanding how to support the development of resilience capacities. ReBUILD, a research consortium which operated in 2020-2026, focused on building empirical evidence on this topic in relation to fragile and shock-prone (FASP) settings, where this is most urgent, challenging and neglected. title: The Political Economy Of Uneven Economic Development In South Asia: Structural Inequalities, Institutional Constraints, And Pathways To Inclusive Economic Growth
abstract: Despite being one the world’s fastest-growing economic regions, the South Asian region continues to experience substantial disparities in economic development. The developmental benefits are fragmented and unequally distributed across regions and social groups. The gap exists on four different levels: regional, social, political and opportunity. The region remains one of the least economically integrated regions. title: History and current value of ancient barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) varieties – a review
abstract: Ancient barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) varieties were not subjected to modern breeding. They were well adapted to their environment but lost importance over time due to the development and cultivation of higher-yielding varieties. This contributed to a loss of plant genetic resources. However, in the context of climate change and a growing population, as well as increasing consumer interest in new and high-quality products, these ancient barley varieties are receiving renewed attention. title: UNBALANCED GOVERNANCE OF CLIMATE FUNDING INSTRUMENTS: A GLOBAL SOUTH PERSPECTIVE
abstract: This article examines how international climate finance governance reproduces structural inequalities between the Global North and South. It adopts a qualitative, critical and comparative approach, combining documentary analysis of major multilateral climate funds from 2015 to 2025 with multilevel governance theory, dependency theory and postcolonial perspectives. The analysis identifies restrictive accreditation requirements, unequal institutional capacities, the predominance of loans, geographical and sectoral concentration of resources, and the marginalization of local knowledge. title: Unlocking Affixes in the ESL Community College Classroom: The Language of Law, Science, and Technology
abstract: Since vocabulary plays a significant role in second language acquisition, expansive vocabulary targets should be set and pursued. This paper explores the results of introducing affixes to develop vocabulary and increase motivation for beginner to intermediate-level English language learners (ELLs) pursuing academic disciplines in law, science, and technology at a New York City community college. journal: Journal of International Crisis and Risk Communication Research

title: Efforts to Combat Illegal Cigarettes by the Medan Customs and Excise Office
abstract: The circulation of illegal cigarettes is an excise crime that threatens state revenue and can distort competition in the tobacco industry. This study examines how the Medan Customs and Excise Supervision and Service Office of Intermediate Customs Type B (KPPBC TMP B Medan) handles the circulation of illegal cigarettes through preventive and repressive law enforcement. It also adopts a statutory approach that examines the relevant laws and regulations. The research applies an empirical-juridical approach and legal interpretation based on statutory provisions. title: SOLID WASTE DISPOSAL AND MANAGEMENT IN THE LECTURE AREAS OF FEDERAL POLYTECHNIC BIDA, NIGERIA
abstract: Solid waste, a type of land pollution comprises of any discarded solid or semi-solid material resulting from anthropogenic and animal activities in households, industry, institutions, commercial establishments, and public spaces. The research aims to study solid wastes disposal and management in the lecture areas of the Federal Polytechnic, Bida. Descriptive research design was employed for the research. 100 questionnaires were administered to the respondents, inclusive of 60 students, 20 academic staff and 20 administrative staff based on the proportion of their population size. journal: International Journal of African Development and Sustainable Research

title: Adoption and Impact of Climate-Smart Technologies on Agrifood Systems in Vihiga County, Kenya
abstract: Agrifood systems in sub-Saharan Africa face significant challenges from climate change, threatening food security and rural livelihoods. Climate-smart technologies (CSTs) offer a viable way to strengthen resilience, productivity, and sustainability in smallholder farming systems. This study examines the adoption and impact of CSTs in Vihiga County, a high-potential agricultural region in western Kenya with small landholdings and high vulnerability to climate variability. Using a mixed-methods approach, the study assesses the extent of CST adoption, key drivers and barriers, and socio-economic
journal: African Journal of Climate Change and Resource Sustainability

title: Bringing social cohesion into forest landscape restoration: Identifying future pathways toward more integrated social‐ecological restoration
abstract: Abstract Forest Landscape Restoration (FLR) is increasingly recognized as a key strategy to address land degradation, biodiversity loss and climate change. However, its long‐term success depends not only on ecological outcomes but also on social processes that shape restoration implementation and sustainability. This study explores the relationship between social cohesion and FLR in central Togo, examining how social cohesion influences FLR implementation and how participation in restoration activities can, in turn, shape social cohesion. title: A Comparative Conceptual Analysis of "bənê hā'ĕlōhîm" ("Sons of God") in the Qur'ān and Jewish Texts: Examining the Attribution of Polytheism to Jews in the Story of 'Uzayr in Qur'ān
abstract: This paper offers a comparative conceptual analysis of the expression bənê hā’ĕlōhîm (בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים, “Sons of God”) within Jewish theology and the Qur’ānic reference to ʿUzayr in verse Q 9:30. Employing an intertextual framework informed by Julia Kristeva’s theory of textual transposition and late antique Qur’anic hermeneutics, this study reassesses the dialogue between the Qur’anic corpus and its Biblical/post-Biblical subtexts. title: Sustainability of Chandragiri Hills: An Application of the GSTC Attraction Standard
abstract: Nepal is rapidly growing its commercial tourism industry that apples continuous sustainability assessment to determine whether the large-scale tourism project potentially benefit the local communities economically along with protecting the environment. This research paper examines the sustainability of Chandragiri Hills, one of the best tourism destination with the infrastructure in Kathmandu Valley, applying the Global Sustainable Tourism Council (GSTC) attraction standard framework. title: Anonymita nebo peníze: jak české dezinformační weby (ne)dodržují zákony
abstract: Článek se zabývá finančními příjmy českých dezinformačních webů a otázkou, zda tyto weby dodržují relevantní právní regulaci. Téma vychází z existujícího výzkumu, který identifikuje finanční příjem generovaný prostřednictvím online obsahu jako důležitý faktor motivující řadu aktérů k vytváření a šíření dezinformací. Tento článek navazuje na výzkum finanční motivace dezinformátorů v českém prostředí, na jehož základě identifikuje tři relevantní zdroje finančních příjmů dezinformačních webů: online reklamu, neoznačenou reklamu a příspěvky čtenářstva, na které se zaměřuje provedená právní a obsah
journal: Časopis pro právní vědu a praxi

title: Older adults’ intention to use extended reality in China’s Yellow River Basin: an extended Technology Acceptance Model with intergenerational support
abstract: As older adults become an important segment of China’s tourism market and family-based multigenerational travel becomes more prevalent, extended reality (XR)-enabled cultural heritage tourism raises a broader question about older adults’ access to technology-mediated cultural participation. Although XR may enrich cultural heritage tourism, older adults’ engagement with XR may be shaped by digital barriers and varying levels of family-based support. title: Caderno de Resumos do Workshop Internacional As Ciências Naturais frente a uma nova ordem mundial: Debates a partir do Ano Geofísico Internacional (1957-1958)
abstract: Os anos de 2027-2028 celebram os 70 anos da realização do Ano Geofísico Internacional – AGI, 1957-1958. title: Elevating Indigenous Voices for a Just Energy Transition
abstract: In the face of an accelerating climate crisis and shifting geopolitical power balances, the world is pursuing a “green transition” in which electrification is central. Electrification demands critical raw materials, including rare earth elements, a large share of which lie beneath Indigenous lands. Although the UN affirms Indigenous peoples’ right to own, use, develop, and control their traditional lands, these rights are routinely overruled, including on “national security” grounds. title: Criminal governance and the shift from local to transnational actor: a case study on the evolution of the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC)
abstract: Abstract This paper examines the relationship between criminal governance and the internationalization of organized crime, using the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) expansion towards Europe as a case study. It argues that governance can facilitate the transnational expansion of criminal organizations by fostering internal cohesion, regulating illicit markets, and enabling civilian control. title: Peran Keputusan Pembelian Dalam Membentuk Kepuasan Pelanggan Pada E-Commerce Fashion Di Kota Depok
abstract: Perkembangan e-commerce telah meningkatkan persaingan pada industri fashion sehingga pelaku usaha perlu memperhatikan kualitas produk, kualitas layanan, dan promosi penjualan untuk mendorong keputusan pembelian dan meningkatkan kepuasan pelanggan. abstract: Introduction: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease damaging the supportive structure of teeth. It has systemic impacts including cardiac autonomic dysfunction. Heart Rate Variability (HRV) measures an objective analysis of the extent of autonomic regulation and where decreased parasympathetic activity coupled with increased sympathetic predominance was determined to correlate well with risk in cardiovascular events. title: From Pesticide Pollution to Healthy Soils: Policy Assessment and Reform Options in Germany
abstract: Soil pollution in the EU and Germany is a pressing environmental issue. Multiple stressors contribute to soil pollution, including the use of plant protection products (here: pesticides). Policy goals, however, demand that the EU and Germany protect biodiversity and soils. Against this background, the present article adopts a qualitative governance analysis to investigate the extent to which German pesticide policies contribute to reduced pesticide pollution risks as well as biodiversity and soil health goals. title: Learning Ethics in the Qur’an
abstract: The ethics of learning constitute an essential aspect of Islamic education—particularly within pesantren (Islamic boarding schools)—which demands a balance between the mastery of knowledge and the cultivation of character. The narrative of Prophet Moses and al-Khiḍr in Q.S. Al-Kahf [18]: 65–82 provides a Qur’anic basis for examining these dimensions of learning. This study aims to analyze the ethics of learning in the narrative and their relevance to contemporary pesantren education through a tafsīr tarbawī approach. title: Beyond the campervan lifestyle: A social cartography of contemporary campervan tourism
abstract: Campervan tourism has become an increasingly important segment of outdoor recreation and tourism, with growing economic, environmental, and territorial impacts. Despite its relevance, research has largely focused on specific subcultures, destinations, or sustainability issues, and a systematic understanding of campervan users as a differentiated social population remains lacking. This article addresses that gap through the largest empirical study of campervan users currently available in the academic literature (N = 2845). title: Wildlife corridor delineation and habitat suitability modelling for key mammal species in Old Oyo National Park, Nigeria: a geospatial approach
abstract: Old Oyo National Park (OONP), a 2,512 km² Guinea savanna reserve in Oyo State, Nigeria, lacks a published spatial analysis integrating habitat suitability, movement corridors, land-cover change, and human-wildlife conflict (HWC) risk. title: “Against a darkening background”: dark Age mechanics in Total War: Attila
abstract: This article addresses the role of mechanics in facilitating time travel for players of strategy games, with a particular focus on games that address the Fall of Rome and a central case study around Total War: Attila. It argues that, while strategy game mechanics can provide a deep and complex account of historical forces, their representations of the past are often stymied by genre conventions that generally lead to a flat and narrow perspective of global history which fundamentally undermines their ability to transport their players into a different period or culture. title: Hacia una estrategia de accesibilidad y visibilidad del patrimonio contemporáneo: análisis y diagnóstico del sistema de gestión de la información de Andalucía
abstract: Esta investigación se centra en el patrimonio inmueble contemporáneo ofreciendo un protocolo para el análisis y diagnóstico de los Sistemas de Información de Patrimonio Cultural (SIPC) con el fin de mejorar la accesibilidad y visibilidad. title: Modernisation of the public management system in Ukraine
abstract: The existence of Ukraine as an independent subject in the international arena provides for a modern legal and democratic system of public management, which serves as the basis for the evolutionary transformation of socio-political relations in the period of post-war development of the state. The purpose of the study is to determine the areas of improvement and renewal of the public management system in Ukraine by considering the main stages of its historical development and functioning of the components of the public management system at the present stage. title: The Settlement Experiences of the Kerinchi Tribe in Malaysia: A Study on the Role of Kinship Networks
abstract: This article examines the kinship network of the Kerinchi (Kerinci) tribe in Indonesia and their diaspora’s migration patterns to Malaysia, considering the dynamic policy landscape between the two countries. Kinship, a cornerstone of Kerinchi culture, plays a crucial role in shaping identity and maintaining social cohesion, particularly through matrilineal inheritance, migration support, and intergenerational bonds. title: Primitive Tribal Groups in the Nilgiris District with Special Reference to the Kattunayakan Tribe
abstract: The Nilgiris district of Tamil Nadu is home to all six of the State's Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs): the Todas, Kotas, Kurumbas, Irulas, Paniyans and Kattunayakans. This paper examines these groups with special reference to the Kattunayakans, a forest-dwelling community concentrated in the Gudalur and Pandalur taluks along the Mudumalai forests. Kattunayakans are traditionally honey gatherers and collectors of non-timber forest produce, and they hold a deep ecological knowledge of plants, bees and elephants. title: Cultural Heterotopias and the Spatial Logic of Guilt and Shame: A Comparative Reading of The Scarlet Letter and The New Year’s Sacrifice
abstract: This paper offers a culturally oriented comparative reading of Nathaniel Hawthorne’s The Scarlet Letter (1850) and Lu Xun’s The New Year’s Sacrifice (1924) through Michel Foucault’s theory of heterotopia. abstract: Abstract Extradition treaties grant the parties considerable discretion: why? What are the functions of this treaty design? abstract: Abstract Proximity is traditionally viewed as crucial for overcoming the search and transfer costs associated with imperfectly codified knowledge. abstract: This article highlights the importance of analytical frameworks in enhancing the resilience of local communities to crisis-related threats, as they enable the identification and systematic organization of key factors influencing a community’s capacity to cope with crises. abstract: Abstract In EU energy and agri‐food law, ‘security’ is constantly invoked to justify legal action and to guide the adoption and interpretation of law. This article compares the concepts of energy security and food security, focusing on their relationship to sustainability, and asks whether invoking security enables or obstructs each sector's environmental transformation. abstract: On 29 June 2026, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi instructed the Headquarters for Ocean Policy to begin revising Japan’s Arctic Policy, Japan’s first comprehensive Arctic policy document (2015). title: Geoinformación marítima para la decisión antártica de Chile
abstract: La creciente variabilidad ambiental y la intensificación del uso marítimo de la Antártica elevan las exigencias de planificación, coordinación y apoyo a la decisión. title: When Alexander Did Not Visit Jerusalem in 332-331 BCE
abstract: The famous legend of Alexander the Great’s respectful visit to Jerusalem represents the positive relationship between Hellenistic kings and the Jewish people. abstract: This paper focuses on how the American comics anthology Gay Comix, which ran for 26 issues from 1980 to 1998, addressed the AIDS crisis. abstract: Abstract The native forest bird community on Kaua‘i, one of the main Hawaiian Islands, is facing an extinction crisis, with the endangered endemic Oreomystis bairdi (‘Akikiki) at the forefront. The standardized survey in 2018 estimated the global population size of O. bairdi at 120–886 individuals, while the 2023 survey detected none. Extensive range-wide searches in 2024 detected only 4 individuals, and by August 2025 only one female was known to persist. abstract: Abstract Large tree-cavities (LTC) are conspicuous structures with specific ecological functions in large trees. title: Developmental constraints on bisexuality in compound cones of Ephedra (Gnetales) and implications on the independent origin of bisexual flowers
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: In Ephedra foeminea, Welwitschia and Gnetum spp. (representing all genera of extant Gnetales) male cones have sterile ovules releasing pollination drops to attract pollinators. This condition is unknown in other gymnosperms and resembles the independently evolved bisexuality of angiosperm flowers. Patterns of bisexuality are insufficiently documented in Ephedra, despite their historical importance in Wettstein's pseudanthial theory of the origin of angiosperm flowers. abstract: Abstract The claim that Europe is strategically weak and incapable of defending itself, as most recently articulated by US President Donald Trump, has become a recurring feature of transatlantic political discourse in recent years. This article argues that Europe’s perceived weakness is not primarily the result of political complacency or strategic irresponsibility but rather the cumulative outcome of deliberate legal, institutional, and normative constraints embedded in the post–WWII security order. abstract: Abstract Pathogenic spillovers from animals into humans have catalyzed epidemics throughout history. They result from multiple factors. One such factor, human-animal contact, remains poorly understood. Current studies often neglect variability in human-animal engagements across ecological zones and the broader processes bringing people, animals, and pathogens into engagement. We investigated factors and longer-term processes shaping human-animal contacts and risks of zoonotic spillover in a region experiencing landscape fragmentation. abstract: Teleoperating a Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) in complex underwater environments presents unique challenges. Dynamic, three dimensional obstacles and unseen water currents pose real risks to expensive robotic hardware in environments in which recovery can be next to impossible. This paper explores the cognitive effects of haptic feedback to improve vehicle safety in such environments. abstract: Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) satellite networks are reshaping maritime connectivity, offering much lower latency and higher capacity than traditional geostationary (GEO) links. abstract: Multi-fin bioinspired propulsion systems have seen a rise in interest recently due to natural occurrence in animal systems and emerging technology. abstract: Abstract The sea ice albedo feedback is the process by which Arctic warming causes sea ice retreat, which due to the reduction in surface albedo leads to further Arctic warming through increased solar absorption. abstract: Abstract Background The global prevalence of exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) under six months is still below the target of 60%. Adolescent mothers undergo the simultaneous transition to adulthood and parenthood, which can complicate breastfeeding. Although numerous studies have examined breastfeeding among adolescent mothers in Southeast Asia, most are quantitative and provide limited insight into the underlying reasons and lived experiences. title: Prevalence of and factors associated with diarrheal disease among under-five children in South and Southeast Asian communities: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Diarrheal disease remains a leading cause of childhood illness and death in South and Southeast Asia, yet region-wide syntheses of its prevalence are sparse. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to estimate the pooled prevalence of diarrheal disease among children under five years in South and Southeast Asia, to describe its spatio-temporal and socioeconomic variation, and to identify factors associated with diarrheal disease. abstract: Pigeons and quail contribute to poultry production, nutrition, and livelihoods in Bangladesh; however, their role in avian influenza virus (AIV) circulation remains poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Marine plastic litter is a major environmental problem across all oceans, including remote regions. Here, we described the characteristics and spatial distribution of marine litter stranded on the beaches of Trindade Island, in the South Atlantic Ocean, 1200 km off the South American mainland, before the establishment of marine protected areas and the initiation of a long-term research program on the island. abstract: This study examines people-place relationships in shallow bays on the Swedish Baltic Sea coast prior to ecological restoration. Using surveys and in-depth interviews, combined with biophysical assessments, it characterizes nearby property owners' cultural ecosystem services (CES) and sense of place (SOP), examines if they are impacted by environmental degradation, and explores links between CES/SOP and restoration processes. abstract: Abstract This present study evaluated the effects of a commercial formulation based on fenthion on survival, hatching, and growth of Artemia salina, and characterized the environmental risk of this insecticide to marine and estuarine ecosystems. The fenthion-based commercial formulation was tested at concentrations ranging from 0.001 up to 731 mg/L using different bioassays: a standard 48-h acute test, a 14-day long-term test, and also two 72-h assays (one for cyst hatching, another for growth inhibition). Brazilian coastline is a mosaic of complex marine habitats, including extensive rocky shores on south-southeast and the largest coral reef formation of Atlantic in southeast-northeast. title: When the shoreline disappears: seawalls, nagisa , and the perceptual conditions of coastal knowing in post-3.11 Japan
abstract: Following the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and tsunami, extensive coastal defences transformed not only the physical shoreline of northeast Japan but also the everyday conditions through which the sea can be perceived and encountered. This article examines these transformations at three sites within Kesennuma City, Miyagi Prefecture: Koizumi Beach, Kesennuma Inner Bay, and Ōshima’s Tanakahama Beach. title: Radionuclide geochemistry and radiological implications of deep-sea ferromanganese crusts from the Rio Grande Rise
abstract: Ferromanganese (Fe-Mn) crusts are hydrogenetic marine deposits that incorporate naturally occurring radionuclides during their formation, making them valuable archives of marine geochemical processes. This study investigates the distribution of radionuclides, 222 Rn emanation, and radiological properties of 15 Fe-Mn crust samples from the Rio Grande Rise (RGR), South Atlantic Ocean, spanning water depths of 650-5218 m. abstract: Globally, intertidal molluscs are integral to the subsistence, commercial, and cultural identities of coastal and inland communities dependent on marine resources for survival. Despite their importance, the knowledge of intertidal zones in South Africa remains fragmented across ecological, socio-economic, and biotechnological disciplines. abstract: This article examines how maritime culture can be transmitted to young children through relationships among families, coastal communities, and early childhood education institutions in Indonesia. Although children living near the sea encounter maritime occupations, material objects, and ecological practices in everyday life, geographical proximity alone does not ensure cultural understanding or environmental responsibility. This study examines pisolite-bearing horizons within the Pleistocene coastal successions of Eivissa (Balearic Islands, western Mediterranean) using field sedimentology, quantitative morphometry, petrography, and X-ray diffraction (XRD). abstract: Low-frequency underwater acoustic sources face a fundamental trade-off between miniaturization and output power, which severely constrains their use in marine geological exploration. title: CASPIAN SEA LEVEL AND COASTLINE DYNAMICS FROM SATELLITE DATA
abstract: The Caspian Sea is the world's largest enclosed water body, and its level serves as an integral indicator of the regional climatic and hydrological balance. abstract: Long–term monitoring of marine fouling assemblages and non‑indigenous species (NIS) has been historically scarce globally, particularly in island ecosystems, limiting the ability to distinguish transient detections from persistent populations. Using an 11–year monitoring dataset (2013–2025; 33 surveys, 131 sampling events) across four Madeira Archipelago marinas, we evaluated spatio-temporal patterns in biofouling assemblages. However, the ecological consequences of the organic matter released following bloom collapse via viral infection are poorly understood. abstract: This article contributes to and expands the environmental history of recreational fishing through examining the development of recreational fishing in late colonial Luanda, Angola, 1945–1975. It draws on colonial archives, newspapers, tourism magazines, specialised fishing periodicals and oral testimonies to argue that recreational fishing developed through processes of dwelling in different coastal environments as practitioners and practices took shape in relation to their ecological conditions and possibilities. abstract: The Echigo Plain in central Japan is an actively subsiding sedimentary basin influenced by tectonic subsidence and anthropogenic activity. This study presents a physics-based white-box thermodynamic model for air-cooled chillers in data center cooling applications. title: From Diving Sites Toward Sustainable Underwater Trails: Formal and Informal Routes, Underwater Attractions, and Nature Conservation Considerations in Selected Polish Case Studies
abstract: Inland diving sites may contain routes, attractions, and infrastructure, but these elements do not determine how a future underwater tourist trail should be organized. This study applies an emerging pre-implementation framework using an 85-record database of Polish inland diving sites compiled from specialist diving sources, operator and institutional materials, maps, and scientific publications. abstract: Abstract Coastal households in eastern India are increasingly affected by recurrent cyclones, flooding, storm surges, salinity intrusion, and coastal erosion, yet household-level evidence on multidimensional vulnerability remains limited. This study assesses household vulnerability to coastal hazards in Puri and Kendrapara districts of Odisha, India, and identifies the major socio-economic and preparedness-related determinants of vulnerability. abstract: This essay examines the role of poetry as a medium of survival, testimony and ethical witness in the context of Mediterranean migration crises, focusing on the works of Eritrean poet Segen Tesfalidet and Sudanese poet Abdel Wahab Yousif (Latino). abstract: Molybdenum (Mo) isotope compositions have been widely applied as a paleoredox proxy to reconstruct past ocean deoxygenation, particularly from organic-rich sediments such as sapropels and Black Shales. title: Evaluating the potential role of extreme dives by swordfish (Xiphias gladius)
abstract: Abstract Movements of swordfish ( Xiphias gladius ) typically follow the diel vertical migration of mesopelagic animals, spending daylight hours at ~ 600 m and nights near the surface. abstract: Internal solitary waves (ISWs) are frequently observed in the Indonesian seas, where strong tides, complex topography, and stratified water masses generate energetic internal wave activity. abstract: Despite the ecological and economic importance of Ria de Aveiro, Portugal, little is known about the diversity and seasonal dynamics of fungal communities. abstract: This study aims to analyze strategies for the economic empowerment of coastal communities in order to strengthen the local economy. abstract: Contact dermatitis is an occupational skin disease that may affect seaweed farmers because of repeated exposure to seawater, humidity, marine organisms, and irritants. abstract: ABSTRACT In a changing global ocean certain fish populations are approaching the upper limits of their thermal tolerance. abstract: Robust 3D reconstruction across varying environmental conditions remains a critical challenge for robotic perception, particularly when transitioning between air and water. abstract: Abstract Essential habitats often shift throughout ontogeny as different life stages have distinct life history requirements. The scalloped hammerhead shark (Sphyrna lewini) is a cosmopolitan species known to undergo ontogenetic habitat shifts. However, the characteristics of habitats considered important for the species varies among and within geographic regions. abstract: Introduction/Objective: Spiroisoxazoline is a unique class of spiroheterocyclic scaffold that has gained significant attention from medicinal chemists in recent years due to its structural rigidity, chirality, and broad spectrum of biological activities. abstract: The article presents data on the first report for the Black Sea of the non-indigenous red alga Ahnfeltia plicata, first registered in Odesa Bay (Ukraine) in 2023. abstract: Large-diameter steel pipe piles (LDSPPs) are increasingly used for offshore wind turbines, marine terminals, long-span bridges, and other heavily loaded infrastructure. abstract: Place identity is expressed through symbols, practices, and visual representations. Translating regional identity into textile motifs requires a systematic approach that connects local visual sources with meaningful design decisions. This study aims to identify Pangandaran's visual identity sources, translate them into textile motif compositions, and evaluate the resulting prototype. abstract: This study describes a new Dysommina species, based on two specimens collected at a depth of ca. 600 m in the Lakshadweep Sea off south-western India. abstract: Little attention has been devoted to exploring the personal experiences of those who served with the Royal Navy during the First World War. abstract: Maritime chokepoints stand in a paradoxical position in the international legal order. abstract: Abstract Background: Nonmelanoma skin cancer (NMSC) is the most common malignancy worldwide, yet comprehensive national mortality surveillance remains limited in the United States (U.S.). title: Lithology, Mineralogy and Quartz Grain Morphoscopy of the SB Well, Birisso (eastern Ivorian basin): a Paleoenvironmental Approach
abstract: This study focuses on 13 samples from the SB well of Birisso, in the eastern onshore part of the Ivorian sedimentary basin, born from the opening of the South Atlantic during the Cretaceous. It combines lithology, binocular mineralogy and morphoscopy of quartz grains to reconstitute the depositional environments. The shaft shows four units with decreasing grain size upwards: purplish sands and clays at the base, fine sands with ferruginous sandstone, bitumen and marl in the middle, then a lateritic armour at the top. abstract: The people of Mwoakilloa (population < 200) and the Mwoakilloan diaspora (ca. 2000) represent a resilient Oceanic culture that has adapted to both island life and migration across the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM) and to the United States. We describe collaborative work by Mwoakilloan speakers with linguists documenting their language and culture through oral environmental narratives recorded in both English and Mwoakilloan. abstract: This research documents and analyzes the vernacular wisdom embedded in the traditional timber and bamboo architecture of Pelaga Village, a highland settlement in Badung, Bali, Indonesia, situated at 650–1,100 meters above sea level. Through field surveys, architectural documentation, and environmental monitoring, this study examines how indigenous construction techniques and local material knowledge adapt to the cool tropical mountain microclimate. title: El archivo audiovisual como insumo necesario para la investigación escénica
abstract: This essay argues considering audiovisual archives as a valuable resource for the analyses of Latin American theatre, because they help articulate theatrical productions with their political, economic, and social context. A research process may begin with seeing the performance itself, but the experience expands when it is seen again through audiovisual media, which helps critics appreciate the production’s connection to broader ideas and emotions. title: A new Pan-sirenian from the late Eocene of Romania
abstract: Palaeogene sea-grass communities of Tethyan shallow marine ecosystems encompassed a diverse range of animals, including the ancestors of present-day sirenians. The fossil record of this group from the Eocene of Romania is relatively extensive; however, most occurrences consist only of isolated ribs and, less frequently, skull bones, vertebrae, or elements of the appendicular skeleton. abstract: Thalassotherapy, a health practice dating back to ancient times in coastal areas, is closely linked to the originsof tourism in several regions. abstract: Amidst the Cold War in the world and the national liberation movement in Vietnam, the 1954 Geneva Accords resulted in the temporary division of Vietnam and imposed an urgent mandate for troop regroupment. While referencing copious archival materials and associated documents, this article researches the issue of troop regroupment and transfer in the South of Vietnam during 1954-1955 from the perspective of the Party’s strategic vision and implementation in practice. title: On-site, subannual climate records decouple Neolithic expansion from climate instability
abstract: How the life of prehistoric people was influenced by climate change and extreme events often remains elusive. Finding appropriate spatiotemporal scales is the major challenge for studies with socioenvironmental questions. This challenge can be overcome by sourcing climatic information from archaeological sites, alongside traces of human agency. For instance, extreme cold-events have been proposed as causing a standstill in early farming expansion across the Mediterranean 8600-8000 years ago. abstract: Abstract Background The biofilm of Klebsiella pneumoniae is a critical factor in antibiotic resistance and pathogenicity. Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) are nanoscale vesicular structures produced by Gram-negative organisms, and they have been demonstrated to be involved in various aspects of the physiology and pathogenesis of K. pneumoniae. However, significant knowledge gaps remain regarding the specific role of K. pneumoniae OMVs in biofilm regulation. title: An agent‐based approach for designing effective protection for endangered species
abstract: Abstract The main threat to New Zealand dolphins is entanglement in fishing nets. We developed an agent‐based model (ABM) to assess how area‐based controls on fishing methods can reduce fishing mortality and population declines. The model incorporates the behavior and distributions of dolphins and fishing vessels, and realistic displacement of fishing effort when protection is extended. title: Fecal DNA metabarcoding reveals how sexual dimorphism and bite force influence seasonal changes in diets of diamondback terrapins (Malaclemys terrapin littoralis)
abstract: Diamondback terrapins (DBTs, Malaclemys terrapin ) exhibit pronounced sexual dimorphism, yet the functional consequences of this morphology for trophic ecology remain poorly resolved. We examined sex- and size-dependent dietary shifts using fecal DNA metabarcoding of DBTs captured from February-August over a three-year period and integrated these data with bite force measurements to assess biomechanical constraints on prey use. abstract: Post-baking operations in bakery processing environments create opportunities for microbial recontamination through food-contact surfaces that may remain contaminated after routine sanitation. This study investigated the persistence, biofilm forming ability, and disinfectant tolerance of Bacillus cereus isolates recovered from food-contact surfaces in a bakery processing environment. The objective of this research is to provide a description of the principles and standards of green maintenance and to study how these can be implemented in Historic Jeddah while taking into account the unique architectural features of traditional Hejazi buildings, including coral and *Manqabi* stone and wooden *Rawashins* (decorative bay window with a table). abstract: Abstract The weedy seadragon Phyllopteryx taeniolatus (family Syngnathidae) is an iconic fish endemic to Australia’s southern coast. There are indirect indications of population declines over the last decade, with large numbers of individuals washed up in 2022, and the impacts of such events are exacerbated by limited dispersal and spatial differences in genetics. abstract: Iron is required for photosynthesis and thus affects carbon fixation rates in widespread aquatic regions where availability is limited. Turnover of aquatic photosynthetically derived fixed carbon is largely constrained by bacterial activity, but it is unknown how algal iron limitation alters dissolved organic matter composition and subsequent processing through the microbial loop. abstract: Nature is often treated as a passive object in environmental management, yet Nusantara ecological archives preserve other ways of understanding human-nonhuman relations. This article examines how primary manuscripts, published documentation of oral traditions and customary practices, official documentary sources, and secondary scholarship articulate nature as an ecological subject. title: Fishery monitoring reveals a rare and seasonal occurrence of the threatened tope shark Galeorhinus galeus (Linnaeus, 1758) within a restricted bathymetric range in the state of Santa Catarina, southern Brazil
abstract: This study aimed to report new records of the tope shark Galeorhinus galeus, a critically endangered species in Brazil, based on onboard monitoring of artisanal bottom gillnet fisheries in southern Brazil, emphasizing its seasonal occurrence and strong association with a narrow depth range. Data were collected between 2021 and 2025 across 168 monitored fishing operations. title: Soil nutrient status of smallholder farms in Kenya
abstract: Declining soil fertility remains a major cause of reduced crop production among smallholder farmers in sub-Saharan Africa. This is partly attributed to the blanket application of inappropriate fertilizers. Most fertilizer recommendations are based on soil analyses conducted in the 1990s, which have since become obsolete. title: Greenhouse Gases and Climate from a Physical-Chemical Perspective
abstract: In our previous publications we examined the role of carbon dioxide, CO2, in the greenhouse effect according to Physical Chemistry Principles. This work led to arguments that raised doubts about the human-caused origin of climate change, in opposition to renowned climate scientists. Our results are summarized here as a response as well as a contribution to the current discussion. abstract: Background Coastal tourism corridors experience variable traffic demand and require assessment approaches that account for weekend travel, access constraints, and environmentally sensitive locations. This study examines traffic impact assessment (TIA) for the Burapha Chollatit Scenic Road Phase 2 project in Rayong Province, in Thailand’s Eastern Economic Corridor. title: Urban Wastewater and River Health in Bangladesh: A Systematic Evidence Map Revealing a Dhaka Bias and a Neglected Barnoi River
abstract: Background: Urban and industrial wastewater discharge has contributed to river pollution in Bangladesh, raising concerns about water quality and ecosystem health. However, existing research remains unevenly distributed across geographical regions and environmental compartments, particularly in rivers associated with secondary cities. Objective: To map primary field studies of effluent-affected rivers by region, sampled compartment and pollutant group, with particular attention to the Barnoi River near Rajshahi. Study Design: Systematic evidence map, reported in line with PRISMA 2020 and ROSES.

abstract: Abstract The Great Unconformity marks a globally extensive erosive surface linked to climatic shifts 1 and environmental transitions 2 that preceded the Cambrian explosion of life. The processes proposed to explain the formation of the Great Unconformity include glacial erosion during the Snowball Earth 1,3,4 , rifting and plume activity 5–7 , sea-level fall 8 and mantle-driven dynamic topography 6,9–11 . abstract: Abstract Although the characteristics of a region or site can have a large effect on the implications of climate change on wildfire risk, the associated causal relationships are poorly understood. This article reviews 424 studies to identify the environmental factors that mediate and moderate the relationship between climate change and wildfire risk, gathering the associated evidence from the perspective of regional and site-specific variability. abstract: Coryphaena hippurus (dolphinfish) is an important epipelagic top predator and global fishery resource. Global fishing indices indicate a tenfold increase in catch, and intense fishing may reduce genetic diversity and increase vulnerability to extinction. abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are contaminants associated with anthropogenic activities. This study evaluated PAH exposure in Centropomus parallelus specimens collected from the Port of Santos, São Paulo State (contaminated area), and the Barra do Una Sustainable Development Reserve (reference area). abstract: The Ciénaga Grande de Santa Marta (CGSM), the largest coastal lagoon system in Colombia, supports a diverse ichthyofauna and a highly productive artisanal fishery, yet its fish diversity has never been synthesized within a consistent taxonomic framework. abstract: Leaf beetles of the tribe Haemoniini (Chrysomelidae: Donaciinae) comprise two genera, Macroplea in the Palearctic region and Neohaemonia in the Nearctic region. These beetles are exceptional among aquatic insects in that they complete their entire life cycle underwater, obtaining oxygen either directly from the water or from the tissues of aquatic plants. However, a standardized computational pipeline for systematically integrating microbial, metabolite, and host target information remains lacking. title: The relationship between ENSO state and wildfire extent in the Cape Floristic Region of South Africa
abstract: Background Predictive understanding of how major climatic teleconnections influence fire regimes in Mediterranean-type ecosystems remains limited, despite emerging evidence of regional teleconnection effects on fire activity. abstract: In Indonesia, microplastics (MPs) have become a significant environmental and public health threat due to the rising levels of plastic waste. The issue of microplastic pollution represents a pervasive transnational public health challenge. abstract: ABSTRACT There is increasing awareness of combatting lifestyle diseases through improved nutrition and the important role that adequate intake of omega‐3 long‐chain PUFA has in promoting human health and development. title: Density-dependent emergence of collective phototaxis in a microcrustacean revealed by automated tracking
abstract: Light is a fundamental environmental cue influencing movement, habitat selection, and aggregation in aquatic organisms. While phototaxis has traditionally been studied at the level of individual responses, how social context and density modulate light-driven behavior in non-marine microcrustaceans remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the phototactic response of the ostracod Heterocypris incongruens across three density regimes (single individuals, pairs, and groups of ≥30 individuals). title: Seeing Double
abstract: The subject of this essay is the author’s unrealised proposal for a temporary interior installation commemorating the return of a historic archive to Croome Court — a neo-Palladian house in a landscape garden of international significance near Worcester, UK. The proposed Archive Rooms installation would transform a suite of uninhabited spaces on the first floor of the house into a stimulating setting for exhibitions of artefacts from the returning collection. title: Crafting Collaboration
abstract: This article reflects on the long-running transdisciplinary collaboration between ceramicist Diana Butucariu and musician Erik Lindeborg, tracing their evolving practice from pop-up events to situated works that engage with sustainability, heritage, and place. Collaboration emerges as a process of mutual orientation, developed under conditions of precarity. Past work is reanimated as a research archive, ultimately leading to renewal in the present through the act of writing. abstract: Marine red algae represent an important reservoir of structurally diversified sulfated polysaccharides with promising applications across various fields. In this study, sulfated polysaccharide hydrocolloid isolated from Halymenia floresii wa s collected from Manuali Island in the Southeast Coast of India. On extensive chemical characterization using various analytical techniques the isolated polysaccharide (MW- 365 kda) revealed the presence of glucose (79 mol.%) and galactose (20.98 mol.%) linked with sulphate groups. title: Layering and layered states in single-component stratified flows
abstract: In stratified turbulent flows such as the ocean, layered features (in which well-mixed regions of fluid are separated by sharp interfaces where the density varies rapidly) are a common occurrence. Understanding how and when layers might arise, as well as how they evolve in time, is an ongoing area of study. title: Living on unstable foundations – Tracing climate change-driven housing insecurity in Bordeaux and Rotterdam
abstract: This paper explores climate change-driven housing insecurity by focusing on unstable foundations. With climatic and environmental conditions changing, housing foundations, specifically those built on clay soils and in coastal areas, become unstable as soil properties adapt to prolonged periods of heat and heavy rainfalls. title: Notes on the occurrence of Sida cordata (Burm.f.) Borss.Waalk. (Malvaceae) in Indonesia
abstract: Sida cordata (Burm.f.) Borss.Waalk. is a widely distributed member of the genus Sida (Malvaceae), yet its modern occurrence and distribution on the mainland of Indonesia remain poorly documented following historical records from the Seribu Islands in 1948. Utilizing virtual herbarium networks and digital specimen examinations from major international repositories (such as Naturalis Biodiversity Center), this study updates the distribution of S. cordata in the region. Based on digital voucher evaluations, S. cordata is formally reported as new distribution records for mainland Java (Central Jav

title: ‘A Musical Relationship Between Death and Nature … ’ Nature as Solace and Witness in Behrouz Boochani’s No Friend but the Mountains
abstract: Behrouz Boochani’s No Friend but the Mountains creates a musical and ecological relationship between death, detention, and nature. Written from inside Australia’s Manus Island prison for migrants seeking asylum, Boochani’s poetic prose renders nature not as backdrop but as witness, accomplice, and mourner. Birds, trees, insects, and the ocean form a chorus of protest, echoing the screams, scars, and rhythms of imprisoned life. Using motifs like the Chauka bird and the musical cadence of the dhol, Boochani’s place-based narrative is attuned to ecological temporality and trans-species mourning.
journal: Journal of War and Culture Studies

title: Inter-Agency Consistency of Western North Pacific Tropical Cyclone Best-Track Data as a Function of Proximity to the Korean Peninsula and Intensity
abstract: Multiple agencies independently produce tropical cyclone best-track datasets for the western North Pacific, and these datasets are often regarded as interchangeable in coastal hazard applications. This study examined when this assumption holds. KMA, JMA, and JTWC data for 1977–2024 were matched by cyclone and observation time, and inter-agency differences were analyzed on a response surface defined by intensity and proximity to the Korean Peninsula. title: An Invasive Crab Species Exhibits Greater Daily Behaviour Plasticity Than a Naïve Native Crab Species
abstract: ABSTRACT Behavioural plasticity is considered highly relevant for biological invasions. As daily behavioural rhythmicity is plastic in response to environmental factors, we suggest that it may also be worth considering in the context of invasion success. We explored, under laboratory conditions, the potential role of plasticity in the recent invasion of the Atlantic blue crab ( Callinectes sapidus , Rathbun, 1896) in the Mediterranean Sea, by studying its behavioural rhythmicity in the presence of the native Mediterranean green crab ( Carcinus aestuarii, Nardo, 1847). title: A Review of Current Evidence and Future Directions on Galactogogues in Lactogenic Insufficiency
abstract: Lactogenic insufficiency is a multifactorial condition of inadequate breast milk production that challenges successful breastfeeding and infant nutrition. Galactogogues include pharmaceutical agents, herbal medicines, nutritional supplements, and other natural bioactives, which are widely used to enhance lactation; however, their clinical utility varies. This review summarizes the pathophysiology of lactogenic insufficiency, the classification of galactogogues, and their proposed mechanisms. abstract: Introduction. Lipid complexes (LCs) from Barents Sea brown algae are a valuable source of biologically active compounds for the pharmaceutical industry. Despite the successful use of LCs from Laminaria algae in medicinal preparations, the potential of bladderwrack ( Fucus vesiculosus ) remains underexplored. title: Crafting lines
abstract: This article explores the significance of traditional Romani crafts, specifically wirework, as a vital component of Romani cultural heritage in Norway. It examines how these traditional practices, in which intangible cultural threads are interwoven with material skills, are transmitted and maintained, as well as how they find new meaning in contemporary design. title: Microbial profiling of Drosophila in French Guiana reveals candidate microbial taxa associated with native and invasive host
abstract: Invasive alien species (IAS) threaten biodiversity, human health, and economies, yet host-associated microbiome differences between invasive and native species remain poorly understood in natural systems. We investigated bacterial and fungal microbiomes of IAS and native Drosophila species collected along an anthropisation gradient in French Guiana. IAS occurrence declined strongly from coastal anthropised habitats toward rainforest localities. title: A multi-factor prediction model for chloride concentration in the interface zone of precast and cast-in-place concrete incorporating interfacial amplification and stress effects
abstract: To reasonably predict the chloride concentration in the interface zone of existing precast and cast-in-place concrete structures, this study establishes quantitative relationships between interfacial chloride concentration and governing factors, based on the rational Taylor model. abstract: When Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, the West responded with the most sweeping restrictions imposed on a major economy since 1945. title: Color perro que huye de Andrés Duque, y la forma/lugar del cine inmigrante
abstract: This essay analyzes the film Color perro que huye (2011) by Venezuelan filmmaker Andrés Duque, focusing on the chapter COLOR (20:48-40:33) to examine how the director articulates his migratory experience by recovering his personal archive of digital images. title: Ecoacoustic Exploration of Bone Bolango Bamboo in the Tomini Bay Area for Polopalo Manufacturing as a Nusantara Cultural Heritage
abstract: This study aims to explore the physical-acoustic characteristics of talilo huidu bamboo from Bone Bolango, Tomini Bay area, in the production of Polopalo, while formulating geometric standards to preserve local ecology and cultural heritage. Utilizing a qualitative method as the primary approach, this research integrates oral ethnoorganological studies with sound analysis via Fast Fourier Transform in Audacity as supporting data, alongside the sound philosophy concepts of the Gorontalo community. title: Research on the Impact of Overseas Business Income on the Degree of Enterprise Innovation—An Empirical Analysis Based on China's A-share Listed Companies
abstract: With the continuous advancement of the internationalization of Chinese enterprises, overseas business has become an important factor affecting the innovative development of enterprises. This paper selects panel data of A-share listed companies from 2015 to 2025, adopts the two-way fixed-effects model to test the impact of overseas business income on corporate R&D investment and operating output. abstract: Abstract Regional air pollution controls imposed by the US Clean Air Act of 1970 reduced emissions of precursors to ozone (O 3 ), a radiatively active gas that primarily acts as a greenhouse gas in the troposphere. abstract: For the Jesuits, libraries constituted one of their most valuable assets, as they housed a significant proportion of works linked to Classical Antiquity. Building upon this premise, this article aims to analyze the Ignatians' preservation and dissemination of the Greco-Roman world, in accordance with their educational and evangelizing functions in the New Kingdom of Granada on the eve of their expulsion in 1767. abstract: The Republic of Karelia, situated within the Fennoscandian Shield, represents a unique geological archive spanning more than 3.5 billion years of Earth's history – from the formation of early continental crust and Achaean greenstone belts, through Proterozoic volcanic sedimentary complexes and unique mineral systems, to late glacial events. abstract: Caulerpa seaweed has the potential to be developed as a nutritious food source and a raw material for value-added bioproducts. However, its utilization in Indonesia is still dominated by fresh consumption, while information regarding its nutritional composition, bioactive compounds, food safety, and product development opportunities remains scattered across various studies. abstract: We report the first Georgia, USA, records for the relapsing fever tick, Ornithodoros turicata americanus Marx, a gopher tortoise (Gopherus polyphemus Daudin) burrow commensal and proven vector for human relapsing fever spirochetes and African Swine Fever Virus. During May–June 2026, we documented O. t. americanus at 14 sites (in 8 counties) located in the Atlantic Coastal Plain of southeastern Georgia. title: Fernando Herrero Tejedor, una trayectoria falangista al servicio del régimen franquista (1920-1975)
abstract: Fernando Herrero Tejedor (1920-1975) was a key figure in the political class of the Franco dictatorship. After his initial activities connected to the revolutionary discourse of the Falangists of the 1950s, Herrero Tejedor evolved into the position of an open-minded bureaucrat from various institutional positions at the service of the State and the National Movement, reaching his highest levels when he was named Minister-Secretary General of the Movement in 1975. title: “What Makes It Alright to Dig Up Our Ancestral Remains?”: An Interview With Carmen Lucas, Kwaaymii Laguna Band of Indians
abstract: ABSTRACT Carmen Lucas is a tribal monitor, expert, and elder of the Kwaaymii Laguna Band of Indians, San Diego County, California. She learned about cultural landscapes and Ancestral human remains from her father, the late Tom Lucas—the last full‐blooded descendant of the Kwaaymii—and has been a caretaker of the Kwaaymii Homeland and burial grounds at the former Laguna Indian Reservation for the last 50 years. abstract: Abstract In the interwar period, many industrializing states raised labor standards, introduced worker protections, and established deliberative labor institutions. Iran stands out as a remarkable outlier in this early wave of labor policy. Despite founding membership in the International Labour Organization (ILO), Iran kept labor protections at a bare minimum and workers excluded from decision-making processes altogether. abstract: This article uses a volumetric lens to explore how household rain-harvesting cisterns help (re)shape hydrosocial relations across the semiarid region of Ceará, Northeast Brazil, where vulnerability to climate variability remains high among the rural poor. title: Multivariate assessment of genetic variability in Mundu chilli (Capsicum annuum L.) accessions for yield and quality traits
abstract: Mundu chilli (Capsicum annuum L.) is an important rainfed spice cum vegetable crop cultivated in the coastal regions of Tamil Nadu, valued for its yield stability and quality attributes. The present study evaluated 27 purified Mundu chilli genotypes collected from Ramanathapuram district to assess variability for yield and quality traits using multivariate approaches. The experiment was conducted over three consecutive years (2022–25) in a randomized block design (RBD) with 3 replications. abstract: The North American species of Rhopobota Lederer (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae: Olethreutinae: Eucosmini) are reviewed. All feed as larvae on hollies (Aquifoliaceae: Ilex Tourn. ex L.). abstract: Abstract The biology and history of the decline of the Arctic fox population on the Mednyi Island, Commander Islands, North Pacific, are considered. Currently, this is the smallest and possibly the most ancient island population of canids on Earth. Among the endemics of island faunas, carnivores are generally very rare, and among the canids only the California island fox (Urocyon littoralis) is listed in taxonomic and conservation databases. title: The Architecture of Intoxication: Opium Dens, Use of Bodies and New World Orders
abstract: Abstract What is the relationship between the experience of intoxication and the built environment in which it occurs? This article reflects on how the materiality of spaces of intoxication offers a lens for exploring the interplay between bodily and psychic experiences and their connection to the emerging world orders. We focus on the architecture of so-called opium dens as largely unexplored historical sites, examining how they shaped consumers and embodied tensions between meaning-making and meaning-erasure. abstract: Moving past traditional intellectualist frameworks that privilege printed treatises as monuments of pure conceptual progress, in Un galiléen d’encre et de papier Simon Dumas Primbault undertakes an archaeology of working manuscripts within the Fondo Galileiano at the National Central Library of Florence (BNCF). abstract: This article examines two distinct, and often intertwined, ways in which education produces hate. abstract: This article examines the European Union’s (EU) unsuccessful effort to develop a common strategy toward the South Caucasus and argues that the process nevertheless played a significant role in the evolution of the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) and emerging debates on a common strategy toward Russia. abstract: Alkali-activated materials (AAMs) are emerging sustainable binders with low carbon emissions and promising performance, but their practical application is limited by highly variable and system-dependent setting behaviour. abstract: Abstract Synthetic dyes represent a category of organic compounds that are highly stable, durable, and often resistant to degradation through natural processes. abstract: ABSTRACT This qualitative case study examined how the Center for Science and the Schools (CSATS), a university‐based intermediary organization, sustained partnerships between STEM researchers and K‐12 educators over 20 years (2004–2024). abstract: The study assessed the vulnerability of non-target species in Rastrineobola argentea fishery in Uganda’s artisanal capture fisheries in Lake Victoria. abstract: Lahaul Valley, Himachal Pradesh, is a high-altitude Himalayan region rich in medicinal plant diversity and traditional healthcare knowledge. abstract: Roadsides represent one of the most extensive anthropogenic networks globally, yet no integrative framework currently supports their systemic ecological characterisation and condition assessment. title: Cultural Displacement in English Literature: Dislocation, Hybridity, and the Politics of Belonging
abstract: Cultural displacement, the sense of being removed from one's home culture, language, or sense of place, has been among the most persistent concerns of English-language literature. This article examines how writers from the colonial period to the present have represented the experience of dislocation and the complex identities that follow from it. title: Sweetening the Empire: Sugar and Western-Style Confectionery in Modern Japan and Taiwan
abstract: This dissertation examines how Western-style confectionery such as caramel, chocolate, chewing gum, and other sweets became intertwined with Japan’s empire-building from the Meiji period (1868–1912) to the early postwar years. title: Mobilizing the seafood industry for climate action
abstract: Abstract Large seafood companies face climate-related risks across their operations, with substantial economic and financial implications. Nevertheless, corporate reporting remains limited, with nearly half of the 100 largest companies providing no climate-related disclosures. Reporting, which can be an indicator of action and priorities, has focused primarily on mitigation, with little attention to adaptation. We consider these gaps and propose four priorities to support capacity and pathways for climate-resilient seafood operations.

abstract: Après la départementalisation de la Guyane, de la Guadeloupe, de la Martinique et de La Réunion en 1946, des politiques distinctives s’imposent à leurs habitants. Yet archaeological evidence for past flood events and risk management remains under recognized and under utilized. This paper offers the first synthesis of material traces of past flooding and flood mitigation in medieval and post-medieval England (ca. 1200–1700 CE). abstract: This paper investigates the world views that underpin the naming of medicinal plants in Mankon and Moghamo, both Bamenda Grassfields languages of Cameroon. abstract: Plastics can fragment into micro and nano size particles by the action of environmental drivers in the ecosystem. abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how foraging behavior and diet influence individual reproductive success is a key interest in evolutionary ecology. abstract: Abstract Production of iron oxide magnetic nanoparticles using conventional chemical and physical methods presents sustainability challenges due to often high energy consumption and the use of hazardous reagents. Biological synthesis via magnetotactic bacteria (MTB) offers a greener alternative, but its environmental performance remains unexplored at scale. A novel intersection of American Southwest, Japanese, and Modernist styles, in the decades following the house’s renovation in 1949, O’Keeffe invited photographers into her home, and turned the house into an influential site for the production and distribution of images of a highly marketable desert asceticism. abstract: Abstract The Laurentian Great Lakes are undergoing rapid winter transformations, with profound implications for human societies. abstract: Ecotourism is widely promoted as a development pathway that can simultaneously finance forest conservation, reduce environmental pressure, and raise local incomes. abstract: Abstract When anthropogenic CO 2 emissions cease, global temperature does not stabilize immediately. abstract: Ongoing research on cetaceans is revealing species-specific traits that reflect adaptations to different environmental conditions. Short-finned pilot whales are no exception to this trend. This species exhibits a specific diving behaviour, characterized by short bursts of acceleration at great depths, which likely necessitates special hydrodynamic adaptations in their body structure. title: Performance of coir fibre-reinforced concrete incorporating crushed coconut shells as a partial replacement for coarse aggregates
abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable construction materials has intensified the exploration of agricultural waste as viable alternatives to conventional concrete constituents. This study investigates the durability performance of coir fibre-reinforced concrete incorporating crushed coconut shell aggregates (CCSA) as partial replacements for conventional coarse aggregates. An experimental research design was adopted in which concrete mixes with varying proportions of CCSA and coir fibres were prepared and evaluated. title: Description of two novel species, Flavobacterium suaedicola sp. nov. and Flavobacterium wonjuense sp. nov.
abstract: Two novel bacterial strains, designated HNIBRBA15423T and 25HG05S-40T, were isolated from the root of a halophyte and from a riverbank soil in the Republic of Korea, respectively. Cells of both strains were Gram-stain-negative, yellow-pigmented, non-motile, and rod-shaped. title: Morphological variation in Middle-Late Pleistocene stone points: a pan-African perspective
abstract: Stone points are central to defining the African Middle Stone Age (MSA), yet their morphological variability has rarely been quantitatively examined at a continental scale. Longstanding distinctions between ‘specific’ industries (e.g., Aterian, Still Bay, Howiesons Poort) and more geographically widespread ‘generic’ MSA assemblages remain unresolved, in part because typological definitions of these cultural entities were historically based on qualitative assessments of limited samples. title: Nonlinear Responses of Chemodiversity to Total Organic Carbon Content in Lake Sediments
abstract: Abstract Lake littoral sediments are critical carbon cycle hotspots that bridge terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. The chemodiversity of dissolved organic matter (DOM) in these sediments reflects ecosystem multifunctionality, particularly regarding carbon storage. However, the relationship between DOM chemodiversity and sediment total organic carbon (TOC) content, a critical quality‐quantity nexus, remains poorly understood. title: Evidence of Spatial Redistribution Without Detectable Genetic Change in the Greater Caribbean Manatee ( Trichechus manatus manatus ) Population of Puerto Rico
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the genetic diversity and spatial dynamics of small, isolated populations is essential for species conservation. The Greater Caribbean manatee ( Trichechus manatus manatus ) population in Puerto Rico is classified as endangered and has previously shown limited mitochondrial haplotype diversity. In this study, we analysed mitochondrial DNA control region sequences from 36 samples collected between 2010 and 2021 and compared them to 115 previously published sequences. title: New larval host plants for a few Indian butterflies (Lepidoptera: Rhopalocera)
abstract: The present communication reports new larval host plants for four Indian Butterflies. Based on field surveys and rearing experiments, Crateva adansonii DC., Lepidium didymum L., and Barleria cristata L. were established as larval host plants of Belenois aurota (Fabricius, 1793), Pieris canidia (Linnaeus, 1768), and Junonia orithya (Linnaeus, 1758) respectively; and Pongamia pinnata (L.) Pierre. and Bauhinia racemosa Lam. as larval host plants for Leptotes plinius (Fabricius, 1793).

title: Oviposition Inside Land Snail Shells (Caracolus carocolla) by the Salamanquita Común (Sphaerodactylus grandisquamis guarionex) in a Subtropical Moist Forest of the Puerto Rican Karst
abstract: Los cambios en el tamaño corporal afectan el comportamiento de los organismos y pueden facilitar nuevas interacciones ecológicas. En la herpetofauna, la miniaturización ha evolucionado de manera independiente en múltiples ocasiones; sin embargo, la historia natural de las especies miniaturizadas ha sido poco estudiada. Reportamos evidencia de oviposición por la salamanquita común (Sphaerodactylus grandisquamis guarionex) en las conchas vacías del caracol arbóreo puertorriqueño (Caracolus carocolla). title: Little effect of further aging on soil-weathered plastics
abstract: Abstract Plastic waste accumulates in soils, impacting structure, biota, and ecosystem functioning. Understanding the persistence and aging of plastics in soil is therefore important. However, aging occurs over timescales which cannot be covered in conventional experiments. Many studies therefore focus on simulated weathering of pristine polymers over short timescales, but these experiments do not consider potentially different aging behaviour after extended environmental exposure. title: Household Container Characteristics Associated with Mosquito Larval Presence in a Highland Community of Tana Toraja, Indonesia
abstract: Introduction: Dengue continues to pose a major mosquito-borne public health problem in tropical countries, including Indonesia, where household water containers frequently serve as habitats for mosquito larvae. However, studies examining household container characteristics associated with mosquito larval presence in highland communities remain limited. Methods: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted in Bombongan Urban Village, Makale District, Tana Toraja Regency, South Sulawesi, Indonesia. title: Hydration Product Evolution and Thermodynamic Modeling of Aluminosilicate Glasses in Supersulfated Cementitious Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT Supersulfated cement (SSC) is considered a promising low‐carbon cementitious material. However, the intrinsic characteristics of aluminosilicate glasses and their hydration behavior remain insufficiently understood. This study systematically investigates the hydration reactivity, phase evolution, and thermodynamic properties of synthesized aluminosilicate glasses with representative compositions in SSC systems. title: Transcriptomic insights into dichlorvos removal by Luteovulum azotoformans EBL0706 and its potential application for reducing pesticide residues on vegetables
abstract: Dichlorvos (DDVP), a widely used organophosphorus pesticide, poses considerable risks to environmental and food safety, making its effective removal an important objective. Microbial remediation offers a sustainable alternative to physicochemical treatments; however, the molecular responses associated with DDVP removal in phototrophic bacteria remain poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Hominin and faunal fossil collections are valuable scientific resources for investigating past populations, making it critically important to preserve these rare materials and prioritise minimally destructive methods. Electron spin resonance (ESR) dating of tooth enamel typically requires laboratory irradiation of powdered subsamples; however, the effects of this treatment on organic biomolecules, and therefore their potential reuse for amino acid geochronology (AAG), remain largely unknown. title: Mammalian lower jaw (Metatheria) from the Late Cretaceous Lance Formation (Wyoming, USA)
abstract: Abstract The public excavation and preparation of sixteen sediment blocks of a Late Cretaceous Lance Formation bonebed (Eastern Wyoming, USA) yielded a well-preserved mammalian lower jaw. title: Stress-resilient dryland cereals: A review on mechanisms of drought and salinity tolerance
abstract: Millets and sorghum, considered as dryland cereals are particularly known for their capability to grow in adverse environments. The tolerance mechanisms to major abiotic stressors remain fragmented across physiological, biochemical and molecular studies. This review aims to scrutinise and synthesise the major tolerance mechanisms that millets perform under drought and saline stress. title: The rapid spread of invasive smallmouth bass and chain pickerel and a changing Nova Scotia fishery
abstract: In the 1940s, Smallmouth Bass (Micropterus dolomieu) and Chain Pickerel (Esox niger) were confirmed in 14 lakes collectively in southwest Nova Scotia. By 2025, Smallmouth Bass had been documented in 340 lakes, while Chain Pickerel had been reported in 180 lakes, representing approximately 34% of the province’s lentic habitats. The initial spread of Smallmouth Bass was facilitated by government-sanctioned stocking; however, over the past 80 years, the range of both species has expanded due to natural migration and illegal introductions. title: Drivers of bird species turnover in the largest archipelago of China: Insights from zeta (ζ) diversity and multi‐site generalized dissimilarity modelling ( MS ‐ GDM )
abstract: Species turnover, the spatial dissimilarity in species composition, is a central concept in island biogeography and community ecology. Traditional pairwise beta diversity metrics are limited to two-site comparisons and cannot fully resolve the mechanisms driving turnover across multiple communities. Zeta (ζ) diversity overcomes this limitation by quantifying multi-site species sharing and capturing how both rare and widespread species contribute to species turnover along a continuum. abstract: Purpose – This study investigates the effects of work experience, technical competence, and navigation information systems on the safety and traffic-flow performance of ship pilotage operations in the Barito River, Indonesia, with job satisfaction examined as a mediating variable.Methodology – A quantitative explanatory research design was employed using a cross-sectional survey of 42 active ship pilots. title: Morphological abnormalities in erythrocytes as a preliminary indicator of genotoxicity of nano-tire rubber in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
abstract: Despite recent research interest in the toxic effects of tires, there is a lack of data on the genotoxicity of tire rubber particles in aquatic organisms. This study aimed to detect the cellular and genetic abnormalities affecting erythrocytes in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) exposed to tire rubber nanoparticles (TRNPs ≤1 μm) using a micronucleus assay. title: Revisitar o passado, regenerar o presente, reimaginar o futuro: a prática artística diaspórica de Mónica de Miranda
abstract: Aquest article aborda l’obra de l’artista afrodescendent Mónica de Miranda (nascuda a Portugal dos anys després de la Revolució dels Clavells) com un exemple paradigmàtic d’una generació jove d’artistes portuguesos que exploren la seva condició híbrida i diaspòrica en un país que tot just ara comença a enfrontar-se amb un passat i un llegat colonials. title: Flight Paths, Movement Distances, and Habitat Use of the Kolar Leaf-Nosed Bat (Hipposideros hypophyllus) and Sympatric Congeners in an Agricultural Landscape of Southern India
abstract: The Kolar leaf-nosed bat, Hipposideros hypophyllus, is a Critically Endangered species currently known from a single cave roost in the Kolar district of Karnataka, India. Despite its restricted distribution, little is known about its movement ecology or the habitats it uses for commuting and foraging. We investigated the flight paths, movement distances, and habitat use of H. hypophyllus, together with observations on the sympatric species H. speoris and H. durgadasi, in and around the Kolar Leaf-Nosed Bat Conservation Reserve.
