title: Structural basis for N-glycopeptide preference in an infant-derived Bifidobacterium bifidum PNGaseA
abstract: N-glycans are abundant nutrient sources for human gut bacteria, which deploy peptide: N-glycosidases to release them from glycoproteins. Breast milk is comprised of a high proportion of N-glycosylated bioactive proteins that can be accessed by infant colonic microbes. Here, we biochemically and structurally characterize a PNGaseA-family enzyme from infant-associated Bifidobacterium bifidum LMG13195. title: Effects of frying, grilling, and sous vide cooking on the nutritional composition and quality characteristics of fish balls
abstract: Comparative information on the effects of conventional and sous vide cooking methods on fish-ball quality remains limited. This study evaluated the effects of frying, grilling, and sous vide cooking on the proximate composition, fatty acid and free amino acid profiles, color, texture, and cooking characteristics of fish balls. Sous vide cooking maintained moisture content (62.14%) close to that of raw samples (63.41%), whereas frying (49.89%) and grilling (53.77%) caused significant moisture loss (P < 0.05). abstract: Abstract The transition from prebiotic chemistry to functional, self-replicating cellular architectures remains an unresolved milestone in origin-of-life research. While conventional paradigms focus heavily on transition-metal ferromagnetism, the role of quantum spin states and localized diamagnetic gradients in macromolecular organization is largely unexamined. title: Checklist of threatened plants of Sabah, Malaysian Borneo
abstract: Covering approximately 10% of Borneo’s land area, Sabah is one of the global hotspots for plant biodiversity, yet it faces increasing threats to its flora due to habitat loss and exploitation. This paper aims to compile a comprehensive checklist of threatened plant species in Sabah based on assessments published in the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species. A total of 660 vascular plant species from 73 families and 199 genera are classified as threatened and compiled in this checklist. abstract: The main purpose of this study was to determine the extent to which records management strategies influence accountability of the table water business in Akwa Ibom State. Two research questions and two null hypotheses were formulated to guide the study. The descriptive survey research design was used for the study. abstract: This article focuses on studying the history of the arrival and development of Islam in the Malay region and its impact on people's lives. This research applies a qualitative descriptive approach as well as a literature study method. Data was collected by reviewing scientific journal articles and historical literature that explain the process of Islam entering the region, trade networks, the role of scholars, Malay kingdoms, and socio-cultural changes. title: Roost site characteristics and habitat associations of bats (Mammalia: Chiroptera) in Kamrup District, Assam, India
abstract: Chiroptera play vital ecological roles as pollinators, seed dispersers, and insect population regulators; however, information on their roost site requirements remains limited in many parts of northeastern India. The present study examined roost site characteristics and habitat associations of Chiroptera in Kamrup District, Assam, India. title: Living the American Dream: Aasta Hansteen’s Transnational Feminist Experience
abstract: This article discusses the Norwegian feminist pioneer and emigrant to the United States, Aasta Hansteen. Hansteen has been studied by many, but her encounters with American feminism and progressive circles have so far received little attention. I argue that her experience as an immigrant made it possible for her to meet American feminists and live out her feminist dream as a free individual. Through her writing, she communicated her experiences and views to Norwegians and Americans on both sides of the Atlantic. title: Cue for dominance? Visuo-chemical communication in males of Sambar Rusa unicolor in subtropical forests of India
abstract: Olfactory signalling among mammals remains understudied, particularly in ungulates. This study documents “preaching,” an olfactory communication behaviour exhibited by male Sambar Deer Rusa unicolor, that involves an upright posture, rubbing of the pre-orbital gland, and sniffing tree bases. Observations were made using camera traps in the Haridwar Range of Rajaji Tiger Reserve, Uttarakhand, India. Six bucks over three years old were observed preaching from February 2024 to March 2024. title: Spasticity in Multiple Sclerosis: 2026 Expert Consensus
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neuroinflammatory disease that significantly impairs quality of life. Spasticity is one of the most frequent and highly disabling features of MS, often accompanied by cramps, pain, bladder dysfunction, sleep disturbances, fatigue, and tremor. Recently, the concept of 'spasticity-plus syndrome' (SPS) has emerged to reflect the interplay among these symptoms. title: Metazoan diversification characterized by elevated rates of evolution during the middle Ediacaran to earliest Cambrian
abstract: To test causal hypotheses for the emergence of animal body plans, we analyze rates of molecular and phenotypic evolution across Opisthokonta, focusing on divergences within the Tonian-Ordovician interval. title: “To a cupped hand’s size”: Reading Poetics of Scale in Edith Tiempo’s Poetry
abstract: Edith Cutaran Lopez-Tiempo’s body of work, alongside her stature as Philippine National Artist for Literature, has generated substantial scholarship on the fertile imaginaries and intersections of formalist poetics, the institutionalization of the writing workshop, and Philippine poetry in English. Building on these contributions, I turn instead to Tiempo’s negotiation of self-fashioning, memory work, and imaginative practice as a way of articulating questions of scale in her oeuvre. abstract: This paper explores a re-reading of the ‘region’ that appears in National Artist Bienvenido Lumbera’s advocacy for valuing regional literature as a foundation of a strong national literature. His discourse against the othering of the regional literature as ‘vernacular’ is encapsuled in the philosophy of his works: that the region represents a precise, immediate worldview, while the national offers a wider, encompassing perspective of the Filipinos (Lumbera 156). title: The alignment of sacred forests with the concept of other effective area-based conservation measures
abstract: Abstract Sacred natural sites, while not always formally recognised as protected areas, can protect biodiversity via the customs and practices that prohibit exploitation for spiritual reasons. As such, these sites may align with the concept of other effective area-based conservation measures (OECMs), which recognise places that protect biodiversity outside formal protected areas. title: Iberian copper and Bronze Age Europe: Late Bronze Age mining and supply at Las Minillas (Badajoz, Spain)
abstract: Despite abundant copper deposits, the deep history of copper mining in Iberia has not been as extensively studied as in other European ore-rich areas. Here, the authors present new radiocarbon dates that demonstrate Late Bronze Age copper mining at Las Minillas, near Granja de Torrehermosa (southern Spain). title: Precipitation Probability Distribution, Percent Runoff, and Trend Analysis for 25 Reservoir Basins in Texas from 1980–2019
abstract: This study analyzed precipitation probability distributions, percent runoff, and trends in precipitation from 1980 to 2019 in the Brazos, Colorado, Guadalupe, Neches, Red, and Trinity river basins in Texas for 25 U.S. Army Corps of Engineers reservoirs and 15 other reservoirs for the purpose of flood risk and water-resource management. title: Methodological Concerns and Interpretation of Archaeometric Data in Recent Provenance Claims Concerning the Riace Bronzes
abstract: ABSTRACT Recent claims proposing a Syracusan provenance for the Riace Bronzes rely on selective petrographic, geochemical, and taphonomic evidence that raises crucial methodological questions. This paper critically reassesses the analytical premises and inferential logic underlying these claims, showing that they bypass established protocols in ceramic and sediment provenance studies, lack statistically meaningful reference groups, and raise concerns on the interpretation of archaeometric, radiocarbon, and lead isotope data. abstract: ABSTRACT Continental roots are the ultimate sources for many giant metal deposits including rare‐earth elements (REEs). Co‐existing carbonatites and other COH‐rich magmatic rocks like kimberlites and lamproites in many polymetallic mineralisation areas likely represent different branches of similar COH‐rich mantle melt precursors. title: Quantifying Carbon Storage in Black Ash Wetlands Following Emerald Ash Borer and Forest Management
abstract: Abstract The impacts of non-native Emerald Ash Borer (EAB) are likely to be most severe in black ash wetlands, possibly requiring preemptive forest management to maintain ecosystem functions such as carbon storage. We used a silvicultural experiment in northern Minnesota to evaluate how EAB-induced mortality and preemptive management affect total ecosystem carbon storage and the distribution of carbon among ecosystem pools. title: New elevational limits of Himalayan mammals in eastern Sikkim, India
abstract: The eastern Himalaya is recognised as one of the most important biodiversity hotspots in the world. title: Plant taxonomic diversity of Barunei Hill, Eastern Ghats, India
abstract: The present study on Barunei Hill documented 149 plant species. Out of 149, native species and non-native species are 125 and 24, respectively. Native species belong to 112 genera and 50 families at the same time non-native species represent 23 genera and 15 families. Of the 125 native species, 43 are trees, 37 herbs, 29 shrubs, and 16 lianas/twiners/climbers. abstract: Abstract Building on long-standing hypotheses of a hurricane-fire interaction, this study assesses empirical evidence for hurricane-driven increases in wildfire activity along the Gulf Coast of the United States. title: Climate change impacts on biodiversity and ecosystem-based adaptation mechanisms in Azerbaijan
abstract: Climate change is altering ecosystems, species distributions and the services that support human well-being, while habitat loss and unsustainable resource use intensify ecological vulnerability. This narrative review examines the major pathways through which warming, hydrological change and extreme events affect biodiversity and identifies adaptation mechanisms relevant to Azerbaijan. The paper synthesizes authoritative global assessments, peer-reviewed literature and selected national policy documents, with emphasis on forests, mountain ecosystems, freshwater habitats, agricultural landscapes
journal: Journal of Green Economy and Optimization Research

title: Development of CaO/Al2O3 bifunctional catalyst for biodiesel production from jatropha oil: optimization and kinetic study
abstract: Biodiesel production from non-edible Jatropha curcas oil, which have high free fatty acid (FFA) content, presents technical challenges due to soap formation during conventional base-catalyzed transesterification. This often necessitates a costly and time-consuming acid pretreatment. To address this, the study developed a bifunctional heterogeneous calcium-/aluminum oxide (CaO/Al 2 O 3 ) catalyst synthesized from calcined snail shells (SS) and impregnated with alumina. The catalyst enables direct transesterification of high-FFA jatropha oil, thereby simplifying the process and reducing wastage.

abstract: BACKGROUND: Ningbo experienced a local dengue outbreak in 2018-2019, followed by the implementation and relaxation of COVID-19 pandemic interventions. METHODS: We analyzed routine dengue cases and mosquito surveillance data from 2017 to 2024, using descriptive analyses to assess the epidemiological characteristics, and a mathematical model was developed to estimate the basic reproduction number (R0). title: Green hydrogen and alternative fuels for climate mitigation: a cross-sectoral techno-economic and deployment perspective
abstract: Green hydrogen and its low-carbon derivatives are increasingly considered for decarbonising sectors in which direct electrification is technically constrained or cannot replace a required molecular feedstock. This review examines the technical, techno-economic, environmental, infrastructure, and deployment conditions that determine where green hydrogen and hydrogen-derived alternative fuels can provide effective climate-mitigation pathways across major end-use sectors. abstract: The Clifton Formation hosts two thin, uneconomic Middle Pennsylvanian coals associated with erect, lycopod-cast forests exposed along the southern shore of Chaleur Bay, New Brunswick, Canada. The study focuses on the depositional setting of coal and mudrock deposits, mudrock (B/Ga) geochemistry, coal geochemistry and petrography, and the palynology of the peat forest and assemblages recovered from clastic paleosols associated with beds entombing standing trees. Here, we report a strategy that co-assembles a designed protease-inhibitory peptide amphiphile (PA) with patient-derived wound fluid (WF) to reconstruct the complete biofilm life cycle in vitro. abstract: Abstract This study focuses on the region near the Mendocino Triple Junction (MTJ), where the Gorda slab geometry is not well constrained in terms of its depth and configuration. abstract: This study aimed to develop and validate the “SCSCE Model” (Sala Noi Model), an interdisciplinary local learning management framework using Lanna traditional crafts to foster community innovators. abstract: The effects of increasing dietary inclusion levels of olive pomace (OP) on growth performance, zootechnical indices, body composition, energy metabolism, and lipid peroxidation were evaluated in juvenile Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ). Five experimental diets, formulated to be isoproteic (37% crude protein) and isolipidic (9% lipids), included 0% (OP 0 ), 5% (OP 5 ), 10% (OP 10 ), 15% (OP 15 ), and 20% (OP 20 ) OP. title: 40-kyr of environmental history of the southeastern sector of paleolake Cuitzeo, central-western Mexico: Insights from abiotic and biotic proxies
abstract: We present a multiproxy reconstruction of environmental changes recorded in the southeastern sector of Lake Cuitzeo (central-western Mexico) over the last ∼40 kyr. Our study integrates abiotic (major-element geochemistry, rock-magnetic parameters, pH, and electrical conductivity) and biotic proxies (diatoms and pollen) from a ∼10 m-long sedimentary core (Cz-07). title: Beyond Rivalry: Economic Diplomacy and Managed Interdependence between Saudi Arabia and Iran
abstract: This comprehensive research paper examines the potential of economic diplomacy and regulated interdependence to convert the Saudi-Iranian enmity from destructive confrontation into sustainable coexistence. Illustration on contemporary studies from academic sources and leading research institutions, the article argues that, despite the prominence of sectarian politics, it does not inevitably determine the results of rivalries. title: Climate change impacts of recurring office fit-outs: a prospective life cycle assessment of circular economy-based improvements
abstract: Abstract Purpose Buildings with long service life are associated with recurring greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions arising from repeated activities such as refurbishments over time, which can significantly contribute to the cumulative climate change impact. In particular, multi-tenant office buildings, where fit-outs typically occur every 2–10 years, contribute approximately a quarter of GHG emissions over the building service life. This study applies prospective LCA (pLCA) to quantify the climate change impact over the service life of a tenanted office building and assesses the effect of circular
journal: The International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment

title: Attending to change: Dynamic drafting as creative practice research in contemporary retellings of medieval Icelandic literature
abstract: This article discusses the role of drafting as an iterative, dynamic aspect of creative writing that can form a component of practice-led methods with its own questions and research contributions. The article reflects on the author’s experiences of field work undertaken in Iceland during the composition of a creative response to a medieval Icelandic saga. It then examines how substantial revisions that occur during the life of a project can form the basis for critical reflections that are, in turn, related to earlier scholarship about the source text. A major shift occurred in the author’s cre

title: El discurso escondido de las Galápagos: Una relectura de The Encantadas, or Enchanted Isles de Herman Melville
abstract: This article examines the source of a counternarrative on Latin American and Ecuadorian historiography, by reinterpreting the seventh story of Herman Melville's The Encantadas (1856). If one of Melville's interests is his inability to accept or reject the Emersonianism, it is useful to identify the specificity of his criticism of transcendental philosophy by looking at his short stories. His stories allowed the author of Moby Dick to recreate a model of resistance based on the representation of the Galapagos, a crucial space for modernity in Western thought.

title: Mercury contamination impairs the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis of a neotropical caiman
abstract: The capacity to regulate corticosterone release following a stressful event is an essential component of the physiological flexibility required to maintain homeostasis and ensure adaptive responses to environmental change. We show that wild smooth-fronted caimans with elevated blood mercury (Hg) concentrations exhibited reduced peak corticosterone levels during standardized stress tests, indicating a dampened maximal stress response. Hg blood concentrations were negatively correlated with corticosterone responsiveness, suggesting impairment of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis function. Thes

title: Interacting Effects of Climate and Land Use on Biodiversity: A Guide to What They Are and Why They Matter
abstract: ABSTRACT Problem Climate and land‐use change are two key drivers of biodiversity change. Their widespread effects on species and communities have prompted fears that interactions between the two drivers could cause severe biodiversity loss. title: Biomimicry-informed deconstruction of the cognitive system for Sino–Western hybrid architecture: A case study of Lushan UNESCO Global Geopark
abstract: Sino–Western hybrid architecture serves as a medium for cross-cultural exchange; however, its preservation faces two major challenges: unclear conservation standards and differing perceptions of cultural value. The hybrid architectural forms at Lushan developed in response to local terrain and climate, but the difficulty in defining authenticity for such buildings complicates conservation efforts. This study examines the villa cluster in Guling town, Lushan, employing biomimicry not as a design methodology but as an analytical framework to evaluate hybrid heritage through characteristics of en
journal: Journal of Chinese Architecture and Urbanism
institutions: Nanchang Business College of Jiangxi Agricultural University

title: Recent Decline in Global Atmospheric COS Driven by Reduced Anthropogenic CS 2 Emissions
abstract: Abstract Carbonyl sulfide (COS) is an atmospheric tracer for carbon cycle processes. Global observations reveal a rapid decline in COS concentrations beginning in 2016, but the cause of this decline is unknown. Here we show that this decrease is unexpected. Previous COS trends followed rayon production which emits CS 2 , a COS precursor. However, the recent COS decline coincides with increasing rayon output. Multiple independent observing systems, including NOAA's global flask network and NDACC FTIR retrievals, show a consistent tropospheric COS trend of −1.2 ± 0.1% yr −1 from 2016 to 2022, ev
institutions: NSF National Center for Atmospheric Research

title: Cholera in Sub-Saharan Africa: From the Biology of Vibrio Cholerae to the Challenges of Surveillance, with a Focus on the Democratic Republic of the Congo
abstract: Cholera remains a major public health problem in sub-Saharan Africa, where limited water and sanitation, population displacement, conflict and weak health systems sustain recurrent epidemics. Interpreting its epidemiology requires linking the biology of Vibrio cholerae, antimicrobial resistance, and the performance of surveillance and diagnosis. title: Structural Resilience and Institutional Response: An Empirical Study of Economic Recovery Pathways in UK Cities Following the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: The study empirically examines city-level data in the UK for 2019-2023, systematically accounting for the spatial divergence and the drivers of it along three main lines of inquiry: the recovery of incomes, the recovery of welfare spending, and the recovery of regional inequality following the COVID-19 pandemic, using a fixed-effects panel model approach. The results show a strong “Matthew Effect” in the recovery after the pandemic. Higher-skilled, industrial and institutional cities like metros and tech cities like Cambridge had a stronger performance regarding income and welfare security, ev
journal: Asia Pacific Economic and Management Review

title: Asymmetric Warfare in the Iran–USA Conflict: Strategies and Security Implications
abstract: The clash between the Islamic Republic of Iran and the United States is one of the most obvious contemporary examples of asymmetric warfare: a regional power (IR) vs. a global military power opponent (USA) that the IR cannot match on an even footing. This article will explore how Iran has turned its structural disadvantage into strategic advantage and how the United States has responded in terms of its posture to the war between Israel and Iran, which began in June 2025 and culminated in the US–Israeli campaign of 28 February 2026. title: Stability of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi-protist interaction networks strengthens vegetation-soil quality in plantations
abstract: Abstract Improving plantation quality is a key strategy for mitigating climate change. However, the mechanisms by which microbial diversity and interactions jointly affect ecosystem quality remain poorly understood. Here, we evaluated how arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) and protistan consumer diversity and interactions were related to soil (SQI) and vegetation (VQI) quality across 108 Pinus tabuliformis and Ulmus pumila plantation plots during spring and autumn. title: Isolation and Screening of Endophytic Fungi from Nyctanthes arbor-tristis and Eucalyptus sp. for Lipolytic Activity and Lipid Accumulation Potential
abstract: Medicinal plants host a diverse range of endophytic fungi. These fungi are a great source of valuable lipids and hydrolytic enzymes. The objective of this investigation was to isolate endophytic fungi from the bark of Nyctanthes arbor-tristis and Eucalyptus sp. from Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, India and to screen them for lipolytic activity and to assess their lipid accumulation potential. In total, 13 fungal isolates were recovered on PDA supplemented with chloramphenicol and were examined for their lipase activity through tributyrin and tween 80 agar media. title: Extreme light rare earth element enrichment in carbonatite-related rare earth element deposits driven by coupled immiscibility, fractional crystallization, and melt–wall rock metasomatism
abstract: Carbonatite-related rare earth elements (REE) deposits are the primary global source of light rare earth elements (LREE) resources. All known giant to supergiant carbonatite-related REE deposits show extreme LREE enrichment and relative heavy rare earth elements (HREE) depletion; however, the mechanism of LREE/HREE fractionation during the formation, evolution, and mineralization of carbonatitic magmas remains unclear. abstract: Taking into account the threat of spread of new dangerous pathogens (such as SARS-CoV-2) and natural disasters often accompanied by infectious disease, there is a pressing need to find and choose, basing on experimental investigations, effective combinations of disinfectant substances approved for the surface disinfection in the presence of people. The paper describes the results of experimental microbiological studies on the decontamination of smooth surfaces. title: Temporal trends in age at menarche among Sri Lankan girls: A review of published evidence (1950–2009)
abstract: Mean age at menarche (MAM) is a sensitive biological indicator of childhood nutrition and broader socio-economic conditions of a population, and its decline over time is well documented in developed countries. Several studies have been conducted in Sri Lanka since 1950 to estimate the MAM in different regions, ethnic groups and socio-economic strata, but the published evidence has not previously been collated. PubMed, Google Scholar, ResearchGate and the Sri Lanka Journals Online platform were searched and primary Sri Lankan publications reporting MAM were retrieved for the period 1950 to 2009
journal: Sri Lanka Journal of Obstetrics and Gynaecology

title: A mid‐Cretaceous monocot flower from the Dakota Sandstone of Kansas and its potential implications for the fossil record of palms
abstract: PREMISE: Although the megafossil flora of the upper Albian-lower Cenomanian Dakota Formation in Kansas is well known for angiosperms, monocots have not been reported previously. METHODS: A mesofossil flower was discovered by X-ray analysis of a specimen collected more than a century ago from the Dakota Sandstone of central Kansas. A mid-Cretaceous (ca. 100 Ma) age is inferred from its stratigraphic provenance close to the Albian-Cenomanian boundary. title: Sustainability-Oriented School Leadership, Environmental Management Practices, and Climate Resilience Among School Heads in Sapa-Sapa I District, Tawi-Tawi: Basis for a Sustainable School Governance Framework
abstract: This study examined sustainability-oriented school leadership, environmental management practices, and climate resilience among selected school heads in Sapa-Sapa I District, Tawi-Tawi, as a basis for developing a Sustainable School Governance Framework. Anchored in the Whole-Institution Approach to Education for Sustainable Development, Sustainable Educational Leadership, and Organizational Climate Resilience, the study employed a descriptive-correlational design using a structured five-point Likert-scale questionnaire. Descriptive statistics and Kendall's tau-b correlation were applied to 12

title: Combining enhanced basalt weathering with soda saline soil: A novel CO₂ mineralisation strategy
abstract: Enhanced rock weathering in saline–alkaline soils can couple CO₂ mineralisation with reclamation of salt-affected land. title: Retrieval of ultraviolet aerosol absorption from radiation measurements in young wildfire plumes
abstract: Abstract. Aerosols play an important role for atmospheric radiative transfer in biomass burning (BB) plumes, where they control photochemistry, direct radiative forcing, and radiation-induced atmospheric dynamics. The optical properties of BB aerosol, however, remain poorly constrained, with respect to their absorptive properties at ultraviolet and visible wavelengths. In-situ observations show considerable variability due to heterogeneity in BB plumes, and different measurement methods do not agree with each other. title: Kofumicins A−D, Antibacterial Glycosylated Linear Polyene Polyketides from Kutzneria kofuensis , Identified via Bacterial Activity Metabolomics
abstract: Abstract Four previously unreported glycosylated linear polyene polyketides, kofumicins A−D (1−4), were isolated from Kutzneria kofuensisNRRL 24061 and were found to inhibit Staphylococcus aureus growth. The kofumicins were identified from the crude extract using a bacterial activity metabolomics-guided approach, which employs split-flow HPLC-UV/MS to generate microtiter plate arrays enabling dereplication and bioactivity assessment prior to isolation. title: Riqueza y distribución de Asteraceae en la Península de Yucatán, México
abstract: Antecedentes: La diversidad alfa cuantifica la biodiversidad a escala local e incluye los componentes taxonómicos y filogenéticos. title: Automatic astrometric calibration of low-cost all-sky cameras
abstract: All-sky cameras support weather monitoring, amateur astronomy, fireball and space-debris detection, and measurements of light pollution. These applications require reliable astrometric calibration despite imperfect camera alignment and variable observing conditions. We present an open-source procedure that combines a compact fisheye model, an exact rotation to account for camera tilt, and automatic star matching. title: Framing Peninsular Crypto‐Jews as Part of the Sephardic Diaspora
abstract: ABSTRACT When we talk about the Sephardic diaspora, we often talk about Iberian conversos who leave the Peninsula, supposedly to live openly as Jews in places like Algiers, Venice, Amsterdam or the Ottoman Empire. But what about those conversos who continued to identify in some way as Jews but who remained in Spain and Portugal? To what extent can we talk about them as part of the Sephardic diaspora as we understand it today? title: Economic Value of Bukittinggi City Regional Public Library: Travel Cost Approach and Contingency Valuation
abstract: Regional public libraries deliver services without charging admission, making their benefits difficult to observe in local budget accounts. This study estimated the economic value of the Bukittinggi City Regional Public Library and examined correlates of annual visit frequency and willingness to pay (WTP) for voluntary contributions. title: Development of an Instrument to Assess Service Quality and Resource Adequacy in Midwifery Laboratories
abstract: Background: Midwifery laboratories are essential for developing clinical competencies, yet service quality and resource adequacy are frequently assessed separately. Objectives: This study aimed to develop and internally evaluate an integrated instrument for assessing midwifery laboratory quality. Methods: Five experts validated the instrument, and 446 midwifery students with laboratory experience completed a 44 item questionnaire. title: Two Millennia of Landscape Transformation in the Siegerland (Western Germany) as Evidenced by Pollen, Lipid Biomarkers and Archaeological Record
abstract: The Siegerland (W-Germany) exhibits distinct phases of intensive metallurgy during the Iron Age (2nd – 1st centuries BC) and Middle Ages (9th – 16th centuries AD) that coincide with landscape transformations and shifts in local subsistence economies. Multi-proxy analyses of alluvial sediments – pollen, non-pollen palynomorphs, coprophilous fungal spores, and lipid biomarkers – provide insights into these land use changes. title: Adaptive Thermal Comfort Assessment in Mixed-Mode Office Buildings Under Current and Future Sub-Saharan Tropical Hot and Dry Climate Scenarios
abstract: Mixed-mode offices in sub-Saharan hot semi-arid climates face growing thermal stress, yet long-term evidence remains scarce. This study addresses this gap via a stress-test framework (RCP8.5) applied to a compressed earth bricks office in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. A calibrated DesignBuilder/EnergyPlus model evaluated four strategies—free-running (FR), natural ventilation (NV), mixed-mode (MM), and fully air-conditioned (AC)—under current (2023) and future horizons (2030, 2060, 2090). title: Radiocarbon reveals depleted carbon in attached benthic assemblages of persistent pools in a tropical non-perennial river
abstract: Abstract Radiocarbon-depleted ("old") carbon can be bioavailable in aquatic ecosystems, but its role in persistent-pool food webs of non-perennial rivers is largely unknown. We measured hydrochemistry, environmental tracers and carbon isotopes in water and biota from four main-channel pools and one floodplain spring along the Martuwarra Fitzroy River, Western Australia, over two dry seasons. title: “What Roles for Women?”: Gendering the New International Economic Order at the UN Regional Economic Commission for Africa
abstract: ABSTRACT The 1974 declaration of the New International Economic Order (NIEO), which came just ahead of the UN's International Women's Year (IWY) in 1975, attempted a major renegotiation of global inequality without reference to gender. Through the rest of the 1970s, women at the African Training and Research Centre for Women (ATRCW) in Addis Ababa, itself an initiative of the IWY, leveraged the power of the NIEO to support their undervalued work on African women's economic lives. title: Helminth Fauna of the Caucasian Toad, Bufo verrucosissimus (Pallas, 1814) (Amphibia: Bufonidae), Collected from Türkiye
abstract: This study presents a helminthological investigation of 35 individuals (13♀♀ and 22♂♂) of the Caucasian toad, Bufo verrucosissimus (Pallas, 1814), collected from Artvin and Mersin provinces in Türkiye during 2024–2025. abstract: This study examined the modernisation efforts of the Dutch East Indies colonial government through the operation of the Semarang-Cirebon railway line under the Semarang-Cheribon Stoomtram Maatschappij (SCS) from 1895 until 1910. The method used was the historical method with the socioeconomic approach. title: Dimming the fire of life: Cocooned aestivating frogs as a model of intrinsic metabolic depression
abstract: Abstract Metabolic depression occurs across a diverse array of invertebrate and vertebrate animals during aestivation (summer dormancy). abstract: Background Heavy metals such as copper are known water pollutants that can be extremely harmful to the environment and pose serious risks to human health and aquatic organisms. title: Climate and agrochemical price shocks in Vietnamese agriculture: A computable general equilibrium analysis of compound vulnerabilities and policy responses
abstract: Viet Nam ranks among the world’s five most climate-vulnerable nations, with agriculture contributing 13% of GDP and employing 28% of the labor force. Global agrochemical supply chain disruptions have tripled fertilizer prices, constraining farmers’ adaptive capacity precisely when climate-induced productivity losses are mounting. title: Do Protected Areas Affect the Income Levels in Remote Regions? Evidence from Italian Inner Areas
abstract: Abstract The economic impact of protected areas (PAs) on local development remains a debated topic in regional economics, particularly in peripheral regions facing demographic and economic decline. While protected areas provide essential ecological benefits, their effects on local economies remain debated, with concerns about land-use restrictions potentially limiting economic opportunities alongside potential gains from tourism and ecosystem services. title: Post-operative pain following single-visit endodontic treatment using sodium hypochlorite versus chlorhexidine as intracanal disinfectants: An in vivo study
abstract: Post-operative pain after single visit root canal treatment remains a common clinical challenge and the optimal irrigant for balancing pain control with antimicrobial efficacy is uncertain. Therefore, it is of interest to compare the post-operative pain and antibacterial efficacy of 3% sodium hypochlorite and 2% chlorhexidine in 80 patients undergoing single-visit endodontic treatment. title: The Efficacy of Instructional Tool in Reading Skills on Foundational Literacy for Basic Graders
abstract: This study examined the reading skills of Grade 3 learners and their relationship with academic performance in English in selected public elementary schools in the Bantayan District, Schools Division of Cebu Province, during School Year 2026–2027. Specifically, it assessed learners’ proficiency in phonemic awareness, phonics, text recognition, vocabulary, and comprehension; described the profiles of the teacher and learner respondents; and determined whether a significant relationship existed between reading skills and academic performance in English. abstract: Sick Building Syndrome (SBS) is a medical condition characterized by non-specific symptoms such as eye, nose, throat irritation, headache, fatigue, dizziness and poor concentration experienced by occupants of a building, which improve after vacating the building. SBS is caused by chemical, biological, physical, psychological and environmental pollutants. In educational settings, SBS affects teachers and students' performance, attention and behaviour. This study focuses on the term emission , central to environmental discourse, particularly in international legislation. abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how internal (corporate) and external (country‐level) governance mechanisms jointly influence corporate biodiversity disclosure under SDG 15 (CBD_SDG15) in emerging Asian economies. Drawing on stakeholder theory and institutional theory, the study conceptualises internal and external governance as complementary governance mechanisms operating across organisational and national levels. title: Finding Third ways? The dynamics of settlement on customary land conflict In Papua, Indonesia
abstract: This article examines alternative approaches to the resolution of customary land conflicts in Papua, which emerge as both private and communal disputes and are continually shaped by competing narratives of development. The study employs a constructivist approach, which views customary land not merely as a legal or economic asset but as a socially constructed space whose meaning is negotiated through interaction, authority relations, and historical experience. abstract: This review explores the nutritional implications of plant-based diets, including veganism and vegetarianism. Plant-based diets offer numerous health benefits, providing essential nutrients like vitamins, minerals, and macronutrients. However, exclusive plant-based diets may lead to potential deficiencies in protein, calcium, vitamin D, vitamin B12, zinc, and iron. title: Hipparionine Fossils From A New Locality Gazlope, Sakhi Sarwar, Sulaiman Range, South Punjab, Pakistan
abstract: ABSTRACT Hipparionine fossils from the newly explored Gazlope locality of the Sulaiman Range, Sakhi Sarwar, District Dera Ghazi Khan, South Punjab, are reported and described in detail. The recovered material comprises isolated upper and lower premolars and molars. abstract: Despite the overwhelming scientific consensus on anthropogenic climate change, public skepticism and motivational deficits persist. abstract: Literacy is fundamentally an act of meaning-making that requires bridging micro-level linguistic choices with macro-level text structures across genres. title: Toward the Fall of Cirebon: Political Crisis and the Negotiation of Protection in Cirebon–VOC Diplomatic Correspondence, 1680
abstract: This article examines Cirebon’s incorporation into the hegemony of the Dutch East India Company (Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie, VOC) in the period leading up to the Batavia–Cirebon Treaty of 7 January 1681. It takes as its primary sources the diplomatic correspondence exchanged between the rulers of Cirebon and the VOC in December 1680 to reconstruct the political dynamics preceding the treaty. abstract: Drymarchon corais is a generalist species, with a diet that includes amphibians, lizards, amphisbaenians, other snakes, eggs, birds, and small mammals. On 9 August 2025 we recorded an adult D. corais preying on a juvenile Boa constrictor. abstract: E-commerce has become a major force driving industrial upgrading, urban expansion, and urban–rural integration. Yet it remains unclear whether classical theories of urban land expansion can adequately explain the digital era, particularly in terms of when and at what scale E-commerce begins to reshape urban space in traditional manufacturing cities. abstract: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) remain the leading cause of global mortality, with hypertension as a key modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular diseases. Nutritional status is considered an important determinant of hypertension due to its association with energy balance, dietary patterns, and metabolic conditions. abstract: The growing population is responsible for energy consumption all over the world resulting in the depletion of the fossil fuel reservoir. In recent decades out of many techniques, Microbial fuel cell (MFC) have served as three stop solution for electricity production, reducing global warming, producing value added products while simultaneously remediating wastewater. abstract: This study aimed to identify and compare the stylistic characteristics of Gandai dance across North Bengkulu, Mukomuko, and Silaut, Indonesia. A qualitative descriptive-comparative approach was employed. Data were collected through observations, interviews, and documentation. abstract: After a recollection of some of my encounters with Gilles Brassard, on the occasion of his 70th birthday I present, first, a new idea on the creation of new information at a limited rate. abstract: Abstract Sequential flower color change after anthesis is a distinctive trait with both adaptive significance and ornamental value; however, its molecular basis remains poorly understood. In ‘Mutabilis’ rose, petals undergo a light-dependent color transition involving coordinated remodeling of anthocyanin and carotenoid metabolism. title: The Names of the Jinn Kings of Java: An Alternative Approach to Treating Demonic Possession
abstract: One of the cultural traditions in the Nusantara is knowing the names of the spirit kings of Java, found in the Kidungan literature attributed to Sunan Kalijaga, though few truly understand its philosophical depth. Using a phenomenological approach, this study examines its application for spiritual disturbances, particularly in treating spirit possession where literal interpretations often dominate. abstract: Most Western Balkans (WB) economies heavily rely on lignite for electricity production, contributing to some of Europe’s most severe air pollution levels. Consequently, electricity costs are likely to rise as carbon pricing becomes operational, with the potential additional risk of interfering in the European Union (EU) accession process if national emission ceilings are not met. abstract: ABSTRACT Aim There is an urgent need to identify sustainable development pathways promoting biodiversity recovery. Biodiversity indicators summarising this complexity vary in their sensitivity to different forms of biodiversity change, but the extent to which indicator choice affects estimated responses to drivers such as land‐use change is currently unclear. abstract: Abstract Most disaster risk assessments use asset damages as their central metric, often neglecting distributional impacts and affected people’s coping and recovery capacity. This study aimed to identify parasite taxa and determine their prevalence and mean intensity in cultured freshwater fish in Tarakan City, North Kalimantan, Indonesia. The study was conducted in May 2026 at the Fisheries Biology Laboratory, Borneo Tarakan University. It varies strongly across time and space, with tropical butterflies experiencing temperatures close to their thermal limits. Climate change with more frequent heat waves may push species closer to these limits. Butterflies are known to thermoregulate, which is influenced by their morphology and behaviour. abstract: Urban trees are important components of green infrastructure, contributing to biodiversity conservation, climate regulation, and carbon storage. Quantifying the composition, structure, and carbon storage capacity of urban tree communities is therefore important for sustainable urban planning and climate change mitigation. This study evaluated species composition, diversity, structural characteristics, biomass, carbon storage, and the economic value of stored carbon in 15 Temmuz National Garden, Kahramanmaraş, Türkiye. abstract: Food systems are currently undergoing a transformation focused on the cultivation of alternative proteins such as fungal meat and microalgae to enhance sustainability. Using a comparative case-study analysis, this paper assesses this change using Sam Grant’s (2017) regenerative lens to understand how alternative proteins benefit the environments they are cultivated in. abstract: Flooding affects an estimated 70% of the global poor, highlighting the need to understand how disaster risk reduction investments may contribute to poverty and inequality reduction. Despite evidence of their potential socio-economic benefits, flood protection investments (FPIs) remained questioned as poverty reduction tools relative to conventional policies, largely due to lack of comparative studies in flood-prone rural contexts. abstract: Gender disparity in higher education is primarily rooted in unequal access to power, which is often a result of limited education and low income. An uneducated woman is less able to advocate for herself or her children, continuing cycles of inequality. This study explores gender inequality in higher education through a case study of Bagmati Municipality in the Sarlahi District of Nepal. abstract: Environmental microbiomes are sources of diverse antibiotic resistance determinants that can be mobilized and transferred to human pathogens under a selection pressure from antibiotics. Hospital sewers contain more antibiotics than most environments and are thus increasingly recognised as potential arenas for resistance evolution. At the time, Lumbera had just earned his PhD from Indiana University as a Fulbright scholar. Naturally, his colonial education and aesthetic preference shaped his approach as a critic and scholar. abstract: Despite the Mambilla Plateau in Taraba State having favourable conditions for Arabica coffee cultivation, including a cool climate, high altitude and fertile volcanic soils, coffee remains an underutilised cash crop in Nigeria. abstract: Probiotics and yeast cell wall extracts are used in aquaculture feeds, although their effects on growth performance and intestinal health may vary depending on the supplement and fish species. title: Two Approaches to the Study of the Opium War
abstract: The First Opium War is both a conventional starting point for modern Chinese history and an event readily reduced to political slogans. Mao Haijian’s The Qing Empire and the Opium War reconstructs the Qing military, intelligence, and decision-making processes behind the defeat; Julia Lovell’s The Opium War places the conflict within British imperial commerce and the politics of public memory. Reading the two books comparatively, this essay examines responsibility for defeat, the origins of the conflict, and the subsequent making and forgetting of war memory. abstract: Multiple tissues and feather types from seven adult male bald eagles (Haliaeetus leucocephalus, kitpu) were analysed for lead, mercury, arsenic, selenium, uranium and other elements via ICP-MS and direct mercury analyzer. abstract: Planococcus sp. CAU13 produces a dark pigment, the identity of which is the focus of this study. Initial extraction methods utilized known procedures for carotenoid extraction, as Planococcus members are known to produce yellow to orange pigmented carotenoids. abstract: Candida auris is an emerging multidrug-resistant fungal pathogen and a major global health threat, highlighting the urgent need for new therapeutics. We screened ~2,600 FDA-approved drugs and clinical compounds and identified darapladib (DAL), a phospholipase A2 inhibitor, as a potent antifungal agent against multidrug-resistant C. auris. abstract: El derecho penal transnacional ha consolidado un imperio policial global que colisiona con los fundamentos del Estado de derecho. A través de los Acuerdos de Asistencia Legal Mutua –aalm–, se ha institucionalizado el trasplante de prácticas policiales a escala internacional, a menudo para eludir una supervisión judicial efectiva. title: From green transition to local sustainability: The role of locality and territorial embeddedness
abstract: The green transition is increasingly framed through decarbonisation, technological innovation and regulatory change, yet these approaches do not by themselves explain why comparable sustainability policies generate different outcomes across territories. abstract: Long Walk to Freedom is an important text because it shows how a person retains the ability to build a future and reclaim the dignity lost through mass oppression. This research paper does not look at Nelson Mandela simply as a rising leader; instead, it focuses on moving away from the old myths of leadership toward understanding him as a practical man. abstract: An Italian history textbook can acknowledge colonial violence while retaining a national narrative organized around Italian action. This article asks how Black History and selected concepts associated with Critical Race Theory can change that organization without imposing a United States chronology. It combines a documentary reading of the 2012 and 2025 national curricular guidance with an interpretive comparison of two published longitudinal studies: an analysis of 58 textbooks issued between 1936 and 2020 and a study of 42 images in 21 textbooks published between 1950 and 2022. abstract: Climate change-induced abiotic stresses, particularly drought and salinity, severely constrain global agricultural productivity. While natural plant-microbe interactions enhance stress tolerance, their efficacy is often inconsistent under extreme conditions. Synthetic symbiosis—engineering rhizosphere microbiomes and plant-microbe interfaces—presents a theoretical framework and future approach to bypass these limitations. abstract: Climate change and potential future pandemics pose interconnected and cascading threats to health systems, particularly in disaster-prone regions such as North Aceh Regency, Indonesia. However, empirical evidence on district-level health system preparedness that simultaneously addresses climate and pandemic risks remains limited. Purpose: This study aimed to assess health system preparedness, identify community vulnerabilities, and formulate context-specific adaptation strategies for addressing climate-related risks and potential future pandemics in North Aceh Regency. abstract: This article surveys a number of passages in Jer 40–44 that are crucial for the portrayal of the remnant of Judah within the narrative of the Judean refugees who flee to Egypt following the destruction of Jerusalem in 586/587 BCE. The intent of the study is to describe the portrayal of the remnant as it is reflected in the textual history of the book of Jeremiah. abstract: HIV diagnoses are increasing among women in the UK. abstract: This article charts the colonial career of Charles Symmons (1804–87), the inaugural Protector of Aborigines (1840–55) in Perth, Western Australia. abstract: This paper presents and contextualises a set of stone receptacles and a lid recovered during recent excavations at the Late Antique fortified settlement on the islet of Lukovac (Rab Island, NE Adriatic, Croatia). On the basis of stylistic and technical features, supported by regional analogies from Roman Dalmatia, the Po Valley and the Italian Regio X, the finds are interpreted as Early Imperial cinerary urns. Our findings indicate that while current hydrogen storage technology is costly and inefficient, reducing hydrogen costs to 12.5% of current levels and increasing round-trip efficiency to 70% could make it competitive. abstract: This review examines sustainable sources of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) and their potential roles in oxidative stress and inflammation. abstract: Abstract Qadhad is a traditional Yemeni slaked-lime mortar renowned for its exceptional waterproofing properties, particularly in cisterns, reservoirs, and masonry structures that have remained functional for centuries. abstract: In zoological facilities, the high density of species, presence of various arthropod vectors, and potential interaction with free-ranging wildlife hosts and vectors may increase the risk of vector-borne infections. abstract: Teluk Bintuni Regency in West Papua ranks among Indonesia’s richest regions by gross regional domestic product (GRDP) per capita, yet a quarter of its population is poor. This study examines how education gaps shape local people’s access to employment in an economy dominated by the Tangguh liquefied natural gas (LNG) project. title: False reports of physical dormancy in seeds of gymnosperms and angiosperms
abstract: Abstract Eighteen families of angiosperms but no families of gymnosperms have been documented anatomically (palisade layer of macrosclereids with a light line and a water gap in the seed coat or endocarp – physical dormancy [PY] syndrome) and/or physiologically (imbibition tests of scarified versus nonscarified seeds) to contain species with PY. title: Some Remarks on the Most Glaciotectonically Deformed Lignite Deposits in the World – Sieniawa, Western Poland
abstract: In the area around the village of Sieniawa in western Poland, lignite has been exploited on an industrial scale for over 150 years. The deposits where mining is carried out, initially underground and now opencast, were strongly deformed glaciotectonically during the Pleistocene. The lignite seam in the exploited deposits creates numerous folds and thrusts/nappes, giving them complex geology. As a result, the lignite deposits in the vicinity of Sieniawa are considered the most disturbed of all the world’s deposits still being mined.

abstract: PURPOSE: Physiotherapeutic scoliosis-specific exercises (PSSE) are widely used in the nonoperative management of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS). Although recommended in international guidelines, uncertainty remains regarding their effectiveness, indications, and long-term clinical relevance. abstract: Las metodologías activas y las narrativas digitales (digital storytelling, DST) ofrecen posibilidades para fortalecer competencias vinculadas con la lectura, la escritura y el pensamiento crítico; sin embargo, la evidencia sobre su integración explícita en contextos escolares permanece limitada. abstract: We consider the problem of transporting an open liquid-filled container along a straight line in minimum time while preventing liquid spilling. abstract: A circular economy seeks to retain the value of products, materials, and resources within the economy while reducing waste generation and pressure on virgin-resource extraction. abstract: Para establecer la relación a la que se refiere el título se hizo uso de reflexiones conjuntas entre autores en torno a la imaginación y creatividad de Julio Cortázar, al tropo de las ruinas, especialmente de la Biblioteca de Sarajevo y el performance de Kounellis. title: Adoption Drivers of Blood-based Multi-cancer Early Detection Testing: a Seven-country Population Survey
abstract: Introduction: Blood-based multi-cancer early detection (MCED) tests have the potential to complement existing cancer screening programs and expand screening opportunities for cancers lacking established population-based screening pathways. Successful implementation will depend not only on test performance, but also on public acceptance and engagement. This study evaluated interest in MCED testing and identified demographic, healthcare access, and experiential factors associated with willingness to undergo testing across seven countries.

title: El descenso de la migración interna en México
abstract: Este estudio analiza el descenso de la migración interna en México utilizando información censal de 2000, 2010 y 2020. Los resultados muestran una disminución de la intensidad migratoria reciente, asociada principalmente a los cambios en la estructura por edad derivados de la transición demográfica. La reducción de la población joven ha contribuido al debilitamiento de los flujos migratorios y a una reconfiguración territorial de los movimientos internos del país.

abstract: Abstract Amid growing calls for Australian universities to engage meaningfully with Indigenous knowledges, this article examines how Indigenous-led, place-based inquiry can reorient academic practice toward culturally regenerative possibilities. Drawing on a Cooperative Inquiry conducted with Whadjuk Noongar Boodjar, we follow six Noongar-led experiences involving Country, language, ceremony, deep time, embodiment and more-than-human relations. abstract: The intraspecific variation in elytral maculation of Cylindera (Cylindera) sauteri (Horn, 1912) and Cylindera (Cylindera) pseudocylindriformis (Horn, 1913) (Coleoptera: Cicindelidae) has not previously been studied in detail. abstract: Vehicle emission-induced air pollution is a significant environmental and public health issue in rapidly urbanizing areas. This research assesses the correlation between major air contaminants (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, NOx, and SO₂) and airborne microbial density across 32 urban sites in Nagpur, India. Airborne bacteria were sampled using the passive settle plate technique and analyzed for colony morphology, Gram staining, and hemolytic activity. abstract: Maize (Zea mays L.) is an important cereal crop with high nutrient requirements, particularly nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P) and potassium (K). However, inefficient utilisation of N, can result in substantial nutrient losses and increased production costs. Nano-fertilisers such as nano urea and nano zinc have emerged as promising alternative to conventional fertilisers. title: Logística e innovación bajo fuego: Acelerar la experiencia militar
abstract: El empirismo de Clausewitz sostiene que el conocimiento práctico del campo de batalla supera cualquier modelo teórico, no existen fórmulas universales y el mando debe adaptarse a las circunstancias reales. El conflicto en Ucrania ha redefinido el diseño de la guerra, obligando a los ejércitos a innovar en terreno y fortalecer el apoyo logístico. Ante futuros escenarios volátiles y complejos, se vuelve urgente agilizar la toma de decisiones en el frente, donde la adaptación táctica es decisiva para la supervivencia.

title: THE ROLE AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES OF THE “KARAKALPAKFILM” STUDIO IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF UZBEKISTAN’S NATIONAL CINEMATOGRAPHY
abstract: This article analyzes the development of cinema art in Karakalpakstan during the years of independence and the achievements of the “Karakalpakfilm” studio. It examines the establishment of the “Karakalpakfilm” film studio, its activities, and its achievements from a historical and analytical perspective. Particular attention is paid to the impact of state programs and reforms aimed at supporting national cinema during the years of independence on the studio's activities. title: Giant Impacts Preferentially Remove Low-mass Atmospheres: A Generalised Scaling Law for Impact-driven Atmospheric Loss
abstract: Abstract Impact-driven atmospheric loss plays a key role in shaping the diversity of planetary atmospheres. However, existing prescriptions for calculating loss from a given impact neglect the critical role of atmospheric mass on loss, and thus often severely miscalculate the extent of loss. Using 3D smoothed particle hydrodynamics simulations, we quantify atmospheric loss during giant impacts onto planets with 1%–20% mass fraction atmospheres and show that less massive (lower-pressure) atmospheres are significantly easier to remove. title: Detoxification enzyme modulation and larvicidal efficacy of Klebsiella pneumoniae (PX652414) and Proteus mirabilis (PZ337687) metabolites in mosquito vectors
abstract: Abstract Mosquitoes of the Anopheles , Aedes , and Culex genera serve as vectors for significant human and animal diseases. The increasing prevalence of insecticide resistance, primarily mediated by detoxification enzymes, highlights the urgent need for innovative biocontrol strategies. abstract: This study models the seasonal and latitudinal redistribution of orbital insolation for five Pleistocene-Holocene periods: MIS 11 (~400 ka), the Last Interglacial (~125 ka), the Last Glacial Maximum (~21 ka), the early Holocene (~11.7 ka), and the present (0 ka BP = 1950 CE), across nine latitudes from 65°S to 65°N. title: Cultural elements of resistance to colonial imperialism: A study based on Bharathiyar’s national poems
abstract: After the Renaissance, European colonial powers expanded their rule across many regions, and British colonisation in India and Sri Lanka gave rise to several freedom movements. Subramania Bharathiyar poet, writer, journalist, freedom fighter, and social reformer lived within this turbulent period, and his poems played a key role in shaping public thought in British India. abstract: La presente investigación tuvo como objetivo comprender cómo abordan los padres la constitución de la identidad sexual en niños y niñas en Educación Parvularia en la comuna de Chillán, región de Ñuble, a partir del empleo del juego. abstract: Moisture deficit heavily constrains common bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L .) production in Ethiopia, serving as a critical limitation in areas characterized by erratic rainfall. To address this challenge, forty-three common bean genotypes were evaluated in a greenhouse experiment at Hawassa University in 2022 to identify drought-tolerant materials. abstract: Introducción. El trabajo nocturno es una modalidad frecuente en los servicios sanitarios que puede alterar los ritmos circadianos, el sueño y los hábitos de vida, favoreciendo posibles alteraciones metabólicas. title: Examination of the Canyon Tourism Potential of Burdur Province
abstract: Canyons are geographical structures consisting of deep valleys formed by a deep cleft and rivers on the earth’s surface, and are areas where many tourism activities can be carried out. Canyons have emerged as alternative tourist areas preferred in tourism in recent years, and canyon tourism has come to the fore as canyons have started to come to the fore in tourism activities. abstract: This study examined the effects of dietary Yucca schidigera and Bacillus coagulans on meat quality, oxidative stability, volatile compounds, and gut microbiota in Jiuyuan Black chickens. abstract: Este artículo examina el lugar y la función del concepto de esse obiectivum en las glosas de Tomás de Vio Cayetano a cuatro cuestiones de la Prima Pars de la Summa theologiae de Tomás de Aquino. abstract: The philosophy of "Satu Tungku Tiga Batu" (One Stove Three Stones) in Fakfak Regency, West Papua, is a model of local wisdom proven effective in maintaining harmony among religious communities (Islam, Protestantism, and Catholicism). abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Large α 0 ‐thalassemia deletions involving both HBA1 and HBA2 genes are rare in South Asian populations and remain under‐characterized. abstract: This article examines the significance of international networks for early Norwegian Pentecostal pioneer missions through the case study of Erling and Alvina Andresen in Argentina. The Andresens were from Norway and were missionaries in Argentina from 1926 to 1969. During their time in Argentina, they were considered missionaries from three different denominations: the Pentecostal Movement in Norway, the Scandinavian Assemblies of God in the USA, and the Pentecostal Assemblies of Canada. title: Synthesis of knowledge to develop comprehensive guidelines for the in situ and ex situ conservation of European yew ( Taxus baccata L.)
abstract: Taxus baccata L. (common yew) is a tertiary relict conifer and one of the longest-lived tree species in Europe, yet it has experienced one of the most severe population declines among European forest trees. This review synthesises current knowledge on the biology, ecology, distribution, genetic diversity, and conservation of T. baccata, with particular emphasis on the preservation of its genetic resources under ongoing environmental change. abstract: Saturated fatty acids can reduce water uptake in cementitious materials but may retard early reactions and compromise strength. abstract: This article investigates the construction, demolition, and subsequent reconstruction efforts surrounding the bell tower commissioned by Kaptan Yorgi Pasha, who served as Giresun’s mayor from 1885 to 1904. abstract: The objective of this systematic review was to identify and analyze the clinical and anatomical factors associated with supraglotoplasty failure in pediatric patients with laryngomalacia, considering their influence on surgical outcomes and the need for reoperation. abstract: Rakstā analizēta Latvijas un Zviedrijas sūtņu korespondence, lai izpētītu galvenos faktorus, kas ietekmēja diplomātiskos sakarus no 1925. līdz 1930. gadam, saistībā ar ģeopolitisko situāciju Baltijas jūras reģionā. abstract: Abstract True metabolizable energy (TME) assays were first developed to refine poultry diets but have since been adapted by wildlife biologists and conservation planners to determine the assimilable energy within natural wetland foods (i.e., seeds, invertebrates, vegetation) for waterfowl. Bioenergetic models incorporate TME values to quantify the energetic carrying capacity of wetlands. abstract: This article examines how international human rights law addresses transgenerational harms: present or continuing violations whose effects impair the rights of subsequent generations. Drawing on the ICCPR, ICESCR other UN treaties, and regional jurisprudence, it focuses on two areas in which such harms are especially visible: Indigenous peoples’ rights and environmental degradation and climate change. title: Seed origin effects on growth, physiological and biochemical traits of Moringa oleifera seedlings grown under drought and salinity conditions
abstract: The versatile plant Moringa oleifera has spread beyond its native range and is now widely cultivated across diverse geographic regions. Global climate change requires careful seed selection before planting to ensure adaptation to the target environment. abstract: Abstract The emerald ash borer ( Agrilus planipennis ) is an invasive insect in the United States that preferentially feeds on ash ( Fraxinus spp.) trees, causing widespread ash decline. abstract: Fe–Mn–Al–C lightweight steels are promising candidates for weight‐sensitive structural components. abstract: This article focuses on the structural assessment of the Church of the Body of Christ in Jankovce, in eastern Slovakia, built in the 18th century, which was severely damaged by an earthquake in October 2023. abstract: La monitorización electrocardiográfica ambulatoria mediante Holter de 24 horas constituye una herramienta fundamental para correlacionar síntomas como síncope o mareos con arritmias transitorias. abstract: Post-fire straw mulching is widely used to reduce soil erosion and facilitate vegetation recovery in fire-affected ecosystems. However, straw mulch may introduce agricultural weedy species, raising concerns about their persistence and potential effects on post-fire plant community assembly. This study evaluated the medium-term ecological implications of straw mulch application using a post-fire chronosequence in semi-arid Mediterranean ecosystems of southeastern Spain. title: The Climate Impasse: Disavowal, Exhaustion and Everyday Life in the Climate Crisis
abstract: ABSTRACT The consequences of climate‐related disasters and emergencies are becoming increasingly stark. And yet in many places, consensus on climate action appears unattainable. I call this problem the climate impasse. In this paper, I draw on emerging theory on affect and negativity to characterise this impasse in three ways. I argue first that, rather than solely addressing governments' failure to act, this impasse develops through people's different lived experiences of the climate crisis. title: Experiencias con los modelos pedagógicos aplicados por docentes de una institución de carácter privado en la ciudad de Popayán, Colombia
abstract: Colombian schools are required to state a pedagogical model in their Institutional Educational Project (PEI); however, the way teachers understand and enact it does not always match what is declared. This article interprets the experiences of teachers at a private school in Popayán, Colombia, with the pedagogical models they apply, and analyzes their relationship with the socio-constructivist model stated in the institutional educational project (PEI, for its Spanish acronym). title: Impact of temperature variability on mortality during extreme heat and cold conditions over 20 years: A time-space-stratified case-crossover study
abstract: Background Climate change-induced temperature variability poses growing health risks. The effects of this variability on mortality are well established; however, its specific impact during extreme heat and cold conditions remains understudied. This represents a knowledge gap, as the human body’s physiological capacity to adapt to sudden temperature shifts is compromised when ambient temperatures are extreme. To address this, our study examined the relationship between mortality and temperature variability in Hong Kong for a 21-year period. Methods A time-space-stratified case-crossover design

title: The populist contagion: how the mainstreaming of right-wing populist rhetoric reduces public support for international aid
abstract: This article examines whether the diffusion of populist rhetoric from populist to mainstream parties reduces public support for international organisations (IOs) and multilateral aid. We argue that when mainstream parties adopt populist anti-IO rhetoric, support for aid decreases not just amongst citizens, which hold populist attitudes and support populist parties, but also among more moderate voters. title: Cultural Insights from Arabic Poetry in the Cairo Genizah
abstract: Abstract Unlike other Genizah writings, such as letters or legal documents, poetry offers a flexible medium for expressing emotions and relationships. Rooted in ancient Arabic oral traditions, colloquial Arabic poetry exemplifies oral recitation remaining central to cultural transmission and identity formation even after poetry began to be preserved in written forms. This article studies examples of Arabic poetry in the Cairo Genizah that are cultural expressions, with a particular focus on folk and colloquial Arabic poetry. title: Eventos adversos asociados a la seroterapia y estrategias de atención segura en el accidente ofídico pediátrico: revisión exploratoria.
abstract: El accidente ofídico en pacientes pediátricos representa una emergencia que puede generar complicaciones importantes debido al efecto del veneno y a las posibles reacciones adversas derivadas del uso del antiveneno. El propósito de la revisión fue analizar la evidencia disponible sobre estos eventos adversos y las medidas utilizadas para garantizar una atención segura. Para ello, se efectuó una revisión exploratoria basada en los criterios del Joanna Briggs Institute y PRISMA-ScR, consultando bases de datos como PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ScienceDirect, LILACS y WHO IRIS, con estudios publicados

title: Tecnología y conservación del idioma Ngäbere en comunidades indígenas de Costa Rica
abstract: El ngäbere, lengua hablada en cinco territorios indígenas de Costa Rica, enfrenta un proceso de desplazamiento que amenaza la continuidad del patrimonio lingüístico y cultural del pueblo Ngäbe-Buglé. Este estudio tuvo como objetivo desarrollar herramientas tecnológicas para su documentación, revitalización y transmisión intergeneracional mediante un diccionario digital interactivo y una aplicación móvil con vocabulario, traducciones en audio y contenidos culturales. title: Assessment of Environmental Noise Pollution Across Urban Land-use Types and Self-reported Health Impacts in Ayobo Community, Lagos State, Nigeria
abstract: Noise pollution has become a major environmental health concern in rapidly urbanizing cities of developing countries as a result of increasing traffic, commercial activities, and widespread dependence on electricity generators. This study assessed environmental noise levels and evaluated residents’ perceptions of noise sources, associated health effects, and mitigation measures in Ayobo community, Lagos State, Nigeria. abstract: Summary The Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt is a biogeographical province, and its eastern sub-province faces intense pressures from land-use and land-cover change (LULCC). This study integrates a systematic conservation planning approach, species distribution models and LULCC projections to identify areas that facilitate the conservation of endemic biodiversity under a dynamic conceptual framework. title: Analysis of Decision Support Systems Using the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) Method to Determine Socioeconomic Inequality Priorities (Case Study: Pelabuhanratu District)
abstract: The development of tourism in the UNESCO Global Geopark Ciletuh-Palabuhanratu area has contributed to regional economic growth; However, the benefits have not been equally distributed, resulting in socioeconomic disparities among local communities. This study aims to analyze socioeconomic inequality and determine the priority weight of its influencing indicators using the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) method. abstract: This study evaluates the market reaction to the official announcement of the Green Equity Designation policy by the Indonesia Stock Exchange. Using a sample of twenty-two companies listed on the SRI-KEHATI Index over an eleven-day observation window (t-5 to t+5), the research applies an event-study methodology with a Market-Adjusted Model. title: Effects of combining virtual nature exposure and hypnosis on quality of life in patients with hematologic malignancies undergoing hematopoietic cell transplant: Protocol for an efficacy trial
abstract: Introduction: Hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) is a key treatment for patients with hematological malignancies, but often results in adverse effects that impact both physical and psychological well-being. This calls for the development of interventions aiming at reducing psychosocial impact of HCT. Among interventions, nature exposure appears promising and efficient via virtual reality. Combined to techniques increasing attention resources allocated to positive elements such as hypnosis, it could represent an innovative solution to preserve quality of life. title: Gastrointestinal Helminths in Brown Bears in Erzurum, Türkiye: Biological Bridge, a Threat to Humans
abstract: Abstract Changes in land use, habitat fragmentation, and global climate fluctuations are reshaping pathogen circulation dynamics by increasing the permeability of the interface among wildlife, domestic animals, and humans. In this context, wild mammals play a crucial role as natural reservoirs for parasites and sources of environmental contamination. The primary aim of this study is to microscopically and molecularly identify gastrointestinal helminth eggs detected in bear fecal samples, as well as adult parasites found in two dead bears. abstract: Abstract This paper presents evidence for the demand‐driven propagation of job losses in the context of the United States during the Great Recession. Using county‐level tradable job losses driven by aggregate shocks as an instrument, it shows that retail and restaurant (R&R) employment fell by 0.37% for every 1% of job loss in the rest of the county's economy. title: Optimizing cross-border CCS policy: an integrated energy–carbon–cost framework for source–host credit allocation
abstract: Cross-border carbon capture and storage (CCS) can support industrial decarbonisation where emissions and storage resources are unevenly distributed. Existing optimisation studies mainly minimise techno-economic cost and rarely integrate energy penalties, country-level emissions accounting, domestic-versus-export allocation, and source–host credit sharing. This study develops a mixed-integer linear programming framework that selects domestic or export storage, shipping routes, offshore pipelines, and sinks while tracking operational emissions, costs, and source–host credit allocation. title: Algunos desafíos del Pacto de derechos civiles y políticos en el 60 aniversario
abstract: Este trabajo realiza algunas reflexiones en el 60 aniversario del Pacto de derechos civiles y políticos sobre algunos desafíos. De un lado los relativos a la interpretación de la noción de dignidad humana y su relevancia para acotar los titulares de los derechos. De otro lado aborda la importancia de las transformaciones de la vida internacional para el PDCP, que han puesto los derechos humanos en una situación de riesgo por la crisis de las organizaciones internacionales y los cambios en la distribución del poder internacional, que requieren de nuevos consensos normativos e institucionales. abstract: This study is based on the cultural heritage documentation of District Charsadda, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Pakistan by the roles of Melmastia as cultural hospitality roles. Charsadda is hub of Pakhtune cultural display in habited by different Pakhtune tribes. The study adopts a qualitative research design to explore the nature of hospitality in everyday life and communal life and its effect on the construction of social identity, cultural continuity and sense of community. title: Activity patterns and predator-prey temporal overlap of sympatric felids in the Atlantic Forest
abstract: Abstract While dietary niche partitioning is considered the primary long-term mechanism preventing competition among sympatric carnivores, coexistence, particularly in fragmented landscapes, depends strongly on resource partitioning across spatial and temporal dimensions. In the highly threatened Atlantic Forest, understanding felid time partitioning is essential for elucidating mechanisms reducing intraguild interactions. title: One Romanticism, Many Voices: Nazrul’s Encounter with the English Romantics and the Shaping of a Global Romantic Tradition
abstract: This study undertakes a comparative analysis of the poems of Kazi Nazrul Islam and the works of major English Romantic poets— Blake, Wordsworth, Coleridge, Shelley, Byron, Keats— through the methods of influence studies and thematology to trace the influence the Romantics exerted on Nazrul and to discern the convergences and divergences in their treatment of various literary themes, with the additional aim of assessing Nazrul’s contribution to shaping, recalibrating and extending the limits of global Romanticism through the indigenization of Romantic tropes. title: O IMPACTO DO PESO DAS MOCHILAS ESCOLARES NAS ALTERAÇÕES POSTURAIS EM CRIANÇAS E ADOLESCENTES: Revisão integrativa
abstract: Introdução: O transporte de mochilas escolares faz parte da rotina de crianças e adolescentes e pode produzir adaptações biomecânicas e alterações posturais, especialmente quando há excesso de carga ou distribuição assimétrica.
