title: Intersectional gender inequities in access to malaria information, knowledge, and attitudes toward malaria services in Oromia, Ethiopia: a mixed-methods study
abstract: Abstract Background Malaria remains a significant public health issue in Ethiopia, particularly for vulnerable populations like women and children. Gender-based inequalities in malaria knowledge, attitudes, and access to information persist, intersected by socio-economic and cultural factors. This study explores these intersectional gender inequalities in malaria information access and attitudes toward preventive services in the Jimma Zone, Oromia Region, Ethiopia. title: Linking Empathy to Psychological Intimate Partner Violence: The Mediation Analysis of Two Competitive Mediating Pathways
abstract: While empathy training has long been considered a cornerstone of clinical interventions for intimate partner violence (IPV), emerging evidence on the link between empathy and IPV perpetration suggests an inconsistent association. Guided by the double-edged sword theory and integrating attachment theoretical perspectives within the Chinese cultural context, this study established a competitive mediation model to explain this counterintuitive relationship. title: Hepatic transcriptome, intestinal microbiome, and metabolite profiles associated with MASLD, MASH, and fibrosis in patients undergoing bariatric surgery
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is prevalent in obesity and can progress to steatohepatitis (MASH), fibrosis, cirrhosis and liver failure. The intestinal microbiome (IM) and metabolites may play a role in MASLD severity but their potential relationships with the hepatic transcriptome are not clear. We investigated these relationships in 93 patients undergoing bariatric surgery who provided blood and fecal samples prior to surgery for biochemical, metabolite (serum, fecal) and IM (metagenomics) measurements. title: Early Baseball on Prince Edward Island: How the Game Began in Canada’s Smallest Province
abstract: Baseball arrived on Prince Edward Island through the same networks of travel, trade, and migration that connected the Island to the wider world. First introduced through visiting fishermen and strengthened by growing ties between Island communities, the game gradually moved from informal contests in fields and public spaces into organized clubs, interprovincial competition, and established leagues. title: Children and adolescents across 23 communities learn about animals in diverse environments and through multiple activities
abstract: Abstract Children's interactions with animals shape their understanding of the biological world and humans' place in it. Understanding where children report they encounter and gain their knowledge of animals can provide insight into the early experiences that help shape human attitudes and connections to nature. To date, there is limited information on how children across diverse communities and age groups interact with animals and learn about them in their daily lives. title: Clinicopathologic characteristics and survival outcomes of gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms in Peru: A 15-year retrospective cohort study
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Incidence of gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (GEP-NENs) has increased globally; however, data from Latin America remain scarce. This study aimed to describe the sociodemographic and clinicopathologic characteristics, treatment modalities, survival outcomes, and prognostic factors of GEP-NENs in a 15-year single-center cohort at a national referral cancer center in Lima, Peru. abstract: Mitochondrial complex IV (CIV) is an integral part of the mitochondrial electron transport chain (ETC) and plays a pivotal role in maintaining mitochondrial function. In contrast to the long-standing recognition of its dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease (AD), the exact role of CIV deficit in the pathogenesis of this neurodegenerative disorder remains poorly defined. title: Crowding-induced phase transition in Oedaleus asiaticus as a developmental stage-gated, irreversible multi-gene switch
abstract: Solitary-phase Oedaleus asiaticus (Bei-Bienko) can switch to the far more destructive gregarious phase as population density rises, posing a serious threat to agriculture, animal husbandry and local economies. The current investigation assessed how developmental stages and population density impacted phase transitions and which genes served as key regulatory elements of this process. title: Measurements and modeling of urban secondary organic aerosol formation potential as a function of precursor volatility class in the Los Angeles area during summer 2022
abstract: Abstract. Urban secondary organic aerosol (SOA) contributes to degraded air quality which can affect human health. Improvements in Los Angeles (LA), CA air quality have mainly plateaued since 2010. In summer 2022, measurements were made to quantify the SOA formation potential (SOA-FP) in ambient LA air. Two oxidation flow reactors (OFRs) ingested ambient air: one was equipped with an electrically conductive polymer inlet that denuded lower volatility species, and the other was run without an inlet. This allowed the separate quantification of SOA-FP from higher vs. lower volatility precursors.

title: Elevated atmospheric CO2 reshapes soil metal(loid) mobility and stress responses in Enchytraeus crypticus: a multi-level analysis from molecular to population endpoints
abstract: Projected increases in atmospheric CO 2 may alter soil properties and modify the ecotoxicity of metal(loid)-contaminated soils, yet their combined effects on invertebrates remain poorly understood. This study evaluated how elevated atmospheric CO 2 (600–1000 ppm), encompassing levels projected under future IPCC scenarios by 2100, influences soil physicochemistry, metal(loid) availability, and the biological responses of Enchytraeus crypticus in control and metal(loid)-contaminated soils, relative to standard CO 2 conditions (400–500 ppm). abstract: Justification: Research-Based Learning (RBL) strengthens higher education; however, evidence regarding its relationship with scientific competencies is scarce in the initial training of History and Social Sciences teachers, where limitations in critical thinking, research motivation, and academic production persist. Objective: To analyze the relationship between RBL and scientific competencies among students of History and Social Sciences Education at the National University of Chimborazo. abstract: Abstract Contemporary cities in the global South are being reshaped through the intersecting logics of burgeoning real estate sectors and diasporic investment. This article examines the case of Pakistan to explore how emigration trajectories and remittance practices contribute to the transformation of urban landscapes in countries of origin through processes of emigre city‐making. abstract: Cet article analyse le lexique vestimentaire dans Les Chiffons du rêve de Madeleine Chapsal, montrant qu’il dépasse la simple description pour fonctionner comme opérateur poétique à part entière. title: Parental playfulness among Chinese families: associations with young children’s behavioral, social, and emotional development
abstract: Parent–child early interaction is crucial for promoting children’s development. This study explored associations of self-reported and observed parental playfulness with young children’s social, emotional, and behavioral development. Participants included 95 three to six-year-old child (53 girls, 42 boys; Mage = 58.9 months, SD = 12 months) and parent dyads from Shenzhen, China. abstract: The one-dimensional shear-wave-propagation problem is analytically investigated for an inhomogeneous viscoelastic layer characterized by shear modulus varying exponentially with depth. Unlike commonly employed power-law models which exhibit unbounded stiffness at infinity, the present formulation maintains bounded stiffness in the whole domain, thereby enabling physically meaningful representations of surface layers of arbitrary thickness with either depth increasing or decreasing stiffness profiles. title: Sorption of Cu(II) by Soil and Soil Components: Sorption Experiments and Surface Complexation Modeling
abstract: Sorption of Cu(II) by different horizons of a podzolic soil (A(O)EL, EL, and IIBD) was studied in model laboratory experiments and described using surface complexation models. abstract: La producción ovina constituye una actividad pecuaria de gran importancia para las familias rurales del Altiplano Central Mexicano debido a su contribución a la alimentación, generación de ingresos y aprovechamiento de recursos locales. El objetivo de este estudio fue caracterizar los aspectos sociales, productivos, técnicos y económicos de las unidades extensivas de producción ovina. title: Conditional Survival of Gallbladder Cancer After Curative‐Intent Surgery: Impact of Disease Stage, Surgical Extent, and Adjuvant Therapy
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Gallbladder cancer is a rare but aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis even after curative-intent surgery. Conventional survival estimates provide fixed probabilities from diagnosis and fail to reflect the evolving prognosis of patients who have already survived several years. Conditional survival (CS) offers time-updated prognostic information, but evidence in gallbladder cancer remains limited. title: Administrative Empowerment and Agricultural Crowding-Out: The Effect of County-To-City Upgrading on Grain Production in China
abstract: How administrative-division adjustments influence agricultural production constitutes a vital issue to unpack the linkage between county-level urbanization and food security across China. This paper treats China's new round of county-to-city upgrading (CCU policy) as a quasi-natural experiment and uses county-level panel data from 2000 to 2022 to examine its effect on total grain production through a staggered difference-in-differences approach. abstract: The fundamental biochemical and stereochemical difference in how cell membrane lipids are built between Archaea on one side, and Bacteria and Eukarya on the other is known as the lipid divide. title: Elevated CO2 primes drought resistance in mulberry via multi-omics reprogramming of carbon and redox metabolism
abstract: Abstract Drought stress severely constrains the growth and productivity of woody perennials. While elevated CO2 (ECO2) can mitigate drought stress, the systemic mechanisms underlying this synergy remain largely unexplored in horticultural species. Here, we integrated physiological assays with transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses to investigate how ECO2 (710 ppm/760 ppm) enhances drought resistance in mulberry (Morus alba L.), an economically important tree crop. abstract: Abstract Serratia spp. are common spoilage bacteria in meat. This study screened five Serratia strains with significant proteolytic and lipolytic activities (Serratia bozhouensis YB10, Serratia myotis YB16, Serratia quinivorans NC6, Serratia liquefaciens NC12, and Serratia grimesii NC17) from 34 meat-borne Enterobacteriaceae isolates. abstract: La hemorragia digestiva alta no variceal refractaria al tratamiento endoscópico constituye una emergencia con desenlace potencialmente mortal, particularmente cuando la hemostasia endoscópica no es factible, fracasa o se presenta resangrado. title: Investigation of the Current Status of Beekeeping Enterprises and Beekeeping Activities in Çorum Province
abstract: This study was conducted to determine the structural status, technical practices, and primary challenges of beekeeping enterprises in Çorum province and to propose sectoral solutions. The research material consists of primary data obtained through face-to-face surveys from 183 beekeeping enterprises operating in the center and districts of Çorum. Descriptive statistical analyses were employed to identify the socio-economic and technical factors influencing enterprise structure and productivity. title: Es el derecho... educación y tecnologías en tiempos de inteligencia artificial
abstract: En este ensayo recorro algunos de los hitos que se produjeron en materia de educación y tecnologías en los últimos 25 años e invito a seguir pensando en clave de derecho las cuestiones vinculadas con la inclusión digital. title: Becoming-weather: posthuman pedagogy in times of climate and nature emergency in Ireland
abstract: In Ireland, weather has long shaped people’s understandings of place and numerous myths and folktales highlight embodied experiences of the land. Yet, many of these traditional relationships with weather and the environment seem increasingly disconnected from contemporary life and education. In response to the escalating climate and nature emergency, this paper argues that embodied encounters with weather offer valuable possibilities for rethinking education for sustainable development (ESD) in Irish secondary education, going beyond human-centred approaches. title: “Nutritional and Structural Characterization of Mango and Potato Peel Powders and Foxtail Millet for Sustainable Functional Food Development”
abstract: Background and Aim: The increasing demand for sustainable and nutrient-dense functional foods has driven interest in the valorization of agro-industrial by-products. Mango peel, potato peel, and foxtail millet are underutilized resources with considerable nutritional and functional potential. title: Current situation and prospects for the recovery of pineapple waste (Ananas comosus) in the value chains of South Kivu, Eastern DRC
abstract: Despite its economic potential, the pineapple value chain in South Kivu generates substantial organic waste, creating environmental and socio-economic challenges. Although the technical potential for valorizing pineapple waste is documented globally, no study has assessed waste flows at the actor level across the entire chain in this region. This study quantifies and characterizes pineapple waste from production on Idjwi Island to collection, processing, retail and consumption in Bukavu. title: Certezas fragmentadas. La procelosa vida del “comandante Morales”
abstract: Hidden among inaccuracies, the life of Commander Morales allows for debate about the use of document as providers of certainty. Sources are always partial in several senses and their fragmentary contribution requires conceiving them as imperfect pieces of a puzzle in permanent construction, ultimately incomplete and distorted, where there is no room for shortcuts. Several interesting lives come together in a village near the front to compose a portrait of the Republican rearguard that calls into question the usual narrative and leads us to reflect on the limits of historical knowledge.

abstract: Abstract Hunting is a central, culturally embedded relationship between people and nature, yet also drives wildlife declines with far‐reaching consequences for ecosystems and people. It is also a highly diverse practice, involving a wide range of actors and hunting techniques, both of which determine the social‐ecological impacts of hunting. However, the geography of different types of hunting remains unclear, constituting a barrier for conservation and sustainability planning. title: The train and the abyss: Israeli Hebrew and the dialectic of old, new, and in-between
abstract: This paper examines the pseudo-restoration of Hebrew and its status in modern Israel as a case study in how an ‘ancient’ language is mobilised for national identity and political myth-making. abstract: Different authors have analyzed the occurrence of crashes involving vulnerable users, but most studies focus on pedestrians and cyclists. title: Minor moments of more-than-human encounters: Rethinking climate change education in early childhood
abstract: In the context of intensifying climate crises, early childhood education is increasingly positioned as a site for cultivating the capacities, sensitivities, and solidarities needed for more sustainable futures (Spiteri & Pace, 2023; UNESCO & MECCE, 2024). Yet dominant approaches to climate change education continue to privilege cognitive, anthropocentric, and developmental framings, emphasizing knowledge transmission and individual responsibility while overlooking children’s relational and ecological entanglements. title: An evolutionary perspective on the conservation of endogenous Ah receptor activation
abstract: ABSTRACT The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) senses environmental and physiological cues by responding to a wide range of chemicals, thereby mediating diverse physiological functions. There are four sources of AHR agonists: anthropogenic, microbial, dietary, and host origin. The structural diversity and potency of the chemicals that activate the AHR makes it difficult to discern key ligands that facilitate various activities. abstract: Purpose is to evaluate the impact of the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic on selected temporal and organizational parameters of prehospital emergency care for patients with suspected stroke in the Ústí nad Labem Region by comparing system performance before and during the pandemic. Materials and Methods. A retrospective observational study was conducted using data from the Electronic Patient Record system of the Ústí nad Labem Region Emergency Medical Service. title: Indicator-based diagnosis of carbon metabolism in production–living–ecological spaces: Land-use transitions, ecological network relationships, and terrain-constrained carbon flows in the Nanling Mountains, China
abstract: Land-use changes among production–living–ecological (PLE) spaces are critical drivers of regional carbon metabolism. Although these changes have been extensively examined in urban agglomerations and plains, their carbon metabolic mechanisms in mountainous areas remain inadequately explored. In this study, ecological network analysis (ENA) was used to identify ecological interactions among PLE spatial categories and evaluate the utility of the carbon metabolism network. abstract: The oxygen radical absorbance capacity (ORAC) value assigned to a serving of beans may depend on whether the reference sample is raw, cooked, or drawn from a different recipe. Even when two preparations receive the same score, sodium added during cooking may distinguish them in a way that matters for blood pressure. Comparing food composition research, observational studies, and feeding trials helps clarify the role of ORAC in hypertension research. title: Harnessing benefits of vermicompost for sustainable agriculture: improving soil health, crop productivity and environmental sustainability
abstract: Vermicompost (VC) is an effective organic amendment of soil that is produced through the non-thermophilic biodegradation of organic waste by earthworms and microbes. This study focuses on identifying influence of VC on soil physical properties and biological functions such as soil structure, bulk density, and water-holding capacity, as well as its contribution to nutrient availability and microbial activity. title: Sulfidation Reaction Mechanisms of Olivine and Diopside at Mercury's Reducing Conditions
abstract: Abstract The surface of Mercury contains elevated amounts of sulfur of up to 4 wt.%. Volcanic degassing of S from the interior of the planet could have initiated sulfidation reactions between the degassed S and surface materials in the planet's past, leading to the observed surface S enrichment. Mercury's highly reducing conditions cause nominally lithophile elements, such as Mg and Ca, to become chalcophile and to form sulfides such as oldhamite (CaS) and niningerite (MgS) when reacting with S. title: A Numerical Study of the Equatorial Wind Jet Response to the X2.2 Solar Flare on 6 September 2017
abstract: Abstract Using paired Thermosphere–Ionosphere–Electrodynamics General Circulation Model (TIEGCM) simulations, we investigated the response of the equatorial thermospheric zonal wind jet to the X2.2 solar flare that peaked at 09:10 UT on 6 September 2017. title: THE SOUTHWESTERN FRONTIER OF DAI NAM (1802 - 1867): A GEOPOLITICAL AND STRATEGIC ANALYSIS
abstract: The article looks at the defensive policy that the Nguyen Dynasty carried out on the Southwest border of Cochinchina (Nam Bo) from 1802-1867. This is examined through geopolitics and military strategic thinking. The Southwest border was a strategic location that connected the Mekong Delta to the countries of Cambodia (Chan Lap) and Siam (Siam La). It was considered a geopolitical bulwark (“phen dau”) that safeguarded the security of the whole southern region and the sovereignty of the Nguyen Dynasty. title: Sovereignty by Omission: Rethinking Agamben's State of Exception
abstract: ABSTRACT This article revisits Agamben's state of exception. Homo Sacer and State of Exception frame camps as spaces where law is suspended and life reduced to “bare life.” This decisionist paradigm underestimates the institutional and economic complexity of refugee management. This article proposes the concept of sovereignty by omission: Exclusion produced not by a decisive suspension of law but by legal ambiguity, bureaucratic deferral, and systemic inaction. title: How sustainable finance initiatives and forums address environmental issues, including climate change, and the challenges they face
abstract: Abstract An increasing number of transnational sustainable finance initiatives and forums are focusing on shifting and mobilizing private finance. Consequently, it has become more difficult to grasp the big picture concerning their roles and effects, including how they overlap and synergize. This study examined how transnational sustainable finance initiatives and forums contribute to scaling up private finance and investment and encourage private sector participation. abstract: Nitrosamines impurities are highly mutagenic which are generally produced from the chemical reactions between amino groups like secondary amines and tertiary amines and nitro sating agents prominently. title: The Impact of Executives’ Overseas Background on Corporate ESG: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Listed Companies
abstract: Within the dual background of the “dual carbon” strategy and the standardized development of ESG in capital markets, exploring the driving mechanisms of corporate ESG performance is crucial, for promoting the sustainable operation of listed companies. This research takes Chinese A-share listed companies, from 2009 to 2023, as the research sample and, empirically analyzes the impact of executives’ overseas background on corporate ESG performance, based on upper echelons theory. abstract: In this paper, we reflect on the central role of teachers’ actions in the initial construction of algebraic practice in the classroom, as well as on the value of the collective space as a condition that enhances this process. We emphasize how this practice can foster the development of habits for interpreting information in numerical expressions and transforming them in ways that enable new interpretations. title: Effect of Weed Control Methods on the Performance of Maize (Zea mays L.) Varieties in the Northern Guinea and Sudan Savanna Zones of Kebbi State
abstract: Effective weed control and varietal selection are important for maize productivity in savanna agroecological zones. This study evaluated the responses of three maize varieties to five weed control treatments in two field trials conducted during the 2025 wet season in Aliero and Yauri, Kebbi State, Nigeria. Each experiment used a 3 × 5 factorial arrangement in a randomized complete block design with three replications. The varieties were SAMMAZ-9, SAMMAZ-51, and SAMMAZ-59. title: Climate effects on flowering cues of ornithophilous plants in a Costa Rican cloud forest
abstract: ABSTRACT The influence of a changing climate on the phenology of organisms in a region is dependent on how regional climate cues or modifies the timing of local life history events and how those cues are changing over time. There is extensive evidence of phenolological shifts in flowering time over the past 50 years in response to increasing temperatures in temperate regions, but far less is known about tropical regions where seasonality is less temperature driven. title: Delineating structural features and estimating source depths in the Ngoc Linh complex, central Vietnam, using magnetic data
abstract: The Ngoc Linh complex is a key metamorphic domain within the Kontum Massif of central Vietnam and preserves records of the tectonic evolution of the Indochina Block. However, the subsurface structural framework of the complex remains poorly understood owing to the limited number of geophysical investigations, limiting insights into its tectonic evolution and crustal architecture. title: What Predicts Entrepreneurship? The Quagmire of Entrepreneurial Desirability
abstract: Entrepreneurial action begins with the availability of an opportunity and with an individual's perception that entrepreneurship represents a desirable and feasible course of action. Building on the entrepreneurial event model, this study examines the factors associated with the entrepreneurial desirability among individuals who received exposure to entrepreneurship training and activities in Pokhara Metropolitan City, Nepal. title: Sustainability Investing in Family Offices: Evidence from Singapore
abstract: Family offices are increasingly recognised as a potentially important source of capital for sustainability-related investment. However, relatively little is known about how they make such decisions, particularly in Asia. This paper fills that knowledge gap and contributes important new empirical evidence by analysing the decision-making processes of family offices operating out of Singapore. abstract: Circadian biology is recognized for its importance to physiology and metabolism, with implications for healthy aging and disease risk. abstract: Abstract In the present study, the density, morphological characteristic and mechanical properties at both room and elevated temperatures of titanium microparticle-reinforced AZ91 matrix composites were evaluated. abstract: This article aims to situate itself within religious anthropological scholarship through a comparative study of Indigenous religious transformation in Malaysia and Bangladesh. Methodologically, the study combines phenomenological interpretation with a decolonial perspective rooted in relational ontology, seeing humans as embedded in land, ancestry, kinship, and community. title: Reproductive and biochemical dynamics of local Iraqi bucks across seasonal variations
abstract: The primary objective of this research was to assess how environmental shifts and thermal stress induced by summer and winter conditions affect seminal traits, seminal plasma biochemical profiles, testosterone levels, and reproductive success in local Iraqi bucks. The experiment was conducted using 14 healthy, sexually mature males, with semen samples collected weekly throughout the duration of the research work. title: Forest landscape connectivity increased in China from 1990 to 2020
abstract: Enhancing landscape connectivity to counter biodiversity decline and ecosystem deterioration has aroused growing global concerns. Nonetheless, comprehensive quantitative assessments of both structural and potential functional connectivity in forest landscapes over long time series and large spatial scales are still limited. Moreover, few studies integrate such connectivity measures with forest cover percentage (FC) to provide a diagnostic perspective on landscape dynamics. title: Protecting birds in protected areas: a multi-scale analysis of forest structure and species occurrence
abstract: Protected areas are cornerstones of avian conservation, yet forest-associated bird communities continue to decline even within protected lands. The capacity of a protected area to sustain bird populations depends on both internal habitat quality and the surrounding landscape context, yet the relative importance of these scales remains poorly understood. We evaluate how forest structure at three nested spatial scales (local, park, and county) influences the occurrence of forest-associated birds within protected areas. title: Book Publishing Activities of the Union for the Liberation of Ukraine in Europe (1914–1918)
abstract: The article analyzes the distinctive features of the book publishing activities of the Union for the Liberation of Ukraine (ULU) during the First World War. These activities became possible due to financial support from Germany and Austria-Hungary, part of which was directed towards information and propaganda campaigns serving both the interests of the Central Powers and the promotion of the Ukrainian question in Europe. title: Living with the Stones: Intangible Heritage, Storytelling, and Contemporary Engagements with Megalithic Landscapes
abstract: This article explores how contemporary intangible cultural heritage (ICH) is produced and negotiated through lived engagements with megalithic sites in Portugal and Scotland. While prehistoric stone circles are commonly interpreted through archaeological and expert-led frameworks, the present study foregrounds personal narratives, sensory encounters, and imaginative practices as forms of ICH which are central to how these sites acquire meaning in the present. title: Traumatismo craneoencefálico en motociclistas: Síntesis de la evidencia con contextualización para Paraguay
abstract: Introducción: en Paraguay, los motociclistas fueron el 58 % de las muertes viales en 2024; en una serie hospitalaria de motociclistas fallecidos, el 86,9 % presentaba lesión craneoencefálica. El objetivo fue sintetizar la evidencia sobre mecanismos, factores modificables y prevención del traumatismo craneoencefálico (TCE) en motociclistas, distinguiendo evidencia directa e indirecta, y contextualizarla para Paraguay.Materiales y métodos: revisión narrativa (selección intencionada, no exhaustiva) con búsquedas documentadas en PubMed/MEDLINE, LILACS, SciELO y fuentes oficiales (octubre de 2026).

title: Biodiversity credits hold promise, yet credit-generating protocols require safeguards to realize potential
abstract: Abstract Given the existing gap in biodiversity funding, mobilizing private finance will be essential to achieving global biodiversity conservation goals, especially across lower- and middle-income countries with limited capacity and public finance. The emerging voluntary biodiversity market (VBM) holds promise to leverage private finance for biodiversity, but credit-generating protocols must be robust to prevent greenwashing and maximize effectiveness. abstract: Introduction. The choice of construction technology affects not only the organization of the construction process but also its duration and, consequently, the project’s payback period. The growing trend towards construction in dense urban environments necessitates the active development of underground space. The complexity and labour-intensive nature of assessing the effectiveness of various technologies at the design documentation stage often lead designers to opt for traditional construction methods. title: El juego terapéutico en la hospitalización pediátrica: una estrategia de atención integral más allá del manejo del dolor
abstract: During pediatric hospitalization, invasive and painful procedures are frequently performed and may cause anxiety and fear, particularly among children who, due to their age, may not fully understand the situation. If pain is not adequately managed, it may be associated with negative consequences, such as sleep disturbances, needle phobia, and reluctance or refusal to seek or receive healthcare. title: Food-derived bioactive molecules as regulators of lipid metabolism: Discovery, molecular targets, applications and perspectives
abstract: Understanding how food-derived bioactive molecules regulate lipid metabolism has become a central issue in molecular nutritional science. Recent advances have demonstrated that these molecules function not merely as nutrients but as signaling regulators acting on specific molecular targets. This review summarizes the discovery and molecular mechanisms of food-derived peptides, proteins, amino acids, and polyphenols involved in lipid metabolism. title: The Humanitarian Principles: Relativity Revisited
abstract: Abstract The principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, and independence are widely viewed as integral to humanitarian assistance. Yet, despite shaping the work of many humanitarians, the international legal status of these principles is unclear. title: Evidence on the Robustness of the Links Between Social Relationships and Mortality
abstract: Despite a substantial literature on the links between social relationships and mortality, the size of the relative risks from loneliness, social isolation, and living alone, remain controversial. Further research is therefore important given demographic changes meaning that more people are living alone, for longer, and with chronic health conditions. Using 19 waves of high-quality Australian longitudinal data we provide new evidence using multiple measures of social relationships, model specifications, and adjustments for confounding. title: Assessment of phytochemicals and developmental toxicity of Litsea cubeba (Lours.) Pers. fruit extract using zebrafish embryo as a model
abstract: Litsea cubeba (Lours.) Pers. is an aromatic plant whose fruits are extensively used in traditional medicine and as flavouring ingredients. Although widely used, the information regarding its phytochemical constituents and toxicity remains scarce. This study focused on identifying the phytochemicals present in the methanolic fruit extract of L. cubeba, as well as evaluating the embryotoxicity and developmental toxicity using zebrafish embryos as a model. title: Morphological and molecular identification of Magnaporthe oryzae causing finger millet blast disease in Kenya
abstract: Finger millet { Eleusine coracana (L.) Gaertn.} is an underutilized climate-resilient cereal crop with excellent nutraceutical properties. It is an important subsistence crop to the majority smallholder women farmers in western and eastern parts of Kenya, where it is grown under low input mixed cropping systems. One of the challenges limiting its production is blast disease caused by Magnaporthe oryzae (syn. Pyricularia oryzae ). title: Theatre translation in Brazil from the 16th to the 20th century: a history of containment and resistance
abstract: While studies of literary translation historiography in Brazil have offered invaluable insights, few have focused on theatre. This article bridges that gap by asking how translation has shaped Brazilian theatre and how it has functioned as containment or resistance in times of censorship and control. Adopting a primarily historicist approach, it draws on a broad body of scholarship and critical Brazilian voices to examine the discursive mechanisms through which theatre history has been constructed. title: La perspectiva de género en la investigación histórica sobre filósofas medievales
abstract: La pregunta central de este trabajo es: ¿qué aporta la perspectiva de género a la investigación histórica y, por ende, a las historias de la filosofía medieval? Frente a tal interrogante se defiende que se trata de una herramienta teórica indispensable para cuestionar el androcentrismo y la historia tradicional, así como para comprender las aportaciones de las mujeres a lo largo del tiempo.

title: GIANTS UNDER A MICROSCOPE: REVEALING SAUROPODOMORPH DINOSAUR PALEOBIOLOGY THROUGH THE BONE AND TOOTH MICROSTRUCTURE
abstract: The paleobiology of sauropodomorph dinosaurs has historically garnered considerable interest, primarily because this clade includes the largest terrestrial vertebrates. Bone and tooth microstructures are crucial sources of paleobiological data, and many paleohistological studies have focused on this group. Here we review and synthesize the main advances in an understanding of sauropodomorph paleobiology derived from osteological and dental histology. title: Bistability of ice-shelf cavity circulation and melt under coastal polynya forcing
abstract: Antarctic ice shelves play a key role in controlling the mass loss of the Antarctic Ice Sheet. Increasing evidence from regional studies suggests the possibility of abrupt transitions from low to high basal melt regimes under future climate forcing. The computational cost and complexity of these realistic simulations yet limit their ability to systematically investigate the steady-state response of ice shelves to incremental forcing, the reversibility of abrupt transitions and the underlying positive feedback loops. title: Don't Lose the Thread: Empowering Long-Horizon LLM Agents with Cognitive Resource Self-Allocation
abstract: Agents powered by large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable progress in solving complex reasoning tasks. However, LLM agents often falter on long-horizon tasks due to cognitive overload, as their working memory becomes cluttered with expanding and irrelevant information, which dilutes their attention and hinders effective planning and reasoning. To mitigate this challenge, we introduce Cognitive Resource Self-Allocation (CORAL), a novel reasoning paradigm that empowers agents to proactively optimize their context. title: A Large Eddy Simulation Study of Turbine Pitch Motion Effects on Power Generation in Fully Developed Floating Wind Turbine Arrays
abstract: Interactions between floating wind turbines and the marine atmospheric boundary layer affect turbine wakes and power output. This study examines the impact of turbine representations and platform pitching motion on power predictions for aligned floating wind turbine arrays. abstract: Wildfire seasons have become 84 days longer in the current days than in the 1970s, causing enormous threats to one's financial status and short- and long-term health. During the fire, public agencies send out emergency messages to provide warnings and orders. Although 26 million people in the US have limited English proficiency, over 80% of those messages are only delivered in English, which can cause disproportionate information distribution and awareness. title: An analytical framework for wave-coherent airflow over fast surface waves
abstract: Classical theories attribute wind-wave momentum transfer to a critical layer, where the mean wind speed equals the wave phase speed. For waves that travel faster than the near-surface wind, this layer may lie outside the wave boundary layer or be absent altogether. We develop an analytical description of the wave-coherent airflow in this regime for a prescribed mean wind, using a Wentzel--Kramers--Brillouin--Jeffreys (WKBJ) approximation to the viscous Orr--Sommerfeld equation in wave-following coordinates. title: Two-dimensional binary Lennard-Jones mixtures with ECMC
abstract: We discuss reversible and non-reversible local Monte Carlo algorithms for long-range two-dimensional binary Lennard-Jones mixtures. We illustrate how the factorized Metropolis filter efficiently handles long-range interactions even for binary mixtures, using an adapted cell-veto strategy. We then benchmark the non-reversible event-chain Monte Carlo (ECMC) algorithm against the factorized Metropolis algorithm. title: Co-Optimization of Network Topology and Variable Impedance Devices under Dynamic Line Ratings Using Iterative McCormick Relaxation
abstract: Grid Enhancing Technologies (GETs), such as Network Topology Optimization (NTO), Dynamic Line Rating (DLR), and Variable Impedance Devices (VIDs) are increasingly deployed in power transmission grids to address congestion and improve grid utilization. However, their growing adoption necessitates coordinated operation to fully exploit their benefits. This paper presents a unified co-optimization framework that integrates NTO, DLR, and VID to alleviate congestion and minimize operational costs. abstract: Continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs) and speculative drafters offer efficient language generation but are typically evaluated differently: CDLMs generate independently through iterative refinement, whereas drafters propose text for target-model verification and correction. We compare their architectures without verification, using LangFlow for CDLMs and adapting DSpark's Markov and recurrent-head architectures for standalone generation. This uncertainty is particularly important in the far-infrared (FIR) spectral region, where the optical properties of natural mineral dust, especially its complex refractive index (CRI), remain poorly known. abstract: In clonal organisms, the genetic individual (genet) may consist of several physiological individuals (ramets). abstract: We study the effect of constant vorticity on the Benjamin-Feir instability of small-amplitude Stokes waves in infinite depth. title: Stationary Structures of the Boussinesq equations
abstract: We investigate the steady configurations supported by the inviscid two-dimensional Boussinesq equations in the periodic channel. We show steady laminar velocity fields (closed non-contractible fluid trajectories) coupled to non-decreasing density stratifications are necessarily stratified shear flows. title: Coexistence of superconductivity and magnetic order in BaFe$_2$S$_3$: evidence for orbital-selective delocalization
abstract: Understanding how superconductivity emerges from correlated electronic states is a central challenge in condensed matter physics. The quasi-one-dimensional spin-ladder compound \bfs\ serves as a unique platform to study this interplay, as it lacks the two-dimensional square lattice characteristic of most iron-based superconductors. title: GARDEN: Generalist Autonomous Reward Design Through Evidence Navigation for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) enables teams of agents, such as robots and autonomous vehicles, to learn coordinated behavior, but what such teams learn is largely determined by their reward function. Because task success alone provides too little guidance for learning, intermediate rewards are usually designed by hand, and this effort must often be repeated whenever the environment or the team changes. Large language models (LLMs) can automate the effort by writing reward functions as code, yet the resulting rewards are typically designed and tested in a single setting.

title: An Open-Source Hybrid Ray-Tracing and 3GPP Channel Simulator for Non-Terrestrial Network
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid channel simulation framework that combines site-specific ray tracing (RT) with 3GPP-compliant statistical channel simulation for non-terrestrial networks (NTNs). The proposed approach uses RT to generate dominant propagation paths and augments them with statistically generated paths and subpaths to provide richer multipath realizations under practical simulation complexity. title: Weak-coupling selection and finite-torus entropy in the triangular Ising antiferromagnet
abstract: An antiferromagnetic second-neighbor interaction favors stripe order in the triangular-lattice Ising antiferromagnet, but uniform stripes cannot satisfy odd periodic boundaries. At each fixed odd size $L\geq5$, we minimize this interaction over the ground states of the zero-field nearest-neighbor model on an $L\times L$ torus. We prove a minimum total interface length of $4L$ and classify all $L^2(L^2-1)/2$ selected states. Under the uniform measure on these states, the area fractions of the three stripe orientations approach a uniform distribution over all nonnegative triples summing to one.

title: ROD-Dataset: A Pedestrian-Perspective Benchmark of Urban Obstacle Classes for YOLO-Based Detection
abstract: Two groups of pedestrians face avoidable risk on the city sidewalk: people living with visual impairment, who reach an obstacle before anything warns them, and people walking with divided attention, who register a hazard late or not at all. A vision system can warn them only about obstacles it has learned to recognize, so its training data limits the protection it offers. title: The neutrino fog for inelastic dark matter
abstract: We characterize the behavior of the neutrino fog for inelastic dark matter scattering on xenon. The inelastic scattering kinematics reshape the recoil spectrum of the signal and produce a qualitatively different neutrino fog landscape. In some regions of the inelastic parameter space the fog is completely absent for future xenon experiments at any scale, while in other regions the fog is dispelled only to reappear at larger exposures. title: Long-Term Trend of Noctilucent Cloud Altitude Detected: A Comparison of Positional Data with Historical Measurements
abstract: A large number of photometric and photographic position data of noctilucent clouds (NLC) obtained at 54-61 deg N, 29-50 deg E in 2020-2026 is used, comprising about 20,000 individual measurements of the altitude of NLC fragments recorded by a number of cameras. Comparison with published long-base triangulation measurements starting from 1890 reveals a descending trend in NLC altitude with a 99.5% confidence level. title: X-ray magnetic circular dichroism in altermagnets: insights from symmetry
abstract: Altermagnets are a unique subset of antiferromagnets possessing ferromagnet-like responses that are odd in the Néel vector, making X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) a natural probe of ground state altermagnetic order. Because the relativistic ingredient of XMCD at the $L$-edge is supplied predominantly by core-level spin--orbit coupling (SOC), the dichroic signal can reflect the non-relativistic order of the valence electrons. abstract: The observed bimodal radius distribution of close-in small planets provides important constraints on their formation and evolution. Two atmospheric escape mechanisms, photoevaporation and core-powered mass loss, have been widely invoked to explain this distribution. abstract: Entanglement entropy scaling links geometry to quantum correlations and diagnoses quantum criticality. title: Effect of sampling on the descriptive distributions of correlated random walks
abstract: Random walks are commonly used to model movement throughout the sciences, from the motion of particles and molecules to the observed behaviour of animals and crowds. abstract: Abstract Age and growth-related data provide key insights into life-history strategies, yet remain scarce for neotropical amphibians, particularly arboreal species inhabiting highly seasonal environments. We used skeletochronology to conduct the first empirical assessment of sex-specific aging and somatic growth patterns of an arboreal frog from the Pacific dry forest of Ecuador. We found limited support for the “breed fast, die young” pace of life that would be expected in highly seasonal environments. abstract: PURPOSE: Dry Eye Disease (DED) is highly prevalent among university students and may be influenced by modifiable factors such as psychological stress and sleep disturbance. The primary objective of this study was to investigate the associations of sleep disturbance and perceived stress with DED, while the secondary objective was to evaluate their potential interaction. abstract: Context Large shifts in species distributions are projected under future climate scenarios, yet long-term empirical evidence remains scarce, particularly for invertebrates. title: How climate change already impacts people who use alcohol and other drugs: Australian service staff perspectives
abstract: Increased prevalence and intensity of extreme weather events, as well as more gradual climatic shifts, have disproportionate impacts for people who experience poverty and stigmatisation. This includes many who engage with alcohol and other drug (AoD) services. abstract: The emergence of biomolecular homochirality requires both an initial symmetry-breaking event and a mechanism to amplify and preserve a chiral imbalance. abstract: The geomorphic history of Grand Canyon, and especially Western Grand Canyon, remains unsettled. abstract: Abstract Perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) offer exceptional colour purity and efficiency for next-generation display applications. Despite the recent advances in device stability, achieving long-term stable PeLEDs under display-relevant conditions remains a critical challenge. The actual device half-life (T 50 ) experimentally measured for visible PeLEDs were in most cases limited to below 1000 h for any given brightness, in contrast to the much longer extrapolated lifetimes reported. abstract: Abstract Background Migration is a complex behaviour, requiring individuals to integrate genetic, environmental and social information to reach distant goals, with important consequences for individuals, populations and communities. However, despite its ecological importance, our understanding of the development of migration behaviour across an organism’s lifetime is lacking for most taxa. abstract: ABSTRACT Real-time radiation monitoring in high-dose-rate environments such as nuclear decommissioning sites requires robust sensing technologies that can withstand extreme conditions. A promising approach is fiber-optic radiation detection, in which scintillation light is remotely collected through an optical fiber. However, this approach is hampered by noise from the optical fiber itself, particularly for shorter-wavelength emissions. title: A microfluidic model of bacterial keratitis to quantify the efficacy of anti-infective compounds under flow
abstract: AIMS: Bacterial infections of the cornea, also known as bacterial keratitis, are a major cause of blindness. The corneal surface is protected against infection by the flow of tear fluid, which displaces potential pathogens and debris. Whilst fluid flow is known to influence the behaviour of both bacterial and epithelial cells, most models of corneal infection use static conditions. Here, we develop a microfluidic model to directly visualise interactions between bacteria and human corneal epithelial cells (HCE2) in physiologically relevant flow conditions. abstract: As the global climate crisis intensifies, and with the establishment of the 1.5℃ temperature control target by the Paris Agreement, relying only on emission reduction makes it difficult to reach the net zero target. abstract: Trilobite biofacies are often indicative of particular paleoecological settings and can reveal spatial paleogeographic changes. title: Glycocalyx Remodeling Shapes Cancer Cell Mechanics
abstract: The glycocalyx - a complex meshwork of sugars, proteins, and lipids - coats all human cells and plays a crucial role in cell signaling and immune system regulation. While an understanding of its biochemical functions is emerging, its influence on cell mechanics remains comparably underexplored. abstract: Background: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is defined as glucose intolerance first recognized during pregnancy.it is one of the most common metabolic disorders complicating pregnancy. there is an increased burden of GDM and its significant consequences for maternal and child health. abstract: Since the emergence of molecular phylogenetics, several genera within the Zygnematophyceae have been shown to be polyphyletic. title: RGB Image-Based Retrieval of Extinction Coefficients and Ångström Exponent for Fog Characterization
abstract: Abstract Fog is a meteorological phenomenon that significantly impacts traffic safety and public health. However, real-time monitoring remains challenging due to the spatially sparse distribution of dedicated observation networks. This is particularly problematic given the highly localized nature of fog formation. This study proposes an RGB image-based method to derive fog optical properties—specifically the extinction coefficient at three visible wavelengths (R:597nm, G:534nm, B:459nm) and the Ångström exponent (AE)— from pixel intensity differences of objects located at known distances. abstract: Layered crustal structures modulate the static co‑seismic displacement field. This study uses numerical simulation to investigate how elastic layered media, including high‑velocity layers (HVL) and low‑velocity layers (LVL), affect static co‑seismic displacement fields, with application to the 1976 Tangshan earthquake. abstract: Eucalyptus L’Hér. spp. is one of the most important plantation tree crops worldwide. The present study reviews contemporary biotechnological approaches to its improvement. Key advantages of eucalyptus include high productivity, rapid growth, broad economic applications – ranging from pulp and timber production to essential oil extraction and carbon sequestration, as well as its ability to adapt to diverse soil and climatic conditions and accumulate biomass intensively. abstract: Flooding in the Lake Titicaca basin poses a critical risk to communities and infrastructure, and endangers human lives. Dikes are commonly used to protect against flooding, but their stability is essential to their effectiveness. This study examines the stability of embankment slopes on the Ilave River dams through hydraulic and geotechnical modelling, using the limit equilibrium method with specialized software. abstract: ABSTRACT To synergistically enhance the strength‐ductility trade‑off and achieve uniform degradation in Fe‐Zn alloys, heterostructured alloy microtubes were fabricated via layer‑by‑layer electrodeposition on a rotating soluble aluminum mandrel. abstract: Catfish (Clarias sp.) is an economically important freshwater aquaculture commodity in Indonesia. However, bacterial infections can compromise fish health and growth performance, highlighting the need for natural feed additives that support sustainable aquaculture. abstract: This essay examines error management culture as a higher-order dynamic capability that fosters organizational learning, innovation, psychological safety, and strategic renewal. abstract: In Northern Europe, growing a mixture of shade-tolerant spruce and light-demanding birch instead of monocultures of either species is a potential way to improve forest resilience and adaptation to climate change. Planting both species at the establishment phase is a rare practice in silviculture, but it can be a viable approach for success in designing the mixture. abstract: A field experiment was conducted during kharif 2020 at the Fodder Demonstration Unit, National Dairy Development Board, Anand, Gujarat, to evaluate ten maize cultivars for fodder yield and silage quality using a randomized block design with three replications. abstract: Teaching waste poses a pedagogical difficulty: the matter that most demands critical attention is the matter students least want to touch. abstract: : Bacterial spot, caused by Xanthomonas arboricola pv . pruni ( Xap ), is a major disease impacting peach production in the southeastern United States. abstract: ABSTRACT Introduced to Hawai‘i in 2016, Lema equestris has become a garden pest commonly reported on Solanum americanum , which is grown as a native and cultural plant in Hawai‘i and supports native vertebrates elsewhere across Oceania. Originally identified as L. solani , the species was later found to have been misidentified. abstract: Abstract In recent years, with the advancement of precision nutrition and biotherapy concepts, the demand for efficient and targeted delivery of functional active substances, especially probiotics, has become increasingly urgent. Chitosan, a natural, non-toxic, and biodegradable alkaline cationic polysaccharide, has emerged as a key material for constructing intelligent delivery systems due to its unique biological properties and modifiability. abstract: Nucleophilic substitution reactions are among the most commonly executed reactions employed in the synthesis of pharmaceutical compounds. Alkyl halides or pseudohalides are typically employed as the electrophilic reagents in these reactions, but both the reactions in which these electrophilic species are formed and the processes used to generate the precursors required for these reactions are highly resource intensive and result in very significant waste generation. abstract: The degradation of arable lands is becoming widespread and leads to significant loss of soil organic matter (SOM), expressed both in quantitative losses and in qualitative changes in the molecular and elemental composition of SOM. abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how infection‐related traits vary across parasite populations and host stages is key to predicting host–parasite dynamics in complex life cycles. title: Reduction of Tree Water Stress by Large Herbivores in an African Savanna
abstract: Large mammalian herbivores (LMH) play complex roles in shaping tree cover and composition in savannas by suppressing trees through browsing and reducing competition from neighbouring trees and understory vegetation. Where LMH are declining, release from browsing and intensification of competition has unpredictable physiological consequences. abstract: La creciente demanda alimentaria induce a la degradación de los recursos naturales, posicionando al sistema silvopastoril (SSP) como una alternativa de mitigación ambiental. title: Politicisation and intervention repertoires of democratic and hybrid-authoritarian states: evidence from intrastate conflicts in the wider Mediterranean
abstract: Abstract This article examines how regime type shapes the politicisation and depoliticisation of intervention behaviour in intrastate conflicts. Focusing on external interventions across the wider Mediterranean region, it explains why democratic and hybrid-authoritarian states employ different intervention repertoires. We argue that domestic audience costs and institutional constraints shape the political feasibility, visibility, and escalation thresholds of external support. title: Effect of Water Content on the Tribological Properties of Grease
abstract: ABSTRACT In mechanical lubrication systems, grease can become contaminated with water due to seal failure and high ambient humidity. Water can alter the fibrous network of the thickener in grease, leading to base‐oil separation, reduced consistency and abnormal oil bleeding. In this study, experiments were combined with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the tribological behaviour of lubricating systems with different water contents, together with changes in parameters such as density distribution and system height. title: Screech in rocket nozzles undergoing free shock separation
abstract: Flow separation in rocket nozzles generates intense side loads that can lead to structural damage affecting space flight safety. Recent studies have hypothesised that a screech-like resonance loop may be responsible for such oscillations in the free shock separation (FSS) regime. In this work, we aim to confirm if screech is indeed present in this flow. title: Propulsion systems for a starshade rendezvous mission with the Habitable World Observatory
abstract: We assess how propulsion and operational constraints shape the exo-Earth characterization performance of a starshade rendezvous architecture for a Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO)–like telescope at Sun–Earth L2. Using end-to-end Monte Carlo mission simulations with EXOSIMS, we model two representative starshade point designs: a 60 m occulter optimized for visible-band (VIS) spectroscopy (500 to 1000 nm) and a 35 m occulter optimized for near-ultraviolet (NUV) characterization (250 to 550 nm). title: Complementary hemispheric functions during spontaneous exploration in Hermann’s tortoises
abstract: Brain lateralization is a widespread feature of vertebrate nervous systems, yet evidence from reptiles remains limited. We investigated behavioural lateralization in Hermann's tortoises (Testudo hermanni) during spontaneous exploration of a novel environment. Forty-six adult tortoises were observed in a rectangular arena allowing free exploration of two lateral end-zones connected by a central corridor, over three sessions, revealing a dissociation in the direction of lateralization across different behavioural measures. title: L'éducation malgache et l'apprentissage numérique à Madagascar
abstract: Cet article analyse l'évolution historique du système éducatif malgache, depuis les pratiques d'éducation traditionnelle et orale précoloniales jusqu'aux tentatives contemporaines d'intégration des technologies de l'information et de la communication (TIC) dans l'enseignement. En mobilisant une approche historique appuyée sur une revue bibliographique systématique, l'étude retrace les grandes ruptures pédagogiques : l'apport des missionnaires protestants sous Radama Ier, la structuration coloniale française (1896–1960), la malgachisation socialiste (1975–1991), les réformes post-démocratiques

title: Perancangan Film Pendek Animasi 2D Mengenai Dampak Polusi Cahaya Terhadap Lingkungan dan Ekosistem

Di Indonesia, penyebaran informasi mengenai dampak polusi cahaya masih terbatas, terutama melalui media yang menarik dan mudah dipahami oleh masyarakat usia muda. title: Revision of Asparagus L. sect. Myrsiphyllum (Willd.) Baker ex H.Perrier (Asparagaceae) from Madagascar, with the description of five new species and two new varieties
abstract: Asparagus L. sect. Myrsiphyllum (Willd.) Baker ex H.Perrier, which includes the members of the genus with phylloclades, is defined and revised for Madagascar and the Comoro Islands based primarily on morphological evidence. This builds on earlier treatments of the group, taking into account the wealth of new material now available. In this study, nine species are recognised, including five species and two varieties that are new to science: A. andriamihajarivoi M.Pignal & Phillipson sp. nov., A. bambusiformis M.Pignal & Phillipson sp. nov., A. laticladus M.Pignal & Phillipson sp. nov., A. messm

title: Direct electrification and hydrogen-based pathways in EU passenger transport: Energy, environmental, and material implications
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen-based passenger transport pathways are increasingly considered as potential decarbonization options in the European Union’s (EU) energy transition, particularly for long-distance and high-utilization applications where direct electrification may face operational constraints. However, their representation in Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs) and their system-wide energy, environmental, and material implications remain insufficiently assessed. title: Comparative mobilization and bioaccumulation of cadmium and lead in apple orchards and associated screening level ecological and human health risks
abstract: Abstract Lead (Pb) and cadmium (Cd) accumulate in agricultural soils through long-term agrochemical use, posing ecosystem and food-safety risks; whether these inputs elevate Pb and Cd in edible fruit had not previously been quantified for Iranian apple orchards. This screening-level, multi-index study assessed Pb and Cd across the fertilizer/pesticide–soil–fruit continuum in Padena, Semirom, combining paired soil and root-stem-fruit tissue analysis ( n = 36) with ecological and deterministic human health risk indices for adults and children. abstract: Marine surface vehicles (MSVs) have attracted considerable attention for their commercial, scientific, and military applications. Owing to their favorable performance-to-cost ratio, shipboard cameras are widely used to detect and recognize potentially hazardous situations across diverse operational scenarios. However, visual perception is inevitably degraded by restricted conditions, including irregular motion of the imaging platform, adverse weather, and long imaging distances. title: CineCap: Structured Reasoning with Spatio-Temporal Anchors for Cinematographic Video Captioning
abstract: Cinematographic captioning aims to describe how a video is filmed using professional film-language concepts such as camera movement, shot size, depth of field, composition, and shooting angle. This capability is important for fine-grained video understanding and controllable movie-quality video generation, yet remains underexplored in existing multimodal large language models. title: Muography Simulations for Carbon Capture and Storage Monitoring
abstract: Muography can monitor CO2 storage through reservoir density changes, but site-scale simulations are costly: reservoirs can be deep and borehole detectors are small. title: Smooth Threshold GARCH: Quasi Maximum Likelihood Estimation and Empirical Evidence
abstract: It is well established that the volatility of daily stock returns responds asymmetrically to news, as described by the news impact curve (NIC), which relates volatility to the previous return. Empirical studies suggest that (i) volatility reacts more strongly to negative returns than to positive returns of the same magnitude, (ii) the point of asymmetry, where the NIC attains its minimum, is positive, and (iii) returns above this point often do not increase volatility at all. title: Gearbox cavities: Ultrahigh wave confinement via broken rotational symmetry
abstract: Cavity enhancement of emission from a point source typically relies on structures that preserve its cylindrical symmetry, such as circular Bragg gratings. Combining inverse design with fundamental limits, we show that breaking this symmetry is necessary to maximize the local density of states in lossless two-dimensional cavities. Symmetry-broken designs exceed limits over all cylindrically symmetric structures by up to eight orders of magnitude, acting as ``gearboxes'' that convert the source's emission into high-angular-momentum waves trapped behind a centrifugal barrier.

title: Advance identification of where the 2026 Kumamoto earthquake would begin
abstract: Long-term forecasts say how likely a fault segment is to rupture, not where the rupture will begin. The b-value, the slope of the earthquake size distribution, falls as stress rises. After the 2016 Kumamoto sequence in Japan, b-values rose along the ruptured faults but fell in the unruptured central part of the Hinagu fault zone, which we identified in 2019 as where the next rupture was most likely to begin. title: The Generalised Kessler Syndrome and the Persian Gulf
abstract: The term Kessler syndrome was coined for a runaway orbital cascade creating a high-density debris field. The idea is generalised and applied to supply chains. An additive channel enables failures to generate further failures; a subtractive channel erodes the capacity to contain and restore.
